   then every bucket net automatically satisfies \((DCR1)\).  For independent
   uniform resident directions, \((DCR3)\) holds with probability at least
   \(1-m^{-2}\) when \(D\ge C_K\log^3m\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Under \((DCR1)\), the high-correlation tail \(H_{\rm hi}\) in
   \((LHS1)\) is zero.  Under \((DCR2)\), it is already within the desired
   polylogarithmic storage allowance.  Therefore
   \cref{cor:low-high-compressed-cap-storage}, with \(s=\rho_{j+1}\), gives
   \[
      \sum_A|A|^{1+\rho_{j+1}}
      \le
      m^{1+\rho_j}\log^{O_c(1)}m
   \]
   after verifying and resampling the randomized cap panel when the proof uses
   an expectation.  This is exactly \((CBK3)\).  The assumed metadata bound and
   \((CBK1)\)--\((CBK2)\) are the other two checklist items, so
   \cref{cor:compressed-bucket-rung-checklist} applies, and hence
   \cref{prop:success-normalized-bucket-dag} supplies the rung.

   If \((DCR3)\) holds for all of \(P\), then each \(N_i\subseteq P\), so
   \((DCR1)\) is immediate.  For the random-position statement, the standard
   spherical cap bound gives
   \(\Pr[\ip{X}{Y}>K\log\log m/\log m]\le
   \exp(-\Omega_K(D\log^2\log m/\log^2m))\) for two independent uniform
   directions.  A union bound over at most \(m^2\) pairs gives \((DCR3)\) with
   probability at least \(1-m^{-2}\) after increasing \(C_K\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cap-prefix pricing of compressed-cap high tails]
   \label{cor:compressed-cap-high-tail-prefix-pricing}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:low-high-compressed-cap-storage}, and assume in addition that
   \(0<\theta_m\le1/2\) and that the current local filter-cover instance is the
   unit-sphere case of
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-paid-prefix-quadratic}, with \(o=0\), \(R=1\),
   \(\gamma=\theta_m\), child exponent \(0\le\rho_+\le1\), and all centers
   \(x\in P\) available.  Thus
   \[
      c_x=\theta_m x,
      \qquad
      R_+=\sqrt{1-\theta_m^2},
      \qquad
      W_x=P\cap B(c_x,R_+),
      \tag{CHT1}
   \]
   with activation \(a_x^+\), paid degree \(d_x^+(y)\), and query price
   \(A_x^+\) as in \((CPQ3)\)--\((CPQ5)\).

   For a realized cap panel and bucket nets \(N_i\), define the
   high-correlation tail multiplicity
   \[
      M_x(y)
      =
      \left|
      \{i:\ x,y\in N_i,\ x\ne y,\ \ip{x}{y}>\theta_m\}
      \right|,
      \qquad
      H_{\rm hi}=\sum_{x,y\in P}M_x(y).
      \tag{CHT2}
   \]
   Split it by the cap-centered paid degree:
   \[
      M_x^{\rm pay}(y)=\min\{M_x(y),d_x^+(y)\},
      \qquad
      M_x^{\rm over}(y)=\bigl(M_x(y)-d_x^+(y)\bigr)_+ ,
      \tag{CHT3}
   \]
   and put
   \[
      H_{\rm over}=\sum_{x,y}M_x^{\rm over}(y).
      \tag{CHT4}
   \]
   If \(M^{\rm pay}\equiv0\), set \(J_{\rm pay}=1\).  Otherwise suppose the
   positive values of \(M_x^{\rm pay}(y)\) lie in a certified dyadic range with
   dynamic-range factor \(J_{\rm pay}\).  Fix \(\Lambda>0\), and suppose every
   paid-clipped dyadic superlevel
   \[
      U_{x,t}^{\rm pay}=\{y:M_x^{\rm pay}(y)\ge t\}
      \tag{CHT5}
   \]
   with \(t|U_{x,t}^{\rm pay}|\ge\Lambda\) has cap-centered child price below
   \(\Lambda\):
   \[
      e^{B_0\theta_m^2}\Psi(R_+)
      \left(
         A_x^+|U_{x,t}^{\rm pay}|^{\rho_+}
         +\sigma |U_{x,t}^{\rm pay}|^{1+\rho_+}
      \right)
      <\Lambda .
      \tag{CHT6}
   \]
   Then either a \((B_0+3)\)-quadratic cap-centered paid-prefix repair fires, or
   \[
      H_{\rm hi}\le H_{\rm over}+2mJ_{\rm pay}\Lambda .
      \tag{CHT7}
   \]
   Consequently, in a no-repair residual satisfying \((CHT6)\),
   \[
      \E\sum_{A\in\mathcal A}|A|^{1+s}
      \le
      m^{1+\rho}\log^{O_{A,K}(1)}m
      +
      \E H_{\rm over}
      +
      2mJ_{\rm pay}\Lambda .
      \tag{CHT8}
   \]
   If \(H_{\rm over}\) and the fixed dyadic tail in \((CHT8)\) are
   \(m^{1+\rho}\polylog m\), then the shared-DAG storage hypothesis \((CBK3)\)
   follows after the same verified resampling step as in
   \cref{cor:low-high-compressed-cap-storage}.

   Thus the high-correlation output of compressed cap buckets is not a
   free-standing Renyi storage problem.  Its paid part is either a
   same-prefix quadratic dense repair or a fixed dyadic tail, and the only
   potentially polynomial survivor is the explicit overload
   \(H_{\rm over}\), where cap incidence exceeds the cap-centered paid
   near-pair degree.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(M_x(y)>0\), then \(\ip{x}{y}>\theta_m\).  By
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-pair-star-reporter}, this implies
   \(y\in W_x\), so the support condition \((CCH1)\) holds for the
   multiplicity family \(M_x(y)\).

   Apply \cref{cor:clipped-cap-centered-high-correlation-handoff} with
   \(\gamma=\theta_m\).  Its threshold form \((CCH7)\), together with the
   price assumption \((CHT6)\), gives exactly the alternative: either a
   \((B_0+3)\)-quadratic cap-centered paid-prefix repair fires, or
   \[
      H_{\rm hi}\le H_{\rm over}+2|P|J_{\rm pay}\Lambda .
   \]
   Since \(|P|\le m\), this proves \((CHT7)\).

   In a no-repair residual satisfying \((CHT6)\), substitute \((CHT7)\) into
   \((LHS2)\).  The term \(2mJ_{\rm pay}\Lambda\) is deterministic under the
   certified dynamic-range bound, so taking expectation gives \((CHT8)\).  The
   final deterministic storage statement is the same Markov-and-verification
   resampling argument used at the end of
   \cref{cor:low-high-compressed-cap-storage}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Compressed-cap high tails are storage-only after quadratic repair]
   \label{cor:compressed-cap-high-tail-storage-only}
   Work in a localized compressed-cap rung satisfying the query and metadata
   hypotheses of \cref{cor:diffuse-compressed-cap-rung}, but do not assume the
   diffuse condition \((DCR1)\).  Assume the high-tail verifier is run in the
   setting of \cref{cor:compressed-cap-high-tail-prefix-pricing}, with
   \(\gamma=\theta_m\), and that the paid-clipped levels satisfy the price
   precondition \((CHT6)\) for a certified threshold \(\Lambda\).

   If no cap-centered paid-prefix repair fires and the overload plus fixed
   dyadic tail obeys
   \[
      \E H_{\rm over}
      +
      2mJ_{\rm pay}\Lambda
      \le
      m^{1+\rho_j}\log^{O_c(1)}m,
      \tag{CSO1}
   \]
   then, after verified Las Vegas resampling of the randomized cap panel, all
   hypotheses of \cref{prop:success-normalized-bucket-dag} hold for this rung
   with polylogarithmic loss.

   If a cap-centered paid-prefix repair does fire, the retained child is a
   \((B_0+3)\)-quadratic local repair.  Consequently, on any localized
   near-neighbor lineage, an arbitrary sequence of such paid-prefix repairs
   contributes only a polylogarithmic multiplicative toll, provided their
   certified child radii satisfy the cap-recentering radius certificates.

   Thus the compressed-cap positive-correlation branch has no remaining
   geometric-depth obstruction.  After the low-correlation co-load estimate and
   the paid-prefix screen, the only storage quantity that still has to be
   sponsored, merged, or separated by generated columns is the overload
   \(H_{\rm over}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   In the no-repair case, \cref{cor:compressed-cap-high-tail-prefix-pricing}
   gives the storage estimate \((CHT8)\).  Substituting \((CSO1)\) into that
   estimate yields
   \[
      \E\sum_{A\in\mathcal A}|A|^{1+\rho_{j+1}}
      \le
      m^{1+\rho_j}\log^{O_c(1)}m .
   \]
   The builder verifies the realized left side of \((CBK3)\) and resamples
   rejected cap panels; Markov's inequality gives constant expected resampling
   after increasing the implicit logarithmic constant.  Hence the shared-DAG
   storage condition \((CBK3)\) holds on the accepted panel.  The query and
   metadata hypotheses are exactly the other checklist items in
   \cref{cor:compressed-bucket-rung-checklist}, so
   \cref{prop:success-normalized-bucket-dag} applies.

   If the paid-prefix verifier fires, the same corollary identifies the column
   as a \((B_0+3)\)-quadratic cap-centered paid-prefix repair.  Along a
   localized lineage, the cap-recentering radius certificates are the
   hypotheses \((QPT1)\) of
   \cref{cor:quadratic-positive-toll-compiler}.  Applying that compiler with
   \(A=B_0+3\) gives a total factor \(\log^{O_c(1)}n\) for all such fired
   repairs.  Therefore repeated paid high-tail repairs do not create a
   superpolylogarithmic overhead; any surviving polynomial obstruction must be
   the overload term left in \((CHT8)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Compressed-cap overload is a Hall-tail object]
   \label{cor:compressed-cap-overload-hall-tail}
   Work in the no-repair residual of
   \cref{cor:compressed-cap-high-tail-prefix-pricing}.  Atomize the
   high-correlation compressed-cap incidences by creating, for every ordered
   pair \((x,y)\) with \(M_x(y)>0\), one atom \(i=(x,y)\) with point
   \(p_i=y\), weight \(b_i=M_x(y)\), and singleton admissible center set
   \(\mathcal X_i=\{x\}\).  Interpret
   \cref{lem:cap-centered-transport-hall} with congestion \(C=1\), the
   cap-centered children \(W_x\), and the paid degrees \(d_x^+(y)\) from
   \((CHT1)\).

   Let
   \[
      \mathcal A_{\rm over}
      =
      \{(x,y):M_x(y)>d_x^+(y)\}.
      \tag{CHO1}
   \]
   Then \(\mathcal A_{\rm over}\) has Hall excess exactly
   \[
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\mathcal A_{\rm over}}M_x(y)
      -
      \sum_{(x,y,q)\in N(\mathcal A_{\rm over})}
         \alpha_{y,q}a_x^+(q)
      =
      H_{\rm over}.
      \tag{CHO2}
   \]
   Consequently, for every \(0\le\Omega<H_{\rm over}\), the cap-centered Hall
   condition \((COD1)\) fails with allowed tail \(\Omega\).

   If the positive overload values
   \[
      O_x(y)=\bigl(M_x(y)-d_x^+(y)\bigr)_+
      \tag{CHO3}
   \]
   lie in a certified dyadic range \([O_{\min},O_{\max}]\), and
   \[
      J_{\rm over}
      =
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{O_{\max}}{O_{\min}}\right\rceil ,
      \tag{CHO4}
   \]
   then there are a center \(x\in P\) and dyadic level \(t\) such that the pure
   overload star
   \[
      U_{x,t}^{\rm over}=\{y:O_x(y)\ge t\}
      \tag{CHO5}
   \]
   is contained in \(W_x\) and satisfies
   \[
      t|U_{x,t}^{\rm over}|
      >
      \frac{\Omega}{2mJ_{\rm over}} .
      \tag{CHO6}
   \]

   Suppose such a pure overload star is canonicalized to one shared child
   \(\kappa\) with witness net \(A_\kappa\subseteq U_{x,t}^{\rm over}\), tuple
   order \(k_\kappa\), and storage price \(u_\kappa\).  Treat every atom
   \((x,y)\in\mathcal A_{\rm over}\) with \(y\in U_{x,t}^{\rm over}\) as a
   weighted occurrence of this same child, with occurrence weight \(M_x(y)\).
   Then the reciprocal weighted-multiplicity identity of
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-overload-weighted-storage} charges this overload
   cohort by one copy of \(u_\kappa\), not by one copy per compressed-cap
   incidence.

   Thus \(H_{\rm over}\) is the standard Hall/sponsor residual used later in
   the proof.  Either it admits bounded-congestion transport into paid
   cap-centered degrees, or it exposes a dyadic pure overload star that enters
   the shared-child storage, sponsor-flow, and generated-column interfaces.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If atom \((x,y)\) is present, then \(M_x(y)>0\), so the proof of
   \cref{cor:compressed-cap-high-tail-prefix-pricing} gives \(y\in W_x\) and
   \(\ip{x}{y}>\theta_m\).  Hence the cap-centered Hall support hypothesis
   \((CTH1)\) holds with admissible center set \(\{x\}\).

   For a fixed overloaded pair \((x,y)\), the neighboring capacity nodes are
   exactly the triples \((x,y,q)\) with \((y,q)\in\mathcal N\) and
   \(a_x^+(q)>0\).  Their total capacity is
   \[
      \sum_{q:(y,q)\in\mathcal N}\alpha_{y,q}a_x^+(q)
      =
      d_x^+(y).
   \]
   Summing over \(\mathcal A_{\rm over}\) gives \((CHO2)\).  If
   \(\Omega<H_{\rm over}\), this subset violates \((COD1)\), so the Hall
   condition fails with allowed tail \(\Omega\).

   Apply \cref{cor:cap-centered-overload-dichotomy} and then
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-hall-overload-stars} to this failed Hall cut, using
   the canonical selector \(s(x,y)=x\) and \(C=1\).  For the selected atoms,
   \(B_x^s(y)=M_x(y)\), so the overload multiplicity \((COS2)\) is precisely
   \(O_x(y)\) from \((CHO3)\).  Since the center set has size at most \(m\),
   the dyadic layer-cake conclusion gives \((CHO5)\)--\((CHO6)\) and the
   containment \(U_{x,t}^{\rm over}\subseteq W_x\).

   The final storage statement is exactly
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-overload-weighted-storage} applied to this pure
   overload star and to the selected overloaded atoms.  That corollary is stated
   for weighted atom occurrences, so the integer compressed-cap multiplicity
   \(M_x(y)\) is used only as the occurrence weight.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Generated-column endpoint for compressed-cap overload]
   \label{cor:compressed-cap-overload-generated-column}
   Work after the canonicalization step of
   \cref{cor:compressed-cap-overload-hall-tail}.  Let
   \(\mathcal C_{\rm ccap}\) be the finite family of distinct canonical
   overload children retained from the dyadic pure overload stars.  A child
   \(\kappa\in\mathcal C_{\rm ccap}\) has witness net
   \(A_\kappa\), price factor \(\psi_\kappa\), exponent
   \(0\le\rho_\kappa\le1\), and storage price
   \[
      u_\kappa=\psi_\kappa|A_\kappa|^{1+\rho_\kappa}.
      \tag{CCG1}
   \]
   The reciprocal occurrence identity for these children uses the raw
   compressed-cap multiplicities \(M_x(y)\), as in
   \cref{cor:compressed-cap-overload-hall-tail}.  For sponsorship, however,
   use the smaller excess atom pool
   \[
      \mathcal I_{\rm ccap}=\{(x,y):O_x(y)>0\},
      \qquad b_{x,y}=O_x(y),
      \tag{CCG2}
   \]
   so that \(\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{\rm ccap}}b_i=H_{\rm over}\).  Let
   \(\mathcal E_{\rm ccap}\subseteq
   \mathcal I_{\rm ccap}\times\mathcal C_{\rm ccap}\) be any certified
   compatibility relation; the natural one relates an overload atom \((x,y)\)
   to every retained child canonicalized from a pure overload star centered at
   \(x\) and containing \(y\).  Fix \(\beta\ge1\).

   If every child subset \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal C_{\rm ccap}\)
   satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal U}u_\kappa
      \le
      \beta
      \sum_{i\in N_{\rm ccap}(\mathcal U)}b_i,
      \qquad
      N_{\rm ccap}(\mathcal U)
      =
      \{i:\exists\kappa\in\mathcal U,\ (i,\kappa)\in\mathcal E_{\rm ccap}\},
      \tag{CCG3}
   \]
   then the retained compressed-cap overload children have shared storage
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal C_{\rm ccap}}u_\kappa
      \le
      \beta H_{\rm over},
      \tag{CCG4}
   \]
   and their weighted reciprocal pair-witness storage is charged once per
   distinct canonical child.

   If \((CCG3)\) fails, there is an unsponsored cut
   \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal C_{\rm ccap}\).  Put
   \[
      P(\mathcal U)=\sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal U}u_\kappa,\qquad
      B(\mathcal U)=\sum_{i\in N_{\rm ccap}(\mathcal U)}b_i,\qquad
      E^\beta(\mathcal U)=P(\mathcal U)-\beta B(\mathcal U).
      \tag{CCG5}
   \]
   For any \(0<\varepsilon<1\), either every cut is
   \(\varepsilon\)-unsupported and \((CCG3)\) holds with
   \(\beta/(1-\varepsilon)\) in place of \(\beta\), or there is a strong cut
   \(E^\beta(\mathcal U)>\varepsilon P(\mathcal U)>0\).  In the latter case,
   after any generated-merge template family satisfying
   \((UCG2)\)--\((UCG5)\) is admitted, either some generated top prefix is a
   positive shared merge, or there is a dyadic child-price layer
   \[
      L=\{\kappa\in\mathcal U:\theta\le u_\kappa<2\theta\}
      \tag{CCG6}
   \]
   such that, with \(D(\mathcal U)\) as in \((UCG9)\),
   \[
      \theta |L|
      \ge
      \frac{E^\beta(\mathcal U)}{2D(\mathcal U)}
      \tag{CCG7}
   \]
   and, unless the layer is storage-dominated as in \((UCG13)\),
   \[
      N_{\rm gen}(L,\theta)
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{E^\beta(\mathcal U)}
              {8D(\mathcal U)\psi_\star A\,|L|^\rho}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{CCG8}
   \]

   Equivalently, let \(\mathcal R_L\) be any finite family of materializable
   generated records for the exposed layer \(L\), each with represented set
   \(C_R\subseteq L\) and certified shared price \(P_R\).  Assume every record
   is valid for the layer, meaning that if it is admitted as a generated
   template then it captures at least \(\theta\) units of cut price from each
   \(\kappa\in C_R\), and assume \(\mathcal R_L\) covers \(L\).  If the
   no-generated-prefix residual survives, then the covering LP
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Phi_L=\min
      & \displaystyle\sum_{R\in\mathcal R_L}P_R\lambda_R\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{R:\,\kappa\in C_R}\lambda_R\ge1
        \qquad(\kappa\in L),\\[0.8em]
      & \lambda_R\ge0
   \end{array}
      \tag{CCG9}
   \]
   satisfies
   \[
      \Phi_L\ge\frac{\theta |L|}{2}
      \ge
      \frac{E^\beta(\mathcal U)}{4D(\mathcal U)} .
      \tag{CCG10}
   \]
   Hence finite LP duality gives weights \(y_\kappa\ge0\) on \(L\) with
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa\in L}y_\kappa
      \ge
      \frac{\theta |L|}{2},
      \qquad
      \sum_{\kappa\in C_R}y_\kappa\le P_R
      \quad(R\in\mathcal R_L).
      \tag{CCG11}
   \]

   Thus the compressed-cap storage branch has the same endpoint as the generic
   child-panel machinery: either the excess \(H_{\rm over}\) sponsors the
   shared children, a generated merge reduces a strong cut, or one dyadic layer
   carries an explicit weighted range/list-decoding dual obstruction.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The weighted occurrence part is the final assertion of
   \cref{cor:compressed-cap-overload-hall-tail}: raw multiplicities \(M_x(y)\)
   make every canonicalized overload star contribute one copy of its shared
   child price.  The sponsor accounting is separate.  Applying
   \cref{cor:generic-child-panel-sponsor-flow} to the child panel
   \(\mathcal C_{\rm ccap}\), sponsor atoms \(\mathcal I_{\rm ccap}\), weights
   \(b_i\), compatibility relation \(\mathcal E_{\rm ccap}\), and parameter
   \(\beta\) gives \((CCG3)\Rightarrow(CCG4)\), since the total sponsor mass is
   \(H_{\rm over}\).

   If \((CCG3)\) fails, apply
   \cref{cor:generic-unsponsored-cut-generated-column} to the same child panel.
   Its notation \((UCG1)\) is exactly \((CCG5)\).  The weak-cut alternative
   gives the inflated parameter \(\beta/(1-\varepsilon)\), while the strong-cut
   alternative gives \((CCG6)\)--\((CCG8)\).

   For the LP statement, let \(\lambda\) be feasible in \((CCG9)\).  Then
   \[
      \sum_{R\in\mathcal R_L}\lambda_R|C_R|
      =
      \sum_{\kappa\in L}\sum_{R:\,\kappa\in C_R}\lambda_R
      \ge |L|.
   \]
   If \(\Phi_L<\theta|L|/2\), some feasible solution has
   \[
      \sum_R\lambda_R(\theta|C_R|-2P_R)>0,
   \]
   so a record \(R\) satisfies \(\theta|C_R|>2P_R\).  Its corresponding
   generated template prefix then satisfies the positive-prefix inequality
   \((UCG3)\), contradicting the no-generated-prefix residual.  Therefore
   \(\Phi_L\ge\theta|L|/2\), and \((CCG7)\) gives the second inequality in
   \((CCG10)\).  Since \(\mathcal R_L\) covers \(L\), the LP is feasible and
   bounded, and its dual is exactly \((CCG11)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Compressed-cap overload dual low-cover screen]
   \label{cor:compressed-cap-overload-dual-low-cover-screen}
   Work in the no-generated-prefix residual of
   \cref{cor:compressed-cap-overload-generated-column}, and fix a dual
   weighting \(y_\kappa\) satisfying \((CCG11)\) on the exposed layer \(L\).
   Let \(L_0\subseteq L\) be nonempty, put \(K=|L_0|\), and suppose
   \[
      y_\kappa\ge\delta>0
      \qquad(\kappa\in L_0).
      \tag{CCL1}
   \]
   Assume \(L_0\) has a certified generated-record cover by a partition
   \(L_0=L_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup L_J\) into nonempty parts: for every \(i\)
   there is a valid materializable generated record \(R_i\in\mathcal R_L\)
   with
   \[
      L_i\subseteq C_{R_i},
      \qquad
      P_{R_i}
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(A|L_i|^\rho+\zeta |L_i|^{1+\rho}\right),
      \qquad 0<\rho<1 .
      \tag{CCL2}
   \]
   Then every no-prefix residual obeys
   \[
      \delta K
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(AJ^{1-\rho}K^\rho+\zeta K^{1+\rho}\right).
      \tag{CCL3}
   \]
   Hence, when \(A>0\) and
   \[
      \delta>2\psi_\star\zeta K^\rho,
      \tag{CCL4}
   \]
   any surviving residual has
   \[
      J
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{\delta K^{1-\rho}}{2\psi_\star A}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{CCL5}
   \]
   When \(\zeta=0\), the same conclusion holds with \(2\psi_\star A\) replaced
   by \(\psi_\star A\).

   Equivalently, if a range, list-decoding, additive-quantization, facility, or
   tensor cover theorem gives such covers with
   \[
      J\le C_{\rm gen}\lambda^{-\Delta},
      \tag{CCL6}
   \]
   then every surviving residual satisfies
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(
         A C_{\rm gen}^{1-\rho}\lambda^{-\Delta(1-\rho)}K^{\rho-1}
         +\zeta K^\rho
      \right).
      \tag{CCL7}
   \]
   Violation of \((CCL7)\) contradicts the dual constraints \((CCG11)\), and
   therefore produces a positive generated prefix.

   The same lower bound has a packing form.  Let \(d_{\rm gen}\) be a
   pseudometric on \(L_0\), let \(E\subseteq L_0\) be maximal
   \(\Delta_{\rm gen}\)-separated, and assign every \(\kappa\in L_0\) to one
   covering ball \(B_{\rm gen}(e,\Delta_{\rm gen})\), \(e\in E\).  If each
   assigned ball has a valid generated record satisfying \((CCL2)\), then
   \(|E|\) obeys \((CCL5)\) under \((CCL4)\), with the same \(\zeta=0\)
   sharpening.

   Finally, if \(W=\{\kappa\in L:y_\kappa>0\}\),
   \(y_{\min}=\min_Wy_\kappa\), and
   \(y_{\max}=\max_Wy_\kappa\), then for
   \[
      J_y=1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{y_{\max}}{y_{\min}}\right\rceil
      \tag{CCL8}
   \]
   some dyadic dual layer
   \[
      L_j=\{\kappa:2^jy_{\min}\le y_\kappa<2^{j+1}y_{\min}\},
      \qquad
      \delta_j=2^jy_{\min},
      \tag{CCL9}
   \]
   satisfies
   \[
      \delta_j|L_j|
      \ge
      \frac{\theta|L|}{4J_y}
      \ge
      \frac{E^\beta(\mathcal U)}{8D(\mathcal U)J_y}.
      \tag{CCL10}
   \]
   Thus a compressed-cap overload survivor is not merely an LP dual: after
   dyadic unweighting it is a dual-heavy layer on which every certified
   low-cover, low-doubling, range, AQ, facility, tensor, or list-decoding cover
   must have the entropy lower bound \((CCL5)\), unless the
   \(K^{1+\rho}\) storage term already dominates.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For each cover part, \((CCL1)\) and the dual constraint \((CCG11)\) give
   \[
      \delta |L_i|
      \le
      \sum_{\kappa\in L_i}y_\kappa
      \le
      \sum_{\kappa\in C_{R_i}}y_\kappa
      \le P_{R_i}.
   \]
   Summing over \(i\) and using \((CCL2)\) gives
   \[
      \delta K
      \le
      \psi_\star
      \left(
         A\sum_i|L_i|^\rho+\zeta\sum_i|L_i|^{1+\rho}
      \right).
   \]
   Holder's inequality and convexity give
   \[
      \sum_i|L_i|^\rho\le J^{1-\rho}K^\rho,
      \qquad
      \sum_i|L_i|^{1+\rho}\le K^{1+\rho},
   \]
   proving \((CCL3)\).  If \((CCL4)\) holds, the storage term in \((CCL3)\)
   is smaller than \(\delta K/2\), and rearranging gives \((CCL5)\).  With
   \(\zeta=0\), the storage term is absent and the sharper constant follows.
   Substituting \((CCL6)\) in \((CCL3)\) and dividing by \(K\) gives
   \((CCL7)\).  If \((CCL7)\) is violated, at least one record violates
   \((CCG11)\), so
   \cref{cor:compressed-cap-overload-generated-column} gives the positive
   generated-prefix alternative.

   The packing statement follows because balls centered at any maximal
   \(\Delta_{\rm gen}\)-separated set cover \(L_0\); assigning each child to a
   covering ball gives a generated-record cover with \(J=|E|\).

   For the dyadic claim, the layers in \((CCL9)\) partition \(W\), and
   \(y_\kappa<2\delta_j\) on \(L_j\).  Hence
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa\in L}y_\kappa
      \le
      2\sum_j\delta_j|L_j|.
   \]
   Since \((CCG11)\) gives
   \(\sum_{\kappa\in L}y_\kappa\ge\theta|L|/2\), some layer satisfies the first
   inequality in \((CCL10)\).  The second inequality is \((CCG7)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Compressed-cap overload packing-energy endpoint]
   \label{cor:compressed-cap-overload-packing-energy-endpoint}
   Work in the no-generated-prefix residual of
   \cref{cor:compressed-cap-overload-dual-low-cover-screen}.  Let
   \(L_0\subseteq L\) be a dual-heavy layer with \(K=|L_0|\) and
   \(y_\kappa\ge\delta>0\) on \(L_0\).  Let \(d_{\rm gen}\) be a certified
   generated metric on \(L_0\), and suppose every \(\Delta_{\rm gen}\)-ball has
   a valid generated record satisfying \((CCL2)\).  If \(A>0\) and \((CCL4)\)
   holds, then every maximal \(\Delta_{\rm gen}\)-separated
   \(E\subseteq L_0\) satisfies the packing lower bound \((CCL5)\).

   Suppose each \(\kappa\in E\) has a representative
   \(x_\kappa\in\mathbb S^{D-1}\).  Let \(U_G\) be any certified bucket drawn
   from a law \(G\), partition \(E_{\ne}^2\) into profiles \(\Pi_E\), and assume
   \[
      \Pr_G[x_\kappa,x_{\kappa'}\in U_G]\le e^{-I_\pi}
      \qquad((\kappa,\kappa')\in\pi).
      \tag{CCE1}
   \]
   Then, for
   \[
      X_E(G)=\sum_{\kappa\in E}\mathbf 1\{x_\kappa\in U_G\},
      \tag{CCE2}
   \]
   one has
   \[
      \E_GX_E(G)^2
      \le
      \sum_{\kappa\in E}\Pr_G[x_\kappa\in U_G]
      +
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi_E}|\pi|e^{-I_\pi}.
      \tag{CCE3}
   \]
   In particular, if
   \[
      I_\pi\ge\log|\pi|+\Lambda
      \qquad(\pi\in\Pi_E),
      \tag{CCE4}
   \]
   then the total distinct-pair contribution is at most
   \[
      |\Pi_E|e^{-\Lambda}.
      \tag{CCE5}
   \]

   Now specialize to a finite weighted centered Gaussian cap panel
   \(\mathcal R\).  For each \(r\in\mathcal R\), let \(w_r\ge0\),
   \(G_r\sim N(0,I_D)\), and
   \[
      U_r=\{x:\ip{G_r}{x}\ge T_r\}.
      \tag{CCE6}
   \]
   Assume \(m\ge3\), \(|E|\le m\), \(A_{\rm cap},K_{\rm corr}\ge0\),
   \(0\le\rho_{\rm cap}\le1\),
   \[
      T_r^2\ge2\log m-A_{\rm cap}\log\log m,
      \qquad
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r
      \le m^{1+\rho_{\rm cap}}\log^{A_{\rm cap}}m ,
      \tag{CCE7}
   \]
   and put
   \[
      \theta_m=K_{\rm corr}\frac{\log\log m}{\log m}<1 .
      \tag{CCE8}
   \]
   Split ordered distinct pairs into
   \[
      E_{\rm lo}=
      \{(\kappa,\kappa'):\ip{x_\kappa}{x_{\kappa'}}\le\theta_m\},
      \qquad
      E_{\rm hi}=E_{\ne}^2\setminus E_{\rm lo}.
      \tag{CCE9}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r
      \sum_{\kappa\in E}\Pr[x_\kappa\in U_r]
      \le
      m^{1+\rho_{\rm cap}}\log^{3A_{\rm cap}/2}m
      \tag{CCE10}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r
      \sum_{(\kappa,\kappa')\in E_{\rm lo}}
      \Pr[x_\kappa,x_{\kappa'}\in U_r]
      \le
      m^{1+\rho_{\rm cap}}
      \log^{2A_{\rm cap}+2K_{\rm corr}+1}m .
      \tag{CCE11}
   \]

   Define
   \[
      \omega_{\kappa,\kappa'}
      =
      \mathbf 1_{\{(\kappa,\kappa')\in E_{\rm hi}\}}
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r
      \Pr[x_\kappa,x_{\kappa'}\in U_r],
      \qquad
      W_{\rm hi}=\sum_{\kappa,\kappa'\in E}\omega_{\kappa,\kappa'} .
      \tag{CCE12}
   \]
   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), set \(J_\omega=1\).  Otherwise assume the positive
   \(\omega_{\kappa,\kappa'}\)'s lie in a certified dyadic range
   \([\omega_{\min},\omega_{\max}]\), put
   \[
      J_\omega=
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{\omega_{\max}}{\omega_{\min}}\right\rceil,
      \tag{CCE13}
   \]
   and define dyadic high-correlation stars
   \[
      V_{\kappa,t}
      =
      \{\kappa'\in E:\omega_{\kappa,\kappa'}\ge t\},
      \qquad
      t=\omega_{\min}2^j,\quad0\le j<J_\omega .
      \tag{CCE14}
   \]
   Then every nonempty \(V_{\kappa,t}\) lies in the cap ball
   \[
      x_{\kappa'}\in
      B\!\left(x_\kappa,\sqrt{2(1-\theta_m)}\right),
      \tag{CCE15}
   \]
   and for every \(\Lambda_\star>0\), either
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}\le2|E|J_\omega\Lambda_\star,
      \tag{CCE16}
   \]
   or some dyadic high-correlation star satisfies
   \[
      t|V_{\kappa,t}|\ge\Lambda_\star .
      \tag{CCE17}
   \]
   Moreover, if such a star has a valid materializable generated record
   \(R_{\kappa,t}\in\mathcal R_L\) with
   \(V_{\kappa,t}\subseteq C_{R_{\kappa,t}}\) and
   \[
      P_{R_{\kappa,t}}<\delta |V_{\kappa,t}|,
      \tag{CCE18}
   \]
   then \((CCG11)\) is violated, so the compressed-cap overload residual has a
   positive generated prefix.

   Consequently the compressed-cap overload branch reaches the standard
   entropy-energy endpoint: a generated-metric packing is paid by the bucket
   second moment, or a high-correlation star returns to generated-prefix search;
   in a surviving residual every such star has certified generated price at
   least its dual mass \(\delta |V_{\kappa,t}|\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The packing lower bound is the packing part of
   \cref{cor:compressed-cap-overload-dual-low-cover-screen}.

   Expanding the second moment gives
   \[
      \E_GX_E(G)^2
      =
      \sum_{\kappa\in E}\Pr_G[x_\kappa\in U_G]
      +
      \sum_{\substack{\kappa,\kappa'\in E\\\kappa\ne\kappa'}}
         \Pr_G[x_\kappa,x_{\kappa'}\in U_G].
   \]
   Summing the profile bounds \((CCE1)\) gives \((CCE3)\), and \((CCE4)\)
   gives \((CCE5)\).

   Apply \cref{cor:weighted-polylog-low-correlation-coload} to the indexed
   representative family \((x_\kappa)_{\kappa\in E}\), the weighted panel
   \(\mathcal R\), and the low-correlation pair set \(E_{\rm lo}\).  The
   hypotheses \((CCE7)\)--\((CCE8)\) are exactly \((WPLC1)\)--\((WPLC2)\),
   with \(A=A_{\rm cap}\), \(K=K_{\rm corr}\), and
   \(\rho=\rho_{\rm cap}\).  This proves \((CCE10)\)--\((CCE11)\).

   If \(\kappa'\in V_{\kappa,t}\), then
   \(\omega_{\kappa,\kappa'}>0\), so
   \((\kappa,\kappa')\in E_{\rm hi}\).  Therefore
   \(\ip{x_\kappa}{x_{\kappa'}}>\theta_m\), and
   \[
      \|x_\kappa-x_{\kappa'}\|^2
      =
      2-2\ip{x_\kappa}{x_{\kappa'}}
      <
      2(1-\theta_m),
   \]
   proving \((CCE15)\).

   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), then \((CCE16)\) is immediate.  Otherwise, for fixed
   \(\kappa\), the dyadic layer-cake estimate gives
   \[
      \sum_{j=0}^{J_\omega-1}
      \omega_{\min}2^j
      |V_{\kappa,\omega_{\min}2^j}|
      \ge
      \frac12\sum_{\kappa'\in E}\omega_{\kappa,\kappa'} .
   \]
   Summing over \(\kappa\), if every dyadic star had
   \(t|V_{\kappa,t}|<\Lambda_\star\), then
   \(W_{\rm hi}/2<|E|J_\omega\Lambda_\star\), proving \((CCE16)\).  The
   contrapositive gives \((CCE17)\).

   Finally, \(V_{\kappa,t}\subseteq E\subseteq L_0\), so every member has dual
   weight at least \(\delta\).  If \((CCE18)\) holds, then
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa'\in C_{R_{\kappa,t}}}y_{\kappa'}
      \ge
      \sum_{\kappa'\in V_{\kappa,t}}y_{\kappa'}
      \ge
      \delta |V_{\kappa,t}|
      >
      P_{R_{\kappa,t}},
   \]
   contradicting \((CCG11)\).  By
   \cref{cor:compressed-cap-overload-generated-column}, that contradiction is
   the positive generated-prefix alternative.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Compressed-cap overload cap-star storage split]
   \label{cor:compressed-cap-overload-cap-star-storage-split}
   Work in the no-generated-prefix residual and notation of
   \cref{cor:compressed-cap-overload-packing-energy-endpoint}.  Assume every
   nonempty dyadic high-correlation star \(V_{\kappa,t}\) has a valid
   materializable generated record \(R_{\kappa,t}\in\mathcal R_L\) with
   \(V_{\kappa,t}\subseteq C_{R_{\kappa,t}}\) and common price envelope
   \[
      P_{R_{\kappa,t}}
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(Ah_{\kappa,t}^{\rho}
      +\zeta h_{\kappa,t}^{1+\rho}\right),
      \qquad
      h_{\kappa,t}=|V_{\kappa,t}|,\quad 0<\rho<1 .
      \tag{CCS1}
   \]
   Then every nonempty dyadic high-correlation star satisfies
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(Ah_{\kappa,t}^{\rho-1}
      +\zeta h_{\kappa,t}^{\rho}\right).
      \tag{CCS2}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      H_-^{\rm ccap}
      =
      \left(\frac{2\psi_\star A}{\delta}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \tag{CCS3}
   \]
   with \(H_-^{\rm ccap}=0\) when \(A=0\).  If \(\zeta>0\), also put
   \[
      H_+^{\rm ccap}
      =
      \left(\frac{\delta}{2\psi_\star\zeta}\right)^{1/\rho}.
      \tag{CCS4}
   \]
   Then every nonempty star obeys
   \[
      h_{\kappa,t}\le H_-^{\rm ccap}
      \qquad\text{or}\qquad
      \bigl(\zeta>0\text{ and }h_{\kappa,t}\ge H_+^{\rm ccap}\bigr).
      \tag{CCS5}
   \]
   Equivalently, any materialized star with
   \[
      h_{\kappa,t}>H_-^{\rm ccap}
      \quad\text{and, when }\zeta>0,\quad
      h_{\kappa,t}<H_+^{\rm ccap}
      \tag{CCS6}
   \]
   is itself a positive generated prefix.

   If \(\zeta>0\) and the forbidden interval is empty, then
   \[
      \delta\le2\psi_\star A^\rho\zeta^{1-\rho}.
      \tag{CCS7}
   \]

   Let \(\mathcal S_{\rm ccap}\) be the set of nonempty dyadic compressed-cap
   overload stars in the storage-dominated alternative
   \(h_{\kappa,t}\ge H_+^{\rm ccap}\), and define for
   \(s=(\kappa,t)\in\mathcal S_{\rm ccap}\)
   \[
      A_s^{\rm ccap}=V_{\kappa,t},
      \qquad
      h_s=|A_s^{\rm ccap}|=h_{\kappa,t},
      \qquad
      u_s^{\rm ccap}=\psi_\star\zeta\,t\,h_s^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{CCS8}
   \]
   If \(\zeta=0\), interpret \(\mathcal S_{\rm ccap}=\emptyset\).  Then every
   no-prefix compressed-cap overload residual satisfies
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      2|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-^{\rm ccap}
      +
      \frac4\delta
      \sum_{s\in\mathcal S_{\rm ccap}}u_s^{\rm ccap}.
      \tag{CCS9}
   \]

   Consequently the high-correlation return from compressed-cap overload has no
   separate branching rule.  It is a bounded-cardinality fixed tail plus the
   storage-dominated priced child panel
   \(\{(A_s^{\rm ccap},u_s^{\rm ccap})\}\), which may be submitted to the
   generic shared-cover compiler and exact distinct-storage certificates just as
   in \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-cap-star-storage-split}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   In a no-generated-prefix residual, \((CCE18)\) cannot hold.  Hence every
   nonempty materialized star satisfies
   \[
      \delta h_{\kappa,t}\le P_{R_{\kappa,t}} .
   \]
   Combining this with \((CCS1)\) and dividing by \(h_{\kappa,t}>0\) proves
   \((CCS2)\).

   If \(h_{\kappa,t}>H_-^{\rm ccap}\), then
   \[
      \psi_\star A h_{\kappa,t}^{\rho-1}<\frac{\delta}{2}.
   \]
   Thus \((CCS2)\) can hold only if
   \(\psi_\star\zeta h_{\kappa,t}^{\rho}\ge\delta/2\).  When \(\zeta=0\) this
   is impossible; when \(\zeta>0\), it is exactly
   \(h_{\kappa,t}\ge H_+^{\rm ccap}\).  This proves \((CCS5)\), and
   \((CCS6)\) is its contrapositive combined with
   \cref{cor:compressed-cap-overload-packing-energy-endpoint}.

   If \(\zeta>0\) and \(H_-^{\rm ccap}\ge H_+^{\rm ccap}\), then
   \[
      \left(\frac{2\psi_\star A}{\delta}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \ge
      \left(\frac{\delta}{2\psi_\star\zeta}\right)^{1/\rho}.
   \]
   Raising to \(\rho(1-\rho)\) and rearranging gives \((CCS7)\).

   It remains to prove \((CCS9)\).  If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), it is immediate.
   Otherwise the layer-cake estimate from
   \cref{cor:compressed-cap-overload-packing-energy-endpoint} gives
   \[
      \frac12W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \sum_{\kappa\in E}\sum_t t\,h_{\kappa,t}.
      \tag{CCS10}
   \]
   Split the sum into the bounded side \(h_{\kappa,t}\le H_-^{\rm ccap}\) and
   the storage-dominated side.  Since \(t\le\omega_{\max}\), the bounded side
   contributes at most \(|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-^{\rm ccap}\).  For a
   storage-dominated star, the definition of \(H_+^{\rm ccap}\) gives
   \[
      \delta\le2\psi_\star\zeta h_{\kappa,t}^{\rho},
   \]
   and hence
   \[
      t\,h_{\kappa,t}
      \le
      \frac2\delta\psi_\star\zeta\,t\,h_{\kappa,t}^{1+\rho}
      =
      \frac2\delta u_{(\kappa,t)}^{\rm ccap}.
      \tag{CCS11}
   \]
   Substituting these two estimates in \((CCS10)\) proves \((CCS9)\).  When
   \(\zeta=0\), the storage-dominated side is empty and the same argument gives
   the fixed-tail bound alone.

   Finally, \((CCS8)\) is the standard priced child-panel form after absorbing
   the dyadic intensity \(t\) into the child price factor
   \(t\psi_\star\zeta\).  The cited generic compiler and storage certificates
   are stated for arbitrary priced child panels, so no additional
   compressed-cap materialization rule is needed.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Weighted polylogarithmic low-correlation co-load cutoff]
   \label{cor:weighted-polylog-low-correlation-coload}
   Let \(m\ge3\), \(P\subset\mathbb S^{D-1}\) with \(|P|\le m\), and let
   \(\mathcal R\) be a finite weighted cap panel.  For each
   \(r\in\mathcal R\), let \(w_r\ge0\), let \(G_r\sim N(0,I_D)\), and let
   \[
      U_r=\{x:\ip{G_r}{x}\ge T_r\},
      \qquad
      T_r^2\ge2\log m-A\log\log m .
      \tag{WPLC1}
   \]
   Independence among the \(G_r\)'s is not needed for the following first-moment
   bounds.  Fix constants \(A,K\ge0\), \(0\le\rho\le1\), and assume
   \[
      W:=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r
      \le m^{1+\rho}\log^A m .
      \tag{WPLC2}
   \]
   Let \(\theta_m=K\log\log m/\log m<1\), and let
   \(E_{\rm lo}\subseteq P\times P\) be any set of ordered pairs with
   \(|E_{\rm lo}|\le m^2\) and \(\ip{x}{y}\le\theta_m\) for every
   \((x,y)\in E_{\rm lo}\).  Then
   \[
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r
      \sum_{x\in P}\Pr[x\in U_r]
      \le
      m^{1+\rho}\log^{3A/2}m
      \tag{WPLC3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r
      \sum_{(x,y)\in E_{\rm lo}}\Pr[x,y\in U_r]
      \le
      m^{1+\rho}\log^{2A+2K+1}m .
      \tag{WPLC4}
   \]

   Thus the low-correlation storage estimate is homogeneous in cap
   multiplicity.  Fractional panels, weighted Hall atoms, and soft decoder
   cohorts may be analyzed without rounding them to an integer number of
   identical cap occurrences; only their total certified weight \(W\) enters
   the low-correlation co-load bound.  The same statement holds verbatim when
   \(P\) is an indexed family of unit vectors, possibly with repeated
   representatives, with all sums taken over indices.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The one-point and two-point bounds used in
   \cref{cor:polylog-low-correlation-coload} hold for each \(r\) separately,
   because every \(T_r\) satisfies \((WPLC1)\).  Hence
   \[
      \sum_{x\in P}\Pr[x\in U_r]\le m^{-1}\log^{A/2}m\,|P|
      \le \log^{A/2}m,
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{(x,y)\in E_{\rm lo}}\Pr[x,y\in U_r]
      \le \log^{A+2K}m
   \]
   up to the same harmless extra logarithmic power as in \((PLC4)\).  Multiply
   these two pointwise bounds by \(w_r\), sum over \(r\), and use
   \(W\le m^{1+\rho}\log^A m\).
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[The Renyi target is entropy minus energy]
   \label{rem:renyi-entropy-energy-target}
   \Cref{cor:tuple-profile-renyi-certificate} is the promised self-contained
   form of the notes10 list-decoding target.  The combinatorial term
   \(\log M_\pi\) is the spherical packing entropy of separated tuples in a
   bucket, while \(I_\pi\) is the Gaussian cap-intersection energy.  Proving
   \((CB1)\) and \((CB2)\) for a tensorized spherical filter family therefore
   reduces to checking that every relevant tuple profile has
   \[
      \text{packing entropy}-\text{cap energy}
      \le
      \text{recursive Renyi budget}+O_c(\log\log m).
   \]
   For pair profiles, \cref{cor:two-point-tuple-profile-gaussian} makes this
   completely explicit: if the profile has pair correlation at most \(\theta\)
   and both shifted thresholds are at least \(\beta\), the energy term is at
   least \(\beta^2/(1+\theta)\).
   The intended worst-case use is therefore a dichotomy, not a uniform
   occurrence-moment theorem.  After fixing a correlation cutoff, the
   low-correlation pair profiles are bounded by this entropy-energy estimate.
   The high-correlation profiles are handed to
   \cref{lem:high-correlation-pair-star-reporter} and
   \cref{cor:dense-star-gaussian-profile-layer}, which convert their weighted
   incidence into smaller-radius star superlevels for the dense-filter
   separator.  Thus a large high-correlation contribution is not a failure of
   tensoring; it is exactly the signal that a dense column should be proposed.
   \Cref{cor:tuple-profile-compressed-bucket-storage} supplies the matching
   low-correlation storage compiler: once the first list moment and the
   two-point tuple-profile energy are both within the desired storage budget, the
   occurrence moment and the weaker shared-DAG distinct-net sum both satisfy
   \((CB2)\).
   By \cref{lem:first-moment-query-compression}, the query side needs only the
   success-normalized first moment of the queried bucket or net, relative to
   the near hit probability \(a_j(q,p)\).  The space side uses the exponent
   \(1+\rho_{j+1}\le2\) under the stored-filter law and can be controlled by
   the first and second tuple profile sums.  Those tuple sums bound the
   occurrence-weighted moment
   \(\sum_F |N_F|^{1+\rho_{j+1}}\), which remains a sufficient condition for
   \((CB2)\) by \cref{lem:occurrence-moments-dominate-dag}.  The actual
   shared-DAG requirement is weaker: it charges only
   \(\sum_A|A|^{1+\rho_{j+1}}\) over distinct canonical nets, while occurrence
   multiplicities are charged separately as retained filter metadata.
   \Cref{lem:positive-correlation-occurrence-obstruction} shows why this
   distinction is not cosmetic.  In a positive-correlation tangent cap, the
   occurrence co-load and even the occurrence \((1+r)\)-moment can be
   polynomially too large, although many cap occurrences may induce the same
   or nearly the same compressed net.  Thus the final worst-case storage proof
   must use distinct-net quotienting, dense-cap sharing, or an equivalent
   canonicalization argument; a pure occurrence-moment proof would target a
   false statement.
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[Flat shells give the data-independent exponent]\label{lem:flat-shell-obstruction}
   Consider the tempting one-layer reduction that takes a bounded-diameter ball,
   decomposes it into radial shells around its center, and runs the smooth
   spherical filter directly on every data-query shell pair. On equal shells of
   radius $R$, the induced spherical correlations are
   \[
      a_R=1-\frac{r^2}{2R^2},
      \qquad
      b_R=1-\frac{c^2r^2}{2R^2}.
   \]
   Hence
   \[
      \rho(a_R,b_R)
      =
      \frac{2-c^2x}{c^2(2-x)},
      \qquad
      x=\frac{r^2}{2R^2},
   \]
   and in particular
   \[
      \rho(a_R,b_R)\to\frac1{c^2}
      \quad\text{as } R/r\to\infty .
   \]
   Since $1/c^2>\rho_c=1/(2c^2-1)$ for every $c>1$, flat shelling a
   polylogarithmic-radius localized ball would lose a fixed polynomial factor
   in $n$. The optimal exponent occurs only near the critical normalization
   where the far correlation is $b\simeq0$ and the near correlation is
   $a\simeq1-1/c^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For equal radii, the shell formulas give angular chord distances
   $r^2/R^2$ and $c^2r^2/R^2$. Since
   $\|u-v\|^2=2-2\ip{u}{v}$ on the unit sphere, the displayed correlations
   follow. Put $x=r^2/(2R^2)$. Then
   \[
      1-a_R=x,\quad 1-b_R=c^2x,\quad
      1+a_R=2-x,\quad 1+b_R=2-c^2x.
   \]
   Substituting into the balanced spherical exponent
   $\rho(a,b)=(1-a)(1+b)/((1+a)(1-b))$ gives the displayed expression and
   its limit. The inequality $1/c^2>1/(2c^2-1)$ is equivalent to $c^2>1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Continuation-sampled detector tokens]\label{lem:continuation-detector}
   In any continuation-mass score block, a detector token can be sampled as follows. At a retained prefix $u$, assign every retained child $v$ its one-point continuation mass $H(v)$ for the remaining schedule, choose one child with probability proportional to $H(v)$, and kill the token if the total retained child mass is zero. Then the resulting detector law is normalized: for every prefix-free family $\mathcal U$,
   \[
      \sum_{u\in\mathcal U}\Prb[\text{the token reaches }u]\le1.
   \]
   The same construction applies to the adaptive schedule of \cref{def:regular-adaptive-score}, using the exact conditional continuation mass for the remaining predictable schedule.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   A detector token has a single current prefix. At each score step it either dies or moves to exactly one child. Hence the events that it first reaches members of a prefix-free family are disjoint. Summing their probabilities gives at most one. The adaptive case is identical because the continuation masses are predictable once the current prefix is fixed.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Detector path probability and sibling inflation]\label{lem:detector-inflation}
   For a retained score prefix $u$, let
   \[
      D(u)=\sum_{v:\,v\text{ retained child of }u}H(v),
      \qquad
      \Gamma(u)=\frac{D(u)}{H(u)}
   \]
   whenever $H(u)>0$. If $v$ is a retained prefix and $u\prec v$ ranges over the proper prefixes of $v$, then the continuation-sampled detector law satisfies
   \[
      \Prb[\text{one detector token reaches }v]
      =
      \frac{H(v)}{H(\varnothing)}
      \prod_{u\prec v}\Gamma(u)^{-1}.
   \]
   In particular, for a retained accepting leaf $v$,
   \[
      \Prb[\text{one detector token reaches }v]
      =
      \frac{1}{H(\varnothing)}
      \prod_{u\prec v}\Gamma(u)^{-1}.
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   At a retained prefix $u$, the detector chooses the next prefix $w$ with probability $H(w)/D(u)$. Multiplying these transition probabilities along the path to $v$ gives
   \[
      \prod_{u\to w\preceq v}\frac{H(w)}{D(u)}
      =
      \prod_{u\to w\preceq v}
      \frac{H(w)}{H(u)}\Gamma(u)^{-1}
      =
      \frac{H(v)}{H(\varnothing)}
      \prod_{u\prec v}\Gamma(u)^{-1}.
   \]
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Off-spine reduction for detector inflation]\label{lem:off-spine-inflation}
   Fix a retained path
   \[
      v_0=\varnothing,\ v_1,\ldots,v_h
   \]
   and reveal the on-spine score increments along this path. Put
   \[
      R_i=\frac{H(v_{i+1})}{H(v_i)}
      \qquad (0\le i<h).
   \]
   Conditional on the revealed spine, the off-spine children satisfy
   \[
      \E\!\left[
         \prod_{i=0}^{h-1}\Gamma(v_i)
         \,\middle|\, v_0,\ldots,v_h
      \right]
      \le
      \prod_{i=0}^{h-1}\left(R_i+\frac{B-1}{B}\right).
   \]
   Consequently, if
   \[
      \sum_{i=0}^{h-1} R_i\le C\log K
   \]
   on a path of score depth at most $K$, then with conditional probability at least $1/2$ over the off-spine children,
   \[
      \prod_{i=0}^{h-1}\Gamma(v_i)\le 2K^C .
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Write $O_i$ for the retained continuation mass of the off-spine children of $v_i$:
   \[
      O_i=\sum_{\substack{w:\,w\text{ retained child of }v_i\\w\ne v_{i+1}}}H(w).
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \Gamma(v_i)=R_i+\frac{O_i}{H(v_i)}.
   \]
   Conditional on the spine, the off-spine child subtrees at different levels are independent. Also, by the defining harmonicity of continuation mass before the finite children are realized,
   \[
      \E[O_i\mid v_0,\ldots,v_h]
      \le
      \frac{B-1}{B}H(v_i),
   \]
   where the inequality only uses that discarding non-retained children can decrease the sum. Therefore
   \[
      \E\!\left[
         \prod_i\Gamma(v_i)
         \,\middle|\, v_0,\ldots,v_h
      \right]
      =
      \prod_i
      \E\!\left[
         R_i+\frac{O_i}{H(v_i)}
         \,\middle|\, v_0,\ldots,v_h
      \right]
      \le
      \prod_i\left(R_i+\frac{B-1}{B}\right).
   \]
   Since $(B-1)/B\le1$, the displayed spine-ratio condition gives
   \[
      \prod_i\left(R_i+\frac{B-1}{B}\right)
      \le
      \prod_i(1+R_i)
      \le
      \exp\!\left(\sum_iR_i\right)
      \le
      K^C.
   \]
   Markov's inequality gives the final claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[A sufficient detector-shadowing target]\label{cor:detector-shadowing-target}
   Suppose a retained prefix $v$ of depth at most $K$ satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{u\prec v}\frac{H(u^+)}{H(u)}\le C\log K,
   \]
   where $u^+$ is the next prefix of $v$. Then, with probability at least $1/2$ over the off-spine score children,
   \[
      \Prb[\text{one detector token reaches }v]
      \ge
      \frac{H(v)}{2K^C H(\varnothing)}.
   \]
   Thus
   \[
      O\!\left(K^C\frac{H(\varnothing)}{H(v)}\log^{A_c}n\right)
   \]
   continuation-sampled detector tokens hit $v$ with probability at least $1-n^{-A_c}$, conditional on the same off-spine event. For an accepting leaf $H(v)=1$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Combine \cref{lem:detector-inflation} and \cref{lem:off-spine-inflation}. The final amplification bound is the elementary estimate
   \[
      \left(1-\frac{H(v)}{2K^CH(\varnothing)}\right)^{
         C'K^C(H(\varnothing)/H(v))\log^{A_c}n}
      \le
      n^{-A_c}
   \]
   after increasing the constant $C'$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[The spine-ratio condition is an early-prefix condition]\label{rem:linear-spine-ratio}
   The logarithmic spine-ratio condition in \cref{cor:detector-shadowing-target} should not be expected for a full accepting score path. In the homogeneous spherical block, consider the deterministic linear spine with score $S_\ell=\ell t$. If $r=k-\ell$, then
   \[
      \frac{H_{\ell+1}((\ell+1)t)}{H_\ell(\ell t)}
      =
      \frac{1}{B}\,
      \frac{\overline\Phi(t\sqrt{r-1})}
           {\overline\Phi(t\sqrt r)}
      =
      B^{-(1-a)/2}\exp(O_{a,b}(1/r))
   \]
   for $r\ge2$, by Mills' ratio and $t^2=(1+a)\log B$. Thus a typical tilted near spine can have
   \[
      \sum_{\ell<k}\frac{H_{\ell+1}(S_{\ell+1})}{H_\ell(S_\ell)}
      =
      \Theta_{a,b}(k),
   \]
   not $O(\log k)$. Consequently \cref{cor:detector-shadowing-target} is useful for early activation prefixes, where the relevant detector cost is $H(\varnothing)/H(v)$, but long near routes need an aggregate detector-mass argument over many possible good prefixes, or else the ordinary continuation path must reach a cap-free scan.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Why detector shadowing is still nontrivial]\label{rem:detector-shadowing-obstruction}
   A tempting shortcut would be to claim that the inflation product in \cref{lem:detector-inflation} is always at most one, so every retained accepting leaf $v$ is reached with probability at least $1/H(\varnothing)$. This would be true if the realized child masses satisfied
   \[
      H(u)=\sum_{v:\,v\text{ child of }u}H(v)
   \]
   at every sampled score node. The analytic continuation mass used by the decoder is only harmonic in expectation over the next Gaussian children, however. After the $B$ children of a finite branching node are realized, the sibling sum can be larger than $H(u)$, and a detector token can be diverted toward atypically large siblings. Thus detector tokens are normalized for prefix-free accounting by \cref{lem:continuation-detector}, but they do not automatically shadow an ordinary tame-good near leaf. This is the remaining probabilistic content in the cohort-or-leaf route.
\end{remark}

\section{The certified score-and-ball process}

We now describe the Euclidean part as one branching process. A node of the process carries both a cumulative Gaussian score state and a certified Euclidean ball. Gaussian score edges perform filtering inside the current ball; recentering edges are deterministic branches that move to a smaller certified ball while retaining the score prefix and updating the coordinate offset. Thus the geometric recursion is not a separate wrapper around the score tree.

\subsection{Two elementary geometric facts}

The first fact certifies the radius decrease obtained from a spherical cap.

\begin{lemma}[Cap recentering]\label{lem:cap}
   Let $P$ lie on the sphere of radius $R$ centered at $o$, and suppose
   \[
      \ip{(p-o)/R}{w}\ge\gamma
   \]
   for every $p$ in a cap $C\subseteq P$, where $\|w\|_2=1$. Then
   \[
      C\subseteq
      \Ball\!\left(o+\gamma Rw,\,R\sqrt{1-\gamma^2}\right).
   \]
   In particular, if $\gamma=\Theta_c(\eta)$, the certified child radius satisfies
   \[
      R_C\le R(1-\Theta_c(\eta^2)).
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For $p\in C$,
   \begin{align*}
      \|p-(o+\gamma Rw)\|_2^2
                                           &=\|p-o\|_2^2+\gamma^2R^2-2\gamma R\ip{p-o}{w}\\
                                           &\le R^2+\gamma^2R^2-2\gamma^2R^2\\
                                           &=R^2(1-\gamma^2).
   \end{align*}
   The final estimate follows from $\sqrt{1-x}=1-\Theta(x)$ for sufficiently small positive $x$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Tiny-positive cap chains have polylogarithmic depth]
   \label{cor:tiny-positive-cap-chain}
   Let
   \[
      R_0\ge R_1\ge\cdots\ge R_h\ge r
   \]
   be a chain of certified spherical cap recenterings.  At step \(i\), suppose
   the retained set is contained in a cap of margin \(\gamma_i\ge\gamma_0\),
   where \(0<\gamma_0<1/2\), so that
   \[
      R_{i+1}\le R_i\sqrt{1-\gamma_i^2}.
      \tag{TPC1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      h\le \frac{4\log(R_0/r)}{\gamma_0^2}.
      \tag{TPC2}
   \]
   In particular, on the localized instances of \cref{lem:localization}, if
   \(R_0/r\le\log^C n\) and
   \[
      \gamma_0=K\,\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}
      \tag{TPC3}
   \]
   with \(0<\gamma_0<1/2\), then every such recentering lineage has length at
   most
   \[
      O_{C,K}\!\left(\frac{\log^2 n}{\log\log n}\right).
      \tag{TPC4}
   \]

   Thus the positive-correlation branch left by
   \cref{cor:polylog-low-correlation-coload} cannot force a superpolylogarithmic
   number of genuine radius contractions.  A star superlevel with normalized
   correlations \(\ip{x}{y}\ge\gamma_0\) may be submitted to the dense verifier
   using the point-centered ball \(B(x,\sqrt{2(1-\gamma_0)})\), but for radius
   progress it also lies in the cap-recentered ball from \cref{lem:cap}, whose
   squared relative radius is \(1-\gamma_0^2\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   From \(0<\gamma_i<1\) and \((TPC1)\),
   \[
      \log\frac{R_i}{R_{i+1}}
      \ge
      -\frac12\log(1-\gamma_i^2)
      \ge
      \frac{\gamma_i^2}{2}
      \ge
      \frac{\gamma_0^2}{2}.
   \]
   Summing over \(i<h\) gives
   \[
      \log\frac{R_0}{r}
      \ge
      \log\frac{R_0}{R_h}
      =
      \sum_{i=0}^{h-1}\log\frac{R_i}{R_{i+1}}
      \ge
      \frac{h\gamma_0^2}{2}.
   \]
   This proves the stronger bound with constant \(2\); \((TPC2)\) leaves slack
   for harmless shell-width and certification constants.  Substituting
   \(R_0/r\le\log^C n\) and \((TPC3)\) gives \((TPC4)\).

   Finally, if \(y\) satisfies \(\ip{x}{y}\ge\gamma_0\) on a unit sphere, then
   the set of such \(y\)'s is exactly a cap in direction \(x\).  Applying
   \cref{lem:cap} gives the cap-recentered ball with relative squared radius
   \(1-\gamma_0^2\), while the point-centered inclusion follows from
   \(\|x-y\|^2=2-2\ip{x}{y}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Quadratic cap-margin budget]
   \label{cor:quadratic-cap-margin-budget}
   In the setting of \cref{cor:tiny-positive-cap-chain}, but allowing the
   margins \(\gamma_i\) to vary, suppose \(0<\gamma_i<1/2\) and
   \[
      R_{i+1}\le R_i\sqrt{1-\gamma_i^2}
      \qquad(0\le i<h).
      \tag{QCB1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \sum_{i=0}^{h-1}\gamma_i^2
      \le
      4\log(R_0/r).
      \tag{QCB2}
   \]
   Consequently, on the localized instances of \cref{lem:localization}, where
   \(R_0/r\le\log^C n\), any nonnegative lineage tolls \(\xi_i\) satisfying
   \[
      \xi_i\le A\gamma_i^2
      \tag{QCB3}
   \]
   have
   \[
      \sum_i\xi_i=O_{A,C}(\log\log n),
      \qquad
      \prod_i e^{\xi_i}\le \log^{O_{A,C}(1)}n .
      \tag{QCB4}
   \]
   Moreover, for any base margin \(\gamma_0>0\), the dyadic band
   \[
      I_k=\{i:2^k\gamma_0\le\gamma_i<2^{k+1}\gamma_0\}
      \tag{QCB5}
   \]
   obeys
   \[
      |I_k|
      \le
      \frac{4\log(R_0/r)}{2^{2k}\gamma_0^2}.
      \tag{QCB6}
   \]

   Thus the positive-correlation branch should be charged by margin-squared
   local surplus, not by a unit toll per dense star.  A unit toll only gives the
   depth bound in \cref{cor:tiny-positive-cap-chain}; a quadratic toll sums to
   \(O(\log\log n)\) inside the localized polylogarithmic radius ball.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   As in the proof of \cref{cor:tiny-positive-cap-chain},
   \[
      \log\frac{R_i}{R_{i+1}}
      \ge
      -\frac12\log(1-\gamma_i^2)
      \ge
      \frac{\gamma_i^2}{2}.
   \]
   Summing over \(i<h\) gives
   \[
      \frac12\sum_{i<h}\gamma_i^2
      \le
      \log\frac{R_0}{R_h}
      \le
      \log\frac{R_0}{r}.
   \]
   This proves \((QCB2)\) with constant \(2\); the displayed constant \(4\)
   leaves slack for the same shell-width and certification constants as above.
   The localized toll statement follows by multiplying \((QCB2)\) by \(A\) and
   using \(R_0/r\le\log^C n\).  Finally, every \(i\in I_k\) contributes at
   least \(2^{2k}\gamma_0^2\) to the sum in \((QCB2)\), proving \((QCB6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Quadratic local repair]\label{def:quadratic-local-repair}
   Fix a prefix of the cumulative score-and-ball process and a certified ball
   of radius \(R\).  Suppose the unresolved positive-correlation obstruction at
   this prefix is certified by a cap margin \(\gamma\) and is replaced by a
   same-prefix finite family of filters, dense records, or recursive children.
   The repair is \(A\)-quadratic if, relative to the parent potential charge at
   the same prefix, its normalized query toll, storage toll, and inverse
   near-lineage survival toll are all at most
   \[
      \exp(A\gamma^2).
      \tag{QLR}
   \]
   The phrase ``same-prefix'' is part of the definition: the repair may inherit
   the current score prefix and activation, but it may not pay for a fresh
   independent score clock or a separate global restart.
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Quadratic positive-correlation toll compiler]
   \label{cor:quadratic-positive-toll-compiler}
   On a localized instance with \(R_0/r\le\log^C n\), consider any successful
   near-neighbor lineage whose positive-correlation repairs are certified by cap
   margins \(\gamma_i\) and satisfy the radius certificates
   \[
      R_{i+1}\le R_i\sqrt{1-\gamma_i^2}.
      \tag{QPT1}
   \]
   If each such repair is \(A\)-quadratic in the sense of
   \cref{def:quadratic-local-repair}, then the total multiplicative toll of all
   positive-correlation repairs on the lineage is only polylogarithmic:
   \[
      \prod_i \exp(A\gamma_i^2)
      \le
      \log^{O_{A,C}(1)} n.
      \tag{QPT2}
   \]
   Equivalently, the remaining positive-correlation task is local: it is enough
   to prove a same-prefix repair whose loss is proportional to the squared cap
   margin.  A proof that charges one full constant factor per cap recentering
   would only use \cref{cor:tiny-positive-cap-chain} and would still leave the
   \(\exp(O(\log^2 n/\log\log n))\) tiny-margin overhead.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Taking logarithms of the product in \((QPT2)\) gives
   \(A\sum_i\gamma_i^2\).  The radius certificates \((QPT1)\) are exactly the
   hypotheses of \cref{cor:quadratic-cap-margin-budget}, hence
   \[
      A\sum_i\gamma_i^2
      \le
      O_A(\log(R_0/r))
      \le
      O_{A,C}(\log\log n).
   \]
   Exponentiating gives \((QPT2)\).
\end{proof}

The second fact shows that thin radial shells do not degrade the approximation factor.

\begin{lemma}[Angular gap on two shells]\label{lem:shell}
   Let data points have radius $S$ and let the query have radius $T$ around a common center. Put $\Delta=|S-T|$. If a data-query pair has Euclidean distance at most $r$, its squared angular chord distance is at most
   \[
      d_1^2=\frac{r^2-\Delta^2}{ST}.
   \]
   If its Euclidean distance is greater than $cr$, its squared angular chord distance is greater than
   \[
      d_2^2=\frac{c^2r^2-\Delta^2}{ST}.
   \]
   Whenever the near case is feasible,
   \[
      \frac{d_2^2}{d_1^2}\ge c^2.
   \]
   The same statements hold with $1+O_c(\eta)$ multiplicative slack for shells of relative width $O_c(\eta)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For normalized directions $u=(p-o)/S$ and $v=(q-o)/T$,
   \[
      \|p-q\|_2^2=(S-T)^2+ST\|u-v\|_2^2.
   \]
   Solving for $\|u-v\|_2^2$ gives the first two formulas. Moreover,
   \[
      \frac{c^2r^2-\Delta^2}{r^2-\Delta^2}
      \ge c^2
   \]
   because $(c^2-1)\Delta^2\ge0$. Shell discretization perturbs $S$, $T$, and $\Delta$ by relative $O_c(\eta)$, which yields the final claim.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Posterior stopping}

Fix a geometric node containing $m$ points in a certified ball $\Ball(o,R)$. The next two lemmas use the continuation-sampled detector law of \cref{lem:continuation-detector}, not the ordinary retained-prefix multiplicity of the continuation decoder. A detector token follows one score channel at a time, or dies, so every prefix-free set has total detector mass at most one.

Let $\mu(u)$ be the probability that one detector token driven by a uniformly random data point in the node reaches score prefix $u$, and let $\nu_q(u)$ be the corresponding one-token detector probability for query $q$. Thus, for every prefix-free family $\mathcal U$,
\[
   \sum_{u\in\mathcal U}\mu(u)\le1,
   \qquad
   \sum_{u\in\mathcal U}\nu_q(u)\le1.
\]
For a deterministic child cluster $C$ of relative size $\alpha=|C|/m$, let $\mu_C(u)$ be the detector prefix law conditioned on the point belonging to $C$. The posterior mass of $C$ at prefix $u$ is
\[
   Z_C(u)=\frac{\alpha\mu_C(u)}{\mu(u)}.
\]
Let $\mathcal A_C$ be the first-hit frontier on which $Z_C(u)\ge\tau$.

Put
\[
   \rho=\rho_c,
   \qquad
   s=1-\rho.
\]
The Bellman detector mass assigned to prefix $u$ is
\[
   w_q(u)=\mu(u)^s\nu_q(u)^\rho.
\]

\begin{lemma}[Posterior first-hit inequality]\label{lem:first-hit}
   For every prefix-free first-hit frontier $\mathcal A_C$,
   \[
      \sum_{u\in\mathcal A_C} w_q(u)
      \le
      \left(\frac{\alpha}{\tau}\right)^s.
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   On $\mathcal A_C$, the inequality $Z_C(u)\ge\tau$ gives
   \[
      \mu(u)\le \frac{\alpha}{\tau}\mu_C(u).
   \]
   Therefore
   \[
      \sum_{u\in\mathcal A_C}\mu(u)^s\nu_q(u)^\rho
      \le
      \left(\frac{\alpha}{\tau}\right)^s
      \sum_{u\in\mathcal A_C}\mu_C(u)^s\nu_q(u)^\rho.
   \]
   Since $s+\rho=1$ and $\mathcal A_C$ is prefix-free, Hölder's inequality gives
   \[
      \sum_{u\in\mathcal A_C}\mu_C(u)^s\nu_q(u)^\rho
      \le
      \left(\sum_{u\in\mathcal A_C}\mu_C(u)\right)^s
      \left(\sum_{u\in\mathcal A_C}\nu_q(u)\right)^\rho
      \le1.
   \]
\end{proof}

This lemma is deliberately stated for normalized detector mass. It would be false if $\mu$ and $\nu_q$ were interpreted as the raw number of retained ordinary prefixes in the branching continuation decoder; a point or query can occupy many such prefixes. Ordinary retained-prefix work is controlled separately by continuation mass in \cref{lem:continuation-work}.

\subsection{Radius Bellman cancellation}

Use the recursive query potential
\[
   F(m,R)=m^\rho\left(\frac Rr\right)^{2s}.
\]
Suppose child $C$ has size $\alpha m$ and certified radius $R_C=\lambda R$. Activate it at posterior threshold
\[
   \tau=\lambda^2.
\]
Then the fractional cost of entering and recursively searching $C$ is exactly
\[
   \left(\frac{\alpha}{\lambda^2}\right)^s
   F(\alpha m,\lambda R)
   =
   \alpha F(m,R).
\]
Thus disjoint activated children consume at most the parent potential, because $\sum_C\alpha_C\le1$. No cap geometry, balance condition, or bound on the number of children appears in this cancellation. Geometry enters only through the certified radii $R_C$. \Cref{fig:bellman} shows the cancellation schematically.

\node[draw,rounded corners,fill=blue!8] (c1) at (-3.4,-2) {$C_1:\ \alpha_1 m,\ \lambda_1 R$};
\node[draw,rounded corners,fill=blue!8] (c2) at (0,-2) {$C_2:\ \alpha_2 m,\ \lambda_2 R$};
\node[draw,rounded corners,fill=blue!8] (c3) at (3.4,-2) {$\cdots$};
\draw[->] (par) -- (c1) node[midway,left,font=\scriptsize]{$\tau_1=\lambda_1^2$};
