      \ip{A_uG_u^+r}{h}.
      \tag{LMS7}
   \]
   Therefore
   \[
      A_{u,h}(s)
      =
      \sup_{r\in\mathcal R_u(s)}
      \ip{-A_uG_u^+r}{h}.
      \tag{LMS8}
   \]
   Taking the supremum over \(h\in E_u\) and exchanging the two suprema gives
   \((LMS3)\).  The implications \((LMS4)\Rightarrow(LMR5)\) and
   \((LMS5)\Rightarrow(LMR10)\) are immediate from \((LMS3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Anchor-fiber internal-tail certificate]
   \label{cor:anchor-fiber-internal-tail-certificate}
   Continue with the notation of
   \cref{cor:support-function-internal-tail-certificate}.  Suppose the
   anchored excess set is generated by an anchor map
   \(\alpha_u:P_u\to C_u\),
   \[
      E_u=\{z-\iota(\alpha_u(z)):z\in P_u\}.
      \tag{LMT1}
   \]
   For each anchor \(c\in C_u\), define its fiber
   \[
      P_{u,c}=\{z\in P_u:\alpha_u(z)=c\},
      \tag{LMT2}
   \]
   and the fiber support function
   \[
      \Phi_{u,c}(y)
      =
      \sup_{z\in P_{u,c}}\ip{y}{z-\iota(c)} .
      \tag{LMT3}
   \]
   We use the convention that the supremum over an empty fiber is
   \(-\infty\).
   Then
   \[
      \Phi_u(y)=\max_{c\in C_u}\Phi_{u,c}(y).
      \tag{LMT4}
   \]
   Consequently, for every \(s\ge0\),
   \[
      \sup_{h\in E_u}A_{u,h}(s)
      =
      \sup_{r\in\mathcal R_u(s)}
      \max_{c\in C_u}
      \Phi_{u,c}\!\left(-A_uG_u^+r\right).
      \tag{LMT5}
   \]

   In particular, the dyadic cumulative-tail condition \((LMR10)\) follows if
   for every \(k\ge0\), every \(r\in\mathcal R_u(k\delta)\), and every
   \(c\in C_u\),
   \[
      \sup_{z\in P_{u,c}}
      \ip{-A_uG_u^+r}{z-\iota(c)}
      \le
      C_u e^{-(\lambda+\eta_u)k\delta}.
      \tag{LMT6}
   \]
   More generally, it is enough to verify \((LMT6)\) over any enlarged
   certified fiber relaxations \(\widetilde P_{u,c}\supseteq P_{u,c}\); if the
   enlarged fibers are linear relaxations, each check is an ordinary LP with a
   fully explicit objective.

   Thus a failed internal-tail bound produces a concrete triple
   \[
      (k,r,c)
      \tag{LMT7}
   \]
   and a fractional point \(z\) in the anchor fiber of \(c\) for which the
   down-score selector objective separates \(z\) from its anchor.  This is the
   finite LP/SA obstruction that a low-rate code proof must rule out.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \((LMT1)\)--\((LMT2)\),
   \[
      E_u=\bigcup_{c\in C_u}\{z-\iota(c):z\in P_{u,c}\}.
      \tag{LMT8}
   \]
   Taking the support function of this finite union gives
   \[
      \Phi_u(y)
      =
      \sup_{h\in E_u}\ip{y}{h}
      =
      \max_{c\in C_u}
      \sup_{z\in P_{u,c}}\ip{y}{z-\iota(c)}
      =
      \max_{c\in C_u}\Phi_{u,c}(y),
   \]
   proving \((LMT4)\).  Combining \((LMT4)\) with
   \cref{cor:support-function-internal-tail-certificate} proves \((LMT5)\).
   The implication \((LMT6)\Rightarrow(LMR10)\) is then immediate from
   \((LMT5)\).  Enlarging a fiber can only increase the supremum, so bounds
   proved over \(\widetilde P_{u,c}\) also hold over \(P_{u,c}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Singleton down-influence certificate]
   \label{cor:singleton-down-influence-certificate}
   Continue with the notation of
   \cref{cor:anchor-fiber-internal-tail-certificate}.  Let
   \(e_j\in\mathbb R^N\) be the \(j\)-th standard basis vector and define the
   influence of the true codeword \(c_j\) on the anchor fiber of \(c\) by
   \[
      I_{u,c,j}
      =
      \left(
      \sup_{z\in P_{u,c}}
      \ip{-A_uG_u^+e_j}{z-\iota(c)}
      \right)_+ .
      \tag{LMV1}
   \]
   If, for every dyadic level \(k\ge0\) and every anchor \(c\in C_u\),
   \[
      \sum_{j:\ M(u)-W(c_j)\ge k\delta} I_{u,c,j}
      \le
      C_u e^{-(\lambda+\eta_u)k\delta},
      \tag{LMV2}
   \]
   then the anchor-fiber selector bound \((LMT6)\) holds, and hence the
   dyadic cumulative-tail condition \((LMR10)\) follows.

   Thus it is not necessary to certify every fractional down-score selector
   \(r\) directly.  It is enough to prove an exponential tail for the
   singleton influence profile \(j\mapsto I_{u,c,j}\) below the local leader,
   uniformly over anchor fibers.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix \(k\), \(c\), and \(r\in\mathcal R_u(k\delta)\).  Put
   \(y_j=-A_uG_u^+e_j\).  Since \(r_j=0\) outside
   \(S_u(k\delta)\),
   \[
      -A_uG_u^+r=\sum_{j\in S_u(k\delta)}r_jy_j .
   \]
   The support function of any set is subadditive and positively homogeneous
   for nonnegative scalars, so
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \Phi_{u,c}(-A_uG_u^+r)
      &\le
      \sum_{j\in S_u(k\delta)}r_j\Phi_{u,c}(y_j)\\
      &\le
      \sum_{j\in S_u(k\delta)} I_{u,c,j}\\
      &\le
      C_u e^{-(\lambda+\eta_u)k\delta}.
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{LMV3}
   \]
   This is exactly \((LMT6)\).  The final implication is
   \cref{cor:anchor-fiber-internal-tail-certificate}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Singleton Boltzmann-influence certificate]
   \label{cor:singleton-boltzmann-influence-certificate}
   Continue with the notation of
   \cref{cor:singleton-down-influence-certificate}, and put
   \(g_j=M(u)-W(c_j)\).  Suppose that, for some \(\Xi_u\ge0\), every anchor
   fiber satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{j=1}^N e^{\lambda g_j} I_{u,c,j}\le \Xi_u
      \qquad(c\in C_u).
      \tag{LMW1}
   \]
   Then every anchored excess \(h\in E_u\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{j=1}^N
      a_u(h)_j^-\exp\!\bigl(\lambda(M(u)-W(c_j))\bigr)
      \le \Xi_u .
      \tag{LMW2}
   \]
   Consequently, if in addition
   \[
      \sum_ja_u(h)_j^-\le1,
      \qquad
      M(u)\kappa_u(h)\le R_u
      \qquad(h\in E_u),
      \tag{LMW3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      e^{\lambda R_u}(1+\Xi_u)
      \exp\!\left(
         \lambda\omega_u^\perp
         +\frac{\lambda^2(r_u^\perp)^2}{2}
      \right)
      \le A_\lambda ,
      \tag{LMW4}
   \]
   then the conditional tilted-excess bound \((LPT2)\) holds with
   \(A_\lambda\).  At \(\lambda=T/b\), a polylogarithmic bound in \((LMW4)\)
   therefore gives the LP/SA threshold reporter polylogarithmic expected
   overhead.

   This is the softest singleton form of the projected-bias target: prove one
   Boltzmann-weighted influence sum per anchor fiber, rather than a dyadic tail
   for every selector.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix \(h=z-\iota(c)\in E_u\), with \(z\in P_{u,c}\), and write
   \(a=a_u(h)\).  For nonnegative weights \(w_j=e^{\lambda g_j}\),
   \[
      \sum_jw_ja_j^-
      =
      \sup_{0\le r_j\le w_j}
      \left(-\sum_jr_ja_j\right).
      \tag{LMW5}
   \]
   As in \((LMS7)\),
   \[
      -\sum_jr_ja_j=\ip{-A_uG_u^+r}{h}.
   \]
   By support-function subadditivity and the definition of \(I_{u,c,j}\),
   \[
      \ip{-A_uG_u^+r}{h}
      \le
      \Phi_{u,c}(-A_uG_u^+r)
      \le
      \sum_jr_jI_{u,c,j}.
      \tag{LMW6}
   \]
   Taking the supremum over \(0\le r_j\le w_j\) and using \((LMW1)\) gives
   \((LMW2)\).

   Conditions \((LMW2)\)--\((LMW3)\) are exactly \((LMQ4)\), so
   \cref{cor:boltzmann-negative-tail-certificate} gives the conditional
   tilted-excess bound under \((LMW4)\).  The overhead statement follows from
   \cref{cor:conditional-tilted-excess-certificate}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Simplex-envelope influence compiler]
   \label{cor:simplex-envelope-influence-compiler}
   Continue with the notation of
   \cref{cor:singleton-boltzmann-influence-certificate}.  Suppose that every
   certified anchor fiber is contained in the \(q\)-ary product simplex,
   \[
      z_{i,a}\ge0,
      \qquad
      \sum_{a\in[q]}z_{i,a}=1
      \qquad(i=1,\ldots,b).
      \tag{LMX1}
   \]
   For \(j\in[N]\), define the inverse-Gram objective table
   \[
      y_{u,j}=-A_uG_u^+e_j\in\R^{bq},
      \tag{LMX2}
   \]
   and its coordinate envelope around an anchor \(c\in C_u\) by
   \[
      \Delta_{u,c,j}
      =
      \sum_{i=1}^b
      \left(
         \max_{a\in[q]}y_{u,j}(i,a)-y_{u,j}(i,c_i)
      \right).
      \tag{LMX3}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      I_{u,c,j}\le \Delta_{u,c,j}
      \qquad(c\in C_u,\ j\in[N]).
      \tag{LMX4}
   \]
   Hence the Boltzmann singleton condition \((LMW1)\) follows from the purely
   coordinatewise bound
   \[
      \sum_{j=1}^N
      e^{\lambda(M(u)-W(c_j))}\Delta_{u,c,j}
      \le \Xi_u
      \qquad(c\in C_u).
      \tag{LMX5}
   \]

   More generally, let \(\mathcal B_{u,c}\) be any partition of \(C_u\), for
   instance distance or overlap shells around \(c\).  If
   \[
      \Delta_{u,c,j}\le D_{u,c}(B)
      \qquad(j\in B,\ B\in\mathcal B_{u,c})
      \tag{LMX6}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{B\in\mathcal B_{u,c}}
      D_{u,c}(B)
      \sum_{j\in B}e^{\lambda(M(u)-W(c_j))}
      \le \Xi_u ,
      \tag{LMX7}
   \]
   then \((LMW1)\) holds for the anchor \(c\).  Thus an LP/SA proof may be split
   into two code-theoretic tasks: bound the inverse-Gram envelope
   \(\Delta_{u,c,j}\) by distance or overlap, and bound the corresponding
   planted tilted score enumerator.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix \(c\in C_u\), \(j\in[N]\), and \(z\in P_{u,c}\).  By \((LMX1)\),
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \ip{y_{u,j}}{z-\iota(c)}
      &=
      \sum_{i=1}^b
      \left(
         \sum_{a\in[q]}y_{u,j}(i,a)z_{i,a}
         -y_{u,j}(i,c_i)
      \right)\\
      &\le
      \sum_{i=1}^b
      \left(
         \max_{a\in[q]}y_{u,j}(i,a)-y_{u,j}(i,c_i)
      \right)
      =
      \Delta_{u,c,j}.
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{LMX8}
   \]
   Taking the supremum over \(z\in P_{u,c}\), the positive part, and recalling
   \(y_{u,j}=-A_uG_u^+e_j\), proves \((LMX4)\).  Multiplying \((LMX4)\) by
   \(e^{\lambda(M(u)-W(c_j))}\) and summing gives \((LMX5)\Rightarrow(LMW1)\).
   The partitioned form \((LMX6)\)--\((LMX7)\) is the same inequality with the
   sum over \(j\) grouped by \(B\in\mathcal B_{u,c}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Mobility-envelope influence compiler]
   \label{cor:mobility-envelope-influence-compiler}
   Continue with the notation of
   \cref{cor:simplex-envelope-influence-compiler}.  Suppose that for every
   anchor fiber \(P_{u,c}\) we have certified off-anchor mobility bounds
   \[
      z_{i,a}\le \mu_{u,c}(i,a)
      \qquad
      (z\in P_{u,c},\ a\ne c_i),
      \tag{LMY1}
   \]
   in addition to the simplex constraints \((LMX1)\).  Define
   \[
      \Lambda_{u,c,j}
      =
      \sum_{i=1}^b\sum_{a\ne c_i}
      \mu_{u,c}(i,a)
      \bigl(y_{u,j}(i,a)-y_{u,j}(i,c_i)\bigr)_+ ,
      \tag{LMY2}
   \]
   where \(y_{u,j}=-A_uG_u^+e_j\).  Then
   \[
      I_{u,c,j}\le \Lambda_{u,c,j}
      \qquad(c\in C_u,\ j\in[N]).
      \tag{LMY3}
   \]
   Consequently \((LMW1)\) follows from
   \[
      \sum_{j=1}^N
      e^{\lambda(M(u)-W(c_j))}\Lambda_{u,c,j}
      \le \Xi_u
      \qquad(c\in C_u).
      \tag{LMY4}
   \]

   The mobility form is the version meant for an actual LP/SA proof.  The
   unrestricted product-simplex envelope \((LMX3)\) is useful for diagnostics,
   but a polylogarithmic theorem should normally certify that, inside each
   anchor fiber, only a small set of off-anchor symbols can move by a nonnegligible
   amount.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix \(c\in C_u\), \(j\in[N]\), and \(z\in P_{u,c}\).  Since
   \(z_{i,c_i}=1-\sum_{a\ne c_i}z_{i,a}\), we have
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \ip{y_{u,j}}{z-\iota(c)}
      &=
      \sum_{i=1}^b\sum_{a\ne c_i}
      \bigl(y_{u,j}(i,a)-y_{u,j}(i,c_i)\bigr)z_{i,a}\\
      &\le
      \sum_{i=1}^b\sum_{a\ne c_i}
      \mu_{u,c}(i,a)
      \bigl(y_{u,j}(i,a)-y_{u,j}(i,c_i)\bigr)_+
      =
      \Lambda_{u,c,j}.
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{LMY5}
   \]
   Taking the supremum over \(z\in P_{u,c}\) and the positive part proves
   \((LMY3)\).  Multiplying by the Boltzmann weights and summing gives
   \((LMY4)\Rightarrow(LMW1)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Aggregate mobility selector certificate]
   \label{cor:aggregate-mobility-selector-certificate}
   Continue with the notation of
   \cref{cor:mobility-envelope-influence-compiler}.  For a nonnegative selector
   \(\theta\in\R_+^N\), define the aggregate inverse-Gram objective
   \[
      Y_u(\theta)=-A_uG_u^+\theta
      \tag{LMZ1}
   \]
   and the mobility support envelope
   \[
      \mathfrak M_{u,c}(\theta)
      =
      \sum_{i=1}^b\sum_{a\ne c_i}
      \mu_{u,c}(i,a)
      \bigl(Y_u(\theta)(i,a)-Y_u(\theta)(i,c_i)\bigr)_+ .
      \tag{LMZ2}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \Phi_{u,c}\!\left(-A_uG_u^+\theta\right)
      \le
      \mathfrak M_{u,c}(\theta)
      \qquad(c\in C_u,\ \theta\ge0).
      \tag{LMZ3}
   \]

   Consequently the dyadic selector certificate \((LMT6)\) follows if
   \[
      \sup_{\theta\in\mathcal R_u(k\delta)}
      \mathfrak M_{u,c}(\theta)
      \le
      C_u e^{-(\lambda+\eta_u)k\delta}
      \qquad(k\ge0,\ c\in C_u).
      \tag{LMZ4}
   \]

   There is also a direct Boltzmann form.  Put
   \[
      w_j=\exp(\lambda(M(u)-W(c_j))).
      \tag{LMZ5}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sup_{0\le\theta_j\le w_j}
      \mathfrak M_{u,c}(\theta)
      \le \Xi_u
      \qquad(c\in C_u),
      \tag{LMZ6}
   \]
   then every anchored excess \(h\in E_u\) satisfies \((LMW2)\).  Hence, under
   the scalar and orthogonal hypotheses \((LMW3)\)--\((LMW4)\), the conditional
   tilted-excess bound \((LPT2)\) follows with \(A_\lambda\).

   This is the aggregate version of the mobility route.  Since
   \((x+y)_+\le x_++y_+\), the singleton mobility bound \((LMY4)\) implies
   \((LMZ6)\).  The converse need not hold: \((LMZ6)\) keeps cancellations among
   the columns of \(G_u^+\) before the positive part is taken.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix \(z\in P_{u,c}\).  The same block-simplex calculation as in \((LMY5)\),
   with \(y_{u,j}\) replaced by the aggregate objective \(Y_u(\theta)\), gives
   \[
      \ip{Y_u(\theta)}{z-\iota(c)}
      \le
      \mathfrak M_{u,c}(\theta).
      \tag{LMZ7}
   \]
   Taking the supremum over \(z\in P_{u,c}\) proves \((LMZ3)\).  Combining
   \((LMZ3)\) with \cref{cor:anchor-fiber-internal-tail-certificate} gives the
   dyadic implication \((LMZ4)\Rightarrow(LMT6)\).

   For the Boltzmann form, fix \(h=z-\iota(c)\in E_u\).  By \((LMW5)\),
   \[
      \sum_jw_ja_u(h)_j^-
      =
      \sup_{0\le\theta_j\le w_j}
      \ip{-A_uG_u^+\theta}{h}.
      \tag{LMZ8}
   \]
   Applying \((LMZ3)\) inside this supremum and then \((LMZ6)\) gives
   \((LMW2)\).  Together with \((LMW3)\)--\((LMW4)\), this is the same final
   implication used in
   \cref{cor:singleton-boltzmann-influence-certificate}.

   Finally, by subadditivity of the positive part and the definition of
   \(\Lambda_{u,c,j}\),
   \[
      \mathfrak M_{u,c}(\theta)
      \le
      \sum_j\theta_j\Lambda_{u,c,j}.
      \tag{LMZ9}
   \]
   Thus \((LMY4)\) implies \((LMZ6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Box-dual mobility certificate]
   \label{cor:box-dual-mobility-certificate}
   Continue with the notation of
   \cref{cor:aggregate-mobility-selector-certificate}.  For every off-anchor
   coordinate-symbol pair \((i,a)\), \(a\ne c_i\), define
   \[
      \ell_{u,c,i,a}(j)
      =
      y_{u,j}(i,a)-y_{u,j}(i,c_i),
      \qquad j\in[N].
      \tag{LNA1}
   \]
   Then, for every nonnegative box \(0\le \theta_j\le w_j\),
   \[
      \sup_{0\le \theta_j\le w_j}
      \mathfrak M_{u,c}(\theta)
      =
      \sup_{0\le \beta_{i,a}\le\mu_{u,c}(i,a)}
      \sum_{j=1}^N
      w_j
      \left(
         \sum_{i=1}^b\sum_{a\ne c_i}
         \beta_{i,a}\ell_{u,c,i,a}(j)
      \right)_+ .
      \tag{LNA2}
   \]
   Consequently the Boltzmann aggregate condition \((LMZ6)\) is equivalent to
   \[
      \sup_{0\le \beta_{i,a}\le\mu_{u,c}(i,a)}
      \sum_{j=1}^N
      e^{\lambda(M(u)-W(c_j))}
      \left(
         \sum_{i=1}^b\sum_{a\ne c_i}
         \beta_{i,a}\ell_{u,c,i,a}(j)
      \right)_+
      \le \Xi_u .
      \tag{LNA3}
   \]
   Likewise, the dyadic aggregate condition \((LMZ4)\) is equivalent to
   \[
      \sup_{0\le \beta_{i,a}\le\mu_{u,c}(i,a)}
      \sum_{j:\ M(u)-W(c_j)\ge k\delta}
      \left(
         \sum_{i=1}^b\sum_{a\ne c_i}
         \beta_{i,a}\ell_{u,c,i,a}(j)
      \right)_+
      \le
      C_u e^{-(\lambda+\eta_u)k\delta}.
      \tag{LNA4}
   \]

   Thus a failed mobility certificate exposes a concrete off-anchor multiplier
   pattern \(\beta\).  The remaining low-rate code theorem can be stated as a
   tilted positive-part enumerator bound for every such pattern.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(Y_u(\theta)=\sum_j\theta_jy_{u,j}\), for every off-anchor
   \((i,a)\),
   \[
      Y_u(\theta)(i,a)-Y_u(\theta)(i,c_i)
      =
      \sum_{j=1}^N\theta_j\ell_{u,c,i,a}(j).
      \tag{LNA5}
   \]
   Using \(\mu x_+=\sup_{0\le\beta\le\mu}\beta x\), we get
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \mathfrak M_{u,c}(\theta)
      &=
      \sup_{0\le \beta_{i,a}\le\mu_{u,c}(i,a)}
      \sum_{i=1}^b\sum_{a\ne c_i}
      \beta_{i,a}
      \sum_{j=1}^N\theta_j\ell_{u,c,i,a}(j)\\
      &=
      \sup_{0\le \beta_{i,a}\le\mu_{u,c}(i,a)}
      \sum_{j=1}^N
      \theta_j
      \left(
         \sum_{i=1}^b\sum_{a\ne c_i}
         \beta_{i,a}\ell_{u,c,i,a}(j)
      \right).
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{LNA6}
   \]
   Taking the supremum over the compact box \(0\le\theta_j\le w_j\) and exchanging
   the two finite-dimensional suprema gives \((LNA2)\), because
   \[
      \sup_{0\le\theta_j\le w_j}\sum_j\theta_jv_j
      =
      \sum_jw_j(v_j)_+ .
      \tag{LNA7}
   \]
   Taking \(w_j=e^{\lambda(M(u)-W(c_j))}\) gives \((LNA3)\).  Taking
   \(w_j=\mathbf 1_{\{M(u)-W(c_j)\ge k\delta\}}\) gives \((LNA4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Laplace-tail mobility enumerator compiler]
   \label{cor:laplace-tail-mobility-enumerator}
   Continue with the notation of
   \cref{cor:box-dual-mobility-certificate}.  For an off-anchor mobility pattern
   \(\beta\), write
   \[
      L_{u,c,\beta}(j)
      =
      \sum_{i=1}^b\sum_{a\ne c_i}
      \beta_{i,a}\ell_{u,c,i,a}(j).
      \tag{LNB1}
   \]
   For nonnegative weights \(w=(w_j)\), define the weighted positive-part
   enumerator and its tail function by
   \[
      P_{u,c,w}(\beta)=\sum_{j=1}^Nw_j(L_{u,c,\beta}(j))_+,
      \qquad
      T_{u,c,w,\beta}(t)=\sum_{j:\ L_{u,c,\beta}(j)\ge t}w_j .
      \tag{LNB2}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      P_{u,c,w}(\beta)
      =
      \int_0^\infty T_{u,c,w,\beta}(t)\,dt .
      \tag{LNB3}
   \]
   In particular, if for some \(H_{u,c}\ge0\) and \(\nu>0\),
   \[
      T_{u,c,w,\beta}(t)\le H_{u,c}e^{-\nu t}
      \qquad(t\ge0,\ 0\le\beta_{i,a}\le\mu_{u,c}(i,a)),
      \tag{LNB4}
   \]
   then
   \[
      \sup_{0\le\beta\le\mu_{u,c}}P_{u,c,w}(\beta)
      \le \frac{H_{u,c}}{\nu}.
      \tag{LNB5}
   \]
   A convenient sufficient condition for \((LNB5)\) is the Laplace bound
   \[
      \sup_{0\le\beta\le\mu_{u,c}}
      \sum_{j=1}^Nw_j\exp(\nu L_{u,c,\beta}(j))
      \le H_{u,c},
      \tag{LNB6}
   \]
   which also implies \((LNB5)\) with \(H_{u,c}/\nu\).

   Therefore the Boltzmann aggregate certificate \((LNA3)\) follows by taking
   \(w_j=\exp(\lambda(M(u)-W(c_j)))\) and proving either \((LNB4)\) or
   \((LNB6)\) with \(H_{u,c}/\nu\le\Xi_u\).  The dyadic certificate \((LNA4)\)
   follows by taking \(w_j=\mathbf 1_{\{M(u)-W(c_j)\ge k\delta\}}\) and
   \(H_{u,c}/\nu\le C_u e^{-(\lambda+\eta_u)k\delta}\).

   Thus the remaining code theorem may be stated in the standard language of
   tilted tail bounds or tilted moment bounds for the scalar score
   \(L_{u,c,\beta}(j)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For each real \(x\), \(x_+=\int_0^\infty\mathbf 1_{\{x\ge t\}}\,dt\).  Since
   \(N<\infty\), summing this identity over \(j\) with weights \(w_j\) proves
   \((LNB3)\).  The tail implication \((LNB4)\Rightarrow(LNB5)\) follows by
   integrating \(H_{u,c}e^{-\nu t}\).

   For the Laplace form, Markov's inequality gives
   \[
      T_{u,c,w,\beta}(t)
      \le
      e^{-\nu t}
      \sum_{j=1}^Nw_j\exp(\nu L_{u,c,\beta}(j)).
      \tag{LNB7}
   \]
   Hence \((LNB6)\) implies \((LNB4)\), and therefore \((LNB5)\).  The final
   Boltzmann and dyadic statements are exactly
   \cref{cor:box-dual-mobility-certificate} with these two choices of \(w\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Balanced Gram form of mobility scores]
   \label{cor:balanced-gram-mobility-scores}
   Continue with the notation of
   \cref{cor:laplace-tail-mobility-enumerator}.  For an off-anchor mobility
   pattern \(\beta\), define the ambient block-balanced direction
   \(d_{u,c,\beta}\in\R^{bq}\) by
   \[
      d_{u,c,\beta}(i,a)
      =
      \begin{cases}
         \beta_{i,a}, & a\ne c_i,\\[2mm]
         -\displaystyle\sum_{a'\ne c_i}\beta_{i,a'}, & a=c_i .
      \end{cases}
      \tag{LNC1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \sum_{a\in[q]}d_{u,c,\beta}(i,a)=0
      \qquad(i=1,\ldots,b),
      \tag{LNC2}
   \]
   and, writing
   \[
      \zeta_{u,c,\beta}=A_u^\top d_{u,c,\beta},
      \qquad
      s_{u,c,\beta}=G_u^+\zeta_{u,c,\beta},
      \tag{LNC3}
   \]
   the mobility score from \((LNB1)\) has the exact Gram form
   \[
      L_{u,c,\beta}(j)=-s_{u,c,\beta}(j)
      =
      -\left(G_u^+A_u^\top d_{u,c,\beta}\right)_j .
      \tag{LNC4}
   \]
   Equivalently,
   \[
      \zeta_{u,c,\beta}(j)
      =
      \sum_{i=1}^b\sum_{a\ne c_i}
      \beta_{i,a}
      \bigl(
         \mathbf 1_{\{c_j(i)=a\}}
         -
         \mathbf 1_{\{c_j(i)=c_i\}}
      \bigr).
      \tag{LNC5}
   \]
   Therefore the Boltzmann aggregate mobility certificate \((LNA3)\) is exactly
   \[
      \sup_{0\le\beta\le\mu_{u,c}}
      \sum_{j=1}^N
      e^{\lambda(M(u)-W(c_j))}
      \left(s_{u,c,\beta}(j)\right)^-
      \le \Xi_u ,
      \tag{LNC6}
   \]
   and the Laplace sufficient condition \((LNB6)\) is exactly
   \[
      \sup_{0\le\beta\le\mu_{u,c}}
      \sum_{j=1}^N
      w_j\exp\!\left(-\nu s_{u,c,\beta}(j)\right)
      \le H_{u,c}.
      \tag{LNC7}
   \]
   Finally, the projection of \(d_{u,c,\beta}\) onto the codeword span is
   \(A_uG_u^+\zeta_{u,c,\beta}\), and
   \[
      \bigl\|A_uG_u^+\zeta_{u,c,\beta}\bigr\|_2^2
      =
      \zeta_{u,c,\beta}^\top G_u^+\zeta_{u,c,\beta}.
      \tag{LNC8}
   \]
   Thus the remaining mobility theorem is a one-sided moment bound for
   inverse-Gram coefficients of block-balanced directions, not a separate
   pseudocodeword-support statement.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By the definition of \(d_{u,c,\beta}\), each coordinate block sums to zero,
   proving \((LNC2)\).  Also
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \ip{y_{u,j}}{d_{u,c,\beta}}
      &=
      \sum_{i=1}^b\sum_{a\ne c_i}
      \beta_{i,a}\bigl(y_{u,j}(i,a)-y_{u,j}(i,c_i)\bigr)\\
      &=
      L_{u,c,\beta}(j).
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{LNC9}
   \]
   Since \(y_{u,j}=-A_uG_u^+e_j\) and \(G_u^+\) is symmetric,
   \[
      L_{u,c,\beta}(j)
      =
      \ip{-A_uG_u^+e_j}{d_{u,c,\beta}}
      =
      -e_j^\top G_u^+A_u^\top d_{u,c,\beta},
   \]
   which is \((LNC4)\).  Formula \((LNC5)\) is obtained by taking the inner
   product of \(d_{u,c,\beta}\) with the \(j\)th one-hot codeword column
   \(\iota(c_j)\).  Substituting \(L_{u,c,\beta}(j)=-s_{u,c,\beta}(j)\) into
   \((LNA3)\) and \((LNB6)\) gives \((LNC6)\) and \((LNC7)\).

   The last identity is the same projection identity used in
   \cref{cor:gram-projection-certificate}: \(A_uG_u^+A_u^\top\) is the
   orthogonal projection onto the column span of \(A_u\), and
   \(\zeta_{u,c,\beta}\in\operatorname{range}(G_u)\).  Hence
   \[
      \|A_uG_u^+\zeta_{u,c,\beta}\|_2^2
      =
      \zeta_{u,c,\beta}^\top G_u^+G_uG_u^+\zeta_{u,c,\beta}
      =
      \zeta_{u,c,\beta}^\top G_u^+\zeta_{u,c,\beta}.
   \]
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Score-leader anchoring]
   \label{cor:score-leader-anchoring}
   Work at a branch-and-bound node \(u\), and let
   \[
      c_\star=c_{j_\star}\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{c_j\in C_u}W(c_j),
      \qquad
      M(u)=W(c_\star),
      \tag{LND1}
   \]
   with deterministic tie-breaking.  Define the score-measurable anchor map
   \[
      \alpha_u(z)=c_\star\qquad(z\in P_u),
      \tag{LND2}
   \]
   so the only nonempty anchor fiber is \(P_{u,c_\star}=P_u\), and
   \[
      E_u^\star=\{z-\iota(c_\star):z\in P_u\}.
      \tag{LND3}
   \]
   Then the anchored excess domination \((LPF6)\) holds with \(E_u^\star\):
   \[
      U(u)-M(u)
      \le
      X_u^\star(w):=\sup_{h\in E_u^\star}\ip{w}{h}.
      \tag{LND4}
   \]
   Moreover the conditional projection, Boltzmann negative-tail, anchor-fiber,
   mobility, box-dual, Laplace-tail, and balanced-Gram certificates above remain
   valid with this single random fiber, provided their hypotheses are verified
   almost surely after conditioning on \(\mathcal G_u=\sigma(W(c):c\in C_u)\).

   In particular, in the Boltzmann mobility certificate \((LNC6)\), the anchor
   column has weight
   \[
      e^{\lambda(M(u)-W(c_\star))}=1 .
      \tag{LND5}
   \]
   Thus the diagonal self-mobility of the anchor is not multiplied by the
   potentially large Boltzmann penalty attached to a low-scoring anchor.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For every \(z\in P_u\),
   \[
      \ip{w}{z}
      =
      W(c_\star)+\ip{w}{z-\iota(c_\star)}
      \le
      M(u)+X_u^\star(w).
   \]
   Taking the supremum over \(z\in P_u\) proves \((LND4)\).

   The remaining certificates use the anchor set only through the realized
   excess set and through quantities measurable with respect to
   \(\mathcal G_u\).  The leader \(c_\star\), the fiber \(P_{u,c_\star}\), and
   the mobility bounds for that fiber are \(\mathcal G_u\)-measurable once the
   true codeword scores in the node are revealed.  Conditioning on
   \(\mathcal G_u\), the orthogonal Gaussian residual in
   \cref{cor:conditional-gaussian-projection-certificate} is still independent,
   and all support-function, box-duality, and Laplace steps are deterministic
   finite-dimensional inequalities for the realized fiber.  Hence the proofs
   apply verbatim with this score-measurable anchor.  Finally, \((LND5)\) is
   immediate from \(M(u)=W(c_\star)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Diagonal-preconditioned leader-mobility split]
   \label{cor:diagonal-preconditioned-leader-mobility}
   Continue with the score-leader anchor of
   \cref{cor:score-leader-anchoring} and the balanced Gram notation of
   \cref{cor:balanced-gram-mobility-scores}.  For an off-anchor mobility pattern
   \(\beta\), put
   \[
      B_\beta=\sum_{i=1}^b\sum_{a\ne c_\star(i)}\beta_{i,a},
      \qquad
      \zeta_\beta=A_u^\top d_{u,c_\star,\beta},
      \tag{LNE1}
   \]
   and write the inverse-Gram coefficient vector as
   \[
      s_\beta=G_u^+\zeta_\beta
      =
      \frac1b\,\zeta_\beta+r_\beta,
      \qquad
      r_\beta=\left(G_u^+-\frac1b I\right)\zeta_\beta .
      \tag{LNE2}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \zeta_\beta(j_\star)=-B_\beta,
      \tag{LNE3}
   \]
   and, for the Boltzmann weights
   \(w_j=e^{\lambda(M(u)-W(c_j))}\),
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \sum_{j=1}^N w_j(s_\beta(j))^-
      &\le
      \frac{B_\beta}{b}
      +
      \frac1b\sum_{j\ne j_\star}w_j(\zeta_\beta(j))^-\\
      &\qquad+
      \sum_{j=1}^Nw_j|r_\beta(j)|.
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{LNE4}
   \]
   Consequently the leader-anchored Boltzmann mobility certificate \((LNC6)\)
   follows if the three quantities on the right-hand side of \((LNE4)\) have
   total supremum at most \(\Xi_u\) over \(0\le\beta\le\mu_{u,c_\star}\).

   In the ideal diagonal model \(G_u=bI\), the residual term \(r_\beta\) vanishes,
   and the remaining theorem is exactly an off-anchor planted enumerator bound
   for \((\zeta_\beta(j))^-\), plus the explicit self-mobility budget
   \(B_\beta/b\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Formula \((LNE3)\) follows from \((LNC5)\): for \(j=j_\star\), every
   coordinate has \(c_j(i)=c_\star(i)\), so each off-anchor symbol contributes
   the second indicator and not the first.

   Since \(s_\beta=b^{-1}\zeta_\beta+r_\beta\), the scalar inequality
   \((x+y)^-\le x^-+|y|\) gives
   \[
      (s_\beta(j))^-
      \le
      \frac1b(\zeta_\beta(j))^-+|r_\beta(j)|.
      \tag{LNE5}
   \]
   Multiplying by \(w_j\) and summing proves \((LNE4)\), using
   \(w_{j_\star}=1\) from \((LND5)\) and
   \((\zeta_\beta(j_\star))^-=B_\beta\).  The certificate implication is exactly
   \((LNC6)\).  If \(G_u=bI\), then \(G_u^+-b^{-1}I=0\), so \(r_\beta=0\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Coordinate-overlap load closure]
   \label{cor:coordinate-overlap-load-closure}
   Continue with the notation of
   \cref{cor:diagonal-preconditioned-leader-mobility}.  For a mobility pattern
   \(\beta\), define its per-coordinate mass
   \[
      B_{\beta,i}=\sum_{a\ne c_\star(i)}\beta_{i,a},
      \qquad
      B_\beta=\sum_{i=1}^bB_{\beta,i}.
      \tag{LNF1}
   \]
   Define the Boltzmann coordinate-overlap loads of the score leader by
   \[
      \Lambda_i
      =
      \sum_{\substack{j\ne j_\star\\ c_j(i)=c_\star(i)}}
      e^{\lambda(M(u)-W(c_j))}
      \qquad(i=1,\ldots,b),
      \tag{LNF2}
   \]
   and the preconditioning residual envelope
   \[
      \mathfrak E_u^{\rm gram}(\mu)
      =
      \sup_{0\le\beta\le\mu_{u,c_\star}}
      \sum_{j=1}^N
      e^{\lambda(M(u)-W(c_j))}
      \left|
         \left(
            \left(G_u^+-\frac1bI\right)A_u^\top d_{u,c_\star,\beta}
         \right)_j
      \right|.
      \tag{LNF3}
   \]
   Then, for every \(0\le\beta\le\mu_{u,c_\star}\),
   \[
      \sum_{j=1}^N
      e^{\lambda(M(u)-W(c_j))}
      (s_\beta(j))^-
      \le
      \frac1b\sum_{i=1}^bB_{\beta,i}(1+\Lambda_i)
      +
      \mathfrak E_u^{\rm gram}(\mu).
      \tag{LNF4}
   \]
   Consequently the leader-anchored Boltzmann mobility certificate \((LNC6)\)
   follows from the deterministic check
   \[
      \sup_{0\le\beta\le\mu_{u,c_\star}}
      \frac1b\sum_{i=1}^bB_{\beta,i}(1+\Lambda_i)
      +
      \mathfrak E_u^{\rm gram}(\mu)
      \le \Xi_u .
      \tag{LNF5}
   \]
   A coarser but simpler sufficient condition is
   \[
      \frac{1+\Lambda_{\max}}{b}
      \sum_{i=1}^b\sum_{a\ne c_\star(i)}\mu_{u,c_\star}(i,a)
      +
      \mathfrak E_u^{\rm gram}(\mu)
      \le \Xi_u,
      \qquad
      \Lambda_{\max}=\max_i\Lambda_i .
      \tag{LNF6}
   \]

   Thus the off-anchor planted enumerator is a weighted list-recovery load:
   low-rate code geometry only has to prevent large Boltzmann mass from sharing
   many still-mobile coordinates with the current score leader, up to the
   separate inverse-Gram residual \(\mathfrak E_u^{\rm gram}(\mu)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   From \((LNC5)\), with \(c=c_\star\),
   \[
      \zeta_\beta(j)
      =
      \sum_{i:\ c_j(i)\ne c_\star(i)}
      \beta_{i,c_j(i)}
      -
      \sum_{i:\ c_j(i)=c_\star(i)}B_{\beta,i}.
      \tag{LNF7}
   \]
   The first sum is nonnegative.  Hence
   \[
      (\zeta_\beta(j))^-
      \le
      \sum_{i:\ c_j(i)=c_\star(i)}B_{\beta,i}.
      \tag{LNF8}
   \]
   Multiplying \((LNF8)\) by the Boltzmann weights and summing over
   \(j\ne j_\star\) gives
   \[
      \sum_{j\ne j_\star}
      e^{\lambda(M(u)-W(c_j))}(\zeta_\beta(j))^-
      \le
      \sum_{i=1}^bB_{\beta,i}\Lambda_i .
      \tag{LNF9}
   \]
   Combining this with \((LNE4)\), \((LNE3)\), and the definition of
   \(\mathfrak E_u^{\rm gram}(\mu)\) proves \((LNF4)\).  Taking the supremum over
   \(0\le\beta\le\mu_{u,c_\star}\) proves \((LNF5)\), and \((LNF6)\) follows from
   \(B_{\beta,i}\le\sum_{a\ne c_\star(i)}\mu_{u,c_\star}(i,a)\) and
   \(\Lambda_i\le\Lambda_{\max}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Convex-hull residual mobility certificate]
   \label{cor:convex-residual-mobility-certificate}
   Work at a branch-and-bound node \(u\).  Let
   \[
      K_u=\operatorname{conv}\{\iota(c):c\in C_u\}
      \tag{LNG1}
   \]
   be the true codeword convex hull inside the product of coordinate simplices.
   Suppose that each \(z\in P_u\) is assigned a convex witness \(x(z)\in K_u\),
   and put
   \[
      h(z)=z-x(z),
      \qquad
      E_u^{\rm res}=\{h(z):z\in P_u\}.
      \tag{LNG2}
   \]
   Assume the positive residual mass has certified coordinate-symbol bounds
   \[
      h(z)_{i,a}^+\le\mu_u(i,a)
      \qquad(z\in P_u,\ i\in[b],\ a\in[q]).
      \tag{LNG3}
   \]
   Then the anchored excess domination \((LPF6)\) holds with \(E_u^{\rm res}\):
   \[
      U(u)-M(u)
      \le
      X_u^{\rm res}(w):=\sup_{h\in E_u^{\rm res}}\ip{w}{h}.
      \tag{LNG4}
   \]

   For a nonnegative selector \(\theta\in\R_+^N\), write
   \(Y_u(\theta)=-A_uG_u^+\theta\) as before and define
   \[
      \mathfrak R_u(\theta)
      =
      \sum_{i=1}^b\sum_{a\in[q]}
      \mu_u(i,a)
      \left(
         Y_u(\theta)(i,a)-\min_{a'\in[q]}Y_u(\theta)(i,a')
      \right)_+ .
      \tag{LNG5}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \sup_{h\in E_u^{\rm res}}\ip{Y_u(\theta)}{h}
      \le
      \mathfrak R_u(\theta)
      \qquad(\theta\ge0).
      \tag{LNG6}
   \]
   Consequently, with Boltzmann weights
   \(w_j=\exp(\lambda(M(u)-W(c_j)))\), the residual version of the Boltzmann
   negative-tail certificate follows from
   \[
      \sup_{0\le\theta_j\le w_j}
      \mathfrak R_u(\theta)
      \le \Xi_u .
      \tag{LNG7}
   \]

   Equivalently, \((LNG7)\) is the transported balanced-direction bound
   \[
      \sup_{\substack{
         0\le\beta_{i,a}\le\mu_u(i,a),\ \pi_{i,a}\ge0\\
         \sum_a\pi_{i,a}=\sum_a\beta_{i,a}\ \forall i
      }}
      \sum_{j=1}^N
      w_j
      \left(
         -\left(G_u^+A_u^\top d_{\beta,\pi}\right)_j
      \right)_+
      \le \Xi_u ,
      \tag{LNG8}
   \]
   where
   \[
      d_{\beta,\pi}(i,a)=\beta_{i,a}-\pi_{i,a},
      \qquad
      \sum_a d_{\beta,\pi}(i,a)=0 .
      \tag{LNG9}
   \]

   Thus the score-leader certificate can be replaced by a genuinely fractional
   one: if \(z=\iota(c)\) is already a true codeword, choose \(x(z)=z\), so
   \(h(z)=0\).  Integral low-scoring codewords are no longer charged as mobility;
   only the residual displacement from the true convex hull has to satisfy the
   inverse-Gram tail bound.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For \(z\in P_u\), the witness \(x(z)\in K_u\) is a convex combination of true
   codewords in \(C_u\).  Hence
   \[
      \ip{w}{x(z)}
      \le
      M(u),
      \tag{LNG10}
   \]
   and therefore
   \[
      \ip{w}{z}
      =
      \ip{w}{x(z)}+\ip{w}{h(z)}
      \le
      M(u)+X_u^{\rm res}(w).
      \tag{LNG11}
   \]
   Taking the supremum over \(z\in P_u\) proves \((LNG4)\).

   Fix \(h=h(z)\in E_u^{\rm res}\).  Since both \(z\) and \(x(z)\) lie in the
   product of coordinate simplices, each coordinate block of \(h\) has sum zero.
   For a fixed coordinate \(i\), write
   \[
      \beta_{i,a}=h_{i,a}^+,
      \qquad
      \pi_{i,a}=h_{i,a}^- .
      \tag{LNG12}
   \]
   Then \(0\le\beta_{i,a}\le\mu_u(i,a)\), \(\pi_{i,a}\ge0\), and
   \(\sum_a\pi_{i,a}=\sum_a\beta_{i,a}\).  Thus, for any vector \(Y\),
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \sum_aY(i,a)h_{i,a}
      &=
      \sum_aY(i,a)(\beta_{i,a}-\pi_{i,a})\\
      &\le
      \sum_a\beta_{i,a}
      \left(Y(i,a)-\min_{a'}Y(i,a')\right)\\
      &\le
      \sum_a\mu_u(i,a)
      \left(Y(i,a)-\min_{a'}Y(i,a')\right)_+ .
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{LNG13}
   \]
   Summing \((LNG13)\) over \(i\) with \(Y=Y_u(\theta)\) proves \((LNG6)\).

   The same support-function identity used in \((LMZ8)\), now with
   \(E_u^{\rm res}\), gives
   \[
      \sum_jw_j a_u(h)_j^-
      =
      \sup_{0\le\theta_j\le w_j}\ip{-A_uG_u^+\theta}{h}.
      \tag{LNG14}
   \]
   Combining \((LNG6)\) with \((LNG7)\) gives the residual Boltzmann negative-tail
   bound.

   Finally,
   \[
      \mathfrak R_u(\theta)
      =
      \sup_{\substack{
         0\le\beta_{i,a}\le\mu_u(i,a),\ \pi_{i,a}\ge0\\
         \sum_a\pi_{i,a}=\sum_a\beta_{i,a}\ \forall i
      }}
      \ip{-A_uG_u^+\theta}{d_{\beta,\pi}} .
      \tag{LNG15}
   \]
   The feasible set is compact, so exchanging the two finite-dimensional suprema
   over \(\theta\) and \((\beta,\pi)\) gives \((LNG8)\), exactly as in the proof of
   \cref{cor:box-dual-mobility-certificate}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Residual Hall verifier]
   \label{cor:residual-hall-verifier}
   Continue with the notation of
   \cref{cor:convex-residual-mobility-certificate}.  Fix a nonnegative residual
   budget \(\mu\in\R_+^{bq}\).  The witness assignment required in
   \((LNG2)\)--\((LNG3)\) exists for every \(z\in P_u\) if and only if, for every
   nonnegative symbol-score table \(y\in\R_+^{bq}\),
   \[
      \sup_{z\in P_u}\ip{y}{z}
      -
      \max_{c\in C_u}\ip{y}{\iota(c)}
      \le
      \ip{y}{\mu}.
      \tag{LNH1}
   \]
   Equivalently, every failed residual budget exposes a concrete separator:
   there are \(z\in P_u\) and \(y\ge0\) such that
   \[
      \ip{y}{z}
      >
      \max_{c\in C_u}\ip{y}{\iota(c)}
      +
      \ip{y}{\mu}.
      \tag{LNH2}
   \]

   Thus the convex-hull residual hypothesis is not a black box.  It can be
   checked by the same primitives used by a certified decoder: optimize the
   nonnegative score table \(y\) over the relaxation \(P_u\), optimize it over
   true codewords, and compare the gap to the residual price \(\ip{y}{\mu}\).
   In the special case \(\mu=0\), \((LNH1)\) is exactly the assertion
   \(P_u\subseteq K_u\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix \(z\in P_u\).  The condition \(h(z)^+\le\mu\) for some
   \(h(z)=z-x(z)\), \(x(z)\in K_u\), is equivalent to
   \[
      z-\mu\in K_u-\R_+^{bq}.
      \tag{LNH3}
   \]
   Indeed, \(z-\mu\le x(z)\) coordinatewise is the same as
   \(z-\mu=x(z)-s\) for some \(s\ge0\).

   If \((LNH3)\) holds, then for every \(y\ge0\),
   \[
      \ip{y}{z-\mu}
      \le
      \max_{x\in K_u}\ip{y}{x}
      =
      \max_{c\in C_u}\ip{y}{\iota(c)}.
      \tag{LNH4}
   \]
   This is \((LNH1)\) for the fixed \(z\), and taking the supremum over
   \(z\in P_u\) preserves it.

   Conversely, suppose \((LNH3)\) fails for some \(z\).  The set
   \(K_u-\R_+^{bq}\) is a closed convex polyhedron, so the finite-dimensional
   separation theorem gives a vector \(y\) such that
   \[
      \ip{y}{z-\mu}
      >
      \sup_{x\in K_u,\ s\ge0}\ip{y}{x-s}.
      \tag{LNH5}
   \]
   The supremum on the right is finite only when \(y\ge0\); then it equals
   \(\max_{x\in K_u}\ip{y}{x}\).  Since a linear functional on \(K_u\) is
   maximized at a codeword vertex, \((LNH5)\) becomes \((LNH2)\).  This proves the
   equivalence.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Priced residual-gap duality]
   \label{cor:priced-residual-gap-duality}
   Continue with the notation of \cref{cor:residual-hall-verifier}.  For a
   nonnegative price table \(r\in\R_+^{bq}\), define the one-sided priced
   distance from \(z\in P_u\) to the true codeword convex hull by
   \[
      D_u^+(z;r)
      =
      \inf_{x\in K_u}
      \sum_{i=1}^b\sum_{a\in[q]}r_{i,a}(z_{i,a}-x_{i,a})_+ .
      \tag{LNI1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      D_u^+(z;r)
      =
      \sup_{0\le y\le r}
      \left(
         \ip{y}{z}
         -
         \max_{c\in C_u}\ip{y}{\iota(c)}
      \right).
      \tag{LNI2}
   \]
   Consequently,
   \[
      D_u^+(P_u;r)
      :=
      \sup_{z\in P_u}D_u^+(z;r)
      =
      \sup_{0\le y\le r}
      \left(
         \sup_{z\in P_u}\ip{y}{z}
         -
         \max_{c\in C_u}\ip{y}{\iota(c)}
      \right).
      \tag{LNI3}
   \]

   For an arbitrary objective \(Y\in\R^{bq}\), set
   \[
      r_Y(i,a)=Y(i,a)-\min_{a'\in[q]}Y(i,a')\ge0 .
      \tag{LNI4}
   \]
   Since both \(z\) and \(K_u\) lie in the product of coordinate simplices,
   \[
      \sup_{z\in P_u}
      \left(
         \ip{Y}{z}
         -
         \max_{c\in C_u}\ip{Y}{\iota(c)}
      \right)
      \le
      D_u^+(P_u;r_Y).
      \tag{LNI5}
   \]

   Thus a direction-wise convex-hull gap can be certified without choosing a
   global residual budget \(\mu\).  For the inverse-Gram selector objectives
   \(Y_u(\theta)=-A_uG_u^+\theta\), the build-time separator only has to search
   clipped nonnegative score tables \(0\le y\le r_{Y_u(\theta)}\) and compare
   their relaxation optimum to their true-code optimum.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For a scalar \(t\), \(r\,t_+=\sup_{0\le y\le r}yt\).  Therefore, for fixed
   \(z\),
   \[
      \sum_{i,a}r_{i,a}(z_{i,a}-x_{i,a})_+
      =
      \sup_{0\le y\le r}\ip{y}{z-x}.
      \tag{LNI6}
   \]
   The sets \(K_u\) and \(\{y:0\le y\le r\}\) are polytopes, and the displayed
   expression is a finite linear program in the variables \((x,t)\).  Its dual
   has variables \(0\le y\le r\), so finite-dimensional LP duality gives
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      D_u^+(z;r)
      &=
      \inf_{x\in K_u}\sup_{0\le y\le r}\ip{y}{z-x}\\
      &=
      \sup_{0\le y\le r}
      \left(
         \ip{y}{z}-\sup_{x\in K_u}\ip{y}{x}
      \right).
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{LNI7}
   \]
   A linear functional on \(K_u\) is maximized at a codeword vertex, proving
   \((LNI2)\).  Taking the supremum over \(z\in P_u\) and exchanging the two
   suprema gives \((LNI3)\).

   For \((LNI5)\), fix \(z\in P_u\) and \(x\in K_u\).  Since each coordinate
   block of \(z-x\) sums to zero,
   \[
      \ip{Y}{z-x}
      =
      \sum_{i,a}r_Y(i,a)(z_{i,a}-x_{i,a})
      \le
      \sum_{i,a}r_Y(i,a)(z_{i,a}-x_{i,a})_+ .
      \tag{LNI8}
   \]
   Taking the infimum over \(x\in K_u\) gives
   \[
      \ip{Y}{z}-\max_{c\in C_u}\ip{Y}{\iota(c)}
      \le
      D_u^+(z;r_Y),
      \tag{LNI9}
   \]
   and then taking the supremum over \(z\in P_u\) proves \((LNI5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Direct coefficient projection certificate]
   \label{cor:direct-coefficient-projection-certificate}
   Work in the branch-and-bound setting of
   \cref{cor:conditional-tilted-excess-certificate}.  At a node \(u\), enumerate
   \(C_u=\{c_1,\ldots,c_N\}\), let \(A_u\) and \(G_u=A_u^\top A_u\) be as in
   \cref{cor:gram-projection-certificate}, and put \(W_j=W(c_j)\),
   \(M=M(u)=\max_jW_j\).  For each \(z\in P_u\), suppose we have selected a
   score-span coefficient vector \(b_u(z)\in\R^N\) satisfying
   \[
      A_ub_u(z)=\Pi_u z
      \qquad
      \text{equivalently}\qquad
      G_ub_u(z)=A_u^\top z,
      \tag{LNJ1}
   \]
   and define
   \[
      \kappa_u(z)=\sum_{j=1}^Nb_u(z)_j .
      \tag{LNJ2}
   \]
   Let
   \[
      \omega_u^{P,\perp}
      =
      \E_g\sup_{z\in P_u}\ip{g}{\Pi_u^\perp z},
      \qquad
      r_u^{P,\perp}
      =
      \sup_{z\in P_u}\|\Pi_u^\perp z\|_2 ,
      \tag{LNJ3}
   \]
   where \(g\sim N(0,I_{bq})\).  Suppose that, almost surely after conditioning
   on the true codeword scores in \(u\), every \(z\in P_u\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{j=1}^Nb_u(z)_j^-\le1,
      \qquad
      M(\kappa_u(z)-1)\le R_u,
      \tag{LNJ4}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{j=1}^N
      b_u(z)_j^-\exp\!\bigl(\lambda(M-W_j)\bigr)
      \le \Xi_u .
      \tag{LNJ5}
   \]
   If
   \[
      e^{\lambda R_u}(1+\Xi_u)
      \exp\!\left(
         \lambda\omega_u^{P,\perp}
         +\frac{\lambda^2(r_u^{P,\perp})^2}{2}
      \right)
      \le A_\lambda ,
      \tag{LNJ6}
   \]
   then the conditional tilted-excess bound \((LPT2)\) holds with \(A_\lambda\).
   Hence, at the Gaussian tilt \(\lambda=T/b\), a polylogarithmic bound in
   \((LNJ6)\) gives the LP/SA threshold reporter polylogarithmic expected
   overhead.

   This certificate avoids choosing an anchor or convex witness.  A true
   codeword \(z=\iota(c_k)\) may choose \(b_u(z)=e_k\), and a convex combination
   of true codewords may choose the same convex coefficients.  The only
   projection obstruction is therefore negative score-span coefficient mass of
   genuinely fractional pseudocodewords, weighted by the internal score gaps
   below the local maximum.  The canonical Moore--Penrose choice
   \(G_u^+A_u^\top z\) is allowed when it has the desired tail, but it is not
   forced in linearly dependent subcodes.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(L_u=\operatorname{span}\{\iota(c_j):j\in[N]\}\).  Conditioning on
   \(\mathcal G_u=\sigma(W_j:j\in[N])\), the projection of the Gaussian score
   table onto \(L_u\) is \(A_uG_u^+W_u\), where \(W_u=(W_1,\ldots,W_N)\), and the
   orthogonal residual remains an independent standard Gaussian vector on
   \(L_u^\perp\).  For \(z\in P_u\),
   \[
      \ip{\Pi_u w}{z}
      =
      \ip{w}{A_ub_u(z)}
      =
      \sum_{j=1}^Nb_u(z)_jW_j .
      \tag{LNJ7}
   \]
   Therefore
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \ip{\Pi_u w}{z}-M
      &=
      M(\kappa_u(z)-1)
      +
      \sum_{j=1}^Nb_u(z)_j(W_j-M)\\
      &\le
      R_u+
      \sum_{j=1}^Nb_u(z)_j^-(M-W_j).
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{LNJ8}
   \]
   The inequality uses \(W_j\le M\), so positive coefficients cannot increase the
   second term, and then \((LNJ4)\).

   Put \(g_j=M-W_j\ge0\) and \(\beta(z)=\sum_jb_u(z)_j^-\le1\).  As in
   \((LMQ7)\), convexity of the exponential and the unused mass \(1-\beta(z)\)
   at gap zero give
   \[
      \exp\!\left(
         \lambda\sum_jb_u(z)_j^-g_j
      \right)
      \le
      1+\sum_jb_u(z)_j^-e^{\lambda g_j}
      \le
      1+\Xi_u .
      \tag{LNJ9}
   \]
   Combining \((LNJ8)\)--\((LNJ9)\),
   \[
      \sup_{z\in P_u}
      \exp\!\left(\lambda(\ip{\Pi_u w}{z}-M)\right)
      \le e^{\lambda R_u}(1+\Xi_u).
      \tag{LNJ10}
   \]

   Now
   \[
      U(u)-M
      =
      \sup_{z\in P_u}\bigl(\ip{\Pi_u w}{z}-M+\ip{\Pi_u^\perp w}{z}\bigr)
      \le
      B_u+Y_u^\perp,
      \tag{LNJ11}
   \]
   where \(e^{\lambda B_u}\le e^{\lambda R_u}(1+\Xi_u)\) by \((LNJ10)\), and
   \[
      Y_u^\perp=\sup_{z\in P_u}\ip{g}{\Pi_u^\perp z},
      \qquad g\sim N(0,I_{bq}),
      \tag{LNJ12}
   \]
   is independent of \(\mathcal G_u\), has expectation \(\omega_u^{P,\perp}\),
   and is \(r_u^{P,\perp}\)-Lipschitz.  The Gaussian moment bound gives
   \[
      \E\exp(\lambda Y_u^\perp)
      \le
      \exp\!\left(
         \lambda\omega_u^{P,\perp}
         +\frac{\lambda^2(r_u^{P,\perp})^2}{2}
      \right).
      \tag{LNJ13}
   \]
   Multiplying this with \((LNJ10)\) proves
   \[
      \E[\exp(\lambda(U(u)-M(u)))\mid\mathcal G_u]\le A_\lambda,
   \]
   which is \((LPT2)\) with \(X_u=U(u)-M(u)\).  The overhead conclusion is
   \cref{cor:conditional-tilted-excess-certificate}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Negative coefficient tail dual verifier]
   \label{cor:negative-coefficient-tail-dual}
   Continue with the notation of
   \cref{cor:direct-coefficient-projection-certificate}.  For nonnegative
   coefficient prices \(\omega\in\R_+^N\), define
   \[
      \mathcal N_u(z;\omega)
      =
      \inf_{\substack{b\in\R^N\\ A_ub=\Pi_u z}}
      \sum_{j=1}^N\omega_j b_j^-,
      \qquad
      \mathcal N_u(P_u;\omega)=\sup_{z\in P_u}\mathcal N_u(z;\omega).
      \tag{LNK1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \mathcal N_u(P_u;\omega)
      =
      \sup_{\substack{y\in L_u\\ -\omega_j\le \ip{y}{\iota(c_j)}\le0\ \forall j}}
      \sup_{z\in P_u}\ip{y}{z}.
      \tag{LNK2}
   \]
   Consequently, for \(\Xi_u>0\), the two negative-tail hypotheses in
   \cref{cor:direct-coefficient-projection-certificate} follow from the single
   finite check
   \[
      \mathcal N_u(P_u;\omega^\lambda+\Xi_u\mathbf 1_N)\le\Xi_u,
      \qquad
      \omega^\lambda_j=\exp(\lambda(M(u)-W(c_j))).
      \tag{LNK3}
   \]

   A failed check is a concrete separator: a vector \(y\in L_u\) whose score on
   every true codeword lies in the interval \([-\omega_j,0]\), and a fractional
   point \(z\in P_u\) with \(\ip{y}{z}\) too large.  Thus the negative coefficient
   theorem can be attacked by finite-dimensional relaxation maximization under
   clipped true-codeword score constraints.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix \(z\).  The primal LP for \(\mathcal N_u(z;\omega)\) is
   \[
      \min \sum_j\omega_jt_j
      \quad\text{subject to}\quad
      A_ub=\Pi_u z,\quad t_j\ge -b_j,\quad t_j\ge0 .
      \tag{LNK4}
   \]
   Its dual has an ambient vector \(y\) for the equality constraint and is
   \[
      \max \ip{y}{\Pi_u z}
      \quad\text{subject to}\quad
      -\omega_j\le \ip{y}{\iota(c_j)}\le0
      \quad(j=1,\ldots,N).
      \tag{LNK5}
   \]
   This is the elementary conjugate identity for the scalar function
   \(\omega_j(-b_j)_+\): its dual slope lies in \([-\omega_j,0]\).  Since the
   objective and constraints depend on \(y\) only through its projection onto
   \(L_u\), we may take \(y\in L_u\).  Then
   \(\ip{y}{\Pi_u z}=\ip{y}{z}\).  Strong duality gives \((LNK2)\) after taking
   the supremum over \(z\in P_u\) and exchanging the two suprema.

   If \((LNK3)\) holds, then for every \(z\in P_u\) the LP optimum is attained by
   a single coefficient vector satisfying \(A_ub=\Pi_u z\) and
   \[
      \sum_j\omega^\lambda_jb_j^-+\Xi_u\sum_jb_j^-\le\Xi_u .
      \tag{LNK6}
   \]
   Hence \(\sum_jb_j^-\le1\) and
   \(\sum_j\omega^\lambda_jb_j^-\le\Xi_u\), which are exactly the two
   negative-tail hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:direct-coefficient-projection-certificate}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Coefficient scalar-leakage witness]
   \label{cor:coefficient-scalar-leakage-witness}
   Continue with the notation of
   \cref{cor:direct-coefficient-projection-certificate}.  Suppose there is a
   vector \(\ell_u\in\R^{bq}\) and a scalar \(\sigma_u\) such that
   \[
      A_u^\top\ell_u=\mathbf 1_N,
      \qquad
      \ip{\ell_u}{z}=\sigma_u\quad(z\in P_u).
      \tag{LNL1}
   \]
   Then every coefficient representation \(A_ub=\Pi_u z\) satisfies
   \[
      \kappa_u(z)-\sigma_u
      =
      -\ip{\Pi_u^\perp\ell_u}{\Pi_u^\perp z}.
      \tag{LNL2}
   \]
   Hence
   \[
      |\kappa_u(z)-\sigma_u|
      \le
      \|\Pi_u^\perp\ell_u\|_2\, r_u^{P,\perp}
      \qquad(z\in P_u).
      \tag{LNL3}
   \]
   In particular, if \(\sigma_u=1\) and
   \[
      |M(u)|\,\|\Pi_u^\perp\ell_u\|_2\, r_u^{P,\perp}\le R_u,
      \tag{LNL4}
   \]
   then the scalar leakage condition \(M(u)(\kappa_u(z)-1)\le R_u\) in
   \((LNJ4)\) holds for every \(z\in P_u\).  If \(\ell_u\in L_u\), the leakage is
   zero.

   For ordinary \(q\)-ary simplex relaxations, one may take
   \(\ell_u=\mathbf 1_{B_i}\), the indicator of any coordinate block \(B_i\),
   because \(A_u^\top \mathbf 1_{B_i}=\mathbf 1_N\) and
   \(\ip{\mathbf 1_{B_i}}{z}=1\) on the simplex.  Thus scalar leakage is again
   either exact zero or paid by the already present orthogonal radius.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(A_ub=\Pi_u z\).  Since \(A_u^\top\ell_u=\mathbf 1_N\),
   \[
      \kappa_u(z)=\mathbf 1_N^\top b=\ip{\ell_u}{A_ub}
      =\ip{\ell_u}{\Pi_u z}.
      \tag{LNL5}
   \]
   By \((LNL1)\), \(\sigma_u=\ip{\ell_u}{z}\).  Subtracting gives
   \[
      \kappa_u(z)-\sigma_u
      =
      \ip{\ell_u}{\Pi_u z-z}
      =
      -\ip{\Pi_u^\perp\ell_u}{\Pi_u^\perp z},
   \]
   proving \((LNL2)\).  Cauchy's inequality gives \((LNL3)\), and \((LNL4)\)
   gives the required scalar leakage bound.  The coordinate-block claim follows
   because every codeword and every point of the product-simplex relaxation has
   exactly one unit of mass in coordinate block \(i\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Near-optimal score-gap form of the tail verifier]
   \label{cor:near-optimal-score-gap-tail-verifier}
   Continue with the notation of
   \cref{cor:negative-coefficient-tail-dual}, and suppose \(P_u\) lies in the
   product of the \(q\)-ary coordinate simplices.  For a table
   \(Y\in\R^{bq}\), define its block-minimum shift
   \[
      Y^\circ_{i,a}=Y_{i,a}-\min_{\alpha\in[q]}Y_{i,\alpha}\ge0,
      \tag{LNM1}
   \]
   and its true-codeword deficit profile
   \[
      \Delta_Y(c_j)
      =
      \max_{k\in[N]}\ip{Y^\circ}{\iota(c_k)}
      -
      \ip{Y^\circ}{\iota(c_j)} .
      \tag{LNM2}
   \]
   Let
   \[
      \mathcal R_u^{\mathrm{gap}}(\omega)
      =
      \left\{
         Y^\circ:\ Y\in L_u,\ \Delta_Y(c_j)\le\omega_j\ \forall j
      \right\}.
      \tag{LNM3}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sup_{R\in\mathcal R_u^{\mathrm{gap}}(\omega)}
      \left(
         \sup_{z\in P_u}\ip{R}{z}
         -
         \max_{j\in[N]}\ip{R}{\iota(c_j)}
      \right)
      \le B_u ,
      \tag{LNM4}
   \]
   then
   \[
      \mathcal N_u(P_u;\omega)\le B_u .
      \tag{LNM5}
   \]
   In particular, \((LNK3)\) follows from \((LNM4)\) with
   \(B_u=\Xi_u\) and \(\omega=\omega^\lambda+\Xi_u\mathbf1_N\).

   Thus the negative coefficient tail can be certified by an ordinary
   nonnegative score-table gap: every table whose near-optimal true codewords are
   clipped by the prices \(\omega_j\) must have relaxation optimum within
   \(B_u\) of its best true codeword.  The signed separator of
   \cref{cor:negative-coefficient-tail-dual} has disappeared; only the
   block-shifted score gaps matter.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a feasible separator \(y\in L_u\) in \((LNK2)\), and write
   \(s_j=\ip{y}{\iota(c_j)}\in[-\omega_j,0]\).  Put
   \(m=\max_j s_j\le0\), and let \(R=y^\circ\).  Since every point of \(P_u\) and
   every codeword has one unit of mass in each coordinate block, the block shift
   subtracts the same constant from all their scores.  Hence
   \[
      \max_k\ip{R}{\iota(c_k)}-\ip{R}{\iota(c_j)}
      =
      m-s_j
      \le \omega_j ,
      \tag{LNM6}
   \]
   so \(R\in\mathcal R_u^{\mathrm{gap}}(\omega)\).  For every \(z\in P_u\),
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \ip{y}{z}
      &=
      \ip{R}{z}
      -
      \max_k\ip{R}{\iota(c_k)}
      +m\\
      &\le
      \ip{R}{z}
      -
      \max_k\ip{R}{\iota(c_k)},
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{LNM7}
   \]
   because \(m\le0\).  Taking the supremum over \(z\in P_u\) and then over all
   feasible \(y\) in \((LNK2)\) proves \((LNM5)\).  The final statement is
   \cref{cor:negative-coefficient-tail-dual}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite score-band LP/SA compiler]
   \label{cor:finite-score-band-lp-sa-compiler}
   Work in the branch-and-bound setting of
   \cref{cor:conditional-tilted-excess-certificate}, and keep the notation of
   \cref{cor:direct-coefficient-projection-certificate} and
   \cref{cor:near-optimal-score-gap-tail-verifier}.  Suppose \(P_u\) lies in the
   product of the \(q\)-ary coordinate simplices.  Fix \(\lambda>0\) and
   \(\Xi_u>0\), and define the combined internal-gap prices
   \[
      \Omega_{u,j}
      =
      \exp\!\bigl(\lambda(M(u)-W(c_j))\bigr)+\Xi_u .
      \tag{LNN1}
   \]
   Assume the finite score-band gap condition
   \[
      \sup_{R\in\mathcal R_u^{\mathrm{gap}}(\Omega_u)}
      \left(
         \sup_{z\in P_u}\ip{R}{z}
         -
         \max_{j\in[N]}\ip{R}{\iota(c_j)}
      \right)
      \le \Xi_u .
      \tag{LNN2}
   \]
   Also suppose there is a balance witness \(\ell_u\) with
   \(A_u^\top\ell_u=\mathbf 1_N\) and \(\ip{\ell_u}{z}=1\) for all \(z\in P_u\),
   and that, for some \(R_u\ge0\),
   \[
      |M(u)|\,\|\Pi_u^\perp\ell_u\|_2\,r_u^{P,\perp}\le R_u .
      \tag{LNN3}
   \]
   If
   \[
      e^{\lambda R_u}(1+\Xi_u)
      \exp\!\left(
         \lambda\omega_u^{P,\perp}
         +\frac{\lambda^2(r_u^{P,\perp})^2}{2}
      \right)
      \le A_\lambda ,
      \tag{LNN4}
   \]
   then the conditional tilted-excess bound \((LPT2)\) holds with \(A_\lambda\).
   Consequently, at the Gaussian tilt \(\lambda=T/b\), a polylogarithmic bound in
   \((LNN4)\) gives the LP/SA threshold reporter polylogarithmic expected
   overhead.

   This is the direct finite theorem target for a low-rate LP or constant-level
   Sherali--Adams decoder: for the random internal-gap prices \(\Omega_u\), every
   nonnegative block-shifted score table whose true-codeword deficits are
   \(\Omega_u\)-near-optimal must have relaxation optimum within \(\Xi_u\) of the
   best true codeword; scalar leakage and orthogonal residuals are then the only
   remaining terms.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{cor:near-optimal-score-gap-tail-verifier}, \((LNN2)\) implies
   \[
      \mathcal N_u(P_u;\Omega_u)\le\Xi_u .
      \tag{LNN5}
   \]
   Since \(\Omega_u=\omega^\lambda+\Xi_u\mathbf 1_N\), where
   \(\omega^\lambda_j=\exp(\lambda(M(u)-W(c_j)))\),
   \cref{cor:negative-coefficient-tail-dual} gives, for every \(z\in P_u\), a
   coefficient vector \(b_u(z)\) with \(A_ub_u(z)=\Pi_u z\) and
   \[
      \sum_j b_u(z)_j^-\le1,
      \qquad
      \sum_j b_u(z)_j^-\exp(\lambda(M(u)-W(c_j)))\le\Xi_u .
      \tag{LNN6}
   \]
   The balance witness and \((LNN3)\), through
   \cref{cor:coefficient-scalar-leakage-witness}, give
   \[
      M(u)(\kappa_u(z)-1)\le R_u
      \qquad(z\in P_u)
      \tag{LNN7}
   \]
   for the same coefficient vectors.  Thus the hypotheses \((LNJ4)\)--\((LNJ5)\)
   of \cref{cor:direct-coefficient-projection-certificate} hold.  Applying that
   corollary with \((LNN4)\) proves \((LPT2)\), and
   \cref{cor:conditional-tilted-excess-certificate} gives the overhead statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Integral score-band obstruction]
   \label{cor:integral-score-band-obstruction}
   Continue with the notation of
   \cref{cor:finite-score-band-lp-sa-compiler}.  For any candidate point
   \(x\in\Delta_q^b\), define its finite score-band gap by
   \[
      \Gamma_u(x;\omega)
      =
      \sup_{R\in\mathcal R_u^{\mathrm{gap}}(\omega)}
      \left(
         \ip{R}{x}
         -
         \max_{j\in[N]}\ip{R}{\iota(c_j)}
      \right).
      \tag{LNN8}
   \]
   If the score-band condition \((LNN2)\) holds for a relaxation \(P_u\), then
   \[
      \Gamma_u(x;\Omega_u)\le\Xi_u
      \qquad(x\in P_u).
      \tag{LNN9}
   \]
   Consequently, if a proposed LP, Sherali--Adams, Tanner, or local-projection
   relaxation contains an integral pseudocodeword \(x=\iota(a)\notin
   \operatorname{conv}\{\iota(c_j)\}\) with
   \[
      \Gamma_u(\iota(a);\Omega_u)>\Xi_u ,
      \tag{LNN10}
   \]
   then that relaxation cannot satisfy the frozen finite score-band target.

   For integral \(a\), \(\Gamma_u(\iota(a);\omega)\) is itself a finite
   chart LP: choose the block-minimum chart of \(R\), impose the true-codeword
   deficit bounds defining \(\mathcal R_u^{\mathrm{gap}}(\omega)\), and maximize
   \(\ip{R}{\iota(a)}-\max_j\ip{R}{\iota(c_j)}\).  This is the direct
   obstruction tested by \texttt{impl/score\_band\_lp\_stress.py}.  The
   remaining code theorem must therefore prove not only that true codewords
   decode, but that every high-score local pseudocodeword has been cut off by
   the retained LP/SA or Tanner constraints.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(x\in P_u\),
   \[
      \ip{R}{x}-\max_j\ip{R}{\iota(c_j)}
      \le
      \sup_{z\in P_u}\ip{R}{z}
      -
      \max_j\ip{R}{\iota(c_j)}
      \tag{LNN11}
   \]
   for every \(R\in\mathcal R_u^{\mathrm{gap}}(\Omega_u)\).  Taking the
   supremum over \(R\) and applying \((LNN2)\) proves \((LNN9)\).  The
   contrapositive gives the obstruction \((LNN10)\).

   For an integral \(a\), \(\ip{R}{\iota(a)}\) is the sum of one selected symbol
   score per block.  Fixing a block-minimum chart linearizes the nonnegativity
   of \(R=Y^\circ\), while the scalar \(\max_j\ip{R}{\iota(c_j)}\) is represented
   by the same variable \(m\) used in \((LNP1)\)--\((LNP3)\).  Hence the
   displayed supremum is the maximum of finitely many ordinary LPs.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Projected-source vertex score-band obstruction]
   \label{cor:local-marginal-vertex-score-band-obstruction}
   Continue with the notation of
   \cref{cor:integral-score-band-obstruction}.  Let \(Q_u\) be any finite
   local-marginal relaxation whose variables are nonnegative local-check
   assignment weights satisfying affine consistency constraints, and let
   \(S_uQ_u\subseteq\Delta_q^b\) be its projected unary source polytope.  Let
   \(\mathcal W_u=\operatorname{vert}(S_uQ_u)\) be the vertices of this
   projected source polytope.  Then
   \[
      \sup_{x\in S_uQ_u}\Gamma_u(x;\Omega_u)
      =
      \max_{w\in\mathcal W_u}\Gamma_u(w;\Omega_u).
      \tag{LNN12}
   \]
   Consequently, the finite score-band condition \((LNN2)\) holds for the
   local-marginal relaxation \(P_u=S_uQ_u\) if and only if
   \[
      \Gamma_u(w;\Omega_u)\le\Xi_u
      \qquad(w\in\mathcal W_u).
      \tag{LNN13}
   \]
   In particular, any projected-source vertex \(w\) with
   \[
      \Gamma_u(w;\Omega_u)>\Xi_u
      \tag{LNN14}
   \]
   is a concrete fractional obstruction to the frozen finite score-band target.

   This is the exact finite verifier used by
   \texttt{impl/score\_band\_lp\_stress.py}: form the projected unary source
   polytope \(S_uQ_u\), enumerate its vertices directly, and solve the
   fixed-source chart LP for each projected-source vertex.  Projecting every
   vertex of \(Q_u\) is a valid but larger check, since every vertex of
   \(S_uQ_u\) is the image of a vertex of \(Q_u\).  Integral pseudowords are
   just the integral projected-source vertices; after they disappear, any
   remaining failure of \((LNN2)\) must be witnessed by one of the genuinely
   fractional projected-source vertices.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For fixed \(\omega\), \(\Gamma_u(x;\omega)\) is a supremum of affine
   functions of \(x\):
   \[
      \Gamma_u(x;\omega)
      =
      \sup_{R\in\mathcal R_u^{\mathrm{gap}}(\omega)}
      \left(
         \ip{R}{x}
         -
         \max_j\ip{R}{\iota(c_j)}
      \right).
      \tag{LNN15}
   \]
   Hence \(\Gamma_u(\cdot;\omega)\) is convex.  Since \(S_uQ_u\) is a finite
   polytope, every \(x\in S_uQ_u\) is a convex combination of projected-source
   vertices \(w\in\mathcal W_u\).  Convexity gives
   \[
      \Gamma_u(x;\Omega_u)
      \le
      \max_{w\in\mathcal W_u}\Gamma_u(w;\Omega_u),
      \tag{LNN16}
   \]
   while the reverse inequality follows because every \(w\in\mathcal W_u\)
   lies in \(S_uQ_u\).  This proves \((LNN12)\).  Combining \((LNN12)\) with
   \cref{cor:integral-score-band-obstruction}, applied to
   \(P_u=S_uQ_u\), gives the equivalence \((LNN13)\) and the obstruction
   \((LNN14)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Projected-unary integrality reduction]
   \label{cor:projected-unary-integrality-reduction}
   Continue in the setting of
   \cref{cor:local-marginal-vertex-score-band-obstruction}.  Suppose every
   projected-source vertex is integral: for every \(w\in\mathcal W_u\) there is
   a word \(a(w)\in[q]^b\) such that \(w=\iota(a(w))\).  Let
   \[
      \mathcal A_u
      =
      \{a(w):w\in\mathcal W_u\}.
      \tag{LNN17}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \Gamma_u(\iota(a);\Omega_u)\le\Xi_u
      \qquad(a\in\mathcal A_u),
      \tag{LNN18}
   \]
   then the finite score-band condition \((LNN2)\) holds for
   \(P_u=S_uQ_u\).  In particular, if every word in \(\mathcal A_u\) is an
   actual codeword of the local panel, then
   \[
      \sup_{x\in S_uQ_u}\Gamma_u(x;\Omega_u)=0.
      \tag{LNN19}
   \]

   Thus a full-overlap Tanner/SA route has a concrete finite target: prove that
   the projected unary overlap polytope has only integral vertices, and prove
   that the surviving integral words are either true codewords or satisfy the
   integral score-band bound from
   \cref{cor:integral-score-band-obstruction}.  This is stronger than merely
   deleting integral pseudowords from a unary-glued relaxation, as shown by the
   \(N=10,b=5,q=2\) fractional obstruction in
   \cref{rem:frozen-score-band-target}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{cor:local-marginal-vertex-score-band-obstruction},
   \((LNN2)\) for \(S_uQ_u\) is equivalent to checking
   \(\Gamma_u(w;\Omega_u)\le\Xi_u\) on all \(w\in\mathcal W_u\).  Under the
   integrality hypothesis these checks are exactly \((LNN18)\).  If
   \(a\in\mathcal A_u\) is a true codeword, then for every score table \(R\),
   \[
      \ip{R}{\iota(a)}
      \le
      \max_j\ip{R}{\iota(c_j)},
      \tag{LNN20}
   \]
   so \(\Gamma_u(\iota(a);\Omega_u)=0\).  If every \(a\in\mathcal A_u\) is a
   true codeword, \((LNN12)\) gives \((LNN19)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Two-deletion-injective overlap closure]
   \label{cor:two-deletion-injective-overlap-closure}
   Let \(C_u=\{c_1,\ldots,c_N\}\subseteq[q]^b\), and suppose that for every
   \(T\subseteq[b]\) with \(|T|=b-2\), the projection
   \(c\mapsto c|_T\) is injective on \(C_u\).  Equivalently, the local panel
   has minimum Hamming distance at least \(3\).  Let \(Q_u^{\mathrm{loo}}\) be
   the leave-one-out full-overlap relaxation: for each
   \(i\in[b]\) it has a probability distribution on the punctured assignments
   \(c_j|_{[b]\setminus\{i\}}\), and for every pair \(i\ne k\) these
   distributions agree after marginalizing to
   \([b]\setminus\{i,k\}\).  Then its projected unary source polytope is exactly
   the true codeword hull,
   \[
      S_uQ_u^{\mathrm{loo}}
      =
      \operatorname{conv}\{\iota(c_j):j\in[N]\}.
   \]
   Consequently every projected unary vertex is a true codeword and
   \[
      \sup_{x\in S_uQ_u^{\mathrm{loo}}}\Gamma_u(x;\Omega_u)=0.
   \]

   Thus one concrete way to discharge the finite low-rate panel obligation is
   not another score-band certificate: use a leave-one-out Tanner/SA overlap
   lift of a low-rate panel whose two-coordinate deletions are injective.  The
   overlap lift then has neither fractional projected vertices nor integral
   pseudowords.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The two-deletion injectivity assumption also makes every one-coordinate
   deletion \(c\mapsto c|_{[b]\setminus\{i\}}\) injective, so each local
   assignment can be labeled by its unique codeword \(c_j\).  Write
   \(\mu_i(j)\) for the mass of \(c_j|_{[b]\setminus\{i\}}\) in the \(i\)th
   leave-one-out view.  Fix \(i\ne k\).  Since
   \(c\mapsto c|_{[b]\setminus\{i,k\}}\) is injective, the marginal mass of the
   overlap pattern \(c_j|_{[b]\setminus\{i,k\}}\) in the \(i\)th view is exactly
   \(\mu_i(j)\), and in the \(k\)th view it is exactly \(\mu_k(j)\).  Pairwise
   overlap consistency therefore gives \(\mu_i(j)=\mu_k(j)\) for all
   \(i,k,j\).  Hence all local views share one distribution
   \(\lambda_j\ge0\), \(\sum_j\lambda_j=1\).

   The projected unary source of such a feasible point is then
   \(\sum_j\lambda_j\iota(c_j)\).  Conversely, any distribution
   \((\lambda_j)\) on the true codewords defines consistent leave-one-out local
   marginals by assigning mass \(\lambda_j\) to each punctured codeword
   \(c_j|_{[b]\setminus\{i\}}\).  This proves the displayed hull equality.
   The zero score-band gap follows from
   \cref{cor:projected-unary-integrality-reduction}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Polylogarithmic cost of two-deletion injectivity]
   \label{cor:polylog-cost-two-deletion-injective-panel}
   Fix \(q\ge2\).  For every \(b\) there is a code
   \(C\subseteq[q]^b\) with minimum Hamming distance at least \(3\) and
   \[
      |C|
      \ge
      \frac{q^b}
      {1+b(q-1)+\binom b2(q-1)^2}.
   \]
   Consequently, for every requested local list size \(N\), one can choose a
   two-deletion-injective \(q\)-ary panel of size at least \(N\) with
   \[
      q^b \le N\cdot \operatorname{poly}_q(\log N).
   \]
   For constant \(q\), this is only a polylogarithmic ambient-size loss.
   Combining this panel with
   \cref{cor:two-deletion-injective-overlap-closure} discharges the frozen
   finite leave-one-out overlap obligation \((LNN2)\) with zero local
   score-band gap and only polylogarithmic code-selection slack.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Greedily build \(C\).  Each selected word rules out only words at Hamming
   distance at most \(2\), at most
   \[
      B_{q,b}(2)
      =
      1+b(q-1)+\binom b2(q-1)^2
   \]
   words including itself.  The greedy process therefore selects at least
   \(q^b/B_{q,b}(2)\) words, and the selected words are pairwise at distance at
   least \(3\).

   Given \(N\), take the least \(b\) with \(q^b\ge N B_{q,b}(2)\).  Since
   \(B_{q,b}(2)=O_q(b^2)\), this least \(b\) satisfies
   \(b=\log_q N+O_q(\log\log N)\).  Hence
   \(q^b\le N\operatorname{poly}_q(\log N)\).  The final sentence follows from
   \cref{cor:two-deletion-injective-overlap-closure}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Convex-hull dominance screen for projected-source vertices]
   \label{cor:local-vertex-convex-hull-dominance-screen}
   Continue in the setting of
   \cref{cor:local-marginal-vertex-score-band-obstruction}.  For a projected
   source \(x\in\Delta_q^b\), define its true-hull dominance deficit by
   \[
      \delta_u(x)
      =
      1-
      \sup\left\{
         \sum_{j=1}^N a_j:
         a_j\ge0,
         \sum_{j=1}^N a_j\iota(c_j)\le x
      \right\},
      \tag{LNN21}
   \]
   where the inequality is coordinatewise.  Let
   \[
      \delta_u^{\mathrm{loc}}
      =
      \max_{w\in\mathcal W_u}\delta_u(w),
      \qquad
      \Gamma_u^{\Delta}(\Omega_u)
      =
      \sup_{z\in\Delta_q^b}\Gamma_u(z;\Omega_u).
      \tag{LNN22}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \sup_{x\in S_uQ_u}\Gamma_u(x;\Omega_u)
      \le
      \delta_u^{\mathrm{loc}}\,\Gamma_u^{\Delta}(\Omega_u).
      \tag{LNN23}
   \]
   Consequently, the finite score-band condition \((LNN2)\) holds for
   \(P_u=S_uQ_u\) whenever
   \[
      \delta_u^{\mathrm{loc}}\,\Gamma_u^{\Delta}(\Omega_u)\le\Xi_u.
      \tag{LNN24}
   \]

   This is a sufficient condition, not a replacement for the exact vertex
   check.  It isolates a concrete structural theorem for the local code: every
   projected-source vertex should be mostly dominated by the true-code convex
   hull.  If this dominance deficit is too large, the proof must use a sharper
   residual product-gap bound than the global product-simplex gap
   \(\Gamma_u^\Delta\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix \(w\in\mathcal W_u\), and let
   \(t=1-\delta_u(w)\).  If \(t=0\), the desired bound is immediate from the
   definition of \(\Gamma_u^\Delta\).  If \(t=1\), then \(w\) lies in the true
   codeword convex hull and \(\Gamma_u(w;\Omega_u)=0\).  Otherwise choose nonnegative
   coefficients \(a_j\) with total mass arbitrarily close to \(t\) and
   \(\sum_j a_j\iota(c_j)\le w\).  Put
   \[
      h=t^{-1}\sum_j a_j\iota(c_j)
      \in\operatorname{conv}\{\iota(c_j):j\in[N]\}.
      \tag{LNN25}
   \]
   Since \(w\) and \(h\) have unit mass in every coordinate block and
   \(th\le w\), the residual
   \[
      z=\frac{w-th}{1-t}
      \tag{LNN26}
   \]
   lies in \(\Delta_q^b\) when \(t<1\).  Moreover
   \(w=th+(1-t)z\).  For every \(R\),
   \[
      \ip{R}{h}\le\max_j\ip{R}{\iota(c_j)},
      \tag{LNN27}
   \]
   and therefore \(\Gamma_u(h;\Omega_u)=0\).  Convexity of
   \(\Gamma_u(\cdot;\Omega_u)\), proved in
   \cref{cor:local-marginal-vertex-score-band-obstruction}, gives
   \[
      \Gamma_u(w;\Omega_u)
      \le
      (1-t)\Gamma_u(z;\Omega_u)
      \le
      \delta_u(w)\Gamma_u^\Delta(\Omega_u).
      \tag{LNN28}
   \]
   Maximizing over \(w\in\mathcal W_u\) and using \((LNN12)\) proves
   \((LNN23)\).  The sufficient condition \((LNN24)\) follows directly from
   \((LNN2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Band-limited residual-budget compiler]
   \label{cor:band-limited-residual-budget-compiler}
   Continue with the notation of
   \cref{cor:finite-score-band-lp-sa-compiler}.  Let \(\mu_u\in\R_+^{bq}\) be a
   residual budget valid in the sense of \cref{cor:residual-hall-verifier}:
   for every nonnegative score table \(Y\),
   \[
      \sup_{z\in P_u}\ip{Y}{z}
      -
      \max_{j\in[N]}\ip{Y}{\iota(c_j)}
      \le
      \ip{Y}{\mu_u}.
      \tag{LNO1}
   \]
   If the same budget has small mass against every combined-price score band,
   \[
      \sup_{R\in\mathcal R_u^{\mathrm{gap}}(\Omega_u)}
      \ip{R}{\mu_u}
      \le
      \Xi_u ,
      \tag{LNO2}
   \]
   then the finite score-band gap condition \((LNN2)\) holds.  Consequently, if
   the balance-witness and orthogonal conditions \((LNN3)\)--\((LNN4)\) also
   hold, then the conditional tilted-excess bound \((LPT2)\) holds with
   \(A_\lambda\), and the LP/SA threshold reporter has polylogarithmic expected
   overhead whenever \(A_\lambda=\log^{O(1)}n\) at \(\lambda=T/b\).

   A failed residual route is again finite: either \((LNO1)\) fails and
   \cref{cor:residual-hall-verifier} exposes a nonnegative score table separating
   \(P_u\) from the true codeword hull plus \(\mu_u\), or \((LNO2)\) fails and
   returns a near-optimal band score table \(R\) that places too much mass on the
   proposed residual coordinates.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \((LNO1)\) to any
   \(R\in\mathcal R_u^{\mathrm{gap}}(\Omega_u)\).  Since \(R\ge0\),
   \[
      \sup_{z\in P_u}\ip{R}{z}
      -
      \max_{j\in[N]}\ip{R}{\iota(c_j)}
      \le
      \ip{R}{\mu_u}
      \le
      \Xi_u ,
      \tag{LNO3}
   \]
   where the last inequality is \((LNO2)\).  Taking the supremum over all such
   \(R\) proves \((LNN2)\).  The overhead statement is then exactly
   \cref{cor:finite-score-band-lp-sa-compiler}.  The failure alternatives are
   the negations of \((LNO1)\) and \((LNO2)\), with the first certified by
   \cref{cor:residual-hall-verifier}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Min-chart verifier for band-limited residuals]
   \label{cor:min-chart-band-residual-verifier}
   Continue with the notation of
   \cref{cor:band-limited-residual-budget-compiler}.  Fix nonnegative prices
   \(\omega\in\R_+^N\) on the true codewords \(c_1,\ldots,c_N\), and fix a
   nonnegative residual budget \(\mu\in\R_+^{bq}\).  For a block-minimum chart
   \(\tau=(\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_b)\in[q]^b\), let
   \(\mathsf B_{u,\tau}(\mu,\omega)\) be the value of the linear program
   \[
      \sup_{Y\in L_u,\ m\in\R}
      \sum_{i=1}^b\sum_{a\in[q]}
      \mu_{i,a}\bigl(Y_{i,a}-Y_{i,\tau_i}\bigr)
      \tag{LNP1}
   \]
   subject to
   \[
      Y_{i,a}\ge Y_{i,\tau_i}
      \qquad(i\in[b],\ a\in[q]),
      \tag{LNP2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \ip{Y}{\iota(c_j)}\le m,
      \qquad
      m-\ip{Y}{\iota(c_j)}\le\omega_j
      \qquad(j=1,\ldots,N).
      \tag{LNP3}
   \]
   Then, with the convention that an unbounded chart has value \(+\infty\),
   \[
      \sup_{R\in\mathcal R_u^{\mathrm{gap}}(\omega)}\ip{R}{\mu}
      =
      \max_{\tau\in[q]^b}\mathsf B_{u,\tau}(\mu,\omega).
      \tag{LNP4}
   \]
   Consequently, the band-mass condition \((LNO2)\) is equivalent to the finite
   family of ordinary LP checks
   \[
      \mathsf B_{u,\tau}(\mu,\Omega_u)\le\Xi_u
      \qquad(\tau\in[q]^b).
      \tag{LNP5}
   \]
   A failed check is explicit: it returns a minimum chart \(\tau\), a
   score-span table \(Y\in L_u\), and a scalar \(m\) whose block-minimum shift is
   an \(\Omega_u\)-near-optimal score band placing more than \(\Xi_u\) mass on
   the proposed residual budget.

   This is only a build-time verifier.  In the logarithmic terminal regime
   \(q=\log^{O(1)}n\) and \(b=\Theta(\log n/\log\log n)\), the number of charts
   can be polynomial in \(n\), but it does not enter the retained query
   algorithm once the residual certificate has passed.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   First fix a chart \(\tau\) and a feasible pair \((Y,m)\) in
   \((LNP1)\)--\((LNP3)\).  By \((LNP2)\), the block-minimum shift of \(Y\) is
   the table
   \[
      R_{i,a}=Y_{i,a}-Y_{i,\tau_i}\ge0 .
      \tag{LNP6}
   \]
   Since every codeword has exactly one symbol in each coordinate block,
   replacing \(Y\) by \(R\) subtracts the same scalar
   \(\sum_iY_{i,\tau_i}\) from every true-codeword score.  Therefore the deficit
   profile is unchanged, and \((LNP3)\) gives
   \[
      \max_k\ip{R}{\iota(c_k)}-\ip{R}{\iota(c_j)}
      \le \omega_j
      \qquad(j=1,\ldots,N).
      \tag{LNP7}
   \]
   Thus \(R\in\mathcal R_u^{\mathrm{gap}}(\omega)\), and the objective in
   \((LNP1)\) is exactly \(\ip{R}{\mu}\).  Hence every chart value is at most the
   left side of \((LNP4)\).

   Conversely, take any \(R\in\mathcal R_u^{\mathrm{gap}}(\omega)\).  By
   definition, \(R=Y^\circ\) for some \(Y\in L_u\).  Choose
   \(\tau_i\in\arg\min_{a\in[q]}Y_{i,a}\) in every coordinate block, and set
   \(m=\max_j\ip{Y}{\iota(c_j)}\).  Then \((Y,m)\) is feasible for the chart
   \(\tau\): \((LNP2)\) holds by the choice of \(\tau\), and \((LNP3)\) is just
   the bound \(\Delta_Y(c_j)=\Delta_R(c_j)\le\omega_j\).  Its objective equals
   \(\ip{Y^\circ}{\mu}=\ip{R}{\mu}\).  Taking the supremum over \(R\) proves the
   reverse inequality in \((LNP4)\).  Substituting
   \(\omega=\Omega_u\) gives \((LNP5)\), and the failed-check statement is the
   displayed optimizer of a violated chart LP.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Deficit-transport dual for min charts]
   \label{cor:min-chart-deficit-transport-dual}
   In the setting of \cref{cor:min-chart-band-residual-verifier}, define the
   block-centered residual vector
   \[
      d_\tau(\mu)_{i,a}
      =
      \mu_{i,a}
      -
      \mathbf 1_{\{a=\tau_i\}}\sum_{\alpha\in[q]}\mu_{i,\alpha}.
      \tag{LNQ1}
   \]
   Let
   \[
      K_\tau(\alpha)
      =
      \sum_{i=1}^b\sum_{a\in[q]}
      \alpha_{i,a}\bigl(e_{i,a}-e_{i,\tau_i}\bigr),
      \qquad
      \alpha_{i,a}\ge0,
      \tag{LNQ2}
   \]
   where \(e_{i,a}\) is the coordinate-symbol basis vector.  Then the chart
   value in \((LNP1)\) equals
   \[
      \mathsf B_{u,\tau}(\mu,\omega)
      =
      \inf
      \left\{
         \sum_{j=1}^N\omega_j\theta_j^+:
         \begin{array}{l}
            \theta\in\R^N,\ \sum_j\theta_j=0,\ \alpha\ge0,\\
            d_\tau(\mu)+K_\tau(\alpha)+A_u\theta\in L_u^\perp
         \end{array}
      \right\}.
      \tag{LNQ3}
   \]
   Equivalently, after projecting onto the true-codeword span,
   \[
      \Pi_u\bigl(d_\tau(\mu)+K_\tau(\alpha)\bigr)
      =
      -A_u\theta .
      \tag{LNQ4}
   \]
   Equivalently, define the chart score map
   \[
      h_\tau(\eta)_j
      =
      \sum_{i=1}^b\sum_{a\in[q]}
      \eta_{i,a}
      \left(
         \mathbf 1_{\{c_j(i)=a\}}
         -
         \mathbf 1_{\{c_j(i)=\tau_i\}}
      \right)
      \qquad(\eta\in\R_+^{bq}).
      \tag{LNQ5}
   \]
   Then \((LNQ3)\) is the same as the codeword-score system
   \[
      h_\tau(\mu)+h_\tau(\alpha)+G_u\theta=0,
      \qquad
      \sum_j\theta_j=0,
      \qquad
      \alpha\ge0,
      \tag{LNQ6}
   \]
   with objective \(\sum_j\omega_j\theta_j^+\).  This form involves only the
   true-codeword Gram matrix and the chart-incidence scores.

   Thus the condition
   \(\mathsf B_{u,\tau}(\mu,\Omega_u)\le\Xi_u\) has a purely finite certificate:
   the block-centered residual can be neutralized, modulo directions orthogonal
   to all true codewords, by upward moves away from the chart minima and by a
   zero-total signed combination of true codewords whose positive part costs at
   most \(\Xi_u\) under the near-leader prices \(\Omega_u\).

   Combining this with \cref{cor:min-chart-band-residual-verifier}, the
   band-limited residual condition \((LNO2)\) is equivalent to the existence,
   for every chart \(\tau\), of such \((\alpha,\theta)\) with
   \[
      \sum_j\Omega_{u,j}\theta_j^+\le\Xi_u .
      \tag{LNQ7}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Write the objective in \((LNP1)\) as \(\ip{d_\tau(\mu)}{Y}\).  Use the
   inequality form
   \[
      Y_{i,\tau_i}-Y_{i,a}\le0,\qquad
      \ip{Y}{\iota(c_j)}-m\le0,\qquad
      m-\ip{Y}{\iota(c_j)}-\omega_j\le0 .
      \tag{LNQ8}
   \]
   For a maximization problem, nonnegative multipliers
   \(\alpha_{i,a},\beta_j,\gamma_j\) give the upper-bound Lagrangian
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \ip{d_\tau(\mu)}{Y}
      &-
      \sum_{i,a}\alpha_{i,a}(Y_{i,\tau_i}-Y_{i,a})\\
      &-
      \sum_j\beta_j(\ip{Y}{\iota(c_j)}-m)
      -
      \sum_j\gamma_j(m-\ip{Y}{\iota(c_j)}-\omega_j).
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{LNQ9}
   \]
   The coefficient of \(m\) is \(\sum_j\beta_j-\sum_j\gamma_j\), so finite
   supremum over \(m\in\R\) requires these sums to be equal.  The coefficient of
   \(Y\), restricted to \(Y\in L_u\), is
   \[
      d_\tau(\mu)+K_\tau(\alpha)+A_u(\gamma-\beta).
      \tag{LNQ10}
   \]
   Finite supremum over \(Y\in L_u\) is therefore equivalent to this vector
   lying in \(L_u^\perp\).  Under these two equalities, the Lagrangian supremum
   is \(\sum_j\omega_j\gamma_j\).  Linear-programming duality gives
   \[
      \mathsf B_{u,\tau}(\mu,\omega)
      =
      \inf
      \left\{
         \sum_j\omega_j\gamma_j:
         \begin{array}{l}
         \alpha,\beta,\gamma\ge0,\\
         \sum_j\beta_j=\sum_j\gamma_j,\\
         d_\tau(\mu)+K_\tau(\alpha)+A_u(\gamma-\beta)\in L_u^\perp
         \end{array}
      \right\}.
      \tag{LNQ11}
   \]
   Set \(\theta=\gamma-\beta\).  The equality of the total masses gives
   \(\sum_j\theta_j=0\).  Conversely, for any zero-sum \(\theta\), the cheapest
   nonnegative decomposition is \(\gamma_j=\theta_j^+\) and
   \(\beta_j=\theta_j^-\).  Substituting this in \((LNQ11)\) proves \((LNQ3)\).
   Since \(A_u\theta\in L_u\), the orthogonality condition is equivalent to the
   projected identity \((LNQ4)\).
