   \operatorname{gain}_{\alpha,\tau,\sigma}(Z)
   \ge
   \pi_1A_\alpha-\pi_2mT_\tau-\mathsf D_H(\tau)-\pi_um\sigma,
   \tag{WS5}
   \]
   where
   \[
      \operatorname{gain}_{\alpha,\tau,\sigma}(z)
      =
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\alpha_{p,q}\mathbf 1\{p\in U_z\}\chi_z(q)
      -
      |U_z|\sum_q\tau_q\chi_z(q)
      -
      \sigma |U_z|.
   \]
   Consequently, if budgets \(L,S\) satisfy
   \[
      \pi_2m\le\frac{\pi_1L}{4},
      \qquad
      \pi_um\le\frac{\pi_1S}{4},
      \tag{WS6}
   \]
   and the dual prices have surplus
   \[
      A_\alpha>L T_\tau+\sigma S,
      \tag{WS7}
   \]
   then either some spherical bucket \(z\in\mathcal Z\) has positive reduced
   gain, or
   \[
      \mathsf D_H(\tau)>\frac{\pi_1}{2}A_\alpha .
      \tag{WS8}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Average the reduced gain over \(Z\sim\Pi\).  The useful demand term is bounded
   from below by \((WS1)\):
   \[
      \E\sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \alpha_{p,q}\mathbf 1\{p\in U_Z\}\chi_Z(q)
      \ge \pi_1A_\alpha .
   \]
   For the query-price term, split the bucket into \(H(q)\) and its complement:
   \[
      \E\sum_q\tau_q\chi_Z(q)|U_Z|
      =
      \mathsf D_H(\tau)
      +
      \sum_q\tau_q
      \sum_{x\notin H(q)}
      \Pr[x\in U_Z,\ \chi_Z(q)=1].
   \]
   By \((WS2)\), the second summand is at most
   \[
      \pi_2\sum_q\tau_q|P\setminus H(q)|
      \le \pi_2mT_\tau .
   \]
   Finally, \((WS3)\) gives
   \[
      \E |U_Z|=\sum_{x\in P}\Pr[x\in U_Z]\le \pi_um.
   \]
   Combining the three estimates proves \((WS5)\).

   Under \((WS6)\) and \((WS7)\),
   \[
      \pi_2mT_\tau+\pi_um\sigma
      \le
      \frac{\pi_1}{4}(LT_\tau+S\sigma)
      <
      \frac{\pi_1}{4}A_\alpha .
   \]
   If also \(\mathsf D_H(\tau)\le\pi_1A_\alpha/2\), then \((WS5)\) gives
   \[
      \E_{Z\sim\Pi}\operatorname{gain}_{\alpha,\tau,\sigma}(Z)
      >
      \frac{\pi_1}{4}A_\alpha\ge0.
   \]
   Hence at least one bucket has positive reduced gain.  The contrapositive is
   exactly \((WS8)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Guard-bounded spherical reduced-gain test]
   \label{cor:guard-bounded-spherical-reduced-gain}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:weighted-spherical-reduced-gain}.  Assume in
   addition that the bucket law has query activation probability
   \[
      \Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[\chi_Z(q)=1]\le\pi_q
      \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q),
      \tag{GBS1}
   \]
   and that the high-correlation sets are guard-small:
   \[
      |H(q)|\le\gamma m
      \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q).
      \tag{GBS2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \gamma m\max_q\pi_q\le\frac{\pi_1L}{4},
      \tag{GBS3}
   \]
   while \((WS6)\)--\((WS7)\) hold, then some spherical bucket
   \(z\in\mathcal Z\) has positive reduced gain.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The guard-small and query-activation hypotheses give
   \[
      \mathsf D_H(\tau)
      =
      \E_Z\sum_q\tau_q\chi_Z(q)|U_Z\cap H(q)|
      \le
      \sum_q\tau_q\Pr[\chi_Z(q)=1]|H(q)|
      \le
      \frac{\pi_1L}{4}T_\tau .
   \]
   Combining this with \((WS6)\), the total penalty in \((WS5)\) is at most
   \[
      \frac{\pi_1L}{4}T_\tau
      +
      \frac{\pi_1L}{4}T_\tau
      +
      \frac{\pi_1S}{4}\sigma
      =
      \frac{\pi_1}{2}LT_\tau+\frac{\pi_1}{4}S\sigma .
   \]
   Since \(A_\alpha>LT_\tau+S\sigma\),
   \[
      \frac12LT_\tau+\frac14S\sigma
      \le
      \frac12A_\alpha-\frac14S\sigma
      <
      A_\alpha .
   \]
   Therefore \((WS5)\) gives positive expected reduced gain over
   \(Z\sim\Pi\), so some bucket in the support has positive reduced gain.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dual-weighted guard spherical test]
   \label{cor:dual-weighted-guard-spherical-reduced-gain}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:weighted-spherical-reduced-gain}.  For each
   query constraint put
   \[
      a_q=\Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[\chi_Z(q)=1].
   \]
   Assume \((WS6)\)--\((WS7)\).  If the high-correlation sets satisfy the
   dual-weighted guard bound
   \[
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}\tau_q a_q |H(q)|
      \le
      \frac{\pi_1}{2}A_\alpha ,
      \tag{DWG1}
   \]
   then some spherical bucket \(z\in\mathcal Z\) has positive reduced gain.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(U_Z\cap H(q)\subseteq H(q)\),
   \[
      \mathsf D_H(\tau)
      =
      \E_Z\sum_q\tau_q\chi_Z(q)|U_Z\cap H(q)|
      \le
      \sum_q\tau_q a_q|H(q)|.
   \]
   Thus \((DWG1)\) gives
   \(\mathsf D_H(\tau)\le\pi_1A_\alpha/2\).  By
   \cref{lem:weighted-spherical-reduced-gain}, under \((WS6)\)--\((WS7)\) the
   absence of a positive-gain spherical bucket would force
   \(\mathsf D_H(\tau)>\pi_1A_\alpha/2\), a contradiction.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Low-guard containment spherical test]
   \label{cor:low-guard-contained-spherical-reduced-gain}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:dual-weighted-guard-spherical-reduced-gain}.  Let the low-guard
   domain be defined by a threshold \(\gamma\):
   \[
      \Omega_{\rm low}
      =
      \left\{q:
      |P\cap B(q,cr)|<\gamma |P|
      \right\}.
   \]
   Suppose every priced query lies in \(\Omega_{\rm low}\) and the
   high-correlation set used by the spherical law is contained in the resident
   guard ball,
   \[
      H(q)\subseteq P\cap B(q,cr)
      \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q).
      \tag{LGC1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \gamma |P| \sum_q\tau_qa_q
      \le
      \frac{\pi_1}{2}A_\alpha ,
      \tag{LGC2}
   \]
   while \((WS6)\)--\((WS7)\) hold, then some spherical bucket has positive
   reduced gain.  In particular, it is enough that
   \[
      \gamma |P|\max_q a_q\le \frac{\pi_1L}{2}.
      \tag{LGC3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By low-guard containment, \(|H(q)|<\gamma |P|\) for every priced query.
   Hence
   \[
      \sum_q\tau_qa_q|H(q)|
      \le
      \gamma |P|\sum_q\tau_qa_q .
   \]
   Condition \((LGC2)\) gives \((DWG1)\), so
   \cref{cor:dual-weighted-guard-spherical-reduced-gain} applies.

   If \((LGC3)\) holds, then
   \[
      \gamma |P|\sum_q\tau_qa_q
      \le
      \frac{\pi_1L}{2}\sum_q\tau_q
      <
      \frac{\pi_1}{2}A_\alpha ,
   \]
   where the last strict inequality is \((WS7)\).  Thus \((LGC2)\) holds.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Contained high-correlation local cover]
   \label{cor:contained-high-correlation-local-cover}
   Work in a finite local filter-cover instance with resident set \(P\),
   \(|P|=m\), query constraints \(\mathcal Q\), near-pair demands
   \(\mathcal N\), query budget \(L\), and storage budget \(S\).  Suppose the
   retained filter universe contains the spherical buckets \(z\in\mathcal Z\)
   from \cref{lem:weighted-spherical-reduced-gain}, with
   \(T_z=S_z=|U_z|\).  Assume \((WS1)\)--\((WS3)\) and \((WS6)\).  Let
   \(a_q=\Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[\chi_Z(q)=1]\).  For a guard threshold \(\gamma_0\),
   assume every priced query constraint is low-guard and every
   high-correlation set is contained in the resident guard ball:
   \[
      q\in\Omega_{\rm low},
      \qquad
      H(q)\subseteq P\cap B(q,cr)
      \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q),
      \tag{CHC1}
   \]
   where
   \[
      \Omega_{\rm low}
      =
      \{q:|P\cap B(q,cr)|<\gamma_0m\}.
   \]
   If
   \[
      \gamma_0m\max_q a_q\le\frac{\pi_1L}{2},
      \tag{CHC2}
   \]
   then the finite filter-cover LP over any universe containing these spherical
   buckets is feasible with query budget \(L\) and storage budget \(S\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose the LP were infeasible.  By
   \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual}, there is a nonnegative dual price
   system \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\) with surplus
   \[
      A_\alpha>L\sum_q\tau_q+\sigma S
   \]
   and nonpositive reduced gain on every retained filter column.  In
   particular, every spherical bucket \(z\in\mathcal Z\) has nonpositive reduced
   gain in the sense of \cref{lem:weighted-spherical-reduced-gain}.  Conditions
   \((WS6)\) and the displayed surplus are exactly the hypotheses
   \((WS6)\)--\((WS7)\), while \((CHC1)\)--\((CHC2)\) imply \((LGC1)\) and
   \((LGC3)\).  Therefore
   \cref{cor:low-guard-contained-spherical-reduced-gain} gives a spherical
   bucket with positive reduced gain, contradicting the dual certificate.
   Hence the finite filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Guard-ball spherical fallback]
   \label{cor:guard-ball-spherical-fallback}
   Work in the same finite local filter-cover setting as
   \cref{cor:contained-high-correlation-local-cover}.  Suppose the spherical
   bucket law satisfies the near-hit and update bounds \((WS1)\) and \((WS3)\),
   and satisfies the direct guard-ball far bound
   \[
      \Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[x\in U_Z,\ \chi_Z(q)=1]\le\pi_2
      \qquad
      \bigl(q\in\mathcal Q,\ x\notin P\cap B(q,cr)\bigr).
      \tag{GBF1}
   \]
   Assume the budget inequalities
   \[
      \pi_2m\le\frac{\pi_1L}{4},
      \qquad
      \pi_um\le\frac{\pi_1S}{4},
      \tag{GBF2}
   \]
   and put \(a_q=\Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[\chi_Z(q)=1]\).  If every query constraint lies
   in the low-guard domain
   \[
      |P\cap B(q,cr)|<\gamma_0m
      \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q),
      \tag{GBF3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \gamma_0m\max_q a_q\le\frac{\pi_1L}{2},
      \tag{GBF4}
   \]
   then the finite filter-cover LP over any universe containing the spherical
   buckets is feasible with query budget \(L\) and storage budget \(S\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{cor:contained-high-correlation-local-cover} with
   \[
      H(q)=P\cap B(q,cr).
   \]
   Then every demanded pair \((p,q)\) with \(\|p-q\|\le r\) has \(p\in H(q)\),
   and \((GBF1)\) is exactly \((WS2)\) for this choice of \(H\).  Conditions
   \((GBF2)\), \((GBF3)\), and \((GBF4)\) give \((WS6)\), \((CHC1)\), and
   \((CHC2)\), respectively.  The cited corollary gives feasibility.
\end{proof}

For the smooth product or Gaussian cap family, \(\pi_1\) is the near collision
probability, \(\pi_2\) is the ordinary far co-load probability, and \(\pi_u\) is
the update probability.  The usual exponent calculation is precisely
\(\pi_2m/\pi_1\le m^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m\) and
\(\pi_um/\pi_1\le m^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m\) after the standard logical
scaling.  Thus \cref{lem:weighted-spherical-reduced-gain} proves the spherical
half of the desired primal-dual dichotomy: a surplus dual obstruction that is
not defeated by ordinary spherical filters must put large price on
high-correlation bucket mass.  The dense-filter theorem only has to convert that
weighted high-correlation co-load into positive-gain radius-contracting columns.
\Cref{cor:dual-weighted-guard-spherical-reduced-gain} is the sharper
low-guard form: the obstruction is not the worst query's high-correlation set,
but the query-price weighted activation mass
\(\sum_q\tau_q\Pr[\chi_Z(q)=1]|H(q)|\).  When the chosen
high-correlation set is contained in the resident \(cr\)-guard ball,
\cref{cor:low-guard-contained-spherical-reduced-gain} shows that the resident
guard removes this obstruction on the low-guard domain.
\Cref{cor:contained-high-correlation-local-cover} packages this as a local LP
certificate: in the contained-cap regime, no dense scalar reporter is needed at
all, because the spherical buckets themselves separate every surplus dual.
\Cref{cor:guard-ball-spherical-fallback} is the most useful specialization:
when the primitive law has the ordinary far collision bound outside the true
resident \(cr\)-guard ball, low-guard nodes are solved by spherical buckets
alone.  Dense/list-decoding reporters are needed only for the remaining
annular high-correlation leakage not covered by this direct far bound.

\begin{lemma}[High-correlation dense-slice separator]
   \label{lem:high-correlation-dense-slice-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:weighted-spherical-reduced-gain}.  Assume
   every demanded pair satisfies \(p\in H(q)\).  For each base bucket
   \(z\in\mathcal Z\) and query \(q\in\mathcal Q\), put
   \[
      V_{z,q}=U_z\cap H(q),
      \qquad
      A_{z,q}=\sum_{\substack{p:(p,q)\in\mathcal N\\ p\in V_{z,q}}}
      \alpha_{p,q}.
   \]
   Suppose the dense candidate universe contains every nonempty singleton-query
   slice \(D_{z,q}\) with update side \(V_{z,q}\), activation only at \(q\), and
   certified dense prices \(T_{z,q},S_{z,q}\).  Its reduced gain is
   \[
      G_{z,q}=A_{z,q}-\tau_qT_{z,q}-\sigma S_{z,q}.
      \tag{DS1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \E_{Z\sim\Pi}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}G_{Z,q}>0,
      \tag{DS2}
   \]
   then some dense slice \(D_{z,q}\) has positive reduced gain in the
   filter-cover dual.

   In particular, if \((WS1)\) holds and
   \[
      \E_{Z\sim\Pi}\sum_q
      \bigl(\tau_qT_{Z,q}+\sigma S_{Z,q}\bigr)
      <
      \pi_1A_\alpha,
      \tag{DS3}
   \]
   then a positive-gain dense slice exists.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The first claim is just averaging: if every dense slice had nonpositive
   reduced gain, then the expectation in \((DS2)\) would be nonpositive.

   For the sufficient condition, the average captured demand is
   \[
      \E_Z\sum_qA_{Z,q}
      =
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \alpha_{p,q}\Pr_Z[p\in U_Z\cap H(q)].
   \]
   Since \(p\in H(q)\) for every demand, this is at least
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \alpha_{p,q}\Pr_Z[p\in U_Z,\ \chi_Z(q)=1].
   \]
   By \((WS1)\), the latter is at least
   \[
      \pi_1\sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\alpha_{p,q}
      =
      \pi_1A_\alpha .
   \]
   Subtracting the average dense prices, \((DS3)\) gives \((DS2)\).
\end{proof}

When \(H(q)\) is a spherical cap, the slices in
\cref{lem:high-correlation-dense-slice-separator} are genuine certified dense
filters.  For example, if the resident points lie on the unit sphere and
\[
   H_\beta(q)=\{x\in P:\ip{x}{q}\ge\beta\},
\]
then every \(V_{z,q}\subseteq H_\beta(q)\) lies in the Euclidean ball centered
at \(\beta q\) of radius \(\sqrt{1-\beta^2}\).  Thus it may be priced as a
radius-contracting child, for instance by
\[
   T_{z,q}=|V_{z,q}|^{\rho_D}\Psi(\sqrt{1-\beta^2}),
   \qquad
   S_{z,q}=|V_{z,q}|^{1+\rho_D}\Psi(\sqrt{1-\beta^2}),
\]
or by any sharper certified descendant Pareto price.  The singleton-query
activation is only a finite-signature normal form: in a retained all-query
structure, equivalent slices with the same activation signature are merged and
priced once by \cref{lem:finite-signature-filter-cover}.

\begin{corollary}[Spherical-or-dense moment obstruction]
   \label{cor:spherical-dense-moment-obstruction}
   In the setting of \cref{lem:weighted-spherical-reduced-gain} and
   \cref{lem:high-correlation-dense-slice-separator},
   assume the budget and surplus inequalities \((WS6)\)--\((WS7)\).  If no
   spherical bucket and no high-correlation dense slice has positive reduced
   gain, then both
   \[
      \mathsf D_H(\tau)>\frac{\pi_1}{2}A_\alpha
      \tag{SD1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \E_{Z\sim\Pi}\sum_q
      \bigl(\tau_qT_{Z,q}+\sigma S_{Z,q}\bigr)
      \ge
      \pi_1A_\alpha
      \tag{SD2}
   \]
   hold.  Thus any remaining dual obstruction must simultaneously have large raw
   high-correlation co-load and large recursive dense-slice moment.  The
   geometric task is to rule out this simultaneous pair under the proposed
   dense-slice pricing, or to quotient the slices until \((SD2)\) falls below the
   demand captured in \cref{lem:high-correlation-dense-slice-separator}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If no spherical bucket has positive reduced gain, then
   \cref{lem:weighted-spherical-reduced-gain} gives \((SD1)\).  If no dense slice
   has positive reduced gain, the contrapositive of the sufficient condition
   \((DS3)\) in \cref{lem:high-correlation-dense-slice-separator} gives
   \((SD2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Dense-slice prefix separation]
   \label{lem:dense-slice-prefix-separation}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:high-correlation-dense-slice-separator}, and
   fix query and storage budgets \(L_q>0\) and \(S_0>0\).  Suppose a slice
   \(V_{z,q}\) is certified inside a radius-contracting child with closed-form
   price factor \(\psi_{z,q}\) and exponent \(\rho_D\).  Order the points of
   \(V_{z,q}\) by the singleton-query demand prices
   \[
      \beta_1\ge\beta_2\ge\cdots\ge\beta_M,
      \qquad
      \beta_i=\alpha_{p_i,q}\mathbf 1\{(p_i,q)\in\mathcal N\},
   \]
   and put \(A_k=\sum_{i\le k}\beta_i\).  For every cardinality \(k\) satisfying
   the atom bounds
   \[
      \psi_{z,q}k^{\rho_D}\le L_q,
      \qquad
      \psi_{z,q}k^{1+\rho_D}\le S_0,
      \tag{DP1}
   \]
   let \(D_{z,q,k}\) be the singleton-query dense child whose update side is the
   first \(k\) points in this order and whose certified prices are
   \[
      T_{z,q,k}=\psi_{z,q}k^{\rho_D},
      \qquad
      S_{z,q,k}=\psi_{z,q}k^{1+\rho_D}.
      \tag{DP2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      A_k>\psi_{z,q}\bigl(\tau_qk^{\rho_D}+\sigma k^{1+\rho_D}\bigr)
      \tag{DP3}
   \]
   for some atom-safe \(k\), then \(D_{z,q,k}\) has positive reduced gain.
   Conversely, if no atom-safe dense prefix of \(V_{z,q}\) has positive reduced
   gain, then every atom-safe \(k\) satisfies
   \[
      \frac{A_k}{k}
      \le
      \psi_{z,q}\bigl(\tau_qk^{\rho_D-1}+\sigma k^{\rho_D}\bigr).
      \tag{DP4}
   \]
   In particular, for every price level \(\theta>0\), if
   \[
      h_\theta=
      \left|\{p\in V_{z,q}:(p,q)\in\mathcal N,\ \alpha_{p,q}\ge\theta\}\right|
   \]
   is atom-safe and nonzero, then
   \[
      \theta
      \le
      \psi_{z,q}\bigl(\tau_qh_\theta^{\rho_D-1}
      +\sigma h_\theta^{\rho_D}\bigr).
      \tag{DP5}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The reduced gain of the prefix child \(D_{z,q,k}\) is exactly
   \[
      A_k-\tau_q\psi_{z,q}k^{\rho_D}
      -\sigma\psi_{z,q}k^{1+\rho_D}.
   \]
   Thus \((DP3)\) is precisely positive reduced gain.  If no atom-safe prefix has
   positive gain, the same displayed expression is nonpositive for every
   atom-safe \(k\), and division by \(k\) gives \((DP4)\).

   For the level-set form, let \(h=h_\theta\).  The first \(h\) points in the
   sorted order all have price at least \(\theta\), so \(A_h\ge\theta h\).  If
   \(\theta\) violated \((DP5)\), then \(A_h\) would violate \((DP4)\), giving a
   positive-gain prefix.  This proves the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

Thus the dense side of the dichotomy can be made fully fractional at the level
of price superlevels.  A remaining dual obstruction cannot merely hide a small
expensive core inside a large high-correlation slice: such a core would appear as
one of the prefixes in \cref{lem:dense-slice-prefix-separation}.  What remains is
a diffuse obstruction in which every query-local high-price level set inside
every high-correlation bucket lies below the Renyi density envelope \((DP5)\).
This is the weighted pseudo-random condition that the next geometric step must
combine with the spherical co-load lower bound \((SD1)\).

\begin{lemma}[Dense-slice quotient separation]
   \label{lem:dense-slice-quotient-separation}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:high-correlation-dense-slice-separator}.
   Let \(\mathcal G\) be a finite family of certified dense quotient filters.
   Each \(G\in\mathcal G\) has update side \(U_G\subseteq P\), activation
   predicate \(a_G:\mathcal Q\to\{0,1\}\), and certified prices \(T_G,S_G\).
   Suppose also that \(G\) is assigned a finite set of primitive slices
   \[
      \mathcal I_G\subseteq\mathcal Z\times\mathcal Q
   \]
   such that, for every \((z,q)\in\mathcal I_G\),
   \[
      V_{z,q}\subseteq U_G,
      \qquad
      a_G(q)=1 .
      \tag{DQ1}
   \]
   Define the quotient demand captured by \(G\) as
   \[
      A_G=
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \alpha_{p,q}\mathbf 1\{p\in U_G\}a_G(q).
      \tag{DQ2}
   \]
   If a probability law \(\Gamma\) on \(\mathcal G\) satisfies
   \[
      \E_{G\sim\Gamma}
      \left[
         A_G
         -
         T_G\sum_q\tau_qa_G(q)
         -
         \sigma S_G
      \right]
      >0,
      \tag{DQ3}
   \]
   then some quotient filter \(G\) has positive reduced gain in the
   filter-cover dual.

   Moreover, put
   \[
      b_G=
      \max\left\{
         1,\;
         \max_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
         \left|
            \{z:(z,q)\in\mathcal I_G,\ p\in V_{z,q}\}
         \right|
      \right\}.
      \tag{DQ4}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      A_G
      \ge
      \frac1{b_G}
      \sum_{(z,q)\in\mathcal I_G}A_{z,q}.
      \tag{DQ5}
   \]
   Hence the stronger check
   \[
      \E_{G\sim\Gamma}
      \left[
         \frac1{b_G}
         \sum_{(z,q)\in\mathcal I_G}A_{z,q}
         -
         T_G\sum_q\tau_qa_G(q)
         -
         \sigma S_G
      \right]
      >0
      \tag{DQ6}
   \]
   also exposes a positive-gain quotient.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The expression inside \((DQ3)\) is exactly the reduced gain of the filter
   \(G=(U_G,a_G,T_G,S_G)\).  If its average over \(\Gamma\) is positive, at least
   one member of \(\mathcal G\) has positive gain.

   For \((DQ5)\), expand the assigned primitive demand:
   \[
      \sum_{(z,q)\in\mathcal I_G}A_{z,q}
      =
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \alpha_{p,q}
      \left|
         \{z:(z,q)\in\mathcal I_G,\ p\in V_{z,q}\}
      \right|.
   \]
   By \((DQ1)\), every primitive incidence counted on the right also satisfies
   \(p\in U_G\) and \(a_G(q)=1\).  By the definition of \(b_G\), each demand pair
   is counted at most \(b_G\) times.  Therefore the last display is at most
   \(b_GA_G\), which proves \((DQ5)\).  Combining \((DQ5)\) with \((DQ6)\) gives
   \((DQ3)\).
\end{proof}

This is the exact dual form of dense merging.  If many singleton slices are
different views of the same smaller-radius region, the proof need not pay their
storage repeatedly: it may propose a quotient \(G\), verify its activation
predicate and descendant price once, and use \cref{lem:dense-slice-quotient-separation}
to test whether the merged column has positive reduced gain.  Thus the remaining
dense theorem is not a clustering theorem in Lloyd form; it is a geometric
separator for quotients whose primitive demand is large compared with their
query-price overlap, storage price, and duplicate-incidence factor \(b_G\).

\begin{lemma}[Reduced-gain quotient refinement]
   \label{lem:reduced-gain-quotient-refinement}
   Work in the finite filter-cover dual with prices
   \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\).  Let
   \(G=(U,a,T,S)\) be a certified quotient column with \(K=|U|\), exponent
   \(0<\rho<1\), price factor \(\psi\), and prices
   \[
      T=\psi K^\rho,
      \qquad
      S=\psi K^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{RGQ1}
   \]
   Write
   \[
      \mathsf T_a=\sum_q\tau_qa(q),
      \qquad
      A_G=\sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \alpha_{p,q}\mathbf 1\{p\in U\}a(q).
      \tag{RGQ2}
   \]
   Suppose \(G\) has positive reduced gain:
   \[
      A_G>\psi\bigl(K^\rho\mathsf T_a+\sigma K^{1+\rho}\bigr).
      \tag{RGQ3}
   \]

   Let \(G_i=(U_i,a_i,T_i,S_i)\) be a demand-preserving certified refinement:
   the sets \(U_i\) form a partition of \(U\), \(K_i=|U_i|>0\), every activation
   satisfies \(a_i(q)\le a(q)\), and
   \[
      \sum_iA_i=A_G,
      \qquad
      A_i=\sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \alpha_{p,q}\mathbf 1\{p\in U_i\}a_i(q).
      \tag{RGQ4}
   \]
   Assume each child has the same exponent and prices
   \[
      T_i=\psi_iK_i^\rho,
      \qquad
      S_i=\psi_iK_i^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{RGQ5}
   \]
   If the refinement is price-compatible,
   \[
      \sum_i\psi_iK_i^\rho\le\psi K^\rho,
      \qquad
      \sum_i\psi_iK_i^{1+\rho}\le\psi K^{1+\rho},
      \tag{RGQ6}
   \]
   then some child \(G_i\) has positive reduced gain:
   \[
      A_i>
      \psi_iK_i^\rho\sum_q\tau_qa_i(q)
      +
      \sigma\psi_iK_i^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{RGQ7}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose every child has nonpositive reduced gain.  Since \(a_i(q)\le a(q)\),
   this implies
   \[
      A_i
      \le
      \psi_iK_i^\rho\sum_q\tau_qa_i(q)
      +
      \sigma\psi_iK_i^{1+\rho}
      \le
      \psi_iK_i^\rho\mathsf T_a
      +
      \sigma\psi_iK_i^{1+\rho}.
   \]
   Summing over \(i\), using demand preservation \((RGQ4)\), and applying
   \((RGQ6)\) gives
   \[
      A_G
      \le
      \mathsf T_a\sum_i\psi_iK_i^\rho
      +
      \sigma\sum_i\psi_iK_i^{1+\rho}
      \le
      \psi\bigl(K^\rho\mathsf T_a+\sigma K^{1+\rho}\bigr),
   \]
   contradicting \((RGQ3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Renyi-spread quotient obstruction]
   \label{cor:renyi-spread-quotient-obstruction}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{lem:reduced-gain-quotient-refinement}.  Suppose every child price
   factor satisfies \(\psi_i\le\psi_\star\le\psi\).  If \(G\) has positive
   reduced gain but no child \(G_i\) has positive reduced gain, then
   \[
      \sum_iK_i^\rho>\frac{\psi}{\psi_\star}K^\rho.
      \tag{RSQ1}
   \]
   Equivalently, for \(z_i=K_i/K\),
   \[
      \sum_i z_i^\rho>\frac{\psi}{\psi_\star}.
      \tag{RSQ2}
   \]
   Thus a surviving positive quotient cannot be concentrated in a
   radius-discounted low-Renyi-spread refinement.  For padded ball prices,
   \(\psi=\Psi(R)\) and \(\psi_\star=\Psi(R_\star)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((RSQ1)\) failed, then
   \[
      \sum_i\psi_iK_i^\rho
      \le
      \psi_\star\sum_iK_i^\rho
      \le
      \psi K^\rho .
   \]
   Also \(\psi_\star\le\psi\) and the partition is disjoint, so
   \[
      \sum_i\psi_iK_i^{1+\rho}
      \le
      \psi_\star\sum_iK_i^{1+\rho}
      \le
      \psi K^{1+\rho}.
   \]
   Hence the refinement is price-compatible, and
   \cref{lem:reduced-gain-quotient-refinement} would force a positive child,
   contrary to the hypothesis.  Dividing by \(K^\rho\) gives \((RSQ2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Low-spread quotient closure]
   \label{cor:low-spread-quotient-closure}
   In the setting of
   \cref{cor:renyi-spread-quotient-obstruction}, assume the child refinement is
   certified at radius price \(\psi_\star=\Psi(R_\star)\), while the parent has
   price \(\psi=\Psi(R)\).  If
   \[
      \sum_iK_i^\rho
      \le
      \frac{\Psi(R)}{\Psi(R_\star)}K^\rho,
      \tag{LSQ1}
   \]
   then some refined child quotient has positive reduced gain.

   Consequently, if a residual dual has no positive smaller-radius quotient,
   every positive quotient exposed by the spherical/dense-slice system must
   remain high-spread under every demand-preserving radius-\(R_\star\)
   refinement:
   \[
      \sum_i\left(\frac{K_i}{K}\right)^\rho
      >
      \frac{\Psi(R)}{\Psi(R_\star)}.
      \tag{LSQ2}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The first claim is the contrapositive of
   \cref{cor:renyi-spread-quotient-obstruction}.  The final statement is the
   same implication rewritten for the normalized child sizes.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Quotient spread gives packing entropy]
   \label{cor:quotient-spread-packing-entropy}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:low-spread-quotient-closure}.  Let
   \(G=(U,a,T,S)\) be a positive reduced-gain quotient with parent radius price
   \(\Psi(R)\).  Fix a smaller radius \(R_\star\).  Suppose the available child
   universe has the following closure property: for every cover of \(U\) by
   certified balls \(B_1,\ldots,B_J\) of radius \(R_\star\), assigning each
   \(p\in U\) to one covering ball and activating every child on the captured
   queries gives a demand-preserving quotient refinement whose child price
   factors are at most \(\Psi(R_\star)\).

   If none of these radius-\(R_\star\) children has positive reduced gain, then
   every certified radius-\(R_\star\) ball cover of \(U\) has size
   \[
      J>
      \left(\frac{\Psi(R)}{\Psi(R_\star)}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{QSPE1}
   \]
   If, in addition, every point-centered ball \(B(x,R_\star)\) with \(x\in U\)
   is an available certified child container, then \(U\) contains an
   \(R_\star\)-separated subset \(E\) with
   \[
      |E|>
      \left(\frac{\Psi(R)}{\Psi(R_\star)}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{QSPE2}
   \]
   The uniform law \(\nu_E\) on \(E\) has exact Renyi effective support
   \[
      \left(\sum_{x\in E}\nu_E(x)^s\right)^{1/(1-s)}
      =
      |E|
      \qquad(0\le s<1),
      \tag{QSPE3}
   \]
   and the separated ordered-pair count at scale \(R_\star\) is at least
   \[
      |E|(|E|-1).
      \tag{QSPE4}
   \]
   Thus a quotient residual that survives all smaller-radius children supplies
   an explicit packing-entropy witness for the spherical/list-decoding
   tuple-profile estimates.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(B_1,\ldots,B_J\) be any certified radius-\(R_\star\) cover of \(U\).
   Assign each point of \(U\) to one covering ball, and let \(K_i\) be the
   nonzero assigned sizes.  By the closure hypothesis this is a
   demand-preserving refinement with child price factors at most
   \(\Psi(R_\star)\).  Since no child has positive reduced gain,
   \cref{cor:renyi-spread-quotient-obstruction} gives
   \[
      \sum_iK_i^\rho>
      \frac{\Psi(R)}{\Psi(R_\star)}K^\rho,
      \qquad K=|U|.
   \]
   On the other hand, by Hölder,
   \[
      \sum_iK_i^\rho\le J^{1-\rho}K^\rho .
   \]
   Combining the two inequalities gives \((QSPE1)\).

   For the packing consequence, let \(E\subseteq U\) be a maximal
   \(R_\star\)-separated subset, where
   separated means that distinct points have distance \(>R_\star\).  Maximality
   implies that the radius-\(R_\star\) balls centered at points of \(E\) cover
   \(U\).  By the point-centered certification hypothesis, this is an available
   certified cover.  Applying \((QSPE1)\) to it gives \((QSPE2)\).

   The Renyi identity \((QSPE3)\) is immediate from
   \(\nu_E(x)=1/|E|\).  Since distinct points of \(E\) are
   \(R_\star\)-separated, every ordered pair \((x,y)\in E^2\), \(x\ne y\), is a
   separated pair at scale \(R_\star\), proving \((QSPE4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Spread packing entropy-energy screen]
   \label{cor:spread-packing-entropy-energy-screen}
   In the setting of \cref{cor:quotient-spread-packing-entropy}, let
   \(E\subseteq U\) be the separated set from \((QSPE2)\), with \(M=|E|\).  Let
   \(U_G\) be any Gaussian-cap or spherical-code bucket, and partition the
   ordered distinct pairs
   \[
      E_{\ne}^2=\{(x,y)\in E^2:x\ne y\}
   \]
   into finitely many profiles \(\Pi_E\).  Suppose every pair in profile
   \(\pi\in\Pi_E\) has certified bucket-intersection energy at least \(I_\pi\),
   in the sense that
   \[
      \Pr[x,y\in U_G]\le e^{-I_\pi}
      \qquad ((x,y)\in\pi).
      \tag{SPEE1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \E |E\cap U_G|^2
      \le
      \sum_{x\in E}\Pr[x\in U_G]
      +
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi_E}|\pi|e^{-I_\pi}.
      \tag{SPEE2}
   \]
   In particular, if
   \[
      I_\pi\ge\log|\pi|+\Lambda
      \qquad(\pi\in\Pi_E),
      \tag{SPEE3}
   \]
   then the distinct-pair contribution of the spread packing is at most
   \[
      |\Pi_E|e^{-\Lambda}.
      \tag{SPEE4}
   \]
   Thus the spherical/list-decoding side pays a high-spread quotient exactly by
   proving that cap-intersection energy dominates the packing entropy
   \(\log|\pi|\) on the separated profiles; failure of this inequality is the
   high-correlation signal that should feed the dense-star or quotient
   separator.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Expand the second moment:
   \[
      \E |E\cap U_G|^2
      =
      \sum_{x\in E}\Pr[x\in U_G]
      +
      \sum_{\substack{x,y\in E\\x\ne y}}\Pr[x,y\in U_G].
   \]
   Summing the bound \((SPEE1)\) over the profiles gives \((SPEE2)\).  If
   \((SPEE3)\) holds, then each profile contributes at most \(e^{-\Lambda}\) to
   the second sum, proving \((SPEE4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Spread-packing entropy failure gives a star signal]
   \label{cor:spread-packing-star-signal}
   In the setting of \cref{cor:spread-packing-entropy-energy-screen}, assume
   after the spherical normalization that \(E\subseteq\mathbb S^{D-1}\).  Let
   \(\pi\subseteq E_{\ne}^2\) be one separated-pair profile, and assign
   nonnegative weights \(\omega_{x,y}\) to pairs in \(\pi\).  Split
   \[
      \pi=\pi_{\rm lo}\dot\cup\pi_{\rm hi}.
   \]
   Suppose the low part has certified weighted contribution at most \(B_{\rm lo}\):
   \[
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\pi_{\rm lo}}\omega_{x,y}\le B_{\rm lo}.
      \tag{SPSS1}
   \]
   Suppose every high edge is genuinely high-correlation,
   \[
      (x,y)\in\pi_{\rm hi}
      \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
      \ip{x}{y}\ge\underline\theta
      \qquad(-1<\underline\theta<1).
      \tag{SPSS2}
   \]
   For \(x,y\in E\), put
   \[
      M_x(y)=\omega_{x,y}\mathbf 1\{(x,y)\in\pi_{\rm hi}\},
      \qquad
      W_{\rm hi}=\sum_{x,y\in E}M_x(y).
      \tag{SPSS3}
   \]
   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), set \(J_\omega=1\).  Otherwise suppose the positive
   values of \(M_x(y)\) lie in
   \([\omega_{\min},\omega_{\max}]\), and let
   \[
      J_\omega=1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{\omega_{\max}}{\omega_{\min}}\right\rceil
      \tag{SPSS4}
   \]
   and define dyadic star superlevels
   \[
      U_{x,t}=\{y\in E:M_x(y)\ge t\},
      \qquad
      t\in\{\omega_{\min}2^j:0\le j<J_\omega\}.
      \tag{SPSS5}
   \]
   Then every nonempty \(U_{x,t}\) is contained in the certified smaller ball
   \[
      U_{x,t}\subseteq
      E\cap B\!\left(x,\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)}\right).
      \tag{SPSS6}
   \]
   Moreover, for every \(\Lambda>0\), either
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}\le 2|E|J_\omega\Lambda,
      \tag{SPSS7}
   \]
   or some dyadic star satisfies
   \[
      t|U_{x,t}|\ge\Lambda.
      \tag{SPSS8}
   \]
   Consequently, if the dyadic family contains no high-correlation star of
   scale at least \(\Lambda\), then the whole profile contribution obeys
   \[
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\pi}\omega_{x,y}
      \le
      B_{\rm lo}+2|E|J_\omega\Lambda.
      \tag{SPSS9}
   \]

   In particular, taking
   \(\omega_{x,y}=\Pr[x,y\in U_G]\) identifies the precise obstruction left by
   \cref{cor:spread-packing-entropy-energy-screen}: any excess over the
   low-correlation entropy-energy payment must organize into a smaller-radius
   pair-star candidate, which the algorithm submits to the dense verifier.  The
   exact paid usefulness of that candidate is then checked by
   \cref{cor:pair-star-dense-column-generator} and
   \cref{cor:paid-pair-star-panel-certificate}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(y\in U_{x,t}\), then \(M_x(y)>0\), so \((x,y)\in\pi_{\rm hi}\).  By
   \((SPSS2)\),
   \[
      \|x-y\|^2=2-2\ip{x}{y}\le2(1-\underline\theta),
   \]
   proving \((SPSS6)\).

   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), then \((SPSS7)\) and \((SPSS9)\) are immediate.  Hence
   assume \(W_{\rm hi}>0\).

   For fixed \(x\), the dyadic layer-cake estimate gives
   \[
      \sum_{j=0}^{J_\omega-1}\omega_{\min}2^j|U_{x,\omega_{\min}2^j}|
      \ge
      \frac12\sum_{y\in E}M_x(y).
   \]
   Summing over \(x\in E\), if every dyadic star had
   \(t|U_{x,t}|<\Lambda\), then
   \[
      \frac12W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \sum_{x\in E}\sum_{j=0}^{J_\omega-1}
      \omega_{\min}2^j|U_{x,\omega_{\min}2^j}|
      <
      |E|J_\omega\Lambda,
   \]
   which is \((SPSS7)\).  The contrapositive gives \((SPSS8)\).  Combining
   \((SPSS1)\) and \((SPSS7)\) proves \((SPSS9)\) under the no-star condition.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Paid integrated star residual for spread profiles]
   \label{cor:paid-integrated-spread-star-residual}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:spread-packing-star-signal}, and also fix a
   finite filter-cover dual \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\) on near-pair demands
   \(\mathcal N\) with near radius \(r\).  For every possible star center
   \(x\in E\), put
   \[
      R_x=\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)},
      \qquad
      W_x=P\cap B(x,R_x),
      \qquad
      a_x(q)=\mathbf 1\{\|q-x\|\le R_x+r\},
      \tag{PSSR1}
   \]
   and define the paid degree and query price
   \[
      d_x(y)=
      \sum_{q:\,(y,q)\in\mathcal N}\alpha_{y,q}a_x(q),
      \qquad
      A_x=\sum_q\tau_qa_x(q).
      \tag{PSSR2}
   \]
   Suppose the dense verifier may add, for every \(x\in E\) and every
   cardinality \(h\le |W_x|\), the best paid \(h\)-point prefix of \(W_x\) with
   prices
   \[
      T_{x,h}=\psi_xh^{\rho_x},
      \qquad
      S_{x,h}=\psi_xh^{1+\rho_x},
      \qquad 0<\rho_x<1 .
      \tag{PSSR3}
   \]
   Finally suppose the high-correlation multiplicities are dominated by the paid
   near-shadow degrees,
   \[
      M_x(y)\le d_x(y)
      \qquad(x,y\in E).
      \tag{PSSR4}
   \]

   If no such smaller-radius paid prefix has positive reduced gain, then,
   writing \(t_j=\omega_{\min}2^j\) when \(W_{\rm hi}>0\) and interpreting the
   \(j\)-sums below as empty when \(W_{\rm hi}=0\),
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      2\sum_{x\in E}\sum_{j=0}^{J_\omega-1}
      \psi_x
      \left(
         A_x|U_{x,t_j}|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |U_{x,t_j}|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right),
      \tag{PSSR5}
   \]
   Consequently the whole weighted profile satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\pi}\omega_{x,y}
      \le
      B_{\rm lo}
      +
      2\sum_{x\in E}\sum_{j=0}^{J_\omega-1}
      \psi_x
      \left(
         A_x|U_{x,t_j}|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |U_{x,t_j}|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{PSSR6}
   \]
   Equivalently, a violation of \((PSSR6)\) exposes a positive reduced-gain
   smaller-radius prefix.  Thus the high-correlation part of a failed
   entropy-energy profile is charged by the integrated Renyi price of the
   dyadic paid star levels, not by a worst-case \(|E|J_\omega\) overlap bound.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The case \(W_{\rm hi}=0\) is immediate, so assume \(W_{\rm hi}>0\).  By
   \cref{cor:spread-packing-star-signal}, every \(U_{x,t_j}\) is contained in
   \(W_x\).  Since no \(h\)-point paid prefix in \(W_x\) has positive gain,
   the top-prefix optimality argument of
   \cref{lem:star-prefix-weak-type-residual} gives, for every \(x\) and \(j\),
   \[
      \sum_{y\in U_{x,t_j}}d_x(y)
      \le
      \psi_x
      \left(
         A_x|U_{x,t_j}|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |U_{x,t_j}|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{PSSR7}
   \]
   On the other hand,
   \[
      t_j|U_{x,t_j}|
      \le
      \sum_{y\in U_{x,t_j}}M_x(y)
      \le
      \sum_{y\in U_{x,t_j}}d_x(y),
      \tag{PSSR8}
   \]
   where the first inequality is the definition of the superlevel and the
   second is \((PSSR4)\).  Summing \((PSSR8)\) over \(x,j\), using \((PSSR7)\),
   and applying the dyadic layer-cake lower bound from the proof of
   \cref{cor:spread-packing-star-signal},
   \[
      \frac12W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \sum_{x,j}t_j|U_{x,t_j}|,
   \]
   proves \((PSSR5)\).  Adding the low contribution bound \((SPSS1)\) gives
   \((PSSR6)\).  The final statement is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Paid cover residual for quotient stars]
   \label{cor:paid-cover-quotient-star-residual}
   Work in a finite filter-cover dual with near-pair radius \(r\).  Let
   \(G=(U,a,T,S)\) be a quotient column, and write its captured demand as
   \[
      A_G=\sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \alpha_{p,q}\mathbf 1\{p\in U\}a(q).
      \tag{PCQ1}
   \]
   Let \(\mathcal X\) be a finite set of candidate centers.  For each
   \(x\in\mathcal X\), fix a radius \(R_x\), put
   \[
      W_x=P\cap B(x,R_x),
      \qquad
      a_x(q)=\mathbf 1\{\|q-x\|\le R_x+r\},
      \qquad
      A_x=\sum_q\tau_qa_x(q),
      \tag{PCQ2}
   \]
   and let \(\psi_x,\rho_x\) be certified child price parameters.  Suppose
   \(U\) is assigned to the centers by a map \(\kappa:U\to\mathcal X\) such
   that
   \[
      p\in B(\kappa(p),R_{\kappa(p)})
      \qquad(p\in U),
      \tag{PCQ3}
   \]
   and write \(U_x=\{p\in U:\kappa(p)=x\}\).

   Assume the dense verifier may add, for every \(x\) and every
   \(1\le h\le |W_x|\), the best paid \(h\)-point prefix of \(W_x\), activated
   by \(a_x\), with prices
   \[
      T_{x,h}=\psi_xh^{\rho_x},
      \qquad
      S_{x,h}=\psi_xh^{1+\rho_x}.
      \tag{PCQ4}
   \]
   If no such prefix has positive reduced gain, then the quotient demand is
   bounded by the integrated cover price
   \[
      A_G
      \le
      \sum_{x\in\mathcal X:U_x\ne\emptyset}
      \psi_x
      \left(
         A_x|U_x|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |U_x|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{PCQ5}
   \]
   Equivalently, if some assigned smaller-ball cover satisfies the strict
   reverse inequality in \((PCQ5)\), then one of its paid prefixes is a positive
   reduced-gain dense column.

   In particular, if \(G\) has positive reduced gain with parent price
   \(T=\psi K^\rho\), \(S=\psi K^{1+\rho}\), \(K=|U|\), and
   \[
      \sum_x
      \psi_x
      \left(
         A_x|U_x|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |U_x|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right)
      \le
      \psi\left(K^\rho\sum_q\tau_qa(q)+\sigma K^{1+\rho}\right),
      \tag{PCQ6}
   \]
   then some smaller-radius paid prefix has positive reduced gain.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For \(p\in U\), define the parent paid degree
   \[
      b(p)=\sum_{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\alpha_{p,q}a(q).
   \]
   Then \(A_G=\sum_{p\in U}b(p)\).  For \(x\in\mathcal X\), define the
   ball-thickened paid degree
   \[
      d_x(p)=\sum_{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\alpha_{p,q}a_x(q)
      \qquad(p\in W_x).
   \]
   If \(p\in U_x\) and \(a(q)=1\) for a near pair \((p,q)\), then
   \[
      \|q-x\|\le\|q-p\|+\|p-x\|\le r+R_x,
   \]
   so \(a_x(q)=1\).  Hence
   \[
      b(p)\le d_x(p)\qquad(p\in U_x).
      \tag{PCQ7}
   \]

   Since no \(h\)-point prefix of \(W_x\) has positive reduced gain, the best
   \(h\)-prefix bound gives
   \[
      \sum_{i\le h}d_x(p_i)
      \le
      \psi_x\left(A_xh^{\rho_x}+\sigma h^{1+\rho_x}\right)
      \tag{PCQ8}
   \]
   where \(p_1,p_2,\ldots\) are the points of \(W_x\) sorted by decreasing
   \(d_x\).  The top \(|U_x|\) prefix dominates the particular subset \(U_x\).
   Combining this with \((PCQ7)\) yields
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U_x}b(p)
      \le
      \sum_{p\in U_x}d_x(p)
      \le
      \psi_x
      \left(
         A_x|U_x|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |U_x|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
   \]
   Summing over \(x\) proves \((PCQ5)\).  The strict reverse implication is its
   contrapositive.

   For the final claim, positive reduced gain of \(G\) says
   \[
      A_G>
      \psi\left(K^\rho\sum_q\tau_qa(q)+\sigma K^{1+\rho}\right).
   \]
   Together with \((PCQ6)\), this gives the strict reverse of \((PCQ5)\), so a
   smaller-radius paid prefix has positive reduced gain.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Inherited-activation paid cover closure]
   \label{cor:inherited-activation-paid-cover}
   Let \(G\) be a parent quotient filter with update side \(U\), activation
   \(a\), prices
   \[
      T=\psi K^\rho,\qquad S=\psi K^{1+\rho},\qquad K=|U|,
   \]
   and positive reduced gain
   \[
      A_G>
      \psi\left(K^\rho\mathsf T_a+\sigma K^{1+\rho}\right),
      \qquad
      \mathsf T_a=\sum_q\tau_qa(q).
      \tag{IAC1}
   \]
   The conclusion below is a reduced-gain statement for the finite demand
   system.  If \(a\) is a retained routing-safe predicate for \(U\), then the
   produced inherited-activation child is also a globally valid retained dense
   filter; otherwise it is a local finite-demand column that must later be
   replaced by a certified query wrapper.
   Suppose \(U\) is assigned to smaller certified balls
   \(W_x=P\cap B(x,R_x)\) by sets \(U_x\subseteq U\cap W_x\) forming a
   partition of \(U\).  For each \(x\), let \(\psi_x,\rho_x\) be certified
   child price parameters, and suppose the dense verifier may add every
   inherited-activation prefix of \(U\cap W_x\): if \(H\subseteq U\cap W_x\)
   has size \(h\), the column has update side \(H\), activation \(a\), and
   prices
   \[
      T_{x,h}^{\uparrow}=\psi_xh^{\rho_x},
      \qquad
      S_{x,h}^{\uparrow}=\psi_xh^{1+\rho_x}.
      \tag{IAC2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_x\psi_x
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|U_x|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |U_x|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right)
      \le
      \psi\left(K^\rho\mathsf T_a+\sigma K^{1+\rho}\right),
      \tag{IAC3}
   \]
   then some inherited-activation smaller-radius prefix has positive reduced
   gain.

   In particular, if the children use the same exponent \(\rho\), the cover
   closes whenever
   \[
      \sum_x\psi_x|U_x|^\rho\le\psi K^\rho,
      \qquad
      \sum_x\psi_x|U_x|^{1+\rho}\le\psi K^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{IAC4}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For \(p\in U\), use the parent paid degree
   \[
      b(p)=\sum_{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\alpha_{p,q}a(q),
      \qquad
      A_G=\sum_{p\in U}b(p).
   \]
   If no inherited-activation prefix of \(U\cap W_x\) has positive reduced
   gain, then after sorting \(U\cap W_x\) by decreasing \(b\), every prefix of
   size \(h\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{i\le h}b(p_i)
      \le
      \psi_x\left(\mathsf T_a h^{\rho_x}+\sigma h^{1+\rho_x}\right).
      \tag{IAC5}
   \]
   The top \(|U_x|\) prefix dominates the assigned subset \(U_x\), so
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U_x}b(p)
      \le
      \psi_x
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|U_x|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |U_x|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
   \]
   Summing over \(x\) gives
   \[
      A_G\le
      \sum_x\psi_x
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|U_x|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |U_x|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right),
   \]
   contradicting \((IAC1)\) and \((IAC3)\).  Hence some prefix is positive.
   The final statement is the special case of \((IAC3)\) obtained from
   \((IAC4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Inherited-activation cover spread gives packing]
   \label{cor:inherited-activation-cover-spread-packing}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:inherited-activation-paid-cover}, and assume the children use the
   same exponent \(\rho\).  Fix a smaller radius \(R_\star\) with child price
   factor \(\psi_\star\le\psi\).  Suppose that for every certified ball
   \(B(c,R_\star)\) the dense verifier may add inherited-activation prefixes of
   \(U\cap B(c,R_\star)\) with price factor at most \(\psi_\star\).

   If no inherited-activation prefix at radius \(R_\star\) has positive reduced
   gain, then every certified radius-\(R_\star\) ball cover of \(U\) has size
   \[
      J>
      \left(\frac{\psi}{\psi_\star}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{IACP1}
   \]
   If, in addition, every point-centered ball \(B(x,R_\star)\), \(x\in U\), is
   certified, then \(U\) contains an \(R_\star\)-separated set \(E\) with
   \[
      |E|>
      \left(\frac{\psi}{\psi_\star}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{IACP2}
   \]

   Thus, for a retained routing-safe parent filter, the standard certified-ball
   recursion is the same filter-cover refinement as the high-spread witness for
   spherical or list-decoding estimates: a low-fanout smaller-ball cover would
   close inside the same activation predicate, while failure of all such covers
   supplies separated packing entropy.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(B_1,\ldots,B_J\) be any certified radius-\(R_\star\) ball cover of
   \(U\), and assign each point of \(U\) to one covering ball.  Let \(K_i\) be
   the nonzero assigned sizes.  If
   \[
      J\le\left(\frac{\psi}{\psi_\star}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)},
   \]
   then Hölder gives
   \[
      \sum_i\psi_\star K_i^\rho
      \le
      \psi_\star J^{1-\rho}K^\rho
      \le
      \psi K^\rho .
   \]
   Also, since the assigned sets are disjoint and \(\psi_\star\le\psi\),
   \[
      \sum_i\psi_\star K_i^{1+\rho}
      \le
      \psi_\star K^{1+\rho}
      \le
      \psi K^{1+\rho}.
   \]
   Hence \((IAC4)\) holds for this inherited-activation refinement, and
   \cref{cor:inherited-activation-paid-cover} would force a positive
   radius-\(R_\star\) prefix, contrary to the hypothesis.  Therefore
   \((IACP1)\) holds.

   For the separated-set statement, take \(E\subseteq U\) maximal with pairwise
   distances \(>R_\star\).  Maximality implies that the point-centered
   radius-\(R_\star\) balls around \(E\) cover \(U\).  These balls are certified
   by assumption, so \((IACP1)\) gives \((IACP2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Inherited-activation Renyi center law]
   \label{cor:inherited-activation-renyi-center-law}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:inherited-activation-cover-spread-packing}.  Write \(K=|U|\).
   Suppose no inherited-activation prefix at radius \(R_\star\) has positive
   reduced gain.  Then every assigned certified point-centered cover
   \[
      U=\dot\bigcup_{x\in E}U_x,
      \qquad
      U_x\subseteq U\cap B(x,R_\star),
      \qquad x\in U,
      \tag{IACL1}
   \]
   with nonempty cells satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{x\in E}\left(\frac{|U_x|}{K}\right)^\rho
      >
      \frac{\psi}{\psi_\star}.
      \tag{IACL2}
   \]
   In particular, if every point-centered ball \(B(x,R_\star)\), \(x\in U\), is
   certified, \(E\) is a maximal \(R_\star\)-separated subset of \(U\), and
   \(U_x\) are any induced nearest-center cells, the center law
   \[
      \lambda_x=\frac{|U_x|}{K}
      \qquad(x\in E)
      \tag{IACL3}
   \]
   is supported on an \(R_\star\)-separated set and has Renyi effective support
   larger than \((\psi/\psi_\star)^{1/(1-\rho)}\).

   Moreover, let the positive values of \(\lambda_x\) lie in
   \([\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}]\), set
   \[
      J_\lambda=
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{\lambda_{\max}}{\lambda_{\min}}\right\rceil,
      \qquad
      \theta_j=\lambda_{\min}2^j,
      \tag{IACL4}
   \]
   and define dyadic center levels
   \[
      E_j=\{x\in E:\theta_j\le\lambda_x<2\theta_j\},
      \qquad
      M_j=\sum_{x\in E_j}\lambda_x .
      \tag{IACL5}
   \]
   Some level \(j\) satisfies
   \[
      M_j^\rho |E_j|^{1-\rho}
      >
      \frac{1}{J_\lambda}\frac{\psi}{\psi_\star}.
      \tag{IACL6}
   \]
   Since the cells are nonempty, \(J_\lambda\le1+\lceil\log_2K\rceil\).  Thus an
   unclosed same-activation quotient supplies either the full weighted center law
   \((\lambda_x)\), usable directly in paid-product screens with center weights,
   or a single dyadic separated subpacking losing only a logarithmic factor in
   the Renyi mass-entropy product.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Consider any assigned cover \((IACL1)\), and put \(K_x=|U_x|\).  If
   \[
      \sum_{x\in E}\psi_\star K_x^\rho\le\psi K^\rho,
   \]
   then the storage side is automatic:
   \[
      \sum_{x\in E}\psi_\star K_x^{1+\rho}
      \le
      \psi_\star K^{1+\rho}
      \le
      \psi K^{1+\rho}.
   \]
   Hence \((IAC4)\) would hold for this inherited-activation refinement, and
   \cref{cor:inherited-activation-paid-cover} would produce a positive
   radius-\(R_\star\) prefix, contrary to the hypothesis.  Therefore the displayed
   query inequality fails for every assigned cover, and division by
   \(\psi_\star K^\rho\) gives \((IACL2)\).

   A maximal \(R_\star\)-separated set covers \(U\) by point-centered
   radius-\(R_\star\) balls, so the first part applies to any induced cells.  The
   Renyi effective-support statement is just the identity
   \[
      \left(\sum_{x\in E}\lambda_x^\rho\right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      >
      \left(\frac{\psi}{\psi_\star}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
   \]

   For the dyadic claim, the levels \(E_j\) partition the support of
   \(\lambda\), and \((IACL2)\) gives
   \[
      \sum_j\sum_{x\in E_j}\lambda_x^\rho>\frac{\psi}{\psi_\star}.
   \]
   Thus some \(j\) has
   \[
      \sum_{x\in E_j}\lambda_x^\rho
      >
      \frac{1}{J_\lambda}\frac{\psi}{\psi_\star}.
   \]
   Jensen's inequality on \(E_j\) gives
   \[
      \sum_{x\in E_j}\lambda_x^\rho
      \le
      |E_j|^{1-\rho}
      \left(\sum_{x\in E_j}\lambda_x\right)^\rho
      =
      |E_j|^{1-\rho}M_j^\rho ,
   \]
   proving \((IACL6)\).  Finally, nonempty assigned cells have
   \(1/K\le\lambda_x\le1\), so the stated bound on \(J_\lambda\) follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Inherited-activation spread-star residual]
   \label{cor:inherited-activation-spread-star-residual}
   Work in a finite filter-cover dual with near-pair demands \(\mathcal N\), and
   let \(G=(U,a,T,S)\) be a parent quotient whose activation \(a\) is retained
   routing-safe for \(U\).  Put
   \[
      \mathsf T_a=\sum_q\tau_qa(q),
      \qquad
      b(y)=\sum_{q:\,(y,q)\in\mathcal N}\alpha_{y,q}a(q)
      \qquad(y\in U).
      \tag{IASR0}
   \]
   Let \(E\subseteq U\) be a separated packing, and work with one profile
   \(\pi\subseteq E_{\ne}^2\) and weights \(\omega_{x,y}\) as in
   \cref{cor:spread-packing-star-signal}.  Assume the high edges have
   correlation at least \(\underline\theta\), and define \(M_x(y)\),
   \(W_{\rm hi}\), \(J_\omega\), and dyadic superlevels \(U_{x,t_j}\) by
   \((SPSS3)\)--\((SPSS5)\).  For every star center \(x\in E\), let
   \(R_x=\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)}\), and suppose the dense verifier may add
   every inherited-activation prefix of \(U\cap B(x,R_x)\) with prices
   \[
      T_{x,h}=\psi_xh^{\rho_x},
      \qquad
      S_{x,h}=\psi_xh^{1+\rho_x},
      \qquad 0<\rho_x<1 .
      \tag{IASR1}
   \]
   Finally suppose the high-correlation multiplicities are dominated by the
   parent paid degree,
   \[
      M_x(y)\le b(y)\qquad(x,y\in E).
      \tag{IASR2}
   \]

   If no inherited-activation prefix from these star containers has positive
   reduced gain, then, interpreting the \(j\)-sum as empty when \(W_{\rm hi}=0\),
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      2\sum_{x\in E}\sum_{j=0}^{J_\omega-1}
      \psi_x
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|U_{x,t_j}|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |U_{x,t_j}|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{IASR3}
   \]
   Consequently, if the low part of the profile has contribution at most
   \(B_{\rm lo}\), then the whole weighted profile satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\pi}\omega_{x,y}
      \le
      B_{\rm lo}
      +
      2\sum_{x\in E}\sum_{j=0}^{J_\omega-1}
      \psi_x
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|U_{x,t_j}|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |U_{x,t_j}|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{IASR4}
   \]
   Equivalently, a violation of \((IASR4)\) exposes a positive reduced-gain
   smaller-radius prefix using the parent activation \(a\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), then both claims are immediate.  Otherwise, by
   \cref{cor:spread-packing-star-signal}, every \(U_{x,t_j}\) is contained in
   \(E\cap B(x,R_x)\subseteq U\cap B(x,R_x)\).  Since no inherited-activation
   prefix in \(U\cap B(x,R_x)\) has positive gain, the top-prefix argument gives
   \[
      \sum_{y\in U_{x,t_j}} b(y)
      \le
      \psi_x
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|U_{x,t_j}|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |U_{x,t_j}|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{IASR5}
   \]
   The superlevel definition and domination \((IASR2)\) give
   \[
      t_j|U_{x,t_j}|
      \le
      \sum_{y\in U_{x,t_j}}M_x(y)
      \le
      \sum_{y\in U_{x,t_j}}b(y).
      \tag{IASR6}
   \]
   Summing \((IASR6)\) over \(x,j\), using \((IASR5)\), and applying the dyadic
   layer-cake lower bound from the proof of
   \cref{cor:spread-packing-star-signal},
   \[
      \frac12W_{\rm hi}\le\sum_{x,j}t_j|U_{x,t_j}|,
   \]
   proves \((IASR3)\).  Adding the low contribution bound gives \((IASR4)\),
   and the final statement is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Clipped inherited-activation spread-star residual]
   \label{cor:clipped-inherited-activation-spread-star-residual}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:inherited-activation-spread-star-residual}, but do not assume the
   pointwise domination \((IASR2)\).  Define the parent-paid and overload parts
   of the high-correlation multiplicities by
   \[
      M_x^\cap(y)=\min\{M_x(y),b(y)\},
      \qquad
      M_x^+(y)=\bigl(M_x(y)-b(y)\bigr)_+ ,
      \tag{CISR1}
   \]
   and put
   \[
      W_\cap=\sum_{x,y\in E}M_x^\cap(y),
      \qquad
      W_+=\sum_{x,y\in E}M_x^+(y),
      \qquad
      W_{\rm hi}=W_\cap+W_+ .
      \tag{CISR2}
   \]
   If \(W_\cap>0\), let the positive values of \(M_x^\cap(y)\) lie in
   \([m_\cap^-,m_\cap^+]\), set
   \[
      J_\cap=1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{m_\cap^+}{m_\cap^-}\right\rceil,
      \qquad
      s_j=m_\cap^-2^j\quad(0\le j<J_\cap),
      \tag{CISR3}
   \]
   and define clipped superlevels
   \[
      V_{x,s_j}=\{y\in E:M_x^\cap(y)\ge s_j\}.
      \tag{CISR4}
   \]
   If \(W_\cap=0\), interpret the \(j\)-sums below as empty.

   If no inherited-activation prefix from the star containers
   \(U\cap B(x,R_x)\) has positive reduced gain, then
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      W_+
      +
      2\sum_{x\in E}\sum_{j=0}^{J_\cap-1}
      \psi_x
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|V_{x,s_j}|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |V_{x,s_j}|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{CISR5}
   \]
   Consequently, if the low part of the profile has contribution at most
   \(B_{\rm lo}\), then
   \[
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\pi}\omega_{x,y}
      \le
      B_{\rm lo}
      +
      W_+
      +
      2\sum_{x\in E}\sum_{j=0}^{J_\cap-1}
      \psi_x
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|V_{x,s_j}|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |V_{x,s_j}|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{CISR6}
   \]

   In particular, any paid-product high-correlation law
   \[
      M_x(y)=\lambda_x\theta_{x,y}b(y),
      \qquad
      0\le\lambda_x\le1,\quad 0\le\theta_{x,y}\le1,
      \tag{CISR7}
   \]
   has \(W_+=0\).  For such laws the high-correlation handoff is already
   compatible with the parent activation: all remaining mass is paid by
   inherited star-prefix prices, unless a positive inherited prefix is exposed.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The case \(W_\cap=0\) gives \(W_{\rm hi}=W_+\), so assume \(W_\cap>0\).
   If \(y\in V_{x,s_j}\), then \(M_x(y)>0\); hence \((x,y)\) is a
   high-correlation edge and, as in
   \cref{cor:spread-packing-star-signal}, \(y\in U\cap B(x,R_x)\).  Since no
   inherited-activation prefix in this container has positive gain, the same
   top-prefix bound used in \((IASR5)\) gives
   \[
      \sum_{y\in V_{x,s_j}} b(y)
      \le
      \psi_x
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|V_{x,s_j}|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |V_{x,s_j}|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{CISR8}
   \]
   By definition of the clipped superlevel,
   \[
      s_j|V_{x,s_j}|
      \le
      \sum_{y\in V_{x,s_j}}M_x^\cap(y)
      \le
      \sum_{y\in V_{x,s_j}}b(y).
      \tag{CISR9}
   \]
   Summing \((CISR9)\), applying \((CISR8)\), and using the dyadic layer-cake
   bound
   \[
      \frac12W_\cap\le\sum_{x\in E}\sum_{j=0}^{J_\cap-1}s_j|V_{x,s_j}|
   \]
   proves
   \[
      W_\cap
      \le
      2\sum_{x,j}
      \psi_x
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|V_{x,s_j}|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |V_{x,s_j}|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
   \]
   Since \(W_{\rm hi}=W_\cap+W_+\), this is \((CISR5)\).  Adding the
   low-correlation contribution gives \((CISR6)\).  Finally, \((CISR7)\)
   implies \(M_x(y)\le b(y)\) for every \(x,y\), so \(M_x^+(y)=0\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Paid-product spread-packing handoff]
   \label{cor:paid-product-spread-packing-handoff}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:inherited-activation-spread-star-residual}.  Let
   \(0\le\lambda_x\le1\) be arbitrary center weights on \(E\), and let
   \(0\le\kappa_{x,y}\le1\) be arbitrary pair weights on one profile
   \(\pi\subseteq E_{\ne}^2\).  Define the paid-product profile weights
   \[
      \omega_{x,y}=\lambda_x b(y)\kappa_{x,y}
      \qquad((x,y)\in\pi),
      \tag{PPSH1}
   \]
   and split \(\pi=\pi_{\rm lo}\dot\cup\pi_{\rm hi}\).  Suppose every high edge
   has correlation at least \(\underline\theta\).  Put
   \[
      M_x(y)=\lambda_xb(y)\kappa_{x,y}
      \mathbf 1\{(x,y)\in\pi_{\rm hi}\},
      \qquad
      W_{\rm hi}=\sum_{x,y\in E}M_x(y),
      \tag{PPSH2}
   \]
   and form the dyadic high-correlation superlevels \(U_{x,t_j}\) from
   \((SPSS4)\)--\((SPSS5)\) using these multiplicities.  If the low part is
   certified by
   \[
      B_{\rm lo}\ge
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\pi_{\rm lo}}\lambda_xb(y)\kappa_{x,y},
      \tag{PPSH3}
   \]
   and no inherited-activation prefix from the star containers
   \(U\cap B(x,\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)})\) has positive reduced gain, then
   \[
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\pi}\lambda_xb(y)\kappa_{x,y}
      \le
      B_{\rm lo}
      +
      2\sum_{x\in E}\sum_{j=0}^{J_\omega-1}
      \psi_x
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|U_{x,t_j}|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |U_{x,t_j}|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{PPSH4}
   \]

   In particular, if \(\kappa_{x,y}=\Pr[x,y\in U_G]\) for a spherical or
   Gaussian bucket and the low part of profile \(\pi\) has
   \(\kappa_{x,y}\le e^{-I_\pi}\), then one may take
   \[
      B_{\rm lo}
      =
      e^{-I_\pi}
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\pi_{\rm lo}}\lambda_xb(y).
      \tag{PPSH5}
   \]
   Thus the entropy-energy handoff can be run with paid-product cross moments
   \[
      \E\sum_{(x,y)\in\pi}
      \lambda_xb(y)\mathbf 1\{x,y\in U_G\},
      \tag{PPSH6}
   \]
   rather than with raw pair counts.  These weighted moments have no overload
   term: for every center \(x\), the induced high-correlation star multiplicity
   is pointwise dominated by the parent paid degree \(b(y)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(0\le\lambda_x,\kappa_{x,y}\le1\), the high-correlation
   multiplicities in \((PPSH2)\) satisfy
   \[
      M_x(y)\le b(y)\qquad(x,y\in E).
   \]
   Hence the domination hypothesis \((IASR2)\) of
   \cref{cor:inherited-activation-spread-star-residual} holds for the weights
   \((PPSH1)\).  Applying that corollary with the low contribution certificate
   \((PPSH3)\) gives \((PPSH4)\).  The specialization \((PPSH5)\) is the
   pointwise low-correlation energy bound multiplied by the paid-product weights
   and summed over \(\pi_{\rm lo}\).  Finally, \((PPSH6)\) is exactly the same
   statement with \(\kappa_{x,y}=\Pr[x,y\in U_G]\), by linearity of
   expectation.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Bipartite paid-product spread handoff]
   \label{cor:bipartite-paid-product-spread-handoff}
   Work in a finite filter-cover dual with near-pair demands \(\mathcal N\).
   Let \(G=(U,a,T,S)\) be a parent quotient whose activation \(a\) is retained
   routing-safe for \(U\), and define
   \[
      \mathsf T_a=\sum_q\tau_qa(q),
      \qquad
      b(y)=\sum_{q:\,(y,q)\in\mathcal N}\alpha_{y,q}a(q)
      \qquad(y\in U).
      \tag{BPSH0}
   \]
   Let \(X\subseteq U\) be any finite set of centers and let \(Y\subseteq U\) be
   any finite paid side.  For a profile
   \(\pi\subseteq X\times Y\), choose center weights \(0\le\lambda_x\le1\) and
   pair weights \(0\le\kappa_{x,y}\le1\).  Split
   \(\pi=\pi_{\rm lo}\dot\cup\pi_{\rm hi}\), and suppose the high edges satisfy
   \[
      (x,y)\in\pi_{\rm hi}
      \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
      \ip{x}{y}\ge\underline\theta
      \qquad(-1<\underline\theta<1).
      \tag{BPSH1}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      R_\star=\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)}
   \]
   and suppose the dense verifier may add every inherited-activation prefix of
   \(U\cap B(x,R_\star)\), \(x\in X\), with prices
   \[
      T_{x,h}=\psi_xh^{\rho_x},
      \qquad
      S_{x,h}=\psi_xh^{1+\rho_x},
      \qquad 0<\rho_x<1.
      \tag{BPSH2}
   \]
   Define high-correlation multiplicities
   \[
      M_x(y)=\lambda_xb(y)\kappa_{x,y}
      \mathbf 1\{(x,y)\in\pi_{\rm hi}\},
      \qquad
      W_{\rm hi}=\sum_{x\in X}\sum_{y\in Y}M_x(y).
      \tag{BPSH3}
   \]
   If \(W_{\rm hi}>0\), let the positive values of \(M_x(y)\) lie in
   \([\omega_{\min},\omega_{\max}]\), set
   \[
      J_\omega=
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{\omega_{\max}}{\omega_{\min}}\right\rceil,
      \qquad
      t_j=\omega_{\min}2^j\quad(0\le j<J_\omega),
      \tag{BPSH4}
   \]
   and define
   \[
      U_{x,t_j}=\{y\in Y:M_x(y)\ge t_j\}.
      \tag{BPSH5}
   \]
   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), interpret all \(j\)-sums below as empty.

   If the low part is certified by
   \[
      B_{\rm lo}\ge
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\pi_{\rm lo}}\lambda_xb(y)\kappa_{x,y},
      \tag{BPSH6}
   \]
   and no inherited-activation prefix from these star containers has positive
   reduced gain, then
   \[
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\pi}\lambda_xb(y)\kappa_{x,y}
      \le
      B_{\rm lo}
      +
      2\sum_{x\in X}\sum_{j=0}^{J_\omega-1}
      \psi_x
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|U_{x,t_j}|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |U_{x,t_j}|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{BPSH7}
   \]

   In particular, the separated set supplied by
   \cref{cor:inherited-activation-cover-spread-packing} may be used only on the
   center side \(X\); the paid side \(Y\) may remain the whole parent update set
   \(U\).  Thus the next entropy-energy estimate need only prove spread or
   profile entropy for the center coordinates, while the near-pair demand is
   retained exactly through the parent paid measure \(b(y)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(y\in U_{x,t_j}\), then \(M_x(y)>0\), so \((x,y)\in\pi_{\rm hi}\).
   Hence \((BPSH1)\) gives
   \[
      \|x-y\|^2=2-2\ip{x}{y}\le2(1-\underline\theta)=R_\star^2,
   \]
   and therefore \(U_{x,t_j}\subseteq U\cap B(x,R_\star)\).

   Since no inherited-activation prefix in this container has positive gain,
   the same top-prefix argument as in \((IASR5)\) gives, for every \(x,j\),
   \[
      \sum_{y\in U_{x,t_j}}b(y)
      \le
      \psi_x
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|U_{x,t_j}|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |U_{x,t_j}|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{BPSH8}
   \]
   Because \(0\le\lambda_x,\kappa_{x,y}\le1\), we have \(M_x(y)\le b(y)\).
   Thus
   \[
      t_j|U_{x,t_j}|
      \le
      \sum_{y\in U_{x,t_j}}M_x(y)
      \le
      \sum_{y\in U_{x,t_j}}b(y).
      \tag{BPSH9}
   \]
   The dyadic layer-cake inequality gives
   \[
      \frac12W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \sum_{x\in X}\sum_{j=0}^{J_\omega-1}t_j|U_{x,t_j}|.
   \]
   Combining this with \((BPSH8)\)--\((BPSH9)\) bounds \(W_{\rm hi}\) by the
   price sum in \((BPSH7)\).  Adding the low contribution bound \((BPSH6)\)
   proves the displayed inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Bipartite paid-transport spread handoff]
   \label{cor:bipartite-paid-transport-spread-handoff}
   Work in the same finite dual setting as
   \cref{cor:bipartite-paid-product-spread-handoff}.  Let \(X\subseteq U\) be
   a finite set of centers, let \(Y\subseteq U\) be a finite paid side, and let
   \[
      0\le w_{x,y}\le b(y)
      \qquad(x\in X,\ y\in Y)
      \tag{BTSH1}
   \]
   be arbitrary transport weights.  For a profile \(\pi\subseteq X\times Y\),
   choose pair weights \(0\le\kappa_{x,y}\le1\), split
   \(\pi=\pi_{\rm lo}\dot\cup\pi_{\rm hi}\), and suppose the high edges satisfy
   \[
      (x,y)\in\pi_{\rm hi}
      \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
      \ip{x}{y}\ge\underline\theta
      \qquad(-1<\underline\theta<1).
      \tag{BTSH2}
   \]
   Put \(R_\star=\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)}\), and suppose the dense verifier
   may add every inherited-activation prefix of \(U\cap B(x,R_\star)\),
   \(x\in X\), with prices
   \[
      T_{x,h}=\psi_xh^{\rho_x},
      \qquad
      S_{x,h}=\psi_xh^{1+\rho_x},
      \qquad 0<\rho_x<1.
      \tag{BTSH3}
   \]
   Define high-correlation multiplicities
   \[
      M_x(y)=w_{x,y}\kappa_{x,y}
      \mathbf 1\{(x,y)\in\pi_{\rm hi}\},
      \qquad
      W_{\rm hi}=\sum_{x\in X}\sum_{y\in Y}M_x(y).
      \tag{BTSH4}
   \]
   If \(W_{\rm hi}>0\), let the positive values of \(M_x(y)\) define dyadic
   levels \(t_j\) and superlevels
   \[
      U_{x,t_j}=\{y\in Y:M_x(y)\ge t_j\}
      \tag{BTSH5}
   \]
   as in \((BPSH4)\)--\((BPSH5)\).  If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), interpret the sum over
   \(j\) below as empty.

   If the low part is certified by
   \[
      B_{\rm lo}\ge
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\pi_{\rm lo}}w_{x,y}\kappa_{x,y},
      \tag{BTSH6}
   \]
   and no inherited-activation prefix from these star containers has positive
   reduced gain, then
   \[
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\pi}w_{x,y}\kappa_{x,y}
      \le
      B_{\rm lo}
      +
      2\sum_{x\in X}\sum_j
      \psi_x
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|U_{x,t_j}|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |U_{x,t_j}|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{BTSH7}
   \]

   Thus the high-correlation handoff does not require a product law
   \(\lambda_xb(y)\).  It is enough that the routed weight of every
   center--paid-point edge is pointwise dominated by the original paid degree.
   In particular, an assigned paid transport \(w_{c(y),y}=b(y)\) and
   \(w_{x,y}=0\) for \(x\ne c(y)\) is admissible whenever \(c(y)\in X\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(y\in U_{x,t_j}\), then \(M_x(y)>0\), so \((x,y)\in\pi_{\rm hi}\).  Hence
   \((BTSH2)\) gives
   \[
      \|x-y\|^2=2-2\ip{x}{y}\le2(1-\underline\theta)=R_\star^2,
   \]
   and therefore \(U_{x,t_j}\subseteq U\cap B(x,R_\star)\).

   Since no inherited-activation prefix in this container has positive gain, the
   top-prefix bound gives, for every \(x,j\),
   \[
      \sum_{y\in U_{x,t_j}}b(y)
      \le
      \psi_x
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|U_{x,t_j}|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |U_{x,t_j}|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{BTSH8}
   \]
   Since \(0\le\kappa_{x,y}\le1\), \((BTSH1)\) gives
   \(M_x(y)\le b(y)\) for every \(x,y\).  Hence
   \[
      t_j|U_{x,t_j}|
      \le
      \sum_{y\in U_{x,t_j}}M_x(y)
      \le
      \sum_{y\in U_{x,t_j}}b(y).
      \tag{BTSH9}
   \]
   The dyadic layer-cake inequality gives
   \[
      \frac12W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \sum_{x\in X}\sum_jt_j|U_{x,t_j}|.
   \]
   Combining this with \((BTSH8)\)--\((BTSH9)\) gives
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      2\sum_{x\in X}\sum_j
      \psi_x
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|U_{x,t_j}|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |U_{x,t_j}|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right)
   \]
   whenever no inherited prefix is positive.  Adding the low contribution
   \((BTSH6)\) proves \((BTSH7)\).  The assigned-transport statement is immediate
   from \(w_{c(y),y}=b(y)\) and all other routed weights equal to zero.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Paid level-set spread packing]
   \label{cor:paid-level-set-spread-packing}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:bipartite-paid-product-spread-handoff}.  Fix a smaller radius
   \(R_\star\), a price factor \(\psi_\star>0\), and an exponent
   \(0<\rho_\star<1\).  Assume the dense verifier may add every
   inherited-activation prefix of \(U\cap B(x,R_\star)\), \(x\in U\), with
   prices
   \[
      T_{x,h}=\psi_\star h^{\rho_\star},
      \qquad
      S_{x,h}=\psi_\star h^{1+\rho_\star}.
      \tag{PLSP0}
   \]
   Suppose no such prefix has positive reduced gain.  For \(t>0\), put
   \[
      Y_t=\{y\in U:b(y)\ge t\}.
   \]
   Then every assigned point-centered \(R_\star\)-cover of \(Y_t\),
   \[
      Y_t=\dot\bigcup_i H_i,
      \qquad
      H_i\subseteq Y_t\cap B(x_i,R_\star),
      \qquad x_i\in U,
      \tag{PLSP1}
   \]
   satisfies
   \[
      t|Y_t|
      \le
      \psi_\star
      \sum_i
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a |H_i|^{\rho_\star}
         +
         \sigma |H_i|^{1+\rho_\star}
      \right).
      \tag{PLSP2}
   \]

   In particular, let \(X_t\subseteq Y_t\) be any maximal
   \(R_\star\)-separated set, so the balls \(B(x,R_\star)\), \(x\in X_t\),
   cover \(Y_t\).  For the induced assignment cells,
   \[
      t|Y_t|
      \le
      \psi_\star
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a |X_t|^{1-\rho_\star}|Y_t|^{\rho_\star}
         +
         \sigma |Y_t|^{1+\rho_\star}
      \right).
      \tag{PLSP3}
   \]
   Consequently, if \(\mathsf T_a>0\) and
   \(t|Y_t|>\psi_\star\sigma |Y_t|^{1+\rho_\star}\), then
   \[
      |X_t|
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{
            t|Y_t|-\psi_\star\sigma |Y_t|^{1+\rho_\star}
         }{
            \psi_\star\mathsf T_a |Y_t|^{\rho_\star}
         }
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho_\star)}.
      \tag{PLSP4}
   \]

   Finally, if \(B=\sum_{y\in U}b(y)>0\), let the positive values of \(b(y)\)
   lie in \([b_{\min},b_{\max}]\), set
   \[
      J_b=1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{b_{\max}}{b_{\min}}\right\rceil,
      \qquad
      t_j=b_{\min}2^j\quad(0\le j<J_b),
      \tag{PLSP5}
   \]
   and define \(Y_j=Y_{t_j}\).  Some dyadic paid superlevel satisfies
   \[
      t_j|Y_j|\ge \frac{B}{2J_b}.
      \tag{PLSP6}
   \]
   Thus a surviving inherited-activation residual has a logarithmically large
   paid superlevel whose own support is spread in the precise no-cheap-cover
   sense \((PLSP2)\).  The center side in
   \cref{cor:bipartite-paid-product-spread-handoff} may therefore be chosen
   from a paid superlevel, not merely from an unweighted packing of \(U\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(H\subseteq Y_t\cap B(x,R_\star)\) have size \(h\).  Since the inherited
   prefix of size \(h\) in \(U\cap B(x,R_\star)\) has nonpositive reduced gain,
   the best \(h\)-point prefix sorted by the parent paid degree \(b\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{y\in H}b(y)
      \le
      \psi_\star
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a h^{\rho_\star}
         +
         \sigma h^{1+\rho_\star}
      \right).
      \tag{PLSP7}
   \]
   But every \(y\in H\subseteq Y_t\) has \(b(y)\ge t\), so
   \[
      t|H|
      \le
      \psi_\star
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a |H|^{\rho_\star}
         +
         \sigma |H|^{1+\rho_\star}
      \right).
      \tag{PLSP8}
   \]
   Applying this to each assigned cell \(H_i\) and summing gives \((PLSP2)\).

   If \(X_t\) is maximal \(R_\star\)-separated in \(Y_t\), maximality gives an
   assigned cover by the balls centered at \(X_t\).  Let \(h_x\) be the cell
   sizes.  Since \(\sum_xh_x=|Y_t|\), concavity gives
   \[
      \sum_{x\in X_t}h_x^{\rho_\star}
      \le
      |X_t|^{1-\rho_\star}|Y_t|^{\rho_\star},
      \qquad
      \sum_{x\in X_t}h_x^{1+\rho_\star}
      \le
      |Y_t|^{1+\rho_\star}.
   \]
   Substitution in \((PLSP2)\) proves \((PLSP3)\), and rearranging
   \((PLSP3)\) gives \((PLSP4)\) when the numerator is positive.

   For the dyadic claim, each \(y\) with \(b(y)>0\) has an index \(k\) with
   \(t_k\le b(y)<2t_k\).  Hence
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{0\le j<J_b\\t_j\le b(y)}}t_j
      \ge t_k
      >
      \frac12 b(y).
   \]
   Summing over \(y\in U\) gives
   \[
      \sum_{j=0}^{J_b-1}t_j|Y_j|
      \ge \frac12\sum_{y\in U}b(y)
      =\frac B2 .
   \]
   The pigeonhole principle proves \((PLSP6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Paid-superlevel entropy-energy handoff]
   \label{cor:paid-superlevel-entropy-energy-handoff}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:paid-level-set-spread-packing}, and fix a level \(t>0\) with
   \(Y=Y_t\ne\emptyset\).  Let \(X\subseteq Y\) be a nonempty
   \(R_\star\)-separated center set, for instance a maximal separated set supplied
   by \cref{cor:paid-level-set-spread-packing}, and write \(m_X=|X|\).  Let
   \(0\le\kappa_{x,y}\le1\) be any pair weights on \(X\times Y\), for example
   \[
      \kappa_{x,y}=\Pr[x,y\in U_G]
   \]
   for one spherical or Gaussian bucket law.  Partition \(X\times Y\) into
   finitely many profiles \(\Pi\), and for each profile choose a split
   \[
      \pi=\pi_{\rm lo}\dot\cup\pi_{\rm hi}.
   \]
   Suppose the low part of profile \(\pi\) has certified energy \(I_\pi\):
   \[
      \kappa_{x,y}\le e^{-I_\pi}
      \qquad ((x,y)\in\pi_{\rm lo}),
      \tag{PSEH1}
   \]
   while every high edge has correlation at least \(\underline\theta_\pi\):
   \[
      (x,y)\in\pi_{\rm hi}
      \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
      \ip{x}{y}\ge\underline\theta_\pi .
      \tag{PSEH2}
   \]
   Put \(R_\pi=\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta_\pi)}\), and assume the dense
   verifier may add inherited-activation prefixes of
   \(U\cap B(x,R_\pi)\), \(x\in X\), with prices
   \[
      T_{\pi,x,h}=\psi_{\pi,x}h^{\rho_{\pi,x}},
      \qquad
      S_{\pi,x,h}=\psi_{\pi,x}h^{1+\rho_{\pi,x}},
      \qquad 0<\rho_{\pi,x}<1.
      \tag{PSEH3}
   \]
   For each profile define the center-averaged paid-product contribution
   \[
      W_\pi
      =
      \frac1{m_X}
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\pi}b(y)\kappa_{x,y},
      \tag{PSEH4}
   \]
   and the low paid profile mass
   \[
      L_\pi
      =
      \frac1{m_X}
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\pi_{\rm lo}}b(y).
      \tag{PSEH5}
   \]
   For the high part, put
   \[
      M_{\pi,x}(y)
      =
      \frac1{m_X}b(y)\kappa_{x,y}\mathbf 1\{(x,y)\in\pi_{\rm hi}\}.
      \tag{PSEH6}
   \]
   If \(W_{\pi,{\rm hi}}=\sum_{x,y}M_{\pi,x}(y)>0\), let its positive values
   have dyadic levels \(s_{\pi,j}\) as in \((BPSH4)\), and write
   \[
      U_{\pi,x,j}=\{y\in Y:M_{\pi,x}(y)\ge s_{\pi,j}\}.
      \tag{PSEH7}
   \]
   If \(W_{\pi,{\rm hi}}=0\), interpret the \(j\)-sum below as empty.

   If no inherited-activation prefix from any of these high-correlation star
   containers has positive reduced gain, then
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi} W_\pi
      \le
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi} e^{-I_\pi}L_\pi
      +
      2\sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\sum_{x\in X}\sum_j
      \psi_{\pi,x}
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|U_{\pi,x,j}|^{\rho_{\pi,x}}
         +
         \sigma |U_{\pi,x,j}|^{1+\rho_{\pi,x}}
      \right).
      \tag{PSEH8}
   \]
   Equivalently, if the center-averaged paid-product moment on the left
   exceeds the low-correlation entropy-energy term plus the displayed inherited
   star prices, then one of the inherited prefixes has positive reduced gain.

   If \(t\) is chosen as one of the dyadic paid levels from
   \cref{cor:paid-level-set-spread-packing}, then
   \[
      \sum_{y\in Y}b(y)\ge t|Y|\ge \frac1{2J_b}\sum_{y\in U}b(y),
      \tag{PSEH9}
   \]
   and any maximal \(R_\star\)-separated \(X\subseteq Y\) also satisfies the
   no-cheap-cover spread bound \((PLSP3)\).  Hence the profile entropy used in
   \((PSEH1)\) is supplied by a paid superlevel carrying a logarithmic fraction
   of the actual dual demand, not by an unrelated unweighted packing.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a profile \(\pi\).  Apply
   \cref{cor:bipartite-paid-product-spread-handoff} with center set \(X\), paid
   side \(Y\), center weights \(\lambda_x=1/m_X\), pair weights
   \(\kappa_{x,y}\), and the high-correlation threshold
   \(\underline\theta_\pi\).  The low certificate \((BPSH6)\) may be taken as
   \[
      B_{\rm lo}^{\pi}
      =
      e^{-I_\pi}L_\pi,
   \]
   because of \((PSEH1)\).  The high multiplicities in \((BPSH3)\) are exactly
   \(M_{\pi,x}(y)\), and their dyadic superlevels are the sets
   \(U_{\pi,x,j}\).  Thus \((BPSH7)\) gives
   \[
      W_\pi
      \le
      e^{-I_\pi}L_\pi
      +
      2\sum_{x\in X}\sum_j
      \psi_{\pi,x}
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|U_{\pi,x,j}|^{\rho_{\pi,x}}
         +
         \sigma |U_{\pi,x,j}|^{1+\rho_{\pi,x}}
      \right).
   \]
   Summing over \(\pi\in\Pi\) proves \((PSEH8)\).  The contrapositive is the
   positive-prefix statement.

   Finally, \((PSEH9)\) is \((PLSP6)\) together with the trivial inequality
   \(\sum_{y\in Y}b(y)\ge t|Y|\), and the spread assertion is exactly
   \((PLSP3)\) for a maximal separated center set.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fiberized paid-superlevel exposure]
   \label{cor:fiberized-paid-superlevel-exposure}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:paid-superlevel-entropy-energy-handoff}.  Let
   \(\pi(x,y)\) denote the profile containing \((x,y)\), with
   \(\pi(x,y)_{\rm lo}\) and \(\pi(x,y)_{\rm hi}\) denoting its chosen split
   pieces, and define the low-exposure kernel
   \[
      \mathcal E_{\rm lo}(x,y)
      =
      \begin{cases}
         e^{-I_{\pi(x,y)}} ,
         & (x,y)\in \pi(x,y)_{\rm lo},\\
         0,
         & (x,y)\in \pi(x,y)_{\rm hi}.
      \end{cases}
      \tag{FPSE1}
   \]
   For \(y\in Y\), put
   \[
      \mathsf e_X(y)=\frac1{m_X}\sum_{x\in X}\mathcal E_{\rm lo}(x,y),
      \qquad
      B_Y=\sum_{y\in Y}b(y),
      \qquad
      \overline{\mathsf e}_{b}
      =
      \begin{cases}
         B_Y^{-1}\sum_{y\in Y}b(y)\mathsf e_X(y),& B_Y>0,\\
         0,& B_Y=0 .
      \end{cases}
      \tag{FPSE2}
   \]
   Then the low-correlation term in \((PSEH8)\) is exactly
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}e^{-I_\pi}L_\pi
      =
      \sum_{y\in Y}b(y)\mathsf e_X(y)
      =
      B_Y\overline{\mathsf e}_{b}.
      \tag{FPSE3}
   \]
   Consequently, if no inherited-activation prefix from the high-correlation star
   containers has positive reduced gain, then
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}W_\pi
      \le
      B_Y\overline{\mathsf e}_{b}
      +
      2\sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\sum_{x\in X}\sum_j
      \psi_{\pi,x}
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|U_{\pi,x,j}|^{\rho_{\pi,x}}
         +
         \sigma |U_{\pi,x,j}|^{1+\rho_{\pi,x}}
      \right).
      \tag{FPSE4}
   \]
   In particular, the low-correlation part of the paid-superlevel residual is a
