   single \(b\)-weighted fiber exposure.  It is enough to prove an aggregate
   estimate such as
   \[
      \overline{\mathsf e}_{b}\le\varepsilon_{\rm lo}
      \tag{FPSE5}
   \]
   for the chosen spherical or list-decoding panel; the profile partition then
   disappears from the query-local accounting except through the high-correlation
   inherited-prefix prices.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Expanding \((PSEH5)\) and summing over the disjoint profile partition gives
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}e^{-I_\pi}L_\pi
      =
      \frac1{m_X}
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\pi_{\rm lo}}b(y)e^{-I_\pi}.
   \]
   Since every pair \((x,y)\in X\times Y\) belongs to exactly one profile, this is
   \[
      \sum_{y\in Y}b(y)
      \frac1{m_X}
      \sum_{x\in X}\mathcal E_{\rm lo}(x,y),
   \]
   which is \((FPSE3)\).  Substituting this identity into \((PSEH8)\) proves
   \((FPSE4)\).  The final statement is just the specialization of
   \((FPSE4)\) under \((FPSE5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Uniform-energy paid-fiber screen]
   \label{cor:uniform-energy-paid-fiber-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:fiberized-paid-superlevel-exposure}.  Suppose the low-exposure
   kernel has a pointwise energy floor
   \[
      \mathcal E_{\rm lo}(x,y)\le e^{-\Lambda}
      \qquad(x\in X,\ y\in Y)
      \tag{UEPF1}
   \]
   for some \(\Lambda\ge0\).  Then
   \[
      \overline{\mathsf e}_{b}\le e^{-\Lambda}
      \tag{UEPF2}
   \]
   and, if no inherited-activation prefix from the high-correlation star
   containers has positive reduced gain,
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}W_\pi
      \le
      e^{-\Lambda}B_Y
      +
      2\sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\sum_{x\in X}\sum_j
      \psi_{\pi,x}
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|U_{\pi,x,j}|^{\rho_{\pi,x}}
         +
         \sigma |U_{\pi,x,j}|^{1+\rho_{\pi,x}}
      \right).
      \tag{UEPF3}
   \]
   Thus, unlike the earlier separated-pair entropy-energy screen, the
   low-correlation paid-fiber branch only needs a uniform energy floor.  Choosing
   \(\Lambda=A\log\log n\) makes this term at most
   \((\log n)^{-A}B_Y\), with no additional factor depending on the number of
   profiles or separated centers.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   From \((FPSE2)\) and \((UEPF1)\), \(\mathsf e_X(y)\le e^{-\Lambda}\) for
   every \(y\in Y\).  Averaging with weights \(b(y)\) gives \((UEPF2)\).
   Substitution in \((FPSE4)\) proves \((UEPF3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Gaussian margin paid-fiber screen]
   \label{cor:gaussian-margin-paid-fiber-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:bipartite-paid-product-spread-handoff}, and assume
   \(X\cup Y\subseteq\mathbb S^{D-1}\).  Assume \(X\ne\emptyset\), and write
   \[
      m_X=|X|,
      \qquad
      B_Y=\sum_{y\in Y}b(y).
   \]
   Let
   \[
      U_G=\{u:\ip{G}{u}\ge T\},
      \qquad
      G\sim N(\mu,I_D),
      \qquad
      \kappa_{x,y}=\Pr[x,y\in U_G].
   \]
   Fix \(-1<\theta_0<1\) and \(\Lambda\ge0\), and put
   \[
      s_\Lambda=2\sqrt{(1+\theta_0)\Lambda},
      \qquad
      m_G(u)=T-\ip{\mu}{u}.
      \tag{GMPF1}
   \]
   Define the margin-defect contribution
   \[
      W_{\rm marg}
      =
      \frac1{m_X}
      \sum_{\substack{x\in X,\ y\in Y\\ m_G(x)+m_G(y)<s_\Lambda}}
      b(y)\kappa_{x,y}.
      \tag{GMPF2}
   \]
   On the complementary pairs \(m_G(x)+m_G(y)\ge s_\Lambda\), split
   \[
      \pi_{\rm lo}
      =
      \{(x,y):m_G(x)+m_G(y)\ge s_\Lambda,\ \ip{x}{y}\le\theta_0\},
      \qquad
      \pi_{\rm hi}
      =
      \{(x,y):m_G(x)+m_G(y)\ge s_\Lambda,\ \ip{x}{y}>\theta_0\}.
      \tag{GMPF3}
   \]
   Suppose the dense verifier may add inherited-activation prefixes of
   \(U\cap B(x,R_0)\), \(x\in X\), where
   \[
      R_0=\sqrt{2(1-\theta_0)},
      \tag{GMPF4}
   \]
   with prices
   \[
      T_{x,h}=\psi_0h^{\rho_0},
      \qquad
      S_{x,h}=\psi_0h^{1+\rho_0},
      \qquad 0<\rho_0<1.
      \tag{GMPF5}
   \]
   For high pairs define
   \[
      M_x(y)=
      \frac1{m_X}b(y)\kappa_{x,y}
      \mathbf 1\{m_G(x)+m_G(y)\ge s_\Lambda,\ \ip{x}{y}>\theta_0\}.
      \tag{GMPF6}
   \]
   If the positive values of \(M_x(y)\) have dyadic levels \(u_j\) as in
   \((BPSH4)\), set
   \[
      U_{x,j}=\{y\in Y:M_x(y)\ge u_j\},
      \tag{GMPF7}
   \]
   and interpret the sum over \(j\) as empty when no positive values exist.

   If no inherited-activation prefix from these radius-\(R_0\) star containers
   has positive reduced gain, then
   \[
      \frac1{m_X}\sum_{x\in X}\sum_{y\in Y}b(y)\kappa_{x,y}
      \le
      W_{\rm marg}
      +
      e^{-\Lambda}B_Y
      +
      2\sum_{x\in X}\sum_j
      \psi_0
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|U_{x,j}|^{\rho_0}
         +
         \sigma |U_{x,j}|^{1+\rho_0}
      \right).
      \tag{GMPF8}
   \]
   Consequently, with \(\Lambda=A\log\log n\), the nondefective
   low-correlation part costs only \((\log n)^{-A}B_Y\).  The remaining work is
   explicit: high-correlation nondefective pairs are charged to inherited dense
   prefixes, and only the margin-defect term \(W_{\rm marg}\) still needs a
   separate first-moment, guard, or terminal-scan payment.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   On \(\pi_{\rm lo}\), \((GMPF1)\) and \((GMPF3)\) give
   \[
      m_G(x)+m_G(y)\ge s_\Lambda,
      \qquad
      \ip{x}{y}\le\theta_0.
   \]
   The two-point Gaussian certificate \((TPG3)\)--\((TPG4)\) therefore gives
   \[
      \kappa_{x,y}\le
      \exp\left(-\frac{s_\Lambda^2}{4(1+\theta_0)}\right)
      =
      e^{-\Lambda}.
      \tag{GMPF9}
   \]
   Apply \cref{cor:bipartite-paid-product-spread-handoff} to the nondefective
   profile
   \[
      \pi=\{(x,y):m_G(x)+m_G(y)\ge s_\Lambda\},
   \]
   with center weights \(\lambda_x=1/m_X\), pair weights \(\kappa_{x,y}\), common
   high-correlation threshold \(\theta_0\), and prices \((GMPF5)\).  By
   \((GMPF9)\), the low certificate may be chosen as
   \[
      B_{\rm lo}\le
      e^{-\Lambda}\frac1{m_X}
      \sum_{x\in X}\sum_{y\in Y}b(y)
      =
      e^{-\Lambda}B_Y .
   \]
   The high multiplicities in \((BPSH3)\) are exactly \((GMPF6)\), and their
   dyadic superlevels are \((GMPF7)\).  Thus \((BPSH7)\) bounds the nondefective
   paid-product contribution by the last two terms in \((GMPF8)\).  Adding the
   exact defective contribution \((GMPF2)\) proves the display.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Margin-defect first-moment payment]
   \label{cor:margin-defect-first-moment-payment}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:gaussian-margin-paid-fiber-screen}.  Write
   \[
      p_G(u)=\Pr[u\in U_G],
      \qquad
      \bar p_X=\frac1{m_X}\sum_{x\in X}p_G(x),
      \qquad
      P_Y=\sum_{y\in Y}b(y)p_G(y).
      \tag{MDFM1}
   \]
   For a real threshold \(\gamma\), define the one-sided margin loads
   \[
      \bar p_X^{<\gamma}
      =
      \frac1{m_X}\sum_{\substack{x\in X\\ m_G(x)<\gamma}}p_G(x),
      \qquad
      P_Y^{<\gamma}
      =
      \sum_{\substack{y\in Y\\ m_G(y)<\gamma}}b(y)p_G(y).
      \tag{MDFM2}
   \]
   Then, for every \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\),
   \[
      W_{\rm marg}
      \le
      B_Y\bar p_X^{<\gamma}
      +
      P_Y^{<s_\Lambda-\gamma}.
      \tag{MDFM3}
   \]
   Also, without using the margin condition,
   \[
      W_{\rm marg}
      \le
      \sqrt{B_Y\bar p_XP_Y}.
      \tag{MDFM4}
   \]
   More sharply in the one-sided regime,
   \[
      W_{\rm marg}
      \le
      \min\{B_Y\bar p_X,\ P_Y\}.
      \tag{MDFM5}
   \]
   In particular, if the one-point active loads obey
   \[
      \bar p_X\le\eta_X,
      \qquad
      P_Y\le\eta_YB_Y,
      \tag{MDFM6}
   \]
   then
   \[
      W_{\rm marg}
      \le
      B_Y\min\{\eta_X,\eta_Y,\sqrt{\eta_X\eta_Y}\}.
      \tag{MDFM7}
   \]
   Thus the margin defect left by
   \cref{cor:gaussian-margin-paid-fiber-screen} is paid by ordinary
   first-moment active-load accounting.  If it is not small, the obstruction is
   an explicit one-point active-load obstruction, not a high-correlation dense
   branching obstruction.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let
   \[
      D=\{(x,y)\in X\times Y:m_G(x)+m_G(y)<s_\Lambda\}.
   \]
   For any \(\gamma\), \(D\) is contained in the union of
   \[
      D_X=\{(x,y):m_G(x)<\gamma\},
      \qquad
      D_Y=\{(x,y):m_G(y)<s_\Lambda-\gamma\}.
   \]
   Since \(\kappa_{x,y}=\Pr[x,y\in U_G]\le p_G(x)\) and also
   \(\kappa_{x,y}\le p_G(y)\),
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      W_{\rm marg}
      &\le
      \frac1{m_X}\sum_{(x,y)\in D_X}b(y)p_G(x)
      +
      \frac1{m_X}\sum_{(x,y)\in D_Y}b(y)p_G(y)\\
      &=
      B_Y\bar p_X^{<\gamma}
      +
      P_Y^{<s_\Lambda-\gamma},
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   which proves \((MDFM3)\).

   For the Cauchy bound, use
   \[
      \kappa_{x,y}\le \sqrt{p_G(x)p_G(y)}
   \]
   and discard the restriction to \(D\):
   \[
      W_{\rm marg}
      \le
      \left(\frac1{m_X}\sum_{x\in X}\sqrt{p_G(x)}\right)
      \left(\sum_{y\in Y}b(y)\sqrt{p_G(y)}\right).
   \]
   Cauchy's inequality gives
   \[
      \frac1{m_X}\sum_{x\in X}\sqrt{p_G(x)}
      \le \sqrt{\bar p_X},
      \qquad
      \sum_{y\in Y}b(y)\sqrt{p_G(y)}
      \le \sqrt{B_YP_Y},
   \]
   proving \((MDFM4)\).

   The one-sided bound follows by discarding the margin restriction and using
   either endpoint of \(\kappa_{x,y}\):
   \[
      W_{\rm marg}
      \le
      \frac1{m_X}\sum_{x\in X}\sum_{y\in Y}b(y)p_G(x)
      =
      B_Y\bar p_X,
   \]
   and similarly
   \[
      W_{\rm marg}
      \le
      \frac1{m_X}\sum_{x\in X}\sum_{y\in Y}b(y)p_G(y)
      =
      P_Y .
   \]
   This proves \((MDFM5)\).  Combining \((MDFM4)\), \((MDFM5)\), and
   \((MDFM6)\) proves \((MDFM7)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Gaussian paid-fiber first-moment closure]
   \label{cor:gaussian-paid-fiber-first-moment-closure}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:gaussian-margin-paid-fiber-screen}, and use the notation of
   \cref{cor:margin-defect-first-moment-payment}.  Define the inherited
   high-correlation price
   \[
      \mathsf P_{\rm hi}
      =
      2\sum_{x\in X}\sum_j
      \psi_0
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|U_{x,j}|^{\rho_0}
         +
         \sigma |U_{x,j}|^{1+\rho_0}
      \right).
      \tag{GPFC1}
   \]
   If no inherited-activation prefix from the radius-\(R_0\) star containers has
   positive reduced gain, then, for every \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\),
   \[
      \frac1{m_X}\sum_{x\in X}\sum_{y\in Y}b(y)\kappa_{x,y}
      \le
      e^{-\Lambda}B_Y
      +
      B_Y\bar p_X^{<\gamma}
      +
      P_Y^{<s_\Lambda-\gamma}
      +
      \mathsf P_{\rm hi}.
      \tag{GPFC2}
   \]
   Also,
   \[
      \frac1{m_X}\sum_{x\in X}\sum_{y\in Y}b(y)\kappa_{x,y}
      \le
      e^{-\Lambda}B_Y
      +
      \sqrt{B_Y\bar p_XP_Y}
      +
      \mathsf P_{\rm hi}.
      \tag{GPFC3}
   \]
   More sharply,
   \[
      \frac1{m_X}\sum_{x\in X}\sum_{y\in Y}b(y)\kappa_{x,y}
      \le
      e^{-\Lambda}B_Y
      +
      \min\{B_Y\bar p_X,\ P_Y\}
      +
      \mathsf P_{\rm hi}.
      \tag{GPFC4}
   \]
   Consequently, if
   \[
      \bar p_X\le\eta_X,
      \qquad
      P_Y\le\eta_YB_Y,
      \tag{GPFC5}
   \]
   then
   \[
      \frac1{m_X}\sum_{x\in X}\sum_{y\in Y}b(y)\kappa_{x,y}
      \le
      B_Y\left(e^{-\Lambda}+\min\{\eta_X,\eta_Y,\sqrt{\eta_X\eta_Y}\}\right)
      +
      \mathsf P_{\rm hi}.
      \tag{GPFC6}
   \]
   In particular, taking \(\Lambda=A\log\log n\) and
   \(\min\{\eta_X,\eta_Y,\sqrt{\eta_X\eta_Y}\}\le(\log n)^{-A}\)
   makes the non-high-correlation part at most
   \(2B_Y(\log n)^{-A}\).  Thus this branch has no profile-entropy or
   layer-cake loss: after inherited dense-prefix prices are charged, it is closed
   by the same one-point active-load estimates already used for query work.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Combine \((GMPF8)\) with the truncated margin-defect bound \((MDFM3)\) to get
   \((GPFC2)\), with the Cauchy margin-defect bound \((MDFM4)\) to get
   \((GPFC3)\), and with the one-sided margin-defect bound \((MDFM5)\) to get
   \((GPFC4)\).  Substituting \((GPFC5)\) into \((GPFC3)\) and \((GPFC4)\)
   proves \((GPFC6)\).
   The final statement is the displayed parameter choice.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Total-load Gaussian paid-fiber separator]
   \label{cor:total-load-gaussian-paid-fiber-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:gaussian-paid-fiber-first-moment-closure}, assume \(B_Y>0\), and
   write
   \[
      A_G=
      \frac1{m_X}\sum_{x\in X}\sum_{y\in Y}b(y)\kappa_{x,y}.
      \tag{GTLS1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      A_G
      >
      e^{-\Lambda}B_Y
      +
      \min\{B_Y\bar p_X,\ P_Y\}
      +
      \mathsf P_{\rm hi},
      \tag{GTLS2}
   \]
   then some inherited-activation prefix from one of the radius-\(R_0\) star
   containers has positive reduced gain.

   In particular, suppose that
   \[
      A_G\ge aB_Y,
      \qquad
      \mathsf P_{\rm hi}\le\xi A_G
      \qquad(a>0,\ 0\le\xi<1),
      \tag{GTLS3}
   \]
   and put
   \[
      \delta=(1-\xi)a-e^{-\Lambda}.
      \tag{GTLS4}
   \]
   If \(\delta>0\) and either
   \[
      \bar p_X<\delta
      \qquad\text{or}\qquad
      P_Y<\delta B_Y,
      \tag{GTLS5}
   \]
   then an inherited-activation prefix has positive reduced gain.

   Thus the algorithmic Gaussian paid-fiber screen only needs two total
   first-moment load monitors, \(\bar p_X\) and \(P_Y/B_Y\).  The optimized
   margin split below is a diagnostic strengthening; it is not a separate
   branch needed by the retained data structure when the ordinary active-load
   certificate is available.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If no inherited-activation prefix has positive reduced gain, then
   \cref{cor:gaussian-paid-fiber-first-moment-closure}, specifically
   \((GPFC4)\), gives the reverse of \((GTLS2)\).  Hence \((GTLS2)\) forces a
   positive prefix.

   Under \((GTLS3)\), \(B_Y\le A_G/a\).  If \((GTLS5)\) holds, then
   \[
      e^{-\Lambda}B_Y+\min\{B_Y\bar p_X,\ P_Y\}+\mathsf P_{\rm hi}
      <
      \bigl(e^{-\Lambda}+\delta\bigr)B_Y+\xi A_G
      =
      (1-\xi)aB_Y+\xi A_G
      \le A_G .
   \]
   Therefore \((GTLS2)\) holds, and the first part applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Weighted Gaussian paid-fiber separator]
   \label{cor:weighted-gaussian-paid-fiber-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:bipartite-paid-product-spread-handoff}, and assume
   \(X\cup Y\subseteq\mathbb S^{D-1}\).  Let
   \((\lambda_x)_{x\in X}\) be a probability law on \(X\).  Let
   \[
      U_G=\{u:\ip{G}{u}\ge T\},
      \qquad
      G\sim N(\mu,I_D),
      \qquad
      \kappa_{x,y}=\Pr[x,y\in U_G],
   \]
   and put
   \[
      B_Y=\sum_{y\in Y}b(y),
      \qquad
      A_\lambda=\sum_{x\in X}\lambda_x\sum_{y\in Y}b(y)\kappa_{x,y}.
      \tag{WGFS1}
   \]
   Fix \(-1<\theta_0<1\) and \(\Lambda\ge0\), and define
   \[
      s_\Lambda=2\sqrt{(1+\theta_0)\Lambda},
      \qquad
      m_G(u)=T-\ip{\mu}{u},
      \qquad
      R_0=\sqrt{2(1-\theta_0)} .
      \tag{WGFS2}
   \]
   Suppose the dense verifier may add inherited-activation prefixes of
   \(U\cap B(x,R_0)\), \(x\in X\), with common prices
   \[
      T_{x,h}=\psi_0h^{\rho_0},
      \qquad
      S_{x,h}=\psi_0h^{1+\rho_0},
      \qquad 0<\rho_0<1.
      \tag{WGFS3}
   \]
   For high nondefective pairs define
   \[
      M_x^\lambda(y)=
      \lambda_x b(y)\kappa_{x,y}
      \mathbf 1\{m_G(x)+m_G(y)\ge s_\Lambda,\ \ip{x}{y}>\theta_0\}.
      \tag{WGFS4}
   \]
   Let \(U^\lambda_{x,j}\) be the dyadic superlevels of the positive values of
   \(M_x^\lambda(y)\), as in \((BPSH4)\)--\((BPSH5)\), and interpret the sum over
   \(j\) as empty when no positive values occur.  Put
   \[
      \mathsf P_{\rm hi}^\lambda
      =
      2\sum_{x\in X}\sum_j
      \psi_0
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|U^\lambda_{x,j}|^{\rho_0}
         +
         \sigma |U^\lambda_{x,j}|^{1+\rho_0}
      \right).
      \tag{WGFS5}
   \]
   Finally define one-point active loads
   \[
      p_G(u)=\Pr[u\in U_G],
      \qquad
      \bar p_\lambda=\sum_{x\in X}\lambda_xp_G(x),
      \qquad
      P_Y=\sum_{y\in Y}b(y)p_G(y),
      \tag{WGFS6}
   \]
   and for \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\),
   \[
      \bar p_\lambda^{<\gamma}
      =
      \sum_{\substack{x\in X\\m_G(x)<\gamma}}\lambda_xp_G(x),
      \qquad
      P_Y^{<\gamma}
      =
      \sum_{\substack{y\in Y\\m_G(y)<\gamma}}b(y)p_G(y).
      \tag{WGFS7}
   \]

   If no inherited-activation prefix from the radius-\(R_0\) star containers has
   positive reduced gain, then, for every \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\),
   \[
      A_\lambda
      \le
      e^{-\Lambda}B_Y
      +
      B_Y\bar p_\lambda^{<\gamma}
      +
      P_Y^{<s_\Lambda-\gamma}
      +
      \mathsf P_{\rm hi}^\lambda ,
      \tag{WGFS8}
   \]
   and in particular
   \[
      A_\lambda
      \le
      e^{-\Lambda}B_Y
      +
      \min\{B_Y\bar p_\lambda,\ P_Y\}
      +
      \mathsf P_{\rm hi}^\lambda .
      \tag{WGFS9}
   \]

   Consequently, assume \(B_Y>0\) and suppose
   \[
      A_\lambda\ge aB_Y,
      \qquad
      \mathsf P_{\rm hi}^\lambda\le\xi A_\lambda
      \qquad(a>0,\ 0\le\xi<1),
      \tag{WGFS10}
   \]
   and put
   \[
      \delta=(1-\xi)a-e^{-\Lambda}.
      \tag{WGFS11}
   \]
   If \(\delta>0\) and either
   \[
      \bar p_\lambda<\delta
      \qquad\text{or}\qquad
      P_Y<\delta B_Y,
      \tag{WGFS12}
   \]
   then an inherited-activation prefix has positive reduced gain.

   Thus the high-spread branch may feed the Gaussian paid-fiber separator with
   the Renyi center law from
   \cref{cor:inherited-activation-renyi-center-law}.  No dyadic flattening of the
   center law is needed unless a later geometric estimate requires uniform
   centers.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Define the weighted margin-defect contribution
   \[
      W_{\rm marg}^\lambda
      =
      \sum_{\substack{x\in X,\ y\in Y\\m_G(x)+m_G(y)<s_\Lambda}}
      \lambda_x b(y)\kappa_{x,y}.
      \tag{WGFS13}
   \]
   On the nondefective profile
   \[
      \pi=\{(x,y):m_G(x)+m_G(y)\ge s_\Lambda\},
   \]
   split into low and high parts by the threshold \(\ip{x}{y}\le\theta_0\).  On
   the low part the two-point Gaussian certificate gives, exactly as in
   \((GMPF9)\),
   \[
      \kappa_{x,y}\le e^{-\Lambda}.
   \]
   Apply \cref{cor:bipartite-paid-product-spread-handoff} to this profile with
   center weights \(\lambda_x\), pair weights \(\kappa_{x,y}\), threshold
   \(\theta_0\), and prices \((WGFS3)\).  Since \(\sum_x\lambda_x=1\), the low
   certificate is bounded by
   \[
      e^{-\Lambda}\sum_x\lambda_x\sum_y b(y)=e^{-\Lambda}B_Y,
   \]
   and the high superlevels are exactly \(U^\lambda_{x,j}\).  Therefore, if no
   inherited prefix is positive,
   \[
      A_\lambda
      \le
      W_{\rm marg}^\lambda+e^{-\Lambda}B_Y+\mathsf P_{\rm hi}^\lambda .
      \tag{WGFS14}
   \]

   For a split \(\gamma\), the defect set in \((WGFS13)\) is contained in the
   union of
   \[
      \{(x,y):m_G(x)<\gamma\}
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      \{(x,y):m_G(y)<s_\Lambda-\gamma\}.
   \]
   Using \(\kappa_{x,y}\le p_G(x)\) on the first set and
   \(\kappa_{x,y}\le p_G(y)\) on the second gives
   \[
      W_{\rm marg}^\lambda
      \le
      B_Y\bar p_\lambda^{<\gamma}+P_Y^{<s_\Lambda-\gamma}.
   \]
   Substituting this into \((WGFS14)\) proves \((WGFS8)\).

   Discarding the margin restriction and using either endpoint gives
   \[
      W_{\rm marg}^\lambda
      \le
      B_Y\bar p_\lambda,
      \qquad
      W_{\rm marg}^\lambda
      \le
      P_Y,
   \]
   because \(\sum_x\lambda_x=1\).  This proves \((WGFS9)\).

   Under \((WGFS10)\), if \((WGFS12)\) holds then
   \[
      e^{-\Lambda}B_Y+\min\{B_Y\bar p_\lambda,\ P_Y\}
      +\mathsf P_{\rm hi}^\lambda
      <
      \bigl(e^{-\Lambda}+\delta\bigr)B_Y+\xi A_\lambda
      =
      (1-\xi)aB_Y+\xi A_\lambda
      \le A_\lambda .
   \]
   Thus \((WGFS9)\) would be violated if no prefix were positive.  Hence some
   inherited-activation prefix has positive reduced gain.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Weighted margin-tail obstruction]
   \label{cor:weighted-margin-tail-obstruction}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:weighted-gaussian-paid-fiber-separator}, and assume \(B_Y>0\).
   Define the optimized weighted margin-tail defect
   \[
      \mathsf M_\lambda
      =
      \inf_{\gamma\in\mathbb R}
      \left(
         B_Y\bar p_\lambda^{<\gamma}
         +
         P_Y^{<s_\Lambda-\gamma}
      \right).
      \tag{WMTO1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      A_\lambda>
      e^{-\Lambda}B_Y+\mathsf M_\lambda+\mathsf P_{\rm hi}^\lambda,
      \tag{WMTO2}
   \]
   then some inherited-activation prefix from one of the radius-\(R_0\) star
   containers has positive reduced gain.

   Conversely, suppose no inherited-activation prefix has positive reduced gain,
   and suppose
   \[
      A_\lambda\ge aB_Y,
      \qquad
      \mathsf P_{\rm hi}^\lambda\le\xi A_\lambda
      \qquad(a>0,\ 0\le\xi<1).
      \tag{WMTO3}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \mathsf M_\lambda
      \ge
      \bigl((1-\xi)a-e^{-\Lambda}\bigr)B_Y .
      \tag{WMTO4}
   \]
   Since
   \[
      \mathsf M_\lambda\le\min\{B_Y\bar p_\lambda,\ P_Y\},
      \tag{WMTO5}
   \]
   a surviving weighted Gaussian paid-fiber residual with
   \(\delta=(1-\xi)a-e^{-\Lambda}>0\) must satisfy
   \[
      \bar p_\lambda\ge\delta,
      \qquad
      P_Y\ge\delta B_Y .
      \tag{WMTO6}
   \]
   Thus, after the weighted paid-product mass and inherited high-correlation
   price are controlled, the only surviving obstruction is simultaneous total
   active load on the Renyi center law and on the paid side.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((WMTO2)\) holds, choose \(\gamma\) so that
   \[
      B_Y\bar p_\lambda^{<\gamma}
      +
      P_Y^{<s_\Lambda-\gamma}
      <
      A_\lambda-e^{-\Lambda}B_Y-\mathsf P_{\rm hi}^\lambda .
   \]
   Then \((WGFS8)\) would be violated unless a positive inherited prefix exists.

   Conversely, if no prefix is positive, \((WGFS8)\) holds for every \(\gamma\).
   Taking the infimum over \(\gamma\), using
   \(A_\lambda-\mathsf P_{\rm hi}^\lambda\ge(1-\xi)A_\lambda\), and then
   \(A_\lambda\ge aB_Y\), gives \((WMTO4)\).

   To prove \((WMTO5)\), choose \(\gamma\) larger than every margin \(m_G(x)\) on
   \(X\) and also so large that \(s_\Lambda-\gamma\) is smaller than every margin
   on \(Y\).  Then \(P_Y^{<s_\Lambda-\gamma}=0\), giving
   \(\mathsf M_\lambda\le B_Y\bar p_\lambda\).  Choosing \(\gamma\) smaller than
   every margin on \(X\) and also so small that \(s_\Lambda-\gamma\) is larger
   than every margin on \(Y\), gives \(\mathsf M_\lambda\le P_Y\).  Combining
   \((WMTO4)\), \((WMTO5)\), and \(B_Y>0\) proves \((WMTO6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Transport Gaussian paid-fiber separator]
   \label{cor:transport-gaussian-paid-fiber-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:bipartite-paid-transport-spread-handoff}, and assume
   \(X\cup Y\subseteq\mathbb S^{D-1}\).  Let \(w_{x,y}\ge0\) be paid transport
   weights satisfying \(w_{x,y}\le b(y)\), and put
   \[
      B_w=\sum_{x\in X}\sum_{y\in Y}w_{x,y}.
      \tag{TGFS1}
   \]
   Assume \(B_w>0\).  Let
   \[
      U_G=\{u:\ip{G}{u}\ge T\},
      \qquad
      G\sim N(\mu,I_D),
      \qquad
      \kappa_{x,y}=\Pr[x,y\in U_G],
   \]
   and define the transported paid-product moment
   \[
      A_w=\sum_{x\in X}\sum_{y\in Y}w_{x,y}\kappa_{x,y}.
      \tag{TGFS2}
   \]
   Fix \(-1<\theta_0<1\) and \(\Lambda\ge0\), and put
   \[
      s_\Lambda=2\sqrt{(1+\theta_0)\Lambda},
      \qquad
      m_G(u)=T-\ip{\mu}{u},
      \qquad
      R_0=\sqrt{2(1-\theta_0)} .
      \tag{TGFS3}
   \]
   Suppose the dense verifier may add inherited-activation prefixes of
   \(U\cap B(x,R_0)\), \(x\in X\), with common prices
   \[
      T_{x,h}=\psi_0h^{\rho_0},
      \qquad
      S_{x,h}=\psi_0h^{1+\rho_0},
      \qquad 0<\rho_0<1.
      \tag{TGFS4}
   \]
   For high nondefective transported pairs define
   \[
      M_x^w(y)=
      w_{x,y}\kappa_{x,y}
      \mathbf 1\{m_G(x)+m_G(y)\ge s_\Lambda,\ \ip{x}{y}>\theta_0\}.
      \tag{TGFS5}
   \]
   Let \(U^w_{x,j}\) be the dyadic superlevels of the positive values of
   \(M_x^w(y)\), and interpret the sum over \(j\) as empty when no positive
   values occur.  Put
   \[
      \mathsf P_{\rm hi}^w
      =
      2\sum_{x\in X}\sum_j
      \psi_0
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a|U^w_{x,j}|^{\rho_0}
         +
         \sigma |U^w_{x,j}|^{1+\rho_0}
      \right).
      \tag{TGFS6}
   \]
   Finally define transported one-point active loads
   \[
      p_G(u)=\Pr[u\in U_G],
      \qquad
      P_X^w=\sum_{x,y}w_{x,y}p_G(x),
      \qquad
      P_Y^w=\sum_{x,y}w_{x,y}p_G(y),
      \tag{TGFS7}
   \]
   and, for \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\),
   \[
      P_X^{w,<\gamma}
      =
      \sum_{\substack{x,y\\m_G(x)<\gamma}}w_{x,y}p_G(x),
      \qquad
      P_Y^{w,<\gamma}
      =
      \sum_{\substack{x,y\\m_G(y)<\gamma}}w_{x,y}p_G(y).
      \tag{TGFS8}
   \]

   If no inherited-activation prefix from the radius-\(R_0\) star containers has
   positive reduced gain, then, for every \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\),
   \[
      A_w
      \le
      e^{-\Lambda}B_w
      +
      P_X^{w,<\gamma}
      +
      P_Y^{w,<s_\Lambda-\gamma}
      +
      \mathsf P_{\rm hi}^w ,
      \tag{TGFS9}
   \]
   and in particular
   \[
      A_w
      \le
      e^{-\Lambda}B_w
      +
      \min\{P_X^w,\ P_Y^w\}
      +
      \mathsf P_{\rm hi}^w .
      \tag{TGFS10}
   \]

   Consequently, suppose
   \[
      A_w\ge aB_w,
      \qquad
      \mathsf P_{\rm hi}^w\le\xi A_w
      \qquad(a>0,\ 0\le\xi<1),
      \tag{TGFS11}
   \]
   and put \(\delta=(1-\xi)a-e^{-\Lambda}\).  If \(\delta>0\) and either
   \[
      P_X^w<\delta B_w
      \qquad\text{or}\qquad
      P_Y^w<\delta B_w,
      \tag{TGFS12}
   \]
   then an inherited-activation prefix has positive reduced gain.

   Finally, if the transport is assigned by a map \(c:Y\to X\),
   \(w_{c(y),y}=b(y)\), \(w_{x,y}=0\) for \(x\ne c(y)\), and
   \[
      \kappa_{c(y),y}\ge a
      \qquad(y\in Y,\ b(y)>0),
      \tag{TGFS13}
   \]
   then \(A_w\ge aB_w\).  Thus the paid-product lower bound can be supplied by a
   local assigned-cover geometry, without first forcing the center and paid
   measures into an independent product law.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Define the transported margin-defect contribution
   \[
      W_{\rm marg}^w
      =
      \sum_{\substack{x,y\\m_G(x)+m_G(y)<s_\Lambda}}
      w_{x,y}\kappa_{x,y}.
      \tag{TGFS14}
   \]
   On the nondefective profile
   \[
      \pi=\{(x,y):m_G(x)+m_G(y)\ge s_\Lambda\},
   \]
   split into low and high parts by the threshold \(\ip{x}{y}\le\theta_0\).  On
   the low part, the same two-point Gaussian certificate used in \((WGFS14)\)
   gives \(\kappa_{x,y}\le e^{-\Lambda}\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:bipartite-paid-transport-spread-handoff} to the high part with
   transport weights \(w_{x,y}\), pair weights \(\kappa_{x,y}\), threshold
   \(\theta_0\), and prices \((TGFS4)\), we get, if no inherited prefix is
   positive,
   \[
      A_w
      \le
      W_{\rm marg}^w+e^{-\Lambda}B_w+\mathsf P_{\rm hi}^w .
      \tag{TGFS15}
   \]

   For a split \(\gamma\), the defect set is contained in the union of
   \[
      \{(x,y):m_G(x)<\gamma\}
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      \{(x,y):m_G(y)<s_\Lambda-\gamma\}.
   \]
   Using \(\kappa_{x,y}\le p_G(x)\) on the first set and
   \(\kappa_{x,y}\le p_G(y)\) on the second gives
   \[
      W_{\rm marg}^w
      \le
      P_X^{w,<\gamma}+P_Y^{w,<s_\Lambda-\gamma}.
   \]
   Substituting into \((TGFS15)\) proves \((TGFS9)\).  Discarding the margin
   restrictions and using either endpoint gives
   \(W_{\rm marg}^w\le P_X^w\) and \(W_{\rm marg}^w\le P_Y^w\), proving
   \((TGFS10)\).

   Under \((TGFS11)\), if \((TGFS12)\) holds then
   \[
      e^{-\Lambda}B_w+\min\{P_X^w,\ P_Y^w\}+\mathsf P_{\rm hi}^w
      <
      \bigl(e^{-\Lambda}+\delta\bigr)B_w+\xi A_w
      =
      (1-\xi)aB_w+\xi A_w
      \le A_w .
   \]
   This violates \((TGFS10)\) unless a positive inherited prefix exists.

   The assigned-transport lower bound is immediate:
   \[
      A_w
      =
      \sum_{y\in Y}b(y)\kappa_{c(y),y}
      \ge
      a\sum_{y\in Y}b(y)
      =
      aB_w .
   \]
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Assigned Gaussian transport lower bound]
   \label{cor:assigned-gaussian-transport-lower-bound}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:transport-gaussian-paid-fiber-separator}.  Suppose the transport is
   assigned by a map \(c:Y\to X\):
   \[
      w_{c(y),y}=b(y),
      \qquad
      w_{x,y}=0\quad(x\ne c(y)).
      \tag{AGTL1}
   \]
   If, for parameters \(0<\theta_-\le1\) and \(M\ge0\),
   \[
      \ip{c(y)}{y}\ge\theta_-,
      \qquad
      m_G(c(y))\le M,
      \qquad
      m_G(y)\le M
      \qquad(y\in Y,\ b(y)>0),
      \tag{AGTL2}
   \]
   then
   \[
      A_w\ge a_{\theta_-,M}B_w,
      \qquad
      a_{\theta_-,M}
      =
      \frac14\,
      \overline\Phi\!\left(\frac{M}{\sqrt{\theta_-}}\right).
      \tag{AGTL3}
   \]
   Consequently this assigned cover supplies the paid-product lower-bound
   hypothesis \((TGFS11)\) with \(a=a_{\theta_-,M}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{lem:positive-correlation-gaussian-cap-lower}, every assigned edge
   with \(b(y)>0\) satisfies
   \[
      \kappa_{c(y),y}\ge a_{\theta_-,M}.
   \]
   The final assigned-transport clause of
   \cref{cor:transport-gaussian-paid-fiber-separator} gives \((AGTL3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Upper-margin assigned transport has polylog normalized load]
   \label{cor:upper-margin-assigned-transport-load}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:assigned-gaussian-transport-lower-bound}.  Write
   \[
      \overline\Phi(t)=\Pr[Z\ge t],
      \qquad Z\sim N(0,1).
   \]
   Suppose that, for parameters \(0<\theta_-\le1\) and \(M\ge0\), every assigned
   paid edge satisfies
   \[
      \ip{c(y)}{y}\ge\theta_-,
      \qquad
      m_G(c(y)),m_G(y)\le M
      \qquad(y\in Y,\ b(y)>0).
      \tag{UATL1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      A_w\ge a_{\theta_-,M}B_w,
      \qquad
      a_{\theta_-,M}
      =
      \frac14\overline\Phi\!\left(\frac{M}{\sqrt{\theta_-}}\right),
      \tag{UATL2}
   \]
   while the transported endpoint active loads obey
   \[
      P_X^w\le B_w,
      \qquad
      P_Y^w\le B_w.
      \tag{UATL3}
   \]
   Hence the success-normalized endpoint loads satisfy
   \[
      \frac{P_X^w}{A_w},
      \frac{P_Y^w}{A_w}
      \le
      \frac{4}{\overline\Phi(M/\sqrt{\theta_-})}
      \le
      C_{\theta_-}(1+M)
      \exp\!\left(\frac{M^2}{2\theta_-}\right).
      \tag{UATL4}
   \]
   In particular, if \(M^2\le C\log\log n\), the normalized endpoint loads are
   \(\log^{O_{\theta_-,C}(1)}n\).

   If, more sharply, the same assigned edges also satisfy
   \(m_G(c(y)),m_G(y)\ge M_-\) for some \(0\le M_-\le M\), then
   \[
      P_X^w,P_Y^w\le\overline\Phi(M_-)B_w,
      \qquad
      \frac{P_X^w}{A_w},\frac{P_Y^w}{A_w}
      \le
      4\frac{\overline\Phi(M_-)}
              {\overline\Phi(M/\sqrt{\theta_-})}.
      \tag{UATL5}
   \]

   Thus the assigned Gaussian branch only needs an upper margin cutoff, not a
   genuine two-sided margin window, to obtain polylogarithmic
   success-normalized query load.  The remaining geometric task is to produce
   upper-margin assigned transports with chargeable shared storage, or else
   expose a finite-prefix dense repair.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The upper margin bound in \((UATL1)\) gives \((UATL2)\) by
   \cref{cor:assigned-gaussian-transport-lower-bound}.  Since one-point
   probabilities are at most one, summing over assigned transport mass gives
   \((UATL3)\).  Dividing \((UATL3)\) by \((UATL2)\) gives the first inequality
   in \((UATL4)\).  The second inequality follows from
   \cref{lem:gaussian-tail-ratio} with \(u=0\) and
   \(v=M/\sqrt{\theta_-}\), absorbing universal constants into
   \(C_{\theta_-}\).

   Under the additional lower margin condition, monotonicity of
   \(\overline\Phi\) gives, for every assigned edge,
   \[
      p_G(c(y))=\overline\Phi(m_G(c(y)))\le\overline\Phi(M_-),
      \qquad
      p_G(y)=\overline\Phi(m_G(y))\le\overline\Phi(M_-).
   \]
   Summing and dividing by \((UATL2)\) proves \((UATL5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Bounded-margin truncation alternative]
   \label{cor:bounded-margin-assigned-truncation}
   Work in the assigned-transport setting of
   \cref{cor:transport-gaussian-paid-fiber-separator}.  Suppose the transport is
   assigned by \(c:Y\to X\) and satisfies
   \[
      \ip{c(y)}{y}\ge\theta_-
      \qquad(y\in Y,\ b(y)>0)
      \tag{BMAT1}
   \]
   for some \(0<\theta_-\le1\).  For \(M\ge0\), define the upper-margin
   subtransport
   \[
      Y_{\le M}
      =
      \{y\in Y:b(y)>0,\ m_G(c(y))\le M,\ m_G(y)\le M\},
      \qquad
      B_{\le M}=\sum_{y\in Y_{\le M}}b(y).
      \tag{BMAT2}
   \]
   If \(B_{\le M}>0\), let \(A_{\le M}\), \(P_{X,\le M}\), and \(P_{Y,\le M}\)
   denote the transported hit moment and endpoint active loads
   \((TGFS2)\), \((TGFS7)\) computed after restricting \(w\) to
   \(Y_{\le M}\).  Then
   \[
      A_{\le M}
      \ge
      \frac14\overline\Phi\!\left(\frac{M}{\sqrt{\theta_-}}\right)B_{\le M},
      \tag{BMAT3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \frac{P_{X,\le M}}{A_{\le M}},
      \frac{P_{Y,\le M}}{A_{\le M}}
      \le
      \frac{4}{\overline\Phi(M/\sqrt{\theta_-})}.
      \tag{BMAT4}
   \]
   Consequently, if \(M^2\le C\log\log n\) and
   \(B_{\le M}\ge \zeta B_w\), then this restricted assigned transport supplies
   hit mass at least
   \[
      \frac{\zeta}{4}
      \overline\Phi\!\left(\frac{M}{\sqrt{\theta_-}}\right)B_w
      \tag{BMAT5}
   \]
   with only \(\log^{O_{\theta_-,C}(1)}n\) success-normalized endpoint load.

   Otherwise, if \(B_{\le M}<\zeta B_w\), then the complementary paid mass
   \[
      B_{>M}=B_w-B_{\le M}
      \tag{BMAT6}
   \]
   is larger than \((1-\zeta)B_w\) and is supported on the explicit high-margin
   obstruction
   \[
      m_G(c(y))>M
      \quad\text{or}\quad
      m_G(y)>M .
      \tag{BMAT7}
   \]
   Thus failure to find an inverse-polylogarithmic amount of upper-margin
   assigned transport is no longer an amorphous active-load obstruction: almost
   all paid mass is certified to lie behind a high Gaussian margin on the center
   side or on the paid side.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Restricting an assigned transport preserves the domination
   \(w_{x,y}\le b(y)\), the assignment form, and the correlation lower bound.
   Applying \cref{cor:upper-margin-assigned-transport-load} to the restricted
   transport gives \((BMAT3)\)--\((BMAT4)\).  The displayed hit lower bound
   \((BMAT5)\) follows from \(B_{\le M}\ge\zeta B_w\), and the polylogarithmic
   load statement follows from \((UATL4)\).

   If \(B_{\le M}<\zeta B_w\), then \(B_{>M}>(1-\zeta)B_w\) by definition.
   The complement of \(Y_{\le M}\) is exactly the set of assigned paid edges for
   which at least one of the two upper-margin inequalities fails, proving
   \((BMAT7)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[High-margin assigned residual is finite-prefix or spread]
   \label{cor:high-margin-assigned-prefix-spread}
   Work in a finite filter-cover dual.  Let \(Y\subseteq P\) carry paid degrees
   \(b(y)\ge0\), let \(X\subseteq P\) be assigned centers, and let
   \(c:Y\to X\).  Let \(a\) be the inherited activation whose query price is
   \[
      \mathsf T_a=\sum_q \tau_q a(q).
      \tag{HMAP0}
   \]
   Fix \(M\ge0\) and a Gaussian cap margin \(m_G\).  Define the high-margin
   assigned residual
   \[
      Y_{>M}
      =
      \{y\in Y:b(y)>0,\ m_G(c(y))>M\ \text{or}\ m_G(y)>M\},
      \qquad
      B_{>M}=\sum_{y\in Y_{>M}}b(y).
      \tag{HMAP1}
   \]
   Suppose that for every \(x\in X\) the verifier may add every
   inherited-activation prefix of a certified cell container \(W_x\supseteq
   \{y\in Y:c(y)=x\}\), with prices
   \[
      T_{x,h}=\psi_xh^{\rho_x},
      \qquad
      S_{x,h}=\psi_xh^{1+\rho_x},
      \qquad 0<\rho_x<1 .
      \tag{HMAP2}
   \]
   A prefix \(U\subseteq W_x\) of size \(h\) has positive reduced gain when
   \[
      \sum_{y\in U}b(y)
      >
      \psi_x
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a h^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma h^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{HMAP3}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      H_x=\{y\in Y_{>M}:c(y)=x\},
      \qquad
      h_x=|H_x|.
      \tag{HMAP4}
   \]
   If no such inherited-activation prefix has positive reduced gain, then
   \[
      B_{>M}
      \le
      \sum_{x:h_x>0}
      \psi_x
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a h_x^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma h_x^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{HMAP5}
   \]
   Equivalently, a strict reverse inequality in \((HMAP5)\) exposes one
   positive inherited finite-prefix repair.

   In particular, if all high-margin cells use a common exponent \(\rho\) and
   price factor at most \(\psi_\star\), and if
   \[
      B_{>M}
      >
      \psi_\star
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a\sum_xh_x^\rho
         +
         \sigma\sum_xh_x^{1+\rho}
      \right),
      \tag{HMAP6}
   \]
   then a positive inherited prefix exists.  Thus a surviving high-margin
   assigned residual must have radius-discounted Renyi spread large enough to
   pay for its own inherited prefixes; it is no longer a separate Gaussian
   active-load obstruction.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed \(x\), sort the points of \(W_x\) by decreasing paid degree
   \(b(y)\).  If no inherited-activation prefix in \(W_x\) is positive, then
   every top \(h\)-prefix satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{i\le h}b(y_i)
      \le
      \psi_x\left(
         \mathsf T_a h^{\rho_x}+\sigma h^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{HMAP7}
   \]
   The top \(h_x\)-prefix dominates the particular subset \(H_x\).  Hence
   \[
      \sum_{y\in H_x}b(y)
      \le
      \psi_x
      \left(
         \mathsf T_a h_x^{\rho_x}+\sigma h_x^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
   \]
   Summing over \(x\) proves \((HMAP5)\).  The reverse implication is its
   contrapositive, and \((HMAP6)\) is the common-price specialization.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Assigned Gaussian transport trichotomy]
   \label{cor:assigned-gaussian-transport-trichotomy}
   Work in the assigned-transport setting of
   \cref{cor:bounded-margin-assigned-truncation}.  Thus
   \(w_{c(y),y}=b(y)\), \(w_{x,y}=0\) for \(x\ne c(y)\), \(B_w=\sum_yb(y)>0\),
   and
   \[
      \ip{c(y)}{y}\ge\theta_-
      \qquad(y\in Y,\ b(y)>0).
      \tag{AGTC1}
   \]
   Fix \(0<\zeta<1\), \(M\ge0\), and let \(a\) be the inherited activation with
   query price
   \[
      \mathsf T_a=\sum_q \tau_q a(q).
      \tag{AGTC2}
   \]
   Assume that for every assigned center \(x\) the dense verifier may add
   inherited-activation prefixes of a certified cell container
   \(W_x\supseteq\{y\in Y:c(y)=x\}\), with prices
   \[
      T_{x,h}=\psi_xh^{\rho_x},
      \qquad
      S_{x,h}=\psi_xh^{1+\rho_x},
      \qquad 0<\rho_x<1 .
      \tag{AGTC3}
   \]
   On the unit sphere one may take
   \(W_x=P\cap B(x,\sqrt{2(1-\theta_-)})\) whenever those point-centered
   containers are certified.  Write
   \(\overline\Phi(t)=\Pr[Z\ge t]\), \(Z\sim N(0,1)\).

   Then at least one of the following alternatives holds.

   \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
      \item The upper-margin subtransport
      \[
         Y_{\le M}=\{y:b(y)>0,\ m_G(c(y))\le M,\ m_G(y)\le M\}
      \]
      has \(B_{\le M}\ge\zeta B_w\).  In this case it supplies transported hit
      mass
      \[
         A_{\le M}
         \ge
         \frac{\zeta}{4}
         \overline\Phi\!\left(\frac{M}{\sqrt{\theta_-}}\right)B_w
         \tag{AGTC4}
      \]
      and endpoint loads normalized by \(A_{\le M}\) at most
      \(4/\overline\Phi(M/\sqrt{\theta_-})\).  In particular, if
      \(M^2\le C\log\log n\) and \(\zeta\ge(\log n)^{-K}\), this is an
      inverse-polylogarithmic hit subtransport with polylogarithmic normalized
      endpoint load.

      \item Some inherited-activation prefix inside one of the assigned
      containers \(W_x\) has positive reduced gain.

      \item The high-margin residual
      \[
         Y_{>M}=\{y:b(y)>0,\ m_G(c(y))>M\ \text{or}\ m_G(y)>M\}
      \]
      carries almost all paid mass,
      \[
         B_{>M}>(1-\zeta)B_w,
         \tag{AGTC5}
      \]
      and is price dominated by its assigned cell profile:
      \[
         B_{>M}
         \le
         \sum_{x:h_x>0}
         \psi_x
         \left(
            \mathsf T_a h_x^{\rho_x}
            +
            \sigma h_x^{1+\rho_x}
         \right),
         \qquad
         h_x=|\{y\in Y_{>M}:c(y)=x\}|.
         \tag{AGTC6}
      \]
   \end{enumerate}

   Thus the assigned Gaussian branch has no fourth active-load case: after an
   inverse-polylogarithmic upper-margin truncation is ruled out, the leftover
   either already closes by a finite prefix or is an explicitly priced
   high-margin Renyi-cover residual.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(B_{\le M}\ge\zeta B_w\), then
   \cref{cor:bounded-margin-assigned-truncation} gives \((AGTC4)\) and the
   stated normalized endpoint-load bound.  The inverse-polylogarithmic
   specialization follows from the final estimate in
   \cref{cor:upper-margin-assigned-transport-load}.

   Otherwise \(B_{\le M}<\zeta B_w\), so the same truncation corollary gives
   \(B_{>M}>(1-\zeta)B_w\).  Apply
   \cref{cor:high-margin-assigned-prefix-spread} to the assigned high-margin
   residual.  If one of its inherited prefixes is positive, alternative
   \((ii)\) holds.  If none is positive, the bound \((AGTC6)\) is exactly
   \((HMAP5)\).

   Finally, if \(X\cup Y\subseteq\mathbb S^{D-1}\), then
   \[
      \|y-c(y)\|^2=2-2\ip{c(y)}{y}\le2(1-\theta_-),
   \]
   proving the advertised point-centered container choice whenever that ball is
   among the certified children.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Assigned high-margin residual has automatic storage]
   \label{cor:assigned-high-margin-storage-split}
   Work in the third alternative of
   \cref{cor:assigned-gaussian-transport-trichotomy}.  Assume the high-margin
   cells use a common exponent \(\rho\), and put
   \[
      K=|Y|,
      \qquad
      H=|Y_{>M}|,
      \qquad
      Q_{\rm hm}=\sum_x\psi_xh_x^\rho,
      \qquad
      S_{\rm hm}=\sum_x\psi_xh_x^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{AGSS1}
   \]
   If all used child price factors satisfy \(\psi_x\le\psi_\star\le\psi\),
   then
   \[
      S_{\rm hm}
      \le
      \psi_\star H^{1+\rho}
      \le
      \psi K^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{AGSS2}
   \]
   Moreover, if no inherited prefix is positive, then
   \[
      B_{>M}
      \le
      \mathsf T_a Q_{\rm hm}+\sigma S_{\rm hm},
      \tag{AGSS3}
   \]
   and, when \(\mathsf T_a>0\),
   \[
      Q_{\rm hm}
      \ge
      \frac{(B_{>M}-\sigma S_{\rm hm})_+}{\mathsf T_a}
      \ge
      \frac{(B_{>M}-\sigma\psi_\star H^{1+\rho})_+}{\mathsf T_a}.
      \tag{AGSS4}
   \]

   In particular, if \(\mathsf T_a>0\) and the parent paid mass has surplus
   \[
      B_w\ge \beta\,
      \psi\bigl(\mathsf T_aK^\rho+\sigma K^{1+\rho}\bigr)
      \tag{AGSS5}
   \]
   and the upper-margin alternative has failed, so
   \(B_{>M}>(1-\zeta)B_w\), then
   \[
      Q_{\rm hm}
      >
      (1-\zeta)\beta\,\psi K^\rho
      +
      \frac{\bigl((1-\zeta)\beta\psi-\psi_\star\bigr)
             \sigma K^{1+\rho}}
           {\mathsf T_a}
      \tag{AGSS6}
   \]
   whenever \((1-\zeta)\beta\psi\ge\psi_\star\).  Thus, after the deterministic
   assigned cells are fixed, shared storage is not the remaining high-margin
   obstruction; a surviving high-margin branch must expose a large
   radius-discounted Renyi query price \(Q_{\rm hm}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since the sets \(H_x=\{y\in Y_{>M}:c(y)=x\}\) are disjoint and
   \(\sum_xh_x=H\le K\), convexity of \(t^{1+\rho}\) on \(\mathbb R_+\) gives
   \[
      \sum_xh_x^{1+\rho}\le H^{1+\rho}\le K^{1+\rho}.
   \]
   Multiplying by \(\psi_x\le\psi_\star\le\psi\) proves \((AGSS2)\).
   Inequality \((AGSS3)\) is exactly \((AGTC6)\) written with the notation
   \((AGSS1)\).  Rearranging it and using \((AGSS2)\) gives \((AGSS4)\).

   Under \((AGSS5)\) and failure of the upper-margin alternative,
   \[
      B_{>M}>(1-\zeta)\beta\,
      \psi(\mathsf T_aK^\rho+\sigma K^{1+\rho}).
   \]
   Substituting this lower bound into \((AGSS4)\), using \(H\le K\), and
   assuming \((1-\zeta)\beta\psi\ge\psi_\star\) so the positive part is active,
   gives \((AGSS6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Endpoint split for high-margin assigned residuals]
   \label{cor:assigned-high-margin-endpoint-split}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:assigned-high-margin-storage-split}.  Let
   \(p_G(u)=\Pr[u\in U_G]=\overline\Phi(m_G(u))\), and split the high-margin
   residual disjointly as
   \[
      Y_{\rm cen}=\{y\in Y_{>M}:m_G(c(y))>M\},
      \qquad
      Y_{\rm pay}=Y_{>M}\setminus Y_{\rm cen}.
      \tag{AGHS1}
   \]
   Then every \(y\in Y_{\rm pay}\) has \(m_G(y)>M\).  Put
   \[
      B_{\rm cen}=\sum_{y\in Y_{\rm cen}}b(y),
      \qquad
      B_{\rm pay}=\sum_{y\in Y_{\rm pay}}b(y),
      \tag{AGHS2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      h_x^{\rm cen}=|\{y\in Y_{\rm cen}:c(y)=x\}|,
      \qquad
      Q_{\rm cen}=\sum_x\psi_x(h_x^{\rm cen})^\rho,
      \qquad
      S_{\rm cen}=\sum_x\psi_x(h_x^{\rm cen})^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{AGHS3}
   \]
   If no inherited prefix is positive, then the center-high part satisfies
   \[
      B_{\rm cen}
      \le
      \mathsf T_aQ_{\rm cen}+\sigma S_{\rm cen}.
      \tag{AGHS4}
   \]
   If all used child price factors satisfy \(\psi_x\le\psi_\star\), then
   \[
      S_{\rm cen}\le\psi_\star |Y_{\rm cen}|^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{AGHS5}
   \]
   The paid-high part has one-point paid active load
   \[
      P_{\rm pay}
      =
      \sum_{y\in Y_{\rm pay}}b(y)p_G(y)
      \le
      \overline\Phi(M)B_{\rm pay},
      \tag{AGHS6}
   \]
   while the center-high Renyi query price has Gaussian active load
   \[
      Q_{\rm cen}^{G}
      =
      \sum_x\psi_x(h_x^{\rm cen})^\rho p_G(x)
      \le
      \overline\Phi(M)Q_{\rm cen}.
      \tag{AGHS7}
   \]

   Consequently, for every \(0<\eta<1\), either
   \(B_{\rm pay}\ge\eta B_{>M}\), in which case an \(\eta\)-fraction of the
   high-margin residual is a paid-endpoint first-moment tail by \((AGHS6)\), or
   \(B_{\rm cen}>(1-\eta)B_{>M}\), in which case almost all high-margin mass is
   controlled by the center-high Renyi price \((AGHS4)\), whose actual Gaussian
   active query load is suppressed by the tail factor \(\overline\Phi(M)\) in
   \((AGHS7)\).  If \(M^2\ge C\log\log n\), this suppression is
   \((\log n)^{-\Omega_C(1)}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(Y_{>M}\) is defined by
   \(m_G(c(y))>M\) or \(m_G(y)>M\), every point not placed in \(Y_{\rm cen}\)
   must satisfy \(m_G(y)>M\).  The partition gives
   \(B_{\rm cen}+B_{\rm pay}=B_{>M}\).

   Apply the sorting argument from
   \cref{cor:high-margin-assigned-prefix-spread} to the subcollection
   \(Y_{\rm cen}\).  The top \(h_x^{\rm cen}\)-prefix of \(W_x\) dominates
   the assigned subset \(\{y\in Y_{\rm cen}:c(y)=x\}\), so if no inherited
   prefix is positive,
   \[
      \sum_{y\in Y_{\rm cen}:c(y)=x}b(y)
      \le
      \psi_x\left(
         \mathsf T_a(h_x^{\rm cen})^\rho
         +
         \sigma(h_x^{\rm cen})^{1+\rho}
      \right).
   \]
   Summing over \(x\) gives \((AGHS4)\).  Inequality \((AGHS5)\) follows from
   \(\sum_xh_x^{\rm cen}=|Y_{\rm cen}|\), disjointness, and convexity of
   \(t^{1+\rho}\).

   For \(y\in Y_{\rm pay}\), \(p_G(y)=\overline\Phi(m_G(y))\le
   \overline\Phi(M)\), proving \((AGHS6)\).  If \(h_x^{\rm cen}>0\), then
   some assigned point in \(Y_{\rm cen}\) has center \(x\), so
   \(m_G(x)>M\) and \(p_G(x)\le\overline\Phi(M)\).  Summing these inequalities
   proves \((AGHS7)\).  The final dichotomy is the disjoint mass split, and the
   displayed inverse-polylogarithmic tail estimate follows from the Chernoff
   bound \(\overline\Phi(M)\le e^{-M^2/2}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Tail-rate screen for high-margin assigned residuals]
   \label{cor:high-margin-tail-rate-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:assigned-high-margin-endpoint-split}, and suppose the restricted
   assigned transports on \(Y_{\rm cen}\) and \(Y_{\rm pay}\) satisfy the
   hypotheses of \cref{cor:transport-gaussian-paid-fiber-separator} with the same
   Gaussian filter \(U_G\), parameters \(\theta_0,\Lambda\), and inherited
   star-prefix price model.  For
   \[
      Z\in\{Y_{\rm cen},Y_{\rm pay}\}
   \]
   let \(B_Z\), \(A_Z\), \(P_{X,Z}\), \(P_{Y,Z}\), and
   \(\mathsf P_{{\rm hi},Z}\) denote \(B_w\), \(A_w\), \(P_X^w\), \(P_Y^w\), and
   \(\mathsf P_{\rm hi}^w\) from
   \cref{cor:transport-gaussian-paid-fiber-separator} after restricting to
   \(w_{c(y),y}=b(y)\mathbf 1_{\{y\in Z\}}\).  If no inherited star prefix has
   positive reduced gain, then every nonempty restricted side obeys
   \[
      A_Z
      \le
      \bigl(e^{-\Lambda}+\overline\Phi(M)\bigr)B_Z
      +
      \mathsf P_{{\rm hi},Z}.
      \tag{HMTR1}
   \]
   Consequently, if
   \[
      \mathsf P_{{\rm hi},Z}\le \xi A_Z
      \qquad(0\le\xi<1),
      \tag{HMTR2}
   \]
   then
   \[
      \frac{A_Z}{B_Z}
      \le
      \frac{e^{-\Lambda}+\overline\Phi(M)}{1-\xi}.
      \tag{HMTR3}
   \]
   Equivalently, any certified lower bound
   \[
      A_Z>aB_Z,
      \qquad
      a>\frac{e^{-\Lambda}+\overline\Phi(M)}{1-\xi},
      \tag{HMTR4}
   \]
   together with \((HMTR2)\), forces a positive inherited star prefix.

   Thus the high-margin residual has a sharp remaining form: after the
   high-correlation inherited-prefix price is controlled, each endpoint side can
   survive only with paid-product rate at the Gaussian tail scale
   \(e^{-\Lambda}+\overline\Phi(M)\).  With
   \(M^2,\Lambda=\Theta(\log\log n)\), this rate is inverse-polylogarithmic.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Restricting the assigned transport to \(Z\) preserves the domination
   \(w_{x,y}\le b(y)\), the assigned form, and all hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:transport-gaussian-paid-fiber-separator}.  If no inherited star
   prefix is positive, \((TGFS10)\) gives
   \[
      A_Z
      \le
      e^{-\Lambda}B_Z+\min\{P_{X,Z},P_{Y,Z}\}
      +\mathsf P_{{\rm hi},Z}.
      \tag{HMTR5}
   \]
   If \(Z=Y_{\rm cen}\), then \(m_G(c(y))>M\) on \(Z\), and hence
   \[
      P_{X,Z}
      =
      \sum_{y\in Z}b(y)p_G(c(y))
      \le
      \overline\Phi(M)B_Z .
      \tag{HMTR6}
   \]
   If \(Z=Y_{\rm pay}\), then \(m_G(y)>M\) on \(Z\), so
   \[
      P_{Y,Z}
      =
      \sum_{y\in Z}b(y)p_G(y)
      \le
      \overline\Phi(M)B_Z .
      \tag{HMTR7}
   \]
   In either case
   \(\min\{P_{X,Z},P_{Y,Z}\}\le\overline\Phi(M)B_Z\), and \((HMTR1)\) follows
   from \((HMTR5)\).  If \(B_Z>0\) and \((HMTR2)\) holds, then
   \[
      (1-\xi)A_Z
      \le
      \bigl(e^{-\Lambda}+\overline\Phi(M)\bigr)B_Z,
   \]
   which is \((HMTR3)\).  The lower-bound alternative \((HMTR4)\) is the
   contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Inverse-polylog exposure threshold for high-margin residuals]
   \label{cor:high-margin-polylog-exposure-threshold}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:high-margin-tail-rate-screen}.  Define the
   combined high-margin quantities
   \[
      B_{\rm hm}=B_{\rm cen}+B_{\rm pay},
      \qquad
      A_{\rm hm}=A_{Y_{\rm cen}}+A_{Y_{\rm pay}},
      \qquad
      \mathsf P_{{\rm hi},{\rm hm}}
      =
      \mathsf P_{{\rm hi},Y_{\rm cen}}
      +
      \mathsf P_{{\rm hi},Y_{\rm pay}} .
      \tag{HMPE1}
   \]
   If no inherited star prefix has positive reduced gain, then
   \[
      A_{\rm hm}
      \le
      \bigl(e^{-\Lambda}+\overline\Phi(M)\bigr)B_{\rm hm}
      +
      \mathsf P_{{\rm hi},{\rm hm}} .
      \tag{HMPE2}
   \]
   Consequently, if \(B_{\rm hm}>0\) and
   \[
      \mathsf P_{{\rm hi},{\rm hm}}\le\xi A_{\rm hm}
      \qquad(0\le\xi<1),
      \tag{HMPE3}
   \]
   then
   \[
      \frac{A_{\rm hm}}{B_{\rm hm}}
      \le
      \frac{e^{-\Lambda}+\overline\Phi(M)}{1-\xi}.
      \tag{HMPE4}
   \]
   Equivalently, for any exposure target \(\chi>0\), the three conditions
   \[
      A_{\rm hm}\ge\chi B_{\rm hm},
      \qquad
      \mathsf P_{{\rm hi},{\rm hm}}\le\xi A_{\rm hm},
      \qquad
      e^{-\Lambda}+\overline\Phi(M)<(1-\xi)\chi
      \tag{HMPE5}
   \]
   force a positive inherited star prefix.

   In particular, fix \(K>0\) and \(\xi\le1/2\).  If
   \[
      \chi=(\log n)^{-K},
      \qquad
      \Lambda\ge(K+3)\log\log n,
      \qquad
      M^2\ge2(K+3)\log\log n,
      \tag{HMPE6}
   \]
   then \((HMPE5)\)'s tail inequality holds for all sufficiently large \(n\).
   Thus the remaining high-margin theorem only has to certify an
   inverse-polylogarithmic paid-product exposure \(A_{\rm hm}\ge\chi B_{\rm hm}\)
   after inherited high-correlation prices are controlled; no constant-rate
   exposure is needed.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \((HMTR1)\) to the two restricted sides \(Y_{\rm cen}\) and
   \(Y_{\rm pay}\), omitting an empty side.  Summing the two inequalities gives
   \((HMPE2)\).  Under \((HMPE3)\),
   \[
      (1-\xi)A_{\rm hm}
      \le
      \bigl(e^{-\Lambda}+\overline\Phi(M)\bigr)B_{\rm hm},
   \]
   and division by \(B_{\rm hm}>0\) gives \((HMPE4)\).  The forcing statement
   \((HMPE5)\) is the contrapositive of \((HMPE4)\).

   Finally, \(\overline\Phi(M)\le e^{-M^2/2}\), so \((HMPE6)\) gives
   \[
      e^{-\Lambda}+\overline\Phi(M)
      \le
      2(\log n)^{-(K+3)}
      <
      \frac12(\log n)^{-K}
      \le
      (1-\xi)\chi
   \]
   for all sufficiently large \(n\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Two-cutoff high-margin window reduction]
   \label{cor:two-cutoff-high-margin-window}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:assigned-high-margin-endpoint-split}, and assume the assigned edges
   satisfy
   \[
      \ip{c(y)}{y}\ge\theta_-
      \qquad(y\in Y_{>M},\ b(y)>0)
      \tag{HMW1}
   \]
   for some \(0<\theta_-\le1\).  Let \(U>M\), and split
   \[
      Y_{(M,U]}
      =
      \{y\in Y_{>M}:m_G(c(y))\le U,\ m_G(y)\le U\},
      \qquad
      Y_{>U}=Y_{>M}\setminus Y_{(M,U]} .
      \tag{HMW2}
   \]
   Write \(B_{(M,U]}=\sum_{y\in Y_{(M,U]}}b(y)\).  If \(B_{(M,U]}>0\), and
   \(A_{(M,U]}\), \(P_{X,(M,U]}\), and \(P_{Y,(M,U]}\) denote the transported hit
   moment and endpoint active loads after restricting to \(Y_{(M,U]}\), then
   \[
      A_{(M,U]}
      \ge
      \frac14\overline\Phi\!\left(\frac{U}{\sqrt{\theta_-}}\right)
      B_{(M,U]},
      \tag{HMW3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \frac{P_{X,(M,U]}}{A_{(M,U]}},
      \frac{P_{Y,(M,U]}}{A_{(M,U]}}
      \le
      \frac{4}{\overline\Phi(U/\sqrt{\theta_-})}.
      \tag{HMW4}
   \]

   For the very-high residual, define the endpoint split at level \(U\)
   \[
      Y_{{\rm cen},>U}=\{y\in Y_{>U}:m_G(c(y))>U\},
      \qquad
      Y_{{\rm pay},>U}=Y_{>U}\setminus Y_{{\rm cen},>U}.
      \tag{HMW5}
   \]
   Then every \(y\in Y_{{\rm pay},>U}\) has \(m_G(y)>U\).  Put
   \[
      B_{{\rm cen},>U}=\sum_{y\in Y_{{\rm cen},>U}}b(y),
      \qquad
      B_{{\rm pay},>U}=\sum_{y\in Y_{{\rm pay},>U}}b(y),
      \tag{HMW6}
   \]
   and
   \[
      h_x^{>U}=|\{y\in Y_{{\rm cen},>U}:c(y)=x\}|,
      \qquad
      Q_{{\rm cen},>U}=\sum_x\psi_x(h_x^{>U})^\rho,
      \qquad
      S_{{\rm cen},>U}=\sum_x\psi_x(h_x^{>U})^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{HMW7}
   \]
   If no inherited prefix is positive, then
   \[
      B_{{\rm cen},>U}
      \le
      \mathsf T_aQ_{{\rm cen},>U}+\sigma S_{{\rm cen},>U}.
      \tag{HMW8}
   \]
   The paid-side endpoint tail and the center-side active Renyi price obey
   \[
      \sum_{y\in Y_{{\rm pay},>U}}b(y)p_G(y)
      \le
      \overline\Phi(U)B_{{\rm pay},>U},
      \tag{HMW9}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_x\psi_x(h_x^{>U})^\rho p_G(x)
      \le
      \overline\Phi(U)Q_{{\rm cen},>U}.
      \tag{HMW10}
   \]

   Consequently, for every \(0<\eta<1\), either
   \(B_{(M,U]}\ge\eta B_{>M}\), in which case the bounded high-margin window
   supplies transported hit mass at least
   \[
      \frac{\eta}{4}
      \overline\Phi\!\left(\frac{U}{\sqrt{\theta_-}}\right)B_{>M}
      \tag{HMW11}
   \]
   with success-normalized endpoint load bounded by \((HMW4)\), or
   \(B_{>U}>(1-\eta)B_{>M}\), in which case almost all of the high-margin
   residual has moved to the stronger endpoint-tail level \(U\) and is governed by
   \((HMW8)\)--\((HMW10)\).

   In particular, if \(U^2\le C\log\log n\) and
   \(\eta\ge(\log n)^{-K}\), the first alternative is an inverse-polylogarithmic
   hit subtransport with polylogarithmic normalized endpoint load.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   On \(Y_{(M,U]}\), both assigned endpoint margins are at most \(U\), and the
   correlation lower bound \((HMW1)\) holds.  Applying
   \cref{cor:upper-margin-assigned-transport-load} with cutoff \(U\) gives
   \((HMW3)\)--\((HMW4)\).

   Since \(Y_{>U}\) is the complement of \(Y_{(M,U]}\) inside \(Y_{>M}\), every
   point in \(Y_{>U}\) has \(m_G(c(y))>U\) or \(m_G(y)>U\).  Therefore every point
   not placed in \(Y_{{\rm cen},>U}\) satisfies \(m_G(y)>U\).

   The proof of \((HMW8)\) is the same sorting argument as in
   \cref{cor:assigned-high-margin-endpoint-split}, applied to the subcollection
   \(Y_{{\rm cen},>U}\): the top \(h_x^{>U}\)-prefix of \(W_x\) dominates the
   assigned subset with center \(x\), and no positive inherited prefix gives
   \[
      \sum_{y\in Y_{{\rm cen},>U}:c(y)=x}b(y)
      \le
      \psi_x\left(
         \mathsf T_a(h_x^{>U})^\rho+\sigma(h_x^{>U})^{1+\rho}
      \right).
   \]
   Summing over \(x\) proves \((HMW8)\).

   For \(y\in Y_{{\rm pay},>U}\),
   \(p_G(y)=\overline\Phi(m_G(y))\le\overline\Phi(U)\), proving \((HMW9)\).  If
   \(h_x^{>U}>0\), then some assigned point in \(Y_{{\rm cen},>U}\) has center
   \(x\), so \(m_G(x)>U\) and \(p_G(x)\le\overline\Phi(U)\).  Summing gives
   \((HMW10)\).

   The final dichotomy is the disjoint mass split
   \(B_{>M}=B_{(M,U]}+B_{>U}\), together with \((HMW3)\)--\((HMW4)\).  The
   inverse-polylogarithmic specialization follows from the Gaussian tail-ratio
   bound in \((UATL4)\), with \(U^2\le C\log\log n\), and the assumed
   \(\eta\ge(\log n)^{-K}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[High-margin margin ladder reduction]
   \label{cor:high-margin-margin-ladder}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:two-cutoff-high-margin-window}.  Let
   \[
      M=M_0<M_1<\cdots<M_J=U
      \tag{HML1}
   \]
   be any finite margin ladder.  For \(1\le j\le J\), define the margin band
   \[
      Y_j=
      \{y\in Y_{>M}:m_G(c(y))\le M_j,\ m_G(y)\le M_j,
      \max\{m_G(c(y)),m_G(y)\}>M_{j-1}\},
      \tag{HML2}
   \]
   and put \(B_j=\sum_{y\in Y_j}b(y)\).  Let
   \[
      Y_{>U}=\{y\in Y_{>M}:m_G(c(y))>U\ \text{or}\ m_G(y)>U\}.
      \tag{HML3}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      B_{>M}=\sum_{j=1}^J B_j+B_{>U}.
      \tag{HML4}
   \]
   For every nonempty band \(Y_j\), its restricted assigned transport has
   transported hit moment
   \[
      A_j\ge
      \frac14\overline\Phi\!\left(\frac{M_j}{\sqrt{\theta_-}}\right)B_j,
      \tag{HML5}
   \]
   and success-normalized endpoint loads bounded by
   \[
      \frac{P_{X,j}}{A_j},\frac{P_{Y,j}}{A_j}
      \le
      \frac{4}{\overline\Phi(M_j/\sqrt{\theta_-})}.
      \tag{HML6}
   \]

   Consequently, for any \(0<\eta<1/J\), either some band has
   \(B_j\ge\eta B_{>M}\), in which case it gives hit mass at least
   \[
      \frac{\eta}{4}
      \overline\Phi\!\left(\frac{M_j}{\sqrt{\theta_-}}\right)B_{>M}
      \tag{HML7}
   \]
   with normalized endpoint load bounded by \((HML6)\), or else
   \[
      B_{>U}>(1-J\eta)B_{>M}.
      \tag{HML8}
   \]
   In the second alternative, the residual \(Y_{>U}\), split at level \(U\),
   satisfies the endpoint-tail and center-price estimates
   \((HMW8)\)--\((HMW10)\) from
   \cref{cor:two-cutoff-high-margin-window}.

   In particular, if \(U^2\le C\log\log n\), \(J\le(\log n)^K\), and
   \(\eta=1/(2J)\), then either some ladder band is an
   inverse-polylogarithmic hit subtransport with polylogarithmic normalized
   endpoint load, or at least half of the high-margin residual lies above the
   final cutoff \(U\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The sets \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_J,Y_{>U}\) are disjoint and partition \(Y_{>M}\) by
   the value of \(\max\{m_G(c(y)),m_G(y)\}\), proving \((HML4)\).

   On \(Y_j\), both assigned endpoint margins are at most \(M_j\), and the
   correlation lower bound inherited from \((HMW1)\) holds.  Applying
   \cref{cor:upper-margin-assigned-transport-load} with cutoff \(M_j\) gives
   \((HML5)\)--\((HML6)\).

   If no band has \(B_j\ge\eta B_{>M}\), then
   \(\sum_jB_j<J\eta B_{>M}\).  Using \((HML4)\) gives \((HML8)\).  The tail
   estimates for \(Y_{>U}\) are exactly the second part of
   \cref{cor:two-cutoff-high-margin-window} at cutoff \(U\).

   The final specialization follows from \((HML7)\), the Gaussian tail-ratio
   estimate used in \((UATL4)\), and \(1/(2J)\ge(2\log^K n)^{-1}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Gaussian paid-fiber separator criterion]
   \label{cor:gaussian-paid-fiber-separator-criterion}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:gaussian-paid-fiber-first-moment-closure}, and write
   \[
      A_G=
      \frac1{m_X}\sum_{x\in X}\sum_{y\in Y}b(y)\kappa_{x,y}.
      \tag{GPFS1}
   \]
   For a margin split \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\), define
   \[
      E_G(\gamma)
      =
      e^{-\Lambda}
      +
      \bar p_X^{<\gamma}
      +
      \begin{cases}
         B_Y^{-1}P_Y^{<s_\Lambda-\gamma},&B_Y>0,\\
         0,&B_Y=0 .
      \end{cases}
      \tag{GPFS2}
   \]
   If, for some \(\gamma\),
   \[
      A_G>E_G(\gamma)B_Y+\mathsf P_{\rm hi},
      \tag{GPFS3}
   \]
   then some inherited-activation prefix from one of the radius-\(R_0\) star
   containers has positive reduced gain.

   In particular, suppose that for some \(a>0\) and \(0\le\xi<1\),
   \[
      A_G\ge aB_Y,
      \qquad
      \mathsf P_{\rm hi}\le \xi A_G,
      \qquad
      E_G(\gamma)<(1-\xi)a .
      \tag{GPFS4}
   \]
   Then an inherited-activation prefix has positive reduced gain.
   Thus the Gaussian paid-fiber branch can be separated by three scalar
   certificates: a paid-product lower bound \(A_G\ge aB_Y\), truncated
   one-point margin loads making \(E_G(\gamma)\) inverse-polylogarithmic, and an
   inherited prefix-price bound \(\mathsf P_{\rm hi}\le\xi A_G\).  No profile
   entropy or layer-cake slack is part of this final separator test.

   The total-load Cauchy bound \((GPFC3)\) is a closure estimate, not a useful
   positive separator trigger: since
   \(A_G\le\sqrt{B_Y\bar p_XP_Y}\), a criterion based only on the product
   \(\bar p_XP_Y\) would be tautological.  The strict separator information is
   exactly the margin truncation in \(E_G(\gamma)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If no inherited-activation prefix has positive reduced gain, then
   \cref{cor:gaussian-paid-fiber-first-moment-closure} gives
   \(A_G\le E_G(\gamma)B_Y+\mathsf P_{\rm hi}\), contradicting \((GPFS3)\).

   Under \((GPFS4)\), \(B_Y\le A_G/a\), so
   \[
      E_G(\gamma)B_Y+\mathsf P_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \left(\frac{E_G(\gamma)}{a}+\xi\right)A_G
      <
      A_G .
   \]
   Hence \((GPFS3)\) holds, and the first part applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Margin-tail obstruction normal form]
   \label{cor:margin-tail-obstruction-normal-form}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:gaussian-paid-fiber-separator-criterion}, and assume \(B_Y>0\).
   Define the optimized margin-tail defect
   \[
      \mathsf M_G
      =
      \inf_{\gamma\in\mathbb R}
      \left(
         B_Y\bar p_X^{<\gamma}
         +
         P_Y^{<s_\Lambda-\gamma}
      \right).
      \tag{MTON1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      A_G>e^{-\Lambda}B_Y+\mathsf M_G+\mathsf P_{\rm hi},
      \tag{MTON2}
   \]
   then some inherited-activation prefix from one of the radius-\(R_0\) star
   containers has positive reduced gain.

   Conversely, suppose no inherited-activation prefix has positive reduced gain,
   and suppose
   \[
      A_G\ge aB_Y,
      \qquad
      \mathsf P_{\rm hi}\le\xi A_G
      \qquad(a>0,\ 0\le\xi<1).
      \tag{MTON3}
   \]
   Then the residual must satisfy the explicit margin-tail obstruction
   \[
      \mathsf M_G
      \ge
      \bigl((1-\xi)a-e^{-\Lambda}\bigr)B_Y .
      \tag{MTON4}
   \]
   Thus after a paid-product lower bound and an inherited-price fractional bound
   are known, the only way this Gaussian branch can survive is for every margin
   split to leave polynomially nonnegligible active probability on one side.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let
   \[
      \Delta=A_G-e^{-\Lambda}B_Y-\mathsf M_G-\mathsf P_{\rm hi}>0 .
   \]
   Choose \(\gamma\) with
   \[
      B_Y\bar p_X^{<\gamma}
      +
      P_Y^{<s_\Lambda-\gamma}
      \le \mathsf M_G+\Delta/2 .
   \]
   Then
   \[
      A_G>
      \left(e^{-\Lambda}
      +\bar p_X^{<\gamma}
      +B_Y^{-1}P_Y^{<s_\Lambda-\gamma}\right)B_Y
      +\mathsf P_{\rm hi}
      +
      \Delta/2 .
   \]
   This gives the strict criterion \((GPFS3)\), so
   \cref{cor:gaussian-paid-fiber-separator-criterion} applies.

   For the converse, no positive prefix and
   \cref{cor:gaussian-paid-fiber-first-moment-closure} imply, for every
   \(\gamma\),
   \[
      A_G
      \le
      e^{-\Lambda}B_Y
      +
      B_Y\bar p_X^{<\gamma}
      +
      P_Y^{<s_\Lambda-\gamma}
      +
      \mathsf P_{\rm hi}.
   \]
   Taking the infimum over \(\gamma\), using
   \(A_G-\mathsf P_{\rm hi}\ge(1-\xi)A_G\), and then \(A_G\ge aB_Y\), gives
   \((MTON4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Margin-tail obstruction is a one-point load obstruction]
   \label{cor:margin-tail-total-load-dichotomy}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:margin-tail-obstruction-normal-form}.  Then
   \[
      \mathsf M_G
      \le
      \min\{B_Y\bar p_X,\ P_Y\}.
      \tag{MTLD1}
   \]
   Consequently, suppose no inherited-activation prefix has positive reduced
   gain and \((MTON3)\) holds.  If
   \[
      \delta=(1-\xi)a-e^{-\Lambda}>0,
      \tag{MTLD2}
   \]
   then necessarily
   \[
      \bar p_X\ge\delta,
      \qquad
      P_Y\ge\delta B_Y .
      \tag{MTLD3}
   \]
   Equivalently, if either endpoint total active load is below this threshold,
   the Gaussian paid-fiber branch must already expose a positive inherited
   prefix.  Thus the optimized split defect does not create a new geometric
   branch under ordinary one-point active-load accounting; a surviving margin
   tail is exactly a simultaneous load obstruction on both endpoints.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since the sets are finite, choose \(\gamma\) larger than every margin
   \(m_G(x)\) on \(X\) and also so large that \(s_\Lambda-\gamma\) is smaller
   than every margin on \(Y\).  Then \(P_Y^{<s_\Lambda-\gamma}=0\), and
   \((MTON1)\) gives \(\mathsf M_G\le B_Y\bar p_X\).  Choosing \(\gamma\)
   smaller than every margin on \(X\) and also so small that
   \(s_\Lambda-\gamma\) is larger than every margin on \(Y\), gives
   \(\mathsf M_G\le P_Y\).  This proves \((MTLD1)\).

   Under no positive inherited prefix and \((MTON3)\),
   \cref{cor:margin-tail-obstruction-normal-form} gives
   \(\mathsf M_G\ge\delta B_Y\).  Combining this with \((MTLD1)\) and \(B_Y>0\)
   proves \((MTLD3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Paid Renyi-cover obstruction]
   \label{cor:paid-renyi-cover-obstruction}
   In the setting of \cref{cor:paid-cover-quotient-star-residual}, suppose
   \(G\) has positive reduced gain with
   \[
      T=\psi K^\rho,
      \qquad
      S=\psi K^{1+\rho},
      \qquad
      K=|U|,
      \qquad
      \mathsf T_a=\sum_q\tau_qa(q).
      \tag{PRC1}
   \]
   If no smaller-radius paid prefix from this assigned cover has positive
   reduced gain, then this cover satisfies the strict paid inflation inequality
   \[
      \sum_x\psi_xA_x|U_x|^{\rho_x}
      +
      \sigma\sum_x\psi_x|U_x|^{1+\rho_x}
      >
      \psi\bigl(K^\rho\mathsf T_a+\sigma K^{1+\rho}\bigr).
      \tag{PRC2}
   \]

   In particular, assume the assigned children use the same exponent \(\rho\)
   and are query-compatible with the parent activation,
   \[
      a_x(q)\le a(q)
      \qquad(x,\ q).
      \tag{PRC3}
   \]
   If their Renyi prices are parent-compatible,
   \[
      \sum_x\psi_x|U_x|^\rho\le\psi K^\rho,
      \qquad
      \sum_x\psi_x|U_x|^{1+\rho}\le\psi K^{1+\rho},
      \tag{PRC4}
   \]
   then some smaller-radius paid prefix has positive reduced gain.

   Consequently, if every child price factor obeys
   \(\psi_x\le\psi_\star\le\psi\), then any surviving query-compatible assigned
   cover must have
   \[
      \sum_x|U_x|^\rho>\frac{\psi}{\psi_\star}K^\rho .
      \tag{PRC5}
   \]
   Thus the remaining obstruction for a positive quotient is no longer an
   arbitrary paid-demand issue: after query-compatible localization, it is the
   same Renyi-spread obstruction as in
   \cref{cor:renyi-spread-quotient-obstruction}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Positive reduced gain gives
   \[
      A_G>\psi\bigl(K^\rho\mathsf T_a+\sigma K^{1+\rho}\bigr).
   \]
   If no assigned paid prefix closes, \cref{cor:paid-cover-quotient-star-residual}
   gives
   \[
      A_G
      \le
      \sum_x\psi_x
      \left(
         A_x|U_x|^{\rho_x}
         +
         \sigma |U_x|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right),
   \]
   which proves \((PRC2)\).

   Under \((PRC3)\), \(A_x=\sum_q\tau_qa_x(q)\le\mathsf T_a\) for every \(x\).
   Combining this with \((PRC4)\) gives
   \[
      \sum_x\psi_xA_x|U_x|^\rho
      +
      \sigma\sum_x\psi_x|U_x|^{1+\rho}
      \le
      \psi\bigl(K^\rho\mathsf T_a+\sigma K^{1+\rho}\bigr),
   \]
   contradicting \((PRC2)\).  Therefore some paid prefix must have positive
   reduced gain.

   For the final statement, suppose a surviving query-compatible assigned cover
   had
   \[
      \sum_x|U_x|^\rho\le\frac{\psi}{\psi_\star}K^\rho .
   \]
   Since \(\psi_x\le\psi_\star\), the first inequality in \((PRC4)\) follows.
   The sets \(U_x\) partition \(U\), so
   \[
      \sum_x\psi_x|U_x|^{1+\rho}
      \le
      \psi_\star\sum_x|U_x|^{1+\rho}
      \le
      \psi K^{1+\rho},
   \]
   proving the second inequality in \((PRC4)\).  The previous paragraph would
   force a positive paid prefix, contrary to survival.  Hence \((PRC5)\) holds.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Activation-inflation screen for assigned covers]
   \label{cor:activation-inflation-assigned-cover}
   In the setting of \cref{cor:paid-renyi-cover-obstruction}, assume the
   assigned children have the same exponent \(\rho\).  For each child put
   \[
      E_x=\sum_q\tau_q\bigl(a_x(q)-a(q)\bigr)_+ .
      \tag{AIS1}
   \]
   Let
   \[
      \Delta_T
      =
      \psi K^\rho-\sum_x\psi_x|U_x|^\rho,
      \qquad
      \Delta_S
      =
      \psi K^{1+\rho}-\sum_x\psi_x|U_x|^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{AIS2}
   \]
   If no smaller-radius paid prefix from the assigned cover has positive
   reduced gain, then
   \[
      \sum_x\psi_x|U_x|^\rho E_x
      >
      \mathsf T_a\Delta_T+\sigma\Delta_S .
      \tag{AIS3}
   \]
   Consequently, any assigned refinement with
   \(\Delta_T,\Delta_S\ge0\) and
   \[
      \sum_x\psi_x|U_x|^\rho E_x
      \le
      \mathsf T_a\Delta_T+\sigma\Delta_S
      \tag{AIS4}
   \]
   must contain a smaller-radius paid prefix of positive reduced gain.

   In particular, if the children are query-compatible with the parent
   activation, then \(E_x=0\) for every \(x\), and any Renyi-price compatible
   refinement closes.  More generally, a surviving Renyi-price compatible
   refinement has a strictly positive activation-inflation toll.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(a_x(q)\le a(q)+(a_x(q)-a(q))_+\), we have
   \[
      A_x=\sum_q\tau_qa_x(q)\le \mathsf T_a+E_x .
      \tag{AIS5}
   \]
   If no smaller-radius paid prefix closes, \((PRC2)\) gives
   \[
      \sum_x\psi_xA_x|U_x|^\rho
      +
      \sigma\sum_x\psi_x|U_x|^{1+\rho}
      >
      \psi\bigl(K^\rho\mathsf T_a+\sigma K^{1+\rho}\bigr).
      \tag{AIS6}
   \]
   Combining \((AIS5)\) and \((AIS6)\) yields
   \[
      \mathsf T_a\sum_x\psi_x|U_x|^\rho
      +
      \sum_x\psi_x|U_x|^\rho E_x
      +
      \sigma\sum_x\psi_x|U_x|^{1+\rho}
      >
      \psi\bigl(K^\rho\mathsf T_a+\sigma K^{1+\rho}\bigr).
   \]
   Rearranging is exactly \((AIS3)\).  The contrapositive gives \((AIS4)\).
   Query compatibility gives \(E_x=0\), so the final claims are immediate.
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:reduced-gain-quotient-refinement} is the finite-cover analogue of the
Hall-shadow refinement lemma.  It says that once a quotient has positive
reduced gain, any demand-preserving split whose radius discount pays the Renyi
query-price increase must contain a positive child quotient.  Therefore the
high-spread condition in \cref{cor:low-spread-quotient-closure} is an actual
dual residual certificate: if spherical buckets and all smaller-radius quotients
fail, the remaining positive object must be diffuse across every certified
radius-contracting refinement.  \Cref{cor:quotient-spread-packing-entropy}
turns that diffuse residual into a separated packing with explicit Renyi
effective support.  \Cref{cor:spread-packing-entropy-energy-screen} then states
the exact spherical payment: cap-intersection energy must dominate the separated
profile entropy.  \Cref{cor:spread-packing-star-signal} adds the contrapositive
handoff: after the low-correlation energy part is paid, any remaining profile
mass must appear as a smaller-radius high-correlation star whose paid value is
tested by the dense-column verifier.
\Cref{cor:paid-integrated-spread-star-residual} gives the exact residual form:
if the star multiplicities are paid responsibilities and all dense prefixes
fail, then the high-correlation profile mass is bounded by the integrated Renyi
price of those star superlevels.  \Cref{cor:paid-cover-quotient-star-residual}
then removes the responsibility assumption for quotient covers: assigning the
parent update side to smaller balls automatically dominates the parent paid
demand by the ball-thickened paid degrees.  Thus a positive quotient survives a
smaller-radius cover only when that cover's integrated paid Renyi price is at
least the parent demand.  \Cref{cor:paid-renyi-cover-obstruction} sharpens this
into the useful dichotomy: a surviving cover is either not query-compatible with
the parent activation, or it has the same Renyi-spread excess as the older
unpaid obstruction.  The clean retained version is
\cref{cor:inherited-activation-paid-cover}: once the parent activation is itself
a safe filter predicate, every smaller-radius child may inherit that activation,
so low Renyi fanout closes with no extra activation term.  The
ball-thickened-child analysis is needed only when the inherited activation is a
finite-demand or analysis predicate that must be replaced by a standalone
geometric wrapper.  \Cref{cor:inherited-activation-cover-spread-packing} then
feeds a surviving same-activation quotient directly to the packing-entropy side:
failure of all low-fanout certified-ball covers is exactly the separated-set
witness required by \cref{cor:spread-packing-entropy-energy-screen}.
\Cref{cor:inherited-activation-renyi-center-law} keeps the sharper unbalanced
information: the Voronoi cell masses of any point-centered separated cover form
a center law with large Renyi effective support, and one dyadic center level
retains this mass-entropy product up to a logarithmic factor.  Thus the
paid-product handoff below can use the natural center weights \(\lambda_x\)
instead of first flattening the residual to a raw packing cardinality.
\Cref{cor:inherited-activation-spread-star-residual} applies the same
same-activation idea to entropy-energy failures: high-correlation pair mass
dominated by the parent paid degree is paid by inherited star-prefix prices,
without introducing ball-thickened query activation.
\Cref{cor:clipped-inherited-activation-spread-star-residual} removes the
pointwise domination assumption from the accounting by clipping arbitrary
high-correlation multiplicities against the parent paid degree.  The clipped
part is paid by the same inherited star-prefix prices; the only new obstruction
is the overload \(W_+\), where the entropy-energy handoff uses a point more
often than its parent paid degree allows.  In particular, paid-product pair
weights of the form \(\lambda_x\theta_{x,y}b(y)\) have no overload, so the
spread-packing analysis should be run with such paid weights whenever possible
rather than with an arbitrary unweighted packing law.
\Cref{cor:paid-product-spread-packing-handoff} records this as an explicit
replacement for the raw second-moment handoff: the spherical/list-decoding
profile can be tested against the weighted cross moment
\(\sum_{x,y}\lambda_xb(y)\Pr[x,y\in U_G]\).  Low-correlation pairs are paid by
the usual entropy-energy estimate, while high-correlation pairs feed inherited
star prefixes with no overload term.
\Cref{cor:bipartite-paid-product-spread-handoff} removes the remaining
unnecessary restriction that the paid point \(y\) lie in the separated packing:
the packing supplies only the center side, and the second coordinate may range
over all of \(U\) with weight \(b(y)\).  This is the right target for the next
geometric estimate, because positive reduced gain controls the total paid mass
on \(U\), whereas high-spread controls the entropy of available centers.
\Cref{cor:paid-level-set-spread-packing} tightens this target further: if all
inherited paid prefixes fail, then one dyadic paid superlevel carries a
\(1/O(\log)\) fraction of the parent paid mass and every smaller-ball cover of
that superlevel has Renyi price at least its level mass.  Thus the
entropy-energy side should choose centers from a paid superlevel rather than
from an arbitrary unweighted packing; this removes the false route in which the
paid measure is disjoint from the spread witness.
\Cref{cor:paid-superlevel-entropy-energy-handoff} composes this paid-superlevel
witness with the paid-product profile screen: after averaging uniformly over
the paid centers, low-correlation profiles are charged by their certified
energy and high-correlation profiles either pay inherited star-prefix prices or
expose a positive inherited dense prefix.  This is the first place where the
center entropy, paid mass, and dense-prefix fallback are all in the same
statement.
\Cref{cor:fiberized-paid-superlevel-exposure} removes the remaining profile
bookkeeping from the low-correlation side: the sum
\(\sum_\pi e^{-I_\pi}L_\pi\) is exactly the \(b\)-weighted average, over paid
points \(y\), of the low exposure seen from the separated center set \(X\).
Thus the next geometric/list-decoding target is a single paid-fiber exposure
bound on a paid superlevel; profiles remain only as a way to certify energies
and route high-correlation mass to inherited prefixes.
\Cref{cor:uniform-energy-paid-fiber-screen} sharpens this further: the paid
average kills the center-count entropy, so a uniform energy floor
\(I\ge\Lambda\) pays the whole low branch by \(e^{-\Lambda}B_Y\).  With
\(\Lambda=A\log\log n\), this is an inverse-polylogarithmic loss, not a
profile-entropy toll.
\Cref{cor:gaussian-margin-paid-fiber-screen} gives the corresponding Gaussian
normal form.  Nondefective pairs with combined cap margin
\(m_G(x)+m_G(y)\ge2\sqrt{(1+\theta_0)\Lambda}\) and correlation at most
\(\theta_0\) have energy at least \(\Lambda\); nondefective pairs above
\(\theta_0\) feed inherited dense prefixes.  The only leftover term is the
explicit margin-defect contribution \(W_{\rm marg}\), which should be paid by
first-moment, guard, or terminal-scan accounting rather than by dense branching.
\Cref{cor:margin-defect-first-moment-payment} gives the promised payment: the
defect is bounded by truncated one-point active loads on either endpoint, and
also by the symmetric Cauchy estimate
\(\sqrt{B_Y\bar p_XP_Y}\).  Therefore a polylogarithmic one-point active-load
bound makes the whole Gaussian paid-fiber branch polylogarithmic after the
inherited-prefix high-correlation part is charged.
\Cref{cor:gaussian-paid-fiber-first-moment-closure} records the composed
branch-closure inequality explicitly: paid-product mass is at most the
inverse-polylogarithmic energy term, plus ordinary one-point active load, plus
the inherited high-correlation recursive price.  This is the local algebraic
form needed by the final dense/spherical separator.
\Cref{cor:total-load-gaussian-paid-fiber-separator} is the algorithmic form of
