      \frac{b\,\psi_W}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_W}K^{\rho_W}}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_W}K^{1+\rho_W}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{HMC1}
   \]
   If the local filter-cover LP is infeasible, then there is a query sublayer
   \(Y\subseteq Q'\) satisfying
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Y}b_q-C D_W^\theta(Y)>\frac{B_{\rm tot}}2 .
      \tag{HMC2}
   \]
   In particular,
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Y}b_q>\frac{B_{\rm tot}}2,
      \qquad
      D_W^\theta(Y)
      <
      \frac1C
      \left(\sum_{q\in Y}b_q-\frac{B_{\rm tot}}2\right)
      \le \frac1C\sum_{q\in Y}b_q .
      \tag{HMC3}
   \]
   Conversely, if for some \(W,K,C,\theta\) satisfying \((HMC1)\) every query
   sublayer obeys
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Y}b_q-C D_W^\theta(Y)\le\frac{B_{\rm tot}}2,
      \tag{HMC4}
   \]
   then the single-seed annular layer yields the scalar reporter required by
   \cref{asm:weighted-annular-scalar-reporter}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{cor:cut-certified-annular-reporter} with
   \(M_0=B_{\rm tot}/2\).  The affordability condition \((CCR2)\) becomes
   exactly \((HMC1)\), and the cut violation \((CCR3)\) becomes \((HMC2)\).
   The two inequalities in \((HMC3)\) are immediate from \((HMC2)\) and
   nonnegativity of \(D_W^\theta(Y)\).

   For the converse, \((HMC4)\) is exactly the cut condition \((CCR1)\) with
   \(M_0=B_{\rm tot}/2\).  Together with \((HMC1)\), the first part of
   \cref{cor:cut-certified-annular-reporter} gives the reporter.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Cut-recycled annular sublayer]
   \label{lem:cut-recycled-annular-sublayer}
   Work under the hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:half-mass-excess-cut-obstruction}, and suppose a query sublayer
   \(Y\subseteq Q'\) satisfies the excess-cut conclusion \((HMC2)\).  Let
   \(m=|P|\), write \(Q'=Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}\), and put
   \[
      \mathcal D_m=\{2^\ell:0\le\ell\le\lceil\log_2m\rceil\},
      \qquad
      \mathcal D_m(\Delta)
      =
      \{\Delta'\in\mathcal D_m:\Delta\le\Delta'\le m\},
      \qquad
      H_m(\Delta)=|\mathcal D_m(\Delta)|.
   \]
   If \(B_Y=\sum_{q\in Y}b_q\), then there are a dyadic level
   \(\Delta'\in\mathcal D_m(\Delta)\) and a cut-restricted annular layer
   \[
      Y'=\{q\in Y: |B(q)|\ge\Delta'\}
      \tag{CRA1}
   \]
   such that
   \[
      \Delta'\sum_{q\in Y'}\bar\tau_q
      \ge
      \frac{B_Y}{2H_m(\Delta)}
      >
      \frac{B_{\rm tot}}{4H_m(\Delta)} .
      \tag{CRA2}
   \]
   Define the near-shadow capacity restricted to \(Y'\) by
   \[
      D_{W,Y'}^\theta(Y')
      =
      \sum_{p\in N_W(Y')}
      \sum_{\substack{q\in Y'\\(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}
      \bar\gamma^\theta_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
   \]
   Then
   \[
      D_{W,Y'}^\theta(Y')
      \le
      D_W^\theta(Y)
      <
      \frac{B_Y-B_{\rm tot}/2}{C}
      \le
      \frac{B_Y}{C}
      \le
      \frac{2H_m(\Delta)}{C}\,
      \Delta'\sum_{q\in Y'}\bar\tau_q .
      \tag{CRA3}
   \]
   In particular, if \(Y\) comes from an infeasible local cover through
   \cref{cor:single-seed-near-shadow-prefix-obstruction}, then
   \[
      \Delta'\sum_{q\in Y'}\bar\tau_q
      >
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}
      {16J K_{|P|}H_m(\Delta)} .
      \tag{CRA4}
   \]
   Here \(K_{|P|}=1+\lceil\log_2|P|\rceil\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For \(q\in Y\subseteq Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}\), the integer
   \(h_q=|B(q)|\) is at least \(\Delta\).  Since \(\Delta\) and the levels in
   \(\mathcal D_m\) are dyadic,
   \[
      h_q
      \le
      2\sum_{\Delta'\in\mathcal D_m(\Delta)}
      \Delta'\mathbf 1\{h_q\ge\Delta'\}.
   \]
   Multiplying by \(\bar\tau_q\), summing over \(Y\), and using
   \(b_q=\bar\tau_qh_q\) gives
   \[
      B_Y
      \le
      2\sum_{\Delta'\in\mathcal D_m(\Delta)}
      \Delta'\sum_{\substack{q\in Y:\\ |B(q)|\ge\Delta'}}\bar\tau_q .
   \]
   Averaging over the \(H_m(\Delta)\) levels gives a level \(\Delta'\) satisfying
   the first inequality in \((CRA2)\).  The second inequality is \((HMC2)\), since
   \(D_W^\theta(Y)\ge0\).

   The capacity comparison follows from monotonicity: \(Y'\subseteq Y\), so
   \(N_W(Y')\subseteq N_W(Y)\), and the degree restricted to \(Y'\) is bounded by
   the degree restricted to \(Q'\).  Therefore
   \(D_{W,Y'}^\theta(Y')\le D_W^\theta(Y)\).  The strict middle inequality is
   \((HMC2)\), and the final inequality is the rearranged lower bound in
   \((CRA2)\).

   Finally, \((SPO1)\) gives
   \(B_{\rm tot}\ge\Delta\sum_{q\in Q'}\bar\tau_q
   >(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa/(4JK_{|P|})\).  Combining this with
   \((CRA2)\) gives \((CRA4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Recycled-sublayer separator suffices]
   \label{cor:recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}
   Work under the hypotheses of \cref{cor:annular-reporter-local-cover}, assume
   the primitive law has finite support, and assume the retained container family
   is prefix-closed as in
   \cref{cor:single-seed-near-shadow-prefix-obstruction}.  Suppose the following
   separator property holds for every guarded normalized residual and every
   single-seed annular query layer \(Q'=Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}\) satisfying
   \((SAQ1)\)--\((SAQ2)\).  There are a retained container \(W\), a size
   certificate \(|W|\le K\), a congestion parameter \(C>0\), and
   \(0\le\theta\le1\) satisfying the affordability inequality \((HMC1)\), such
   that, with
   \[
      m=|P|,
      \qquad
      \mathcal D_m=\{2^\ell:0\le\ell\le\lceil\log_2m\rceil\},
      \qquad
      H_m(\Delta)
      =
      |\{\Delta'\in\mathcal D_m:\Delta\le\Delta'\le m\}|,
   \]
   every dyadic level \(\Delta'\in\mathcal D_m\) with \(\Delta'\ge\Delta\) and
   every cut-restricted layer
   \[
      Y'\subseteq\{q\in Q': |B_{z,\beta}(q)|\ge\Delta'\}
   \]
   with
   \[
      \Delta'\sum_{q\in Y'}\bar\tau_q
      >
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}
      {16J K_{|P|}H_m(\Delta)}
      \tag{RSS1}
   \]
   satisfies the near-shadow lower bound
   \[
      D_{W,Y'}^\theta(Y')
      >
      \frac{2H_m(\Delta)}{C}\,
      \Delta'\sum_{q\in Y'}\bar\tau_q .
      \tag{RSS2}
   \]
   where \(D_{W,Y'}^\theta(Y')\) is the restricted near-shadow capacity from
   \cref{lem:cut-recycled-annular-sublayer}.
   Then the enlarged local filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose the enlarged local LP were infeasible.  By
   \cref{cor:single-seed-near-shadow-prefix-obstruction}, there is a guarded
   normalized residual and a single-seed annular query layer
   \(Q'=Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}\) satisfying \((SAQ1)\)--\((SAQ2)\) and \((SPO1)\).
   Apply the assumed separator property to this layer and obtain
   \(W,K,C,\theta\) satisfying \((HMC1)\).

   Since the local LP is infeasible, \cref{cor:half-mass-excess-cut-obstruction}
   gives a half-mass excess cut \(Y\subseteq Q'\).  Applying
   \cref{lem:cut-recycled-annular-sublayer} to this cut produces a dyadic
   \(\Delta'\) and a cut-restricted layer \(Y'\).  The load lower bound
   \((CRA4)\) is exactly \((RSS1)\), while \((CRA3)\) gives the opposite of
   \((RSS2)\).  This contradiction rules out local infeasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Lagrange screen for recycled sublayers]
   \label{lem:lagrange-recycled-sublayer-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}, and fix
   \(W,C,\theta,\Delta'\).  Put
   \[
      Q_{\Delta'}=\{q\in Q': |B_{z,\beta}(q)|\ge\Delta'\},
      \qquad
      \ell_q=\Delta'\bar\tau_q ,
   \]
   \[
      s_q=s_{W,\theta}(q)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{p\in W\\(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}
      \bar\gamma^\theta_{p,q}r_{p,q},
      \qquad
      A=\frac{2H_m(\Delta)}{C},
   \]
   and let \(\Lambda>0\).  If there is a number \(\lambda>0\) such that
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}
      \bigl((A+\lambda)\ell_q-s_q\bigr)_+
      \le
      \lambda\Lambda ,
      \tag{LRS1}
   \]
   then every subset \(Y'\subseteq Q_{\Delta'}\) with
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Y'}\ell_q>\Lambda
      \tag{LRS2}
   \]
   satisfies
   \[
      D_{W,Y'}^\theta(Y')
      >
      A\sum_{q\in Y'}\ell_q .
      \tag{LRS3}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For \(Y'\subseteq Q_{\Delta'}\), the restricted near-shadow capacity is
   additive in the selected queries:
   \[
      D_{W,Y'}^\theta(Y')
      =
      \sum_{q\in Y'}s_q .
   \]
   If \((LRS3)\) failed for some \(Y'\) satisfying \((LRS2)\), then
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}
      \bigl((A+\lambda)\ell_q-s_q\bigr)_+
      &\ge
      \sum_{q\in Y'}\bigl((A+\lambda)\ell_q-s_q\bigr)\\
      &=
      A\sum_{q\in Y'}\ell_q-D_{W,Y'}^\theta(Y')
      +\lambda\sum_{q\in Y'}\ell_q\\
      &\ge
      \lambda\sum_{q\in Y'}\ell_q\\
      &>
      \lambda\Lambda ,
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   contradicting \((LRS1)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Fractional recycled-layer dual normal form]
   \label{lem:fractional-recycled-layer-dual-normal-form}
   Work in the notation of \cref{lem:lagrange-recycled-sublayer-screen}.
   With the convention that the maximum over an empty feasible set is
   \(-\infty\), define the fractional bad-layer value
   \[
      \Phi_{\Delta'}(W,\theta)
      =
      \max
      \left\{
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}} y_q(A\ell_q-s_q):
      0\le y_q\le1,\quad
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}y_q\ell_q\ge\Lambda
      \right\}.
      \tag{FRD1}
   \]
   Then, in the same extended-real convention,
   \[
      \Phi_{\Delta'}(W,\theta)
      =
      \inf_{\lambda\ge0}
      \left\{
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}
      \bigl((A+\lambda)\ell_q-s_q\bigr)_+
      -
      \lambda\Lambda
      \right\}.
      \tag{FRD2}
   \]
   Moreover, for every \(\lambda>0\) and every vector
   \(0\le y_q\le1\),
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}y_q(A\ell_q-s_q)
      \le
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}
      \bigl((A+\lambda)\ell_q-s_q\bigr)_+
      -
      \lambda\Lambda
      -
      \lambda
      \left(
         \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}y_q\ell_q-\Lambda
      \right).
      \tag{FRD3}
   \]
   Consequently, if the dual expression in \((FRD2)\) is at most \(0\) for
   some positive \(\lambda\), then every fractional sublayer \(y\) with
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}y_q\ell_q>\Lambda
   \]
   satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}y_qs_q
      >
      A\sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}y_q\ell_q .
      \tag{FRD4}
   \]
   In particular every integral sublayer \(Y'\subseteq Q_{\Delta'}\) with
   load above \(\Lambda\) satisfies \((LRS3)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The inequality \((FRD3)\) is the pointwise Lagrange upper bound.  Indeed,
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      &\sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}y_q(A\ell_q-s_q)
      +
      \lambda
      \left(
         \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}y_q\ell_q-\Lambda
      \right)\\
      &\qquad =
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}
      y_q\bigl((A+\lambda)\ell_q-s_q\bigr)
      -
      \lambda\Lambda\\
      &\qquad \le
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}
      \bigl((A+\lambda)\ell_q-s_q\bigr)_+
      -
      \lambda\Lambda .
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   Rearranging gives \((FRD3)\).  If the displayed dual expression is at most
   zero and \(\sum_qy_q\ell_q>\Lambda\), then \((FRD3)\) gives
   \[
      \sum_qy_q(A\ell_q-s_q)<0,
   \]
   which is \((FRD4)\).  Taking \(y_q=\mathbf 1_{\{q\in Y'\}}\) gives the
   asserted integral consequence.

   It remains only to identify the exact fractional value.  If
   \(\sum_q\ell_q<\Lambda\), the feasible set in \((FRD1)\) is empty, while
   the right-hand side of \((FRD2)\) tends to \(-\infty\) as
   \(\lambda\to\infty\).  Otherwise \((FRD1)\) is the finite linear program
   \[
      \max\ c^\top y
      \quad\text{subject to}\quad
      -\ell^\top y\le-\Lambda,\quad
      y\le\mathbf 1,\quad
      -y\le0,
   \]
   where \(c_q=A\ell_q-s_q\).  Its dual is
   \[
      \min_{\lambda,u,v\ge0}
      -\lambda\Lambda+\sum_qu_q
      \quad\text{subject to}\quad
      -\lambda\ell_q+u_q-v_q\ge c_q\quad(q\in Q_{\Delta'}).
   \]
   For fixed \(\lambda\), minimizing over \(u_q,v_q\) gives
   \(u_q=(c_q+\lambda\ell_q)_+\).  Thus the dual objective is exactly the
   right-hand side of \((FRD2)\), and finite-dimensional LP duality proves
   equality.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Threshold form of recycled bad layers]
   \label{lem:threshold-recycled-bad-layers}
   Work in the notation of
   \cref{lem:fractional-recycled-layer-dual-normal-form}, and put
   \[
      Q^+=\{q\in Q_{\Delta'}:\ell_q>0\},
      \qquad
      \sigma_q=\frac{s_q}{\ell_q}\quad(q\in Q^+).
   \]
   For \(t>A\), define the low-efficiency prefix statistics
   \[
      L(t)=\sum_{\substack{q\in Q^+\\ \sigma_q\le t}}\ell_q,
      \qquad
      S(t)=\sum_{\substack{q\in Q^+\\ \sigma_q\le t}}s_q,
   \]
   and
   \[
      G(t)=tL(t)-S(t)-(t-A)\Lambda .
      \tag{TRB1}
   \]
   Then the Lagrange screen with multiplier \(\lambda=t-A\) is equivalent
   to
   \[
      G(t)\le0 .
      \tag{TRB2}
   \]
   Moreover, if the fractional bad-layer problem \((FRD1)\) is feasible, it
   has an optimizer \(y\) of the following threshold form.  There is a level
   \(t_*\ge A\) such that
   \[
      y_q=1\quad(\sigma_q<t_*),
      \qquad
      y_q=0\quad(\sigma_q>t_*),
      \tag{TRB3}
   \]
   with arbitrary coefficients \(0\le y_q\le1\) only on the boundary
   \(\sigma_q=t_*\).  Queries with \(\ell_q=0\) may be assigned \(y_q=0\).
   Consequently, if a fractional sublayer of load \(>\Lambda\) and capacity at
   most \(A\) times its load exists, then such a threshold sublayer exists with
   load at least \(\Lambda\) and capacity at most \(A\) times its load.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For \(t=A+\lambda\), the positive part in \((LRS1)\) is nonzero exactly
   when \(\sigma_q\le t\), up to zero-valued boundary terms.  Hence
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}
      \bigl((A+\lambda)\ell_q-s_q\bigr)_+
      =
      tL(t)-S(t),
   \]
   and \((LRS1)\) is precisely \((TRB2)\).

   It remains to record the standard fractional-knapsack structure of
   \((FRD1)\).  Terms with \(\ell_q=0\) have coefficient \(-s_q\le0\) and do
   not help meet the load constraint, so an optimizer may set them to zero.
   Since
   \[
      A\ell_q-s_q=(A-\sigma_q)\ell_q\qquad(q\in Q^+),
   \]
   every query with \(\sigma_q<A\) has positive profit per unit load and may be
   included fully in an optimizer.  Queries with \(\sigma_q=A\) have zero
   profit per unit load and can be used only to meet the load constraint.
   After those levels are fixed, the remaining task, if any load is still
   needed, is to minimize \(\sum_qy_q(\sigma_q-A)\ell_q\) over
   \(\sigma_q>A\) subject to a lower load constraint.  The fractional
   knapsack exchange argument sorts by increasing \(\sigma_q\): if
   \(\sigma_i<\sigma_j\), \(y_i<1\), and \(y_j>0\), moving an equal amount of
   load from \(j\) to \(i\) does not reduce feasibility and strictly improves
   the objective.  Thus an optimizer has the threshold form \((TRB3)\), with
   at most one boundary level partially used.

   If a fractional sublayer has load \(>\Lambda\) and
   \(\sum_qy_qs_q\le A\sum_qy_q\ell_q\), then its objective in \((FRD1)\) is
   nonnegative.  Replacing it by an optimizer preserves nonnegative objective
   and feasibility, and the optimizer has the threshold form just proved.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Finite prefix screen for recycled thresholds]
   \label{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen}
   Work in the notation of \cref{lem:threshold-recycled-bad-layers}.  Let
   \(a_1<\cdots<a_k\) be the distinct values of \(\sigma_q\) that are larger
   than \(A\).  Put \(a_0=A\), and define
   \[
      L_i=\sum_{\substack{q\in Q^+\\ \sigma_q\le a_i}}\ell_q,
      \qquad
      S_i=\sum_{\substack{q\in Q^+\\ \sigma_q\le a_i}}s_q
      \qquad(0\le i\le k),
   \]
   with \(L_\infty=\sum_{q\in Q^+}\ell_q\).  The threshold screen
   \[
      \exists t>A:
      \qquad
      tL(t)-S(t)\le(t-A)\Lambda
      \tag{FPS1}
   \]
   holds if and only if at least one of the following finite alternatives
   holds:
   \[
      A L_0-S_0=0
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      L_0\le\Lambda ,
      \tag{FPS2}
   \]
   \[
      \exists i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}:
      \qquad
      a_iL_i-S_i\le(a_i-A)\Lambda ,
      \tag{FPS3}
   \]
   or
   \[
      L_\infty<\Lambda .
      \tag{FPS4}
   \]
   Thus a threshold certificate can be searched by sorting the finitely many
   efficiencies \(\sigma_q\) and scanning prefix sums.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Let
   \[
      G(t)=tL(t)-S(t)-(t-A)\Lambda .
   \]
   The function \(G\) is continuous and affine on each interval
   \((a_i,a_{i+1})\), with slope \(L_i-\Lambda\).  It is continuous at each
   breakpoint because the newly added queries have \(s_q=a_i\ell_q\).  On the
   last interval \((a_k,\infty)\) its slope is \(L_\infty-\Lambda\).

   The three displayed alternatives are sufficient.  If \((FPS2)\) holds, then
   either \(G(t)=0\) for all sufficiently small \(t>A\) or \(G(t)<0\) for all
   sufficiently small \(t>A\).  If \((FPS3)\) holds, choose \(t=a_i\).  If
   \((FPS4)\) holds, then \(G(t)\to-\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\).

   Conversely suppose \(G(t)\le0\) for some \(t>A\).  If \(t=a_i\) for a
   breakpoint \(i\ge1\), then \((FPS3)\) holds.  If \(t\in(a_i,a_{i+1})\),
   then \(G\) is affine on that interval.  When its slope is nonnegative,
   moving left cannot increase \(G\); if \(i\ge1\) this gives \((FPS3)\).  If
   \(i=0\), then \(G(A)=A L_0-S_0\le0\).  Since every included query has
   \(\sigma_q\le A\), also \(G(A)\ge0\).  Thus \(G(A)=0\), and the fact that
   \(G(t)\le0\) with nonnegative slope forces \(L_0-\Lambda=0\), giving
   \((FPS2)\).  When the slope is negative, moving right cannot increase
   \(G\); if \(i<k\) this gives \((FPS3)\), while if \(i=k\) it gives
   \(L_\infty<\Lambda\).

   It remains to handle \(t>a_k\), including the case \(k=0\).  On
   \((a_k,\infty)\), if the slope \(L_\infty-\Lambda\) is negative then
   \((FPS4)\) holds.  If the slope is nonnegative and \(k\ge1\), moving left to
   \(a_k\) gives \((FPS3)\).  If the slope is nonnegative and \(k=0\), the
   same argument at \(A\) gives \(G(A)=0\), and nonnegative slope plus
   \(G(t)\le0\) again forces \(L_0=\Lambda\), hence \((FPS2)\).  These cases
   exhaust all \(t>A\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Lagrange recycled-sublayer separator suffices]
   \label{cor:lagrange-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}
   Work under the hypotheses of \cref{cor:annular-reporter-local-cover}, assume
   finite primitive support and prefix-closed retained containers as in
   \cref{cor:recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}.  Suppose the following
   positive-part screen holds for every guarded normalized residual and every
   single-seed annular query layer \(Q'=Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}\) satisfying
   \((SAQ1)\)--\((SAQ2)\).  There are a retained container \(W\), a size
   certificate \(|W|\le K\), a congestion parameter \(C>0\), and
   \(0\le\theta\le1\) satisfying \((HMC1)\).  Put
   \[
      m=|P|,
      \qquad
      \mathcal D_m=\{2^\ell:0\le\ell\le\lceil\log_2m\rceil\},
      \qquad
      H_m(\Delta)=|\{\Delta''\in\mathcal D_m:\Delta\le\Delta''\le m\}|.
   \]
   Suppose that for every dyadic \(\Delta'\in\mathcal D_m\) with
   \(\Delta'\ge\Delta\) there is \(\lambda_{\Delta'}>0\) with
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}
      \left(
         \left(\frac{2H_m(\Delta)}{C}+\lambda_{\Delta'}\right)
         \Delta'\bar\tau_q
         -
         s_{W,\theta}(q)
      \right)_+
      \le
      \lambda_{\Delta'}\,
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}
      {16J K_{|P|}H_m(\Delta)} .
      \tag{LRS4}
   \]
   Here \(Q_{\Delta'}=\{q\in Q':|B_{z,\beta}(q)|\ge\Delta'\}\),
   and \(s_{W,\theta}(q)\) is the query-wise near-shadow mass from
   \cref{lem:lagrange-recycled-sublayer-screen}.  Then the enlarged local
   filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{lem:lagrange-recycled-sublayer-screen} at each dyadic
   \(\Delta'\), with
   \[
      \Lambda=
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}
      {16J K_{|P|}H_m(\Delta)} .
   \]
   The screen \((LRS4)\) gives exactly \((RSS2)\) for every layer satisfying
   \((RSS1)\).  Thus the separator property of
   \cref{cor:recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices} holds, and that corollary
   proves local filter-cover feasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Threshold recycled-sublayer separator suffices]
   \label{cor:threshold-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}
   Work under the hypotheses of \cref{cor:annular-reporter-local-cover}, assume
   finite primitive support and prefix-closed retained containers as in
   \cref{cor:recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}.  Suppose the following
   threshold screen holds for every guarded normalized residual and every
   single-seed annular query layer \(Q'=Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}\) satisfying
   \((SAQ1)\)--\((SAQ2)\).  There are a retained container \(W\), a size
   certificate \(|W|\le K\), a congestion parameter \(C>0\), and
   \(0\le\theta\le1\) satisfying \((HMC1)\).  Put
   \[
      m=|P|,
      \qquad
      \mathcal D_m=\{2^\ell:0\le\ell\le\lceil\log_2m\rceil\},
      \qquad
      H_m(\Delta)=|\{\Delta''\in\mathcal D_m:\Delta\le\Delta''\le m\}|,
   \]
   and
   \[
      A=\frac{2H_m(\Delta)}{C},
      \qquad
      \Lambda=
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}
      {16J K_{|P|}H_m(\Delta)} .
   \]
   For each dyadic \(\Delta'\in\mathcal D_m\) with \(\Delta'\ge\Delta\), define
   \[
      Q_{\Delta'}=\{q\in Q':|B_{z,\beta}(q)|\ge\Delta'\},
      \qquad
      \ell_q=\Delta'\bar\tau_q,
      \qquad
      s_q=s_{W,\theta}(q),
   \]
   and, for \(t>A\),
   \[
      L_{\Delta'}(t)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{q\in Q_{\Delta'}\\ \ell_q>0\\ s_q/\ell_q\le t}}
      \ell_q,
      \qquad
      S_{\Delta'}(t)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{q\in Q_{\Delta'}\\ \ell_q>0\\ s_q/\ell_q\le t}}
      s_q .
   \]
   If for every such \(\Delta'\) there exists a threshold \(t_{\Delta'}>A\)
   such that
   \[
      t_{\Delta'}L_{\Delta'}(t_{\Delta'})
      -
      S_{\Delta'}(t_{\Delta'})
      \le
      (t_{\Delta'}-A)\Lambda ,
      \tag{TRS1}
   \]
   then the enlarged local filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a dyadic \(\Delta'\).  Applying
   \cref{lem:threshold-recycled-bad-layers} with \(t=t_{\Delta'}\) shows that
   \((TRS1)\) is exactly the positive-part Lagrange screen \((LRS4)\), with
   multiplier \(\lambda_{\Delta'}=t_{\Delta'}-A>0\).  Since this holds for
   every dyadic level, \cref{cor:lagrange-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}
   proves local feasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite-prefix recycled-sublayer separator suffices]
   \label{cor:finite-prefix-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}
   In \cref{cor:threshold-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}, the threshold
   condition \((TRS1)\) may be replaced by the following finite prefix
   condition at each dyadic \(\Delta'\).  Let \(a_1<\cdots<a_k\) be the
   distinct values larger than \(A\) of
   \(s_{W,\theta}(q)/(\Delta'\bar\tau_q)\) over queries
   \(q\in Q_{\Delta'}\) with \(\bar\tau_q>0\).  Set \(a_0=A\), and define
   \[
      L_i=\sum_{\substack{q\in Q_{\Delta'}\\
                  \bar\tau_q>0\\
                  s_{W,\theta}(q)/(\Delta'\bar\tau_q)\le a_i}}
            \Delta'\bar\tau_q,
      \qquad
      S_i=\sum_{\substack{q\in Q_{\Delta'}\\
                  \bar\tau_q>0\\
                  s_{W,\theta}(q)/(\Delta'\bar\tau_q)\le a_i}}
            s_{W,\theta}(q).
   \]
   If, for every \(\Delta'\), at least one of
   \[
      A L_0-S_0=0\quad\text{and}\quad L_0\le\Lambda ,
      \tag{FPR1}
   \]
   \[
      \exists i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}:
      \qquad
      a_iL_i-S_i\le(a_i-A)\Lambda ,
      \tag{FPR2}
   \]
   or
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{q\in Q_{\Delta'}\\ \bar\tau_q>0}}
      \Delta'\bar\tau_q
      <\Lambda
      \tag{FPR3}
   \]
   holds, then the enlarged local filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For each fixed dyadic \(\Delta'\), this is exactly
   \cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen} applied with
   \(\ell_q=\Delta'\bar\tau_q\) and \(s_q=s_{W,\theta}(q)\).  Hence the
   threshold condition of
   \cref{cor:threshold-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices} holds at every
   dyadic level, and that corollary proves feasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Load-quantile recycled threshold screen]
   \label{lem:load-quantile-recycled-threshold-screen}
   Work in the notation of
   \cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen}.  The threshold screen
   \((FPS1)\) holds if and only if at least one of the following alternatives
   holds:
   \[
      A L_0-S_0=0
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      L_0\le\Lambda ,
      \tag{LQS1}
   \]
   \[
      L_\infty<\Lambda ,
      \tag{LQS2}
   \]
   or
   \[
      L_0<\Lambda\le L_\infty,
      \quad
      a_jL_j-S_j\le(a_j-A)\Lambda ,
      \tag{LQS3}
   \]
   where
   \[
      j=\min\{i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}: L_i\ge\Lambda\}.
      \tag{LQS4}
   \]
   Thus, after sorting the efficiencies, the continuous threshold search reduces
   to the \(A\)-boundary, the terminal load test, and one weighted
   \(\Lambda\)-quantile breakpoint.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Let
   \[
      G(t)=tL(t)-S(t)-(t-A)\Lambda .
   \]
   As in the proof of \cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen}, \(G\)
   is continuous and piecewise affine, and on the interval after breakpoint
   \(a_i\) its slope is \(L_i-\Lambda\).  These slopes are nondecreasing in
   \(i\).

   The alternatives are sufficient: \((LQS1)\) is exactly the boundary
   alternative \((FPS2)\), \((LQS2)\) is \((FPS4)\), and \((LQS3)\) is the
   breakpoint alternative \((FPS3)\) at the first load-crossing index \(j\).

   Conversely suppose \((FPS1)\) holds.  If \(L_\infty<\Lambda\), then
   \((LQS2)\) holds.  Hence assume \(L_\infty\ge\Lambda\).  If \(L_0\ge\Lambda\),
   every right slope is nonnegative, so \(G(t)\ge G(A)\) for all \(t>A\).  Since
   \(G(A)=A L_0-S_0\ge0\), the only way some \(t>A\) can satisfy \(G(t)\le0\) is
   \(G(A)=0\) and \(L_0=\Lambda\), which is \((LQS1)\).  If \(L_0<\Lambda\),
   then the index \(j\) in \((LQS4)\) exists.  For \(i<j\) the slope
   \(L_i-\Lambda\) is negative, and for \(i\ge j\) it is nonnegative.  Therefore
   \(G\) attains its global minimum at \(a_j\).  Since \((FPS1)\) holds,
   \(G(a_j)\le0\), which is \((LQS3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Exact-load recycled quantile screen]
   \label{lem:exact-load-recycled-quantile-screen}
   Work in the notation of
   \cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen}, and assume
   \(L_0<\Lambda\le L_\infty\).  Let
   \[
      j=\min\{i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}:L_i\ge\Lambda\},
      \qquad
      \alpha=\frac{\Lambda-L_{j-1}}{L_j-L_{j-1}} .
      \tag{ELQ1}
   \]
   Define the fractional \(\Lambda\)-load quantile capacity
   \[
      \widehat S_\Lambda
      =
      S_{j-1}+\alpha(S_j-S_{j-1}) .
      \tag{ELQ2}
   \]
   Then the quantile breakpoint condition in \((LQS3)\) is equivalent to
   \[
      \widehat S_\Lambda\ge A\Lambda .
      \tag{ELQ3}
   \]
   Equivalently, in the non-boundary regime \(L_0<\Lambda\le L_\infty\), the
   threshold screen holds if and only if the lowest-efficiency fractional prefix
   of exact load \(\Lambda\) has average capacity at least \(A\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   All mass added between \(L_{j-1}\) and \(L_j\) has efficiency \(a_j\).  Hence
   \[
      S_j-S_{j-1}=a_j(L_j-L_{j-1}),
   \]
   and therefore
   \[
      \widehat S_\Lambda
      =
      S_j-a_j(L_j-\Lambda).
   \]
   The inequality \(\widehat S_\Lambda\ge A\Lambda\) is exactly
   \(a_jL_j-S_j\le(a_j-A)\Lambda\), which is the quantile condition in
   \((LQS3)\).  The final sentence follows from
   \cref{lem:load-quantile-recycled-threshold-screen} under the standing
   assumption \(L_0<\Lambda\le L_\infty\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Variational exact-load recycled screen]
   \label{lem:variational-exact-load-recycled-screen}
   Work in the notation of
   \cref{lem:exact-load-recycled-quantile-screen}.  Define
   \[
      V_\Lambda
      =
      \min
      \left\{
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}y_qs_q:
      0\le y_q\le1,\quad
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}y_q\ell_q=\Lambda
      \right\}.
      \tag{VEL1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      V_\Lambda=\widehat S_\Lambda .
      \tag{VEL2}
   \]
   Consequently, in the non-boundary regime \(L_0<\Lambda\le L_\infty\), the
   threshold screen holds if and only if
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}y_qs_q\ge A\Lambda
      \tag{VEL3}
   \]
   for every fractional sublayer \(0\le y_q\le1\) of exact load
   \(\sum_qy_q\ell_q=\Lambda\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   This is the fractional-knapsack minimum.  If
   \(\sigma_q<\sigma_{q'}\), \(y_q<1\), and \(y_{q'}>0\), choose
   \[
      0<\delta\le\min\{(1-y_q)\ell_q,\ y_{q'}\ell_{q'}\}.
   \]
   Replacing \(y_q\) by \(y_q+\delta/\ell_q\) and \(y_{q'}\) by
   \(y_{q'}-\delta/\ell_{q'}\) preserves the exact load and changes the
   capacity by
   \[
      \delta(\sigma_q-\sigma_{q'})<0 .
   \]
   Hence an optimizer is a lowest-efficiency fractional prefix.  Since
   \(L_0<\Lambda\), every level with \(\sigma_q\le A\) is fully included, and the
   only fractional boundary can occur at the first level \(a_j\) for which
   \(L_j\ge\Lambda\).  Its value is exactly \(\widehat S_\Lambda\).

   Therefore the minimum value of the left side of \((VEL3)\) over exact-load
   fractional sublayers is \(\widehat S_\Lambda\).  The final equivalence follows
   from \cref{lem:exact-load-recycled-quantile-screen}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Exact-load margin extension]
   \label{lem:exact-load-margin-extension}
   Work in the notation of \cref{lem:exact-load-recycled-quantile-screen}, and
   assume
   \[
      \widehat S_\Lambda\ge A\Lambda .
      \tag{ELM1}
   \]
   For \(H\in(\Lambda,L_\infty]\), define
   \[
      V_H=
      \min
      \left\{
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}y_qs_q:
      0\le y_q\le1,\quad
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}y_q\ell_q=H
      \right\}.
      \tag{ELM2}
   \]
   Then, with \(j\) from \((ELQ1)\),
   \[
      V_H
      \ge
      AH+(a_j-A)(H-\Lambda)
      >
      AH .
      \tag{ELM3}
   \]
   Consequently every fractional sublayer \(0\le y_q\le1\) with load
   \(\sum_qy_q\ell_q>\Lambda\) has capacity strictly larger than \(A\) times its
   load.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   By the same fractional-knapsack exchange used in
   \cref{lem:variational-exact-load-recycled-screen}, \(V_H\) is obtained by the
   lowest-efficiency fractional prefix of load \(H\).  Since \(H>\Lambda\), this
   prefix contains the exact \(\Lambda\)-load prefix and then adds only mass with
   efficiency at least \(a_j\).  Therefore
   \[
      V_H\ge \widehat S_\Lambda+a_j(H-\Lambda).
   \]
   Using \((ELM1)\) gives the first inequality in \((ELM3)\).  The second is
   strict because \(L_0<\Lambda\) in the standing hypotheses of
   \cref{lem:exact-load-recycled-quantile-screen}, so the first crossing level
   satisfies \(a_j>A\).  Any fractional sublayer of load \(H\) has capacity at
   least \(V_H\), giving the consequence.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Dominated-load recycled screen]
   \label{lem:dominated-load-recycled-screen}
   Work in the notation of \cref{lem:exact-load-recycled-quantile-screen}.  In
   the non-boundary regime \(L_0<\Lambda\le L_\infty\), the threshold screen
   holds if and only if every probability vector \(\nu\) on \(Q^+\) satisfying
   \[
      0\le\nu_q\le\frac{\ell_q}{\Lambda},
      \qquad
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}\nu_q=1
      \tag{DLR1}
   \]
   has average efficiency at least \(A\):
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}\nu_q\sigma_q\ge A .
      \tag{DLR2}
   \]
   Failure of the threshold screen in this regime is equivalently the existence
   of such a dominated probability vector with average efficiency \(<A\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Exact-load fractional layers \(y\) are in bijection with vectors \(\nu\)
   satisfying \((DLR1)\) by
   \[
      \nu_q=\frac{y_q\ell_q}{\Lambda},
      \qquad
      y_q=\frac{\Lambda\nu_q}{\ell_q}
      \quad(q\in Q^+).
   \]
   Under this change of variables,
   \[
      \frac1\Lambda\sum_{q\in Q^+}y_qs_q
      =
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}\nu_q\frac{s_q}{\ell_q}
      =
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}\nu_q\sigma_q .
   \]
   The claim is therefore exactly
   \cref{lem:variational-exact-load-recycled-screen} divided by \(\Lambda\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Load-quantile recycled-sublayer separator suffices]
   \label{cor:load-quantile-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}
   In \cref{cor:finite-prefix-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}, the finite
   prefix condition may be replaced by the following load-quantile condition at
   each dyadic \(\Delta'\).  With \(a_i,L_i,S_i,L_\infty,A,\Lambda\) as there,
   at least one of
   \[
      A L_0-S_0=0
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      L_0\le\Lambda ,
      \tag{LQR1}
   \]
   \[
      L_\infty<\Lambda ,
      \tag{LQR2}
   \]
   or
   \[
      L_0<\Lambda\le L_\infty,
      \quad
      a_jL_j-S_j\le(a_j-A)\Lambda ,
      \qquad
      j=\min\{i\ge1:L_i\ge\Lambda\}
      \tag{LQR3}
   \]
   holds.  Then the enlarged local filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{lem:load-quantile-recycled-threshold-screen} at each dyadic
   level.  The resulting threshold screen is precisely the hypothesis needed by
   \cref{cor:threshold-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact-load recycled-sublayer separator suffices]
   \label{cor:exact-load-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}
   In \cref{cor:finite-prefix-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}, the finite
   prefix condition may be replaced by the following exact-load quantile
   condition at each dyadic \(\Delta'\).  With \(a_i,L_i,S_i,L_\infty,A,\Lambda\)
   as there, at least one of
   \[
      A L_0-S_0=0
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      L_0\le\Lambda ,
      \tag{ELR1}
   \]
   \[
      L_\infty<\Lambda ,
      \tag{ELR2}
   \]
   or
   \[
      L_0<\Lambda\le L_\infty
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      \widehat S_\Lambda\ge A\Lambda ,
      \tag{ELR3}
   \]
   holds, where \(\widehat S_\Lambda\) is the fractional quantile capacity from
   \cref{lem:exact-load-recycled-quantile-screen}.  Then the enlarged local
   filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   In the third alternative,
   \cref{lem:exact-load-recycled-quantile-screen} gives exactly the quantile
   breakpoint condition \((LQR3)\).  The first two alternatives are \((LQR1)\)
   and \((LQR2)\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:load-quantile-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices} applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Variational exact-load recycled separator suffices]
   \label{cor:variational-exact-load-recycled-separator-suffices}
   In \cref{cor:finite-prefix-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}, the finite
   prefix condition may be replaced by the following variational condition at
   each dyadic \(\Delta'\).  With \(L_0,S_0,L_\infty,A,\Lambda\) as there, at
   least one of
   \[
      A L_0-S_0=0
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      L_0\le\Lambda ,
      \tag{VER1}
   \]
   \[
      L_\infty<\Lambda ,
      \tag{VER2}
   \]
   or
   \[
      L_0<\Lambda\le L_\infty
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}y_qs_{W,\theta}(q)\ge A\Lambda
      \tag{VER3}
   \]
   for every \(0\le y_q\le1\) satisfying
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}} y_q\,\Delta'\bar\tau_q=\Lambda
      \tag{VER4}
   \]
   holds.  Then the enlarged local filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   In the third case, apply
   \cref{lem:variational-exact-load-recycled-screen} with
   \(\ell_q=\Delta'\bar\tau_q\) and \(s_q=s_{W,\theta}(q)\).  The variational
   inequality \((VER3)\)--\((VER4)\) is equivalent to
   \(\widehat S_\Lambda\ge A\Lambda\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:exact-load-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices} applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dominated-load recycled separator suffices]
   \label{cor:dominated-load-recycled-separator-suffices}
   In \cref{cor:finite-prefix-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}, the finite
   prefix condition may be replaced by the following dominated-load condition at
   each dyadic \(\Delta'\).  With \(L_0,S_0,L_\infty,A,\Lambda\) as there, at
   least one of
   \[
      A L_0-S_0=0
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      L_0\le\Lambda ,
      \tag{DLR3}
   \]
   \[
      L_\infty<\Lambda ,
      \tag{DLR4}
   \]
   or
   \[
      L_0<\Lambda\le L_\infty
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}\nu_q
      \frac{s_{W,\theta}(q)}{\Delta'\bar\tau_q}
      \ge A
      \tag{DLR5}
   \]
   for every probability vector \(\nu\) supported on queries with
   \(\bar\tau_q>0\) and satisfying
   \[
      0\le\nu_q\le\frac{\Delta'\bar\tau_q}{\Lambda},
      \qquad
      \sum_q\nu_q=1
      \tag{DLR6}
   \]
   holds.  Then the enlarged local filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   In the third case, apply \cref{lem:dominated-load-recycled-screen} with
   \(\ell_q=\Delta'\bar\tau_q\) and \(s_q=s_{W,\theta}(q)\).  The dominated-load
   inequality \((DLR5)\)--\((DLR6)\) is equivalent to the variational
   exact-load condition, so
   \cref{cor:variational-exact-load-recycled-separator-suffices} applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dominated-load recycled local-cover endpoint]
   \label{cor:dominated-load-recycled-local-cover-endpoint}
   Work under the hypotheses of \cref{cor:annular-reporter-local-cover}, assume
   finite primitive support and prefix-closed retained containers as in
   \cref{cor:recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}.  Suppose the following
   dominated-load separator holds for every guarded normalized residual and
   every single-seed annular query layer \(Q'=Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}\) satisfying
   \((SAQ1)\)--\((SAQ2)\).  There are a retained container \(W\), a size
   certificate \(|W|\le K\), a congestion parameter \(C>0\), and
   \(0\le\theta\le1\) satisfying \((HMC1)\).  Put
   \[
      m=|P|,
      \qquad
      \mathcal D_m=\{2^\ell:0\le\ell\le\lceil\log_2m\rceil\},
      \qquad
      H_m(\Delta)=|\{\Delta''\in\mathcal D_m:\Delta\le\Delta''\le m\}|,
   \]
   \[
      A=\frac{2H_m(\Delta)}{C},
      \qquad
      \Lambda=
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}
      {16J K_{|P|}H_m(\Delta)} .
      \tag{DLE1}
   \]
   For every dyadic \(\Delta'\in\mathcal D_m\) with \(\Delta'\ge\Delta\), define
   \[
      Q_{\Delta'}=\{q\in Q': |B_{z,\beta}(q)|\ge\Delta'\},
      \qquad
      \ell_q=\Delta'\bar\tau_q,
      \qquad
      s_q=s_{W,\theta}(q).
   \]
   Let \(Q_{\Delta'}^+=\{q\in Q_{\Delta'}:\ell_q>0\}\), put
   \[
      \sigma_q=\frac{s_q}{\ell_q}\qquad(q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+),
   \]
   and define
   \[
      L_0=\sum_{\substack{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+\\ \sigma_q\le A}}\ell_q,
      \qquad
      S_0=\sum_{\substack{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+\\ \sigma_q\le A}}s_q,
      \qquad
      L_\infty=\sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}\ell_q .
   \]
   Assume that at least one of the following holds for each \(\Delta'\):
   \[
      A L_0-S_0=0
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      L_0\le\Lambda ,
      \tag{DLE2}
   \]
   \[
      L_\infty<\Lambda ,
      \tag{DLE3}
   \]
   or
   \[
      L_0<\Lambda\le L_\infty
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}\nu_q\sigma_q\ge A
      \tag{DLE4}
   \]
   for every probability vector \(\nu\) on \(Q_{\Delta'}^+\) satisfying
   \[
      0\le\nu_q\le\frac{\ell_q}{\Lambda},
      \qquad
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}\nu_q=1 .
      \tag{DLE5}
   \]
   Then the enlarged local filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The alternatives \((DLE2)\)--\((DLE5)\) are exactly the dominated-load
   condition of \cref{cor:dominated-load-recycled-separator-suffices} at each
   dyadic level, with the constants from
   \cref{cor:threshold-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}.  Hence the finite
   prefix condition holds at every dyadic level, and
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices} proves local
   filter-cover feasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Finite dominated-load proposal game]
   \label{lem:finite-dominated-load-proposal-game}
   Fix the guarded residual and single-seed annular query layer in
   \cref{cor:dominated-load-recycled-local-cover-endpoint}.  Fix also one
   congestion stratum \(C\), and put \(A=2H_m(\Delta)/C\) and \(\Lambda\) as in
   \((DLE1)\).  Let
   \[
      \mathcal I\subseteq
      \{\Delta'\in\mathcal D_m:\Delta'\ge\Delta\}
   \]
   be a nonempty set of active dyadic levels for which
   \[
      Q_{\Delta'}^+=
      \{q\in Q': |B_{z,\beta}(q)|\ge\Delta',\ \Delta'\bar\tau_q>0\}
   \]
   has total load at least \(\Lambda\).  For \(\Delta'\in\mathcal I\), define
   \[
      \mathcal V_{\Delta'}
      =
      \left\{
      \nu\in\R_+^{Q_{\Delta'}^+}:
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}\nu_q=1,\quad
      \nu_q\le\frac{\Delta'\bar\tau_q}{\Lambda}
      \right\}.
      \tag{DPG1}
   \]
   Let \(\mathcal R\) be a finite family of affordable candidate records
   \(R=(W_R,K_R,\theta_R)\) such that \(W_R,K_R,C,\theta_R\) satisfy
   \((HMC1)\).  For \(R\in\mathcal R\), \(\Delta'\in\mathcal I\), and
   \(\nu\in\mathcal V_{\Delta'}\), write
   \[
      s_R^{\Delta'}(q)=s_{W_R,\theta_R}(q),
      \qquad
      \sigma_R^{\Delta'}(q)=
      \frac{s_R^{\Delta'}(q)}{\Delta'\bar\tau_q},
   \]
   and define the dominated-load margin
   \[
      M(R,\Delta',\nu)
      =
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}\nu_q\sigma_R^{\Delta'}(q)-A .
   \]
   Then
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      &\max_{\omega\in\Delta_{\mathcal R}}
      \min_{\Delta'\in\mathcal I}
      \min_{\nu\in\mathcal V_{\Delta'}}
      \sum_{R\in\mathcal R}\omega_R M(R,\Delta',\nu)\\
      &\qquad =
      \min_{\substack{\alpha\in\Delta_{\mathcal I}\\
                      \nu^{\Delta'}\in\mathcal V_{\Delta'}}}
      \max_{R\in\mathcal R}
      \sum_{\Delta'\in\mathcal I}
      \alpha_{\Delta'}M(R,\Delta',\nu^{\Delta'}).
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{DPG2}
   \]
   Consequently, there is a proposal law \(\omega\) whose averaged candidate
   passes every dominated-load test,
   \[
      \sum_{R\in\mathcal R}\omega_R
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}\nu_q\sigma_R^{\Delta'}(q)
      \ge A
      \qquad
      (\Delta'\in\mathcal I,\ \nu\in\mathcal V_{\Delta'}),
      \tag{DPG3}
   \]
   if and only if no level-weighted dominated residual
   \((\alpha,\{\nu^{\Delta'}\})\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{\Delta'\in\mathcal I}
      \alpha_{\Delta'}
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}
      \nu_q^{\Delta'}\sigma_R^{\Delta'}(q)
      < A
      \qquad(R\in\mathcal R).
      \tag{DPG4}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Each \(\mathcal V_{\Delta'}\) is a nonempty finite-dimensional polytope, and
   the margin is linear in \(\nu\).  Hence the inner minimum over
   \(\mathcal V_{\Delta'}\) is attained at an extreme point.  Let
   \[
      \mathcal E=
      \{(\Delta',e):\Delta'\in\mathcal I,
        e\in\operatorname{Ext}(\mathcal V_{\Delta'})\}.
   \]
   This set is finite.  The left side of \((DPG2)\) is the value of the finite
   matrix game
   \[
      \max_{\omega\in\Delta_{\mathcal R}}
      \min_{(\Delta',e)\in\mathcal E}
      \sum_R\omega_RM(R,\Delta',e).
   \]
   Write this value as the linear program
   \[
      \max v
      \quad\text{subject to}\quad
      \sum_R\omega_RM(R,\Delta',e)\ge v\ ((\Delta',e)\in\mathcal E),
      \quad
      \omega\in\Delta_{\mathcal R}.
   \]
   Its finite LP dual is
   \[
      \min z
      \quad\text{subject to}\quad
      \sum_{(\Delta',e)\in\mathcal E}\alpha_{\Delta',e}M(R,\Delta',e)\le z
      \ (R\in\mathcal R),
      \quad
      \alpha\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}.
   \]
   Strong duality gives equality of the two displayed values.  Finally collapse
   the dual distribution over extreme points inside each dyadic level.  Put
   \(\alpha_{\Delta'}=\sum_e\alpha_{\Delta',e}\); if
   \(\alpha_{\Delta'}>0\), define
   \[
      \nu^{\Delta'}
      =
      \alpha_{\Delta'}^{-1}
      \sum_e\alpha_{\Delta',e}e\in\mathcal V_{\Delta'}.
   \]
   Levels with \(\alpha_{\Delta'}=0\) may choose any point of
   \(\mathcal V_{\Delta'}\).  This gives the right side of \((DPG2)\), and the
   converse expansion of each \(\nu^{\Delta'}\) into extreme points gives the
   reverse inequality.

   The final statement is just the sign form of \((DPG2)\).  The compact maxima
   and minima are attained, so failure of \((DPG3)\) is equivalent to the value
   in \((DPG2)\) being strictly negative, which is exactly the existence of
   \((DPG4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact-load form of the dominated proposal obstruction]
   \label{cor:exact-load-dominated-proposal-obstruction}
   In the setting of \cref{lem:finite-dominated-load-proposal-game}, failure of
   the averaged dominated-load test \((DPG3)\) is equivalent to the existence of
   level weights \(\alpha\in\Delta_{\mathcal I}\) and, for each
   \(\Delta'\in\mathcal I\), a fractional exact-load cohort
   \(0\le y_q^{\Delta'}\le1\) on \(Q_{\Delta'}^+\) satisfying
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}
      y_q^{\Delta'}\,\Delta'\bar\tau_q
      =
      \Lambda ,
      \tag{EDP1}
   \]
   such that every affordable record \(R\in\mathcal R\) has deficient averaged
   near-shadow capacity
   \[
      \sum_{\Delta'\in\mathcal I}
      \alpha_{\Delta'}
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}
      y_q^{\Delta'}s_R^{\Delta'}(q)
      <
      A\Lambda .
      \tag{EDP2}
   \]
   Moreover each cohort \(y^{\Delta'}\) decomposes into extreme exact-load
   cohorts.  Equivalently, the same obstruction may be represented by a
   probability law \(\eta\) on pairs \((\Delta',e)\), where \(e\) is an
   exact-load cohort at level \(\Delta'\) with all but at most one coordinate in
   \(\{0,1\}\), such that
   \[
      \E_{(\Delta',e)\sim\eta}
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}e_qs_R^{\Delta'}(q)
      <
      A\Lambda
      \qquad(R\in\mathcal R).
      \tag{EDP3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Starting from the dominated residual \((\alpha,\nu^{\Delta'})\) in
   \((DPG4)\), set
   \[
      y_q^{\Delta'}
      =
      \frac{\Lambda\nu_q^{\Delta'}}{\Delta'\bar\tau_q}.
   \]
   The cap in \((DPG1)\) gives \(0\le y_q^{\Delta'}\le1\), and
   \(\sum_q\nu_q^{\Delta'}=1\) gives \((EDP1)\).  Also
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}
      \nu_q^{\Delta'}\sigma_R^{\Delta'}(q)
      =
      \frac1\Lambda
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}
      y_q^{\Delta'}s_R^{\Delta'}(q),
   \]
   so \((DPG4)\) is exactly \((EDP2)\) after multiplying by \(\Lambda\).
   The converse change of variables is identical:
   \[
      \nu_q^{\Delta'}
      =
      \frac{y_q^{\Delta'}\,\Delta'\bar\tau_q}{\Lambda}.
   \]

   The exact-load feasible region
   \[
      \{0\le y\le1:\sum_qy_q\Delta'\bar\tau_q=\Lambda\}
   \]
   is a bounded polytope, so each \(y^{\Delta'}\) is a convex combination of its
   extreme points.  Expanding these combinations and absorbing the level weight
   \(\alpha_{\Delta'}\) into the coefficients gives the law \(\eta\) and preserves
   the strict inequalities in \((EDP2)\) by linearity, giving \((EDP3)\).

   It remains only to identify the extreme points.  If two coordinates \(i,j\)
   are both strictly between \(0\) and \(1\), moving a small amount of load from
   \(i\) to \(j\) or from \(j\) to \(i\) preserves \((EDP1)\) and remains
   feasible, so the point is not extreme.  Hence an extreme point has at most one
   fractional coordinate.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact-load cohort-law separator]
   \label{cor:exact-load-cohort-law-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:finite-dominated-load-proposal-game}.  Let
   \(\mathcal E_{\rm load}\) be the finite family of pairs \((\Delta',e)\) where
   \(\Delta'\in\mathcal I\) and \(e\) is an extreme exact-load cohort at that
   level:
   \[
      0\le e_q\le1,\qquad
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}e_q\,\Delta'\bar\tau_q=\Lambda,
      \qquad
      e_q=0\text{ for }q\notin Q_{\Delta'}^+ .
   \]
   Suppose that every probability law \(\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}\)
   admits an affordable record \(R\in\mathcal R\) with
   \[
      \E_{(\Delta',e)\sim\eta}
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}e_qs_R^{\Delta'}(q)
      \ge A\Lambda .
      \tag{CLS1}
   \]
   Then there is a proposal law \(\omega\in\Delta_{\mathcal R}\) satisfying the
   averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\).

   Conversely, if no such proposal law exists, then there is a cohort law
   \(\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}\) such that every affordable record
   violates \((CLS1)\) strictly.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   This is the contrapositive of
   \cref{cor:exact-load-dominated-proposal-obstruction}.  If \((DPG3)\) fails,
   that corollary gives a law \(\eta\) over extreme exact-load cohorts satisfying
   \((EDP3)\), which is the strict failure of \((CLS1)\) for every
   \(R\in\mathcal R\).  Therefore, if every cohort law has some record satisfying
   \((CLS1)\), \((DPG3)\) cannot fail.  The converse is exactly the same
   implication read forward.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cohort-law scalar prefix normal form]
   \label{cor:cohort-law-scalar-prefix-normal-form}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:exact-load-cohort-law-separator}.  For a
   cohort law \(\eta\) and a segment parameter \(0\le\theta\le1\), define the
   cohort scalar degree
   \[
      d_\eta^\theta(p)
      =
      \E_{(\Delta',e)\sim\eta}
      \sum_{\substack{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+\\(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}
      e_q\,\bar\gamma^\theta_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{CSP1}
   \]
   For a retained parent container \(W_0\), an integer \(1\le K\le |W_0|\), and
   \(\theta\), let
   \[
      D_\eta^\theta(W_0,K)
      =
      \max_{\substack{U\subseteq W_0\\ |U|=K}}
      \sum_{p\in U}d_\eta^\theta(p).
      \tag{CSP2}
   \]
   Assume that every maximizing subset \(U\) in \((CSP2)\) can be materialized as
   an affordable record \((U,K,\theta)\in\mathcal R\) whenever
   \(U,K,C,\theta\) satisfy \((HMC1)\).  If every cohort law \(\eta\) admits
   \(W_0,K,\theta\) satisfying \((HMC1)\) and
   \[
      D_\eta^\theta(W_0,K)\ge A\Lambda ,
      \tag{CSP3}
   \]
   then the averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) such that
   every materializable affordable prefix template satisfies the strict prefix
   envelope
   \[
      D_\eta^\theta(W_0,K)< A\Lambda .
      \tag{CSP4}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For any retained record \(R=(U,K,\theta)\), Fubini's theorem and the
   definition of \(s_R^{\Delta'}\) give
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \E_{(\Delta',e)\sim\eta}
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}e_qs_R^{\Delta'}(q)
      &=
      \E_{(\Delta',e)\sim\eta}
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}
      e_q
      \sum_{\substack{p\in U\\(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}
      \bar\gamma^\theta_{p,q}r_{p,q}\\
      &=
      \sum_{p\in U}d_\eta^\theta(p).
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{CSP5}
   \]
   Thus, if \(U\) is a maximizing \(K\)-subset of \(W_0\) and \((CSP3)\) holds,
   the materialized record satisfies \((CLS1)\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:exact-load-cohort-law-separator} gives \((DPG3)\).

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, the same corollary gives a cohort law
   \(\eta\) for which every affordable record has strict capacity \(<A\Lambda\).
   Applying \((CSP5)\) to the materialized top-\(K\) records gives \((CSP4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact top-prefix cohort game]
   \label{cor:exact-top-prefix-cohort-game}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:cohort-law-scalar-prefix-normal-form}.  Let
   \(\mathcal T_{\rm ex}\) be a finite pool of affordable exact-prefix records.
   A record \(T\in\mathcal T_{\rm ex}\) consists of
   \[
      T=(W_T,\theta_T,K_T,U_T),
      \qquad
      U_T\subseteq W_T,\quad |U_T|=K_T,
   \]
   and is assumed to be materializable as an affordable retained record
   \((U_T,K_T,\theta_T)\in\mathcal R\).  For a cohort law \(\eta\), define
   \[
      V_\eta(T)=\sum_{p\in U_T}d_\eta^{\theta_T}(p),
      \qquad
      G_{\rm ex}(T,\eta)=V_\eta(T)-A\Lambda .
      \tag{ETP1}
   \]
   We use the same notation for any materializable affordable exact-prefix
   record, whether or not it belongs to the displayed finite pool.
   Then
   \[
      \max_{\omega\in\Delta_{\mathcal T_{\rm ex}}}
      \min_{\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}}
      \sum_{T\in\mathcal T_{\rm ex}}\omega_TG_{\rm ex}(T,\eta)
      =
      \min_{\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}}
      \max_{T\in\mathcal T_{\rm ex}}G_{\rm ex}(T,\eta).
      \tag{ETP2}
   \]
   If the common value in \((ETP2)\) is nonnegative, then the averaged
   dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) such
   that every materializable affordable exact-prefix record satisfies
   \[
      G_{\rm ex}(T,\eta)<0 .
      \tag{ETP3}
   \]

   Thus the logarithmic threshold in
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-template-separation-game} is not intrinsic to the
   dominated-load minimax problem.  It appears only when the separator reports a
   weaker superlevel, mass, or soft-prefix certificate.  An oracle that can
   materialize the exact top \(K\)-prefix for the cohort degree may target the
   sharper value \(A\Lambda\) directly.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(\mathcal T_{\rm ex}\) and \(\mathcal E_{\rm load}\) are finite and
   \(G_{\rm ex}(T,\eta)\) is linear in \(\eta\) and \(\omega\), \((ETP2)\) is
   the finite matrix-game minimax theorem.

   If the value is nonnegative, then for every cohort law \(\eta\) some record
   \(T\) in the support of a maximizing mixed strategy has
   \(V_\eta(T)\ge A\Lambda\).  By \((CSP5)\), the retained record
   \((U_T,K_T,\theta_T)\) satisfies the cohort capacity inequality \((CLS1)\).
   Hence \cref{cor:exact-load-cohort-law-separator} gives \((DPG3)\).

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then
   \cref{cor:cohort-law-scalar-prefix-normal-form} supplies a cohort law
   satisfying the strict envelope \((CSP4)\) for every materializable affordable
   exact prefix.  For every \(T\),
   \[
      V_\eta(T)
      \le
      D_\eta^{\theta_T}(W_T,K_T)
      <
      A\Lambda ,
   \]
   which is \((ETP3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact-prefix column generation]
   \label{cor:exact-prefix-column-generation}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:exact-top-prefix-cohort-game}.  Let
   \(\mathcal U_{\rm ex}\) be a finite full universe of materializable affordable
   exact-prefix records.  Suppose that for every cohort law \(\eta\) a build-time
   separator either returns a record \(T\in\mathcal U_{\rm ex}\) with
   \[
      G_{\rm ex}(T,\eta)\ge0
      \tag{EPC0}
   \]
   or certifies
   \[
      \max_{T\in\mathcal U_{\rm ex}}G_{\rm ex}(T,\eta)<0 .
      \tag{EPC1}
   \]
   Start with any nonempty finite pool
   \(\mathcal P\subseteq\mathcal U_{\rm ex}\), and repeatedly solve
   \[
      v_{\rm ex}(\mathcal P)
      =
      \min_{\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}}
      \max_{T\in\mathcal P}G_{\rm ex}(T,\eta).
      \tag{EPC2}
   \]
   If \(v_{\rm ex}(\mathcal P)\ge0\), then \((DPG3)\) holds.  If
   \(v_{\rm ex}(\mathcal P)<0\), call the separator on a minimizing cohort law
   \(\eta_{\mathcal P}\).  A successful call adds its returned record to the
   pool; a certificate \((EPC1)\) proves that this exact-prefix universe cannot
   close the dominated-load certificate.

   Consequently, if
   \[
      \min_{\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}}
      \max_{T\in\mathcal U_{\rm ex}}G_{\rm ex}(T,\eta)\ge0,
      \tag{EPC3}
   \]
   the procedure terminates after at most \(|\mathcal U_{\rm ex}|\) successful
   additions with a finite pool proving \((DPG3)\).  The separator and game solves
   are preprocessing only; the retained index pays only for the final verified
   pool, and the sharp threshold remains \(A\Lambda\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(v_{\rm ex}(\mathcal P)\ge0\), then
   \cref{cor:exact-top-prefix-cohort-game} applied to the current pool gives
   \((DPG3)\).

   Suppose \(v_{\rm ex}(\mathcal P)<0\), and choose a minimizer
   \(\eta_{\mathcal P}\) in \((EPC2)\).  Then
   \[
      G_{\rm ex}(T,\eta_{\mathcal P})<0
      \qquad(T\in\mathcal P).
      \tag{EPC4}
   \]
   Thus any separator output satisfying \((EPC0)\) is not already in
   \(\mathcal P\), so each successful call strictly enlarges the pool.  Since
   \(\mathcal U_{\rm ex}\) is finite, this can happen at most
   \(|\mathcal U_{\rm ex}|\) times.

   If the separator certifies \((EPC1)\), then the full universe has negative
   value at \(\eta_{\mathcal P}\), so \((EPC3)\) is false.  Under \((EPC3)\), the
   certificate \((EPC1)\) can never be valid, and finite enlargement must
   eventually reach a pool with nonnegative restricted value.  The final resource
   statement is the separation between build-time search and retained verified
   exact-prefix records in the finite cover LP.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One-sided exact-prefix value column generation]
   \label{cor:one-sided-exact-prefix-value-column-generation}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:exact-prefix-column-generation}.  For a
   cohort law \(\eta\), call \((T,X)\) a one-sided exact-prefix report if
   \(T\in\mathcal U_{\rm ex}\) and
   \[
      0\le X\le V_\eta(T).
      \tag{OEX0}
   \]
   The report is separating if
   \[
      X\ge A\Lambda .
      \tag{OEX1}
   \]
   Suppose that for every cohort law \(\eta\) a build-time oracle either returns
   a separating one-sided exact-prefix report or certifies
   \[
      \max_{T\in\mathcal U_{\rm ex}}G_{\rm ex}(T,\eta)<0 .
      \tag{OEX2}
   \]
   Then the column-generation procedure of
   \cref{cor:exact-prefix-column-generation} remains complete with this
   one-sided oracle: on a successful call, add only the verified hard record
   \(T\) to the pool, and score it in all later restricted games by its exact
   payoff \(G_{\rm ex}(T,\cdot)\).

   Consequently, if the full universe satisfies \((EPC3)\), the procedure
   terminates after finitely many successful one-sided reports with a hard-record
   pool proving \((DPG3)\).  If the oracle returns \((OEX2)\), then this exact
   universe cannot close the sharp dominated-load certificate.

   More generally, fix a cohort law \(\eta\).  A finite law, or a sampleable law
   with integrable certified surplus, over one-sided exact-prefix reports is a
   valid separator source whenever
   \[
      \E[X-A\Lambda]\ge0 .
      \tag{OEX3}
   \]
   Repeated preprocessing samples until \(X\ge A\Lambda\), and the retained
   object is again only the corresponding hard record \(T\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   A separating report satisfies
   \[
      G_{\rm ex}(T,\eta)
      =
      V_\eta(T)-A\Lambda
      \ge
      X-A\Lambda
      \ge0 .
      \tag{OEX4}
   \]
   Hence a successful one-sided oracle call is a valid separator output
   satisfying \((EPC0)\).  If the current restricted value is negative at the
   minimizing law \(\eta_{\mathcal P}\), every current pool record has
   \(G_{\rm ex}(T,\eta_{\mathcal P})<0\).  Therefore any successful one-sided
   report has \(T\notin\mathcal P\) and strictly enlarges the pool.  The
   column-generation and no-column claims are now exactly
   \cref{cor:exact-prefix-column-generation}.

   For the proposal-law statement, if a finite law has nonnegative expectation
   in \((OEX3)\), some support report has \(X-A\Lambda\ge0\).  For a sampleable
   law, if \(\Pr[X-A\Lambda\ge0]=0\), then \(X-A\Lambda<0\) almost surely; by
   integrability its expectation would be strictly negative, contradicting
   \((OEX3)\).  Thus a separating report has positive probability, and
   independent repetitions give the Las Vegas separator.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sublist-closed exact-prefix separator]
   \label{cor:sublist-closed-exact-prefix-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:exact-prefix-column-generation}.  Let
   \(\mathcal B_{\rm ex}\) be a finite family of exact-prefix templates
   \(B=(W_B,K_B,\theta_B)\), with \(1\le K_B\le |W_B|\), such that every
   \(K_B\)-point subset \(U\subseteq W_B\) is materializable as an affordable
   retained record \((U,K_B,\theta_B)\in\mathcal R\).  Let
   \(\mathcal U_{\rm ex}(\mathcal B_{\rm ex})\) be the induced finite universe of
   exact-prefix records \(T=(W_B,\theta_B,K_B,U)\).  For a cohort law \(\eta\),
   put
   \[
      H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)
      =
      D_\eta^{\theta_B}(W_B,K_B)-A\Lambda .
      \tag{SCE0}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \max_{T\in\mathcal U_{\rm ex}(\mathcal B_{\rm ex})}G_{\rm ex}(T,\eta)
      =
      \max_{B\in\mathcal B_{\rm ex}}H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta).
      \tag{SCE1}
   \]
   Consequently, if
   \[
      \min_{\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}}
      \max_{B\in\mathcal B_{\rm ex}}H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)\ge0,
      \tag{SCE2}
   \]
   then the averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) such
   that every materializable sublist-closed exact-prefix template satisfies
   \[
      H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)<0 .
      \tag{SCE3}
   \]

   Finally, suppose a build-time oracle, for every cohort law \(\eta\), either
   returns \(B\in\mathcal B_{\rm ex}\) together with a maximizing
   \(K_B\)-subset \(U\subseteq W_B\) satisfying \(H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)\ge0\), or
   certifies
   \[
      \max_{B\in\mathcal B_{\rm ex}}H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)<0 .
      \tag{SCE4}
   \]
   Then this oracle is a complete separator for
   \(\mathcal U_{\rm ex}(\mathcal B_{\rm ex})\) in
   \cref{cor:exact-prefix-column-generation}.  Under \((SCE2)\), ordinary column
   generation finds a finite verified pool proving \((DPG3)\).  The only records
   charged to the retained index are the maximizing subsets actually returned by
   the oracle.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix \(\eta\) and \(B=(W_B,K_B,\theta_B)\).  By definition,
   \(D_\eta^{\theta_B}(W_B,K_B)\) is the maximum of
   \(\sum_{p\in U}d_\eta^{\theta_B}(p)\) over all \(K_B\)-subsets of \(W_B\).
   For the corresponding exact record \(T=(W_B,\theta_B,K_B,U)\), this sum is
   \(V_\eta(T)\).  Hence maximizing \(G_{\rm ex}(T,\eta)\) over all induced
   records with this fixed template gives \(H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)\), and maximizing
   over \(B\) gives \((SCE1)\).

   If \((SCE2)\) holds, then the full exact-record universe has nonnegative value
   by \((SCE1)\), so \cref{cor:exact-prefix-column-generation} gives
   \((DPG3)\).  If \((DPG3)\) fails, then
   \cref{cor:exact-top-prefix-cohort-game} gives a cohort law for which every
   materializable exact-prefix record has negative \(G_{\rm ex}\).  Applying this
   to a maximizing subset of each sublist-closed template gives \((SCE3)\).

   For the oracle statement, a successful output gives an exact record
   \(T=(W_B,\theta_B,K_B,U)\) with
   \[
      G_{\rm ex}(T,\eta)=H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)\ge0,
   \]
   while \((SCE4)\) is exactly \((EPC1)\) by \((SCE1)\).  Thus the hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:exact-prefix-column-generation} hold for the induced exact-record
   universe, proving the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[No-loss exact cardinality net]
   \label{cor:no-loss-exact-cardinality-net}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:sublist-closed-exact-prefix-separator}.  Let
   \(b\ge1\).  Suppose the searched exact-prefix templates are organized by
   retained parent containers and segment parameters, with a finite cardinality
   net \(\mathcal K^{\rm ex}_{W,\theta}\) satisfying: for every
   \(1\le h\le |W|\) there is \(K\in\mathcal K^{\rm ex}_{W,\theta}\) such that
   \[
      h\le K\le b h,
      \tag{ECN0}
   \]
   and every \(K\)-point sublist of \(W\) is materializable as an affordable
   exact-prefix record.  Let \(\mathcal B_{\rm ex}\) be the resulting finite
   template family \(B=(W,K,\theta)\), with
   \(K\in\mathcal K^{\rm ex}_{W,\theta}\).

   If every cohort law \(\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}\) admits a
   searched retained parent \(W\), segment \(\theta\), and analytic prefix size
   \(1\le h\le |W|\) satisfying
   \[
      D_\eta^\theta(W,h)\ge A\Lambda ,
      \tag{ECN1}
   \]
   then \((SCE2)\) holds for this \(\mathcal B_{\rm ex}\), and hence the
   averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) such that
   every searched retained parent \(W\), segment \(\theta\), and analytic prefix
   size \(1\le h\le |W|\) satisfies
   \[
      D_\eta^\theta(W,h)<A\Lambda .
      \tag{ECN2}
   \]
   In particular, powers of two are enough, with \(b=2\), and introduce no
   threshold loss on the exact-prefix route.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The cohort degrees are nonnegative, so the top-prefix mass is monotone in the
   prefix size:
   \[
      h\le K
      \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
      D_\eta^\theta(W,h)\le D_\eta^\theta(W,K).
      \tag{ECN3}
   \]
   If \((ECN1)\) holds, choose \(K\in\mathcal K^{\rm ex}_{W,\theta}\) satisfying
   \((ECN0)\).  Then \((ECN3)\) gives
   \(D_\eta^\theta(W,K)\ge A\Lambda\), so the template
   \(B=(W,K,\theta)\) has \(H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)\ge0\).  This is exactly the
   pointwise condition implying \((SCE2)\), and
   \cref{cor:sublist-closed-exact-prefix-separator} gives \((DPG3)\).

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then
   \cref{cor:sublist-closed-exact-prefix-separator} gives a cohort law \(\eta\)
   for which every net template has \(H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)<0\).  Given any analytic
   \(h\), choose \(K\in\mathcal K^{\rm ex}_{W,\theta}\) with \(h\le K\le bh\).
   Then
   \[
      D_\eta^\theta(W,h)
      \le
      D_\eta^\theta(W,K)
      <
      A\Lambda ,
   \]
   proving \((ECN2)\).  Powers of two are \(2\)-dense from above.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Exact-template linearization]
   \label{rem:exact-template-linearization}
   The exact-template payoff
   \[
      H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)=D_\eta^{\theta_B}(W_B,K_B)-A\Lambda
   \]
   should be used as a fixed-\(\eta\) separation objective, not as a bilinear
   matrix-game payoff in the template variable.  Indeed,
   \(D_\eta^\theta(W,K)\) is the maximum over \(K\)-subsets \(U\subseteq W\) of
   the linear function
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U}d_\eta^\theta(p),
   \]
   so it is convex in the cohort law \(\eta\).  The finite minimax theorem applies
   only after linearizing the template by materializing the maximizing sublist
   \(U\), namely to the exact record payoff \(G_{\rm ex}(T,\eta)\) in
   \cref{cor:exact-top-prefix-cohort-game}.  Thus
   \cref{cor:sublist-closed-exact-prefix-separator},
   \cref{cor:no-loss-exact-cardinality-net}, and the proposal-law statements below
   are separation-oracle statements for the current cohort law: they find a
   positive exact record or certify that the searched template universe has no
   positive exact record for that \(\eta\).  They do not assert a separate
   mixed-template minimax theorem for \(H_{\rm ex}\).
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Average-mass exact-prefix screen]
   \label{cor:average-mass-exact-prefix-screen}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:no-loss-exact-cardinality-net}.  Fix a
   cohort law \(\eta\), a searched retained parent \(W\), a segment
   \(\theta\), and a cardinality \(K\in\mathcal K^{\rm ex}_{W,\theta}\).  Let
   \(S\subseteq W\) have size \(s\ge K\), and suppose preprocessing gives a
   one-sided mass certificate
   \[
      0\le M\le\sum_{p\in S}d_\eta^\theta(p).
      \tag{AEX0}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      D_\eta^\theta(W,K)\ge \frac{K}{s}M.
      \tag{AEX1}
   \]
   Consequently, if
   \[
      \frac{K}{s}M\ge A\Lambda ,
      \tag{AEX2}
   \]
   then the template \(B=(W,K,\theta)\) has \(H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)\ge0\), and
   materializing the top \(K\)-subset of \(W\) gives a valid exact-prefix
   separator output.

   More generally, a finite law, or a sampleable law with integrable certified
   surplus, over reports \((W,\theta,K,S,s,M)\) satisfying \((AEX0)\) is a valid
   exact-prefix proposal law whenever
   \[
      \E\left[\frac{K}{s}M-A\Lambda\right]\ge0 .
      \tag{AEX3}
   \]
   In the sampled case, repeated preprocessing samples and verifies reports until
   one satisfies \((AEX2)\); only the resulting deterministic top-\(K\) record is
   retained.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Order the points of \(S\) by decreasing \(d_\eta^\theta\)-value, and let
   \(U\subseteq S\) be the first \(K\) points.  Since the average of the top
   \(K\) values is at least the average over all \(s\) values,
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U}d_\eta^\theta(p)
      \ge
      \frac{K}{s}\sum_{p\in S}d_\eta^\theta(p)
      \ge
      \frac{K}{s}M .
   \]
   Because \(U\) is one feasible \(K\)-subset of \(W\), this proves \((AEX1)\).
   Condition \((AEX2)\) then gives \(D_\eta^\theta(W,K)\ge A\Lambda\), hence
   \(H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)\ge0\), and
   \cref{cor:sublist-closed-exact-prefix-separator} accepts the materialized
   top-\(K\) record.

   The finite-law statement follows by averaging: if the expectation in
   \((AEX3)\) is nonnegative, one support report has nonnegative certified
   surplus.  For a sampleable law, put \(\Psi=KM/s-A\Lambda\).  If
   \(\Pr[\Psi\ge0]=0\), then \(\Psi<0\) almost surely, and integrability would
   force \(\E\Psi<0\), contradicting \((AEX3)\).  Thus a report satisfying
   \((AEX2)\) has positive probability, and independent repetitions give the
   Las Vegas separator.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Average-density exact-prefix scale choice]
   \label{cor:average-density-exact-prefix-scale-choice}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:no-loss-exact-cardinality-net}.  Fix a
   cohort law \(\eta\), searched retained parent \(W\), segment \(\theta\), and
   subset \(S\subseteq W\) of size \(s\ge1\).  Suppose preprocessing gives a
   one-sided mass certificate
   \[
      0\le M\le\sum_{p\in S}d_\eta^\theta(p)
      \tag{DEX0}
   \]
   and
   \[
      M\ge A\Lambda>0 .
      \tag{DEX1}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      h_*=
      \left\lceil\frac{A\Lambda\,s}{M}\right\rceil .
      \tag{DEX2}
   \]
   Then \(1\le h_*\le s\).  If the exact cardinality net contains
   \(K\in\mathcal K^{\rm ex}_{W,\theta}\) with
   \[
      h_*\le K\le b h_*,
      \tag{DEX3}
   \]
   then the template \(B=(W,K,\theta)\) has \(H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)\ge0\), and
   materializing the top \(K\)-subset gives a valid exact-prefix separator output.

   More generally, a finite law, or a sampleable law with integrable \(M-A\Lambda\),
   over coarse reports \((W,\theta,S,s,M)\) satisfying \((DEX0)\) is a valid
   exact-prefix proposal source whenever
   \[
      \E[M-A\Lambda]\ge0.
      \tag{DEX4}
   \]
   The separator samples until \((DEX1)\) holds, chooses \(h_*\) and then any net
   \(K\) satisfying \((DEX3)\), which exists by \((ECN0)\), and stores only the
   resulting deterministic top-\(K\) record.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(M\le\sum_{p\in S}d_\eta^\theta(p)\) and \((DEX1)\) holds, \(M>0\).
   Also \(A\Lambda s/M\le s\), so \(1\le h_*\le s\).  From \((DEX2)\),
   \[
      \frac{h_*}{s}M\ge A\Lambda .
      \tag{DEX5}
   \]
   The top \(h_*\) points of \(S\) have mass at least \(h_*M/s\), so
   \(D_\eta^\theta(W,h_*)\ge A\Lambda\).  Since the top-prefix value is monotone
   in the cardinality and \(K\ge h_*\), we get
   \(D_\eta^\theta(W,K)\ge A\Lambda\), i.e. \(H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)\ge0\).

   For a finite law, nonnegative expectation in \((DEX4)\) implies one support
   report has \(M\ge A\Lambda\).  For a sampleable law, if
   \(\Pr[M-A\Lambda\ge0]=0\), then \(M-A\Lambda<0\) almost surely; integrability
   would force \(\E[M-A\Lambda]<0\), contradicting \((DEX4)\).  Hence a closing
   report has positive probability, and independent repetitions give the
   Las Vegas separator.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Soft average-density exact-prefix scale choice]
   \label{cor:soft-average-density-exact-prefix-scale-choice}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:no-loss-exact-cardinality-net}.  Fix a
   cohort law \(\eta\), searched retained parent \(W\), and segment \(\theta\).
   Let \(\pi=(\pi_p)_{p\in W}\) be a responsibility vector with
   \(0\le\pi_p\le1\), and put
   \[
      \mu=\sum_{p\in W}\pi_p .
      \tag{SDEX0}
   \]
   Suppose preprocessing gives a one-sided soft value certificate
   \[
      0\le X\le\sum_{p\in W}\pi_p d_\eta^\theta(p)
      \tag{SDEX1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      X\ge A\Lambda>0 .
      \tag{SDEX2}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      h_*=
      \left\lceil\frac{A\Lambda\,\mu}{X}\right\rceil .
      \tag{SDEX3}
   \]
   Then \(1\le h_*\le |W|\).  If the exact cardinality net contains
   \(K\in\mathcal K^{\rm ex}_{W,\theta}\) with
   \[
      h_*\le K\le b h_*,
      \tag{SDEX4}
   \]
   then the template \(B=(W,K,\theta)\) has \(H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)\ge0\), and
   materializing the top \(K\)-subset gives a valid exact-prefix separator output.

   More generally, a finite law, or a sampleable law with integrable \(X-A\Lambda\),
   over soft reports \((W,\theta,\pi,\mu,X)\) satisfying \(0\le\pi_p\le1\) and
   \((SDEX0)\)--\((SDEX1)\) is a valid exact-prefix proposal source whenever
   \[
      \E[X-A\Lambda]\ge0 .
      \tag{SDEX5}
   \]
   The separator samples until \((SDEX2)\) holds, chooses \(h_*\) and then any
   net \(K\) satisfying \((SDEX4)\), which exists by \((ECN0)\), and stores only
   the resulting deterministic top-\(K\) record.  The hard-support statement
   \cref{cor:average-density-exact-prefix-scale-choice} is the special case
   \(\pi=\mathbf 1_S\), \(\mu=|S|\), and \(X=M\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Under \((SDEX2)\), \((SDEX1)\) implies \(\mu>0\).  Since
   \(A\Lambda\le X\) and \(\mu\le |W|\), we have
   \(1\le h_*\le\lceil\mu\rceil\le |W|\).

   Order \(W=\{p_1,\ldots,p_m\}\) so that
   \(d_i=d_\eta^\theta(p_i)\) is nonincreasing, and put
   \(D(h)=\sum_{i\le h}d_i\).  Let \(F(t)\) be the fractional top-\(t\) mass,
   \[
      F(t)=D(\lfloor t\rfloor)
      +(t-\lfloor t\rfloor)d_{\lfloor t\rfloor+1},
      \qquad 0\le t\le m,
      \tag{SDEX6}
   \]
   with the last term omitted at \(t=m\).  Since \(\pi\in[0,1]^W\) has total
   mass \(\mu\), the fractional rearrangement bound gives
   \[
      \sum_{p\in W}\pi_p d_\eta^\theta(p)\le F(\mu).
      \tag{SDEX7}
   \]
   Also \(F(t)\) is nondecreasing and \(F(t)/t\) is nonincreasing for
   \(t>0\).  Therefore, for every integer \(h\),
   \[
      D(h)=F(h)
      \ge
      \min\{h/\mu,1\}\,F(\mu)
      \ge
      \min\{h/\mu,1\}\,X .
      \tag{SDEX8}
   \]
   Applying this to \(h=h_*\), if \(h_*<\mu\) then
   \(D(h_*)\ge h_*X/\mu\ge A\Lambda\), while if \(h_*\ge\mu\) then
   \(D(h_*)\ge X\ge A\Lambda\).  Thus
   \(D_\eta^\theta(W,h_*)\ge A\Lambda\).  Monotonicity in the cardinality and
   \(K\ge h_*\) give \(D_\eta^\theta(W,K)\ge A\Lambda\), hence
   \(H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)\ge0\).

   For a finite law, nonnegative expectation in \((SDEX5)\) implies one support
   report has \(X\ge A\Lambda\).  For a sampleable law, if
   \(\Pr[X-A\Lambda\ge0]=0\), then \(X-A\Lambda<0\) almost surely; integrability
   would force \(\E[X-A\Lambda]<0\), contradicting \((SDEX5)\).  Hence a
   closing report has positive probability, and independent repetitions give the
   Las Vegas separator.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Soft exact-prefix relaxation is tight]
   \label{cor:soft-exact-prefix-relaxation-tight}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:no-loss-exact-cardinality-net}.  For a
   cohort law \(\eta\), a searched retained parent \(W\), a segment \(\theta\),
   and a responsibility vector \(0\le\pi_p\le1\), define
   \[
      P_\eta^\theta(W,\pi)
      =
      \sum_{p\in W}\pi_p d_\eta^\theta(p).
      \tag{SER0}
   \]
   If every cohort law \(\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}\) admits a
   searched \(W,\theta\) and a responsibility vector \(\pi\in[0,1]^W\) satisfying
   \[
      P_\eta^\theta(W,\pi)\ge A\Lambda ,
      \tag{SER1}
   \]
   then the averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) such that
   every searched \(W,\theta\) and every responsibility vector
   \(\pi\in[0,1]^W\) satisfy
   \[
      P_\eta^\theta(W,\pi)<A\Lambda .
      \tag{SER2}
   \]
   Thus soft responsibilities, capped marginals, and learned assignment weights
   introduce no relaxation gap on the sharp exact-prefix route: they are only a
   proposal language for finding one hard top-prefix column.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((SER1)\) holds, apply
   \cref{cor:soft-average-density-exact-prefix-scale-choice} with
   \(X=P_\eta^\theta(W,\pi)\).  This gives a materialized top-prefix separator
   for every cohort law, hence \((DPG3)\).

   Conversely suppose \((DPG3)\) fails.  By
   \cref{cor:no-loss-exact-cardinality-net}, there is a cohort law \(\eta\) for
   which every searched retained parent \(W\), segment \(\theta\), and analytic
   prefix size \(1\le h\le |W|\) obeys \(D_\eta^\theta(W,h)<A\Lambda\).
   Fix \(W,\theta\), order \(W=\{p_1,\ldots,p_m\}\) so that
   \(d_i=d_\eta^\theta(p_i)\) is nonincreasing, and let \(F\) be the fractional
   top-mass curve from \((SDEX6)\).  For any \(\pi\in[0,1]^W\) with
   \(\mu=\sum_p\pi_p\), the rearrangement bound gives
   \[
      P_\eta^\theta(W,\pi)\le F(\mu).
      \tag{SER3}
   \]
   If \(\mu=0\), then \(P_\eta^\theta(W,\pi)=0<A\Lambda\).  If
   \(k<\mu<k+1\), then \(F(\mu)\) is a convex combination of
   \(D_\eta^\theta(W,k)\) and \(D_\eta^\theta(W,k+1)\), with
   \(D_\eta^\theta(W,0)=0\).  Both endpoint values are \(<A\Lambda\).  If
   \(\mu\) is an integer, \(F(\mu)=D_\eta^\theta(W,\mu)<A\Lambda\).  Hence
   \(P_\eta^\theta(W,\pi)<A\Lambda\) for every responsibility vector, proving
   \((SER2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite soft exact-prefix oracle]
   \label{cor:finite-soft-exact-prefix-oracle}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:no-loss-exact-cardinality-net}.  Let
   \(\mathcal B_{\rm soft}\) be a finite pool of soft templates
   \(B=(W_B,\theta_B,\pi_B)\), where \(W_B\) is a searched retained parent,
   \(0\le\pi_{B,p}\le1\), and all top-prefix records in \(W_B\) at retained
   cardinalities are materializable as in \((ECN0)\).  Let
   \(\mathcal T_{\rm ex}(\mathcal B_{\rm soft})\) be the finite hard universe
   consisting of every materializable record
   \[
      T=(W_B,\theta_B,K,U),
      \qquad
      B\in\mathcal B_{\rm soft},\quad
      K\in\mathcal K_{W_B,\theta_B},\quad
      U\subseteq W_B,\quad |U|=K .
      \tag{FSE0}
   \]
   Define
   \[
      P_\eta(B)
      =
      \sum_{p\in W_B}\pi_{B,p}d_\eta^{\theta_B}(p),
      \qquad
      G_{\rm soft}(B,\eta)=P_\eta(B)-A\Lambda .
      \tag{FSE1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \max_{\omega\in\Delta_{\mathcal B_{\rm soft}}}
      \min_{\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}}
      \sum_{B\in\mathcal B_{\rm soft}}\omega_BG_{\rm soft}(B,\eta)
      =
      \min_{\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}}
      \max_{B\in\mathcal B_{\rm soft}}G_{\rm soft}(B,\eta).
      \tag{FSE2}
   \]
   If the common value is nonnegative, then the averaged dominated-load
   certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.  Equivalently, it is enough that every cohort
   law \(\eta\) have some soft template \(B\in\mathcal B_{\rm soft}\) with
   \[
      P_\eta(B)\ge A\Lambda .
      \tag{FSE3}
   \]

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) such that
   every soft template in the pool satisfies
   \[
      P_\eta(B)<A\Lambda .
      \tag{FSE4}
   \]

   Thus a finite pool of \(k\)-means++, additive-quantization, learned,
   list-recovery, or LP-range-reporting soft panels may be used at the sharp
   \(A\Lambda\) threshold.  The retained index stores only the hard top-prefix
   record materialized from a positive soft template; failed soft templates are
   discarded.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The equality \((FSE2)\) is the finite matrix-game minimax theorem, since
   \(G_{\rm soft}(B,\eta)\) is linear in both the mixed template law and the
   cohort law.

   If the common value is nonnegative, then every cohort law \(\eta\) has a
   template \(B=(W,\theta,\pi)\) satisfying \((FSE3)\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:soft-average-density-exact-prefix-scale-choice} with
   \(X=P_\eta(B)\) materializes a hard top-prefix separator for this cohort law.
   By construction this separator belongs to the finite hard universe
   \(\mathcal T_{\rm ex}(\mathcal B_{\rm soft})\).  Thus, for every \(\eta\),
   some \(T\in\mathcal T_{\rm ex}(\mathcal B_{\rm soft})\) has
   \(G_{\rm ex}(T,\eta)\ge0\), where \(G_{\rm ex}\) is defined in \((ETP1)\).
   Applying \cref{cor:exact-top-prefix-cohort-game} to this finite induced hard
