   universe gives \((DPG3)\).

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then
   \cref{cor:soft-exact-prefix-relaxation-tight} supplies a cohort law \(\eta\)
   for which every searched \(W,\theta\) and every responsibility vector
   \(\pi\in[0,1]^W\) has value below \(A\Lambda\).  In particular every
   \(B\in\mathcal B_{\rm soft}\) satisfies \((FSE4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Soft exact-prefix column generation]
   \label{cor:soft-exact-prefix-column-generation}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:finite-soft-exact-prefix-oracle}.  Let
   \(\mathcal U_{\rm soft}\) be a finite implicit universe of soft templates,
   and let \(\mathcal U_{\rm ex}(\mathcal U_{\rm soft})\) be the finite induced
   universe of all materializable exact-prefix records in their retained parents
   at retained cardinalities.  Thus every positive soft template can be converted
   by \cref{cor:soft-average-density-exact-prefix-scale-choice} into a record in
   \(\mathcal U_{\rm ex}(\mathcal U_{\rm soft})\).  Throughout,
   \(G_{\rm ex}\) is the hard-record payoff from \((ETP1)\).
   Suppose that for every cohort law \(\eta\), a build-time separator either
   returns \(B\in\mathcal U_{\rm soft}\) with
   \[
      G_{\rm soft}(B,\eta)\ge0
      \tag{FSC0}
   \]
   or certifies
   \[
      \max_{B\in\mathcal U_{\rm soft}}G_{\rm soft}(B,\eta)<0 .
      \tag{FSC1}
   \]
   Start with any nonempty finite hard-record pool
   \(\mathcal P\subseteq\mathcal U_{\rm ex}(\mathcal U_{\rm soft})\), and
   repeatedly solve
   \[
      v_{\rm ex}(\mathcal P)
      =
      \min_{\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}}
      \max_{T\in\mathcal P}G_{\rm ex}(T,\eta).
      \tag{FSC2}
   \]
   If \(v_{\rm ex}(\mathcal P)\ge0\), then \((DPG3)\) holds.  If
   \(v_{\rm ex}(\mathcal P)<0\), call the soft separator on a minimizing cohort
   law.  A successful call returns a soft template \(B\); materialize the hard
   top-prefix record \(T_B(\eta)\in\mathcal U_{\rm ex}(\mathcal U_{\rm soft})\)
   exposed by \cref{cor:soft-average-density-exact-prefix-scale-choice} and add
   that verified hard record to \(\mathcal P\).  A certificate \((FSC1)\) proves
   that this implicit soft universe cannot close the sharp exact-prefix
   certificate.

   Consequently, if
   \[
      \min_{\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}}
      \max_{B\in\mathcal U_{\rm soft}}G_{\rm soft}(B,\eta)\ge0,
      \tag{FSC3}
   \]
   then the procedure terminates after at most
   \(|\mathcal U_{\rm ex}(\mathcal U_{\rm soft})|\) successful additions with a
   finite hard-record pool proving \((DPG3)\).  All soft templates and failed
   separator calls are build-time evidence only; the retained index pays only for
   the verified hard prefixes actually added to \(\mathcal P\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(v_{\rm ex}(\mathcal P)\ge0\), then
   \cref{cor:exact-top-prefix-cohort-game} applied to the current hard pool gives
   \((DPG3)\).  If \(v_{\rm ex}(\mathcal P)<0\), choose a minimizing cohort law
   \(\eta_{\mathcal P}\).  Every current hard record has
   \(G_{\rm ex}(T,\eta_{\mathcal P})<0\).  A separator output satisfying
   \((FSC0)\) has \(P_{\eta_{\mathcal P}}(B)\ge A\Lambda\), so
   \cref{cor:soft-average-density-exact-prefix-scale-choice} materializes a hard
   exact-prefix record \(T_B(\eta_{\mathcal P})\) with
   \(G_{\rm ex}(T_B(\eta_{\mathcal P}),\eta_{\mathcal P})\ge0\).  This record is
   not already in \(\mathcal P\), and each successful call strictly enlarges the
   hard pool.  Since the induced hard universe is finite, this happens at most
   \(|\mathcal U_{\rm ex}(\mathcal U_{\rm soft})|\) times.  If the separator
   certifies \((FSC1)\), then \((FSC3)\) is false at \(\eta_{\mathcal P}\).
   Under \((FSC3)\), that certificate cannot be valid, so finite enlargement
   eventually reaches a nonnegative restricted exact-record value.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact-prefix proposal-law separator]
   \label{cor:exact-prefix-proposal-law-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:sublist-closed-exact-prefix-separator}, and fix a cohort law
   \(\eta\).  Let \(\zeta\) be a finite probability law over
   \(\mathcal B_{\rm ex}\).  If
   \[
      \E_{B\sim\zeta}H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)\ge0,
      \tag{SEP0}
   \]
   then the support of \(\zeta\) contains a template \(B\) with
   \(H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)\ge0\).  Materializing a maximizing \(K_B\)-subset of this
   \(B\) gives a valid exact-prefix separator output.

   Conversely, if the exact no-column certificate
   \[
      \max_{B\in\mathcal B_{\rm ex}}H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)<0
      \tag{SEP1}
   \]
   holds, then every finite proposal law over \(\mathcal B_{\rm ex}\) satisfies
   \[
      \E_{B\sim\zeta}H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)<0 .
      \tag{SEP2}
   \]

   The same conclusion has a Las Vegas sampled form.  Suppose preprocessing has a
   sampleable law \(\mathfrak B_\eta\) on \(\mathcal B_{\rm ex}\), the random
   variable \(H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)\) is integrable, and
   \[
      \E_{B\sim\mathfrak B_\eta}H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)\ge0.
      \tag{SEP3}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \Pr_{B\sim\mathfrak B_\eta}[H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)\ge0]>0.
      \tag{SEP4}
   \]
   Repeated independent sampling from \(\mathfrak B_\eta\), followed by exact
   top-\(K_B\) materialization and verification of \(H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)\ge0\), is
   therefore a Las Vegas separator for the current cohort law.  If the probability
   in \((SEP4)\) is \(\pi_\eta\), the expected number of samples is
   \(1/\pi_\eta\).  Only the accepted deterministic top-prefix record is retained.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If every support template had \(H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)<0\), the finite average in
   \((SEP0)\) would be negative.  Thus some support template has nonnegative
   \(H_{\rm ex}\), and \cref{cor:sublist-closed-exact-prefix-separator} makes its
   maximizing subset a valid exact-prefix separator output.

   Under \((SEP1)\), every support template has strictly negative \(H_{\rm ex}\),
   so every finite average is strictly negative, proving \((SEP2)\).

   For the sampled statement, if the event in \((SEP4)\) had probability zero,
   then \(H_{\rm ex}(B,\eta)<0\) almost surely.  Since \(H_{\rm ex}\) is
   integrable, its expectation would be strictly negative, contradicting
   \((SEP3)\).  The Las Vegas and expected-sample claims are the standard
   geometric waiting-time calculation, and each successful sample is a valid
   separator by the first paragraph.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sampled soft exact-prefix proposal separator]
   \label{cor:sampled-soft-exact-prefix-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:exact-prefix-proposal-law-separator}.  A soft
   exact-prefix proposal for a cohort law \(\eta\) is a tuple
   \[
      R=(W_R,K_R,\theta_R,\pi_R,X_R)
   \]
   such that \(B_R=(W_R,K_R,\theta_R)\in\mathcal B_{\rm ex}\),
   \[
      0\le \pi_{R,p}\le1,\qquad
      \sum_{p\in W_R}\pi_{R,p}\le K_R,
      \tag{SEP5}
   \]
   and the proposal gives a one-sided value certificate
   \[
      0\le X_R\le
      \sum_{p\in W_R}\pi_{R,p}d_\eta^{\theta_R}(p).
      \tag{SEP6}
   \]
   Assume that whenever such a tuple is sampled, preprocessing can materialize a
   \(K_R\)-point maximizer
   \[
      U_R^*\in
      \arg\max_{\substack{U\subseteq W_R\\ |U|=K_R}}
      \sum_{p\in U}d_\eta^{\theta_R}(p).
      \tag{SEP7}
   \]
   If preprocessing has a sampleable law on soft exact-prefix proposals with
   integrable surplus and
   \[
      \E\bigl[X_R-A\Lambda\bigr]\ge0,
      \tag{SEP8}
   \]
   then repeated sampling, exact materialization of \(U_R^*\), and verification of
   \(X_R\ge A\Lambda\) form a Las Vegas exact-prefix separator for the current
   cohort law.

   Thus a randomized \(k\)-means++, additive-quantization, range-reporting,
   list-recovery, or learned panel may be analyzed through soft inclusion
   responsibilities and a one-sided lower value certificate while staying on the
   sharp \(A\Lambda\) threshold.  The retained index stores only the deterministic
   exact-prefix record \((U_R^*,K_R,\theta_R)\), never the soft proposal itself.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For any admissible proposal, the exact top-\(K_R\) set dominates the soft
   responsibility vector.  The polytope
   \[
      \left\{x\in[0,1]^{W_R}:\sum_{p\in W_R}x_p\le K_R\right\}
   \]
   has integral vertices, each the indicator of a subset of size at most \(K_R\).
   Since \(d_\eta^{\theta_R}(p)\ge0\), the maximum of
   \(\sum_p x_pd_\eta^{\theta_R}(p)\) over this polytope is attained by a
   \(K_R\)-point top prefix.  Hence
   \[
      D_\eta^{\theta_R}(W_R,K_R)
      =
      \sum_{p\in U_R^*}d_\eta^{\theta_R}(p)
      \ge
      \sum_{p\in W_R}\pi_{R,p}d_\eta^{\theta_R}(p)
      \ge X_R .
      \tag{SEP9}
   \]
   Therefore \(X_R\ge A\Lambda\) implies
   \(H_{\rm ex}(B_R,\eta)\ge0\).

   Put \(\Psi_R=X_R-A\Lambda\).  If
   \(\Pr[\Psi_R\ge0]=0\), then \(\Psi_R<0\) almost surely, and integrability
   would force \(\E\Psi_R<0\), contradicting \((SEP8)\).  Thus a sample with
   \(X_R\ge A\Lambda\) has positive probability.  Such a sample gives
   \(H_{\rm ex}(B_R,\eta)\ge0\) by the previous paragraph, so
   \cref{cor:sublist-closed-exact-prefix-separator} accepts the materialized
   exact-prefix record.  Independent repetitions give the Las Vegas separator.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cohort-law weak-type superlevel normal form]
   \label{cor:cohort-law-weak-type-superlevel}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:cohort-law-scalar-prefix-normal-form}.  For a cohort law \(\eta\),
   a segment parameter \(\theta\), a retained parent container \(W_0\), and a
   level \(\delta>0\), put
   \[
      U_{\eta,\theta,\delta}(W_0)
      =
      \{p\in W_0:d_\eta^\theta(p)\ge\delta\},
      \qquad
      h_{\eta,\theta,\delta}(W_0)=|U_{\eta,\theta,\delta}(W_0)|.
      \tag{CWS1}
   \]
   Assume that every nonempty set \(U_{\eta,\theta,\delta}(W_0)\) can be
   materialized as an affordable record
   \[
      (U_{\eta,\theta,\delta}(W_0),
       h_{\eta,\theta,\delta}(W_0),\theta)\in\mathcal R
   \]
   whenever its size certificate and \(\theta\) satisfy \((HMC1)\).  If every
   cohort law \(\eta\) admits \(W_0,\theta,\delta\) with
   \(h=h_{\eta,\theta,\delta}(W_0)>0\), such that the superlevel record
   \((U_{\eta,\theta,\delta}(W_0),h,\theta)\) satisfies \((HMC1)\), and
   \[
      \delta h\ge A\Lambda ,
      \tag{CWS2}
   \]
   then the averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) such that
   every materializable affordable superlevel satisfies the strict weak-type
   envelope
   \[
      \delta\,h_{\eta,\theta,\delta}(W_0)<A\Lambda .
      \tag{CWS3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((CWS2)\) holds, then the materialized superlevel record \(R=(U,h,\theta)\)
   has capacity, by \((CSP5)\),
   \[
      \E_{(\Delta',e)\sim\eta}
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}e_qs_R^{\Delta'}(q)
      =
      \sum_{p\in U}d_\eta^\theta(p)
      \ge
      \delta h
      \ge
      A\Lambda .
   \]
   Hence \((CLS1)\) holds for this cohort law, and
   \cref{cor:exact-load-cohort-law-separator} gives \((DPG3)\).

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then
   \cref{cor:cohort-law-scalar-prefix-normal-form} gives a cohort law satisfying
   the strict prefix envelope \((CSP4)\).  For a materializable affordable
   superlevel with \(h>0\), the top \(h\) points in \(W_0\) have mass at least
   \(\delta h\), so
   \[
      \delta h
      \le
      D_\eta^\theta(W_0,h)
      <
      A\Lambda .
   \]
   This is \((CWS3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Certified cohort-law superlevel reporter]
   \label{cor:certified-cohort-law-superlevel-reporter}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:cohort-law-weak-type-superlevel}.  For a
   cohort law \(\eta\), call
   \[
      (W_0,\theta,\delta,U,K,X)
   \]
   an \(\eta\)-superlevel report if
   \[
      U=\{p\in W_0:d_\eta^\theta(p)\ge\delta\},
      \qquad
      h=|U|>0,
      \tag{CWR0}
   \]
   the report gives one-sided certificates
   \[
      h\le K,
      \qquad
      0\le X\le \delta h,
      \tag{CWR1}
   \]
   and the retained record with update side \(U\), size certificate \(K\), and
   segment parameter \(\theta\) is affordable:
   \[
      (U,K,\theta)\in\mathcal R .
      \tag{CWR2}
   \]
   Here \(K\) may be a certified upper bound rather than the exact size; if the
   retained pool stores only exact-size records, take \(K=h\).

   Suppose that every cohort law \(\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}\)
   admits an \(\eta\)-superlevel report satisfying
   \[
      X\ge A\Lambda .
      \tag{CWR3}
   \]
   Then the averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.  More
   generally, it is enough that every \(\eta\) admits a finite probability law
   \(\zeta\) over \(\eta\)-superlevel reports with
   \[
      \E_{(W_0,\theta,\delta,U,K,X)\sim\zeta}X\ge A\Lambda ,
      \tag{CWR4}
   \]
   since some deterministic report in the support then satisfies \((CWR3)\).

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) for
   which every affordable \(\eta\)-superlevel report satisfies
   \[
      X<A\Lambda .
      \tag{CWR5}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \((W_0,\theta,\delta,U,K,X)\) be an \(\eta\)-superlevel report satisfying
   \((CWR3)\).  Since every point of \(U\) has
   \(d_\eta^\theta(p)\ge\delta\),
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U}d_\eta^\theta(p)\ge\delta h\ge X\ge A\Lambda .
      \tag{CWR6}
   \]
   By \((CSP5)\), the affordable retained record \(R=(U,K,\theta)\) therefore
   satisfies the cohort capacity inequality \((CLS1)\).  If every cohort law has
   such a report, \cref{cor:exact-load-cohort-law-separator} gives \((DPG3)\).
   The randomized-report variant follows because a finite average at least
   \(A\Lambda\) has some support point with \(X\ge A\Lambda\).

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then
   \cref{cor:exact-load-cohort-law-separator} supplies a cohort law \(\eta\) for
   which every affordable retained record has cohort capacity strictly below
   \(A\Lambda\).  For any affordable \(\eta\)-superlevel report,
   \[
      X\le\delta h\le \sum_{p\in U}d_\eta^\theta(p)<A\Lambda ,
   \]
   which is \((CWR5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Certified cohort-law mass reporter]
   \label{cor:certified-cohort-law-mass-reporter}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:certified-cohort-law-superlevel-reporter}.
   For a cohort law \(\eta\), call \((W_0,\theta,K,V,B)\) an
   \(\eta\)-mass report if \(K\ge1\), \(V>0\), \(B>0\), and it certifies
   \[
      |W_0|\le K,
      \qquad
      V\le\sum_{p\in W_0}d_\eta^\theta(p),
      \qquad
      d_\eta^\theta(p)\le B\quad(p\in W_0).
      \tag{CMR0}
   \]
   Define
   \[
      J_{B,K,V}
      =
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{2BK}{V}\right\rceil,
      \qquad
      \delta_j=B2^{-j}
      \quad(1\le j\le J_{B,K,V}),
      \tag{CMR1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      U_j=\{p\in W_0:d_\eta^\theta(p)\ge\delta_j\}.
      \tag{CMR2}
   \]
   Assume that every nonempty dyadic superlevel \(U_j\) from \((CMR2)\) can be
   retained with the same size certificate:
   \[
      (U_j,K,\theta)\in\mathcal R .
      \tag{CMR3}
   \]
   The certified yield of the mass report is
   \[
      Y(W_0,\theta,K,V,B)=\frac{V}{4J_{B,K,V}} .
      \tag{CMR4}
   \]
   If every cohort law \(\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}\) admits an
   \(\eta\)-mass report with
   \[
      Y(W_0,\theta,K,V,B)\ge A\Lambda ,
      \tag{CMR5}
   \]
   then the averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.  More
   generally, it is enough that every \(\eta\) admits a finite probability law
   \(\zeta\) over \(\eta\)-mass reports with
   \[
      \E_{(W_0,\theta,K,V,B)\sim\zeta}
      Y(W_0,\theta,K,V,B)
      \ge A\Lambda .
      \tag{CMR6}
   \]

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) for
   which every \(\eta\)-mass report satisfying \((CMR0)\)--\((CMR3)\) has
   \[
      Y(W_0,\theta,K,V,B)<A\Lambda .
      \tag{CMR7}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix an \(\eta\)-mass report and write \(J=J_{B,K,V}\),
   \(Y=V/(4J)\), and
   \[
      M=\sum_{p\in W_0}d_\eta^\theta(p).
   \]
   Since \(0\le d_\eta^\theta(p)\le B\) on \(W_0\), the dyadic layer-cake bound
   gives
   \[
      M
      \le
      B2^{-J}K
      +
      2\sum_{j=1}^J\delta_j|U_j| .
      \tag{CMR8}
   \]
   Indeed, for each \(x\in[0,B]\),
   \(x\le B2^{-J}+2\sum_{j=1}^J\delta_j{\bf 1}\{x\ge\delta_j\}\), and summing
   this inequality over \(x=d_\eta^\theta(p)\) gives \((CMR8)\).
   By the choice of \(J\), \(B2^{-J}K\le V/4\).  Since \(M\ge V\), we get
   \[
      \sum_{j=1}^J\delta_j|U_j|\ge\frac{3V}{8}.
   \]
   Hence some \(j\) satisfies
   \[
      \delta_j|U_j|>\frac{V}{4J}=Y.
      \tag{CMR9}
   \]
   For this \(j\), \(U_j\) is nonempty and affordable by \((CMR3)\), so
   \[
      (W_0,\theta,\delta_j,U_j,K,Y)
   \]
   is an \(\eta\)-superlevel report: its lower certificate obeys
   \(0\le Y\le \delta_j|U_j|\).  If \((CMR5)\) holds, then this report satisfies
   \((CWR3)\), and
   \cref{cor:certified-cohort-law-superlevel-reporter} gives \((DPG3)\).  If a
   finite law satisfies \((CMR6)\), one report in its support has yield at least
   \(A\Lambda\), so the same argument applies.

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then
   \cref{cor:certified-cohort-law-superlevel-reporter} gives a cohort law
   \(\eta\) for which every affordable \(\eta\)-superlevel report has
   certificate \(<A\Lambda\).  Applying the layer-cake construction above to any
   \(\eta\)-mass report produces an affordable superlevel report with
   certificate \(Y(W_0,\theta,K,V,B)\).  Therefore this yield must be
   \(<A\Lambda\), which is \((CMR7)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Explicit cohort-law mass envelope]
   \label{cor:explicit-cohort-law-mass-envelope}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:certified-cohort-law-mass-reporter}.  For
   \(B,K>0\), put
   \[
      L_{B,K}
      =
      1+\left\lceil
      \log_2\max\left\{2,\frac{2BK}{A\Lambda}\right\}
      \right\rceil .
      \tag{CME0}
   \]
   Suppose every cohort law \(\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}\) admits an
   \(\eta\)-mass report \((W_0,\theta,K,V,B)\) satisfying
   \[
      V\ge 4A\Lambda L_{B,K}.
      \tag{CME1}
   \]
   Then the averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.  More
   generally, it is enough that every \(\eta\) admits a finite probability law
   over \(\eta\)-mass reports with
   \[
      \E\frac{V}{4L_{B,K}}\ge A\Lambda .
      \tag{CME2}
   \]

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) for
   which every \(\eta\)-mass report satisfies the explicit logarithmic envelope
   \[
      V<4A\Lambda L_{B,K}.
      \tag{CME3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If a report satisfies \((CME1)\), then \(V\ge A\Lambda\).  Since
   \((CMR0)\) implies \(V\le BK\), we have
   \[
      J_{B,K,V}
      =
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{2BK}{V}\right\rceil
      \le L_{B,K}.
   \]
   Therefore \(Y(W_0,\theta,K,V,B)=V/(4J_{B,K,V})\ge A\Lambda\), and
   \cref{cor:certified-cohort-law-mass-reporter} gives \((DPG3)\).  If the
   averaged condition \((CME2)\) holds, some report in the finite support has
   \(V/(4L_{B,K})\ge A\Lambda\), hence satisfies \((CME1)\).

   Conversely, suppose \((DPG3)\) fails, and take the cohort law from
   \cref{cor:certified-cohort-law-mass-reporter}.  For any mass report, if
   \(V<A\Lambda\), then \((CME3)\) is immediate because \(L_{B,K}\ge1\).  If
   \(V\ge A\Lambda\), then \(J_{B,K,V}\le L_{B,K}\), while \((CMR7)\) gives
   \(V/(4J_{B,K,V})<A\Lambda\).  Hence
   \(V<4A\Lambda J_{B,K,V}\le4A\Lambda L_{B,K}\), proving \((CME3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Capped marginal cohort-law mass reporter]
   \label{cor:capped-marginal-cohort-law-mass-reporter}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:explicit-cohort-law-mass-envelope}.  Fix a
   cohort law \(\eta\).  A reportable capped list law consists of a finite
   probability law \(\zeta\) over subsets \(W_s\subseteq P\), together with
   \(0\le\theta\le1\), an integer size certificate \(K\ge1\), and a height
   certificate \(B>0\), such that every \(s\) in the support satisfies
   \[
      |W_s|\le K,
      \qquad
      d_\eta^\theta(p)\le B\quad(p\in W_s),
      \tag{CMM0}
   \]
   and every nonempty dyadic degree superlevel of \(W_s\) can be retained with
   size certificate \(K\), as required in \((CMR3)\).  Let
   \[
      \pi_p=\Pr_{s\sim\zeta}[p\in W_s],
      \qquad
      V_\pi=\sum_p\pi_p\,d_\eta^\theta(p).
      \tag{CMM1}
   \]
   If every cohort law \(\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}\) admits a
   reportable capped list law satisfying
   \[
      V_\pi\ge4A\Lambda L_{B,K},
      \tag{CMM2}
   \]
   then the averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.  More
   generally, it is enough to have a finite outer probability law over
   reportable capped list laws with
   \[
      \E\frac{V_\pi}{4L_{B,K}}\ge A\Lambda .
      \tag{CMM3}
   \]

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) for
   which every reportable capped list law satisfies the marginal envelope
   \[
      V_\pi<4A\Lambda L_{B,K}.
      \tag{CMM4}
   \]

   In particular, suppose a retained parent container \(W\) is closed under
   all sublists of size at most \(K\) in the sense that every \(W_s\subseteq W\)
   with \(|W_s|\le K\) satisfies the reportability condition above.  Then it is
   enough to give soft responsibilities \(0\le\pi_p\le1\) on \(W\) with
   \[
      \sum_{p\in W}\pi_p\le K,
      \qquad
      d_\eta^\theta(p)\le B\quad(p\in W),
      \qquad
      \sum_{p\in W}\pi_p d_\eta^\theta(p)\ge4A\Lambda L_{B,K}.
      \tag{CMM5}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For an outcome \(s\), put
   \[
      V_s=\sum_{p\in W_s}d_\eta^\theta(p).
   \]
   Every outcome with \(V_s>0\) is an \(\eta\)-mass report
   \((W_s,\theta,K,V_s,B)\), and all outcomes have the same \(B,K\).  Moreover
   \[
      \E_{s\sim\zeta}V_s=V_\pi .
   \]
   If \((CMM2)\) holds, then the conditional law on the positive-\(V_s\)
   outcomes is a finite law over \(\eta\)-mass reports with
   \[
      \E\frac{V_s}{4L_{B,K}}\ge \frac{V_\pi}{4L_{B,K}}\ge A\Lambda .
   \]
   Applying \((CME2)\) gives \((DPG3)\).  The outer-law variant is the same
   averaging argument after first sampling the capped list law and then its
   list outcome.

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, take the cohort law from
   \cref{cor:explicit-cohort-law-mass-envelope}.  Each positive-\(V_s\) outcome
   is an \(\eta\)-mass report, so \((CME3)\) gives
   \(V_s<4A\Lambda L_{B,K}\); zero outcomes also satisfy this strict bound.
   Since the support is finite, averaging gives \((CMM4)\).

   For the final claim, use the standard integral decomposition of the capped
   hypersimplex.  The polytope
   \[
      \{x\in[0,1]^W:\sum_{p\in W}x_p\le K\}
   \]
   has only integral vertices: if two coordinates are fractional, one may
   perturb them in opposite directions; if exactly one coordinate is fractional,
   either the sum constraint is slack and that coordinate can be perturbed, or
   the sum is the integer \(K\), which is impossible with all other coordinates
   integral.  Thus any responsibility vector satisfying \(\sum_p\pi_p\le K\) is
   a convex combination of indicators of subsets of size at most \(K\).  The
   assumed sublist closure makes this a reportable capped list law with marginals
   \(\pi\), and \((CMM5)\) is exactly \((CMM2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite capped-marginal proposal oracle]
   \label{cor:finite-capped-marginal-cohort-oracle}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:capped-marginal-cohort-law-mass-reporter}.  For every cohort law
   \(\eta\), every \(0\le\theta\le1\), and every point \(p\),
   \[
      0\le d_\eta^\theta(p)\le1.
      \tag{FCM0}
   \]
   Let \(\mathcal B\) be a finite pool of reportable capped-marginal templates.
   A template \(B\in\mathcal B\) consists of a segment parameter
   \(\theta_B\), an integer size certificate \(K_B\ge1\), and inclusion
   marginals \(\pi_{B,p}\) that are realized by a reportable capped list law
   with height certificate \(1\).  Put
   \[
      L_B
      =
      1+\left\lceil
      \log_2\max\left\{2,\frac{2K_B}{A\Lambda}\right\}
      \right\rceil ,
      \tag{FCM1}
   \]
   and, for a cohort law \(\eta\),
   \[
      V_\eta(B)=\sum_p\pi_{B,p}d_\eta^{\theta_B}(p),
      \qquad
      G(B,\eta)=\frac{V_\eta(B)}{4L_B}-A\Lambda .
      \tag{FCM2}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \max_{\omega\in\Delta_{\mathcal B}}
      \min_{\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}}
      \sum_{B\in\mathcal B}\omega_BG(B,\eta)
      =
      \min_{\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}}
      \max_{B\in\mathcal B}G(B,\eta).
      \tag{FCM3}
   \]
   Consequently, if either side of \((FCM3)\) is nonnegative, then the averaged
   dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.  Equivalently, it is enough that
   every cohort law \(\eta\) have some template \(B\in\mathcal B\) with
   \[
      V_\eta(B)\ge4A\Lambda L_B .
      \tag{FCM4}
   \]

   Conversely, if no randomized law on \(\mathcal B\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_B\omega_B\frac{V_\eta(B)}{4L_B}\ge A\Lambda
      \qquad(\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}),
      \tag{FCM5}
   \]
   then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) such that every template in the finite
   pool satisfies
   \[
      V_\eta(B)<4A\Lambda L_B .
      \tag{FCM6}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The unit-height bound follows from \(0\le e_q\le1\), \(0\le r_{p,q}\le1\),
   and \((GNR1)\):
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \sum_p d_\eta^\theta(p)
      &=
      \E_{(\Delta',e)\sim\eta}
      \sum_q e_q
      \sum_{\substack{p:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}
      \bar\gamma^\theta_{p,q}r_{p,q}\\
      &\le
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\bar\gamma^\theta_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      =
      \mathsf M(\bar\gamma^\theta)
      =
      1 .
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   Hence each summand is in \([0,1]\), proving \((FCM0)\).

   Since \(\mathcal E_{\rm load}\) and \(\mathcal B\) are finite and
   \(G(B,\eta)\) is linear in \(\eta\) and \(\omega\), \((FCM3)\) is the finite
   matrix-game minimax theorem.  If the value is nonnegative, choose a
   maximizing law \(\omega\).  For every cohort law \(\eta\),
   \[
      \sum_B\omega_B\frac{V_\eta(B)}{4L_B}\ge A\Lambda .
   \]
   Sampling \(B\sim\omega\) and then sampling the capped list law realizing its
   marginals gives the finite outer law required in \((CMM3)\), with the common
   height certificate \(1\) for each sampled template.  Therefore
   \cref{cor:capped-marginal-cohort-law-mass-reporter} gives \((DPG3)\).  The
   pointwise condition \((FCM4)\) is exactly the statement that the right side of
   \((FCM3)\) is nonnegative.

   If no randomized law satisfies \((FCM5)\), the value in \((FCM3)\) is
   strictly negative.  A minimizing cohort law \(\eta\) then has
   \(\max_BG(B,\eta)<0\), which is exactly \((FCM6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Logarithmic top-prefix cohort separator]
   \label{cor:logarithmic-top-prefix-cohort-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-capped-marginal-cohort-oracle}.  Let \(\mathcal T\) be a
   finite family of retained prefix templates \(T=(W_T,K_T,\theta_T)\), with
   \(1\le K_T\le |W_T|\), such that every sublist \(U\subseteq W_T\) with
   \(|U|\le K_T\) is reportable with size certificate \(K_T\).  Put
   \[
      L_T
      =
      1+\left\lceil
      \log_2\max\left\{2,\frac{2K_T}{A\Lambda}\right\}
      \right\rceil .
      \tag{LTP0}
   \]
   If every cohort law \(\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}\) admits a
   template \(T\in\mathcal T\) satisfying
   \[
      D_\eta^{\theta_T}(W_T,K_T)
      \ge
      4A\Lambda L_T,
      \tag{LTP1}
   \]
   then the averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) such
   that every retained prefix template \(T\in\mathcal T\) satisfies
   \[
      D_\eta^{\theta_T}(W_T,K_T)
      <
      4A\Lambda L_T .
      \tag{LTP2}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix \(\eta\) and \(T=(W_T,K_T,\theta_T)\).  Let \(U_T\) be a maximizing
   \(K_T\)-point subset in the definition of \(D_\eta^{\theta_T}(W_T,K_T)\).
   Since \(K_T\le |W_T|\), this subset exists.  By the sublist-closure
   hypothesis, the point-mass capped list law on \(U_T\) is reportable with size
   certificate \(K_T\) and height certificate \(1\), using \((FCM0)\).  Its
   marginal mass is exactly
   \[
      V_\eta(T)=D_\eta^{\theta_T}(W_T,K_T).
   \]
   Therefore \((LTP1)\) is the capped-marginal condition \((CMM2)\) for this
   deterministic law, and
   \cref{cor:capped-marginal-cohort-law-mass-reporter} gives \((DPG3)\) when
   every cohort law has such a template.

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then
   \cref{cor:capped-marginal-cohort-law-mass-reporter} gives a cohort law
   \(\eta\) for which every reportable capped list law satisfies \((CMM4)\).
   Applying that envelope to the point-mass law on the maximizing prefix
   \(U_T\) gives \((LTP2)\) for every \(T\in\mathcal T\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dyadic-depth cancellation in the cohort prefix threshold]
   \label{cor:cohort-prefix-depth-cancellation}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:logarithmic-top-prefix-cohort-separator}, and substitute the
   constants \(A,\Lambda\) from \((DLE1)\).  Define
   \[
      \Theta_C
      =
      4A\Lambda
      =
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}
      {2CJK_{|P|}} .
      \tag{CDC0}
   \]
   Then the sufficient prefix condition \((LTP1)\) is equivalently
   \[
      D_\eta^{\theta_T}(W_T,K_T)
      \ge
      \Theta_C
      \left(
         1+\left\lceil
         \log_2\max\left\{2,\frac{8K_T}{\Theta_C}\right\}
         \right\rceil
      \right).
      \tag{CDC1}
   \]
   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) such
   that every retained prefix template satisfies the strict reverse of
   \((CDC1)\).

   In particular, the number \(H_m(\Delta)\) of dyadic annular size levels does
   not appear in the final prefix threshold.  It cancels between the efficiency
   threshold \(A=2H_m(\Delta)/C\) and the exact-load cohort mass
   \(\Lambda\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Multiplying the definitions in \((DLE1)\) gives
   \[
      4A\Lambda
      =
      4\cdot\frac{2H_m(\Delta)}{C}\cdot
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}
      {16J K_{|P|}H_m(\Delta)}
      =
      \Theta_C .
   \]
   Also \(A\Lambda=\Theta_C/4\), hence
   \[
      \frac{2K_T}{A\Lambda}=\frac{8K_T}{\Theta_C}.
   \]
   Substituting these identities into \((LTP1)\) and \((LTP2)\) gives
   \((CDC1)\) and its strict reverse.  The cancellation statement is the same
   algebra read off from the displayed product.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cardinality-net cohort prefix envelope]
   \label{cor:cardinality-net-cohort-prefix-envelope}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:cohort-prefix-depth-cancellation}.  Let
   \(b\ge1\).  Suppose the retained prefix templates are organized by retained
   parent containers and segment parameters, with a finite cardinality net
   \(\mathcal K_{W,\theta}\) satisfying: for every
   \(1\le h\le |W|\) there is \(K\in\mathcal K_{W,\theta}\) such that
   \[
      h\le K\le b h,
      \tag{CNC0}
   \]
   and every sublist of \(W\) of size at most such a \(K\) is reportable with
   size certificate \(K\).  Put
   \[
      L_b(h)
      =
      1+\left\lceil
      \log_2\max\left\{2,\frac{8bh}{\Theta_C}\right\}
      \right\rceil .
      \tag{CNC1}
   \]
   If every cohort law \(\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}\) admits
   \(W,\theta,h\) with \(1\le h\le |W|\) such that
   \[
      D_\eta^\theta(W,h)\ge\Theta_C L_b(h),
      \tag{CNC2}
   \]
   then the averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) such
   that every retained parent container \(W\), segment \(\theta\), and analytic
   prefix size \(1\le h\le |W|\) satisfies
   \[
      D_\eta^\theta(W,h)<\Theta_C L_b(h).
      \tag{CNC3}
   \]
   For dyadic cardinalities one may take \(b=2\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((CNC2)\) holds, choose \(K\in\mathcal K_{W,\theta}\) satisfying
   \((CNC0)\).  The top \(K\)-prefix contains at least as much cohort mass as
   the top \(h\)-prefix, so
   \[
      D_\eta^\theta(W,K)\ge D_\eta^\theta(W,h).
   \]
   Also \(K\le bh\), hence the logarithmic factor in \((CDC1)\) for \(K\) is at
   most \(L_b(h)\).  Therefore the retained template \((W,K,\theta)\) satisfies
   \((CDC1)\), and
   \cref{cor:cohort-prefix-depth-cancellation} gives \((DPG3)\).

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then
   \cref{cor:cohort-prefix-depth-cancellation} gives a cohort law \(\eta\) for
   which every retained net size \(K\in\mathcal K_{W,\theta}\) satisfies the
   strict reverse of \((CDC1)\).  Given any analytic \(h\), choose
   \(K\in\mathcal K_{W,\theta}\) with \(h\le K\le bh\).  Since
   \(D_\eta^\theta(W,h)\le D_\eta^\theta(W,K)\), and the \(K\)-threshold is at
   most \(\Theta_C L_b(h)\), we get \((CNC3)\).

   Powers of two are \(2\)-dense from above, giving the final claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite prefix-template separation game]
   \label{cor:finite-prefix-template-separation-game}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-cohort-prefix-envelope}, and fix a finite retained
   prefix-record pool \(\mathcal P_b\).  A record
   \(T\in\mathcal P_b\) consists of
   \[
      T=(W_T,\theta_T,h_T,K_T,U_T),
      \qquad
      U_T\subseteq W_T,\quad |U_T|=h_T,
      \qquad
      h_T\le K_T\le b h_T,
      \tag{FPT0}
   \]
   where \(K_T\in\mathcal K_{W_T,\theta_T}\) and every sublist of \(W_T\) of
   size at most \(K_T\) is reportable with size certificate \(K_T\).  Define
   the cohort value and verified surplus
   \[
      V_\eta(T)=\sum_{p\in U_T}d_\eta^{\theta_T}(p),
      \qquad
      G(T,\eta)=V_\eta(T)-\Theta_C L_b(h_T).
      \tag{FPT1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \max_{\omega\in\Delta_{\mathcal P_b}}
      \min_{\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}}
      \sum_{T\in\mathcal P_b}\omega_TG(T,\eta)
      =
      \min_{\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}}
      \max_{T\in\mathcal P_b}G(T,\eta).
      \tag{FPT2}
   \]
   If the common value in \((FPT2)\) is nonnegative, then the averaged
   dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) such
   that, for this pool and indeed for every retained prefix-record pool
   satisfying \((FPT0)\), the strict inequalities
   \[
      G(T,\eta)<0
      \qquad(T\in\mathcal P_b)
      \tag{FPT3}
   \]
   hold.
   This same \(\eta\) is independent of the chosen finite pool.

   In particular, when the pool contains all reportable \(h\)-subsets of each
   retained parent \(W\), optimizing over \(U_T\) for fixed \(W,\theta,h\) is
   exactly the top-prefix quantity \(D_\eta^\theta(W,h)\).  Thus the build-time
   separation objective is the verified score
   \[
      D_\eta^\theta(W,h)-\Theta_C L_b(h),
      \tag{FPT4}
   \]
   or equivalently the ratio \(D_\eta^\theta(W,h)/L_b(h)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The set \(\mathcal E_{\rm load}\) is finite, and \(G(T,\eta)\) is linear in
   \(\eta\) for each fixed retained record \(T\).  Hence \((FPT2)\) is the
   finite matrix-game minimax theorem.

   If the value is nonnegative, choose a maximizing law \(\omega\).  For every
   cohort law \(\eta\), the \(\omega\)-average of \(G(T,\eta)\) is nonnegative,
   so some support record has \(G(T,\eta)\ge0\).  For that record,
   \[
      D_\eta^{\theta_T}(W_T,h_T)\ge V_\eta(T)\ge\Theta_C L_b(h_T),
   \]
   because \(U_T\) is one feasible \(h_T\)-subset of \(W_T\).  Therefore
   \((CNC2)\) holds for every cohort law, and
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-cohort-prefix-envelope} gives \((DPG3)\).

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-cohort-prefix-envelope} gives a cohort law
   \(\eta\) satisfying the strict envelope \((CNC3)\) for every retained
   \(W,\theta,h\).  For any record \(T\),
   \[
      V_\eta(T)
      \le
      D_\eta^{\theta_T}(W_T,h_T)
      <
      \Theta_C L_b(h_T),
   \]
   which is \((FPT3)\).

   The final statement is only the definition of
   \(D_\eta^\theta(W,h)\) as the maximum \(d_\eta^\theta\)-mass over
   \(h\)-subsets of \(W\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Prefix-template column generation]
   \label{cor:prefix-template-column-generation}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-template-separation-game}.  Let
   \(\mathcal U_b\) be a finite full universe of retained prefix records
   satisfying \((FPT0)\).  Suppose that for every cohort law \(\eta\) one has
   a separation oracle that either returns a record \(T\in\mathcal U_b\) with
   \[
      G(T,\eta)\ge0
      \tag{PTC0}
   \]
   or certifies
   \[
      \max_{T\in\mathcal U_b}G(T,\eta)<0 .
      \tag{PTC1}
   \]
   Then the following column-generation procedure is complete for this
   universe.  Start with any nonempty finite pool
   \(\mathcal P\subseteq\mathcal U_b\).  Repeatedly solve the restricted game
   \[
      v(\mathcal P)
      =
      \min_{\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}}
      \max_{T\in\mathcal P}G(T,\eta).
      \tag{PTC2}
   \]
   If \(v(\mathcal P)\ge0\), then \((DPG3)\) holds.  If
   \(v(\mathcal P)<0\), let \(\eta_{\mathcal P}\) be a minimizer and call the
   separator on \(\eta_{\mathcal P}\).  If it returns \(T\), add \(T\) to the
   pool; if it certifies \((PTC1)\), then the full universe
   \(\mathcal U_b\) cannot satisfy the prefix-template sufficient condition.

   Consequently, if
   \[
      \min_{\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}}
      \max_{T\in\mathcal U_b}G(T,\eta)\ge0,
      \tag{PTC3}
   \]
   the procedure terminates after at most \(|\mathcal U_b|\) successful
   additions with a pool proving \((DPG3)\).  The cost of solving the games and
   running the separator is preprocessing only; the retained index pays only
   for the final verified pool.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(v(\mathcal P)\ge0\), then
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-template-separation-game} applied to the current
   pool gives \((DPG3)\).

   Suppose \(v(\mathcal P)<0\) and let \(\eta_{\mathcal P}\) attain the
   minimum in \((PTC2)\).  Then
   \[
      G(T,\eta_{\mathcal P})<0
      \qquad(T\in\mathcal P),
      \tag{PTC4}
   \]
   because the maximum over the current pool is negative.  Hence any separator
   output satisfying \((PTC0)\) is not already in \(\mathcal P\), so a
   successful call strictly enlarges the pool.  Since \(\mathcal U_b\) is
   finite, there can be at most \(|\mathcal U_b|\) successful additions.

   If the separator certifies \((PTC1)\) at some minimizer, then the full
   universe has negative value at that cohort law, so \((PTC3)\) is false.  In
   particular, \(\mathcal U_b\) does not contain a prefix record satisfying
   \((CNC2)\) for that \(\eta\), and this prefix universe alone cannot close
   the dominated-load certificate through
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-cohort-prefix-envelope}.

   Under \((PTC3)\), the certificate \((PTC1)\) can never be valid.  Therefore
   the finite enlargement process must eventually reach a pool with
   nonnegative restricted value, and the first paragraph gives \((DPG3)\).
   The last sentence is just the separation between build-time search and the
   retained verified records in the finite cover LP.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One-sided prefix-value column generation]
   \label{cor:one-sided-prefix-value-column-generation}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:prefix-template-column-generation}.  For a cohort law \(\eta\),
   call \((T,X)\) a one-sided prefix-value report if \(T\in\mathcal U_b\) and
   \[
      0\le X\le V_\eta(T).
      \tag{OPV0}
   \]
   The report is separating if
   \[
      X\ge \Theta_C L_b(h_T).
      \tag{OPV1}
   \]
   Suppose that for every cohort law \(\eta\) a build-time oracle either
   returns a separating one-sided prefix-value report or certifies
   \[
      \max_{T\in\mathcal U_b}G(T,\eta)<0 .
      \tag{OPV2}
   \]
   Then the column-generation procedure of
   \cref{cor:prefix-template-column-generation} remains complete when the
   separator call is replaced by this one-sided oracle: on a successful call,
   add only the verified record \(T\) to the pool, and score it in all later
   restricted games by its exact payoff \(G(T,\cdot)\).

   Consequently, if the full universe satisfies \((PTC3)\), the procedure
   terminates after finitely many successful one-sided reports with a pool
   proving \((DPG3)\).  If the oracle returns \((OPV2)\), then the full universe
   cannot satisfy the prefix-template sufficient condition.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   A separating report satisfies
   \[
      G(T,\eta)
      =
      V_\eta(T)-\Theta_C L_b(h_T)
      \ge
      X-\Theta_C L_b(h_T)
      \ge0 .
      \tag{OPV3}
   \]
   Hence a successful one-sided oracle call is also a valid separator output
   satisfying \((PTC0)\).  If the current restricted value is negative at the
   minimizing law \(\eta_{\mathcal P}\), every current pool record has
   \(G(T,\eta_{\mathcal P})<0\); therefore any successful one-sided report has
   \(T\notin\mathcal P\) and strictly enlarges the pool.  The rest is exactly
   \cref{cor:prefix-template-column-generation}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One-sided proposal-law prefix separator]
   \label{cor:one-sided-proposal-law-prefix-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:one-sided-prefix-value-column-generation}, and fix a cohort law
   \(\eta\).  A finite \(\eta\)-proposal law is a finite probability law
   \(\zeta\) over pairs \(R=(T_R,X_R)\) such that
   \[
      T_R\in\mathcal U_b,
      \qquad
      0\le X_R\le V_\eta(T_R).
      \tag{OPL0}
   \]
   Define its certified surplus by
   \[
      \Psi_\eta(R)
      =
      X_R-\Theta_C L_b(h_{T_R}).
      \tag{OPL1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \E_{R\sim\zeta}\Psi_\eta(R)\ge0,
      \tag{OPL2}
   \]
   then the support of \(\zeta\) contains a separating one-sided prefix-value
   report.  Consequently the separator call in
   \cref{cor:one-sided-prefix-value-column-generation} may be implemented by
   any randomized, batched, or learned proposal generator whose realized finite
   support is verified by \((OPL0)\) and whose certified average surplus
   satisfies \((OPL2)\); only the exposed deterministic record \(T_R\) is added
   to the retained pool.

   Conversely, if the exact full-universe certificate \((OPV2)\) holds for
   \(\eta\), then every finite \(\eta\)-proposal law satisfies
   \[
      \E_{R\sim\zeta}\Psi_\eta(R)<0 .
      \tag{OPL3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If every support point had \(\Psi_\eta(R)<0\), the finite average would be
   negative.  Hence \((OPL2)\) gives some \(R=(T_R,X_R)\) with
   \(\Psi_\eta(R)\ge0\), which is exactly \((OPV1)\) together with
   \((OPV0)\).

   Conversely, if \((OPV2)\) holds, then for every report in the support,
   \[
      \Psi_\eta(R)
      \le
      V_\eta(T_R)-\Theta_C L_b(h_{T_R})
      =
      G(T_R,\eta)
      <
      0 .
   \]
   Averaging gives \((OPL3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sampled one-sided prefix separator]
   \label{cor:sampled-one-sided-prefix-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:one-sided-prefix-value-column-generation}.  Fix a cohort law
   \(\eta\), and suppose preprocessing has a sampleable law \(\mathfrak P_\eta\)
   on one-sided prefix-value reports \(R=(T_R,X_R)\) satisfying \((OPV0)\).
   Let
   \[
      \Psi_\eta(R)=X_R-\Theta_C L_b(h_{T_R})
      \tag{SOP0}
   \]
   and assume \(\Psi_\eta\) is integrable and
   \[
      \E_{R\sim\mathfrak P_\eta}\Psi_\eta(R)\ge0.
      \tag{SOP1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \Pr_{R\sim\mathfrak P_\eta}[\Psi_\eta(R)\ge0]>0.
      \tag{SOP2}
   \]
   Consequently, repeated independent sampling from \(\mathfrak P_\eta\), with
   exact verification of \((OPV0)\) and \(\Psi_\eta(R)\ge0\) after each sample,
   is a Las Vegas separator: it halts almost surely with a separating
   one-sided prefix-value report, and if the probability in \((SOP2)\) is
   \(\pi_\eta\), its expected number of samples is \(1/\pi_\eta\).

   Therefore the column-generation procedure remains complete with uncharged
   randomized preprocessing if, for every minimizing cohort law encountered by
   the restricted game, either an exact oracle certifies \((OPV2)\) or
   preprocessing supplies such a sampleable law.  The retained index still pays
   only for the deterministic verified records that are actually accepted.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(\Pr[\Psi_\eta(R)\ge0]=0\), then \(\Psi_\eta(R)<0\) almost surely.  Since
   \(\Psi_\eta\) is integrable, this implies
   \(\E\Psi_\eta(R)<0\) unless \(\Psi_\eta=0\) almost surely, which contradicts
   \(\Psi_\eta<0\) almost surely.  Hence \((SOP2)\) follows from \((SOP1)\).

   A sample with \(\Psi_\eta(R)\ge0\) satisfies \(X_R\ge\Theta_C L_b(h_{T_R})\),
   so it is separating by \((OPV1)\).  Independent repetitions hit this event
   almost surely, and the geometric waiting-time formula gives expectation
   \(1/\pi_\eta\).  The final statement is
   \cref{cor:one-sided-prefix-value-column-generation}: every successful
   sampled report is a valid separator output, while \((OPV2)\) is the exact
   no-column certificate.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sampled soft-prefix proposal separator]
   \label{cor:sampled-soft-prefix-proposal-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:sampled-one-sided-prefix-separator}.  A soft prefix proposal for a
   cohort law \(\eta\) is a tuple
   \[
      R=(W_R,\theta_R,h_R,K_R,\pi_R,X_R)
   \]
   such that \(1\le h_R\le |W_R|\) is an integer,
   \(h_R\le K_R\le b h_R\), \(K_R\in\mathcal K_{W_R,\theta_R}\), every sublist
   of \(W_R\) of size at most \(K_R\) is reportable with size certificate
   \(K_R\),
   \[
      0\le \pi_{R,p}\le1,\qquad
      \sum_{p\in W_R}\pi_{R,p}\le h_R,
      \tag{SFP0}
   \]
   and the proposal gives a one-sided value certificate
   \[
      0\le X_R\le
      \sum_{p\in W_R}\pi_{R,p}d_\eta^{\theta_R}(p).
      \tag{SFP1}
   \]
   Assume that whenever such a tuple is sampled, preprocessing can materialize an
   \(h_R\)-point maximizer
   \[
      U_R^*\in
      \arg\max_{\substack{U\subseteq W_R\\ |U|=h_R}}
      \sum_{p\in U}d_\eta^{\theta_R}(p),
      \tag{SFP2}
   \]
   and that the corresponding record
   \(T_R=(W_R,\theta_R,h_R,K_R,U_R^*)\) lies in \(\mathcal U_b\).  If
   preprocessing has a sampleable law on soft prefix proposals with integrable
   surplus and for which
   \[
      \E\bigl[X_R-\Theta_C L_b(h_R)\bigr]\ge0,
      \tag{SFP3}
   \]
   then repeated sampling, exact materialization of \(U_R^*\), and verification of
   \(X_R\ge\Theta_C L_b(h_R)\) form a Las Vegas separator for the current cohort
   law.

   Thus a randomized \(k\)-means++, additive-quantization, range-reporting, or
   learned panel may be analyzed only through soft inclusion responsibilities and
   a one-sided lower value certificate.  The retained index still stores only the
   deterministic prefix record \(T_R\), never the soft proposal itself.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For any admissible proposal, the top-\(h_R\) set \(U_R^*\) dominates the soft
   responsibility vector.  Indeed, the polytope
   \[
      \left\{x\in[0,1]^{W_R}:\sum_{p\in W_R}x_p\le h_R\right\}
   \]
   has integral vertices, and every such vertex is the indicator of a subset of
   size at most \(h_R\).  Since \(d_\eta^{\theta_R}(p)\ge0\), the maximum of the
   linear functional \(\sum_p x_p d_\eta^{\theta_R}(p)\) over this polytope is
   attained by an \(h_R\)-point top prefix.  Hence
   \[
      V_\eta(T_R)
      =
      \sum_{p\in U_R^*}d_\eta^{\theta_R}(p)
      \ge
      \sum_{p\in W_R}\pi_{R,p}d_\eta^{\theta_R}(p)
      \ge X_R .
      \tag{SFP4}
   \]
   Therefore \((T_R,X_R)\) is a one-sided prefix-value report in the sense of
   \((OPV0)\).  Its surplus is exactly
   \(X_R-\Theta_C L_b(h_R)\), so \((SFP3)\) is the expectation hypothesis
   \((SOP1)\) for the induced law on one-sided reports.  Applying
   \cref{cor:sampled-one-sided-prefix-separator} gives positive probability of a
   separating sample and the stated Las Vegas separator.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cardinality-net cohort superlevel reporter]
   \label{cor:cardinality-net-cohort-superlevel-reporter}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-cohort-prefix-envelope}.  For a cohort law
   \(\eta\), a retained parent container \(W\), a segment parameter \(\theta\),
   and a level \(\delta>0\), call
   \[
      (W,\theta,\delta,U,h,K,X)
   \]
   a certified cardinality-net superlevel report if
   \[
      U\subseteq W,\qquad |U|=h>0,\qquad
      d_\eta^\theta(p)\ge\delta\quad(p\in U),
      \tag{CNS0}
   \]
   \[
      K\in\mathcal K_{W,\theta},
      \qquad h\le K\le bh,
      \tag{CNS1}
   \]
   every sublist of \(W\) of size at most \(K\) is reportable with size
   certificate \(K\), and the report gives the one-sided certificate
   \[
      0\le X\le\delta h .
      \tag{CNS2}
   \]
   Its certified surplus is
   \[
      \Phi_\eta(W,\theta,\delta,U,h,K,X)
      =
      X-\Theta_C L_b(h).
      \tag{CNS3}
   \]
   If every cohort law \(\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}\) admits a
   certified cardinality-net superlevel report with
   \[
      \Phi_\eta(W,\theta,\delta,U,h,K,X)\ge0,
      \tag{CNS4}
   \]
   then the averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.  More
   generally, it is enough that every \(\eta\) admits a finite probability law
   over such reports with
   \[
      \E\Phi_\eta(W,\theta,\delta,U,h,K,X)\ge0,
      \tag{CNS5}
   \]
   because some deterministic report in the support has nonnegative certified
   surplus.

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) for
   which every certified cardinality-net superlevel report satisfies
   \[
      \Phi_\eta(W,\theta,\delta,U,h,K,X)<0.
      \tag{CNS6}
   \]
   In particular every such report has
   \[
      \delta h<\Theta_C L_b(h).
      \tag{CNS7}
   \]

   In the finite-universe setting of
   \cref{cor:prefix-template-column-generation}, any report satisfying
   \((CNS4)\) whose record
   \[
      T=(W,\theta,h,K,U)
   \]
   lies in the implicit universe \(\mathcal U_b\) is a valid separator output:
   it satisfies \(G(T,\eta)\ge0\).
   Equivalently, \((T,X)\) is a separating one-sided prefix-value report in the
   sense of \cref{cor:one-sided-prefix-value-column-generation}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \((W,\theta,\delta,U,h,K,X)\) be a report satisfying \((CNS4)\).  Since
   every point of \(U\) has \(d_\eta^\theta(p)\ge\delta\),
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U}d_\eta^\theta(p)\ge\delta h\ge X
      \ge\Theta_C L_b(h).
      \tag{CNS8}
   \]
   Hence the top \(h\)-prefix in \(W\) also has mass at least
   \(\Theta_C L_b(h)\), so \((CNC2)\) holds for this cohort law.  If every
   cohort law has such a report, then
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-cohort-prefix-envelope} gives \((DPG3)\).  The
   randomized-report variant follows because a finite average of
   \(\Phi_\eta\) is nonnegative only if some support report has
   \(\Phi_\eta\ge0\).

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-cohort-prefix-envelope} gives a cohort law
   \(\eta\) satisfying \((CNC3)\) for every retained parent, segment, and
   analytic prefix size.  For any certified report, the reported list is one
   \(h\)-subset of \(W\), so
   \[
      X\le\delta h
      \le
      \sum_{p\in U}d_\eta^\theta(p)
      \le
      D_\eta^\theta(W,h)
      <
      \Theta_C L_b(h).
      \tag{CNS9}
   \]
   This proves \((CNS6)\), and \((CNS7)\) follows from the same displayed
   inequality without \(X\).

   Finally, in the finite prefix-template game the corresponding record has
   \[
      V_\eta(T)
      =
      \sum_{p\in U}d_\eta^\theta(p)
      \ge X\ge\Theta_C L_b(h),
   \]
   hence \(G(T,\eta)\ge0\).
\end{proof}

The lemma is the fractional version of the dominated-load endpoint.  It does not
claim the remaining geometric theorem.  Rather, after terminal low-load levels
and the \(A\)-boundary alternative have been dealt with by
\((DLE2)\)--\((DLE3)\), a finite proposal pool fails only if the dual can choose
level weights and one dominated query distribution per level so that every
affordable record has mean efficiency below \(A\).  By
\cref{cor:exact-load-dominated-proposal-obstruction}, the same obstruction is a
law over exact-load cohorts, each integral except for one boundary query.  Thus a
list-decoding, LP-range-reporting, additive-quantization, or seeded clustering
oracle should be analyzed against the single weighted cohort objective in
\((EDP2)\) or \((EDP3)\).  Equivalently,
\cref{cor:exact-load-cohort-law-separator} says that the remaining finite-pool
theorem is to beat every law over these cohorts by one affordable retained
record.  Finally,
\cref{cor:cohort-law-scalar-prefix-normal-form} rewrites that record search as a
scalar top-prefix problem for the cohort degree \(d_\eta^\theta\), not as a
choice of disjoint dense clusters.  \Cref{cor:exact-top-prefix-cohort-game} and
\cref{cor:exact-prefix-column-generation} record the sharp build-time version:
if exact top-prefix records can be separated in a finite implicit universe,
ordinary column generation closes the dominated-load certificate at threshold
\(A\Lambda\), with no dyadic reporter loss.
\Cref{cor:one-sided-exact-prefix-value-column-generation} is the same sharp
route with one-sided value certificates: a reporter may lower-bound one hard
record's current cohort value, while the retained LP stores that record and
uses its exact payoff in every later restricted game.
\Cref{cor:sublist-closed-exact-prefix-separator} compresses this separator for
sublist-closed containers to the scalar objective
\(D_\eta^\theta(W,K)-A\Lambda\).
\Cref{cor:no-loss-exact-cardinality-net} removes exact-cardinality search on this
route: a dyadic net of retained cardinalities is enough and does not change the
threshold.
\Cref{cor:average-mass-exact-prefix-screen} turns coarse mass certificates into
the same exact-prefix separator: mass \(M\) on \(s\) reported points certifies a
top-\(K\) value at least \(KM/s\), again with no layer-cake loss.
\Cref{cor:average-density-exact-prefix-scale-choice} removes the need for the
proposal to guess \(K\): a coarse support-mass report with \(M\ge A\Lambda\)
chooses \(h_*=\lceil A\Lambda s/M\rceil\) and rounds up through the retained
cardinality net at the same sharp threshold.
\Cref{cor:soft-average-density-exact-prefix-scale-choice} gives the same
scale choice for soft responsibilities: a proposal certifies only total soft
mass \(\mu\) and value \(X\), and the exact verifier chooses
\(h_*=\lceil A\Lambda\mu/X\rceil\) before materializing one hard top prefix.
\Cref{cor:soft-exact-prefix-relaxation-tight} records the converse: if the
exact-prefix route fails for a cohort law, every responsibility vector in every
searched container has soft value below \(A\Lambda\).  Soft panels are therefore
not a weaker theorem target, only a way to search for the hard prefix.
\Cref{cor:finite-soft-exact-prefix-oracle} makes this finite and minimax:
generated \(k\)-means++, AQ, learned, list-recovery, or LP-range-reporting soft
panels may be scored at the sharp \(A\Lambda\) threshold, but a successful panel
is immediately compiled into a materialized exact-prefix record.
\Cref{cor:soft-exact-prefix-column-generation} gives the corresponding
build-time algorithm: solve the restricted hard-record game, ask the soft
separator only for evidence against the minimizing cohort law, and retain only
the verified hard prefix exposed by that evidence.
\Cref{rem:exact-template-linearization} records the important caveat: these
template objectives are separation objectives for a fixed cohort law; minimax is
still performed over the materialized exact records, where the payoff is linear.
\Cref{cor:exact-prefix-proposal-law-separator} and
\cref{cor:sampled-soft-exact-prefix-separator} are the randomized build-time
forms of the same sharp separator: positive expected certified surplus exposes
one deterministic top-prefix record, and only that record is retained.  In the
weak-type form of
\cref{cor:cohort-law-weak-type-superlevel}, the remaining range-reporting target
is just to find one affordable scalar superlevel with \(\delta h\ge A\Lambda\).
\Cref{cor:certified-cohort-law-superlevel-reporter} is the build-facing version:
the decoder need only give a one-sided lower certificate \(X\le\delta h\) and a
certified size bound \(K\) for the exact retained superlevel; any finite
randomized panel whose expected certificate reaches \(A\Lambda\) exposes a
deterministic affordable record.  Thus \(k\)-means++ panels, additive
quantization, list recovery, or LP range reporting can be analyzed through
certified superlevel reports rather than exact dense-cluster choices.
\Cref{cor:certified-cohort-law-mass-reporter} removes the need to guess the
level directly: it is enough to certify total cohort degree \(V\) in a retained
container, a pointwise height bound \(B\), and a size bound \(K\).  A dyadic
layer-cake then finds a reportable superlevel with certified yield
\(V/O(\log(BK/V))\).
\Cref{cor:explicit-cohort-law-mass-envelope} removes the remaining implicit
level dependence: failure leaves one cohort law for which every retained mass
certificate obeys \(V=O(A\Lambda\log(2BK/(A\Lambda)))\).  Thus the geometric
theorem can target a direct mass violation rather than optimizing over
thresholds.
\Cref{cor:capped-marginal-cohort-law-mass-reporter} is the soft proposal
interface: a \(k\)-means++, additive-quantization, or list-decoding panel may
output a finite law over capped hard lists and be analyzed only through its
inclusion marginals.  If the parent container is closed under sublists, even a
responsibility vector with total mass at most \(K\) is enough, by integral
decomposition of the capped hypersimplex.
\Cref{cor:finite-capped-marginal-cohort-oracle} packages the build step as a
finite matrix game over generated soft panels: either a randomized panel law
beats every cohort law at the explicit logarithmic mass threshold, or one cohort
law witnesses that every generated panel is below threshold.  Because the
cohort degrees have unit height under \((GNR1)\), the logarithmic factor depends
only on the size certificate \(K_B\).
\Cref{cor:logarithmic-top-prefix-cohort-separator} removes the last soft
artifact for sublist-closed retained containers: it is enough to find a
top-\(K\) prefix whose cohort-degree mass beats
\(4A\Lambda\bigl(1+\lceil\log_2\max\{2,2K/(A\Lambda)\}\rceil\bigr)\).  Failure
leaves the same explicit prefix envelope for every retained template.
\Cref{cor:cohort-prefix-depth-cancellation} substitutes the annular constants:
\(4A\Lambda=(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa/(2CJK_{|P|})\), so the dyadic level
count \(H_m(\Delta)\) cancels out of the retained prefix threshold.
\Cref{cor:cardinality-net-cohort-prefix-envelope} removes exact-cardinality
search: a factor-\(b\) retained cardinality net, in particular dyadic sizes
with \(b=2\), leaves only the explicit envelope with \(K\) replaced by \(bh\).
\Cref{cor:exact-prefix-column-generation} is the corresponding sharp finite
form when exact top-prefix separation is available during preprocessing: solve
the restricted cohort game, add any exact-prefix record with nonnegative surplus
\(V_\eta(T)-A\Lambda\), and charge only the final verified pool.  This route has
no logarithmic threshold; the logarithmic forms below are for weaker reporters
that cannot materialize the exact cohort-degree prefix directly.
\Cref{cor:one-sided-exact-prefix-value-column-generation} lets an approximate
range-reporting, AQ, or list-decoding separator stay on this sharp route as long
as it gives a one-sided lower certificate \(X\le V_\eta(T)\) with
\(X\ge A\Lambda\); the retained record is still scored exactly later.
\Cref{cor:sublist-closed-exact-prefix-separator} is the practical exact-prefix
interface for sublist-closed retained containers: the build oracle optimizes
\(D_\eta^\theta(W,K)-A\Lambda\), materializes the maximizing \(K\)-subset, and
stores only that verified subset.
\Cref{cor:no-loss-exact-cardinality-net} shows that this optimization only needs
a factor-\(b\) cardinality net, for instance dyadic sizes: monotonicity of
\(D_\eta^\theta(W,K)\) replaces exact \(K\) without the logarithmic threshold
used by weaker reporters.
\Cref{cor:average-mass-exact-prefix-screen} is the coarse-report interface on
the sharp route: a container report need only lower-certify total mass \(M\) on
support size \(s\), then choose \(K\) with \(KM/s\ge A\Lambda\).
\Cref{cor:average-density-exact-prefix-scale-choice} makes that choice
automatic on a retained cardinality net: if the report already has
\(M\ge A\Lambda\), the analytic scale \(h_*=\lceil A\Lambda s/M\rceil\) closes
after net rounding, with no extra logarithmic price.
\Cref{cor:soft-average-density-exact-prefix-scale-choice} is the responsibility
version for AQ, learned, or randomized soft panels: the proposal certifies
\(X\le\sum_p\pi_p d_\eta^\theta(p)\), sets
\(h_*=\lceil A\Lambda\sum_p\pi_p/X\rceil\), and still retains only an exact
hard prefix.
\Cref{cor:soft-exact-prefix-relaxation-tight} shows this soft interface has no
relaxation gap: if no hard exact prefix closes, no admissible responsibility
vector has value \(A\Lambda\) either.
\Cref{cor:finite-soft-exact-prefix-oracle} and
\cref{cor:soft-exact-prefix-column-generation} are the finite column-generation
form of this statement: soft proposal families are separation oracles for the
sharp hard-prefix game, and failed soft proposals are discarded without entering
the retained LP.
\Cref{cor:exact-prefix-proposal-law-separator} and
\cref{cor:sampled-soft-exact-prefix-separator} make randomized proposal panels
compatible with this sharp interface: it is enough to certify nonnegative
expected surplus \(H_{\rm ex}\), or even a one-sided soft lower bound
\(X-A\Lambda\), because preprocessing can sample until one verified top-prefix
column appears.
\Cref{cor:finite-prefix-template-separation-game} is the final finite
column-generation form of this target: preprocessing may spend arbitrary time
proposing \(W,\theta,h\) and candidate sublists, but the retained column is
accepted only when the verified surplus
\(V_\eta(T)-\Theta_C L_b(h_T)\) is nonnegative against the current cohort law.
If the dominated-load certificate fails, one cohort law witnesses negative
surplus for every generated template.
\Cref{cor:prefix-template-column-generation} turns this into an exact
build-time algorithm for any finite implicit universe: solve the restricted
game, ask the separator for a nonnegative-surplus prefix against the minimizing
cohort law, and add only verified records.  If the full universe satisfies the
prefix condition, this terminates after finitely many additions; if the
separator proves no such prefix exists, the certificate identifies the actual
cohort-law obstruction for that universe.
\Cref{cor:one-sided-prefix-value-column-generation} weakens the required
separator output further: the build oracle may return any retained record with a
one-sided lower value certificate \(X\le V_\eta(T)\) beating
\(\Theta_C L_b(h_T)\); later games still use the exact verified payoff of the
record.
\Cref{cor:one-sided-proposal-law-prefix-separator} makes this compatible with
randomized proposal mechanisms: a finite \(k\)-means++, additive-quantization,
range-reporting, or list-decoding batch is useful exactly when its verified
average one-sided surplus is nonnegative, and then averaging exposes one
deterministic column.
\Cref{cor:sampled-one-sided-prefix-separator} removes even the finite-batch
enumeration requirement from the theorem target: a sampleable proposal law with
nonnegative expected verified surplus can be searched by unlimited
preprocessing until a separating report is found, and only that report is
retained.
\Cref{cor:sampled-soft-prefix-proposal-separator} gives the same interface for
soft responsibilities: a proposal may output fractional inclusion weights, after
which preprocessing materializes the exact top-degree prefix and retains only
that deterministic record.
\Cref{cor:cardinality-net-cohort-superlevel-reporter} removes the need for the
separator to optimize an exact top prefix: any certified threshold list with
one-sided value \(X\ge\Theta_C L_b(h)\) is already a valid column, and failure
leaves the strict weak-type cap \(\delta h<\Theta_C L_b(h)\) for every retained
threshold-list report.
Pools with different congestion guesses may be split into dyadic \(C\)-strata and
tested by the same game within each stratum.

\begin{corollary}[Load-quantile recycled obstruction profile]
   \label{cor:load-quantile-recycled-obstruction-profile}
   Work in the notation of
   \cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen}.  The threshold screen
   \((FPS1)\) fails if and only if
   \[
      L_\infty\ge\Lambda ,
      \tag{LQO1}
   \]
   the boundary alternative fails, namely
   \[
      A L_0-S_0>0
      \qquad\text{or}\qquad
      L_0>\Lambda ,
      \tag{LQO2}
   \]
   and, whenever \(L_0<\Lambda\), the first load-crossing index
   \[
      j=\min\{i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}:L_i\ge\Lambda\}
      \tag{LQO3}
   \]
   satisfies the strict quantile deficit
   \[
      a_jL_j-S_j>(a_j-A)\Lambda .
      \tag{LQO4}
   \]
   Thus every failed scan has either \(L_0\ge\Lambda\), where the \(A\)-boundary
   already blocks the screen, or one strict deficit at the weighted
   \(\Lambda\)-quantile breakpoint.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   This is the exact negation of
   \cref{lem:load-quantile-recycled-threshold-screen}.  Failure of \((LQS2)\) is
   \((LQO1)\).  Since \(A L_0-S_0\ge0\), failure of \((LQS1)\) is \((LQO2)\).  If
   \(L_0<\Lambda\), then \((LQO1)\) makes the index \(j\) in \((LQO3)\)
   well-defined, and failure of \((LQS3)\) is exactly \((LQO4)\).  If
   \(L_0\ge\Lambda\), the quantile alternative \((LQS3)\) is inapplicable, so no
   additional condition remains.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact-load recycled obstruction profile]
   \label{cor:exact-load-recycled-obstruction-profile}
   Work in the notation of
   \cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen}.  The threshold screen
   \((FPS1)\) fails if and only if \(L_\infty\ge\Lambda\), the boundary
   alternative \((LQS1)\) fails, and, in the non-boundary case
   \(L_0<\Lambda\), the fractional \(\Lambda\)-load quantile capacity satisfies
   \[
      \widehat S_\Lambda<A\Lambda .
      \tag{ELO1}
   \]
   Thus, after excluding terminal low load and the \(A\)-boundary case, the
   entire residual obstruction is that the lowest-efficiency fractional prefix
   of exact load \(\Lambda\) has average capacity strictly below \(A\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   This is \cref{cor:load-quantile-recycled-obstruction-profile} with the
   quantile deficit \((LQO4)\) rewritten by
   \cref{lem:exact-load-recycled-quantile-screen}.  The exact-load rewrite is
   needed only when \(L_0<\Lambda\), which is precisely the non-boundary case in
   which the quantile breakpoint is active.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Variational exact-load recycled obstruction profile]
   \label{cor:variational-exact-load-recycled-obstruction-profile}
   Work in the notation of
   \cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen}.  The threshold screen
   \((FPS1)\) fails if and only if \(L_\infty\ge\Lambda\), the boundary
   alternative \((LQS1)\) fails, and, in the non-boundary case \(L_0<\Lambda\),
   there exists a fractional sublayer \(0\le y_q\le1\) of exact load
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}y_q\ell_q=\Lambda
      \tag{VEO1}
   \]
   whose capacity is strictly deficient:
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}y_qs_q<A\Lambda .
      \tag{VEO2}
   \]
   Moreover, the deficient sublayer may be chosen as the lowest-efficiency
   fractional prefix from \cref{lem:exact-load-recycled-quantile-screen}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{lem:variational-exact-load-recycled-screen}, the minimum capacity
   among exact-load fractional sublayers is \(\widehat S_\Lambda\).  Thus the
   exact-load obstruction \((ELO1)\) from
   \cref{cor:exact-load-recycled-obstruction-profile} is equivalent to the
   existence of a fractional sublayer satisfying \((VEO1)\)--\((VEO2)\), and an
   optimizer is the lowest-efficiency fractional prefix.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dominated-load recycled obstruction profile]
   \label{cor:dominated-load-recycled-obstruction-profile}
   Work in the notation of
   \cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen}.  The threshold screen
   \((FPS1)\) fails if and only if \(L_\infty\ge\Lambda\), the boundary
   alternative \((LQS1)\) fails, and, in the non-boundary case \(L_0<\Lambda\),
   there exists a probability vector \(\nu\) satisfying
   \[
      0\le\nu_q\le\frac{\ell_q}{\Lambda},
      \qquad
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}\nu_q=1,
      \tag{DLO1}
   \]
   whose average efficiency is strictly deficient:
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}\nu_q\sigma_q<A .
      \tag{DLO2}
   \]
   Moreover, the deficient \(\nu\) may be chosen by filling the lowest
   efficiencies up to the load cap \(\ell_q/\Lambda\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   This is \cref{cor:variational-exact-load-recycled-obstruction-profile} under
   the change of variables from \cref{lem:dominated-load-recycled-screen}.  The
   extremal choice follows from the lowest-efficiency prefix optimizer in
   \cref{lem:variational-exact-load-recycled-screen}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite-prefix recycled obstruction profile]
   \label{cor:finite-prefix-recycled-obstruction-profile}
   Work in the notation of
   \cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen}.  The threshold screen
   \((FPS1)\) fails if and only if
   \[
      L_\infty\ge\Lambda ,
      \tag{FPO1}
   \]
   \[
      a_iL_i-S_i>(a_i-A)\Lambda
      \qquad(1\le i\le k),
      \tag{FPO2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      A L_0-S_0>0
      \qquad\text{or}\qquad
      L_0>\Lambda .
      \tag{FPO3}
   \]
   Equivalently, every remaining failed finite-prefix scan has a strict
   positive breakpoint deficit profile
   \[
      a_i(L_i-\Lambda)-(S_i-A\Lambda)>0
      \qquad(1\le i\le k),
      \tag{FPO4}
   \]
   together with large total load and a nontrivial \(A\)-boundary obstruction.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   This is the exact negation of the three finite alternatives in
   \cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen}.  The only point to note
   is that \(A L_0-S_0\ge0\), because every query in the \(a_0=A\) prefix has
   \(\sigma_q\le A\).  Thus failure of \((FPS2)\) is exactly \((FPO3)\), while
   failure of \((FPS3)\) and \((FPS4)\) gives \((FPO2)\) and \((FPO1)\).
   The displayed form \((FPO4)\) is just \((FPO2)\) rearranged.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Integrated recycled-threshold obstruction]
   \label{lem:integrated-recycled-threshold-obstruction}
   Work in the notation of
   \cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen}.  Define
   the low-efficiency shortfall curve
   \[
      M(t)=
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}(t-\sigma_q)_+\ell_q
      =
      tL(t)-S(t)
      \qquad(t>A),
   \]
   and the excess-area curve
   \[
      E(t)=M(t)-(t-A)\Lambda .
      \tag{ITO1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      E(t)=
      A L_0-S_0
      +
      \int_A^t (L(u)-\Lambda)\,du
      \qquad(t>A),
      \tag{ITO2}
   \]
   where \(L(u)=\sum_{\sigma_q\le u}\ell_q\).  Consequently the threshold
   screen \((FPS1)\) fails if and only if
   \[
      A L_0-S_0
      +
      \int_A^t (L(u)-\Lambda)\,du
      >
      0
      \qquad\text{for every }t>A.
      \tag{ITO3}
   \]
   In particular, a failed finite-prefix scan is equivalently a cumulative
   excess-load profile whose area never drops to zero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The equality \(M(t)=tL(t)-S(t)\) follows by grouping the terms with
   \(\sigma_q\le t\).  Extend \(M\) continuously to \(A\).  It is continuous and
   piecewise affine, and its derivative agrees with the step function \(L(u)\)
   away from the finitely many efficiency breakpoints.  Also
   \[
      M(A)=\sum_{\sigma_q\le A}(A-\sigma_q)\ell_q=A L_0-S_0.
   \]
   Integrating this step function from \(A\) to \(t\) gives
   \[
      M(t)=A L_0-S_0+\int_A^t L(u)\,du,
   \]
   and subtracting \((t-A)\Lambda\) gives \((ITO2)\).  The threshold screen is
   exactly the existence of \(t>A\) with \(E(t)\le0\), so its failure is
   \((ITO3)\).
\end{proof}

The transport formulation is useful because it cleanly separates the two
remaining tasks.  The annular witnesses are far points and still cannot be used
as cover columns.  A geometric or list-recovery argument must instead construct
a low-congestion transport from those annular incidences into actual
near-shadow mass.  If it does, \cref{lem:annular-shadow-transport-reporter}
turns that transport into the same verified scalar reporter as before.  If the
LP remains infeasible, \cref{cor:annular-shadow-transport-obstruction} and
\cref{cor:annular-shadow-congestion-lower-bound} say that every such transport
must have large congestion.  \Cref{lem:annular-shadow-cut-normal-form} and
\cref{cor:cut-certified-annular-reporter} make the same failure cut-based:
for every proposed retained container and target mass, some sublayer of the
annular queries has annular demand larger than its true near-shadow neighborhood
capacity plus the allowed unshipped tail.  Thus the current irreducible
obstruction can be stated as a purely geometric Hall failure: a query-price-heavy
annular layer exists, but no retained smaller-radius container receives a large
fraction of its incidences into the true near-shadow potential at
Renyi-affordable congestion.  \Cref{cor:half-mass-excess-cut-obstruction}
removes the last target-mass parameter: any container whose half-mass transport
would be affordable must have a sublayer \(Y\) with excess
\(\sum_{q\in Y}b_q-C D_W^\theta(Y)>B_{\rm tot}/2\).  The next geometric theorem
can therefore try to rule out these excess cuts directly, or else feed the
large-excess sublayer back into the spherical far-load analysis.
\Cref{lem:cut-recycled-annular-sublayer} makes that feedback canonical: every
such cut contains a dyadic cut-restricted annular layer that preserves a
logarithmic fraction of the annular load while the proposed retained core sees
only \(O(H_m(\Delta)/C)\) times that load as true near-shadow capacity.  Thus the
remaining obstruction can be searched as a weighted list-recovery/range-reporting
problem on these recycled sublayers, rather than as a choice of disjoint dense
clusters.  Equivalently,
\cref{cor:recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices} says that a separator only has
to rule out those recycled layers for one affordable retained container; doing so
closes the local fractional cover.
\Cref{lem:lagrange-recycled-sublayer-screen} and
\cref{cor:lagrange-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices} give the additive form
of the same target: for each dyadic annular size level, it is enough to find a
positive multiplier \(\lambda\) for which the total positive query deficit
\(\sum_q((2H/C+\lambda)\Delta'\bar\tau_q-s_{W,\theta}(q))_+\) is below the
Lagrange budget.  \Cref{lem:fractional-recycled-layer-dual-normal-form}
identifies this condition as the positive-multiplier dual certificate for a
fractional bad-sublayer knapsack.  Thus the remaining separator can be searched
as a one-dimensional dual screen over query-wise near-shadow masses, rather
than as an all-subsets Hall check.  \Cref{lem:threshold-recycled-bad-layers}
gives the matching primal search form: any fractional bad sublayer is witnessed
by a low-efficiency prefix in the ratios \(s_{W,\theta}(q)/(\Delta'\bar\tau_q)\),
with at most one fractional boundary level.
\Cref{cor:threshold-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices} packages this into a
build-facing certificate: for each dyadic annular size level it is enough to
sort queries by that efficiency and find one threshold whose low-efficiency
prefix passes the scalar inequality.
\Cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen} and
\cref{cor:finite-prefix-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices} make the search
finite: only the sorted prefix breakpoints, the right-limit at \(A\), and the
terminal low-total-load case can certify the threshold screen.
\Cref{lem:load-quantile-recycled-threshold-screen} and
\cref{cor:load-quantile-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices} sharpen this
further: because the excess curve is convex, all positive breakpoints collapse
to the first one whose cumulative load reaches \(\Lambda\).  The build-time
certificate is therefore a weighted-quantile test, not a full prefix scan.
\Cref{lem:exact-load-recycled-quantile-screen} and
\cref{cor:exact-load-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices} remove the remaining
overshoot from that test in the non-boundary case: the reporter only has to
certify that the lowest-efficiency fractional prefix of exact load \(\Lambda\)
has capacity at least \(A\Lambda\).
\Cref{lem:variational-exact-load-recycled-screen} and
\cref{cor:variational-exact-load-recycled-separator-suffices} remove the sorting
language entirely: equivalently, every fractional sublayer of exact load
\(\Lambda\) must have near-shadow capacity at least \(A\Lambda\).
\Cref{lem:exact-load-margin-extension} shows why this exact-load condition is
not merely a boundary artifact: once it holds, every larger fractional layer has
strict positive margin because all additional load has efficiency \(>A\).
\Cref{lem:dominated-load-recycled-screen} and
\cref{cor:dominated-load-recycled-separator-suffices} normalize the exact-load
condition further: it is enough to prove that every probability distribution
dominated by the normalized query load has average near-shadow efficiency at
least \(A\).
\Cref{cor:dominated-load-recycled-local-cover-endpoint} packages this as the
current local theorem target: one affordable retained container must pass the
dominated-load mean-efficiency test at every dyadic annular level, and then the
local fractional cover is feasible.
\Cref{lem:finite-dominated-load-proposal-game} gives the corresponding fully
fractional finite-pool target: after terminal and boundary alternatives are
removed, either a proposal law over affordable retained records passes every
dominated-load test in the averaged sense, or a single level-weighted family of
dominated query distributions prices every affordable record below \(A\).  This
is the column-generation obstruction that a list-decoding, range-reporting, or
additive-quantization theorem should beat.
\Cref{cor:exact-load-dominated-proposal-obstruction} rewrites that obstruction as
a law over exact-load cohorts, each with at most one fractional query.  This is
the discrete cohort form needed for finite reporter or integer-materialization
arguments.
\Cref{cor:exact-load-cohort-law-separator} turns it into the sharp finite-pool
separator target: every law over those exact-load cohorts must be beaten by one
affordable retained record.
\Cref{cor:cohort-law-scalar-prefix-normal-form} then removes the last record
notation: a cohort law induces a scalar degree \(d_\eta^\theta\) on data points,
and the retained oracle only has to find an affordable top-\(K\) prefix with mass
at least \(A\Lambda\).
\Cref{cor:cohort-law-weak-type-superlevel} gives the equivalent weak-type
superlevel target: find a materializable affordable superlevel with
\(\delta h\ge A\Lambda\), or else every such superlevel obeys the strict cap
\(\delta h<A\Lambda\).
\Cref{cor:load-quantile-recycled-obstruction-profile} gives the matching
failure form: after the terminal and \(A\)-boundary cases are excluded, one
strict deficit at this weighted quantile is the entire obstruction.
\Cref{cor:exact-load-recycled-obstruction-profile} rewrites the same residual as
\(\widehat S_\Lambda<A\Lambda\), which is the clean exact-load form for the
remaining range-reporting/list-recovery theorem.
\Cref{cor:variational-exact-load-recycled-obstruction-profile} gives the
