      >
      b\,\psi\left(
         A_y\mu^\rho
         +
         \sigma\,\mu^{1-\rho}(\mu+\mu^2)^\rho
      \right).
      \tag{MIL3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The random list has
   \[
      \E V(\mathcal L)=V_\pi,
      \qquad
      \E K=\mu .
   \]
   Since \(0<\rho<1\), Jensen gives \(\E K^\rho\le\mu^\rho\).  Log-convexity of
   \(L_p\)-moments between powers \(1\) and \(2\) gives
   \[
      \E K^{1+\rho}
      \le
      (\E K)^{1-\rho}(\E K^2)^\rho
      \le
      \mu^{1-\rho}M_2^\rho .
   \]
   Thus \((MIL2)\) implies \((RLP1)\), and
   \cref{lem:random-list-proposal-criterion} applies.  For independent Bernoulli
   inclusion,
   \[
      \E K^2
      =
      \mu^2+\sum_{p\in W}\pi_p(1-\pi_p)
      \le
      \mu^2+\mu,
   \]
   giving \((MIL3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Query-layer seeded and marginal proposals]
   \label{cor:query-layer-seeded-marginal-proposals}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:random-list-proposal-criterion}, and fix
   fractional query weights \(0\le y_q\le1\).  For
   \(t\in(0,1]\), let \(Q_t(y)\) and \(A_t\) be as in
   \cref{lem:query-layer-random-list-proposal}.

   First, in the seeded setting of
   \cref{cor:seeded-list-proposal-criterion}, define
   \[
      V_{s,t}
      =
      \sum_{p\in L_s}
      \sum_{q\in Q_t(y):(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{QSM1}
   \]
   If \((SLP1)\) holds for the fractional weights \(y\), then there is a
   threshold \(t\in(0,1]\) such that
   \[
      \E_sV_{s,t}
      >
      b\,\psi\left(
         A_t\,\E_sK_s^\rho+\sigma\,\E_sK_s^{1+\rho}
      \right).
      \tag{QSM2}
   \]
   Hence some deterministic seed \(s\) and the ordinary query layer \(Q_t(y)\)
   expose an available paid prefix with positive repair reduced gain.

   Second, in the marginal-incidence setting of
   \cref{cor:marginal-list-proposal-criterion}, define
   \[
      V_{\pi,t}
      =
      \sum_{p\in W}\pi_p
      \sum_{q\in Q_t(y):(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{QSM3}
   \]
   If \((MIL2)\) holds for the fractional weights \(y\), then there is a
   threshold \(t\in(0,1]\) such that
   \[
      V_{\pi,t}
      >
      b\,\psi\left(
         A_t\mu^\rho+\sigma\,\mu^{1-\rho}M_2^\rho
      \right).
      \tag{QSM4}
   \]
   Hence the marginal proposal on the ordinary query layer \(Q_t(y)\) exposes
   an available paid prefix with positive repair reduced gain.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The seeded law \(s\mapsto L_s\) is a random list law, so
   \cref{lem:query-layer-random-list-proposal} applied to \((SLP1)\) gives
   \((QSM2)\).  Applying \cref{cor:seeded-list-proposal-criterion} with the
   integral query weights \(\mathbf 1_{Q_t(y)}\) gives the deterministic seed
   and positive prefix.

   For the marginal statement, layer-cake gives
   \[
      V_\pi=\int_0^1V_{\pi,t}\,dt,
      \qquad
      A_y=\int_0^1A_t\,dt .
   \]
   If \((MIL2)\) holds, then
   \[
      \int_0^1
      \left[
         V_{\pi,t}-b\,\psi A_t\mu^\rho
      \right]dt
      >
      b\,\psi\sigma\,\mu^{1-\rho}M_2^\rho .
   \]
   Some threshold \(t\) therefore satisfies \((QSM4)\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:marginal-list-proposal-criterion} with integral query weights
   \(\mathbf 1_{Q_t(y)}\) gives the positive prefix.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[List-proposal separation implies the hit-kernel cover]
   \label{cor:list-proposal-hit-kernel-cover}
   Work in the setting of \cref{asm:paid-atomized-prefix-separator}, and assume
   every container has exponent \(0<\rho_W<1\) and \(b\)-dense available
   cardinalities in the sense of \((CNW0)\).  Suppose that every nonnegative
   price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\)
   admits a certified container \(W\), fractional query weights \(0\le y_q\le1\),
   and one of the following certificates:
   \begin{itemize}
      \item a random list \(\mathcal L\subseteq W\) satisfying \((RLP1)\);
      \item a finite seed law satisfying \((SLP1)\);
      \item inclusion marginals and a second-moment bound satisfying \((MIL2)\).
   \end{itemize}
   Then \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose the hit-kernel cover were infeasible.  As in the proof of
   \cref{cor:atomized-paid-core-hit-kernel-cover}, there is a nonnegative price
   system satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) with nonpositive repair reduced gain
   on every Boolean core record, hence on every available paid prefix.  Apply
   the assumed list-proposal separator to this price system.  In the first case,
   \cref{lem:random-list-proposal-criterion} exposes an available paid prefix
   with positive repair reduced gain.  In the second and third cases,
   \cref{cor:seeded-list-proposal-criterion} and
   \cref{cor:marginal-list-proposal-criterion} do the same.  This contradicts
   the residual nonpositive-gain certificate.  Hence the primitive hit-kernel
   cover is feasible.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Boolean query-layer list-proposal separator]
   \label{cor:boolean-query-layer-list-proposal-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:list-proposal-hit-kernel-cover}.  The
   hypothesis of that corollary is equivalent to the following Boolean-query
   form.  Every nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) admits a certified container \(W\), an ordinary query
   layer \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\), and, writing
   \[
      A_{Q'}=\sum_{q\in Q'}\tau_q,
      \qquad
      \rho=\rho_W,\qquad
      \psi=\psi_W,
   \]
   one of the following certificates:
   \begin{itemize}
      \item a random list \(\mathcal L\subseteq W\), with \(K=|\mathcal L|\),
      such that
      \[
         \E\sum_{p\in\mathcal L}
         \sum_{q\in Q':(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
         >
         b\,\psi\left(
            A_{Q'}\,\E K^\rho+\sigma\,\E K^{1+\rho}
         \right);
         \tag{BQL1}
      \]
      \item a finite seed law \(s\sim\nu\), with certified lists
      \(L_s\subseteq W\) and \(K_s=|L_s|\), such that
      \[
         \E_s
         \sum_{p\in L_s}
         \sum_{q\in Q':(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
         >
         b\,\psi\left(
            A_{Q'}\,\E_sK_s^\rho+\sigma\,\E_sK_s^{1+\rho}
         \right);
         \tag{BQL2}
      \]
      \item inclusion marginals \(0\le\pi_p\le1\) and a second-moment bound
      \(M_2\), with \(\mu=\sum_{p\in W}\pi_p\), such that
      \[
         \sum_{p\in W}\pi_p
         \sum_{q\in Q':(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
         >
         b\,\psi\left(
            A_{Q'}\mu^\rho+\sigma\,\mu^{1-\rho}M_2^\rho
         \right).
         \tag{BQL3}
      \]
   \end{itemize}
   Consequently the Boolean-query form also implies
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The Boolean-query form implies the hypothesis of
   \cref{cor:list-proposal-hit-kernel-cover} by taking
   \(y=\mathbf 1_{Q'}\).  Conversely, suppose the hypothesis of
   \cref{cor:list-proposal-hit-kernel-cover} holds with fractional query weights
   \(y\).  In the random-list case,
   \cref{lem:query-layer-random-list-proposal} gives a threshold
   \(Q'=Q_t(y)\) satisfying \((BQL1)\).  In the seeded and marginal cases,
   \cref{cor:query-layer-seeded-marginal-proposals} gives a threshold
   \(Q'=Q_t(y)\) satisfying \((BQL2)\) or \((BQL3)\), respectively.  Thus the two
   separator hypotheses are equivalent.  Feasibility of the hit-kernel cover is
   then \cref{cor:list-proposal-hit-kernel-cover}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Deterministic query-list verifier]
   \label{lem:deterministic-query-list-verifier}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:random-list-proposal-criterion}.  Let
   \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\) be an ordinary query layer, and put
   \[
      A_{Q'}=\sum_{q\in Q'}\tau_q .
   \]
   For a proposed certified list \(L\subseteq W\), let \(K=|L|\) and
   \[
      V_{Q'}(L)=
      \sum_{p\in L}
      \sum_{q\in Q':(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{DQL1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      V_{Q'}(L)
      >
      b\,\psi\left(A_{Q'}K^\rho+\sigma K^{1+\rho}\right),
      \tag{DQL2}
   \]
   then an available paid prefix of \(W\), sorted by the ordinary query-layer
   degree
   \[
      p\mapsto
      \sum_{q\in Q':(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
   \]
   has positive repair reduced gain.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{lem:random-list-proposal-criterion} with fractional query weights
   \(y=\mathbf 1_{Q'}\) and with the degenerate random list law supported on
   \(L\).  Then \(\E K^\rho=K^\rho\), \(\E K^{1+\rho}=K^{1+\rho}\), and
   \(\E V(\mathcal L)=V_{Q'}(L)\), so \((DQL2)\) is \((RLP1)\).  The proof of
   \cref{lem:random-list-proposal-criterion} rounds \(K\) down to an available
   cardinality and replaces \(L\) by the corresponding top-degree prefix, which
   is the claimed positive-gain Boolean core.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Canonical query side for a proposed list]
   \label{lem:canonical-query-side-list-verifier}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:deterministic-query-list-verifier}.  For a
   proposed certified list \(L\subseteq W\), put \(K=|L|\) and
   \[
      h_L(q)=
      \sum_{p\in L:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{CQL1}
   \]
   Define the canonical positive-margin query layer
   \[
      Q^+(L)=
      \{q\in\mathcal Q:h_L(q)>b\,\psi K^\rho\tau_q\}.
      \tag{CQL2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}
      \bigl(h_L(q)-b\,\psi K^\rho\tau_q\bigr)_+
      >
      b\,\psi\sigma K^{1+\rho},
      \tag{CQL3}
   \]
   then \(Q^+(L)\) and \(L\) satisfy \((DQL2)\).  Consequently an available
   paid prefix of \(W\) has positive repair reduced gain.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed list \(L\) and cardinality \(K\), the surplus in \((DQL2)\) before
   paying storage is
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q'}
      \left(h_L(q)-b\,\psi K^\rho\tau_q\right).
   \]
   This is maximized over Boolean query layers by taking exactly the positive
   coordinates, namely \(Q'=Q^+(L)\), and the maximum is the left side of
   \((CQL3)\).  If \((CQL3)\) holds, then the positive-margin query layer
   satisfies
   \[
      V_{Q^+(L)}(L)
      >
      b\,\psi\left(A_{Q^+(L)}K^\rho+\sigma K^{1+\rho}\right),
   \]
   which is \((DQL2)\).  The final conclusion is
   \cref{lem:deterministic-query-list-verifier}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Query-free list proposal separator]
   \label{cor:query-free-list-proposal-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:boolean-query-layer-list-proposal-separator}.
   It is enough to prove the following query-free proposal statement.  For every
   nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\), there is a finite seed law \(s\sim\nu\) such that seed
   \(s\) chooses a certified container \(W_s\in\mathcal W\) and a certified list
   \(L_s\subseteq W_s\).  Writing
   \[
      K_s=|L_s|,
      \qquad
      \rho_s=\rho_{W_s},
      \qquad
      \psi_s=\psi_{W_s},
   \]
   and
   \[
      h_s(q)=
      \sum_{p\in L_s:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
      \tag{QFL1}
   \]
   assume
   \[
      \E_s
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}
      \bigl(h_s(q)-b\,\psi_sK_s^{\rho_s}\tau_q\bigr)_+
      >
      b\,\E_s\!\left[\psi_s\sigma K_s^{1+\rho_s}\right].
      \tag{QFL2}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Inequality \((QFL2)\) implies that some deterministic seed \(s\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_q
      \bigl(h_s(q)-b\,\psi_sK_s^{\rho_s}\tau_q\bigr)_+
      >
      b\,\psi_s\sigma K_s^{1+\rho_s}.
      \tag{QFL3}
   \]
   Applying \cref{lem:canonical-query-side-list-verifier} inside \(W_s\) to the
   list \(L_s\) exposes an available paid prefix with positive repair reduced
   gain.  As in the proof of
   \cref{cor:joint-query-list-proposal-separator}, this gives a positive Boolean
   column for every surplus price system satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\), so
   \cref{cor:atomized-paid-core-hit-kernel-cover} yields the primitive hit-kernel
   cover.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Query-free marginal proposal separator]
   \label{cor:query-free-marginal-proposal-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:boolean-query-layer-list-proposal-separator}.
   It is enough to prove the following soft, query-free proposal statement.  For
   every nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\), there is a finite seed law \(s\sim\nu\) such that seed
   \(s\) chooses a certified container \(W_s\in\mathcal W\), inclusion marginals
   \(0\le \pi_{s,p}\le1\) on \(W_s\), and a realizable second-moment bound
   \(M_{2,s}\).  Write
   \[
      \mu_s=\sum_{p\in W_s}\pi_{s,p},
      \qquad
      \rho_s=\rho_{W_s},
      \qquad
      \psi_s=\psi_{W_s},
   \]
   and
   \[
      h_s(q)=
      \sum_{p\in W_s:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
         \pi_{s,p}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{QFM1}
   \]
   Assume
   \[
      \E_s
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}
      \bigl(h_s(q)-b\,\psi_s\mu_s^{\rho_s}\tau_q\bigr)_+
      >
      b\,\E_s\!\left[
         \psi_s\sigma\,\mu_s^{1-\rho_s}M_{2,s}^{\rho_s}
      \right].
      \tag{QFM2}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Inequality \((QFM2)\) implies that some deterministic seed \(s\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_q
      \bigl(h_s(q)-b\,\psi_s\mu_s^{\rho_s}\tau_q\bigr)_+
      >
      b\,\psi_s\sigma\,\mu_s^{1-\rho_s}M_{2,s}^{\rho_s}.
      \tag{QFM3}
   \]
   Let
   \[
      Q_s^+=
      \{q\in\mathcal Q:h_s(q)>b\,\psi_s\mu_s^{\rho_s}\tau_q\}.
      \tag{QFM4}
   \]
   Then \((QFM3)\) is exactly
   \[
      \sum_{p\in W_s}\pi_{s,p}
      \sum_{q\in Q_s^+:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      >
      b\,\psi_s\left(
         \mu_s^{\rho_s}\sum_{q\in Q_s^+}\tau_q
         +\sigma\,\mu_s^{1-\rho_s}M_{2,s}^{\rho_s}
      \right).
      \tag{QFM5}
   \]
   This is the Boolean-query marginal certificate \((BQL3)\) for the ordinary
   query layer \(Q_s^+\).  Since the argument applies to every surplus price
   system satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\), the Boolean-query separator
   hypothesis holds in its marginal form.  Hence
   \cref{cor:boolean-query-layer-list-proposal-separator} gives the primitive
   hit-kernel cover.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Independent soft proposal separator]
   \label{cor:independent-soft-proposal-separator}
   In \cref{cor:query-free-marginal-proposal-separator}, it is enough that the
   seed law output only \(W_s\) and marginals \(0\le\pi_{s,p}\le1\), with
   \[
      \mu_s=\sum_{p\in W_s}\pi_{s,p},
      \qquad
      h_s(q)=
      \sum_{p\in W_s:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
         \pi_{s,p}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
   \]
   and that
   \[
      \E_s
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}
      \bigl(h_s(q)-b\,\psi_s\mu_s^{\rho_s}\tau_q\bigr)_+
      >
      b\,\E_s\!\left[
         \psi_s\sigma\,\mu_s^{1-\rho_s}(\mu_s+\mu_s^2)^{\rho_s}
      \right].
      \tag{ISP1}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.  In particular, on seeds
   with \(\mu_s\ge1\), the storage term in \((ISP1)\) is at most
   \(2\psi_s\sigma\mu_s^{1+\rho_s}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Realize each soft bucket by independent Bernoulli inclusion with probabilities
   \(\pi_{s,p}\).  Its list size \(K_s\) has
   \[
      \E[K_s^2]
      =
      \mu_s^2+\sum_{p\in W_s}\pi_{s,p}(1-\pi_{s,p})
      \le \mu_s^2+\mu_s .
   \]
   Thus \((ISP1)\) is \((QFM2)\) with
   \(M_{2,s}=\mu_s+\mu_s^2\), and
   \cref{cor:query-free-marginal-proposal-separator} applies.  If
   \(\mu_s\ge1\), then
   \[
      \mu_s^{1-\rho_s}(\mu_s+\mu_s^2)^{\rho_s}
      \le 2^{\rho_s}\mu_s^{1+\rho_s}
      \le 2\mu_s^{1+\rho_s}.
   \]
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite soft-bucket separation oracle]
   \label{cor:finite-soft-bucket-separation}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:independent-soft-proposal-separator}.  Let
   \(\mathcal B\) be a finite build-time pool of soft buckets.  A bucket
   \(B\in\mathcal B\) consists of a certified container \(W_B\in\mathcal W\) and
   marginals \(0\le\pi_{B,p}\le1\) on \(W_B\).  Put
   \[
      \mu_B=\sum_{p\in W_B}\pi_{B,p},
      \qquad
      \rho_B=\rho_{W_B},
      \qquad
      \psi_B=\psi_{W_B},
   \]
   and, for a price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\),
   \[
      h_B(q)=
      \sum_{p\in W_B:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
         \pi_{B,p}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
   \]
   Define the independent-soft reduced gain
   \[
      \mathsf{SG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(B)
      =
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}
      \bigl(h_B(q)-b\,\psi_B\mu_B^{\rho_B}\tau_q\bigr)_+
      -
      b\,\psi_B\sigma\,\mu_B^{1-\rho_B}(\mu_B+\mu_B^2)^{\rho_B}.
      \tag{FSB1}
   \]
   If every nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) has
   \[
      \max_{B\in\mathcal B}\mathsf{SG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(B)>0,
      \tag{FSB2}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.  More generally, it is
   enough that for every such price system preprocessing can produce a finite
   law on \(\mathcal B\) with positive expected \(\mathsf{SG}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((FSB2)\) holds for a price system, take the seed law in
   \cref{cor:independent-soft-proposal-separator} to be the point mass on a
   maximizing bucket \(B\).  Inequality \((ISP1)\) is exactly
   \(\mathsf{SG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(B)>0\).  Since this applies to every
   surplus price system satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\), the independent-soft
   separator gives the hit-kernel cover.

   The law version is the same averaging argument: if
   \(\E_{B\sim\nu}\mathsf{SG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(B)>0\), then some bucket in
   the support has positive soft gain, reducing to the point-mass case.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Fixed-mass soft buckets are near-hard]
   \label{lem:fixed-mass-soft-buckets-near-hard}
   Fix a certified container \(W\in\mathcal W\), a price system
   \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\), and a mass \(0\le\mu\le |W|\).  Let
   \[
      \Delta_W(\mu)=
      \{\pi\in[0,1]^W:\sum_{p\in W}\pi_p=\mu\}.
   \]
   For \(\pi\in\Delta_W(\mu)\), put
   \[
      h_\pi(q)=
      \sum_{p\in W:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
         \pi_p\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
   \]
   and define the fixed-mass soft score
   \[
      \Phi_\mu(\pi)
      =
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}
      \bigl(h_\pi(q)-b\,\psi_W\mu^{\rho_W}\tau_q\bigr)_+ .
      \tag{FMS1}
   \]
   Then \(\Phi_\mu\) is maximized over \(\Delta_W(\mu)\) by a vector with at
   most one fractional coordinate.  In particular, if \(\mu\) is an integer,
   the maximum is attained by a hard list \(L\subseteq W\) of size \(\mu\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For fixed \(\mu\), every \(h_\pi(q)\) is linear in \(\pi\), and
   \(x\mapsto x_+\) is convex.  Therefore \(\Phi_\mu\) is convex on the compact
   polytope \(\Delta_W(\mu)\), so it has a maximizer at an extreme point of that
   polytope.

   It remains only to identify the extreme points.  If two coordinates
   \(p_1,p_2\) are strictly between \(0\) and \(1\), then for sufficiently small
   \(\varepsilon>0\) both vectors obtained by adding \(\varepsilon\) to
   \(\pi_{p_1}\) and subtracting it from \(\pi_{p_2}\), or vice versa, remain in
   \(\Delta_W(\mu)\).  Their average is \(\pi\), so \(\pi\) is not extreme.
   Thus every extreme point has at most one fractional coordinate.  If
   \(\mu\) is an integer, the sum of the integral coordinates already differs
   from \(\mu\) by an integer, so the possible fractional coordinate must in
   fact be \(0\) or \(1\).  The maximizer is then an indicator vector
   \(\mathbf 1_L\) with \(|L|=\mu\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Soft gain has a near-hard maximizer]
   \label{cor:soft-gain-near-hard-maximizer}
   In the setting of \cref{cor:finite-soft-bucket-separation}, fix a container
   \(W\) and optimize \(\mathsf{SG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}\) over all marginals
   on \(W\).  A maximizer exists whose support is a hard list plus at most one
   fractional point.  If the maximizing mass is integral, the maximizer is a
   hard list.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(\pi^\star\) be any global maximizer over the compact cube
   \([0,1]^W\), and put \(\mu^\star=\sum_p\pi^\star_p\).  The full soft gain at
   fixed mass \(\mu^\star\) is the fixed-mass score
   \(\Phi_{\mu^\star}(\pi)\) minus the term
   \[
      b\,\psi_W\sigma\,(\mu^\star)^{1-\rho_W}
      (\mu^\star+(\mu^\star)^2)^{\rho_W},
   \]
   which depends only on the mass.  By
   \cref{lem:fixed-mass-soft-buckets-near-hard}, there is a near-hard
   \(\pi'\in\Delta_W(\mu^\star)\) with
   \(\Phi_{\mu^\star}(\pi')\ge\Phi_{\mu^\star}(\pi^\star)\).  Since the storage
   term is unchanged, \(\pi'\) is also a global soft-gain maximizer.  If
   \(\mu^\star\) is integral, the same lemma makes \(\pi'\) a hard list.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Positive soft gain rounds to a hard list]
   \label{cor:positive-soft-gain-hard-list}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:finite-soft-bucket-separation}, and fix one
   container \(W\).  Suppose some marginals \(\pi\in[0,1]^W\), with
   \(\mu=\sum_p\pi_p\), have positive independent-soft reduced gain:
   \[
      \sum_q
      \bigl(h_\pi(q)-b\,\psi_W\mu^{\rho_W}\tau_q\bigr)_+
      >
      b\,\psi_W\sigma\,\mu^{1-\rho_W}(\mu+\mu^2)^{\rho_W}.
      \tag{PSH1}
   \]
   Then there is an ordinary hard list \(L\subseteq W\) such that, with
   \(K=|L|\),
   \[
      \sum_q
      \left(
         \sum_{p\in L:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
         -b\,\psi_WK^{\rho_W}\tau_q
      \right)_+
      >
      b\,\psi_W\sigma K^{1+\rho_W}.
      \tag{PSH2}
   \]
   Consequently the deterministic query-free list verifier exposes a positive
   available paid prefix inside \(W\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{lem:fixed-mass-soft-buckets-near-hard}, after replacing \(\pi\) by
   a no-worse vector of the same mass, we may assume
   \[
      \pi=\mathbf 1_{L_0}+\theta\mathbf 1_x,
      \qquad
      0\le\theta<1,
      \qquad
      x\notin L_0,
   \]
   with the evident degenerate interpretation when \(\theta=0\).  Let the
   random hard list \(\mathcal L\) be \(L_0\cup\{x\}\) with probability
   \(\theta\) and \(L_0\) otherwise, and put \(K=|\mathcal L|\).  Then
   \[
      \E K=\mu,
      \qquad
      \E K^2=\mu^2+\theta(1-\theta)\le\mu^2+\mu.
      \tag{PSH3}
   \]

   For each \(q\), set
   \[
      X_q=
      \sum_{p\in\mathcal L:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      -b\,\psi_WK^{\rho_W}\tau_q .
   \]
   Since \(0<\rho_W<1\), Jensen gives
   \(\E K^{\rho_W}\le\mu^{\rho_W}\).  Hence
   \[
      \E X_q
      \ge
      h_\pi(q)-b\,\psi_W\mu^{\rho_W}\tau_q .
   \]
   Convexity of \(x_+\) gives
   \[
      \E(X_q)_+
      \ge
      (\E X_q)_+
      \ge
      \bigl(h_\pi(q)-b\,\psi_W\mu^{\rho_W}\tau_q\bigr)_+ .
      \tag{PSH4}
   \]
   Summing over \(q\), and using \((PSH1)\), gives
   \[
      \E\sum_q(X_q)_+
      >
      b\,\psi_W\sigma\,\mu^{1-\rho_W}(\mu+\mu^2)^{\rho_W}.
      \tag{PSH5}
   \]
   Log-convexity of \(L_p\)-moments between powers \(1\) and \(2\), together
   with \((PSH3)\), gives
   \[
      \E K^{1+\rho_W}
      \le
      (\E K)^{1-\rho_W}(\E K^2)^{\rho_W}
      \le
      \mu^{1-\rho_W}(\mu+\mu^2)^{\rho_W}.
      \tag{PSH6}
   \]
   Therefore the two-point hard-list law satisfies
   \[
      \E\sum_q(X_q)_+
      >
      b\,\psi_W\sigma\,\E K^{1+\rho_W}.
   \]
   Some outcome \(L\) of the law must satisfy \((PSH2)\).  Applying
   \cref{lem:canonical-query-side-list-verifier} to this hard list gives the
   final positive available prefix.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite hard-list separation oracle]
   \label{cor:finite-hard-list-separation}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:query-free-list-proposal-separator}.  Let
   \(\mathcal H\) be a finite build-time pool of certified hard lists.  An
   element \(H\in\mathcal H\) consists of a certified container
   \(W_H\in\mathcal W\) and a list \(L_H\subseteq W_H\).  Put
   \[
      K_H=|L_H|,
      \qquad
      \rho_H=\rho_{W_H},
      \qquad
      \psi_H=\psi_{W_H},
   \]
   and, for a price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\),
   \[
      h_H(q)=
      \sum_{p\in L_H:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
   \]
   Define the hard-list reduced gain
   \[
      \mathsf{HG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(H)
      =
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}
      \bigl(h_H(q)-b\,\psi_HK_H^{\rho_H}\tau_q\bigr)_+
      -
      b\,\psi_H\sigma K_H^{1+\rho_H}.
      \tag{FHL1}
   \]
   If every nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) has
   \[
      \max_{H\in\mathcal H}\mathsf{HG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(H)>0,
      \tag{FHL2}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.  More generally, it is
   enough that every such price system admit a finite law on \(\mathcal H\)
   with positive expected \(\mathsf{HG}\).

   In particular, in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-soft-bucket-separation}, a positive soft-bucket certificate
   over a container \(W\) implies a positive hard-list certificate over the same
   container.  Thus an oracle over all hard lists in the generated containers is
   at least as strong as the corresponding soft-bucket oracle.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(H\) has positive hard-list reduced gain, the point-mass seed law on
   \((W_H,L_H)\) satisfies \((QFL2)\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:query-free-list-proposal-separator} gives the primitive
   hit-kernel cover.  If a law on \(\mathcal H\) has positive expected
   \(\mathsf{HG}\), then some list in its finite support has positive
   \(\mathsf{HG}\), reducing to the point-mass case.

   The final claim is exactly \cref{cor:positive-soft-gain-hard-list}: positive
   independent-soft reduced gain in a container rounds to an ordinary hard list
   with positive canonical query-free gain.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Hard-list separation reduces to top-degree prefixes]
   \label{cor:hard-list-prefix-separation}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:finite-hard-list-separation}, and fix a
   nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\).  For a certified
   container \(W\), an ordinary query layer \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\), and an
   integer \(1\le K\le |W|\), let \(P_K(W,Q')\) be any \(K\)-point subset of
   \(W\) maximizing the query-layer paid degree
   \[
      \sum_{p\in L}
      \sum_{q\in Q':(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      \qquad(|L|=K).
   \]
   Define its prefix gain by
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \mathsf{PG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(W,Q',K)
      &=
      \sum_{p\in P_K(W,Q')}
      \sum_{q\in Q':(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}  \\
      &\quad
      -b\,\psi_WK^{\rho_W}\sum_{q\in Q'}\tau_q
      -b\,\psi_W\sigma K^{1+\rho_W}.
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{HLP1}
   \]
   If some hard list \(H=(W_H,L_H)\) has positive hard-list reduced gain, then
   with \(K=|L_H|\) and
   \[
      Q^+(H)=
      \{q\in\mathcal Q:h_H(q)>b\,\psi_HK^{\rho_H}\tau_q\},
      \tag{HLP2}
   \]
   the top-degree prefix \(P_K(W_H,Q^+(H))\) has positive prefix gain.
   Consequently its hard-list reduced gain is also positive.

   Hence, whenever the build-time universe is closed under this
   query-layer top-\(K\) replacement, the finite hard-list oracle of
   \cref{cor:finite-hard-list-separation} may be replaced by a separation
   search over triples \((W,Q',K)\) and the scalar test \((HLP1)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(H=(W,L)\), put \(K=|L|\), \(\rho=\rho_W\), and \(\psi=\psi_W\).  By
   definition,
   \[
      \mathsf{HG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(H)
      =
      \sum_q\bigl(h_H(q)-b\,\psi K^\rho\tau_q\bigr)_+
      -
      b\,\psi\sigma K^{1+\rho}.
   \]
   The positive part is obtained by the query layer \(Q^+(H)\), so
   \[
      \sum_{p\in L}
      \sum_{q\in Q^+(H):(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      >
      b\,\psi K^\rho\sum_{q\in Q^+(H)}\tau_q
      +
      b\,\psi\sigma K^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{HLP3}
   \]
   The set \(P_K(W,Q^+(H))\) maximizes the left side among all \(K\)-point
   subsets of \(W\), so it also satisfies \((HLP3)\).  This is precisely
   \[
      \mathsf{PG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(W,Q^+(H),K)>0 .
   \]
   Finally, let \(H'=(W,P_K(W,Q^+(H)))\).  Then
   \[
      \mathsf{HG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(H')
      \ge
      \mathsf{PG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(W,Q^+(H),K),
   \]
   because the hard-list hinge is the maximum over all query layers and the
   right side evaluates it only on \(Q^+(H)\).  This proves the replacement
   claim and the oracle reduction.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fractional query weights threshold to prefix certificates]
   \label{cor:fractional-query-prefix-separation}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:hard-list-prefix-separation}.  Fix a
   certified container \(W\) and an integer \(1\le K\le |W|\).  For
   \(0\le y_q\le1\), define
   \[
      d_y^\gamma(p)
      =
      \sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
   \]
   and let \(D_{W,y}^\gamma(K)\) be the sum of the largest \(K\) values of
   \(d_y^\gamma(p)\) over \(p\in W\).  If some fractional query weighting
   satisfies
   \[
      D_{W,y}^\gamma(K)
      >
      b\,\psi_WK^{\rho_W}\sum_q\tau_qy_q
      +
      b\,\psi_W\sigma K^{1+\rho_W},
      \tag{FQP1}
   \]
   then there is an ordinary query layer \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\) such that
   the top-degree prefix \(P_K(W,Q')\) has positive prefix gain
   \((HLP1)\).  Conversely, a positive prefix-gain triple \((W,Q',K)\) gives
   \((FQP1)\) with \(y=\mathbf 1_{Q'}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Define
   \[
      F(y)=
      D_{W,y}^\gamma(K)
      -
      b\,\psi_WK^{\rho_W}\sum_q\tau_qy_q
      -
      b\,\psi_W\sigma K^{1+\rho_W}.
   \]
   The function \(D_{W,y}^\gamma(K)\) is the maximum, over \(K\)-subsets
   \(L\subseteq W\), of the linear form
   \[
      \sum_{p\in L}\sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
   \]
   Hence \(F\) is convex on the cube \([0,1]^{\mathcal Q}\).  If \(F(y)>0\)
   for some fractional \(y\), then the maximum of \(F\) over the cube is
   positive and is attained at an extreme point \(y'=\mathbf 1_{Q'}\).  For
   this extreme point, \(D_{W,y'}^\gamma(K)\) is exactly the paid degree of
   \(P_K(W,Q')\) on the Boolean query layer \(Q'\), so \(F(y')>0\) is
   \((HLP1)\).  The converse is the same identity with \(y=\mathbf 1_{Q'}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite prefix separation oracle]
   \label{cor:finite-prefix-separation}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:fractional-query-prefix-separation}.  Let
   \(\mathcal P\) be a finite build-time pool of certified prefix templates.
   A template \(C\in\mathcal P\) consists of a certified container
   \(W_C\in\mathcal W\) and an available cardinality \(1\le K_C\le |W_C|\).
   For a price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\), define the prefix reduced-cost
   value
   \[
      \mathsf{PX}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(C)
      =
      \max_{0\le y_q\le1}
      \left[
         D_{W_C,y}^\gamma(K_C)
         -
         b\,\psi_CK_C^{\rho_C}\sum_q\tau_qy_q
         -
         b\,\psi_C\sigma K_C^{1+\rho_C}
      \right],
      \tag{FPS1}
   \]
   where \(\rho_C=\rho_{W_C}\) and \(\psi_C=\psi_{W_C}\).  Suppose the finite
   hard-list universe contains, for every \(C\in\mathcal P\) and every Boolean
   query layer \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\), the top-degree prefix
   \(P_{K_C}(W_C,Q')\).  If every nonnegative price system
   \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) has
   \[
      \max_{C\in\mathcal P}\mathsf{PX}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(C)>0,
      \tag{FPS2}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.

   Equivalently, \((FPS1)\) may be maximized over Boolean query layers:
   \[
      \mathsf{PX}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(C)
      =
      \max_{Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q}
      \mathsf{PG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(W_C,Q',K_C).
      \tag{FPS3}
   \]
   Thus preprocessing may use fractional query weights, cutting planes,
   range-reporting, or list-decoding to find a positive template, but the
   retained column is the ordinary Boolean prefix returned by the maximizer in
   \((FPS3)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For fixed \(C\), \cref{cor:fractional-query-prefix-separation} says exactly
   that the fractional maximum in \((FPS1)\) is positive if and only if some
   Boolean query layer \(Q'\) gives positive prefix gain for
   \(P_{K_C}(W_C,Q')\).  This proves \((FPS3)\).  Under the closure assumption,
   that prefix is an available hard list and has positive hard-list reduced
   gain by \cref{cor:hard-list-prefix-separation}.  Therefore \((FPS2)\)
   implies the hypothesis of \cref{cor:finite-hard-list-separation}, and the
   primitive hit-kernel cover follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cardinality-net prefix reduction]
   \label{cor:cardinality-net-prefix-reduction}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:finite-prefix-separation}.  Let
   \(\mathcal W_0\) be a finite family of certified containers, and suppose the
   prefix-template pool contains, for each \(W\in\mathcal W_0\), templates
   \((W,k)\) whose cardinalities \(\mathcal K_W\) are \(b_0\)-dense from below:
   for every \(1\le K\le |W|\), some \(k\in\mathcal K_W\) satisfies
   \[
      K/b_0\le k\le K .
      \tag{CNP1}
   \]
   Suppose that every nonnegative price system
   \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) admits
   \(W\in\mathcal W_0\), an integer \(1\le K\le |W|\), and fractional query
   weights \(0\le y_q\le1\) such that
   \[
      D_{W,y}^{\gamma}(K)
      >
      b\,b_0\,\psi_W\left(
         K^{\rho_W}\sum_q\tau_qy_q+\sigma K^{1+\rho_W}
      \right).
      \tag{CNP2}
   \]
   Then the finite prefix-template separator of
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-separation} holds, and hence
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.

   In particular, dyadic cardinalities give \(b_0=2\).  Thus the geometric
   separator may search arbitrary prefix sizes analytically, while the retained
   finite template pool keeps only logarithmically many cardinalities per
   container at a constant-factor slack loss.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a price system and a witness \(W,K,y\) satisfying \((CNP2)\).  Choose
   \(k\in\mathcal K_W\) satisfying \((CNP1)\).  Let
   \(a_1\ge a_2\ge\cdots\) be the sorted paid degrees
   \(d_y^\gamma(p)\) inside \(W\).  Since the \(a_i\) are nonnegative,
   \[
      D_{W,y}^\gamma(k)=\sum_{i\le k}a_i
      \ge
      \frac{k}{K}\sum_{i\le K}a_i
      \ge
      \frac1{b_0}D_{W,y}^\gamma(K).
      \tag{CNP3}
   \]
   Combining \((CNP2)\) and \((CNP3)\) gives
   \[
      D_{W,y}^{\gamma}(k)
      >
      b\,\psi_W\left(
         K^{\rho_W}\sum_q\tau_qy_q+\sigma K^{1+\rho_W}
      \right).
   \]
   Since \(k\le K\) and \(0\le\rho_W\le1\), the right side is at least
   \[
      b\,\psi_W\left(
         k^{\rho_W}\sum_q\tau_qy_q+\sigma k^{1+\rho_W}
      \right).
   \]
   Therefore the template \(C=(W,k)\) has
   \(\mathsf{PX}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(C)>0\).  This verifies \((FPS2)\), and
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-separation} gives the hit-kernel cover.  The dyadic
   statement follows because powers of two are \(2\)-dense from below.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite prefix residual envelope]
   \label{cor:finite-prefix-residual-envelope}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:finite-prefix-separation}.  If the finite
   prefix-template separator fails, then there is a nonnegative price system
   \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) such that, for
   every template \(C=(W_C,K_C)\in\mathcal P\) and every fractional query
   weighting \(0\le y_q\le1\),
   \[
      D_{W_C,y}^\gamma(K_C)
      \le
      b\,\psi_C\left(
         K_C^{\rho_C}\sum_q\tau_qy_q+\sigma K_C^{1+\rho_C}
      \right).
      \tag{FPRE1}
   \]
   Equivalently, the same envelope holds for every Boolean query layer
   \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\):
   \[
      \sum_{p\in P_{K_C}(W_C,Q')}
      \sum_{q\in Q':(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      \le
      b\,\psi_C\left(
         K_C^{\rho_C}\sum_{q\in Q'}\tau_q+\sigma K_C^{1+\rho_C}
      \right).
      \tag{FPRE2}
   \]
   Thus the remaining geometric theorem may be stated as ruling out a paid
   residual price system satisfying these top-degree prefix envelopes for the
   retained container/cardinality templates.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Failure of the finite prefix-template separator means that some nonnegative
   price system satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) has
   \(\mathsf{PX}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(C)\le0\) for every
   \(C\in\mathcal P\).  Expanding the definition \((FPS1)\) gives
   \((FPRE1)\) for every fractional query weighting.  The Boolean form
   \((FPRE2)\) is the same statement with \(y=\mathbf 1_{Q'}\), using the
   identity \((FPS3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cardinality-net residual for all prefix sizes]
   \label{cor:cardinality-net-prefix-residual}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:finite-prefix-residual-envelope}.  Let
   \(\mathcal W_0\) be a finite family of certified containers, and suppose
   that, for each \(W\in\mathcal W_0\), the template pool contains
   cardinalities \(\mathcal K_W\) that are \(b_0\)-dense from above:
   for every \(1\le K\le |W|\), some \(k\in\mathcal K_W\) satisfies
   \[
      K\le k\le b_0K .
      \tag{CNR1}
   \]
   If the finite prefix-template separator fails, then the residual price system
   from \cref{cor:finite-prefix-residual-envelope} satisfies, for every
   \(W\in\mathcal W_0\), every integer \(1\le K\le |W|\), and every fractional
   query weighting \(0\le y_q\le1\),
   \[
      D_{W,y}^\gamma(K)
      \le
      b\,\psi_W\left(
         b_0^{\rho_W}K^{\rho_W}\sum_q\tau_qy_q
         +
         \sigma b_0^{1+\rho_W}K^{1+\rho_W}
      \right).
      \tag{CNR2}
   \]
   In particular, since \(0\le\rho_W\le1\), the right side is at most
   \[
      b\,b_0^2\,\psi_W
      \left(
         K^{\rho_W}\sum_q\tau_qy_q+\sigma K^{1+\rho_W}
      \right).
      \tag{CNR3}
   \]
   Thus dyadic retained cardinalities leave an arbitrary-size paid residual
   envelope with only a constant-factor loss.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let the residual price system be the one from
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-residual-envelope}.  Fix \(W,K,y\), and choose
   \(k\in\mathcal K_W\) satisfying \((CNR1)\).  Since \(k\ge K\), monotonicity
   of top-prefix sums gives
   \[
      D_{W,y}^\gamma(K)\le D_{W,y}^\gamma(k).
   \]
   Applying \((FPRE1)\) to the retained template \(C=(W,k)\) gives
   \[
      D_{W,y}^\gamma(k)
      \le
      b\,\psi_W\left(k^{\rho_W}\sum_q\tau_qy_q+\sigma k^{1+\rho_W}\right).
   \]
   The upper bound \(k\le b_0K\) yields \((CNR2)\).  Finally
   \(b_0^{\rho_W}\le b_0^2\) and \(b_0^{1+\rho_W}\le b_0^2\) for
   \(b_0\ge1\) and \(0\le\rho_W\le1\), proving \((CNR3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[All-size prefix weak-type residual]
   \label{cor:all-size-prefix-weak-type-residual}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:cardinality-net-prefix-residual}.  Assume
   \(0<\rho_W<1\).  If the finite prefix-template separator fails, then the
   residual price system from \cref{cor:finite-prefix-residual-envelope}
   satisfies the following for every \(W\in\mathcal W_0\), every fractional
   query weighting \(0\le y_q\le1\), and every level \(\delta>0\).  Put
   \[
      A_y=\sum_q\tau_qy_q,\qquad
      h_\delta=
      |\{p\in W:d_y^\gamma(p)\ge\delta\}|,
      \qquad
      \rho=\rho_W,\qquad
      \psi=\psi_W .
   \]
   If \(h_\delta>0\), then
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      b\,\psi\left(
         b_0^\rho A_yh_\delta^{\rho-1}
         +
         \sigma b_0^{1+\rho}h_\delta^\rho
      \right).
      \tag{ASW1}
   \]
   Consequently, if \(\sigma=0\), then
   \[
      h_\delta
      \le
      \left(\frac{b\,b_0^\rho\psi A_y}{\delta}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)}.
      \tag{ASW2}
   \]
   If \(\sigma>0\), at least one of
   \[
      h_\delta
      \le
      \left(\frac{2b\,b_0^\rho\psi A_y}{\delta}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \tag{ASW3}
   \]
   or
   \[
      h_\delta
      \ge
      \left(\frac{\delta}
                 {2b\,b_0^{1+\rho}\psi\sigma}\right)^{1/\rho}
      \tag{ASW4}
   \]
   holds.  Moreover, if \(A_y>0\), \(\sigma>0\), and
   \[
      k_\star=\frac{(1-\rho)A_y}{\rho\sigma b_0},
   \]
   then every nonzero superlevel with
   \(a^{-1}k_\star\le h_\delta\le ak_\star\) satisfies
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      a\,b\,b_0\,C_\rho\,\psi A_y^\rho\sigma^{1-\rho},
      \qquad
      C_\rho=\rho^{-\rho}(1-\rho)^{-(1-\rho)}.
      \tag{ASW5}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(h_\delta>0\), then the top \(h_\delta\) points of \(W\) by
   \(d_y^\gamma\)-degree all have degree at least \(\delta\).  Hence
   \[
      D_{W,y}^\gamma(h_\delta)\ge \delta h_\delta .
   \]
   Applying \((CNR2)\) with \(K=h_\delta\) and dividing by \(h_\delta\) gives
   \((ASW1)\).

   When \(\sigma=0\), rearranging \((ASW1)\) gives \((ASW2)\).  When
   \(\sigma>0\), at least one of the two summands on the right of \((ASW1)\)
   is at least \(\delta/(2b\psi)\), giving \((ASW3)\) or \((ASW4)\).

   For the balanced statement, minimize
   \[
      b_0^\rho A_yh^{\rho-1}
      +
      \sigma b_0^{1+\rho}h^\rho
   \]
   over \(h>0\).  The stationary point is
   \(k_\star=(1-\rho)A_y/(\rho\sigma b_0)\), and the minimum is
   \[
      C_\rho\,b_0\,A_y^\rho\sigma^{1-\rho}.
   \]
   If \(h_\delta=\lambda k_\star\) with
   \(\lambda\in[a^{-1},a]\), the same calculation as in
   \cref{lem:paid-prefix-weak-type} increases the value by at most a factor
   \(a\).  Combining with \((ASW1)\) gives \((ASW5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[All-size weak-type prefix separator]
   \label{cor:all-size-weak-type-prefix-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:cardinality-net-prefix-residual}, and
   assume every container in \(\mathcal W_0\) has exponent \(0<\rho_W<1\).
   Suppose that every nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\)
   satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) admits a container
   \(W\in\mathcal W_0\), fractional query weights \(0\le y_q\le1\), and a level
   \(\delta>0\), with \(h_\delta=|\{p\in W:d_y^\gamma(p)\ge\delta\}|>0\),
   satisfying one of the following forbidden weak-type alternatives.  Writing
   \(A_y=\sum_q\tau_qy_q\), \(\rho=\rho_W\), and \(\psi=\psi_W\):
   if \(\sigma=0\),
   \[
      h_\delta
      >
      \left(\frac{b\,b_0^\rho\psi A_y}{\delta}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)};
      \tag{ASWS1}
   \]
   if \(\sigma>0\),
   \[
      h_\delta
      >
      \left(\frac{2b\,b_0^\rho\psi A_y}{\delta}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      h_\delta
      <
      \left(\frac{\delta}
                 {2b\,b_0^{1+\rho}\psi\sigma}\right)^{1/\rho};
      \tag{ASWS2}
   \]
   or, for some \(a\ge1\), \(A_y>0\), \(\sigma>0\),
   \[
      a^{-1}\frac{(1-\rho)A_y}{\rho\sigma b_0}
      \le h_\delta\le
      a\frac{(1-\rho)A_y}{\rho\sigma b_0},
      \qquad
      \delta>
      a\,b\,b_0\,C_\rho\,\psi A_y^\rho\sigma^{1-\rho}.
      \tag{ASWS3}
   \]
   Then the finite prefix-template separator holds.  Consequently
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible, and the local and global
   endpoints of \cref{cor:finite-prefix-local-filter-cover} and
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-polylog-endpoint} apply.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the finite prefix-template separator failed, then
   \cref{cor:all-size-prefix-weak-type-residual} would apply to the residual
   price system.  Alternative \((ASWS1)\) contradicts \((ASW2)\).  Alternative
   \((ASWS2)\) contradicts the disjunction \((ASW3)\)--\((ASW4)\).  Alternative
   \((ASWS3)\) contradicts \((ASW5)\).  Hence no residual failure is possible,
   so the finite prefix-template separator holds.  The remaining conclusions
   are \cref{cor:finite-prefix-separation},
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-local-filter-cover}, and
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-polylog-endpoint}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[All-size aggregate list-moment residual]
   \label{cor:all-size-aggregate-list-moment-residual}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:all-size-prefix-weak-type-residual}.  If
   the finite prefix-template separator fails, then the residual price system
   from \cref{cor:finite-prefix-residual-envelope} satisfies the following
   averaged envelope.  Fix \(W\in\mathcal W_0\), fractional query weights
   \(0\le y_q\le1\), and a finite nonnegative level weighting
   \((\lambda_i,\delta_i)_i\).  Put
   \[
      h_i=|\{p\in W:d_y^\gamma(p)\ge\delta_i\}|,
      \qquad
      M_0=\sum_i\lambda_i,
      \qquad
      M_1=\sum_i\lambda_i h_i,
   \]
   \[
      M_{1+\rho}=\sum_i\lambda_i h_i^{1+\rho},
      \qquad
      B=\sum_i\lambda_i\delta_i h_i,
      \qquad
      A_y=\sum_q\tau_qy_q,
      \qquad
      \rho=\rho_W,\quad \psi=\psi_W .
   \]
   Then
   \[
      B
      \le
      b\,\psi\left(
         b_0^\rho A_yM_0^{1-\rho}M_1^\rho
         +
         \sigma b_0^{1+\rho}M_{1+\rho}
      \right).
      \tag{ASLM1}
   \]
   If the supported levels have \(h_i\le H\), then
   \[
      B
      \le
      b\,\psi\left(
         b_0^\rho A_yM_0^{1-\rho}M_1^\rho
         +
         \sigma b_0^{1+\rho}H^\rho M_1
      \right).
      \tag{ASLM2}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(M_0=0\), then \(B=M_1=M_{1+\rho}=0\), and the claim is trivial.
   Assume \(M_0>0\).  For every level with \(h_i>0\), multiplying \((ASW1)\) by
   \(h_i\) gives
   \[
      \delta_i h_i
      \le
      b\,\psi\left(
         b_0^\rho A_yh_i^\rho
         +
         \sigma b_0^{1+\rho}h_i^{1+\rho}
      \right).
      \tag{ASLM3}
   \]
   The same inequality is trivial when \(h_i=0\).  Multiplying by
   \(\lambda_i\) and summing gives
   \[
      B
      \le
      b\,\psi\left(
         b_0^\rho A_y\sum_i\lambda_i h_i^\rho
         +
         \sigma b_0^{1+\rho}M_{1+\rho}
      \right).
   \]
   By concavity of \(x^\rho\),
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_i h_i^\rho
      \le
      M_0^{1-\rho}M_1^\rho .
   \]
   This proves \((ASLM1)\).  If \(h_i\le H\) on the support, then
   \(M_{1+\rho}\le H^\rho M_1\), giving \((ASLM2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[All-size aggregate list-moment separator]
   \label{cor:all-size-aggregate-list-moment-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:all-size-weak-type-prefix-separator}.  It
   is enough to prove the following averaged geometric statement.  Every
   nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) admits a container \(W\in\mathcal W_0\), fractional
   query weights \(0\le y_q\le1\), and a finite nonnegative level weighting
   whose quantities \(B,M_0,M_1,M_{1+\rho}\) violate \((ASLM1)\).  It is also
   enough to violate the capped form \((ASLM2)\) for a certified cap \(H\) with
   \(h_i\le H\) on the supported levels.

   Under this averaged separator, the finite prefix-template separator holds.
   Consequently \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible, and the local and
   global endpoints of \cref{cor:finite-prefix-local-filter-cover} and
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-polylog-endpoint} apply.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the finite prefix-template separator failed, then
   \cref{cor:all-size-aggregate-list-moment-residual} would apply to the
   residual price system, ruling out both the uncapped and capped violations.
   Therefore no residual failure is possible.  Feasibility and the endpoint
   conclusions follow from \cref{cor:finite-prefix-separation},
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-local-filter-cover}, and
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-polylog-endpoint}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[All-size average list-size panel criterion]
   \label{cor:all-size-average-list-size-panel}
   In \cref{cor:all-size-aggregate-list-moment-separator}, a probability law
   \(\nu\) on finitely many levels is sufficient if, with
   \(H_\delta=|\{p\in W:d_y^\gamma(p)\ge\delta\}|\),
   \[
      \E_{\delta\sim\nu}\delta H_\delta
      >
      b\,\psi\left(
         b_0^\rho A_y\bigl(\E_{\delta\sim\nu}H_\delta\bigr)^\rho
         +
         \sigma b_0^{1+\rho}\E_{\delta\sim\nu}H_\delta^{1+\rho}
      \right).
      \tag{ASAP1}
   \]
   In a capped-list form, it is enough that \(H_\delta\le H\) on the support of
   \(\nu\) and
   \[
      \E_{\delta\sim\nu}\delta H_\delta
      >
      b\,\psi\left(
         b_0^\rho A_y\bigl(\E_{\delta\sim\nu}H_\delta\bigr)^\rho
         +
         \sigma b_0^{1+\rho}H^\rho\E_{\delta\sim\nu}H_\delta
      \right).
      \tag{ASAP2}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Use the finite level panel with weights \(\lambda_\delta=\nu(\delta)\).  Then
   \(M_0=1\), \(M_1=\E H_\delta\),
   \(M_{1+\rho}=\E H_\delta^{1+\rho}\), and
   \(B=\E \delta H_\delta\).  The displayed inequalities are exactly violations
   of \((ASLM1)\) and \((ASLM2)\), respectively, so
   \cref{cor:all-size-aggregate-list-moment-separator} applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[All-size random-list proposal separator]
   \label{cor:all-size-random-list-proposal}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:cardinality-net-prefix-residual}.  Suppose
   every nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) admits a container \(W\in\mathcal W_0\), fractional
   query weights \(0\le y_q\le1\), and a random certified list
   \(\mathcal L\subseteq W\).  Put
   \[
      A_y=\sum_q\tau_qy_q,\qquad
      K=|\mathcal L|,\qquad
      V(\mathcal L)=\sum_{p\in\mathcal L}d_y^\gamma(p),
      \qquad
      \rho=\rho_W,\quad \psi=\psi_W .
   \]
   If
   \[
      \E V(\mathcal L)
      >
      b\,\psi\left(
         b_0^\rho A_y\,\E K^\rho
         +
         \sigma b_0^{1+\rho}\,\E K^{1+\rho}
      \right),
      \tag{ASRL1}
   \]
   then the finite prefix-template separator holds.  Consequently
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible, and the local and global
   endpoints of \cref{cor:finite-prefix-local-filter-cover} and
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-polylog-endpoint} apply.

   In particular, it is enough to prove the slightly stronger but simpler
   moment bound
   \[
      \E V(\mathcal L)
      >
      b\,\psi\left(
         b_0^\rho A_y\,(\E K)^\rho
         +
         \sigma b_0^{1+\rho}\,\E K^{1+\rho}
      \right).
      \tag{ASRL2}
   \]
   If \(K\le H\) almost surely, it is enough that
   \[
      \E V(\mathcal L)
      >
      b\,\psi\left(
         b_0^\rho A_y\,(\E K)^\rho
         +
         \sigma b_0^{1+\rho}H^\rho\,\E K
      \right).
      \tag{ASRL3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose the finite prefix-template separator failed.  Let the residual price
   system be the one from \cref{cor:finite-prefix-residual-envelope}.  For a
   list outcome with \(K=0\), \(V(\mathcal L)=0\).  For an outcome with
   \(K\ge1\), the top \(K\)-prefix in \(W\) has paid degree at least
   \(V(\mathcal L)\), so \((CNR2)\) gives
   \[
      V(\mathcal L)
      \le
      b\,\psi\left(
         b_0^\rho A_yK^\rho
         +
         \sigma b_0^{1+\rho}K^{1+\rho}
      \right).
   \]
   Averaging contradicts \((ASRL1)\).  Hence no residual failure is possible,
   proving the separator and endpoint conclusions.  Jensen gives
   \(\E K^\rho\le(\E K)^\rho\), so \((ASRL2)\) implies \((ASRL1)\).  If
   \(K\le H\), then \(K^{1+\rho}\le H^\rho K\), giving the capped form.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[All-size marginal proposal separator]
   \label{cor:all-size-marginal-proposal}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:all-size-random-list-proposal}.  Suppose
   every nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) admits a container \(W\in\mathcal W_0\), fractional
   query weights \(0\le y_q\le1\), inclusion marginals \(0\le\pi_p\le1\) on
   \(W\), and a realizable second-moment bound as below.  Put
   \[
      A_y=\sum_q\tau_qy_q,\qquad
      \mu=\sum_{p\in W}\pi_p,
      \qquad
      V_\pi=\sum_{p\in W}\pi_p d_y^\gamma(p),
      \qquad
      \rho=\rho_W,\quad \psi=\psi_W .
   \]
   Suppose these marginals are realized by a random list
   \(\mathcal L\subseteq W\) with
   \[
      \E|\mathcal L|^2\le M_2 .
      \tag{ASMP1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      V_\pi
      >
      b\,\psi\left(
         b_0^\rho A_y\mu^\rho
         +
         \sigma b_0^{1+\rho}\mu^{1-\rho}M_2^\rho
      \right),
      \tag{ASMP2}
   \]
   then the finite prefix-template separator holds, and hence the same local
   and global endpoints apply.

   In particular, for independent Bernoulli inclusion it is enough that
   \[
      V_\pi
      >
      b\,\psi\left(
         b_0^\rho A_y\mu^\rho
         +
         \sigma b_0^{1+\rho}\mu^{1-\rho}(\mu+\mu^2)^\rho
      \right).
      \tag{ASMP3}
   \]
   On proposals with \(\mu\ge1\), the storage term in \((ASMP3)\) is at most
   \(2b\,\psi\sigma b_0^{1+\rho}\mu^{1+\rho}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The random list has
   \[
      \E V(\mathcal L)=V_\pi,\qquad \E K=\mu .
   \]
   As before, Jensen gives \(\E K^\rho\le\mu^\rho\).  Log-convexity of
   \(L_p\)-moments between powers \(1\) and \(2\) gives
   \[
      \E K^{1+\rho}
      \le
      (\E K)^{1-\rho}(\E K^2)^\rho
      \le
      \mu^{1-\rho}M_2^\rho .
   \]
   Hence \((ASMP2)\) implies \((ASRL1)\), and
   \cref{cor:all-size-random-list-proposal} applies.  For independent
   Bernoulli inclusion,
   \[
      \E K^2
      =
      \mu^2+\sum_{p\in W}\pi_p(1-\pi_p)
      \le
      \mu^2+\mu,
   \]
   giving \((ASMP3)\).  If \(\mu\ge1\), then
   \[
      \mu^{1-\rho}(\mu+\mu^2)^\rho
      \le 2^\rho\mu^{1+\rho}\le2\mu^{1+\rho}.
   \]
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Query-free all-size list proposal separator]
   \label{cor:query-free-all-size-list-proposal}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:all-size-random-list-proposal}.  It is
   enough to prove the following query-free proposal statement.  For every
   nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\), there is a finite seed law \(s\sim\nu\) such that
   seed \(s\) chooses a certified container \(W_s\in\mathcal W_0\) and a
   certified list \(L_s\subseteq W_s\).  Put
   \[
      K_s=|L_s|,
      \qquad
      \rho_s=\rho_{W_s},
      \qquad
      \psi_s=\psi_{W_s},
   \]
   and
   \[
      h_s(q)=
      \sum_{p\in L_s:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{QASL1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \E_s
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}
      \bigl(h_s(q)-b\,b_0^{\rho_s}\psi_sK_s^{\rho_s}\tau_q\bigr)_+
      >
      b\,\E_s\!\left[
         \psi_s\sigma b_0^{1+\rho_s}K_s^{1+\rho_s}
      \right],
      \tag{QASL2}
   \]
   then the finite prefix-template separator holds.  Consequently
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible, and the local and global
   endpoints of \cref{cor:finite-prefix-local-filter-cover} and
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-polylog-endpoint} apply.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Inequality \((QASL2)\) implies that some deterministic seed \(s\) satisfies
   the same strict inequality.  Let
   \[
      Q_s^+
      =
      \{q:h_s(q)>b\,b_0^{\rho_s}\psi_sK_s^{\rho_s}\tau_q\}.
      \tag{QASL3}
   \]
   For the integral query weights \(y=\mathbf 1_{Q_s^+}\),
   \[
      V(L_s)=\sum_{q\in Q_s^+}h_s(q),
      \qquad
      A_y=\sum_{q\in Q_s^+}\tau_q .
   \]
   The positive-margin inequality is exactly the deterministic instance of
   \((ASRL1)\) for the point-mass random list \(L_s\).  Hence
   the hypothesis of \cref{cor:all-size-random-list-proposal} holds for the
   given price system.  Since the argument applies to every price system
   satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\), that corollary gives the finite
   prefix-template separator and the endpoint conclusions.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Query-free all-size marginal proposal separator]
   \label{cor:query-free-all-size-marginal-proposal}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:all-size-marginal-proposal}.  It is enough
   to prove the following soft query-free proposal statement.  For every
   nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\), there is a finite seed law \(s\sim\nu\) such that
   seed \(s\) chooses a certified container \(W_s\in\mathcal W_0\), inclusion
   marginals \(0\le\pi_{s,p}\le1\) on \(W_s\), and a realizable second-moment
   bound \(M_{2,s}\).  Put
   \[
      \mu_s=\sum_{p\in W_s}\pi_{s,p},
      \qquad
      \rho_s=\rho_{W_s},
      \qquad
      \psi_s=\psi_{W_s},
   \]
   and
   \[
      h_s(q)=
      \sum_{p\in W_s:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
         \pi_{s,p}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{QASM1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \E_s
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}
      \bigl(h_s(q)-b\,b_0^{\rho_s}\psi_s\mu_s^{\rho_s}\tau_q\bigr)_+
      >
      b\,\E_s\!\left[
         \psi_s\sigma b_0^{1+\rho_s}
         \mu_s^{1-\rho_s}M_{2,s}^{\rho_s}
      \right],
      \tag{QASM2}
   \]
   then the finite prefix-template separator holds, and hence the same local
   and global endpoints apply.

   In particular, independent Bernoulli realization gives the sufficient
   condition obtained from \((QASM2)\) by replacing \(M_{2,s}\) with
   \(\mu_s+\mu_s^2\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Inequality \((QASM2)\) implies that some deterministic seed \(s\) satisfies
   the same strict inequality.  Let
   \[
      Q_s^+
      =
      \{q:h_s(q)>b\,b_0^{\rho_s}\psi_s\mu_s^{\rho_s}\tau_q\}.
      \tag{QASM3}
   \]
   For \(y=\mathbf 1_{Q_s^+}\),
   \[
      V_\pi
      =
      \sum_{q\in Q_s^+}h_s(q),
      \qquad
      A_y=\sum_{q\in Q_s^+}\tau_q .
   \]
   The deterministic positive-margin inequality is exactly \((ASMP2)\) for
   this integral query layer.  Thus the hypothesis of
   \cref{cor:all-size-marginal-proposal} holds for the given price system.
   Since the argument applies to every price system satisfying
   \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\), that corollary gives the finite prefix-template
   separator.  The Bernoulli statement is the special case \((ASMP3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite all-size soft-bucket separation oracle]
   \label{cor:finite-all-size-soft-bucket-separation}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:query-free-all-size-marginal-proposal}.
   Let \(\mathcal B\) be a finite build-time pool of soft buckets.  A bucket
   \(B\in\mathcal B\) consists of a certified container
   \(W_B\in\mathcal W_0\), inclusion marginals \(0\le\pi_{B,p}\le1\) on
   \(W_B\), and a realizable second-moment bound \(M_{2,B}\).  Put
   \[
      \mu_B=\sum_{p\in W_B}\pi_{B,p},
      \qquad
      \rho_B=\rho_{W_B},
      \qquad
      \psi_B=\psi_{W_B},
   \]
   and, for a price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\),
   \[
      h_B(q)=
      \sum_{p\in W_B:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
         \pi_{B,p}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
   \]
   Define the all-size soft reduced gain
   \[
      \mathsf{ASG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(B)
      =
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}
      \bigl(
         h_B(q)-b\,b_0^{\rho_B}\psi_B\mu_B^{\rho_B}\tau_q
      \bigr)_+
      -
      b\,\psi_B\sigma b_0^{1+\rho_B}
      \mu_B^{1-\rho_B}M_{2,B}^{\rho_B}.
      \tag{FASB1}
   \]
   If every nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) has
   \[
      \max_{B\in\mathcal B}\mathsf{ASG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(B)>0,
      \tag{FASB2}
   \]
   then the finite prefix-template separator holds.  Consequently
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible, and the local and global
   endpoints of \cref{cor:finite-prefix-local-filter-cover} and
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-polylog-endpoint} apply.

   More generally, it is enough that every such price system admit a finite
   law on \(\mathcal B\) with positive expected \(\mathsf{ASG}\).  For
   independent Bernoulli realization one may use
   \(M_{2,B}=\mu_B+\mu_B^2\); if \(\mu_B\ge1\), the storage term in
   \((FASB1)\) is at most
   \[
      2b\,\psi_B\sigma b_0^{1+\rho_B}\mu_B^{1+\rho_B}.
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((FASB2)\) holds for a price system, take the seed law in
   \cref{cor:query-free-all-size-marginal-proposal} to be the point mass on a
   maximizing bucket \(B\).  Inequality \((QASM2)\) is exactly
   \(\mathsf{ASG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(B)>0\).  Since this applies to every
   price system satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\), the query-free all-size
   marginal proposal separator gives the finite prefix-template separator and
   the endpoint conclusions.

   The finite-law version is the same averaging argument.  Positive expected
   \(\mathsf{ASG}\) implies that some bucket in the support has positive
   all-size soft gain.  The Bernoulli claim is the special case \((ASMP3)\).
   If \(\mu_B\ge1\), then
   \[
      \mu_B^{1-\rho_B}(\mu_B+\mu_B^2)^{\rho_B}
      \le 2^{\rho_B}\mu_B^{1+\rho_B}
      \le2\mu_B^{1+\rho_B},
   \]
   giving the displayed storage simplification.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[All-size soft gain materializes as a hard list]
   \label{cor:all-size-soft-gain-hard-list}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:finite-all-size-soft-bucket-separation}.
   Fix one soft bucket \(B\), and suppose its marginals are realized by a
   random list \(\mathcal L\subseteq W_B\) with
   \(\E|\mathcal L|^2\le M_{2,B}\).  If
   \[
      \mathsf{ASG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(B)>0,
      \tag{ASH1}
   \]
   then some hard list \(L\subseteq W_B\), with \(K=|L|\), satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}
      \left(
         \sum_{p\in L:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
         -b\,b_0^{\rho_B}\psi_BK^{\rho_B}\tau_q
      \right)_+
      >
      b\,\psi_B\sigma b_0^{1+\rho_B}K^{1+\rho_B}.
      \tag{ASH2}
   \]
   Thus positive soft gain is only a proposal certificate: a positive ordinary
   hard-list all-size certificate already exists inside the same container.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Put \(K=|\mathcal L|\) and, for each query \(q\),
   \[
      X_q=
      \sum_{p\in\mathcal L:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      -b\,b_0^{\rho_B}\psi_BK^{\rho_B}\tau_q .
   \]
   Since \(0<\rho_B<1\), Jensen gives
   \(\E K^{\rho_B}\le\mu_B^{\rho_B}\).  Therefore
   \[
      \E X_q
      \ge
      h_B(q)-b\,b_0^{\rho_B}\psi_B\mu_B^{\rho_B}\tau_q .
   \]
   By convexity of \(x\mapsto x_+\),
   \[
      \E(X_q)_+
      \ge
      \bigl(
         h_B(q)-b\,b_0^{\rho_B}\psi_B\mu_B^{\rho_B}\tau_q
      \bigr)_+ .
      \tag{ASH3}
   \]
   Summing \((ASH3)\) and using \((ASH1)\) yields
   \[
      \E\sum_q(X_q)_+
      >
      b\,\psi_B\sigma b_0^{1+\rho_B}
      \mu_B^{1-\rho_B}M_{2,B}^{\rho_B}.
      \tag{ASH4}
   \]
   Log-convexity of \(L_p\)-moments between powers \(1\) and \(2\) gives
   \[
      \E K^{1+\rho_B}
      \le
      (\E K)^{1-\rho_B}(\E K^2)^{\rho_B}
      \le
      \mu_B^{1-\rho_B}M_{2,B}^{\rho_B}.
      \tag{ASH5}
   \]
   Combining \((ASH4)\) and \((ASH5)\),
   \[
      \E\left[
         \sum_q(X_q)_+
         -
         b\,\psi_B\sigma b_0^{1+\rho_B}K^{1+\rho_B}
      \right]>0 .
   \]
   Hence at least one outcome \(L\) of \(\mathcal L\) satisfies \((ASH2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite all-size hard-list separation oracle]
   \label{cor:finite-all-size-hard-list-separation}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:query-free-all-size-list-proposal}.  Let
   \(\mathcal H\) be a finite build-time pool of certified hard lists.  An
   element \(H\in\mathcal H\) consists of a certified container
   \(W_H\in\mathcal W_0\) and a list \(L_H\subseteq W_H\).  Put
   \[
      K_H=|L_H|,
      \qquad
      \rho_H=\rho_{W_H},
      \qquad
      \psi_H=\psi_{W_H},
   \]
   and
   \[
      h_H(q)=
      \sum_{p\in L_H:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
   \]
   Define the all-size hard-list reduced gain
   \[
      \mathsf{AHG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(H)
      =
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}
      \bigl(h_H(q)-b\,b_0^{\rho_H}\psi_HK_H^{\rho_H}\tau_q\bigr)_+
      -
      b\,\psi_H\sigma b_0^{1+\rho_H}K_H^{1+\rho_H}.
      \tag{FAHL1}
   \]
   If every nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) has
   \[
      \max_{H\in\mathcal H}\mathsf{AHG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(H)>0,
      \tag{FAHL2}
   \]
   then the finite prefix-template separator holds, and hence the same local
   and global endpoints apply.  A finite law on \(\mathcal H\) with positive
   expected \(\mathsf{AHG}\) is again sufficient.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(H\) has positive all-size hard-list reduced gain, the point-mass seed
   law on \((W_H,L_H)\) satisfies \((QASL2)\).  Thus
   \cref{cor:query-free-all-size-list-proposal} gives the finite
   prefix-template separator and the endpoint conclusions.  The law version
   reduces to the point-mass version by averaging.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[All-size hard-list separation reduces to prefixes]
   \label{cor:all-size-hard-list-prefix-separation}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:finite-all-size-hard-list-separation}, and
   fix a nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\).  For a certified
   container \(W\in\mathcal W_0\), an ordinary query layer
   \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\), and an integer \(1\le K\le |W|\), let
   \(P_K(W,Q')\) be any \(K\)-point subset of \(W\) maximizing
   \[
      \sum_{p\in L}
      \sum_{q\in Q':(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      \qquad(|L|=K).
   \]
   Define the all-size prefix gain
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \mathsf{APG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(W,Q',K)
      &=
      \sum_{p\in P_K(W,Q')}
      \sum_{q\in Q':(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}  \\
      &\quad
      -b\,b_0^{\rho_W}\psi_WK^{\rho_W}\sum_{q\in Q'}\tau_q
      -b\,\psi_W\sigma b_0^{1+\rho_W}K^{1+\rho_W}.
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{AHLP1}
   \]
   If some hard list \(H=(W_H,L_H)\) has positive all-size hard-list reduced
   gain, then with \(K=|L_H|\) and
   \[
      Q^+(H)=
      \{q\in\mathcal Q:
        h_H(q)>b\,b_0^{\rho_H}\psi_HK^{\rho_H}\tau_q\},
      \tag{AHLP2}
   \]
   the top-degree prefix \(P_K(W_H,Q^+(H))\) has positive all-size prefix gain.
   Consequently its all-size hard-list reduced gain is also positive.

   Hence, whenever the build-time universe is closed under this
   query-layer top-\(K\) replacement, the finite all-size hard-list oracle of
   \cref{cor:finite-all-size-hard-list-separation} may be replaced by a
   separation search over triples \((W,Q',K)\) and the scalar test
   \((AHLP1)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(H=(W,L)\), put \(K=|L|\), \(\rho=\rho_W\), and \(\psi=\psi_W\).  By
   definition,
   \[
      \mathsf{AHG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(H)
      =
      \sum_q\bigl(h_H(q)-b\,b_0^\rho\psi K^\rho\tau_q\bigr)_+
      -
      b\,\psi\sigma b_0^{1+\rho}K^{1+\rho}.
   \]
   The positive part is obtained by the query layer \(Q^+(H)\), so positive
   all-size hard-list gain implies
   \[
      \sum_{p\in L}
      \sum_{q\in Q^+(H):(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      >
      b\,b_0^\rho\psi K^\rho\sum_{q\in Q^+(H)}\tau_q
      +
      b\,\psi\sigma b_0^{1+\rho}K^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{AHLP3}
   \]
   The prefix \(P_K(W,Q^+(H))\) maximizes the left side among all \(K\)-point
   subsets of \(W\), so it also satisfies \((AHLP3)\).  This is precisely
   \[
      \mathsf{APG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(W,Q^+(H),K)>0 .
   \]
   If \(H'=(W,P_K(W,Q^+(H)))\), then
   \[
      \mathsf{AHG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(H')
      \ge
      \mathsf{APG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(W,Q^+(H),K),
   \]
   because the hard-list hinge is the maximum over all query layers and the
   right side evaluates it only on \(Q^+(H)\).  This proves the replacement
   claim and the oracle reduction.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[All-size fractional query weights threshold to prefixes]
   \label{cor:all-size-fractional-query-prefix-separation}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:all-size-hard-list-prefix-separation}.  Fix
   a certified container \(W\in\mathcal W_0\) and an integer
   \(1\le K\le |W|\).  For \(0\le y_q\le1\), define
   \[
      d_y^\gamma(p)=
      \sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
   \]
   and let \(D_{W,y}^\gamma(K)\) be the sum of the largest \(K\) values of
   \(d_y^\gamma(p)\) over \(p\in W\).  If some fractional query weighting
   satisfies
   \[
      D_{W,y}^\gamma(K)
      >
      b\,b_0^{\rho_W}\psi_WK^{\rho_W}\sum_q\tau_qy_q
      +
      b\,\psi_W\sigma b_0^{1+\rho_W}K^{1+\rho_W},
      \tag{AFQP1}
   \]
   then there is an ordinary query layer \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\) such that
   the top-degree prefix \(P_K(W,Q')\) has positive all-size prefix gain
   \((AHLP1)\).  Conversely, a positive all-size prefix-gain triple
   \((W,Q',K)\) gives \((AFQP1)\) with \(y=\mathbf 1_{Q'}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Define
   \[
      F(y)=
      D_{W,y}^\gamma(K)
      -
      b\,b_0^{\rho_W}\psi_WK^{\rho_W}\sum_q\tau_qy_q
      -
      b\,\psi_W\sigma b_0^{1+\rho_W}K^{1+\rho_W}.
   \]
   The function \(D_{W,y}^\gamma(K)\) is the maximum, over \(K\)-subsets
   \(L\subseteq W\), of the linear form
   \[
      \sum_{p\in L}\sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
   \]
   Hence \(F\) is convex on the cube \([0,1]^{\mathcal Q}\).  If \(F(y)>0\)
   for some fractional \(y\), the maximum of \(F\) over the cube is positive
   and is attained at an extreme point \(y'=\mathbf 1_{Q'}\).  At this extreme
   point, \(D_{W,y'}^\gamma(K)\) is exactly the paid degree of
   \(P_K(W,Q')\) on the Boolean query layer \(Q'\), so \(F(y')>0\) is
   \((AHLP1)\).  The converse is the same identity with \(y=\mathbf 1_{Q'}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite all-size prefix separation oracle]
   \label{cor:finite-all-size-prefix-separation}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:all-size-fractional-query-prefix-separation}.  Let
   \(\mathcal P\) be a finite build-time pool of certified prefix templates.
   A template \(C\in\mathcal P\) consists of a certified container
   \(W_C\in\mathcal W_0\) and an available cardinality
   \(1\le K_C\le |W_C|\).  For a price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\), define
   the all-size prefix reduced-cost value
   \[
      \mathsf{APX}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(C)
      =
      \max_{0\le y_q\le1}
      \left[
         D_{W_C,y}^\gamma(K_C)
         -
         b\,b_0^{\rho_C}\psi_CK_C^{\rho_C}\sum_q\tau_qy_q
         -
         b\,\psi_C\sigma b_0^{1+\rho_C}K_C^{1+\rho_C}
      \right],
      \tag{FAPS1}
   \]
   where \(\rho_C=\rho_{W_C}\) and \(\psi_C=\psi_{W_C}\).  Suppose the finite
   hard-list universe contains, for every \(C\in\mathcal P\) and every Boolean
   query layer \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\), the top-degree prefix
   \(P_{K_C}(W_C,Q')\).  If every nonnegative price system
   \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) has
   \[
      \max_{C\in\mathcal P}\mathsf{APX}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(C)>0,
      \tag{FAPS2}
   \]
   then the finite prefix-template separator holds, and hence the same local
   and global endpoints apply.

   Equivalently,
   \[
      \mathsf{APX}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(C)
      =
      \max_{Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q}
      \mathsf{APG}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(W_C,Q',K_C).
      \tag{FAPS3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For fixed \(C\), \cref{cor:all-size-fractional-query-prefix-separation}
   says exactly that the fractional maximum in \((FAPS1)\) is positive if and
   only if some Boolean query layer \(Q'\) gives positive all-size prefix gain
   for \(P_{K_C}(W_C,Q')\).  This proves \((FAPS3)\).  Under the closure
   assumption, that prefix is an available hard list and has positive all-size
   hard-list reduced gain by
   \cref{cor:all-size-hard-list-prefix-separation}.  Therefore \((FAPS2)\)
   implies the hypothesis of \cref{cor:finite-all-size-hard-list-separation},
   and the finite prefix-template separator and endpoint conclusions follow.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[All-size prefix residual envelope]
   \label{cor:all-size-prefix-residual-envelope}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:finite-all-size-prefix-separation}.  If the
   finite prefix-template separator fails, then there is a nonnegative price
   system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) such that,
   for every template \(C=(W_C,K_C)\in\mathcal P\) and every fractional query
   weighting \(0\le y_q\le1\),
   \[
      D_{W_C,y}^\gamma(K_C)
      \le
      b\,\psi_C\left(
         b_0^{\rho_C}K_C^{\rho_C}\sum_q\tau_qy_q
         +
         \sigma b_0^{1+\rho_C}K_C^{1+\rho_C}
      \right).
      \tag{APRE1}
   \]
   Equivalently, the same envelope holds for every Boolean query layer
   \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\):
   \[
      \sum_{p\in P_{K_C}(W_C,Q')}
      \sum_{q\in Q':(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      \le
      b\,\psi_C\left(
         b_0^{\rho_C}K_C^{\rho_C}\sum_{q\in Q'}\tau_q
         +
         \sigma b_0^{1+\rho_C}K_C^{1+\rho_C}
      \right).
      \tag{APRE2}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the conclusion failed, then every price system satisfying
   \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) would have some template \(C\) and fractional query
   weighting \(y\) violating \((APRE1)\), which is exactly
   \(\mathsf{APX}_{\gamma,\tau,\sigma}(C)>0\).  Thus \((FAPS2)\) would hold,
   and \cref{cor:finite-all-size-prefix-separation} would give the finite
   prefix-template separator, a contradiction.  The Boolean form \((APRE2)\)
   is the same statement with \(y=\mathbf 1_{Q'}\), using \((FAPS3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Normalized all-size prefix obstruction]
   \label{cor:normalized-all-size-prefix-obstruction}
   Failure of the all-size prefix separator in
   \cref{cor:finite-all-size-prefix-separation} implies the existence of a
   nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying \((APC1)\) and
   the normalization
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}=1,
      \qquad
      L\sum_q\tau_q+\sigma S<\frac1{\pi_1},
      \tag{NAPO1}
   \]
   such that every retained prefix template satisfies \((APRE1)\).
   Conversely, any normalized witness satisfying \((NAPO1)\), \((APC1)\), and
   \((APRE1)\) for every retained template can be rescaled to a surplus price
   system satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) with no positive all-size prefix
   column.

   Thus the remaining geometric theorem may be stated scale-free: every unit
   paid-mass dual obeying the query/storage budget in \((NAPO1)\) must expose
   one certified container/cardinality template and one query weighting that
   violates \((APRE1)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) be the residual price system from
   \cref{cor:all-size-prefix-residual-envelope}, and put
   \[
      M=\sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
   \]
   By \((APC2)\), \(M>0\).  Divide \(\gamma,\tau,\sigma\) by \(M\).  The
   constraint \((APC1)\) is homogeneous, because both sides are linear in the
   prices.  The envelope \((APRE1)\) is also homogeneous.  Finally \((APC2)\)
   becomes
   \[
      1>\pi_1\left(L\sum_q\tau_q+\sigma S\right),
   \]
   which is \((NAPO1)\).

   Conversely, multiplying a normalized witness by any positive scalar
   preserves \((APC1)\) and \((APRE1)\), and the strict inequality in
   \((NAPO1)\) becomes exactly \((APC2)\).  Since \((APRE1)\) is equivalent to
   nonpositive \(\mathsf{APX}\) on every retained template, no positive
   all-size prefix column exists for the rescaled price system.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Normalized all-size weak-type obstruction]
   \label{cor:normalized-all-size-weak-type-obstruction}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:normalized-all-size-prefix-obstruction},
   and let \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) be a normalized obstruction.  Fix a
   retained container/cardinality template \(C=(W,K)\in\mathcal P\), fractional
   query weights \(0\le y_q\le1\), and a level \(\delta>0\).  Put
   \[
      d_y^\gamma(p)=
      \sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
      \qquad
      h_\delta=
      |\{p\in W:d_y^\gamma(p)\ge\delta\}|.
   \]
   If \(h_\delta=K>0\), and if
   \(A_y=\sum_q\tau_qy_q\), \(\rho=\rho_W\), and \(\psi=\psi_W\), then
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      b\,\psi\left(
         b_0^\rho A_yh_\delta^{\rho-1}
         +
         \sigma b_0^{1+\rho}h_\delta^\rho
      \right).
      \tag{NAW1}
   \]
   Consequently, when \(0<\rho<1\), the same weak-type alternatives as in
   \((ASW2)\)--\((ASW5)\) hold for every retained exact superlevel cardinality.

   If in addition \(L,S>0\), then the normalized budget gives the absolute
   scale-free envelope
   \[
      \delta
      <
      \frac{b\,\psi}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{b_0^\rho h_\delta^{\rho-1}}{L}
         +
         \frac{b_0^{1+\rho}h_\delta^\rho}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{NAW2}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since the top \(h_\delta\) points of \(W\) by \(d_y^\gamma\)-degree all have
   degree at least \(\delta\),
   \[
      D_{W,y}^\gamma(h_\delta)\ge\delta h_\delta .
   \]
   The hypothesis \(h_\delta=K\) lets us apply \((APRE1)\) to the retained
   template \(C=(W,K)\).  Dividing by \(h_\delta\) gives \((NAW1)\).  The
   weak-type alternatives are obtained from \((NAW1)\) by the same algebra as
   in \cref{cor:all-size-prefix-weak-type-residual}.

   Finally, \(0\le y_q\le1\) gives \(A_y\le\sum_q\tau_q\).  By \((NAPO1)\),
   \(L\sum_q\tau_q<\pi_1^{-1}\) and \(\sigma S<\pi_1^{-1}\), so
   \(A_y<(\pi_1L)^{-1}\) and \(\sigma<(\pi_1S)^{-1}\).  Substituting these two
   estimates into \((NAW1)\) gives \((NAW2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Normalized weak-type separator]
   \label{cor:normalized-weak-type-separator}
   In the setting of \cref{cor:finite-all-size-prefix-separation}, assume
   \(L,S>0\).  Suppose every nonnegative price system satisfying \((APC1)\),
   \((NAPO1)\), and
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}=1
   \]
   admits a retained template \(C=(W,K)\in\mathcal P\), fractional query
   weights \(0\le y_q\le1\), and a level \(\delta>0\) such that
   \(K=|\{p\in W:d_y^\gamma(p)\ge\delta\}|>0\) and
   \[
      \delta
      \ge
      \frac{b\,\psi_W}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{b_0^{\rho_W}K^{\rho_W-1}}{L}
         +
         \frac{b_0^{1+\rho_W}K^{\rho_W}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{NWS1}
   \]
   Then the finite prefix-template separator holds, and hence the local and
   global endpoints of \cref{cor:finite-prefix-local-filter-cover} and
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-polylog-endpoint} apply.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the finite prefix-template separator failed, then
   \cref{cor:normalized-all-size-prefix-obstruction} would give a normalized
   obstruction.  Applying the assumed weak-type separator to that obstruction
   gives a retained exact superlevel satisfying \((NWS1)\), contradicting the
   strict upper bound \((NAW2)\) from
   \cref{cor:normalized-all-size-weak-type-obstruction}.  Hence no normalized
   obstruction exists, so the finite prefix-template separator must hold.  The
   endpoint conclusions follow from \cref{cor:finite-prefix-local-filter-cover}
   and \cref{cor:finite-prefix-polylog-endpoint}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Normalized cardinality-net weak-type obstruction]
   \label{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-weak-type-obstruction}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:normalized-all-size-prefix-obstruction},
   and let \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) be a normalized obstruction.  Fix a
   retained container \(W\) whose available cardinalities are
   \(\beta\)-dense from above: for every \(1\le h\le |W|\), some retained
   template \((W,K)\in\mathcal P\) has
   \[
      h\le K\le\beta h .
      \tag{NCW0}
   \]
   For fractional query weights \(0\le y_q\le1\) and a level \(\delta>0\), put
   \[
      d_y^\gamma(p)=
      \sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
      \qquad
      h_\delta=
      |\{p\in W:d_y^\gamma(p)\ge\delta\}|.
   \]
   If \(h_\delta>0\), and if
   \(A_y=\sum_q\tau_qy_q\), \(\rho=\rho_W\), and \(\psi=\psi_W\), then
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      b\,\psi\left(
         \beta^\rho b_0^\rho A_yh_\delta^{\rho-1}
         +
         \beta^{1+\rho}\sigma b_0^{1+\rho}h_\delta^\rho
      \right).
      \tag{NCW1}
   \]
   If in addition \(L,S>0\), then
   \[
      \delta
      <
      \frac{b\,\psi}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{\beta^\rho b_0^\rho h_\delta^{\rho-1}}{L}
         +
         \frac{\beta^{1+\rho}b_0^{1+\rho}h_\delta^\rho}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{NCW2}
   \]
   Thus dyadic retained cardinalities remove the exact-cardinality condition in
   \cref{cor:normalized-all-size-weak-type-obstruction} at another constant
   factor.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Choose a retained template \((W,K)\in\mathcal P\) satisfying \((NCW0)\) with
   \(h=h_\delta\).  The top \(h_\delta\) points of \(W\) by \(d_y^\gamma\)-degree
   all have degree at least \(\delta\), so
   \[
      D_{W,y}^\gamma(K)\ge D_{W,y}^\gamma(h_\delta)
      \ge\delta h_\delta .
   \]
