   Applying \((APRE1)\) to the retained template \((W,K)\), using
   \(K\le\beta h_\delta\), and dividing by \(h_\delta\) gives \((NCW1)\).
   The normalized budget argument used for \((NAW2)\) gives \((NCW2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Normalized cardinality-net weak-type separator]
   \label{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-weak-type-separator}
   In the setting of \cref{cor:finite-all-size-prefix-separation}, assume
   \(L,S>0\) and that the retained cardinalities of every retained container
   are \(\beta\)-dense from above as in \((NCW0)\).  Suppose every nonnegative
   price system satisfying \((APC1)\), \((NAPO1)\), and
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}=1
   \]
   admits a retained container \(W\), fractional query weights
   \(0\le y_q\le1\), and a level \(\delta>0\) such that
   \(h_\delta=|\{p\in W:d_y^\gamma(p)\ge\delta\}|>0\) and
   \[
      \delta
      \ge
      \frac{b\,\psi_W}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{\beta^{\rho_W}b_0^{\rho_W}h_\delta^{\rho_W-1}}{L}
         +
         \frac{\beta^{1+\rho_W}b_0^{1+\rho_W}h_\delta^{\rho_W}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{NCWS1}
   \]
   Then the finite prefix-template separator holds, and hence the local and
   global endpoints of \cref{cor:finite-prefix-local-filter-cover} and
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-polylog-endpoint} apply.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the finite prefix-template separator failed, then
   \cref{cor:normalized-all-size-prefix-obstruction} would give a normalized
   obstruction.  The assumed cardinality-net weak-type witness for that
   obstruction contradicts the strict upper bound \((NCW2)\) from
   \cref{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-weak-type-obstruction}.  Hence no
   normalized obstruction exists, so the finite prefix-template separator must
   hold.  The endpoint conclusions again follow from
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-local-filter-cover} and
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-polylog-endpoint}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Normalized aggregate list-moment obstruction]
   \label{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-aggregate-list-moment-obstruction}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-weak-type-obstruction}, and assume
   \(0<\rho_W<1\).  Fix the retained container \(W\) and fractional query
   weights \(y\), choose a finite nonnegative level weighting
   \((\lambda_i,\delta_i)_i\), and put
   \[
      h_i=|\{p\in W:d_y^\gamma(p)\ge\delta_i\}|,
      \qquad
      M_0=\sum_i\lambda_i,
      \qquad
      M_1=\sum_i\lambda_i h_i,
   \]
   \[
      M_{1+\rho}=\sum_i\lambda_i h_i^{1+\rho},
      \qquad
      B=\sum_i\lambda_i\delta_i h_i,
      \qquad
      A_y=\sum_q\tau_qy_q,
      \qquad
      \rho=\rho_W,\quad \psi=\psi_W .
   \]
   Then
   \[
      B
      \le
      b\,\psi\left(
         \beta^\rho b_0^\rho A_yM_0^{1-\rho}M_1^\rho
         +
         \beta^{1+\rho}\sigma b_0^{1+\rho}M_{1+\rho}
      \right).
      \tag{NCAM1}
   \]
   If \(L,S>0\) and \(M_1>0\), then
   \[
      B
      <
      \frac{b\,\psi}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{\beta^\rho b_0^\rho M_0^{1-\rho}M_1^\rho}{L}
         +
         \frac{\beta^{1+\rho}b_0^{1+\rho}M_{1+\rho}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{NCAM2}
   \]
   If the supported levels have \(h_i\le H\), the second term in both
   envelopes may be replaced by the corresponding capped term
   \(H^\rho M_1\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(M_0=0\), then \(B=M_1=M_{1+\rho}=0\), and \((NCAM1)\) is trivial.
   Assume \(M_0>0\).  For every level with \(h_i>0\), multiplying \((NCW1)\)
   by \(h_i\) gives
   \[
      \delta_i h_i
      \le
      b\,\psi\left(
         \beta^\rho b_0^\rho A_yh_i^\rho
         +
         \beta^{1+\rho}\sigma b_0^{1+\rho}h_i^{1+\rho}
      \right).
      \tag{NCAM3}
   \]
   The same inequality is trivial when \(h_i=0\).  Multiplying by
   \(\lambda_i\), summing, and using concavity of \(x^\rho\) gives
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_i h_i^\rho
      \le
      M_0^{1-\rho}M_1^\rho,
   \]
   which proves \((NCAM1)\).  If \(M_1>0\), then the normalized budget
   \((NAPO1)\) gives \(A_y<(\pi_1L)^{-1}\) and
   \(\sigma<(\pi_1S)^{-1}\), and substituting these strict bounds gives
   \((NCAM2)\).  The capped variant follows from
   \(M_{1+\rho}\le H^\rho M_1\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Normalized aggregate list-moment separator]
   \label{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-aggregate-list-moment-separator}
   In the setting of
   \cref{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-weak-type-separator}, assume
   \(0<\rho_W<1\) for every retained container.  It is enough to prove the
   following averaged geometric statement.  Every nonnegative price system
   satisfying \((APC1)\), \((NAPO1)\), and
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}=1
   \]
   admits a retained container \(W\), fractional query weights
   \(0\le y_q\le1\), and a finite nonnegative level weighting with \(M_1>0\)
   such that
   \[
      B
      \ge
      \frac{b\,\psi_W}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{\beta^{\rho_W}b_0^{\rho_W}M_0^{1-\rho_W}M_1^{\rho_W}}{L}
         +
         \frac{\beta^{1+\rho_W}b_0^{1+\rho_W}M_{1+\rho_W}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{NCAMS1}
   \]
   It is also enough to prove the same violation with the storage term replaced
   by \( \beta^{1+\rho_W}b_0^{1+\rho_W}H^{\rho_W}M_1/S\) for a certified cap
   \(H\) with \(h_i\le H\) on the supported levels.

   Under this averaged separator, the finite prefix-template separator holds,
   and hence the local and global endpoints of
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-local-filter-cover} and
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-polylog-endpoint} apply.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the finite prefix-template separator failed, then
   \cref{cor:normalized-all-size-prefix-obstruction} would give a normalized
   obstruction.  The averaged witness in \((NCAMS1)\) contradicts the strict
   normalized aggregate envelope \((NCAM2)\) from
   \cref{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-aggregate-list-moment-obstruction};
   the capped version uses the capped envelope in the same corollary.  Hence no
   normalized obstruction exists, so the finite prefix-template separator must
   hold.  The endpoint conclusions follow from
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-local-filter-cover} and
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-polylog-endpoint}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Normalized average list-size panel criterion]
   \label{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-average-list-size-panel}
   In \cref{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-aggregate-list-moment-separator}, a
   probability law \(\nu\) on finitely many levels is sufficient if, with
   \(H_\delta=|\{p\in W:d_y^\gamma(p)\ge\delta\}|\) and
   \(\E_{\delta\sim\nu}H_\delta>0\), writing
   \(\rho=\rho_W\) and \(\psi=\psi_W\),
   \[
      \E_{\delta\sim\nu}\delta H_\delta
      \ge
      \frac{b\,\psi}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{\beta^\rho b_0^\rho
               \bigl(\E_{\delta\sim\nu}H_\delta\bigr)^\rho}{L}
         +
         \frac{\beta^{1+\rho}b_0^{1+\rho}
               \E_{\delta\sim\nu}H_\delta^{1+\rho}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{NCAP1}
   \]
   In a capped-list form, it is enough that \(H_\delta\le H\) on the support of
   \(\nu\) and
   \[
      \E_{\delta\sim\nu}\delta H_\delta
      \ge
      \frac{b\,\psi}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{\beta^\rho b_0^\rho
               \bigl(\E_{\delta\sim\nu}H_\delta\bigr)^\rho}{L}
         +
         \frac{\beta^{1+\rho}b_0^{1+\rho}
               H^\rho\E_{\delta\sim\nu}H_\delta}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{NCAP2}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Use the finite level panel with weights \(\lambda_\delta=\nu(\delta)\).  Then
   \(M_0=1\), \(M_1=\E H_\delta\),
   \(M_{1+\rho}=\E H_\delta^{1+\rho}\), and
   \(B=\E \delta H_\delta\).  The displayed inequalities are exactly the
   normalized aggregate violations in
   \cref{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-aggregate-list-moment-separator}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Normalized random-list proposal separator]
   \label{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-random-list-proposal}
   In the setting of
   \cref{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-aggregate-list-moment-separator}, it is
   enough to prove the following proposal statement.  Every nonnegative price
   system satisfying \((APC1)\), \((NAPO1)\), and
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}=1
   \]
   admits a retained container \(W\), fractional query weights
   \(0\le y_q\le1\), and a random certified list \(\mathcal L\subseteq W\).
   Put
   \[
      K=|\mathcal L|,
      \qquad
      V(\mathcal L)=\sum_{p\in\mathcal L}d_y^\gamma(p),
      \qquad
      \rho=\rho_W,\quad \psi=\psi_W .
   \]
   If \(\E K>0\) and
   \[
      \E V(\mathcal L)
      \ge
      \frac{b\,\psi}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{\beta^\rho b_0^\rho\E K^\rho}{L}
         +
         \frac{\beta^{1+\rho}b_0^{1+\rho}\E K^{1+\rho}}{S}
      \right),
      \tag{NCRL1}
   \]
   then the finite prefix-template separator holds, and hence the same local
   and global endpoints apply.  It is sufficient to replace \(\E K^\rho\) by
   \((\E K)^\rho\).  If \(K\le H\) almost surely, it is sufficient that
   \[
      \E V(\mathcal L)
      \ge
      \frac{b\,\psi}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{\beta^\rho b_0^\rho(\E K)^\rho}{L}
         +
         \frac{\beta^{1+\rho}b_0^{1+\rho}H^\rho\E K}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{NCRL2}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose the finite prefix-template separator failed, and let
   \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) be the normalized obstruction from
   \cref{cor:normalized-all-size-prefix-obstruction}.  Put
   \(A_y=\sum_q\tau_qy_q\).  For a nonempty list outcome, choose a retained
   cardinality \(K'\) for \(W\) with
   \(K\le K'\le\beta K\).  The top \(K'\)-prefix has paid degree at least
   \(V(\mathcal L)\), so \((APRE1)\) gives
   \[
      V(\mathcal L)
      \le
      b\,\psi\left(
         \beta^\rho b_0^\rho A_yK^\rho
         +
         \beta^{1+\rho}\sigma b_0^{1+\rho}K^{1+\rho}
      \right).
   \]
   The same inequality is trivial when \(K=0\).  Averaging and substituting the
   strict normalized budget bounds contradict \((NCRL1)\), because
   \(\E K>0\).  Jensen gives \(\E K^\rho\le(\E K)^\rho\), and
   \(K^{1+\rho}\le H^\rho K\) gives the capped form.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Normalized marginal proposal separator]
   \label{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-marginal-proposal}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-random-list-proposal}.  It is enough to
   find, for every normalized price system, a retained container \(W\),
   fractional query weights \(0\le y_q\le1\), inclusion marginals
   \(0\le\pi_p\le1\), and a realizable second-moment bound.  Put
   \[
      \mu=\sum_{p\in W}\pi_p,
      \qquad
      V_\pi=\sum_{p\in W}\pi_p d_y^\gamma(p),
      \qquad
      \rho=\rho_W,\quad \psi=\psi_W .
   \]
   Suppose the marginals are realized by a random list \(\mathcal L\subseteq W\)
   with
   \[
      \E|\mathcal L|^2\le M_2 .
      \tag{NCMP1}
   \]
   If \(\mu>0\) and
   \[
      V_\pi
      \ge
      \frac{b\,\psi}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{\beta^\rho b_0^\rho\mu^\rho}{L}
         +
         \frac{\beta^{1+\rho}b_0^{1+\rho}\mu^{1-\rho}M_2^\rho}{S}
      \right),
      \tag{NCMP2}
   \]
   then the finite prefix-template separator holds, and hence the same local
   and global endpoints apply.

   For independent Bernoulli inclusion, it is enough that
   \[
      V_\pi
      \ge
      \frac{b\,\psi}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{\beta^\rho b_0^\rho\mu^\rho}{L}
         +
         \frac{\beta^{1+\rho}b_0^{1+\rho}\mu^{1-\rho}
               (\mu+\mu^2)^\rho}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{NCMP3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The realizing random list has
   \[
      \E V(\mathcal L)=V_\pi,\qquad \E K=\mu .
   \]
   Jensen gives \(\E K^\rho\le\mu^\rho\).  Log-convexity of \(L_p\)-moments
   between powers \(1\) and \(2\) gives
   \[
      \E K^{1+\rho}
      \le
      (\E K)^{1-\rho}(\E K^2)^\rho
      \le
      \mu^{1-\rho}M_2^\rho .
   \]
   Hence \((NCMP2)\) implies \((NCRL1)\), so
   \cref{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-random-list-proposal} applies.  For
   independent Bernoulli inclusion,
   \[
      \E K^2
      =
      \mu^2+\sum_{p\in W}\pi_p(1-\pi_p)
      \le
      \mu^2+\mu,
   \]
   giving \((NCMP3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Query-free normalized list proposal separator]
   \label{cor:query-free-normalized-list-proposal}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-random-list-proposal}.  It is enough to
   prove the following query-free proposal statement.  Every nonnegative price
   system satisfying \((APC1)\), \((NAPO1)\), and
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}=1
   \]
   admits a retained container \(W\) and a random certified list
   \(\mathcal L\subseteq W\).  Put
   \[
      K=|\mathcal L|,
      \qquad
      \widehat V(\mathcal L)=
      \sum_{p\in\mathcal L}
      \sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
      \qquad
      \rho=\rho_W,\quad \psi=\psi_W .
   \]
   If \(\E K>0\) and
   \[
      \E\widehat V(\mathcal L)
      \ge
      \frac{b\,\psi}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{\beta^\rho b_0^\rho\E K^\rho}{L}
         +
         \frac{\beta^{1+\rho}b_0^{1+\rho}\E K^{1+\rho}}{S}
      \right),
      \tag{QNRL1}
   \]
   then the finite prefix-template separator holds, and hence the same local
   and global endpoints apply.  It is sufficient to replace \(\E K^\rho\) by
   \((\E K)^\rho\).  If \(K\le H\) almost surely, it is enough to replace the
   storage moment by \(H^\rho\E K\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-random-list-proposal} with the
   fractional query weights \(y_q=1\) for every \(q\).  Then
   \(d_y^\gamma(p)=\sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}\), so
   \(V(\mathcal L)=\widehat V(\mathcal L)\).  The displayed sufficient
   conditions are exactly \((NCRL1)\) and its two simpler variants.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Query-free normalized marginal proposal separator]
   \label{cor:query-free-normalized-marginal-proposal}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-marginal-proposal}.  It is enough to
   prove the following soft query-free proposal statement.  Every nonnegative
   price system satisfying \((APC1)\), \((NAPO1)\), and
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}=1
   \]
   admits a retained container \(W\), inclusion marginals \(0\le\pi_p\le1\) on
   \(W\), and a realizable second-moment bound \(M_2\).  Put
   \[
      \mu=\sum_{p\in W}\pi_p,
      \qquad
      \widehat V_\pi=
      \sum_{p\in W}\pi_p
      \sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
      \qquad
      \rho=\rho_W,\quad \psi=\psi_W .
   \]
   If \(\mu>0\) and
   \[
      \widehat V_\pi
      \ge
      \frac{b\,\psi}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{\beta^\rho b_0^\rho\mu^\rho}{L}
         +
         \frac{\beta^{1+\rho}b_0^{1+\rho}\mu^{1-\rho}M_2^\rho}{S}
      \right),
      \tag{QNMP1}
   \]
   then the finite prefix-template separator holds, and hence the same local
   and global endpoints apply.  For independent Bernoulli inclusion, one may
   replace \(M_2\) by \(\mu+\mu^2\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-marginal-proposal} with
   \(y_q=1\) for every query.  Then \(V_\pi=\widehat V_\pi\), and
   \((QNMP1)\) is exactly \((NCMP2)\).  The Bernoulli statement is the
   corresponding specialization \((NCMP3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite normalized soft-bucket oracle]
   \label{cor:finite-normalized-soft-bucket-oracle}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:query-free-normalized-marginal-proposal}.  Let \(\mathcal B\) be a
   finite build-time pool of soft buckets.  A bucket \(B\in\mathcal B\)
   consists of a retained container \(W_B\), inclusion marginals
   \(0\le\pi_{B,p}\le1\) on \(W_B\), and a realizable second-moment bound
   \(M_{2,B}\).  Put
   \[
      \mu_B=\sum_{p\in W_B}\pi_{B,p},
      \qquad
      \rho_B=\rho_{W_B},
      \qquad
      \psi_B=\psi_{W_B},
   \]
   and, for a normalized price system,
   \[
      \widehat V_B=
      \sum_{p\in W_B}\pi_{B,p}
      \sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
   \]
   Define the normalized soft-bucket gain
   \[
      \mathsf{NSG}_{\gamma}(B)
      =
      \widehat V_B
      -
      \frac{b\,\psi_B}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{\beta^{\rho_B}b_0^{\rho_B}\mu_B^{\rho_B}}{L}
         +
         \frac{\beta^{1+\rho_B}b_0^{1+\rho_B}
               \mu_B^{1-\rho_B}M_{2,B}^{\rho_B}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{FNSB1}
   \]
   If every nonnegative price system satisfying \((APC1)\), \((NAPO1)\), and
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}=1
   \]
   has
   \[
      \max_{B\in\mathcal B:\,\mu_B>0}\mathsf{NSG}_{\gamma}(B)\ge0,
      \tag{FNSB2}
   \]
   then the finite prefix-template separator holds, and hence the same local
   and global endpoints apply.

   More generally, it is enough that every normalized price system admit a
   finite law on \(\mathcal B\) with positive expected mass
   \(\E\mu_B>0\) and nonnegative expected \(\mathsf{NSG}_{\gamma}\).  For
   independent Bernoulli realization one may use
   \(M_{2,B}=\mu_B+\mu_B^2\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((FNSB2)\) holds for a normalized price system, take the proposal in
   \cref{cor:query-free-normalized-marginal-proposal} to be the maximizing
   bucket.  Inequality \((QNMP1)\) is exactly
   \(\mathsf{NSG}_{\gamma}(B)\ge0\), and \(\mu_B>0\) is part of the maximum.
   Since this applies to every normalized price system, the query-free
   normalized marginal proposal separator gives the finite prefix-template
   separator and the endpoint conclusions.

   For the finite-law version, nonnegative expected gain and positive expected
   mass imply that at least one bucket in the support has \(\mu_B>0\) and
   nonnegative gain; otherwise the expectation would be negative on the
   positive-mass part and zero on the zero-mass part.  The deterministic
   argument applies to that bucket.  The Bernoulli claim is the special case of
   \((QNMP1)\) with \(M_{2,B}=\mu_B+\mu_B^2\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Normalized soft gain materializes as a hard list]
   \label{cor:normalized-soft-gain-hard-list}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:finite-normalized-soft-bucket-oracle}.  Let
   \(B\) be one soft bucket with \(\mu_B>0\), and suppose its marginals are
   realized by a random list \(\mathcal L\subseteq W_B\) with
   \(\E|\mathcal L|^2\le M_{2,B}\).  For a hard list \(H\subseteq W_B\), put
   \[
      K_H=|H|,
      \qquad
      \widehat V(H)=
      \sum_{p\in H}
      \sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
   \]
   and define its normalized hard-list gain by
   \[
      \mathsf{NHG}_{\gamma}(W_B,H)
      =
      \widehat V(H)
      -
      \frac{b\,\psi_B}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{\beta^{\rho_B}b_0^{\rho_B}K_H^{\rho_B}}{L}
         +
         \frac{\beta^{1+\rho_B}b_0^{1+\rho_B}K_H^{1+\rho_B}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{NSH1}
   \]
   If \(\mathsf{NSG}_{\gamma}(B)\ge0\), then some realization
   \(H\subseteq W_B\) has \(K_H>0\) and
   \[
      \mathsf{NHG}_{\gamma}(W_B,H)\ge0 .
      \tag{NSH2}
   \]
   Thus the soft normalized oracle is only a proposal certificate: any
   successful soft bucket contains a successful ordinary hard list inside the
   same container.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(K=|\mathcal L|\).  Since \(0<\rho_B<1\),
   \[
      \E K^{\rho_B}\le \mu_B^{\rho_B},
      \qquad
      \E K^{1+\rho_B}
      \le
      (\E K)^{1-\rho_B}(\E K^2)^{\rho_B}
      \le
      \mu_B^{1-\rho_B}M_{2,B}^{\rho_B}.
   \]
   Also \(\E\widehat V(\mathcal L)=\widehat V_B\).  Therefore
   \[
      \E\,\mathsf{NHG}_{\gamma}(W_B,\mathcal L)
      \ge
      \mathsf{NSG}_{\gamma}(B)\ge0 .
   \]
   Since \(\mu_B>0\), the event \(K>0\) has positive probability.  The gain of
   the empty list is \(0\), so the expectation can be nonnegative only if some
   positive-size outcome has nonnegative hard-list gain.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite normalized hard-list oracle]
   \label{cor:finite-normalized-hard-list-oracle}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:query-free-normalized-list-proposal}.  Let \(\mathcal H\) be a
   finite build-time pool of certified hard lists.  An element
   \(H\in\mathcal H\) consists of a retained container \(W_H\) and a list
   \(L_H\subseteq W_H\).  Put
   \[
      K_H=|L_H|,
      \qquad
      \rho_H=\rho_{W_H},
      \qquad
      \psi_H=\psi_{W_H},
   \]
   and
   \[
      \widehat V_H=
      \sum_{p\in L_H}
      \sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
   \]
   Define
   \[
      \mathsf{NHG}_{\gamma}(H)
      =
      \widehat V_H
      -
      \frac{b\,\psi_H}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{\beta^{\rho_H}b_0^{\rho_H}K_H^{\rho_H}}{L}
         +
         \frac{\beta^{1+\rho_H}b_0^{1+\rho_H}K_H^{1+\rho_H}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{FNH1}
   \]
   If every nonnegative price system satisfying \((APC1)\), \((NAPO1)\), and
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}=1
   \]
   has
   \[
      \max_{H\in\mathcal H:\,K_H>0}\mathsf{NHG}_{\gamma}(H)\ge0,
      \tag{FNH2}
   \]
   then the finite prefix-template separator holds, and hence the same local
   and global endpoints apply.  A finite law on \(\mathcal H\) with positive
   expected size and nonnegative expected \(\mathsf{NHG}_{\gamma}\) is again
   sufficient.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(H\) has nonnegative normalized hard-list gain and \(K_H>0\), the
   point-mass list proposal satisfies \((QNRL1)\).  Thus
   \cref{cor:query-free-normalized-list-proposal} gives the finite
   prefix-template separator and the endpoint conclusions.  The law version
   reduces to a deterministic positive-size hard list by the same averaging
   argument used in \cref{cor:finite-normalized-soft-bucket-oracle}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Normalized hard-list separation reduces to prefixes]
   \label{cor:normalized-hard-list-prefix-reduction}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:finite-normalized-hard-list-oracle}, and
   fix a normalized price system.  For a retained container \(W\) and an
   integer \(1\le K\le |W|\), let \(P_K^{\rm tot}(W)\) be any \(K\)-point
   subset of \(W\) maximizing the total paid degree
   \[
      \sum_{p\in A}
      \sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      \qquad(|A|=K).
   \]
   Put
   \[
      D_W^\gamma(K)=
      \sum_{p\in P_K^{\rm tot}(W)}
      \sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
   \]
   and define the normalized prefix gain
   \[
      \mathsf{NPG}_{\gamma}(W,K)
      =
      D_W^\gamma(K)
      -
      \frac{b\,\psi_W}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{\beta^{\rho_W}b_0^{\rho_W}K^{\rho_W}}{L}
         +
         \frac{\beta^{1+\rho_W}b_0^{1+\rho_W}K^{1+\rho_W}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{NHP1}
   \]
   If a hard list \(H=(W_H,L_H)\) has \(K_H>0\) and
   \(\mathsf{NHG}_{\gamma}(H)\ge0\), then the total-degree prefix
   \(P_{K_H}^{\rm tot}(W_H)\) has
   \[
      \mathsf{NPG}_{\gamma}(W_H,K_H)\ge0 .
      \tag{NHP2}
   \]
   Consequently, whenever the build-time universe is closed under this
   total-degree top-\(K\) replacement, the finite normalized hard-list oracle
   may be replaced by a separation search over retained
   container/cardinality pairs and the scalar test \((NHP1)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The prefix \(P_{K_H}^{\rm tot}(W_H)\) maximizes the captured paid mass among
   all \(K_H\)-subsets of \(W_H\), while the normalized recursive cost depends
   only on \(W_H\) and \(K_H\).  Replacing \(L_H\) by that prefix can only
   increase \(\mathsf{NHG}_{\gamma}\).  This proves \((NHP2)\), and the oracle
   reduction follows from \cref{cor:finite-normalized-hard-list-oracle}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite normalized prefix oracle]
   \label{cor:finite-normalized-prefix-oracle}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:normalized-hard-list-prefix-reduction}.  Let \(\mathcal P\) be a
   finite build-time pool of retained prefix templates.  A template
   \(C\in\mathcal P\) consists of a retained container \(W_C\) and an available
   cardinality \(1\le K_C\le |W_C|\).  Define
   \[
      \mathsf{NPX}_{\gamma}(C)
      =
      D_{W_C}^\gamma(K_C)
      -
      \frac{b\,\psi_C}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{\beta^{\rho_C}b_0^{\rho_C}K_C^{\rho_C}}{L}
         +
         \frac{\beta^{1+\rho_C}b_0^{1+\rho_C}K_C^{1+\rho_C}}{S}
      \right),
      \tag{FNP1}
   \]
   where \(\rho_C=\rho_{W_C}\) and \(\psi_C=\psi_{W_C}\).  Suppose the
   hard-list universe can materialize, for every \(C\in\mathcal P\), the
   total-degree prefix \(P_{K_C}^{\rm tot}(W_C)\) for the current price system.
   If every nonnegative price system satisfying \((APC1)\), \((NAPO1)\), and
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}=1
   \]
   has
   \[
      \max_{C\in\mathcal P}\mathsf{NPX}_{\gamma}(C)\ge0,
      \tag{FNP2}
   \]
   then the finite prefix-template separator holds, and hence the same local
   and global endpoints apply.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(C\) has nonnegative normalized prefix gain, materialize the
   total-degree prefix \(P_{K_C}^{\rm tot}(W_C)\).  By
   \cref{cor:normalized-hard-list-prefix-reduction}, this is a nonnegative
   normalized hard-list column, and
   \cref{cor:finite-normalized-hard-list-oracle} gives the finite
   prefix-template separator and the endpoint conclusions.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[All-size normalized prefix separator]
   \label{cor:all-size-normalized-prefix-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:finite-normalized-prefix-oracle}.  Suppose
   that, for every retained container \(W\) appearing in \(\mathcal P\), the
   retained cardinalities are \(\chi\)-dense from above: for every
   \(1\le K\le |W|\), some template \((W,K')\in\mathcal P\) has
   \[
      K\le K'\le\chi K .
      \tag{ANP0}
   \]
   It is enough to prove the following scalar geometric statement.  Every
   nonnegative price system satisfying \((APC1)\), \((NAPO1)\), and
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}=1
   \]
   admits a retained container \(W\) and an integer \(1\le K\le |W|\) such that
   \[
      D_W^\gamma(K)
      \ge
      \frac{b\,\psi_W}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_W}K^{\rho_W}}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_W}K^{1+\rho_W}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{ANP1}
   \]
   Then the finite prefix-template separator holds, and hence the same local
   and global endpoints apply.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Choose a retained \(K'\) satisfying \((ANP0)\).  Monotonicity gives
   \(D_W^\gamma(K')\ge D_W^\gamma(K)\), while
   \(K'\le\chi K\) gives
   \[
      \frac{b\,\psi_W}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{\beta^{\rho_W}b_0^{\rho_W}(K')^{\rho_W}}{L}
         +
         \frac{\beta^{1+\rho_W}b_0^{1+\rho_W}(K')^{1+\rho_W}}{S}
      \right)
      \le
      \text{the right side of }(ANP1).
   \]
   Hence the retained template \(C=(W,K')\) has
   \(\mathsf{NPX}_{\gamma}(C)\ge0\).  Since this applies to every normalized
   price system, \cref{cor:finite-normalized-prefix-oracle} gives the finite
   prefix-template separator and the endpoint conclusions.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Scalar normalized prefix residual]
   \label{cor:scalar-normalized-prefix-residual}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:all-size-normalized-prefix-separator}.  If
   the scalar geometric statement \((ANP1)\) fails, then there exists a
   normalized price system satisfying \((APC1)\), \((NAPO1)\), and unit paid
   mass such that, for every retained container \(W\) and every
   \(1\le K\le |W|\),
   \[
      D_W^\gamma(K)
      <
      \frac{b\,\psi_W}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_W}K^{\rho_W}}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_W}K^{1+\rho_W}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{SNP1}
   \]
   Consequently, for total paid degrees
   \[
      d^\gamma(p)=
      \sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
      \qquad
      h_\delta(W)=|\{p\in W:d^\gamma(p)\ge\delta\}|,
   \]
   every retained container \(W\) and every level \(\delta>0\) with
   \(h_\delta(W)>0\) satisfy
   \[
      \delta
      <
      \frac{b\,\psi_W}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_W}h_\delta(W)^{\rho_W-1}}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_W}h_\delta(W)^{\rho_W}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{SNP2}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Failure of the scalar geometric statement means that some normalized price
   system has no retained container/cardinality pair satisfying \((ANP1)\),
   which is exactly \((SNP1)\).

   For the weak-type form, put \(h=h_\delta(W)\).  The top \(h\) points of
   \(W\) by total paid degree all have degree at least \(\delta\), so
   \(D_W^\gamma(h)\ge\delta h\).  Applying \((SNP1)\) with \(K=h\) and
   dividing by \(h\) gives \((SNP2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Scalar weak-type normalized prefix separator]
   \label{cor:scalar-weak-type-normalized-prefix-separator}
   In the setting of \cref{cor:all-size-normalized-prefix-separator}, it is
   enough to prove the following weak-type statement.  Every nonnegative price
   system satisfying \((APC1)\), \((NAPO1)\), and unit paid mass admits a
   retained container \(W\) and a level \(\delta>0\), with
   \(h_\delta(W)>0\), such that
   \[
      \delta
      \ge
      \frac{b\,\psi_W}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_W}h_\delta(W)^{\rho_W-1}}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_W}h_\delta(W)^{\rho_W}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{SWNP1}
   \]
   Then the finite prefix-template separator holds, and hence the same local
   and global endpoints apply.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the scalar geometric statement \((ANP1)\) failed, then
   \cref{cor:scalar-normalized-prefix-residual} would give a normalized
   residual satisfying the strict weak-type upper bound \((SNP2)\) for every
   retained container and every level.  The assumed weak-type witness
   \((SWNP1)\) contradicts this residual.  Hence \((ANP1)\) holds for every
   normalized price system, and
   \cref{cor:all-size-normalized-prefix-separator} gives the endpoint.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Scalar aggregate normalized prefix residual]
   \label{cor:scalar-aggregate-normalized-prefix-residual}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:scalar-normalized-prefix-residual}.  If the
   scalar geometric statement \((ANP1)\) fails, then the normalized residual
   from \cref{cor:scalar-normalized-prefix-residual} satisfies the following
   averaged envelope.  Fix a retained container \(W\), a finite nonnegative
   level weighting \((\lambda_i,\delta_i)_i\), and put
   \[
      h_i=h_{\delta_i}(W),
      \qquad
      M_0=\sum_i\lambda_i,
      \qquad
      M_1=\sum_i\lambda_i h_i,
   \]
   \[
      M_{1+\rho}=\sum_i\lambda_i h_i^{1+\rho},
      \qquad
      B=\sum_i\lambda_i\delta_i h_i,
      \qquad
      \rho=\rho_W,\quad \psi=\psi_W .
   \]
   Then
   \[
      B
      <
      \frac{b\,\psi}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^\rho M_0^{1-\rho}M_1^\rho}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho}M_{1+\rho}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{SANP1}
   \]
   If the supported levels have \(h_i\le H\), then the storage term may be
   replaced by
   \[
      \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho}H^\rho M_1}{S}.
      \tag{SANP2}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(M_0=0\), the claim is trivial.  Multiplying \((SNP2)\) at level
   \(\delta_i\) by \(h_i\) gives
   \[
      \delta_i h_i
      <
      \frac{b\,\psi}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^\rho h_i^\rho}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho}h_i^{1+\rho}}{S}
      \right),
   \]
   with the inequality trivial when \(h_i=0\).  Sum with weights
   \(\lambda_i\), and use concavity of \(x^\rho\):
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_i h_i^\rho
      \le
      M_0^{1-\rho}M_1^\rho .
   \]
   This proves \((SANP1)\).  The capped form follows from
   \(M_{1+\rho}\le H^\rho M_1\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Scalar aggregate normalized prefix separator]
   \label{cor:scalar-aggregate-normalized-prefix-separator}
   In the setting of \cref{cor:all-size-normalized-prefix-separator}, it is
   enough to prove the following averaged statement.  Every nonnegative price
   system satisfying \((APC1)\), \((NAPO1)\), and unit paid mass admits a
   retained container \(W\) and a finite nonnegative level weighting with
   \(M_1>0\) such that
   \[
      B
      \ge
      \frac{b\,\psi_W}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_W}
               M_0^{1-\rho_W}M_1^{\rho_W}}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_W}M_{1+\rho_W}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{SANPS1}
   \]
   It is also enough to prove the same violation with the capped storage term
   \((\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_W}H^{\rho_W}M_1/S\), for a certified cap \(H\)
   with \(h_i\le H\) on the supported levels.

   Under either averaged separator, the finite prefix-template separator holds,
   and hence the same local and global endpoints apply.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((ANP1)\) failed, then
   \cref{cor:scalar-aggregate-normalized-prefix-residual} would give the
   strict averaged upper bound \((SANP1)\), or its capped variant, for the
   normalized residual.  This contradicts the assumed averaged witness.  Hence
   \((ANP1)\) holds for every normalized price system, and
   \cref{cor:all-size-normalized-prefix-separator} gives the endpoint.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Scalar average superlevel panel]
   \label{cor:scalar-average-superlevel-panel}
   In \cref{cor:scalar-aggregate-normalized-prefix-separator}, a probability
   law \(\nu\) on finitely many levels is sufficient if, with
   \(H_\delta=h_\delta(W)\), \(\E_{\delta\sim\nu}H_\delta>0\), and
   \(\rho=\rho_W\), \(\psi=\psi_W\),
   \[
      \E_{\delta\sim\nu}\delta H_\delta
      \ge
      \frac{b\,\psi}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^\rho
               \bigl(\E_{\delta\sim\nu}H_\delta\bigr)^\rho}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho}
               \E_{\delta\sim\nu}H_\delta^{1+\rho}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{SASP1}
   \]
   In a capped form, it is enough that \(H_\delta\le H\) on the support of
   \(\nu\) and
   \[
      \E_{\delta\sim\nu}\delta H_\delta
      \ge
      \frac{b\,\psi}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^\rho
               \bigl(\E_{\delta\sim\nu}H_\delta\bigr)^\rho}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho}
               H^\rho\E_{\delta\sim\nu}H_\delta}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{SASP2}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Use the finite level panel with weights \(\lambda_\delta=\nu(\delta)\).
   Then \(M_0=1\), \(M_1=\E H_\delta\),
   \(M_{1+\rho}=\E H_\delta^{1+\rho}\), and
   \(B=\E\delta H_\delta\).  The displayed inequalities are exactly the
   averaged separator conditions in
   \cref{cor:scalar-aggregate-normalized-prefix-separator}.
\end{proof}

\begin{assumption}[Scalar dense-overlap separator]
   \label{asm:scalar-dense-overlap-separator}
   Work in the local primitive-hit-kernel setting used by
   \cref{cor:finite-normalized-prefix-oracle}, with budgets \(L,S>0\), retained
   containers, and a cardinality net as in
   \cref{cor:all-size-normalized-prefix-separator}.  Every normalized price
   system satisfying \((APC1)\), \((NAPO1)\), and
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}=1
   \]
   admits a retained container \(W\) and a finite probability law \(\nu\) on
   positive total-degree levels with \(\E_{\delta\sim\nu}H_\delta>0\) such that
   the scalar average panel inequality \((SASP1)\) holds.  It is also
   sufficient if the capped form \((SASP2)\) holds for a certified cap \(H\).
\end{assumption}

\begin{corollary}[Certified scalar superlevel reporter]
   \label{cor:certified-scalar-superlevel-reporter}
   Work in the setting of \cref{asm:scalar-dense-overlap-separator}.  It is
   enough to prove the following reporter statement.  For every normalized price
   system there are a retained container \(W\) and a finite probability law
   \(\nu\) on reported levels \(\delta>0\).  Write
   \[
      H_\delta=h_\delta(W)
      =
      |\{p\in W:d^\gamma(p)\ge\delta\}|,
      \qquad
      d^\gamma(p)=
      \sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
   \]
   The reporter certifies lower hit quantities \(X_\delta\) and upper size
   quantities \(K_\delta\) such that
   \[
      0\le X_\delta\le\delta H_\delta,
      \qquad
      H_\delta\le K_\delta
      \tag{CSR0}
   \]
   for every reported level, and \(\E_{\nu}X_\delta>0\).  If
   \[
      \E_{\nu}X_\delta
      \ge
      \frac{b\,\psi_W}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_W}
               (\E_{\nu}K_\delta)^{\rho_W}}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_W}
               \E_{\nu}K_\delta^{1+\rho_W}}{S}
      \right),
      \tag{CSR1}
   \]
   then the witness required in
   \cref{asm:scalar-dense-overlap-separator} exists for this price system.  In
   a capped version, it is enough that \(K_\delta\le H\) on the support of \(\nu\) and
   \[
      \E_{\nu}X_\delta
      \ge
      \frac{b\,\psi_W}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_W}
               (\E_{\nu}K_\delta)^{\rho_W}}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_W}
               H^{\rho_W}\E_{\nu}K_\delta}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{CSR2}
   \]
   Consequently, if every normalized price system admits such a certified
   reported panel, then the scalar dense-overlap separator gives the local
   filter cover of \cref{cor:scalar-dense-overlap-local-cover}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \((CSR0)\),
   \[
      \E_{\nu}\delta H_\delta\ge\E_{\nu}X_\delta,
      \qquad
      \E_{\nu}H_\delta\le\E_{\nu}K_\delta,
      \qquad
      \E_{\nu}H_\delta^{1+\rho_W}
      \le
      \E_{\nu}K_\delta^{1+\rho_W}.
   \]
   Since \(\E X_\delta>0\), also \(\E H_\delta>0\).  Therefore \((CSR1)\)
   implies the exact scalar average panel inequality \((SASP1)\) for the same
   container and level law.  The capped case is identical, using
   \(H_\delta\le K_\delta\le H\) to get
   \(H_\delta^{1+\rho_W}\le H^{\rho_W}K_\delta\), which gives \((SASP2)\).
   Thus the reported panel is a valid witness for
   \cref{asm:scalar-dense-overlap-separator}.  The final claim is
   \cref{cor:scalar-dense-overlap-local-cover}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One-level certified superlevel separator]
   \label{cor:one-level-certified-superlevel-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{asm:scalar-dense-overlap-separator}.  Suppose
   that for every normalized price system there is a retained certified
   container \(W\) and a level \(\delta>0\) such that
   \[
      h=h_\delta(W)
      =
      |\{p\in W:d^\gamma(p)\ge\delta\}|>0,
   \]
   and
   \[
      \delta h
      \ge
      \frac{b\,\psi_W}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_W}h^{\rho_W}}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_W}h^{1+\rho_W}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{OCS1}
   \]
   Then the scalar dense-overlap separator holds.  Consequently the local cover
   and global endpoint consequences of
   \cref{cor:scalar-dense-overlap-local-cover} and
   \cref{cor:certified-scalar-reporter-polylog-endpoint}
   apply whenever this one-level condition is verified at every node.

   Conversely, if the scalar dense-overlap separator fails for the retained
   container family, then there is a normalized paid residual for which every
   retained container and every nonempty total-degree superlevel satisfies the
   strict reverse inequality
   \[
      \delta h_\delta(W)
      <
      \frac{b\,\psi_W}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_W}h_\delta(W)^{\rho_W}}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_W}h_\delta(W)^{1+\rho_W}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{OCS2}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For the first claim, apply
   \cref{cor:certified-scalar-superlevel-reporter} with the point-mass level
   law \(\nu=\delta_\delta\), the exact hit certificate
   \(X_\delta=\delta h_\delta(W)\), and the exact size certificate
   \(K_\delta=h_\delta(W)\).  Then \((CSR1)\) is precisely \((OCS1)\), so the
   required scalar dense-overlap witness exists for every normalized price
   system.  The local and global consequences are the cited corollaries.

   For the converse, failure of the scalar dense-overlap separator means that
   some normalized price system has no average panel satisfying \((SASP1)\) or
   \((SASP2)\).  In particular, no point-mass exact level law can satisfy
   \((SASP1)\).  Expanding that point-mass inequality gives exactly the strict
   reverse bound \((OCS2)\) for every retained \(W\) and every nonempty level.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Diffuse scalar residual from small containers]
   \label{cor:diffuse-scalar-residual}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:scalar-normalized-prefix-residual}.  Suppose
   the scalar geometric statement \((ANP1)\) fails, and let
   \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) be the normalized residual from
   \cref{cor:scalar-normalized-prefix-residual}.  Put
   \[
      d^\gamma(p)=
      \sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
      \qquad
      C_W=
      \frac{b\,\psi_W}{\pi_1}.
   \]
   Then every retained container \(W\) and every \(1\le K\le |W|\) satisfy
   \[
      \sum_{p\in P_K^{\rm tot}(W)}d^\gamma(p)
      <
      C_W
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_W}K^{\rho_W}}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_W}K^{1+\rho_W}}{S}
      \right),
      \tag{DSR1}
   \]
   where \(P_K^{\rm tot}(W)\) is the top-\(K\) total-degree prefix in \(W\).
   In particular, the total paid mass inside \(W\) is bounded by the right-hand
   side of \((DSR1)\) with \(K=|W|\).

   If the retained family contains every singleton \(\{p\}\), with
   \(C_{\{p\}}\le C_1\) and exponents \(0\le\rho_{\{p\}}\le1\), then
   \[
      d^\gamma(p)
      <
      C_1\left(
         \frac{1}{L}+\frac{\chi\beta b_0}{S}
      \right)
      \max\{1,\chi\beta b_0\}
      \qquad(p\in P).
      \tag{DSR2}
   \]
   Consequently, since the normalized paid mass is one,
   \[
      |\{p:d^\gamma(p)>0\}|
      >
      \frac{1}{
      C_1\left(
         L^{-1}+(\chi\beta b_0)S^{-1}
      \right)\max\{1,\chi\beta b_0\}} .
      \tag{DSR3}
   \]
   Thus a residual that defeats all retained one-level dense superlevels must
   spread its paid mass over many resident points and, more generally, cannot
   put more than the Renyi mass in \((DSR1)\) inside any retained smaller-radius
   container.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The first statement is exactly \((SNP1)\) after substituting the notation
   \(C_W=b\psi_W/\pi_1\).  Taking \(K=|W|\) gives the total-mass bound for \(W\).

   For a singleton \(W=\{p\}\), use \(K=1\) in \((DSR1)\).  Since
   \(0\le\rho_{\{p\}}\le1\), both
   \((\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_{\{p\}}}\) and
   \((\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_{\{p\}}}\) are bounded by
   \(\max\{1,\chi\beta b_0\}\) and
   \((\chi\beta b_0)\max\{1,\chi\beta b_0\}\), respectively.  This gives
   \((DSR2)\).  Finally,
   \[
      1=\sum_{p\in P}d^\gamma(p)
      \le
      |\{p:d^\gamma(p)>0\}|\max_p d^\gamma(p),
   \]
   and \((DSR3)\) follows from \((DSR2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Lorentz profile of a scalar residual]
   \label{cor:lorentz-scalar-residual-profile}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:diffuse-scalar-residual}.  Fix a retained
   container \(W\), and order its points so that
   \[
      d^\gamma(p_1)\ge d^\gamma(p_2)\ge\cdots\ge d^\gamma(p_{|W|}).
   \]
   Put \(a=\chi\beta b_0\), \(\rho=\rho_W\), and \(C_W=b\psi_W/\pi_1\).  Then
   every rank \(1\le i\le |W|\) satisfies
   \[
      d^\gamma(p_i)
      <
      C_W\left(
         \frac{a^\rho i^{\rho-1}}{L}
         +
         \frac{a^{1+\rho}i^\rho}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{LSR1}
   \]
   Equivalently, every retained container has weak Lorentz profile
   \[
      \sup_{1\le K\le |W|}
      \frac{\sum_{i\le K}d^\gamma(p_i)}
      {a^\rho K^\rho/L+a^{1+\rho}K^{1+\rho}/S}
      <
      C_W .
      \tag{LSR2}
   \]
   Therefore a scalar reporter for the residual cannot be obtained by merely
   selecting the first unusually heavy ranks in any retained container; it must
   either find a container whose profile violates \((LSR2)\) or use a spherical
   or tensor mechanism that exploits this entire diffuse profile.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The weak Lorentz bound \((LSR2)\) is exactly \((DSR1)\) in sorted notation.
   For \((LSR1)\), use
   \[
      i\,d^\gamma(p_i)
      \le
      \sum_{j\le i}d^\gamma(p_j)
   \]
   and then apply \((LSR2)\) with \(K=i\), dividing by \(i\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Scalar dense-overlap separator gives a local cover]
   \label{cor:scalar-dense-overlap-local-cover}
   Work in the local setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-local-filter-cover}.  Suppose the primitive
   spherical hit kernel satisfies \((PPLC1)\), the retained prefix pool has the
   all-size cardinality-net closure required in
   \cref{cor:all-size-normalized-prefix-separator}, and
   \cref{asm:scalar-dense-overlap-separator} holds for the induced paid
   primitive-hit instance.  Then the ordinary finite filter-cover LP
   \((\mathsf{FC}_{\mathcal N})\) is feasible with query budget \(L\) and
   storage budget \(S\).  Under the atom bounds of
   \cref{lem:poisson-filter-cover-materialization}, the feasible fractional
   cover materializes into retained overlapping filters with logarithmic budget
   inflation.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{asm:scalar-dense-overlap-separator} and
   \cref{cor:scalar-average-superlevel-panel}, every normalized paid dual has a
   scalar aggregate prefix violation.  Hence
   \cref{cor:scalar-aggregate-normalized-prefix-separator} gives the finite
   prefix-template separator.  Applying
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-local-filter-cover} to the primitive hit kernel
   satisfying \((PPLC1)\) gives feasibility of
   \((\mathsf{FC}_{\mathcal N})\) with budgets \(L,S\).  The materialization
   statement is \cref{lem:poisson-filter-cover-materialization}.
\end{proof}

This is the fully fractional dense-overlap target in its most compressed form.
The separator does not choose a disjoint family of dense clusters.  It only has
to show that every normalized paid residual has one retained container whose
total-degree level panel captures enough mass compared with the absolute
\(K^\rho/L\) and \(K^{1+\rho}/S\) moments.  If it fails, then
\cref{cor:scalar-normalized-prefix-residual} and
\cref{cor:scalar-aggregate-normalized-prefix-residual} give the exact residual:
every retained container and every reported level panel obeys the reverse
Renyi list-size inequality.  Thus the remaining geometric theorem is not an
overlap accounting theorem; the LP has already handled overlap.  It is a
weighted range-reporting or list-decoding theorem ruling out that scalar
residual, or showing that such a residual is pseudo-random enough for the
ordinary spherical reduced-gain test.
\Cref{cor:certified-scalar-superlevel-reporter} is the promised LP
range-reporting interface: the reporter may be approximate, but it must provide
one-sided certificates.  Lower hit certificates protect coverage, upper size
certificates protect recursive query and storage moments, and the final
retained column is still the exact top-degree prefix verified by the finite LP.
\Cref{cor:diffuse-scalar-residual} records the complementary pseudo-randomness
forced by failure: if singleton containers are retained, no point can carry
more than \(O(1/L+1/S)\) paid mass, and every retained smaller-radius container
has only the Renyi amount of paid mass allowed by \((DSR1)\).  This is the
diffuse residual that a spherical fallback or tensor reporter must exploit.
\Cref{cor:lorentz-scalar-residual-profile} rewrites the same obstruction as a
rank profile: after sorting any retained container by paid degree, every prefix
lies below the \(K^\rho/L+K^{1+\rho}/S\) envelope.
\Cref{cor:guard-bounded-spherical-reduced-gain} explains the matching
spherical side on the low-guard domain: if the high-correlation set charged by
the spherical proof is already guard-small, then it cannot be the obstruction
to positive spherical reduced gain.  The sharper dual-weighted form,
\cref{cor:dual-weighted-guard-spherical-reduced-gain}, shows that only the
query-price weighted active guard mass matters.  In particular, by
\cref{cor:low-guard-contained-spherical-reduced-gain}, if the high-correlation
sets are contained in the resident \(cr\)-guard balls, then low-guard queries
can obstruct spherical reduced gain only through activation-weighted guard mass
that exceeds the surplus dual demand.  In the budget-compatible contained case,
\cref{cor:contained-high-correlation-local-cover} gives the local finite cover
directly from spherical buckets.  The remaining scalar reporter theorem is
therefore about high-correlation mass that either leaks outside the resident
guard containment used by this corollary, or survives the guard in the
dual-weighted sense, and is not concentrated in any retained smaller-radius
container.

\Cref{cor:finite-all-size-soft-bucket-separation} is the cardinality-net
version of the dense-overlap column generator.  A proposal family may contain
arbitrarily overlapping soft dense regions, but a bucket is accepted only if
its canonical positive-margin query side pays for the dyadic query loss
\(b_0^\rho\) and the dyadic storage loss \(b_0^{1+\rho}\).  By
\cref{cor:all-size-soft-gain-hard-list}, even this soft certificate is not a
new materialization requirement: any positive soft bucket contains a positive
hard-list witness.  \Cref{cor:all-size-hard-list-prefix-separation} then
replaces the witness by a top-degree prefix for one Boolean query layer, and
\cref{cor:finite-all-size-prefix-separation} is the resulting finite
range-reporting objective: maximize \((FAPS1)\) over certified
container/cardinality templates, retain only the verified Boolean prefix, and
discard all failed proposals.  If this objective fails,
\cref{cor:normalized-all-size-prefix-obstruction} leaves a single normalized
dual obstruction with unit paid mass and query/storage price below
\(\pi_1^{-1}\); proving that no such obstruction can satisfy all envelopes
\((APRE1)\) is now exactly the dense-overlap separator.  The weak-type form in
\cref{cor:normalized-all-size-weak-type-obstruction} says more concretely that
any retained exact superlevel must obey the absolute density cap \((NAW2)\);
\cref{cor:normalized-weak-type-separator} is the corresponding scale-free
range-reporting target.  The cardinality-net form in
\cref{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-weak-type-obstruction} and
\cref{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-weak-type-separator}
removes the exact-cardinality artifact, so a dyadic or output-sensitive
range-reporting routine only needs to find an arbitrary retained superlevel
above the scale-free cap \((NCWS1)\).  The normalized aggregate and proposal
forms in
\cref{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-aggregate-list-moment-obstruction},
\cref{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-aggregate-list-moment-separator},
\cref{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-random-list-proposal}, and
\cref{cor:normalized-cardinality-net-marginal-proposal}
turn this into the build-time-heavy interface: a range-reporting,
list-decoding, AQ, or randomized clustering proposal only has to beat the
absolute \(K^\rho\) query and \(K^{1+\rho}\) storage moments under the
normalized dual prices.  The query-free normalized forms in
\cref{cor:query-free-normalized-list-proposal},
\cref{cor:query-free-normalized-marginal-proposal}, and
\cref{cor:finite-normalized-soft-bucket-oracle}
are the finite column-generation target: after normalization, a proposed
bucket may simply be scored by its total captured paid near-pair mass minus the
absolute recursive query and storage moments.  Finally,
\cref{cor:normalized-soft-gain-hard-list},
\cref{cor:normalized-hard-list-prefix-reduction}, and
\cref{cor:finite-normalized-prefix-oracle}
collapse the normalized oracle to a scalar total-degree prefix search over
retained container/cardinality templates.  The all-size form in
\cref{cor:all-size-normalized-prefix-separator},
\cref{cor:scalar-normalized-prefix-residual}, and
\cref{cor:scalar-weak-type-normalized-prefix-separator}
removes the dyadic cardinality artifact from that final target: a geometric
proof may find any total-degree superlevel that violates the scalar residual
\((SNP2)\).  The averaged forms
\cref{cor:scalar-aggregate-normalized-prefix-residual},
\cref{cor:scalar-aggregate-normalized-prefix-separator}, and
\cref{cor:scalar-average-superlevel-panel}
let an output-sensitive reporter certify a whole panel of levels by its
aggregate captured mass and Renyi list-size moments.

\begin{corollary}[Joint query-list proposal separator]
   \label{cor:joint-query-list-proposal-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:boolean-query-layer-list-proposal-separator}.
   It is enough to prove the following joint proposal statement.  For every
   nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\), there is a finite seed law \(s\sim\nu\) such that seed
   \(s\) chooses a certified container \(W_s\in\mathcal W\), an ordinary query
   layer \(Q_s\subseteq\mathcal Q\), and a certified list \(L_s\subseteq W_s\).
   Writing
   \[
      K_s=|L_s|,
      \qquad
      A_s=\sum_{q\in Q_s}\tau_q,
      \qquad
      \rho_s=\rho_{W_s},
      \qquad
      \psi_s=\psi_{W_s},
   \]
   and
   \[
      V_s=
      \sum_{p\in L_s}
      \sum_{q\in Q_s:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
      \tag{JQL1}
   \]
   assume
   \[
      \E_s V_s
      >
      b\,\E_s\!\left[
         \psi_s\left(
            A_sK_s^{\rho_s}+\sigma K_s^{1+\rho_s}
         \right)
      \right].
      \tag{JQL2}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((JQL2)\) holds, then some deterministic seed \(s\) satisfies
   \[
      V_s>
      b\,\psi_s\left(A_sK_s^{\rho_s}+\sigma K_s^{1+\rho_s}\right).
      \tag{JQL3}
   \]
   By \cref{lem:deterministic-query-list-verifier}, this seed exposes an
   available paid prefix with positive repair reduced gain.  Thus every surplus
   price system satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) has a positive Boolean column,
   and \cref{cor:atomized-paid-core-hit-kernel-cover} gives the primitive
   hit-kernel cover.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:query-free-marginal-proposal-separator} is the current most compact
build-time target.  A proposal routine chooses only the container and a soft
update measure, plus a second-moment bound for a list realizing those
marginals.  The query side is the canonical positive-margin layer.
\Cref{cor:independent-soft-proposal-separator} gives the most direct checklist:
for independent thinning, a soft bucket of expected size \(\mu\ge1\) pays query
price \(\psi\mu^\rho\) and storage price \(O(\psi\sigma\mu^{1+\rho})\).  Hard
lists are the special case \(\pi=\mathbf 1_L\) and \(M_2=|L|^2\), covered by
\cref{cor:query-free-list-proposal-separator}; the deterministic verifier then
replaces the proposed list by the available top-degree prefix before checking
exact reduced gain.  Thus \(k\)-means++ seeding, additive-quantization
responsibilities, LP/range-reporting violator search, and tensor or lattice
list decoders can all be analyzed as laws over container/marginal pairs, while
the final verifier still keeps an ordinary Boolean filter column.
\Cref{cor:finite-soft-bucket-separation} is the corresponding build-time
oracle: after generating any finite pool of such soft buckets, preprocessing
only has to maximize the explicit scalar score \((FSB1)\) against the current
dual.  Failed buckets are discarded; query time and space charge only the
verified Boolean columns obtained from positive-gain buckets.
\Cref{lem:fixed-mass-soft-buckets-near-hard} adds an important simplification:
once the total mass of a soft bucket is fixed, the best responsibility vector is
hard except possibly for one point.  Soft buckets are therefore a convenient
proposal and averaging language; the exact verifier can always be driven toward
ordinary lists or one-point fractional perturbations.
\Cref{cor:positive-soft-gain-hard-list} goes one step further: any positive
soft reduced-gain certificate already contains a positive ordinary hard-list
certificate after rounding the single fractional point.  Thus soft AQ or
facility responsibilities help find promising regions, but the proof need only
retain hard lists and their canonical query layers.
\Cref{cor:finite-hard-list-separation} is the resulting clean oracle: with
unbounded preprocessing, search any finite family of certified
container/list pairs using the scalar hinge score \((FHL1)\).  Positive lists
are verified and converted to ordinary Boolean columns; soft buckets are only a
proposal language for finding such lists.
\Cref{cor:hard-list-prefix-separation} removes the last arbitrary-list feature
from this oracle: after the dual prices are fixed, a positive list can be
replaced by the top \(K\) points in the same container for one Boolean query
layer.  Thus LP range reporting, list decoding, or additive-code reporters only
need to find high paid-degree prefixes for priced query layers, followed by the
same exact reduced-gain verifier.
\Cref{cor:fractional-query-prefix-separation} keeps fractional query weights
available as an analysis tool: any positive fractional weighting thresholds to
one Boolean query layer before the retained column is formed.
\Cref{cor:finite-prefix-separation} is the resulting exact finite oracle.  For
each certified container and retained cardinality, maximize the scalar
top-\(K\) reduced-cost objective \((FPS1)\); positivity is equivalent to an
ordinary Boolean prefix filter with positive gain.

\begin{assumption}[Balanced aggregate list-size separator]
   \label{asm:balanced-aggregate-list-size-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{asm:paid-atomized-prefix-separator}, and assume
   every container has exponent \(0<\rho_W<1\) and \(b\)-dense available
   cardinalities in the sense of \((CNW0)\).  There is a constant
   \(\varepsilon>0\) such that every nonnegative price system
   \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) admits a certified
   container \(W\), fractional query weighting \(0\le y_q\le1\), and a finite
   nonnegative level panel that is \(\varepsilon\)-balanced in the sense of
   \cref{def:success-normalized-aggregate-list-panel}.  It is also sufficient to
   produce the capped-list version, with some certified cap \(H\) for the
   supported level cardinalities.
\end{assumption}

\begin{corollary}[Balanced list-size separation implies the hit-kernel cover]
   \label{cor:balanced-list-size-hit-kernel-cover}
   In the setting of \cref{asm:balanced-aggregate-list-size-separator}, if the
   balanced aggregate list-size separator holds, then
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   An \(\varepsilon\)-balanced panel violates \((ALR1)\), because
   \[
      \mathsf{Hit}(\Lambda)
      >
      \mathsf{Qry}(\Lambda)+\mathsf{Store}(\Lambda).
   \]
   In the capped-list case it violates the capped inequality in
   \cref{cor:aggregate-list-moment-prefix-hit-kernel-cover}.  That corollary
   therefore gives the primitive hit-kernel cover.
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:paid-prefix-weak-type} gives a direct separator screen.  If, for some
certified container and fractional query weighting, a paid-degree superlevel has
cardinality strictly above the query-priced bound \((PWT2)\) and strictly below
the storage-priced bound \((PWT3)\), then the residual envelope is impossible,
so \cref{lem:weighted-atomized-prefix-normal-form} exposes a positive-gain paid
prefix.  In the balanced range \(h_\delta\asymp A_y/\sigma\), it is enough to
beat the single density threshold
\[
   \psi A_y^\rho\sigma^{1-\rho}
\]
up to the constant \(C_\rho\).  This is the local geometric quantity that a
ball, cap, range-reporting, or list-decoding separator should try to force from
the spherical high-correlation co-load.
\Cref{lem:forbidden-weak-type-superlevel} and
\cref{cor:weak-type-prefix-hit-kernel-cover} make this operational: a proposed
geometric separator only has to return one certified superlevel in the
forbidden middle regime, after which the finite cover duality supplies the
positive column and the hit-kernel cover.
\Cref{lem:cardinality-net-weak-type-superlevel} removes the exact-cardinality
artifact from this target.  If the available prefix sizes form a constant-net,
for example the powers of two, then a list-decoding or range-reporting
separator may return an arbitrary heavy superlevel with only the displayed
constant slack; the verifier rounds its cardinality down to an available prefix
and the final retained column is still an ordinary paid prefix.
\Cref{lem:layer-cake-weak-type-separator} gives the averaged version needed for
list-size arguments: it is enough to prove that a weighted collection of levels,
or a truncated Lorentz moment of the paid-degree sequence, has positive surplus
over the recursive query/storage envelope.  A positive average cannot hide; one
level is already a forbidden weak-type superlevel after cardinality rounding.
\Cref{lem:aggregate-list-moment-weak-type-separator} is the list-size form of
the same statement.  The query side needs only the aggregate list mass \(M_1\)
through the concave power \(M_0^{1-\rho}M_1^\rho\); the storage side is the
\((1+\rho)\)-moment \(M_{1+\rho}\), or the cruder cap \(H^\rho M_1\).  Thus a
spherical or lattice list-decoding theorem can aim to lower-bound the captured
paid mass \(B\) while upper-bounding only these average list-size quantities.
\Cref{def:success-normalized-aggregate-list-panel} makes this the same
success-normalized potential as in the compressed-bucket picture: the useful
quantity is not raw list size, but list query/storage cost divided by captured
hit mass.  \Cref{asm:balanced-aggregate-list-size-separator} is therefore the
plug-in theorem target for tensorized spherical filters, range-reporting
violator search, lattice decoders, or any other proposal mechanism.  A proposed
geometric proof only has to output one balanced aggregate panel; the LP
materialization then turns that averaged certificate into ordinary retained
filters.
\Cref{lem:average-list-size-panel-criterion} gives the normalized probability
form of the same target.  After choosing a finite law over levels, the geometric
proof only has to show
\[
   \E[\text{captured paid list mass}]
   >
   \psi\left(
      \widehat A_y(\E[\text{list size}])^\rho
      +
      \sigma\E[\text{list size}^{1+\rho}]
   \right),
\]
or the capped analogue.  This is the exact average Renyi list-size statement
suggested by the compressed-bucket route; large lists are allowed if their
\((1+\rho)\)-moment is paid by the captured hit mass.
\Cref{lem:random-list-proposal-criterion} removes the remaining threshold-list
artifact.  A build-time routine may output any random list \(\mathcal L\) inside
a certified container.  If its expected paid value beats the same query and
storage moments of \(K=|\mathcal L|\), the exact verifier replaces it by an
available top-degree prefix with positive reduced gain.  Thus \(k\)-means++,
facility search, AQ buckets, LP range reporting, or list/lattice decoders only
need to generate high value-per-moment lists; they do not need to align their
raw output with the final retained prefix.
\Cref{lem:query-layer-random-list-proposal} removes the remaining fractional
query-weight artifact from this interface: any successful fractional-query list
certificate has an ordinary threshold query layer with the same surplus.
\Cref{cor:seeded-list-proposal-criterion} and
\cref{cor:marginal-list-proposal-criterion} are the two forms most useful for
implementation and for geometry.  A seeded decoder only has to prove an average
value-per-moment inequality over its seed law; one good seed then exists and is
verified exactly.  A soft or randomized decoder can instead certify only the
inclusion marginals and a second moment of the emitted list.
\Cref{cor:query-layer-seeded-marginal-proposals} combines these two reductions:
seeded and marginal certificates may also be materialized on an ordinary
threshold query layer.  Thus fractional query weights are only an analysis
device; the retained filters are still Boolean query-side activations.  This
turns the remaining separator into a concrete moment problem for geometric
neighborhoods, facility cells, additive-code buckets, or list-decoding output
sets.
\Cref{cor:query-free-marginal-proposal-separator} removes the query side from
the proposal mechanism as well.  A soft bucket only has to specify update
marginals and a realizable second moment; the canonical positive-margin query
layer is chosen after the dual prices are known, and the final retained object
is still the exact top-degree Boolean prefix.  This is the fractional analogue
of dense-overlap column generation: preprocessing may search over soft
facilities, additive-quantization codes, or list-decoder panels, but the LP pays
only for the verified column it keeps.
\Cref{cor:independent-soft-proposal-separator} is the simplest operational
version: independent thinning turns a responsibility vector of mass \(\mu\) into
a valid proposal with second moment at most \(\mu+\mu^2\), hence with the usual
\(\mu^{1+\rho}\) storage charge once \(\mu\ge1\).
\Cref{cor:finite-soft-bucket-separation} turns this into an exact finite
column-generation oracle: for any generated pool of soft buckets, the only
build-time optimization objective is the scalar reduced gain \((FSB1)\), and
positive gain is both necessary and sufficient for that pool to defeat the
current surplus dual.
\Cref{cor:aggregate-list-moment-residual-envelope} is the matching obstruction:
if the hit-kernel cover fails, every finite list-size panel obeys \((ALR1)\).
Thus a proof of the polylog endpoint can now target a single averaged
inequality, rather than locating a profitable dense cluster or superlevel by
hand.

\Cref{cor:paid-compression-hit-kernel-cover} is the fractional dense-filter
cover in its paid form.  The separator does not choose disjoint dense clusters.
It only has to prove that any overbudget value-proportional primitive law can be
compressed, fractionally and with arbitrary overlap, into cheaper Pareto cores.
Query overlap is charged by
\(\sum_C\lambda_CT_C\mathbf 1\{q\in Q'_C\}\), storage by
\(\sum_C\lambda_CS_C\), and coverage is inherited from the primitive hit
kernel.  Thus ordinary spherical slices, singleton dense slices, quotient
cores, \(k\)-means-style facilities, additive-quantization buckets, and
list-decoding outputs are all merely proposal mechanisms for the same paid
reduced-cost inequality \((PCOV4)\).  When the family is closed under canonical
assignment, \cref{lem:canonical-paid-core-hinge} removes the assignment and
query-side choices too: preprocessing only has to search for an update core
whose paid whole-slice support violates the hinge inequality \((CPH4)\).
\Cref{lem:atomized-paid-core-hinge} is sharper still.  It allows a core to
capture only the paid primitive atoms that actually lie in its update side, so
the support term becomes the hit-kernel-weighted quantity
\[
   \bar h_U^\gamma(q)
   =
   \sum_{p\in U:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
\]
The remaining dense theorem can therefore be stated without choosing primitive
slice assignments at all: every surplus singleton-saturated paid dual must
contain a radius-contracting core whose atomized support violates \((APH4)\).
\Cref{lem:weighted-atomized-prefix-normal-form} pushes this to the prefix level:
inside a certified container, every fractional query weighting induces paid
degrees \(d_y^\gamma(p)\), and the best \(k\)-point core is simply the top-\(k\)
prefix.  Thus failure of all paid prefixes is equivalent to the explicit
degree envelope \((WAE1)\)--\((WAE2)\), which is the concrete residual packing
condition left for geometry.
\Cref{asm:paid-atomized-prefix-separator} and
\cref{cor:paid-prefix-hit-kernel-cover} make this a complete dense-side
criterion: every surplus paid dual only has to violate one certified
container-prefix envelope.  If it does not, then
\cref{cor:paid-prefix-residual-envelope} gives the exact counterexample format
that the spherical residual or the next geometric separator must rule out.
\Cref{lem:paid-prefix-weak-type} converts that counterexample into an explicit
level-set dichotomy: residual paid mass is either query-price small, storage
massive, or below the balanced density \(C_\rho\psi A_y^\rho\sigma^{1-\rho}\).
\Cref{cor:weak-type-prefix-hit-kernel-cover} is the corresponding acceptance
criterion: any geometric, range-reporting, or list-decoding routine that always
finds a forbidden weak-type superlevel proves the primitive hit-kernel cover.

\begin{assumption}[Compression-dual separator]
   \label{asm:compression-dual-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:residual-separator-local-cover}.  Fix a
   finite family \(\mathcal R\) of query-weighted Pareto-core records as in
   \cref{lem:slice-core-compression-dual}, and enlarge the finite filter
   universe by all threshold activations of the underlying cores appearing in
   those records.  The family \(\mathcal R\) is compression-dual separating if,
   for every surplus dual price system
   \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying \((RS1)\) and having nonpositive reduced
   gain on the spherical buckets, whole high-correlation dense slices, and
   atom-safe primitive dense prefixes, the associated compression dual
   \((SCD\text{-}D)\) has no feasible \(\beta\) satisfying \((SCDD1)\).
\end{assumption}

\begin{corollary}[Compression-dual separation implies local cover]
   \label{cor:compression-dual-local-cover}
   In the setting of \cref{asm:compression-dual-separator}, if
   \(\mathcal R\) is compression-dual separating, then the finite filter-cover
   LP \((\mathsf{FC}_{\mathcal N})\) is feasible with query budget \(L\) and
   storage budget \(S\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose the filter-cover LP were infeasible.  By
   \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual}, there is a surplus dual price system
   with nonpositive reduced gain on every retained column.  In particular it has
   nonpositive gain on the spherical buckets, whole high-correlation dense
   slices, and atom-safe primitive prefixes.  Compression-dual separation rules
   out alternative \textup{(ii)} of
   \cref{lem:slice-core-compression-dual}, so alternative \textup{(i)} holds:
   there is a slice-to-core domination certificate of price
   \(<\mathsf A_{\rm hc}\).  By \cref{lem:slice-to-core-domination}, some
   threshold activation of an underlying core represented in \(\mathcal R\) has
   positive reduced gain.  This activation is a retained column of the enlarged
   universe, contradicting the dual certificate.  Hence the cover LP is
   feasible.
\end{proof}

\Cref{asm:compression-dual-separator} is the exact finite form of the remaining
dense-versus-pseudo-random theorem.  One must rule out a simultaneous pair of
certificates: a filter-cover dual \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\) that defeats
spherical buckets and primitive dense slices, and a compression dual \(\beta\)
under which every proposed radius-contracting core is no better than its
Pareto price.  A proof may do this by a geometric argument, by adding richer
core records, or by showing that such a \(\beta\)-spread residual already
violates the spherical reduced-gain test.

The exact weighted form is stronger than the dyadic core screen above.  The
dyadic objective \(\theta_jc_U(q)\) lower-bounds \(a_U(q)\) on one price layer
and is useful when the proposal generator wants an unweighted counting problem.
But the filter-cover proof itself does not need to pay that dyadic loss: an
offline separator with access to the dual prices can optimize \((WPC2)\)
directly, and the retained column is still the same ordinary query activation
\((U,Q_\alpha^+(U))\).  Thus demand-layering is a build-time simplification, not
an inherent overhead in the fractional dense-cover theorem.

\begin{assumption}[Layer quotient separator]
   \label{asm:layer-quotient-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:residual-separator-local-cover}.  Suppose a
   surplus dual price system \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfies \((RS1)\) and
   has nonpositive reduced gain on the spherical buckets, whole
   high-correlation dense slices, and atom-safe dense prefixes.  Partition the
   positive demand prices \(\alpha_{p,q}\) into dyadic classes
   \(\mathcal N_j\) as in \cref{lem:dyadic-quotient-packing}.

   The quotient family \(\mathcal G\) is layer separating if, for every such
   residual dual, there is a dyadic class \(j\) and a quotient
   \(G\in\mathcal G\) such that
   \[
      \theta_j C_j(G)>P(G),
      \tag{LQS1}
   \]
   with \(C_j(G)\) and \(P(G)\) defined in
   \cref{cor:unweighted-quotient-coverage-screen}.
\end{assumption}

\begin{corollary}[Layer separation implies local cover]
   \label{cor:layer-separation-local-cover}
   In the setting of \cref{cor:residual-separator-local-cover}, if the quotient
   family is layer separating in the sense of
   \cref{asm:layer-quotient-separator}, then the finite filter-cover LP
   \((\mathsf{FC}_{\mathcal N})\) is feasible with query budget \(L\) and
   storage budget \(S\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose the LP were infeasible.  By \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual} there
   is a surplus dual system with nonpositive reduced gain on every column in the
   finite universe.  In particular, the spherical buckets, whole dense slices,
   and atom-safe prefixes do not have positive gain.  The layer separator
   therefore returns \(j\) and \(G\) satisfying \((LQS1)\).  By
   \cref{cor:unweighted-quotient-coverage-screen}, this quotient has positive
   reduced gain, contradicting the dual certificate.  Hence the LP is feasible.
\end{proof}

\Cref{asm:layer-quotient-separator} is the most concrete form of the remaining
fractional dense-overlap theorem.  It asks only for an unweighted coverage
separator on one dyadic price layer, while the final acceptance test remains the
original weighted reduced-gain inequality.  Thus \(k\)-means++, additive vector
quantization, cap nets, range-reporting violator search, or lattice/list
decoders are all proposal mechanisms for the same certificate; none is assumed
correct until it produces a quotient satisfying \((LQS1)\) and hence the exact
dual inequality.

\begin{corollary}[Quotient-packing local cover criterion]
   \label{cor:quotient-packing-local-cover}
   In the setting of \cref{cor:residual-separator-local-cover}, suppose that for
   every surplus dual price system \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying \((RS1)\),
   at least one of the following holds:
   a spherical bucket has positive reduced gain; a whole high-correlation dense
   slice has positive reduced gain; an atom-safe dense prefix has positive
   reduced gain; or there is a quotient-packing law \(\Gamma\) on \(\mathcal G\)
   satisfying \((QP3)\).  Then the finite filter-cover LP is feasible with query
   budget \(L\) and storage budget \(S\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the LP were infeasible, \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual} would give a
   surplus dual price system with nonpositive reduced gain on every column in the
   finite universe.  The first three alternatives are then impossible because the
   universe contains the spherical buckets, whole dense slices, and atom-safe
   dense prefixes.  The last alternative is impossible by
   \cref{lem:quotient-packing-reduced-gain}, since \((QP3)\) would expose a
   positive-gain quotient column.  This contradicts the assumed alternative for
   every surplus dual.
\end{proof}

Thus the remaining geometric task can be stated in an algorithmic column-generation
form: against every residual dual, construct a quotient-packing law \(\Gamma\)
with \(\mathsf A_\Gamma>\mathsf P_\Gamma\).  Expensive preprocessing may search
for this law by clustering, cap nets, additive quantization, or learned seeds,
but the retained proof object is only the verified quotient family and the
inequality \((QP3)\).

\begin{lemma}[Finite-signature filter-cover compiler]
   \label{lem:finite-signature-filter-cover}
   Let $\Omega$ be a query domain for one resident node \(P\), and let
   $\mathcal F$ be a finite priced-filter universe.  Suppose preprocessing
   supplies a finite signature set \(\Sigma\), a decoder
   \(\sigma:\Omega\to\Sigma\), active bits \(a_A(\sigma_0)\in\{0,1\}\), and
   witness supersets \(W_{\sigma_0}\subseteq P\) such that, for every
   \(q\in\Omega\) with \(\sigma(q)=\sigma_0\),
   \[
      a_A(q)=a_A(\sigma_0)\qquad(A\in\mathcal F),
      \qquad
      \{p\in P:\|p-q\|\le r\}\subseteq W_{\sigma_0}.
      \tag{FS1}
   \]
   Each filter \(A\) has update side \(U_A\), certified query price \(T_A\),
   and certified storage price \(S_A\).  Assume the finite signature LP
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \text{\rm find} & \lambda_A\ge0\\[0.4em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{A:p\in U_A}a_A(\sigma_0)\lambda_A\ge1
        \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma,\ p\in W_{\sigma_0}),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_Aa_A(\sigma_0)T_A\lambda_A\le L_{\sigma_0}
        \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_AS_A\lambda_A\le S
   \end{array}
   \tag{$\mathsf{SFC}_\Sigma$}
   \]
   is feasible, and that the atom bounds
   \[
      a_A(\sigma_0)T_A\le L_{\sigma_0}
      \qquad(A\in\mathcal F,\ \sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \qquad
      S_A\le S
      \tag{FS2}
   \]
   hold.  Put
   \[
      M_\Sigma=\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}|W_{\sigma_0}|,
      \qquad
      B\ge
      \max\left\{
         1,\log(4(M_\Sigma+1)),\log(8(|\Sigma|+1))
      \right\}.
   \]
   Then preprocessing can retain an integral multiset of filters \(\mathcal R\)
   such that every query \(q\in\Omega\) has certified active cost
   \[
      \sum_{A\in\mathcal R}a_A(q)T_A
      \le
      3B\,L_{\sigma(q)},
   \]
   total storage
   \[
      \sum_{A\in\mathcal R}S_A\le3BS,
   \]
   and routing correctness for all near pairs: if \(p\in P\) and
   \(\|p-q\|\le r\), then some retained active filter \(A\in\mathcal R\)
   satisfies \(p\in U_A\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{lem:poisson-filter-cover-materialization} with query constraint
   set \(\Sigma\) and demand set
   \[
      \mathcal N_\Sigma
      =
      \{(p,\sigma_0):\sigma_0\in\Sigma,\ p\in W_{\sigma_0}\}.
   \]
   The coverage coefficient is
   \[
      c_A(p,\sigma_0)=\mathbf 1\{p\in U_A\}a_A(\sigma_0),
   \]
   and the LP \((\mathsf{SFC}_\Sigma)\) is exactly
   \((\mathsf{FC}_{\mathcal N_\Sigma})\).  The materialization lemma gives a
   retained multiset whose signature loads and storage are bounded by the
   displayed factors and whose every finite demand is covered.

   Now fix an actual query \(q\), let \(\sigma_0=\sigma(q)\), and let
   \(p\in P\) satisfy \(\|p-q\|\le r\).  By \((FS1)\), \(p\in W_{\sigma_0}\).
   The retained finite cover contains some \(A\) with \(p\in U_A\) and
   \(a_A(\sigma_0)=1\).  Again by \((FS1)\), \(a_A(q)=1\).  Thus the query probes
   a retained child containing the near point.  The active-cost bound for the
   actual query is the signature-load bound for \(\sigma_0\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Exact-near-set finite-signature compiler]
   \label{lem:exact-near-set-filter-cover}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:finite-signature-filter-cover}, but suppose
   the signature records the exact unresolved near set.  Thus preprocessing
   supplies sets \(N_{\sigma_0}\subseteq P\) such that, for every
   \(q\in\Omega\) with \(\sigma(q)=\sigma_0\),
   \[
      a_A(q)=a_A(\sigma_0)\qquad(A\in\mathcal F),
      \qquad
      \{p\in P:\|p-q\|\le r\}=N_{\sigma_0}.
      \tag{EN1}
   \]
   Write \(\Sigma^+=\{\sigma_0\in\Sigma:N_{\sigma_0}\ne\emptyset\}\) and
   \[
