      E_{\rm can}
      =
      \E_z\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}E_{z,b},
      \qquad
      U_{\rm can}
      =
      \E_z\left[
         \Gamma_z+
         \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}U_{z,\kappa}
      \right],
      \tag{SCS2}
   \]
   where \(\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)=\{\kappa_{z,b}:b\in\mathcal B_z\}\).
   Suppose these seedwise aggregate panels are certified observable profiles:
   retaining one seed panel stores each canonical child once, pays the record
   metadata \(\Gamma_z\), and has hit/query/error profile bounded by the sums in
   \((SCS1)\)--\((SCS2)\).  If there is \(a>0\) such that
   \[
      H_{\rm can}(\sigma_0)\ge a+E_{\rm can}
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+),
      \tag{SCS3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      L_{\rm can}(\sigma_0)\le aL_{\sigma_0}
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \qquad
      U_{\rm can}\le aS,
      \tag{SCS4}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Thus child storage is charged to distinct canonical identifiers inside the
   retained panel, while occurrence multiplicity remains visible only through
   query load, hit/error accounting, and the explicit metadata term
   \(\Gamma_z\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For each seed \(z\), let
   \(\Pi_z=(H_z,L_z,U_z^{\rm prof},E_z^{\rm prof})\) be the certified
   aggregate observable profile with
   \[
      H_z=\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}H_{z,b},\qquad
      L_z=\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}L_{z,b},\qquad
      E_z^{\rm prof}=\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}E_{z,b},
   \]
   and
   \[
      U_z^{\rm prof}=
      \Gamma_z+
      \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}U_{z,\kappa}.
   \]
   Use the probabilities of the finite seed law as the weights
   \(\omega_{\Pi_z}\) in
   \cref{cor:single-panel-success-normalized-profile}, grouping identical
   aggregate profiles if desired.  The aggregate quantities in that corollary
   are precisely \(H_{\rm can},L_{\rm can},U_{\rm can},E_{\rm can}\).  Hence
   \((SCS3)\)--\((SCS4)\) imply feasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Local-error shared-canonical panel storage certificate]
   \label{cor:local-error-shared-canonical-panel-storage}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:local-error-observable-profile-cover}.  Let a finite seed
   \(z\sim\nu\) produce a finite decoded panel \(\mathcal B_z\).  Each record
   \(b\in\mathcal B_z\) has certified hit and query-load components
   \(H_{z,b}(\sigma_0)\) and \(L_{z,b}(\sigma_0)\), and a certified local error
   vector \(E_{z,b}(\sigma_0)\) with
   \(0\le E_{z,b}(\sigma_0)\le H_{z,b}(\sigma_0)\).  Records also point to
   canonical child identifiers \(\kappa_{z,b}\in\mathcal C_z\), where every
   child \(\kappa\in\mathcal C_z\) has certified storage price
   \(U_{z,\kappa}\).  Let \(\Gamma_z\ge0\) be any additional metadata price, and
   define
   \[
      H_{\rm lcan}(\sigma_0)
      =
      \E_z\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}H_{z,b}(\sigma_0),
      \qquad
      L_{\rm lcan}(\sigma_0)
      =
      \E_z\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}L_{z,b}(\sigma_0),
      \tag{LSCS1}
   \]
   \[
      E_{\rm lcan}(\sigma_0)
      =
      \E_z\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}E_{z,b}(\sigma_0),
      \qquad
      U_{\rm lcan}
      =
      \E_z\left[
         \Gamma_z+
         \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}U_{z,\kappa}
      \right].
      \tag{LSCS2}
   \]
   Suppose these seedwise aggregate panels are certified local-error profiles:
   retaining one seed panel stores each canonical child once, pays
   \(\Gamma_z\), and has hit/query/local-error profile bounded by the sums in
   \((LSCS1)\)--\((LSCS2)\).  If there is \(a>0\) such that
   \[
      H_{\rm lcan}(\sigma_0)-E_{\rm lcan}(\sigma_0)\ge a
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+),
      \tag{LSCS3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      L_{\rm lcan}(\sigma_0)\le aL_{\sigma_0}
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \qquad
      U_{\rm lcan}\le aS,
      \tag{LSCS4}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Thus the shared-DAG storage accounting can use the same local-error
   denominator as the decoded-panel cover: repeated occurrences affect query
   load and local error, while each canonical child is stored once.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For each seed \(z\), let
   \(\Pi_z=(H_z,L_z,U_z^{\rm prof},E_z^{\rm prof}(\cdot))\) be the certified
   aggregate local-error profile with
   \[
      H_z=\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}H_{z,b},\qquad
      L_z=\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}L_{z,b},\qquad
      E_z^{\rm prof}(\sigma_0)=
      \sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}E_{z,b}(\sigma_0),
   \]
   and
   \[
      U_z^{\rm prof}=
      \Gamma_z+
      \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}U_{z,\kappa}.
   \]
   Use the probabilities of the finite seed law as the weights in the aggregate
   part of \cref{cor:local-error-observable-profile-cover}.  The resulting
   aggregates are exactly
   \(H_{\rm lcan},E_{\rm lcan},L_{\rm lcan},U_{\rm lcan}\).  Conditions
   \((LSCS3)\)--\((LSCS4)\) are \((LEPC2)\)--\((LEPC3)\), so feasibility
   follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Shared-canonical panel reduced-gain separator]
   \label{cor:shared-canonical-panel-reduced-gain}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:local-error-shared-canonical-panel-storage}, but fix a finite
   seed universe \(\mathcal Z\).  A seed \(z\in\mathcal Z\) produces a decoded
   panel \(\mathcal B_z\), local-error records
   \((H_{z,b},L_{z,b},E_{z,b}(\cdot))\), canonical child identifiers
   \(\kappa_{z,b}\), child storage prices \(U_{z,\kappa}\), and metadata price
   \(\Gamma_z\).  Put
   \[
      H_z(\sigma_0)=\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}H_{z,b}(\sigma_0),
      \qquad
      L_z(\sigma_0)=\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}L_{z,b}(\sigma_0),
      \tag{SCR1}
   \]
   \[
      E_z(\sigma_0)=\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}E_{z,b}(\sigma_0),
      \qquad
      U_z^{\rm sh}=
      \Gamma_z+
      \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}U_{z,\kappa}.
      \tag{SCR2}
   \]
   Thus \(U_z^{\rm sh}\) charges each canonical child stored by the panel once,
   while repeated bucket records still contribute to \(H_z,L_z,E_z\).

   For a normalized exact-signature price system
   \((\beta,\tau,\theta)\) satisfying \((ESNO1)\), define the panel reduced gain
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \operatorname{PGain}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(z)
      &=
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}
      \beta_{\sigma_0}
      \bigl(H_z(\sigma_0)-E_z(\sigma_0)\bigr)  \\
      &\qquad
      -
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}
      \tau_{\sigma_0}L_z(\sigma_0)
      -
      \theta U_z^{\rm sh}.
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{SCR3}
   \]
   If every normalized price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\) admits a finite law
   \(\nu\) on \(\mathcal Z\) such that
   \[
      \E_{z\sim\nu}
      \operatorname{PGain}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(z)>0,
      \tag{SCR4}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.  Equivalently, because the seed
   universe is finite, every surplus dual must have one deterministic seed
   \(z\) with positive panel gain.  Conversely, if the local-error profile
   cover generated by the aggregate seed profiles is infeasible, then some
   normalized price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\) has
   \[
      \operatorname{PGain}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(z)\le0
      \qquad(z\in\mathcal Z).
      \tag{SCR5}
   \]

   In benefit-per-price form, write
   \[
      B_z=
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}
      \beta_{\sigma_0}
      \bigl(H_z(\sigma_0)-E_z(\sigma_0)\bigr),
      \qquad
      R_z=
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}L_z(\sigma_0)
      +\theta U_z^{\rm sh}.
      \tag{SCR6}
   \]
   Apart from the immediate zero-price positive-benefit case, a proposal law
   has positive expected panel gain exactly when the \(R\)-size-biased law has
   mean \(B_z/R_z\) larger than one.  Thus a bucket-net, additive-code,
   list-decoding, facility, or \(k\)-means-style build routine should be judged
   by dual benefit per shared recursive panel price, not by raw bucket mass or
   by the number of generated records.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Each seed \(z\) defines the aggregate local-error profile
   \[
      \Pi_z=(H_z,L_z,U_z^{\rm sh},E_z(\cdot)).
   \]
   By the certification hypothesis in
   \cref{cor:local-error-shared-canonical-panel-storage}, retaining this seed
   panel realizes that profile: hit, query load, and local error are the sums
   over records, while storage is the shared price \(U_z^{\rm sh}\).

   Consider the local-error profile cover
   \((\mathsf{LORPC}_\Sigma)\) over the finite profile family
   \(\{\Pi_z:z\in\mathcal Z\}\).  If it were infeasible,
   \cref{cor:local-error-observable-profile-cover} would give a normalized
   price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\) such that every profile obeys
   \[
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}
      \beta_{\sigma_0}\bigl(H_z(\sigma_0)-E_z(\sigma_0)\bigr)
      \le
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}L_z(\sigma_0)
      +\theta U_z^{\rm sh}.
   \]
   This is exactly
   \(\operatorname{PGain}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(z)\le0\) for every seed, and it
   contradicts \((SCR4)\).  Hence the local-error profile cover is feasible,
   and \cref{cor:local-error-observable-profile-cover} implies
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\).  The converse statement is the same Farkas
   certificate read directly from that corollary.

   Finally, if some seed has \(R_z=0\) and \(B_z>0\), it already has positive
   panel gain.  Otherwise, assuming \(\E_\nu R_z>0\) and no zero-price
   positive-benefit seed, size-biasing by \(R_z\) gives
   \[
      \E_{\nu^R}\frac{B_z}{R_z}
      =
      \frac{\E_\nu B_z}{\E_\nu R_z},
   \]
   so \(\E_\nu(B_z-R_z)>0\) is equivalent to
   \(\E_{\nu^R}B_z/R_z>1\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One-sided shared-panel column generation]
   \label{cor:one-sided-shared-panel-column-generation}
   Work in the finite seed universe of
   \cref{cor:shared-canonical-panel-reduced-gain}, and let
   \(\mathcal Z_\star\) be the full set of certified decoded panels that
   preprocessing is allowed to retain.  At a restricted active set
   \(E\subseteq\mathcal Z_\star\), solve the local-error profile cover
   \((\mathsf{LORPC}_\Sigma)\) using only the aggregate profiles
   \(\{\Pi_z:z\in E\}\).  Suppose that whenever this restricted cover is
   infeasible, preprocessing receives a normalized dual price system
   \((\beta,\tau,\theta)\) for the restricted problem and an oracle either
   returns an inactive seed \(z\in\mathcal Z_\star\setminus E\) with a
   verifiable one-sided certificate
   \[
      0<X\le
      \operatorname{PGain}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(z),
      \tag{OSPC1}
   \]
   or certifies the no-positive condition
   \[
      \operatorname{PGain}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(z)\le0
      \qquad(z\in\mathcal Z_\star\setminus E).
      \tag{OSPC2}
   \]
   If the full profile cover over \(\mathcal Z_\star\) is feasible, then this
   one-sided oracle reaches a feasible restricted profile cover after finitely
   many successful additions; \((OSPC2)\) cannot occur before feasibility.
   Consequently \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In particular, it is enough to prove the positive separator condition
   \[
      \max_{z\in\mathcal Z_\star}
      \operatorname{PGain}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(z)>0
      \tag{OSPC3}
   \]
   for every normalized exact-signature price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\).
   Under \((OSPC3)\), restricted column generation over decoded panels closes
   the local exact-signature cover using only verified positive panels.

   The same statement holds for randomized build-time proposals: if, at every
   infeasible restricted solve for which a positive inactive panel exists, a
   sampleable proposal law returns a seed with a verified certificate
   \((OSPC1)\) with probability at least \(p_E\), then Las Vegas repetition
   finds a valid augmentation after expected at most \(1/p_E\) proposals.
   Failed proposals and unverifiable certificates are discarded and are never
   charged to the retained index.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The restricted local-error profile cover is a finite LP.  If it is
   infeasible, the Farkas certificate supplied by
   \cref{cor:local-error-observable-profile-cover}, restricted to the active
   profile family, is a normalized price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\) and
   \[
      \operatorname{PGain}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(z)\le0
      \qquad(z\in E).
      \tag{OSPC4}
   \]
   A report satisfying \((OSPC1)\) therefore invalidates the current restricted
   dual certificate, so adding that seed strictly enlarges the restricted pool
   by a useful profile.

   If the oracle instead certifies \((OSPC2)\), then \((OSPC4)\) on active
   seeds and \((OSPC2)\) on inactive seeds combine to give
   \[
      \operatorname{PGain}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(z)\le0
      \qquad(z\in\mathcal Z_\star).
   \]
   By the converse direction of
   \cref{cor:shared-canonical-panel-reduced-gain}, equivalently Farkas'
   lemma for \((\mathsf{LORPC}_\Sigma)\), this proves infeasibility of the full
   profile cover over \(\mathcal Z_\star\).  Thus, if the full profile cover is
   feasible, a no-positive certificate cannot occur.  Since
   \(\mathcal Z_\star\) is finite, repeated successful additions terminate only
   after the restricted profile cover becomes feasible.  Feasibility of
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) then follows from
   \cref{cor:local-error-observable-profile-cover}.

   If \((OSPC3)\) holds for every normalized price system satisfying
   \((ESNO1)\), then the full profile cover cannot be infeasible, again by the
   converse Farkas certificate: an infeasible full cover would have nonpositive
   panel gain for every \(z\in\mathcal Z_\star\).  Hence the preceding
   paragraph applies.  The randomized statement is the same geometric waiting
   argument as in \cref{lem:sampled-proposal-law-separation}, with exact
   verification of \((OSPC1)\) before a seed is added.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Weighted shared-panel Renyi separator]
   \label{cor:weighted-shared-panel-renyi-separator}
   Work in the finite shared-panel universe of
   \cref{cor:shared-canonical-panel-reduced-gain}.  Assume each seed panel is a
   recursive compressed-net panel with local-error records
   \[
      b\in\mathcal B_z:
      \qquad
      (\mathcal H_{z,b},\mathcal Q_{z,b},s_{z,b},
      \varepsilon_{z,b}(\cdot),K_{z,b},\rho_{z,b},\psi_{z,b},\kappa_{z,b}),
   \]
   where \(\mathcal H_{z,b}\subseteq\Sigma^+\) is the captured signature set,
   \(\mathcal Q_{z,b}\subseteq\Sigma\) is the active query-signature set,
   \(0\le s_{z,b}\le1\), \(0\le\rho_{z,b}\le1\), and
   \(K_{z,b},\psi_{z,b}\ge0\).  Let
   \[
      U_z^{\rm sh}
      =
      \Gamma_z+
      \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}
      \psi_{z,\kappa}K_{z,\kappa}^{1+\rho_{z,\kappa}}
      \tag{WSPR0}
   \]
   be the shared canonical child-storage price.

   For normalized prices \((\beta,\tau,\theta)\), define the weighted useful
   hit, active Renyi query load, and first-moment active load of seed \(z\) by
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \mathsf H_z(\beta)
      &=
      \sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}
      \left[
         s_{z,b}\sum_{\sigma_0\in\mathcal H_{z,b}}\beta_{\sigma_0}
         -
         \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}
         \beta_{\sigma_0}\varepsilon_{z,b}(\sigma_0)
      \right],                                      \\
      \mathsf L_z^{(\rho)}(\tau)
      &=
      \sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}
      s_{z,b}\psi_{z,b}K_{z,b}^{\rho_{z,b}}
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\mathcal Q_{z,b}}\tau_{\sigma_0},                 \\
      \mathsf L_z^{(1)}(\tau)
      &=
      \sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}
      s_{z,b}\psi_{z,b}K_{z,b}
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\mathcal Q_{z,b}}\tau_{\sigma_0}.
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{WSPR1}
   \]
   If every normalized price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\) admits a finite law
   \(\nu\) on the seed universe such that
   \[
      \E_{z\sim\nu}\mathsf H_z(\beta)
      >
      \E_{z\sim\nu}\left[
         \mathsf L_z^{(\rho)}(\tau)+\theta U_z^{\rm sh}
      \right],
      \tag{WSPR2}
   \]
   then the shared-panel positive separator condition \((SPP1)\) holds.  Hence,
   under the endpoint hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint}, worst-case Euclidean
   ANN has
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   It is enough to prove the first-moment variant
   \[
      \E_{z\sim\nu}\mathsf H_z(\beta)
      >
      \E_{z\sim\nu}\left[
         \mathsf L_z^{(1)}(\tau)+\theta U_z^{\rm sh}
      \right],
      \tag{WSPR3}
   \]
   whenever every nonzero compressed child has \(K_{z,b}\ge1\).  Thus the query
   half of the weighted separator is the usual success-normalized active-load
   estimate; the genuinely superlinear part is the shared canonical storage
   moment in \(U_z^{\rm sh}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The record profiles in \cref{cor:local-error-bucket-net-ratio} have
   \[
      H_{z,b}(\sigma_0)=
      s_{z,b}\mathbf 1\{\sigma_0\in\mathcal H_{z,b}\},
      \qquad
      L_{z,b}(\sigma_0)=
      s_{z,b}\psi_{z,b}K_{z,b}^{\rho_{z,b}}
      \mathbf 1\{\sigma_0\in\mathcal Q_{z,b}\},
   \]
   with local error vector \(\varepsilon_{z,b}(\sigma_0)\).  Substituting these
   expressions into \((SCR3)\) gives exactly
   \[
      \operatorname{PGain}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(z)
      =
      \mathsf H_z(\beta)
      -
      \mathsf L_z^{(\rho)}(\tau)
      -
      \theta U_z^{\rm sh}.
      \tag{WSPR4}
   \]
   Therefore \((WSPR2)\) says that the expected panel gain under \(\nu\) is
   positive.  Since the seed universe is finite, one deterministic seed has
   positive panel gain, giving \((SPP1)\).  The endpoint conclusion is
   \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint}.

   If \(K_{z,b}=0\), the corresponding record has zero query price by
   convention.  For every nonzero child, \(K_{z,b}\ge1\) and
   \(0\le\rho_{z,b}\le1\), hence \(K_{z,b}^{\rho_{z,b}}\le K_{z,b}\).  Thus
   \(\mathsf L_z^{(\rho)}(\tau)\le\mathsf L_z^{(1)}(\tau)\) pointwise, so
   \((WSPR3)\) implies \((WSPR2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Certified-storage weighted panel separator]
   \label{cor:certified-storage-weighted-panel-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:weighted-shared-panel-renyi-separator}.  Suppose the analysis of a
   seed panel supplies a certified storage envelope
   \[
      \widehat U_z\ge U_z^{\rm sh}
      \qquad(z\in\mathcal Z_\star),
      \tag{CSWP1}
   \]
   where \(U_z^{\rm sh}\) is the actual shared canonical child-storage price
   charged by the retained panel.  If every normalized price system satisfying
   \((ESNO1)\) admits a finite seed law \(\nu\) such that
   \[
      \E_{z\sim\nu}\mathsf H_z(\beta)
      >
      \E_{z\sim\nu}\left[
         \mathsf L_z^{(\rho)}(\tau)+\theta\widehat U_z
      \right],
      \tag{CSWP2}
   \]
   then the shared-panel positive separator condition \((SPP1)\) holds.  It is
   enough, under the nonzero-child convention of
   \cref{cor:weighted-shared-panel-renyi-separator}, to prove
   \[
      \E_{z\sim\nu}\mathsf H_z(\beta)
      >
      \E_{z\sim\nu}\left[
         \mathsf L_z^{(1)}(\tau)+\theta\widehat U_z
      \right].
      \tag{CSWP3}
   \]

   Consequently, any dyadic-tail, tuple-profile, multiplicity-discounted, or
   other list-decoding storage theorem may be used as a black-box upper
   certificate only for \(\widehat U_z\).  The retained data structure still
   stores the actual canonical children and is charged by \(U_z^{\rm sh}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(\theta\ge0\), \((CSWP1)\) gives
   \[
      \mathsf L_z^{(\rho)}(\tau)+\theta U_z^{\rm sh}
      \le
      \mathsf L_z^{(\rho)}(\tau)+\theta\widehat U_z
      \qquad(z\in\mathcal Z_\star).
   \]
   Thus \((CSWP2)\) implies \((WSPR2)\), and
   \cref{cor:weighted-shared-panel-renyi-separator} gives \((SPP1)\).  The
   first-moment version follows from the same pointwise inequality
   \(K^\rho\le K\) used in that corollary.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Certified-storage weighted residual envelope]
   \label{cor:certified-storage-weighted-residual}
   Work in the finite universe and with the certified storage envelopes of
   \cref{cor:certified-storage-weighted-panel-separator}.  Suppose the
   certified-storage weighted separator fails on this universe: there is a
   normalized price system \((\beta,\tau,\theta)\) satisfying \((ESNO1)\) for
   which no finite seed law satisfies \((CSWP2)\).  Then every seed obeys
   \[
      \mathsf H_z(\beta)
      \le
      \mathsf L_z^{(\rho)}(\tau)+\theta\widehat U_z
      \qquad(z\in\mathcal Z_\star),
      \tag{CSWR1}
   \]
   and, equivalently, every finite law \(\nu\) on \(\mathcal Z_\star\) obeys
   \[
      \E_{z\sim\nu}\mathsf H_z(\beta)
      \le
      \E_{z\sim\nu}\left[
         \mathsf L_z^{(\rho)}(\tau)+\theta\widehat U_z
      \right].
      \tag{CSWR2}
   \]
   In the first-moment query-load relaxation, failure of \((CSWP3)\) is exactly
   the residual envelope
   \[
      \E_{z\sim\nu}\mathsf H_z(\beta)
      \le
      \E_{z\sim\nu}\left[
         \mathsf L_z^{(1)}(\tau)+\theta\widehat U_z
      \right]
      \qquad(\nu\text{ finite}).
      \tag{CSWR3}
   \]

   Thus the remaining geometric/list-decoding theorem can be stated without LP
   variables or column generation: every normalized exact-signature dual must
   admit one proposed panel law violating the weighted residual envelope
   \((CSWR2)\), or the stronger first-moment envelope \((CSWR3)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If some deterministic seed violated \((CSWR1)\), then the point mass at that
   seed would satisfy \((CSWP2)\), contradicting the assumed failure.  Hence
   every seed satisfies \((CSWR1)\), and averaging gives \((CSWR2)\).
   Conversely, \((CSWR2)\) applied to point masses gives \((CSWR1)\), so the
   deterministic and averaged envelopes are equivalent.  The first-moment form
   is the same argument with \(\mathsf L^{(1)}\) in place of
   \(\mathsf L^{(\rho)}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Query-storage split for weighted residuals]
   \label{cor:certified-storage-residual-split}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:certified-storage-weighted-residual}.  For a finite seed law
   \(\nu\), write
   \[
      A_\nu=\E_{z\sim\nu}\mathsf H_z(\beta),
      \qquad
      Q_\nu^{(\rho)}=\E_{z\sim\nu}\mathsf L_z^{(\rho)}(\tau),
      \qquad
      W_\nu=\theta\,\E_{z\sim\nu}\widehat U_z .
      \tag{CSRS1}
   \]
   If the certified-storage separator \((CSWP2)\) fails, then every finite seed
   law satisfies
   \[
      A_\nu\le Q_\nu^{(\rho)}+W_\nu .
      \tag{CSRS2}
   \]
   Hence, for every \(0<\varepsilon<1\) and every law with \(A_\nu>0\), either
   \[
      Q_\nu^{(\rho)}\ge (1-\varepsilon)A_\nu
      \tag{CSRS3}
   \]
   or
   \[
      W_\nu\ge \varepsilon A_\nu .
      \tag{CSRS4}
   \]
   Conversely, if for every normalized dual price system satisfying
   \((ESNO1)\) there is a finite seed law \(\nu\) and constants \(q,u\ge0\) with
   \(q+u<1\) such that
   \[
      Q_\nu^{(\rho)}\le qA_\nu,
      \qquad
      W_\nu\le uA_\nu,
      \qquad
      A_\nu>0,
      \tag{CSRS5}
   \]
   then the certified-storage separator \((CSWP2)\) holds.

   The same statements hold for the first-moment relaxation after replacing
   \(Q_\nu^{(\rho)}\) by
   \(Q_\nu^{(1)}=\E_{z\sim\nu}\mathsf L_z^{(1)}(\tau)\).  Thus a proposed
   decoded panel law separates precisely when useful priced hit mass beats the
   sum of its active-load ratio and its certified shared-storage ratio; a
   residual counterexample must put comparable mass in one of those two
   obstructions.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Inequality \((CSRS2)\) is exactly \((CSWR2)\) with the notation
   \((CSRS1)\).  If both \((CSRS3)\) and \((CSRS4)\) failed, then
   \(Q_\nu^{(\rho)}+W_\nu<A_\nu\), contradicting \((CSRS2)\).  Conversely,
   \((CSRS5)\) gives
   \[
      Q_\nu^{(\rho)}+W_\nu\le(q+u)A_\nu<A_\nu,
   \]
   which is precisely \((CSWP2)\) for that dual price system.  The first-moment
   version is identical, using \((CSWR3)\) and \((CSWP3)\).
\end{proof}

This split is the fractional-overlap replacement for hard branching counts.
A build-time proposal such as additive quantization, list/lattice decoding,
facility search, or \(k\)-means-style seeding is useful only after it is scored
by the two dimensionless quantities \(Q_\nu/A_\nu\) and \(W_\nu/A_\nu\).  If the
active-load ratio is bounded away from one, the remaining theorem is purely a
certified shared-storage theorem.  If the active-load ratio is already near one,
then the dual residual says that the proposal is mostly re-enumerating active
query mass rather than producing a cost-effective dense filter.

\begin{corollary}[Dual-priced witness-storage separator]
   \label{cor:dual-priced-witness-storage-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:certified-storage-weighted-panel-separator}.  Fix a normalized
   dual price system \((\beta,\tau,\theta)\) satisfying \((ESNO1)\), a finite
   seed law \(\nu\), and write \(A_\nu,Q_\nu^{(\rho)}\) as in \((CSRS1)\).
   Suppose the certified storage envelope for every seed has a witness decomposition
   \[
      \widehat U_z
      \le
      \Gamma_z+\sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal K_z}u_{z,\kappa},
      \qquad
      u_{z,\kappa}\ge0,
      \tag{DPW1}
   \]
   where \(\Gamma_z\) is nonrecursive metadata and each \(u_{z,\kappa}\) is the
   certified storage price of one distinct canonical child.  Let \(\Omega\) be
   a finite witness universe.  For each pair \((z,\kappa)\), let
   \(\pi_{z,\kappa}\) be a probability law on \(\Omega\).  Assume there are
   certified witness-congestion envelopes \(J(\omega)\ge0\) satisfying
   \[
      \theta\,
      \E_{z\sim\nu}
      \sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal K_z}
      u_{z,\kappa}\pi_{z,\kappa}(\omega)
      \le
      J(\omega)
      \qquad(\omega\in\Omega).
      \tag{DPW2}
   \]
   If \(A_\nu>0\) and, for some \(q,u\ge0\) with \(q+u<1\),
   \[
      Q_\nu^{(\rho)}\le qA_\nu,
      \tag{DPW3}
   \]
   \[
      \theta\,\E_{z\sim\nu}\Gamma_z
      +
      \sum_{\omega\in\Omega}J(\omega)
      \le
      uA_\nu,
      \tag{DPW4}
   \]
   then this dual price system has a positive certified-storage separator
   \((CSWP2)\).  The same conclusion holds in the first-moment relaxation after
   replacing \(Q_\nu^{(\rho)}\) by \(Q_\nu^{(1)}\).

   Consequently, dyadic tails, tuple-profile tails, multiplicity-discounted
   witnesses, LP range reports, or list-decoding witnesses may all be analyzed
   through the same dual-priced storage interface: every distinct child pays
   its recursive storage price once, distributes that price over certified
   witnesses, and the geometric theorem only has to bound the resulting
   witness congestion relative to useful priced hit.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since each \(\pi_{z,\kappa}\) is a probability law,
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal K_z}u_{z,\kappa}
      =
      \sum_{\omega\in\Omega}
      \sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal K_z}
      u_{z,\kappa}\pi_{z,\kappa}(\omega).
   \]
   Taking expectation over \(z\), multiplying by \(\theta\), and using
   \((DPW2)\) gives
   \[
      \theta\E_{z\sim\nu}\widehat U_z
      \le
      \theta\E_{z\sim\nu}\Gamma_z
      +
      \sum_{\omega\in\Omega}J(\omega)
      \le
      uA_\nu .
   \]
   Together with \((DPW3)\), this gives
   \[
      Q_\nu^{(\rho)}+\theta\E_{z\sim\nu}\widehat U_z
      \le(q+u)A_\nu<A_\nu,
   \]
   which is exactly \((CSWP2)\) for the seed law \(\nu\).  The first-moment
   version is identical.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Distinct-canonical bucket-net certificate]
   \label{cor:distinct-canonical-bucket-net}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:bucket-net-ratio-form}.  In addition to the
   record data of \cref{cor:recursive-compressed-net-panel}, suppose every
   record \(b\in\mathcal B_z\) points to a canonical child identifier
   \(\kappa_{z,b}\).  The child identifier \(\kappa\) has integer size
   \(K_{z,\kappa}\), exponent \(0\le\rho_{z,\kappa}\le1\), and price factor
   \(\psi_{z,\kappa}\), and record \(b\) uses the corresponding values
   \(K_{z,b}=K_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\),
   \(\rho_{z,b}=\rho_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\), and
   \(\psi_{z,b}=\psi_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\).  Let \(\Gamma_z\ge0\) bound all
   nonrecursive panel metadata and occurrence-pointer storage, and put
   \[
      U_{\rm can}
      =
      \E_z\left[
         \Gamma_z+
         \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}
         \psi_{z,\kappa}K_{z,\kappa}^{1+\rho_{z,\kappa}}
      \right].
      \tag{DCB1}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise let \(a_*\) be
   as in \((BNR1)\).  Suppose \(a_*>0\), the active first moments satisfy
   \[
      \E_z\sum_{b:\sigma_0\in\mathcal Q_{z,b}}
      s_{z,b}\psi_{z,b}K_{z,b}
      \le
      a_*L_{\sigma_0}
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \tag{DCB2}
   \]
   and the distinct-canonical storage satisfies
   \[
      U_{\rm can}\le a_*S .
      \tag{DCB3}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In particular, the storage theorem needed for a bucket-net/list-decoding
   implementation is not the occurrence moment
   \(\E_z\sum_b\psi_{z,b}K_{z,b}^{1+\rho_{z,b}}\).  It is the distinct
   canonical child bound \((DCB1)\), plus the explicit metadata budget
   \(\E_z\Gamma_z\).  Multiple decoded records may point to the same recursive
   child at no additional child-index storage cost.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), use the zero cover.  Otherwise \(a_*>0\).
   For each record, \(K_{z,b}^{\rho_{z,b}}\le K_{z,b}\), with zero-price
   records interpreted as in
   \cref{cor:first-moment-active-load-query}.  Hence \((DCB2)\) implies the
   query inequality \(L_{\rm net}(\sigma_0)\le a_*L_{\sigma_0}\).  The hit
   inequality is the definition of \(a_*\), and \((DCB3)\) is the shared
   storage inequality \((SCS4)\) for the aggregate panel profile whose record
   hit/query/error components are \((RCN1)\)--\((RCN2)\) and whose child storage
   is charged by \((DCB1)\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:shared-canonical-panel-storage} gives feasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Local-error distinct-canonical bucket-net certificate]
   \label{cor:local-error-distinct-canonical-bucket-net}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:local-error-bucket-net-ratio}.  In addition
   to the record data there, suppose every record \(b\in\mathcal B_z\) points to
   a canonical child identifier \(\kappa_{z,b}\).  The child identifier
   \(\kappa\) has integer size \(K_{z,\kappa}\), exponent
   \(0\le\rho_{z,\kappa}\le1\), and price factor \(\psi_{z,\kappa}\), and
   record \(b\) uses the corresponding values
   \(K_{z,b}=K_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\),
   \(\rho_{z,b}=\rho_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\), and
   \(\psi_{z,b}=\psi_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\).  Let \(\Gamma_z\ge0\) bound all
   nonrecursive panel metadata and occurrence-pointer storage, and put
   \[
      U_{\rm lcan}
      =
      \E_z\left[
         \Gamma_z+
         \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}
         \psi_{z,\kappa}K_{z,\kappa}^{1+\rho_{z,\kappa}}
      \right].
      \tag{LDCB1}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise let
   \(a_{\rm loc}\) be as in \((LBNR2)\).  Suppose \(a_{\rm loc}>0\), the active
   first moments satisfy
   \[
      \E_z\sum_{b:\sigma_0\in\mathcal Q_{z,b}}
      s_{z,b}\psi_{z,b}K_{z,b}
      \le
      a_{\rm loc}L_{\sigma_0}
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \tag{LDCB2}
   \]
   and the distinct-canonical storage satisfies
   \[
      U_{\rm lcan}\le a_{\rm loc}S .
      \tag{LDCB3}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   This is the local-error storage target for decoded bucket nets: the useful
   hit denominator is \(a_{\rm loc}\), but recursive child storage is still paid
   only once per distinct canonical child.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), use the zero cover.  Otherwise \(a_{\rm loc}>0\).
   For each record, \(K_{z,b}^{\rho_{z,b}}\le K_{z,b}\), with zero-price
   records interpreted as in
   \cref{cor:local-error-first-moment-active-load}.  Hence \((LDCB2)\) implies
   the query inequality \(L_{\rm net}(\sigma_0)\le a_{\rm loc}L_{\sigma_0}\).
   The useful-hit inequality is the definition of \(a_{\rm loc}\).  The storage
   inequality \((LDCB3)\) is \((LSCS4)\) for the aggregate local-error panel
   profile whose record hit/query/local-error components are those of
   \cref{cor:local-error-bucket-net-ratio} and whose child storage is charged by
   \((LDCB1)\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:local-error-shared-canonical-panel-storage} gives feasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite-signature compressed-bucket bridge]
   \label{cor:finite-signature-compressed-bucket-bridge}
   Work at one resident node in the exact-signature setting of
   \cref{lem:exact-near-set-filter-cover}.  Let a finite seed \(z\sim\nu\)
   produce decoded compressed-bucket records \(\mathcal B_z\), with active
   signature sets \(\mathcal Q_{z,b}\), captured signature sets
   \(\mathcal H_{z,b}\), hit weights \(s_{z,b}\), local errors
   \(\varepsilon_{z,b}(\sigma_0)\), and canonical child identifiers
   \(\kappa_{z,b}\) as in
   \cref{cor:local-error-distinct-canonical-bucket-net}.  If
   \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the node is already feasible.  Otherwise define the
   useful hit denominator
   \[
      a_{\rm cb}
      =
      \inf_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}
      \E_z\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}
      \left(
         s_{z,b}\mathbf 1\{\sigma_0\in\mathcal H_{z,b}\}
         -
         \varepsilon_{z,b}(\sigma_0)
      \right),
      \tag{FCB1}
   \]
   and suppose \(a_{\rm cb}>0\).  Suppose the success-normalized active load
   satisfies
   \[
      \E_z\sum_{b:\sigma_0\in\mathcal Q_{z,b}}
      s_{z,b}\psi_{z,b}K_{z,b}
      \le
      a_{\rm cb}L_{\sigma_0}
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \tag{FCB2}
   \]
   while the shared canonical child storage satisfies
   \[
      \E_z\left[
         \Gamma_z+
         \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}
         \psi_{z,\kappa}K_{z,\kappa}^{1+\rho_{z,\kappa}}
      \right]
      \le
      a_{\rm cb}S .
      \tag{FCB3}
   \]
   Then the node has a feasible exact-signature finite-filter cover
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) with query budgets \(L_{\sigma_0}\) and storage
   budget \(S\).

   Thus the compressed-bucket step is not a second, hard-branching recursion
   rule.  It is a finite fractional filter-cover certificate: the quantity
   \(a_{\rm cb}\) is the near-witness coverage denominator, \((FCB2)\) is the
   query-local overlap bound after division by this denominator, and \((FCB3)\)
   charges each canonical recursive child once.  False active buckets are
   included in the left side of \((FCB2)\), and repeated decoded occurrences
   only affect query load and metadata.

   Consequently, suppose that after bounded-diameter localization every
   resident node \(P\), \(|P|=N\), admits such a finite compressed-bucket
   certificate, with
   \[
      L_{\sigma_0}\le N^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S\le N^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      \rho_c=\frac1{2c^2-1},
      \tag{FCB4}
   \]
   finite-signature entropy
   \(\log(2+|\Sigma|+|\Sigma^+|)\le\log^{O_c(1)}n\), decoder time
   \(d\,N^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n\), the atom bounds needed by
   \cref{lem:exact-near-set-filter-cover}, and strictly smaller certified
   radius for every nonterminal child.  If the child price factors
   \(\psi_{z,\kappa}K_{z,\kappa}^{\rho_{z,\kappa}}\) and
   \(\psi_{z,\kappa}K_{z,\kappa}^{1+\rho_{z,\kappa}}\) are the full certified
   descendant query and storage prices, then the global ANN bounds are
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the zero exact-signature cover is feasible, so
   assume \(\Sigma^+\ne\emptyset\).  The denominator \(a_{\rm cb}\) is exactly
   \(a_{\rm loc}\) from \((LBNR2)\) after expanding the record hit and local
   error profiles.  Conditions \((FCB2)\) and \((FCB3)\) are precisely
   \((LDCB2)\) and \((LDCB3)\), with \(a_{\rm loc}=a_{\rm cb}\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:local-error-distinct-canonical-bucket-net} gives feasibility of
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\).

   For the endpoint statement, apply the exact-near-set version of
   \cref{prop:fractional-filter-cover-polylog} with the budgets in \((FCB4)\).
   The preceding feasibility statement supplies the required local cover at
   each node, and the price-factor hypothesis says that a retained bucket
   column is charged by the full descendant cost.  Therefore overlapping dense
   or spherical bucket columns are paid by the local LP load constraints rather
   than multiplied along a hard recursion tree.  The global coordinate array is
   stored once, as in \cref{prop:fractional-filter-cover-polylog}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Dyadic tail certificate for distinct child storage]
   \label{lem:dyadic-tail-distinct-child-storage}
   Work with one seed \(z\) in the setting of
   \cref{cor:distinct-canonical-bucket-net}, and write the certified storage
   price of a distinct canonical child as
   \[
      u_{z,\kappa}=
      \psi_{z,\kappa}K_{z,\kappa}^{1+\rho_{z,\kappa}} .
   \]
   For \(i\in\mathbb Z\), let
   \[
      C_z(i)=
      \left|\{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z):
      2^i\le u_{z,\kappa}<2^{i+1}\}\right|.
      \tag{DTS1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}u_{z,\kappa}
      \le
      2\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}2^iC_z(i),
      \tag{DTS2}
   \]
   with only finitely many nonzero terms.  Equivalently, for the tail counts
   \[
      N_z(t)=
      \left|\{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z):u_{z,\kappa}\ge t\}\right|,
      \tag{DTS3}
   \]
   one has the exact layer-cake identity
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}u_{z,\kappa}
      =
      \int_0^\infty N_z(t)\,dt .
      \tag{DTS4}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The dyadic classes in \((DTS1)\) partition the positive-price children.  A
   child in class \(i\) has price less than \(2^{i+1}\), so summing over classes
   gives \((DTS2)\).  Zero-price children contribute neither side.

   For the layer-cake form, use
   \[
      u_{z,\kappa}=\int_0^\infty \mathbf 1\{t\le u_{z,\kappa}\}\,dt
   \]
   for each finite child price and interchange the finite sum and the integral.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Layer-cake distinct-storage bucket-net certificate]
   \label{cor:layer-cake-distinct-storage-bucket-net}
   Work in either of the following two settings:
   the scalar distinct-storage setting of
   \cref{cor:distinct-canonical-bucket-net}, with \(a=a_*\) and active
   first-moment condition \((DCB2)\), or the local-error setting of
   \cref{cor:local-error-distinct-canonical-bucket-net}, with
   \(a=a_{\rm loc}\) and active first-moment condition \((LDCB2)\).  For each
   seed \(z\), define \(u_{z,\kappa}\) and \(N_z(t)\) as in
   \cref{lem:dyadic-tail-distinct-child-storage}.  If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\),
   the cover is feasible.  Otherwise suppose \(a>0\), the corresponding active
   first-moment condition holds, and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \E_z\int_0^\infty N_z(t)\,dt
      \le
      aS .
      \tag{LCDS1}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Thus the dyadic large-child formulation is only a convenient discretization.
   The exact storage theorem is an integrated tail bound for the number of
   distinct canonical children whose recursive price exceeds \(t\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By the layer-cake identity \((DTS4)\),
   \[
      \E_z\int_0^\infty N_z(t)\,dt
      =
      \E_z\sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}u_{z,\kappa}.
   \]
   Hence \((LCDS1)\) is exactly the storage condition \((DCB3)\) in the scalar
   setting and \((LDCB3)\) in the local-error setting.  The conclusion follows
   from \cref{cor:distinct-canonical-bucket-net} and
   \cref{cor:local-error-distinct-canonical-bucket-net}, respectively.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dyadic distinct-storage bucket-net certificate]
   \label{cor:dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:distinct-canonical-bucket-net}.  For each
   seed \(z\), define \(u_{z,\kappa}\) and \(C_z(i)\) as in
   \cref{lem:dyadic-tail-distinct-child-storage}.  If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\),
   the cover is feasible.  Otherwise let \(a_*\) be as in \((BNR1)\).  Suppose
   \(a_*>0\), the active first moments satisfy \((DCB2)\), and the dyadic
   distinct-child tail bound
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      2\E_z\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}2^iC_z(i)
      \le
      a_*S
      \tag{DDS1}
   \]
   holds.  Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Thus the remaining storage geometry may be stated as a large-child counting
   theorem: at each recursive price scale \(2^i\), bound the number of distinct
   canonical bucket nets with price in that dyadic class.  This is strictly the
   shared-DAG quantity; repeated decoded occurrences of the same canonical net
   do not increase \(C_z(i)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{lem:dyadic-tail-distinct-child-storage}, the left side of
   \((DCB1)\) is at most the left side of \((DDS1)\).  Hence \((DDS1)\) implies
   \((DCB3)\), and \cref{cor:distinct-canonical-bucket-net} applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Local-error dyadic distinct-storage bucket-net certificate]
   \label{cor:local-error-dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:local-error-distinct-canonical-bucket-net}.  For each seed \(z\),
   define \(u_{z,\kappa}\) and \(C_z(i)\) as in
   \cref{lem:dyadic-tail-distinct-child-storage}.  If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\),
   the cover is feasible.  Otherwise let \(a_{\rm loc}\) be as in \((LBNR2)\).
   Suppose \(a_{\rm loc}>0\), the active first moments satisfy \((LDCB2)\), and
   the dyadic distinct-child tail bound
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      2\E_z\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}2^iC_z(i)
      \le
      a_{\rm loc}S
      \tag{LDDS1}
   \]
   holds.  Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Thus local-error accounting and shared-DAG storage commute: local errors
   improve the hit denominator, while dyadic large-child counting remains the
   same storage theorem.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{lem:dyadic-tail-distinct-child-storage}, the left side of
   \((LDCB1)\) is at most the left side of \((LDDS1)\).  Hence \((LDDS1)\)
   implies \((LDCB3)\), and
   \cref{cor:local-error-distinct-canonical-bucket-net} applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Tuple witnesses for distinct child tails]
   \label{lem:tuple-witness-distinct-child-tail}
   Work at one resident node \(P\), fix a separation scale \(\delta>0\), and
   let \(\mathcal T_k(P,\delta)\) be as in
   \cref{lem:packing-list-tuple-moment}.  In the setting of
   \cref{lem:dyadic-tail-distinct-child-storage}, suppose that for every
   dyadic price class \(i\) we choose an integer \(k_i\ge1\) and a number
   \(R_i>0\).  Each distinct canonical child \(\kappa\) in class \(i\) has an
   associated separated net \(A_{z,\kappa}\subseteq P\), and satisfies the
   witness lower bound
   \[
      \left|
      \{(x_1,\ldots,x_{k_i})\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta):
      x_j\in A_{z,\kappa}\ \forall j\}
      \right|
      \ge R_i .
      \tag{TWT1}
   \]
   For a tuple \(\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)\), let
   \[
      M_z(i,\mathbf x)
      =
      \left|
      \{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z):
      2^i\le u_{z,\kappa}<2^{i+1},
      \ x_j\in A_{z,\kappa}\ \forall j\}
      \right|.
      \tag{TWT2}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      C_z(i)
      \le
      \frac1{R_i}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)}
      M_z(i,\mathbf x).
      \tag{TWT3}
   \]

   In particular, if every child in class \(i\) has
   \(|A_{z,\kappa}|\ge K_i\), then one may take \(R_i=K_i^{k_i}\), since
   repetitions are allowed in \(\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Sum the witness lower bound \((TWT1)\) over all distinct canonical children
   in the dyadic class \(i\):
   \[
      R_iC_z(i)
      \le
      \sum_{\substack{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z):\\
                      2^i\le u_{z,\kappa}<2^{i+1}}}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)}
      \mathbf 1\{x_j\in A_{z,\kappa}\ \forall j\}.
   \]
   Interchanging the two finite sums gives
   \(\sum_{\mathbf x}M_z(i,\mathbf x)\), and division by \(R_i\) proves
   \((TWT3)\).  If \(|A_{z,\kappa}|\ge K_i\), then every ordered \(k_i\)-tuple
   from \(A_{z,\kappa}\), with repetitions, belongs to
   \(\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)\) because the distinct entries of
   \(A_{z,\kappa}\) are \(\delta\)-separated.  Hence there are at least
   \(K_i^{k_i}\) witnesses.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Multiplicity-discounted tuple witnesses]
   \label{lem:multiplicity-discounted-tuple-witness}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{lem:tuple-witness-distinct-child-tail}, and suppose the decoded panel
   contains occurrence records \(b\in\mathcal B_z\) pointing to the same
   canonical child identifiers \(\kappa_{z,b}\).  For a distinct child
   \(\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)\), let
   \[
      m_z(\kappa)
      =
      \left|\{b\in\mathcal B_z:\kappa_{z,b}=\kappa\}\right|
      \tag{MDT0}
   \]
   be its occurrence multiplicity.  For
   \(\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)\), define the
   multiplicity-discounted tuple incidence
   \[
      \widetilde M_z(i,\mathbf x)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{b\in\mathcal B_z:\\
         2^i\le u_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}<2^{i+1}\\
         x_j\in A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\ \forall j}}
      \frac1{m_z(\kappa_{z,b})}.
      \tag{MDT1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      C_z(i)
      \le
      \frac1{R_i}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)}
      \widetilde M_z(i,\mathbf x).
      \tag{MDT2}
   \]

   In particular, if every distinct child \(\kappa\) in class \(i\) has
   occurrence multiplicity at least \(M_i\ge1\), and
   \[
      M_z^{\rm occ}(i,\mathbf x)
      =
      \left|
      \{b\in\mathcal B_z:
      2^i\le u_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}<2^{i+1},\
      x_j\in A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\ \forall j\}
      \right|,
      \tag{MDT3}
   \]
   then
   \[
      C_z(i)
      \le
      \frac1{R_iM_i}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)}
      M_z^{\rm occ}(i,\mathbf x).
      \tag{MDT4}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed tuple \(\mathbf x\), group the sum in \((MDT1)\) by canonical
   child identifier.  Each child \(\kappa\) contributes either zero, if not all
   entries of \(\mathbf x\) lie in \(A_{z,\kappa}\), or
   \(m_z(\kappa)\cdot m_z(\kappa)^{-1}=1\), if
   all entries of \(\mathbf x\) lie in \(A_{z,\kappa}\).  Hence
   \[
      \widetilde M_z(i,\mathbf x)
      =
      M_z(i,\mathbf x),
   \]
   where \(M_z(i,\mathbf x)\) is the distinct-child tuple incidence in
   \((TWT2)\).  Therefore \((MDT2)\) is exactly \((TWT3)\).

   If every child in the dyadic class has multiplicity at least \(M_i\), then
   each occurrence term satisfies
   \(m_z(\kappa_{z,b})^{-1}\le M_i^{-1}\).  Thus
   \(\widetilde M_z(i,\mathbf x)\le M_i^{-1}M_z^{\rm occ}(i,\mathbf x)\), and
   substituting this into \((MDT2)\) gives \((MDT4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Integrated tuple-tail distinct-storage certificate]
   \label{cor:integrated-tuple-tail-distinct-storage}
   Work in either of the two settings of
   \cref{cor:layer-cake-distinct-storage-bucket-net}, with the corresponding
   value of \(a\).  Fix a separation scale \(\delta>0\).  For every \(t>0\),
   suppose that an integer \(k(t)\ge1\), a number \(R(t)>0\), and certified
   measurable envelopes \(J_t(\mathbf x)\ge0\) are chosen so that every distinct
   child \(\kappa\) with \(u_{z,\kappa}\ge t\) has an associated separated net
   \(A_{z,\kappa}\subseteq P\) satisfying
   \[
      \left|
      \{(x_1,\ldots,x_{k(t)})\in\mathcal T_{k(t)}(P,\delta):
      x_j\in A_{z,\kappa}\ \forall j\}
      \right|
      \ge R(t),
      \tag{ITD1}
   \]
   and, with
   \[
      M_z(t,\mathbf x)
      =
      \left|
      \{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z):
      u_{z,\kappa}\ge t,\
      x_j\in A_{z,\kappa}\ \forall j\}
      \right|,
      \tag{ITD2}
   \]
   one has
   \[
      \E_zM_z(t,\mathbf x)\le J_t(\mathbf x).
      \tag{ITD3}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise suppose \(a>0\),
   the corresponding active first-moment condition holds, and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \int_0^\infty
      \frac1{R(t)}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k(t)}(P,\delta)}
      J_t(\mathbf x)\,dt
      \le
      aS .
      \tag{ITD4}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Equivalently, if for each \(t\) the tuple set is partitioned into profile
   classes \(\Pi_t\), every tuple in profile \(\pi\in\Pi_t\) has
   \(J_t(\mathbf x)\le e^{-I_{t,\pi}}\), and the profile has size
   \(N_{t,\pi}\), it is enough to replace the inner tuple sum in \((ITD4)\) by
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi_t}N_{t,\pi}e^{-I_{t,\pi}} .
      \tag{ITD5}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix \(t>0\).  Summing the witness bound \((ITD1)\) over all children with
   \(u_{z,\kappa}\ge t\) and interchanging finite sums gives
   \[
      N_z(t)
      \le
      \frac1{R(t)}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k(t)}(P,\delta)}
      M_z(t,\mathbf x).
      \tag{ITD6}
   \]
   Taking expectation and using \((ITD3)\),
   \[
      \E_zN_z(t)
      \le
      \frac1{R(t)}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k(t)}(P,\delta)}
      J_t(\mathbf x).
   \]
   Integrating this inequality over \(t\) and applying \((ITD4)\) gives
   \((LCDS1)\).  Therefore
   \cref{cor:layer-cake-distinct-storage-bucket-net} proves feasibility.  The
   profile form is just summation of the pointwise envelope over each profile
   class.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Price-weighted witness-packing storage certificate]
   \label{cor:price-weighted-witness-packing-storage}
   Work in either of the two settings of
   \cref{cor:layer-cake-distinct-storage-bucket-net}, with the corresponding
   value of \(a\).  Let \(\Omega\) be a finite witness universe.  For every seed
   \(z\) and every distinct canonical child
   \(\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)\), suppose preprocessing certifies a
   probability law \(\pi_{z,\kappa}\) on \(\Omega\).  Let \(u_{z,\kappa}\) be the
   child storage price from \((DTS4)\).  Suppose there are certified envelopes
   \(J(\omega)\ge0\) such that
   \[
      \E_z
      \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}
      u_{z,\kappa}\pi_{z,\kappa}(\omega)
      \le
      J(\omega)
      \qquad(\omega\in\Omega).
      \tag{PWP1}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise suppose \(a>0\),
   the corresponding active first-moment condition holds, and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}J(\omega)\le aS .
      \tag{PWP2}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In the tuple specialization, \(\Omega\) may be a finite union of separated
   tuple sets \(\mathcal T_k(P,\delta)\), and \(\pi_{z,\kappa}\) is supported on
   tuple witnesses lying inside the separated net \(A_{z,\kappa}\).  Then the
   remaining storage theorem is a price-weighted tuple-congestion bound: every
   distinct child pays its full recursive storage price once, and the geometric
   proof only has to show that no tuple or tuple profile receives too much total
   paid child price.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For each seed \(z\),
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}u_{z,\kappa}
      &=
      \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}
      u_{z,\kappa}
      \sum_{\omega\in\Omega}\pi_{z,\kappa}(\omega) \\
      &=
      \sum_{\omega\in\Omega}
      \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}
      u_{z,\kappa}\pi_{z,\kappa}(\omega).
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   Taking expectation over \(z\) and applying \((PWP1)\) gives
   \[
      \E_z\sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}u_{z,\kappa}
      \le
      \sum_{\omega\in\Omega}J(\omega).
   \]
   Therefore \((PWP2)\) implies the layer-cake storage condition \((LCDS1)\), and
   \cref{cor:layer-cake-distinct-storage-bucket-net} gives feasibility.  The
   tuple specialization is the same argument with a witness universe whose atoms
   are certified tuples.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Uniform tuple witness-packing certificate]
   \label{cor:uniform-tuple-witness-packing-storage}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:price-weighted-witness-packing-storage}.  Fix a separation scale
   \(\delta>0\) and a finite set of tuple orders \(\mathcal K\subset\mathbb N\).
   For every distinct child \(\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)\), suppose there
   is a certified separated net \(A_{z,\kappa}\subseteq P\) and a chosen order
   \(k_{z,\kappa}\in\mathcal K\) such that
   \[
      |A_{z,\kappa}|\ge1,
      \qquad
      A_{z,\kappa}\text{ is }\delta\text{-separated}.
      \tag{UTW0}
   \]
   For \(k\in\mathcal K\) and
   \(\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_k(P,\delta)\), define the price-weighted tuple
   congestion
   \[
      W_z(k,\mathbf x)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z):\\
         k_{z,\kappa}=k,\ x_j\in A_{z,\kappa}\ \forall j}}
      \frac{u_{z,\kappa}}{|A_{z,\kappa}|^k}.
      \tag{UTW1}
   \]
   Suppose there are certified envelopes \(J_k(\mathbf x)\ge0\) with
   \[
      \E_z W_z(k,\mathbf x)\le J_k(\mathbf x)
      \qquad(k\in\mathcal K,\ \mathbf x\in\mathcal T_k(P,\delta)).
      \tag{UTW2}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise suppose \(a>0\),
   the corresponding active first-moment condition holds, and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \sum_{k\in\mathcal K}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_k(P,\delta)}J_k(\mathbf x)
      \le aS .
      \tag{UTW3}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In particular, if
   \(u_{z,\kappa}=\psi_{z,\kappa}|A_{z,\kappa}|^{1+\rho_{z,\kappa}}\) with
   \(0\le\rho_{z,\kappa}\le1\) and one takes \(k_{z,\kappa}=2\), then each
   tuple-incidence is weighted by
   \[
      \psi_{z,\kappa}|A_{z,\kappa}|^{\rho_{z,\kappa}-1}\le\psi_{z,\kappa}.
      \tag{UTW4}
   \]
   Thus, up to the child price factor \(\psi\), the storage theorem can be
   attacked as an ordinary pair-congestion bound for distinct canonical nets.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let
   \[
      \Omega=\bigcup_{k\in\mathcal K}\{k\}\times\mathcal T_k(P,\delta).
   \]
   For a child \(\kappa\), define \(\pi_{z,\kappa}\) to be the uniform law on
   ordered \(k_{z,\kappa}\)-tuples from \(A_{z,\kappa}\), embedded in the
   corresponding component of \(\Omega\).  Because \(A_{z,\kappa}\) is
   \(\delta\)-separated and repetitions are allowed in
   \(\mathcal T_k(P,\delta)\), this is a probability law on \(\Omega\).  For an
   atom \((k,\mathbf x)\),
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa}u_{z,\kappa}\pi_{z,\kappa}(k,\mathbf x)
      =
      W_z(k,\mathbf x).
   \]
   Hence \((UTW2)\) is exactly \((PWP1)\) for the witness universe \(\Omega\), and
   \((UTW3)\) is \((PWP2)\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:price-weighted-witness-packing-storage} proves feasibility.

   The final statement is the identity
   \[
      \frac{u_{z,\kappa}}{|A_{z,\kappa}|^2}
      =
      \psi_{z,\kappa}|A_{z,\kappa}|^{\rho_{z,\kappa}-1},
   \]
   and the inequality follows from \(|A_{z,\kappa}|\ge1\) and
   \(\rho_{z,\kappa}\le1\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Occurrence-discounted tuple storage congestion]
   \label{cor:occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:uniform-tuple-witness-packing-storage}, and suppose the decoded
   panel contains occurrence records \(b\in\mathcal B_z\) pointing to the same
   canonical child identifiers \(\kappa_{z,b}\).  Let
   \[
      m_z(\kappa)=|\{b\in\mathcal B_z:\kappa_{z,b}=\kappa\}|
      \tag{ODT0}
   \]
   be the occurrence multiplicity of a distinct child.  For
   \(k\in\mathcal K\) and \(\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_k(P,\delta)\), define
   \[
      \widehat W_z(k,\mathbf x)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{b\in\mathcal B_z:\\
         k_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}=k,\
         x_j\in A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\ \forall j}}
      \frac{
         u_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}
      }{
         m_z(\kappa_{z,b})\,|A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}|^k
      } .
      \tag{ODT1}
   \]
   Suppose there are certified envelopes \(\widehat J_k(\mathbf x)\ge0\) with
   \[
      \E_z\widehat W_z(k,\mathbf x)\le\widehat J_k(\mathbf x)
      \qquad(k\in\mathcal K,\ \mathbf x\in\mathcal T_k(P,\delta)).
      \tag{ODT2}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise suppose \(a>0\),
   the corresponding active first-moment condition holds, and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \sum_{k\in\mathcal K}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_k(P,\delta)}\widehat J_k(\mathbf x)
      \le aS .
      \tag{ODT3}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In particular, for the pair specialization \(k=2\) and
   \(u_{z,\kappa}=\psi_{z,\kappa}|A_{z,\kappa}|^{1+\rho_{z,\kappa}}\), it is
   enough to bound, for each \((x,y)\in\mathcal T_2(P,\delta)\), the expected
   occurrence sum
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{b\in\mathcal B_z:\\ x,y\in A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}}}
      \frac{
         \psi_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}|A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}|^{\rho_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}-1}
      }{
         m_z(\kappa_{z,b})
      },
      \tag{ODT4}
   \]
   which is at most the same sum with the numerator
   \(\psi_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\).  Thus an occurrence-based decoder may prove the
   shared-DAG storage bound by reciprocal-multiplicity-weighted pair congestion.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed tuple \((k,\mathbf x)\), group the occurrence sum \((ODT1)\) by
   canonical child identifier.  A child \(\kappa\) with
   \(k_{z,\kappa}=k\) and \(x_j\in A_{z,\kappa}\) for all \(j\) contributes
   \[
      m_z(\kappa)\cdot
      \frac{u_{z,\kappa}}{m_z(\kappa)|A_{z,\kappa}|^k}
      =
      \frac{u_{z,\kappa}}{|A_{z,\kappa}|^k},
   \]
   and otherwise contributes zero.  Hence
   \[
      \widehat W_z(k,\mathbf x)=W_z(k,\mathbf x).
      \tag{ODT5}
   \]
   Conditions \((ODT2)\)--\((ODT3)\) are therefore exactly the hypotheses
   \((UTW2)\)--\((UTW3)\), and
   \cref{cor:uniform-tuple-witness-packing-storage} gives feasibility.

   The displayed pair specialization is \((ODT1)\) with \(k=2\) and the stated
   storage price.  Since \(|A_{z,\kappa}|\ge1\) and
   \(\rho_{z,\kappa}\le1\), each factor
   \(|A_{z,\kappa}|^{\rho_{z,\kappa}-1}\) is at most one.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Weighted occurrence-discounted tuple storage]
   \label{cor:weighted-occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:uniform-tuple-witness-packing-storage}.  For each seed \(z\), let
   \(\mathcal B_z^w\) be a finite weighted occurrence family.  An occurrence
   \(b\in\mathcal B_z^w\) has weight \(\omega_{z,b}>0\) and points to a
   canonical child \(\kappa_{z,b}\).  Let
   \[
      \mathcal C_z^w=\{\kappa_{z,b}:b\in\mathcal B_z^w\},
      \qquad
      m_z^w(\kappa)
      =
      \sum_{b:\,\kappa_{z,b}=\kappa}\omega_{z,b}
      \tag{WODT0}
   \]
   be the distinct weighted children and their weighted occurrence
   multiplicities.  Each \(\kappa\in\mathcal C_z^w\) has the same certificates
   as in \cref{cor:uniform-tuple-witness-packing-storage}: tuple order
   \(k_{z,\kappa}\in\mathcal K\), witness net \(A_{z,\kappa}\), and storage
   price \(u_{z,\kappa}\).

   For \(k\in\mathcal K\) and
   \(\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_k(P,\delta)\), define the weighted
   occurrence-discounted congestion
   \[
      \widehat W_z^w(k,\mathbf x)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{b\in\mathcal B_z^w:\\
         k_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}=k,\
         x_j\in A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\ \forall j}}
      \frac{
         \omega_{z,b}u_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}
      }{
         m_z^w(\kappa_{z,b})\,|A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}|^k
      } .
      \tag{WODT1}
   \]
   Suppose there are certified envelopes \(\widehat J_k^w(\mathbf x)\ge0\)
   such that
   \[
      \E_z\widehat W_z^w(k,\mathbf x)\le\widehat J_k^w(\mathbf x)
      \qquad(k\in\mathcal K,\ \mathbf x\in\mathcal T_k(P,\delta)).
      \tag{WODT2}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise suppose
   \(a>0\), the corresponding active first-moment condition from
   \cref{cor:uniform-tuple-witness-packing-storage} holds, and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \sum_{k\in\mathcal K}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_k(P,\delta)}
      \widehat J_k^w(\mathbf x)
      \le aS .
      \tag{WODT3}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In the pair specialization \(k=2\), if
   \(u_{z,\kappa}=\psi_{z,\kappa}|A_{z,\kappa}|^{1+\rho_{z,\kappa}}\) with
   \(0\le\rho_{z,\kappa}\le1\), it is enough to bound
   \[
      \E_z
      \sum_{\substack{b\in\mathcal B_z^w:\\ x,y\in A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}}}
      \frac{\omega_{z,b}\psi_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}}
           {m_z^w(\kappa_{z,b})}
      \le J^w(x,y).
      \tag{WODT4}
   \]
   and to have
   \(\E_z\Gamma_z+\sum_{(x,y)\in\mathcal T_2(P,\delta)}J^w(x,y)\le aS\).
   Thus weighted Hall atoms, fractional cohorts, and soft decoder records can
   be used directly in the shared-storage theorem; the analysis divides by
   their total weighted multiplicity instead of first expanding them into
   integer unit occurrences.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed tuple \((k,\mathbf x)\), group the weighted occurrence sum
   \((WODT1)\) by canonical child.  A child \(\kappa\) contributes only when
   \(k_{z,\kappa}=k\) and \(x_j\in A_{z,\kappa}\) for every \(j\).  In that
   case its total contribution is
   \[
      \sum_{b:\,\kappa_{z,b}=\kappa}
      \frac{\omega_{z,b}u_{z,\kappa}}
           {m_z^w(\kappa)|A_{z,\kappa}|^k}
      =
      \frac{u_{z,\kappa}}{|A_{z,\kappa}|^k}.
   \]
   Hence \(\widehat W_z^w(k,\mathbf x)\) is exactly the distinct-child tuple
   congestion \(W_z(k,\mathbf x)\) from \((UTW1)\), with the distinct child set
   \(\mathcal C_z^w\).  Conditions \((WODT2)\)--\((WODT3)\) are therefore the
   hypotheses \((UTW2)\)--\((UTW3)\), and
   \cref{cor:uniform-tuple-witness-packing-storage} gives feasibility.

   In the pair specialization,
   \[
      \frac{u_{z,\kappa}}{|A_{z,\kappa}|^2}
      =
      \psi_{z,\kappa}|A_{z,\kappa}|^{\rho_{z,\kappa}-1}
      \le \psi_{z,\kappa},
   \]
   because \(|A_{z,\kappa}|\ge1\) and \(\rho_{z,\kappa}\le1\).  Thus
   \((WODT4)\) supplies the pair envelopes required by \((WODT2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Reciprocal-multiplicity pair-congestion certificate]
   \label{cor:reciprocal-multiplicity-pair-congestion}
   Work in the pair specialization \(k=2\) of
   \cref{cor:occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage}, and assume
   \[
      u_{z,\kappa}=\psi_{z,\kappa}|A_{z,\kappa}|^{1+\rho_{z,\kappa}},
      \qquad 0\le\rho_{z,\kappa}\le1,
      \qquad |A_{z,\kappa}|\ge1 .
      \tag{RMP0}
   \]
   Suppose there are certified envelopes \(J(x,y)\ge0\), indexed by
   \((x,y)\in\mathcal T_2(P,\delta)\), such that
   \[
      \E_z
      \sum_{\substack{b\in\mathcal B_z:\\
         x,y\in A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}}}
      \frac{\psi_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}}{m_z(\kappa_{z,b})}
      \le
      J(x,y).
      \tag{RMP1}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise suppose
   \(a>0\), the corresponding active first-moment condition holds, and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\mathcal T_2(P,\delta)}J(x,y)
      \le aS .
      \tag{RMP2}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Thus, after the ordinary success-normalized active candidate-load estimate
   has paid the query side, the shared-storage side may be proved by a single
   pair-congestion theorem: each decoded occurrence contributes only
   \(1/m_z(\kappa)\) of the price factor of its canonical child to every
   separated pair contained in that child.  The size factor
   \(|A_{z,\kappa}|^{\rho_{z,\kappa}-1}\) from the exact storage price is
   nonpositive in the exponent and only helps.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   In the pair specialization, \((ODT4)\) shows that the actual
   occurrence-discounted tuple congestion is
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{b\in\mathcal B_z:\\x,y\in A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}}}
      \frac{
         \psi_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}
         |A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}|^{\rho_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}-1}
      }{
         m_z(\kappa_{z,b})
      } .
   \]
   By \((RMP0)\), each factor
   \(|A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}|^{\rho_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}-1}\le1\).  Hence \((RMP1)\)
   supplies the envelope \(\widehat J_2(x,y)=J(x,y)\) required by
   \((ODT2)\).  Condition \((RMP2)\) is then \((ODT3)\) with
   \(\mathcal K=\{2\}\), and
   \cref{cor:occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage} gives feasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Pair-profile occurrence-discounted storage certificate]
   \label{cor:pair-profile-occurrence-discounted-storage}
   Work in the pair specialization \(k=2\) of
   \cref{cor:occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage}.  Partition
   \(\mathcal T_2(P,\delta)\) into finite profile classes \(\Pi\).  For each
   profile \(\pi\in\Pi\), let \(N_\pi\) be its cardinality, and suppose there is
   a certified envelope \(B_\pi\ge0\) such that
   \[
      \E_z\widehat W_z(2,x,y)\le B_\pi
      \qquad((x,y)\in\pi).
      \tag{POD1}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise suppose \(a>0\),
   the corresponding active first-moment condition holds, and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+\sum_{\pi\in\Pi}N_\pi B_\pi\le aS .
      \tag{POD2}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In particular, if a geometric or list-decoding analysis gives
   \[
      B_\pi\le C_\pi e^{-I_\pi},
      \tag{POD3}
   \]
   where \(I_\pi\) is a cap-intersection or decoder energy and \(C_\pi\) is the
   largest certified price factor for occurrences in that profile, then it is
   enough to prove the entropy-energy inequality
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}N_\pi C_\pi e^{-I_\pi}
      \le aS .
      \tag{POD4}
   \]
   This is the profile form of the remaining shared-DAG storage theorem.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Define \(\widehat J_2(x,y)=B_\pi\) for \((x,y)\in\pi\).  Then \((POD1)\) is
   exactly the envelope condition \((ODT2)\), and
   \[
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\mathcal T_2(P,\delta)}\widehat J_2(x,y)
      =
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}N_\pi B_\pi .
   \]
   Hence \((POD2)\) is \((ODT3)\), and
   \cref{cor:occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage} gives feasibility.  The final
   statement is obtained by substituting \((POD3)\) into \((POD2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Multiplicity-layer pair-profile certificate]
   \label{cor:multiplicity-layer-pair-profile-storage}
   Work in the pair specialization of
   \cref{cor:occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage}, with
   \(u_{z,\kappa}=\psi_{z,\kappa}|A_{z,\kappa}|^{1+\rho_{z,\kappa}}\).
   Partition \(\mathcal T_2(P,\delta)\) into finite profile classes \(\Pi\).
   For \(\pi\in\Pi\), let \(N_\pi\) be its cardinality.
   For \((x,y)\in\pi\) and \(\ell\ge0\), define the undiscounted occurrence
   congestion in multiplicity layer \(\ell\) by
   \[
      V_z(\pi,\ell;x,y)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{b\in\mathcal B_z:\ x,y\in A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\\
            2^\ell\le m_z(\kappa_{z,b})<2^{\ell+1}}}
      \psi_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}
      |A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}|^{\rho_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}-1}.
      \tag{MLP1}
   \]
   Suppose there are envelopes \(A_{\pi,\ell}\ge0\) such that
   \[
      \E_z V_z(\pi,\ell;x,y)\le A_{\pi,\ell}
      \qquad((x,y)\in\pi,\ \ell\ge0).
      \tag{MLP2}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise suppose \(a>0\),
   the corresponding active first-moment condition holds, and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}N_\pi
      \sum_{\ell\ge0}2^{-\ell}A_{\pi,\ell}
      \le aS .
      \tag{MLP3}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In particular, if a profile analysis gives
   \[
      A_{\pi,\ell}\le C_{\pi,\ell}e^{-I_{\pi,\ell}},
      \tag{MLP4}
   \]
   then it is enough to prove the discounted entropy-energy inequality
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}N_\pi
      \sum_{\ell\ge0}
      2^{-\ell}C_{\pi,\ell}e^{-I_{\pi,\ell}}
      \le aS .
      \tag{MLP5}
   \]
   Thus high occurrence multiplicity appears as a literal \(2^{-\ell}\)
   storage discount.  Low-multiplicity profiles must be paid by cap-intersection
   or decoder energy; high-multiplicity profiles may be paid by quotienting many
   decoded records to one canonical child.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For \((x,y)\in\pi\), decompose the discounted occurrence sum \((ODT4)\) by
   the dyadic layer containing \(m_z(\kappa_{z,b})\).  Every record in layer
   \(\ell\) has reciprocal multiplicity at most \(2^{-\ell}\), so
   \[
      \widehat W_z(2,x,y)
      \le
      \sum_{\ell\ge0}2^{-\ell}V_z(\pi,\ell;x,y).
   \]
   Taking expectations and using \((MLP2)\) gives the pair-profile envelope
   \[
      B_\pi=\sum_{\ell\ge0}2^{-\ell}A_{\pi,\ell}.
   \]
   Condition \((MLP3)\) is therefore \((POD2)\) for this envelope, and
   \cref{cor:pair-profile-occurrence-discounted-storage} gives feasibility.
   Substituting \((MLP4)\) gives \((MLP5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Aggregate multiplicity-profile storage certificate]
   \label{cor:aggregate-multiplicity-profile-storage}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:multiplicity-layer-pair-profile-storage}.  For each profile
   \(\pi\in\Pi\) and layer \(\ell\ge0\), define the aggregate undiscounted
   layer congestion
   \[
      \mathcal V_z(\pi,\ell)
      =
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\pi}V_z(\pi,\ell;x,y).
      \tag{AMP1}
   \]
   Suppose there are certified aggregate envelopes
   \(\mathcal A_{\pi,\ell}\ge0\) such that
   \[
      \E_z\mathcal V_z(\pi,\ell)\le\mathcal A_{\pi,\ell}
      \qquad(\pi\in\Pi,\ \ell\ge0).
      \tag{AMP2}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise suppose \(a>0\),
   the corresponding active first-moment condition holds, and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\sum_{\ell\ge0}
      2^{-\ell}\mathcal A_{\pi,\ell}
      \le aS .
      \tag{AMP3}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In particular, it is enough to prove an aggregate entropy-energy estimate
   \[
      \mathcal A_{\pi,\ell}
      \le
      C_{\pi,\ell}\exp(H_{\pi,\ell}-I_{\pi,\ell}),
      \tag{AMP4}
   \]
   where \(H_{\pi,\ell}\) is the logarithmic number or mass of pair occurrences
   in the profile layer and \(I_{\pi,\ell}\) is the corresponding
   cap-intersection or decoder energy, together with
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \sum_{\pi,\ell}
      2^{-\ell}C_{\pi,\ell}\exp(H_{\pi,\ell}-I_{\pi,\ell})
      \le aS .
      \tag{AMP5}
   \]
   Thus the storage proof does not need a uniform worst-pair bound inside a
   profile.  It may bound the whole profile-layer mass directly.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For each separated pair \((x,y)\), set
   \[
      \widehat J_2(x,y)=\E_z\widehat W_z(2,x,y).
   \]
   This is a valid envelope for \((ODT2)\) with equality.  If \((x,y)\in\pi\),
   the proof of \cref{cor:multiplicity-layer-pair-profile-storage} gives
   pointwise in \(z\)
   \[
      \widehat W_z(2,x,y)
      \le
      \sum_{\ell\ge0}2^{-\ell}V_z(\pi,\ell;x,y).
   \]
   Summing over \((x,y)\in\pi\), taking expectations, and using \((AMP2)\)
   gives
   \[
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\pi}\widehat J_2(x,y)
      \le
      \sum_{\ell\ge0}2^{-\ell}\mathcal A_{\pi,\ell}.
   \]
   Summing over profiles and applying \((AMP3)\) yields \((ODT3)\), so
   \cref{cor:occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage} gives feasibility.  The final
   claim follows by substituting \((AMP4)\) into \((AMP3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Gaussian aggregate profile-layer storage test]
   \label{cor:gaussian-aggregate-profile-layer-storage}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:aggregate-multiplicity-profile-storage}.  Fix a profile
   \(\pi\) and multiplicity layer \(\ell\).  Suppose the undiscounted layer
   congestion admits the following certified expansion before the Gaussian cap
   tests are evaluated:
   \[
      \mathcal V_z(\pi,\ell)
      \le
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{\pi,\ell}}
      w_r
      \sum_{(x,y)\in E_r}
      \mathbf 1\{x,y\in U_{G_r}\},
      \tag{GAP1}
   \]
   where \(w_r\ge0\), \(E_r\subseteq\pi\), and
   \(U_{G_r}=\{u:\ip{G_r}{u}\ge T_r\}\) with
   \(G_r\sim N(\mu_r,I)\).  Assume that for every \(r\) and every
   \((x,y)\in E_r\),
   \[
      -1<\theta_{\pi,\ell}<1,
      \qquad
      \ip{x}{y}\le\theta_{\pi,\ell},
      \qquad
      T_r-\ip{\mu_r}{x}\ge\beta_{\pi,\ell},
      \qquad
      T_r-\ip{\mu_r}{y}\ge\beta_{\pi,\ell},
      \tag{GAP2}
   \]
   with \(\beta_{\pi,\ell}\ge0\).  Put
   \[
      W_{\pi,\ell}
      =
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{\pi,\ell}}w_r|E_r|.
      \tag{GAP3}
   \]
   Then \((AMP2)\) holds with
   \[
      \mathcal A_{\pi,\ell}
      =
      W_{\pi,\ell}
      \exp\left(
         -\frac{\beta_{\pi,\ell}^2}{1+\theta_{\pi,\ell}}
      \right).
      \tag{GAP4}
   \]
   Consequently, if
   \[
      W_{\pi,\ell}\le C_{\pi,\ell}e^{H_{\pi,\ell}},
      \tag{GAP5}
   \]
   then \((AMP4)\) holds with
   \[
      I_{\pi,\ell}
      =
      \frac{\beta_{\pi,\ell}^2}{1+\theta_{\pi,\ell}} .
      \tag{GAP6}
   \]
   Thus a Gaussian cap or list-decoding implementation only has to certify
   three profile-layer quantities: weighted incidence entropy \(H_{\pi,\ell}\),
   threshold margin \(\beta_{\pi,\ell}\), and maximum pair correlation
   \(\theta_{\pi,\ell}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{lem:two-point-gaussian-cap-energy}, every summand in \((GAP1)\)
   satisfies
   \[
      \Pr[x,y\in U_{G_r}]
      \le
      \exp\left(
         -\frac{\beta_{\pi,\ell}^2}{1+\theta_{\pi,\ell}}
      \right).
   \]
   Linearity of expectation in \((GAP1)\) gives \((GAP4)\).  If \((GAP5)\)
   holds, substitute \(W_{\pi,\ell}\le C_{\pi,\ell}e^{H_{\pi,\ell}}\) into
   \((GAP4)\) to obtain \((AMP4)\) with \((GAP6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[High-correlation pair-star reporter]
   \label{lem:high-correlation-pair-star-reporter}
   Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb S^{D-1}\), let \(\mathcal R\) be finite, and for
   each \(r\in\mathcal R\) let \(w_r\ge0\) and
   \(E_r\subseteq P\times P\).  Suppose every retained edge is
   \(\underline\theta\)-correlated:
   \[
      (x,y)\in E_r
      \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
      \ip{x}{y}\ge\underline\theta
      \qquad(-1<\underline\theta<1).
      \tag{HPS1}
   \]
   Define the weighted star multiplicities
   \[
      M_x(y)=\sum_{r:\ (x,y)\in E_r}w_r,
      \qquad
      W=\sum_{x,y\in P}M_x(y)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r|E_r|.
      \tag{HPS2}
   \]
   For \(t>0\), put
   \[
      U_{x,t}=\{y\in P:M_x(y)\ge t\}.
      \tag{HPS3}
   \]
   Then every \(U_{x,t}\) is contained in the smaller Euclidean ball
   \[
      U_{x,t}\subseteq P\cap B\!\left(x,\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)}\right),
      \tag{HPS4}
   \]
   and the exact layer-cake identity
   \[
      W=\sum_{x\in P}\int_0^\infty |U_{x,t}|\,dt
      \tag{HPS5}
   \]
   holds.

   In particular, suppose all positive multiplicities \(M_x(y)\) lie in
   \([M_{\min},M_{\max}]\), where \(0<M_{\min}\le M_{\max}\), and let
   \[
      J=1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{M_{\max}}{M_{\min}}\right\rceil .
      \tag{HPS6}
   \]
   Then there are \(x\in P\) and a dyadic level
   \(t\in\{2^jM_{\min}:0\le j<J\}\) such that
   \[
      t\,|U_{x,t}|
      \ge
      \frac{W}{2|P|J}.
      \tag{HPS7}
   \]
   Thus any profile layer with large weighted high-correlation incidence either
   has small total incidence \(W\), or exposes a certified smaller-radius
   superlevel \(U_{x,t}\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   If \(y\in U_{x,t}\), then \(M_x(y)>0\), so \((x,y)\in E_r\) for some \(r\)
   with \(w_r>0\).  By \((HPS1)\),
   \[
      \|x-y\|^2=2-2\ip{x}{y}\le2(1-\underline\theta),
   \]
   proving \((HPS4)\).

   For every fixed ordered pair \((x,y)\),
   \[
      M_x(y)=\int_0^\infty \mathbf 1\{M_x(y)\ge t\}\,dt .
   \]
   Summing over ordered pairs gives \((HPS5)\).

   Choose \(x\) with
   \[
      \sum_yM_x(y)\ge W/|P|.
   \]
   For a positive number \(m\in[M_{\min},M_{\max}]\),
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{0\le j<J:\\ 2^jM_{\min}\le m}}2^jM_{\min}
      \ge \frac m2 .
   \]
   Therefore
   \[
      \sum_{j=0}^{J-1}2^jM_{\min}|U_{x,2^jM_{\min}}|
      \ge
      \frac12\sum_yM_x(y)
      \ge
      \frac{W}{2|P|}.
   \]
   One of the \(J\) dyadic levels satisfies \((HPS7)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cap-centered pair-star reporter]
   \label{cor:cap-centered-pair-star-reporter}
   In the setting of \cref{lem:high-correlation-pair-star-reporter}, assume in
   addition that \(0<\underline\theta\le1/2\).  Then every reported star
   superlevel also satisfies the cap-centered certificate
   \[
      U_{x,t}\subseteq B\!\left(\underline\theta x,\sqrt{1-\underline\theta^2}\right)
      \qquad(P\subseteq\mathbb S^{D-1}).
      \tag{CPS1}
   \]
   In the scaled form, if \(P\subseteq o+R\mathbb S^{D-1}\) and the correlation
   condition is
   \[
      \ip{(x-o)/R}{(y-o)/R}\ge\underline\theta,
      \tag{CPS2}
   \]
   then
   \[
      U_{x,t}
      \subseteq
      B\!\left(o+\underline\theta(x-o),\,R\sqrt{1-\underline\theta^2}\right).
      \tag{CPS3}
   \]

   Therefore a positive-correlation pair-star should be submitted to the dense
   verifier with the cap-centered child radius \(R\sqrt{1-\underline\theta^2}\),
   not only with the point-centered guard ball from \((HPS4)\).  When the child
   is priced by the padded potentials \(F_4,G_4\), the geometric reprice from
   the parent radius to this cap-centered child is
   \(\exp(O(\underline\theta^2))\) by
   \cref{cor:padded-radius-quadratic-reprice}.  Thus the star reporter already
   supplies the geometric part of the quadratic local-repair target; the
   remaining local content is the paid-prefix reduced-gain inequality.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   In the unit-sphere case, if \(y\in U_{x,t}\), then \(M_x(y)>0\), so some
   retained edge \((x,y)\in E_r\) has positive weight.  By \((HPS1)\),
   \(\ip{x}{y}\ge\underline\theta\).  Applying \cref{lem:cap} with center
   \(o=0\), radius \(R=1\), direction \(w=x\), and margin
   \(\gamma=\underline\theta\) proves \((CPS1)\).

   The scaled statement is the same argument after normalizing
   \(x\mapsto(x-o)/R\) and \(y\mapsto(y-o)/R\), then scaling back by \(R\).  The
   final paragraph follows by substituting
   \(\gamma=\underline\theta\) into
   \cref{cor:padded-radius-quadratic-reprice}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dense-star alternative for Gaussian profile layers]
   \label{cor:dense-star-gaussian-profile-layer}
   In the setting of
   \cref{cor:gaussian-aggregate-profile-layer-storage}, suppose in addition
   that every edge in every \(E_r\) satisfies
   \[
      \ip{x}{y}\ge\underline\theta_{\pi,\ell}
      \qquad(-1<\underline\theta_{\pi,\ell}<1),
      \tag{DSG1}
   \]
   and that the positive weighted star multiplicities from \((HPS2)\) lie in a
   certified range \([M_{\min},M_{\max}]\).  If \(J\) is as in \((HPS6)\) and
   \(W_{\pi,\ell}\) is the incidence weight in \((GAP3)\), then either
   \(W_{\pi,\ell}=0\), or there are a center \(x\in P\), a dyadic level \(t\),
   and a certified smaller-radius superlevel
   \[
      U_{x,t}\subseteq
      P\cap B\!\left(x,\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta_{\pi,\ell})}\right)
      \tag{DSG2}
   \]
   with
   \[
      t|U_{x,t}|
      \ge
      \frac{W_{\pi,\ell}}{2|P|J}.
      \tag{DSG3}
   \]
   Consequently, failure of the Gaussian entropy-energy inequality in a
   high-correlation profile layer can be routed to the dense-cover separator:
   a range reporter only has to search these star superlevels and submit the
   deterministic candidate to the finite filter-cover verifier.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{lem:high-correlation-pair-star-reporter} to the weighted edge
   family \((\mathcal R_{\pi,\ell},w_r,E_r)\).  The total incidence \(W\) in
   \((HPS2)\) is \(W_{\pi,\ell}\) by \((GAP3)\), and the radius claim is
   \((HPS4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Correlation-split Gaussian profile layer]
   \label{cor:correlation-split-gaussian-profile-layer}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:gaussian-aggregate-profile-layer-storage}.  Suppose every edge set
   is partitioned as
   \[
      E_r=E_r^{\rm lo}\,\dot\cup\,E_r^{\rm hi}.
   \]
   Assume the low-correlation part satisfies, for every
   \((x,y)\in E_r^{\rm lo}\),
   \[
      \ip{x}{y}\le\theta_{\rm lo},
      \qquad
      T_r-\ip{\mu_r}{x}\ge\beta_{\rm lo},
      \qquad
      T_r-\ip{\mu_r}{y}\ge\beta_{\rm lo},
      \tag{CSG0}
   \]
