   where \(-1<\theta_{\rm lo}<1\) and \(\beta_{\rm lo}\ge0\).  Put
   \[
      W_{\rm lo}=\sum_r w_r|E_r^{\rm lo}|,
      \qquad
      W_{\rm hi}=\sum_r w_r|E_r^{\rm hi}|.
      \tag{CSG1}
   \]
   Then the low-correlation contribution alone satisfies the aggregate storage
   envelope
   \[
      \mathcal A_{\rm lo}
      =
      W_{\rm lo}
      \exp\!\left(-\frac{\beta_{\rm lo}^2}{1+\theta_{\rm lo}}\right).
      \tag{CSG2}
   \]

   For the high-correlation part, assume every edge in every \(E_r^{\rm hi}\)
   has correlation at least \(\underline\theta\), with
   \(-1<\underline\theta<1\), and that the positive star multiplicities induced
   by \((E_r^{\rm hi})_r\) lie in a certified range
   \([M_{\min},M_{\max}]\).  Let
   \[
      J_{\rm hi}
      =
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{M_{\max}}{M_{\min}}\right\rceil .
      \tag{CSG3}
   \]
   For every threshold \(\Lambda>0\), either
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}\le 2|P|J_{\rm hi}\Lambda,
      \tag{CSG4}
   \]
   or there are a center \(x\in P\) and a dyadic level \(t\) such that
   \[
      U_{x,t}\subseteq P\cap B\!\left(x,\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)}\right)
      \tag{CSG5}
   \]
   and
   \[
      t|U_{x,t}|\ge\Lambda.
      \tag{CSG6}
   \]

   Consequently, after all high-correlation star records with certified scale
   at least \(\Lambda\) have been proposed to the dense-filter verifier, the
   unresolved part of this profile layer is bounded by the residual envelope
   \[
      \mathcal A_{\rm lo}+2|P|J_{\rm hi}\Lambda.
      \tag{CSG7}
   \]
   A violation of this residual envelope must expose one of the proposed
   smaller-radius star records.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{cor:gaussian-aggregate-profile-layer-storage} to the restricted
   expansion containing only the low-correlation edge sets \(E_r^{\rm lo}\).
   Conditions \((CSG0)\) are exactly the Gaussian profile hypotheses \((GAP2)\)
   for that restricted expansion, giving \((CSG2)\).

   For the high-correlation part, apply
   \cref{lem:high-correlation-pair-star-reporter} to the weighted edge family
   \((w_r,E_r^{\rm hi})_r\).  If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), then \((CSG4)\) is immediate.
   Otherwise \((HPS7)\) gives a dyadic star with
   \[
      t|U_{x,t}|\ge \frac{W_{\rm hi}}{2|P|J_{\rm hi}} .
   \]
   Thus, if \((CSG4)\) fails, this star satisfies \((CSG5)\)--\((CSG6)\).

   The final statement is the same dichotomy read contrapositively: if no
   proposed high-correlation star of scale at least \(\Lambda\) remains to be
   handled by the dense verifier, then the high-correlation incidence is at most
   \(2|P|J_{\rm hi}\Lambda\), while the low-correlation contribution is bounded
   by \((CSG2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Star-superlevel column verifier]
   \label{lem:star-superlevel-column-verifier}
   Work in a finite filter-cover instance
   \((P,\mathcal Q,\mathcal N)\) as in
   \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual}, where every demand
   \((p,q)\in\mathcal N\) satisfies \(\|p-q\|\le r\).  Let
   \(U\subseteq P\) be certified inside a ball \(B(x,R_U)\), and define the
   ball-thickened query activation
   \[
      a_U(q)=\mathbf 1\{\|q-x\|\le R_U+r\}
      \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q).
      \tag{SVC1}
   \]
   Let \(T_U,S_U\) be certified query and storage prices for the child on
   \(U\).  Then
   \[
      A_U=(U,a_U,T_U,S_U)
      \tag{SVC2}
   \]
   is a valid dense-filter column: if \(p\in U\) and \(\|p-q\|\le r\), then
   \(a_U(q)=1\).

   For any filter-cover dual prices \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\), its reduced gain
   is exactly
   \[
      \mathsf G(U)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{(p,q)\in\mathcal N:\\ p\in U}}
         \alpha_{p,q}a_U(q)
      -
      T_U\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}\tau_qa_U(q)
      -
      \sigma S_U .
      \tag{SVC3}
   \]
   If \(\mathsf G(U)>0\), then \(A_U\) is a positive reduced-gain column and
   the finite column-generation step of
   \cref{cor:filter-cover-column-generation} may add it.  Conversely, if a
   finite star family \(\mathcal U_\star\) contains no positive column, then
   every \(U\in\mathcal U_\star\) satisfies the explicit residual inequality
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{(p,q)\in\mathcal N:\\ p\in U}}
         \alpha_{p,q}a_U(q)
      \le
      T_U\sum_q\tau_qa_U(q)+\sigma S_U .
      \tag{SVC4}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   If \(p\in U\subseteq B(x,R_U)\) and \(\|p-q\|\le r\), then
   \[
      \|q-x\|\le\|q-p\|+\|p-x\|\le r+R_U,
   \]
   so \(a_U(q)=1\).  Thus \((SVC2)\) satisfies the filter correctness condition
   used in \cref{def:fractional-dense-filter-cover}.  Formula \((SVC3)\) is
   \cref{cor:filter-cover-column-generation}'s reduced-gain definition applied
   to this column.  Positive gain is therefore an admissible column-generation
   certificate, and nonpositive gain for every member of a finite star family is
   exactly \((SVC4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Pair-star reporter as dense-column generator]
   \label{cor:pair-star-dense-column-generator}
   In the setting of
   \cref{lem:high-correlation-pair-star-reporter}, also fix a finite
   filter-cover instance \((P,\mathcal Q,\mathcal N)\) with near radius \(r\).
   For each nonempty reported superlevel \(U_{x,t}\), put
   \[
      R_\star=\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)}
      \tag{PSG1}
   \]
   and equip \(U_{x,t}\) with the activation
   \[
      a_{x,t}(q)=\mathbf 1\{\|q-x\|\le R_\star+r\}.
      \tag{PSG2}
   \]
   Let \(T_{x,t},S_{x,t}\) be any certified descendant prices for this
   smaller-radius child.  For dual prices \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\), define
   \[
      \mathsf G(x,t)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{(p,q)\in\mathcal N:\\ p\in U_{x,t}}}
         \alpha_{p,q}a_{x,t}(q)
      -
      T_{x,t}\sum_q\tau_qa_{x,t}(q)
      -
      \sigma S_{x,t}.
      \tag{PSG3}
   \]
   If some dyadic reporter level has \(\mathsf G(x,t)>0\), then the fractional
   dense-filter cover has a valid positive-gain dense column.  If no dyadic
   reporter level has positive gain, then the residual dual satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{(p,q)\in\mathcal N:\\ p\in U_{x,t}}}
         \alpha_{p,q}a_{x,t}(q)
      \le
      T_{x,t}\sum_q\tau_qa_{x,t}(q)+\sigma S_{x,t}
      \tag{PSG4}
   \]
   for every reported star.  Thus the high-correlation pair-star construction
   is a safe build-time proposal mechanism: it may generate many overlapping
   candidates, but only the exact reduced-gain test \((PSG3)\) can retain one,
   and \((PSG4)\) is the precise no-star condition left for the diffuse
   spherical/list-decoding analysis.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \((HPS4)\), every nonempty \(U_{x,t}\) lies in \(B(x,R_\star)\).  Apply
   \cref{lem:star-superlevel-column-verifier} with \(U=U_{x,t}\) and
   \(R_U=R_\star\).  The displayed gain and residual inequalities are exactly
   \((SVC3)\) and \((SVC4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Star-prefix weak-type residual]
   \label{lem:star-prefix-weak-type-residual}
   Work in a finite filter-cover instance as in
   \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual}.  Let \(\mathcal X\) be a finite set of
   certified star centers.  For \(x\in\mathcal X\), let
   \(W_x\subseteq P\cap B(x,R_x)\) be a certified container, let
   \[
      a_x(q)=\mathbf 1\{\|q-x\|\le R_x+r\},
      \tag{SPW0}
   \]
   and let the child price for a \(K\)-point prefix of \(W_x\) be
   \[
      T_{x,K}=\psi_xK^{\rho_x},
      \qquad
      S_{x,K}=\psi_xK^{1+\rho_x},
      \qquad 0<\rho_x<1 .
      \tag{SPW1}
   \]
   For dual prices \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\), define the star paid degrees and
   query price
   \[
      d_x(p)=
      \sum_{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\alpha_{p,q}a_x(q),
      \qquad
      A_x=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}\tau_qa_x(q).
      \tag{SPW2}
   \]
   Order \(W_x=\{p_1,p_2,\ldots\}\) so that
   \(d_x(p_1)\ge d_x(p_2)\ge\cdots\).  Suppose that, after the current dual
   prices are known, the column generator may add, for every available
   cardinality \(K\in\mathcal K_x\), the star prefix
   \(U_{x,K}=\{p_1,\ldots,p_K\}\) with activation \(a_x\) and prices
   \((SPW1)\).  Equivalently, the finite universe may contain all
   \(K\)-subsets of \(W_x\), with the verifier selecting the best one.  If no
   such star prefix has positive reduced gain, then
   \[
      \sum_{i\le K}d_x(p_i)
      \le
      \psi_x\left(A_xK^{\rho_x}+\sigma K^{1+\rho_x}\right)
      \qquad(x\in\mathcal X,\ K\in\mathcal K_x).
      \tag{SPW3}
   \]
   Consequently every \(U\subseteq W_x\) with \(|U|=K\in\mathcal K_x\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U}d_x(p)
      \le
      \psi_x\left(A_xK^{\rho_x}+\sigma K^{1+\rho_x}\right).
      \tag{SPW4}
   \]

   If \(\mathcal K_x\) is \(b\)-dense from below, meaning that every
   \(1\le h\le |W_x|\) has some \(K\in\mathcal K_x\) with \(h/b\le K\le h\),
   then every nonempty paid-degree superlevel
   \[
      H_{x,\delta}=\{p\in W_x:d_x(p)\ge\delta\},
      \qquad h=|H_{x,\delta}|,
      \tag{SPW5}
   \]
   obeys the weak-type cap
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      \psi_x\left(
         b^{1-\rho_x}A_xh^{\rho_x-1}
         +\sigma h^{\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{SPW6}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The reduced gain of \(U_{x,K}\) is
   \[
      \sum_{i\le K}d_x(p_i)
      -
      \psi_xK^{\rho_x}A_x
      -
      \sigma\psi_xK^{1+\rho_x}.
   \]
   Nonpositive gain for every available prefix is exactly \((SPW3)\).  Since
   the top \(K\) prefix maximizes \(\sum_{p\in U}d_x(p)\) among \(K\)-subsets of
   \(W_x\), \((SPW4)\) follows.

   For the weak-type statement, choose \(K\in\mathcal K_x\) with
   \(h/b\le K\le h\).  The top \(K\) points all have degree at least \(\delta\),
   so \(\delta K\le\sum_{i\le K}d_x(p_i)\).  Dividing \((SPW3)\) by \(K\) gives
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      \psi_x\left(A_xK^{\rho_x-1}+\sigma K^{\rho_x}\right).
   \]
   Because \(\rho_x-1<0\), \(K\ge h/b\) gives
   \(K^{\rho_x-1}\le b^{1-\rho_x}h^{\rho_x-1}\), while \(K\le h\) gives
   \(K^{\rho_x}\le h^{\rho_x}\).  This proves \((SPW6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Pair-star weak-type normal form]
   \label{cor:pair-star-weak-type-normal-form}
   In the setting of
   \cref{cor:pair-star-dense-column-generator}, let
   \(\mathcal X_\star\) be the finite set of centers produced by the reporter,
   and put
   \[
      W_x=P\cap B(x,R_\star),
      \qquad
      a_x(q)=\mathbf 1\{\|q-x\|\le R_\star+r\}.
      \tag{PWN1}
   \]
   Suppose the dense-filter column generator may add the best paid prefix of
   each \(W_x\) at every cardinality, priced as
   \[
      T_{x,K}=\psi_\star K^{\rho_\star},
      \qquad
      S_{x,K}=\psi_\star K^{1+\rho_\star}.
      \tag{PWN2}
   \]
   If no reported center yields a positive-gain prefix, then every reported
   pair-star superlevel \(U_{x,t}\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U_{x,t}}
      \sum_{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
         \alpha_{p,q}a_x(q)
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(
         A_x|U_{x,t}|^{\rho_\star}
         +\sigma |U_{x,t}|^{1+\rho_\star}
      \right),
      \tag{PWN3}
   \]
   where \(A_x=\sum_q\tau_qa_x(q)\).  Equivalently, a high-correlation
   pair-star reporter is useful only through a paid-degree violation of
   \((PWN3)\): geometric incidence alone proposes the center and smaller radius,
   while the exact finite-cover verifier chooses the best paid prefix.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{lem:star-prefix-weak-type-residual} with
   \(R_x=R_\star\), \(\psi_x=\psi_\star\), \(\rho_x=\rho_\star\), and
   \(\mathcal K_x=\{1,\ldots,|W_x|\}\).  Since \(U_{x,t}\subseteq W_x\) by
   \((HPS4)\), \((SPW4)\) gives \((PWN3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cap-centered paid-prefix quadratic criterion]
   \label{cor:cap-centered-paid-prefix-quadratic}
   Work in a finite local filter-cover instance as in
   \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual}.  Suppose the current resident set lies
   on a certified sphere
   \[
      P\subseteq o+R\mathbb S^{D-1},
      \qquad R\ge r,
      \tag{CPQ1}
   \]
   and fix a cap margin \(0<\gamma\le1/2\).  Let \(\mathcal X\subseteq P\) be a
   finite family of reported high-correlation centers, and for \(x\in\mathcal X\)
   put
   \[
      c_x=o+\gamma(x-o),
      \qquad
      R_+=R\sqrt{1-\gamma^2},
      \qquad
      W_x=P\cap B(c_x,R_+),
      \tag{CPQ2}
   \]
   with query activation
   \[
      a_x^+(q)=\mathbf 1\{\|q-c_x\|\le R_++r\}.
      \tag{CPQ3}
   \]
   Let \(B_0\ge0\), and price every \(K\)-point prefix of \(W_x\) by the
   same-prefix padded child potentials
   \[
      T_{x,K}=e^{B_0\gamma^2}\Psi(R_+)K^\rho,
      \qquad
      S_{x,K}=e^{B_0\gamma^2}\Psi(R_+)K^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{CPQ4}
   \]
   Define the cap-centered paid degrees and query price
   \[
      d_x^+(p)=
      \sum_{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\alpha_{p,q}a_x^+(q),
      \qquad
      A_x^+=\sum_q\tau_qa_x^+(q).
      \tag{CPQ5}
   \]
   Order \(W_x=\{p_1,p_2,\ldots\}\) by nonincreasing \(d_x^+(p)\).  If, for
   some \(x\) and \(K\),
   \[
      \sum_{i\le K}d_x^+(p_i)
      >
      e^{B_0\gamma^2}\Psi(R_+)
      \left(A_x^+K^\rho+\sigma K^{1+\rho}\right),
      \tag{CPQ6}
   \]
   then the top prefix \(U=\{p_1,\ldots,p_K\}\) is a valid positive
   same-prefix dense column.  Its geometric query, storage, and inverse-survival
   tolls are bounded by
   \[
      \exp((B_0+3)\gamma^2)
      \tag{CPQ7}
   \]
   relative to the parent padded potential scale, so this retained prefix is a
   \((B_0+3)\)-quadratic local repair in the sense of
   \cref{def:quadratic-local-repair}.

   Conversely, if no such cap-centered paid prefix has positive reduced gain and
   the available cardinalities are \(b\)-dense from below, then every cap-centered
   paid-degree superlevel
   \[
      H_{x,\delta}^+=\{p\in W_x:d_x^+(p)\ge\delta\},
      \qquad h=|H_{x,\delta}^+|>0,
      \tag{CPQ8}
   \]
   obeys
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      e^{B_0\gamma^2}\Psi(R_+)
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho}A_x^+h^{\rho-1}
         +\sigma h^\rho
      \right).
      \tag{CPQ9}
   \]

   Thus the remaining positive-correlation theorem can be stated without any
   extra geometric loss: a residual must either violate the explicit
   cap-centered weak-type bound \((CPQ9)\), producing a quadratic repair, or be
   handled by the diffuse low-correlation/list-decoding certificate.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For any \(p\in W_x\) and any near query \(q\) with \(\|p-q\|\le r\),
   \[
      \|q-c_x\|\le\|q-p\|+\|p-c_x\|\le r+R_+,
   \]
   so \(a_x^+(q)=1\).  Hence every prefix of \(W_x\) with activation \(a_x^+\)
   is a valid dense-filter column by
   \cref{lem:star-superlevel-column-verifier}.  Its reduced gain is exactly the
   left side of \((CPQ6)\) minus the right side, so \((CPQ6)\) gives a positive
   same-prefix column.

   The child prices in \((CPQ4)\) are
   \(e^{B_0\gamma^2}F_4(K,R_+)\) and
   \(e^{B_0\gamma^2}G_4(K,R_+)\).  By
   \cref{cor:padded-radius-quadratic-reprice}, the parent-radius and child-radius
   padded scales differ by at most \(e^{3\gamma^2}\), and the inverse of the
   geometric thinning factor \(\Psi(R_+)/\Psi(R)\) is the same ratio.  Therefore
   the radius normalization and survival parts together contribute at most the
   factor in \((CPQ7)\), while the prefix is retained in the same score prefix.

   If no positive prefix exists, apply
   \cref{lem:star-prefix-weak-type-residual} with centers \(c_x\), radii
   \(R_+\), activations \(a_x^+\),
   \(\psi_x=e^{B_0\gamma^2}\Psi(R_+)\), \(\rho_x=\rho\), and the given
   \(b\)-dense cardinality family.  This is exactly \((CPQ9)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[High-correlation stars feed cap-centered paid prefixes]
   \label{cor:high-correlation-stars-feed-cap-prefix}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-paid-prefix-quadratic}.  Let
   \((\mathcal R,w_r,E_r)\) be a weighted high-correlation edge family with
   \(E_r\subseteq\mathcal X\times P\), whose normalized correlations are at
   least the same margin \(\gamma\):
   \[
      (x,p)\in E_r
      \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
      \ip{(x-o)/R}{(p-o)/R}\ge\gamma .
      \tag{HCP1}
   \]
   Let
   \[
      M_x(p)=\sum_{r:\,(x,p)\in E_r}w_r,
      \qquad
      U_{x,t}=\{p\in P:M_x(p)\ge t\}.
      \tag{HCP2}
   \]
   Assume the high-correlation multiplicity is lower-certified by the
   cap-centered paid degree:
   \[
      M_x(p)\le d_x^+(p)
      \qquad(x\in\mathcal X,\ p\in P).
      \tag{HCP3}
   \]
   Then each nonempty \(U_{x,t}\) is contained in the cap-centered child
   \(W_x\), and if
   \[
      t|U_{x,t}|
      >
      e^{B_0\gamma^2}\Psi(R_+)
      \left(
         A_x^+|U_{x,t}|^\rho
         +\sigma |U_{x,t}|^{1+\rho}
      \right),
      \tag{HCP4}
   \]
   the finite-cover verifier exposes a \((B_0+3)\)-quadratic local repair.

   Conversely, in a residual where no cap-centered paid prefix has positive
   reduced gain, every reported level satisfies the reverse inequality
   \[
      t|U_{x,t}|
      \le
      e^{B_0\gamma^2}\Psi(R_+)
      \left(
         A_x^+|U_{x,t}|^\rho
         +\sigma |U_{x,t}|^{1+\rho}
      \right).
      \tag{HCP5}
   \]

   In particular, suppose all positive multiplicities \(M_x(p)\) lie in
   \([M_{\min},M_{\max}]\), and let \(J\) be the dyadic dynamic range from
   \((HPS6)\).  Put
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\sum_pM_x(p).
      \tag{HCP6}
   \]
   If no cap-centered paid prefix fires, then there are a dyadic level \(t\)
   and center \(x\) for which
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      2|P|J\,e^{B_0\gamma^2}\Psi(R_+)
      \left(
         A_x^+|U_{x,t}|^\rho
         +\sigma |U_{x,t}|^{1+\rho}
      \right).
      \tag{HCP7}
   \]
   Equivalently, if every dyadic level whose layer-cake mass is at least
   \(\Lambda\) has cap-centered child price below \(\Lambda\), then either a
   quadratic repair fires or
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}\le2|P|J\Lambda .
      \tag{HCP8}
   \]

   Thus the high-correlation star layer-cake is now priced against the
   cap-centered child itself.  The residual obstruction is no longer an
   unpriced geometric star; it is the explicit price envelope \((HCP5)\) for all
   cap-centered paid levels.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The containment \(U_{x,t}\subseteq W_x\) is exactly the scaled cap-centered
   certificate \((CPS3)\) from
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-pair-star-reporter}, with
   \(\underline\theta=\gamma\).  If \(p\in U_{x,t}\), then
   \(d_x^+(p)\ge M_x(p)\ge t\) by \((HCP3)\).  Therefore, for
   \(K=|U_{x,t}|\), the top \(K\) points of \(W_x\) in the order of
   \(d_x^+\) have total paid degree at least \(t|U_{x,t}|\).  Inequality
   \((HCP4)\) is precisely the positive-prefix condition \((CPQ6)\), so
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-paid-prefix-quadratic} gives the quadratic repair.

   If no cap-centered paid prefix has positive reduced gain, then the top
   \(K=|U_{x,t}|\) paid-degree prefix has total degree at most its
   \(K\)-point price in \((CPQ6)\).  Since \(U_{x,t}\) has total paid degree at
   least \(t|U_{x,t}|\), \((HCP5)\) follows.

   For the dyadic statement, apply
   \cref{lem:high-correlation-pair-star-reporter} to the normalized edge family.
   It gives a dyadic center and level with
   \[
      t|U_{x,t}|\ge\frac{W_{\rm hi}}{2|P|J}.
   \]
   Combining this lower bound with \((HCP5)\) gives \((HCP7)\).  Finally, if
   \(W_{\rm hi}>2|P|J\Lambda\), the selected dyadic level has
   \(t|U_{x,t}|>\Lambda\); by the assumed price bound below \(\Lambda\),
   \((HCP4)\) holds and a quadratic repair fires.  The contrapositive is
   \((HCP8)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Clipped cap-centered high-correlation handoff]
   \label{cor:clipped-cap-centered-high-correlation-handoff}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-paid-prefix-quadratic}.  Let \(M_x(p)\ge0\) be any
   finite high-correlation star multiplicity supported on pairs satisfying
   \[
      M_x(p)>0
      \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
      \ip{(x-o)/R}{(p-o)/R}\ge\gamma .
      \tag{CCH1}
   \]
   Split it into the part already paid by the cap-centered near-pair degree and
   the overload
   \[
      M_x^{\rm pay}(p)=\min\{M_x(p),d_x^+(p)\},
      \qquad
      M_x^{\rm over}(p)=\bigl(M_x(p)-d_x^+(p)\bigr)_+ .
      \tag{CCH2}
   \]
   For \(t>0\), put
   \[
      U^{\rm pay}_{x,t}=\{p:M_x^{\rm pay}(p)\ge t\}.
      \tag{CCH3}
   \]
   Then each nonempty \(U^{\rm pay}_{x,t}\) is contained in the cap-centered
   child \(W_x\).  If
   \[
      t|U^{\rm pay}_{x,t}|
      >
      e^{B_0\gamma^2}\Psi(R_+)
      \left(
         A_x^+|U^{\rm pay}_{x,t}|^\rho
         +\sigma |U^{\rm pay}_{x,t}|^{1+\rho}
      \right),
      \tag{CCH4}
   \]
   then the finite-cover verifier exposes a \((B_0+3)\)-quadratic local repair.
   Conversely, if no cap-centered paid prefix has positive reduced gain, then
   every paid-clipped superlevel satisfies the reverse inequality in
   \((CCH4)\).

   In particular, let
   \[
      W_{\rm pay}=\sum_{x,p}M_x^{\rm pay}(p),
      \qquad
      W_{\rm over}=\sum_{x,p}M_x^{\rm over}(p),
      \qquad
      W_{\rm hi}=\sum_{x,p}M_x(p).
      \tag{CCH5}
   \]
   If all positive values of \(M_x^{\rm pay}(p)\) lie in
   \([M_{\min},M_{\max}]\), let
   \(J=1+\lceil\log_2(M_{\max}/M_{\min})\rceil\).  In a residual with no
   cap-centered paid-prefix repair, either \(W_{\rm pay}=0\), or there are a
   center \(x\) and dyadic level \(t\) for which
   \[
      W_{\rm pay}
      \le
      2|P|J\,e^{B_0\gamma^2}\Psi(R_+)
      \left(
         A_x^+|U^{\rm pay}_{x,t}|^\rho
         +\sigma |U^{\rm pay}_{x,t}|^{1+\rho}
      \right).
      \tag{CCH6}
   \]
   Equivalently, if every paid-clipped dyadic level with
   \(t|U^{\rm pay}_{x,t}|\ge\Lambda\) has cap-centered child price below
   \(\Lambda\), then either a quadratic repair fires or
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}\le W_{\rm over}+2|P|J\Lambda .
      \tag{CCH7}
   \]

   Thus the domination hypothesis in
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-stars-feed-cap-prefix} is not an all-or-nothing
   assumption: the dominated part of any high-correlation layer is automatically
   charged at the cap-centered child scale, and the only unpriced residue is the
   explicit overload \(W_{\rm over}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Form a weighted edge family whose records are the pairs \((x,p)\) with
   \(M_x^{\rm pay}(p)>0\), with edge set \(\{(x,p)\}\) and weight
   \(M_x^{\rm pay}(p)\).  Because \(M_x^{\rm pay}(p)>0\) implies \(M_x(p)>0\),
   the support condition \((CCH1)\) gives the high-correlation hypothesis
   \((HCP1)\).  The induced star multiplicity is exactly
   \(M_x^{\rm pay}(p)\), and by construction it is dominated by
   \(d_x^+(p)\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-stars-feed-cap-prefix} to this clipped family
   gives the containment, the repair criterion \((CCH4)\), and the no-repair
   reverse inequality.

   The dyadic statement is the final part of
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-stars-feed-cap-prefix} applied to the clipped
   multiplicities.  Finally
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      =
      \sum_{x,p}\min\{M_x(p),d_x^+(p)\}
      +
      \sum_{x,p}(M_x(p)-d_x^+(p))_+
      =
      W_{\rm pay}+W_{\rm over},
   \]
   so the threshold form gives \((CCH7)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cap-centered responsibility-to-prefix compiler]
   \label{cor:cap-centered-responsibility-prefix-compiler}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:clipped-cap-centered-high-correlation-handoff}.  Suppose a reporter
   supplies coefficients
   \[
      0\le\eta_{x,p,q}\le1
      \qquad(x\in\mathcal X,\ (p,q)\in\mathcal N)
      \tag{CRP1}
   \]
   supported only when \(p\in W_x\) and \((x,p)\) satisfies the
   high-correlation condition \((CCH1)\).  Define
   \[
      M_x^\eta(p)
      =
      \sum_{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
         \eta_{x,p,q}\,\alpha_{p,q}a_x^+(q).
      \tag{CRP2}
   \]
   Then \(M^\eta\) has zero overload:
   \[
      M_x^\eta(p)\le d_x^+(p)
      \qquad(x\in\mathcal X,\ p\in P).
      \tag{CRP3}
   \]
   Consequently every conclusion of
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-stars-feed-cap-prefix} applies to
   \(M^\eta\).  In particular, if the positive values of \(M_x^\eta(p)\) have
   dyadic range \(J_\eta\), then in a no-repair residual the total assigned
   high-correlation responsibility
   \[
      W_\eta=\sum_{x,p}M_x^\eta(p)
      \tag{CRP4}
   \]
   is either zero or is bounded by the cap-centered child price envelope
   \[
      W_\eta
      \le
      2|P|J_\eta\,e^{B_0\gamma^2}\Psi(R_+)
      \left(
         A_x^+|U^\eta_{x,t}|^\rho
         +\sigma |U^\eta_{x,t}|^{1+\rho}
      \right)
      \tag{CRP5}
   \]
   for some reported dyadic superlevel
   \(U^\eta_{x,t}=\{p:M_x^\eta(p)\ge t\}\).  If that price is below the
   selected layer mass, the same layer is a \((B_0+3)\)-quadratic repair.

   More generally, any nonnegative transport \(f_{x,p,q}\) supported on the
   same triples and satisfying, for some \(C>0\),
   \[
      f_{x,p,q}\le C\,\alpha_{p,q}a_x^+(q)
      \tag{CRP6}
   \]
   induces such responsibilities by
   \[
      \eta_{x,p,q}=
      \begin{cases}
      f_{x,p,q}/(C\,\alpha_{p,q}a_x^+(q)),
         &\alpha_{p,q}a_x^+(q)>0,\\
      0, &\alpha_{p,q}a_x^+(q)=0,
      \end{cases}
      \tag{CRP7}
   \]
   and the assigned responsibility mass is \(C^{-1}\sum_{x,p,q}f_{x,p,q}\).
   Hence a bounded-congestion high-correlation transport is already a
   cap-centered paid-prefix certificate; only the untransported overload remains
   outside the quadratic toll accounting.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(0\le\eta_{x,p,q}\le1\),
   \[
      M_x^\eta(p)
      \le
      \sum_{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\alpha_{p,q}a_x^+(q)
      =
      d_x^+(p),
   \]
   proving \((CRP3)\).  The support condition supplies \((CCH1)\), so
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-stars-feed-cap-prefix} applies directly to the
   multiplicities \(M^\eta\), giving \((CRP5)\) and the repair statement.

   If \(f\) satisfies \((CRP6)\), then the definition \((CRP7)\) gives
   \(0\le\eta_{x,p,q}\le1\) on every positive-capacity triple and zero
   otherwise.  Substituting \((CRP7)\) into \((CRP2)\) shows that
   \[
      \sum_{x,p}M_x^\eta(p)
      =
      \frac1C\sum_{x,p,q}f_{x,p,q},
   \]
   which proves the transport statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Cap-centered transport Hall normal form]
   \label{lem:cap-centered-transport-hall}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-responsibility-prefix-compiler}, and fix a
   congestion \(C>0\).  Let \(\mathcal I\) be a finite set of
   high-correlation atoms.  Each atom \(i\in\mathcal I\) has a point
   \(p_i\in P\), a weight \(b_i\ge0\), and a finite admissible center set
   \(\mathcal X_i\subseteq\mathcal X\), such that
   \[
      x\in\mathcal X_i
      \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
      p_i\in W_x
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      \ip{(x-o)/R}{(p_i-o)/R}\ge\gamma .
      \tag{CTH1}
   \]
   Define the capacity nodes
   \[
      \mathcal J
      =
      \{(x,p,q):x\in\mathcal X,\ p\in P,\ (p,q)\in\mathcal N\},
      \tag{CTH2}
   \]
   with capacities
   \[
      c_{x,p,q}=C\,\alpha_{p,q}a_x^+(q),
      \tag{CTH3}
   \]
   and join atom \(i\) to \((x,p,q)\in\mathcal J\) when
   \(p=p_i\), \(x\in\mathcal X_i\), and \(c_{x,p,q}>0\).  Let
   \(\Phi_C\) be the maximum value of a nonnegative flow
   \(h_{i,x,q}\) over these incidence edges satisfying
   \[
      \sum_{x,q}h_{i,x,q}\le b_i
      \qquad(i\in\mathcal I),
      \tag{CTH4}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{i:\,p_i=p,\ x\in\mathcal X_i}h_{i,x,q}
      \le c_{x,p,q}
      \qquad((x,p,q)\in\mathcal J).
      \tag{CTH5}
   \]
   For \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal I\), write \(N(\mathcal A)\) for the
   adjacent capacity nodes.  Then
   \[
      \Phi_C
      =
      \min_{\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal I}
      \left\{
         \sum_{i\in\mathcal I\setminus\mathcal A}b_i
         +
         \sum_{(x,p,q)\in N(\mathcal A)}
            C\,\alpha_{p,q}a_x^+(q)
      \right\}.
      \tag{CTH6}
   \]
   Consequently, for any \(0\le M_0\le B:=\sum_i b_i\), a
   cap-centered transport of mass at least \(M_0\) exists if and only if every
   atom subset \(\mathcal A\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{i\in\mathcal A}b_i
      \le
      C\sum_{(x,p,q)\in N(\mathcal A)}\alpha_{p,q}a_x^+(q)
      +
      B-M_0 .
      \tag{CTH7}
   \]
   Equivalently, if no transport of mass \(M_0\) exists, then some atom subset
   has Hall overload
   \[
      \sum_{i\in\mathcal A}b_i
      -
      C\sum_{(x,p,q)\in N(\mathcal A)}\alpha_{p,q}a_x^+(q)
      >
      B-M_0 .
      \tag{CTH8}
   \]

   Any feasible flow of value \(M\) aggregates to
   \[
      f_{x,p,q}
      =
      \sum_{i:\,p_i=p,\ x\in\mathcal X_i}h_{i,x,q},
      \tag{CTH9}
   \]
   which satisfies \((CRP6)\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-responsibility-prefix-compiler} converts the flow
   into a cap-centered responsibility assignment of total mass \(M/C\).  Under
   the dyadic and price hypotheses of that corollary, a sufficiently large
   transport either gives a \((B_0+3)\)-quadratic repair or is paid by the
   cap-centered child price envelope.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Build the finite network with a source edge of capacity \(b_i\) into each
   atom \(i\), infinite-capacity edges from atoms to their adjacent capacity
   nodes, and a sink edge of capacity \(c_{x,p,q}\) out of each capacity node.
   A finite source--sink cut is determined by the atom set
   \(\mathcal A\) left on the source side; all nodes in \(N(\mathcal A)\) must
   also lie on the source side.  The cheapest such cut has capacity
   \[
      \sum_{i\notin\mathcal A}b_i+\sum_{j\in N(\mathcal A)}c_j,
   \]
   which is \((CTH6)\) by max-flow/min-cut.  Rewriting
   \(\Phi_C\ge M_0\) with \(B=\sum_i b_i\) gives \((CTH7)\), and its negation
   gives \((CTH8)\).

   Finally, if \(h\) is feasible, then \((CTH5)\) gives
   \(f_{x,p,q}\le C\alpha_{p,q}a_x^+(q)\).  The adjacency condition and
   \((CTH1)\) give exactly the support required in
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-responsibility-prefix-compiler}.  Applying that
   corollary proves the responsibility and repair-envelope conclusions.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cap-centered overload dichotomy]
   \label{cor:cap-centered-overload-dichotomy}
   In the setting of \cref{lem:cap-centered-transport-hall}, fix an allowed
   unassigned tail \(0\le\Omega\le B\).  If every atom subset satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{i\in\mathcal A}b_i
      \le
      C\sum_{(x,p,q)\in N(\mathcal A)}\alpha_{p,q}a_x^+(q)
      +\Omega,
      \tag{COD1}
   \]
   then at least \(B-\Omega\) atom mass can be transported into cap-centered
   paid degrees, and therefore at least \((B-\Omega)/C\) responsibility mass is
   handled by the quadratic cap-prefix mechanism.  If \((COD1)\) fails, then
   the surviving obstruction is the explicit finite Hall cut
   \[
      \sum_{i\in\mathcal A}b_i
      >
      C\sum_{(x,p,q)\in N(\mathcal A)}\alpha_{p,q}a_x^+(q)
      +\Omega .
      \tag{COD2}
   \]

   Thus the overload term in
   \cref{cor:clipped-cap-centered-high-correlation-handoff} may be replaced by
   a finite cut-separation problem: either a bounded-congestion transport feeds
   the cap-centered paid-prefix verifier, or a particular atom subset has more
   high-correlation mass than its cap-centered paid neighborhood plus the
   permitted tail.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{lem:cap-centered-transport-hall} with \(M_0=B-\Omega\).  The
   Hall condition \((CTH7)\) is exactly \((COD1)\), while its failure is
   \((COD2)\).  The transported responsibility mass and the cap-prefix
   conclusion are the final paragraph of
   \cref{lem:cap-centered-transport-hall}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cap-centered Hall cuts reduce to pure overload stars]
   \label{cor:cap-centered-hall-overload-stars}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:cap-centered-overload-dichotomy}.  Suppose
   the Hall condition fails, so that an atom subset
   \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal I\) satisfies \((COD2)\).  Choose any selector
   \(s(i)\in\mathcal X_i\) for \(i\in\mathcal A\), and define the selected
   atom multiplicity
   \[
      B_x^s(p)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{i\in\mathcal A:\\ p_i=p,\ s(i)=x}} b_i .
      \tag{COS1}
   \]
   Its scaled cap-centered overload is
   \[
      O_x^s(p)
      =
      \left(\frac{B_x^s(p)}{C}-d_x^+(p)\right)_+ .
      \tag{COS2}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \sum_{x,p}O_x^s(p)>\frac{\Omega}{C}.
      \tag{COS3}
   \]
   Moreover, whenever \(O_x^s(p)>0\), the point \(p\) lies in the cap-centered
   child \(W_x\) and satisfies
   \[
      \ip{(x-o)/R}{(p-o)/R}\ge\gamma .
      \tag{COS4}
   \]

   If all positive overload values \(O_x^s(p)\) lie in
   \([O_{\min},O_{\max}]\), let
   \[
      J_{\rm over}
      =
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{O_{\max}}{O_{\min}}\right\rceil .
      \tag{COS5}
   \]
   Then there are a selected center \(x\) and a dyadic threshold \(t\) such that
   the pure overload star
   \[
      U^{\rm over}_{x,t}
      =
      \{p:O_x^s(p)\ge t\}
      \tag{COS6}
   \]
   is contained in \(W_x\) and obeys
   \[
      t|U^{\rm over}_{x,t}|
      >
      \frac{\Omega}{2C|\mathcal X|J_{\rm over}} .
      \tag{COS7}
   \]

   Thus a failed cap-centered transport is not an arbitrary overlap event.  It
   contains one ordinary cap-centered star on which the raw high-correlation
   atom load exceeds the entire cap-centered paid near-pair degree.  The next
   geometric separator may target these pure overload stars directly; if no
   such star has large layer-cake mass, the Hall cut could not have exceeded
   the allowed tail.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since the selected capacity nodes form a subset of \(N(\mathcal A)\),
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{x,p,q:\\ B_x^s(p)>0}}
         \alpha_{p,q}a_x^+(q)
      \le
      \sum_{(x,p,q)\in N(\mathcal A)}\alpha_{p,q}a_x^+(q).
      \tag{COS8}
   \]
   Combining \((COD2)\) with \((COS8)\) gives
   \[
      \frac1C\sum_{x,p}B_x^s(p)
      -
      \sum_{\substack{x,p:\\ B_x^s(p)>0}}d_x^+(p)
      >
      \frac{\Omega}{C}.
      \tag{COS9}
   \]
   The left side is at most
   \(\sum_{x,p}(B_x^s(p)/C-d_x^+(p))_+\), proving \((COS3)\).

   If \(O_x^s(p)>0\), then \(B_x^s(p)>0\), so some selected atom
   \(i\in\mathcal A\) has \(p_i=p\) and \(s(i)=x\).  The selector is admissible,
   hence \((CTH1)\) gives \(p\in W_x\) and the correlation certificate
   \((COS4)\).

   Finally apply the dyadic layer-cake argument from
   \cref{lem:high-correlation-pair-star-reporter} to the nonnegative
   multiplicities \(O_x^s(p)\), using \((COS3)\) for their total mass and
   averaging over the at most \(|\mathcal X|\) selected centers.  This gives
   \((COS7)\), and the containment in \(W_x\) follows from \((COS4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cap-centered overload cohorts are weighted storage occurrences]
   \label{cor:cap-centered-overload-weighted-storage}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:cap-centered-hall-overload-stars}, and fix a
   dyadic pure overload star \(U=U^{\rm over}_{x,t}\) supplied by that corollary.
   Suppose preprocessing canonicalizes this star to one recursive child
   \(\kappa=\kappa(x,U)\), with nonempty certified witness net
   \(A_\kappa\subseteq U\), tuple order \(k_\kappa\ge1\), and storage price
   \(u_\kappa\).  Let every selected atom \(i\in\mathcal A\) with
   \(s(i)=x\) and \(p_i\in U\) be a weighted occurrence of this same child,
   with occurrence weight \(b_i\).  Its weighted multiplicity is
   \[
      m_\kappa
      =
      \sum_{\substack{i\in\mathcal A:\\s(i)=x,\ p_i\in U}}b_i
      =
      \sum_{p\in U}B_x^s(p).
      \tag{COW1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      m_\kappa\ge C\,t|U|.
      \tag{COW2}
   \]
   Moreover, for every tuple
   \(\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_{k_\kappa})\), the total contribution of this
   overload cohort to the weighted reciprocal-multiplicity witness congestion is
   exactly
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{i\in\mathcal A:\\s(i)=x,\ p_i\in U}}
      \frac{b_i\,u_\kappa}
           {m_\kappa |A_\kappa|^{k_\kappa}}
      \mathbf 1\{a_j\in A_\kappa\ \forall j\}
      =
      \frac{u_\kappa}{|A_\kappa|^{k_\kappa}}
      \mathbf 1\{a_j\in A_\kappa\ \forall j\}.
      \tag{COW3}
   \]
   In the pair case \(k_\kappa=2\), if
   \(u_\kappa=\psi_\kappa|A_\kappa|^{1+\rho_\kappa}\) with
   \(0\le\rho_\kappa\le1\), this contribution is
   \[
      \psi_\kappa |A_\kappa|^{\rho_\kappa-1}
      \mathbf 1\{a_1,a_2\in A_\kappa\}
      \le
      \psi_\kappa\mathbf 1\{a_1,a_2\in A_\kappa\}.
      \tag{COW4}
   \]

   Consequently a pure overload star need not be materialized as
   \(m_\kappa\) integer recursive copies.  Once all such stars are
   canonicalized to shared children, the overload branch is governed by the
   weighted occurrence-discounted storage certificate of
   \cref{cor:weighted-occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage}: prove the resulting
   price-weighted tuple congestion envelopes, and the shared-DAG storage
   accounting charges each overload child once.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(p\in U\), then \(O_x^s(p)\ge t\).  By the definition \((COS2)\),
   \[
      \frac{B_x^s(p)}{C}-d_x^+(p)\ge t,
   \]
   and \(d_x^+(p)\ge0\).  Hence \(B_x^s(p)\ge Ct\).  Summing over \(p\in U\)
   gives \((COW2)\).

   For \((COW3)\), all selected occurrences in the cohort point to the same
   canonical child \(\kappa\).  Therefore the child, witness net, tuple order,
   and storage price are common, and
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{i\in\mathcal A:\\s(i)=x,\ p_i\in U}}
      \frac{b_i}{m_\kappa}=1.
   \]
   Multiplying by \(u_\kappa|A_\kappa|^{-k_\kappa}\) and by the common tuple
   indicator proves \((COW3)\).  The pair specialization is the substitution
   \(u_\kappa=\psi_\kappa|A_\kappa|^{1+\rho_\kappa}\); since
   \(|A_\kappa|\ge1\) and \(\rho_\kappa\le1\), the final inequality follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Weighted overload-cohort correlation split]
   \label{cor:weighted-overload-cohort-correlation-split}
   Let \(m\ge3\), \(P\subset\mathbb S^{D-1}\) with \(|P|\le m\), and let
   \(\mathcal C\) be a finite family of canonical overload children.  Fix
   constants \(A\ge0\) and \(K>0\).  A child \(\kappa\in\mathcal C\) has a
   fixed price weight \(\psi_\kappa\ge0\), a threshold \(T_\kappa\), a centered
   Gaussian cap label
   \(G_\kappa\sim N(0,I_D)\), and a retained witness set
   \(A_\kappa\subseteq P\) satisfying
   \[
      A_\kappa\subseteq
      U_\kappa:=\{x\in P:\ip{G_\kappa}{x}\ge T_\kappa\},
      \qquad
      T_\kappa^2\ge2\log m-A\log\log m .
      \tag{WOCS1}
   \]
   The price weights and thresholds are fixed when the cap first-moment bound is
   applied; random or adaptive prices are handled by first splitting into
   dyadic price classes.  Assume
   \[
      \Psi:=\sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal C}\psi_\kappa
      \le m^{1+\rho}\log^A m,
      \qquad 0\le\rho\le1 .
      \tag{WOCS2}
   \]
   Let
   \[
      \theta_m=K\frac{\log\log m}{\log m},
      \qquad 0<\theta_m\le\frac12 .
      \tag{WOCS3}
   \]
   For the pair-storage specialization of
   \cref{cor:weighted-occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage}, the contribution of
   these children is bounded by the price-weighted pair incidence
   \[
      \mathcal W_2
      =
      \sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal C}
      \psi_\kappa
      \sum_{a,b\in A_\kappa}1 .
      \tag{WOCS4}
   \]
   Split this incidence into
   \[
      \mathcal W_{\rm lo}
      =
      \sum_{\kappa}
      \psi_\kappa
      \sum_{\substack{a,b\in A_\kappa:\\ \ip{a}{b}\le\theta_m}}1,
      \qquad
      \mathcal W_{\rm hi}=\mathcal W_2-\mathcal W_{\rm lo}.
      \tag{WOCS5}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \E\,\mathcal W_{\rm lo}
      \le
      m^{1+\rho}\log^{2A+2K+1}m .
      \tag{WOCS6}
   \]

   For any fixed realized panel, define the high-correlation multiplicities
   \[
      M_a(b)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{\kappa\in\mathcal C:\\
         a,b\in A_\kappa,\ \ip{a}{b}>\theta_m}}
      \psi_\kappa ,
      \qquad
      \mathcal W_{\rm hi}=\sum_{a,b\in P}M_a(b).
      \tag{WOCS7}
   \]
   If \(\mathcal W_{\rm hi}=0\), put \(J_{\rm hi}=1\).  Otherwise suppose the
   positive values of \(M_a(b)\) lie in \([M_{\min},M_{\max}]\), and put
   \[
      J_{\rm hi}=
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{M_{\max}}{M_{\min}}\right\rceil .
      \tag{WOCS8}
   \]
   For every scale \(\Lambda>0\), either
   \[
      \mathcal W_{\rm hi}\le2mJ_{\rm hi}\Lambda,
      \tag{WOCS9}
   \]
   or there are a center \(a\in P\) and a dyadic level \(t\) such that
   \[
      V_{a,t}:=\{b\in P:M_a(b)\ge t\}
      \subseteq
      B\!\left(\theta_m a,\sqrt{1-\theta_m^2}\right)
      \tag{WOCS10}
   \]
   and
   \[
      t|V_{a,t}|\ge\Lambda .
      \tag{WOCS11}
   \]

   Consequently, after reciprocal weighted multiplicity has canonicalized each
   overload cohort to one shared child as in
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-overload-weighted-storage}, the storage proof has no
   separate integer-materialization branch: low-correlation pair congestion is
   paid by \((WOCS6)\), while any unbudgeted high-correlation congestion is a
   cap-centered smaller-radius star \((WOCS10)\)--\((WOCS11)\) that must be
   submitted to the paid-prefix verifier or to the shared-child tuple-congestion
   certificate.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   In the pair specialization, a canonical child with storage price
   \(u_\kappa=\psi_\kappa|A_\kappa|^{1+\rho_\kappa}\) contributes at most
   \(\psi_\kappa\mathbf 1\{a,b\in A_\kappa\}\) to any ordered pair
   \((a,b)\), because \(|A_\kappa|^{\rho_\kappa-1}\le1\).  This is exactly the
   reduction in \((COW4)\) and \((WODT4)\), giving \((WOCS4)\).

   Let
   \[
      E_{\rm lo}=\{(a,b)\in P\times P:\ip{a}{b}\le\theta_m\}.
   \]
   Since \(A_\kappa\subseteq U_\kappa\),
   \[
      \mathcal W_{\rm lo}
      \le
      \sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal C}\psi_\kappa
      \sum_{(a,b)\in E_{\rm lo}}
      \mathbf 1\{a,b\in U_\kappa\}.
   \]
   Taking expectation over the cap labels and applying
   \cref{cor:weighted-polylog-low-correlation-coload} with weights
   \(w_\kappa=\psi_\kappa\) proves \((WOCS6)\).

   If \(\mathcal W_{\rm hi}=0\), then \((WOCS9)\) is immediate.  Otherwise
   apply
   \cref{lem:high-correlation-pair-star-reporter} to the weighted edge family
   whose records are the children \(\kappa\), whose edge set is
   \[
      E_\kappa^{\rm hi}
      =
      \{(a,b)\in A_\kappa\times A_\kappa:\ip{a}{b}>\theta_m\},
   \]
   and whose record weight is \(\psi_\kappa\).  The total incidence in
   \((HPS2)\) is \(\mathcal W_{\rm hi}\), and every retained edge has
   correlation at least \(\theta_m\).  If
   \(\mathcal W_{\rm hi}>2mJ_{\rm hi}\Lambda\), \((HPS7)\) gives a dyadic
   superlevel with \(t|V_{a,t}|>\Lambda\).  The cap-centered containment
   \((WOCS10)\) is \((CPS1)\) from
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-pair-star-reporter}.  The contrapositive gives
   \((WOCS9)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cap-prefix pricing of overload-cohort high stars]
   \label{cor:overload-cohort-cap-prefix-tail}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:weighted-overload-cohort-correlation-split}.  Assume in addition
   that the local filter-cover instance satisfies
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-paid-prefix-quadratic} with \(o=0\), \(R=1\),
   \(\gamma=\theta_m\), and with all centers \(a\in P\) available.  Thus
   \[
      c_a=\theta_m a,
      \qquad
      R_+=\sqrt{1-\theta_m^2},
      \qquad
      W_a=P\cap B(c_a,R_+),
      \tag{OCPT1}
   \]
   with activation \(a_a^+\), paid degree \(d_a^+(b)\), and query price
   \(A_a^+\) as in \((CPQ3)\)--\((CPQ5)\).

   Let \(M_a(b)\) be the high-correlation multiplicity from \((WOCS7)\), and
   split it by the cap-centered paid degree:
   \[
      M_a^{\rm pay}(b)=\min\{M_a(b),d_a^+(b)\},
      \qquad
      M_a^{\rm over}(b)=\bigl(M_a(b)-d_a^+(b)\bigr)_+ .
      \tag{OCPT2}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      \mathcal W_{\rm over}=\sum_{a,b}M_a^{\rm over}(b).
      \tag{OCPT3}
   \]
   If \(M^{\rm pay}\equiv0\), put \(J_{\rm pay}=1\).  Otherwise assume the
   positive values of \(M_a^{\rm pay}(b)\) lie in a certified dyadic range with
   dynamic-range factor \(J_{\rm pay}\).  Fix a scale \(\Lambda>0\).  Suppose
   that every paid-clipped dyadic level
   \[
      U_{a,t}^{\rm pay}=\{b:M_a^{\rm pay}(b)\ge t\}
      \tag{OCPT4}
   \]
   with \(t|U_{a,t}^{\rm pay}|\ge\Lambda\) has cap-centered child price below
   \(\Lambda\):
   \[
      e^{B_0\theta_m^2}\Psi(R_+)
      \left(
         A_a^+|U_{a,t}^{\rm pay}|^\rho
         +\sigma |U_{a,t}^{\rm pay}|^{1+\rho}
      \right)
      <\Lambda .
      \tag{OCPT5}
   \]
   Then either a \((B_0+3)\)-quadratic cap-centered paid-prefix repair fires, or
   the realized high-correlation pair congestion obeys
   \[
      \mathcal W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \mathcal W_{\rm over}+2mJ_{\rm pay}\Lambda .
      \tag{OCPT6}
   \]
   Consequently, in a no-repair residual satisfying \((OCPT5)\),
   \[
      \E\,\mathcal W_2
      \le
      m^{1+\rho}\log^{2A+2K+1}m
      +
      \E\,\mathcal W_{\rm over}
      +
      2mJ_{\rm pay}\Lambda .
      \tag{OCPT7}
   \]

   Thus the high-correlation side of a certified overload cohort has only one
   unpaid component after cap-prefix verification: the explicit cap-centered
   overload \(\mathcal W_{\rm over}\).  That is the same object routed by
   \cref{lem:cap-centered-transport-hall} and
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-overload-weighted-storage}; the low and cap-paid
   parts no longer require a separate branching analysis.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(M_a(b)>0\), then \((a,b)\) appears in the high-correlation edge set of
   some overload child, so \(\ip{a}{b}>\theta_m\).  By
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-pair-star-reporter} with
   \(\underline\theta=\theta_m\), this implies \(b\in W_a\).  Hence the support
   condition \((CCH1)\) holds for the multiplicities \(M_a(b)\).

   Apply \cref{cor:clipped-cap-centered-high-correlation-handoff} to these
   multiplicities with margin \(\gamma=\theta_m\).  Its threshold form
   \((CCH7)\), together with the price condition \((OCPT5)\), says exactly that
   either a \((B_0+3)\)-quadratic repair fires or
   \[
      \mathcal W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \mathcal W_{\rm over}+2|P|J_{\rm pay}\Lambda .
   \]
   Since \(|P|\le m\), this gives \((OCPT6)\).

   Finally \(\mathcal W_2=\mathcal W_{\rm lo}+\mathcal W_{\rm hi}\).  In a
   no-repair residual satisfying \((OCPT5)\), combine \((OCPT6)\) with the
   low-correlation expectation bound \((WOCS6)\) and take expectation over the
   cap labels.  This proves \((OCPT7)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Overload-cohort tail is a Hall cut]
   \label{cor:overload-cohort-tail-hall-cut}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:overload-cohort-cap-prefix-tail}, and atomize the high-correlation
   incidences of the canonical overload children as follows.  For every
   \(\kappa\in\mathcal C\) and every
   \[
      (a,b)\in A_\kappa\times A_\kappa,
      \qquad
      \ip{a}{b}>\theta_m,
   \]
   create an atom \(i=(\kappa,a,b)\) with point \(p_i=b\), weight
   \(b_i=\psi_\kappa\), and singleton admissible center set
   \(\mathcal X_i=\{a\}\).  Use congestion \(C=1\) in
   \cref{lem:cap-centered-transport-hall}.  Then the atom system satisfies the
   cap-centered Hall hypotheses, and the atom subset
   \[
      \mathcal A_{\rm over}
      =
      \{(\kappa,a,b):a,b\in A_\kappa,\ \ip{a}{b}>\theta_m,
        M_a(b)>d_a^+(b)\}
      \tag{OCH1}
   \]
   has Hall excess exactly
   \[
      \sum_{i\in\mathcal A_{\rm over}}b_i
      -
      \sum_{(a,b,q)\in N(\mathcal A_{\rm over})}
         \alpha_{b,q}a_a^+(q)
      =
      \mathcal W_{\rm over}.
      \tag{OCH2}
   \]
   Consequently, for every \(0\le\Omega<\mathcal W_{\rm over}\), the Hall
   condition \((COD1)\) fails with allowed tail \(\Omega\).

   If the positive values of
   \[
      O_a(b):=\bigl(M_a(b)-d_a^+(b)\bigr)_+
      \tag{OCH3}
   \]
   lie in a certified range \([O_{\min},O_{\max}]\), and
   \[
      J_{\rm over}
      =
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{O_{\max}}{O_{\min}}\right\rceil ,
      \tag{OCH4}
   \]
   then there are a center \(a\in P\) and dyadic level \(t\) such that the pure
   overload star
   \[
      U_{a,t}^{\rm over}=\{b:O_a(b)\ge t\}
      \tag{OCH5}
   \]
   is contained in \(W_a\) and obeys
   \[
      t|U_{a,t}^{\rm over}|
      >
      \frac{\Omega}{2mJ_{\rm over}} .
      \tag{OCH6}
   \]
   If this star is canonicalized to one shared child, then
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-overload-weighted-storage} applies to the selected
   weighted atoms with no integer expansion: the cohort contributes one child
   storage price to the reciprocal weighted tuple-congestion certificate.

   Thus the \(\mathcal W_{\rm over}\) term in \((OCPT7)\) is not a new storage
   phenomenon.  It is exactly the Hall-cut excess whose dyadic witnesses are the
   pure overload stars already routed to the weighted shared-DAG storage
   theorem.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If an atom \(i=(\kappa,a,b)\) is present, then \(M_a(b)>0\).  The proof of
   \cref{cor:overload-cohort-cap-prefix-tail} shows that \(b\in W_a\), and
   \(\ip{a}{b}>\theta_m\) is the required cap-centered correlation certificate
   for \(\gamma=\theta_m\).  Hence \((CTH1)\) holds with
   \(\mathcal X_i=\{a\}\).

   For a fixed overloaded pair \((a,b)\), all atoms
   \((\kappa,a,b)\in\mathcal A_{\rm over}\) have total weight \(M_a(b)\).  Their
   neighboring capacity nodes are exactly the triples \((a,b,q)\) with
   \((b,q)\in\mathcal N\) and \(a_a^+(q)>0\); their total capacity is
   \[
      \sum_{q:(b,q)\in\mathcal N}\alpha_{b,q}a_a^+(q)=d_a^+(b).
   \]
   Summing over overloaded pairs proves \((OCH2)\), because non-overloaded
   pairs do not appear in \(\mathcal A_{\rm over}\).  If
   \(\Omega<\mathcal W_{\rm over}\), then \((COD1)\) is violated by
   \(\mathcal A_{\rm over}\).

   Apply \cref{cor:cap-centered-overload-dichotomy} and then
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-hall-overload-stars} to this failed Hall cut, with
   the canonical selector \(s(i)=a\).  Since the available center set is
   \(P\), \(|\mathcal X|\le m\), and the scaled overload \(O_x^s(p)\) in
   \((COS2)\) is precisely \(O_a(b)\).  This gives \((OCH5)\)--\((OCH6)\).
   The final storage statement is exactly
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-overload-weighted-storage} for the resulting pure
   overload star.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact storage closure for Hall-tail overload stars]
   \label{cor:hall-tail-overload-exact-storage}
   Work in the pair specialization of
   \cref{cor:weighted-occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage} and in the setting of
   \cref{cor:overload-cohort-tail-hall-cut}.  For each build seed \(z\), let
   \(\mathcal S_z\) be a finite family of dyadic pure overload stars produced
   by the Hall-tail separator and canonicalized to shared children.  A star
   \(s\in\mathcal S_z\) has a canonical child \(\kappa_{z,s}\).  Each
   distinct child \(\kappa\in\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}\) has a nonempty witness
   net \(A_{z,\kappa}\subseteq P\) and storage price
   \[
      u_{z,\kappa}
      =
      \psi_{z,\kappa}|A_{z,\kappa}|^{1+\rho_{z,\kappa}},
      \qquad 0\le\rho_{z,\kappa}\le1 .
      \tag{HTS1}
   \]
   The Hall atoms selected by \(s\) are weighted occurrences of
   \(\kappa_{z,s}\), with their Hall weights as occurrence weights, exactly as
   in \cref{cor:cap-centered-overload-weighted-storage}.  Let
   \(\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}\) be the distinct canonical children that occur
   after grouping all these weighted occurrences.

   Define the exact Hall-tail pair load
   \[
      L_z^{\rm tail}(x,y)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{\kappa\in\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}:\\
         x,y\in A_{z,\kappa}}}
      \psi_{z,\kappa}|A_{z,\kappa}|^{\rho_{z,\kappa}-1}.
      \tag{HTS2}
   \]
   Then the weighted occurrence-discounted pair congestion of all Hall-tail
   stars is exactly \(L_z^{\rm tail}(x,y)\).  In particular,
   \[
      \sum_{x,y\in P}L_z^{\rm tail}(x,y)
      =
      \sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}}u_{z,\kappa}.
      \tag{HTS3}
   \]
   Hence, if
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \E_z\sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}}u_{z,\kappa}
      \le aS
      \tag{HTS4}
   \]
   under the active first-moment hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:weighted-occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage}, then the Hall-tail
   overload stars satisfy the weighted tuple-storage certificate.  Equivalently,
   the remaining Hall-tail storage theorem is only the distinct-child price
   bound \((HTS4)\): reciprocal weighted multiplicity and uniform pair witnesses
   already supply all pair envelopes.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix \(z\) and a tuple \((x,y)\).  By
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-overload-weighted-storage}, every weighted occurrence
   belonging to a pure overload star contributes to the weighted
   occurrence-discounted pair congestion exactly as an occurrence of its
   canonical child, divided by that child's total weighted multiplicity.  After
   grouping occurrences by canonical child, the total contribution of any
   \(\kappa\in\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}\) containing \(x,y\) is therefore
   \[
      \frac{u_{z,\kappa}}{|A_{z,\kappa}|^2}
      =
      \psi_{z,\kappa}|A_{z,\kappa}|^{\rho_{z,\kappa}-1},
   \]
   and it is zero if \(x\) or \(y\) is not in \(A_{z,\kappa}\).  This proves
   \((HTS2)\) as the exact congestion envelope.

   Summing \((HTS2)\) over ordered pairs gives
   \[
      \sum_{x,y\in P}L_z^{\rm tail}(x,y)
      =
      \sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}}
      \psi_{z,\kappa}|A_{z,\kappa}|^{\rho_{z,\kappa}-1}
      |A_{z,\kappa}|^2
      =
      \sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}}u_{z,\kappa},
   \]
   proving \((HTS3)\).  Taking
   \(J^{\rm tail}(x,y)=\E_zL_z^{\rm tail}(x,y)\), condition \((HTS4)\) is
   exactly \((WODT3)\), and the first paragraph supplies \((WODT2)\).  Thus
   \cref{cor:weighted-occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage} proves feasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Benefit-priced Hall-tail materialization]
   \label{cor:benefit-priced-hall-tail-materialization}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:hall-tail-overload-exact-storage}.  For each seed \(z\), suppose
   every materialized Hall-tail star \(s\in\mathcal S_z\) carries a finite
   selected Hall-atom cohort \(\mathcal I_{z,s}\), with atom weights
   \(b_{z,i}>0\), and points to its canonical child \(\kappa_{z,s}\).  Put
   \[
      \mu_{z,s}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{z,s}}b_{z,i},
      \qquad
      M_z^{\rm tail}(\kappa)
      =
      \sum_{s:\,\kappa_{z,s}=\kappa}\mu_{z,s}.
      \tag{HBP1}
   \]
   Suppose the canonicalizer materializes only benefit-priced children: for
   some \(\beta\ge1\),
   \[
      u_{z,\kappa}\le \beta M_z^{\rm tail}(\kappa)
      \qquad(\kappa\in\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}).
      \tag{HBP2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \beta\,\E_z\sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}}
         M_z^{\rm tail}(\kappa)
      \le aS
      \tag{HBP3}
   \]
   under the active first-moment hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:weighted-occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage}, then the Hall-tail
   overload stars satisfy the weighted tuple-storage certificate.

   In particular, it is enough that every distinct child \(\kappa\) have a
   sponsoring star \(s(\kappa)\) with \(\kappa_{z,s(\kappa)}=\kappa\) and
   \[
      u_{z,\kappa}\le \beta\mu_{z,s(\kappa)}.
      \tag{HBP4}
   \]
   For a pure overload star supplied by
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-overload-weighted-storage}, the checkable sufficient
   condition
   \[
      u_{z,\kappa_{z,s}}\le
      \beta\, C_s\,t_s\,|U_s|
      \tag{HBP5}
   \]
   implies \((HBP4)\), where \(C_s,t_s,U_s\) are the congestion constant,
   dyadic overload level, and star update set in \((COW2)\).

   Finally, if the selected cohorts have overlap at most \(\chi_z\) against a
   seedwise Hall-tail atom mass \(\mathsf H_z\),
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}}M_z^{\rm tail}(\kappa)
      =
      \sum_{s\in\mathcal S_z}\mu_{z,s}
      \le \chi_z\mathsf H_z,
      \tag{HBP6}
   \]
   then \((HBP3)\) follows from
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+\beta\,\E_z[\chi_z\mathsf H_z]\le aS .
      \tag{HBP7}
   \]
   Thus the Hall-tail storage target can be enforced by a build-time rule:
   retain only stars whose recursive child price is sponsored by their own
   Hall mass, and prove a bounded-overlap estimate for the retained cohorts.
   Any remaining obstruction is an unsupported child with
   \(u_{z,\kappa}>\beta M_z^{\rm tail}(\kappa)\), not an integer
   materialization or pair-envelope failure.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \((HBP2)\),
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}}u_{z,\kappa}
      \le
      \beta\sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}}M_z^{\rm tail}(\kappa).
   \]
   Taking expectation and using \((HBP3)\) gives \((HTS4)\), so
   \cref{cor:hall-tail-overload-exact-storage} applies.

   If \((HBP4)\) holds, then
   \(M_z^{\rm tail}(\kappa)\ge\mu_{z,s(\kappa)}\), so \((HBP2)\) follows.  For
   a pure overload star, \((COW2)\) gives
   \(\mu_{z,s}\ge C_s t_s|U_s|\); hence \((HBP5)\) implies \((HBP4)\).
   The bounded-overlap implication is just the substitution of \((HBP6)\) into
   \((HBP3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Disjoint sponsored Hall-tail schedule]
   \label{cor:disjoint-sponsored-hall-tail-schedule}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:benefit-priced-hall-tail-materialization}.  For each seed \(z\),
   let \(\mathcal I_z^{\rm tail}\) be the Hall-tail atom pool with weights
   \(b_{z,i}\), and write
   \[
      \mathsf H_z=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_z^{\rm tail}}b_{z,i}.
      \tag{DHS1}
   \]
   Suppose the materializer assigns to every retained star \(s\in\mathcal S_z\)
   a sponsor cohort
   \[
      \mathcal I_{z,s}\subseteq\mathcal I_z^{\rm tail},
      \qquad
      \mu_{z,s}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{z,s}}b_{z,i},
      \tag{DHS2}
   \]
   and these cohorts are pairwise disjoint.  Suppose also that every distinct
   retained child is benefit-sponsored by the retained cohorts,
   \[
      u_{z,\kappa}\le
      \beta\sum_{s:\,\kappa_{z,s}=\kappa}\mu_{z,s}
      \qquad(\kappa\in\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}).
      \tag{DHS3}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+\beta\,\E_z\mathsf H_z\le aS
      \tag{DHS4}
   \]
   under the active first-moment hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:weighted-occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage}, then the Hall-tail
   overload stars satisfy the weighted tuple-storage certificate.

   Equivalently, a build may use the following safe rule.  Maintain unused
   Hall-tail atoms.  Retain a candidate star only when it can reserve an unused
   sponsor cohort whose mass certifies \((DHS3)\) for its canonical child, and
   then remove that cohort from the unused pool.  This rule has overlap one.
   If it cannot retain a candidate child, the residual obstruction is explicit:
   that child has recursive price larger than \(\beta\) times its available
   unused Hall sponsor mass.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Pairwise disjointness gives
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}}M_z^{\rm tail}(\kappa)
      =
      \sum_{s\in\mathcal S_z}\mu_{z,s}
      \le
      \mathsf H_z .
   \]
   Thus \((HBP6)\) holds with \(\chi_z=1\).  Condition \((DHS3)\) is exactly
   \((HBP2)\), and \((DHS4)\) is \((HBP7)\) with \(\chi_z=1\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:benefit-priced-hall-tail-materialization} proves the storage
   certificate.

   The greedy rule constructs pairwise disjoint cohorts by removing every
   reserved sponsor cohort from the unused pool.  If a candidate child cannot be
   retained by this rule, the negation of its retention test is precisely the
   final displayed unsupported-child condition.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fractional sponsor Hall cut]
   \label{cor:fractional-sponsor-hall-cut}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:hall-tail-overload-exact-storage}.  For each seed \(z\), let
   \(\mathcal I_z^{\rm tail}\) be a finite Hall-tail atom pool with weights
   \(b_{z,i}>0\), and let
   \[
      \mathsf H_z=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_z^{\rm tail}}b_{z,i}.
      \tag{FHC1}
   \]
   Let \(\mathcal E_z\subseteq
   \mathcal I_z^{\rm tail}\times\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}\) be the certified
   compatibility relation saying which Hall atoms may sponsor which retained
   child.  Fix \(\beta\ge1\), and define the child sponsor demand
   \[
      d_{z,\kappa}=u_{z,\kappa}/\beta .
      \tag{FHC2}
   \]
   The following are equivalent.

   First, there is a fractional sponsor assignment
   \(h_{z,i,\kappa}\ge0\), supported on \(\mathcal E_z\), such that
   \[
      \sum_{i:\,(i,\kappa)\in\mathcal E_z}h_{z,i,\kappa}
      \ge d_{z,\kappa}
      \qquad(\kappa\in\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}),
      \tag{FHC3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa:\,(i,\kappa)\in\mathcal E_z}h_{z,i,\kappa}
      \le b_{z,i}
      \qquad(i\in\mathcal I_z^{\rm tail}).
      \tag{FHC4}
   \]
   Second, every child subset \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}\)
   satisfies the sponsor Hall inequality
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal U}d_{z,\kappa}
      \le
      \sum_{i\in N_z(\mathcal U)}b_{z,i},
      \qquad
      N_z(\mathcal U)=
      \{i:\exists\kappa\in\mathcal U,\ (i,\kappa)\in\mathcal E_z\}.
      \tag{FHC5}
   \]
   If the equivalent conditions hold and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+\beta\,\E_z\mathsf H_z\le aS
      \tag{FHC6}
   \]
   under the active first-moment hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:weighted-occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage}, then the Hall-tail
   overload stars satisfy the weighted tuple-storage certificate.

   If the equivalent conditions fail, there is an explicit sponsor cut
   \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}\) such that
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal U}u_{z,\kappa}
      >
      \beta\sum_{i\in N_z(\mathcal U)}b_{z,i}.
      \tag{FHC7}
   \]
   Thus failure of disjoint sponsorship is itself a finite Hall obstruction:
   some retained child set has more recursive storage price than the total
   compatible Hall mass available to sponsor it.  Since the atoms are weighted,
   any feasible fractional assignment can be implemented by splitting atom
   weights, with no integer materialization loss.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Build the finite network with a source edge of capacity \(b_{z,i}\) into each
   atom \(i\), infinite-capacity edges from \(i\) to \(\kappa\) whenever
   \((i,\kappa)\in\mathcal E_z\), and a sink edge of capacity
   \(d_{z,\kappa}\) out of each child \(\kappa\).  A flow saturating all child
   sink edges is exactly an assignment satisfying \((FHC3)\)--\((FHC4)\).

   By max-flow/min-cut, such a flow exists iff every finite cut has capacity at
   least \(\sum_\kappa d_{z,\kappa}\).  A finite cut is determined by the child
   set \(\mathcal U\) left on the sink side; all atoms in \(N_z(\mathcal U)\)
   must also lie on that side to avoid infinite crossing edges.  Rewriting the
   cut inequality gives exactly \((FHC5)\).  Failure of \((FHC5)\), after
   multiplying by \(\beta\), is \((FHC7)\).

   If the assignment exists, then
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}}u_{z,\kappa}
      =
      \beta\sum_{\kappa}d_{z,\kappa}
      \le
      \beta\sum_i b_{z,i}
      =
      \beta\mathsf H_z .
   \]
   Taking expectation and using \((FHC6)\) gives \((HTS4)\), so
   \cref{cor:hall-tail-overload-exact-storage} proves the storage certificate.
   Splitting a weighted atom according to the finitely many positive outgoing
   flow values realizes the fractional assignment as weighted sponsor records.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sponsor-cut generated-column screen]
   \label{cor:sponsor-cut-generated-column-screen}
   Work with a failed sponsor cut
   \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}\) from
   \cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-hall-cut}, and write its excess as
   \[
      E_z(\mathcal U)
      =
      \sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal U}u_{z,\kappa}
      -
      \beta\sum_{i\in N_z(\mathcal U)}b_{z,i}
      >0 .
      \tag{SGC1}
   \]
   Let \(\mathcal T\) be any finite family of generated compression templates
   for these retained children.  A template \(T\in\mathcal T\) has a finite
   child container \(\mathcal C_T\subseteq\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}\),
   nonnegative capture weights \(g_{T,\kappa}\le u_{z,\kappa}\), available
   cardinalities \(\mathcal K_T\), and certified prices
   \(\overline P_T(K)\).  Assume that for every
   \(K\in\mathcal K_T\) and \(V\subseteq\mathcal C_T\) with \(|V|=K\),
   preprocessing can materialize a generated retained column \(A(T,V)\) whose
   one-time recursive storage price is at most \(\overline P_T(K)\) and whose
   capture of the cut is at least
   \[
      G_T(V;\mathcal U)
      =
      \sum_{\kappa\in V\cap\mathcal U}g_{T,\kappa}.
      \tag{SGC2}
   \]
   Order \(\mathcal C_T\) by nonincreasing
   \(g_{T,\kappa}\mathbf 1_{\{\kappa\in\mathcal U\}}\).  If for some \(T\) and
   \(K\in\mathcal K_T\) the top prefix \(V_K\) satisfies
   \[
      G_T(V_K;\mathcal U)>2\overline P_T(K),
      \tag{SGC3}
   \]
   then \(A(T,V_K)\) is a positive generated column for the sponsor-cut
   residual: it removes more than twice its retained recursive price from the
   left side of the cut.  Equivalently, after paying for this column once, the
   cut excess drops by at least
   \(G_T(V_K;\mathcal U)-\overline P_T(K)>0\).

   Conversely, if no generated prefix satisfies \((SGC3)\), then every
   compatible assigned cover \(L=\bigsqcup_jL_j\) of any child subset
   \(L\subseteq\mathcal U\) by template copies \(T_j\), with
   \(L_j\subseteq\mathcal C_{T_j}\), \(|L_j|\in\mathcal K_{T_j}\), and
   \(g_{T_j,\kappa}\ge w_\kappa\) on \(L_j\), obeys
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa\in L}w_\kappa
      \le
      2\sum_j\overline P_{T_j}(|L_j|).
      \tag{SGC4}
   \]
   In particular, suppose all used templates satisfy the common price envelope
   \[
      \overline P_T(K)
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(AK^\rho+\zeta K^{1+\rho}\right),
      \qquad 0<\rho<1,
      \tag{SGC5}
   \]
   and a layer \(L\subseteq\mathcal U\) has weights
   \(w_\kappa\ge\theta>0\).  If \(L\) is coverable by \(J\) such generated
   template copies, then every no-generated-column sponsor residual satisfies
   \[
      \theta |L|
      \le
      2\psi_\star\left(AJ^{1-\rho}|L|^\rho+\zeta |L|^{1+\rho}\right).
      \tag{SGC6}
   \]
   Hence a sponsor cut can survive generated-column search only through the
   same metric-entropy obstruction as
   \cref{cor:no-cell-metric-cover-screen}: any dyadic child-price layer whose
   generated cover violates \((SGC6)\) already contains a verified positive
   top-prefix column.  The remaining geometric task is therefore to prove that
   strong sponsor cuts always have such a low-price generated cover, or else
   that their high-entropy residual is separated by the spherical branch.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For fixed \(T\) and \(K\), the top \(K\) prefix maximizes
   \(G_T(V;\mathcal U)\) over all \(K\)-subsets of \(\mathcal C_T\).  If
   \((SGC3)\) holds, the materialized column captures cut
   demand \(G_T(V_K;\mathcal U)\) and costs at most \(\overline P_T(K)\).
   Replacing that captured portion by the generated column changes the cut
   balance by at most
   \[
      -G_T(V_K;\mathcal U)+\overline P_T(K)<0,
   \]
   so the column has positive reduced gain against the cut residual.  The
   stronger factor \(2\) is kept to match the one-sided shared-capture screens.

   If no prefix satisfies \((SGC3)\), then for each assigned part \(L_j\) the
   top \(|L_j|\) prefix of \(T_j\) has capture at least
   \(\sum_{\kappa\in L_j}w_\kappa\).  Since \((SGC3)\) fails for that prefix,
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa\in L_j}w_\kappa
      \le
      2\overline P_{T_j}(|L_j|).
   \]
   Summing over \(j\) gives \((SGC4)\).  Under \((SGC5)\), Hölder's inequality
   gives
   \[
      \sum_j |L_j|^\rho\le J^{1-\rho}|L|^\rho,
      \qquad
      \sum_j |L_j|^{1+\rho}\le |L|^{1+\rho}.
   \]
   If \(w_\kappa\ge\theta\) on \(L\), then
   \(\theta|L|\le\sum_{\kappa\in L}w_\kappa\).  Substitution in \((SGC4)\)
   proves \((SGC6)\).  The final sentence is the contrapositive and is the
   sponsor-cut specialization of
   \cref{cor:dyadic-shared-capture-top-prefix-compiler} and
   \cref{cor:no-cell-metric-cover-screen}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sponsor cuts either inflate or expose one layer]
   \label{cor:sponsor-cut-inflate-or-layer}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-hall-cut}.  For
   \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}\), write
   \[
      P_z(\mathcal U)=\sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal U}u_{z,\kappa},
      \qquad
      B_z(\mathcal U)=\sum_{i\in N_z(\mathcal U)}b_{z,i},
      \qquad
      E_z^\beta(\mathcal U)=P_z(\mathcal U)-\beta B_z(\mathcal U).
      \tag{SCL1}
   \]
   Fix \(0<\varepsilon<1\), and put
   \[
      \beta_\varepsilon=\frac{\beta}{1-\varepsilon}.
      \tag{SCL2}
   \]
   If every child subset satisfies
   \[
      E_z^\beta(\mathcal U)\le\varepsilon P_z(\mathcal U),
      \tag{SCL3}
   \]
   then the sponsor Hall inequalities hold with parameter
   \(\beta_\varepsilon\):
   \[
      P_z(\mathcal U)\le\beta_\varepsilon B_z(\mathcal U)
      \qquad(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}).
      \tag{SCL4}
   \]
   Consequently, if
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+\beta_\varepsilon\,\E_z\mathsf H_z\le aS
      \tag{SCL5}
   \]
   under the active first-moment hypotheses, the Hall-tail overload stars
   satisfy the weighted tuple-storage certificate.

   Otherwise there is a strong sponsor cut \(\mathcal U\) with
   \[
      E_z^\beta(\mathcal U)>\varepsilon P_z(\mathcal U)>0 .
      \tag{SCL6}
   \]
   Let \(\mathcal U^+=\{\kappa\in\mathcal U:u_{z,\kappa}>0\}\), and define
   \[
      D_z(\mathcal U)
      =
      1+\left\lceil
         \log_2
         \frac{\max_{\kappa\in\mathcal U^+}u_{z,\kappa}}
              {\min_{\kappa\in\mathcal U^+}u_{z,\kappa}}
      \right\rceil .
      \tag{SCL7}
   \]
   Then some dyadic child-price layer
   \[
      L=\{\kappa\in\mathcal U:
         \theta\le u_{z,\kappa}<2\theta\}
      \tag{SCL8}
   \]
   satisfies
   \[
      \theta |L|
      \ge
      \frac{P_z(\mathcal U)}{2D_z(\mathcal U)}
      \ge
      \frac{E_z^\beta(\mathcal U)}{2D_z(\mathcal U)} .
      \tag{SCL9}
   \]
   Feeding this layer to \cref{cor:sponsor-cut-generated-column-screen} with
   weights \(w_\kappa=\theta\) gives the following concrete alternative: either
   a generated top-prefix column is positive, or every generated cover of this
   layer obeys the metric-entropy bound \((SGC6)\).  Thus only strong sponsor
   cuts with high generated-cover entropy remain after allowing the constant
   inflation \(\beta\mapsto\beta_\varepsilon\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((SCL3)\) holds, then
   \[
      P_z(\mathcal U)-\beta B_z(\mathcal U)
      \le
      \varepsilon P_z(\mathcal U),
   \]
   which rearranges to \((1-\varepsilon)P_z(\mathcal U)\le
   \beta B_z(\mathcal U)\), proving \((SCL4)\).  But \((SCL4)\) is exactly the
   Hall inequality \((FHC5)\) for the demand
   \(d_{z,\kappa}=u_{z,\kappa}/\beta_\varepsilon\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-hall-cut} gives a fractional sponsor flow with
   parameter \(\beta_\varepsilon\), and \((SCL5)\) gives the storage
   certificate by the first part of that corollary.

   If \((SCL3)\) fails, then \((SCL6)\) holds for some \(\mathcal U\).  In
   particular \(P_z(\mathcal U)>0\), so \(\mathcal U^+\) is nonempty and
   \(D_z(\mathcal U)\) is well-defined.  Partition \(\mathcal U^+\) into the
   dyadic layers in \((SCL8)\), taking
   \(\theta=2^j\min_{\mathcal U^+}u_{z,\kappa}\).  There are at most
   \(D_z(\mathcal U)\) nonempty layers, and on each layer
   \(\theta\ge u_{z,\kappa}/2\).  Therefore
   \[
      \sum_{\text{layers }L}\theta_L|L|
      \ge
      \frac12P_z(\mathcal U).
   \]
   One layer satisfies the first inequality in \((SCL9)\), while the second
   follows from \(E_z^\beta(\mathcal U)\le P_z(\mathcal U)\).  Since
   \(w_\kappa=\theta\le u_{z,\kappa}\) on \(L\), this layer is an admissible
   input to \cref{cor:sponsor-cut-generated-column-screen}.  Its contrapositive
   gives the final alternative.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Strong sponsor layers require generated entropy]
   \label{cor:strong-sponsor-layer-generated-entropy}
   Work in the strong-cut alternative of
   \cref{cor:sponsor-cut-inflate-or-layer}, and let
   \(L\subseteq\mathcal U\) be the dyadic layer from \((SCL8)\), with
   \(K=|L|\), price level \(\theta\), and cut range factor
   \(D=D_z(\mathcal U)\).  Let \(\mathcal T\) be a generated template family
   satisfying the hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:sponsor-cut-generated-column-screen}, and assume the common price
   envelope
   \[
      \overline P_T(h)
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(Ah^\rho+\zeta h^{1+\rho}\right),
      \qquad 0<\rho<1,
      \tag{SGE1}
   \]
   for every used template and available cardinality.

   Define \(N_{\rm gen}^{\rm sp}(L,\theta)\) to be the least number \(J\) of
   nonempty generated template copies needed to cover \(L\) by parts
   \(L_1,\ldots,L_J\), with each \(|L_j|\) available for its template and
   \[
      L_j\subseteq\mathcal C_{T_j},
      \qquad
      g_{T_j,\kappa}\ge\theta
      \quad(\kappa\in L_j).
      \tag{SGE2}
   \]
   If no such cover exists, set \(N_{\rm gen}^{\rm sp}(L,\theta)=\infty\).
   If a cover with \(J\) parts satisfies
   \[
      \theta K
      >
      2\psi_\star\left(AJ^{1-\rho}K^\rho+\zeta K^{1+\rho}\right),
      \tag{SGE3}
   \]
   then some generated top-prefix column is positive.

   Consequently, if no generated top-prefix column is positive, then either the
   layer is storage-dominated,
   \[
      \theta\le4\psi_\star\zeta K^\rho,
      \tag{SGE4}
   \]
   or else
   \[
      N_{\rm gen}^{\rm sp}(L,\theta)
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{\theta K^{1-\rho}}{4\psi_\star A}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{E_z^\beta(\mathcal U)}
              {8D\,\psi_\star A\,K^\rho}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{SGE5}
   \]
   When \(\zeta=0\), the first lower bound in \((SGE5)\) holds with
   \(4\psi_\star A\) replaced by \(2\psi_\star A\).  Thus a strong sponsor cut
   with non-storage-dominated exposed layer is closed by any low-entropy
   generated cover of that layer; if it survives, the residual is a quantified
   high-generated-entropy object.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   A cover satisfying \((SGE2)\) is an admissible cover in
   \cref{cor:sponsor-cut-generated-column-screen} with weights
   \(w_\kappa=\theta\).  If no generated top-prefix column were positive, then
   \((SGC6)\) would give
   \[
      \theta K
      \le
      2\psi_\star\left(AJ^{1-\rho}K^\rho+\zeta K^{1+\rho}\right),
   \]
   contradicting \((SGE3)\).  Hence a positive column exists.

   Conversely assume no positive generated top-prefix column exists and
   \((SGE4)\) fails.  If \(J=N_{\rm gen}^{\rm sp}(L,\theta)\) were smaller than
   the first threshold in \((SGE5)\), then
   \[
      2\psi_\star A J^{1-\rho}K^\rho<\frac12\theta K,
   \]
   while failure of \((SGE4)\) gives
   \(2\psi_\star\zeta K^{1+\rho}<\theta K/2\).  Thus \((SGE3)\) would hold,
   forcing a positive column, a contradiction.  This proves the first lower
   bound in \((SGE5)\).  The second follows from
   \[
      \theta K\ge \frac{E_z^\beta(\mathcal U)}{2D}
   \]
   in \((SCL9)\).  When \(\zeta=0\), the storage term is absent and the same
   argument uses \(2\psi_\star A J^{1-\rho}K^\rho<\theta K\), giving the
   displayed constant \(2\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Low-doubling sponsor layers close]
   \label{cor:low-doubling-sponsor-layer-close}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:strong-sponsor-layer-generated-entropy}.  Suppose a generated
   container family at scale \(\lambda\in(0,1]\) certifies
   \[
      N_{\rm gen}^{\rm sp}(L,\theta)
      \le
      C_{\rm sp}\lambda^{-\delta}.
      \tag{SGD1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \theta
      >
      2\psi_\star\left(
         A C_{\rm sp}^{1-\rho}
         \lambda^{-\delta(1-\rho)}K^{\rho-1}
         +\zeta K^\rho
      \right),
      \tag{SGD2}
   \]
   then some generated top-prefix column is positive.  It is enough to verify
   the stronger cut-excess condition
   \[
      \frac{E_z^\beta(\mathcal U)}{2D K}
      >
      2\psi_\star\left(
         A C_{\rm sp}^{1-\rho}
         \lambda^{-\delta(1-\rho)}K^{\rho-1}
         +\zeta K^\rho
      \right),
      \tag{SGD3}
   \]
   since \((SCL9)\) gives \(\theta\ge E_z^\beta(\mathcal U)/(2DK)\).

   Conversely, if no generated top-prefix column is positive, then every
   certified low-doubling cover bound \((SGD1)\) must satisfy the density
   envelope
   \[
      \theta
      \le
      2\psi_\star\left(
         A C_{\rm sp}^{1-\rho}
         \lambda^{-\delta(1-\rho)}K^{\rho-1}
         +\zeta K^\rho
      \right).
      \tag{SGD4}
   \]
   In particular, when \(\zeta=0\) and \(\lambda<1\), any surviving layer with
   positive numerator obeys the generated-dimension lower bound
   \[
      \delta
      \ge
      \frac{
         \log\!\left(
            E_z^\beta(\mathcal U)/
            (4D\psi_\star A K^\rho)
         \right)
         -(1-\rho)\log C_{\rm sp}
      }{
         (1-\rho)\log(1/\lambda)
      }.
      \tag{SGD5}
   \]
   With \(\zeta>0\) and \(\lambda<1\), the same statement holds after replacing
   \(E_z^\beta(\mathcal U)/(2DK)\) by
   \(E_z^\beta(\mathcal U)/(2DK)-2\psi_\star\zeta K^\rho\), when this
   quantity is positive.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Substitute \(J=C_{\rm sp}\lambda^{-\delta}\) into \((SGE3)\) and divide by
   \(K\).  This gives \((SGD2)\Rightarrow(SGE3)\), so
   \cref{cor:strong-sponsor-layer-generated-entropy} produces a positive
   generated top-prefix column.  Condition \((SGD3)\) implies \((SGD2)\) by
   \((SCL9)\).

   The contrapositive gives \((SGD4)\): if a certified cover violated the
   displayed envelope, then \((SGD2)\) would hold.  Combining \((SGD4)\) with
   \(\theta\ge E_z^\beta(\mathcal U)/(2DK)\) gives
   \[
      \frac{E_z^\beta(\mathcal U)}{2DK}
      \le
      2\psi_\star A C_{\rm sp}^{1-\rho}
      \lambda^{-\delta(1-\rho)}K^{\rho-1}
      +2\psi_\star\zeta K^\rho .
   \]
   When \(\zeta=0\) and \(\lambda<1\), rearranging and taking logarithms gives
   \((SGD5)\) if the numerator is positive.  With \(\zeta>0\), first subtract
   the storage term and then apply the same rearrangement, again for
   \(\lambda<1\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sponsor entropy gives a packing witness]
   \label{cor:sponsor-layer-packing-witness}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:strong-sponsor-layer-generated-entropy}, and assume no generated
   top-prefix column is positive.  Let \(d_{\rm gen}\) be any pseudometric on
   the exposed layer \(L\), and fix a scale \(\Delta>0\).  Suppose that for
   every \(\kappa_0\in L\), the \(d_{\rm gen}\)-ball
   \[
      B_{\rm gen}(\kappa_0,\Delta)
      =
      \{\kappa\in L:d_{\rm gen}(\kappa,\kappa_0)\le\Delta\}
      \tag{SPW1}
   \]
   is certified by a generated template copy satisfying \((SGE2)\), with all
   realized cardinalities available and with the common price envelope
   \((SGE1)\).  If \(A>0\) and the layer is not storage-dominated,
   \[
      \theta>4\psi_\star\zeta K^\rho ,
      \tag{SPW2}
   \]
   then every cover of \(L\) by \(d_{\rm gen}\)-balls of radius \(\Delta\) has
   size at least
   \[
      \left(
         \frac{\theta K^{1-\rho}}{4\psi_\star A}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{SPW3}
   \]
   Consequently every maximal \(\Delta\)-separated subset
   \(E\subseteq L\) satisfies the same lower bound.  In terms of the strong cut
   excess,
   \[
      |E|
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{E_z^\beta(\mathcal U)}
              {8D\,\psi_\star A\,K^\rho}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{SPW4}
   \]
   When \(\zeta=0\), the constants \(4\) and \(8\) in \((SPW3)\)--\((SPW4)\)
   may be replaced by \(2\) and \(4\), respectively.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_J\) be any cover of \(L\) by radius-\(\Delta\)
   \(d_{\rm gen}\)-balls.  Assign each \(\kappa\in L\) to one covering ball.
   By the certification hypothesis, this is an admissible generated cover in
   the definition of \(N_{\rm gen}^{\rm sp}(L,\theta)\).  Since no generated
   top-prefix column is positive and \((SPW2)\) rules out the storage-dominated
   alternative, \((SGE5)\) gives \((SPW3)\).

   If \(E\) is maximal \(\Delta\)-separated, then the balls
   \(B_{\rm gen}(\kappa,\Delta)\), \(\kappa\in E\), cover \(L\); otherwise one
