   could add an uncovered point of \(L\) to \(E\).  Applying \((SPW3)\) to this
   cover gives the same lower bound for \(|E|\).  Finally \((SCL9)\) gives
   \(\theta K\ge E_z^\beta(\mathcal U)/(2D)\), which turns \((SPW3)\) into
   \((SPW4)\).  When \(\zeta=0\), use the sharper constant in the final
   sentence of \cref{cor:strong-sponsor-layer-generated-entropy}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sponsor packing feeds the spherical energy screen]
   \label{cor:sponsor-packing-spherical-energy-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:sponsor-layer-packing-witness}, and let
   \(E\subseteq L\) be a separated witness.  Suppose every
   \(\kappa\in E\) has a representative \(x_\kappa\in\mathbb S^{d-1}\).  Let
   \(U_G\) be any spherical, Gaussian-cap, code, or list-decoded bucket drawn
   from a law \(G\), and partition the ordered distinct pairs
   \(E_{\ne}^2\) into finitely many profiles \(\Pi_E\).  Assume each profile
   \(\pi\in\Pi_E\) has a certified pair-intersection energy
   \[
      \Pr_G[x_\kappa,x_{\kappa'}\in U_G]\le e^{-I_\pi}
      \qquad((\kappa,\kappa')\in\pi),
      \tag{SPS1}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      X_E(G)=\sum_{\kappa\in E}\mathbf 1\{x_\kappa\in U_G\}.
      \tag{SPS2}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \E_G X_E(G)^2
      \le
      \sum_{\kappa\in E}\Pr_G[x_\kappa\in U_G]
      +
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi_E}|\pi|e^{-I_\pi}.
      \tag{SPS3}
   \]
   In particular, if
   \[
      I_\pi\ge\log|\pi|+\Lambda
      \qquad(\pi\in\Pi_E),
      \tag{SPS4}
   \]
   then the distinct-pair contribution of the sponsor packing is at most
   \[
      |\Pi_E|e^{-\Lambda}.
      \tag{SPS5}
   \]
   Thus a strong sponsor layer that survives generated columns has been reduced
   to the standard spherical/list-decoding entropy-energy target: either the
   bucket law pays the separated packing by \((SPS5)\), or a profile violating
   \((SPS4)\) is the high-correlation signal to feed back into the existing
   dense-star and shared-prefix verifiers.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Expand the second moment:
   \[
      \E_G X_E(G)^2
      =
      \sum_{\kappa\in E}\Pr_G[x_\kappa\in U_G]
      +
      \sum_{\substack{\kappa,\kappa'\in E\\ \kappa\ne\kappa'}}
         \Pr_G[x_\kappa,x_{\kappa'}\in U_G].
   \]
   Summing \((SPS1)\) over the profile partition proves \((SPS3)\).  Under
   \((SPS4)\), each profile contributes at most \(e^{-\Lambda}\), giving
   \((SPS5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Energy-failing sponsor profiles expose stars]
   \label{cor:sponsor-profile-star-signal}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:sponsor-packing-spherical-energy-screen}.  Fix one profile
   \(\pi\subseteq E_{\ne}^2\), and assign nonnegative weights
   \(\omega_{\kappa,\kappa'}\) to its ordered pairs.  Split
   \[
      \pi=\pi_{\rm lo}\dot\cup\pi_{\rm hi}.
   \]
   Suppose the low part has certified weight
   \[
      \sum_{(\kappa,\kappa')\in\pi_{\rm lo}}
         \omega_{\kappa,\kappa'}
      \le B_{\rm lo},
      \tag{SEF1}
   \]
   and every high edge has representative correlation at least
   \[
      \ip{x_\kappa}{x_{\kappa'}}\ge\underline\theta
      \qquad((\kappa,\kappa')\in\pi_{\rm hi})
      \tag{SEF2}
   \]
   for some \(-1<\underline\theta<1\).  Define
   \[
      M_\kappa(\kappa')
      =
      \omega_{\kappa,\kappa'}
      \mathbf 1_{\{(\kappa,\kappa')\in\pi_{\rm hi}\}},
      \qquad
      W_{\rm hi}=\sum_{\kappa,\kappa'\in E}M_\kappa(\kappa').
      \tag{SEF3}
   \]
   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), set \(J_\omega=1\).  Otherwise assume the positive
   values of \(M_\kappa(\kappa')\) lie in a certified dyadic range
   \([\omega_{\min},\omega_{\max}]\), put
   \[
      J_\omega=
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{\omega_{\max}}{\omega_{\min}}\right\rceil,
      \tag{SEF4}
   \]
   and define the sponsor-star superlevels
   \[
      V_{\kappa,t}
      =
      \{\kappa'\in E:M_\kappa(\kappa')\ge t\},
      \qquad
      t\in\{\omega_{\min}2^j:0\le j<J_\omega\}.
      \tag{SEF5}
   \]
   Then every nonempty \(V_{\kappa,t}\) has representatives in the spherical
   cap ball
   \[
      x_{\kappa'}\in
      B\!\left(x_\kappa,\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)}\right)
      \qquad(\kappa'\in V_{\kappa,t}).
      \tag{SEF6}
   \]
   Moreover, for every \(\Lambda>0\), either
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}\le2|E|J_\omega\Lambda,
      \tag{SEF7}
   \]
   or some sponsor star satisfies
   \[
      t|V_{\kappa,t}|\ge\Lambda .
      \tag{SEF8}
   \]
   Consequently, if no such dyadic sponsor star has scale at least \(\Lambda\),
   then the whole profile weight is bounded by
   \[
      \sum_{(\kappa,\kappa')\in\pi}\omega_{\kappa,\kappa'}
      \le
      B_{\rm lo}+2|E|J_\omega\Lambda .
      \tag{SEF9}
   \]
   Taking
   \(\omega_{\kappa,\kappa'}=\Pr_G[x_\kappa,x_{\kappa'}\in U_G]\) shows that
   any sponsor profile whose spherical energy is not paid by the low part must
   expose a concrete high-correlation star of retained children.  That star is
   the object submitted to the existing generated-column, dense-star, or
   shared-prefix verifier.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(\kappa'\in V_{\kappa,t}\), then
   \(M_\kappa(\kappa')>0\), so \((\kappa,\kappa')\in\pi_{\rm hi}\).  By
   \((SEF2)\),
   \[
      \|x_\kappa-x_{\kappa'}\|^2
      =
      2-2\ip{x_\kappa}{x_{\kappa'}}
      \le2(1-\underline\theta),
   \]
   proving \((SEF6)\).

   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), then \((SEF7)\) and \((SEF9)\) are immediate.  Assume
   \(W_{\rm hi}>0\).  For fixed \(\kappa\), the dyadic layer-cake estimate gives
   \[
      \sum_{j=0}^{J_\omega-1}
      \omega_{\min}2^j
      |V_{\kappa,\omega_{\min}2^j}|
      \ge
      \frac12\sum_{\kappa'\in E}M_\kappa(\kappa').
   \]
   Summing over \(\kappa\in E\), if every dyadic sponsor star had
   \(t|V_{\kappa,t}|<\Lambda\), then
   \[
      \frac12W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \sum_{\kappa\in E}\sum_{j=0}^{J_\omega-1}
      \omega_{\min}2^j
      |V_{\kappa,\omega_{\min}2^j}|
      <
      |E|J_\omega\Lambda,
   \]
   which is \((SEF7)\).  The contrapositive gives \((SEF8)\), and adding
   \((SEF1)\) proves \((SEF9)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Generated sponsor-star envelope]
   \label{cor:generated-sponsor-star-envelope}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:sponsor-profile-star-signal}, and assume
   that no generated top-prefix column is positive for the underlying sponsor
   cut \(\mathcal U\).  Thus \(E\subseteq\mathcal U\).  If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\),
   interpret the sums below as empty.  Otherwise, for every nonempty dyadic
   sponsor star \(V_{\kappa,t}\) in \((SEF5)\), suppose preprocessing has a
   generated template copy \(T_{\kappa,t}\) such that
   \[
      V_{\kappa,t}\subseteq\mathcal C_{T_{\kappa,t}},
      \qquad
      g_{T_{\kappa,t},\kappa'}\ge\theta
      \quad(\kappa'\in V_{\kappa,t}),
      \tag{GSE1}
   \]
   the cardinality \(h_{\kappa,t}=|V_{\kappa,t}|\) is available, and the
   certified one-time price is \(\overline P_{\kappa,t}(h_{\kappa,t})\).
   Then every such star satisfies
   \[
      \theta h_{\kappa,t}
      \le
      2\overline P_{\kappa,t}(h_{\kappa,t}),
      \tag{GSE2}
   \]
   and the high-correlation profile mass obeys
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \frac4\theta
      \sum_{\kappa\in E}\sum_t
      t\,\overline P_{\kappa,t}(h_{\kappa,t}).
      \tag{GSE3}
   \]
   In particular, if all used sponsor-star templates satisfy the common
   envelope
   \[
      \overline P_{\kappa,t}(h)
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(Ah^\rho+\zeta h^{1+\rho}\right),
      \qquad 0<\rho<1,
      \tag{GSE4}
   \]
   then every no-column residual satisfies
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \frac{4\psi_\star}{\theta}
      \sum_{\kappa\in E}\sum_t
      t\left(Ah_{\kappa,t}^{\rho}
      +\zeta h_{\kappa,t}^{1+\rho}\right).
      \tag{GSE5}
   \]
   Equivalently, violation of \((GSE3)\), or of \((GSE5)\) under
   \((GSE4)\), exposes a positive generated top-prefix column.  Thus a
   high-correlation sponsor profile is either paid by the integrated generated
   price of its dyadic stars, or one of those stars is materialized immediately
   as a sponsor-cut column.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The case \(W_{\rm hi}=0\) is immediate, so assume \(W_{\rm hi}>0\).  Fix a
   nonempty star \(V_{\kappa,t}\) and write \(h=h_{\kappa,t}\).  If
   \(\theta h>2\overline P_{\kappa,t}(h)\), then the top \(h\)-prefix of
   \(T_{\kappa,t}\), ordered by
   \(g_{T_{\kappa,t},\cdot}\mathbf 1_{\{\cdot\in\mathcal U\}}\), has
   sponsor-cut capture at least \(\theta h\), because
   \(V_{\kappa,t}\subseteq E\subseteq\mathcal U\) and \((GSE1)\) holds on
   \(V_{\kappa,t}\).  This violates
   \((SGC3)\), so
   \cref{cor:sponsor-cut-generated-column-screen} would produce a positive
   generated column.  Since no such column is positive, \((GSE2)\) holds.

   The layer-cake estimate in the proof of
   \cref{cor:sponsor-profile-star-signal} gives
   \[
      \frac12W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \sum_{\kappa\in E}\sum_t t\,h_{\kappa,t}.
   \]
   Multiplying \((GSE2)\) by \(t/\theta\) and summing over the dyadic stars
   gives \((GSE3)\).  Substituting \((GSE4)\) gives \((GSE5)\), and the final
   statement is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[No-column sponsor stars have a price gap]
   \label{cor:no-column-sponsor-star-price-gap}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:generated-sponsor-star-envelope}, and
   assume the common price envelope \((GSE4)\).  In a no-generated-column
   sponsor residual, every nonempty dyadic sponsor star satisfies
   \[
      \theta
      \le
      2\psi_\star\left(Ah_{\kappa,t}^{\rho-1}
      +\zeta h_{\kappa,t}^{\rho}\right).
      \tag{GSG1}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      H_-=\left(\frac{4\psi_\star A}{\theta}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \tag{GSG2}
   \]
   with \(H_-=0\) when \(A=0\).  If \(\zeta>0\), also put
   \[
      H_+=\left(\frac{\theta}{4\psi_\star\zeta}\right)^{1/\rho}.
      \tag{GSG3}
   \]
   Then every nonempty dyadic sponsor star obeys
   \[
      h_{\kappa,t}\le H_-
      \qquad\text{or}\qquad
      \bigl(\zeta>0\text{ and }h_{\kappa,t}\ge H_+\bigr).
      \tag{GSG4}
   \]
   In particular, when \(\zeta=0\), every surviving star has
   \(h_{\kappa,t}\le H_-\).  Equivalently, any reported sponsor star with
   \(h_{\kappa,t}>H_-\) and, when \(\zeta>0\), \(h_{\kappa,t}<H_+\), is itself
   a positive generated top-prefix column.

   Thus the integrated generated-price residual has no medium-cardinality
   high-correlation stars: after generated-column search, the only survivors
   are the bounded-cardinality sublinear branch and the storage-dominated
   large-star branch.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Combining \((GSE2)\) and \((GSE4)\), and dividing by \(h_{\kappa,t}>0\),
   gives \((GSG1)\).  If \(h_{\kappa,t}>H_-\), then
   \[
      2\psi_\star A h_{\kappa,t}^{\rho-1}<\frac\theta2 .
   \]
   Hence \((GSG1)\) can hold only if
   \(2\psi_\star\zeta h_{\kappa,t}^{\rho}\ge\theta/2\).  When \(\zeta=0\)
   this is impossible, and when \(\zeta>0\) it is exactly
   \(h_{\kappa,t}\ge H_+\).  The final statement is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Balanced sponsor-star scalar gate]
   \label{cor:balanced-sponsor-star-scalar-gate}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:no-column-sponsor-star-price-gap}.  If
   \(\zeta>0\) and the forbidden cardinality interval is empty, in the sense
   that \(H_-\ge H_+\), then
   \[
      \theta\le 4\psi_\star A^\rho\zeta^{1-\rho}.
      \tag{GSG5}
   \]
   Equivalently, if
   \[
      4\psi_\star A^\rho\zeta^{1-\rho}<\theta ,
      \tag{GSG6}
   \]
   then \(H_-<H_+\), and every reported sponsor star whose cardinality lies in
   the nonempty window
   \[
      H_-<h_{\kappa,t}<H_+
      \tag{GSG7}
   \]
   is a positive generated top-prefix column.

   When \(\zeta=0\), interpret \(H_+=\infty\) and
   \(A^\rho\zeta^{1-\rho}=0\).  Then \((GSG6)\) holds for every
   \(\theta>0\), and the forbidden window is simply \(h_{\kappa,t}>H_-\).

   Thus a sponsor-star residual has only two scalar explanations: either the
   balanced query/storage price \(A^\rho\zeta^{1-\rho}\) is already large at
   the capture scale, or medium-cardinality high-correlation stars are
   impossible and the remaining proof may separately target the small and
   storage-dominated tails.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Assume \(\zeta>0\).  The inequality \(H_-\ge H_+\) is, by the definitions
   \((GSG2)\)--\((GSG3)\),
   \[
      \left(\frac{4\psi_\star A}{\theta}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \ge
      \left(\frac{\theta}{4\psi_\star\zeta}\right)^{1/\rho}.
   \]
   Raising both sides to the power \(\rho(1-\rho)\) and rearranging gives
   \[
      (4\psi_\star A)^\rho(4\psi_\star\zeta)^{1-\rho}\ge\theta,
   \]
   which is \((GSG5)\).  Its contrapositive gives \(H_-<H_+\) under
   \((GSG6)\), and \cref{cor:no-column-sponsor-star-price-gap} then makes every
   star in the window \((GSG7)\) a positive column.  The case \(\zeta=0\) is
   the final sentence of \cref{cor:no-column-sponsor-star-price-gap}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Bounded sponsor stars are a fixed tail]
   \label{cor:bounded-sponsor-stars-fixed-tail}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:no-column-sponsor-star-price-gap}.  If
   \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), there is nothing to prove.  Otherwise let
   \(\omega_{\max}\) and \(J_\omega\) be the dyadic range data from
   \((SEF4)\), and fix a threshold \(\Lambda_+\ge0\).  Suppose that every
   nonempty dyadic sponsor star satisfying the storage-dominated alternative
   \[
      \zeta>0,\qquad h_{\kappa,t}\ge H_+
      \tag{GSF1}
   \]
   has scale
   \[
      t\,h_{\kappa,t}\le\Lambda_+ .
      \tag{GSF2}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      2|E|J_\omega
      \max\{\omega_{\max}H_-,\,\Lambda_+\}.
      \tag{GSF3}
   \]
   Equivalently, if
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      >
      2|E|J_\omega
      \max\{\omega_{\max}H_-,\,\Lambda_+\},
      \tag{GSF4}
   \]
   then some no-column sponsor star is storage-dominated and satisfies
   \(t\,h_{\kappa,t}>\Lambda_+\).  When \(\zeta=0\), the storage-dominated
   alternative is absent, so every no-column residual obeys
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}\le2|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_- .
      \tag{GSF5}
   \]

   Thus the bounded-cardinality side of the sponsor-star price gap is no longer
   a live polynomial obstruction.  It contributes only the explicit fixed tail
   \(|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-\); any excess high-correlation mass must appear
   in a large storage-dominated star.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Assume \(W_{\rm hi}>0\).  Put
   \[
      \Lambda=\max\{\omega_{\max}H_-,\,\Lambda_+\}.
   \]
   Fix a nonempty dyadic sponsor star.  By
   \cref{cor:no-column-sponsor-star-price-gap}, either
   \(h_{\kappa,t}\le H_-\), or the storage-dominated alternative \((GSF1)\)
   holds.  In the first case \(t\le\omega_{\max}\), so
   \(t h_{\kappa,t}\le\omega_{\max}H_-\le\Lambda\).  In the second case
   \((GSF2)\) gives \(t h_{\kappa,t}\le\Lambda_+\le\Lambda\).  Therefore every
   dyadic sponsor star has scale at most \(\Lambda\).  The layer-cake proof of
   \cref{cor:sponsor-profile-star-signal} gives
   \[
      \frac12W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \sum_{\kappa\in E}\sum_t t\,h_{\kappa,t}
      \le
      |E|J_\omega\Lambda,
   \]
   proving \((GSF3)\).  The excess statement is the contrapositive.  If
   \(\zeta=0\), \cref{cor:no-column-sponsor-star-price-gap} puts every
   nonempty star in the first case, so the same proof gives \((GSF5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Storage-dominated sponsor stars are fractional storage]
   \label{cor:storage-dominated-sponsor-stars-fractional-tail}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:bounded-sponsor-stars-fixed-tail}.  Let
   \(\mathcal S_{\rm st}\) be the set of nonempty dyadic sponsor stars
   \(s=(\kappa,t)\) satisfying the storage-dominated alternative \((GSF1)\),
   and write
   \[
      h_s=h_{\kappa,t}=|V_{\kappa,t}|,
      \qquad
      u_s^{\rm frac}=\psi_\star\zeta\,t\,h_s^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{SFT1}
   \]
   If \(\zeta=0\), interpret \(\mathcal S_{\rm st}=\emptyset\).  Then every
   no-column sponsor-star residual satisfies
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      2|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-
      +
      \frac8\theta\sum_{s\in\mathcal S_{\rm st}}u_s^{\rm frac}.
      \tag{SFT2}
   \]
   In particular, the storage-dominated branch is an integrated fractional
   storage tail.  After absorbing the dyadic intensity into the price factor,
   \[
      \psi_s^{\rm frac}=t\psi_\star\zeta,
      \qquad
      u_s^{\rm frac}=\psi_s^{\rm frac}h_s^{1+\rho},
      \tag{SFT3}
   \]
   the family of storage-dominated sponsor stars is a valid input to the
   distinct-storage certificates of
   \cref{cor:price-weighted-witness-packing-storage} and
   \cref{cor:weighted-occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage}.
   Thus, to place the storage-dominated contribution in \((SFT2)\) inside any
   desired allowance \(B_{\rm st}\), it is enough to prove for the fractional
   star panel generated at the node the storage estimate
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \E_z\sum_{s\in\mathcal S_{{\rm st},z}}u_s^{\rm frac}
      \le
      \frac\theta8 B_{\rm st}
      \tag{SFT4}
   \]
   or any stronger shared-canonical version certified by those corollaries.
   Failure of \((SFT4)\) is precisely a distinct-child storage-tail failure for
   these fractional star children; it is not a separate dense-branching or
   integer-materialization obstruction.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), the statement is immediate.  Assume first that
   \(\zeta>0\).  The layer-cake estimate from
   \cref{cor:sponsor-profile-star-signal} gives
   \[
      \frac12W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \sum_{\kappa\in E}\sum_t t\,h_{\kappa,t}.
      \tag{SFT5}
   \]
   Split the dyadic stars into the bounded side \(h_{\kappa,t}\le H_-\) and
   the storage-dominated side.  The bounded side contributes at most
   \(|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-\), since \(t\le\omega_{\max}\).  For
   \(s\in\mathcal S_{\rm st}\), \((GSF1)\) and the definition of \(H_+\) give
   \[
      \theta\le4\psi_\star\zeta h_s^\rho .
      \tag{SFT6}
   \]
   Multiplying by \(t h_s/\theta\) gives
   \[
      t h_s
      \le
      \frac4\theta\psi_\star\zeta\,t\,h_s^{1+\rho}
      =
      \frac4\theta u_s^{\rm frac}.
      \tag{SFT7}
   \]
   Substituting the two bounds into \((SFT5)\) proves \((SFT2)\).

   If \(\zeta=0\), \cref{cor:no-column-sponsor-star-price-gap} puts every
   nonempty dyadic star on the bounded side, so the same argument gives
   \((GSF5)\), which is \((SFT2)\) with an empty storage sum.

   Finally, \((SFT3)\) is only a relabeling of the star's fractional storage
   price as an ordinary child price factor.  With witness net
   \(A_s=V_{\kappa,t}\), the star has exact storage price
   \(\psi_s^{\rm frac}|A_s|^{1+\rho}=u_s^{\rm frac}\), so the cited
   price-weighted and weighted-occurrence storage certificates apply directly.
   Condition \((SFT4)\) is the corresponding integrated storage bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Generic fractional child-panel shared-cover compiler]
   \label{cor:fractional-child-panel-shared-cover-compiler}
   Let \(\mathcal A\) be a finite family of fractional child records.  Each
   \(a\in\mathcal A\) has residual storage price \(u_a\ge0\).  Let
   \(\mathcal R\) be a finite family of candidate shared records.  A record
   \(c\in\mathcal R\) has one-time recursive storage price \(P_c\ge0\) and
   certified cover coefficients \(0\le g_{c,a}\le1\).  Define
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Phi=\min
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{a\in\mathcal A}u_ae_a
        +\sum_{c\in\mathcal R}P_c\lambda_c\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        e_a+\sum_{c\in\mathcal R}\lambda_cg_{c,a}\ge1
        \qquad(a\in\mathcal A),\\[0.8em]
      & e_a\ge0,\qquad \lambda_c\ge0 .
   \end{array}
      \tag{FCP1}
   \]
   Its dual is
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Phi=\max
      & \displaystyle \sum_{a\in\mathcal A}y_a\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & 0\le y_a\le u_a
        \qquad(a\in\mathcal A),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{a\in\mathcal A}g_{c,a}y_a\le P_c
        \qquad(c\in\mathcal R).
   \end{array}
      \tag{FCP2}
   \]

   Now let \(\mathcal T\) be a finite family of generated shared-record
   templates.  A template \(T\) has a search container
   \(\mathcal A_T\subseteq\mathcal A\), certified capture weights
   \(\alpha_{T,a}\in[0,1]\), finite available cardinalities
   \(\mathcal K_T\), and certified prices \(\overline P_T(K)\).  Assume
   materialization: for every \(K\in\mathcal K_T\) and every
   \(U\subseteq\mathcal A_T\) with \(|U|=K\), preprocessing can create a shared
   record \(c(T,U)\in\mathcal R\) satisfying
   \[
      P_{c(T,U)}\le\overline P_T(K),
      \qquad
      g_{c(T,U),a}\ge
      \alpha_{T,a}\mathbf 1_{\{a\in U\}}
      \quad(a\in\mathcal A).
      \tag{FCP3}
   \]
   For any vector \(y\) with \(0\le y_a\le u_a\), for instance the dual of a
   restricted shared-cover LP, order \(\mathcal A_T=\{a_1,a_2,\ldots\}\) by
   nonincreasing \(\alpha_{T,a}y_a\).  If, for some available \(K\),
   \[
      \sum_{j\le K}\alpha_{T,a_j}y_{a_j}>\overline P_T(K),
      \tag{FCP4}
   \]
   then \(c(T,\{a_1,\ldots,a_K\})\) violates the corresponding shared-record
   dual constraint and is an improving shared-cover column.
   Conversely, if no available top prefix for \(T\) is improving, then every
   \(K\)-subset \(U\subseteq\mathcal A_T\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{a\in U}\alpha_{T,a}y_a\le\overline P_T(K).
      \tag{FCP5}
   \]

   The generated-cover relaxation
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Psi^{\rm gen}=\min
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{a\in\mathcal A}u_ae_a
        +\sum_{T\in\mathcal T}
         \sum_{K\in\mathcal K_T}
         \sum_{\substack{U\subseteq\mathcal A_T\\ |U|=K}}
         \lambda_{T,U}\overline P_T(K)\\[0.9em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        e_a+
        \sum_{T\in\mathcal T}
        \sum_{K\in\mathcal K_T}
        \sum_{\substack{U\subseteq\mathcal A_T\\ |U|=K}}
        \lambda_{T,U}\alpha_{T,a}\mathbf 1_{\{a\in U\}}
        \ge1
        \qquad(a\in\mathcal A),\\[0.9em]
      & e_a\ge0,\qquad \lambda_{T,U}\ge0
   \end{array}
      \tag{FCP6}
   \]
   satisfies \(\Phi\le\Psi^{\rm gen}\).  Hence if
   \(\Psi^{\rm gen}\le\Theta\), the generated prefixes close the child panel
   at allowance \(\Theta\).  Conversely, if \(\Psi^{\rm gen}>\Theta\), then
   there is one dual weighting \(y_a\) with
   \[
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal A}y_a>\Theta,\qquad
      0\le y_a\le u_a,
      \tag{FCP7}
   \]
   such that every generated template satisfies all subset tests \((FCP5)\).

   Finally, suppose a template \(T\) has \(b_T\)-dense available
   cardinalities and prices of the form
   \[
      \overline P_T(K)
      =
      \psi_T(A_TK^\rho+\zeta_TK^{1+\rho}),
      \qquad 0<\rho<1 .
      \tag{FCP8}
   \]
   If no available top prefix for \(T\) is improving, then every nonempty
   degree superlevel
   \[
      H_{T,\delta}=\{a\in\mathcal A_T:\alpha_{T,a}y_a\ge\delta\},
      \qquad h=|H_{T,\delta}|,
      \tag{FCP9}
   \]
   obeys
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      \psi_T\left(
         b_T^{1-\rho}A_Th^{\rho-1}
         +\zeta_Th^\rho
      \right).
      \tag{FCP10}
   \]
   Thus every storage tail that has been reduced to priced fractional child
   records has the same algorithmic interface: solve one finite shared-cover
   LP, add a positive generated prefix, or expose one no-prefix dual residual
   for the geometric/list-decoding separator.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The primal \((FCP1)\) is finite and feasible by taking \(e_a=1\).  Assign a
   dual variable \(y_a\ge0\) to each cover constraint.  The coefficient of
   \(e_a\) gives \(y_a\le u_a\), and the coefficient of \(\lambda_c\) gives
   \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}g_{c,a}y_a\le P_c\).  Finite LP duality proves
   \((FCP2)\).

   If \((FCP4)\) holds, then by \((FCP3)\)
   \[
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal A}g_{c(T,U_K),a}y_a
      \ge
      \sum_{j\le K}\alpha_{T,a_j}y_{a_j}
      >
      \overline P_T(K)
      \ge
      P_{c(T,U_K)} ,
   \]
   where \(U_K=\{a_1,\ldots,a_K\}\).  Hence this record violates the current
   dual constraint and is an improving column.  For fixed \(K\), the top
   \(K\)-prefix maximizes \(\sum_{a\in U}\alpha_{T,a}y_a\), proving the
   converse \((FCP5)\).

   Any feasible solution of \((FCP6)\) materializes a feasible solution of
   \((FCP1)\) by replacing each active \((T,U)\) with \(c(T,U)\), using
   \((FCP3)\) for coverage and \(P_{c(T,U)}\le\overline P_T(|U|)\) for price.
   Therefore \(\Phi\le\Psi^{\rm gen}\).  The dual of \((FCP6)\) is obtained
   from \((FCP7)\) plus all subset constraints \((FCP5)\), so finite LP duality
   gives the no-prefix residual when \(\Psi^{\rm gen}>\Theta\).

   For the weak-type envelope, choose \(K\in\mathcal K_T\) with
   \(h/b_T\le K\le h\).  The top \(K\)-prefix has total degree at least
   \(K\delta\).  Since no prefix is improving,
   \[
      K\delta\le\overline P_T(K)
      =
      \psi_T(A_TK^\rho+\zeta_TK^{1+\rho}).
   \]
   Divide by \(K\), use \(K\ge h/b_T\) in the negative exponent
   \(K^{\rho-1}\), and use \(K\le h\) in \(K^\rho\), giving \((FCP10)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Generic child-panel low-cover and packing screen]
   \label{cor:fractional-child-panel-low-cover-screen}
   Work in the no-generated-cover residual of
   \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-shared-cover-compiler}: a dual weighting
   \(y_a\) satisfies \((FCP7)\), and every generated template in
   \(\mathcal T\) satisfies the subset tests \((FCP5)\).  Let
   \(L\subseteq\mathcal A\) be nonempty, with \(K=|L|\).  Suppose \(L\) is
   assigned to generated templates by a map \(\kappa:L\to\mathcal T\) such
   that, for each nonempty part
   \[
      L_T=\{a\in L:\kappa(a)=T\},
      \qquad K_T=|L_T|,
      \tag{GCL1}
   \]
   one has \(K_T\in\mathcal K_T\), \(L_T\subseteq\mathcal A_T\), and certified
   lower degrees \(w_a\) satisfying
   \[
      0\le w_a\le\alpha_{\kappa(a),a}y_a
      \qquad(a\in L).
      \tag{GCL2}
   \]
   Then every no-generated-cover residual obeys
   \[
      \sum_{a\in L}w_a
      \le
      \sum_{T:\,K_T>0}\overline P_T(K_T).
      \tag{GCL3}
   \]

   Assume moreover that \(w_a\ge\delta>0\) on \(L\), and that all used
   templates satisfy the common price envelope
   \[
      \overline P_T(h)
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(Ah^\rho+\zeta h^{1+\rho}\right),
      \qquad 0<\rho<1 .
      \tag{GCL4}
   \]
   If the assignment uses \(J\) nonempty template parts, then
   \[
      \delta K
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(AJ^{1-\rho}K^\rho+\zeta K^{1+\rho}\right).
      \tag{GCL5}
   \]
   Consequently, if \(A>0\) and
   \[
      \delta>2\psi_\star\zeta K^\rho,
      \tag{GCL6}
   \]
   every surviving residual has
   \[
      J
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{\delta K^{1-\rho}}{2\psi_\star A}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{GCL7}
   \]
   When \(\zeta=0\), the same conclusion holds, for \(A>0\), with
   \(2\psi_\star A\) replaced by \(\psi_\star A\) in \((GCL7)\).

   Equivalently, if a certified low-doubling, range, additive-quantization, or
   list-decoded cover gives an assignment with
   \[
      J\le C_{\rm gen}\lambda^{-\Delta},
      \tag{GCL8}
   \]
   then any surviving residual must satisfy
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(
         A C_{\rm gen}^{1-\rho}
         \lambda^{-\Delta(1-\rho)}K^{\rho-1}
         +\zeta K^\rho
      \right).
      \tag{GCL9}
   \]
   Violation of \((GCL9)\) exposes a positive generated prefix.

   Finally, let \(d_{\rm gen}\) be any pseudometric on \(L\), and suppose that
   for every \(a_0\in L\) the ball
   \[
      B_{\rm gen}(a_0,\Delta_{\rm gen})
      =
      \{a\in L:d_{\rm gen}(a,a_0)\le\Delta_{\rm gen}\}
      \tag{GCL10}
   \]
   has a generated template copy \(T_{a_0}\in\mathcal T\) with
   \[
      B_{\rm gen}(a_0,\Delta_{\rm gen})\subseteq\mathcal A_{T_{a_0}},
      \qquad
      |B_{\rm gen}(a_0,\Delta_{\rm gen})|\in\mathcal K_{T_{a_0}},
      \tag{GCL11}
   \]
   and certified current capture
   \[
      \alpha_{T_{a_0},a}y_a\ge\delta
      \qquad(a\in B_{\rm gen}(a_0,\Delta_{\rm gen})).
      \tag{GCL12}
   \]
   If \(E\subseteq L\) is maximal \(\Delta_{\rm gen}\)-separated, then under
   \(A>0\) and \((GCL6)\)
   \[
      |E|
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{\delta K^{1-\rho}}{2\psi_\star A}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \tag{GCL13}
   \]
   with the same \(\zeta=0\) sharpening as above.  Thus failure of generated
   low-cover closure creates a separated packing witness in whatever certified
   generated metric was used by the cover family.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For a nonempty part \(L_T\), \((GCL2)\) gives
   \[
      \sum_{a\in L_T}w_a
      \le
      \sum_{a\in L_T}\alpha_{T,a}y_a .
   \]
   Since \(L_T\subseteq\mathcal A_T\) and \(K_T\in\mathcal K_T\), the subset
   test \((FCP5)\) gives
   \[
      \sum_{a\in L_T}\alpha_{T,a}y_a\le\overline P_T(K_T).
   \]
   Summing over nonempty parts proves \((GCL3)\).

   If \(w_a\ge\delta\), then \(\delta K\le\sum_{a\in L}w_a\).  Under
   \((GCL4)\), Holder's inequality gives
   \[
      \sum_TK_T^\rho\le J^{1-\rho}K^\rho,
      \qquad
      \sum_TK_T^{1+\rho}\le K^{1+\rho}.
   \]
   Substituting in \((GCL3)\) proves \((GCL5)\).  If \(A>0\) and \((GCL6)\)
   holds, the storage term in \((GCL5)\) is less than \(\delta K/2\), so
   \[
      \frac{\delta K}{2}
      \le
      \psi_\star A J^{1-\rho}K^\rho ,
   \]
   which rearranges to \((GCL7)\).  When \(\zeta=0\), the storage term is
   absent and the same rearrangement starts from
   \(\delta K\le\psi_\star AJ^{1-\rho}K^\rho\).

   Dividing \((GCL5)\) by \(K\) and substituting \((GCL8)\) gives
   \((GCL9)\).  If \((GCL9)\) is violated, the contrapositive of the same
   argument says that some assigned generated part violates \((FCP5)\), hence
   \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-shared-cover-compiler} supplies a positive
   generated prefix.

   If \(E\) is maximal separated, the balls
   \(B_{\rm gen}(a,\Delta_{\rm gen})\), \(a\in E\), cover \(L\).  Assign each
   point of \(L\) to one covering ball.  By \((GCL11)\)--\((GCL12)\), this
   assignment satisfies \((GCL1)\)--\((GCL2)\) with one nonempty template part
   per chosen ball and \(w_a=\delta\).  Applying the preceding cover lower
   bound to this cover gives \((GCL13)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Generic child-panel packing energy screen]
   \label{cor:fractional-child-panel-packing-energy-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-low-cover-screen}, and let
   \(E\subseteq L\) be a separated packing witness.  Suppose every
   \(a\in E\) has a representative \(x_a\in\mathbb S^{d-1}\).  Let \(U_G\) be
   a spherical, Gaussian-cap, code, range/list-decoded, or other certified
   bucket drawn from a law \(G\).  Partition the ordered distinct pairs
   \(E_{\ne}^2\) into finitely many profiles \(\Pi_E\).  Assume each profile
   \(\pi\in\Pi_E\) has a certified pair-intersection energy
   \[
      \Pr_G[x_a,x_{a'}\in U_G]\le e^{-I_\pi}
      \qquad((a,a')\in\pi).
      \tag{GPE1}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      X_E(G)=\sum_{a\in E}\mathbf 1\{x_a\in U_G\}.
      \tag{GPE2}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \E_GX_E(G)^2
      \le
      \sum_{a\in E}\Pr_G[x_a\in U_G]
      +
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi_E}|\pi|e^{-I_\pi}.
      \tag{GPE3}
   \]
   In particular, if
   \[
      I_\pi\ge\log|\pi|+\Lambda
      \qquad(\pi\in\Pi_E),
      \tag{GPE4}
   \]
   then the total distinct-pair contribution of the generic child-panel
   packing is at most
   \[
      |\Pi_E|e^{-\Lambda}.
      \tag{GPE5}
   \]
   Therefore every no-prefix child-panel residual has a common endpoint:
   either the chosen bucket law pays the separated packing by the
   entropy-energy estimate \((GPE5)\), or some profile violating \((GPE4)\) is
   the unique high-correlation signal that must be returned to the generated
   prefix/shared-cover machinery.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Expanding the second moment gives
   \[
      \E_GX_E(G)^2
      =
      \sum_{a\in E}\Pr_G[x_a\in U_G]
      +
      \sum_{\substack{a,a'\in E\\a\ne a'}}
         \Pr_G[x_a,x_{a'}\in U_G].
   \]
   Summing the profile bounds \((GPE1)\) over the partition proves
   \((GPE3)\).  Under \((GPE4)\), each profile contributes at most
   \(e^{-\Lambda}\), giving \((GPE5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Generic child-panel high-correlation return]
   \label{cor:fractional-child-panel-high-correlation-return}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-packing-energy-screen}, and keep the
   no-prefix child-panel dual \(y_a\) from \((FCP7)\).  Fix one profile
   \(\pi\subseteq E_{\ne}^2\), assign nonnegative weights
   \(\omega_{a,a'}\) to its ordered pairs, and split
   \[
      \pi=\pi_{\rm lo}\dot\cup\pi_{\rm hi}.
   \]
   Suppose the low part has certified weight
   \[
      \sum_{(a,a')\in\pi_{\rm lo}}\omega_{a,a'}\le B_{\rm lo},
      \tag{GHR1}
   \]
   and every high edge has representative correlation at least
   \[
      \ip{x_a}{x_{a'}}\ge\underline\theta
      \qquad((a,a')\in\pi_{\rm hi})
      \tag{GHR2}
   \]
   for some \(-1<\underline\theta<1\).  Define
   \[
      M_a(a')=\omega_{a,a'}\mathbf 1_{\{(a,a')\in\pi_{\rm hi}\}},
      \qquad
      W_{\rm hi}=\sum_{a,a'\in E}M_a(a').
      \tag{GHR3}
   \]
   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), set \(J_\omega=1\).  Otherwise assume the positive
   values of \(M_a(a')\) lie in a certified dyadic range
   \([\omega_{\min},\omega_{\max}]\), put
   \[
      J_\omega=
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{\omega_{\max}}{\omega_{\min}}\right\rceil,
      \tag{GHR4}
   \]
   and define the high-correlation stars
   \[
      V_{a,t}=\{a'\in E:M_a(a')\ge t\},
      \qquad
      t\in\{\omega_{\min}2^j:0\le j<J_\omega\}.
      \tag{GHR5}
   \]
   Then every nonempty \(V_{a,t}\) has representatives in the cap ball
   \[
      x_{a'}\in B\!\left(x_a,\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)}\right)
      \qquad(a'\in V_{a,t}).
      \tag{GHR6}
   \]

   Now let \(\chi>0\).  For every nonempty \(V_{a,t}\), suppose preprocessing
   has a generated shared-record template \(T_{a,t}\in\mathcal T\) satisfying
   the materialization hypothesis \((FCP3)\), with
   \[
      V_{a,t}\subseteq\mathcal A_{T_{a,t}},
      \qquad
      h_{a,t}=|V_{a,t}|\in\mathcal K_{T_{a,t}},
      \tag{GHR7}
   \]
   and certified current dual capture
   \[
      \alpha_{T_{a,t},a'}y_{a'}\ge\chi
      \qquad(a'\in V_{a,t}).
      \tag{GHR8}
   \]
   If, for some star,
   \[
      \chi h_{a,t}>\overline P_{T_{a,t}}(h_{a,t}),
      \tag{GHR9}
   \]
   then \(T_{a,t}\) contains an improving generated prefix for the current
   child-panel shared-cover LP.  If no such improving prefix exists, then
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \frac2\chi
      \sum_{a\in E}\sum_t
         t\,\overline P_{T_{a,t}}(h_{a,t}),
      \tag{GHR10}
   \]
   and hence
   \[
      \sum_{(a,a')\in\pi}\omega_{a,a'}
      \le
      B_{\rm lo}
      +
      \frac2\chi
      \sum_{a\in E}\sum_t
         t\,\overline P_{T_{a,t}}(h_{a,t}).
      \tag{GHR11}
   \]

   In particular, if all used templates satisfy the common envelope
   \[
      \overline P_{T_{a,t}}(h)
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(Ah^\rho+\zeta h^{1+\rho}\right),
      \tag{GHR12}
   \]
   then every no-prefix residual satisfies
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \frac{2\psi_\star}{\chi}
      \sum_{a\in E}\sum_t
      t\left(Ah_{a,t}^{\rho}+\zeta h_{a,t}^{1+\rho}\right).
      \tag{GHR13}
   \]
   Thus an energy-deficient high-correlation child-panel profile either
   returns immediately as a positive generated shared-cover prefix, or it is
   paid by the integrated generated price of its dyadic cap stars.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(a'\in V_{a,t}\), then \(M_a(a')>0\), so \((a,a')\in\pi_{\rm hi}\).
   By \((GHR2)\),
   \[
      \|x_a-x_{a'}\|^2
      =
      2-2\ip{x_a}{x_{a'}}
      \le 2(1-\underline\theta),
   \]
   proving \((GHR6)\).

   Fix a nonempty star \(V_{a,t}\).  If \((GHR9)\) holds, then the top
   \(h_{a,t}\)-prefix of \(T_{a,t}\), ordered by
   \(\alpha_{T_{a,t},u}y_u\), has total degree at least \(\chi h_{a,t}\), by
   \((GHR8)\).  This is larger than its certified price, so
   \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-shared-cover-compiler} supplies an
   improving generated shared-cover column.  Therefore, in a no-prefix
   residual,
   \[
      \chi h_{a,t}\le\overline P_{T_{a,t}}(h_{a,t})
      \tag{GHR14}
   \]
   for every nonempty dyadic star.

   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), then \((GHR10)\)--\((GHR11)\) are immediate.
   Otherwise the dyadic layer-cake estimate gives
   \[
      \frac12W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \sum_{a\in E}\sum_t t\,h_{a,t}.
   \]
   Multiplying \((GHR14)\) by \(t/\chi\) and summing gives \((GHR10)\).
   Adding the low bound \((GHR1)\) proves \((GHR11)\), and substituting
   \((GHR12)\) proves \((GHR13)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Generic returned cap-star storage split]
   \label{cor:fractional-child-panel-cap-star-storage-split}
   Work in the no-prefix setting of
   \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-high-correlation-return}, and assume the
   common envelope \((GHR12)\).  Every nonempty dyadic cap star satisfies
   \[
      \chi
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(Ah_{a,t}^{\rho-1}
      +\zeta h_{a,t}^{\rho}\right).
      \tag{GCS1}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      H_-^\star
      =
      \left(\frac{2\psi_\star A}{\chi}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \tag{GCS2}
   \]
   with \(H_-^\star=0\) when \(A=0\).  If \(\zeta>0\), also put
   \[
      H_+^\star
      =
      \left(\frac{\chi}{2\psi_\star\zeta}\right)^{1/\rho}.
      \tag{GCS3}
   \]
   Then every nonempty returned cap star obeys
   \[
      h_{a,t}\le H_-^\star
      \qquad\text{or}\qquad
      \bigl(\zeta>0\text{ and }h_{a,t}\ge H_+^\star\bigr).
      \tag{GCS4}
   \]
   Equivalently, any star with
   \[
      h_{a,t}>H_-^\star
      \quad\text{and, when }\zeta>0,\quad
      h_{a,t}<H_+^\star
      \tag{GCS5}
   \]
   is itself an improving generated shared-cover prefix.

   If \(\zeta>0\) and the forbidden interval is empty, then
   \[
      \chi\le 2\psi_\star A^\rho\zeta^{1-\rho}.
      \tag{GCS6}
   \]

   Let \(\mathcal A^\star_{\rm st}\) be the set of nonempty returned cap stars
   in the storage-dominated alternative \(h_{a,t}\ge H_+^\star\), and define
   for \(r=(a,t)\in\mathcal A^\star_{\rm st}\)
   \[
      A_r^\star=V_{a,t},\qquad
      h_r=|A_r^\star|=h_{a,t},\qquad
      \psi_r^\star=t\psi_\star\zeta,\qquad
      u_r^\star=\psi_r^\star h_r^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{GCS7}
   \]
   If \(\zeta=0\), interpret \(\mathcal A^\star_{\rm st}=\emptyset\).  Then
   every no-prefix residual satisfies
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      2|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-^\star
      +
      \frac4\chi
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal A^\star_{\rm st}}u_r^\star .
      \tag{GCS8}
   \]

   Consequently, every high-correlation child-panel return has the same normal
   form: a bounded fixed tail plus another priced fractional child panel.  The
   storage-dominated records \(r\in\mathcal A^\star_{\rm st}\), with update
   sets \(A_r^\star\) and prices \(u_r^\star\), may be used directly as the
   input family \(\mathcal A\) in
   \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-shared-cover-compiler} and in the
   distinct-storage certificates
   \cref{cor:price-weighted-witness-packing-storage} and
   \cref{cor:weighted-occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage}; equivalently, their
   storage can be certified by the exact pair-witness identity in
   \cref{cor:generic-child-panel-pair-witness-storage}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Combining the no-prefix inequality \((GHR14)\) with the common envelope
   \((GHR12)\), and dividing by \(h_{a,t}>0\), gives \((GCS1)\).  If
   \(h_{a,t}>H_-^\star\), then
   \[
      \psi_\star A h_{a,t}^{\rho-1}<\frac\chi2 .
   \]
   Hence \((GCS1)\) can hold only if
   \(\psi_\star\zeta h_{a,t}^{\rho}\ge\chi/2\).  When \(\zeta=0\) this is
   impossible, and when \(\zeta>0\) it is exactly
   \(h_{a,t}\ge H_+^\star\).  This proves \((GCS4)\), while \((GCS5)\) is the
   contrapositive combined with
   \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-high-correlation-return}.

   If \(\zeta>0\) and \(H_-^\star\ge H_+^\star\), then
   \[
      \left(\frac{2\psi_\star A}{\chi}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \ge
      \left(\frac{\chi}{2\psi_\star\zeta}\right)^{1/\rho}.
   \]
   Raising to \(\rho(1-\rho)\) and rearranging gives \((GCS6)\).

   It remains to prove the tail bound.  If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), the claim is
   immediate.  Otherwise the dyadic layer-cake estimate gives
   \[
      \frac12W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \sum_{a\in E}\sum_t t\,h_{a,t}.
      \tag{GCS9}
   \]
   Split the sum into the bounded side \(h_{a,t}\le H_-^\star\) and the
   storage-dominated side.  The bounded side contributes at most
   \(|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-^\star\).  For a storage-dominated star, the
   definition of \(H_+^\star\) gives
   \[
      \chi\le2\psi_\star\zeta h_{a,t}^{\rho},
   \]
   and therefore
   \[
      t\,h_{a,t}
      \le
      \frac2\chi\psi_\star\zeta\,t\,h_{a,t}^{1+\rho}
      =
      \frac2\chi u_{(a,t)}^\star .
      \tag{GCS10}
   \]
   Substituting these two estimates in \((GCS9)\) proves \((GCS8)\).  When
   \(\zeta=0\), there is no storage-dominated side and the same argument gives
   \((GCS8)\) with an empty sum.

   Finally, \((GCS7)\) is exactly the standard child-panel storage price after
   absorbing the dyadic intensity \(t\) into the price factor.  This is the
   input format required by the cited shared-cover and distinct-storage
   certificates.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Flattened closure for returned child panels]
   \label{cor:flattened-child-panel-closure}
   Let \(\mathfrak A\) be any finite universe of priced fractional child
   records, with prices \(u_a\ge0\).  Think of \(\mathfrak A\) as the build-time
   closure of an initial child panel under all materializable storage-dominated
   high-correlation returns of
   \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-cap-star-storage-split}.  Let
   \(\mathfrak T\) be a finite universe of generated shared-record templates
   over \(\mathfrak A\), satisfying the materialization hypothesis \((FCP3)\)
   with template prices \(\overline P_T(K)\).  Run the generated-cover
   relaxation \((FCP6)\) once on the full universe
   \((\mathfrak A,\mathfrak T)\), and call its value
   \(\Psi_{\mathfrak A}^{\rm gen}\).

   If \(\Psi_{\mathfrak A}^{\rm gen}\le\Theta\), then every initial panel whose
   returned storage records lie in \(\mathfrak A\) is represented by residual
   fractional copies plus shared generated records of total price at most
   \(\Theta\), in addition to the explicit bounded fixed tails from
   \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-cap-star-storage-split}.

   If \(\Psi_{\mathfrak A}^{\rm gen}>\Theta\), then there is a single dual
   weighting \(y_a\) on all returned records satisfying
   \[
      \sum_{a\in\mathfrak A}y_a>\Theta,\qquad
      0\le y_a\le u_a,
      \tag{FCL1}
   \]
   and for every generated template \(T\in\mathfrak T\), every available
   cardinality \(K\in\mathcal K_T\), and every
   \(U\subseteq\mathcal A_T\) with \(|U|=K\),
   \[
      \sum_{a\in U}\alpha_{T,a}y_a\le\overline P_T(K).
      \tag{FCL2}
   \]
   Equivalently, every available top prefix in every reachable returned panel
   has nonpositive reduced cost against the same dual \(y\).

   Consequently repeated high-correlation returns do not create a multiplicative
   recursion overhead.  They may be flattened at build time into one finite
   generated-cover LP over the closure universe.  After flattening, the only
   remaining geometric task is to separate the single no-prefix dual
   \((FCL1)\)--\((FCL2)\), rather than to coordinate an adaptive sequence of
   child-panel failures.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-shared-cover-compiler} with
   \(\mathcal A=\mathfrak A\) and \(\mathcal T=\mathfrak T\).  If the full
   generated-cover value is at most \(\Theta\), the feasible solution of
   \((FCP6)\) materializes a feasible shared-cover solution of price at most
   \(\Theta\).  Since every returned storage-dominated record from the initial
   panel belongs to \(\mathfrak A\), this single solution covers the whole
   returned closure; the bounded-cardinality terms were already separated as
   explicit fixed tails in
   \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-cap-star-storage-split}.

   If the value is larger than \(\Theta\), finite LP duality in the same
   corollary gives \((FCP7)\) and all subset tests \((FCP5)\) for the full
   universe.  These are exactly \((FCL1)\)--\((FCL2)\).  Because
   \(\mathfrak A\) and \(\mathfrak T\) contain the returned records and
   templates by construction, any later top-prefix generated from a returned
   panel is one of the tested subsets, and therefore cannot be an improving
   column against this dual.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Flattened dual panel screen]
   \label{cor:flattened-dual-panel-screen}
   Work in the no-prefix dual residual \((FCL1)\)--\((FCL2)\) of
   \cref{cor:flattened-child-panel-closure}.  Let \(I\) be a finite panel of
   generated templates from the flattened universe.  For each \(i\in I\), choose
   a template \(T_i\in\mathfrak T\), an available cardinality
   \(K_i\in\mathcal K_{T_i}\), and nonnegative lower capture weights
   \(0\le w_{i,a}\le\alpha_{T_i,a}y_a\) on a finite set
   \(L_i\subseteq\mathcal A_{T_i}\).  Let \(U_i\) be the \(K_i\)-element top
   prefix of \(\mathcal A_{T_i}\) ordered by \(\alpha_{T_i,a}y_a\), and suppose
   preprocessing certifies
   \[
      \underline M_i
      \le
      \sum_{a\in L_i}w_{i,a},
      \qquad
      \overline P_i\ge\overline P_{T_i}(K_i).
      \tag{FDP1}
   \]
   If, for panel weights \(\lambda_i\ge0\),
   \[
      |L_i|\le K_i
      \qquad(\lambda_i>0),
      \tag{FDP2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_i\underline M_i
      >
      \sum_i\lambda_i\overline P_i,
      \tag{FDP3}
   \]
   then some flattened generated top prefix violates \((FCL2)\), and hence is a
   positive shared-cover column for the closure LP.

   Equivalently, in a surviving flattened no-prefix residual, every such
   lower-certified panel satisfies
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_i\underline M_i
      \le
      \sum_i\lambda_i\overline P_i .
      \tag{FDP4}
   \]
   Thus a range-reporting, additive-quantization, facility, list-decoding,
   lattice, or sampled clustering routine may be analyzed by aggregate
   lower-certified capture against the single dual \(y\).  Positive aggregate
   surplus always hardens to one deterministic generated top prefix already
   present in the flattened closure universe.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose no generated top prefix violates \((FCL2)\).  For each active
   \(i\), the top prefix \(U_i\) maximizes
   \(\sum_{a\in U}\alpha_{T_i,a}y_a\) among all \(K_i\)-subsets of
   \(\mathcal A_{T_i}\).  Since \(|L_i|\le K_i\), augment \(L_i\) arbitrarily
   to a \(K_i\)-subset \(L_i'\subseteq\mathcal A_{T_i}\).  Then
   \[
      \sum_{a\in L_i}w_{i,a}
      \le
      \sum_{a\in L_i}\alpha_{T_i,a}y_a
      \le
      \sum_{a\in L_i'}\alpha_{T_i,a}y_a
      \le
      \sum_{a\in U_i}\alpha_{T_i,a}y_a
      \le
      \overline P_{T_i}(K_i)
      \le
      \overline P_i .
   \]
   Multiplying by \(\lambda_i\) and summing gives \((FDP4)\), contradicting
   \((FDP3)\).  Hence some active top prefix must violate \((FCL2)\).  By
   \cref{cor:flattened-child-panel-closure}, this violation is exactly a
   positive generated shared-cover column in the full closure LP.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Flattened dual dyadic low-cover screen]
   \label{cor:flattened-dual-dyadic-low-cover}
   Work in the no-prefix dual residual \((FCL1)\)--\((FCL2)\), and put
   \(W=\{a\in\mathfrak A:y_a>0\}\).  By \((FCL1)\), \(W\ne\emptyset\).  Let
   \(y_{\min}=\min_{a\in W}y_a\), \(y_{\max}=\max_{a\in W}y_a\), and
   \[
      J_y=1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{y_{\max}}{y_{\min}}\right\rceil .
      \tag{FDY1}
   \]
   Then some dyadic layer
   \[
      L=\{a\in W:\delta\le y_a<2\delta\},
      \qquad \delta=2^jy_{\min},
      \tag{FDY2}
   \]
   satisfies
   \[
      \delta |L|
      \ge
      \frac1{2J_y}\sum_{a\in\mathfrak A}y_a
      >
      \frac{\Theta}{2J_y}.
      \tag{FDY3}
   \]

   Fix any such layer \(L\).  Suppose preprocessing certifies an assigned
   generated cover \(L=L_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup L_M\) with templates
   \(T_i\in\mathfrak T\), available cardinalities
   \(K_i\in\mathcal K_{T_i}\), and prices \(\overline P_i\ge
   \overline P_{T_i}(K_i)\), such that
   \[
      L_i\subseteq\mathcal A_{T_i},\qquad
      |L_i|\le K_i,\qquad
      \alpha_{T_i,a}\ge\eta_i
      \quad(a\in L_i),
      \tag{FDY4}
   \]
   for some \(\eta_i\ge0\).  If
   \[
      \delta\sum_{i=1}^M\eta_i|L_i|
      >
      \sum_{i=1}^M\overline P_i,
      \tag{FDY5}
   \]
   then some flattened generated top prefix violates \((FCL2)\), and hence
   gives a positive shared-cover column.

   Consequently every surviving no-prefix residual satisfies \((FDY5)\) with
   the reverse inequality for every certified assigned cover.  In particular,
   if \(\eta_i\ge\eta\) and
   \[
      \overline P_i
      \le
      \psi\left(A|L_i|^\rho+\zeta |L_i|^{1+\rho}\right),
      \qquad 0<\rho<1,
      \tag{FDY6}
   \]
   for all active parts, then the residual obeys
   \[
      \eta\delta |L|
      \le
      \psi\left(A M^{1-\rho}|L|^\rho+\zeta |L|^{1+\rho}\right).
      \tag{FDY7}
   \]
   Hence, when \(A>0\) and
   \[
      \eta\delta>2\psi\zeta |L|^\rho,
      \tag{FDY8}
   \]
   every such cover has
   \[
      M
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{\eta\delta |L|^{1-\rho}}{2\psi A}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{FDY9}
   \]
   If \(\zeta=0\), the same conclusion holds with \(2\psi A\) replaced by
   \(\psi A\).

   Thus the flattened separator may be attacked on one almost-uniform dual
   layer: either a certified geometric cover violates \((FDY7)\) and hardens to
   a positive generated prefix, or that layer supplies an explicit
   cover-number/list-size obstruction.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The dyadic layers in \((FDY2)\) partition \(W\).  On a layer with parameter
   \(\delta\), each element has \(y_a<2\delta\), so
   \[
      \sum_j\delta_j|L_j|
      \ge
      \frac12\sum_{a\in\mathfrak A}y_a .
   \]
   One layer contributes at least the average over \(J_y\) layers, and
   \((FCL1)\) gives the strict lower bound by \(\Theta\).

   For every cover part define lower capture weights
   \[
      w_{i,a}=\eta_i\delta\,\mathbf 1_{\{a\in L_i\}} .
   \]
   By \((FDY2)\) and \((FDY4)\),
   \(w_{i,a}\le\alpha_{T_i,a}y_a\) on \(L_i\).  Taking
   \(\underline M_i=\eta_i\delta |L_i|\) and panel weights
   \(\lambda_i=1\), conditions \((FDP1)\)--\((FDP2)\) are exactly
   \((FDY4)\) and the price certificates.  If \((FDY5)\) holds, then
   \((FDP3)\) holds, so
   \cref{cor:flattened-dual-panel-screen} produces a violating generated top
   prefix.

   The reverse inequality is the contrapositive in a surviving no-prefix
   residual.  Under \((FDY6)\) and \(\eta_i\ge\eta\), this gives
   \[
      \eta\delta |L|
      \le
      \psi\left(A\sum_i|L_i|^\rho+\zeta\sum_i|L_i|^{1+\rho}\right).
   \]
   Since the \(L_i\)'s partition \(L\),
   \[
      \sum_i|L_i|^\rho\le M^{1-\rho}|L|^\rho,\qquad
      \sum_i|L_i|^{1+\rho}\le |L|^{1+\rho},
   \]
   proving \((FDY7)\).  If \((FDY8)\) holds, the storage term in \((FDY7)\) is
   less than half of the left-hand side, and rearranging gives \((FDY9)\).  With
   \(\zeta=0\), the storage term is absent and the sharper constant follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Flattened dyadic packing witness]
   \label{cor:flattened-dyadic-packing-witness}
   Work with a dyadic layer \(L\) from
   \cref{cor:flattened-dual-dyadic-low-cover}, with parameters \((\delta,\eta)\)
   and price envelope \((FDY6)\).  Let \(d_{\rm gen}\) be a certified generated
   pseudometric on \(L\), and let \(\Delta_{\rm gen}>0\).  Assume that every
   assigned \(d_{\rm gen}\)-ball in \(L\) is materializable as a generated cover
   part with capture at least \(\eta\): for every \(e\in L\) and every nonempty
   \(B\subseteq L\cap B_{\rm gen}(e,\Delta_{\rm gen})\), preprocessing can
   certify a template \(T_B\), an available cardinality
   \(K_B\ge |B|\), and a price
   \[
      \overline P_B
      \le
      \psi\left(A|B|^\rho+\zeta |B|^{1+\rho}\right),
      \tag{FPW1}
   \]
   with \(\alpha_{T_B,a}\ge\eta\) for every \(a\in B\).

   Let \(E\subseteq L\) be any maximal \(\Delta_{\rm gen}\)-separated set.  If
   the flattened no-prefix residual survives, then
   \[
      \eta\delta |L|
      \le
      \psi\left(A |E|^{1-\rho}|L|^\rho+\zeta |L|^{1+\rho}\right).
      \tag{FPW2}
   \]
   In particular, under \((FDY8)\),
   \[
      |E|
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{\eta\delta |L|^{1-\rho}}{2\psi A}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \tag{FPW3}
   \]
   when \(A>0\), with the same \(\zeta=0\) sharpening as in
   \cref{cor:flattened-dual-dyadic-low-cover}.

   Equivalently, any generated metric with a certified covering estimate
   \[
      |E|\le M_{\rm gen}
      \tag{FPW4}
   \]
   closes the flattened residual whenever the right side of \((FPW2)\), with
   \(M_{\rm gen}\) in place of \(|E|\), is smaller than
   \(\eta\delta |L|\).  Thus a surviving flattened obstruction supplies a
   concrete separated packing witness in the generated metric, at exactly the
   entropy scale needed by the spherical/list-decoding energy screens.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(E\) is maximal, the balls
   \(L\cap B_{\rm gen}(e,\Delta_{\rm gen})\), \(e\in E\), cover \(L\).  Assign
   every \(a\in L\) to one covering center \(e(a)\), and let
   \(L_e=\{a:e(a)=e\}\).  Empty parts are discarded.  By the materialization
   hypothesis, these assigned balls satisfy \((FDY4)\) and \((FDY6)\) with
   \(M\le |E|\) and common capture \(\eta\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:flattened-dual-dyadic-low-cover} gives \((FPW2)\).  The lower
   bound \((FPW3)\) is the corresponding consequence of \((FDY9)\).

   Finally, if a certified upper bound \(M_{\rm gen}\) makes \((FPW2)\) false,
   then the assigned ball cover violates \((FDY7)\); by
   \cref{cor:flattened-dual-dyadic-low-cover}, this hardens to a positive
   generated top prefix.  The contrapositive is the claimed packing witness.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Flattened dyadic entropy-energy handoff]
   \label{cor:flattened-dyadic-entropy-energy-handoff}
   Work with a separated witness \(E\subseteq L\) supplied by
   \cref{cor:flattened-dyadic-packing-witness}.  Suppose every
   \(a\in E\) has a representative \(x_a\in\mathbb S^{d-1}\).  Let \(U_G\) be a
   spherical, Gaussian-cap, code, range/list-decoded, or other certified bucket
   drawn from a law \(G\), and partition the ordered distinct pairs
   \(E_{\ne}^2\) into finitely many profiles \(\Pi_E\).  Assume each profile
   \(\pi\in\Pi_E\) has a certified pair-intersection energy
   \[
      \Pr_G[x_a,x_{a'}\in U_G]\le e^{-I_\pi}
      \qquad((a,a')\in\pi).
      \tag{FEE1}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      X_E(G)=\sum_{a\in E}\mathbf 1\{x_a\in U_G\}.
      \tag{FEE2}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \E_GX_E(G)^2
      \le
      \sum_{a\in E}\Pr_G[x_a\in U_G]
      +
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi_E}|\pi|e^{-I_\pi}.
      \tag{FEE3}
   \]
   In particular, if
   \[
      I_\pi\ge\log|\pi|+\Lambda
      \qquad(\pi\in\Pi_E),
      \tag{FEE4}
   \]
   then the distinct-pair contribution of the flattened packing is at most
   \[
      |\Pi_E|e^{-\Lambda}.
      \tag{FEE5}
   \]

   Finally, fix one profile \(\pi\subseteq E_{\ne}^2\), assign nonnegative
   weights \(\omega_{a,a'}\) to its ordered pairs, and split
   \(\pi=\pi_{\rm lo}\dot\cup\pi_{\rm hi}\).  Suppose
   \[
      \sum_{(a,a')\in\pi_{\rm lo}}\omega_{a,a'}\le B_{\rm lo},
      \tag{FEE6}
   \]
   and every high edge has representative correlation at least
   \[
      \ip{x_a}{x_{a'}}\ge\underline\theta
      \qquad((a,a')\in\pi_{\rm hi})
      \tag{FEE7}
   \]
   for some \(-1<\underline\theta<1\).  Define
   \[
      M_a(a')=\omega_{a,a'}\mathbf 1_{\{(a,a')\in\pi_{\rm hi}\}},
      \qquad
      W_{\rm hi}=\sum_{a,a'\in E}M_a(a').
      \tag{FEE8}
   \]
   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), set \(J_\omega=1\).  Otherwise suppose the positive
   values of \(M_a(a')\) lie in a certified dyadic range
   \([\omega_{\min},\omega_{\max}]\), and put
   \[
      J_\omega=
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{\omega_{\max}}{\omega_{\min}}\right\rceil .
      \tag{FEE9}
   \]
   For dyadic levels \(t=\omega_{\min}2^j\), define
   \[
      V_{a,t}=\{a'\in E:M_a(a')\ge t\}.
      \tag{FEE10}
   \]
   Then every nonempty \(V_{a,t}\) has representatives in the cap ball
   \[
      x_{a'}\in B\!\left(x_a,\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)}\right),
      \tag{FEE11}
   \]
   and for every \(\Lambda_\star>0\), either
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}\le2|E|J_\omega\Lambda_\star,
      \tag{FEE12}
   \]
   or some dyadic high-correlation star satisfies
   \[
      t|V_{a,t}|\ge\Lambda_\star .
      \tag{FEE13}
   \]
   Consequently, if no exposed star has scale at least \(\Lambda_\star\), then
   the whole profile weight is bounded by
   \[
      \sum_{(a,a')\in\pi}\omega_{a,a'}
      \le
      B_{\rm lo}+2|E|J_\omega\Lambda_\star .
      \tag{FEE14}
   \]

   Thus a flattened no-prefix residual has reached the common terminal proof
   object: low generated cover closes it, entropy-energy pays the separated
   packing, or one finite high-correlation star is exposed for the generated
   prefix and smaller-radius dense verifiers.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Expanding the second moment gives
   \[
      \E_GX_E(G)^2
      =
      \sum_{a\in E}\Pr_G[x_a\in U_G]
      +
      \sum_{\substack{a,a'\in E\\a\ne a'}}
         \Pr_G[x_a,x_{a'}\in U_G].
   \]
   Summing \((FEE1)\) over the profile partition proves \((FEE3)\).  Under
   \((FEE4)\), each profile contributes at most \(e^{-\Lambda}\), giving
   \((FEE5)\).

   For the star statement, if \(a'\in V_{a,t}\), then \(M_a(a')>0\), so
   \((a,a')\in\pi_{\rm hi}\).  By \((FEE7)\),
   \[
      \|x_a-x_{a'}\|^2=2-2\ip{x_a}{x_{a'}}\le2(1-\underline\theta),
   \]
   proving \((FEE11)\).

   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), then \((FEE12)\) and \((FEE14)\) are immediate.  Assume
   \(W_{\rm hi}>0\).  The dyadic layer-cake estimate gives
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}\le2\sum_{a\in E}\sum_j t_j|V_{a,t_j}|,
      \qquad t_j=\omega_{\min}2^j.
   \]
   If every dyadic star has \(t_j|V_{a,t_j}|<\Lambda_\star\), then
   \(W_{\rm hi}\le2|E|J_\omega\Lambda_\star\).  Otherwise \((FEE13)\) holds.
   Adding the low contribution \((FEE6)\) gives \((FEE14)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Flattened high-correlation star screen]
   \label{cor:flattened-high-correlation-star-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:flattened-dyadic-entropy-energy-handoff}, and keep the flattened
   no-prefix dual \(y\) from \((FCL1)\)--\((FCL2)\).  For every nonempty dyadic
   high-correlation star \(V_{a,t}\) from \((FEE10)\), put
   \(h_{a,t}=|V_{a,t}|\).  Suppose preprocessing supplies a generated template
   \(T_{a,t}\in\mathfrak T\), an available cardinality
   \(h_{a,t}\in\mathcal K_{T_{a,t}}\), and a certified capture floor
   \(\chi>0\) satisfying
   \[
      V_{a,t}\subseteq\mathcal A_{T_{a,t}},
      \qquad
      \alpha_{T_{a,t},b}y_b\ge\chi
      \quad(b\in V_{a,t}).
      \tag{FHS1}
   \]
   If, for some star,
   \[
      \chi h_{a,t}>
      \overline P_{T_{a,t}}(h_{a,t}),
      \tag{FHS2}
   \]
   then the star is a one-record lower-capture panel satisfying
   \((FDP1)\)--\((FDP3)\), and hence some flattened generated top prefix
   violates \((FCL2)\).

   Consequently, in a surviving flattened no-prefix residual,
   \[
      \chi h_{a,t}
      \le
      \overline P_{T_{a,t}}(h_{a,t})
      \tag{FHS3}
   \]
   for every nonempty star.  Hence
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \frac2\chi
      \sum_{a\in E}\sum_t
         t\,\overline P_{T_{a,t}}(h_{a,t}).
      \tag{FHS4}
   \]

   If all used templates satisfy the common envelope
   \[
      \overline P_{T_{a,t}}(h)
      \le
      \psi\left(Ah^\rho+\zeta h^{1+\rho}\right),
      \qquad 0<\rho<1,
      \tag{FHS5}
   \]
   then every nonempty surviving star satisfies
   \[
      \chi\le\psi\left(Ah_{a,t}^{\rho-1}+\zeta h_{a,t}^{\rho}\right).
      \tag{FHS6}
   \]
   Define
   \[
      H_-=\left(\frac{2\psi A}{\chi}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \tag{FHS7}
   \]
   with \(H_-=0\) when \(A=0\).  If \(\zeta>0\), also define
   \[
      H_+=\left(\frac{\chi}{2\psi\zeta}\right)^{1/\rho}.
      \tag{FHS8}
   \]
   Then every nonempty surviving star is either bounded,
   \(h_{a,t}\le H_-\), or storage-dominated,
   \(\zeta>0\) and \(h_{a,t}\ge H_+\).

   Let \(\mathcal R_{\rm st}\) be the storage-dominated stars, and for
   \(r=(a,t)\in\mathcal R_{\rm st}\) define the returned fractional child record
   \[
      A_r=V_{a,t},\qquad
      \psi_r=t\psi\zeta,\qquad
      u_r=\psi_r|A_r|^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{FHS9}
   \]
   If \(\zeta=0\), interpret \(\mathcal R_{\rm st}=\emptyset\).  When
   \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), also interpret \(\omega_{\max}=0\).  Then
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      2|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-
      +
      \frac4\chi\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{\rm st}}u_r .
      \tag{FHS10}
   \]

   Thus every high-correlation star returned by the flattened entropy-energy
   handoff has the same terminal form as the generic child-panel branch:
   immediate lower-certified generated prefix, bounded fixed tail, or a
   storage-dominated returned child record for the flattened closure LP.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed nonempty star, take a one-record panel in
   \cref{cor:flattened-dual-panel-screen} with
   \(L_1=V_{a,t}\), \(K_1=h_{a,t}\),
   \(T_1=T_{a,t}\), \(w_{1,b}=\chi\) on \(V_{a,t}\),
   \(\underline M_1=\chi h_{a,t}\),
   \(\overline P_1=\overline P_{T_{a,t}}(h_{a,t})\), and \(\lambda_1=1\).
   Condition \((FHS1)\) gives \(w_{1,b}\le\alpha_{T_1,b}y_b\), and
   \(|L_1|=K_1\).  Thus \((FHS2)\) is exactly \((FDP3)\), so
   \cref{cor:flattened-dual-panel-screen} gives the violating top prefix.  Its
   contrapositive in a surviving no-prefix residual is \((FHS3)\).

   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), then \((FHS4)\) is immediate.  Otherwise the dyadic
   layer-cake estimate from the proof of
   \cref{cor:flattened-dyadic-entropy-energy-handoff} gives
   \[
      \frac12W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \sum_{a\in E}\sum_t t\,h_{a,t}.
   \]
   Multiplying \((FHS3)\) by \(t/\chi\) and summing proves \((FHS4)\).

   Under \((FHS5)\), dividing \((FHS3)\) by \(h_{a,t}>0\) gives \((FHS6)\).
   If \(h_{a,t}>H_-\), then \(\psi A h_{a,t}^{\rho-1}<\chi/2\).  Therefore
   \((FHS6)\) can hold only if
   \(\psi\zeta h_{a,t}^{\rho}\ge\chi/2\), which is exactly
   \(h_{a,t}\ge H_+\) when \(\zeta>0\), and is impossible when \(\zeta=0\).
   This proves the bounded/storage-dominated dichotomy.

   Split the layer-cake sum into stars with \(h_{a,t}\le H_-\) and
   storage-dominated stars.  The bounded side contributes at most
   \(|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-\).  For a storage-dominated star, the
   definition of \(H_+\) gives
   \[
      \chi\le2\psi\zeta h_{a,t}^{\rho},
   \]
   and hence
   \[
      t h_{a,t}
      \le
      \frac2\chi t\psi\zeta h_{a,t}^{1+\rho}
      =
      \frac2\chi u_{(a,t)} .
   \]
   Substituting these two estimates into the layer-cake bound proves
   \((FHS10)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Budgeted flattened star closure]
   \label{cor:budgeted-flattened-star-closure}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:flattened-high-correlation-star-screen} for one weighted profile
   \(\pi\subseteq E_{\ne}^2\).  Assume the low part has certified weight
   \(B_{\rm lo}\) as in \((FEE6)\), and write
   \[
      U_{\rm st}=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{\rm st}}u_r
      \tag{BFS1}
   \]
   for the total price of the storage-dominated returned star records from
   \((FHS9)\).  If no flattened generated top prefix violates \((FCL2)\), then
   \[
      \sum_{(a,a')\in\pi}\omega_{a,a'}
      \le
      B_{\rm lo}
      +2|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-
      +\frac4\chi U_{\rm st}.
      \tag{BFS2}
   \]
   Consequently a local proof budget \(B_\pi^{\rm bud}\) pays the whole
   profile whenever
   \[
      B_{\rm lo}
      +2|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-
      +\frac4\chi U_{\rm st}
      \le B_\pi^{\rm bud}.
      \tag{BFS3}
   \]
   Conversely, if no prefix fires and the profile is not paid by a budget
   \(B_\pi^{\rm bud}\), then the returned storage panel has certified price
   \[
      U_{\rm st}
      \ge
      \frac{\chi}{4}
      \left(
         B_\pi^{\rm bud}
         -B_{\rm lo}
         -2|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-
      \right)_+ .
      \tag{BFS4}
   \]

   Thus the flattened high-correlation return has an explicit scalar
   normal form.  After prefix search, an unpaid profile is not another adaptive
   branch: it is a bounded fixed tail plus one priced storage-dominated
   returned panel in the closure universe.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \((FEE6)\), the low part contributes at most \(B_{\rm lo}\).  The high
   part is exactly \(W_{\rm hi}\).  If a generated top prefix fires, there is
   nothing to prove, so assume no prefix violates \((FCL2)\).  Then
   \cref{cor:flattened-high-correlation-star-screen} gives
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      2|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-
      +\frac4\chi U_{\rm st}.
   \]
   Adding the low contribution proves \((BFS2)\), and \((BFS3)\) is immediate.
   If the profile is not paid by \(B_\pi^{\rm bud}\), then its weight is larger
   than \(B_\pi^{\rm bud}\).  Combining this strict inequality with
   \((BFS2)\) and rearranging gives \((BFS4)\), with the non-strict inequality
   and positive part covering
   the case in which the fixed terms already exceed the budget.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Returned-star sponsor-cut normal form]
   \label{cor:returned-star-sponsor-cut-normal-form}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:budgeted-flattened-star-closure}.  Assume no flattened generated
   top prefix violates \((FCL2)\), and put
   \[
      F_\pi=
      B_{\rm lo}+2|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-,
      \qquad
      C_\pi=
      \frac{\chi}{4}(B_\pi^{\rm bud}-F_\pi)_+ .
      \tag{RSF1}
   \]
   Let \(\mathcal C_{\rm st}\) be the finite child panel consisting of the
   storage-dominated returned star records \(r\in\mathcal R_{\rm st}\), with
   child prices \(u_r\) from \((FHS9)\).  Let \(\mathcal I_{\rm st}\) be any
   finite pool of sponsor atoms with weights \(b_i>0\), let
   \(\mathcal E_{\rm st}\subseteq
   \mathcal I_{\rm st}\times\mathcal C_{\rm st}\) be a certified
   compatibility relation, and put
   \[
      H_{\rm st}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{\rm st}}b_i,
      \qquad
      P_{\rm st}(\mathcal U)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal U}u_r,
      \qquad
      B_{\rm st}(\mathcal U)=
      \sum_{i\in N_{\rm st}(\mathcal U)}b_i .
      \tag{RSF2}
   \]
   Here
   \(N_{\rm st}(\mathcal U)=
   \{i:\exists r\in\mathcal U,\ (i,r)\in\mathcal E_{\rm st}\}\).
   Fix \(\beta\ge1\) and \(0<\varepsilon<1\).

   If every child subset satisfies the weak sponsor-cut inequality
   \[
      P_{\rm st}(\mathcal U)-\beta B_{\rm st}(\mathcal U)
      \le\varepsilon P_{\rm st}(\mathcal U),
      \tag{RSF3}
   \]
   then the returned-star storage is sponsor-paid after the constant
   inflation \(\beta_\varepsilon=\beta/(1-\varepsilon)\):
   \[
      U_{\rm st}
      =
      P_{\rm st}(\mathcal C_{\rm st})
      \le
      \beta_\varepsilon H_{\rm st}.
      \tag{RSF4}
   \]
   Consequently, if the profile is not paid by \(B_\pi^{\rm bud}\) and
   \[
      \beta_\varepsilon H_{\rm st}<C_\pi,
      \tag{RSF5}
   \]
   then \((RSF3)\) cannot hold for all subsets.  Hence there is a strong
   returned-star sponsor cut \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal C_{\rm st}\) with
   \[
      E^\beta_{\rm st}(\mathcal U)
      :=
      P_{\rm st}(\mathcal U)-\beta B_{\rm st}(\mathcal U)
      >
      \varepsilon P_{\rm st}(\mathcal U)>0 .
      \tag{RSF6}
   \]

   Now let \(\mathcal T_{\rm st}\) be a finite generated-merge template family
   for \(\mathcal C_{\rm st}\), satisfying the materialization and envelope
   hypotheses \((UCG2)\)--\((UCG5)\) with common parameters
   \(A>0,\psi_\star,\zeta,\rho\).  For any strong cut \(\mathcal U\) from
   \((RSF6)\), either some generated top prefix is a positive shared merge in
   the sense of \((UCG3)\), or a dyadic child-price layer
   \[
      L_{\rm st}=\{r\in\mathcal U:\theta\le u_r<2\theta\}
      \tag{RSF7}
   \]
   satisfies
   \[
      \theta|L_{\rm st}|
      \ge
      \frac{E^\beta_{\rm st}(\mathcal U)}
           {2D(\mathcal U)}
      \tag{RSF8}
   \]
   where
   \[
      D(\mathcal U)=
      1+\left\lceil
         \log_2
         \frac{\max_{r\in\mathcal U^+}u_r}
              {\min_{r\in\mathcal U^+}u_r}
      \right\rceil,
      \qquad
      \mathcal U^+=\{r\in\mathcal U:u_r>0\},
      \tag{RSF8a}
   \]
   and, if it is not storage-dominated,
   \[
      \theta>4\psi_\star\zeta |L_{\rm st}|^\rho,
      \tag{RSF9}
   \]
   has generated-cover lower bound
   \[
      N_{\rm gen}(L_{\rm st},\theta)
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{E^\beta_{\rm st}(\mathcal U)}
              {8D(\mathcal U)\psi_\star A\,|L_{\rm st}|^\rho}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{RSF10}
   \]
   Here \(N_{\rm gen}(L_{\rm st},\theta)\) is the least number of generated
   template parts needed to cover \(L_{\rm st}\) with cut capture at least
   \(\theta\) on each assigned child.
   If generated-metric balls on \(L_{\rm st}\) are materializable templates,
   then every maximal separated packing in that metric satisfies the
   corresponding packing lower bound of
   \cref{cor:generic-unsponsored-cut-packing-energy}.

   Thus an unpaid flattened high-correlation profile has a concrete terminal
   obstruction: either sponsor mass pays the returned-star storage, a generated
   shared merge fires, or one dyadic returned-star price layer has the explicit
   low-cover/list-size obstruction \((RSF10)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the profile is not paid by \(B_\pi^{\rm bud}\), then
   \cref{cor:budgeted-flattened-star-closure} gives
   \(U_{\rm st}\ge C_\pi\).  This is the only use of the profile budget.

   Suppose first that \((RSF3)\) holds for every
   \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal C_{\rm st}\).  Then
   \[
      P_{\rm st}(\mathcal U)
      \le
      \frac{\beta}{1-\varepsilon}B_{\rm st}(\mathcal U)
      =
      \beta_\varepsilon B_{\rm st}(\mathcal U)
      \qquad(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal C_{\rm st}).
   \]
   These are exactly the Hall inequalities \((GCF4)\) for the child panel
   \(\mathcal C_{\rm st}\), sponsor atoms \(\mathcal I_{\rm st}\),
   compatibility relation \(\mathcal E_{\rm st}\), and parameter
   \(\beta_\varepsilon\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:generic-child-panel-sponsor-flow} gives \((RSF4)\).  If also
   \((RSF5)\) held in an unpaid profile, then
   \(C_\pi\le U_{\rm st}\le\beta_\varepsilon H_{\rm st}<C_\pi\), a
   contradiction.  Therefore some subset violates \((RSF3)\), which is exactly
   \((RSF6)\).

   For such a strong cut, apply
   \cref{cor:generic-unsponsored-cut-generated-column} to the child panel
   \(\mathcal C_{\rm st}\), sponsor pool \(\mathcal I_{\rm st}\), relation
   \(\mathcal E_{\rm st}\), and generated family \(\mathcal T_{\rm st}\).  Its
   strong-cut branch gives the positive generated-merge alternative or the
   dyadic layer \((RSF7)\).  Equations \((RSF8)\)--\((RSF10)\) are the
   corresponding conclusions \((UCG11)\)--\((UCG13)\) and \((UCG12)\), with
   \(E^\beta\), \(P\), and \(B\) relabeled by their returned-star versions.
   The final packing statement is the generated-metric ball consequence in
   \cref{cor:generic-unsponsored-cut-packing-energy}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Average generated-record screen for returned-star layers]
   \label{cor:average-generated-record-returned-star-layer}
   Work in the strong-cut, no-generated-prefix branch of
   \cref{cor:returned-star-sponsor-cut-normal-form}, and fix the returned-star
   child-price layer
   \[
      L_{\rm st}=\{r\in\mathcal U:\theta\le u_r<2\theta\}.
   \]
   Let \(\nu\) be any finite proposal law over materializable generated records
   for this layer.  A proposed record \(R\) has represented subset
   \(C_R\subseteq L_{\rm st}\) and certified one-time shared price \(P_R\).  It
   is valid if adding \(R\) as a generated-template subset for the sponsor cut
   would capture at least \(\theta\) units of cut price from every
   \(r\in C_R\).  If
   \[
      \E_{R\sim\nu}\bigl[\theta |C_R|-2P_R\bigr]>0,
      \tag{RGA1}
   \]
   then some generated record has positive reduced cost, so the no-prefix
   branch is impossible.

   Consequently every surviving no-prefix returned-star layer obeys, for every
   such proposal law,
   \[
      \theta\sum_{r\in L_{\rm st}}h_r
      \le
      2\E_{R\sim\nu}P_R,
      \qquad
      h_r=\Pr_{R\sim\nu}[r\in C_R].
      \tag{RGA2}
   \]
   In particular, if \(h_r\ge a_L\) for all \(r\in L_{\rm st}\), then
   \[
      a_L\theta |L_{\rm st}|
      \le
      2\E_{R\sim\nu}P_R .
      \tag{RGA3}
   \]

   If each generated record has list size \(H_R=|C_R|\) and satisfies
   \[
      P_R\le
      \psi_\star\left(AH_R^\rho+\zeta H_R^{1+\rho}\right),
      \qquad 0<\rho<1 ,
      \tag{RGA4}
   \]
   then a no-prefix residual with marginal hit \(a_L\) forces
   \[
      a_L\theta |L_{\rm st}|
      \le
      2\psi_\star
      \left(A\,\E H_R^\rho+\zeta\,\E H_R^{1+\rho}\right).
      \tag{RGA5}
   \]
   Combining \((RGA3)\) with \((RSF8)\), every surviving returned-star layer
   satisfies
   \[
      \E_{R\sim\nu}P_R
      \ge
      \frac{a_L\,E^\beta_{\rm st}(\mathcal U)}
           {4D(\mathcal U)}
      \tag{RGA6}
   \]
   for every valid proposal law with marginal hit \(a_L\).

   Thus a tensorized spherical, range-reporting, additive-quantization,
   facility, list-decoding, lattice, or seeded-clustering proposal law closes
   the returned-star layer as soon as its expected certified price is below the
   normalized hit lower bound in \((RGA6)\).  Otherwise the layer has a genuine
   average list-size obstruction.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((RGA1)\) holds, then at least one generated record \(R\) satisfies
   \(\theta|C_R|>2P_R\).  Since \(R\) captures at least \(\theta\) from each
   child in \(C_R\), the top prefix of the corresponding generated template at
   cardinality \(|C_R|\) satisfies the positive-merge inequality \((UCG3)\).
   This contradicts the no-generated-prefix branch.

   Therefore every surviving no-prefix residual has
   \(\E[\theta|C_R|-2P_R]\le0\).  Since
   \[
      \E|C_R|=\sum_{r\in L_{\rm st}}\Pr[r\in C_R]
      =\sum_{r\in L_{\rm st}}h_r,
   \]
   this is \((RGA2)\).  The uniform marginal lower bound gives \((RGA3)\), and
   substituting the price envelope \((RGA4)\) gives \((RGA5)\).  Finally,
   \((RSF8)\) gives
   \(\theta|L_{\rm st}|\ge
   E^\beta_{\rm st}(\mathcal U)/(2D(\mathcal U))\), so \((RGA3)\) implies
   \((RGA6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fractional generated cover for returned-star layers]
   \label{cor:fractional-generated-cover-returned-star-layer}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:average-generated-record-returned-star-layer}, and let
   \(\mathcal R_{\rm st,L}\) be a finite family of materializable generated
   records for \(L_{\rm st}\).  Each \(R\in\mathcal R_{\rm st,L}\) has
   represented subset \(C_R\subseteq L_{\rm st}\) and certified shared price
   \(P_R\), and is valid in the sense of
   \cref{cor:average-generated-record-returned-star-layer}.  Assume
   \(\mathcal R_{\rm st,L}\) covers \(L_{\rm st}\).  Consider the finite
   covering LP
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Phi_{\rm st,L}=\min
      & \displaystyle\sum_{R\in\mathcal R_{\rm st,L}}P_R\lambda_R\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{R:\,r\in C_R}\lambda_R\ge1
        \qquad(r\in L_{\rm st}),\\[0.8em]
      & \lambda_R\ge0 .
   \end{array}
      \tag{RFG1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \Phi_{\rm st,L}<\frac{\theta |L_{\rm st}|}{2},
      \tag{RFG2}
   \]
   then some generated top prefix has positive reduced cost, so the no-prefix
   residual is impossible.  Conversely, if the no-prefix residual survives,
   then
   \[
      \Phi_{\rm st,L}\ge\frac{\theta |L_{\rm st}|}{2}
      \ge
      \frac{E^\beta_{\rm st}(\mathcal U)}{4D(\mathcal U)} .
      \tag{RFG3}
   \]
   Equivalently, finite LP duality gives weights \(y_r\ge0\) on
   \(r\in L_{\rm st}\) such that
   \[
      \sum_{r\in L_{\rm st}}y_r
      \ge
      \frac{\theta |L_{\rm st}|}{2},
      \qquad
      \sum_{r\in C_R}y_r\le P_R
      \quad(R\in\mathcal R_{\rm st,L}).
      \tag{RFG4}
   \]

   The weighted residual contains an almost-uniform heavy layer.  Let
   \(W=\{r\in L_{\rm st}:y_r>0\}\).  If \(W\ne\emptyset\), put
   \[
      y_{\min}=\min_{r\in W}y_r,\qquad
      y_{\max}=\max_{r\in W}y_r,\qquad
      J_y=1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{y_{\max}}{y_{\min}}\right\rceil .
      \tag{RFG5}
   \]
   Then some dyadic layer
   \[
      L_0=\{r\in W:\delta\le y_r<2\delta\}
      \tag{RFG6}
   \]
   satisfies
   \[
      \delta |L_0|
      \ge
      \frac{1}{2J_y}\sum_{r\in L_{\rm st}}y_r
      \ge
      \frac{\theta |L_{\rm st}|}{4J_y}.
      \tag{RFG7}
   \]

   Finally suppose \(L_0\) has a certified generated cover by a partition
   \(L_0=L_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup L_J\) into nonempty parts.  For each \(i\) there
   is \(R_i\in\mathcal R_{\rm st,L}\) with
   \[
      L_i\subseteq C_{R_i},\qquad
      P_{R_i}\le
      \psi_\star\left(A|L_i|^\rho+\zeta |L_i|^{1+\rho}\right),
      \qquad 0<\rho<1 .
      \tag{RFG8}
   \]
   Then every no-prefix residual obeys
   \[
      \delta |L_0|
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(AJ^{1-\rho}|L_0|^\rho
      +\zeta |L_0|^{1+\rho}\right).
      \tag{RFG9}
   \]
   Hence, if \(A>0\) and
   \[
      \delta>2\psi_\star\zeta |L_0|^\rho,
      \tag{RFG10}
   \]
   every surviving residual has
   \[
      J
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{\delta |L_0|^{1-\rho}}{2\psi_\star A}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{RFG11}
   \]
   When \(\zeta=0\), the same conclusion holds with \(2\psi_\star A\) replaced
   by \(\psi_\star A\).

   Thus every unpaid returned-star sponsor layer has a deterministic
   verifier-facing normal form: either a finite generated-cover LP has value
   below \(\theta|L_{\rm st}|/2\) and a positive prefix fires, or a single
   dyadic dual-heavy sublayer defeats all certified low-price generated covers
   by the explicit lower bound \((RFG11)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For any feasible \(\lambda\) in \((RFG1)\),
   \[
      \sum_{R\in\mathcal R_{\rm st,L}}\lambda_R|C_R|
      =
      \sum_{r\in L_{\rm st}}\sum_{R:\,r\in C_R}\lambda_R
      \ge |L_{\rm st}|.
      \tag{RFG12}
   \]
   If \((RFG2)\) holds, choose a feasible \(\lambda\) with
   \(\sum_RP_R\lambda_R<\theta|L_{\rm st}|/2\).  Combining with \((RFG12)\)
   gives
   \[
      \sum_R\lambda_R(\theta|C_R|-2P_R)>0,
   \]
   so some record has \(\theta|C_R|>2P_R\).  By
   \cref{cor:average-generated-record-returned-star-layer}, this is a positive
   generated prefix.  Hence a surviving no-prefix residual must satisfy the
   first inequality in \((RFG3)\), and the second is \((RSF8)\).

   The primal is finite and feasible by assumption.  LP duality gives
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Phi_{\rm st,L}=\max
      & \displaystyle\sum_{r\in L_{\rm st}}y_r\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & y_r\ge0,\\[0.6em]
      & \displaystyle\sum_{r\in C_R}y_r\le P_R
        \qquad(R\in\mathcal R_{\rm st,L}),
   \end{array}
      \tag{RFG13}
   \]
   and \((RFG3)\) supplies a dual solution satisfying \((RFG4)\).

   The dyadic layers in \((RFG6)\) partition \(W\).  On a layer with parameter
   \(\delta\), every element has \(y_r<2\delta\), so
   \[
      \sum_{\text{layers }L_j}\delta_j|L_j|
      \ge
      \frac12\sum_{r\in L_{\rm st}}y_r .
   \]
   One layer contributes at least the average over \(J_y\) layers, and
   \((RFG4)\) gives \((RFG7)\).

   For each cover part \(L_i\), the dual constraint in \((RFG4)\) and
   \(L_i\subseteq C_{R_i}\) give
   \[
      \delta |L_i|
      \le
      \sum_{r\in L_i}y_r
      \le
      \sum_{r\in C_{R_i}}y_r
      \le P_{R_i}.
   \]
