   Summing over \(i\), applying \((RFG8)\), and using
   \[
      \sum_i|L_i|^\rho\le J^{1-\rho}|L_0|^\rho,
      \qquad
      \sum_i|L_i|^{1+\rho}\le |L_0|^{1+\rho},
   \]
   proves \((RFG9)\).  Under \((RFG10)\), the storage term is less than half
   the left side, and rearranging gives \((RFG11)\).  If \(\zeta=0\), the
   storage term is absent and the sharper constant follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Returned-star dual packing-energy handoff]
   \label{cor:returned-star-dual-packing-energy-handoff}
   Work in the no-prefix residual of
   \cref{cor:fractional-generated-cover-returned-star-layer}.  Fix the dyadic
   dual-heavy sublayer \(L_0\) from \((RFG6)\), put \(K=|L_0|\), and keep its
   lower dual weight \(\delta\).  Let \(d_{\rm gen}\) be a certified generated
   pseudometric on \(L_0\), and let \(\Delta_{\rm gen}>0\).  Assume that for
   every \(e\in L_0\) and every nonempty
   \(B\subseteq L_0\cap B_{\rm gen}(e,\Delta_{\rm gen})\), preprocessing has a
   materializable generated record \(R_B\in\mathcal R_{\rm st,L}\) with
   \[
      B\subseteq C_{R_B},
      \qquad
      P_{R_B}
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(A|B|^\rho+\zeta |B|^{1+\rho}\right),
      \qquad 0<\rho<1 .
      \tag{RPE1}
   \]
   If \(E\subseteq L_0\) is maximal \(\Delta_{\rm gen}\)-separated, then every
   surviving no-prefix residual satisfies
   \[
      \delta K
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(A|E|^{1-\rho}K^\rho+\zeta K^{1+\rho}\right).
      \tag{RPE2}
   \]
   In particular, under \((RFG10)\),
   \[
      |E|
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{\delta K^{1-\rho}}{2\psi_\star A}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \tag{RPE3}
   \]
   when \(A>0\), with the same \(\zeta=0\) sharpening as in
   \cref{cor:fractional-generated-cover-returned-star-layer}.

   Suppose now that every \(r\in E\) has a representative
   \(x_r\in\mathbb S^{d-1}\).  Let \(U_G\) be a spherical, Gaussian-cap, code,
   range/list-decoded, lattice, or other certified bucket drawn from a law
   \(G\), and partition the ordered distinct pairs \(E_{\ne}^2\) into profiles
   \(\Pi_E\).  If each profile \(\pi\in\Pi_E\) has certified pair energy
   \[
      \Pr_G[x_r,x_{r'}\in U_G]\le e^{-I_\pi}
      \qquad ((r,r')\in\pi),
      \tag{RPE4}
   \]
   and
   \[
      X_E(G)=\sum_{r\in E}\mathbf 1\{x_r\in U_G\},
      \tag{RPE5}
   \]
   then
   \[
      \E_GX_E(G)^2
      \le
      \sum_{r\in E}\Pr_G[x_r\in U_G]
      +
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi_E}|\pi|e^{-I_\pi}.
      \tag{RPE6}
   \]
   Hence \(I_\pi\ge\log|\pi|+\Lambda\) for every profile makes the total
   distinct-pair contribution at most \(|\Pi_E|e^{-\Lambda}\).

   Finally fix one weighted profile \(\pi\subseteq E_{\ne}^2\).  Give its
   ordered pairs weights \(\omega_{r,r'}\ge0\), split
   \(\pi=\pi_{\rm lo}\dot\cup\pi_{\rm hi}\), and assume
   \[
      \sum_{(r,r')\in\pi_{\rm lo}}\omega_{r,r'}\le B_{\rm lo},
      \qquad
      \ip{x_r}{x_{r'}}\ge\underline\theta
      \quad((r,r')\in\pi_{\rm hi})
      \tag{RPE7}
   \]
   for some \(-1<\underline\theta<1\).  Put
   \[
      M_r(r')=\omega_{r,r'}\mathbf 1_{\{(r,r')\in\pi_{\rm hi}\}},
      \qquad
      W_{\rm hi}=\sum_{r,r'\in E}M_r(r').
      \tag{RPE8}
   \]
   If \(W_{\rm hi}>0\), assume the positive values of \(M_r(r')\) lie in a
   certified dyadic range \([\omega_{\min},\omega_{\max}]\), put
   \(J_\omega=1+\lceil\log_2(\omega_{\max}/\omega_{\min})\rceil\), and define
   dyadic stars
   \[
      V_{r,t}=\{r'\in E:M_r(r')\ge t\},
      \qquad t=\omega_{\min}2^j,\quad 0\le j<J_\omega .
      \tag{RPE9}
   \]
   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), set \(J_\omega=1\) and \(\omega_{\max}=0\).  Every
   nonempty \(V_{r,t}\) lies in the cap ball
   \[
      x_{r'}\in B\!\left(x_r,\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)}\right).
      \tag{RPE10}
   \]
   Moreover, if such a star has a materializable generated record
   \(R_{r,t}\in\mathcal R_{\rm st,L}\) with
   \(V_{r,t}\subseteq C_{R_{r,t}}\) and
   \[
      P_{R_{r,t}}<\delta |V_{r,t}|,
      \tag{RPE11}
   \]
   then the dual constraint \((RFG4)\) is violated, so the returned-star
   residual has a positive generated prefix.

   Consequently, if every nonempty dyadic star is materialized with the common
   envelope
   \[
      P_{R_{r,t}}
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(Ah_{r,t}^\rho+\zeta h_{r,t}^{1+\rho}\right),
      \qquad h_{r,t}=|V_{r,t}|,
      \tag{RPE12}
   \]
   then in any surviving residual
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(Ah_{r,t}^{\rho-1}+\zeta h_{r,t}^{\rho}\right)
      \tag{RPE13}
   \]
   for every nonempty star.  With
   \[
      H_-^{\rm st}
      =
      \left(\frac{2\psi_\star A}{\delta}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \tag{RPE14}
   \]
   interpreted as \(0\) when \(A=0\), and
   \(H_+^{\rm st}=(\delta/(2\psi_\star\zeta))^{1/\rho}\) when \(\zeta>0\),
   every surviving star is either bounded,
   \(h_{r,t}\le H_-^{\rm st}\), or storage-dominated,
   \(\zeta>0\) and \(h_{r,t}\ge H_+^{\rm st}\).  If
   \(\mathcal S_{\rm st}^{\rm ret}\) denotes the storage-dominated stars and
   \[
      u_s^{\rm ret}=\psi_\star\zeta\,t\,h_s^{1+\rho}
      \qquad(s=(r,t)\in\mathcal S_{\rm st}^{\rm ret}),
      \tag{RPE15}
   \]
   then
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      2|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-^{\rm st}
      +
      \frac4\delta
      \sum_{s\in\mathcal S_{\rm st}^{\rm ret}}u_s^{\rm ret}.
      \tag{RPE16}
   \]

   Thus the returned-star low-cover obstruction has the same closed interface
   as the flattened and cap-overload duals: low generated cover gives a
   positive prefix, a separated packing is paid by entropy-energy, and any
   remaining high-correlation excess is a single explicit star-price tail.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(E\) is maximal, the balls
   \(L_0\cap B_{\rm gen}(e,\Delta_{\rm gen})\), \(e\in E\), cover \(L_0\).
   Assign each \(r\in L_0\) to one covering ball and discard empty parts.
   The records from \((RPE1)\) give a certified generated cover of the form
   \((RFG8)\) with at most \(|E|\) parts.  Applying \((RFG9)\) proves
   \((RPE2)\), and \((RPE3)\) is the corresponding consequence of
   \((RFG11)\).

   Expanding the second moment gives
   \[
      \E_GX_E(G)^2
      =
      \sum_{r\in E}\Pr_G[x_r\in U_G]
      +
      \sum_{\substack{r,r'\in E\\r\ne r'}}
         \Pr_G[x_r,x_{r'}\in U_G].
   \]
   Summing the profile bounds \((RPE4)\) over the partition proves
   \((RPE6)\), and the displayed entropy condition gives the stated
   \(|\Pi_E|e^{-\Lambda}\) bound.

   If \(r'\in V_{r,t}\), then \(M_r(r')>0\), so \((r,r')\in\pi_{\rm hi}\).
   By \((RPE7)\),
   \[
      \|x_r-x_{r'}\|^2=2-2\ip{x_r}{x_{r'}}\le2(1-\underline\theta),
   \]
   proving \((RPE10)\).  Also \(V_{r,t}\subseteq E\subseteq L_0\), and every
   member of \(L_0\) has dual weight at least \(\delta\).  Thus \((RPE11)\)
   implies
   \[
      \sum_{r'\in C_{R_{r,t}}}y_{r'}
      \ge
      \sum_{r'\in V_{r,t}}y_{r'}
      \ge
      \delta |V_{r,t}|
      >
      P_{R_{r,t}},
   \]
   contradicting \((RFG4)\).  By
   \cref{cor:fractional-generated-cover-returned-star-layer}, this
   contradiction is exactly the positive-prefix alternative.

   In a surviving no-prefix residual, therefore,
   \(\delta h_{r,t}\le P_{R_{r,t}}\) for every materialized nonempty star.
   Combining this with \((RPE12)\) and dividing by \(h_{r,t}>0\) proves
   \((RPE13)\).  The bounded/storage-dominated dichotomy follows from the same
   scalar rearrangement used in
   \cref{cor:flattened-high-correlation-star-screen}: if
   \(h_{r,t}>H_-^{\rm st}\), then the \(Ah^{\rho-1}\) term in \((RPE13)\) is
   less than \(\delta/2\), so \(\zeta>0\) and
   \(h_{r,t}\ge H_+^{\rm st}\).

   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), then \((RPE16)\) is immediate.  Otherwise the dyadic
   layer-cake estimate gives
   \[
      \frac12 W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \sum_{r\in E}\sum_t t\,h_{r,t}.
   \]
   Split this sum into bounded and storage-dominated stars.  The bounded side
   contributes at most \(|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-^{\rm st}\).  For a
   storage-dominated star, the definition of \(H_+^{\rm st}\) gives
   \[
      \delta\le2\psi_\star\zeta h_{r,t}^{\rho},
   \]
   and hence
   \[
      t h_{r,t}
      \le
      \frac2\delta\psi_\star\zeta\,t\,h_{r,t}^{1+\rho}
      =
      \frac2\delta u_{(r,t)}^{\rm ret}.
   \]
   Substituting these estimates in the layer-cake bound proves \((RPE16)\).
   When \(\zeta=0\), the storage-dominated family is empty and the same
   argument gives only the bounded fixed tail.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Returned-star tail shared-cover adapter]
   \label{cor:returned-star-tail-shared-cover-adapter}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:returned-star-dual-packing-energy-handoff}, and write
   \(\mathcal S=\mathcal S_{\rm st}^{\rm ret}\).  For
   \(s=(r,t)\in\mathcal S\), put
   \[
      A_s^{\rm ret}=V_{r,t},
      \qquad
      u_s=u_s^{\rm ret}.
      \tag{RTS1}
   \]
   Let \(\mathcal R^{\rm ret}\) be a finite family of candidate shared records
   for this tail.  A record \(c\in\mathcal R^{\rm ret}\) has one-time recursive
   storage price \(P_c\ge0\) and certified coverage coefficients
   \(0\le g_{c,s}\le1\).  Define
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Phi^{\rm ret}=\min
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{s\in\mathcal S}u_se_s
        +\sum_{c\in\mathcal R^{\rm ret}}P_c\lambda_c\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        e_s+\sum_{c\in\mathcal R^{\rm ret}}\lambda_c g_{c,s}\ge1
        \qquad(s\in\mathcal S),\\[0.8em]
      & e_s\ge0,\qquad \lambda_c\ge0 .
   \end{array}
      \tag{RTS2}
   \]
   Its dual is
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Phi^{\rm ret}=\max
      & \displaystyle\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}y_s\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & 0\le y_s\le u_s
        \qquad(s\in\mathcal S),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{s\in\mathcal S}g_{c,s}y_s\le P_c
        \qquad(c\in\mathcal R^{\rm ret}).
   \end{array}
      \tag{RTS3}
   \]

   Consequently the storage-dominated term in \((RPE16)\) may be paid by the
   shared-cover value.  For any desired allowance \(B_{\rm ret}\) and fixed
   overhead \(\Gamma\ge0\), the returned-star high-correlation profile is paid
   within
   \[
      2|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-^{\rm st}+B_{\rm ret}
      \tag{RTS4}
   \]
   whenever
   \[
      \Gamma+\Phi^{\rm ret}\le\frac{\delta}{4}B_{\rm ret}.
      \tag{RTS5}
   \]
   If \(\Phi^{\rm ret}>\Theta\), then there is a dual weighting satisfying
   \[
      \sum_{s\in\mathcal S}y_s>\Theta,\qquad
      0\le y_s\le u_s,\qquad
      \sum_sg_{c,s}y_s\le P_c
      \quad(c\in\mathcal R^{\rm ret}).
      \tag{RTS6}
   \]

   Finally suppose a generated template \(T\) has a search container
   \(\mathcal S_T\subseteq\mathcal S\), capture weights
   \(a_{T,s}\in[0,1]\), available cardinalities \(\mathcal K_T\), and certified
   prices \(\overline P_T(K)\).  Assume every \(U\subseteq\mathcal S_T\) with
   \(|U|=K\in\mathcal K_T\) can be materialized as a record \(c(T,U)\) with
   \[
      P_{c(T,U)}\le\overline P_T(K),
      \qquad
      g_{c(T,U),s}\ge a_{T,s}\mathbf 1_{\{s\in U\}} .
      \tag{RTS7}
   \]
   In a dual residual \(y\), order \(\mathcal S_T=\{s_1,s_2,\ldots\}\) by
   nonincreasing \(a_{T,s}y_s\).  If, for some \(K\in\mathcal K_T\),
   \[
      \sum_{j\le K}a_{T,s_j}y_{s_j}>\overline P_T(K),
      \tag{RTS8}
   \]
   then \(c(T,\{s_1,\ldots,s_K\})\) is an improving shared-cover column.  If no
   such prefix is improving, every \(K\)-subset \(U\subseteq\mathcal S_T\)
   satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{s\in U}a_{T,s}y_s\le\overline P_T(K).
      \tag{RTS9}
   \]

   Thus the second returned-star tail is not a new recursive branch.  It is an
   ordinary finite priced child panel: either it is paid by one shared-cover LP,
   or it exposes the same top-prefix dual obstruction already used by the
   flattened closure.  In a build-time implementation, these tail records and
   templates can be added to the flattened closure universe before the single
   closure LP is solved.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The program \((RTS2)\) is finite and feasible by taking \(e_s=1\).  Assign a
   dual variable \(y_s\ge0\) to each cover constraint.  The coefficients of
   \(e_s\) and \(\lambda_c\) give \(y_s\le u_s\) and
   \(\sum_sg_{c,s}y_s\le P_c\), respectively.  Finite LP duality proves
   \((RTS3)\).

   A feasible primal solution represents each storage-dominated returned star by
   an \(e_s\)-fractional residual copy and by shared records covering it.  The
   objective is the corresponding shared-canonical tail price.  Since
   \((RPE16)\) charges the raw tail only through the coefficient \(4/\delta\),
   replacing that tail by \(\Gamma+\Phi^{\rm ret}\) and using \((RTS5)\) gives
   the payment bound \((RTS4)\).  The dual obstruction \((RTS6)\) is the
   contrapositive of strong duality.

   If \((RTS8)\) holds and \(U_K=\{s_1,\ldots,s_K\}\), then \((RTS7)\) gives
   \[
      \sum_sg_{c(T,U_K),s}y_s
      \ge
      \sum_{j\le K}a_{T,s_j}y_{s_j}
      >
      \overline P_T(K)
      \ge
      P_{c(T,U_K)} .
   \]
   Hence \(c(T,U_K)\) violates the dual constraint and is an improving column.
   For a fixed \(K\), the top \(K\) elements in the order of \(a_{T,s}y_s\)
   maximize the left side over all \(K\)-subsets, proving \((RTS9)\) when no
   prefix improves.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Flattened panel-separator endpoint]
   \label{cor:flattened-panel-separator-endpoint}
   Work at a localized resident node with full certified panel universe
   \(\mathcal Z_\star\).  Suppose every storage-dominated child panel returned
   by the generic high-correlation child-panel machinery is submitted to a
   finite flattened closure \((\mathfrak A,\mathfrak T)\) as in
   \cref{cor:flattened-child-panel-closure}, with allowance \(\Theta\), and that
   every generated top prefix certified by
   \cref{cor:flattened-dual-panel-screen} is represented in
   \(\mathcal Z_\star\).

   Assume the following flattened separator condition holds for every such
   closure.  Either
   \[
      \Psi_{\mathfrak A}^{\rm gen}\le\Theta,
      \tag{FLT1}
   \]
   or, for the dual \(y\) exposed by
   \cref{cor:flattened-child-panel-closure}, preprocessing certifies a finite
   lower-capture panel satisfying \((FDP1)\)--\((FDP3)\).

   Then the storage-dominated returned panel leaves no live residual: in the
   first case it is paid inside the allowance \(\Theta\), while in the second
   case a positive generated top-prefix column in \(\mathcal Z_\star\) fires.

   Consequently, in the hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:child-panel-split-profile-endpoint}, one may replace the final
   no-prefix child-panel residual by this flattened separator condition.  If the
   condition holds at every localized resident node for every flattened residual
   that is not already paid by sponsor flow, low-correlation energy, or a
   verified dense/generated prefix, then the positive shared-panel separator
   \((SPP1)\) holds at every node and hence
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,\qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed flattened closure, if \((FLT1)\) holds, the first conclusion of
   \cref{cor:flattened-child-panel-closure} gives a residual-plus-shared-record
   representation of total price at most \(\Theta\), apart from the fixed tails
   that were explicitly separated by
   \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-cap-star-storage-split}.  Thus this
   returned panel is paid within the local storage allowance.

   If \((FLT1)\) fails, the same closure corollary supplies the no-prefix dual
   \(y\).  The assumed lower-capture panel satisfies the hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:flattened-dual-panel-screen}, so some generated top prefix violates
   the closure dual.  By the universe hypothesis, this verified prefix is an
   element of \(\mathcal Z_\star\), and therefore gives the positive
   shared-panel column required by \((SPP1)\) for the current exact-signature
   dual.

   Now consider the global hypothesis.  The proof of
   \cref{cor:child-panel-split-profile-endpoint} lists all possible terminal
   alternatives of the generic child-panel, unsponsored-cut, sponsor-tail, and
   cap-overload reductions.  Sponsor flow, low-correlation energy, and verified
   dense/generated prefixes are already terminal there.  Every remaining
   storage-dominated returned panel is terminal by the preceding paragraph:
   either it is paid by its flattened closure or it produces a positive column in
   \(\mathcal Z_\star\).  Hence no normalized exact-signature dual can survive
   without satisfying \((SPP1)\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint} at every localized node
   gives the displayed query and storage bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Generic child-panel pair-witness storage identity]
   \label{cor:generic-child-panel-pair-witness-storage}
   Let \(P\) be a finite metric set and let
   \(\mathcal T_2(P,\delta)\) be the ordered separated-pair universe from
   \cref{lem:packing-list-tuple-moment}; repetitions are allowed.  Let
   \(\mathcal C\) be a finite family of priced child records.  Each
   \(g\in\mathcal C\) has a nonempty certified \(\delta\)-separated witness
   set \(A_g\subseteq P\), a price factor \(\psi_g\ge0\), an exponent
   \(0\le\rho_g\le1\), and storage price
   \[
      u_g=\psi_g|A_g|^{1+\rho_g}.
      \tag{GPW1}
   \]
   Define the pair-congestion weight
   \[
      W(x,y)=
      \sum_{\substack{g\in\mathcal C:\\ x,y\in A_g}}
      \psi_g|A_g|^{\rho_g-1}
      \qquad((x,y)\in\mathcal T_2(P,\delta)).
      \tag{GPW2}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \sum_{g\in\mathcal C}u_g
      =
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\mathcal T_2(P,\delta)}W(x,y).
      \tag{GPW3}
   \]
   Consequently, if \(\mathcal T_2(P,\delta)\) is partitioned into profiles
   \(\Pi\), and \(W(x,y)\le B_\pi\) for every \((x,y)\in\pi\), then
   \[
      \sum_{g\in\mathcal C}u_g
      \le
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}|\pi|B_\pi .
      \tag{GPW4}
   \]

   More generally, suppose a finite weighted occurrence family
   \(\mathcal B\) points to the same child records by a map
   \(\kappa:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C\), with weights \(\omega_b>0\), and let
   \[
      m(g)=\sum_{b:\kappa(b)=g}\omega_b .
      \tag{GPW5}
   \]
   For children with \(m(g)>0\), define
   \[
      \widehat W(x,y)=
      \sum_{\substack{b\in\mathcal B:\\ x,y\in A_{\kappa(b)}}}
      \frac{\omega_b\,\psi_{\kappa(b)}
      |A_{\kappa(b)}|^{\rho_{\kappa(b)}-1}}
           {m(\kappa(b))}.
      \tag{GPW6}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \sum_{g:\,m(g)>0}u_g
      =
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\mathcal T_2(P,\delta)}\widehat W(x,y).
      \tag{GPW7}
   \]

   Thus the storage-dominated output of any generic child-panel return may be
   checked without integer materialization: prove a pair-profile, range-report,
   list-decoding, or low/high-correlation bound for the reciprocal-weighted
   pair congestion \((GPW6)\), and the total shared child storage is certified
   exactly.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a child \(g\).  Since \(A_g\) is \(\delta\)-separated and repetitions
   are allowed in \(\mathcal T_2(P,\delta)\), the ordered pairs
   \((x,y)\in A_g^2\) contribute exactly \(|A_g|^2\) atoms to
   \(\mathcal T_2(P,\delta)\).  Therefore the contribution of \(g\) to the
   right side of \((GPW3)\) is
   \[
      |A_g|^2\psi_g|A_g|^{\rho_g-1}
      =
      \psi_g|A_g|^{1+\rho_g}
      =
      u_g .
   \]
   Summing over children proves \((GPW3)\), and \((GPW4)\) follows by summing
   the profile envelopes.

   For the weighted occurrence form, group the contribution of \((GPW6)\) by
   the stored child \(g\).  The total occurrence weight pointing to \(g\) is
   \(m(g)\), so the reciprocal factor makes those occurrences contribute
   exactly the same pair weight
   \(\psi_g|A_g|^{\rho_g-1}\) as in \((GPW2)\), for each pair contained in
   \(A_g\).  Applying the preceding identity to the represented children gives
   \((GPW7)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Generic sponsor flow for child-panel storage]
   \label{cor:generic-child-panel-sponsor-flow}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:generic-child-panel-pair-witness-storage}, and write
   \(u_g=\psi_g|A_g|^{1+\rho_g}\).  Let \(\mathcal I\) be a finite pool of
   sponsor atoms with weights \(b_i>0\), let
   \(\mathcal E\subseteq\mathcal I\times\mathcal C\) be a certified
   compatibility relation, and fix \(\beta\ge1\).  Put
   \[
      H=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}b_i,
      \qquad
      d_g=u_g/\beta .
      \tag{GCF1}
   \]
   The following are equivalent.

   First, there is a fractional sponsor assignment \(h_{i,g}\ge0\), supported
   on \(\mathcal E\), such that
   \[
      \sum_{i:\,(i,g)\in\mathcal E}h_{i,g}\ge d_g
      \qquad(g\in\mathcal C),
      \tag{GCF2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{g:\,(i,g)\in\mathcal E}h_{i,g}\le b_i
      \qquad(i\in\mathcal I).
      \tag{GCF3}
   \]
   Second, every child subset \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal C\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{g\in\mathcal U}u_g
      \le
      \beta\sum_{i\in N(\mathcal U)}b_i,
      \qquad
      N(\mathcal U)=
      \{i:\exists g\in\mathcal U,\ (i,g)\in\mathcal E\}.
      \tag{GCF4}
   \]
   If these equivalent conditions hold, then
   \[
      \sum_{g\in\mathcal C}u_g\le\beta H .
      \tag{GCF5}
   \]
   Consequently, in any seeded child-panel storage argument, the bound
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+\beta\,\E_z H_z\le aS
      \tag{GCF6}
   \]
   is a sufficient replacement for a direct pair-congestion estimate: by
   \cref{cor:generic-child-panel-pair-witness-storage}, the pair-witness storage
   sum of the represented children is at most the sponsored atom mass.

   If the conditions fail, there is an explicit unsponsored child cut
   \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal C\) with
   \[
      \sum_{g\in\mathcal U}u_g
      >
      \beta\sum_{i\in N(\mathcal U)}b_i .
      \tag{GCF7}
   \]
   Thus the remaining storage theorem should not be stated as an unqualified
   geometry-only pair bound.  It must either produce compatible sponsor mass,
   merge the cut by a shared generated column, or route the cut to a different
   dense/spherical separator.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Build the finite flow network with a source edge of capacity \(b_i\) into
   each sponsor atom \(i\), infinite-capacity edges from \(i\) to \(g\) for
   \((i,g)\in\mathcal E\), and a sink edge of capacity \(d_g\) out of each
   child \(g\).  A flow saturating all child sink edges is exactly an
   assignment satisfying \((GCF2)\)--\((GCF3)\).

   By max-flow/min-cut, such a flow exists iff every finite cut has capacity at
   least \(\sum_g d_g\).  A finite cut is determined by the child set
   \(\mathcal U\) left on the sink side; all atoms in \(N(\mathcal U)\) must
   also lie on that side to avoid infinite crossing edges.  Rewriting the cut
   inequality gives
   \[
      \sum_{g\in\mathcal U}d_g\le\sum_{i\in N(\mathcal U)}b_i,
   \]
   which is \((GCF4)\) after multiplying by \(\beta\).  Failure of the cut
   inequality gives \((GCF7)\).

   If the sponsor flow exists, then
   \[
      \sum_{g\in\mathcal C}u_g
      =
      \beta\sum_gd_g
      \le
      \beta\sum_i b_i
      =
      \beta H,
   \]
   proving \((GCF5)\).  Taking expectations gives the sufficient storage bound
   in \((GCF6)\), while
   \cref{cor:generic-child-panel-pair-witness-storage} identifies this storage
   total with the exact pair-witness congestion sum.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Unsponsored child panels have no geometry-only storage bound]
   \label{lem:unsponsored-child-panel-obstruction}
   Let \(P\) be any \(\delta\)-separated set of size \(m\ge1\), let
   \(0\le\rho\le1\), and let \(M\ge1\).  Form a child panel
   \(\mathcal C=\{1,\ldots,M\}\) in which every child has the same witness set
   \(A_g=P\), price factor \(\psi_g=1\), exponent \(\rho_g=\rho\), and storage
   price \(u_g=m^{1+\rho}\).  Then
   \[
      W(x,y)=M\,m^{\rho-1}
      \qquad((x,y)\in\mathcal T_2(P,\delta)),
      \tag{UCP1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{g\in\mathcal C}u_g
      =
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\mathcal T_2(P,\delta)}W(x,y)
      =
      M\,m^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{UCP2}
   \]
   Hence, for any proposed allowance \(m^{1+\rho}L\), choosing \(M>L\) violates
   the storage bound even though all children have identical witness geometry
   and identical pair profiles.

   Therefore a worst-case child-panel storage theorem cannot depend only on the
   metric geometry or pair-profile shape of the witness sets.  It needs an
   additional multiplicity mechanism: canonical merging, a sponsor flow as in
   \cref{cor:generic-child-panel-sponsor-flow}, or a generated-column separator
   that makes the duplicated children one retained shared record.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(P\) is \(\delta\)-separated and repetitions are allowed, each child
   contributes all \(m^2\) ordered pairs to \(\mathcal T_2(P,\delta)\).  For
   each pair, the contribution of one child is
   \[
      \psi_g|A_g|^{\rho_g-1}=m^{\rho-1}.
   \]
   Summing over the \(M\) children gives \((UCP1)\), and summing over the
   \(m^2\) ordered pairs gives \((UCP2)\).  The final conclusion follows by
   taking \(M>L\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Generic unsponsored-cut generated-column screen]
   \label{cor:generic-unsponsored-cut-generated-column}
   Work with a child panel \(\mathcal C\), child prices \(u_g\), sponsor atoms
   \(\mathcal I\), compatibility relation \(\mathcal E\), and parameter
   \(\beta\) as in
   \cref{cor:generic-child-panel-sponsor-flow}.  For
   \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal C\), write
   \[
      P(\mathcal U)=\sum_{g\in\mathcal U}u_g,\qquad
      B(\mathcal U)=\sum_{i\in N(\mathcal U)}b_i,\qquad
      E^\beta(\mathcal U)=P(\mathcal U)-\beta B(\mathcal U).
      \tag{UCG1}
   \]
   Let \(\mathcal T\) be a finite generated-merge template family.  A template
   \(T\in\mathcal T\) has a child container
   \(\mathcal C_T\subseteq\mathcal C\), capture weights
   \(0\le g_{T,g}\le u_g\), available cardinalities \(\mathcal K_T\), and
   certified prices \(\overline P_T(K)\).  Assume that for every
   \(K\in\mathcal K_T\) and \(V\subseteq\mathcal C_T\) with \(|V|=K\), the
   builder can materialize one shared child record with storage price at most
   \(\overline P_T(K)\) and cut capture at least
   \[
      G_T(V;\mathcal U)=
      \sum_{g\in V\cap\mathcal U}g_{T,g}.
      \tag{UCG2}
   \]

   Order each \(\mathcal C_T\) by nonincreasing
   \(g_{T,g}\mathbf 1_{\{g\in\mathcal U\}}\).  If, for some \(T\) and
   \(K\in\mathcal K_T\), the top prefix \(V_K\) satisfies
   \[
      G_T(V_K;\mathcal U)>2\overline P_T(K),
      \tag{UCG3}
   \]
   then this generated record is a positive merge for the unsponsored cut: it
   decreases the cut imbalance by at least
   \(G_T(V_K;\mathcal U)-\overline P_T(K)>0\).

   Conversely, if no generated prefix satisfies \((UCG3)\), then every
   compatible assigned cover \(L=\bigsqcup_jL_j\) of any
   \(L\subseteq\mathcal U\), with
   \(L_j\subseteq\mathcal C_{T_j}\), \(|L_j|\in\mathcal K_{T_j}\), and
   \(g_{T_j,g}\ge w_g\) on \(L_j\), obeys
   \[
      \sum_{g\in L}w_g
      \le
      2\sum_j\overline P_{T_j}(|L_j|).
      \tag{UCG4}
   \]

   Suppose all templates used by such a cover satisfy
   \[
      \overline P_T(h)
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(Ah^\rho+\zeta h^{1+\rho}\right),
      \qquad 0<\rho<1 .
      \tag{UCG5}
   \]
   If \(w_g\ge\theta>0\) on \(L\), \(K=|L|\), and the cover uses \(J\)
   nonempty template parts, then every no-generated-merge residual satisfies
   \[
      \theta K
      \le
      2\psi_\star\left(AJ^{1-\rho}K^\rho+\zeta K^{1+\rho}\right).
      \tag{UCG6}
   \]

   Finally fix \(0<\varepsilon<1\).  If every child subset satisfies
   \[
      E^\beta(\mathcal U)\le\varepsilon P(\mathcal U),
      \tag{UCG7}
   \]
   then the sponsor Hall inequalities hold with
   \[
      \beta_\varepsilon=\frac{\beta}{1-\varepsilon}.
      \tag{UCG8}
   \]
   Otherwise there is a strong unsponsored cut \(\mathcal U\) with
   \(E^\beta(\mathcal U)>\varepsilon P(\mathcal U)>0\).  Let
   \[
      D(\mathcal U)=
      1+\left\lceil
         \log_2
         \frac{\max_{g\in\mathcal U^+}u_g}
              {\min_{g\in\mathcal U^+}u_g}
      \right\rceil,
      \qquad
      \mathcal U^+=\{g\in\mathcal U:u_g>0\}.
      \tag{UCG9}
   \]
   Then some dyadic child-price layer
   \[
      L=\{g\in\mathcal U:\theta\le u_g<2\theta\}
      \tag{UCG10}
   \]
   satisfies
   \[
      \theta |L|
      \ge
      \frac{P(\mathcal U)}{2D(\mathcal U)}
      \ge
      \frac{E^\beta(\mathcal U)}{2D(\mathcal U)} .
      \tag{UCG11}
   \]
   For this layer, absence of a generated merge implies the generated-cover
   lower bound
   \[
      N_{\rm gen}(L,\theta)
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{\theta |L|^{1-\rho}}{4\psi_\star A}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{E^\beta(\mathcal U)}
              {8D(\mathcal U)\psi_\star A\,|L|^\rho}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \tag{UCG12}
   \]
   whenever \(A>0\) and the layer is not storage-dominated,
   \[
      \theta>4\psi_\star\zeta |L|^\rho .
      \tag{UCG13}
   \]
   Here \(N_{\rm gen}(L,\theta)\) is the least number of generated template
   parts needed to cover \(L\) with \(g_{T,g}\ge\theta\) on each assigned part.
   When \(\zeta=0\), the first denominator \(4\psi_\star A\) in \((UCG12)\)
   may be replaced by \(2\psi_\star A\).

   Thus the generic sponsor obstruction has a single normal form: either a
   constant inflation of \(\beta\) sponsors all children, a generated merge
   decreases a strong cut, or one dyadic child-price layer has high generated
   cover entropy and must be handled by the spherical/list-decoding separator.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For fixed \(T\) and \(K\), the top \(K\)-prefix maximizes
   \(G_T(V;\mathcal U)\) over all \(K\)-subsets of \(\mathcal C_T\).  If
   \((UCG3)\) holds, replacing the captured child price in the cut by the one
   generated record changes the cut balance by at most
   \[
      -G_T(V_K;\mathcal U)+\overline P_T(K)<0,
   \]
   and hence gives a positive merge.  If no prefix satisfies \((UCG3)\), then
   for an assigned part \(L_j\) the top \(|L_j|\)-prefix has capture at least
   \(\sum_{g\in L_j}w_g\), so
   \[
      \sum_{g\in L_j}w_g\le2\overline P_{T_j}(|L_j|).
   \]
   Summing over \(j\) gives \((UCG4)\).  Under \((UCG5)\), Holder's inequality
   gives
   \[
      \sum_j|L_j|^\rho\le J^{1-\rho}K^\rho,\qquad
      \sum_j|L_j|^{1+\rho}\le K^{1+\rho},
   \]
   and \(\theta K\le\sum_{g\in L}w_g\), proving \((UCG6)\).

   If \((UCG7)\) holds for every \(\mathcal U\), then
   \(P(\mathcal U)-\beta B(\mathcal U)\le\varepsilon P(\mathcal U)\), so
   \[
      P(\mathcal U)\le\frac{\beta}{1-\varepsilon}B(\mathcal U)
      =
      \beta_\varepsilon B(\mathcal U).
   \]
   These are exactly the Hall inequalities \((GCF4)\) with parameter
   \(\beta_\varepsilon\).  Therefore
   \cref{cor:generic-child-panel-sponsor-flow} gives the inflated sponsor flow.

   If \((UCG7)\) fails, then \(P(\mathcal U)>0\), so
   \(\mathcal U^+\) is nonempty.  Partition \(\mathcal U^+\) into dyadic
   layers as in \((UCG10)\).  There are at most \(D(\mathcal U)\) nonempty
   layers, and on each layer \(\theta\ge u_g/2\).  Hence
   \[
      \sum_{\text{layers }L}\theta_L|L|
      \ge
      \frac12P(\mathcal U),
   \]
   so one layer satisfies the first inequality in \((UCG11)\); the second
   follows from \(E^\beta(\mathcal U)\le P(\mathcal U)\).

   Apply \((UCG6)\) to a minimum generated cover of that layer with
   \(w_g=\theta\).  If \((UCG13)\) holds, the storage term contributes less
   than \(\theta |L|/2\), so
   \[
      \frac{\theta |L|}{2}
      \le
      2\psi_\star A\,N_{\rm gen}(L,\theta)^{1-\rho}|L|^\rho .
   \]
   Rearranging gives the first lower bound in \((UCG12)\), and substituting
   \((UCG11)\) gives the second.  When \(\zeta=0\), the storage term is absent
   and the same argument starts from
   \(\theta |L|\le2\psi_\star A\,N_{\rm gen}(L,\theta)^{1-\rho}|L|^\rho\),
   giving the stated constant.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Generic unsponsored-cut packing and energy handoff]
   \label{cor:generic-unsponsored-cut-packing-energy}
   Work in the strong-cut, no-generated-merge residual of
   \cref{cor:generic-unsponsored-cut-generated-column}.  Thus \(L\) is the
   dyadic child-price layer in \((UCG10)\), \(K=|L|\), and no generated prefix
   satisfies \((UCG3)\).  Let \(d_{\rm gen}\) be any pseudometric on \(L\), and
   fix a scale \(\Delta_{\rm gen}>0\).  Suppose that for every \(g_0\in L\),
   the \(d_{\rm gen}\)-ball
   \[
      B_{\rm gen}(g_0,\Delta_{\rm gen})
      =
      \{g\in L:d_{\rm gen}(g,g_0)\le\Delta_{\rm gen}\}
      \tag{UPE1}
   \]
   is certified by a generated template part in the sense of
   \((UCG2)\)--\((UCG5)\), with all realized cardinalities available and with
   capture \(g_{T,g}\ge\theta\) on the ball.  If \(A>0\) and the layer is not
   storage-dominated, namely \((UCG13)\) holds, then every maximal
   \(\Delta_{\rm gen}\)-separated set \(E\subseteq L\) satisfies
   \[
      |E|
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{\theta K^{1-\rho}}{4\psi_\star A}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{E^\beta(\mathcal U)}
              {8D(\mathcal U)\psi_\star A\,K^\rho}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{UPE2}
   \]
   When \(\zeta=0\), the constants \(4\) and \(8\) in \((UPE2)\) may be
   replaced by \(2\) and \(4\), respectively.

   Suppose further that each \(g\in E\) has a representative
   \(x_g\in\mathbb S^{d-1}\).  Let \(U_G\) be a spherical, Gaussian-cap, code,
   range/list-decoded, or other certified bucket drawn from a law \(G\), and
   partition the ordered distinct pairs \(E_{\ne}^2\) into finitely many
   profiles \(\Pi_E\).  If every profile \(\pi\in\Pi_E\) has certified
   pair-intersection energy
   \[
      \Pr_G[x_g,x_{g'}\in U_G]\le e^{-I_\pi}
      \qquad((g,g')\in\pi),
      \tag{UPE3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      X_E(G)=\sum_{g\in E}\mathbf 1\{x_g\in U_G\},
      \tag{UPE4}
   \]
   then
   \[
      \E_GX_E(G)^2
      \le
      \sum_{g\in E}\Pr_G[x_g\in U_G]
      +
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi_E}|\pi|e^{-I_\pi}.
      \tag{UPE5}
   \]
   In particular, if
   \[
      I_\pi\ge\log|\pi|+\Lambda
      \qquad(\pi\in\Pi_E),
      \tag{UPE6}
   \]
   then the distinct-pair contribution of the exposed unsponsored layer is at
   most
   \[
      |\Pi_E|e^{-\Lambda}.
      \tag{UPE7}
   \]

   Finally, fix one profile \(\pi\subseteq E_{\ne}^2\), assign nonnegative
   weights \(\omega_{g,g'}\) to its ordered pairs, and split
   \(\pi=\pi_{\rm lo}\dot\cup\pi_{\rm hi}\).  Suppose
   \[
      \sum_{(g,g')\in\pi_{\rm lo}}\omega_{g,g'}\le B_{\rm lo},
      \tag{UPE8}
   \]
   and every high edge has representative correlation at least
   \[
      \ip{x_g}{x_{g'}}\ge\underline\theta
      \qquad((g,g')\in\pi_{\rm hi})
      \tag{UPE9}
   \]
   for some \(-1<\underline\theta<1\).  Define
   \[
      M_g(g')=\omega_{g,g'}\mathbf 1_{\{(g,g')\in\pi_{\rm hi}\}},
      \qquad
      W_{\rm hi}=\sum_{g,g'\in E}M_g(g').
      \tag{UPE10}
   \]
   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), set \(J_\omega=1\).  Otherwise assume the positive
   values of \(M_g(g')\) lie in a certified dyadic range
   \([\omega_{\min},\omega_{\max}]\), and put
   \[
      J_\omega=
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{\omega_{\max}}{\omega_{\min}}\right\rceil .
      \tag{UPE11}
   \]
   For dyadic levels \(t=\omega_{\min}2^j\), define
   \[
      V_{g,t}=\{g'\in E:M_g(g')\ge t\}.
      \tag{UPE12}
   \]
   Then every nonempty \(V_{g,t}\) has representatives in the cap ball
   \[
      x_{g'}\in B\!\left(x_g,\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)}\right),
      \tag{UPE13}
   \]
   and for every \(\Lambda_\star>0\), either
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}\le2|E|J_\omega\Lambda_\star,
      \tag{UPE14}
   \]
   or some dyadic star satisfies
   \[
      t|V_{g,t}|\ge\Lambda_\star .
      \tag{UPE15}
   \]
   Consequently, if no exposed star has scale at least \(\Lambda_\star\), then
   the whole profile weight is bounded by
   \[
      \sum_{(g,g')\in\pi}\omega_{g,g'}
      \le
      B_{\rm lo}+2|E|J_\omega\Lambda_\star .
      \tag{UPE16}
   \]

   Thus the unsponsored-cut residual reaches the same terminal proof object as
   the generic child-panel residual: either generated low-cover closes it,
   spherical/list-decoding energy pays the exposed packing, or a finite
   high-correlation star is returned to the generated-merge/dense-prefix
   verifier.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(E\subseteq L\) be maximal \(\Delta_{\rm gen}\)-separated.  The balls
   \(B_{\rm gen}(g,\Delta_{\rm gen})\), \(g\in E\), cover \(L\); otherwise an
   uncovered point could be added to \(E\).  By the template certification
   hypothesis, this ball cover is an admissible generated cover of \(L\) with
   capture at least \(\theta\) on every assigned child.  Hence
   \(N_{\rm gen}(L,\theta)\le |E|\).  Combining this with the lower bound
   \((UCG12)\) gives \((UPE2)\), including the \(\zeta=0\) sharpening.

   Expanding the second moment gives
   \[
      \E_GX_E(G)^2
      =
      \sum_{g\in E}\Pr_G[x_g\in U_G]
      +
      \sum_{\substack{g,g'\in E\\g\ne g'}}
         \Pr_G[x_g,x_{g'}\in U_G].
   \]
   Summing the profile bounds \((UPE3)\) over the partition proves
   \((UPE5)\).  Under \((UPE6)\), each profile contributes at most
   \(e^{-\Lambda}\), giving \((UPE7)\).

   For the star statement, if \(g'\in V_{g,t}\), then \(M_g(g')>0\), so
   \((g,g')\in\pi_{\rm hi}\).  By \((UPE9)\),
   \[
      \|x_g-x_{g'}\|^2=2-2\ip{x_g}{x_{g'}}\le2(1-\underline\theta),
   \]
   proving \((UPE13)\).

   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), then \((UPE14)\) and \((UPE16)\) are immediate.
   Otherwise, for fixed \(g\), the dyadic layer-cake estimate gives
   \[
      \sum_{j=0}^{J_\omega-1}
      \omega_{\min}2^j
      |V_{g,\omega_{\min}2^j}|
      \ge
      \frac12\sum_{g'\in E}M_g(g').
   \]
   Summing over \(g\in E\), if every dyadic star had
   \(t|V_{g,t}|<\Lambda_\star\), then
   \[
      \frac12W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \sum_{g\in E}\sum_{j=0}^{J_\omega-1}
      \omega_{\min}2^j
      |V_{g,\omega_{\min}2^j}|
      <
      |E|J_\omega\Lambda_\star,
   \]
   which proves \((UPE14)\).  Its contrapositive gives \((UPE15)\), and adding
   the low part \((UPE8)\) gives \((UPE16)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Centered-cap closure for unsponsored-cut packings]
   \label{cor:unsponsored-cut-low-correlation-cap-closure}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:generic-unsponsored-cut-packing-energy}, and suppose
   \(|E|\le m\) with \(m\ge3\).  Let \(\mathcal R\) be a finite weighted
   centered Gaussian cap panel.  For each \(r\in\mathcal R\), let
   \(w_r\ge0\), let \(G_r\sim N(0,I_D)\), and put
   \[
      U_r=\{x:\ip{G_r}{x}\ge T_r\}.
      \tag{UPL1}
   \]
   Fix constants \(A_{\rm cap},K_{\rm corr}\ge0\) and
   \(0\le\rho_{\rm cap}\le1\), and assume
   \[
      T_r^2\ge2\log m-A_{\rm cap}\log\log m
      \qquad(r\in\mathcal R),
      \tag{UPL2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      W_{\mathcal R}:=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r
      \le m^{1+\rho_{\rm cap}}\log^{A_{\rm cap}}m .
      \tag{UPL3}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      \theta_m=K_{\rm corr}\frac{\log\log m}{\log m}<1,
      \tag{UPL4}
   \]
   and split the ordered distinct pairs of \(E\) into
   \[
      E_{\rm lo}=\{(g,g')\in E_{\ne}^2:\ip{x_g}{x_{g'}}\le\theta_m\},
      \qquad
      E_{\rm hi}=E_{\ne}^2\setminus E_{\rm lo}.
      \tag{UPL5}
   \]
   Then the first list moment and low-correlation co-load obey
   \[
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r
      \sum_{g\in E}\Pr[x_g\in U_r]
      \le
      m^{1+\rho_{\rm cap}}\log^{3A_{\rm cap}/2}m,
      \tag{UPL6}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r
      \sum_{(g,g')\in E_{\rm lo}}
         \Pr[x_g,x_{g'}\in U_r]
      \le
      m^{1+\rho_{\rm cap}}
      \log^{2A_{\rm cap}+2K_{\rm corr}+1}m .
      \tag{UPL7}
   \]

   Define the high-correlation weighted pair mass
   \[
      \omega_{g,g'}
      =
      \mathbf 1_{\{(g,g')\in E_{\rm hi}\}}
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r\Pr[x_g,x_{g'}\in U_r],
      \qquad
      W_{\rm hi}=\sum_{g,g'\in E}\omega_{g,g'} .
      \tag{UPL8}
   \]
   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), set \(J_{\omega}=1\).  Otherwise suppose the positive
   values of \(\omega_{g,g'}\) lie in a certified dyadic range
   \([\omega_{\min},\omega_{\max}]\), and put
   \[
      J_{\omega}
      =
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{\omega_{\max}}{\omega_{\min}}\right\rceil .
      \tag{UPL9}
   \]
   For dyadic levels \(t=\omega_{\min}2^j\), let
   \[
      V_{g,t}=\{g'\in E:\omega_{g,g'}\ge t\}.
      \tag{UPL10}
   \]
   Then every nonempty \(V_{g,t}\) is contained in the cap ball
   \[
      x_{g'}\in B\!\left(x_g,\sqrt{2(1-\theta_m)}\right),
      \tag{UPL11}
   \]
   and for every \(\Lambda_\star>0\), either
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}\le2|E|J_\omega\Lambda_\star,
      \tag{UPL12}
   \]
   or some high-correlation star satisfies
   \[
      t|V_{g,t}|\ge\Lambda_\star .
      \tag{UPL13}
   \]
   Consequently, if no exposed high-correlation star has scale at least
   \(\Lambda_\star\), then the whole weighted second moment of the cap panel on
   the unsponsored packing is bounded by
   \[
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r\,\E X_E(U_r)^2
      \le
      m^{1+\rho_{\rm cap}}
      \left(
         \log^{3A_{\rm cap}/2}m
         +
         \log^{2A_{\rm cap}+2K_{\rm corr}+1}m
      \right)
      +
      2|E|J_\omega\Lambda_\star ,
      \tag{UPL14}
   \]
   where \(X_E(U_r)=\sum_{g\in E}\mathbf 1\{x_g\in U_r\}\).

   Thus, for centered cap panels at the large-range threshold, the
   low-correlation part of an exposed unsponsored-cut packing is already paid
   with only polylogarithmic overhead.  Any polynomial residual must be a
   high-correlation cap star, which is the finite object returned to the
   generated-merge or dense-prefix verifier.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply
   \cref{cor:weighted-polylog-low-correlation-coload} to the indexed family
   \((x_g)_{g\in E}\subseteq\mathbb S^{D-1}\), the weighted cap panel
   \(\mathcal R\), and the low-correlation edge set \(E_{\rm lo}\).  The proof
   of that corollary is indexwise and uses only the cardinality bound
   \(|E|\le m\), so possible repeated representatives cause no change.  The
   hypotheses \((UPL2)\)--\((UPL4)\) are exactly \((WPLC1)\)--\((WPLC2)\) and
   the cutoff definition there.  This gives \((UPL6)\)--\((UPL7)\).

   If \(g'\in V_{g,t}\), then \(\omega_{g,g'}>0\), so
   \((g,g')\in E_{\rm hi}\).  By \((UPL5)\),
   \(\ip{x_g}{x_{g'}}>\theta_m\), and hence
   \[
      \|x_g-x_{g'}\|^2=2-2\ip{x_g}{x_{g'}}
      \le2(1-\theta_m),
   \]
   proving \((UPL11)\).

   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), then \((UPL12)\) is immediate.  Otherwise the same
   dyadic layer-cake estimate used in
   \cref{cor:generic-unsponsored-cut-packing-energy} gives
   \[
      \frac12W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \sum_{g\in E}\sum_{j=0}^{J_\omega-1}
      \omega_{\min}2^j
      |V_{g,\omega_{\min}2^j}|.
      \tag{UPL15}
   \]
   If every dyadic star had \(t|V_{g,t}|<\Lambda_\star\), then the right-hand
   side of \((UPL15)\) would be less than
   \(|E|J_\omega\Lambda_\star\), proving \((UPL12)\).  Its contrapositive
   gives \((UPL13)\).

   Finally,
   \[
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r\,\E X_E(U_r)^2
      =
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r
      \sum_{g\in E}\Pr[x_g\in U_r]
      +
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r
      \sum_{(g,g')\in E_{\ne}^2}
      \Pr[x_g,x_{g'}\in U_r].
   \]
   Split the distinct-pair sum into \(E_{\rm lo}\) and \(E_{\rm hi}\).  The
   first two terms are bounded by \((UPL6)\)--\((UPL7)\), while the high part
   is \(W_{\rm hi}\) by definition.  Under the no-large-star hypothesis,
   \((UPL12)\) gives \((UPL14)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cap-prefix tail for unsponsored-cut cap stars]
   \label{cor:unsponsored-cut-cap-prefix-tail}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:unsponsored-cut-low-correlation-cap-closure}, and assume
   \(0<\theta_m\le1/2\).  Suppose the indexed representative family
   \((x_g)_{g\in E}\subseteq\mathbb S^{D-1}\) is a local finite
   filter-cover instance to which
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-paid-prefix-quadratic} applies with
   \(o=0\), \(R=1\), \(\gamma=\theta_m\), and all centers \(g\in E\)
   available.  Thus
   \[
      c_g=\theta_m x_g,
      \qquad
      R_+=\sqrt{1-\theta_m^2},
      \qquad
      W_g=\{g'\in E:\|x_{g'}-c_g\|\le R_+\},
      \tag{UPT1}
   \]
   with activation \(a_g^+\), paid degree \(d_g^+(g')\), and query price
   \(A_g^+\) as in \((CPQ3)\)--\((CPQ5)\), interpreted on the indexed
   family.

   Let \(\omega_{g,g'}\) and \(W_{\rm hi}\) be the high-correlation cap-panel
   weights from \((UPL8)\).  Split them by cap-centered paid degree:
   \[
      \omega^{\rm pay}_{g,g'}
      =
      \min\{\omega_{g,g'},d_g^+(g')\},
      \qquad
      \omega^{\rm over}_{g,g'}
      =
      \bigl(\omega_{g,g'}-d_g^+(g')\bigr)_+,
      \tag{UPT2}
   \]
   and put
   \[
      W_{\rm over}=\sum_{g,g'\in E}\omega^{\rm over}_{g,g'} .
      \tag{UPT3}
   \]
   If \(\omega^{\rm pay}\equiv0\), set \(J_{\rm pay}=1\).  Otherwise assume
   the positive values of \(\omega^{\rm pay}_{g,g'}\) lie in a certified
   dyadic range with dynamic-range factor \(J_{\rm pay}\).  For dyadic levels
   \(t\), define
   \[
      U^{\rm pay}_{g,t}
      =
      \{g'\in E:\omega^{\rm pay}_{g,g'}\ge t\}.
      \tag{UPT4}
   \]
   Fix \(\Lambda>0\).  Suppose every paid-clipped dyadic level with
   \(t|U^{\rm pay}_{g,t}|\ge\Lambda\) has cap-centered child price below
   \(\Lambda\):
   \[
      e^{B_0\theta_m^2}\Psi(R_+)
      \left(
         A_g^+|U^{\rm pay}_{g,t}|^\rho
         +\sigma |U^{\rm pay}_{g,t}|^{1+\rho}
      \right)
      <\Lambda .
      \tag{UPT5}
   \]
   Then either a \((B_0+3)\)-quadratic cap-centered paid-prefix repair fires,
   or
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      W_{\rm over}+2|E|J_{\rm pay}\Lambda .
      \tag{UPT6}
   \]
   Consequently, in a no-repair residual satisfying \((UPT5)\),
   \[
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r\,\E X_E(U_r)^2
      \le
      m^{1+\rho_{\rm cap}}
      \left(
         \log^{3A_{\rm cap}/2}m
         +
         \log^{2A_{\rm cap}+2K_{\rm corr}+1}m
      \right)
      +
      W_{\rm over}+2|E|J_{\rm pay}\Lambda .
      \tag{UPT7}
   \]

   Thus the high-correlation output of the unsponsored-cut cap screen is no
   longer an unpriced star family.  Its cap-paid part is either a same-prefix
   quadratic repair or a fixed dyadic tail, and the only potentially polynomial
   survivor is the explicit cap-centered overload \(W_{\rm over}\), the same
   object handled by the Hall/sponsor and shared-child storage interfaces.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(\omega_{g,g'}>0\), then by \((UPL8)\) we have
   \((g,g')\in E_{\rm hi}\).  Hence \(\ip{x_g}{x_{g'}}>\theta_m\), and
   directly
   \[
      \|x_{g'}-\theta_m x_g\|^2
      =
      1+\theta_m^2-2\theta_m\ip{x_g}{x_{g'}}
      <
      1-\theta_m^2=R_+^2 .
   \]
   Thus \(g'\in W_g\), and the support condition \((CCH1)\) holds for the
   high-correlation multiplicities \(M_g(g')=\omega_{g,g'}\).

   Apply \cref{cor:clipped-cap-centered-high-correlation-handoff} to this
   multiplicity family with margin \(\gamma=\theta_m\).  Its threshold form
   \((CCH7)\), together with the price condition \((UPT5)\), gives exactly:
   either a \((B_0+3)\)-quadratic cap-centered paid-prefix repair fires, or
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      W_{\rm over}+2|E|J_{\rm pay}\Lambda .
   \]
   This is \((UPT6)\).

   Finally expand the weighted second moment as in the proof of
   \cref{cor:unsponsored-cut-low-correlation-cap-closure}.  The diagonal and
   low-correlation terms are bounded by \((UPL6)\)--\((UPL7)\), and the
   high-correlation term is \(W_{\rm hi}\).  Substituting \((UPT6)\) in a
   no-repair residual proves \((UPT7)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Unsponsored cap overload is a Hall-tail storage object]
   \label{cor:unsponsored-cap-overload-hall-tail}
   Work in the no-repair residual of
   \cref{cor:unsponsored-cut-cap-prefix-tail}.  Atomize the
   high-correlation cap-panel incidences by creating, for every pair
   \((g,g')\in E\times E\) with \(\omega_{g,g'}>0\), one atom
   \(i=(g,g')\) with indexed point \(p_i=g'\), atom weight
   \(b_i=\omega_{g,g'}\), and singleton admissible center set
   \(\mathcal X_i=\{g\}\).  Interpret
   \cref{lem:cap-centered-transport-hall} on the indexed representative family
   \((x_g)_{g\in E}\), with \(C=1\), the cap-centered children \(W_g\), and
   the paid degrees \(d_g^+(g')\) from \((UPT1)\).

   Let
   \[
      \mathcal A_{\rm over}
      =
      \{(g,g'):\omega_{g,g'}>d_g^+(g')\}
      \tag{UOH1}
   \]
   and recall
   \(W_{\rm over}=\sum_{g,g'}(\omega_{g,g'}-d_g^+(g'))_+\).  Then
   \(\mathcal A_{\rm over}\) satisfies the Hall-overload identity
   \[
      \sum_{i\in\mathcal A_{\rm over}}b_i
      -
      \sum_{(g,g',q)\in N(\mathcal A_{\rm over})}
         \alpha_{g',q}a_g^+(q)
      =
      W_{\rm over}.
      \tag{UOH2}
   \]
   Hence, for every \(0\le\Omega<W_{\rm over}\), the cap-centered Hall
   condition \((COD1)\) fails with allowed tail \(\Omega\).

   If the positive overload values
   \[
      O_g(g')=(\omega_{g,g'}-d_g^+(g'))_+
      \tag{UOH3}
   \]
   lie in a certified dyadic range \([O_{\min},O_{\max}]\), and
   \[
      J_{\rm over}
      =
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{O_{\max}}{O_{\min}}\right\rceil ,
      \tag{UOH4}
   \]
   then there are \(g\in E\) and a dyadic threshold \(t\) such that
   \[
      U^{\rm over}_{g,t}
      =
      \{g'\in E:O_g(g')\ge t\}
      \tag{UOH5}
   \]
   is contained in \(W_g\) and
   \[
      t|U^{\rm over}_{g,t}|
      >
      \frac{\Omega}{2|E|J_{\rm over}} .
      \tag{UOH6}
   \]

   Suppose such a pure overload star is canonicalized to one shared child
   \(\kappa\) with witness index set
   \(A_\kappa\subseteq U^{\rm over}_{g,t}\), tuple order \(k_\kappa\), and
   storage price \(u_\kappa\).  Treat each overloaded atom
   \((g,g')\in\mathcal A_{\rm over}\) with \(g'\in U^{\rm over}_{g,t}\) as a
   weighted occurrence of the same child, with occurrence weight
   \(\omega_{g,g'}\).  Then the reciprocal weighted-multiplicity identity of
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-overload-weighted-storage} charges this overload
   cohort by one copy of the shared child price \(u_\kappa\), not by one copy
   per overloaded incidence.  Consequently the residual \(W_{\rm over}\) from
   \((UPT7)\) may be fed as an ordinary priced child panel to
   \cref{cor:generic-child-panel-pair-witness-storage},
   \cref{cor:generic-child-panel-sponsor-flow}, and
   \cref{cor:generic-unsponsored-cut-generated-column}.

   Thus the unsponsored cap-panel overload has no separate
   high-correlation materialization branch.  Either it is sponsored by the
   local Hall capacities, or its failed sponsor cut exposes the same dyadic
   cap-centered pure overload stars handled by the shared-child storage and
   generated-column interfaces.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If an atom \(i=(g,g')\) is present, then \(\omega_{g,g'}>0\).  The proof of
   \cref{cor:unsponsored-cut-cap-prefix-tail} shows that
   \(\ip{x_g}{x_{g'}}>\theta_m\) and \(g'\in W_g\).  Thus the indexed version
   of the cap-centered Hall support hypothesis \((CTH1)\) holds with
   admissible center set \(\{g\}\).

   For a fixed overloaded pair \((g,g')\), the only neighboring capacity nodes
   of its singleton atom are the triples \((g,g',q)\) with
   \((g',q)\in\mathcal N\) and \(a_g^+(q)>0\).  Their total capacity is
   \[
      \sum_{q:(g',q)\in\mathcal N}\alpha_{g',q}a_g^+(q)
      =
      d_g^+(g').
   \]
   Summing over the overloaded pairs in \((UOH1)\) gives \((UOH2)\).  If
   \(\Omega<W_{\rm over}\), the subset \(\mathcal A_{\rm over}\) violates
   \((COD1)\), so the Hall condition fails with allowed tail \(\Omega\).

   Apply \cref{cor:cap-centered-overload-dichotomy} and then
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-hall-overload-stars} to this failed Hall cut, using
   the canonical selector \(s(g,g')=g\) and \(C=1\).  The selected atom load at
   index \(g'\) is \(B_g^s(g')=\omega_{g,g'}\), and hence the overload
   multiplicity \((COS2)\) is exactly \(O_g(g')\) from \((UOH3)\).  Since the
   available center set has size \(|E|\), the dyadic layer-cake conclusion of
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-hall-overload-stars} gives
   \((UOH5)\)--\((UOH6)\) and the containment
   \(U^{\rm over}_{g,t}\subseteq W_g\).

   The final storage statement is precisely
   \cref{cor:cap-centered-overload-weighted-storage} applied to this pure
   overload star and to the overloaded atoms selected from it.  The generic
   child-panel storage, sponsor-flow, and generated-column corollaries are
   stated for arbitrary priced child panels, so the canonicalized overload
   children enter those interfaces without further geometric assumptions.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Generated-column normal form for cap-overload children]
   \label{cor:unsponsored-cap-overload-generated-column}
   Work after the canonicalization step of
   \cref{cor:unsponsored-cap-overload-hall-tail}.  Let
   \(\mathcal C_{\rm over}\) be the finite family of distinct canonical
   overload children retained from the dyadic pure overload stars.  A child
   \(\kappa\in\mathcal C_{\rm over}\) has witness set \(A_\kappa\), price
   factor \(\psi_\kappa\), exponent \(0\le\rho_\kappa\le1\), and storage price
   \[
      u_\kappa=\psi_\kappa|A_\kappa|^{1+\rho_\kappa}.
      \tag{UOG1}
   \]
   Let \(\mathcal I_{\rm over}\) be the weighted overload Hall atoms reserved
   as potential sponsors, with weights \(b_i>0\), and let
   \(\mathcal E_{\rm over}\subseteq
   \mathcal I_{\rm over}\times\mathcal C_{\rm over}\) be the certified
   compatibility relation saying that atom \(i\) is allowed to sponsor child
   \(\kappa\).  Fix \(\beta\ge1\).

   If every child subset \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal C_{\rm over}\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal U}u_\kappa
      \le
      \beta
      \sum_{i\in N_{\rm over}(\mathcal U)}b_i,
      \qquad
      N_{\rm over}(\mathcal U)
      =
      \{i:\exists\kappa\in\mathcal U,\ (i,\kappa)\in\mathcal E_{\rm over}\},
      \tag{UOG2}
   \]
   then a fractional sponsor flow pays the shared storage of all retained
   overload children:
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal C_{\rm over}}u_\kappa
      \le
      \beta\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{\rm over}}b_i,
      \tag{UOG3}
   \]
   and the exact pair-witness storage identity
   \((GPW7)\) applies with reciprocal occurrence multiplicity.

   Otherwise there is an unsponsored child cut
   \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal C_{\rm over}\).  For
   \[
      P(\mathcal U)=\sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal U}u_\kappa,\qquad
      B(\mathcal U)=\sum_{i\in N_{\rm over}(\mathcal U)}b_i,\qquad
      E^\beta(\mathcal U)=P(\mathcal U)-\beta B(\mathcal U),
      \tag{UOG4}
   \]
   fix \(0<\varepsilon<1\).  The following generated-column alternative holds
   for every finite generated template family satisfying
   \((UCG2)\)--\((UCG5)\), with \(\mathcal C=\mathcal C_{\rm over}\) and
   common envelope parameters \(A>0,\psi_\star,\zeta,\rho\).

   Either every cut is only \(\varepsilon\)-unsupported and the sponsor flow is
   restored after replacing \(\beta\) by \(\beta/(1-\varepsilon)\), or there is
   a strong cut with \(E^\beta(\mathcal U)>\varepsilon P(\mathcal U)>0\).
   For such a strong cut, either some generated top prefix is a positive shared
   merge in the sense of \((UCG3)\), or one dyadic child-price layer
   \[
      L=\{\kappa\in\mathcal U:\theta\le u_\kappa<2\theta\}
      \tag{UOG5}
   \]
   satisfies
   \[
      \theta |L|
      \ge
      \frac{E^\beta(\mathcal U)}{2D(\mathcal U)}
      \tag{UOG6}
   \]
   and, unless it is storage-dominated as in \((UCG13)\), has generated-cover
   lower bound
   \[
      N_{\rm gen}(L,\theta)
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{E^\beta(\mathcal U)}
              {8D(\mathcal U)\psi_\star A\,|L|^\rho}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{UOG7}
   \]
   If generated-metric balls on this layer are themselves certified templates,
   then every maximal separated packing in that generated metric also satisfies
   the lower bound \((UPE2)\).

   Consequently, after \cref{cor:unsponsored-cap-overload-hall-tail}, the only
   possible polynomial cap-overload survivor is a single strong child-price cut
   whose dyadic layer defeats all generated range/list/AQ/facility templates by
   the explicit entropy lower bound \((UOG7)\).  It is not another
   high-correlation cap-star branch.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The first assertion is exactly
   \cref{cor:generic-child-panel-sponsor-flow} applied to the child panel
   \(\mathcal C_{\rm over}\), sponsor atoms \(\mathcal I_{\rm over}\),
   compatibility relation \(\mathcal E_{\rm over}\), and parameter \(\beta\).
   The pair-witness statement is
   \cref{cor:generic-child-panel-pair-witness-storage}; the reciprocal
   occurrence multiplicities are supplied by
   \cref{cor:unsponsored-cap-overload-hall-tail}.

   If \((UOG2)\) fails, apply
   \cref{cor:generic-unsponsored-cut-generated-column} to the same child panel
   and sponsor relation.  Its notation \((UCG1)\) is precisely \((UOG4)\).
   The weak-cut alternative gives the inflated sponsor parameter
   \(\beta/(1-\varepsilon)\).  The strong-cut alternative gives the dyadic
   layer \((UOG5)\), the mass bound \((UOG6)\), and, in the absence of a
   positive generated prefix and outside the storage-dominated regime, the
   generated-cover lower bound \((UOG7)\).  When generated-metric balls are
   certified template parts, \cref{cor:generic-unsponsored-cut-packing-energy}
   gives the stated packing version.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Average generated-cell separator for cap-overload layers]
   \label{cor:average-generated-cell-cap-overload}
   Work in the strong-cut, no-generated-prefix branch of
   \cref{cor:unsponsored-cap-overload-generated-column}, and fix its dyadic
   child-price layer
   \[
      L=\{\kappa\in\mathcal U:\theta\le u_\kappa<2\theta\}.
   \]
   Let \(\nu\) be any finite proposal law over materializable generated records.
   A record \(R\) has a represented subset \(C_R\subseteq L\) and certified
   one-time shared price \(P_R\), and it is valid in the sense that adding it
   as an available generated-template subset would capture at least
   \(\theta\) units of cut price from each \(\kappa\in C_R\).  If
   \[
      \E_{R\sim\nu}\bigl[\theta |C_R|-2P_R\bigr]>0,
      \tag{AGC1}
   \]
   then some generated record has positive reduced cost and the no-prefix
   residual is impossible.

   Consequently every no-prefix residual obeys, for every such proposal law,
   \[
      \theta\sum_{\kappa\in L}h_\kappa
      \le
      2\E_{R\sim\nu}P_R,
      \qquad
      h_\kappa=\Pr_{R\sim\nu}[\kappa\in C_R].
      \tag{AGC2}
   \]
   In particular, if the law covers the layer with marginal hit probability
   \(h_\kappa\ge a_L\) for all \(\kappa\in L\), then
   \[
      a_L\theta |L|\le2\E_{R\sim\nu}P_R.
      \tag{AGC3}
   \]

   Suppose additionally that each generated record has list size
   \(H_R=|C_R|\) and certified price envelope
   \[
      P_R\le
      \psi_\star\left(AH_R^\rho+\zeta H_R^{1+\rho}\right),
      \qquad 0<\rho<1 .
      \tag{AGC4}
   \]
   Then a no-prefix residual forces the average Renyi list-size obstruction
   \[
      a_L\theta |L|
      \le
      2\psi_\star
      \left(
         A\,\E H_R^\rho+\zeta\,\E H_R^{1+\rho}
      \right).
      \tag{AGC5}
   \]
   Equivalently, any tensorized spherical, range-reporting,
   additive-quantization, facility, or list-decoding proposal law that violates
   \((AGC5)\) is automatically converted by the finite verifier into one
   deterministic positive generated merge.

   Combining \((AGC3)\) with the strong-layer lower bound \((UOG6)\), every
   surviving cap-overload layer satisfies
   \[
      \E_{R\sim\nu}P_R
      \ge
      \frac{a_L\,E^\beta(\mathcal U)}{4D(\mathcal U)}
      \tag{AGC6}
   \]
   for every proposal law with marginal hit \(a_L\).  Thus the remaining
   separator theorem may be stated as a normalized average-price/list-size
   bound for this single layer: prove a proposal law with hit \(a_L\) and
   expected price below the right side of \((AGC6)\), or accept that the
   strong cut has a genuine average list-size obstruction.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((AGC1)\) holds, then at least one generated record \(R\) satisfies
   \(\theta |C_R|>2P_R\).  Since \(R\) captures at least \(\theta\) from every
   child in \(C_R\), the top prefix of the same generated template at
   cardinality \(K=|C_R|\) captures at least \(\theta |C_R|\).  Therefore that
   top prefix satisfies the positive-prefix inequality \((UCG3)\).  This
   contradicts the no-generated-prefix branch and proves the first claim.

   Taking the contrapositive, every no-prefix residual has
   \(\E[\theta|C_R|-2P_R]\le0\).  Since
   \[
      \E|C_R|
      =
      \sum_{\kappa\in L}\Pr[\kappa\in C_R]
      =
      \sum_{\kappa\in L}h_\kappa,
   \]
   this is \((AGC2)\).  The marginal lower bound \(h_\kappa\ge a_L\) gives
   \((AGC3)\), and substituting the price envelope \((AGC4)\) gives
   \((AGC5)\).

   Finally, \((UOG6)\) says
   \(\theta |L|\ge E^\beta(\mathcal U)/(2D(\mathcal U))\).  Combining this
   with \((AGC3)\) gives \((AGC6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fractional generated cover for cap-overload layers]
   \label{cor:fractional-generated-cover-cap-overload}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:average-generated-cell-cap-overload}, and let \(\mathcal R_L\) be
   a finite family of materializable generated records for the exposed layer
   \(L\).  Each record \(R\in\mathcal R_L\) has represented subset
   \(C_R\subseteq L\) and certified shared price \(P_R\).  Assume
   \(\mathcal R_L\) covers \(L\), for example because singleton records are
   available.  Consider the finite covering LP
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Phi_L=\min
      & \displaystyle\sum_{R\in\mathcal R_L}P_R\lambda_R\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{R:\,\kappa\in C_R}\lambda_R\ge1
        \qquad(\kappa\in L),\\[0.8em]
      & \lambda_R\ge0 .
   \end{array}
      \tag{FGC1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \Phi_L<\frac{\theta |L|}{2},
      \tag{FGC2}
   \]
   then some generated top prefix has positive reduced cost, so the no-prefix
   residual is impossible.

   Conversely, if the no-prefix residual survives, then
   \[
      \Phi_L\ge\frac{\theta |L|}{2}
      \ge
      \frac{E^\beta(\mathcal U)}{4D(\mathcal U)} .
      \tag{FGC3}
   \]
   Equivalently, finite LP duality gives a weighting \(y_\kappa\ge0\) on
   \(\kappa\in L\) such that
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa\in L}y_\kappa
      \ge
      \frac{\theta |L|}{2},
      \qquad
      \sum_{\kappa\in C_R}y_\kappa\le P_R
      \quad(R\in\mathcal R_L).
      \tag{FGC4}
   \]

   Thus a surviving cap-overload layer has one normalized weighted
   range/list-decoding obstruction: every materializable generated record
   captures at most its certified price against the same dual weights \(y\).
   A proposed tensor, range-reporting, additive-quantization, facility, or
   list-decoding theorem only has to rule out such a dual weighting by finding
   one record with \(\sum_{\kappa\in C_R}y_\kappa>P_R\), or by proving that no
   such weighted layer can satisfy the geometric hypotheses.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(\lambda\) be any feasible solution of \((FGC1)\).  The cover
   constraints give
   \[
      \sum_{R\in\mathcal R_L}\lambda_R|C_R|
      =
      \sum_{\kappa\in L}\sum_{R:\,\kappa\in C_R}\lambda_R
      \ge |L|.
      \tag{FGC5}
   \]
   If \((FGC2)\) holds, choose a feasible \(\lambda\) with
   \(\sum_RP_R\lambda_R<\theta|L|/2\).  Combining with \((FGC5)\),
   \[
      \sum_R\lambda_R(\theta|C_R|-2P_R)>0 .
   \]
   Hence some record has \(\theta|C_R|>2P_R\).  By
   \cref{cor:average-generated-cell-cap-overload}, the corresponding generated
   top prefix is a positive merge.

   Therefore a no-prefix residual must satisfy the first inequality in
   \((FGC3)\).  The second follows from \((UOG6)\).  Since \(\mathcal R_L\)
   covers \(L\), the primal is finite, feasible, and bounded below.  LP duality
   gives
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Phi_L=\max
      & \displaystyle\sum_{\kappa\in L}y_\kappa\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & y_\kappa\ge0,\\[0.6em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{\kappa\in C_R}y_\kappa\le P_R
        \qquad(R\in\mathcal R_L),
   \end{array}
      \tag{FGC6}
   \]
   and \((FGC3)\) supplies an optimal dual solution satisfying \((FGC4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cap-overload dual low-cover and packing screen]
   \label{cor:cap-overload-dual-low-cover-screen}
   Work in the no-prefix residual of
   \cref{cor:fractional-generated-cover-cap-overload}, and fix a dual weighting
   \(y_\kappa\) satisfying \((FGC4)\).  Let \(L_0\subseteq L\) be nonempty, put
   \(K=|L_0|\), and suppose
   \[
      y_\kappa\ge\delta>0
      \qquad(\kappa\in L_0).
      \tag{FDL1}
   \]
   Assume \(L_0\) has a certified generated cover by a partition
   \(L_0=L_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup L_J\) into \(J\) nonempty parts: for every \(i\)
   there is a materializable generated record \(R_i\in\mathcal R_L\) with
   \[
      L_i\subseteq C_{R_i},
      \qquad
      P_{R_i}\le
      \psi_\star\left(A|L_i|^\rho+\zeta |L_i|^{1+\rho}\right),
      \qquad 0<\rho<1 .
      \tag{FDL2}
   \]
   Then every no-prefix residual obeys
   \[
      \delta K
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(AJ^{1-\rho}K^\rho+\zeta K^{1+\rho}\right).
      \tag{FDL3}
   \]
   Hence, when \(A>0\) and
   \[
      \delta>2\psi_\star\zeta K^\rho,
      \tag{FDL4}
   \]
   every surviving residual has
   \[
      J
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{\delta K^{1-\rho}}{2\psi_\star A}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{FDL5}
   \]
   When \(\zeta=0\), the same conclusion holds with \(2\psi_\star A\) replaced
   by \(\psi_\star A\).

   The same lower bound applies to packing witnesses.  If \(d_{\rm gen}\) is a
   pseudometric on \(L_0\), \(E\subseteq L_0\) is maximal
   \(\Delta_{\rm gen}\)-separated, and after assigning every \(\kappa\in L_0\)
   to one covering ball \(B_{\rm gen}(e,\Delta_{\rm gen})\), \(e\in E\), each
   assigned part has a generated record satisfying \((FDL2)\), then
   \(|E|\) obeys \((FDL5)\) under \((FDL4)\) and the same \(\zeta=0\) sharpening.

   Equivalently, if a range, list-decoding, additive-quantization, facility, or
   tensor container family at scale \(\lambda\) gives such a certified cover with
   \[
      J\le C_{\rm gen}\lambda^{-\Delta},
      \tag{FDL6}
   \]
   then any surviving layer satisfies
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(
         A C_{\rm gen}^{1-\rho}\lambda^{-\Delta(1-\rho)}K^{\rho-1}
         +\zeta K^\rho
      \right).
      \tag{FDL7}
   \]
   Violation of \((FDL7)\) produces a generated record violating \((FGC4)\), and
   therefore a positive generated prefix.

   Finally, the dual obstruction contains a dyadic heavy layer.  If
   \(W=\{\kappa\in L:y_\kappa>0\}\), \(y_{\min}=\min_W y_\kappa\), and
   \(y_{\max}=\max_W y_\kappa\), then for
   \[
      J_y=1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{y_{\max}}{y_{\min}}\right\rceil
      \tag{FDL8}
   \]
   some dyadic layer \(L_j=\{\kappa:2^jy_{\min}\le y_\kappa<2^{j+1}y_{\min}\}\)
   with \(\delta_j=2^jy_{\min}\) satisfies
   \[
      \delta_j|L_j|
      \ge
      \frac{1}{2J_y}\sum_{\kappa\in L}y_\kappa
      \ge
      \frac{\theta |L|}{4J_y}.
      \tag{FDL9}
   \]
   Thus a surviving cap-overload obstruction is not an arbitrary weighted
   object: after dyadic unweighting it is a dual-heavy layer on which every
   certified low-cover, low-doubling, range, AQ, facility, tensor, or
   list-decoding cover must have the lower bound \((FDL5)\), unless the
   \(K^{1+\rho}\) storage term already dominates.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For each cover part, \((FDL1)\) and the dual constraint \((FGC4)\) give
   \[
      \delta |L_i|
      \le
      \sum_{\kappa\in L_i}y_\kappa
      \le
      \sum_{\kappa\in C_{R_i}}y_\kappa
      \le P_{R_i}.
   \]
   Summing over \(i\) and using \((FDL2)\) gives
   \[
      \delta K
      \le
      \psi_\star
      \left(
         A\sum_i|L_i|^\rho+\zeta\sum_i|L_i|^{1+\rho}
      \right).
   \]
   Holder's inequality and convexity give
   \[
      \sum_i|L_i|^\rho\le J^{1-\rho}K^\rho,
      \qquad
      \sum_i|L_i|^{1+\rho}\le K^{1+\rho},
   \]
   proving \((FDL3)\).  If \((FDL4)\) holds, the storage term in \((FDL3)\) is
   smaller than \(\delta K/2\), and rearranging gives \((FDL5)\).  With
   \(\zeta=0\), the storage term is absent and the sharper constant follows.
   Substituting \((FDL6)\) in \((FDL3)\) and dividing by \(K\) gives \((FDL7)\).
   Its violation contradicts the dual feasibility in \((FGC4)\); by
   \cref{cor:fractional-generated-cover-cap-overload}, this is exactly the
   positive-prefix alternative.
   The packing statement follows because the balls centered at any maximal
   \(\Delta_{\rm gen}\)-separated set cover \(L_0\); assigning points to covering
   balls produces a certified generated cover with \(J=|E|\).

   The dyadic layers in \((FDL8)\) partition \(W\).  On \(L_j\), one has
   \(y_\kappa<2\delta_j\), hence
   \[
      \sum_j\delta_j|L_j|
      \ge
      \frac12\sum_{\kappa\in L}y_\kappa .
   \]
   One layer contributes at least the average over \(J_y\) layers, and
   \((FGC4)\) gives \(\sum_{\kappa\in L}y_\kappa\ge\theta|L|/2\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cap-overload dual centered-cap endpoint]
   \label{cor:cap-overload-dual-centered-cap-endpoint}
   Work in the no-prefix residual of
   \cref{cor:fractional-generated-cover-cap-overload}, and let
   \(L_0\subseteq L\) be a dual-heavy layer as in
   \cref{cor:cap-overload-dual-low-cover-screen}, with
   \(K=|L_0|\) and \(y_\kappa\ge\delta>0\) on \(L_0\).  Let \(d_{\rm gen}\) be a
   certified generated metric on \(L_0\), and assume every
   \(\Delta_{\rm gen}\)-ball has a generated-record copy satisfying \((FDL2)\).
   If \(A>0\) and \((FDL4)\) holds, then every maximal
   \(\Delta_{\rm gen}\)-separated \(E\subseteq L_0\) satisfies the packing lower
   bound \((FDL5)\).

   Suppose now that \(|E|\le m\), that each \(\kappa\in E\) has a representative
   \(x_\kappa\in\mathbb S^{D-1}\), and that \(\mathcal R\) is a finite weighted
   centered Gaussian cap panel.  For \(r\in\mathcal R\), let \(w_r\ge0\),
   \(G_r\sim N(0,I_D)\), and
   \[
      U_r=\{x:\ip{G_r}{x}\ge T_r\}.
      \tag{FDE1}
   \]
   Fix constants \(A_{\rm cap},K_{\rm corr}\ge0\) and
   \(0\le\rho_{\rm cap}\le1\), and assume
   \[
      T_r^2\ge2\log m-A_{\rm cap}\log\log m,
      \qquad
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r
      \le m^{1+\rho_{\rm cap}}\log^{A_{\rm cap}}m .
      \tag{FDE2}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      \theta_m=K_{\rm corr}\frac{\log\log m}{\log m}<1,
      \tag{FDE3}
   \]
   and split ordered distinct pairs of \(E\) into
   \[
      E_{\rm lo}=\{(\kappa,\kappa'):\ip{x_\kappa}{x_{\kappa'}}\le\theta_m\},
      \qquad
      E_{\rm hi}=E_{\ne}^2\setminus E_{\rm lo}.
      \tag{FDE4}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r
      \sum_{\kappa\in E}\Pr[x_\kappa\in U_r]
      \le
      m^{1+\rho_{\rm cap}}\log^{3A_{\rm cap}/2}m,
      \tag{FDE5}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r
      \sum_{(\kappa,\kappa')\in E_{\rm lo}}
      \Pr[x_\kappa,x_{\kappa'}\in U_r]
      \le
      m^{1+\rho_{\rm cap}}
      \log^{2A_{\rm cap}+2K_{\rm corr}+1}m .
      \tag{FDE6}
   \]

   Define the high-correlation weighted pair mass
   \[
      \omega_{\kappa,\kappa'}
      =
      \mathbf 1_{\{(\kappa,\kappa')\in E_{\rm hi}\}}
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r
      \Pr[x_\kappa,x_{\kappa'}\in U_r],
      \qquad
      W_{\rm hi}=\sum_{\kappa,\kappa'\in E}\omega_{\kappa,\kappa'} .
      \tag{FDE7}
   \]
   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), set \(J_\omega=1\).  Otherwise assume the positive
   \(\omega_{\kappa,\kappa'}\)'s lie in a certified dyadic range
   \([\omega_{\min},\omega_{\max}]\), put
   \[
      J_\omega=
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{\omega_{\max}}{\omega_{\min}}\right\rceil,
      \tag{FDE8}
   \]
   and define
   \[
      V_{\kappa,t}
      =
      \{\kappa'\in E:\omega_{\kappa,\kappa'}\ge t\},
      \qquad
      t=\omega_{\min}2^j,\quad 0\le j<J_\omega .
      \tag{FDE9}
   \]
   Then every nonempty \(V_{\kappa,t}\) lies in the cap ball
   \[
      x_{\kappa'}\in
      B\!\left(x_\kappa,\sqrt{2(1-\theta_m)}\right),
      \tag{FDE10}
   \]
   and for every \(\Lambda_\star>0\), either
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}\le2|E|J_\omega\Lambda_\star,
      \tag{FDE11}
   \]
   or some dyadic high-correlation star satisfies
   \[
      t|V_{\kappa,t}|\ge\Lambda_\star .
      \tag{FDE12}
   \]
   Moreover, if such a star has a materializable generated record \(R_{\kappa,t}\)
   with \(V_{\kappa,t}\subseteq C_{R_{\kappa,t}}\) and
   \[
      P_{R_{\kappa,t}}<\delta |V_{\kappa,t}|,
      \tag{FDE13}
   \]
   then \((FGC4)\) is violated, so the cap-overload residual has a positive
   generated prefix.

   Consequently a surviving cap-overload dual residual has the following
   endpoint form: centered cap panels pay all one-point and low-correlation
   two-point mass by \((FDE5)\)--\((FDE6)\); any polynomial excess is a dyadic
   high-correlation cap star; and every such star either is too small, or has
   certified generated price at least its dual mass \(\delta |V_{\kappa,t}|\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The packing lower bound is the packing part of
   \cref{cor:cap-overload-dual-low-cover-screen}.

   Apply \cref{cor:weighted-polylog-low-correlation-coload} to the indexed
   representative family \((x_\kappa)_{\kappa\in E}\), the weighted panel
   \(\mathcal R\), and the low-correlation edge set \(E_{\rm lo}\).  The
   hypotheses \((FDE2)\)--\((FDE3)\) are exactly \((WPLC1)\)--\((WPLC2)\) with
   \(A=A_{\rm cap}\), \(K=K_{\rm corr}\), and \(\rho=\rho_{\rm cap}\).  This
   gives \((FDE5)\)--\((FDE6)\).

   If \(\kappa'\in V_{\kappa,t}\), then
   \(\omega_{\kappa,\kappa'}>0\), hence
   \((\kappa,\kappa')\in E_{\rm hi}\).  By \((FDE4)\),
   \(\ip{x_\kappa}{x_{\kappa'}}>\theta_m\), so
   \[
      \|x_\kappa-x_{\kappa'}\|^2
      =
      2-2\ip{x_\kappa}{x_{\kappa'}}
      \le2(1-\theta_m),
   \]
   proving \((FDE10)\).

   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), then \((FDE11)\) is immediate.  Otherwise, for fixed
   \(\kappa\), the dyadic layer-cake estimate gives
   \[
      \sum_{j=0}^{J_\omega-1}
      \omega_{\min}2^j
      |V_{\kappa,\omega_{\min}2^j}|
      \ge
      \frac12\sum_{\kappa'\in E}\omega_{\kappa,\kappa'} .
   \]
   Summing over \(\kappa\), if every dyadic star had
   \(t|V_{\kappa,t}|<\Lambda_\star\), then
   \(W_{\rm hi}/2<|E|J_\omega\Lambda_\star\), proving \((FDE11)\).  The
   contrapositive gives \((FDE12)\).

   Finally, because \(V_{\kappa,t}\subseteq E\subseteq L_0\), every member has
   dual weight at least \(\delta\).  If \((FDE13)\) holds, then
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa'\in C_{R_{\kappa,t}}}y_{\kappa'}
      \ge
      \sum_{\kappa'\in V_{\kappa,t}}y_{\kappa'}
      \ge
      \delta |V_{\kappa,t}|
      >
      P_{R_{\kappa,t}},
   \]
   contradicting the dual constraint \((FGC4)\).  By
   \cref{cor:fractional-generated-cover-cap-overload}, that contradiction is the
   positive generated-prefix alternative.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cap-overload dual cap-star storage split]
   \label{cor:cap-overload-dual-cap-star-storage-split}
   Work in the no-prefix residual and notation of
   \cref{cor:cap-overload-dual-centered-cap-endpoint}.  Assume that every
   nonempty dyadic high-correlation star \(V_{\kappa,t}\) has a materializable
   generated record \(R_{\kappa,t}\) with
   \(V_{\kappa,t}\subseteq C_{R_{\kappa,t}}\) and common price envelope
   \[
      P_{R_{\kappa,t}}
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(Ah_{\kappa,t}^{\rho}
      +\zeta h_{\kappa,t}^{1+\rho}\right),
      \qquad
      h_{\kappa,t}=|V_{\kappa,t}|,\quad 0<\rho<1 .
      \tag{FDS1}
   \]
   Then every nonempty dyadic high-correlation star satisfies
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(Ah_{\kappa,t}^{\rho-1}
      +\zeta h_{\kappa,t}^{\rho}\right).
      \tag{FDS2}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      H_-^{\rm over}
      =
      \left(\frac{2\psi_\star A}{\delta}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \tag{FDS3}
   \]
   with \(H_-^{\rm over}=0\) when \(A=0\).  If \(\zeta>0\), also put
   \[
      H_+^{\rm over}
      =
      \left(\frac{\delta}{2\psi_\star\zeta}\right)^{1/\rho}.
      \tag{FDS4}
   \]
   Then every nonempty star obeys
   \[
      h_{\kappa,t}\le H_-^{\rm over}
      \qquad\text{or}\qquad
      \bigl(\zeta>0\text{ and }h_{\kappa,t}\ge H_+^{\rm over}\bigr).
      \tag{FDS5}
   \]
   Equivalently, any materialized star with
   \[
      h_{\kappa,t}>H_-^{\rm over}
      \quad\text{and, when }\zeta>0,\quad
      h_{\kappa,t}<H_+^{\rm over}
      \tag{FDS6}
   \]
   is itself a positive generated prefix.

   If \(\zeta>0\) and the forbidden interval is empty, then
   \[
      \delta\le2\psi_\star A^\rho\zeta^{1-\rho}.
      \tag{FDS7}
   \]

   Let \(\mathcal S_{\rm over}\) be the set of nonempty dyadic cap-overload stars
   in the storage-dominated alternative \(h_{\kappa,t}\ge H_+^{\rm over}\), and
   define for \(s=(\kappa,t)\in\mathcal S_{\rm over}\)
   \[
      A_s^{\rm over}=V_{\kappa,t},
      \qquad
      h_s=|A_s^{\rm over}|=h_{\kappa,t},
      \qquad
      u_s^{\rm over}=\psi_\star\zeta\,t\,h_s^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{FDS8}
   \]
   If \(\zeta=0\), interpret \(\mathcal S_{\rm over}=\emptyset\).  Then every
   no-prefix cap-overload dual residual satisfies
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      2|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-^{\rm over}
      +
      \frac4\delta
      \sum_{s\in\mathcal S_{\rm over}}u_s^{\rm over}.
      \tag{FDS9}
   \]

   Consequently, after centered-cap low-correlation payment, the cap-overload
   dual branch has no cap-specific high-correlation recursion.  It is an explicit
   bounded-cardinality fixed tail plus a storage-dominated priced child panel
   \(\{(A_s^{\rm over},u_s^{\rm over})\}\), which may be submitted to the generic
   shared-cover compiler and distinct-storage certificates exactly as in
   \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-cap-star-storage-split}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   In a no-prefix residual, \((FDE13)\) cannot hold.  Therefore every nonempty
   materialized star satisfies
   \[
      \delta h_{\kappa,t}\le P_{R_{\kappa,t}} .
   \]
   Combining this with \((FDS1)\) and dividing by \(h_{\kappa,t}>0\) proves
   \((FDS2)\).

   If \(h_{\kappa,t}>H_-^{\rm over}\), then
   \[
      \psi_\star A h_{\kappa,t}^{\rho-1}<\frac{\delta}{2}.
   \]
   Thus \((FDS2)\) can hold only if
   \(\psi_\star\zeta h_{\kappa,t}^{\rho}\ge\delta/2\).  When \(\zeta=0\), this
   is impossible; when \(\zeta>0\), it is exactly
   \(h_{\kappa,t}\ge H_+^{\rm over}\).  This proves \((FDS5)\), and \((FDS6)\)
   is its contrapositive combined with
   \cref{cor:cap-overload-dual-centered-cap-endpoint}.

   If \(\zeta>0\) and \(H_-^{\rm over}\ge H_+^{\rm over}\), then
   \[
      \left(\frac{2\psi_\star A}{\delta}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \ge
      \left(\frac{\delta}{2\psi_\star\zeta}\right)^{1/\rho}.
   \]
   Raising to \(\rho(1-\rho)\) and rearranging gives \((FDS7)\).

   It remains to prove \((FDS9)\).  If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), it is immediate.
   Otherwise the layer-cake estimate from
   \cref{cor:cap-overload-dual-centered-cap-endpoint} gives
   \[
      \frac12W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \sum_{\kappa\in E}\sum_t t\,h_{\kappa,t}.
      \tag{FDS10}
   \]
   Split the sum into the bounded side \(h_{\kappa,t}\le H_-^{\rm over}\) and the
   storage-dominated side.  Since \(t\le\omega_{\max}\), the bounded side
   contributes at most \(|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-^{\rm over}\).  For a
   storage-dominated star, the definition of \(H_+^{\rm over}\) gives
   \[
      \delta\le2\psi_\star\zeta h_{\kappa,t}^{\rho},
   \]
   and hence
   \[
      t\,h_{\kappa,t}
      \le
      \frac2\delta\psi_\star\zeta\,t\,h_{\kappa,t}^{1+\rho}
      =
      \frac2\delta u_{(\kappa,t)}^{\rm over}.
      \tag{FDS11}
   \]
   Substituting these two estimates in \((FDS10)\) proves \((FDS9)\).  When
