   \(\zeta=0\), the storage-dominated side is empty and the same argument gives
   the fixed-tail bound alone.

   Finally, \((FDS8)\) is the standard priced child-panel form after absorbing the
   dyadic intensity \(t\) into the child price factor
   \(t\psi_\star\zeta\).  The cited generic compiler and storage certificates are
   stated for arbitrary priced child panels, so no additional cap-overload
   materialization rule is needed.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Shared-cover reduction for cap-overload storage tails]
   \label{cor:cap-overload-storage-tail-shared-cover}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:cap-overload-dual-cap-star-storage-split} for one no-prefix
   residual, and write \(\mathcal S=\mathcal S_{\rm over}\).  For
   \(s\in\mathcal S\), put \(u_s=u_s^{\rm over}\).  Let
   \(\mathcal R^{\rm over}\) be a finite family of candidate shared records.
   A record \(c\in\mathcal R^{\rm over}\) has one-time recursive storage price
   \(P_c\ge0\) and certified coverage coefficients \(0\le g_{c,s}\le1\).  Define
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Phi^{\rm over}=\min
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{s\in\mathcal S}u_se_s
        +\sum_{c\in\mathcal R^{\rm over}}P_c\lambda_c\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        e_s+\sum_{c\in\mathcal R^{\rm over}}\lambda_c g_{c,s}\ge1
        \qquad(s\in\mathcal S),\\[0.8em]
      & e_s\ge0,\qquad \lambda_c\ge0 .
   \end{array}
      \tag{FOS1}
   \]
   Its dual is
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Phi^{\rm over}=\max
      & \displaystyle \sum_{s\in\mathcal S}y_s\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & 0\le y_s\le u_s
        \qquad(s\in\mathcal S),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{s\in\mathcal S}g_{c,s}y_s\le P_c
        \qquad(c\in\mathcal R^{\rm over}).
   \end{array}
      \tag{FOS2}
   \]

   Consequently the storage-dominated term in \((FDS9)\) may be replaced by
   \(\Phi^{\rm over}\): for any desired allowance \(B_{\rm over}\) and
   nonnegative fixed overhead \(\Gamma\), the cap-overload high-correlation
   return is bounded by
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      2|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-^{\rm over}
      +B_{\rm over}
      \tag{FOS3}
   \]
   whenever
   \[
      \Gamma+\Phi^{\rm over}\le\frac{\delta}{4}B_{\rm over}.
      \tag{FOS4}
   \]
   If \(\Phi^{\rm over}>\Theta\), then there is a dual weighting \(y_s\) with
   \[
      \sum_{s\in\mathcal S}y_s>\Theta,\qquad
      0\le y_s\le u_s,\qquad
      \sum_sg_{c,s}y_s\le P_c
      \quad(c\in\mathcal R^{\rm over}).
      \tag{FOS5}
   \]

   Finally suppose a generated template \(T\) has a search container
   \(\mathcal S_T\subseteq\mathcal S\), capture weights \(a_{T,s}\in[0,1]\),
   available cardinalities \(\mathcal K_T\), and certified prices
   \(\overline P_T(K)\), and that every \(U\subseteq\mathcal S_T\) with
   \(|U|=K\in\mathcal K_T\) can be materialized as a record \(c(T,U)\) with
   \[
      P_{c(T,U)}\le\overline P_T(K),
      \qquad
      g_{c(T,U),s}\ge a_{T,s}\mathbf 1_{\{s\in U\}} .
      \tag{FOS6}
   \]
   In a dual residual \(y\), order \(\mathcal S_T=\{s_1,s_2,\ldots\}\) by
   nonincreasing \(a_{T,s}y_s\).  If, for some \(K\in\mathcal K_T\),
   \[
      \sum_{j\le K}a_{T,s_j}y_{s_j}>\overline P_T(K),
      \tag{FOS7}
   \]
   then \(c(T,\{s_1,\ldots,s_K\})\) is an improving shared-cover column.
   Conversely, if no generated prefix is improving for \(T\), then every
   \(K\)-subset \(U\subseteq\mathcal S_T\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{s\in U}a_{T,s}y_s\le\overline P_T(K).
      \tag{FOS8}
   \]

   Thus the cap-overload storage tail has exactly the same algorithmic
   interface as the fractional sponsor tail: solve one finite shared-cover LP,
   add any positive generated top-prefix column, or expose a single weighted
   no-prefix residual for the range/list/AQ/facility separator.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The program \((FOS1)\) is finite and feasible by taking \(e_s=1\).  Assign a
   dual variable \(y_s\ge0\) to each coverage constraint.  The coefficients of
   \(e_s\) and \(\lambda_c\) give respectively \(y_s\le u_s\) and
   \(\sum_sg_{c,s}y_s\le P_c\), proving \((FOS2)\) by finite LP duality.

   A feasible primal solution represents each storage-dominated overload star
   \(s\) by an \(e_s\)-fractional residual copy and by the shared records
   covering it.  The coverage constraints say this representation covers the
   original unit copy of \(s\), and the objective is the resulting
   shared-canonical storage price.  Since \((FDS9)\) uses the raw sum
   \(\sum_su_s\) only through the coefficient \(4/\delta\), replacing that sum
   by \(\Gamma+\Phi^{\rm over}\) and using \((FOS4)\) gives \((FOS3)\).  The
   dual obstruction \((FOS5)\) is the contrapositive of strong duality.

   If \((FOS7)\) holds and \(U_K=\{s_1,\ldots,s_K\}\), then \((FOS6)\) gives
   \[
      \sum_sg_{c(T,U_K),s}y_s
      \ge
      \sum_{j\le K}a_{T,s_j}y_{s_j}
      >
      \overline P_T(K)
      \ge
      P_{c(T,U_K)} .
   \]
   Hence the dual constraint for \(c(T,U_K)\) is violated, so adding that
   record is an improving column.  For fixed \(K\), the top \(K\) elements in
   the order of \(a_{T,s}y_s\) maximize the left side over all \(K\)-subsets,
   proving the no-prefix subset test \((FOS8)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Generated-cover handoff for cap-overload storage tails]
   \label{cor:cap-overload-storage-tail-generated-cover}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:cap-overload-storage-tail-shared-cover}.  Let \(\mathcal T^{\rm over}\)
   be a finite family of generated shared-record templates satisfying the
   materialization hypothesis \((FOS6)\), with finite available cardinality
   sets.  Consider the generated-cover relaxation
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Psi^{\rm gen,over}=\min
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{s\in\mathcal S}u_se_s
        +\sum_{T\in\mathcal T^{\rm over}}
         \sum_{K\in\mathcal K_T}
         \sum_{\substack{U\subseteq\mathcal S_T\\ |U|=K}}
         \lambda_{T,U}\overline P_T(K)\\[0.9em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        e_s+
        \sum_{T\in\mathcal T^{\rm over}}
        \sum_{K\in\mathcal K_T}
        \sum_{\substack{U\subseteq\mathcal S_T\\ |U|=K}}
        \lambda_{T,U}a_{T,s}\mathbf 1_{\{s\in U\}}
        \ge1
        \qquad(s\in\mathcal S),\\[0.9em]
      & e_s\ge0,\qquad \lambda_{T,U}\ge0 .
   \end{array}
      \tag{FOG1}
   \]
   If \(\Psi^{\rm gen,over}\le\Theta\), then
   \(\Phi^{\rm over}\le\Theta\).  In particular the storage-tail bound
   \((FOS3)\) holds whenever
   \[
      \Gamma+\Psi^{\rm gen,over}\le\frac{\delta}{4}B_{\rm over}.
      \tag{FOG2}
   \]

   Conversely, if \(\Psi^{\rm gen,over}>\Theta\), then there is a dual
   weighting \(y_s\) with
   \[
      \sum_{s\in\mathcal S}y_s>\Theta,
      \qquad
      0\le y_s\le u_s,
      \tag{FOG3}
   \]
   such that every generated template satisfies all subset tests
   \[
      \sum_{s\in U}a_{T,s}y_s\le\overline P_T(K)
      \qquad
      (T\in\mathcal T^{\rm over},\ K\in\mathcal K_T,\
       U\subseteq\mathcal S_T,\ |U|=K).
      \tag{FOG4}
   \]

   Now work in such a no-generated-cover residual.  Let
   \(L\subseteq\mathcal S\) be nonempty, with \(K_L=|L|\), and suppose \(L\) is
   assigned to generated templates by a map \(\kappa:L\to\mathcal T^{\rm over}\)
   so that the nonempty parts
   \[
      L_T=\{s\in L:\kappa(s)=T\},
      \qquad K_T=|L_T|
      \tag{FOG5}
   \]
   satisfy \(K_T\in\mathcal K_T\), \(L_T\subseteq\mathcal S_T\), and certified
   lower degrees
   \[
      0\le w_s\le a_{\kappa(s),s}y_s
      \qquad(s\in L).
      \tag{FOG6}
   \]
   If \(w_s\ge\xi>0\) on \(L\), and all used templates satisfy
   \[
      \overline P_T(h)
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(Ah^\rho+\zeta h^{1+\rho}\right),
      \qquad 0<\rho<1 ,
      \tag{FOG7}
   \]
   while the assignment uses \(J\) nonempty parts, then
   \[
      \xi K_L
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(AJ^{1-\rho}K_L^\rho+\zeta K_L^{1+\rho}\right).
      \tag{FOG8}
   \]
   Hence, if \(A>0\) and
   \[
      \xi>2\psi_\star\zeta K_L^\rho,
      \tag{FOG9}
   \]
   every surviving residual has
   \[
      J
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{\xi K_L^{1-\rho}}{2\psi_\star A}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{FOG10}
   \]
   When \(\zeta=0\), the same bound holds with \(2\psi_\star A\) replaced by
   \(\psi_\star A\).

   Finally, let \(d_{\rm gen}\) be any pseudometric on \(L\).  Suppose that for
   every \(s_0\in L\), the ball
   \[
      B_{\rm gen}(s_0,\Delta_{\rm gen})
      =
      \{s\in L:d_{\rm gen}(s,s_0)\le\Delta_{\rm gen}\}
      \tag{FOG11}
   \]
   has a generated template copy \(T_{s_0}\in\mathcal T^{\rm over}\) with
   \[
      B_{\rm gen}(s_0,\Delta_{\rm gen})\subseteq\mathcal S_{T_{s_0}},
      \qquad
      |B_{\rm gen}(s_0,\Delta_{\rm gen})|\in\mathcal K_{T_{s_0}},
      \tag{FOG12}
   \]
   and certified current capture
   \[
      a_{T_{s_0},s}y_s\ge\xi
      \qquad(s\in B_{\rm gen}(s_0,\Delta_{\rm gen})).
      \tag{FOG13}
   \]
   If \(E\subseteq L\) is maximal \(\Delta_{\rm gen}\)-separated, then under
   \(A>0\) and \((FOG9)\)
   \[
      |E|
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{\xi K_L^{1-\rho}}{2\psi_\star A}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \tag{FOG14}
   \]
   with the same \(\zeta=0\) sharpening.  Thus a cap-overload storage tail that
   survives shared-cover and generated-prefix search is not a new recursion
   branch: unless its storage term already dominates, it exposes a separated
   packing in the chosen generated metric for the common spherical/list-decoding
   energy screen.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Any feasible solution of \((FOG1)\) gives a feasible solution of
   \((FOS1)\): replace each active pair \((T,U)\) by the materialized shared
   record \(c(T,U)\), use \((FOS6)\) for coverage, and use
   \(P_{c(T,U)}\le\overline P_T(|U|)\) for price.  Hence
   \(\Phi^{\rm over}\le\Psi^{\rm gen,over}\), and \((FOG2)\) implies the
   storage-tail bound by \cref{cor:cap-overload-storage-tail-shared-cover}.

   The dual of \((FOG1)\) is exactly \((FOG3)\) plus all subset constraints
   \((FOG4)\).  The primal is finite and feasible by taking \(e_s=1\), so finite
   LP duality gives the stated no-generated-cover residual when
   \(\Psi^{\rm gen,over}>\Theta\).

   For a nonempty part \(L_T\), \((FOG6)\) and the subset test \((FOG4)\) give
   \[
      \sum_{s\in L_T}w_s
      \le
      \sum_{s\in L_T}a_{T,s}y_s
      \le
      \overline P_T(K_T).
   \]
   Summing over the \(J\) parts, using \(w_s\ge\xi\), the price envelope
   \((FOG7)\), and Holder's inequality,
   \[
      \sum_TK_T^\rho\le J^{1-\rho}K_L^\rho,\qquad
      \sum_TK_T^{1+\rho}\le K_L^{1+\rho},
   \]
   proves \((FOG8)\).  Under \((FOG9)\), the storage term in \((FOG8)\) is less
   than \(\xi K_L/2\), and rearranging gives \((FOG10)\).  When \(\zeta=0\),
   that storage term is absent, giving the sharper constant.

   If \(E\) is maximal \(\Delta_{\rm gen}\)-separated, then the balls
   \(B_{\rm gen}(s,\Delta_{\rm gen})\), \(s\in E\), cover \(L\).  Assign every
   \(s\in L\) to one covering ball.  By \((FOG12)\)--\((FOG13)\), this cover
   satisfies \((FOG5)\)--\((FOG6)\) with \(w_s=\xi\).  Applying the preceding
   cover lower bound gives \((FOG14)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cap-overload storage-tail packing energy endpoint]
   \label{cor:cap-overload-storage-tail-packing-energy}
   Work in the no-generated-cover residual of
   \cref{cor:cap-overload-storage-tail-generated-cover}, and let
   \(E\subseteq L\) be a separated packing witness from \((FOG14)\).  Suppose
   every \(s\in E\) has a representative \(x_s\in\mathbb S^{d-1}\).  Let
   \(U_G\) be a spherical, Gaussian-cap, code, range/list-decoded, or other
   certified bucket drawn from a law \(G\).  Partition the ordered distinct
   pairs \(E_{\ne}^2\) into finitely many profiles \(\Pi_E\), and assume
   \[
      \Pr_G[x_s,x_{s'}\in U_G]\le e^{-I_\pi}
      \qquad((s,s')\in\pi,\ \pi\in\Pi_E).
      \tag{FOP1}
   \]
   With
   \[
      X_E(G)=\sum_{s\in E}\mathbf 1\{x_s\in U_G\},
      \tag{FOP2}
   \]
   one has
   \[
      \E_GX_E(G)^2
      \le
      \sum_{s\in E}\Pr_G[x_s\in U_G]
      +
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi_E}|\pi|e^{-I_\pi}.
      \tag{FOP3}
   \]
   In particular, if
   \[
      I_\pi\ge\log|\pi|+\Lambda
      \qquad(\pi\in\Pi_E),
      \tag{FOP4}
   \]
   then the total distinct-pair contribution is at most
   \[
      |\Pi_E|e^{-\Lambda}.
      \tag{FOP5}
   \]

   Conversely, fix an energy-deficient profile
   \(\pi\subseteq E_{\ne}^2\), nonnegative pair weights
   \(\omega_{s,s'}\), and a split
   \[
      \pi=\pi_{\rm lo}\dot\cup\pi_{\rm hi}.
      \tag{FOP6}
   \]
   Suppose
   \[
      \sum_{(s,s')\in\pi_{\rm lo}}\omega_{s,s'}\le B_{\rm lo},
      \tag{FOP7}
   \]
   and every high edge has representative correlation at least
   \[
      \ip{x_s}{x_{s'}}\ge\underline\theta
      \qquad((s,s')\in\pi_{\rm hi}).
      \tag{FOP8}
   \]
   Define
   \[
      M_s(s')=\omega_{s,s'}\mathbf 1_{\{(s,s')\in\pi_{\rm hi}\}},
      \qquad
      W_{\rm hi}=\sum_{s,s'\in E}M_s(s').
      \tag{FOP9}
   \]
   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), set \(J_\omega=1\).  Otherwise assume the positive
   values of \(M_s(s')\) lie in a certified dyadic range
   \([\omega_{\min},\omega_{\max}]\), put
   \[
      J_\omega=
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{\omega_{\max}}{\omega_{\min}}\right\rceil,
      \tag{FOP10}
   \]
   and define
   \[
      V_{s,t}=\{s'\in E:M_s(s')\ge t\},
      \qquad
      t\in\{\omega_{\min}2^j:0\le j<J_\omega\}.
      \tag{FOP11}
   \]
   Then every nonempty \(V_{s,t}\) lies in the cap ball
   \[
      x_{s'}\in B\!\left(x_s,\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)}\right).
      \tag{FOP12}
   \]

   Let \(\chi>0\).  For every nonempty \(V_{s,t}\), suppose preprocessing has
   a generated shared-record template \(T_{s,t}\in\mathcal T^{\rm over}\)
   satisfying the materialization hypothesis \((FOS6)\), with
   \[
      V_{s,t}\subseteq\mathcal S_{T_{s,t}},
      \qquad
      h_{s,t}=|V_{s,t}|\in\mathcal K_{T_{s,t}},
      \tag{FOP13}
   \]
   and certified current dual capture
   \[
      a_{T_{s,t},s'}y_{s'}\ge\chi
      \qquad(s'\in V_{s,t}).
      \tag{FOP14}
   \]
   If, for some star,
   \[
      \chi h_{s,t}>\overline P_{T_{s,t}}(h_{s,t}),
      \tag{FOP15}
   \]
   then the cap-overload storage-tail LP has a positive generated
   shared-cover column.  If no such prefix exists and all used templates obey
   \[
      \overline P_{T_{s,t}}(h)
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(Ah^\rho+\zeta h^{1+\rho}\right),
      \tag{FOP16}
   \]
   then
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \frac{2\psi_\star}{\chi}
      \sum_{s\in E}\sum_t
      t\left(Ah_{s,t}^{\rho}+\zeta h_{s,t}^{1+\rho}\right).
      \tag{FOP17}
   \]

   Moreover, in a no-prefix residual every nonempty returned star satisfies the
   scalar gate
   \[
      \chi
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(Ah_{s,t}^{\rho-1}+\zeta h_{s,t}^{\rho}\right).
      \tag{FOP18}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      H_-^{\rm pack}
      =
      \left(\frac{2\psi_\star A}{\chi}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \tag{FOP19}
   \]
   with \(H_-^{\rm pack}=0\) when \(A=0\), and, when \(\zeta>0\),
   \[
      H_+^{\rm pack}
      =
      \left(\frac{\chi}{2\psi_\star\zeta}\right)^{1/\rho}.
      \tag{FOP20}
   \]
   Thus every nonempty returned star obeys
   \[
      h_{s,t}\le H_-^{\rm pack}
      \qquad\text{or}\qquad
      \bigl(\zeta>0\text{ and }h_{s,t}\ge H_+^{\rm pack}\bigr),
      \tag{FOP21}
   \]
   and the high-correlation mass has the normal form
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      2|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-^{\rm pack}
      +
      \frac4\chi
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal S_{\rm pack}}u_r^{\rm pack}.
      \tag{FOP22}
   \]
   Here \(\mathcal S_{\rm pack}\) is the set of storage-dominated returned stars
   \(r=(s,t)\) with \(h_{s,t}\ge H_+^{\rm pack}\), interpreted as empty when
   \(\zeta=0\), and
   \[
      A_r^{\rm pack}=V_{s,t},\qquad
      u_r^{\rm pack}=\psi_\star\zeta\,t\,h_{s,t}^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{FOP23}
   \]

   Therefore the cap-overload storage-tail residual has the same terminal form
   as every other child-panel residual: the bucket law pays the separated
   packing by entropy-energy, or an energy-deficient high-correlation profile
   either produces a positive generated prefix or returns only a bounded fixed
   tail plus another priced child panel for the same shared-cover and
   distinct-storage interfaces.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The second-moment bound \((FOP3)\) and its entropy consequence \((FOP5)\)
   are \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-packing-energy-screen} applied with
   \(\mathcal A=\mathcal S\).  The cap containment \((FOP12)\), the positive
   prefix criterion \((FOP15)\), and the integrated price bound \((FOP17)\) are
   \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-high-correlation-return} with
   \(\alpha_{T,s}=a_{T,s}\).

   Finally, \((FOP18)\)--\((FOP23)\) are the generic returned cap-star storage
   split, \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-cap-star-storage-split}, in the same
   specialization.  The records in \((FOP23)\) have the standard priced
   child-panel form after absorbing the dyadic intensity \(t\) into the price
   factor, so they may be fed back into
   \cref{cor:cap-overload-storage-tail-shared-cover} or the generic
   distinct-storage certificates.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Shared-cover LP for the fractional sponsor tail]
   \label{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-shared-cover}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:storage-dominated-sponsor-stars-fractional-tail} for one build
   seed \(z\), and write \(\mathcal S=\mathcal S_{{\rm st},z}\).  Each
   \(s\in\mathcal S\) has fractional price \(u_s=u_s^{\rm frac}\).  Let
   \(\mathcal R_z\) be a finite family of candidate shared records.  This is
   the specialization of
   \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-shared-cover-compiler} with
   \(\mathcal A=\mathcal S\); the local notation below is kept because later
   fractional-tail corollaries use the labels \((STC1)\)--\((STC4)\).  A record
   \(c\in\mathcal R_z\) has one-time recursive storage price \(P_c\ge0\) and
   certified coverage coefficients \(0\le g_{c,s}\le1\) for
   \(s\in\mathcal S\).  Consider the finite cover LP
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Phi_z^{\rm st}=\min
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{s\in\mathcal S}u_s e_s
        +\sum_{c\in\mathcal R_z}P_c\lambda_c\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        e_s+\sum_{c\in\mathcal R_z}\lambda_c g_{c,s}\ge1
        \qquad(s\in\mathcal S),\\[0.8em]
      & e_s\ge0,\qquad \lambda_c\ge0 .
   \end{array}
      \tag{STC1}
   \]
   Its dual is
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Phi_z^{\rm st}=\max
      & \displaystyle \sum_{s\in\mathcal S}y_s\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & 0\le y_s\le u_s
        \qquad(s\in\mathcal S),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{s\in\mathcal S}g_{c,s}y_s\le P_c
        \qquad(c\in\mathcal R_z).
   \end{array}
      \tag{STC2}
   \]
   If, for a desired storage-dominated allowance \(B_{\rm st}\),
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+\E_z\Phi_z^{\rm st}
      \le
      \frac\theta8B_{\rm st},
      \tag{STC3}
   \]
   then the storage-dominated contribution in \((SFT2)\) is inside
   \(B_{\rm st}\).  More precisely, every feasible solution of \((STC1)\)
   replaces the individual fractional star children by residual fractional
   copies of price \(u_se_s\) and shared records of total price
   \(\sum_cP_c\lambda_c\).  Thus \(\Phi_z^{\rm st}\) is a shared-canonical
   storage price, and \((STC3)\) is a stronger shared version of \((SFT4)\).

   Conversely, if a seed has \(\Phi_z^{\rm st}>\Theta_z\), then there is a dual
   weighting \(y_s\) with
   \[
      \sum_{s\in\mathcal S}y_s>\Theta_z,\qquad
      0\le y_s\le u_s,\qquad
      \sum_sg_{c,s}y_s\le P_c\quad(c\in\mathcal R_z).
      \tag{STC4}
   \]
   This is the exact no-shared-cover obstruction for the fractional sponsor
   tail: every retained shared record captures at most its one-time recursive
   price against the dual mass.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The primal is finite, feasible by taking \(e_s=1\), and bounded below.
   Assign a dual variable \(y_s\ge0\) to each coverage constraint.  The
   coefficient of \(e_s\) gives \(y_s\le u_s\), and the coefficient of
   \(\lambda_c\) gives \(\sum_sg_{c,s}y_s\le P_c\).  Finite LP duality proves
   \((STC2)\).

   Given a feasible primal solution, keep an \(e_s\)-fractional copy of the
   original star child \(s\) and a \(\lambda_c\)-fractional copy of each shared
   record \(c\).  The coverage inequalities say every original fractional star
   is fully represented by residual plus shared copies.  The total storage
   price of this representation is exactly the objective in \((STC1)\), and
   the price-weighted storage certificates cited in
   \cref{cor:storage-dominated-sponsor-stars-fractional-tail} are linear in
   such fractional copies.  Therefore \(\Phi_z^{\rm st}\) is a valid
   shared-canonical replacement for \(\sum_su_s\) in \((SFT4)\), proving
   \((STC3)\Rightarrow(SFT4)\) with allowance \(B_{\rm st}\).  The final
   statement is the contrapositive of LP strong duality.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Generated-prefix oracle for the fractional sponsor tail]
   \label{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-generated-prefix}
   Work in the dual residual \((STC4)\) of
   \cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-shared-cover}.  Let \(T\) be a generated
   shared-record template with search container
   \(\mathcal S_T\subseteq\mathcal S\), certified capture weights
   \(a_{T,s}\in[0,1]\), available cardinalities \(\mathcal K_T\), and certified
   prices \(\overline P_T(K)\).  Suppose that for every
   \(K\in\mathcal K_T\) and \(U\subseteq\mathcal S_T\) with \(|U|=K\),
   preprocessing can materialize a shared record \(c(T,U)\in\mathcal R_z\)
   satisfying
   \[
      P_{c(T,U)}\le\overline P_T(K),
      \qquad
      g_{c(T,U),s}\ge a_{T,s}\mathbf 1_{\{s\in U\}}
      \quad(s\in\mathcal S).
      \tag{FSG1}
   \]
   Order \(\mathcal S_T=\{s_1,s_2,\ldots\}\) by nonincreasing
   \(a_{T,s}y_s\).  If, for some available \(K\),
   \[
      \sum_{j\le K}a_{T,s_j}y_{s_j}>\overline P_T(K),
      \tag{FSG2}
   \]
   then \(c(T,\{s_1,\ldots,s_K\})\) is an improving shared-cover column for
   \((STC1)\).  Conversely, if no generated prefix is improving for \(T\), then
   every \(K\)-subset \(U\subseteq\mathcal S_T\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{s\in U}a_{T,s}y_s\le\overline P_T(K).
      \tag{FSG3}
   \]

   If, additionally, the prices have the common sponsor form
   \[
      \overline P_T(K)
      =
      \psi_T\left(A_TK^\rho+\zeta_TK^{1+\rho}\right),
      \qquad 0<\rho<1,
      \tag{FSG4}
   \]
   and the available cardinalities are \(b_T\)-dense from below, then every
   nonempty dual-degree superlevel
   \[
      H_{T,\delta}=\{s\in\mathcal S_T:a_{T,s}y_s\ge\delta\},
      \qquad h=|H_{T,\delta}|
      \tag{FSG5}
   \]
   in a no-prefix residual obeys
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      \psi_T\left(
         b_T^{1-\rho}A_Th^{\rho-1}
         +\zeta_Th^\rho
      \right).
      \tag{FSG6}
   \]
   Hence the remaining geometric task for the fractional sponsor tail is a
   standard generated-cell separation problem: find a range/list/AQ/facility
   template whose current dual-weighted prefix beats its certified one-time
   price, or prove that every generated cell satisfies the weak-type envelope
   \((FSG6)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((FSG2)\) holds, then by \((FSG1)\)
   \[
      \sum_sg_{c(T,U_K),s}y_s
      \ge
      \sum_{j\le K}a_{T,s_j}y_{s_j}
      >
      \overline P_T(K)
      \ge
      P_{c(T,U_K)} .
   \]
   Thus the dual constraint of \((STC2)\) for this shared record is violated,
   so column generation may add it as an improving record.  For fixed \(K\),
   the top \(K\) elements maximize \(\sum_{s\in U}a_{T,s}y_s\), proving the
   converse \((FSG3)\).

   For the weak-type statement, choose \(K\in\mathcal K_T\) with
   \(h/b_T\le K\le h\).  The top \(K\) prefix has total degree at least
   \(K\delta\).  Since no prefix is improving,
   \[
      K\delta\le\overline P_T(K)
      =
      \psi_T(A_TK^\rho+\zeta_TK^{1+\rho}).
   \]
   Divide by \(K\), use \(K\ge h/b_T\) in the negative exponent
   \(K^{\rho-1}\), and use \(K\le h\) in \(K^\rho\), obtaining \((FSG6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Generated-cover dichotomy for the fractional sponsor tail]
   \label{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-generated-cover-dichotomy}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-shared-cover} for one seed \(z\), and
   let \(\mathcal T\) be a finite family of generated shared-record templates
   satisfying the materialization hypothesis \((FSG1)\), with finite available
   cardinality sets.  Consider the surrogate generated-cover LP
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Psi_z^{\rm gen,st}=\min
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{s\in\mathcal S}u_s e_s
        +\sum_{T\in\mathcal T}
         \sum_{K\in\mathcal K_T}
         \sum_{\substack{U\subseteq\mathcal S_T\\ |U|=K}}
         \lambda_{T,U}\overline P_T(K)\\[0.9em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        e_s+
        \sum_{T\in\mathcal T}
        \sum_{K\in\mathcal K_T}
        \sum_{\substack{U\subseteq\mathcal S_T\\ |U|=K}}
        \lambda_{T,U}a_{T,s}\mathbf 1_{\{s\in U\}}
        \ge1
        \qquad(s\in\mathcal S),\\[0.9em]
      & e_s\ge0,\qquad \lambda_{T,U}\ge0 .
   \end{array}
      \tag{FGD1}
   \]
   If \(\Psi_z^{\rm gen,st}\le\Theta_z\), then
   \(\Phi_z^{\rm st}\le\Theta_z\); in particular the generated prefixes close
   the fractional sponsor tail at that local storage allowance.  Consequently,
   the global condition
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+\E_z\Psi_z^{\rm gen,st}
      \le
      \frac\theta8B_{\rm st}
      \tag{FGD2}
   \]
   is sufficient for the storage-dominated contribution in \((SFT2)\) to lie
   inside \(B_{\rm st}\).

   Conversely, if \(\Psi_z^{\rm gen,st}>\Theta_z\), then there is a dual
   weighting \(y_s\) with
   \[
      \sum_{s\in\mathcal S}y_s>\Theta_z,
      \qquad
      0\le y_s\le u_s,
      \tag{FGD3}
   \]
   such that every generated template satisfies all subset tests
   \[
      \sum_{s\in U}a_{T,s}y_s\le\overline P_T(K)
      \qquad
      (T\in\mathcal T,\ K\in\mathcal K_T,\ U\subseteq\mathcal S_T,\ |U|=K).
      \tag{FGD4}
   \]
   Equivalently, after ordering \(\mathcal S_T\) by nonincreasing
   \(a_{T,s}y_s\), every available top prefix satisfies the no-improvement
   inequality \((FSG3)\).  Thus a failed generated-cover attempt exposes one
   no-prefix dual residual for all templates in \(\mathcal T\), not a family of
   unrelated local failures.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Any feasible solution of \((FGD1)\) gives a feasible solution of the
   shared-cover LP \((STC1)\): replace each active pair \((T,U)\) by the
   materialized shared record \(c(T,U)\), use the capture domination in
   \((FSG1)\), and use
   \(P_{c(T,U)}\le\overline P_T(|U|)\) to dominate the price.  Hence
   \(\Phi_z^{\rm st}\le\Psi_z^{\rm gen,st}\).  The local closure and the
   expected statement \((FGD2)\) then follow from
   \cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-shared-cover}.

   The dual of \((FGD1)\) is
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Psi_z^{\rm gen,st}=\max
      & \displaystyle \sum_{s\in\mathcal S}y_s\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & 0\le y_s\le u_s,\\[0.6em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{s\in U}a_{T,s}y_s\le\overline P_T(K)
        \qquad
        (T\in\mathcal T,\ K\in\mathcal K_T,\ U\subseteq\mathcal S_T,\ |U|=K).
   \end{array}
      \tag{FGD5}
   \]
   The primal is finite and feasible by taking \(e_s=1\), so finite LP duality
   applies.  If \(\Psi_z^{\rm gen,st}>\Theta_z\), an optimal dual gives
   \((FGD3)\)--\((FGD4)\).  For fixed \(T\) and \(K\), the top \(K\) prefix in
   the order of \(a_{T,s}y_s\) maximizes the left side of \((FGD4)\), giving
   the equivalent top-prefix form.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fractional sponsor-tail low-cover closure]
   \label{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-low-cover-closure}
   Work in the no-generated-cover dual residual
   \((FGD3)\)--\((FGD4)\) of
   \cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-generated-cover-dichotomy}.  Let
   \(L\subseteq\mathcal S\) be nonempty, with \(K=|L|\).  Suppose \(L\) is
   assigned to generated templates by a map \(\kappa:L\to\mathcal T\) such
   that, for each nonempty part
   \[
      L_T=\{s\in L:\kappa(s)=T\},
      \qquad K_T=|L_T|,
      \tag{FLC1}
   \]
   one has \(K_T\in\mathcal K_T\), \(L_T\subseteq\mathcal S_T\), and certified
   lower degrees \(w_s\) satisfying
   \[
      0\le w_s\le a_{\kappa(s),s}y_s
      \qquad(s\in L).
      \tag{FLC2}
   \]
   Then every no-generated-cover residual obeys
   \[
      \sum_{s\in L}w_s
      \le
      \sum_{T:\,K_T>0}\overline P_T(K_T).
      \tag{FLC3}
   \]

   In particular, suppose \(w_s\ge\delta>0\) on \(L\), and all used templates
   satisfy the common price envelope
   \[
      \overline P_T(h)
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(Ah^\rho+\zeta h^{1+\rho}\right),
      \qquad 0<\rho<1 .
      \tag{FLC4}
   \]
   If the assignment uses \(J\) nonempty template parts, then
   \[
      \delta K
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(AJ^{1-\rho}K^\rho+\zeta K^{1+\rho}\right).
      \tag{FLC5}
   \]
   Consequently, when
   \[
      \delta>2\psi_\star\zeta K^\rho,
      \tag{FLC6}
   \]
   every surviving residual has
   \[
      J
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{\delta K^{1-\rho}}{2\psi_\star A}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{FLC7}
   \]
   When \(\zeta=0\), the same conclusion holds with \(2\psi_\star A\) replaced
   by \(\psi_\star A\) in \((FLC7)\).

   Thus any low-price generated cover of a dual-heavy star layer is already a
   positive shared-cover column.  A genuine residual must either be dominated
   by the storage term in \((FLC5)\), or have large generated-cover entropy.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For a nonempty part \(L_T\), \((FLC2)\) gives
   \[
      \sum_{s\in L_T}w_s
      \le
      \sum_{s\in L_T}a_{T,s}y_s .
   \]
   Since \(L_T\subseteq\mathcal S_T\) and \(K_T\in\mathcal K_T\), the subset
   test \((FGD4)\) gives
   \[
      \sum_{s\in L_T}a_{T,s}y_s\le\overline P_T(K_T).
   \]
   Summing over nonempty parts proves \((FLC3)\).

   If \(w_s\ge\delta\), then \(\delta K\le\sum_{s\in L}w_s\).  Under
   \((FLC4)\), Holder's inequality gives
   \[
      \sum_TK_T^\rho\le J^{1-\rho}K^\rho,
      \qquad
      \sum_TK_T^{1+\rho}\le K^{1+\rho}.
   \]
   Substituting in \((FLC3)\) proves \((FLC5)\).  If \((FLC6)\) holds, the
   storage term in \((FLC5)\) is less than \(\delta K/2\), so
   \[
      \frac{\delta K}{2}
      \le
      \psi_\star A J^{1-\rho}K^\rho ,
   \]
   which rearranges to \((FLC7)\).  When \(\zeta=0\), the storage term is
   absent and the same rearrangement starts from
   \(\delta K\le\psi_\star A J^{1-\rho}K^\rho\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Low-doubling fractional sponsor-tail screen]
   \label{cor:low-doubling-fractional-sponsor-tail-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-low-cover-closure}.  For a generated
   container family at scale \(0<\lambda\le1\), let
   \(N_{\rm gen}^{\rm st}(L,\delta,\lambda)\) be the least number of nonempty
   template parts in an assignment satisfying \((FLC1)\)--\((FLC2)\) with
   \(w_s\ge\delta\) on \(L\), and set it to \(\infty\) if no such assignment
   exists.  If \(N_{\rm gen}^{\rm st}(L,\delta,\lambda)=J<\infty\), then every
   no-generated-cover residual obeys
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(
         A J^{1-\rho}K^{\rho-1}
         +\zeta K^\rho
      \right).
      \tag{FLD1}
   \]
   In particular, if a certified low-doubling or list-decoded family gives
   \[
      N_{\rm gen}^{\rm st}(L,\delta,\lambda)
      \le C_{\rm st}\lambda^{-\Delta},
      \tag{FLD2}
   \]
   then a surviving residual must satisfy
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(
         A C_{\rm st}^{1-\rho}
         \lambda^{-\Delta(1-\rho)}K^{\rho-1}
         +\zeta K^\rho
      \right).
      \tag{FLD3}
   \]
   Hence any layer whose dual density violates \((FLD3)\) contains a generated
   top-prefix column improving the shared-cover LP.

   Equivalently, when \(\zeta=0\) and \(0<\lambda<1\), every surviving layer
   with positive numerator has generated dimension at least
   \[
      \Delta
      \ge
      \frac{
         \log\!\left(\delta K^{1-\rho}/(\psi_\star A)\right)
         -(1-\rho)\log C_{\rm st}
      }{
         (1-\rho)\log(1/\lambda)
      }.
      \tag{FLD4}
   \]
   With \(\zeta>0\), the same statement holds after replacing \(\delta\) by
   \(\delta-\psi_\star\zeta K^\rho\), when this quantity is positive.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-low-cover-closure} to an optimal
   assignment with \(J=N_{\rm gen}^{\rm st}(L,\delta,\lambda)\), and divide
   \((FLC5)\) by \(K\).  This proves \((FLD1)\).  Substituting the cover bound
   \((FLD2)\) gives \((FLD3)\).  If \((FLD3)\) is violated, the contrapositive
   of the same closure corollary gives a positive generated prefix, hence an
   improving shared-cover column by
   \cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-generated-prefix}.

   For \(\zeta=0\), rearrange \((FLD3)\) as
   \[
      \lambda^{-\Delta(1-\rho)}
      \ge
      \frac{\delta K^{1-\rho}}
           {\psi_\star A C_{\rm st}^{1-\rho}},
   \]
   and take logarithms.  With \(\zeta>0\), first subtract the storage term in
   \((FLD3)\), provided the resulting numerator is positive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fractional sponsor-tail entropy gives a packing witness]
   \label{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-packing-witness}
   Work in the no-generated-cover residual
   \((FGD3)\)--\((FGD4)\) of
   \cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-generated-cover-dichotomy}, and assume the
   common price envelope \((FLC4)\) for the generated templates used below.
   Let \(L\subseteq\mathcal S\) have size \(K>0\), and let
   \(d_{\rm gen}\) be any pseudometric on \(L\).  Fix a radius
   \(\Delta_{\rm gen}>0\) and a dual density floor \(\delta>0\).  Suppose that
   for every \(s_0\in L\), the ball
   \[
      B_{\rm gen}(s_0,\Delta_{\rm gen})
      =
      \{s\in L:d_{\rm gen}(s,s_0)\le\Delta_{\rm gen}\}
      \tag{FSP1}
   \]
   has a generated template copy \(T_{s_0}\in\mathcal T\) with
   \[
      B_{\rm gen}(s_0,\Delta_{\rm gen})\subseteq\mathcal S_{T_{s_0}},
      \qquad
      |B_{\rm gen}(s_0,\Delta_{\rm gen})|\in\mathcal K_{T_{s_0}},
      \tag{FSP2}
   \]
   and with certified current capture
   \[
      a_{T_{s_0},s}y_s\ge\delta
      \qquad
      (s\in B_{\rm gen}(s_0,\Delta_{\rm gen})).
      \tag{FSP3}
   \]
   If \(A>0\) and the layer is not storage-dominated,
   \[
      \delta>2\psi_\star\zeta K^\rho,
      \tag{FSP4}
   \]
   then every cover of \(L\) by certified balls
   \(B_{\rm gen}(s,\Delta_{\rm gen})\), \(s\in L\), has size at least
   \[
      \left(
         \frac{\delta K^{1-\rho}}{2\psi_\star A}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{FSP5}
   \]
   Consequently every maximal \(\Delta_{\rm gen}\)-separated subset
   \(E\subseteq L\) satisfies the same lower bound.  When \(\zeta=0\), the
   constant \(2\psi_\star A\) in \((FSP5)\) may be replaced by
   \(\psi_\star A\).

   Thus a fractional sponsor-tail residual that survives generated-cover
   search and is not already paid by the storage term contains a large packing
   in every certified generated metric.  This is the same geometric object used
   by the spherical and list-decoding entropy-energy screens.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(B_{\rm gen}(s_1,\Delta_{\rm gen}),\ldots,
   B_{\rm gen}(s_J,\Delta_{\rm gen})\) be any such certified-ball cover of
   \(L\).  Assign each \(s\in L\) to one covering ball.  By
   \((FSP2)\)--\((FSP3)\), this assignment satisfies
   \((FLC1)\)--\((FLC2)\) with \(w_s=\delta\).  Therefore
   \cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-low-cover-closure} applies.  Under
   \((FSP4)\), \((FLC7)\) gives the lower bound \((FSP5)\) for \(J\).

   If \(E\) is maximal \(\Delta_{\rm gen}\)-separated, then the balls
   \(B_{\rm gen}(s,\Delta_{\rm gen})\), \(s\in E\), cover \(L\); otherwise an
   uncovered point could be added to \(E\).  Applying the cover lower bound to
   this cover gives \((FSP5)\) for \(|E|\).  The sharper \(\zeta=0\) constant
   is inherited from \cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-low-cover-closure}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fractional sponsor-tail packing feeds the energy screen]
   \label{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-packing-energy-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-packing-witness}, and let
   \(E\subseteq L\) be a separated witness.  Suppose every \(s\in E\) has a
   representative \(x_s\in\mathbb S^{d-1}\).  This is the specialization of
   \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-packing-energy-screen} with
   \(\mathcal A=\mathcal S\).  Let \(U_G\) be a spherical,
   Gaussian-cap, code, or list-decoded bucket drawn from a law \(G\), and
   partition the ordered distinct pairs \(E_{\ne}^2\) into finitely many
   profiles \(\Pi_E\).  Assume each profile \(\pi\in\Pi_E\) has a certified
   pair-intersection energy
   \[
      \Pr_G[x_s,x_{s'}\in U_G]\le e^{-I_\pi}
      \qquad((s,s')\in\pi).
      \tag{FPE1}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      X_E(G)=\sum_{s\in E}\mathbf 1\{x_s\in U_G\}.
      \tag{FPE2}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \E_G X_E(G)^2
      \le
      \sum_{s\in E}\Pr_G[x_s\in U_G]
      +
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi_E}|\pi|e^{-I_\pi}.
      \tag{FPE3}
   \]
   In particular, if
   \[
      I_\pi\ge\log|\pi|+\Lambda
      \qquad(\pi\in\Pi_E),
      \tag{FPE4}
   \]
   then the distinct-pair contribution of the fractional sponsor-tail packing
   is at most
   \[
      |\Pi_E|e^{-\Lambda}.
      \tag{FPE5}
   \]
   Hence the no-cover fractional tail now has the same endpoint as the earlier
   sponsor-packing residual: either the spherical/list-decoding law pays the
   separated set by entropy-energy, or an energy-deficient profile supplies the
   high-correlation signal for the dense-star and shared-prefix verifiers.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Expanding the second moment gives
   \[
      \E_G X_E(G)^2
      =
      \sum_{s\in E}\Pr_G[x_s\in U_G]
      +
      \sum_{\substack{s,s'\in E\\s\ne s'}}
         \Pr_G[x_s,x_{s'}\in U_G].
   \]
   Summing the profile bounds \((FPE1)\) proves \((FPE3)\).  Under \((FPE4)\),
   each profile contributes at most \(e^{-\Lambda}\), giving \((FPE5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[High-correlation fractional-tail profiles return to prefixes]
   \label{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-high-correlation-return}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-packing-energy-screen}, and keep the
   fractional sponsor-tail dual \(y_s\).  This is the specialization of
   \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-high-correlation-return} with
   \(\mathcal A=\mathcal S\); the local notation below is retained because the
   following cap-star price-gap corollary uses the labels
   \((FHR1)\)--\((FHR14)\).  Fix one profile
   \(\pi\subseteq E_{\ne}^2\), assign nonnegative weights
   \(\omega_{s,s'}\) to its ordered pairs, and split
   \[
      \pi=\pi_{\rm lo}\dot\cup\pi_{\rm hi}.
   \]
   Suppose the low part has certified weight
   \[
      \sum_{(s,s')\in\pi_{\rm lo}}\omega_{s,s'}\le B_{\rm lo},
      \tag{FHR1}
   \]
   and every high edge has representative correlation at least
   \[
      \ip{x_s}{x_{s'}}\ge\underline\theta
      \qquad((s,s')\in\pi_{\rm hi})
      \tag{FHR2}
   \]
   for some \(-1<\underline\theta<1\).  Define
   \[
      M_s(s')=\omega_{s,s'}\mathbf 1_{\{(s,s')\in\pi_{\rm hi}\}},
      \qquad
      W_{\rm hi}=\sum_{s,s'\in E}M_s(s').
      \tag{FHR3}
   \]
   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), set \(J_\omega=1\).  Otherwise assume the positive
   values of \(M_s(s')\) lie in a certified dyadic range
   \([\omega_{\min},\omega_{\max}]\), put
   \[
      J_\omega=
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{\omega_{\max}}{\omega_{\min}}\right\rceil,
      \tag{FHR4}
   \]
   and define the high-correlation stars
   \[
      V_{s,t}=\{s'\in E:M_s(s')\ge t\},
      \qquad
      t\in\{\omega_{\min}2^j:0\le j<J_\omega\}.
      \tag{FHR5}
   \]
   Then every nonempty \(V_{s,t}\) has representatives in the cap ball
   \[
      x_{s'}\in B\!\left(x_s,\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)}\right)
      \qquad(s'\in V_{s,t}).
      \tag{FHR6}
   \]

   Now let \(\chi>0\).  For every nonempty \(V_{s,t}\), suppose preprocessing
   has a generated shared-record template \(T_{s,t}\) satisfying the
   materialization hypothesis \((FSG1)\), with
   \[
      V_{s,t}\subseteq\mathcal S_{T_{s,t}},
      \qquad
      h_{s,t}=|V_{s,t}|\in\mathcal K_{T_{s,t}},
      \tag{FHR7}
   \]
   and certified current dual capture
   \[
      a_{T_{s,t},s'}y_{s'}\ge\chi
      \qquad(s'\in V_{s,t}).
      \tag{FHR8}
   \]
   If, for some star,
   \[
      \chi h_{s,t}>\overline P_{T_{s,t}}(h_{s,t}),
      \tag{FHR9}
   \]
   then \(T_{s,t}\) contains an improving generated prefix for the fractional
   sponsor-tail shared-cover LP.  If no such improving prefix exists, then
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \frac2\chi
      \sum_{s\in E}\sum_t
         t\,\overline P_{T_{s,t}}(h_{s,t}),
      \tag{FHR10}
   \]
   and hence
   \[
      \sum_{(s,s')\in\pi}\omega_{s,s'}
      \le
      B_{\rm lo}
      +
      \frac2\chi
      \sum_{s\in E}\sum_t
         t\,\overline P_{T_{s,t}}(h_{s,t}).
      \tag{FHR11}
   \]

   In particular, if all used templates satisfy the common envelope
   \[
      \overline P_{T_{s,t}}(h)
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(Ah^\rho+\zeta h^{1+\rho}\right),
      \tag{FHR12}
   \]
   then every no-prefix residual satisfies
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \frac{2\psi_\star}{\chi}
      \sum_{s\in E}\sum_t
      t\left(Ah_{s,t}^{\rho}+\zeta h_{s,t}^{1+\rho}\right).
      \tag{FHR13}
   \]
   Thus an energy-deficient high-correlation fractional-tail profile either
   returns immediately as a positive generated shared-cover prefix, or it is
   paid by the integrated generated price of its dyadic cap stars.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(s'\in V_{s,t}\), then \(M_s(s')>0\), so \((s,s')\in\pi_{\rm hi}\).
   By \((FHR2)\),
   \[
      \|x_s-x_{s'}\|^2
      =
      2-2\ip{x_s}{x_{s'}}
      \le 2(1-\underline\theta),
   \]
   proving \((FHR6)\).

   Fix a nonempty star \(V_{s,t}\).  If \((FHR9)\) holds, then the top
   \(h_{s,t}\)-prefix of \(T_{s,t}\), ordered by \(a_{T_{s,t},u}y_u\), has
   total degree at least \(\chi h_{s,t}\), by \((FHR8)\).  This is larger than
   its certified price, so \cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-generated-prefix}
   gives an improving generated shared-cover column.  Therefore, in a
   no-prefix residual,
   \[
      \chi h_{s,t}\le\overline P_{T_{s,t}}(h_{s,t})
      \tag{FHR14}
   \]
   for every nonempty dyadic star.

   If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), then \((FHR10)\)--\((FHR11)\) are immediate.  Otherwise
   the same dyadic layer-cake estimate as in
   \cref{cor:sponsor-profile-star-signal} gives
   \[
      \frac12W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \sum_{s\in E}\sum_t t\,h_{s,t}.
   \]
   Multiplying \((FHR14)\) by \(t/\chi\) and summing gives \((FHR10)\).  Adding
   the low bound \((FHR1)\) proves \((FHR11)\), and substituting \((FHR12)\)
   proves \((FHR13)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fractional-tail cap stars have a price gap]
   \label{cor:fractional-tail-cap-star-price-gap}
   Work in the no-prefix setting of
   \cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-high-correlation-return}, and assume the
   common envelope \((FHR12)\).  This is the specialization of
   \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-cap-star-storage-split} with
   \(\mathcal A=\mathcal S\); the local notation below is retained because
   \cref{cor:fractional-tail-cap-star-storage-interface} uses the labels
   \((FTC1)\)--\((FTC10)\).  Every nonempty dyadic cap star satisfies
   \[
      \chi
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(Ah_{s,t}^{\rho-1}
      +\zeta h_{s,t}^{\rho}\right).
      \tag{FTC1}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      H_-^{\rm cap}
      =
      \left(\frac{2\psi_\star A}{\chi}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \tag{FTC2}
   \]
   with \(H_-^{\rm cap}=0\) when \(A=0\).  If \(\zeta>0\), also put
   \[
      H_+^{\rm cap}
      =
      \left(\frac{\chi}{2\psi_\star\zeta}\right)^{1/\rho}.
      \tag{FTC3}
   \]
   Then every nonempty cap star obeys
   \[
      h_{s,t}\le H_-^{\rm cap}
      \qquad\text{or}\qquad
      \bigl(\zeta>0\text{ and }h_{s,t}\ge H_+^{\rm cap}\bigr).
      \tag{FTC4}
   \]
   Equivalently, any cap star with
   \[
      h_{s,t}>H_-^{\rm cap}
      \quad\text{and, when }\zeta>0,\quad
      h_{s,t}<H_+^{\rm cap}
      \tag{FTC5}
   \]
   is itself an improving generated shared-cover prefix.

   If \(\zeta>0\) and the forbidden interval is empty, then
   \[
      \chi\le 2\psi_\star A^\rho\zeta^{1-\rho}.
      \tag{FTC6}
   \]
   Thus, unless the balanced scalar price is already at the capture scale, the
   no-prefix high-correlation return has no medium cap stars.

   Finally, let \(\mathcal S_{\rm cap}\) be the set of nonempty dyadic cap
   stars in the storage-dominated alternative
   \(h_{s,t}\ge H_+^{\rm cap}\), and define
   \[
      u_{s,t}^{\rm cap}
      =
      \psi_\star\zeta\,t\,h_{s,t}^{1+\rho}
      \qquad((s,t)\in\mathcal S_{\rm cap}).
      \tag{FTC7}
   \]
   If \(\zeta=0\), interpret \(\mathcal S_{\rm cap}=\emptyset\).  Then every
   no-prefix residual satisfies
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      2|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-^{\rm cap}
      +
      \frac4\chi
      \sum_{(s,t)\in\mathcal S_{\rm cap}}u_{s,t}^{\rm cap}.
      \tag{FTC8}
   \]
   Consequently, the high-correlation fractional-tail return leaves only an
   explicit bounded-cardinality tail plus another integrated fractional storage
   tail; it does not create a new medium-scale branching obstruction.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Combining the no-prefix inequality \((FHR14)\) with the common envelope
   \((FHR12)\), and dividing by \(h_{s,t}>0\), gives \((FTC1)\).
   If \(h_{s,t}>H_-^{\rm cap}\), then
   \[
      \psi_\star A h_{s,t}^{\rho-1}<\frac\chi2 .
   \]
   Hence \((FTC1)\) can hold only if
   \(\psi_\star\zeta h_{s,t}^{\rho}\ge\chi/2\).  When \(\zeta=0\) this is
   impossible, and when \(\zeta>0\) it is exactly
   \(h_{s,t}\ge H_+^{\rm cap}\).  This proves \((FTC4)\), while \((FTC5)\) is
   the contrapositive combined with
   \cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-high-correlation-return}.

   If \(\zeta>0\) and \(H_-^{\rm cap}\ge H_+^{\rm cap}\), then
   \[
      \left(\frac{2\psi_\star A}{\chi}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \ge
      \left(\frac{\chi}{2\psi_\star\zeta}\right)^{1/\rho}.
   \]
   Raising to \(\rho(1-\rho)\) and rearranging gives \((FTC6)\).

   It remains to prove the tail bound.  If \(W_{\rm hi}=0\), the claim is
   immediate.  Otherwise the dyadic layer-cake estimate gives
   \[
      \frac12W_{\rm hi}
      \le
      \sum_{s\in E}\sum_t t\,h_{s,t}.
      \tag{FTC9}
   \]
   Split the sum into the bounded side \(h_{s,t}\le H_-^{\rm cap}\) and the
   storage-dominated side.  The bounded side contributes at most
   \(|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-^{\rm cap}\).  For a storage-dominated star,
   the definition of \(H_+^{\rm cap}\) gives
   \[
      \chi\le2\psi_\star\zeta h_{s,t}^{\rho},
   \]
   and therefore
   \[
      t\,h_{s,t}
      \le
      \frac2\chi\psi_\star\zeta\,t\,h_{s,t}^{1+\rho}
      =
      \frac2\chi u_{s,t}^{\rm cap}.
      \tag{FTC10}
   \]
   Substituting these two estimates in \((FTC9)\) proves \((FTC8)\).  When
   \(\zeta=0\), there is no storage-dominated side and the same argument gives
   \((FTC8)\) with an empty sum.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Returned cap stars are ordinary fractional storage]
   \label{cor:fractional-tail-cap-star-storage-interface}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:fractional-tail-cap-star-price-gap}, and consider the
   storage-dominated cap-star family \(\mathcal S_{\rm cap}\) from \((FTC7)\).
   For \(r=(s,t)\in\mathcal S_{\rm cap}\), write
   \[
      A_r^{\rm cap}=V_{s,t},\qquad
      h_r=|A_r^{\rm cap}|=h_{s,t},\qquad
      \psi_r^{\rm cap}=t\psi_\star\zeta .
      \tag{FCS1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      u_r^{\rm cap}
      =
      \psi_r^{\rm cap}h_r^{1+\rho}
      =
      \psi_\star\zeta\,t\,h_{s,t}^{1+\rho}
      \tag{FCS2}
   \]
   is exactly the storage price of the returned cap-star child after absorbing
   the dyadic intensity into its price factor.

   Let \(\mathcal R^{\rm cap}\) be any finite family of candidate shared
   records for these cap-star children.  A record \(c\in\mathcal R^{\rm cap}\)
   has one-time recursive storage price \(P_c\ge0\) and certified cover
   coefficients \(0\le g_{c,r}\le1\) for \(r\in\mathcal S_{\rm cap}\).
   Define
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Phi^{\rm cap}=\min
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{r\in\mathcal S_{\rm cap}}u_r^{\rm cap}e_r
        +\sum_{c\in\mathcal R^{\rm cap}}P_c\lambda_c\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        e_r+\sum_{c\in\mathcal R^{\rm cap}}\lambda_c g_{c,r}\ge1
        \qquad(r\in\mathcal S_{\rm cap}),\\[0.8em]
      & e_r\ge0,\qquad \lambda_c\ge0 .
   \end{array}
      \tag{FCS3}
   \]
   Its dual is
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Phi^{\rm cap}=\max
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{r\in\mathcal S_{\rm cap}}y_r\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & 0\le y_r\le u_r^{\rm cap}
        \qquad(r\in\mathcal S_{\rm cap}),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{r\in\mathcal S_{\rm cap}}g_{c,r}y_r\le P_c
        \qquad(c\in\mathcal R^{\rm cap}).
   \end{array}
      \tag{FCS4}
   \]
   Equations \((FCS3)\)--\((FCS4)\) are the specialization of
   \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-shared-cover-compiler} with
   \(\mathcal A=\mathcal S_{\rm cap}\) and
   \(u_r=u_r^{\rm cap}\).

   Thus the cap-star return has exactly the same shared-cover interface as the
   fractional sponsor tail: a feasible solution of \((FCS3)\) replaces
   individual returned cap-star children by residual fractional copies and
   shared records, while a failed cover exposes one dual weighting \(y_r\) that
   blocks every retained shared record.

   In particular, for any desired cap-tail allowance \(B_{\rm cap}\) and any
   nonnegative fixed overhead \(\Gamma\), the storage-dominated part of
   \((FTC8)\) is within that allowance whenever
   \[
      \Gamma+\Phi^{\rm cap}\le\frac\chi4 B_{\rm cap}
      \tag{FCS5}
   \]
   pointwise, or after averaging over the build seed in the corresponding
   expected form.  Hence the high-correlation return contributes only the
   explicit bounded tail
   \(2|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-^{\rm cap}\) plus an ordinary
   shared-canonical fractional storage-tail problem.  It is not a new
   cap-specific recursion or integer materialization branch.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The identity \((FCS2)\) is the definition \((FTC7)\) with the factor
   \(t\psi_\star\zeta\) renamed as the child price factor.  Thus each returned
   cap star has the standard price form
   \(\psi_r^{\rm cap}|A_r^{\rm cap}|^{1+\rho}\), and may be submitted to the
   same price-weighted witness and occurrence-discounted storage certificates
   as the storage-dominated sponsor stars in
   \cref{cor:storage-dominated-sponsor-stars-fractional-tail}.

   The program \((FCS3)\) is finite and feasible by taking \(e_r=1\).  Finite
   LP duality gives \((FCS4)\).  A feasible primal solution represents each
   cap-star child \(r\) by an \(e_r\)-fractional residual copy and by the shared
   records covering it; the coverage constraints ensure that the original
   cap-star child is fully represented.  Since the cited storage certificates
   are linear in fractional copies and charge a shared record once through
   \(P_c\), the objective \(\Phi^{\rm cap}\) is a valid shared-canonical
   replacement for the raw sum
   \(\sum_{r\in\mathcal S_{\rm cap}}u_r^{\rm cap}\).

   Multiplying this replacement by the coefficient \(4/\chi\) in \((FTC8)\)
   shows that \((FCS5)\) pays the storage-dominated cap-tail contribution
   inside \(B_{\rm cap}\), with \(\Gamma\) accounting for fixed metadata or
   shared-record overhead exactly as in the earlier distinct-storage
   certificates.  The dual statement is the usual contrapositive of finite LP
   duality.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Certified star-panel separator]
   \label{lem:certified-star-panel-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:star-prefix-weak-type-residual}, and assume
   each available cardinality family \(\mathcal K_x\) is \(b_x\)-dense from
   below.  A finite star panel consists of records \(i\in I\), each with a
   center \(x_i\in\mathcal X\), a level \(\delta_i>0\), a nonnegative weight
   \(\lambda_i\), and one-sided certificates \(X_i,K_i\) satisfying
   \[
      0\le X_i\le \delta_i h_i,
      \qquad
      h_i\le K_i,
      \qquad
      h_i=\left|\{p\in W_{x_i}:d_{x_i}(p)\ge\delta_i\}\right|.
      \tag{STP1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_{i\in I}\lambda_iX_i
      >
      \sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i\psi_{x_i}
      \left(
         b_{x_i}^{1-\rho_{x_i}}A_{x_i}K_i^{\rho_{x_i}}
         +\sigma K_i^{1+\rho_{x_i}}
      \right),
      \tag{STP2}
   \]
   then some star prefix has positive reduced gain.

   Conversely, if no star prefix has positive reduced gain, then every finite
   certified star panel satisfies the reverse inequality
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_iX_i
      \le
      \sum_i\lambda_i\psi_{x_i}
      \left(
         b_{x_i}^{1-\rho_{x_i}}A_{x_i}K_i^{\rho_{x_i}}
         +\sigma K_i^{1+\rho_{x_i}}
      \right).
      \tag{STP3}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose no star prefix has positive reduced gain.  By
   \cref{lem:star-prefix-weak-type-residual}, each nonempty superlevel obeys
   \[
      \delta_i h_i
      \le
      \psi_{x_i}
      \left(
         b_{x_i}^{1-\rho_{x_i}}A_{x_i}h_i^{\rho_{x_i}}
         +\sigma h_i^{1+\rho_{x_i}}
      \right).
   \]
   Since \(0<\rho_{x_i}<1\) and \(h_i\le K_i\), the right hand side is at most
   the corresponding \(K_i\)-bound in \((STP3)\).  Together with
   \(X_i\le\delta_i h_i\), this proves \((STP3)\).  Therefore any panel
   satisfying the strict reverse inequality \((STP2)\) contradicts the
   no-positive-prefix hypothesis, so some star prefix has positive reduced
   gain.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Paid pair-star panel certificate]
   \label{cor:paid-pair-star-panel-certificate}
   In the setting of \cref{cor:pair-star-weak-type-normal-form}, suppose a
   build-time reporter returns finitely many pair-star records
   \((x_i,t_i)\), weights \(\lambda_i\ge0\), lower paid-mass certificates
   \(X_i\), and upper size certificates \(K_i\) such that
   \[
      0\le X_i\le
      \sum_{p\in U_{x_i,t_i}}
      \sum_{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
         \alpha_{p,q}a_{x_i}(q),
      \qquad
      |U_{x_i,t_i}|\le K_i .
      \tag{PPC1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_iX_i
      >
      \sum_i\lambda_i\psi_\star
      \left(
         A_{x_i}K_i^{\rho_\star}
         +\sigma K_i^{1+\rho_\star}
      \right),
      \tag{PPC2}
   \]
   then the dense-filter column generator exposes a positive-gain
   smaller-radius prefix.  If no such prefix exists, then every reported
   pair-star panel satisfies the reverse of \((PPC2)\).

   Thus high-correlation incidence becomes algorithmically relevant only after
   it is converted into certified paid mass \(X_i\).  The geometric reporter may
   over-report sizes through \(K_i\), but the final retained object remains the
   exact best paid prefix verified by the finite filter-cover dual.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose no smaller-radius prefix has positive reduced gain.  By
   \cref{cor:pair-star-weak-type-normal-form}, every reported pair-star
   \(U_{x_i,t_i}\) satisfies \((PWN3)\).  Combining \((PWN3)\) with
   \(X_i\le\sum_{p\in U_{x_i,t_i}}d_{x_i}(p)\) and
   \(|U_{x_i,t_i}|\le K_i\) gives
   \[
      X_i
      \le
      \psi_\star
      \left(
         A_{x_i}K_i^{\rho_\star}
         +\sigma K_i^{1+\rho_\star}
      \right).
   \]
   Multiplying by \(\lambda_i\) and summing gives the reverse of \((PPC2)\).
   Therefore any strict violation \((PPC2)\) forces the existence of a
   positive-gain prefix.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Spherical-or-star-panel local cover criterion]
   \label{cor:spherical-star-panel-local-cover}
   Work in a finite local filter-cover instance with resident set \(P\),
   query constraints \(\mathcal Q\), near-pair demands \(\mathcal N\), uniform
   query budget \(L\), and storage budget \(S\).  Suppose the filter universe
   contains the spherical buckets from
   \cref{lem:weighted-spherical-reduced-gain} and, for every pair-star center
   that may be reported, the smaller-radius paid prefixes used in
   \cref{cor:paid-pair-star-panel-certificate}.  Assume the spherical bucket law
   satisfies \((WS1)\)--\((WS6)\).

   Suppose that every nonnegative dual price system \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\)
   with surplus
   \[
      A_\alpha>L\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}\tau_q+\sigma S
      \tag{SPL1}
   \]
   and nonpositive reduced gain on every spherical bucket admits a certified
   paid pair-star panel satisfying \((PPC2)\).  Then the finite filter-cover LP
   \((\mathsf{FC}_{\mathcal N})\) over this universe is feasible with budgets
   \(L,S\).

   Equivalently, under \((WS1)\)--\((WS6)\), the remaining geometric theorem may
   be stated as follows: every spherical residual dual, necessarily satisfying
   the high-correlation obstruction \((WS8)\), must generate a certified
   pair-star panel whose paid mass beats its recursive query/storage Renyi cost.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose the finite cover LP were infeasible.  By
   \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual}, there is a nonnegative dual price system
   satisfying \((SPL1)\) and having nonpositive reduced gain on every column in
   the universe.  In particular, every spherical bucket has nonpositive gain.
   By the assumed star-panel separator, this dual admits a certified paid
   pair-star panel satisfying \((PPC2)\).  Then
   \cref{cor:paid-pair-star-panel-certificate} exposes a positive-gain
   smaller-radius prefix, which is a column of the universe.  This contradicts
   nonpositive gain on every column.  Hence the finite cover LP is feasible.

   The final reformulation follows because, for any such surplus dual with no
   positive spherical bucket, \cref{lem:weighted-spherical-reduced-gain} gives
   the high-correlation alternative \((WS8)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Hit-weighted star panels feed paid prefixes]
   \label{cor:hit-weighted-star-panel-prefix}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{asm:paid-atomized-prefix-separator}, and assume that the available
   cardinalities of every reported container include all sizes.  Fix a
   nonnegative paid price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\).  Suppose a reporter returns finitely many records
   \(i\), each consisting of a certified container \(W_i\in\mathcal W\), a set
   \(U_i\subseteq W_i\), fractional query weights \(0\le y_i(q)\le1\), a
   multiplicity \(\lambda_i\ge0\), a lower paid-mass certificate \(X_i\), and an
   upper size certificate \(K_i\), such that
   \[
      0\le X_i\le
      \sum_{p\in U_i}\sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      y_i(q)\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
      \qquad
      |U_i|\le K_i .
      \tag{HSP1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_iX_i
      >
      \sum_i\lambda_i\psi_{W_i}
      \left(
         K_i^{\rho_{W_i}}\sum_q\tau_qy_i(q)
         +\sigma K_i^{1+\rho_{W_i}}
      \right),
      \tag{HSP2}
   \]
   then an available paid prefix has positive repair reduced gain.  Therefore,
   if every paid dual satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) admits such a certified
   hit-weighted star panel, the primitive hit-kernel cover is feasible by
   \cref{cor:paid-prefix-hit-kernel-cover}.

   In particular, \((HSP2)\) is the hit-kernel analogue of \((PPC2)\).  The
   reporter may be a range reporter, additive-quantization decoder, or
   list-decoding panel; the retained object is still the exact Boolean
   query-layer top prefix supplied by the paid-prefix verifier.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose no available paid prefix has positive repair reduced gain.  By
   \cref{cor:weighted-atomized-prefix-envelope}, for every reported \(i\), every
   fractional query weighting, and every cardinality \(h\le |W_i|\),
   \[
      D_{W_i,y_i}^{\gamma}(h)
      \le
      \psi_{W_i}
      \left(
         h^{\rho_{W_i}}\sum_q\tau_qy_i(q)
         +\sigma h^{1+\rho_{W_i}}
      \right).
   \]
   Put \(h_i=|U_i|\).  If \(h_i=0\), then \((HSP1)\) gives \(X_i=0\).  Otherwise
   the top-\(h_i\) paid-degree sum in \(W_i\) dominates the paid mass of \(U_i\),
   so \((HSP1)\) gives
   \[
      X_i\le D_{W_i,y_i}^{\gamma}(h_i).
   \]
   Since \(h_i\le K_i\) and \(0\le\rho_{W_i}\le1\), this is at most the
   corresponding right hand side with \(K_i\) in place of \(h_i\).  Thus the
   same upper bound also holds in the empty case.  Multiplying by
   \(\lambda_i\) and summing gives the reverse of \((HSP2)\), a contradiction.
   Hence some available paid prefix has positive repair reduced gain.

   If every surplus paid dual admits such a panel, then every price system
   satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) admits a positive paid prefix.  This is
   exactly the paid atomized-prefix separator condition, and
   \cref{cor:paid-prefix-hit-kernel-cover} gives the primitive hit-kernel cover.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Guarded star-panel reporter closes the local cover]
   \label{cor:guarded-star-panel-local-cover}
   Work in the local setting of
   \cref{cor:guarded-normalized-residual-segment}.  Assume the finite core
   universe contains the primitive singleton slice cores \(V_{z,q}\) with their
   certified prices \(T_{z,q},S_{z,q}\), and contains the paid-prefix cores used
   by every reported star container, with all cardinalities in each such
   container available.
   Let \(a_q=\Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[\chi_Z(q)=1]\).  Suppose the following reporter
   theorem holds.

   For every \(\kappa\in[1,\pi_1^{-1}]\) and every nonnegative price system
   \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}=1,
      \qquad
      L\sum_q\tau_q+\sigma S<\kappa,
      \tag{GSP1}
   \]
   \[
      \sum_q\tau_qa_q|H(q)|>\frac{\pi_1\kappa}{2},
      \tag{GSP2}
   \]
   and the primitive singleton constraints
   \[
      A_{z,q}^{\gamma}
      :=
      \sum_{\substack{p:(p,q)\in\mathcal N\\ p\in V_{z,q}}}
      \gamma_{p,q}
      \le
      T_{z,q}\tau_q+\sigma S_{z,q}
      \qquad(z,q),
      \tag{GSP3}
   \]
   the reporter returns a certified hit-weighted star panel satisfying
   \((HSP1)\)--\((HSP2)\).  Then the finite local filter-cover LP is feasible.

   Thus the remaining star-panel theorem need only be proved on the residuals
   that have already survived the spherical reduced-gain test: unit primitive
   hit mass, below-budget normalized price, large activation-weighted
   high-correlation guard mass, and no profitable primitive singleton slice.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose the local cover were infeasible.  By
   \cref{cor:guarded-normalized-residual-segment}, there are
   \(\kappa\in[1,\pi_1^{-1}]\), normalized prices
   \((\bar\tau,\bar\sigma)\), and a segment of nonnegative potentials
   \(\bar\gamma^\theta\), \(0\le\theta\le1\), satisfying \((GNR1)\)--\((GNR4)\).
   Fix any \(\theta\) and put
   \[
      \gamma=\bar\gamma^\theta,\qquad
      \tau=\bar\tau,\qquad
      \sigma=\bar\sigma .
   \]
   Then \((GNR1)\), \((GNR2)\), and \((GNR4)\) are exactly
   \((GSP1)\)--\((GSP2)\).

   It remains to check \((GSP3)\).  Since the primitive singleton slice core
   \(V_{z,q}\) is in the finite universe, \((GNR3)\) applied to that core gives
   \[
      \sum_{q'\in\mathcal Q}
      \bigl(a_{V_{z,q}}^\gamma(q')-T_{z,q}\tau_{q'}\bigr)_+
      \le
      \sigma S_{z,q}.
   \]
   The \(q\)-term alone is therefore at most \(\sigma S_{z,q}\), and
   \(a_{V_{z,q}}^\gamma(q)\ge A_{z,q}^{\gamma}\).  Hence
   \(A_{z,q}^{\gamma}\le T_{z,q}\tau_q+\sigma S_{z,q}\), proving
   \((GSP3)\).

   The reporter hypothesis now supplies a hit-weighted star panel satisfying
   \((HSP1)\)--\((HSP2)\).  The singleton constraints \((GSP3)\) are precisely
   \((APC1)\), and \((GSP1)\) with \(\kappa\le\pi_1^{-1}\) gives
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      =
      1
      >
      \pi_1\left(L\sum_q\tau_q+\sigma S\right),
   \]
   which is \((APC2)\).  By
   \cref{cor:hit-weighted-star-panel-prefix}, an available paid prefix has
   positive hit-weighted repair reduced gain.  For the same prefix \(U\) and
   Boolean query side \(Q'\), the one-potential support
   \(a_U^\gamma(q)\) dominates the hit-weighted support
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{p\in U\\(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
   \]
   because \(0\le r_{p,q}\le1\).  Thus the same prefix violates the
   one-potential hinge envelope \((GNR3)\), contradicting the residual
   certificate.  Therefore the local cover LP is feasible.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Guarded no-star residual envelope]
   \label{cor:guarded-no-star-residual-envelope}
   Work with one price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \((GSP1)\)--\((GSP3)\), and let \(\mathcal W_\star\) be the certified
   star-container family available to the reporter.  For \(W\in\mathcal W_\star\)
   and fractional query weights \(0\le y_q\le1\), define the hit-weighted degree
   \[
      d_{W,y}^{\gamma}(p)
      =
      \sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      \qquad(p\in W),
      \tag{GNE0}
   \]
   and the superlevel
   \[
      H_{W,\delta}(y)=\{p\in W:d_{W,y}^{\gamma}(p)\ge\delta\},
      \qquad h_{W,\delta}(y)=|H_{W,\delta}(y)|.
   \]
   Suppose no certified hit-weighted star panel over \(\mathcal W_\star\)
   satisfies \((HSP1)\)--\((HSP2)\).  Then every \(W\in\mathcal W_\star\), every
   \(0\le y\le1\), and every \(\delta>0\) with
   \(h=h_{W,\delta}(y)>0\) satisfy
   \[
      \delta h
      \le
      \psi_W
      \left(
         h^{\rho_W}\sum_q\tau_qy_q+\sigma h^{1+\rho_W}
      \right).
      \tag{GNE1}
   \]
   More generally, for any finite reported level panel
   \((W_i,y_i,\delta_i,\lambda_i)_i\), after discarding empty levels and writing
   \(h_i=h_{W_i,\delta_i}(y_i)>0\), one has
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_i\delta_i h_i
      \le
      \sum_i\lambda_i\psi_{W_i}
      \left(
         h_i^{\rho_{W_i}}\sum_q\tau_qy_i(q)
         +\sigma h_i^{1+\rho_{W_i}}
      \right).
      \tag{GNE2}
   \]

   If \(0<\rho_W<1\), the pointwise envelope implies the weak-type alternatives
   of \cref{lem:paid-prefix-weak-type} with
   \(A_y=\sum_q\tau_qy_q\), \(\rho=\rho_W\), and \(\psi=\psi_W\).  Thus any
   counterexample to the guarded star-panel theorem must simultaneously satisfy
   the large guard co-load \((GSP2)\) and the no-star weak-type envelope
   \((GNE1)\) for every certified smaller-radius star container.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((GNE2)\) failed, restrict to the nonempty reported levels and submit the
   panel with
   \[
      U_i=H_{W_i,\delta_i}(y_i),\qquad
      X_i=\delta_i h_i,\qquad
      K_i=h_i .
   \]
   For each \(i\),
   \[
      X_i
      =
      \delta_i h_i
      \le
      \sum_{p\in H_{W_i,\delta_i}(y_i)}
      d_{W_i,y_i}^{\gamma}(p),
   \]
   so \((HSP1)\) holds.  The strict failure of \((GNE2)\) is exactly
   \((HSP2)\), contradicting the no-panel hypothesis.  Hence \((GNE2)\) holds.
   The pointwise statement \((GNE1)\) is the single-level case.

   The weak-type alternatives follow by applying
   \cref{lem:paid-prefix-weak-type} to the displayed envelope, or directly by
   the same elementary rearrangement used in its proof.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Guard-shadow mass reporter]
   \label{cor:guard-shadow-mass-reporter}
   Work with one price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \((GSP1)\)--\((GSP3)\).  Fix a certified star container
   \(W\in\mathcal W_\star\), fractional query weights \(0\le y_q\le1\), and
   numbers \(K\ge1\), \(V>0\) such that
   \[
      |W|\le K,
      \qquad
      V\le
      \sum_{p\in W}d_{W,y}^{\gamma}(p).
      \tag{GSM1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      V
      >
      \psi_W
      \left(
         K^{\rho_W}\sum_q\tau_qy_q+\sigma K^{1+\rho_W}
      \right),
      \tag{GSM2}
   \]
   then there is a certified hit-weighted star panel over \(W\) satisfying
   \((HSP1)\)--\((HSP2)\).  Consequently the guarded star-panel reporter
   hypothesis of \cref{cor:guarded-star-panel-local-cover} holds for this
   residual once such a certificate can be produced for every residual price
   system.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Submit the one-record panel with container \(W\), query weights \(y\), update
   side \(U=W\), lower certificate \(X=V\), size certificate \(K_i=K\), and
   multiplicity one.  The certificates in \((GSM1)\) are exactly \((HSP1)\),
   and \((GSM2)\) is exactly the strict surplus inequality \((HSP2)\).  Thus
   this is the required hit-weighted star panel.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Guard-to-shadow transport]
   \label{def:guard-shadow-transport}
   Fix a guarded residual as in \((GSP1)\)--\((GSP3)\), query weights
   \(0\le y_q\le1\), witness sets \(G(q)\subseteq H(q)\), and a certified star
   container \(W\).  A \(C\)-congested guard-to-shadow transport of mass \(M\)
   from the raw guard incidences into \(W\) consists of numbers
   \[
      \pi_{q,x,p}\ge0
      \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q,\ x\in G(q),\ p\in W)
   \]
   and shipped amounts \(0\le s_{q,x}\le1\) such that
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{p\in W:\\(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}\pi_{q,x,p}
      =
      s_{q,x}
      \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q,\ x\in G(q)),
      \tag{GST1}
   \]
   \[
      M=
      \sum_q\tau_qy_q\sum_{x\in G(q)}s_{q,x},
      \tag{GST2}
   \]
   and, for every \(p\in W\),
   \[
      \sum_q\tau_qy_q\sum_{x\in G(q)}\pi_{q,x,p}
      \le
      C\,d_{W,y}^{\gamma}(p).
      \tag{GST3}
   \]
   The weighted-unit case has \(s_{q,x}=1\) for every incidence with
   \(\tau_qy_q>0\); zero-price incidences carry no mass.
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Guard-shadow transport reporter]
   \label{cor:guard-shadow-transport-reporter}
   In the setting of \cref{def:guard-shadow-transport}, suppose
   \(|W|\le K\) and a \(C\)-congested transport of mass \(M>0\) enters \(W\).
   If
   \[
      \frac{M}{C}
      >
      \psi_W
      \left(
         K^{\rho_W}\sum_q\tau_qy_q+\sigma K^{1+\rho_W}
      \right),
      \tag{GST4}
   \]
   then the guarded residual has a certified hit-weighted star panel satisfying
   \((HSP1)\)--\((HSP2)\).

   Conversely, if no such panel exists, every guard-to-shadow transport into
   every certified container satisfies the reverse of \((GST4)\).  In
   particular, with \(y_q=a_q\) and \(G(q)=H(q)\), any weighted-unit transport
   has
   \[
      M=\sum_q\tau_qa_q|H(q)|,
   \]
   so \((GSP2)\) gives \(M>\pi_1\kappa/2\).  Thus a surviving no-star residual
   can only exist if this large guard co-load cannot be transported into any
   affordable smaller-radius star container with bounded congestion.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Summing \((GST3)\) over \(p\in W\) and using \((GST1)\)--\((GST2)\) gives
   \[
      M
      \le
      C\sum_{p\in W}d_{W,y}^{\gamma}(p).
   \]
   Hence \(V=M/C\) satisfies \((GSM1)\).  The inequality \((GST4)\) is exactly
   \((GSM2)\) for this value of \(V\), so
   \cref{cor:guard-shadow-mass-reporter} gives the hit-weighted star panel.
   The converse is the contrapositive.  The final weighted-unit statement is
   the specialization of \((GST2)\) with \(y_q=a_q\), \(G(q)=H(q)\), and all
   positive-price incidences shipped.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Guard-shadow cut normal form]
   \label{lem:guard-shadow-cut-normal-form}
   Work in the setting of \cref{def:guard-shadow-transport}.  Put
   \[
      b_q=\tau_qy_q|G(q)|,
      \qquad
      B_{\rm tot}=\sum_qb_q,
   \]
   and, for \(Y\subseteq\mathcal Q\),
   \[
      N_W(Y)=\{p\in W:\exists q\in Y,\ (p,q)\in\mathcal N\},
      \qquad
      D_{W,y}^{\gamma}(Y)=\sum_{p\in N_W(Y)}d_{W,y}^{\gamma}(p).
   \]
   Let \(\Phi_C(W;y,G)\) be the largest mass \(M\) for which a
   \(C\)-congested guard-to-shadow transport into \(W\) exists.  Then
   \[
      \Phi_C(W;y,G)
      =
      \min_{Y\subseteq\mathcal Q}
      \left\{
         \sum_{q\notin Y}b_q
         +C D_{W,y}^{\gamma}(Y)
      \right\}
      =
      B_{\rm tot}
      -
      \max_{Y\subseteq\mathcal Q}
      \left\{
         \sum_{q\in Y}b_q-CD_{W,y}^{\gamma}(Y)
      \right\}.
      \tag{GSC1}
   \]
   Consequently, for \(0\le M_0\le B_{\rm tot}\), a transport of mass at least
   \(M_0\) exists if and only if every \(Y\subseteq\mathcal Q\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Y}b_q
      \le
      C D_{W,y}^{\gamma}(Y)+B_{\rm tot}-M_0 .
      \tag{GSC2}
   \]
   In particular, a weighted-unit transport of all positive-price guard
   incidences exists if and only if
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Y}b_q\le C D_{W,y}^{\gamma}(Y)
      \qquad(Y\subseteq\mathcal Q).
      \tag{GSC3}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Aggregate the transport variables by query and point.  A transport of mass
   \(M\) is equivalent to nonnegative variables \(f_{q,p}\), supported on
   \(p\in W\) with \((p,q)\in\mathcal N\), such that
   \[
      \sum_{p\in N_W(\{q\})}f_{q,p}\le b_q,
      \qquad
      \sum_{\substack{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}f_{q,p}
      \le C d_{W,y}^{\gamma}(p),
      \qquad
      \sum_{q,p}f_{q,p}=M .
   \]
   The equivalence follows by setting
   \(f_{q,p}=\tau_qy_q\sum_{x\in G(q)}\pi_{q,x,p}\).  Conversely, if
   \(\tau_qy_q>0\), distribute the normalized amounts
   \(f_{q,p}/(\tau_qy_q)\) fractionally among the \(|G(q)|\) identical
   incidences of capacity one; queries with \(\tau_qy_q=0\) carry no mass.

   Thus \(\Phi_C(W;y,G)\) is the optimum of a finite fractional flow LP.  Its
   dual is
   \[
      \min
      \left\{
         \sum_qb_qu_q+C\sum_{p\in W}d_{W,y}^{\gamma}(p)v_p:
         u_q+v_p\ge1\ \text{whenever }(p,q)\in\mathcal N,\quad
         u_q,v_p\ge0
      \right\}.
      \tag{GSC4}
   \]
   Strong duality holds because the finite primal is feasible and bounded.

   For any \(Y\subseteq\mathcal Q\), the Boolean dual
   \[
      u_q=\mathbf 1\{q\notin Y\},
      \qquad
      v_p=\mathbf 1\{p\in N_W(Y)\}
   \]
   is feasible and has value
   \(\sum_{q\notin Y}b_q+CD_{W,y}^{\gamma}(Y)\).

   Conversely, take any feasible dual \((u,v)\) and truncate it to
   \(0\le u_q,v_p\le1\), which cannot increase the objective or destroy the
   constraints.  For \(t\in(0,1]\), let
   \[
      Y_t=\{q:u_q<t\},
      \qquad
      P_t=\{p:v_p\ge1-t\}.
   \]
   If \(q\in Y_t\) and \((p,q)\in\mathcal N\), then
   \(v_p\ge1-u_q>1-t\), so \(N_W(Y_t)\subseteq P_t\).  Hence
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \sum_qb_qu_q+C\sum_pd_{W,y}^{\gamma}(p)v_p
      &=
      \int_0^1
      \left(
         \sum_{q:u_q\ge t}b_q
         +C\sum_{p:v_p\ge1-t}d_{W,y}^{\gamma}(p)
      \right)dt\\
      &\ge
      \int_0^1
      \left(
         \sum_{q\notin Y_t}b_q
         +C D_{W,y}^{\gamma}(Y_t)
      \right)dt\\
      &\ge
      \min_{Y\subseteq\mathcal Q}
      \left\{
         \sum_{q\notin Y}b_q
         +C D_{W,y}^{\gamma}(Y)
      \right\}.
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   This proves \((GSC1)\).  Rewriting \(\Phi_C(W;y,G)\ge M_0\) using the
   second form of \((GSC1)\) gives \((GSC2)\), and \(M_0=B_{\rm tot}\) gives
   \((GSC3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cut-certified guard-shadow reporter]
   \label{cor:cut-certified-guard-shadow-reporter}
   Work in the setting of \cref{def:guard-shadow-transport}, and define
   \(b_q\), \(B_{\rm tot}\), and \(D_{W,y}^{\gamma}\) as in
   \cref{lem:guard-shadow-cut-normal-form}.  Suppose \(|W|\le K\), \(C>0\),
   and \(0<M_0\le B_{\rm tot}\) are such that every \(Y\subseteq\mathcal Q\)
   satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Y}b_q
      \le
      C D_{W,y}^{\gamma}(Y)+B_{\rm tot}-M_0,
      \tag{CSG1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \frac{M_0}{C}
      >
      \psi_W
      \left(
         K^{\rho_W}\sum_q\tau_qy_q+\sigma K^{1+\rho_W}
      \right).
      \tag{CSG2}
   \]
   Then the guarded residual has a certified hit-weighted star panel satisfying
   \((HSP1)\)--\((HSP2)\).

   Conversely, if no such panel exists, then for every choice satisfying
   \((CSG2)\) there is a query cut \(Y\subseteq\mathcal Q\) with
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Y}b_q
      >
      C D_{W,y}^{\gamma}(Y)+B_{\rm tot}-M_0 .
      \tag{CSG3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{lem:guard-shadow-cut-normal-form}, \((CSG1)\) is equivalent to the
   existence of a \(C\)-congested guard-to-shadow transport of mass at least
   \(M_0\) into \(W\).  With \((CSG2)\),
   \cref{cor:guard-shadow-transport-reporter} produces the required panel.  The
   converse is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Half-mass guard-shadow cut obstruction]
   \label{cor:half-mass-guard-shadow-cut-obstruction}
   Work with one price system satisfying \((GSP1)\)--\((GSP3)\).  Let
   \(y_q=a_q\), \(G(q)=H(q)\), and
   \[
      b_q=\tau_qa_q|H(q)|,
      \qquad
      B_{\rm tot}=\sum_qb_q .
   \]
   Fix a certified star container \(W\) with \(|W|\le K\) and a congestion
   parameter \(C>0\).  If \(B_{\rm tot}>0\) and
   \[
      \frac{B_{\rm tot}}{2C}
      >
      \psi_W
      \left(
         K^{\rho_W}\sum_q\tau_qa_q+\sigma K^{1+\rho_W}
      \right),
      \tag{HGC1}
   \]
   then either a certified hit-weighted star panel satisfying
   \((HSP1)\)--\((HSP2)\) exists, or there is a query cut
   \(Y\subseteq\mathcal Q\) such that
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Y}b_q-CD_{W,a}^{\gamma}(Y)>\frac{B_{\rm tot}}2 .
      \tag{HGC2}
   \]
   In particular, under the no-panel hypothesis and \((GSP2)\),
   \[
      B_{\rm tot}>\frac{\pi_1\kappa}{2},
      \tag{HGC3}
   \]
   so the remaining obstruction is a high-price guard sublayer whose paid
   near-shadow capacity in \(W\) is less than its load up to congestion \(C\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{cor:cut-certified-guard-shadow-reporter} with
   \(M_0=B_{\rm tot}/2\).  The affordability condition \((CSG2)\) becomes
   \((HGC1)\).  If the panel conclusion fails, the cut violation \((CSG3)\)
   gives \((HGC2)\).  Finally, \((HGC3)\) is exactly \((GSP2)\) for
   \(y_q=a_q\) and \(G(q)=H(q)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Guard-shadow credit normal form]
   \label{lem:guard-shadow-credit-normal-form}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:guard-shadow-cut-normal-form}.  A
   \(C\)-credit certificate for the proposed container \(W\) is a finite
   nonnegative array
   \[
      f_{q,p}\ge0
      \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q,\ p\in W)
   \]
   supported on near incidences \((p,q)\in\mathcal N\), and satisfying
   \[
      \sum_{p\in N_W(\{q\})}f_{q,p}\le b_q
      \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q),
      \tag{GCR0}
   \]
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}f_{q,p}
      \le C d_{W,y}^{\gamma}(p)
      \qquad(p\in W).
      \tag{GCR1}
   \]
   Let
   \[
      u_q(f)=b_q-\sum_{p\in N_W(\{q\})}f_{q,p},
      \qquad
      U(f)=\sum_qu_q(f)
   \]
   be the uncredited guard load.  Then
   \[
      \inf_f U(f)
      =
      B_{\rm tot}-\Phi_C(W;y,G)
      =
      \max_{Y\subseteq\mathcal Q}
      \left\{
         \sum_{q\in Y}b_q-CD_{W,y}^{\gamma}(Y)
      \right\}.
      \tag{GCR2}
   \]
   The maximum is nonnegative, since \(Y=\emptyset\) is allowed.

   Thus the all-sublayer guard cut obstruction is exactly the minimum total
   deficit left after fractionally assigning paid near-shadow capacity in \(W\)
   to guard-load demands.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The variables \(f_{q,p}\) are precisely the aggregated transport variables
   used in the proof of \cref{lem:guard-shadow-cut-normal-form}.  Their shipped
   mass is
   \[
      M(f)=\sum_{q,p}f_{q,p}=B_{\rm tot}-U(f).
   \]
   Maximizing \(M(f)\) over \((GCR0)\)--\((GCR1)\) gives
   \(\Phi_C(W;y,G)\).  Hence
   \[
      \inf_f U(f)=B_{\rm tot}-\Phi_C(W;y,G).
   \]
   The second equality is the second form of \((GSC1)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Credit-certified guard-shadow reporter]
   \label{cor:credit-certified-guard-shadow-reporter}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:guard-shadow-cut-normal-form}.  Suppose
