   \(|W|\le K\), \(C>0\), and \(0<M_0\le B_{\rm tot}\).  If there is a
   \(C\)-credit certificate \(f\) with
   \[
      U(f)\le B_{\rm tot}-M_0,
      \tag{GCR3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \frac{M_0}{C}
      >
      \psi_W
      \left(
         K^{\rho_W}\sum_q\tau_qy_q+\sigma K^{1+\rho_W}
      \right),
      \tag{GCR4}
   \]
   then the guarded residual has a certified hit-weighted star panel satisfying
   \((HSP1)\)--\((HSP2)\).

   Conversely, if no such panel exists, then for every choice satisfying
   \((GCR4)\) every \(C\)-credit certificate has
   \[
      U(f)>B_{\rm tot}-M_0 .
      \tag{GCR5}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{lem:guard-shadow-credit-normal-form}, \((GCR3)\) implies
   \(\Phi_C(W;y,G)\ge M_0\).  Equivalently, the cut inequalities \((CSG1)\)
   hold.  Together with \((GCR4)\), \cref{cor:cut-certified-guard-shadow-reporter}
   gives the star panel.

   For the converse, suppose no panel exists and \((GCR4)\) holds.  Then
   \cref{cor:cut-certified-guard-shadow-reporter} gives a cut with excess
   greater than \(B_{\rm tot}-M_0\).  By \((GCR2)\), the infimum of \(U(f)\) is
   greater than \(B_{\rm tot}-M_0\), so every credit certificate satisfies
   \((GCR5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Half-mass guard-shadow deficit obstruction]
   \label{cor:half-mass-guard-shadow-deficit-obstruction}
   Work with one price system satisfying \((GSP1)\)--\((GSP3)\), and specialize
   to \(y_q=a_q\), \(G(q)=H(q)\), and
   \[
      b_q=\tau_qa_q|H(q)|,\qquad B_{\rm tot}=\sum_qb_q .
   \]
   Fix a certified star container \(W\) with \(|W|\le K\) and a congestion
   parameter \(C>0\).  Assume \(B_{\rm tot}>0\) and the affordability condition
   \((HGC1)\).  If there is a \(C\)-credit certificate \(f\) for \(W\) with
   \[
      U(f)\le \frac{B_{\rm tot}}2,
      \tag{HGD1}
   \]
   then a certified hit-weighted star panel satisfying \((HSP1)\)--\((HSP2)\)
   exists.

   Conversely, under the no-panel hypothesis, every \(C\)-credit certificate
   for every affordable \(W,K,C\) satisfying \((HGC1)\) obeys
   \[
      U(f)>\frac{B_{\rm tot}}2 .
      \tag{HGD2}
   \]
   With \((GSP2)\), this means that more than a constant fraction of the large
   activation-weighted guard co-load remains uncredited by the paid near-shadow
   of every affordable smaller-radius container:
   \[
      B_{\rm tot}>\frac{\pi_1\kappa}{2}.
      \tag{HGD3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{cor:credit-certified-guard-shadow-reporter} with
   \(M_0=B_{\rm tot}/2\).  Then \((GCR4)\) is exactly \((HGC1)\), and
   \((GCR3)\) is exactly \((HGD1)\).  The converse is \((GCR5)\) with the same
   value of \(M_0\).  Finally, \((HGD3)\) is \((GSP2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fractional guard-credit panel reporter]
   \label{cor:fractional-guard-credit-panel-reporter}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:guard-shadow-cut-normal-form}.  Let
   \(I\) be a finite index set.  For each \(i\in I\), suppose we are given a
   certified star container \(W_i\), a size certificate \(|W_i|\le K_i\), a
   congestion parameter \(C_i>0\), a multiplicity \(\lambda_i>0\), and a
   \(C_i\)-credit certificate \(f_i\) in \(W_i\).  Put
   \[
      M_i=B_{\rm tot}-U(f_i).
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i\frac{M_i}{C_i}
      >
      \sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i\psi_{W_i}
      \left(
         K_i^{\rho_{W_i}}\sum_q\tau_qy_q+\sigma K_i^{1+\rho_{W_i}}
      \right),
      \tag{GCP1}
   \]
   then the guarded residual has a certified hit-weighted star panel satisfying
   \((HSP1)\)--\((HSP2)\).

   Conversely, if no such panel exists, every finite family of credit records
   satisfies the reverse of \((GCP1)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Discard indices with \(M_i=0\).  For each surviving index \(i\), \((GCR1)\)
   gives
   \[
      M_i
      \le
      C_i\sum_{p\in W_i}d_{W_i,y}^{\gamma}(p).
   \]
   Submit the hit-weighted star-panel record with container \(W_i\), query
   weights \(y\), update side \(U_i=W_i\), lower certificate \(X_i=M_i/C_i\),
   size certificate \(K_i\), and multiplicity \(\lambda_i\).  The displayed
   inequality is exactly \((HSP1)\), and \((GCP1)\) gives the strict panel
   surplus \((HSP2)\).

   The converse is the contrapositive of the first statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Joint fractional guard-credit cover]
   \label{cor:joint-fractional-guard-credit-cover}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:guard-shadow-cut-normal-form}.  Let \(I\) be
   a finite set of certified containers \(W_i\), size certificates
   \(|W_i|\le K_i\), congestion parameters \(C_i>0\), and multiplicities
   \(\lambda_i>0\).  Suppose there are nonnegative variables
   \[
      F_{i,q,p}\ge0
      \qquad(i\in I,\ q\in\mathcal Q,\ p\in W_i)
   \]
   supported on near incidences \((p,q)\in\mathcal N\), satisfying the joint
   guard-demand constraints
   \[
      \sum_i\sum_{p\in N_{W_i}(\{q\})}F_{i,q,p}\le b_q
      \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q),
      \tag{JGC1}
   \]
   and the per-container paid-shadow capacities
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}F_{i,q,p}
      \le
      \lambda_iC_i d_{W_i,y}^{\gamma}(p)
      \qquad(i\in I,\ p\in W_i).
      \tag{JGC2}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      M_i=\sum_{q,p}F_{i,q,p}.
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_i\frac{M_i}{C_i}
      >
      \sum_i\lambda_i\psi_{W_i}
      \left(
         K_i^{\rho_{W_i}}\sum_q\tau_qy_q+\sigma K_i^{1+\rho_{W_i}}
      \right),
      \tag{JGC4}
   \]
   then the guarded residual has a certified hit-weighted star panel satisfying
   \((HSP1)\)--\((HSP2)\).

   Thus an overlapping dense family may be certified by a single fractional
   guard-credit flow: query demand is used at most once through \((JGC1)\), but
   the paid-shadow capacities and recursive costs are charged locally to the
   containers that receive the flow.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Discard indices with \(M_i=0\).  For each surviving \(i\), \((JGC2)\) gives
   \[
      M_i
      \le
      \lambda_iC_i\sum_{p\in W_i}d_{W_i,y}^{\gamma}(p).
   \]
   Thus \(X_i=M_i/(\lambda_iC_i)\) is a valid lower certificate for the whole
   container \(W_i\).  Submit the records \(U_i=W_i\) with size certificates
   \(K_i\) and multiplicities \(\lambda_i\).  Their aggregate certified mass is
   \(\sum_iM_i/C_i\), so \((JGC4)\) gives \((HSP2)\), while the displayed
   inequality gives \((HSP1)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite guard-credit flow separator]
   \label{cor:finite-guard-credit-flow-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:guard-shadow-cut-normal-form}.  Let
   \(\mathcal A\) be a finite pool of affordable guard-credit templates.  A
   template \(A\in\mathcal A\) consists of a certified star container \(W_A\),
   a size certificate \(|W_A|\le K_A\), and a congestion parameter \(C_A>0\).
   Put
   \[
      R_A=
      \psi_{W_A}
      \left(
         K_A^{\rho_{W_A}}\sum_q\tau_qy_q+\sigma K_A^{1+\rho_{W_A}}
      \right).
      \tag{FGF0}
   \]
   Suppose the following finite linear program has positive value.  The
   variables are multiplicities \(\lambda_A\ge0\) and flow variables
   \(F_{A,q,p}\ge0\), supported only when \(p\in W_A\) and
   \((p,q)\in\mathcal N\).  Write \(M_A=\sum_{q,p}F_{A,q,p}\).  The constraints
   are
   \[
      \sum_{A\in\mathcal A}
      \sum_{p\in N_{W_A}(\{q\})}F_{A,q,p}\le b_q
      \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q),
      \tag{FGF1}
   \]
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}F_{A,q,p}
      \le
      \lambda_AC_A d_{W_A,y}^{\gamma}(p)
      \qquad(A\in\mathcal A,\ p\in W_A),
      \tag{FGF2}
   \]
   and the objective is
   \[
      \sum_{A\in\mathcal A}\frac{M_A}{C_A}
      -
      \sum_{A\in\mathcal A}\lambda_AR_A .
      \tag{FGF4}
   \]
   If the optimum of \((FGF1)\)--\((FGF4)\) is positive, then the guarded
   residual has a certified hit-weighted star panel satisfying
   \((HSP1)\)--\((HSP2)\).

   Conversely, if no such panel exists, the optimum is nonpositive for every
   finite affordable template pool \(\mathcal A\).  Thus preprocessing may use
   ordinary finite LP optimization or column generation over \(k\)-means++,
   additive-quantization, range-reporting, or list-decoding proposals: only a
   positive verified guard-credit flow is retained.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \((\lambda,F)\) be any feasible solution with positive objective, and
   keep only the templates with \(M_A>0\).  The demand and capacity constraints
   \((FGF1)\)--\((FGF2)\) are exactly \((JGC1)\)--\((JGC2)\) for the active
   templates.  The strict positivity of \((FGF4)\) is exactly the joint surplus
   condition \((JGC4)\).  \Cref{cor:joint-fractional-guard-credit-cover} gives
   the required hit-weighted star panel.

   The converse is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Dual obstruction to finite guard-credit flow]
   \label{lem:finite-guard-credit-flow-dual}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-guard-credit-flow-separator}, and let
   \(\operatorname{val}(\mathcal A)\) denote the optimum of the finite LP
   \((FGF1)\)--\((FGF4)\).  Then
   \[
      \operatorname{val}(\mathcal A)
      =
      \min\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}b_qx_q,
      \tag{FGD0}
   \]
   where the minimum is over nonnegative variables
   \[
      x_q\ge0,\qquad u_{A,p}\ge0
   \]
   satisfying
   \[
      x_q+u_{A,p}
      \ge
      \frac1{C_A}
      \qquad
      (A\in\mathcal A,\ p\in W_A,\ (p,q)\in\mathcal N),
      \tag{FGD1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      C_A\sum_{p\in W_A}d_{W_A,y}^{\gamma}(p)u_{A,p}
      \le
      R_A
      \qquad(A\in\mathcal A).
      \tag{FGD2}
   \]
   Consequently, the finite pool has no positive guard-credit separator if and
   only if there is such a dual certificate with
   \[
      \sum_qb_qx_q=0.
      \tag{FGD3}
   \]

   In particular, after discarding zero-load queries, a failed finite pool has
   a zero-demand-price obstruction: every affordable template must satisfy the
   internal point-capacity inequalities \((FGD1)\)--\((FGD2)\) with
   \(x_q=0\) on the guard load that remains to be credited.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Write the primal in standard finite form with variables \(F_{A,q,p}\ge0\)
   and \(\lambda_A\ge0\).  The demand constraints \((FGF1)\) get dual variables
   \(x_q\ge0\).  The point-capacity constraints \((FGF2)\) get dual variables
   \(u_{A,p}\ge0\).

   The coefficient of \(F_{A,q,p}\) in the dual constraint is
   \(x_q+u_{A,p}\), which must dominate its objective coefficient
   \(1/C_A\).  This gives \((FGD1)\).  The coefficient of
   \(\lambda_A\) is
   \[
      -C_A\sum_{p\in W_A}d_{W_A,y}^{\gamma}(p)u_{A,p},
   \]
   which must dominate the primal objective coefficient \(-R_A\).  This is
   equivalent to \((FGD2)\).  Since the right side of \((FGF2)\) is zero, the
   dual objective is \(\sum_qb_qx_q\), proving \((FGD0)\) by finite-dimensional
   LP duality.

   The primal has the zero feasible solution, so
   \(\operatorname{val}(\mathcal A)\ge0\).  The dual objective is also
   nonnegative.  Hence the optimum is nonpositive exactly when both optima are
   zero, which is \((FGD3)\).  If \(b_q>0\), then \((FGD3)\) forces
   \(x_q=0\), giving the final specialization.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One-template separation of the guard-credit dual]
   \label{cor:one-template-guard-credit-separation}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{lem:finite-guard-credit-flow-dual}.  Let \(B\) be another affordable
   guard-credit template, with parameters
   \(W_B,K_B,C_B,R_B\) defined as in \((FGF0)\), and put
   \[
      \beta_B=\frac1{C_B}.
   \]
   Fix a dual feasible certificate for the pool \(\mathcal A\), and write
   \(x\) for its demand-price vector.  Define
   \[
      \ell_{B,p}(x)=
      \max_{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \{\beta_B-x_q\}
      \qquad(p\in W_B),
      \tag{FGS1}
   \]
   with the convention that the maximum over the empty set is \(-\infty\).
   Then this dual certificate extends over the enlarged pool
   \(\mathcal A\cup\{B\}\) with the same objective value if and only if
   \[
      C_B\sum_{p\in W_B}d_{W_B,y}^{\gamma}(p)
      \bigl(\ell_{B,p}(x)\bigr)_+
      \le R_B .
      \tag{FGS2}
   \]
   Thus a template \(B\) for which \((FGS2)\) fails cuts off this particular
   dual certificate.  More generally, if a finite proposal family
   \(\mathcal B\) cuts off every zero-objective dual certificate of the current
   pool in this sense, then the enlarged pool
   \(\mathcal A\cup\mathcal B\) has positive guard-credit LP value.

   In particular, after discarding queries with \(b_q=0\), every
   zero-objective certificate has \(x_q=0\).  Let
   \[
      E_B=\{p\in W_B:\exists q\in\mathcal Q\text{ with }(p,q)\in\mathcal N\},
      \qquad
      D_B=\sum_{p\in E_B}d_{W_B,y}^{\gamma}(p).
      \tag{FGS3}
   \]
   If
   \[
      D_B>R_B,
      \tag{FGS4}
   \]
   then \(B\) cuts off every zero-objective dual certificate of the current
   pool, and therefore the enlarged pool \(\mathcal A\cup\{B\}\) has positive
   value.  Thus the build-time proposal oracle for the failed guard-credit LP
   may search for a certified smaller-radius container whose active paid-shadow
   mass \(D_B\) beats its recursive query/storage price.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Adding \(B\) to the primal appends the variables \(F_{B,q,p}\) and
   \(\lambda_B\), together with the constraint \((FGF2)\) for this template.
   In the dual, this appends only the variables \(u_{B,p}\ge0\), while the
   demand prices \(x_q\) and the objective value are unchanged.  The new block is
   feasible exactly when
   \[
      x_q+u_{B,p}\ge\beta_B
      \qquad(p\in W_B,\ (p,q)\in\mathcal N),
      \tag{FGS5}
   \]
   and
   \[
      C_B\sum_{p\in W_B}d_{W_B,y}^{\gamma}(p)u_{B,p}
      \le R_B .
      \tag{FGS6}
   \]
   The smallest feasible \(u_{B,p}\) in \((FGS5)\) is
   \[
      u_{B,p}=\bigl(\ell_{B,p}(x)\bigr)_+ .
   \]
   Substituting this into \((FGS6)\) gives \((FGS2)\).

   Thus failure of \((FGS2)\) means exactly that this dual certificate cannot
   remain feasible after \(B\) is added.  If a finite proposal family cuts off
   every zero-objective dual certificate, then the enlarged pool has no
   zero-objective dual.  Since the enlarged LP has nonnegative value and its
   dual optimum is attained, \cref{lem:finite-guard-credit-flow-dual} implies
   that the enlarged finite LP has positive value.

   After zero-load queries are discarded, \((FGD3)\) forces \(x_q=0\) for every
   remaining query.  Hence \(\ell_{B,p}(x)=\beta_B\) for \(p\in E_B\) and
   \(\ell_{B,p}(x)=-\infty\) otherwise.  The left side of \((FGS2)\) is
   \(C_B\beta_BD_B=D_B\).  Thus \((FGS4)\) is exactly the failure of \((FGS2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Scale-free guard-credit proposal test]
   \label{cor:scale-free-guard-credit-proposal}
   Work in the zero-demand-price specialization of
   \cref{cor:one-template-guard-credit-separation}.  A raw proposal consists of
   an affordable certified container \(W\), a size certificate \(|W|\le K\),
   and a congestion parameter \(C>0\).  Define
   \[
      R(W,K,C)=
      \psi_W
      \left(
         K^{\rho_W}\sum_q\tau_qy_q+\sigma K^{1+\rho_W}
      \right),
      \tag{SFG1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      D(W)=\sum_{p\in W}d_{W,y}^{\gamma}(p).
      \tag{SFG2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      D(W)>R(W,K,C),
      \tag{SFG4}
   \]
   then adjoining this single template makes the finite guard-credit LP have
   positive value.

   Consequently, for any finite probability law \(\nu\) over raw proposals,
   if
   \[
      \E_{W\sim\nu}
      \left[
         D(W)-R(W,K_W,C_W)
      \right]>0,
      \tag{SFG6}
   \]
   then some deterministic proposal in its support separates the
   zero-objective guard-credit dual.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The one-template statement is
   \cref{cor:one-template-guard-credit-separation} with \(K_B=K\),
   \(C_B=C\), and \(R_B=R(W,K,C)\).  Condition \((SFG4)\) is exactly
   \((FGS4)\).

   Finally, if the average in \((SFG6)\) is positive, at least one proposal in
   the finite support has positive bracketed value.  Applying the exact-scale
   statement to that proposal gives the deterministic separator.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Lower-certified scale-free guard panel]
   \label{cor:lower-certified-scale-free-guard-panel}
   Work in the zero-demand-price specialization of
   \cref{cor:scale-free-guard-credit-proposal}.  A finite raw proposal panel
   consists of records \(i\in I\), each with an affordable certified container
   \(W_i\), a size certificate \(|W_i|\le K_i\), a congestion parameter
   \(C_i>0\), a lower paid-shadow certificate \(X_i\), and a multiplicity
   \(\lambda_i\ge0\), such that
   \[
      0\le X_i\le D(W_i)
      \qquad(i\in I).
      \tag{LCG1}
   \]
   Put \(R_i=R(W_i,K_i,C_i)\).  If
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_i(X_i-R_i)>0,
      \tag{LCG4}
   \]
   then some deterministic record in the panel separates the zero-objective
   guard-credit dual, and the finite guard-credit LP over the enlarged pool has
   positive value.

   Thus a build-time reporter does not need exact paid-shadow degrees: lower
   mass certificates, upper size certificates, and the direct surplus test are
   sufficient.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((LCG4)\) holds, at least one record satisfies
   \[
      X_i>R_i.
      \tag{LCG6}
   \]
   Since \(X_i\le D(W_i)\), this implies \((FGS4)\) for that template, so
   \cref{cor:one-template-guard-credit-separation} gives the separator and the
   positive LP value.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[High-correlation stars feed guard-credit proposals]
   \label{cor:high-correlation-stars-feed-guard-credit}
   Work in the zero-demand-price specialization of
   \cref{cor:lower-certified-scale-free-guard-panel}.  Let
   \(\mathcal R,w_r,E_r\) be a weighted high-correlation edge family as in
   \cref{lem:high-correlation-pair-star-reporter}, with star multiplicities
   \(M_x(p)\).  For each reported center \(x\), let \(W_x\) be an affordable
   certified star container, with size certificate \(|W_x|\le K_x\) and
   congestion parameter \(C_x>0\).  Suppose that every reported level
   \(U_{x,t}=\{p:M_x(p)\ge t\}\) is contained in \(W_x\), and that the reported
   multiplicity is dominated by paid near-shadow degree:
   \[
      M_x(p)\le d_{W_x,y}^{\gamma}(p)
      \qquad(p\in U_{x,t}).
      \tag{HCG1}
   \]
   Then the record
   \[
      (W_x,K_x,C_x,X_{x,t}),\qquad
      X_{x,t}=t|U_{x,t}|,
      \tag{HCG2}
   \]
   is a valid lower-certified raw guard proposal.  Consequently, any finite
   panel of such records with multiplicities \(\lambda_{x,t}\) satisfying
   \[
      \sum_{x,t}
      \lambda_{x,t}
      \left(X_{x,t}-R(W_x,K_x,C_x)\right)>0
      \tag{HCG3}
   \]
   separates the zero-objective guard-credit dual.

   In particular, assume all positive multiplicities \(M_x(p)\) lie in
   \([M_{\min},M_{\max}]\), let \(J_{\rm mult}\) be as in \((HPS6)\), and put
   \[
      W_{\rm inc}=\sum_{x,p}M_x(p).
   \]
   If every \(W_x\) in the support satisfies \(K_x\le K_0\) and
   \(R(W_x,K_x,C_x)\le R_0\), and if
   \[
      X_0=\frac{W_{\rm inc}}{2|P|J_{\rm mult}}>0,
      \qquad
      X_0>R_0,
      \tag{HCG5}
   \]
   then a single high-correlation star superlevel separates the guard-credit
   dual.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(U_{x,t}\subseteq W_x\), condition \((HCG1)\) gives
   \[
      X_{x,t}
      =
      t|U_{x,t}|
      \le
      \sum_{p\in U_{x,t}}M_x(p)
      \le
      \sum_{p\in W_x}d_{W_x,y}^{\gamma}(p)
      =
      D(W_x).
   \]
   Thus \((HCG2)\) satisfies the lower-certificate condition \((LCG1)\), and
   \((HCG3)\) is exactly \((LCG4)\) for this panel.  The first conclusion is
   therefore \cref{cor:lower-certified-scale-free-guard-panel}.

   For the final sufficient condition, apply
   \cref{lem:high-correlation-pair-star-reporter}.  It gives a center \(x\) and
   a dyadic level \(t\) such that \(X_{x,t}\ge X_0\).  Also
   \(R(W_x,K_x,C_x)\le R_0\).  Hence \((HCG5)\) implies
   \[
      X_{x,t}
      \ge
      X_0
      >
      R_0
      \ge
      R(W_x,K_x,C_x).
   \]
   The one-record panel satisfies \((HCG3)\), so the first conclusion applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fixed-threshold star screen for correlation-split layers]
   \label{cor:correlation-split-fixed-threshold-star-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:correlation-split-gaussian-profile-layer}.  Assume that the
   high-correlation edge family also satisfies the hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-stars-feed-guard-credit}: for every reported
   center \(x\) there is an affordable certified container \(W_x\), every
   superlevel \(U_{x,t}\) is contained in \(W_x\), and the multiplicity
   domination condition \((HCG1)\) holds.  Suppose, uniformly over these
   containers, that
   \[
      K_x\le K_0,
      \qquad
      R(W_x,K_x,C_x)\le R_0 .
      \tag{CFS1}
   \]
   Fix a scale \(\Lambda_0>0\), and assume
   \[
      \Lambda_0>R_0
      \tag{CFS3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}>2|P|J_{\rm hi}\Lambda_0,
      \tag{CFS4}
   \]
   then a single high-correlation star superlevel separates the guard-credit
   dual in the sense of \cref{cor:high-correlation-stars-feed-guard-credit}.

   Equivalently, after all high-correlation star levels with certified scale at
   least \(\Lambda_0\) have been proposed to the exact dense verifier, either
   one such level gives a one-record guard-credit repair, or the
   high-correlation contribution of this profile layer obeys
   \[
      W_{\rm hi}\le 2|P|J_{\rm hi}\Lambda_0,
      \tag{CFS5}
   \]
   and the unresolved profile-layer envelope is at most
   \[
      \mathcal A_{\rm lo}+2|P|J_{\rm hi}\Lambda_0 .
      \tag{CFS6}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((CFS4)\) holds, \cref{cor:correlation-split-gaussian-profile-layer}
   gives a center \(x\) and level \(t\) with
   \[
      X_{x,t}:=t|U_{x,t}|\ge \Lambda_0 .
   \]
   Therefore \((CFS3)\) gives
   \[
      X_{x,t}
      \ge
      \Lambda_0
      >
      R_0
      \ge
      R(W_x,K_x,C_x).
   \]
   The one-record panel satisfies \((HCG3)\), so
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-stars-feed-guard-credit} separates the
   guard-credit dual.

   The second statement is the contrapositive of the first statement together
   with the residual envelope \((CSG7)\) at \(\Lambda=\Lambda_0\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Aggregate fixed-tail correlation-split storage]
   \label{cor:aggregate-correlation-split-fixed-tail-storage}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:aggregate-multiplicity-profile-storage}.  For every active
   profile layer \(i=(\pi,\ell)\), suppose the Gaussian expansion
   \((GAP1)\) is partitioned as in
   \cref{cor:correlation-split-gaussian-profile-layer}.  Let
   \[
      \mathcal A_i^{\rm lo}
      =
      W_i^{\rm lo}
      \exp\!\left(-\frac{\beta_i^2}{1+\theta_i}\right)
      \tag{AFT1}
   \]
   be the certified low-correlation envelope, let \(J_i^{\rm hi}\) be the
   high-correlation dynamic-range factor, and choose a scale \(\Lambda_i>0\).
   Assume the high-correlation star records of layer \(i\) satisfy the
   hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:correlation-split-fixed-threshold-star-screen} with
   \(\Lambda_0=\Lambda_i\), and that the fixed-threshold price inequality
   \((CFS3)\) holds for this choice.

   Suppose no profile layer produces the one-record guard-credit repair from
   \cref{cor:correlation-split-fixed-threshold-star-screen}.  If
   \(\Sigma^+\ne\emptyset\), assume \(a>0\), the corresponding active
   first-moment condition of
   \cref{cor:aggregate-multiplicity-profile-storage} holds, and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \sum_{i=(\pi,\ell)}
      2^{-\ell}
      \left(
         \mathcal A_i^{\rm lo}
         +2|P|J_i^{\rm hi}\Lambda_i
      \right)
      \le aS .
      \tag{AFT2}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Equivalently, under the aggregate bound \((AFT2)\), any failure of the
   exact-signature storage cover must expose at least one fixed-threshold
   high-correlation star repair.  Thus high-correlation profile mass is no
   longer an unpriced storage obstruction: it is either converted to one
   dense repair record or paid by the explicit discounted tail in \((AFT2)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), feasibility is already part of
   \cref{cor:aggregate-multiplicity-profile-storage}.  Otherwise fix an active
   layer \(i=(\pi,\ell)\).  Since no one-record repair is produced and
   \((CFS3)\) holds, \cref{cor:correlation-split-fixed-threshold-star-screen}
   gives
   \[
      W_i^{\rm hi}\le 2|P|J_i^{\rm hi}\Lambda_i .
   \]
   The low-correlation part contributes at most
   \(\mathcal A_i^{\rm lo}\) by
   \cref{cor:correlation-split-gaussian-profile-layer}; the high-correlation
   part contributes at most its raw incidence \(W_i^{\rm hi}\).  Hence
   \[
      \E_z\mathcal V_z(\pi,\ell)
      \le
      \mathcal A_i^{\rm lo}
      +2|P|J_i^{\rm hi}\Lambda_i .
      \tag{AFT3}
   \]
   These are valid aggregate envelopes \((AMP2)\).  Substituting them into
   \((AMP3)\) gives exactly \((AFT2)\), so
   \cref{cor:aggregate-multiplicity-profile-storage} proves feasibility.
   The final statement is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Noncircular fixed-tail scale choice]
   \label{cor:noncircular-fixed-tail-scale-choice}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:aggregate-correlation-split-fixed-tail-storage}.  For every active
   profile layer \(i=(\pi,\ell)\), suppose the high-correlation star records
   have certified bounds
   \[
      K_x\le K_i,
      \qquad
      K_i>0,
      \qquad
      R(W_x,K_x,C_x)\le R_i,
      \qquad
      R_i>0 .
      \tag{NFT1}
   \]
   Define the proposal scale
   \[
      \Lambda_i^\circ=2R_i .
      \tag{NFT3}
   \]
   Then the fixed-threshold price condition \((CFS3)\) holds for layer \(i\)
   with \(K_0=K_i\), \(R_0=R_i\), and
   \(\Lambda_0=\Lambda_i^\circ\).

   Consequently, if no profile layer produces a one-record guard-credit repair
   and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \sum_{i=(\pi,\ell)}
      2^{-\ell}
      \left(
         \mathcal A_i^{\rm lo}
         +4|P|J_i^{\rm hi}R_i
      \right)
      \le aS ,
      \tag{NFT4}
   \]
   with the remaining hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:aggregate-correlation-split-fixed-tail-storage}, then
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Thus the high-correlation tail is checkable without solving for
   \(\Lambda_i\): the local price \(R_i\) and multiplicity dynamic-range factor
   \(J_i^{\rm hi}\) determine the charged storage tail.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(\Lambda_i^\circ=2R_i>R_i\), condition \((CFS3)\) holds.

   Apply \cref{cor:aggregate-correlation-split-fixed-tail-storage} with
   \(\Lambda_i=\Lambda_i^\circ\).  Its high-correlation tail is
   \[
      2|P|J_i^{\rm hi}\Lambda_i^\circ
      =
      4|P|J_i^{\rm hi}R_i,
   \]
   so \((NFT4)\) is exactly the aggregate bound \((AFT2)\) for these explicit
   scales.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Reciprocal-multiplicity fixed-tail storage endpoint]
   \label{cor:reciprocal-multiplicity-fixed-tail-storage}
   Work in the pair specialization of
   \cref{cor:occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage}, with storage prices
   \(u_{z,\kappa}=\psi_{z,\kappa}|A_{z,\kappa}|^{1+\rho_{z,\kappa}}\) and
   \(0\le\rho_{z,\kappa}\le1\).  Partition separated pairs into profiles
   \(\Pi\) and decompose occurrence multiplicities into dyadic layers as in
   \cref{cor:multiplicity-layer-pair-profile-storage}.  For every active layer
   \(i=(\pi,\ell)\), suppose its undiscounted aggregate occurrence congestion
   \(\mathcal V_z(\pi,\ell)\) admits a Gaussian expansion \((GAP1)\), split into
   low- and high-correlation parts as in
   \cref{cor:correlation-split-gaussian-profile-layer}.  Let
   \[
      \mathcal A_i^{\rm lo}
      =
      W_i^{\rm lo}
      \exp\!\left(-\frac{\beta_i^2}{1+\theta_i}\right)
      \tag{RMF1}
   \]
   be the low-correlation envelope, let \(J_i^{\rm hi}\) be the high-correlation
   multiplicity dynamic-range factor, and suppose every high-correlation star
   record in layer \(i\) has certified recursive price at most \(R_i>0\) in the
   sense of \((NFT1)\).

   Suppose no layer produces the one-record guard-credit repair from
   \cref{cor:correlation-split-fixed-threshold-star-screen}.  If
   \(\Sigma^+\ne\emptyset\), assume \(a>0\), the corresponding active
   first-moment condition holds, and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \sum_{i=(\pi,\ell)}
      2^{-\ell}
      \left(
         \mathcal A_i^{\rm lo}+4|P|J_i^{\rm hi}R_i
      \right)
      \le aS .
      \tag{RMF2}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Consequently the compressed-bucket storage obligation has the following
   direct endpoint: reciprocal occurrence multiplicity already contributes the
   factor \(2^{-\ell}\); the low-correlation part must be paid by the
   two-point Gaussian entropy-energy term, and any excess high-correlation mass
   must either be paid by the explicit fixed tail \(4|P|J_i^{\rm hi}R_i\) or
   yield a verified smaller-radius dense/star repair.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The hypotheses are exactly those of
   \cref{cor:noncircular-fixed-tail-scale-choice} after expanding the active
   layer notation.  That corollary sets the noncircular proposal scale
   \(\Lambda_i^\circ=2R_i\), so the high-correlation residual tail in
   \((AFT2)\) becomes \(4|P|J_i^{\rm hi}R_i\).  The aggregate bound \((RMF2)\)
   is therefore \((NFT4)\), and feasibility follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Local entropy-slack screen for reciprocal storage]
   \label{cor:local-entropy-slack-reciprocal-storage}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:reciprocal-multiplicity-fixed-tail-storage}, and let
   \(\mathcal I\) be the finite set of active profile layers
   \(i=(\pi,\ell_i)\).  Put \(M_{\mathcal I}=\max\{1,|\mathcal I|\}\).  Suppose
   no layer produces the one-record guard-credit repair.  If
   \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), feasibility is automatic.  Otherwise assume \(a>0\),
   the corresponding active first-moment condition holds, and for every
   \(i\in\mathcal I\),
   \[
      2^{-\ell_i}\mathcal A_i^{\rm lo}
      \le
      \frac{aS-\E_z\Gamma_z}{2M_{\mathcal I}},
      \qquad
      2^{-\ell_i}4|P|J_i^{\rm hi}R_i
      \le
      \frac{aS-\E_z\Gamma_z}{2M_{\mathcal I}},
      \tag{LES1}
   \]
   with \(aS>\E_z\Gamma_z\).  Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In particular, if \(\mathcal A_i^{\rm lo}=W_i^{\rm lo}
   \exp(-\beta_i^2/(1+\theta_i))\), the first inequality in \((LES1)\) follows
   from the local entropy-slack condition
   \[
      \frac{\beta_i^2}{1+\theta_i}
      \ge
      \log_+
      \frac{
         2M_{\mathcal I}W_i^{\rm lo}
      }{
         2^{\ell_i}(aS-\E_z\Gamma_z)
      } .
      \tag{LES2}
   \]
   Thus, when the number of active profile layers and the metadata term are
   \(\log^{O(1)}n\), the aggregate low-correlation storage check loses only an
   \(O(\log\log n)\) additive energy margin per layer.  The high-correlation
   side is similarly local: each layer only has to make its fixed dense-repair
   tail fit the second inequality of \((LES1)\), or else expose the corresponding
   smaller-radius repair.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Summing \((LES1)\) over \(i\in\mathcal I\) gives
   \[
      \sum_i2^{-\ell_i}
      \left(
         \mathcal A_i^{\rm lo}+4|P|J_i^{\rm hi}R_i
      \right)
      \le
      aS-\E_z\Gamma_z .
   \]
   This is exactly \((RMF2)\), so
   \cref{cor:reciprocal-multiplicity-fixed-tail-storage} applies.

   For the displayed entropy condition, if the logarithm argument is at most
   one then the right side of \((LES2)\) is zero and the first inequality in
   \((LES1)\) is immediate.  Otherwise exponentiating \((LES2)\) gives
   \[
      W_i^{\rm lo}
      \exp\!\left(-\frac{\beta_i^2}{1+\theta_i}\right)
      \le
      \frac{2^{\ell_i}(aS-\E_z\Gamma_z)}{2M_{\mathcal I}},
   \]
   which is the same inequality after multiplying by \(2^{-\ell_i}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Profile-entropy local storage screen]
   \label{cor:profile-entropy-local-storage-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:local-entropy-slack-reciprocal-storage}.  For each active layer
   \(i\in\mathcal I\), suppose the low-correlation contribution has a finite
   refinement \(\mathcal H_i\) with certified weights \(W_{i,h}\ge0\) and
   certified two-point energies \(I_{i,h}\ge0\), such that the low envelope used
   in \((LES1)\) may be sharpened to
   \[
      \widehat{\mathcal A}_i^{\rm lo}
      =
      \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_i}W_{i,h}e^{-I_{i,h}} .
      \tag{PELS1}
   \]
   Put \(H_i=\max\{1,|\mathcal H_i|\}\), and let
   \(B_\star=aS-\E_z\Gamma_z>0\).  Assume that for each \(h\in\mathcal H_i\),
   \[
      I_{i,h}\ge \log_+ W_{i,h}+\Lambda_i .
      \tag{PELS2}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \widehat{\mathcal A}_i^{\rm lo}\le H_ie^{-\Lambda_i}.
      \tag{PELS3}
   \]
   Consequently, the low-correlation half of the local screen follows from
   \[
      \Lambda_i
      \ge
      \log_+
      \frac{2M_{\mathcal I}H_i}{2^{\ell_i}B_\star}.
      \tag{PELS4}
   \]
   If, in addition, every active layer satisfies the same high-correlation
   fixed-tail condition as in \((LES1)\),
   \[
      2^{-\ell_i}4|P|J_i^{\rm hi}R_i
      \le
      \frac{B_\star}{2M_{\mathcal I}},
      \tag{PELS5}
   \]
   and no one-record guard-credit repair fires, then
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible with
   \(\mathcal A_i^{\rm lo}\) replaced by the sharper envelope
   \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_i^{\rm lo}\).

   In particular, when the refinement \(\mathcal H_i\) is the separated-pair
   profile partition from
   \cref{cor:spread-packing-entropy-energy-screen}, condition \((PELS2)\) is
   exactly the profile entropy-energy inequality
   \(I_{i,h}\ge\log W_{i,h}+\Lambda_i\).  A violation is therefore not a new
   storage obstruction: after the usual low/high correlation split, it is the
   star-signal alternative handled by
   \cref{cor:spread-packing-star-signal} and the guard-credit verifier.
   Thus the diffuse storage branch pays only the number of retained
   low-correlation profiles, not the raw number of separated pairs in them.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(W_{i,h}=0\), its contribution to \((PELS1)\) is zero.  Otherwise
   \((PELS2)\) gives
   \[
      W_{i,h}e^{-I_{i,h}}
      \le
      W_{i,h}e^{-\log_+W_{i,h}}e^{-\Lambda_i}
      \le e^{-\Lambda_i}.
   \]
   Summing over \(h\in\mathcal H_i\) proves \((PELS3)\).

   If the logarithm argument in \((PELS4)\) is at most one, then
   \(2^{-\ell_i}H_ie^{-\Lambda_i}\le 2^{-\ell_i}H_i
   \le B_\star/(2M_{\mathcal I})\).  Otherwise exponentiating \((PELS4)\) gives
   the same inequality.  Hence
   \[
      2^{-\ell_i}\widehat{\mathcal A}_i^{\rm lo}
      \le
      \frac{B_\star}{2M_{\mathcal I}} .
   \]
   Together with \((PELS5)\), this is \((LES1)\) for the sharpened low envelope.
   The proof of
   \cref{cor:local-entropy-slack-reciprocal-storage} uses only that envelope as
   an upper bound on the low-correlation contribution, so the same conclusion
   follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Entropy-deficit tail screen for local storage]
   \label{cor:entropy-deficit-tail-local-storage-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:profile-entropy-local-storage-screen}.  For every active layer
   \(i\) and low-correlation subprofile \(h\in\mathcal H_i\), put
   \[
      X_{i,h}=W_{i,h}e^{-I_{i,h}},
      \qquad
      N_i(t)=|\{h\in\mathcal H_i:X_{i,h}\ge t\}|
      \qquad(t>0).
      \tag{EDT1}
   \]
   Let \(B_\star=aS-\E_z\Gamma_z>0\).  If, for every active layer \(i\),
   \[
      2^{-\ell_i}\int_0^\infty N_i(t)\,dt
      \le
      \frac{B_\star}{2M_{\mathcal I}},
      \tag{EDT2}
   \]
   and the high-correlation fixed-tail condition \((PELS5)\) holds, then
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible, provided no one-record guard-credit
   repair fires.

   Equivalently, define dyadic entropy-deficit bins
   \[
      \mathcal H_{i,j}
      =
      \{h\in\mathcal H_i:2^j\le X_{i,h}<2^{j+1}\},
      \qquad j\in\mathbb Z .
      \tag{EDT3}
   \]
   Since only finitely many bins are nonempty, the integral condition follows
   from
   \[
      2^{-\ell_i}
      \sum_{j:\mathcal H_{i,j}\ne\emptyset}
      2^{j+1}|\mathcal H_{i,j}|
      \le
      \frac{B_\star}{2M_{\mathcal I}} .
      \tag{EDT4}
   \]

   Thus the geometric/list-decoding theorem needed by the storage branch may
   be stated as an exponential tail bound for the entropy deficits
   \(\log W_{i,h}-I_{i,h}\).  The uniform profile-count condition
   \((PELS2)\)--\((PELS4)\) is only the crude special case in which all bins lie
   below the same threshold \(e^{-\Lambda_i}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By the layer-cake identity for a finite nonnegative family,
   \[
      \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_i}X_{i,h}
      =
      \int_0^\infty N_i(t)\,dt .
   \]
   Hence \((EDT2)\) is exactly the low-correlation half of \((LES1)\) with the
   sharpened envelope \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_i^{\rm lo}=\sum_hX_{i,h}\).  The
   high-correlation half is \((PELS5)\), so
   \cref{cor:local-entropy-slack-reciprocal-storage} applies as in the proof of
   \cref{cor:profile-entropy-local-storage-screen}.

   The dyadic sufficient condition follows from
   \[
      \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_i}X_{i,h}
      \le
      \sum_{j:\mathcal H_{i,j}\ne\emptyset}
      2^{j+1}|\mathcal H_{i,j}|.
   \]
   Finally, if \(I_{i,h}\ge\log_+W_{i,h}+\Lambda_i\), then
   \(X_{i,h}\le e^{-\Lambda_i}\) for every positive \(W_{i,h}\), and the
   profile-count screen is recovered by bounding the tail integral by
   \(H_ie^{-\Lambda_i}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Positive-moment entropy-deficit screen]
   \label{cor:positive-moment-entropy-deficit-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:entropy-deficit-tail-local-storage-screen}.  For each active layer
   \(i\), choose a cutoff \(\tau_i>0\) and an exponent \(\nu_i>0\), and define
   the positive entropy-deficit moment
   \[
      \mathfrak M_i(\tau_i,\nu_i)
      =
      \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_i}
      \left[
         \left(\frac{X_{i,h}}{\tau_i}\right)^{1+\nu_i}-1
      \right]_+ .
      \tag{PME1}
   \]
   If, for every active layer \(i\),
   \[
      2^{-\ell_i}\tau_i
      \left(
         H_i+\mathfrak M_i(\tau_i,\nu_i)
      \right)
      \le
      \frac{B_\star}{2M_{\mathcal I}},
      \qquad B_\star=aS-\E_z\Gamma_z>0,
      \tag{PME2}
   \]
   and the high-correlation fixed-tail condition \((PELS5)\) holds, then
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible, provided no one-record guard-credit
   repair fires.

   Equivalently, writing the normalized entropy deficit as
   \[
      D_{i,h}=\log X_{i,h}-\log\tau_i,
      \tag{PME3}
   \]
   the remaining low-correlation storage theorem may certify only
   \[
      \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_i}
      \left(e^{(1+\nu_i)D_{i,h}}-1\right)_+,
      \tag{PME4}
   \]
   together with the trivial baseline \(\tau_iH_i\).  Thus a small positive
   moment of entropy excess is sufficient; the proof does not require a
   worst-profile inequality and does not require choosing every dyadic
   entropy-deficit bin explicitly.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For every \(X\ge0\),
   \[
      X
      \le
      \tau_i\left(1+\left[\left(\frac X{\tau_i}\right)^{1+\nu_i}-1\right]_+\right).
      \tag{PME5}
   \]
   Indeed, if \(X\le\tau_i\), the right side is \(\tau_i\ge X\).  If
   \(X>\tau_i\), the bracket is \((X/\tau_i)^{1+\nu_i}-1\), and the right side
   is
   \[
      \tau_i\left(\frac X{\tau_i}\right)^{1+\nu_i}\ge X .
   \]
   Summing \((PME5)\) over \(h\in\mathcal H_i\) gives
   \[
      \sum_hX_{i,h}
      \le
      \tau_i\left(H_i+\mathfrak M_i(\tau_i,\nu_i)\right).
   \]
   Hence \((PME2)\) implies the low-correlation tail condition \((EDT2)\).
   The conclusion follows from
   \cref{cor:entropy-deficit-tail-local-storage-screen}.  Formula \((PME4)\) is
   just \((PME1)\) after substituting \(X_{i,h}/\tau_i=e^{D_{i,h}}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Renyi-moment entropy-deficit screen]
   \label{cor:renyi-moment-entropy-deficit-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:positive-moment-entropy-deficit-screen}.  For each active layer
   \(i\), choose an exponent \(\nu_i>0\) and put
   \[
      Z_i(\nu_i)
      =
      \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_i}X_{i,h}^{1+\nu_i},
      \qquad
      C_{\nu_i}=(1+\nu_i)\nu_i^{-\nu_i/(1+\nu_i)} .
      \tag{RME1}
   \]
   If, for every active layer \(i\),
   \[
      2^{-\ell_i}C_{\nu_i}
      H_i^{\nu_i/(1+\nu_i)}
      Z_i(\nu_i)^{1/(1+\nu_i)}
      \le
      \frac{B_\star}{2M_{\mathcal I}},
      \qquad B_\star=aS-\E_z\Gamma_z>0,
      \tag{RME2}
   \]
   and the high-correlation fixed-tail condition \((PELS5)\) holds, then
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible, provided no one-record guard-credit
   repair fires.

   Equivalently, since \(X_{i,h}=W_{i,h}e^{-I_{i,h}}\), the low-correlation
   storage theorem may be stated as the single log-sum-exp inequality, with the
   convention \(\log0=-\infty\) inside the exponential sum,
   \[
      \log C_{\nu_i}
      +\frac{\nu_i}{1+\nu_i}\log H_i
      +\frac1{1+\nu_i}
       \log\sum_{h\in\mathcal H_i}
       \exp\!\left((1+\nu_i)(\log W_{i,h}-I_{i,h})\right)
      -\ell_i\log2
      \le
      \log\frac{B_\star}{2M_{\mathcal I}} .
      \tag{RME3}
   \]
   Thus the remaining diffuse storage certificate is an averaged Renyi
   list-size bound, not a maximum-profile entropy-margin bound and not a
   dyadic-tail enumeration.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For any cutoff \(\tau_i>0\), the proof of
   \cref{cor:positive-moment-entropy-deficit-screen} gives
   \[
      \sum_h X_{i,h}
      \le
      \tau_i\left(H_i+\mathfrak M_i(\tau_i,\nu_i)\right).
   \]
   Since
   \[
      \left[
         \left(\frac{X_{i,h}}{\tau_i}\right)^{1+\nu_i}-1
      \right]_+
      \le
      \left(\frac{X_{i,h}}{\tau_i}\right)^{1+\nu_i},
   \]
   we have the deterministic bound
   \[
      \tau_i\left(H_i+\mathfrak M_i(\tau_i,\nu_i)\right)
      \le
      \tau_iH_i+\tau_i^{-\nu_i}Z_i(\nu_i).
      \tag{RME4}
   \]
   If \(Z_i(\nu_i)=0\), the left side of \((RME2)\) is zero and the low
   envelope is zero.  Otherwise choose
   \[
      \tau_i=\left(\frac{\nu_iZ_i(\nu_i)}{H_i}\right)^{1/(1+\nu_i)} .
      \tag{RME5}
   \]
   Substituting \((RME5)\) into \((RME4)\) gives
   \[
      \tau_iH_i+\tau_i^{-\nu_i}Z_i(\nu_i)
      =
      C_{\nu_i}H_i^{\nu_i/(1+\nu_i)}
      Z_i(\nu_i)^{1/(1+\nu_i)} .
   \]
   Hence \((RME2)\) implies \((PME2)\) for this optimized cutoff.  The
   conclusion follows from
   \cref{cor:positive-moment-entropy-deficit-screen}.  Formula \((RME3)\) is
   \((RME2)\) after substituting \(X_{i,h}=W_{i,h}e^{-I_{i,h}}\) and taking
   logarithms.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Near-first-moment entropy-deficit screen]
   \label{cor:near-first-moment-entropy-deficit-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:renyi-moment-entropy-deficit-screen}.  For each active layer
   \(i\), set
   \[
      L_i=\max\{1,\log H_i\},
      \qquad
      \nu_i=L_i^{-1},
      \qquad
      Z_i=\sum_{h\in\mathcal H_i}X_{i,h}^{1+\nu_i}.
      \tag{NFM1}
   \]
   If, for every active layer \(i\),
   \[
      2^{-\ell_i}Z_i^{1/(1+\nu_i)}
      \le
      \frac{B_\star}{32M_{\mathcal I}},
      \qquad B_\star=aS-\E_z\Gamma_z>0,
      \tag{NFM2}
   \]
   and the high-correlation fixed-tail condition \((PELS5)\) holds, then
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible, provided no one-record guard-credit
   repair fires.

   Equivalently, with the same \(\log0=-\infty\) convention, the
   low-correlation storage theorem may target
   \[
      \frac1{1+\nu_i}
      \log\sum_{h\in\mathcal H_i}
      \exp\!\left((1+\nu_i)(\log W_{i,h}-I_{i,h})\right)
      -\ell_i\log2
      \le
      \log\frac{B_\star}{32M_{\mathcal I}} .
      \tag{NFM3}
   \]
   This formulation has no explicit \(\log H_i\) loss in the budget.  If the
   active refinement has \(H_i\le\log^{O(1)}n\), the required moment order is
   only \(1+\Omega(1/\log\log n)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(L=L_i\), \(\nu=\nu_i=1/L\), and \(H=H_i\).  Then
   \[
      H^{\nu/(1+\nu)}
      =
      \exp\!\left(\frac{\log H}{L+1}\right)
      \le e .
      \tag{NFM4}
   \]
   Also
   \[
      C_\nu=(1+\nu)\nu^{-\nu/(1+\nu)}
      =
      \left(1+\frac1L\right)L^{1/(L+1)}
      \le
      2e^{1/e}<4 .
      \tag{NFM5}
   \]
   Therefore
   \[
      C_{\nu_i}H_i^{\nu_i/(1+\nu_i)}<16 .
   \]
   Condition \((NFM2)\) implies \((RME2)\), because multiplying its left side
   by this universal factor is still at most
   \(B_\star/(2M_{\mathcal I})\).  The conclusion follows from
   \cref{cor:renyi-moment-entropy-deficit-screen}.  Formula \((NFM3)\) is
   \((NFM2)\) after substituting \(X_{i,h}=W_{i,h}e^{-I_{i,h}}\) and taking
   logarithms.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Variational near-first-moment obstruction]
   \label{cor:variational-near-first-moment-obstruction}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:near-first-moment-entropy-deficit-screen}.  Fix an active layer
   \(i\), put \(p_i=1+\nu_i\), and write
   \[
      d_{i,h}=\log W_{i,h}-I_{i,h}
      \qquad(h\in\mathcal H_i),
      \tag{VNF1}
   \]
   with the convention \(d_{i,h}=-\infty\) when \(W_{i,h}=0\).  For a
   probability law \(\mu\) on \(\mathcal H_i\), let
   \[
      \mathsf h(\mu)=\sum_{h\in\mathcal H_i}\mu_h\log\frac1{\mu_h}
      \tag{VNF2}
   \]
   be its Shannon entropy.  Laws that place positive mass on
   \(d_{i,h}=-\infty\) have value \(-\infty\) below.  Then the local
   near-first-moment condition \((NFM3)\) is equivalent to
   \[
      \sup_{\mu\in\Delta(\mathcal H_i)}
      \left\{
         \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_i}\mu_h d_{i,h}
         +
         \frac{\mathsf h(\mu)}{p_i}
      \right\}
      -\ell_i\log2
      \le
      \log\frac{B_\star}{32M_{\mathcal I}} .
      \tag{VNF3}
   \]
   Consequently, if \((NFM3)\) fails, then the Gibbs law
   \[
      \mu_h^\star
      =
      \frac{X_{i,h}^{p_i}}{\sum_{g\in\mathcal H_i}X_{i,g}^{p_i}}
      \tag{VNF4}
   \]
   on the positive \(X_{i,h}\)'s violates \((VNF3)\).

   Thus the remaining low-correlation storage theorem may be proved in the
   following dual form: for every tilted profile law \(\mu\), either the
   \(\mu\)-average cap-intersection energy dominates the \(\mu\)-average
   profile entropy and weight in \((VNF3)\), or that tilted law supplies the
   dense/star repair already handled by the guard-credit verifier.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The finite Gibbs variational identity says that for real numbers \(a_h\),
   \[
      \log\sum_h e^{a_h}
      =
      \sup_{\mu\in\Delta(\mathcal H_i)}
      \left\{
         \sum_h\mu_ha_h+\mathsf h(\mu)
      \right\},
      \tag{VNF5}
   \]
   with the usual restriction to indices where \(a_h>-\infty\).  Apply this
   with \(a_h=p_id_{i,h}\) and divide by \(p_i\).  This gives
   \[
      \frac1{p_i}\log\sum_h e^{p_id_{i,h}}
      =
      \sup_{\mu\in\Delta(\mathcal H_i)}
      \left\{
         \sum_h\mu_hd_{i,h}+\frac{\mathsf h(\mu)}{p_i}
      \right\}.
   \]
   Since \(e^{d_{i,h}}=X_{i,h}\), this is exactly the left side of \((NFM3)\)
   before subtracting \(\ell_i\log2\).  Hence \((NFM3)\) and \((VNF3)\) are
   equivalent.  If the left side is finite, equality in \((VNF5)\) is attained
   by the Gibbs law \((VNF4)\); if all \(X_{i,h}\) vanish, \((NFM3)\) is
   trivially true and there is no obstruction.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Gibbs water-level storage screen]
   \label{cor:gibbs-water-level-storage-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:variational-near-first-moment-obstruction}.  For each active
   layer \(i\), define the water level
   \[
      \Lambda_i^{\rm Gibbs}
      =
      \frac1{p_i}
      \log\sum_{h\in\mathcal H_i}X_{i,h}^{p_i},
      \qquad p_i=1+\nu_i,
      \tag{GWL1}
   \]
   with value \(-\infty\) if all \(X_{i,h}\) vanish.  If, for every active
   layer \(i\),
   \[
      \Lambda_i^{\rm Gibbs}-\ell_i\log2
      \le
      \log\frac{B_\star}{32M_{\mathcal I}},
      \tag{GWL2}
   \]
   and the high-correlation fixed-tail condition \((PELS5)\) holds, then
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible, provided no one-record guard-credit
   repair fires.

   If \((GWL2)\) fails for a layer with positive \(X_{i,h}\), the unique Gibbs
   law
   \[
      \mu_{i,h}^{\rm Gibbs}
      =
      \frac{X_{i,h}^{p_i}}{\sum_{g\in\mathcal H_i}X_{i,g}^{p_i}}
      \tag{GWL3}
   \]
   satisfies the exact water-level identity
   \[
      d_{i,h}
      +
      \frac1{p_i}\log\frac1{\mu_{i,h}^{\rm Gibbs}}
      =
      \Lambda_i^{\rm Gibbs}
      \qquad
      (\mu_{i,h}^{\rm Gibbs}>0).
      \tag{GWL4}
   \]
   Thus a build-time geometric separator only has to repair this one tilted
   law per failing active layer: either certify that its entropy-energy value is
   below the local budget, or convert the weighted profile law
   \(\mu_i^{\rm Gibbs}\) into one of the dense/star records already accepted by
   the guard-credit verifier.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(X_{i,h}=e^{d_{i,h}}\), condition \((GWL2)\) is exactly \((NFM3)\).
   Hence feasibility follows from
   \cref{cor:near-first-moment-entropy-deficit-screen}.  If some \(X_{i,h}\) is
   positive, \((GWL3)\) is the optimizer from
   \cref{cor:variational-near-first-moment-obstruction}.  For every point in
   its support,
   \[
      \log\frac1{\mu_{i,h}^{\rm Gibbs}}
      =
      \log\sum_gX_{i,g}^{p_i}-p_i\log X_{i,h}.
   \]
   Dividing by \(p_i\) and adding \(d_{i,h}=\log X_{i,h}\) gives \((GWL4)\).
   The final sentence is the contrapositive of the first conclusion together
   with the optimizer statement in
   \cref{cor:variational-near-first-moment-obstruction}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Gibbs-weighted guard-repair criterion]
   \label{cor:gibbs-weighted-guard-repair}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:gibbs-water-level-storage-screen}, and fix a layer \(i\) for which
   \((GWL2)\) fails.  Let
   \(\mu=\mu_i^{\rm Gibbs}\) be the law in \((GWL3)\).  Work also in the
   zero-demand-price guard-credit specialization of
   \cref{cor:lower-certified-scale-free-guard-panel}.  Suppose a build-time
   reporter associates to each \(h\in\mathcal H_i\) with \(\mu_h>0\) a finite
   panel of lower-certified raw guard proposals \(a\in\mathcal R_h\).  Write
   \(X_a\) for the lower paid-shadow certificate and
   \(R_a=R(W_a,K_a,C_a)\) for the recursive query/storage price of record \(a\).
   If there are finite nonnegative weights \(\lambda_{h,a}\) such that
   \[
      \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_i}\mu_h
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal R_h}
         \lambda_{h,a}(X_a-R_a)>0,
      \tag{GGR1}
   \]
   then a one-record guard-credit repair fires.

   Conversely, if no one-record guard-credit repair fires, then every
   Gibbs-weighted certified proposal panel satisfies the reverse inequality
   \[
      \sum_h\mu_h
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal R_h}
         \lambda_{h,a}X_a
      \le
      \sum_h\mu_h
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal R_h}
         \lambda_{h,a}R_a .
      \tag{GGR2}
   \]
   Hence a surviving bad layer has two simultaneous properties: its water level
   beats the local storage budget, and no finite family of dense/star proposals
   has positive surplus when averaged against the single Gibbs law
   \(\mu_i^{\rm Gibbs}\).  The remaining geometric theorem may therefore target
   only this normalized residual: prove a Gibbs-average proposal surplus
   \((GGR1)\), or prove the low-correlation water-level inequality \((GWL2)\)
   directly.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Flatten the profile-indexed panel into one finite raw guard panel by giving
   record \(a\in\mathcal R_h\) the multiplicity
   \(\widetilde\lambda_{h,a}=\mu_h\lambda_{h,a}\).  Each record is
   lower-certified in the sense of
   \cref{cor:lower-certified-scale-free-guard-panel}, so \((GGR1)\) is exactly
   the positive aggregate surplus condition \((LCG4)\) for this flattened
   panel.  That corollary produces a deterministic one-record guard-credit
   separator.  The converse is the contrapositive of the same statement,
   applied to every finite Gibbs-weighted panel.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Partition-local Gibbs residual]
   \label{cor:partition-local-gibbs-residual}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:gibbs-water-level-storage-screen}.  For every active layer \(i\),
   let \(\mathcal P_i\) be a finite partition of
   \(\{h\in\mathcal H_i:X_{i,h}>0\}\), and put
   \(J_i=\max\{1,|\mathcal P_i|\}\).  For each nonempty class
   \(C\in\mathcal P_i\), define its class water level
   \[
      \Lambda_{i,C}^{\rm part}
      =
      \frac1{p_i}\log\sum_{h\in C}X_{i,h}^{p_i}.
      \tag{PLG1}
   \]
   If every active layer and every class satisfy
   \[
      \Lambda_{i,C}^{\rm part}-\ell_i\log2
      \le
      \log\frac{B_\star}
               {32M_{\mathcal I}J_i^{1/p_i}},
      \tag{PLG2}
   \]
   and the high-correlation fixed-tail condition \((PELS5)\) holds, then
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible, provided no one-record guard-credit
   repair fires.

   Conversely, if \((GWL2)\) fails for a layer \(i\), then some class
   \(C\in\mathcal P_i\) violates \((PLG2)\).  For such a class, define the
   conditional Gibbs law
   \[
      \mu_{i,C,h}^{\rm part}
      =
      \frac{X_{i,h}^{p_i}}{\sum_{g\in C}X_{i,g}^{p_i}}
      \qquad(h\in C).
      \tag{PLG3}
   \]
   If a build-time reporter supplies lower-certified raw guard proposals
   \(a\in\mathcal R_h\) and finite nonnegative weights \(\lambda_{h,a}\) with
   \[
      \sum_{h\in C}\mu_{i,C,h}^{\rm part}
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal R_h}\lambda_{h,a}(X_a-R_a)>0,
      \tag{PLG4}
   \]
   then a one-record guard-credit repair fires.  If no such repair fires, every
   violating class satisfies the reverse of \((PLG4)\) for every finite
   certified proposal panel.

   Thus the Gibbs obstruction may be localized before doing geometry.  A proof
   may partition profiles into surprisal bands, tuple-profile classes,
   range-report cells, or even singletons; the only analytic price for this
   localization is the explicit factor \(J_i^{1/p_i}\), which is
   polylogarithmic whenever the chosen partition has polylogarithmic size.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed active layer,
   \[
      \exp(p_i\Lambda_i^{\rm Gibbs})
      =
      \sum_{C\in\mathcal P_i}\exp(p_i\Lambda_{i,C}^{\rm part}).
      \tag{PLG5}
   \]
   If \((PLG2)\) holds for every class, then
   \[
      \exp(p_i\Lambda_i^{\rm Gibbs})
      \le
      J_i
      \left(
         2^{\ell_i}\frac{B_\star}
         {32M_{\mathcal I}J_i^{1/p_i}}
      \right)^{p_i}
      =
      \left(
         2^{\ell_i}\frac{B_\star}{32M_{\mathcal I}}
      \right)^{p_i}.
   \]
   Taking \(p_i\)-th roots gives \((GWL2)\).  Therefore the first conclusion is
   \cref{cor:gibbs-water-level-storage-screen}.  The same calculation read
   contrapositively shows that if \((GWL2)\) fails, at least one class violates
   \((PLG2)\).

   For the repair statement, flatten the class-indexed proposal panel by
   assigning multiplicity
   \(\widetilde\lambda_{h,a}=\mu_{i,C,h}^{\rm part}\lambda_{h,a}\) to record
   \(a\in\mathcal R_h\).  Then \((PLG4)\) is exactly the positive aggregate
   surplus condition \((LCG4)\) of
   \cref{cor:lower-certified-scale-free-guard-panel}, so that corollary gives a
   deterministic one-record repair.  The no-repair residual is the
   contrapositive applied to every finite class-local panel.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Count-energy cell screen]
   \label{cor:count-energy-cell-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:partition-local-gibbs-residual}.  For a nonempty class
   \(C\in\mathcal P_i\), put
   \[
      d_{i,C}^{+}=\max_{h\in C}(\log W_{i,h}-I_{i,h}),
      \qquad
      d_{i,C}^{-}=\min_{h\in C}(\log W_{i,h}-I_{i,h}).
      \tag{CEC1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      d_{i,C}^{-}+\frac1{p_i}\log|C|
      \le
      \Lambda_{i,C}^{\rm part}
      \le
      d_{i,C}^{+}+\frac1{p_i}\log|C|.
      \tag{CEC2}
   \]
   Consequently, the class condition \((PLG2)\) follows from the ordinary
   count-energy inequality
   \[
      d_{i,C}^{+}+\frac1{p_i}\log|C|
      -\ell_i\log2
      \le
      \log\frac{B_\star}
               {32M_{\mathcal I}J_i^{1/p_i}}.
      \tag{CEC3}
   \]
   If \((PLG2)\) fails for \(C\), then necessarily
   \[
      d_{i,C}^{+}+\frac1{p_i}\log|C|
      -\ell_i\log2
      >
      \log\frac{B_\star}
               {32M_{\mathcal I}J_i^{1/p_i}}.
      \tag{CEC4}
   \]
   Conversely, if a reporter certifies the stronger lower count-energy
   violation
   \[
      d_{i,C}^{-}+\frac1{p_i}\log|C|
      -\ell_i\log2
      >
      \log\frac{B_\star}
               {32M_{\mathcal I}J_i^{1/p_i}},
      \tag{CEC5}
   \]
   then \(C\) violates \((PLG2)\).

   In particular, on cells with \(d_{i,C}^{+}-d_{i,C}^{-}\le\Delta\), the exact
   Gibbs water level differs from the elementary statistic
   \(d_{i,C}^{+}+p_i^{-1}\log|C|\) by at most \(\Delta\).  Thus after a finite
   partition into bounded dynamic-range cells, the residual can be stated as a
   count-energy excess in one cell, plus the no-positive guard-panel condition
   of \cref{cor:partition-local-gibbs-residual}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(X_{i,h}=e^{d_{i,h}}\),
   \[
      |C|e^{p_id_{i,C}^{-}}
      \le
      \sum_{h\in C}X_{i,h}^{p_i}
      \le
      |C|e^{p_id_{i,C}^{+}}.
   \]
   Taking logarithms and dividing by \(p_i\) gives \((CEC2)\).  The sufficient
   condition \((CEC3)\) follows by combining the upper bound in \((CEC2)\) with
   \((PLG2)\).  The necessary obstruction \((CEC4)\) is the contrapositive of
   the same implication.  The lower certificate \((CEC5)\) implies \((PLG2)\)
   fails by the lower bound in \((CEC2)\).  The bounded-range statement is
   immediate from \((CEC2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Singleton profile Gibbs residual]
   \label{cor:singleton-profile-gibbs-residual}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:partition-local-gibbs-residual}.  Suppose every active layer uses
   the singleton partition of the positive profiles.  If, for every active
   layer \(i\) and every \(h\in\mathcal H_i\) with \(X_{i,h}>0\),
   \[
      \log W_{i,h}-I_{i,h}-\ell_i\log2
      \le
      \log\frac{B_\star}
               {32M_{\mathcal I}H_i^{1/p_i}},
      \tag{SPG1}
   \]
   and the high-correlation fixed-tail condition \((PELS5)\) holds, then
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible, provided no one-record guard-credit
   repair fires.

   Conversely, if \((GWL2)\) fails for a layer \(i\), then some positive profile
   \(h\in\mathcal H_i\) satisfies
   \[
      \log W_{i,h}-I_{i,h}-\ell_i\log2
      >
      \log\frac{B_\star}
               {32M_{\mathcal I}H_i^{1/p_i}}.
      \tag{SPG2}
   \]
   For such a profile, any finite lower-certified raw guard proposal panel
   \(a\in\mathcal R_h\) with nonnegative weights \(\lambda_a\) and
   \[
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal R_h}\lambda_a(X_a-R_a)>0
      \tag{SPG3}
   \]
   fires a one-record guard-credit repair.  If no such repair fires, every
   finite certified proposal panel for every violating singleton profile
   satisfies the reverse inequality
   \[
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal R_h}\lambda_aX_a
      \le
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal R_h}\lambda_aR_a .
      \tag{SPG4}
   \]

   Thus, when the active refinement has \(H_i=\log^{O(1)}n\), the residual
   storage theorem can be stated without Gibbs notation: every bad layer must
   expose one ordinary profile whose entropy-energy deficit beats the local
   budget by only a polylogarithmic \(H_i^{1/p_i}\) toll, and that profile must
   also evade all certified dense/star guard repairs.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(\mathcal P_i\) be the singleton partition of
   \(\{h:X_{i,h}>0\}\), and let \(J_i=|\mathcal P_i|\).  Then
   \(J_i\le H_i\), and for the singleton class \(C=\{h\}\),
   \[
      \Lambda_{i,C}^{\rm part}
      =
      \log W_{i,h}-I_{i,h}.
   \]
   If \((SPG1)\) holds, then \((PLG2)\) holds for every singleton because
   \(H_i^{1/p_i}\ge J_i^{1/p_i}\).  The first conclusion follows from
   \cref{cor:partition-local-gibbs-residual}.

   If \((GWL2)\) fails, \cref{cor:partition-local-gibbs-residual} gives a
   singleton \(\{h\}\) violating \((PLG2)\) with \(J_i\).  Since
   \(H_i^{1/p_i}\ge J_i^{1/p_i}\), this implies the stronger-looking violation
   \((SPG2)\).  On a singleton, the conditional Gibbs law \((PLG3)\) is the
   point mass at \(h\), so \((SPG3)\) is exactly the class-local surplus
   condition \((PLG4)\), and \((SPG4)\) is its no-repair contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Singleton spread-star repair dichotomy]
   \label{cor:singleton-spread-star-repair}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:singleton-profile-gibbs-residual}.  Fix an active layer \(i\) and
   a positive singleton profile \(h\in\mathcal H_i\), and put
   \[
      X_{i,h}=W_{i,h}e^{-I_{i,h}},
      \qquad
      \Theta_{i,h}=
      \frac{2^{\ell_i}B_\star}
           {32M_{\mathcal I}H_i^{1/p_i}} .
      \tag{SSR0}
   \]
   Suppose a build-time reporter certifies nonnegative numbers
   \(L_h,H_h\) and a finite family \(\mathcal B_h\) of lower-certified raw
   guard records.  Let \(X_b\) and \(R_b\) be the lower paid-shadow certificate
   and recursive price of record \(b\in\mathcal B_h\).  Assume
   \[
      X_{i,h}\le L_h+H_h,
      \tag{SSR1}
   \]
   and that the high-correlation part is captured by the reported star
   layer-cake in the form
   \[
      H_h\le 2\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_h}X_b .
      \tag{SSR2}
   \]
   If the certified low part plus reported recursive star price fits the
   singleton water budget,
   \[
      L_h+2\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_h}R_b
      \le
      \Theta_{i,h},
      \tag{SSR3}
   \]
   then either \(h\) satisfies the singleton bound \((SPG1)\), or a one-record
   guard-credit repair fires.

   Equivalently, if \(h\) violates \((SPG1)\) and no one-record guard-credit
   repair fires, then the same certificates must violate the single price
   inequality
   \[
      L_h+2\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_h}R_b
      >
      \Theta_{i,h}.
      \tag{SSR4}
   \]
   Consequently, if every positive singleton profile in every active layer
   admits certificates satisfying \((SSR1)\)--\((SSR3)\), and the
   high-correlation fixed-tail condition \((PELS5)\) holds, then
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible, provided no one-record guard-credit
   repair fires.

   In the concrete spread-packing or correlation-split instantiation, \(L_h\)
   is the certified low-correlation entropy-energy envelope
   \((SPEE2)\) or \((CSG2)\), \(H_h\) is the remaining high-correlation
   incidence, and \(\mathcal B_h\) is the dyadic star-superlevel panel from
   \cref{cor:spread-packing-star-signal} or
   \cref{cor:correlation-split-gaussian-profile-layer}.  The layer-cake
   estimate gives \((SSR2)\), and
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-stars-feed-guard-credit} supplies the
   lower-certified guard records whenever the star containers and paid-shadow
   domination certificates are available.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The logarithmic singleton condition \((SPG1)\) is exactly
   \(X_{i,h}\le\Theta_{i,h}\).  Suppose no one-record guard-credit repair fires.
   Since each \(b\in\mathcal B_h\) is a lower-certified raw guard record, a
   record with \(X_b>R_b\) would be a one-record positive panel in
   \cref{cor:lower-certified-scale-free-guard-panel}.  Hence
   \(X_b\le R_b\) for every \(b\in\mathcal B_h\).  Combining this with
   \((SSR1)\)--\((SSR3)\) gives
   \[
      X_{i,h}
      \le
      L_h+H_h
      \le
      L_h+2\sum_bX_b
      \le
      L_h+2\sum_bR_b
      \le
      \Theta_{i,h}.
   \]
   Thus \(h\) satisfies \((SPG1)\).  The contrapositive gives \((SSR4)\).

   If every positive singleton profile has such certificates and no repair
   fires, then every profile satisfies \((SPG1)\).  The final feasibility claim
   follows from \cref{cor:singleton-profile-gibbs-residual} together with
   \((PELS5)\).  The concrete instantiation is just the dyadic layer-cake
   bound used in \cref{cor:spread-packing-star-signal} and
   \cref{cor:correlation-split-gaussian-profile-layer}, plus the
   lower-certification statement of
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-stars-feed-guard-credit}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Partition-cell spread-star repair dichotomy]
   \label{cor:partition-cell-spread-star-repair}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:partition-local-gibbs-residual}.  Fix an active layer \(i\), a
   nonempty partition class \(C\in\mathcal P_i\), and write
   \[
      X_{i,h}=W_{i,h}e^{-I_{i,h}},
      \qquad
      X_{i,C}^{(p)}
      =
      \left(\sum_{h\in C}X_{i,h}^{p_i}\right)^{1/p_i},
      \tag{PCS0}
   \]
   \[
      \Theta_{i,C}
      =
      \frac{2^{\ell_i}B_\star}
           {32M_{\mathcal I}J_i^{1/p_i}} .
      \tag{PCS1}
   \]
   Suppose a build-time reporter certifies nonnegative numbers \(L_C,H_C\) and
   a finite family \(\mathcal B_C\) of lower-certified raw guard records, with
   lower paid-shadow certificates \(X_b\) and recursive prices \(R_b\), such
   that
   \[
      X_{i,C}^{(p)}\le L_C+H_C
      \tag{PCS2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      H_C\le2\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_C}X_b .
      \tag{PCS3}
   \]
   If the class low envelope plus reported recursive star price fits the local
   water budget,
   \[
      L_C+2\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_C}R_b
      \le
      \Theta_{i,C},
      \tag{PCS4}
   \]
   then either \(C\) satisfies the partition-local water bound \((PLG2)\), or a
   one-record guard-credit repair fires.

   Equivalently, if \(C\) violates \((PLG2)\) and no one-record guard-credit
   repair fires, then the same class certificates must violate
   \[
      L_C+2\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_C}R_b
      >
      \Theta_{i,C}.
      \tag{PCS5}
   \]
   Consequently, if every active layer and every positive partition class
   admits certificates satisfying \((PCS2)\)--\((PCS4)\), and the
   high-correlation fixed-tail condition \((PELS5)\) holds, then
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible, provided no one-record guard-credit
   repair fires.

   Thus the spread-star repair bridge does not require singletonizing the
   entire profile refinement.  One may first group profiles into
   bounded-dynamic-range cells, surprisal bands, tuple-profile cells, or
   reporter cells; only the chosen partition count \(J_i\), not the raw profile
   count \(H_i\), appears in the water threshold.  For example, if each
   \(h\in C\) has a certified split \(X_{i,h}\le L_h+H_h\), then Minkowski's
   inequality permits the class certificates
   \[
      L_C=\left(\sum_{h\in C}L_h^{p_i}\right)^{1/p_i},
      \qquad
      H_C=\left(\sum_{h\in C}H_h^{p_i}\right)^{1/p_i},
      \tag{PCS6}
   \]
   after which the high-correlation part need only be reported well enough to
   certify \((PCS3)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The partition-local condition \((PLG2)\) is exactly
   \(X_{i,C}^{(p)}\le\Theta_{i,C}\).  Suppose no one-record guard-credit repair
   fires.  As in the proof of
   \cref{cor:singleton-spread-star-repair}, every lower-certified raw record in
   \(\mathcal B_C\) must satisfy \(X_b\le R_b\); otherwise that single record is
   a positive panel for
   \cref{cor:lower-certified-scale-free-guard-panel}.  Hence
   \[
      X_{i,C}^{(p)}
      \le
      L_C+H_C
      \le
      L_C+2\sum_bX_b
      \le
      L_C+2\sum_bR_b
      \le
      \Theta_{i,C},
   \]
   proving \((PLG2)\).  The contrapositive is \((PCS5)\).

   If every positive class satisfies \((PLG2)\), then
   \cref{cor:partition-local-gibbs-residual} gives
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) under \((PELS5)\) and no guard repair.  Finally,
   \((PCS6)\) is the triangle inequality in \(\ell_{p_i}(C)\), applied to the
   pointwise bounds \(X_{i,h}\le L_h+H_h\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Shared-record partition-cell compiler]
   \label{cor:shared-record-partition-cell-compiler}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:partition-cell-spread-star-repair}.  Fix an active layer \(i\), a
   nonempty partition class \(C\in\mathcal P_i\), and a finite shared family
   \(\mathcal B_C\) of lower-certified raw guard records.  For each \(h\in C\)
   let \(\ell_h\ge0\), and for each \(h\in C\), \(b\in\mathcal B_C\), let
   \(z_{h,b}\ge0\).  For every record \(b\), let \(X_b\) and \(R_b\) denote its
   lower paid-shadow certificate and recursive price, and put
   \[
      L_C^{\rm sh}
      =
      \left(\sum_{h\in C}\ell_h^{p_i}\right)^{1/p_i},
      \qquad
      Z_b^{(p)}
      =
      \left(\sum_{h\in C}z_{h,b}^{p_i}\right)^{1/p_i}.
      \tag{SRPC1}
   \]
   Suppose the reporter certifies a profilewise shared decomposition
   \[
      X_{i,h}\le \ell_h+\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_C}z_{h,b}
      \qquad(h\in C),
      \tag{SRPC2}
   \]
   and, for some \(\chi\ge1\), the recordwise aggregation bounds
   \[
      Z_b^{(p)}\le \chi X_b
      \qquad(b\in\mathcal B_C).
      \tag{SRPC3}
   \]
   If the shared low envelope plus the one-time shared record prices fit the
   cell water budget,
   \[
      L_C^{\rm sh}+\chi\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_C}R_b
      \le
      \Theta_{i,C},
      \tag{SRPC4}
   \]
   then either \(C\) satisfies \((PLG2)\), or a one-record guard-credit repair
   fires.

   Equivalently, if \(C\) violates \((PLG2)\) and no one-record repair fires, then
   every such shared decomposition must violate
   \[
      L_C^{\rm sh}+\chi\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_C}R_b
      >
      \Theta_{i,C}.
      \tag{SRPC5}
   \]
   Consequently, if every active layer and positive partition class admits
   certificates satisfying \((SRPC2)\)--\((SRPC4)\), and \((PELS5)\) holds, then
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible, provided no one-record guard-credit
   repair fires.

   In particular, it is enough to certify additive allocations with
   \[
      \sum_{h\in C}z_{h,b}\le \chi X_b
      \qquad(b\in\mathcal B_C),
      \tag{SRPC6}
   \]
   because \(Z_b^{(p)}\le\sum_h z_{h,b}\).  Thus a dense/star record shared by
   many profiles is charged through the single quantity \(Z_b^{(p)}\) and the
   one-time recursive price \(R_b\), rather than through a separate copy of the
   price in every profile where it appears.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose no one-record repair fires.  Since every \(b\in\mathcal B_C\) is a
   lower-certified raw record, \(X_b>R_b\) would itself be a positive one-record
   panel for \cref{cor:lower-certified-scale-free-guard-panel}.  Hence
   \(X_b\le R_b\) for every \(b\).

   Apply Minkowski's inequality in \(\ell_{p_i}(C)\) to \((SRPC2)\):
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      X_{i,C}^{(p)}
      &=
      \left(\sum_{h\in C}X_{i,h}^{p_i}\right)^{1/p_i}  \\
      &\le
      L_C^{\rm sh}
      +
      \sum_{b\in\mathcal B_C}
      \left(\sum_{h\in C}z_{h,b}^{p_i}\right)^{1/p_i} \\
      &=
      L_C^{\rm sh}+\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_C}Z_b^{(p)}  \\
      &\le
      L_C^{\rm sh}+\chi\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_C}X_b
      \le
      L_C^{\rm sh}+\chi\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_C}R_b
      \le
      \Theta_{i,C}.
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   Therefore \(C\) satisfies \((PLG2)\).  The contrapositive is \((SRPC5)\).
   The feasibility claim follows from
   \cref{cor:partition-local-gibbs-residual} as in
   \cref{cor:partition-cell-spread-star-repair}.  Finally, \((SRPC6)\) implies
   \((SRPC3)\) since \(p_i\ge1\) and the \(\ell_{p_i}\) norm is bounded by the
   \(\ell_1\) norm on nonnegative vectors.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Aggregate shared-cell water budget]
   \label{cor:aggregate-shared-cell-water-budget}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:partition-local-gibbs-residual}.  For every active layer \(i\), let
   \(\mathcal P_i\) be a finite partition of the positive profiles.  For every
   nonempty class \(C\in\mathcal P_i\), suppose a reporter gives a shared-record
   certificate as in \cref{cor:shared-record-partition-cell-compiler}, possibly
   with class-dependent \(\chi_{i,C}\).  Write its certified class cost as
   \[
      \mathsf Y_{i,C}
      =
      L_{i,C}^{\rm sh}
      +
      \chi_{i,C}
      \sum_{b\in\mathcal B_{i,C}}R_b .
      \tag{ASCW1}
   \]
   If, for every active layer \(i\),
   \[
      \left(
         \sum_{C\in\mathcal P_i}\mathsf Y_{i,C}^{p_i}
      \right)^{1/p_i}
      \le
      \frac{2^{\ell_i}B_\star}{32M_{\mathcal I}},
      \tag{ASCW2}
   \]
   and the high-correlation fixed-tail condition \((PELS5)\) holds, then
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible, provided no one-record guard-credit
   repair fires.

   Conversely, suppose no one-record guard-credit repair fires and \((GWL2)\)
   fails for an active layer \(i\).  Then every collection of shared-record
   certificates satisfying the profilewise decomposition and recordwise
   aggregation hypotheses \((SRPC2)\)--\((SRPC3)\) must violate
   \[
      \left(
         \sum_{C\in\mathcal P_i}\mathsf Y_{i,C}^{p_i}
      \right)^{1/p_i}
      >
      \frac{2^{\ell_i}B_\star}{32M_{\mathcal I}} .
      \tag{ASCW3}
   \]

   Thus the partition count \(J_i\) is not an inherent multiplicative toll.  The
   uniform bound \((PLG2)\) is the special case
   \(\mathsf Y_{i,C}\le2^{\ell_i}B_\star/(32M_{\mathcal I}J_i^{1/p_i})\) for
   every class.  A reporter may instead spend the layer water budget only on the
   cells that actually carry entropy-deficit mass, and may use a coarse partition
   for low-dynamic-range certification without paying the worst-cell budget on
   every cell.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Assume no one-record guard-credit repair fires.  The proof of
   \cref{cor:shared-record-partition-cell-compiler}, applied to each class
   \(C\), gives
   \[
      X_{i,C}^{(p)}
      \le
      \mathsf Y_{i,C}.
      \tag{ASCW4}
   \]
   Therefore
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \exp(p_i\Lambda_i^{\rm Gibbs})
      &=
      \sum_{C\in\mathcal P_i}
      \left(X_{i,C}^{(p)}\right)^{p_i} \\
      &\le
      \sum_{C\in\mathcal P_i}\mathsf Y_{i,C}^{p_i}.
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   If \((ASCW2)\) holds, taking \(p_i\)-th roots gives \((GWL2)\) for every
   active layer.  Then \cref{cor:gibbs-water-level-storage-screen} gives
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) under \((PELS5)\).

   Conversely, if \((GWL2)\) fails and no repair fires, then the displayed
   inequality forces the aggregate certified costs to exceed the right side of
   \((ASCW2)\), which is \((ASCW3)\).  The final paragraph is just the
   comparison with the uniform budget used in \((PLG2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Layer-global shared-record water compiler]
   \label{cor:layer-global-shared-record-water}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:gibbs-water-level-storage-screen}.  For every active layer \(i\),
   suppose a reporter gives a finite layer-global family \(\mathcal B_i\) of
   lower-certified raw guard records.  For each profile
   \(h\in\mathcal H_i\) let \(\ell_h\ge0\), and for each
   \(h\in\mathcal H_i\), \(b\in\mathcal B_i\), let \(z_{h,b}\ge0\).  For every
   record \(b\), let \(X_b\) and \(R_b\) denote its lower paid-shadow
   certificate and recursive price, and put
   \[
      L_i^{\rm sh}
      =
      \left(\sum_{h\in\mathcal H_i}\ell_h^{p_i}\right)^{1/p_i},
      \qquad
      Z_{i,b}^{(p)}
      =
      \left(\sum_{h\in\mathcal H_i}z_{h,b}^{p_i}\right)^{1/p_i}.
      \tag{LGW1}
   \]
   Suppose the reporter certifies the layerwise shared decomposition
   \[
      X_{i,h}\le \ell_h+\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_i}z_{h,b}
      \qquad(h\in\mathcal H_i),
      \tag{LGW2}
   \]
   and, for some \(\chi_{i,b}\ge1\), the global record aggregation bounds
   \[
      Z_{i,b}^{(p)}\le \chi_{i,b}X_b
      \qquad(b\in\mathcal B_i).
      \tag{LGW3}
   \]
   If, for every active layer \(i\),
   \[
      L_i^{\rm sh}
      +
      \sum_{b\in\mathcal B_i}\chi_{i,b}R_b
      \le
      \frac{2^{\ell_i}B_\star}{32M_{\mathcal I}},
      \tag{LGW4}
   \]
   and the high-correlation fixed-tail condition \((PELS5)\) holds, then
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible, provided no one-record guard-credit
   repair fires.

   Conversely, suppose no one-record guard-credit repair fires and \((GWL2)\)
   fails for an active layer \(i\).  Then every layer-global shared
   decomposition satisfying \((LGW2)\)--\((LGW3)\) must violate
   \[
      L_i^{\rm sh}
      +
      \sum_{b\in\mathcal B_i}\chi_{i,b}R_b
      >
      \frac{2^{\ell_i}B_\star}{32M_{\mathcal I}} .
      \tag{LGW5}
   \]

   In particular, it is enough to certify additive record capacities
   \[
      \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_i}z_{h,b}\le\chi_{i,b}X_b
      \qquad(b\in\mathcal B_i),
      \tag{LGW6}
   \]
   because \(Z_{i,b}^{(p)}\le\sum_hz_{h,b}\).  Thus the reporter partition is
   only a way to find or certify allocations; it need not be part of the final
   water accounting.  A dense/star record that helps profiles in many cells is
   charged once at the layer level, through its global allocation norm, rather
   than once per cell where it appears.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Assume no one-record guard-credit repair fires.  Since every
   \(b\in\mathcal B_i\) is a lower-certified raw guard record, \(X_b>R_b\)
   would itself be a positive one-record panel for
   \cref{cor:lower-certified-scale-free-guard-panel}.  Hence \(X_b\le R_b\) for
   every \(b\).

   Apply Minkowski's inequality in \(\ell_{p_i}(\mathcal H_i)\) to \((LGW2)\):
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \exp(\Lambda_i^{\rm Gibbs})
      &=
      \left(\sum_{h\in\mathcal H_i}X_{i,h}^{p_i}\right)^{1/p_i} \\
      &\le
      L_i^{\rm sh}
      +
      \sum_{b\in\mathcal B_i}
      \left(\sum_{h\in\mathcal H_i}z_{h,b}^{p_i}\right)^{1/p_i} \\
      &=
      L_i^{\rm sh}+\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_i}Z_{i,b}^{(p)} \\
      &\le
      L_i^{\rm sh}+\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_i}\chi_{i,b}X_b \\
      &\le
      L_i^{\rm sh}+\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_i}\chi_{i,b}R_b .
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   If \((LGW4)\) holds, this gives \((GWL2)\) for every active layer.  Then
   \cref{cor:gibbs-water-level-storage-screen} gives
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) under \((PELS5)\).

   Conversely, if \((GWL2)\) fails and no repair fires, the displayed inequality
   forces every certified layer-global shared decomposition to violate
   \((LGW4)\), which is \((LGW5)\).  Finally, \((LGW6)\) implies \((LGW3)\)
   because \(p_i\ge1\) and the \(\ell_{p_i}\) norm is bounded by the
   \(\ell_1\) norm on nonnegative vectors.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[No-discount form of layer-global water]
   \label{cor:no-discount-layer-global-water}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:layer-global-shared-record-water}, and fix one active layer \(i\).
   For any layer-global shared decomposition \((\ell,z,\mathcal B_i)\), define
   its certified water cost
   \[
      \mathsf C_i(\ell,z,\mathcal B_i)
      =
      L_i^{\rm sh}
      +
      \sum_{b\in\mathcal B_i}\chi_{i,b}R_b .
      \tag{NDW1}
   \]
   If no one-record guard-credit repair fires, then every such decomposition
   satisfies
   \[
      \exp(\Lambda_i^{\rm Gibbs})
      \le
      \mathsf C_i(\ell,z,\mathcal B_i).
      \tag{NDW2}
   \]
   Conversely, the empty-record decomposition \(\ell_h=X_{i,h}\) gives
   \[
      \mathsf C_i=
      \left(\sum_{h\in\mathcal H_i}X_{i,h}^{p_i}\right)^{1/p_i}
      =
      \exp(\Lambda_i^{\rm Gibbs}).
      \tag{NDW3}
   \]
   Hence the best possible no-repair layer-global shared water certificate has
   value exactly \(\exp(\Lambda_i^{\rm Gibbs})\).

   Thus global sharing removes duplicate bookkeeping across reporter cells, but
   it does not create slack below the Gibbs water level.  Any strict improvement
   over direct water control must come from a positive guard-credit repair, or
   from a geometric estimate proving the water level itself small.  The
   remaining storage theorem should therefore target \((GWL2)\) directly after
   all profitable records have been materialized, rather than search for a
   fractional allocation whose priced value is below \(\exp(\Lambda_i^{\rm
   Gibbs})\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The proof of \cref{cor:layer-global-shared-record-water} already showed that,
   under no one-record repair,
   \[
      \exp(\Lambda_i^{\rm Gibbs})
      \le
      L_i^{\rm sh}
      +
      \sum_{b\in\mathcal B_i}\chi_{i,b}R_b,
   \]
   which is \((NDW2)\).  For the converse, take \(\mathcal B_i=\emptyset\) and
   \(\ell_h=X_{i,h}\).  Then \(L_i^{\rm sh}\) is exactly the
   \(\ell_{p_i}\)-norm of the profile weights, namely
