   \(\exp(\Lambda_i^{\rm Gibbs})\), and there is no record price.  This proves
   \((NDW3)\) and the equality of the optimum with the Gibbs water level.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dyadic top-prefix water screen]
   \label{cor:dyadic-top-prefix-water-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:gibbs-water-level-storage-screen}, and fix an active layer \(i\).
   Let \(x_1\ge x_2\ge\cdots\ge x_m>0\) be the positive values among
   \(\{X_{i,h}:h\in\mathcal H_i\}\), in nonincreasing order.  If \(m=0\), then
   \((GWL2)\) is automatic.  Otherwise put
   \[
      \Theta_i=\frac{2^{\ell_i}B_\star}{32M_{\mathcal I}},
      \qquad
      \mathcal K_i=\{2^s:0\le s\le\lfloor\log_2m\rfloor\},
      \qquad
      J_i^{\rm pref}=|\mathcal K_i|.
      \tag{TPW1}
   \]
   If every dyadic rank \(k\in\mathcal K_i\) satisfies the weak-type envelope
   \[
      x_k k^{1/p_i}
      \le
      \frac{\Theta_i}{(J_i^{\rm pref})^{1/p_i}},
      \tag{TPW2}
   \]
   then layer \(i\) satisfies \((GWL2)\).

   Conversely, if \((GWL2)\) fails for layer \(i\), then some dyadic rank
   \(k\in\mathcal K_i\) violates \((TPW2)\).  For that rank, any tie-broken top
   \(k\) profiles \(P_k\) certify the lower count-energy excess
   \[
      \log x_k+\frac1{p_i}\log k-\ell_i\log2
      >
      \log\frac{B_\star}
               {32M_{\mathcal I}(J_i^{\rm pref})^{1/p_i}}.
      \tag{TPW3}
   \]

   Thus, after the no-discount correction of
   \cref{cor:no-discount-layer-global-water}, the remaining high-water residual
   can be searched as a dyadic top-prefix problem.  A range-reporting,
   list-decoding, facility, additive-quantization, or seeded-clustering routine
   need not approximate the whole Gibbs law: if it rules out every dyadic
   prefix envelope \((TPW2)\), the layer water inequality follows; if not, it
   receives one concrete prefix whose minimum entropy-deficit weight and
   cardinality already exceed the local budget by only the logarithmic
   \(J_i^{\rm pref}\) toll.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For \(k\in\mathcal K_i\), define the dyadic rank block
   \[
      B_k=\{j:k\le j\le \min\{2k-1,m\}\}.
   \]
   These blocks partition \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\), each has size at most \(k\), and
   every \(j\in B_k\) has \(x_j\le x_k\).  Therefore
   \[
      \sum_{j=1}^m x_j^{p_i}
      \le
      \sum_{k\in\mathcal K_i} kx_k^{p_i}.
      \tag{TPW4}
   \]
   If \((TPW2)\) holds for every dyadic \(k\), then every summand in
   \((TPW4)\) is at most \(\Theta_i^{p_i}/J_i^{\rm pref}\), and hence
   \[
      \sum_{h\in\mathcal H_i}X_{i,h}^{p_i}
      =
      \sum_{j=1}^m x_j^{p_i}
      \le
      \Theta_i^{p_i}.
   \]
   Taking \(p_i\)-th roots gives \((GWL2)\).

   The converse is the contrapositive of the same calculation.  If \((GWL2)\)
   fails, then \(\sum_jx_j^{p_i}>\Theta_i^{p_i}\), so not all dyadic summands
   \(kx_k^{p_i}\) can be at most \(\Theta_i^{p_i}/J_i^{\rm pref}\).  This gives
   a violating rank \(k\).  Since every point in the tie-broken top \(k\)
   prefix has \(X_{i,h}\ge x_k\), the displayed violation of \((TPW2)\) is
   exactly \((TPW3)\) after taking logarithms and subtracting
   \(\ell_i\log2\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dyadic prefix spread-star repair bridge]
   \label{cor:dyadic-prefix-spread-star-repair}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:dyadic-top-prefix-water-screen}.  Fix an active layer \(i\), a
   dyadic rank \(k\in\mathcal K_i\), and a tie-broken top prefix
   \(P_k\subseteq\mathcal H_i\) of size \(k\).  Put
   \[
      \underline X_{i,k}
      =
      k^{1/p_i}\min_{h\in P_k}X_{i,h}
      =
      k^{1/p_i}x_k,
      \qquad
      \Theta_i^{\rm pref}
      =
      \frac{\Theta_i}{(J_i^{\rm pref})^{1/p_i}} .
      \tag{DTR1}
   \]
   Suppose a build-time reporter certifies nonnegative numbers \(L_k,H_k\)
   and a finite family \(\mathcal B_k\) of lower-certified raw guard records,
   with lower paid-shadow certificates \(X_b\) and recursive prices \(R_b\),
   such that
   \[
      \underline X_{i,k}\le L_k+H_k
      \tag{DTR2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      H_k\le2\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}X_b .
      \tag{DTR3}
   \]
   If the prefix low envelope plus reported recursive star price fits the
   dyadic prefix budget,
   \[
      L_k+2\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}R_b
      \le
      \Theta_i^{\rm pref},
      \tag{DTR4}
   \]
   then either the rank \(k\) satisfies the weak-type water envelope
   \((TPW2)\), or a one-record guard-credit repair fires.

   Equivalently, if \(k\) violates \((TPW2)\) and no one-record guard-credit
   repair fires, then every such prefix certificate must violate
   \[
      L_k+2\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}R_b
      >
      \Theta_i^{\rm pref}.
      \tag{DTR5}
   \]
   Consequently, if every active layer and every dyadic top prefix admits
   certificates satisfying \((DTR2)\)--\((DTR4)\), and the high-correlation
   fixed-tail condition \((PELS5)\) holds, then
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible, provided no one-record guard-credit
   repair fires.

   The statistic \(\underline X_{i,k}\) is the weak-type floor of the prefix,
   not the whole prefix \(\ell_{p_i}\)-mass.  Thus a stronger certificate
   \(X_{i,P_k}^{(p)}\le L_k+H_k\), with
   \(X_{i,P_k}^{(p)}=(\sum_{h\in P_k}X_{i,h}^{p_i})^{1/p_i}\), is sufficient
   for \((DTR2)\), but is not required.  This is the form in which an exact
   prefix, range-reporting, list-decoding, facility, or seeded-clustering
   reporter should be used: it only has to price the witnessed dyadic floor, or
   expose a guard record already consumed by the existing verifier.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose no one-record guard-credit repair fires.  Since each
   \(b\in\mathcal B_k\) is a lower-certified raw guard record, \(X_b>R_b\)
   would itself be a positive one-record panel for
   \cref{cor:lower-certified-scale-free-guard-panel}.  Hence \(X_b\le R_b\)
   for every \(b\).  Combining this with \((DTR2)\)--\((DTR4)\) gives
   \[
      \underline X_{i,k}
      \le
      L_k+H_k
      \le
      L_k+2\sum_bX_b
      \le
      L_k+2\sum_bR_b
      \le
      \Theta_i^{\rm pref}.
   \]
   By \((DTR1)\), this is exactly \((TPW2)\) for the rank \(k\).  The
   contrapositive gives \((DTR5)\).

   If every dyadic prefix has certificates satisfying \((DTR2)\)--\((DTR4)\)
   and no repair fires, then every dyadic rank satisfies \((TPW2)\).  Therefore
   \cref{cor:dyadic-top-prefix-water-screen} gives \((GWL2)\) in every active
   layer, and \cref{cor:gibbs-water-level-storage-screen} gives
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) under \((PELS5)\).

   Finally,
   \[
      \underline X_{i,k}^{p_i}
      =
      k\min_{h\in P_k}X_{i,h}^{p_i}
      \le
      \sum_{h\in P_k}X_{i,h}^{p_i},
   \]
   so any upper bound on \(X_{i,P_k}^{(p)}\) also supplies \((DTR2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dyadic prefix low-price residual split]
   \label{cor:dyadic-prefix-low-price-residual}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:dyadic-prefix-spread-star-repair}, and keep the prefix
   certificates \(L_k,H_k,\mathcal B_k\) satisfying \((DTR2)\)--\((DTR3)\).
   Define the normalized low and recursive-price loads
   \[
      \mathsf L_{i,k}
      =
      \frac{L_k}{\Theta_i^{\rm pref}},
      \qquad
      \mathsf P_{i,k}
      =
      \frac{2\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}R_b}{\Theta_i^{\rm pref}} .
      \tag{DSB1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \mathsf L_{i,k}+\mathsf P_{i,k}\le1,
      \tag{DSB2}
   \]
   then either the rank \(k\) satisfies the weak-type water envelope
   \((TPW2)\), or a one-record guard-credit repair fires.

   Equivalently, if \(k\) violates \((TPW2)\) and no one-record guard-credit
   repair fires, then every such certified split has
   \[
      \mathsf L_{i,k}+\mathsf P_{i,k}>1.
      \tag{DSB3}
   \]
   Consequently, for every slack parameter \(0\le a\le1\), a surviving
   violating prefix obeys at least one of
   \[
      L_k>a\Theta_i^{\rm pref},
      \qquad
      2\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}R_b>(1-a)\Theta_i^{\rm pref}.
      \tag{DSB4}
   \]
   In particular, with \(a=1/2\), every surviving bad prefix has either
   \(L_k>\Theta_i^{\rm pref}/2\) or
   \(\sum_bR_b>\Theta_i^{\rm pref}/4\).

   If every dyadic prefix in every active layer admits certificates satisfying
   \((DTR2)\)--\((DTR3)\) and \((DSB2)\), and the high-correlation fixed-tail
   condition \((PELS5)\) holds, then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible,
   provided no one-record guard-credit repair fires.

   Thus the dyadic water residual has only two scalar proof targets.  The
   low branch is an entropy-energy or list-decoding estimate for \(L_k\); the
   high branch is a bound on the one-time recursive price of the reported star
   records, which may be attacked by the shared-prefix or integrated-cover
   screens.  No extra branching multiplicity is hidden in this split.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Condition \((DSB2)\) is exactly \((DTR4)\) after multiplying by
   \(\Theta_i^{\rm pref}\).  The first claim is therefore
   \cref{cor:dyadic-prefix-spread-star-repair}.  The contrapositive gives
   \((DSB3)\), and \((DSB4)\) is the elementary implication that
   \(u+v>1\) forces \(u>a\) or \(v>1-a\).

   If \((DSB2)\) holds for every dyadic prefix and no repair fires, then every
   dyadic rank satisfies \((TPW2)\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:dyadic-top-prefix-water-screen} gives \((GWL2)\) in every active
   layer, and \cref{cor:gibbs-water-level-storage-screen} gives
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) under \((PELS5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dyadic prefix high-star mass residual]
   \label{cor:dyadic-prefix-high-star-mass}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:dyadic-prefix-spread-star-repair}, and keep the prefix
   certificates \(L_k,H_k,\mathcal B_k\) satisfying \((DTR2)\)--\((DTR3)\).
   Define the normalized reported star mass and recursive price
   \[
      \mathsf M_{i,k}^{\star}
      =
      \frac{2\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}X_b}{\Theta_i^{\rm pref}},
      \qquad
      \mathsf P_{i,k}^{\star}
      =
      \frac{2\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}R_b}{\Theta_i^{\rm pref}} .
      \tag{DHP1}
   \]
   If, for some \(0\le a\le1\),
   \[
      L_k\le a\Theta_i^{\rm pref},
      \qquad
      \mathsf M_{i,k}^{\star}\le1-a,
      \tag{DHP2}
   \]
   then the rank \(k\) satisfies the weak-type water envelope \((TPW2)\).

   Equivalently, any dyadic rank \(k\) that violates \((TPW2)\) and admits
   the certified split \((DTR2)\)--\((DTR3)\) must satisfy, for every
   \(0\le a\le1\), at least one of
   \[
      L_k>a\Theta_i^{\rm pref},
      \qquad
      \mathsf M_{i,k}^{\star}>1-a.
      \tag{DHP3}
   \]
   In particular, if the low branch is controlled by
   \(L_k\le a\Theta_i^{\rm pref}\), then the reported star panel carries
   certified lower paid mass
   \[
      2\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}X_b
      >
      (1-a)\Theta_i^{\rm pref}.
      \tag{DHP4}
   \]
   If no one-record guard-credit repair fires, this high-mass panel is also
   price-saturated:
   \[
      \mathsf P_{i,k}^{\star}
      \ge
      \mathsf M_{i,k}^{\star}
      >
      1-a.
      \tag{DHP5}
   \]

   Consequently, if every dyadic prefix in every active layer admits
   certificates satisfying \((DTR2)\)--\((DTR3)\) and \((DHP2)\) for a chosen
   slack \(a\), and \((PELS5)\) holds, then
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Thus the high side of the dyadic residual is not merely an expensive panel:
   it is a large lower-certified paid-mass panel.  In a no-repair residual the
   same panel must have comparable recursive price record by record.  This is
   the exact saturation object to attack with shared-prefix, integrated-cover,
   range-reporting, facility, additive-quantization, or list-decoding
   proposals.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Under \((DHP2)\), the certified split gives
   \[
      \underline X_{i,k}
      \le
      L_k+H_k
      \le
      L_k+2\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}X_b
      \le
      a\Theta_i^{\rm pref}+(1-a)\Theta_i^{\rm pref}
      =
      \Theta_i^{\rm pref}.
   \]
   By \((DTR1)\), this is exactly \((TPW2)\).  The contrapositive is
   \((DHP3)\), and \((DHP4)\) is the second alternative of \((DHP3)\) under
   the low-branch hypothesis.

   If no one-record guard-credit repair fires, the proof of
   \cref{cor:dyadic-prefix-spread-star-repair} shows \(X_b\le R_b\) for every
   lower-certified raw guard record \(b\).  Summing and normalizing gives the
   first inequality in \((DHP5)\), while \((DHP4)\) gives the second.

   If \((DHP2)\) holds for every dyadic prefix, every dyadic rank satisfies
   \((TPW2)\).  Therefore \cref{cor:dyadic-top-prefix-water-screen} gives
   \((GWL2)\) in every active layer, and
   \cref{cor:gibbs-water-level-storage-screen} gives
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) under \((PELS5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dyadic prefix shared-capture compression screen]
   \label{cor:dyadic-prefix-shared-capture-compression}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:dyadic-prefix-high-star-mass}.  Fix \(0\le a\le1\), and suppose
   the low envelope of the dyadic prefix satisfies
   \(L_k\le a\Theta_i^{\rm pref}\).  Let \(\mathcal C_k\) be a finite family of
   lower-certified raw guard records, with lower paid-shadow certificates
   \(Y_c\) and recursive prices \(P_c\).  A shared-capture certificate for the
   reported star panel \(\mathcal B_k\) consists of nonnegative tail variables
   \(e_b\) and nonnegative assignment variables \(z_{b,c}\) such that
   \[
      X_b\le e_b+\sum_{c\in\mathcal C_k}z_{b,c}
      \qquad(b\in\mathcal B_k),
      \tag{DMC1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}z_{b,c}\le Y_c
      \qquad(c\in\mathcal C_k).
      \tag{DMC2}
   \]
   Define its explicit tail and shared recursive price by
   \[
      E_{\rm sh}=2\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}e_b,
      \qquad
      P_{\rm sh}=2\sum_{c\in\mathcal C_k}P_c .
      \tag{DMC3}
   \]
   If
   \[
      E_{\rm sh}+P_{\rm sh}\le(1-a)\Theta_i^{\rm pref},
      \tag{DMC4}
   \]
   then either the rank \(k\) satisfies the weak-type water envelope
   \((TPW2)\), or a one-record guard-credit repair fires.

   Equivalently, if \(k\) violates \((TPW2)\), the low envelope satisfies
   \(L_k\le a\Theta_i^{\rm pref}\), and no one-record guard-credit repair
   fires, then every shared-capture certificate satisfies
   \[
      E_{\rm sh}+P_{\rm sh}>(1-a)\Theta_i^{\rm pref}.
      \tag{DMC5}
   \]
   In normalized form,
   \[
      \mathsf M_{i,k}^{\star}
      \le
      \frac{E_{\rm sh}+P_{\rm sh}}{\Theta_i^{\rm pref}}
      \tag{DMC6}
   \]
   in every no-repair residual.

   Consequently, the high-star branch may be attacked by a shared-cover
   reporter.  It need not reproduce every original star record: it may leave
   explicit tail \(E_{\rm sh}\), but any mass it assigns into a shared record
   is charged once through that record's recursive price.  If this shared
   tail-plus-price falls below the forced high-star mass from
   \cref{cor:dyadic-prefix-high-star-mass}, the existing guard verifier already
   materializes a repair.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose no one-record guard-credit repair fires.  Since every
   \(c\in\mathcal C_k\) is a lower-certified raw guard record, \(Y_c>P_c\)
   would be a positive one-record panel in
   \cref{cor:lower-certified-scale-free-guard-panel}.  Hence \(Y_c\le P_c\) for
   every \(c\).  Summing \((DMC1)\) over \(b\), using \((DMC2)\), and then
   using \(Y_c\le P_c\), gives
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      2\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}X_b
      &\le
      2\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}e_b
      +2\sum_{c\in\mathcal C_k}\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}z_{b,c} \\
      &\le
      E_{\rm sh}+2\sum_{c\in\mathcal C_k}Y_c
      \le
      E_{\rm sh}+P_{\rm sh}.
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{DMC7}
   \]
   If \((DMC4)\) holds, then
   \(2\sum_bX_b\le(1-a)\Theta_i^{\rm pref}\).  Together with
   \(L_k\le a\Theta_i^{\rm pref}\) and \((DTR2)\)--\((DTR3)\), this gives
   \[
      \underline X_{i,k}
      \le
      L_k+H_k
      \le
      L_k+2\sum_bX_b
      \le
      \Theta_i^{\rm pref}.
   \]
   By \((DTR1)\), this is \((TPW2)\).  Therefore, if \((TPW2)\) fails under
   \((DMC4)\), the no-repair assumption was false, and a one-record
   guard-credit repair fires.

   The contrapositive gives \((DMC5)\).  Finally, \((DMC6)\) is just
   \((DMC7)\) divided by \(\Theta_i^{\rm pref}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite dyadic shared-capture LP]
   \label{cor:finite-dyadic-shared-capture-lp}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:dyadic-prefix-shared-capture-compression}.  Let
   \(\mathcal R_k\) be a finite universe of candidate shared records.  Record
   \(c\in\mathcal R_k\) is a lower-certified raw guard record with recursive
   price \(P_c\), lower paid-shadow certificate \(Y_c\), and nonnegative
   capture profile \(h_{c,b}\) over \(b\in\mathcal B_k\), satisfying
   \[
      \sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}h_{c,b}\le Y_c .
      \tag{DLP1}
   \]
   Consider the finite shared-capture cover
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Phi_k^{\rm sh}=\min
      & \displaystyle
        2\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}e_b
        +2\sum_{c\in\mathcal R_k}\lambda_cP_c\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        e_b+\sum_{c\in\mathcal R_k}\lambda_ch_{c,b}\ge X_b
        \qquad(b\in\mathcal B_k),\\[0.8em]
      & e_b\ge0,\qquad \lambda_c\ge0 .
   \end{array}
      \tag{DLP2}
   \]
   Its dual is
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Phi_k^{\rm sh}=\max
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}X_bu_b\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & 0\le u_b\le2
        \qquad(b\in\mathcal B_k),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}h_{c,b}u_b\le2P_c
        \qquad(c\in\mathcal R_k).
   \end{array}
      \tag{DLP3}
   \]

   If, for the chosen slack \(a\),
   \[
      \Phi_k^{\rm sh}\le(1-a)\Theta_i^{\rm pref},
      \tag{DLP4}
   \]
   then either the rank \(k\) satisfies \((TPW2)\), or a one-record
   guard-credit repair fires.  Conversely, if \(k\) violates \((TPW2)\),
   \(L_k\le a\Theta_i^{\rm pref}\), and no one-record repair fires, then
   \[
      \Phi_k^{\rm sh}>(1-a)\Theta_i^{\rm pref}.
      \tag{DLP5}
   \]
   Thus an optimal dual \(u\) of \((DLP3)\) is an exact finite
   no-shared-capture obstruction:
   \[
      \sum_bX_bu_b>(1-a)\Theta_i^{\rm pref},
      \qquad
      \sum_bh_{c,b}u_b\le2P_c
      \quad(c\in\mathcal R_k).
      \tag{DLP6}
   \]

   Moreover, restricted column generation is exact.  If \(E\subseteq\mathcal
   R_k\) is an active record set and \(u^E\) is an optimal dual for the
   restriction of \((DLP2)\) to \(E\), then any inactive record \(c\notin E\)
   with
   \[
      \sum_bh_{c,b}u_b^E>2P_c
      \tag{DLP7}
   \]
   is a valid improving column.  If no inactive record satisfies \((DLP7)\),
   then the restricted optimum equals the full optimum \(\Phi_k^{\rm sh}\).

   Therefore the high-star dyadic residual has a concrete build-time target:
   solve this finite shared-cover LP, or find a shared record with positive
   dual surplus against its current dual.  Expensive preprocessing may search
   for such records by range reporting, facility, additive quantization,
   list/lattice decoding, or seeded clustering; only verified columns are
   retained.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The primal \((DLP2)\) is feasible by taking \(e_b=X_b\) and all
   \(\lambda_c=0\), and it is bounded below.  Assign a dual variable \(u_b\ge0\)
   to each cover constraint.  The coefficient of \(e_b\) gives \(u_b\le2\), and
   the coefficient of \(\lambda_c\) gives
   \(\sum_bh_{c,b}u_b\le2P_c\).  Finite LP duality proves \((DLP3)\).

   Let \((e,\lambda)\) be feasible for \((DLP2)\).  For each \(c\), replace the
   record by a scaled copy of multiplicity \(\lambda_c\), lower certificate
   \(\lambda_cY_c\), and price \(\lambda_cP_c\), and set
   \(z_{b,c}=\lambda_ch_{c,b}\).  By \((DLP1)\),
   \[
      \sum_bz_{b,c}
      =
      \lambda_c\sum_bh_{c,b}
      \le
      \lambda_cY_c .
   \]
   Thus the feasible LP solution is exactly a shared-capture certificate of the
   form \((DMC1)\)--\((DMC3)\), with
   \(E_{\rm sh}+P_{\rm sh}\) equal to the objective value in \((DLP2)\).  Hence
   \((DLP4)\) implies the closure alternative of
   \cref{cor:dyadic-prefix-shared-capture-compression}.  The contrapositive
   gives \((DLP5)\), and \((DLP6)\) is \((DLP5)\) read through the dual
   equality \((DLP3)\).

   For column generation, the restricted primal and dual are the same finite
   programs with \(\mathcal R_k\) replaced by \(E\).  If \((DLP7)\) holds, then
   \(u^E\) violates the dual constraint for the enlarged active set and hence
   cannot certify the enlarged optimum.  If no inactive record violates
   \((DLP7)\), then \(u^E\) is feasible for the full dual.  The full primal is
   a relaxation of the restricted primal, while the full-dual feasible solution
   \(u^E\) has value equal to the restricted optimum; weak duality gives
   equality of the restricted and full optima.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One-sided dyadic shared-capture oracle]
   \label{cor:one-sided-dyadic-shared-capture-oracle}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:finite-dyadic-shared-capture-lp}.  Let
   \(E\subseteq\mathcal R_k\) be the active record set, and let \(u^E\) be an
   optimal dual for the restriction of \((DLP2)\) to \(E\).  A one-sided
   dyadic shared-capture oracle takes \(u^E\) and either returns an inactive
   record \(c\in\mathcal R_k\setminus E\) with a verifiable certificate
   \[
      \underline H_c>2\overline P_c,
      \qquad
      0\le \underline H_c
      \le
      \sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}h_{c,b}u_b^E,
      \qquad
      P_c\le\overline P_c,
      \tag{DSO1}
   \]
   or correctly certifies that every inactive record satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}h_{c,b}u_b^E\le2P_c .
      \tag{DSO2}
   \]
   Then the oracle is complete for the dyadic shared-capture LP: every
   successful output is a valid improving column, and a no-record certificate
   proves that the restricted optimum is the full optimum \(\Phi_k^{\rm sh}\).

   The positive branch may be implemented in uncharged Las Vegas build time.
   If a randomized proposal routine returns a verified certificate satisfying
   \((DSO1)\) with probability at least \(p_E>0\) whenever some inactive record
   violates \((DLP7)\), repeat until a certificate is accepted; unverifiable
   proposals are discarded and never enter the retained structure.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   A certificate \((DSO1)\) implies
   \[
      \sum_bh_{c,b}u_b^E
      \ge
      \underline H_c
      >
      2\overline P_c
      \ge
      2P_c .
   \]
   Hence \((DLP7)\) holds, so
   \cref{cor:finite-dyadic-shared-capture-lp} may add \(c\) as an improving
   column.  If the oracle certifies \((DSO2)\) for all inactive records, then no
   inactive record satisfies \((DLP7)\), and the same corollary proves full
   optimality of the restricted LP.  For the Las Vegas branch, independent
   repetitions fail \(B\) times with probability at most \((1-p_E)^B\), and only
   verified records are retained.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dyadic shared-capture top-prefix compiler]
   \label{cor:dyadic-shared-capture-top-prefix-compiler}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:one-sided-dyadic-shared-capture-oracle}.  A dyadic shared-capture
   prefix template \(T\) consists of a finite search container
   \(\mathcal B_T\subseteq\mathcal B_k\), nonnegative certified capture weights
   \(g_{T,b}\) for \(b\in\mathcal B_T\), extended by \(g_{T,b}=0\) outside
   \(\mathcal B_T\), available cardinalities \(\mathcal K_T\), and upper prices
   \(\overline P_T(K)\).  Assume that for every \(K\in\mathcal K_T\) and every
   \(U\subseteq\mathcal B_T\) with \(|U|=K\), preprocessing can materialize an
   admissible shared record
   \(c(T,U)\in\mathcal R_k\) satisfying
   \[
      P_{c(T,U)}\le\overline P_T(K),
      \qquad
      h_{c(T,U),b}\ge g_{T,b}\mathbf 1_{\{b\in U\}}
      \quad(b\in\mathcal B_k).
      \tag{DST1}
   \]
   For a restricted dyadic dual \(u\), define the template degree
   \[
      d_T^u(b)=g_{T,b}u_b
      \qquad(b\in\mathcal B_T),
      \tag{DST2}
   \]
   and order \(\mathcal B_T=\{b_1,b_2,\ldots\}\) by nonincreasing
   \(d_T^u(b)\).

   If, for some \(K\in\mathcal K_T\),
   \[
      \sum_{j\le K}d_T^u(b_j)>2\overline P_T(K),
      \tag{DST3}
   \]
   then the top prefix \(U_K=\{b_1,\ldots,b_K\}\) materializes a valid positive
   dyadic shared-capture column.  Conversely, if \((DST3)\) fails for every
   available \(K\), then no \(K\)-subset of this template beats its certified
   lower profile:
   \[
      \sum_{b\in U}g_{T,b}u_b
      \le
      2\overline P_T(K)
      \qquad
      (K\in\mathcal K_T,\ U\subseteq\mathcal B_T,\ |U|=K).
      \tag{DST4}
   \]

   Suppose in addition that \(0<\rho_T<1\), the available cardinalities are
   \(b_T\)-dense from below, and
   \[
      \overline P_T(K)
      =
      \psi_T\left(A_TK^{\rho_T}+\zeta_TK^{1+\rho_T}\right).
      \tag{DST5}
   \]
   If no available top prefix has positive dyadic shared surplus, then every
   nonempty degree superlevel
   \[
      H_{T,\delta}=\{b\in\mathcal B_T:d_T^u(b)\ge\delta\},
      \qquad h=|H_{T,\delta}|,
      \tag{DST6}
   \]
   obeys
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      2\psi_T\left(
         b_T^{1-\rho_T}A_Th^{\rho_T-1}
         +\zeta_Th^{\rho_T}
      \right).
      \tag{DST7}
   \]
   Thus a seeded cluster, additive-quantization cell, range-reporting cell, or
   list/lattice-decoded cell is useful exactly when its current dual-weighted
   top prefix beats the one-time recursive price.  The build step may spend
   arbitrary computation proposing templates, but the retained certificate is
   just the deterministic shared record \(c(T,U_K)\) verified by \((DST1)\) and
   \((DST3)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For a prefix \(U_K\), \((DST1)\) and \((DST3)\) give
   \[
      \sum_bh_{c(T,U_K),b}u_b
      \ge
      \sum_{b\in U_K}g_{T,b}u_b
      =
      \sum_{j\le K}d_T^u(b_j)
      >
      2\overline P_T(K)
      \ge
      2P_{c(T,U_K)} .
   \]
   Hence \((DLP7)\) holds, and
   \cref{cor:finite-dyadic-shared-capture-lp} may add \(c(T,U_K)\).  For fixed
   \(K\), the top \(K\) elements by \(d_T^u\) maximize
   \(\sum_{b\in U}g_{T,b}u_b\) over all \(K\)-subsets, so failure of
   \((DST3)\) for that \(K\) gives \((DST4)\).

   For the weak-type residual, let \(h>0\) and choose
   \(K\in\mathcal K_T\) with \(h/b_T\le K\le h\).  The top \(K\) prefix has
   total template degree at least \(K\delta\).  Since no available top prefix is
   positive, \((DST3)\) fails, and
   \[
      K\delta
      \le
      2\overline P_T(K)
      =
      2\psi_T\left(A_TK^{\rho_T}+\zeta_TK^{1+\rho_T}\right).
   \]
   Dividing by \(K\), using \(K\ge h/b_T\) in the negative exponent
   \(K^{\rho_T-1}\), and using \(K\le h\) in \(K^{\rho_T}\), gives
   \((DST7)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Generated-cell dyadic shared-cover dichotomy]
   \label{cor:generated-cell-dyadic-shared-cover-dichotomy}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:dyadic-shared-capture-top-prefix-compiler}, and fix a finite
   family of generated templates \(\mathcal T\).  Consider the surrogate
   generated-cell cover LP
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Psi_k^{\rm gen}=\min
      & \displaystyle
        2\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}e_b
        +2\sum_{T\in\mathcal T}
          \sum_{K\in\mathcal K_T}
          \sum_{\substack{U\subseteq\mathcal B_T\\ |U|=K}}
          \lambda_{T,U}\overline P_T(K)\\[0.9em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        e_b+
        \sum_{T\in\mathcal T}
        \sum_{K\in\mathcal K_T}
        \sum_{\substack{U\subseteq\mathcal B_T\\ |U|=K}}
        \lambda_{T,U}g_{T,b}\mathbf 1_{\{b\in U\}}
        \ge X_b
        \qquad(b\in\mathcal B_k),\\[0.9em]
      & e_b\ge0,\qquad \lambda_{T,U}\ge0 .
   \end{array}
      \tag{DTC1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \Psi_k^{\rm gen}\le(1-a)\Theta_i^{\rm pref},
      \tag{DTC2}
   \]
   then either the dyadic rank \(k\) satisfies \((TPW2)\), or a one-record
   guard-credit repair fires.

   Conversely, if \(k\) violates \((TPW2)\), \(L_k\le a\Theta_i^{\rm pref}\),
   no one-record guard-credit repair fires, and the generated-cell cover does
   not close, meaning \((DTC2)\) fails, then the dual of \((DTC1)\) has a
   feasible solution \(u\) with
   \[
      \sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}X_bu_b>(1-a)\Theta_i^{\rm pref},
      \qquad
      0\le u_b\le2,
      \tag{DTC3}
   \]
   and for every generated template and available cardinality,
   \[
      \sum_{j\le K}d_T^u(b_j)\le2\overline P_T(K),
      \qquad
      T\in\mathcal T,\ K\in\mathcal K_T,
      \tag{DTC4}
   \]
   where \(b_1,b_2,\ldots\) are ordered inside \(\mathcal B_T\) by
   nonincreasing \(d_T^u\).  In particular, every template in the generated
   family satisfies the weak-type residual envelope \((DST7)\) whenever its
   parameters satisfy \((DST5)\).

   Thus generated cells now have an exact minimax role.  A fractional cover by
   their materializable prefixes closes the dyadic high-star branch; otherwise
   the surviving obstruction is a single dual weighting whose top-prefix tests
   fail in every generated cell.  This is the residual that a geometric,
   additive-quantization, range, or list-decoding theorem must rule out.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Any feasible solution of \((DTC1)\) materializes a feasible solution of the
   full dyadic shared-capture LP \((DLP2)\): replace each active
   \((T,U)\) by the admissible record \(c(T,U)\), use
   \((DST1)\) to dominate the cover coefficients, and use
   \(P_{c(T,U)}\le\overline P_T(|U|)\) to dominate the price.  Therefore
   \(\Phi_k^{\rm sh}\le\Psi_k^{\rm gen}\), and \((DTC2)\) implies \((DLP4)\).
   The closure statement follows from
   \cref{cor:finite-dyadic-shared-capture-lp}.

   The dual of \((DTC1)\) is
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Psi_k^{\rm gen}=\max
      & \displaystyle \sum_{b\in\mathcal B_k}X_bu_b\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & 0\le u_b\le2,\\[0.6em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{b\in U}g_{T,b}u_b
        \le2\overline P_T(K)
        \qquad
        (T\in\mathcal T,\ K\in\mathcal K_T,\ U\subseteq\mathcal B_T,\ |U|=K).
   \end{array}
      \tag{DTC5}
   \]
   The primal is finite and feasible by taking \(e_b=X_b\), so finite LP
   duality applies.  If the generated-cell cover does not close in the stated
   no-repair bad-prefix situation, then \((DTC2)\) fails, so
   \(\Psi_k^{\rm gen}>(1-a)\Theta_i^{\rm pref}\).  An optimal dual for
   \((DTC5)\) gives \((DTC3)\).

   For fixed \(T\) and \(K\), the \(K\)-element subset maximizing
   \(\sum_{b\in U}g_{T,b}u_b\) is the top \(K\) prefix in the order of
   \(d_T^u(b)=g_{T,b}u_b\).  Hence the subset constraints in \((DTC5)\) are
   equivalent to \((DTC4)\).  Applying the weak-type part of
   \cref{cor:dyadic-shared-capture-top-prefix-compiler} to each template gives
   \((DST7)\) under \((DST5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dyadic dual-mass low-cover closure]
   \label{cor:dyadic-dual-mass-low-cover-closure}
   Work in the no-cell-dual residual of
   \cref{cor:generated-cell-dyadic-shared-cover-dichotomy}, so a dual \(u\)
   satisfies \((DTC4)\) for every generated template in \(\mathcal T\).  Let
   \(L\subseteq\mathcal B_k\) be any set of dyadic star records, and suppose
   \(L\) is assigned to generated templates by a map \(\kappa:L\to\mathcal T\)
   such that
   \[
      b\in\mathcal B_{\kappa(b)},
      \qquad
      g_{\kappa(b),b}\ge X_b
      \qquad(b\in L).
      \tag{DLC1}
   \]
   For \(T\in\mathcal T\), put
   \[
      L_T=\{b\in L:\kappa(b)=T\},
      \qquad
      K_T=|L_T|,
      \tag{DLC2}
   \]
   and discard empty parts.  Then every such assigned cover obeys
   \[
      \sum_{b\in L}X_bu_b
      \le
      2\sum_{T:\,K_T>0}\overline P_T(K_T),
      \tag{DLC3}
   \]
   provided \(K_T\in\mathcal K_T\) for every nonempty part.  Equivalently, if
   some assigned cover satisfying \((DLC1)\)--\((DLC2)\) has
   \[
      \sum_{b\in L}X_bu_b
      >
      2\sum_{T:\,K_T>0}\overline P_T(K_T),
      \tag{DLC4}
   \]
   then at least one generated template contains a positive dyadic shared
   top-prefix column.

   In particular, suppose all used templates satisfy, for common parameters
   \(0<\rho<1\), \(A,\zeta,\psi_\star\),
   \[
      \overline P_T(K)
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(AK^\rho+\zeta K^{1+\rho}\right)
      \qquad(K\in\mathcal K_T),
      \tag{DLC5}
   \]
   and at most \(J\) templates are used.  With \(K=|L|\), every no-cell-dual
   residual satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{b\in L}X_bu_b
      \le
      2\psi_\star\left(AJ^{1-\rho}K^\rho+\zeta K^{1+\rho}\right).
      \tag{DLC6}
   \]
   Thus any dual-heavy set whose \(X_b\)-capturing cover has smaller Renyi
   price cannot survive: one of the generated cells must already contain the
   verified top-prefix column required by
   \cref{cor:dyadic-shared-capture-top-prefix-compiler}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed nonempty part \(L_T\), every \(b\in L_T\) has
   \(d_T^u(b)=g_{T,b}u_b\ge X_bu_b\) by \((DLC1)\).  The top \(K_T\) prefix of
   \(\mathcal B_T\) by \(d_T^u\)-degree therefore has degree at least
   \[
      \sum_{b\in L_T}X_bu_b .
   \]
   Since the residual satisfies \((DTC4)\),
   \[
      \sum_{b\in L_T}X_bu_b
      \le
      2\overline P_T(K_T).
   \]
   Summing over the nonempty parts gives \((DLC3)\).  Its contrapositive gives
   \((DLC4)\), with the positive column supplied by
   \cref{cor:dyadic-shared-capture-top-prefix-compiler}.

   Under \((DLC5)\), Hölder's inequality gives
   \[
      \sum_TK_T^\rho\le J^{1-\rho}K^\rho,
   \]
   while \(1+\rho\ge1\) and disjointness give
   \[
      \sum_TK_T^{1+\rho}\le K^{1+\rho}.
   \]
   Substituting these two bounds into \((DLC3)\) proves \((DLC6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[No-cell dual entropy witness]
   \label{cor:no-cell-dual-entropy-witness}
   Work in the no-cell-dual residual of
   \cref{cor:generated-cell-dyadic-shared-cover-dichotomy}, and assume the
   common price envelope \((DLC5)\) for every used generated template.  Let
   \(L\subseteq\mathcal B_k\), put \(K=|L|>0\), and suppose
   \[
      X_bu_b\ge\theta
      \qquad(b\in L)
      \tag{DME1}
   \]
   for some \(\theta>0\).  If \(L\) admits an assignment to at most \(J\)
   generated templates satisfying \((DLC1)\)--\((DLC2)\), with every nonempty
   part cardinality available, then
   \[
      \theta K
      \le
      2\psi_\star\left(AJ^{1-\rho}K^\rho+\zeta K^{1+\rho}\right).
      \tag{DME2}
   \]
   Consequently, if the storage term is not already dominant, in the sense that
   \[
      \theta>4\psi_\star\zeta K^\rho,
      \tag{DME3}
   \]
   then every compatible generated-cell cover of \(L\) uses
   \[
      J
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{\theta K^{1-\rho}}{4\psi_\star A}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \tag{DME4}
   \]
   nonempty template parts.  When \(\zeta=0\), the same conclusion holds with
   \(4\) replaced by \(2\) in \((DME4)\).

   In particular, let \(w_b=X_bu_b\), and suppose the positive weights in a set
   \(W\subseteq\mathcal B_k\) lie in \([w_{\min},w_{\max}]\).  With
   \[
      J_w=1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{w_{\max}}{w_{\min}}\right\rceil,
      \tag{DME5}
   \]
   some dyadic layer
   \[
      L_j=\{b\in W:2^jw_{\min}\le w_b<2^{j+1}w_{\min}\}
      \tag{DME6}
   \]
   satisfies, for \(\theta_j=2^jw_{\min}\),
   \[
      \theta_j|L_j|
      \ge
      \frac1{2J_w}\sum_{b\in W}X_bu_b .
      \tag{DME7}
   \]
   Hence any large no-cell dual mass contains an almost-uniform superlevel on
   which either storage price dominates as in \((DME3)\), or the compatible
   generated-cell covering number obeys the lower bound \((DME4)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(X_bu_b\ge\theta\) on \(L\),
   \[
      \theta K\le\sum_{b\in L}X_bu_b .
   \]
   Applying \((DLC6)\) gives \((DME2)\).  If \((DME3)\) holds, then the storage
   contribution in \((DME2)\) is strictly smaller than \(\theta K/2\).  Thus
   \[
      \frac{\theta K}{2}
      \le
      2\psi_\star A J^{1-\rho}K^\rho,
   \]
   which rearranges to \((DME4)\).  When \(\zeta=0\), the storage contribution
   vanishes and the same rearrangement starts from
   \(\theta K\le2\psi_\star AJ^{1-\rho}K^\rho\), giving the constant \(2\).

   The dyadic layers in \((DME6)\) partition the positive weights in \(W\).
   On each layer, \(w_b<2\theta_j\), and therefore
   \[
      \sum_j\theta_j|L_j|
      \ge
      \frac12\sum_{b\in W}w_b .
   \]
   One layer must contribute at least the average over the \(J_w\) possible
   layers, giving \((DME7)\).  Applying the first part to that layer gives the
   final statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[No-cell metric-cover screen]
   \label{cor:no-cell-metric-cover-screen}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:no-cell-dual-entropy-witness}.  Let
   \(L\subseteq\mathcal B_k\) and \(K=|L|>0\) satisfy \((DME1)\).  Suppose
   \(L\) has a certified container cover \(C_1,\ldots,C_J\).  This means that,
   after assigning each \(b\in L\) to one covering container \(C_i\), the parts
   \(L_i=\{b:\kappa(b)=i\}\) have generated template copies \(T_i\in\mathcal T\)
   such that
   \[
      b\in\mathcal B_{T_i},
      \qquad
      g_{T_i,b}\ge X_b
      \qquad(b\in L_i),
      \tag{DMS1}
   \]
   and \(|L_i|\in\mathcal K_{T_i}\) whenever \(L_i\ne\emptyset\).  Then every
   no-cell residual satisfies
   \[
      \theta K
      \le
      2\psi_\star\left(AJ^{1-\rho}K^\rho+\zeta K^{1+\rho}\right).
      \tag{DMS2}
   \]
   Hence, if
   \[
      \theta>4\psi_\star\zeta K^\rho
      \tag{DMS3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      J
      <
      \left(
         \frac{\theta K^{1-\rho}}{4\psi_\star A}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)},
      \tag{DMS4}
   \]
   the cover cannot survive the no-cell residual: some generated template has
   a positive dyadic shared top-prefix column.  When \(\zeta=0\), the same
   statement holds with \(4\) replaced by \(2\) in \((DMS4)\).

   Equivalently, define the certified generated-cover number \(N_{\rm gen}(L)\)
   as the minimum number of container parts in a cover satisfying \((DMS1)\) and
   the cardinality availability condition.  In every no-cell residual, every
   dyadic layer satisfying \((DMS3)\) obeys
   \[
      N_{\rm gen}(L)
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{\theta K^{1-\rho}}{4\psi_\star A}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho)}.
      \tag{DMS5}
   \]
   Thus a low-doubling or list-decoded cover of the layer is enough only after
   it is certified in this generated-template sense, but once certified it is
   charged by the same one-line Renyi cover threshold.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The container assignment gives an assignment of every \(b\in L\) to the
   generated template copy \(T_{\kappa(b)}\).  Conditions \((DMS1)\) and the
   cardinality availability hypothesis are exactly \((DLC1)\)--\((DLC2)\) for
   this assignment, using at most \(J\) templates.  Applying
   \cref{cor:no-cell-dual-entropy-witness} gives \((DMS2)\) and the lower bound
   \((DMS5)\) under \((DMS3)\).  If a cover used fewer parts than the right
   side of \((DMS5)\), it would contradict the no-cell alternative; by
   \cref{cor:dyadic-dual-mass-low-cover-closure}, the contrapositive is a
   positive top-prefix column.  The \(\zeta=0\) constant is inherited from
   \cref{cor:no-cell-dual-entropy-witness}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Low-doubling no-cell density screen]
   \label{cor:low-doubling-no-cell-density-screen}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:no-cell-metric-cover-screen}.  For a
   certified generated-container family \(\mathcal C_\lambda\), let
   \(N_{\rm gen}(L,\lambda)\) be the minimum number of nonempty parts in a cover
   of \(L\) by containers from \(\mathcal C_\lambda\) satisfying \((DMS1)\) and
   the cardinality availability condition.  If \(L\) has size \(K>0\) and
   satisfies \(X_bu_b\ge\theta\) for all \(b\in L\), then every no-cell
   residual satisfies
   \[
      \theta
      \le
      2\psi_\star\left(
         A\,N_{\rm gen}(L,\lambda)^{1-\rho}K^{\rho-1}
         +\zeta K^\rho
      \right).
      \tag{DLD1}
   \]
   In particular, if the family has certified low-doubling growth
   \[
      N_{\rm gen}(L,\lambda)\le C_{\rm dbl}\lambda^{-\delta},
      \qquad 0<\lambda\le1,
      \tag{DLD2}
   \]
   then every no-cell residual obeys the density envelope
   \[
      \theta
      \le
      2\psi_\star\left(
         A\,C_{\rm dbl}^{1-\rho}
         \lambda^{-\delta(1-\rho)}K^{\rho-1}
         +\zeta K^\rho
      \right).
      \tag{DLD3}
   \]
   Therefore a dyadic layer whose weight density violates \((DLD3)\) cannot be
   a genuine no-cell residual: one of the generated template copies in the cover
   contains a positive dyadic shared top-prefix column.

   Equivalently, when \(\zeta=0\), a surviving layer must have generated
   covering dimension at any scale \(0<\lambda<1\) at least
   \[
      \delta
      \ge
      \frac{
         \log\!\left(\theta K^{1-\rho}/(2\psi_\star A)\right)
         -(1-\rho)\log C_{\rm dbl}
      }{
         (1-\rho)\log(1/\lambda)
      },
      \tag{DLD4}
   \]
   whenever the numerator is positive.  With \(\zeta>0\), the same statement
   holds after replacing \(\theta\) by
   \(\theta-2\psi_\star\zeta K^\rho\) when this quantity is positive.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{cor:no-cell-metric-cover-screen} to an optimal generated cover
   with \(J=N_{\rm gen}(L,\lambda)\).  Dividing \((DMS2)\) by \(K\) gives
   \((DLD1)\).  Substituting \((DLD2)\) proves \((DLD3)\).

   If a layer violated \((DLD3)\), the cover with at most
   \(C_{\rm dbl}\lambda^{-\delta}\) parts would violate \((DMS2)\).  The
   contrapositive in \cref{cor:no-cell-metric-cover-screen} then gives the
   positive top-prefix column.

   For \(\zeta=0\), rearrange \((DLD3)\):
   \[
      \lambda^{-\delta(1-\rho)}
      \ge
      \frac{\theta K^{1-\rho}}
           {2\psi_\star A C_{\rm dbl}^{1-\rho}} .
   \]
   Taking logarithms gives \((DLD4)\).  If \(\zeta>0\) and
   \(\theta>2\psi_\star\zeta K^\rho\), subtract the storage term in
   \((DLD3)\) before the same rearrangement.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Paid-responsibility high-correlation star compiler]
   \label{cor:paid-responsibility-high-correlation-star}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-stars-feed-guard-credit}.  Let
   \(\mathcal X\subseteq P\) be a finite set of proposed centers.  For each
   \(x\in\mathcal X\), let \(W_x\) be an affordable certified container with
   size certificate \(|W_x|\le K_x\) and congestion parameter \(C_x>0\).
   Suppose a reporter gives responsibilities
   \[
      0\le \eta_{x,p,q}\le1
      \qquad
      (x\in\mathcal X,\ (p,q)\in\mathcal N)
   \]
   supported only when \(p\in W_x\) and \((x,p)\) is certified
   high-correlation in the sense of \((HPS1)\).  Define
   \[
      M_x(p)=
      \sum_{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \eta_{x,p,q}\,y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{RSG1}
   \]
   Then the star multiplicities \(M_x(p)\) satisfy the domination condition
   \((HCG1)\) for every superlevel \(U_{x,t}=\{p:M_x(p)\ge t\}\).  Therefore
   any finite superlevel panel whose certified lower masses
   \(X_{x,t}=t|U_{x,t}|\) satisfy \((HCG3)\) separates the zero-objective
   guard-credit dual.

   Equivalently, the reporter may work directly with the responsibility tensor:
   the only paid-mass certificate needed for a star level is
   \[
      X_{x,t}=t|\{p:M_x(p)\ge t\}|,
      \tag{RSG2}
   \]
   and this certificate is valid because it is built from a subassignment of
   the paid near-shadow degrees.

   In particular, if all positive \(M_x(p)\) lie in
   \([M_{\min},M_{\max}]\), let \(J_{\rm mult}\) be as in \((HPS6)\) and put
   \[
      W_{\rm resp}=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\sum_{p\in P}M_x(p).
      \tag{RSG3}
   \]
   If \(K_x\le K_0\) and \(R(W_x,K_x,C_x)\le R_0\) for every active center,
   and if
   \[
      X_0=\frac{W_{\rm resp}}{2|P|J_{\rm mult}}>0,
      \qquad
      X_0>R_0,
      \tag{RSG4}
   \]
   then a single responsibility-induced high-correlation star separates the
   guard-credit dual.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For \(p\in W_x\),
   \[
      M_x(p)
      \le
      \sum_{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N}y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      =
      d_{W_x,y}^{\gamma}(p),
   \]
   because every responsibility coefficient is at most one.  This is exactly
   \((HCG1)\).  The first two conclusions are therefore
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-stars-feed-guard-credit}.

   For the final statement, form the weighted edge family by taking one record
   for every positive triple \((x,p,q)\), with edge \((x,p)\) and weight
   \(\eta_{x,p,q}y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}\).  The support hypothesis makes every
   edge high-correlation, and the induced star multiplicities are precisely
   \(M_x(p)\).  Thus
   \cref{lem:high-correlation-pair-star-reporter} gives a center \(x\) and
   level \(t\) with \(X_{x,t}\ge X_0\).  The same comparison as in the final
   paragraph of \cref{cor:high-correlation-stars-feed-guard-credit} then turns
   \((RSG4)\) into the one-record surplus \((HCG3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Pair-compatible guard transport gives responsibility stars]
   \label{cor:pair-compatible-guard-responsibility-star}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:paid-responsibility-high-correlation-star}.  Let
   \(G(q)\subseteq H(q)\cap\mathcal X\) be guard witnesses, and suppose there
   are transport
   variables
   \[
      \pi_{q,x,p}\ge0
      \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q,\ x\in G(q),\ p\in P)
   \]
   supported only when \((p,q)\in\mathcal N\), \(p\in W_x\), and \((x,p)\) is
   certified high-correlation in the sense of \((HPS1)\).  Assume the shipped
   guard mass is
   \[
      M=
      \sum_q\tau_qy_q
      \sum_{x\in G(q)}\sum_p\pi_{q,x,p},
      \tag{PCR1}
   \]
   and the transport is pair-compatible with congestion \(C\):
   \[
      \tau_qy_q\sum_{x\in G(q)}\pi_{q,x,p}
      \le
      C\,y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      \qquad((p,q)\in\mathcal N).
      \tag{PCR2}
   \]
   Then there is a paid-responsibility tensor supported on the same
   high-correlation triples with total responsibility mass
   \[
      W_{\rm resp}
      =
      \frac{M}{C}.
      \tag{PCR3}
   \]
   Consequently, if the positive induced multiplicities lie in
   \([M_{\min},M_{\max}]\), \(J_{\rm mult}\) is as in \((HPS6)\), all active
   containers satisfy \(K_x\le K_0\) and \(R(W_x,K_x,C_x)\le R_0\), and
   \[
      X_0=
      \frac{M}{2C|P|J_{\rm mult}}>0,
      \qquad
      X_0>R_0,
      \tag{PCR4}
   \]
   then a single high-correlation guard star separates the zero-objective
   guard-credit dual.

   Thus the remaining geometric reporter may be phrased as a pair-compatible
   high-correlation shipment of guard load into paid near-shadow capacity; the
   responsibility and layer-cake conversion are automatic.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For triples with \(y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}>0\), define
   \[
      \eta_{x,p,q}=
      \frac{\tau_q\pi_{q,x,p}}{C\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}},
   \]
   and set \(\eta_{x,p,q}=0\) otherwise.  By \((PCR2)\), every such
   \(\eta_{x,p,q}\) lies in \([0,1]\).  Its total responsibility mass is
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \sum_{x,p,q}\eta_{x,p,q}y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      &=
      \frac1C
      \sum_{q,x,p}\tau_qy_q\pi_{q,x,p} \\
      &=
      \frac{M}{C}.
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   The support assumptions are exactly those required by
   \cref{cor:paid-responsibility-high-correlation-star}.  Applying that
   corollary gives the final claim with \(W_{\rm resp}=M/C\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Pair-compatible guard transport cut normal form]
   \label{lem:pair-compatible-guard-cut-normal-form}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:pair-compatible-guard-responsibility-star}.  Fix a pair congestion
   \(C_{\rm pair}>0\).  Let
   \[
      \mathcal I=\{(q,x):q\in\mathcal Q,\ x\in G(q)\},
      \qquad
      b_{q,x}=\tau_qy_q,
      \tag{PCG0}
   \]
   and let
   \[
      \mathcal J=\{(p,q):(p,q)\in\mathcal N\},
      \qquad
      c_{p,q}=C_{\rm pair}\,y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{PCG1}
   \]
   Join \(i=(q,x)\in\mathcal I\) to \(j=(p,q')\in\mathcal J\) when
   \(q'=q\), \(p\in W_x\), and \((x,p)\) is certified high-correlation in the
   sense of \((HPS1)\).  Let \(\Phi_{\rm pc}\) be the maximum of
   \[
      \sum_{(q,x,p)}f_{q,x,p}
   \]
   over nonnegative variables supported on these edges and satisfying
   \[
      \sum_p f_{q,x,p}\le b_{q,x}
      \qquad((q,x)\in\mathcal I),
      \tag{PCG2}
   \]
   \[
      \sum_{x\in G(q)}f_{q,x,p}\le c_{p,q}
      \qquad((p,q)\in\mathcal J).
      \tag{PCG3}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \Phi_{\rm pc}
      =
      \min_{\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal I}
      \left\{
         \sum_{i\in\mathcal I\setminus\mathcal A}b_i
         +
         \sum_{j\in N(\mathcal A)}c_j
      \right\},
      \tag{PCG4}
   \]
   where \(N(\mathcal A)\) is the set of pair-capacity nodes adjacent to
   \(\mathcal A\).  Consequently, for \(0\le M_0\le\sum_ib_i\), a
   pair-compatible high-correlation shipment of mass at least \(M_0\) exists if
   and only if every \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal I\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{i\in\mathcal A}b_i
      \le
      \sum_{j\in N(\mathcal A)}c_j
      +
      \sum_ib_i-M_0 .
      \tag{PCG5}
   \]
   In particular, all guard-incidence mass can be shipped if and only if
   \[
      \sum_{i\in\mathcal A}b_i
      \le
      \sum_{j\in N(\mathcal A)}c_j
      \qquad(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal I).
      \tag{PCG6}
   \]

   Moreover any feasible \(f\) of mass \(M\) induces transport variables
   \(\pi_{q,x,p}=f_{q,x,p}/(\tau_qy_q)\) when \(\tau_qy_q>0\), and zero
   otherwise, satisfying \((PCR1)\)--\((PCR2)\) with \(C=C_{\rm pair}\).
   Thus if the hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:pair-compatible-guard-responsibility-star} hold with this \(M\),
   the same flow produces a separating guard-credit star.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   This is the max-flow/min-cut theorem on the bipartite network with source
   edges of capacities \(b_i\), middle edges \(i\to j\) of infinite capacity
   whenever \(j\in N(\{i\})\), and sink edges of capacities \(c_j\).  A finite
   \(s\)-\(t\) cut is determined by the subset \(\mathcal A\) of left nodes kept
   on the source side; all adjacent right nodes \(N(\mathcal A)\) must also be
   on the source side.  Its capacity is exactly the expression in \((PCG4)\).
   The equivalence \((PCG5)\) is just \(\Phi_{\rm pc}\ge M_0\) rewritten using
   \((PCG4)\), and \((PCG6)\) is the case \(M_0=\sum_ib_i\).

   For the final statement, define \(\pi_{q,x,p}=f_{q,x,p}/(\tau_qy_q)\) on
   positive-load guard incidences and zero otherwise.  Then \((PCG2)\) gives
   \(\sum_p\pi_{q,x,p}\le1\), while
   \[
      \sum_q\tau_qy_q\sum_{x,p}\pi_{q,x,p}
      =
      \sum_{q,x,p}f_{q,x,p}
      =
      M.
   \]
   Finally, \((PCG3)\) is exactly \((PCR2)\) with \(C=C_{\rm pair}\).  Therefore
   \cref{cor:pair-compatible-guard-responsibility-star} applies whenever its
   remaining layer-cake and price hypotheses are satisfied.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Geometric Hall form of pair-compatible guard transport]
   \label{cor:geometric-hall-pair-compatible-guard}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{lem:pair-compatible-guard-cut-normal-form}, and write
   \[
      B_{\rm pc}=\sum_q\tau_qy_q|G(q)|.
      \tag{GHP0}
   \]
   For a sublayer \(G'(q)\subseteq G(q)\), define its certified
   high-correlation paid neighborhood by
   \[
      N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)
      =
      \left\{
         p:(p,q)\in\mathcal N,
         \exists x\in G'(q)\text{ with }p\in W_x
         \text{ and }(x,p)\text{ satisfying }(HPS1)
      \right\}.
      \tag{GHP1}
   \]
   Then a pair-compatible high-correlation shipment of mass at least \(M_0\)
   exists if and only if every choice of sublayers \(G'(q)\subseteq G(q)\)
   satisfies
   \[
      \sum_q\tau_qy_q|G'(q)|
      \le
      C_{\rm pair}
      \sum_q
      \sum_{p\in N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)}
      y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      +
      B_{\rm pc}-M_0 .
      \tag{GHP2}
   \]
   In particular, if no shipment of mass \(B_{\rm pc}/2\) exists, then there is
   a guard sublayer \(G'\) with
   \[
      \sum_q\tau_qy_q|G'(q)|>\frac{B_{\rm pc}}2
      \tag{GHP3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      C_{\rm pair}
      \sum_q
      \sum_{p\in N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)}
      y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      <
      \sum_q\tau_qy_q|G'(q)|-\frac{B_{\rm pc}}2 .
      \tag{GHP4}
   \]

   Conversely, if \((GHP2)\) holds for some \(M_0\), and the induced flow can
   be chosen with positive star multiplicities in a certified range
   \([M_{\min},M_{\max}]\), then
   \cref{cor:pair-compatible-guard-responsibility-star} applies with
   \(M=M_0\).  Thus, under the layer-cake and recursive-price inequalities in
   \((PCR4)\), the geometric Hall inequalities imply a separating
   guard-credit star.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{lem:pair-compatible-guard-cut-normal-form} to the subset
   \[
      \mathcal A=\{(q,x):x\in G'(q)\}.
   \]
   Its load is \(\sum_q\tau_qy_q|G'(q)|\), and its neighboring right nodes are
   precisely the pairs \((p,q)\) with \(p\in N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)\).  Therefore
   \((PCG5)\) is exactly \((GHP2)\).  The half-mass statement is the
   contrapositive with \(M_0=B_{\rm pc}/2\): a failed shipment gives a sublayer
   violating \((GHP2)\), which is \((GHP4)\), and since the right hand side of
   \((GHP4)\) is positive, \((GHP3)\) follows.

   If \((GHP2)\) holds, then \cref{lem:pair-compatible-guard-cut-normal-form}
   gives a shipment of mass \(M_0\).  Under the stated dynamic-range
   certification, the final sentence is exactly
   \cref{cor:pair-compatible-guard-responsibility-star}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Fractional Hall obstruction for pair-compatible guards]
   \label{lem:fractional-pair-compatible-hall-obstruction}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:geometric-hall-pair-compatible-guard}.  Define the fractional
   bad-sublayer value
   \[
      \Psi_{\rm pc}
      =
      \max_{\zeta,\omega}
      \left\{
      \sum_q\tau_qy_q\sum_{x\in G(q)}\zeta_{q,x}
      -
      C_{\rm pair}
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}\,\omega_{p,q}
      \right\},
      \tag{FHG1}
   \]
   where
   \[
      0\le\zeta_{q,x}\le1,
      \qquad
      0\le\omega_{p,q}\le1,
      \tag{FHG2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \zeta_{q,x}\le\omega_{p,q}
      \tag{FHG3}
   \]
   whenever \(x\in G(q)\), \((p,q)\in\mathcal N\), \(p\in W_x\), and
   \((x,p)\) is certified high-correlation in the sense of \((HPS1)\).
   Then a pair-compatible high-correlation shipment of mass at least \(M_0\)
   exists if and only if
   \[
      \Psi_{\rm pc}\le B_{\rm pc}-M_0 .
      \tag{FHG4}
   \]
   In particular, if no half-shipment exists, then
   \[
      \Psi_{\rm pc}>\frac{B_{\rm pc}}2.
      \tag{FHG5}
   \]
   Equivalently, there is a feasible fractional pair
   \((\zeta,\omega)\) with load
   \[
      L(\zeta)=\sum_q\tau_qy_q\sum_{x\in G(q)}\zeta_{q,x}
   \]
   and paid neighborhood capacity
   \[
      C(\omega)=
      C_{\rm pair}
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}\,\omega_{p,q}
   \]
   such that
   \[
      L(\zeta)> \frac{B_{\rm pc}}2,
      \qquad
      C(\omega)<L(\zeta)-\frac{B_{\rm pc}}2 .
      \tag{FHG6}
   \]
   The optimum in \((FHG1)\) may always be chosen integral; then
   \(\zeta\) is the indicator of guard sublayers \(G'(q)\), and
   \(\omega\) is the indicator of the corresponding certified
   high-correlation paid neighborhoods \(N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For an integral choice
   \[
      \zeta_{q,x}=\mathbf 1\{x\in G'(q)\},
   \]
   the cheapest feasible \(\omega\) is exactly the indicator of the neighboring
   paid pair nodes, namely \(p\in N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)\).  Thus the integral value
   of \((FHG1)\) is
   \[
      \sum_q\tau_qy_q|G'(q)|
      -
      C_{\rm pair}
      \sum_q\sum_{p\in N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)}
      y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{FHG7}
   \]
   By \cref{cor:geometric-hall-pair-compatible-guard}, a shipment of mass
   \(M_0\) exists exactly when this quantity is at most \(B_{\rm pc}-M_0\) for
   every sublayer \(G'\).

   It remains only to check that the displayed fractional relaxation has no
   integrality gap.  The constraint matrix of
   \[
      \zeta_{q,x}-\omega_{p,q}\le0
   \]
   over the high-correlation incidence graph is the directed incidence matrix
   of a bipartite graph, with some columns sign-reversed.  Such matrices are
   totally unimodular, and appending the identity rows for the bounds
   \((FHG2)\) preserves total unimodularity.  Since the right hand sides are
   integral, every vertex of the polytope \((FHG2)\)--\((FHG3)\) is integral.
   A linear objective therefore has an integral optimum, and the fractional
   optimum equals the maximum integral value in \((FHG7)\).  This proves
   \((FHG4)\).  The half-shipment statement is the case \(M_0=B_{\rm pc}/2\),
   and \((FHG6)\) is just the inequality
   \(L(\zeta)-C(\omega)>B_{\rm pc}/2\) rewritten.
\end{proof}

The fractional Hall form is the exact local version of the dense-overlap LP at
the current bottleneck.  The variables \(\zeta\) choose guard incidences and the
variables \(\omega\) pay for their certified paid-near-pair closure.  Because
the paid-neighborhood term is a submodular union cost, one should not replace
this condition by a scalar prefix or quantile rule without an additional
geometric separator.  What \cref{lem:fractional-pair-compatible-hall-obstruction}
does give is a finite column-generation target: a proposal family for
k-means++ centers, additive-quantization records, lattice/list decoders, or
LP-range-reporting cells is successful exactly when it separates this
fractional obstruction by producing a lower-certified guard-credit column.

\begin{corollary}[Exact-load Hall closure profile]
   \label{cor:exact-load-pair-compatible-hall-profile}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{lem:fractional-pair-compatible-hall-obstruction}.  For
   \(0\le\Lambda\le B_{\rm pc}\), define the exact-load paid-closure profile
   \[
      S_{\rm pc}(\Lambda)
      =
      \min_{\zeta,\omega}
      C_{\rm pair}
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}\,\omega_{p,q},
      \tag{EHP1}
   \]
   where \((\zeta,\omega)\) satisfy \((FHG2)\)--\((FHG3)\) and the exact-load
   constraint
   \[
      \sum_q\tau_qy_q\sum_{x\in G(q)}\zeta_{q,x}
      =
      \Lambda .
      \tag{EHP2}
   \]
   Then a pair-compatible half-shipment exists if and only if
   \[
      S_{\rm pc}(\Lambda)\ge \Lambda-\frac{B_{\rm pc}}2
      \qquad
      \left(\frac{B_{\rm pc}}2<\Lambda\le B_{\rm pc}\right).
      \tag{EHP3}
   \]
   Equivalently, half-shipment failure is exactly the existence of an
   excess-load level \(\Lambda>B_{\rm pc}/2\) with
   \[
      S_{\rm pc}(\Lambda)<\Lambda-\frac{B_{\rm pc}}2 .
      \tag{EHP4}
   \]

   Moreover \(S_{\rm pc}\) is the lower convex envelope of the integral
   sublayer load-capacity pairs
   \[
      \left(
      \sum_q\tau_qy_q|G'(q)|,\,
      C_{\rm pair}
      \sum_q\sum_{p\in N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)}
      y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      \right),
      \tag{EHP5}
   \]
   where \(G'(q)\subseteq G(q)\).  Hence any exact-load optimizer can be chosen
   as a convex combination of at most two integral guard sublayers.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{lem:fractional-pair-compatible-hall-obstruction}, a half-shipment
   exists if and only if every feasible fractional pair satisfies
   \[
      L(\zeta)-C(\omega)\le \frac{B_{\rm pc}}2 .
      \tag{EHP6}
   \]
   Fixing \(L(\zeta)=\Lambda\), the largest possible value of
   \(L(\zeta)-C(\omega)\) is \(\Lambda-S_{\rm pc}(\Lambda)\).  Therefore
   \((EHP6)\) for all feasible pairs is equivalent to
   \[
      \Lambda-S_{\rm pc}(\Lambda)\le \frac{B_{\rm pc}}2
   \]
   for every \(\Lambda\).  For \(\Lambda\le B_{\rm pc}/2\) this inequality is
   automatic because \(S_{\rm pc}(\Lambda)\ge0\).  For
   \(\Lambda>B_{\rm pc}/2\) it is exactly \((EHP3)\).  This proves the
   half-shipment equivalence and its negation \((EHP4)\).

   The polytope \((FHG2)\)--\((FHG3)\) is integral by the total-unimodularity
   argument in \cref{lem:fractional-pair-compatible-hall-obstruction}.  Project
   this integral polytope to the two coordinates \(L(\zeta)\) and
   \(C(\omega)\).  For any integral choice of guard sublayers, the cheapest
   feasible paid closure is the indicator of
   \(N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)\); adding redundant paid nodes can only increase the
   projected \(C\)-coordinate, or leave it unchanged when their capacity is
   zero.  Therefore the lower envelope of the projected feasible set is the
   lower convex envelope of the integral pairs \((EHP5)\).  Minimizing \(C\) at
   a fixed value of \(L=\Lambda\) takes a point on this planar lower envelope.
   Every such point is either one projected vertex or lies on one edge between
   two projected vertices, so an optimizer is a convex combination of at most
   two integral sublayers.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Integral Hall-deficit normal form]
   \label{cor:integral-hall-deficit-normal-form}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:exact-load-pair-compatible-hall-profile}.  For a guard sublayer
   \(G'(q)\subseteq G(q)\), write
   \[
      L(G')=\sum_q\tau_qy_q|G'(q)|,
      \tag{IHD1}
   \]
   \[
      C(G')=
      C_{\rm pair}
      \sum_q
      \sum_{p\in N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)}
      y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
      \tag{IHD2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \Delta(G')=L(G')-\frac{B_{\rm pc}}2-C(G') .
      \tag{IHD3}
   \]
   Then the exact-load profile has a strict deficit, i.e. \((EHP4)\) holds for
   some \(\Lambda\), if and only if there is an integral guard sublayer \(G'\)
   with
   \[
      \Delta(G')>0 .
      \tag{IHD4}
   \]
   In particular \(L(G')>B_{\rm pc}/2\), and \(G'\) satisfies the Hall cut
   inequality \((GHP4)\).  Moreover, if a deficient exact-load optimizer is
   written as a convex combination of the at most two integral sublayers promised
   by \cref{cor:exact-load-pair-compatible-hall-profile}, at least one of those
   sublayers satisfies \((IHD4)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If an integral \(G'\) satisfies \((IHD4)\), put \(\Lambda=L(G')\).  Since
   \(C(G')\ge0\), the inequality \(\Delta(G')>0\) forces
   \(\Lambda>B_{\rm pc}/2\).  The exact-load profile is at most the paid closure
   of this sublayer:
   \[
      S_{\rm pc}(\Lambda)\le C(G')
      <
      \Lambda-\frac{B_{\rm pc}}2 .
   \]
   Hence \((EHP4)\) holds.

   Conversely, suppose \((EHP4)\) holds at some \(\Lambda\).  By
   \cref{cor:exact-load-pair-compatible-hall-profile}, an optimizer on the lower
   envelope is a convex combination of at most two integral sublayer pairs
   \((L(G_i),C(G_i))\).  The average value of
   \(L(G_i)-B_{\rm pc}/2-C(G_i)\) under this convex combination is
   \[
      \Lambda-\frac{B_{\rm pc}}2-S_{\rm pc}(\Lambda)>0 .
   \]
   Therefore at least one component \(G_i\) has \(\Delta(G_i)>0\).  The final
   Hall-cut statement is just \(\Delta(G_i)>0\) rewritten as \((GHP4)\).
\end{proof}

This exact-load profile is the cautious replacement for a scalar prefix rule.
It removes the all-sublayer Hall quantifier but does not pretend that paid
neighborhood closure is additive over guard incidences.  A build-time separator
may now target the one-dimensional lower envelope
\(\Lambda\mapsto S_{\rm pc}(\Lambda)\): either it proves \((EHP3)\), giving the
half-shipment used by \cref{cor:pair-compatible-hall-guarded-cover}, or it finds
an integral lower-hull sublayer satisfying \((IHD4)\).  That lower-hull witness is
the finite object that
range reporting, list decoding, additive quantization, or seeded clustering
must turn into a lower-certified guard-credit proposal.

\begin{corollary}[Pair-compatible Hall separator closes guarded residuals]
   \label{cor:pair-compatible-hall-guarded-cover}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:guarded-star-panel-local-cover}.  Let
   \(a_q=\Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[\chi_Z(q)=1]\).  Suppose the following Hall-expansion
   reporter theorem holds for every \(\kappa\in[1,\pi_1^{-1}]\) and every
   nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \((GSP1)\)--\((GSP3)\).

   Put \(y_q=a_q\), \(G(q)=H(q)\), and
   \[
      B_{\rm pc}=\sum_q\tau_qa_q|H(q)|.
      \tag{HES0}
   \]
   The reporter supplies a finite center set
   \(\mathcal X\supseteq\bigcup_qH(q)\), affordable certified containers
   \(W_x\), size certificates \(K_x\), and template congestions \(C_x\), together
   with a pair congestion \(C_{\rm pair}>0\), such that the geometric Hall
   inequalities \((GHP2)\) hold with \(M_0=B_{\rm pc}/2\).  Moreover there is a
   feasible shipment of mass \(B_{\rm pc}/2\) whose induced positive
   responsibility multiplicities lie in a certified range
   \([M_{\min},M_{\max}]\).  Let \(J_{\rm mult}\) be as in \((HPS6)\), and
   assume all active centers satisfy
   \[
      K_x\le K_0,
      \qquad
      R(W_x,K_x,C_x)\le R_0,
      \tag{HES1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      X_0=
      \frac{B_{\rm pc}}{4C_{\rm pair}|P|J_{\rm mult}}>0,
      \qquad
      X_0>R_0,
      \tag{HES2}
   \]
   Then the reporter theorem required in
   \cref{cor:guarded-star-panel-local-cover} holds.  Consequently the finite
   local filter-cover LP in that corollary is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a residual price system satisfying \((GSP1)\)--\((GSP3)\).  By
   hypothesis, \((GHP2)\) holds with \(M_0=B_{\rm pc}/2\).  Therefore
   \cref{cor:geometric-hall-pair-compatible-guard} and
   \cref{lem:pair-compatible-guard-cut-normal-form} give a pair-compatible
   high-correlation shipment of mass \(M=B_{\rm pc}/2\).  With the certified
   dynamic range and the price bounds \((HES1)\)--\((HES2)\),
   \cref{cor:pair-compatible-guard-responsibility-star} produces a single
   responsibility-induced high-correlation star whose lower-certified
   scale-free surplus is positive.  Hence
   \cref{cor:lower-certified-scale-free-guard-panel} makes the finite
   guard-credit LP over the reported template pool positive.  Then
   \cref{cor:finite-guard-credit-flow-separator} gives a certified
   hit-weighted star panel satisfying \((HSP1)\)--\((HSP2)\).  This is exactly
   the reporter conclusion assumed in
   \cref{cor:guarded-star-panel-local-cover}; applying that corollary gives
   local filter-cover feasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Hall-profile repair closes guarded residuals]
   \label{cor:hall-profile-repair-guarded-cover}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:guarded-star-panel-local-cover}.  Let
   \(a_q=\Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[\chi_Z(q)=1]\).  Suppose that for every
   \(\kappa\in[1,\pi_1^{-1}]\) and every nonnegative price system
   \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying \((GSP1)\)--\((GSP3)\), the reporter
   supplies a finite center/container universe as in
   \cref{cor:pair-compatible-hall-guarded-cover}.  Put
   \[
      y_q=a_q,\qquad G(q)=H(q),\qquad
      b_q=\tau_qa_q|H(q)|,\qquad
      B_{\rm pc}=\sum_qb_q,
      \tag{HPR0}
   \]
   and let
   \[
      \mathcal Q_+=\{q\in\mathcal Q:b_q>0\}.
      \tag{HPR1}
   \]
   Assume that, for each residual price system, at least one of the following
   two alternatives holds.

   First, the Hall-success alternative holds: the reported containers and a
   pair congestion \(C_{\rm pair}\) satisfy the geometric Hall inequalities
   \((GHP2)\) with \(M_0=B_{\rm pc}/2\), the induced positive responsibility
   multiplicities lie in a certified range \([M_{\min},M_{\max}]\), and the
   price conditions \((HES1)\)--\((HES2)\) hold.

   Second, the Hall-profile repair alternative holds: after restricting the
   guard-credit instance to the loaded query set \(\mathcal Q_+\), the reporter
   returns a finite lower-certified raw guard panel
   \[
      (W_i,K_i,C_i,X_i,\lambda_i)_{i\in I}
   \]
   with affordable certified containers \(W_i\), size certificates
   \(K_i\ge1\), congestion parameters \(C_i>0\), and multiplicities
   \(\lambda_i\ge0\),
   such that
   \[
      0\le X_i\le
      D_+(W_i):=
      \sum_{p\in W_i}
      \sum_{\substack{q\in\mathcal Q_+\\(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}
      a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
      \tag{HPR2}
   \]
   and the positive surplus inequality
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_i
      \left[
         X_i
         -
         \psi_{W_i}
         \left(
            K_i^{\rho_{W_i}}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}\tau_qa_q
            +\sigma K_i^{1+\rho_{W_i}}
         \right)
      \right]>0
      \tag{HPR3}
   \]
   holds.

   Then the reporter theorem required in
   \cref{cor:guarded-star-panel-local-cover} holds.  Consequently the finite
   local filter-cover LP in that corollary is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a residual price system satisfying \((GSP1)\)--\((GSP3)\).

   In the Hall-success alternative, the proof of
   \cref{cor:pair-compatible-hall-guarded-cover} applies verbatim: the Hall
   inequalities give a pair-compatible shipment of mass \(B_{\rm pc}/2\);
   \cref{cor:pair-compatible-guard-responsibility-star} converts it into a
   responsibility-induced high-correlation star; and
   \cref{cor:lower-certified-scale-free-guard-panel} and
   \cref{cor:finite-guard-credit-flow-separator} convert that star into a
   certified hit-weighted star panel satisfying \((HSP1)\)--\((HSP2)\).

   In the repair alternative, restrict the finite guard-credit instance to
   \(\mathcal Q_+\), use \(y_q=a_q\), and extend all query weights by zero
   outside \(\mathcal Q_+\) after the panel is constructed.  The certificates
   \((HPR2)\)--\((HPR3)\) are exactly the lower-certified scale-free
   guard-panel condition \((LCG1)\)--\((LCG4)\) for this restricted instance.
   Hence
   \cref{cor:lower-certified-scale-free-guard-panel} gives a positive
   guard-credit template, and
   \cref{cor:finite-guard-credit-flow-separator} converts the resulting
   positive guard-credit LP into a certified hit-weighted star panel satisfying
   \((HSP1)\)--\((HSP2)\).  Since the panel has zero query weights outside
   \(\mathcal Q_+\), it is also a valid panel for the original residual.

   Thus every residual price system satisfying \((GSP1)\)--\((GSP3)\) admits
   the hit-weighted star panel required by
   \cref{cor:guarded-star-panel-local-cover}.  Applying that corollary gives
   local filter-cover feasibility.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:hall-profile-repair-guarded-cover} is the exact interface for the
lower-hull obstruction of
\cref{cor:exact-load-pair-compatible-hall-profile}.  A failed Hall profile is
not used as a data-structure column by itself; it is only a priced witness that
must be repaired by a verified raw guard panel satisfying \((HPR2)\)--\((HPR3)\).
This is the build-time target for range-reporting cells, list-decoding outputs,
additive-quantization records, or seeded clustering proposals: find paid-shadow
mass on the loaded Hall queries per recursive price, then let the existing
guard-credit LP and paid-prefix verifier retain the actual filter column.

\begin{corollary}[Proposal-law Hall-profile repair]
   \label{cor:proposal-law-hall-profile-repair}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:hall-profile-repair-guarded-cover}, and use
   the notation \((HPR0)\)--\((HPR1)\).  Keep the Hall-success alternative of
   that corollary unchanged.  Suppose that whenever the Hall-success alternative
   is not certified, the reporter supplies a finite probability law \(\nu\) over
   raw records
   \[
      B=(W_B,K_B,C_B,X_B),
   \]
   where \(W_B\) is an affordable certified container, \(K_B\ge1\) is a size
   certificate, \(C_B>0\) is a congestion parameter, and
   \[
      0\le X_B\le
      D_+(W_B):=
      \sum_{p\in W_B}
      \sum_{\substack{q\in\mathcal Q_+\\(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}
      a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      \tag{HDS1}
   \]
   is a lower certificate for loaded-query paid-shadow mass.  Define
   \[
      R_+(B)=
      \psi_{W_B}
      \left(
         K_B^{\rho_{W_B}}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}\tau_qa_q
         +\sigma K_B^{1+\rho_{W_B}}
      \right).
      \tag{HDS2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \E_{B\sim\nu}
      \left[
         X_B-R_+(B)
      \right]>0,
      \tag{HDS3}
   \]
   then the reporter theorem required in
   \cref{cor:guarded-star-panel-local-cover} holds.  Consequently the finite
   local filter-cover LP in that corollary is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Enumerate the finite support of \(\nu\) as \(B_i=(W_i,K_i,C_i,X_i)\), and set
   \(\lambda_i=\nu(B_i)\).  The lower certificate \((HDS1)\) is exactly
   \((HPR2)\), while \((HDS2)\)--\((HDS3)\) are exactly the positive surplus
   condition \((HPR3)\) for this panel.  Thus the repair alternative
   of \cref{cor:hall-profile-repair-guarded-cover} holds whenever the
   Hall-success alternative is absent.  Applying that corollary gives the
   claimed reporter theorem and local LP feasibility.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:proposal-law-hall-profile-repair} is the fractional version of the
``dense clusters as columns'' principle at the current Hall frontier.  When the
half-shipment itself fails,
\cref{cor:exact-load-pair-compatible-hall-profile} exposes a lower-hull Hall
deficit; the proposal mechanism may use that deficit to bias range reports,
list-decoder outputs, additive-quantization cells, or seeded centers.  The
deficit is not retained and is not charged.  The only accepted certificate is the
finite law \(\nu\) whose loaded paid-shadow surplus \((HDS3)\) is positive, after
which the deterministic guard-credit and paid-prefix verifiers produce the
actual filter columns.

\begin{corollary}[Lower-hull Hall proposal separator]
   \label{cor:lower-hull-hall-proposal-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:hall-profile-repair-guarded-cover}, with
   notation as in \((HPR0)\)--\((HPR1)\).  Suppose that for every residual price
   system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying \((GSP1)\)--\((GSP3)\), the reporter
   supplies a finite center/container universe as in
   \cref{cor:pair-compatible-hall-guarded-cover}, and at least one of the
   following two alternatives holds.

   First, the Hall-success alternative of
   \cref{cor:hall-profile-repair-guarded-cover} holds.

   Second, the lower-hull proposal alternative holds: for some declared pair
   congestion \(C_{\rm pair}>0\), the exact-load profile \(S_{\rm pc}\) for the
   reported universe has a strict deficit
   \[
      S_{\rm pc}(\Lambda)<\Lambda-\frac{B_{\rm pc}}2
      \qquad
      \left(\frac{B_{\rm pc}}2<\Lambda\le B_{\rm pc}\right),
      \tag{LHP1}
   \]
   and, using any lower-hull optimizer for this deficit as build-time advice, the
   reporter supplies a finite probability law over raw container records
   satisfying \((HDS1)\)--\((HDS3)\).

   Then the reporter theorem required in
   \cref{cor:guarded-star-panel-local-cover} holds.  Consequently the finite
   local filter-cover LP in that corollary is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the Hall-success alternative holds, the Hall-success proof in
   \cref{cor:hall-profile-repair-guarded-cover} applies verbatim and closes the
   residual.

   Otherwise the lower-hull proposal alternative supplies exactly the finite
   probability law required by
   \cref{cor:proposal-law-hall-profile-repair}.  The lower-hull optimizer is used
   only to find that law; it is discarded once the certificates
   \((HDS1)\)--\((HDS3)\) have been verified.  Applying
   \cref{cor:proposal-law-hall-profile-repair} gives the reporter theorem and
   hence local LP feasibility.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:lower-hull-hall-proposal-separator} is the narrow remaining dense
theorem.  By \cref{cor:exact-load-pair-compatible-hall-profile}, a genuine
failure of the half-shipment is witnessed on the lower convex envelope by at
most two ordinary guard sublayers.  The geometric work is to show that such a
deficit cannot persist without creating a raw container law with positive
\((HDS3)\) surplus on the loaded queries.  This is stronger than choosing a good
set of clusters and weaker than solving the whole recursive cover directly: the
build stage may spend arbitrary time searching the deficit, but the proof only
trusts the verified surplus law and the retained guard-credit columns.

\begin{corollary}[Deficit-restricted proposal law]
   \label{cor:deficit-restricted-proposal-law}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:lower-hull-hall-proposal-separator}.  Suppose
   the Hall-success alternative is not certified, and let \(G'\) be an integral
   Hall-deficit sublayer satisfying \((IHD4)\) in the specialization
   \(y_q=a_q\), as supplied by \cref{cor:integral-hall-deficit-normal-form}.
   For a raw container \(W\), define its paid mass inside this deficient Hall
   shadow by
   \[
      D_{G'}(W)=
      \sum_{p\in W}
      \sum_{\substack{q\in\mathcal Q_+\\p\in N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)}}
      a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{DRP1}
   \]
   Suppose the reporter supplies a finite probability law \(\nu\) over raw
   records \(B=(W_B,K_B,C_B,X_B)\), where \(W_B\) is an affordable certified
   container, \(K_B\ge1\) is a size certificate for \(W_B\), \(C_B>0\), and
   \[
      0\le X_B\le D_{G'}(W_B).
      \tag{DRP2}
   \]
   Define \(R_+(B)\) as in \((HDS2)\).  If
   \[
      \E_{B\sim\nu}
      \left[
         X_B-R_+(B)
      \right]>0,
      \tag{DRP3}
   \]
   then the lower-hull proposal alternative of
   \cref{cor:lower-hull-hall-proposal-separator} holds, and hence the guarded
   residual closes.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For every \(q\) and every guard sublayer \(G'(q)\), the certified neighborhood
   \(N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)\) is a subset of the near-pair fiber
   \(\{p:(p,q)\in\mathcal N\}\).  Therefore
   \[
      D_{G'}(W)\le
      \sum_{p\in W}
      \sum_{\substack{q\in\mathcal Q_+\\(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}
      a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      =
      D_+(W).
   \]
   Thus \((DRP2)\) implies the loaded-shadow lower certificate \((HDS1)\), while
   \((DRP3)\) is exactly \((HDS3)\).  The finite law is therefore a valid
   lower-hull proposal law, so \cref{cor:lower-hull-hall-proposal-separator}
   applies.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:deficit-restricted-proposal-law} is the form a geometric separator
should now prove.  Starting from one positive-excess Hall sublayer \(G'\), it is
enough to find affordable smaller-radius containers whose certified mass covers
the paid neighborhood \(N_{\rm hc}(G')\) with surplus over the recursive price.
The proposal search no longer has to reason about all near
pairs or all dense clusters at once; it only has to separate this one deficient
paid shadow.

\begin{corollary}[Deficient-shadow prefix certificate]
   \label{cor:deficient-shadow-prefix-certificate}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:deficit-restricted-proposal-law}.  Fix an
   affordable certified ambient container \(W\) with price factor \(\psi_W\) and
   exponent \(\rho_W\).  For \(p\in W\), define the deficient-shadow degree
   \[
      d_{G'}(p)=
      \sum_{\substack{q\in\mathcal Q_+\\p\in N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)}}
      a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{DSP1}
   \]
   Let \(U\subseteq W\) be a certified subcontainer, still certified by the
   geometry of \(W\) and with inherited price parameters
   \(\psi_U=\psi_W\), \(\rho_U=\rho_W\).  Put \(h=|U|\ge1\).  Suppose \(X\) is a
   lower certificate for its deficient-shadow mass,
   \[
      0<X\le\sum_{p\in U}d_{G'}(p).
      \tag{DSP2}
   \]
   Define
   \[
      R_W(h)=
      \psi_W
      \left(
         h^{\rho_W}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}\tau_qa_q
         +\sigma h^{1+\rho_W}
      \right).
      \tag{DSP3}
   \]
   If
   \[
      X>R_W(h),
      \tag{DSP4}
   \]
   then the guarded residual closes.

   In particular, if the reporter can certify the top-\(h\) deficient-shadow
   prefix in \(W\), with
   \[
      D_{G',W}(h)=
      \max_{\substack{U\subseteq W\\|U|=h}}
      \sum_{p\in U}d_{G'}(p),
      \tag{DSP5}
   \]
   and \((DSP4)\) holds with \(X=D_{G',W}(h)\), then that one prefix is a valid
   separating proposal.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Use the point mass proposal law on the raw record
   \[
      B=(U,h,1,X).
   \]
   Since \(U\subseteq W\) inherits the certified geometry and price parameters of
   \(W\), it is an affordable certified container with size certificate \(h\),
   and its recursive price is \(R_W(h)\).  By \((DSP2)\), the record satisfies
   \((DRP2)\).  With \(C_B=1\), condition \((DSP4)\) is exactly the strict
   proposal surplus required by
