   \cref{cor:deficit-restricted-proposal-law}, which closes the residual.  The
   top-prefix statement is the same argument with \(U\) chosen to attain
   \((DSP5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Deficient shadows are finite-prefix residuals]
   \label{cor:deficient-shadow-finite-prefix-normal-form}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:deficit-restricted-proposal-law}, and assume
   the paid-prefix verifier of \cref{cor:hit-weighted-star-panel-prefix} is
   available for the current price system.  For the integral Hall-deficit
   sublayer \(G'\), form the finite demand system
   \[
      \mathcal N_{G'}
      =
      \{(p,q):q\in\mathcal Q_+,\ p\in N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)\},
      \qquad
      \widehat\gamma_{p,q}=a_q\gamma_{p,q},
      \qquad
      \widehat\tau_q=a_q\tau_q .
      \tag{DFN1}
   \]
   For a certified container \(W\), cardinality \(h\), and fractional query
   layer \(0\le y_q\le1\), put
   \[
      D_{G',W,y}^{\widehat\gamma}(h)
      =
      \max_{\substack{U\subseteq W\\|U|=h}}
      \sum_{p\in U}
      \sum_{\substack{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N_{G'}}}
      y_q\widehat\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{DFN2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      D_{G',W,y}^{\widehat\gamma}(h)
      >
      \psi_W
      \left(
         h^{\rho_W}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}\widehat\tau_qy_q
         +\sigma h^{1+\rho_W}
      \right),
      \tag{DFN3}
   \]
   then the reporter has a certified hit-weighted star panel satisfying
   \((HSP1)\)--\((HSP2)\).  Consequently the paid-prefix verifier exposes an
   available positive repair prefix.

   Moreover, if \((DFN3)\) holds for a fractional layer \(y\), then it holds
   for some Boolean query layer \(Q\subseteq\mathcal Q_+\).  Thus a surviving
   no-repair residual satisfies the ordinary finite-prefix envelope
   \[
      D_{G',W,y}^{\widehat\gamma}(h)
      \le
      \psi_W
      \left(
         h^{\rho_W}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}\widehat\tau_qy_q
         +\sigma h^{1+\rho_W}
      \right)
      \tag{DFN4}
   \]
   for every searched \((W,h,y)\).  The all-loaded-query certificate
   \cref{cor:deficient-shadow-prefix-certificate} is the special case
   \(y_q\equiv1\), where \((DFN2)\) is \(D_{G',W}(h)\) and the query price is
   \(R_W(h)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(U\subseteq W\) attain \((DFN2)\), and put
   \(X=D_{G',W,y}^{\widehat\gamma}(h)\).  Submit the one-record hit-weighted
   star panel with container \(W\), update side \(U\), size certificate \(h\),
   query weights \(\widetilde y_q=a_qy_q\), lower certificate \(X\), and
   multiplicity \(1\).  Since \(0\le a_q\le1\), the query weights are in
   \([0,1]\).  Also \(\mathcal N_{G'}\subseteq\mathcal N\), so
   \[
      X
      \le
      \sum_{p\in U}
      \sum_{\substack{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}
      \widetilde y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
   \]
   Thus \((HSP1)\) holds.  The strict inequality \((DFN3)\) is exactly the
   one-record instance of \((HSP2)\), so
   \cref{cor:hit-weighted-star-panel-prefix} gives a positive repair prefix.

   For hardening, define the reduced-cost function
   \[
      F(y)=
      D_{G',W,y}^{\widehat\gamma}(h)
      -
      \psi_Wh^{\rho_W}\sum_q\widehat\tau_qy_q
      -
      \psi_W\sigma h^{1+\rho_W}.
   \]
   The prefix term is a maximum of linear functions of \(y\), hence \(F\) is
   convex on \([0,1]^{\mathcal Q_+}\).  If \(F(y)>0\) somewhere, its maximum on
   the cube is positive at an extreme point, i.e. at \(y=\mathbf 1_Q\) for some
   Boolean query layer \(Q\).  The residual envelope is the contrapositive over
   the searched finite pool.  Finally, \(y_q\equiv1\) gives exactly
   \((DSP5)\) and \((DSP3)\).
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:deficient-shadow-prefix-certificate} is the most concrete current
search problem.  Given one positive-excess Hall sublayer, compute or certify a
top deficient-shadow prefix inside an affordable smaller-radius container and
compare its mass with the recursive price.  Thus \(k\)-means++, additive
quantization, LP range reporting, and list decoding are useful only insofar as
they expose such prefixes; the proof does not depend on their sampling rule.
\Cref{cor:deficient-shadow-finite-prefix-normal-form} gives the sharper
query-layer form of the same target: the deficient shadow is an ordinary
finite-prefix demand system after the substitution
\(\widehat\gamma_{p,q}=a_q\gamma_{p,q}\),
\(\widehat\tau_q=a_q\tau_q\).  The reporter may therefore search fractional
query layers and pay only \(\sum_q\widehat\tau_qy_q\); any positive fractional
certificate hardens to one Boolean query layer and one paid prefix.
\Cref{cor:transported-deficient-shadow-certificate} gives the same target in
transport form: a bounded-congestion shipment into one certified subset is
already a lower certificate for the corresponding prefix mass, so no dyadic
degree extraction is needed when the geometric reporter can certify the
shipment directly.
\Cref{lem:restricted-deficient-shadow-transport-cut} supplies the matching
localized min-cut form: a failed shipment into a proposed subset exposes a
smaller Hall cut whose paid-pair capacity is measured only inside that subset.

\begin{corollary}[Transported deficient-shadow certificate]
   \label{cor:transported-deficient-shadow-certificate}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:deficient-shadow-prefix-certificate}.  Let
   \(U\subseteq W\) be a certified subcontainer with \(h=|U|\ge1\), inheriting
   the price parameters of \(W\).  Suppose preprocessing certifies nonnegative
   transported loads \(\ell_p\) on \(U\), total mass \(M\), and congestion
   \(C>0\), satisfying
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U}\ell_p=M,
      \qquad
      \ell_p\le C\,d_{G'}(p)\quad(p\in U).
      \tag{TSC1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \frac{M}{C}>
      \psi_W
      \left(
         h^{\rho_W}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}\tau_qa_q
         +\sigma h^{1+\rho_W}
      \right),
      \tag{TSC2}
   \]
   then the guarded residual closes.

   More generally, a finite panel of such transported records closes whenever
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_i
      \left[
         \frac{M_i}{C_i}
         -
         \psi_{W_i}
         \left(
            h_i^{\rho_{W_i}}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}\tau_qa_q
            +\sigma h_i^{1+\rho_{W_i}}
         \right)
      \right]>0 .
      \tag{TSC3}
   \]

   Consequently, if no retained top prefix in a family
   \((\mathcal W,\mathcal K_W)\) closes, then every transported certificate
   into any certified \(U\subseteq W\) with \(|U|\in\mathcal K_W\) satisfies the
   reverse of \((TSC2)\).  Thus a geometric separator may search for a bounded
   congestion shipment into one certified subset; it need not first expose the
   whole deficient-shadow degree sequence.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Summing the congestion inequalities in \((TSC1)\) gives
   \[
      \frac{M}{C}\le\sum_{p\in U}d_{G'}(p).
   \]
   Thus \(X=M/C\) is a valid lower mass certificate in
   \cref{cor:deficient-shadow-prefix-certificate}.  Condition \((TSC2)\) is
   exactly \((DSP4)\), so the one-record statement follows.

   For the panel statement, a positive sum in \((TSC3)\) implies that some
   record with \(\lambda_i>0\) has positive bracketed surplus.  The one-record
   argument closes for that record.  Finally, if a transported certificate into
   \(U\subseteq W\) with \(|U|=h\in\mathcal K_W\) violated the reverse of
   \((TSC2)\), then the top-\(h\) deficient-shadow prefix in \(W\) would have
   mass at least \(M/C\) and would close by
   \cref{cor:deficient-shadow-prefix-certificate}.  This proves the residual
   statement by contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Restricted deficient-shadow transport cut]
   \label{lem:restricted-deficient-shadow-transport-cut}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:transported-deficient-shadow-certificate},
   and keep the integral Hall-deficit sublayer \(G'\).  Let
   \(U\subseteq W\) be a certified subcontainer.  Define the guard-incidence
   set
   \[
      \mathcal I_{G'}=
      \{(q,x):q\in\mathcal Q_+,\ x\in G'(q)\},
      \qquad
      b_{q,x}=\tau_qa_q .
      \tag{RDT1}
   \]
   For \(C>0\), let \(\Phi_U(C)\) be the maximum mass of a nonnegative flow
   \(f_{q,x,p}\) supported on triples with
   \[
      (q,x)\in\mathcal I_{G'},\qquad
      p\in U\cap W_x,\qquad
      (x,p)\text{ certified high-correlation},\qquad
      (p,q)\in\mathcal N,
      \tag{RDT2}
   \]
   satisfying
   \[
      \sum_p f_{q,x,p}\le b_{q,x}
      \qquad((q,x)\in\mathcal I_{G'}),
      \tag{RDT3}
   \]
   and the pair-compatible paid capacities
   \[
      \sum_{x\in G'(q)} f_{q,x,p}
      \le
      C\,a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      \qquad(p\in U,\ q\in\mathcal Q_+,\ (p,q)\in\mathcal N).
      \tag{RDT4}
   \]
   For \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal I_{G'}\), let
   \(N_U(\mathcal A)\) be the set of pairs \((p,q)\), \(p\in U\), that are
   adjacent to some incidence in \(\mathcal A\) through \((RDT2)\).  Then
   \[
      \Phi_U(C)
      =
      \min_{\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal I_{G'}}
      \left\{
         \sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{G'}\setminus\mathcal A}b_i
         +
         C\sum_{(p,q)\in N_U(\mathcal A)}a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      \right\}.
      \tag{RDT5}
   \]

   Consequently, any feasible flow of mass \(M\) induces transported loads
   \[
      \ell_p=\sum_{q,x}f_{q,x,p}\qquad(p\in U)
      \tag{RDT6}
   \]
   that satisfy \((TSC1)\).  In particular, if
   \[
      \frac{\Phi_U(C)}{C}>R_W(|U|),
      \tag{RDT7}
   \]
   then the guarded residual closes.

   Conversely, if the residual does not close and \(M/C>R_W(|U|)\), then there
   is a cut \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal I_{G'}\) with
   \[
      \sum_{i\in\mathcal A}b_i
      >
      C\sum_{(p,q)\in N_U(\mathcal A)}a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      +
      \sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{G'}}b_i-M .
      \tag{RDT8}
   \]
   Thus failure of a transported deficient-shadow repair inside \(U\) exposes a
   smaller Hall cut localized to \(U\)'s paid shadow.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The identity \((RDT5)\) is the max-flow/min-cut theorem on the finite
   bipartite network whose left nodes are incidences
   \(i=(q,x)\in\mathcal I_{G'}\), whose right nodes are admissible paid pairs
   \((p,q)\) with \(p\in U\), and whose finite sink capacities are
   \(C a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}\).  A finite cut is determined by the subset
   \(\mathcal A\) of left nodes kept on the source side; every adjacent paid-pair
   node must also be kept, and the cut capacity is exactly the expression in
   \((RDT5)\).

   Given a feasible flow of mass \(M\), define \(\ell_p\) by \((RDT6)\).  Then
   \(\sum_p\ell_p=M\).  Summing \((RDT4)\) over \(q\) gives, for each
   \(p\in U\),
   \[
      \ell_p
      \le
      C\sum_{\substack{q\in\mathcal Q_+\\p\in N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)}}
      a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      =
      C d_{G'}(p),
   \]
   because a positive flow to \((p,q)\) implies \(p\in N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)\).
   Hence \((TSC1)\) holds.  If \((RDT7)\) holds, apply
   \cref{cor:transported-deficient-shadow-certificate} with
   \(M=\Phi_U(C)\).

   Finally, if \(M/C>R_W(|U|)\) and every cut had value at least \(M\), then
   \((RDT5)\) would give \(\Phi_U(C)\ge M\), and the transported certificate
   would close the residual.  The contrapositive gives \((RDT8)\), after
   rewriting the cut value inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Flow-value deficient-shadow screen]
   \label{cor:flow-value-deficient-shadow-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{lem:restricted-deficient-shadow-transport-cut}.  Let
   \(\mathcal U\) be a finite family of certified subcontainers \(U\subseteq W\),
   each inheriting the price parameters of its ambient container.  For each
   record \(i\), choose \(U_i\in\mathcal U\), let \(W_i\) be its ambient
   container, choose a congestion \(C_i>0\), and a nonnegative weight
   \(\lambda_i\).  If
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_i
      \left[
         \frac{\Phi_{U_i}(C_i)}{C_i}
         -
         R_{W_i}(|U_i|)
      \right]>0,
      \tag{FVS1}
   \]
   then the guarded residual closes.

   Equivalently, if no transported deficient-shadow repair over
   \(\mathcal U\) closes, then
   \[
      \frac{\Phi_U(C)}{C}\le R_W(|U|)
      \tag{FVS2}
   \]
   for every \(U\in\mathcal U\), ambient \(W\), and every \(C>0\).  Moreover,
   for every target \(M\) with \(M/C>R_W(|U|)\), the localized cut obstruction
   \((RDT8)\) holds.

   Thus the reporter may replace explicit transported-load certificates by
   exact max-flow values.  A positive reduced value \(\Phi_U(C)/C-R_W(|U|)\) is
   already one deterministic dense repair, while failure supplies a finite
   cut certificate inside each proposed subset.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((FVS1)\) holds, at least one record with \(\lambda_i>0\) satisfies
   \[
      \Phi_{U_i}(C_i)/C_i>R_{W_i}(|U_i|).
   \]
   By \((RDT7)\) in
   \cref{lem:restricted-deficient-shadow-transport-cut}, that record closes the
   guarded residual.

   The inequality \((FVS2)\) is the contrapositive of the one-record statement.
   If \(M/C>R_W(|U|)\) and no transported repair closes, then
   \(\Phi_U(C)<M\).  Rewriting the min-cut identity \((RDT5)\) gives a cut
   satisfying \((RDT8)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Infinitesimal flow value equals deficient-shadow mass]
   \label{lem:infinitesimal-flow-deficient-shadow}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{lem:restricted-deficient-shadow-transport-cut}.  For a certified
   subcontainer \(U\), put
   \[
      D_{G'}(U)=
      \sum_{(p,q)\in N_U(\mathcal I_{G'})}
      a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      =
      \sum_{p\in U}d_{G'}(p).
      \tag{IFD1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \frac{\Phi_U(C)}{C}\le D_{G'}(U)
      \qquad(C>0),
      \tag{IFD2}
   \]
   and, if \(D_{G'}(U)>0\), there is \(C_0(U)>0\) such that
   \[
      \Phi_U(C)=C\,D_{G'}(U)
      \qquad(0<C\le C_0(U)).
      \tag{IFD3}
   \]
   Consequently
   \[
      \sup_{C>0}\frac{\Phi_U(C)}{C}=D_{G'}(U).
      \tag{IFD4}
   \]
   In particular, if all congestion scales are allowed, a certified subset
   \(U\) has positive flow-value surplus for some \(C\) if and only if
   \[
      D_{G'}(U)>R_W(|U|).
      \tag{IFD5}
   \]
   Thus the exact flow-value screen is not a stronger geometric separator than
   the deficient-shadow prefix test.  Its role is to provide a build-time
   lower certificate for \(D_{G'}(U)\) when the shadow degrees themselves are
   not materialized.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The identity in \((IFD1)\) is the definition of the deficient-shadow degree:
   a pair \((p,q)\) lies in \(N_U(\mathcal I_{G'})\) exactly when
   \(p\in U\cap N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)\).

   For the upper bound, take \(\mathcal A=\mathcal I_{G'}\) in the min-cut
   formula \((RDT5)\).  This gives
   \[
      \Phi_U(C)\le
      C\sum_{(p,q)\in N_U(\mathcal I_{G'})}
      a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      =
      C D_{G'}(U).
   \]

   For the reverse inequality at small congestion, assume \(D_{G'}(U)>0\).
   For every paid-pair node
   \(j=(p,q)\in N_U(\mathcal I_{G'})\) with
   \(w_j=a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}>0\), choose one adjacent incidence
   \(i(j)=(q,x)\in\mathcal I_{G'}\).  Let
   \[
      s_i=\sum_{j:\ i(j)=i}w_j .
   \]
   If \(s_i>0\), then \(i=(q,x)\) has \(x\in G'(q)\) and
   \(q\in\mathcal Q_+\), so its source capacity
   \(b_i=\tau_qa_q\) is positive.  Define
   \[
      C_0(U)=\min_{i:\ s_i>0}\frac{b_i}{s_i}.
   \]
   For \(0<C\le C_0(U)\), route \(Cw_j\) units of flow from \(i(j)\) to each
   paid-pair node \(j\).  The source load at incidence \(i\) is \(Cs_i\le b_i\),
   and the sink capacity of \(j=(p,q)\) is exactly
   \(C a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}=Cw_j\).  Hence this is a feasible flow of total
   value \(C\sum_jw_j=C D_{G'}(U)\).  Together with the upper bound this proves
   \((IFD3)\) and \((IFD4)\).

   Finally, if \(\Phi_U(C)/C>R_W(|U|)\) for some \(C\), then \((IFD2)\) gives
   \(D_{G'}(U)>R_W(|U|)\).  Conversely, if \((IFD5)\) holds, choose
   \(C\le C_0(U)\) in \((IFD3)\).  Then
   \(\Phi_U(C)/C=D_{G'}(U)>R_W(|U|)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Flow-value screen collapses to shadow-mass separation]
   \label{cor:flow-value-shadow-mass-equivalence}
   In the setting of \cref{cor:flow-value-deficient-shadow-screen}, if the
   reporter is allowed to choose arbitrary positive congestion scales, then
   \((FVS1)\) holds for a finite panel if and only if at least one certified
   subcontainer in the panel satisfies
   \[
      D_{G'}(U)>R_W(|U|).
      \tag{FSM1}
   \]
   Equivalently, the no-flow-value residual \((FVS2)\) over all \(C>0\) is
   exactly the no-shadow-mass residual
   \[
      D_{G'}(U)\le R_W(|U|)
      \tag{FSM2}
   \]
   for every proposed certified subcontainer \(U\).

   Therefore a proof should not rely on optimizing over congestion scales as a
   separate source of power.  The remaining geometric task is to expose one
   affordable smaller-radius subset with enough deficient-shadow mass; max-flow
   certificates are a convenient way to verify such mass from adjacency data.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((FVS1)\) holds, one active record has
   \(\Phi_U(C)/C>R_W(|U|)\), and
   \cref{lem:infinitesimal-flow-deficient-shadow} gives \((FSM1)\).  Conversely,
   if a proposed \(U\) satisfies \((FSM1)\), the same lemma gives a sufficiently
   small congestion \(C\) with \(\Phi_U(C)/C=D_{G'}(U)>R_W(|U|)\), so the
   one-record panel satisfies \((FVS1)\).  The residual statement is the
   contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[No-prefix deficient-shadow envelope]
   \label{cor:no-prefix-deficient-shadow-envelope}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:deficient-shadow-prefix-certificate}.  Let
   \(\mathcal W\) be a finite family of affordable certified ambient containers.
   For each \(W\in\mathcal W\), let \(\mathcal K_W\) be a finite set of
   cardinalities such that the top-\(h\) deficient-shadow prefix in \(W\) is a
   certified subcontainer inheriting the price parameters of \(W\) for every
   \(h\in\mathcal K_W\).  Put
   \[
      D_{G',W}(h)=
      \max_{\substack{U\subseteq W\\|U|=h}}
      \sum_{p\in U}d_{G'}(p),
      \tag{NDE1}
   \]
   If no prefix from the family \((W,h)\), \(W\in\mathcal W\),
   \(h\in\mathcal K_W\), closes the guarded residual through
   \cref{cor:deficient-shadow-prefix-certificate}, then every such pair satisfies
   \[
      D_{G',W}(h)
      \le
      \psi_W
      \left(
         h^{\rho_W}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}\tau_qa_q
         +\sigma h^{1+\rho_W}
      \right)
      \tag{NDE2}
   \]
   whenever \(D_{G',W}(h)>0\).  If \(D_{G',W}(h)=0\), the same bound is interpreted
   as trivial.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   This is the contrapositive of
   \cref{cor:deficient-shadow-prefix-certificate}.  If \((NDE2)\) failed for some
   \(W,h\) with positive top-prefix mass, take \(X=D_{G',W}(h)\).  The definitions
   \((NDE1)\) and \((DSP3)\) give the recursive price, and failure of
   \((NDE2)\) is \((DSP4)\).  Hence that prefix would close the guarded residual.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Tail form of the deficient-shadow envelope]
   \label{cor:tail-deficient-shadow-envelope}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:no-prefix-deficient-shadow-envelope}, and
   assume no searched prefix closes the guarded residual.  For
   \(W\in\mathcal W\) and a threshold \(t>0\), put
   \[
      U_{W,t}=\{p\in W:d_{G'}(p)\ge t\},
      \qquad
      h_{W,t}=|U_{W,t}|.
      \tag{TDE1}
   \]
   If \(h_{W,t}\in\mathcal K_W\) and \(h_{W,t}>0\), then
   \[
      t\,h_{W,t}
      \le
      \psi_W
      \left(
         h_{W,t}^{\rho_W}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}\tau_qa_q
         +\sigma h_{W,t}^{1+\rho_W}
      \right),
      \tag{TDE2}
   \]
   If \(h_{W,t}=0\), the bound is trivial.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(h=h_{W,t}>0\).  Since \(U_{W,t}\) has \(h\) points and each has
   deficient-shadow degree at least \(t\),
   \[
      D_{G',W}(h)\ge t h .
      \tag{TDE4}
   \]
   Applying \((NDE2)\) at this cardinality gives
   \[
      t h
      \le D_{G',W}(h)
      \le
      \psi_W
      \left(
         h^{\rho_W}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}\tau_qa_q
         +\sigma h^{1+\rho_W}
      \right).
   \]
   This proves \((TDE2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Two-price deficient-shadow tail screen]
   \label{cor:two-price-deficient-shadow-screen}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:tail-deficient-shadow-envelope}, and write
   \[
      A_+=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}\tau_qa_q.
      \tag{TDS1}
   \]
   If no searched prefix closes the guarded residual, then for every
   \(W\in\mathcal W\) and threshold \(t>0\) with
   \(h=h_{W,t}\in\mathcal K_W\) and \(h>0\), at least one of the two inequalities
   \[
      t h
      \le
      2\psi_W A_+h^{\rho_W}
      \tag{TDS2}
   \]
   or
   \[
      t h
      \le
      2\psi_W\sigma h^{1+\rho_W}
      \tag{TDS3}
   \]
   holds.  Equivalently, a threshold layer closes the residual whenever it
   simultaneously violates both \((TDS2)\) and \((TDS3)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If both \((TDS2)\) and \((TDS3)\) failed, then
   \[
      \psi_W\left(A_+h^{\rho_W}+\sigma h^{1+\rho_W}\right)
      <
      t h ,
   \]
   contradicting \((TDE2)\).  The final sentence is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Forbidden middle scale for deficient-shadow layers]
   \label{cor:forbidden-middle-deficient-shadow-scale}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:two-price-deficient-shadow-screen}.  Assume
   \(0<\rho_W<1\) for the container under consideration.
   Suppose no searched prefix closes the guarded residual.  Let
   \(W\in\mathcal W\), \(t>0\), and \(h=h_{W,t}\in\mathcal K_W\) with \(h>0\).
   If \(A_+>0\) and \(\sigma>0\), then at least one of the two scale alternatives
   holds:
   \[
      h
      \le
      \left(
         \frac{2\psi_WA_+}{t}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho_W)}
      \tag{FMS1}
   \]
   or
   \[
      h
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{t}{2\psi_W\sigma}
      \right)^{1/\rho_W}.
      \tag{FMS2}
   \]
   Equivalently, any searched threshold layer with cardinality strictly between
   the right hand sides of \((FMS1)\) and \((FMS2)\) closes the residual.

   If \(\sigma=0\), the first alternative \((FMS1)\) must hold whenever
   \(A_+>0\).  If \(A_+=0\), the second alternative \((FMS2)\) must hold whenever
   \(\sigma>0\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{cor:two-price-deficient-shadow-screen}, either \((TDS2)\) or
   \((TDS3)\) holds.  Rewriting \((TDS2)\) gives \((FMS1)\), because
   \(1-\rho_W>0\); rewriting \((TDS3)\) gives \((FMS2)\), because
   \(\rho_W>0\).  The zero-price cases follow from the same alternatives: when
   \(\sigma=0\), \((TDS3)\) cannot hold for \(t,h>0\); when \(A_+=0\),
   \((TDS2)\) cannot hold.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cardinality-net deficient-shadow reporter]
   \label{cor:cardinality-net-deficient-shadow-reporter}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:deficient-shadow-prefix-certificate}.  Let
   \(W\) be an affordable certified ambient container with exponent
   \(0<\rho_W<1\), price factor \(\psi_W\), and available cardinalities
   \(\mathcal K_W\).  Assume that every top-\(k\) deficient-shadow prefix in
   \(W\) is a certified subcontainer with inherited price parameters for
   \(k\in\mathcal K_W\), and that \(\mathcal K_W\) is \(b\)-dense from below:
   for every \(1\le h\le |W|\), some \(k\in\mathcal K_W\) satisfies
   \[
      h/b\le k\le h .
      \tag{CSD1}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      A_+=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}\tau_qa_q .
      \tag{CSD2}
   \]
   For \(t>0\), let
   \[
      h=h_{W,t}=|\{p\in W:d_{G'}(p)\ge t\}|.
   \]
   If \(h>0\) and
   \[
      t>
      \psi_W
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_W}A_+h^{\rho_W-1}
         +\sigma h^{\rho_W}
      \right),
      \tag{CSD3}
   \]
   then the guarded residual closes.

   Consequently, if \(\sigma>0\), it is enough that
   \[
      h>
      b\left(
         \frac{2\psi_WA_+}{t}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho_W)}
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      h<
      \left(
         \frac{t}{2\psi_W\sigma}
      \right)^{1/\rho_W}.
      \tag{CSD4}
   \]
   If \(\sigma=0\), it is enough that the first strict inequality in
   \((CSD4)\) holds, with the harmless convention that its right hand side is
   \(0\) when \(A_+=0\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Choose \(k\in\mathcal K_W\) satisfying \((CSD1)\).  Since \(k\le h\), the
   top-\(k\) deficient-shadow prefix \(U\subseteq W\) has every point of degree
   at least \(t\).  Thus \(X=t k\) is a valid lower certificate for its
   deficient-shadow mass.
   Also, because \(k\ge h/b\) and \(k\le h\),
   \[
      A_+k^{\rho_W-1}+\sigma k^{\rho_W}
      \le
      b^{1-\rho_W}A_+h^{\rho_W-1}+\sigma h^{\rho_W}.
   \]
   Multiplying by \(\psi_Wk\) and using \((CSD3)\) gives
   \[
      \psi_W\left(A_+k^{\rho_W}+\sigma k^{1+\rho_W}\right)
      <
      t k .
   \]
   This is exactly \((DSP4)\) for the prefix \(U\), so
   \cref{cor:deficient-shadow-prefix-certificate} closes the residual.

   Under \((CSD4)\), the query-price summand and the storage-price summand in
   \((CSD3)\) are each strictly less than \(t/(2\psi_W)\), so \((CSD3)\)
   follows.  The case \(\sigma=0\) is the same argument with only the
   query-price summand.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Layer-cake deficient-shadow reporter]
   \label{cor:layer-cake-deficient-shadow-reporter}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-deficient-shadow-reporter}.  For \(t>0\), put
   \[
      h_t=|\{p\in W:d_{G'}(p)\ge t\}|
   \]
   and define the signed level surplus
   \[
      \mathcal E_W(t)
      =
      t h_t
      -
      \psi_W
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_W}A_+h_t^{\rho_W}
         +\sigma h_t^{1+\rho_W}
      \right).
      \tag{DCL1}
   \]
   If \(\mathcal E_W(t)>0\) for some level \(t\), then the guarded residual
   closes.  More generally, if a finite nonnegative level panel
   \((\lambda_i,t_i)_i\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_i\mathcal E_W(t_i)>0,
      \tag{DCL2}
   \]
   then the guarded residual closes.

   In particular, fix \(u>0\), and suppose all reported levels satisfy
   \(t_i\ge u\).  Write \(h_i=h_{t_i}\).  If
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_i t_i h_i
      >
      \psi_W
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_W}A_+\sum_i\lambda_i h_i^{\rho_W}
         +\sigma\sum_i\lambda_i h_i^{1+\rho_W}
      \right),
      \tag{DCL3}
   \]
   then the guarded residual closes.

   Equivalently, for a nonzero panel define
   \[
      M_0=\sum_i\lambda_i,\qquad
      M_1=\sum_i\lambda_i h_i,\qquad
      M_{1+\rho_W}=\sum_i\lambda_i h_i^{1+\rho_W},
      \qquad
      B=\sum_i\lambda_i t_i h_i .
      \tag{DCL4}
   \]
   It is enough that
   \[
      B>
      \psi_W
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_W}A_+M_0^{1-\rho_W}M_1^{\rho_W}
         +\sigma M_{1+\rho_W}
      \right).
      \tag{DCL5}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The inequality \(\mathcal E_W(t)>0\) is exactly \((CSD3)\) multiplied by
   \(h_t\).  Thus a positive level closes by
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-deficient-shadow-reporter}.  If \((DCL2)\) holds,
   at least one level with \(\lambda_i>0\) has \(\mathcal E_W(t_i)>0\), and the
   first conclusion applies.

   Condition \((DCL3)\) is exactly \((DCL2)\) after expanding the level
   surplus.  Finally, because
   \(0<\rho_W<1\), the concavity of \(x^{\rho_W}\) gives
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_i h_i^{\rho_W}
      \le
      M_0^{1-\rho_W}M_1^{\rho_W}.
   \]
   Hence \((DCL5)\) implies \((DCL3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Integral deficient-shadow moment reporter]
   \label{cor:integral-deficient-shadow-moment-reporter}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:layer-cake-deficient-shadow-reporter}.  Let \(0<u<v\) and
   \(s\ge0\).  If
   \[
      \int_u^v t^{s-1}\mathcal E_W(t)\,dt>0,
      \tag{DMI1}
   \]
   then the guarded residual closes.

   It is enough that
   \[
      B_s(u,v)
      >
      \psi_W
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_W}A_+Q_s(u,v)
         +\sigma S_s(u,v)
      \right),
      \tag{DMI2}
   \]
   where
   \[
      B_s(u,v)=\int_u^v t^s h_t\,dt,\qquad
      Q_s(u,v)=\int_u^v t^{s-1}h_t^{\rho_W}\,dt,\qquad
      S_s(u,v)=\int_u^v t^{s-1}h_t^{1+\rho_W}\,dt .
      \tag{DMI3}
   \]
   The captured-mass term has the exact truncated moment form
   \[
      B_s(u,v)
      =
      \frac1{s+1}
      \sum_{p\in W}
      \left(
         \min\{d_{G'}(p),v\}^{s+1}-u^{s+1}
      \right)_+ .
      \tag{DMI4}
   \]

   Moreover, if
   \[
      M_s(u,v)=\int_u^v t^{s-1}\,dt,
      \qquad
      L_s(u,v)=\int_u^v t^{s-1}h_t\,dt ,
      \tag{DMI5}
   \]
   then the coarser sufficient condition
   \[
      B_s(u,v)
      >
      \psi_W
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_W}A_+M_s(u,v)^{1-\rho_W}L_s(u,v)^{\rho_W}
         +\sigma S_s(u,v)
      \right)
      \tag{DMI6}
   \]
   also closes the residual.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((DMI1)\) holds, then \(\mathcal E_W(t)>0\) for some
   \(t\in[u,v]\), because otherwise the integral would be nonpositive.  The
   first conclusion follows from
   \cref{cor:layer-cake-deficient-shadow-reporter}.  The stronger inequality
   \((DMI2)\) implies \((DMI1)\) after expanding \(\mathcal E_W(t)\).

   For \((DMI4)\), write
   \[
      h_t=\sum_{p\in W}\mathbf 1\{d_{G'}(p)\ge t\}
   \]
   and exchange the finite sum with the integral.  This gives
   \[
      \int_u^v t^s h_t\,dt
      =
      \sum_{p\in W}\int_u^v
      t^s\mathbf 1\{d_{G'}(p)\ge t\}\,dt,
   \]
   which is exactly \((DMI4)\).

   Finally, concavity of \(x^{\rho_W}\) with respect to the measure
   \(t^{s-1}dt\) gives
   \[
      Q_s(u,v)
      \le
      M_s(u,v)^{1-\rho_W}L_s(u,v)^{\rho_W}.
   \]
   Therefore \((DMI6)\) implies \((DMI2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dyadic-window deficient-shadow moment reporter]
   \label{cor:dyadic-window-deficient-shadow-moment-reporter}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:integral-deficient-shadow-moment-reporter}.  Fix \(0<u<v\) and
   \(s\ge0\).  Let
   \[
      L=\left\lceil\log_2\frac{v}{u}\right\rceil,
      \qquad
      u_j=2^ju,\qquad
      v_j=\min\{2^{j+1}u,v\}
      \quad(0\le j<L).
      \tag{DWD1}
   \]
   For each nonempty dyadic window \([u_j,v_j]\), put
   \[
      B_j=B_s(u_j,v_j),\qquad
      Q_j=Q_s(u_j,v_j),\qquad
      S_j=S_s(u_j,v_j),
      \tag{DWD2}
   \]
   using the notation of \((DMI3)\).  If
   \[
      \sum_{j=0}^{L-1}
      \left[
         B_j
         -
         \psi_W
         \left(
            b^{1-\rho_W}A_+Q_j+\sigma S_j
         \right)
      \right]>0,
      \tag{DWD3}
   \]
   then the guarded residual closes.

   A coarser sufficient condition is the following.  Define
   \[
      M_j=M_s(u_j,v_j),\qquad
      R_j=L_s(u_j,v_j),
      \tag{DWD4}
   \]
   and suppose
   \[
      \sum_{j=0}^{L-1} B_j
      >
      \psi_W
      \sum_{j=0}^{L-1}
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_W}A_+M_j^{1-\rho_W}R_j^{\rho_W}
         +\sigma S_j
      \right).
      \tag{DWD5}
   \]
   Then the guarded residual closes.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((DWD3)\) holds, one dyadic window has positive summand.  That summand is
   exactly the sufficient condition \((DMI2)\) for the interval
   \([u_j,v_j]\), so \cref{cor:integral-deficient-shadow-moment-reporter}
   closes the residual.  For the second statement, apply the concavity bound
   \(Q_j\le M_j^{1-\rho_W}R_j^{\rho_W}\) from the proof of
   \cref{cor:integral-deficient-shadow-moment-reporter} on each dyadic window.
   Hence \((DWD5)\) implies \((DWD3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dyadic-window deficient-shadow residual envelope]
   \label{cor:dyadic-window-deficient-shadow-residual-envelope}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:dyadic-window-deficient-shadow-moment-reporter}.  Assume no
   deficient-shadow prefix with an available cardinality in \(\mathcal K_W\)
   closes the guarded residual.  Then for every \(0<u<v\), \(s\ge0\), and dyadic
   partition \((u_j,v_j)_{j<L}\) from \((DWD1)\),
   \[
      B_s(u,v)
      \le
      \psi_W
      \sum_{j=0}^{L-1}
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_W}A_+Q_s(u_j,v_j)
         +\sigma S_s(u_j,v_j)
      \right).
      \tag{DWE1}
   \]
   Equivalently, using the capped-moment form of the left hand side,
   \[
      \frac1{s+1}
      \sum_{p\in W}
      \left(
         \min\{d_{G'}(p),v\}^{s+1}-u^{s+1}
      \right)_+
      \le
      \psi_W
      \sum_{j=0}^{L-1}
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_W}A_+Q_s(u_j,v_j)
         +\sigma S_s(u_j,v_j)
      \right).
      \tag{DWE2}
   \]
   In particular, the coarser envelope
   \[
      B_s(u,v)
      \le
      \psi_W
      \sum_{j=0}^{L-1}
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_W}A_+M_j^{1-\rho_W}R_j^{\rho_W}
         +\sigma S_j
      \right)
      \tag{DWE3}
   \]
   holds with \(M_j,R_j,S_j\) as in \((DWD2)\)--\((DWD4)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((DWE1)\) failed, then \((DWD3)\) would hold, because
   \(\sum_jB_s(u_j,v_j)=B_s(u,v)\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:dyadic-window-deficient-shadow-moment-reporter} would close the
   residual, contradicting the hypothesis.  The capped form \((DWE2)\) is
   \((DMI4)\) applied on the full interval \([u,v]\).  Finally,
   \(Q_s(u_j,v_j)\le M_j^{1-\rho_W}R_j^{\rho_W}\) on each window, as in the
   proof of \cref{cor:dyadic-window-deficient-shadow-moment-reporter}, so
   \((DWE1)\) implies \((DWE3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dyadic log-Lorentz deficient-shadow separator]
   \label{cor:dyadic-log-lorentz-deficient-shadow-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:dyadic-window-deficient-shadow-residual-envelope}.  Let
   \(0<u<v\), and let \(u_j,v_j,L\) be as in \((DWD1)\).  Put
   \[
      H_j=|\{p\in W:d_{G'}(p)\ge u_j\}|.
      \tag{DLG1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_{p\in W}\left(\min\{d_{G'}(p),v\}-u\right)_+
      >
      (\log 2)\psi_W
      \sum_{j=0}^{L-1}
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_W}A_+H_j^{\rho_W}
         +\sigma H_j^{1+\rho_W}
      \right),
      \tag{DLG2}
   \]
   then the guarded residual closes.

   Equivalently, if no retained deficient-shadow prefix closes, then
   \((DLG2)\) fails for every interval \(0<u<v\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{cor:dyadic-window-deficient-shadow-residual-envelope} with
   \(s=0\).  The left hand side \(B_0(u,v)\) is exactly the capped linear moment
   in \((DLG2)\).  On the dyadic window \([u_j,v_j]\),
   \[
      M_0(u_j,v_j)=\int_{u_j}^{v_j}\frac{dt}{t}\le\log 2.
   \]
   Since \(h_t\le H_j\) throughout the window,
   \[
      R_j=\int_{u_j}^{v_j}\frac{h_t}{t}\,dt\le(\log 2)H_j,
      \qquad
      S_j=\int_{u_j}^{v_j}\frac{h_t^{1+\rho_W}}{t}\,dt
      \le(\log 2)H_j^{1+\rho_W}.
   \]
   Therefore
   \[
      M_j^{1-\rho_W}R_j^{\rho_W}\le(\log 2)H_j^{\rho_W}.
   \]
   Substituting these estimates into the residual envelope \((DWE3)\) proves
   the contrapositive of \((DLG2)\).  Hence a violation of \((DLG2)\) closes the
   residual.  The final sentence is the same contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fractional log-Lorentz deficient-shadow panel]
   \label{cor:fractional-log-lorentz-deficient-shadow-panel}
   Work in a common deficient-shadow instance in which
   \cref{cor:dyadic-log-lorentz-deficient-shadow-separator} applies to each
   affordable ambient container \(W\) in a finite family \(\mathcal W\).  Thus
   every \(W\) has inherited price parameters \((\psi_W,\rho_W)\), the same
   query and storage prices \(A_+\) and \(\sigma\), and a \(b\)-dense retained
   cardinality net for its deficient-shadow prefixes.

   Let \(i\in I\) range over a finite panel.  Each record chooses a container
   \(W_i\in\mathcal W\), an interval \(0<u_i<v_i\), and a nonnegative weight
   \(\lambda_i\).  Let \(u_{i,j},v_{i,j},L_i\) be the dyadic partition of
   \([u_i,v_i]\) from \((DWD1)\), and put
   \[
      H_{i,j}=|\{p\in W_i:d_{G'}(p)\ge u_{i,j}\}|.
      \tag{FLL1}
   \]
   Define the verified log-Lorentz surplus of record \(i\) by
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \Phi_i
      &=
      \sum_{p\in W_i}
      \left(\min\{d_{G'}(p),v_i\}-u_i\right)_+ \\
      &\quad
      -(\log 2)\psi_{W_i}
      \sum_{j=0}^{L_i-1}
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_{W_i}}A_+H_{i,j}^{\rho_{W_i}}
         +\sigma H_{i,j}^{1+\rho_{W_i}}
      \right).
   \end{aligned}
   \tag{FLL2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i\Phi_i>0,
      \tag{FLL3}
   \]
   then the guarded residual closes.

   Equivalently, if no retained deficient-shadow prefix closes, every finite
   nonnegative panel has nonpositive total surplus.  In particular, any
   finite-support randomized proposal law over such records is useful exactly
   when its expected verified surplus is positive; then some deterministic
   proposed record closes the residual.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((FLL3)\) holds, at least one record with \(\lambda_i>0\) has
   \(\Phi_i>0\).  For that record, \(\Phi_i>0\) is precisely the strict
   inequality \((DLG2)\) for the container \(W_i\) and interval
   \([u_i,v_i]\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:dyadic-log-lorentz-deficient-shadow-separator} closes the guarded
   residual.  The contrapositive gives the nonpositive-panel statement, and the
   randomized-law statement is the special case \(\lambda_i=\nu(i)\) for a
   finite proposal support.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Certified log-Lorentz deficient-shadow panel]
   \label{cor:certified-log-lorentz-deficient-shadow-panel}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:fractional-log-lorentz-deficient-shadow-panel}.  For each record
   \(i\), suppose the reporter gives a certified lower captured mass \(X_i\) and
   certified upper dyadic cardinalities \(K_{i,j}\) satisfying
   \[
      0\le X_i\le
      \sum_{p\in W_i}
      \left(\min\{d_{G'}(p),v_i\}-u_i\right)_+ ,
      \tag{CLL1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      |\{p\in W_i:d_{G'}(p)\ge u_{i,j}\}|\le K_{i,j}
      \qquad(0\le j<L_i).
      \tag{CLL2}
   \]
   Define the certified surplus
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \widehat\Phi_i
      &=
      X_i
      -(\log 2)\psi_{W_i}
      \sum_{j=0}^{L_i-1}
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_{W_i}}A_+K_{i,j}^{\rho_{W_i}}
         +\sigma K_{i,j}^{1+\rho_{W_i}}
      \right).
   \end{aligned}
   \tag{CLL3}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_i\widehat\Phi_i>0,
      \tag{CLL4}
   \]
   then the guarded residual closes.

   Equivalently, if no retained deficient-shadow prefix closes, every finite
   certified panel satisfying \((CLL1)\)--\((CLL2)\) has nonpositive certified
   surplus.  Thus a proposal oracle never has to expose the exact
   deficient-shadow degree sequence: a lower bound on capped captured mass and
   upper bounds on the dyadic superlevel ranks are sufficient certificates.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(H_{i,j}\) be the exact dyadic cardinalities from \((FLL1)\).  By
   \((CLL1)\) the positive term in \(\Phi_i\) is at least \(X_i\).  By
   \((CLL2)\), \(H_{i,j}\le K_{i,j}\), and the functions
   \(x^{\rho_{W_i}}\) and \(x^{1+\rho_{W_i}}\) are nondecreasing on
   \([0,\infty)\).  Hence
   \[
      \Phi_i\ge\widehat\Phi_i
      \qquad(i\in I).
   \]
   If \((CLL4)\) holds, then
   \(\sum_i\lambda_i\Phi_i>0\), so
   \cref{cor:fractional-log-lorentz-deficient-shadow-panel} closes the guarded
   residual.  The contrapositive gives the certified-panel residual statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Mass-support log-Lorentz certificate]
   \label{cor:mass-support-log-lorentz-certificate}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:certified-log-lorentz-deficient-shadow-panel}.  Let \(i\in I\)
   range over a finite panel of records.  Each record chooses a container
   \(W_i\), and gives certificates \(M_i>0\), \(K_i\ge1\), and \(V_i>0\) such
   that
   \[
      M_i\le\sum_{p\in W_i}d_{G'}(p),
      \tag{MSL1}
   \]
   \[
      |\{p\in W_i:d_{G'}(p)>0\}|\le K_i,
      \qquad
      d_{G'}(p)\le V_i\quad(p\in W_i).
      \tag{MSL2}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      u_i=\frac{M_i}{2K_i},\qquad v_i=V_i,
      \qquad
      L_i=\left\lceil\log_2\frac{v_i}{u_i}\right\rceil ,
      \tag{MSL3}
   \]
   Define the mass-support surplus
   \[
      \Theta_i
      =
      \frac{M_i}{2}
      -
      (\log 2)\psi_{W_i}L_i
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_{W_i}}A_+K_i^{\rho_{W_i}}
         +\sigma K_i^{1+\rho_{W_i}}
      \right).
      \tag{MSL4}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_i\Theta_i>0,
      \tag{MSL5}
   \]
   then the guarded residual closes.

   Equivalently, if no retained deficient-shadow prefix closes, every finite
   mass-support panel satisfying \((MSL1)\)--\((MSL2)\) has nonpositive surplus
   \((MSL5)\).  Thus a reporter may certify a useful dense column using only
   three scalars per proposed container: captured shadow mass, support size, and
   maximum deficient-shadow degree.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   First note that \(v_i>u_i\).  Indeed, \((MSL1)\)--\((MSL2)\) imply
   \[
      M_i\le\sum_{p\in W_i}d_{G'}(p)\le K_iV_i=K_iv_i,
   \]
   so \(v_i\ge M_i/K_i>u_i\).  For this interval \([u_i,v_i]\), the capped
   captured mass satisfies
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \sum_{p\in W_i}
      \left(\min\{d_{G'}(p),v_i\}-u_i\right)_+
      &=
      \sum_{p\in W_i}\left(d_{G'}(p)-u_i\right)_+ \\
      &\ge
      \sum_{p\in W_i}d_{G'}(p)
      -u_i|\{p\in W_i:d_{G'}(p)>0\}| \\
      &\ge M_i-u_iK_i=\frac{M_i}{2}.
   \end{aligned}
   \tag{MSL7}
   \]
   Moreover each dyadic superlevel in \([u_i,v_i]\) is contained in the support
   \(\{p:d_{G'}(p)>0\}\), so it has cardinality at most \(K_i\).  Therefore
   \((CLL1)\)--\((CLL2)\) hold for this record with
   \(X_i=M_i/2\) and \(K_{i,j}=K_i\).  The certified surplus \((CLL3)\) is
   exactly \(\Theta_i\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:certified-log-lorentz-deficient-shadow-panel} proves the closing
   statement and its contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Average-density mass-support screen]
   \label{cor:average-density-mass-support-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:mass-support-log-lorentz-certificate}.  For each panel record put
   \[
      \delta_i=\frac{M_i}{K_i},
      \qquad
      \mathfrak L_i=
      \left\lceil\log_2\frac{2V_i}{\delta_i}\right\rceil .
      \tag{ADS1}
   \]
   Then the guarded residual closes whenever
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_iK_i
      \left[
         \frac{\delta_i}{2}
         -
         (\log 2)\psi_{W_i}\mathfrak L_i
         \left(
            b^{1-\rho_{W_i}}A_+K_i^{\rho_{W_i}-1}
            +\sigma K_i^{\rho_{W_i}}
         \right)
      \right]>0.
      \tag{ADS2}
   \]
   In particular, one record closes the residual if
   \[
      \delta_i>
      2(\log 2)\psi_{W_i}\mathfrak L_i
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_{W_i}}A_+K_i^{\rho_{W_i}-1}
         +\sigma K_i^{\rho_{W_i}}
      \right).
      \tag{ADS3}
   \]
   A simpler sufficient two-price screen is
   \[
      \delta_i>
      4(\log 2)\psi_{W_i}\mathfrak L_i\,
      b^{1-\rho_{W_i}}A_+K_i^{\rho_{W_i}-1}
      \tag{ADS4}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \delta_i>
      4(\log 2)\psi_{W_i}\mathfrak L_i\,
      \sigma K_i^{\rho_{W_i}}.
      \tag{ADS5}
   \]
   If \(\sigma=0\), condition \((ADS4)\) alone is sufficient; if \(A_+=0\),
   condition \((ADS5)\) alone is sufficient.

   Consequently, if no retained deficient-shadow prefix closes, every
   mass-support record satisfying \((MSL1)\)--\((MSL2)\) fails \((ADS3)\), and
   in the two-price form it must fail at least one of \((ADS4)\)--\((ADS5)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(\delta_i=M_i/K_i\), the interval in \((MSL3)\) is
   \(u_i=\delta_i/2\), \(v_i=V_i\), and \(L_i=\mathfrak L_i\).
   The mass-support surplus \((MSL4)\) can therefore be written as
   \[
      \Theta_i
      =
      K_i
      \left[
         \frac{\delta_i}{2}
         -
         (\log 2)\psi_{W_i}\mathfrak L_i
         \left(
            b^{1-\rho_{W_i}}A_+K_i^{\rho_{W_i}-1}
            +\sigma K_i^{\rho_{W_i}}
         \right)
      \right].
   \]
   Thus \((ADS2)\) is exactly \((MSL5)\), and
   \cref{cor:mass-support-log-lorentz-certificate} closes the residual.

   If \((ADS3)\) holds for one record, the bracket in \((ADS2)\) is positive,
   so the point-mass panel closes.  Conditions \((ADS4)\)--\((ADS5)\) imply
   \((ADS3)\), because each of the two summands in \((ADS3)\)'s right hand side
   is then less than \(\delta_i/2\) after multiplication by
   \(2(\log 2)\psi_{W_i}\mathfrak L_i\).  The zero-price cases are immediate.
   The residual statement is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Balanced average-density screen]
   \label{cor:balanced-average-density-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:average-density-mass-support-screen}, and assume
   \(0<\rho_{W_i}<1\).  For a record \(i\) with \(A_+>0\) and \(\sigma>0\), put
   \[
      \widehat A_i=b^{1-\rho_{W_i}}A_+,
      \qquad
      K_i^\star=\frac{(1-\rho_{W_i})\widehat A_i}{\rho_{W_i}\sigma},
      \tag{BDS1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      C_{\rho}=\rho^{-\rho}(1-\rho)^{-(1-\rho)}.
      \tag{BDS2}
   \]
   If, for some \(a\ge1\),
   \[
      a^{-1}K_i^\star\le K_i\le aK_i^\star
      \tag{BDS3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \delta_i>
      2a(\log 2)\psi_{W_i}\mathfrak L_i
      C_{\rho_{W_i}}\widehat A_i^{\rho_{W_i}}\sigma^{1-\rho_{W_i}},
      \tag{BDS4}
   \]
   then the guarded residual closes.

   Equivalently, if no retained deficient-shadow prefix closes, every balanced
   mass-support record satisfying \((BDS3)\) must obey the reverse inequality
   in \((BDS4)\).  Thus, at the balanced support scale, the reporter only has to
   beat the single density level
   \[
      \psi_W\mathfrak L\,A_+^{\rho_W}\sigma^{1-\rho_W}
   \]
   up to constants depending on \(\rho_W\), \(b\), and the balance factor.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(\rho=\rho_{W_i}\), \(\widehat A=\widehat A_i\), and
   \(K^\star=K_i^\star\).  The function
   \[
      f(K)=\widehat A K^{\rho-1}+\sigma K^\rho
   \]
   has its stationary point at \(K^\star=(1-\rho)\widehat A/(\rho\sigma)\), and
   \[
      f(K^\star)=C_\rho\widehat A^\rho\sigma^{1-\rho}.
   \]
   If \(K_i=\lambda K^\star\) with \(\lambda\in[a^{-1},a]\), then
   \[
      f(K_i)
      =
      \lambda^{\rho-1}\widehat A(K^\star)^{\rho-1}
      +
      \lambda^\rho\sigma(K^\star)^\rho
      \le
      a f(K^\star).
   \]
   Thus \((BDS4)\) implies the one-record density condition \((ADS3)\), and
   \cref{cor:average-density-mass-support-screen} closes the residual.  The
   final statement is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Balanced top-prefix density screen]
   \label{cor:balanced-top-prefix-density-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:deficient-shadow-prefix-certificate}, and assume
   \(0<\rho_W<1\), \(A_+>0\), and \(\sigma>0\).  Put
   \[
      K_W^\circ=\frac{(1-\rho_W)A_+}{\rho_W\sigma},
      \qquad
      C_{\rho_W}=\rho_W^{-\rho_W}(1-\rho_W)^{-(1-\rho_W)}.
   \]
   Let \(h\ge1\) be an available certified top-prefix cardinality in \(W\), and
   write
   \[
      \delta_h=\frac{D_{G',W}(h)}{h}.
   \]
   If, for some \(a\ge1\),
   \[
      a^{-1}K_W^\circ\le h\le aK_W^\circ
      \tag{TPD1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \delta_h>
      a\psi_W
      C_{\rho_W}A_+^{\rho_W}\sigma^{1-\rho_W},
      \tag{TPD2}
   \]
   then the guarded residual closes.

   The same conclusion holds for an oversized coarse report.  Suppose a
   mass-support record in \(W\) has certificates \(M,K,V\), put
   \(\delta=M/K\), and let \(h\) be an available certified top-prefix
   cardinality with
   \[
      1\le h\le K,
      \qquad
      a^{-1}K_W^\circ\le h\le aK_W^\circ .
      \tag{TPD3}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \delta>
      a\psi_W
      C_{\rho_W}A_+^{\rho_W}\sigma^{1-\rho_W},
      \tag{TPD4}
   \]
   then the top-\(h\) prefix closes the guarded residual.

   In particular, if the retained cardinality net \(\mathcal K_W\) is
   \(b\)-dense from below and every top-\(k\) prefix with
   \(k\in\mathcal K_W\) is certified, then any coarse report with
   \[
      \left\lceil K_W^\circ\right\rceil\le \min\{K,|W|\},
      \qquad
      K_W^\circ\ge1
   \]
   has an available trim \(h\in\mathcal K_W\) satisfying
   \[
      (2b)^{-1}K_W^\circ\le h\le 2bK_W^\circ .
      \tag{TPD5}
   \]
   Thus \((TPD4)\) with \(a=2b\) is enough for such oversized reports.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For the top-prefix statement, use
   \cref{cor:deficient-shadow-prefix-certificate} with
   \(X=D_{G',W}(h)=h\delta_h\).  The function
   \[
      f(x)=A_+x^{\rho_W-1}+\sigma x^{\rho_W}
   \]
   has its stationary point at \(K_W^\circ\), and
   \(f(K_W^\circ)=C_{\rho_W}A_+^{\rho_W}\sigma^{1-\rho_W}\).  If
   \((TPD1)\) holds, then \(f(h)\le a f(K_W^\circ)\).  Therefore \((TPD2)\)
   implies
   \[
      D_{G',W}(h)
      >
      \psi_W
      \left(A_+h^{\rho_W}+\sigma h^{1+\rho_W}\right),
   \]
   which is exactly \((DSP4)\).

   For the coarse report, list the positive deficient-shadow degrees in \(W\)
   as \(x_1\ge x_2\ge\cdots\ge x_s>0\).  The certificate gives
   \(s\le K\) and \(\sum_{\ell=1}^sx_\ell\ge M=K\delta\).  Since \(h\le K\),
   the top-\(h\) prefix mass satisfies
   \[
      D_{G',W}(h)\ge h\delta .
   \]
   Indeed, if \(h\ge s\) this is immediate from \(K\ge h\); if \(h<s\), the top
   \(h\) average is at least the average over all \(s\) positive degrees, which
   is at least \(M/K=\delta\).  Thus \(\delta_h\ge\delta\).  Conditions
   \((TPD3)\)--\((TPD4)\) therefore imply \((TPD1)\)--\((TPD2)\) for the
   top-\(h\) prefix.

   For the final statement, apply the \(b\)-dense net to
   \(h_0=\lceil K_W^\circ\rceil\).  The assumptions give
   \(1\le h_0\le |W|\) and \(h_0\le K\), so there is
   \(h\in\mathcal K_W\) with \(h_0/b\le h\le h_0\).  Since
   \(K_W^\circ\ge1\), this implies
   \[
      \frac{K_W^\circ}{b}\le h\le K_W^\circ+1\le2K_W^\circ,
   \]
   which is stronger than \((TPD5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fixed-threshold balanced density screen]
   \label{cor:fixed-threshold-balanced-density-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:balanced-top-prefix-density-screen}.  For \(a\ge1\), assume
   \[
      \Xi_{W,a}
      =
      a\psi_W C_{\rho_W}A_+^{\rho_W}\sigma^{1-\rho_W}
      >0 .
      \tag{FTD1}
   \]
   If a certified top prefix satisfies \((TPD1)\) and
   \[
      \delta_h>\Xi_{W,a},
      \tag{FTD2}
   \]
   then the guarded residual closes.  If a coarse report has an available
   balanced trim satisfying \((TPD3)\) and
   \[
      \delta>\Xi_{W,a},
      \tag{FTD3}
   \]
   then the guarded residual closes.

   Consequently, if no retained deficient-shadow prefix closes, every retained
   top prefix satisfying \((TPD1)\) obeys the reverse inequality in \((FTD2)\),
   and every coarse report with an available balanced trim satisfying
   \((TPD3)\) obeys the reverse inequality in \((FTD3)\).  Thus the
   reporter-facing target is the fixed density level
   \[
      \psi_W C_{\rho_W}A_+^{\rho_W}\sigma^{1-\rho_W}
   \]
   up to constants and balance factors.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Condition \((FTD2)\) is exactly \((TPD2)\).  The top-prefix conclusion follows from
   \cref{cor:balanced-top-prefix-density-screen}.  The coarse-report statement
   is identical, using \((FTD3)\) to imply \((TPD4)\).  The residual statements
   are the contrapositives.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fractional fixed-threshold density panel]
   \label{cor:fractional-fixed-threshold-density-panel}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:fixed-threshold-balanced-density-screen}.  Let \(i\in I\) range
   over a finite panel of verified balanced-density records with nonnegative
   weights \(\lambda_i\).  Each record has an ambient container \(W_i\), a
   balance factor \(a_i\ge1\), and a certified density \(\delta_i\).  Define
   \[
      \Theta_i
      =
      \Xi_{W_i,a_i}
      =
      a_i\psi_{W_i}C_{\rho_{W_i}}A_+^{\rho_{W_i}}\sigma^{1-\rho_{W_i}},
      \tag{FFD1}
   \]
   with \(\Xi_{W_i,a_i}\) as in \((FTD1)\).  A record is admissible if it is one
   of the following two types.

   First, it may be a retained top-prefix record: an available certified
   top-prefix cardinality \(h_i\) satisfying \((TPD1)\), with
   \[
      \kappa_i=h_i,
      \qquad
      \delta_i=\frac{D_{G',W_i}(h_i)}{h_i}.
      \tag{FFD2}
   \]
   Second, it may be a coarse report with an available balanced trim satisfying
   \((TPD3)\), with certificates \(M_i,K_i,V_i\) and
   \[
      \kappa_i=K_i,
      \qquad
      \delta_i=\frac{M_i}{K_i}.
      \tag{FFD3}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_i\kappa_i(\delta_i-\Theta_i)>0,
      \tag{FFD4}
   \]
   then the guarded residual closes.

   Equivalently, if no retained deficient-shadow prefix closes, every finite
   nonnegative admissible panel has nonpositive surplus \((FFD4)\).  Hence a
   randomized or batched proposal routine may be analyzed only through its
   expected fixed-threshold density surplus; a positive expectation already
   contains one deterministic retained dense column.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since all \(\lambda_i\) and \(\kappa_i\) are nonnegative and every admissible
   record has \(\kappa_i>0\), condition \((FFD4)\) implies that at least one
   record with \(\lambda_i>0\) satisfies \(\delta_i>\Theta_i\).  If that record
   is of top-prefix type, then \((FTD2)\) holds and
   \cref{cor:fixed-threshold-balanced-density-screen} closes the residual.  If
   it is of coarse-trim type, then \((FTD3)\) holds and the same corollary
   closes the residual.  The nonpositive-panel statement is the contrapositive,
   and the randomized-law statement is the special case
   \(\lambda_i=\nu(i)\) for a finite proposal support.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sampled fixed-threshold density search]
   \label{cor:sampled-fixed-threshold-density-search}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:fractional-fixed-threshold-density-panel}.  A randomized
   build-time proposal routine, on seed \(s\), returns a finite admissible panel
   \(I_s\) with nonnegative weights \(\lambda_{s,i}\).  Define its certified
   surplus by
   \[
      Z(s)=
      \sum_{i\in I_s}
         \lambda_{s,i}\kappa_{s,i}
         \bigl(\delta_{s,i}-\Theta_{s,i}\bigr).
      \tag{SFD1}
   \]
   Suppose
   \[
      \E_s Z(s)\ge\Gamma>0,
      \qquad
      Z(s)_+\le M
      \quad\text{almost surely}.
      \tag{SFD2}
   \]
   Then \(B\) independent build-time seeds produce a panel that closes the
   guarded residual with probability at least
   \[
      1-\exp\left(-\frac{B\Gamma}{M}\right).
      \tag{SFD3}
   \]
   In particular, after a successful sampled panel is found, the retained proof
   object may be reduced to one deterministic balanced dense record satisfying
   \(\delta_i>\Theta_i\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   As in \cref{lem:sampled-proposal-law-separation},
   \[
      \Pr_s[Z(s)>0]\ge\frac{\Gamma}{M}.
   \]
   Therefore \(B\) independent seeds all fail to have positive surplus with
   probability at most \(\exp(-B\Gamma/M)\).  If \(Z(s)>0\), then
   \cref{cor:fractional-fixed-threshold-density-panel} applies to the realized
   panel \(I_s\), so one of its records satisfies \(\delta_i>\Theta_i\) and the
   guarded residual closes by
   \cref{cor:fixed-threshold-balanced-density-screen}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fixed-threshold Hall-deficit oracle]
   \label{cor:fixed-threshold-hall-deficit-oracle}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:lower-hull-hall-proposal-separator}.  Keep
   the Hall-success alternative of that corollary unchanged.  Replace its
   lower-hull proposal alternative by the following fixed-threshold repair
   alternative.

   The exact-load Hall profile has a strict deficit \((LHP1)\), and
   \cref{cor:integral-hall-deficit-normal-form} supplies an integral
   positive-excess Hall sublayer \(G'\).  In the deficient-shadow instance
   associated with this \(G'\), the reporter supplies a finite admissible
   fixed-threshold density panel satisfying \((FFD4)\).

   Then the reporter theorem required in
   \cref{cor:guarded-star-panel-local-cover} holds.  Consequently the finite
   local filter-cover LP in that corollary is feasible.

   The same conclusion holds with high-probability build-time separation if,
   in the fixed-threshold repair alternative, a seeded proposal routine returns
   admissible panels whose surplus \(Z(s)\) satisfies \((SFD2)\).  After
   \[
      B\ge \frac{M}{\Gamma}\log\frac1\delta
      \tag{FHO1}
   \]
   independent build-time seeds, a deterministic closing record is found with
   probability at least \(1-\delta\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a residual price system satisfying \((GSP1)\)--\((GSP3)\).  If the
   Hall-success alternative holds, the Hall-success part of
   \cref{cor:lower-hull-hall-proposal-separator} gives the required reporter
   theorem.

   Otherwise the fixed-threshold repair alternative supplies a positive-excess
   Hall sublayer \(G'\) and an admissible fixed-threshold panel with positive
   surplus.  By
   \cref{cor:fractional-fixed-threshold-density-panel}, that panel contains a
   deterministic balanced dense record satisfying the fixed-threshold density
   inequality.  If the record is a top-prefix record,
   \cref{cor:fixed-threshold-balanced-density-screen} gives
   \cref{cor:balanced-top-prefix-density-screen}, which gives the
   deficient-shadow prefix certificate
   \cref{cor:deficient-shadow-prefix-certificate}.  If the record is a coarse
   report, the same fixed-threshold corollary first trims it to such a prefix.
   In either case, \cref{cor:deficit-restricted-proposal-law} supplies the
   lower-hull proposal alternative required by
   \cref{cor:lower-hull-hall-proposal-separator}.  Applying that corollary gives
   the reporter theorem and local filter-cover feasibility.

   For the sampled statement,
   \cref{cor:sampled-fixed-threshold-density-search} and \((FHO1)\) find a
   positive-surplus realized panel with probability at least \(1-\delta\).  Once
   found, the deterministic argument above applies; failed samples are discarded
   and are never part of the retained filter-cover certificate.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Single-record fixed-threshold Hall separator]
   \label{cor:single-record-fixed-threshold-hall-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:fixed-threshold-hall-deficit-oracle}.  Keep
   the Hall-success alternative unchanged.  Suppose that whenever the
   Hall-success alternative is absent, the strict lower-hull deficit exposes an
   integral positive-excess Hall sublayer \(G'\), and the reporter returns one
   admissible balanced-density record in the associated deficient-shadow
   instance satisfying one of the following two conditions.

   First, the record is a retained top-prefix record: it has an ambient
   container \(W\), balance factor \(a\ge1\), retained top-prefix cardinality
   \(h\) satisfying \((TPD1)\), and density
   \[
      \delta_h=\frac{D_{G',W}(h)}{h}
   \]
   with
   \[
      \delta_h>\Xi_{W,a}.
      \tag{SRH1}
   \]
   Second, the record is a coarse report with certificates \(M,K,V\), density
   \(\delta=M/K\), and an available balanced trim satisfying \((TPD3)\), with
   \[
      \delta>\Xi_{W,a}.
      \tag{SRH2}
   \]
   Then the reporter theorem required in
   \cref{cor:guarded-star-panel-local-cover} holds.  Consequently the finite
   local filter-cover LP in that corollary is feasible.

   Equivalently, the fixed-threshold repair alternative of
   \cref{cor:fixed-threshold-hall-deficit-oracle} may be replaced by this
   single-record condition.  Thus the remaining deterministic geometric
   separator does not have to construct an overlapping panel; one verified
   balanced dense record is enough.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   A record satisfying \((SRH1)\) or \((SRH2)\) is a one-element admissible panel
   for \cref{cor:fractional-fixed-threshold-density-panel}, with weight
   \(\lambda=1\), positive \(\kappa\), and positive surplus
   \(\kappa(\delta-\Theta)\).  Hence it supplies the fixed-threshold repair
   alternative required by
   \cref{cor:fixed-threshold-hall-deficit-oracle}.  Applying that corollary gives
   the reporter theorem and local filter-cover feasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Flow-value Hall-deficit oracle]
   \label{cor:flow-value-hall-deficit-oracle}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:lower-hull-hall-proposal-separator}.  Keep
   the Hall-success alternative of that corollary unchanged.  Replace its
   lower-hull proposal alternative by the following flow-value repair
   alternative.

   The exact-load Hall profile has a strict deficit \((LHP1)\), and
   \cref{cor:integral-hall-deficit-normal-form} supplies an integral
   positive-excess Hall sublayer \(G'\).  In the deficient-shadow instance
   associated with this \(G'\), the reporter supplies a finite family of
   certified subcontainers and congestion scales satisfying the positive
   flow-value surplus condition \((FVS1)\).

   Then the reporter theorem required in
   \cref{cor:guarded-star-panel-local-cover} holds.  Consequently the finite
   local filter-cover LP in that corollary is feasible.

   Equivalently, the fixed-threshold repair alternative of
   \cref{cor:fixed-threshold-hall-deficit-oracle} may be replaced by the
   max-flow reduced-gain test \((FVS1)\).  The retained certificate is still a
   deterministic smaller-radius prefix; the max-flow computation is only a
   build-time separator for finding it.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a residual price system satisfying \((GSP1)\)--\((GSP3)\).  If the
   Hall-success alternative holds, the Hall-success part of
   \cref{cor:lower-hull-hall-proposal-separator} gives the required reporter
   theorem.

   Otherwise the flow-value repair alternative supplies \(G'\) and a finite
   family satisfying \((FVS1)\).  By
   \cref{cor:flow-value-deficient-shadow-screen}, some deterministic
   subcontainer and congestion scale have positive reduced flow value.  Then
   \cref{lem:restricted-deficient-shadow-transport-cut} gives a transported
   deficient-shadow certificate, and
   \cref{cor:transported-deficient-shadow-certificate} gives the
   deficient-shadow prefix certificate
   \cref{cor:deficient-shadow-prefix-certificate}.  Finally
   \cref{cor:deficit-restricted-proposal-law} supplies the lower-hull proposal
   alternative required by
   \cref{cor:lower-hull-hall-proposal-separator}.  Applying that corollary gives
   the reporter theorem and local filter-cover feasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Shadow-mass Hall-deficit oracle]
   \label{cor:shadow-mass-hall-deficit-oracle}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:lower-hull-hall-proposal-separator}.  Keep
   the Hall-success alternative of that corollary unchanged.  Replace its
   lower-hull proposal alternative by the following shadow-mass repair
   alternative.

   The exact-load Hall profile has a strict deficit \((LHP1)\), and
   \cref{cor:integral-hall-deficit-normal-form} supplies an integral
   positive-excess Hall sublayer \(G'\).  In the associated deficient-shadow
   instance, the reporter supplies one certified subcontainer \(U\subseteq W\)
   such that
   \[
      D_{G'}(U)>R_W(|U|),
      \tag{SMH1}
   \]
   where
   \[
      D_{G'}(U)=
      \sum_{p\in U}
      \sum_{\substack{q\in\mathcal Q_+\\p\in N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)}}
      a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{SMH2}
   \]

   Then the reporter theorem required in
   \cref{cor:guarded-star-panel-local-cover} holds.  Consequently the finite
   local filter-cover LP in that corollary is feasible.

   Equivalently, when arbitrary positive congestion scales are admissible, the
   flow-value repair alternative in
   \cref{cor:flow-value-hall-deficit-oracle} may be replaced by the
   single-subset shadow-mass surplus test \((SMH1)\).  More generally, any
   finite nonnegative panel with positive average surplus contains such a
   subcontainer.  The retained certificate is a deterministic smaller-radius
   subset; no congestion scale or panel materialization remains in the proof
   obligation.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a residual price system satisfying \((GSP1)\)--\((GSP3)\).  If the
   Hall-success alternative holds, the Hall-success part of
   \cref{cor:lower-hull-hall-proposal-separator} gives the required reporter
   theorem.

   Otherwise the shadow-mass repair alternative supplies \(G'\) and a certified
   subcontainer \(U\subseteq W\) satisfying \((SMH1)\).  With
   \(X=D_{G'}(U)\), this is exactly the deficient-shadow prefix certificate
   \((DSP2)\)--\((DSP4)\) for \(U\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:deficient-shadow-prefix-certificate} closes the guarded residual,
   and \cref{cor:deficit-restricted-proposal-law} supplies the lower-hull
   proposal alternative required by
   \cref{cor:lower-hull-hall-proposal-separator}.  Applying that corollary gives
   the reporter theorem and local filter-cover feasibility.

   If a build-time procedure instead returns a finite nonnegative panel with
   positive average surplus, one active record satisfies \((SMH1)\), so the
   same argument applies.  The final flow-value equivalence is
   \cref{cor:flow-value-shadow-mass-equivalence}: positive flow-value surplus
   over unrestricted congestion scales exists exactly when a certified subset
   has positive shadow-mass surplus.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite-prefix Hall-deficit oracle]
   \label{cor:finite-prefix-hall-deficit-oracle}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:lower-hull-hall-proposal-separator}.  Keep
   the Hall-success alternative unchanged.  Replace the lower-hull proposal
   alternative by the following finite-prefix repair alternative.

   The exact-load Hall profile has a strict deficit \((LHP1)\), and
   \cref{cor:integral-hall-deficit-normal-form} supplies an integral
   positive-excess Hall sublayer \(G'\).  In the associated finite-prefix
   deficient-shadow instance \((DFN1)\), the reporter supplies one certified
   container \(W\), one cardinality \(h\), and one fractional query layer
   \(0\le y_q\le1\) satisfying the strict finite-prefix surplus \((DFN3)\).

   Then the reporter theorem required in
   \cref{cor:guarded-star-panel-local-cover} holds.  Consequently the finite
   local filter-cover LP in that corollary is feasible.

   Equivalently, the single-subset shadow-mass surplus \((SMH1)\) in
   \cref{cor:shadow-mass-hall-deficit-oracle} may be replaced by one positive
   finite-prefix reduced-cost record for the weighted demand system
   \((\mathcal N_{G'},\widehat\gamma,\widehat\tau)\).  This strictly refines the
   all-loaded-query test by allowing the repair to pay only the query layer that
   carries the certified shadow mass.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a residual price system satisfying \((GSP1)\)--\((GSP3)\).  If the
   Hall-success alternative holds, the Hall-success part of
   \cref{cor:lower-hull-hall-proposal-separator} gives the required reporter
   theorem.

   Otherwise the finite-prefix repair alternative supplies \(G'\) and a record
   satisfying \((DFN3)\).  By
   \cref{cor:deficient-shadow-finite-prefix-normal-form}, this record is a
   certified hit-weighted star panel satisfying \((HSP1)\)--\((HSP2)\).  This is
   exactly the reporter conclusion assumed in
   \cref{cor:guarded-star-panel-local-cover}; applying that corollary gives
   local filter-cover feasibility.

   The comparison with \((SMH1)\) is the specialization \(y_q\equiv1\) in
   \cref{cor:deficient-shadow-finite-prefix-normal-form}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Query-layer deficient-shadow residual obstruction]
   \label{cor:query-layer-deficient-shadow-residual-obstruction}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-hall-deficit-oracle}.  Fix a finite prefix-search
   family \((\mathcal W,\mathcal K_W)\) as in
   \cref{cor:no-prefix-deficient-shadow-envelope}.  Suppose the Hall-success
   alternative is not certified, the exact-load Hall profile has a strict
   lower-hull deficit for the declared pair congestion, and no finite-prefix
   record with \(W\in\mathcal W\), \(h\in\mathcal K_W\), and
   \(0\le y_q\le1\) satisfies the surplus condition \((DFN3)\).  Then there is
   an integral guard sublayer \(G'\) such that
   \[
      \Delta(G')>0
      \tag{QLDS1}
   \]
   and, in the associated weighted demand system
   \((\mathcal N_{G'},\widehat\gamma,\widehat\tau)\) of \((DFN1)\),
   \[
      D_{G',W,y}^{\widehat\gamma}(h)
      \le
      \psi_W
      \left(
         h^{\rho_W}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}\widehat\tau_qy_q
         +\sigma h^{1+\rho_W}
      \right)
      \tag{QLDS2}
   \]
   for every \(W\in\mathcal W\), \(h\in\mathcal K_W\), and fractional query
   layer \(0\le y_q\le1\).

   Consequently, fix \(W\in\mathcal W\) and \(0\le y_q\le1\), and write
   \[
      d_{G',y}^{\widehat\gamma}(p)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N_{G'}}}
      y_q\widehat\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
      \qquad
      A_y=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}\widehat\tau_qy_q .
      \tag{QLDS3}
   \]
   For a threshold \(t>0\), put
   \[
      U_{W,y,t}
      =
      \{p\in W:d_{G',y}^{\widehat\gamma}(p)\ge t\},
      \qquad
      h_{W,y,t}=|U_{W,y,t}|.
      \tag{QLDS4}
   \]
   If \(h_{W,y,t}\in\mathcal K_W\) and \(h_{W,y,t}>0\), then
   \[
      t h_{W,y,t}
      \le
      \psi_W
      \left(
         A_yh_{W,y,t}^{\rho_W}
         +\sigma h_{W,y,t}^{1+\rho_W}
      \right).
      \tag{QLDS5}
   \]
   Hence at least one of the two inequalities
   \[
      t h_{W,y,t}\le2\psi_WA_yh_{W,y,t}^{\rho_W},
      \qquad
      t h_{W,y,t}\le2\psi_W\sigma h_{W,y,t}^{1+\rho_W}
      \tag{QLDS6}
   \]
   holds.  If \(0<\rho_W<1\), \(A_y>0\), and \(\sigma>0\), every surviving
   nonzero threshold layer satisfies
   \[
      h_{W,y,t}
      \le
      \left(\frac{2\psi_WA_y}{t}\right)^{1/(1-\rho_W)}
      \quad\text{or}\quad
      h_{W,y,t}
      \ge
      \left(\frac{t}{2\psi_W\sigma}\right)^{1/\rho_W}.
      \tag{QLDS7}
   \]
   Thus the all-loaded deficient-shadow envelopes are only the specialization
   \(y_q\equiv1\); the sharp residual pays the query-layer price \(A_y\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{cor:integral-hall-deficit-normal-form}, the strict exact-load
   deficit supplies an integral guard sublayer \(G'\) satisfying \((QLDS1)\).
   If \((QLDS2)\) failed for some searched \(W,h,y\), then the same triple would
   satisfy the strict surplus condition \((DFN3)\).  By
   \cref{cor:deficient-shadow-finite-prefix-normal-form}, that record is a
   valid positive repair prefix, and
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-hall-deficit-oracle} would close the guarded
   residual, contradicting the hypothesis.

   For the tail form, the top \(h_{W,y,t}\) points of \(W\) by
   \(d_{G',y}^{\widehat\gamma}\)-degree have total mass at least
   \(t h_{W,y,t}\).  Applying \((QLDS2)\) at this cardinality gives
   \((QLDS5)\).  If both inequalities in \((QLDS6)\) failed, their sum would
   contradict \((QLDS5)\).  Rearranging the two alternatives in \((QLDS6)\)
   gives \((QLDS7)\) when \(0<\rho_W<1\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Query-layer random-list deficient-shadow repair]
   \label{cor:query-layer-random-list-deficient-shadow-repair}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:finite-prefix-hall-deficit-oracle}.  Assume
   the Hall-success alternative is absent, the exact-load Hall profile has a
   strict lower-hull deficit, and the integral normal form exposes a
   positive-excess guard sublayer \(G'\).  Fix a finite prefix-search family
   \((\mathcal W,\mathcal K_W)\).  Let \(W\in\mathcal W\) be a certified
   container, fix a fractional query layer \(0\le y_q\le1\), and let
   \(\mathcal L\subseteq W\) be a finite random certified list.  Put
   \[
      K=|\mathcal L|,
      \qquad
      A_y=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}\widehat\tau_qy_q,
      \tag{QRL1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      V(\mathcal L)
      =
      \sum_{p\in\mathcal L}
      \sum_{\substack{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N_{G'}}}
      y_q\widehat\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{QRL2}
   \]
   If \(K\in\mathcal K_W\) almost surely when \(K>0\), and
   \[
      \E V(\mathcal L)
      >
      \psi_W\left(
         A_y\,\E K^{\rho_W}
         +
         \sigma\,\E K^{1+\rho_W}
      \right),
      \tag{QRL3}
   \]
   then the finite-prefix repair alternative of
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-hall-deficit-oracle} holds.

   More generally, suppose \(\mathcal K_W\) is \(b_0\)-dense from above: for
   every \(1\le K\le |W|\), some \(k\in\mathcal K_W\) satisfies
   \(K\le k\le b_0K\).  Then it is enough that
   \[
      \E V(\mathcal L)
      >
      \psi_W\left(
         b_0^{\rho_W}A_y\,\E K^{\rho_W}
         +
         b_0^{1+\rho_W}\sigma\,\E K^{1+\rho_W}
      \right).
      \tag{QRL4}
   \]

   In particular, let \(0\le\pi_p\le1\) be realizable inclusion marginals on
   \(W\), let \(\mu=\sum_{p\in W}\pi_p\), and suppose the realizing random list
   satisfies \(\E K^2\le M_2\).  Define
   \[
      V_\pi
      =
      \sum_{p\in W}\pi_p
      \sum_{\substack{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N_{G'}}}
      y_q\widehat\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{QRL5}
   \]
   Under the same \(b_0\)-dense cardinality net, the repair alternative holds
   if
   \[
      V_\pi
      >
      \psi_W\left(
         b_0^{\rho_W}A_y\,\mu^{\rho_W}
         +
         b_0^{1+\rho_W}\sigma\,\mu^{1-\rho_W}M_2^{\rho_W}
      \right).
      \tag{QRL6}
   \]
   For independent Bernoulli inclusion one may take \(M_2\le\mu+\mu^2\); if
   \(\mu\ge1\), the storage term in \((QRL6)\) is at most
   \(2b_0^{1+\rho_W}\psi_W\sigma\mu^{1+\rho_W}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose no finite-prefix repair holds.  Then
   \cref{cor:query-layer-deficient-shadow-residual-obstruction} gives the
   residual envelope \((QLDS2)\).  For an outcome with \(K=0\), \(V=0\).  For an
   outcome with \(K>0\) and \(K\in\mathcal K_W\), the top \(K\)-prefix in \(W\)
   has \(y\)-weighted deficient-shadow mass at least \(V(\mathcal L)\), so
   \((QLDS2)\) gives
   \[
      V(\mathcal L)
      \le
      \psi_W\left(
         A_yK^{\rho_W}+\sigma K^{1+\rho_W}
      \right).
   \]
   Averaging contradicts \((QRL3)\).  Hence a positive finite-prefix repair
   must exist.

   In the cardinality-net case, choose for each nonzero outcome a retained
   \(k\in\mathcal K_W\) with \(K\le k\le b_0K\).  The top \(k\)-prefix contains
   at least as much \(y\)-weighted mass as \(\mathcal L\), and the residual
   envelope at \(k\) gives
   \[
      V(\mathcal L)
      \le
      \psi_W\left(
         b_0^{\rho_W}A_yK^{\rho_W}
         +
         b_0^{1+\rho_W}\sigma K^{1+\rho_W}
      \right).
   \]
   Averaging contradicts \((QRL4)\).

   For the marginal form, the realizing random list has
   \(\E V(\mathcal L)=V_\pi\) and \(\E K=\mu\).  Jensen gives
   \(\E K^{\rho_W}\le\mu^{\rho_W}\).  Log-convexity of \(L_p\)-moments between
   powers \(1\) and \(2\) gives
   \[
      \E K^{1+\rho_W}
      \le
      (\E K)^{1-\rho_W}(\E K^2)^{\rho_W}
      \le
      \mu^{1-\rho_W}M_2^{\rho_W}.
   \]
   Thus \((QRL6)\) implies \((QRL4)\).  The Bernoulli and \(\mu\ge1\)
   simplifications are the standard bounds
   \(\E K^2\le\mu+\mu^2\) and
   \(\mu^{1-\rho_W}(\mu+\mu^2)^{\rho_W}\le2\mu^{1+\rho_W}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Query-free deficient-shadow list gain]
   \label{cor:query-free-deficient-shadow-list-gain}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:query-layer-random-list-deficient-shadow-repair}.  For a
   deterministic certified list \(L\subseteq W\), put \(K=|L|\) and
   \[
      h_L(q)=
      \sum_{\substack{p\in L:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N_{G'}}}
      \widehat\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{QFG1}
   \]
   If \(K\in\mathcal K_W\) and
   \[
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}
      \bigl(h_L(q)-\psi_WK^{\rho_W}\widehat\tau_q\bigr)_+
      >
      \psi_W\sigma K^{1+\rho_W},
      \tag{QFG2}
   \]
   then the finite-prefix repair alternative of
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-hall-deficit-oracle} holds.

   More generally, if \(\mathcal K_W\) is \(b_0\)-dense from above, it is enough
   that
   \[
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}
      \bigl(h_L(q)-b_0^{\rho_W}\psi_WK^{\rho_W}\widehat\tau_q\bigr)_+
      >
      b_0^{1+\rho_W}\psi_W\sigma K^{1+\rho_W}.
      \tag{QFG3}
   \]

   Finally, let \(0\le\pi_p\le1\) be realizable inclusion marginals on \(W\),
   let \(\mu=\sum_p\pi_p\), let the realizing random list satisfy
   \(\E K^2\le M_2\), and define
   \[
      h_\pi(q)=
      \sum_{\substack{p\in W:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N_{G'}}}
      \pi_p\widehat\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{QFG4}
   \]
   Under the same \(b_0\)-dense cardinality net, the repair alternative holds
   if
   \[
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}
      \bigl(h_\pi(q)-b_0^{\rho_W}\psi_W\mu^{\rho_W}\widehat\tau_q\bigr)_+
      >
      b_0^{1+\rho_W}\psi_W\sigma\,
      \mu^{1-\rho_W}M_2^{\rho_W}.
      \tag{QFG5}
   \]
   For independent Bernoulli inclusion one may take \(M_2\le\mu+\mu^2\), and
   when \(\mu\ge1\) the right hand storage term is at most
   \(2b_0^{1+\rho_W}\psi_W\sigma\mu^{1+\rho_W}\).

   Thus a center, facility, additive-code, or list-decoding proposal can be
   scored without preselecting a query layer: the verifier computes the positive
   part in \((QFG2)\), \((QFG3)\), or \((QFG5)\), then hardens the winning
   positive coordinates to a Boolean query layer.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For \((QFG2)\), define
   \[
      Q^+=
      \{q\in\mathcal Q_+:
        h_L(q)>\psi_WK^{\rho_W}\widehat\tau_q\}.
   \]
   With \(y=\mathbf 1_{Q^+}\), the left side of \((DFN3)\) is at least
   \(\sum_{q\in Q^+}h_L(q)\), because the top \(K\)-prefix in \(W\) dominates
   the list \(L\).  Inequality \((QFG2)\) is exactly
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}h_L(q)
      >
      \psi_W\left(
         K^{\rho_W}\sum_{q\in Q^+}\widehat\tau_q
         +\sigma K^{1+\rho_W}
      \right),
   \]
   so \((DFN3)\) holds and the finite-prefix repair alternative follows.

   For \((QFG3)\), choose \(k\in\mathcal K_W\) with \(K\le k\le b_0K\).  The
   top \(k\)-prefix dominates \(L\), and the same argument with
   \(Q^+=\{q:h_L(q)>b_0^{\rho_W}\psi_WK^{\rho_W}\widehat\tau_q\}\) gives
   \[
      D_{G',W,\mathbf 1_{Q^+}}^{\widehat\gamma}(k)
      >
      \psi_W\left(
         k^{\rho_W}\sum_{q\in Q^+}\widehat\tau_q
         +\sigma k^{1+\rho_W}
      \right),
   \]
   since \(k^{\rho_W}\le b_0^{\rho_W}K^{\rho_W}\) and
   \(k^{1+\rho_W}\le b_0^{1+\rho_W}K^{1+\rho_W}\).  Hence \((DFN3)\) holds.

   For the marginal form, let \(\mathcal L\) be a realizing random list and put
   \(K=|\mathcal L|\).  For each \(q\), define
   \[
      X_q=
      \sum_{\substack{p\in\mathcal L:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N_{G'}}}
      \widehat\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      -
      b_0^{\rho_W}\psi_WK^{\rho_W}\widehat\tau_q .
   \]
   Jensen gives \(\E K^{\rho_W}\le\mu^{\rho_W}\), so
   \[
      \E X_q
      \ge
      h_\pi(q)-b_0^{\rho_W}\psi_W\mu^{\rho_W}\widehat\tau_q .
   \]
   By convexity of \(x\mapsto x_+\),
   \[
      \E(X_q)_+
      \ge
      \bigl(
      h_\pi(q)-b_0^{\rho_W}\psi_W\mu^{\rho_W}\widehat\tau_q
      \bigr)_+ .
   \]
   Summing over \(q\), using \((QFG5)\), and applying the log-convex moment
   bound
   \[
      \E K^{1+\rho_W}
      \le
      (\E K)^{1-\rho_W}(\E K^2)^{\rho_W}
      \le
      \mu^{1-\rho_W}M_2^{\rho_W}
   \]
   shows that
   \[
      \E\left[
      \sum_q(X_q)_+
      -
      b_0^{1+\rho_W}\psi_W\sigma K^{1+\rho_W}
      \right]>0.
   \]
   Some hard-list outcome therefore satisfies \((QFG3)\), and the previous
   paragraph applies.  The Bernoulli and \(\mu\ge1\) simplifications are the
   same as in \cref{cor:query-layer-random-list-deficient-shadow-repair}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Price-compatible query-free refinement]
   \label{cor:price-compatible-query-free-refinement}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:query-free-deficient-shadow-list-gain}.  Let
   \(L\subseteq W\) be a deterministic certified list with \(K=|L|\), price
   factor \(\psi\), and exponent \(\rho\).  Suppose \(L\) is partitioned into
   nonempty certified sublists
   \[
      L=\bigsqcup_{i\in I}L_i,
      \qquad K_i=|L_i|,
   \]
   where \(L_i\subseteq W_i\), the child container \(W_i\) has price factor
   \(\psi_i\) and the same exponent \(\rho\), and the retained cardinalities in
   every \(W_i\) are \(b_0\)-dense from above.  Put
   \[
      h_i(q)=
      \sum_{\substack{p\in L_i:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N_{G'}}}
      \widehat\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
      \qquad
      h_L(q)=\sum_i h_i(q).
      \tag{PQR1}
   \]
   Assume the refinement is price-compatible:
   \[
      \sum_i\psi_iK_i^\rho\le\psi K^\rho,
      \qquad
      \sum_i\psi_iK_i^{1+\rho}\le\psi K^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{PQR2}
   \]
   If the parent list has positive query-free gain
   \[
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}
      \bigl(h_L(q)-b_0^\rho\psi K^\rho\widehat\tau_q\bigr)_+
      >
