      b_0^{1+\rho}\psi\sigma K^{1+\rho},
      \tag{PQR3}
   \]
   then some child list \(L_i\subseteq W_i\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}
      \bigl(h_i(q)-b_0^\rho\psi_iK_i^\rho\widehat\tau_q\bigr)_+
      >
      b_0^{1+\rho}\psi_i\sigma K_i^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{PQR4}
   \]
   Consequently the finite-prefix repair alternative of
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-hall-deficit-oracle} holds.

   Thus an arbitrary positive-gain list may be replaced by a compact or
   ball-like sublist whenever the radius/potential decrease of the refined
   pieces pays for the concave query-price increase
   \(\sum_iK_i^\rho/K^\rho\).  Without \((PQR2)\), such a refinement need not
   preserve positive gain.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For each \(q\), the first inequality in \((PQR2)\) gives
   \[
      b_0^\rho\sum_i\psi_iK_i^\rho\widehat\tau_q
      \le
      b_0^\rho\psi K^\rho\widehat\tau_q .
   \]
   Therefore
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \bigl(h_L(q)-b_0^\rho\psi K^\rho\widehat\tau_q\bigr)_+
      &\le
      \left(
         \sum_i h_i(q)
         -
         b_0^\rho\sum_i\psi_iK_i^\rho\widehat\tau_q
      \right)_+  \\
      &\le
      \sum_i
      \bigl(h_i(q)-b_0^\rho\psi_iK_i^\rho\widehat\tau_q\bigr)_+ ,
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   using subadditivity of \(x\mapsto x_+\) in the final step.  Summing over
   \(q\) and applying \((PQR3)\) yields
   \[
      \sum_i\sum_q
      \bigl(h_i(q)-b_0^\rho\psi_iK_i^\rho\widehat\tau_q\bigr)_+
      >
      b_0^{1+\rho}\psi\sigma K^{1+\rho}.
   \]
   By the second inequality in \((PQR2)\), the right hand side is at least
   \[
      \sum_i b_0^{1+\rho}\psi_i\sigma K_i^{1+\rho}.
   \]
   Hence at least one index \(i\) satisfies \((PQR4)\).  Applying the
   cardinality-net form \((QFG3)\) of
   \cref{cor:query-free-deficient-shadow-list-gain} inside \(W_i\) gives the
   finite-prefix repair alternative.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Bounded-fanout radius-discount refinement]
   \label{cor:bounded-fanout-radius-discount-refinement}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:price-compatible-query-free-refinement}.  Suppose the partition
   has at most \(J\) nonempty pieces and every child price factor satisfies
   \[
      \psi_i\le\theta\psi .
      \tag{BFR1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \theta J^{1-\rho}\le1,
      \tag{BFR2}
   \]
   then the refinement is price-compatible, so any parent list satisfying
   \((PQR3)\) has a child piece satisfying \((PQR4)\).

   In particular, for the padded radius potential
   \[
      \psi(R)=\Psi(R)=1+\left(\frac Rr\right)^4,
   \]
   a refinement of a parent ball of radius \(R\) into at most \(J\) certified
   balls of radii \(R_i\le R_\star\) is price-compatible whenever
   \[
      \frac{\Psi(R_\star)}{\Psi(R)}
      \le
      J^{-(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{BFR3}
   \]
   Thus a bounded-fanout ball decomposition can be used as a compact
   Hall-shadow repair exactly when its radius contraction pays the
   \(J^{1-\rho}\) concave query-price surcharge.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(0<\rho<1\) and the \(K_i\)'s sum to \(K\),
   \[
      \sum_iK_i^\rho
      \le
      J^{1-\rho}K^\rho
      \tag{BFR4}
   \]
   by Hölder's inequality.  Therefore \((BFR1)\)--\((BFR2)\) give
   \[
      \sum_i\psi_iK_i^\rho
      \le
      \theta\psi J^{1-\rho}K^\rho
      \le
      \psi K^\rho .
   \]
   For storage,
   \[
      \sum_iK_i^{1+\rho}\le K^{1+\rho},
   \]
   because the pieces are disjoint and the exponent is at least one.  Also
   \((BFR2)\) implies \(\theta\le1\).  Hence
   \[
      \sum_i\psi_iK_i^{1+\rho}
      \le
      \theta\psi\sum_iK_i^{1+\rho}
      \le
      \psi K^{1+\rho}.
   \]
   This is \((PQR2)\), so
   \cref{cor:price-compatible-query-free-refinement} applies.  The radius
   statement is the specialization \(\psi_i=\Psi(R_i)\), \(\psi=\Psi(R)\), and
   \(R_i\le R_\star\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Renyi-spread Hall-shadow obstruction]
   \label{cor:renyi-spread-hall-shadow-obstruction}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:price-compatible-query-free-refinement}.  Let \(L\) be a
   positive-gain parent list satisfying \((PQR3)\), with size \(K\), price
   factor \(\psi\), and exponent \(0<\rho<1\).  Let
   \[
      L=\bigsqcup_{i\in I}L_i,\qquad K_i=|L_i|
   \]
   be any partition into nonempty certified child lists \(L_i\subseteq W_i\),
   where every \(W_i\) has \(b_0\)-dense retained cardinalities and price factor
   at most a common value \(\psi_\star\le\psi\).  If no child satisfies the
   positive child gain condition \((PQR4)\), then the child-size distribution
   must obey
   \[
      \sum_iK_i^\rho
      >
      \frac{\psi}{\psi_\star}K^\rho .
      \tag{RSH1}
   \]
   Equivalently, for \(z_i=K_i/K\),
   \[
      \sum_i z_i^\rho>\frac{\psi}{\psi_\star},
      \qquad
      \left(\sum_i z_i^\rho\right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      >
      \left(\frac{\psi}{\psi_\star}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{RSH2}
   \]
   Thus a failed smaller-radius refinement is not just a large-fanout object:
   the positive Hall shadow must be spread across many child cells in the
   Renyi-effective sense.  For padded ball prices, \(\psi=\Psi(R)\) and
   \(\psi_\star=\Psi(R_\star)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose instead that
   \[
      \sum_iK_i^\rho
      \le
      \frac{\psi}{\psi_\star}K^\rho .
   \]
   Since every \(\psi_i\le\psi_\star\),
   \[
      \sum_i\psi_iK_i^\rho
      \le
      \psi_\star\sum_iK_i^\rho
      \le
      \psi K^\rho .
   \]
   The storage price is also compatible, because \(\psi_\star\le\psi\) and
   \(1+\rho\ge1\):
   \[
      \sum_i\psi_iK_i^{1+\rho}
      \le
      \psi_\star\sum_iK_i^{1+\rho}
      \le
      \psi K^{1+\rho}.
   \]
   Hence \((PQR2)\) holds.  By
   \cref{cor:price-compatible-query-free-refinement}, some child must satisfy
   \((PQR4)\), contradicting the hypothesis.  Dividing \((RSH1)\) by
   \(K^\rho\) gives the first form of \((RSH2)\); the effective-support form is
   just a monotone reparameterization.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Renyi-cover Hall-shadow closure]
   \label{cor:renyi-cover-hall-shadow-closure}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:price-compatible-query-free-refinement}.  Let \(L\subseteq W\) be
   a positive-gain parent list satisfying \((PQR3)\), with size \(K\), price
   factor \(\psi\), and exponent \(0<\rho<1\).  Let
   \(\mathcal W_\star=\{W_i:i\in I\}\) be a finite family of certified child
   containers, where \(W_i\) has price factor \(\psi_i\), the same exponent
   \(\rho\), and \(b_0\)-dense retained cardinalities.  Suppose there is an
   assignment \(\kappa:L\to I\) with \(p\in W_{\kappa(p)}\) for every \(p\in L\).
   Put
   \[
      L_i=\{p\in L:\kappa(p)=i\},
      \qquad K_i=|L_i|,
   \]
   discarding empty parts.  If the assigned Renyi cover is price-compatible,
   \[
      \sum_i\psi_iK_i^\rho\le\psi K^\rho,
      \qquad
      \sum_i\psi_iK_i^{1+\rho}\le\psi K^{1+\rho},
      \tag{RCH1}
   \]
   then some assigned child \(L_i\subseteq W_i\) satisfies the positive child
   gain condition \((PQR4)\), and hence the finite-prefix repair alternative
   holds.

   Conversely, if no child in the certified family satisfies \((PQR4)\), every
   assignment of \(L\) to that family violates at least one inequality in
   \((RCH1)\).  In particular, if every used child has \(\psi_i\le\psi\), then
   the storage inequality in \((RCH1)\) is automatic for every assignment, and a
   surviving residual must satisfy
   \[
      \sum_i\psi_iK_i^\rho>\psi K^\rho
      \tag{RCH2}
   \]
   for every certified assignment.

   Thus the compactification objective is the assigned Renyi cover price
   \(\sum_i\psi_iK_i^\rho\), not the raw number of clusters.  The bounded-fanout
   and metric-entropy tests below are balanced sufficient conditions for this
   sharper unbalanced cover condition.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The assignment partitions \(L\) into the nonempty certified lists
   \(L_i\subseteq W_i\).  The two inequalities in \((RCH1)\) are exactly the
   price-compatibility hypotheses \((PQR2)\).  Therefore
   \cref{cor:price-compatible-query-free-refinement} gives a child satisfying
   \((PQR4)\), and that corollary supplies the finite-prefix repair.

   The residual statement is the contrapositive.  If no child satisfies
   \((PQR4)\) but some assignment obeyed both inequalities in \((RCH1)\), the
   first part would produce such a child.  Finally, when \(\psi_i\le\psi\),
   disjointness of the assigned pieces gives
   \[
      \sum_i\psi_iK_i^{1+\rho}
      \le
      \psi\sum_iK_i^{1+\rho}
      \le
      \psi K^{1+\rho},
   \]
   so only the query Renyi cover price can fail.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Soft Renyi-cover assignment hardening]
   \label{cor:soft-renyi-cover-assignment-hardening}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:renyi-cover-hall-shadow-closure}, and assume every child used by
   the assignment law has \(\psi_i\le\psi\).  Let \(\kappa\) be any randomized
   feasible assignment of \(L\) to the certified child family, so
   \(p\in W_{\kappa(p)}\) almost surely for every \(p\in L\).  Put
   \[
      S_i=|\{p\in L:\kappa(p)=i\}|,
      \qquad
      \mu_i=\E S_i .
   \]
   If the marginal Renyi cover price satisfies
   \[
      \sum_i\psi_i\mu_i^\rho\le\psi K^\rho,
      \tag{SRH1}
   \]
   then some deterministic assignment in the support of \(\kappa\) satisfies
   \((RCH1)\).  Consequently some child list satisfies the positive child gain
   condition \((PQR4)\), and the finite-prefix repair alternative holds.

   In particular, a fractional feasible assignment
   \(z_{p,i}\ge0\), supported only on pairs \(p\in W_i\), with
   \(\sum_i z_{p,i}=1\) for every \(p\in L\), closes whenever
   \[
      \sum_i\psi_i
      \left(\sum_{p\in L}z_{p,i}\right)^\rho
      \le
      \psi K^\rho .
      \tag{SRH2}
   \]
   Thus a surviving Hall shadow must violate the marginal Renyi-cover
   inequality for every certified soft assignment with child price factors at
   most \(\psi\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(0<\rho<1\), Jensen's inequality gives
   \[
      \E S_i^\rho\le(\E S_i)^\rho=\mu_i^\rho
   \]
   for every \(i\).  Hence, for
   \(Q(\kappa)=\sum_i\psi_iS_i^\rho\),
   \[
      \E Q(\kappa)
      \le
      \sum_i\psi_i\mu_i^\rho
      \le
      \psi K^\rho .
   \]
   Some deterministic outcome of \(\kappa\) therefore has
   \(Q(\kappa)\le\psi K^\rho\).  For that outcome the storage inequality in
   \((RCH1)\) is automatic, because \(\psi_i\le\psi\), the assigned parts are
   disjoint, and
   \[
      \sum_i\psi_iS_i^{1+\rho}
      \le
      \psi\sum_iS_i^{1+\rho}
      \le
      \psi\left(\sum_iS_i\right)^{1+\rho}
      =
      \psi K^{1+\rho}.
   \]
   Thus the deterministic assignment satisfies \((RCH1)\), and
   \cref{cor:renyi-cover-hall-shadow-closure} applies.

   The fractional statement is obtained by independently assigning each
   \(p\in L\) to child \(i\) with probability \(z_{p,i}\).  Then
   \(\mu_i=\sum_{p\in L}z_{p,i}\), and the first part applies.  The residual
   statement is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Metric-entropy Hall-shadow closure]
   \label{cor:metric-entropy-hall-shadow-closure}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:bounded-fanout-radius-discount-refinement}, and suppose the parent
   list \(L\) lies in a certified parent ball with price
   \(\psi=\Psi(R)\).  Let \(\mathcal B_\star\) be a family of available
   certified child ball containers, each with price factor at most
   \(\Psi(R_\star)\), the same exponent \(\rho\), and \(b_0\)-dense retained
   cardinalities.  Define the certified covering number
   \[
      N_\star(L,R_\star)
      =
      \min\left\{
      J:\ L\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^J W_j,\quad W_j\in\mathcal B_\star
      \right\}.
      \tag{MEH1}
   \]
   If \(L\) satisfies the positive parent gain condition \((PQR3)\) and
   \[
      N_\star(L,R_\star)^{1-\rho}\Psi(R_\star)
      \le
      \Psi(R),
      \tag{MEH2}
   \]
   then the finite-prefix repair alternative of
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-hall-deficit-oracle} holds.  More precisely, for
   any certified cover in \((MEH1)\) whose size \(J\) satisfies
   \(J^{1-\rho}\Psi(R_\star)\le\Psi(R)\), assigning every point of \(L\) to one
   covering container yields a child list that satisfies the positive child
   gain condition \((PQR4)\).

   Consequently, suppose the available radius-\(R_\star\) family contains no
   certified child list satisfying the child gain condition \((PQR4)\).  Then
   every positive-gain parent list \(L\) must obey the metric-entropy
   obstruction
   \[
      N_\star(L,R_\star)
      >
      \left(\frac{\Psi(R)}{\Psi(R_\star)}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{MEH3}
   \]
   Thus an unclosed Hall shadow is forced to have large certified covering
   number at every radius whose potential discount is large enough to pay the
   \(J^{1-\rho}\) fanout surcharge.  This is the balanced specialization of
   \cref{cor:renyi-cover-hall-shadow-closure}, obtained by upper-bounding the
   assigned Renyi cover price with Hölder.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Choose a certified cover \(W_1,\ldots,W_J\in\mathcal B_\star\) of \(L\) with
   \(J=N_\star(L,R_\star)\), or any cover satisfying the displayed
   fanout--discount inequality.  Break ties arbitrarily and assign each
   \(p\in L\) to one covering container.  This partitions \(L\) into nonempty
   child lists \(L_i\subseteq W_i\), after discarding empty parts.

   Each child price factor is at most \(\Psi(R_\star)\), so with
   \(\theta=\Psi(R_\star)/\Psi(R)\) we have
   \[
      \psi_i\le\theta\psi .
   \]
   The inequality \(J^{1-\rho}\Psi(R_\star)\le\Psi(R)\) is exactly
   \(\theta J^{1-\rho}\le1\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:bounded-fanout-radius-discount-refinement} applies to the
   partition, and some child satisfies \((PQR4)\).  The finite-prefix repair
   follows from
   \cref{cor:price-compatible-query-free-refinement}.

   The obstruction \((MEH3)\) is the contrapositive: if a positive parent list
   had covering number at most the right hand side, the first part would
   produce a certified child repair in the radius-\(R_\star\) family.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Low-doubling Hall shadows close]
   \label{cor:low-doubling-hall-shadow-close}
   In the setting of
   \cref{cor:metric-entropy-hall-shadow-closure}, let \(0<\lambda\le1\) and
   \(R_\star=\lambda R\).  Suppose a positive-gain parent list \(L\) has a
   certified low-entropy cover
   \[
      N_\star(L,\lambda R)\le C_{\rm dbl}\lambda^{-\delta}
      \tag{LDH1}
   \]
   and the scale parameters satisfy
   \[
      C_{\rm dbl}\lambda^{-\delta}
      \le
      \left(\frac{\Psi(R)}{\Psi(\lambda R)}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)} .
      \tag{LDH2}
   \]
   Then the finite-prefix repair alternative holds.

   In particular, if
   \[
      \delta<\frac{4}{1-\rho},
      \tag{LDH3}
   \]
   then for every fixed \(C_{\rm dbl}\) there is a constant
   \(\lambda=\lambda(\rho,\delta,C_{\rm dbl})\in(0,1]\) such that \((LDH2)\)
   holds whenever \(R\ge r/\lambda\).  Therefore, away from the terminal radius,
   any positive Hall shadow that survives all radius-\(\lambda R\) certified
   child repairs must have no certified doubling cover of dimension below
   \(4/(1-\rho)\) at that scale.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The first claim is \cref{cor:metric-entropy-hall-shadow-closure} with
   \(R_\star=\lambda R\) and the bound \((LDH1)\).

   For the final claim, choose \(\lambda\) small enough that
   \[
      C_{\rm dbl}\lambda^{-\delta}
      \le
      2^{-1/(1-\rho)}\lambda^{-4/(1-\rho)} ,
      \tag{LDH4}
   \]
   which is possible by \((LDH3)\).  If \(R\ge r/\lambda\), then
   \(x=R/r\) satisfies \(\lambda^4x^4\ge1\), and hence
   \[
      \frac{\Psi(R)}{\Psi(\lambda R)}
      =
      \frac{1+x^4}{1+\lambda^4x^4}
      \ge
      \frac{x^4}{2\lambda^4x^4}
      =
      \frac1{2\lambda^4}.
   \]
   Raising to the power \(1/(1-\rho)\) and using \((LDH4)\) gives \((LDH2)\).
   The surviving-shadow statement is the contrapositive of the first claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Low-diameter query-free Hall-shadow seeding]
   \label{cor:low-diameter-query-free-hall-seeding}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:query-free-deficient-shadow-list-gain}, and suppose the current
   resident points lie in one shell around a center \(o\).  For
   \(x\ne o\), write \(\widehat x_o=(x-o)/\|x-o\|\).  Let \(W_0\) be a
   certified ambient container, let \(\omega_p\ge0\) be sampling weights on
   \(W_0\), and let \(\omega(W_0)>0\).  Draw \(T\) independent seeds from
   \(W_0\) with probabilities \(\omega_p/\omega(W_0)\).  Assume there is a
   nonempty hidden list \(A\subseteq W_0\), \(K_A=|A|\), such that
   \[
      \omega(A)\ge\alpha\,\omega(W_0)
      \tag{LQH1}
   \]
   for some \(\alpha>0\), and
   \[
      \|\widehat p_o-\widehat p'_o\|\le\eta
      \qquad(p,p'\in A).
      \tag{LQH2}
   \]
   When a seed \(x\) is sampled, suppose preprocessing proposes a certified cap
   container \(W_x\) containing
   \[
      C_x=
      \left\{
      p\in W_0:
      \langle\widehat x_o,\widehat p_o\rangle
      \ge 1-\frac{\eta^2}{2}
      \right\},
      \tag{LQH3}
   \]
   and the retained cardinalities in \(W_x\) are \(b_0\)-dense from above.
   Define the hidden-list shadow profile
   \[
      h_A(q)=
      \sum_{\substack{p\in A:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N_{G'}}}
      \widehat\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{LQH4}
   \]
   If, for every seed \(x\in A\), the proposed container \(W_x\) with parameters
   \((\psi_x,\rho_x)\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}
      \bigl(h_A(q)-b_0^{\rho_x}\psi_xK_A^{\rho_x}\widehat\tau_q\bigr)_+
      >
      b_0^{1+\rho_x}\psi_x\sigma K_A^{1+\rho_x},
      \tag{LQH5}
   \]
   then the sampled proposal routine finds a finite-prefix repair with
   probability at least \(1-e^{-\alpha T}\).  Exhaustive enumeration of all
   data directions in \(W_0\) finds such a repair deterministically.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \((LQH1)\), the probability that no sampled seed lies in \(A\) is at most
   \((1-\alpha)^T\le e^{-\alpha T}\).  If a sampled seed \(x\) lies in \(A\),
   then \((LQH2)\) gives, for every \(p\in A\),
   \[
      \langle\widehat x_o,\widehat p_o\rangle
      =
      1-\frac12\|\widehat x_o-\widehat p_o\|^2
      \ge
      1-\frac{\eta^2}{2}.
   \]
   Thus \(A\subseteq C_x\subseteq W_x\).  Applying the cardinality-net form
   \((QFG3)\) of \cref{cor:query-free-deficient-shadow-list-gain} inside this
   container, with the deterministic list \(L=A\), shows that \((LQH5)\)
   supplies the finite-prefix repair alternative of
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-hall-deficit-oracle}.  Enumerating all data
   directions includes every \(x\in A\), so the same argument is deterministic
   in the exhaustive build-time variant.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Certified ball repairs are cap-enumerable]
   \label{cor:certified-ball-repair-cap-enumerable}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:low-diameter-query-free-hall-seeding}.  Suppose in addition that
   \(W_0\) lies outside radius \(s_{\min}>0\) from the shell center \(o\),
   \[
      \|p-o\|\ge s_{\min}\qquad(p\in W_0),
      \tag{CBR1}
   \]
   and that the hidden list \(A\) is contained in a certified Euclidean ball
   \(B(c_A,R_A)\).  Put
   \[
      \eta_A=\frac{4R_A}{s_{\min}}.
      \tag{CBR2}
   \]
   If the cap proposal generated by every enumerated seed \(x\in W_0\) includes
   the threshold
   \[
      \left\{
      p\in W_0:
      \langle\widehat x_o,\widehat p_o\rangle
      \ge 1-\frac{\eta_A^2}{2}
      \right\},
      \tag{CBR3}
   \]
   then the low-diameter hypothesis \((LQH2)\) holds for \(A\) with
   \(\eta=\eta_A\).  Consequently, whenever the query-free gain condition
   \((LQH5)\) holds for the certified cap container generated by each
   \(x\in A\), exhaustive enumeration of all resident directions finds a
   finite-prefix Hall-shadow repair deterministically.

   The same statement holds for randomized seeding with miss probability
   \(e^{-\alpha T}\) whenever \(A\) also carries sampling mass
   \(\omega(A)\ge\alpha\omega(W_0)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For \(p,p'\in A\), the Euclidean ball certificate gives
   \(\|p-p'\|\le2R_A\).  Writing \(u=p-o\) and \(v=p'-o\), and assuming
   without loss of generality that \(\|u\|\le\|v\|\), we have
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \left\|\frac{u}{\|u\|}-\frac{v}{\|v\|}\right\|
      &\le
      \left\|\frac{u-v}{\|u\|}\right\|
      +
      \|v\|\left|\frac1{\|u\|}-\frac1{\|v\|}\right|  \\
      &\le
      \frac{2\|u-v\|}{\|u\|}
      \le
      \frac{4R_A}{s_{\min}}
      =
      \eta_A .
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   Thus \(A\) satisfies \((LQH2)\).  The deterministic and randomized
   conclusions are exactly \cref{cor:low-diameter-query-free-hall-seeding}
   applied with \(\eta=\eta_A\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Deficient-shadow residual obstruction]
   \label{cor:deficient-shadow-residual-obstruction}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:lower-hull-hall-proposal-separator}.  Fix a finite prefix-search
   family \((\mathcal W,\mathcal K_W)\) as in
   \cref{cor:no-prefix-deficient-shadow-envelope}.  Suppose the Hall-success
   alternative is not certified, the exact-load Hall profile has a strict
   lower-hull deficit for the declared pair congestion, and no prefix in this
   finite family closes the guarded residual.  Then there is an integral guard
   sublayer \(G'\) such that
   \[
      \Delta(G')>0
      \tag{DSR1}
   \]
   and the deficient-shadow envelope \((NDE2)\) holds for every
   \(W\in\mathcal W\) and \(h\in\mathcal K_W\).  In addition, for any finite
   family \(\mathcal U\) of certified subcontainers \(U\subseteq W\) with
   \(W\in\mathcal W\) and \(|U|\in\mathcal K_W\), the flow-value residual
   \((FVS2)\) holds for every \(U\in\mathcal U\) and every congestion \(C>0\).
   Equivalently, by \cref{cor:flow-value-shadow-mass-equivalence}, every such
   subcontainer satisfies
   \[
      D_{G'}(U)\le R_W(|U|).
      \tag{HSM1}
   \]
   Every target \(M/C>R_W(|U|)\) therefore exposes the localized cut
   obstruction \((RDT8)\).  Consequently the tail envelope \((TDE2)\) holds for
   every threshold \(t>0\) whose superlevel cardinality \(h_{W,t}\) lies in
   \(\mathcal K_W\), and every such threshold layer satisfies the two-price
   alternative \((TDS2)\)--\((TDS3)\).  When \(0<\rho_W<1\), the same layer also
   satisfies the forbidden-middle-scale conclusion \((FMS1)\)--\((FMS2)\).

   Moreover, if \(0<\rho_W<1\) and \(\mathcal K_W\) is \(b\)-dense from below as
   in \((CSD1)\), then no threshold \(t>0\) with \(h_{W,t}>0\) can satisfy
   \((CSD3)\).  In particular, when \(\sigma>0\), no such threshold layer can
   satisfy the constant-slack forbidden-interval condition \((CSD4)\), and no
   finite level panel can satisfy the level-surplus condition \((DCL2)\).
   No interval \(0<u<v\) and exponent \(s\ge0\) can satisfy the integral
   moment-surplus condition \((DMI1)\), and hence neither \((DMI2)\) nor
   \((DMI6)\).  No dyadic partition can satisfy the multiscale window surplus
   condition \((DWD3)\), and hence neither \((DWD5)\).  Equivalently, the
   dyadic-window residual envelopes \((DWE1)\)--\((DWE3)\) hold.  In particular,
   the dyadic log-Lorentz separator inequality \((DLG2)\) fails for every
   interval \(0<u<v\), and every finite fractional log-Lorentz panel has
   nonpositive total surplus \((FLL3)\).  The same is true for every certified
   log-Lorentz panel satisfying \((CLL1)\)--\((CLL2)\): its certified surplus
   \((CLL4)\) is nonpositive.  In particular, every finite mass-support panel
   satisfying \((MSL1)\)--\((MSL2)\) has nonpositive surplus \((MSL5)\), every
   mass-support record fails the average-density screen \((ADS3)\), and every
   balanced mass-support record satisfying \((BDS3)\) fails the balanced density
   screen \((BDS4)\).  Every retained top-prefix record satisfying \((TPD1)\)
   fails \((TPD2)\), and every coarse report with an available balanced trim
   satisfying \((TPD3)\) fails \((TPD4)\).  Equivalently, these records obey the
   fixed-threshold residual bounds obtained by reversing \((FTD2)\)--\((FTD3)\),
   and every finite admissible fixed-threshold density panel has nonpositive
   surplus \((FFD4)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{cor:integral-hall-deficit-normal-form}, the strict exact-load deficit
   supplies an integral guard sublayer \(G'\) satisfying \((DSR1)\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:no-prefix-deficient-shadow-envelope} to this \(G'\) gives
   \((NDE2)\) for every searched prefix, because no such prefix closes the
   residual by hypothesis.  The flow-value statement is the contrapositive of
   \cref{cor:flow-value-deficient-shadow-screen}: if a certified
   \(U\subseteq W\), \(|U|\in\mathcal K_W\), had
   \(\Phi_U(C)/C>R_W(|U|)\), then the top-\(|U|\) deficient-shadow prefix in
   \(W\) would close by
   \cref{cor:deficient-shadow-prefix-certificate}, contradicting the
   hypothesis.  The shadow-mass form \((HSM1)\) is
   \cref{cor:flow-value-shadow-mass-equivalence}.  The cut conclusion is the
   final part of
   \cref{cor:flow-value-deficient-shadow-screen}.  The tail statement is then
   \cref{cor:tail-deficient-shadow-envelope}, and the final two-price alternative
   is \cref{cor:two-price-deficient-shadow-screen}.  The scale conclusion is
   \cref{cor:forbidden-middle-deficient-shadow-scale}.  The final
   cardinality-net exclusion is the contrapositive of
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-deficient-shadow-reporter}, and the panel exclusion
   is the contrapositive of \cref{cor:layer-cake-deficient-shadow-reporter}.
   The integral exclusion is the contrapositive of
   \cref{cor:integral-deficient-shadow-moment-reporter}.  The dyadic-window
   exclusion is the contrapositive of
   \cref{cor:dyadic-window-deficient-shadow-moment-reporter}.  The residual
   envelopes are exactly
   \cref{cor:dyadic-window-deficient-shadow-residual-envelope}.  The final
   log-Lorentz statement is
   \cref{cor:dyadic-log-lorentz-deficient-shadow-separator}.  The panel
   statement is \cref{cor:fractional-log-lorentz-deficient-shadow-panel}.  The
   final certified-panel statement is
   \cref{cor:certified-log-lorentz-deficient-shadow-panel}.  The final
   mass-support statement is
   \cref{cor:mass-support-log-lorentz-certificate}.  The density-screen
   statement is \cref{cor:average-density-mass-support-screen}.  The balanced
   density-screen statement is \cref{cor:balanced-average-density-screen}.  The
   top-prefix and trimmed-prefix density statements are
   \cref{cor:balanced-top-prefix-density-screen}.  The fixed-threshold
   restatement is \cref{cor:fixed-threshold-balanced-density-screen}.  The
   fixed-threshold panel statement is
   \cref{cor:fractional-fixed-threshold-density-panel}.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:query-layer-deficient-shadow-residual-obstruction} is the current
proof bottleneck in one line: rule out the simultaneous existence of a
positive-excess Hall sublayer and the query-layer finite-prefix envelopes
\((QLDS2)\)--\((QLDS5)\) over a rich enough family of affordable smaller-radius
containers.  The older all-loaded shadow-mass obstruction
\cref{cor:deficient-shadow-residual-obstruction} is the specialization
\(y_q\equiv1\).  The useful gain is that a geometric argument, LP range
reporter, list decoder, additive quantizer, or center proposal only pays the
layer price \(A_y=\sum_q\widehat\tau_qy_q\), not the global loaded-query price
\(\sum_q\tau_qa_q\).  The query-layer two-price screen \((QLDS6)\) separates the
remaining failure into a query-price bound or a storage-price bound at every
exposed scale, and \((QLDS7)\) says that a residual layer can survive only by
being small enough for its own query layer or large enough for storage price.
\Cref{cor:query-layer-random-list-deficient-shadow-repair} is the build-time
proposal interface at this level: a randomized list, center set, additive
quantizer output, or list-decoding panel closes as soon as its expected
query-layer captured mass beats the corresponding query/storage Renyi moments.
Thus expensive preprocessing may search heuristically, but the retained proof
object is still one Boolean query layer and one top prefix.
\Cref{cor:query-free-deficient-shadow-list-gain} optimizes out the query layer
for proposal search: a hard list or marginal center law is scored by a positive
part over queries, and any positive score already contains the Boolean query
layer needed by \((DFN3)\).  This is the reduced-gain objective that build-time
\(k\)-means++, facility, AQ, range-reporting, or list-decoding proposals should
try to maximize.
\Cref{cor:price-compatible-query-free-refinement} records the exact accounting
needed to compactify a positive list: a refinement into smaller certified
pieces preserves positive query-free gain whenever the refined aggregate query
and storage prices \(\sum_i\psi_iK_i^\rho\) and
\(\sum_i\psi_iK_i^{1+\rho}\) are no larger than the parent prices.  This is
where radius contraction can pay for the otherwise fatal concavity loss in
\(K^\rho\).
\Cref{cor:bounded-fanout-radius-discount-refinement} gives the usable geometric
screen: a split into \(J\) pieces is safe if each piece has radius-potential
discount at most \(J^{-(1-\rho)}\).  Thus the build-time clustering target is a
bounded-fanout ball decomposition whose certified radii beat this fanout
threshold; if such a decomposition carries the Hall-shadow gain, one child
piece already closes.
\Cref{cor:renyi-spread-hall-shadow-obstruction} gives the sharper unbalanced
form: if no child closes, the list mass cannot merely be covered by many cells;
it must have large Renyi-effective support across the child partition.  This is
the distribution-sensitive quantity a facility or additive-quantization cover
should minimize.
\Cref{cor:renyi-cover-hall-shadow-closure} states the positive version: an
overlapping certified cover closes as soon as some assignment of the Hall shadow
has assigned Renyi price \(\sum_i\psi_iK_i^\rho\) and storage price below the
parent prices.  Thus uneven cluster sizes are charged at their true concave
cost, rather than through the worst-case fanout surrogate.
\Cref{cor:soft-renyi-cover-assignment-hardening} removes the need to guess the
hard assignment during proposal search: any soft membership law whose marginal
loads have Renyi price below the parent hardens to one deterministic assigned
cover.  This is the proof-native interpretation of \(k\)-means++,
facility-location, or additive-quantization soft memberships.
\Cref{cor:metric-entropy-hall-shadow-closure} turns this into a metric
separator: any positive-gain Hall shadow with certified covering number below
\((\Psi(R)/\Psi(R_\star))^{1/(1-\rho)}\) at radius \(R_\star\) already closes.
\Cref{cor:low-doubling-hall-shadow-close} gives the clean large-radius
interpretation: low certified doubling dimension, below \(4/(1-\rho)\), is
enough to force a repair at a constant radius drop.  Hence an unclosed shadow is
not merely ``not found by \(k\)-means''; it must be genuinely high-entropy at
the tested scale.
\Cref{cor:low-diameter-query-free-hall-seeding} gives the corresponding
compact-shadow sampling guarantee.  If the positive-gain list is contained in a
low-diameter shell cap and carries an \(\alpha\)-fraction of the chosen residual
or dual sampling weight, \(T=O(\alpha^{-1}\log(1/\delta))\) seeds find a cap
proposal containing it with probability \(1-\delta\), and exhaustive
enumeration finds it deterministically.  Thus \(k\)-means++-style seeding is
analyzable once the geometric separator proves that some compact positive-gain
Hall shadow exists; the corollary does not by itself prove that existence.
\Cref{cor:certified-ball-repair-cap-enumerable} removes the angular condition
from any repair that is already certified as a small Euclidean ball inside a
shell: radius \(R_A\) at shell radius at least \(s_{\min}\) gives angular
diameter at most \(4R_A/s_{\min}\).  With unrestricted build time, enumerating
all resident centers therefore finds every such certified ball repair; random
seeding is only needed to reduce preprocessing work.

The resulting proof status is deliberately narrower than the number of
available proposal interfaces might suggest.  The lead route is now:
\[
   \text{finite-prefix Hall residual}
   \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
   \begin{cases}
      \text{price-compatible smaller-radius prefix},\\
      \text{or high-Renyi-spread packing}.
   \end{cases}
\]
The first branch is closed by the refinement and metric-entropy lemmas above.
In the second branch, the separated packing should be kept as a weighted Renyi
center law whenever possible; after an optional dyadic center-level extraction it
feeds the entropy-energy/list-decoding screen and then the total-load Gaussian
paid-fiber separator, preferably in the weighted form of
\cref{cor:weighted-gaussian-paid-fiber-separator}.  There the remaining
obstruction is only total active load or a positive inherited prefix, not a new
margin-splitting procedure.
Thus additional clustering, quotient, sampled-center, or posterior wrappers are
progress only if they prove one of these two facts: a positive finite-prefix
repair, or a high-spread paid-fiber exposure bound that triggers
\cref{cor:total-load-gaussian-paid-fiber-separator}.  This is the current
anti-drift checkpoint for the dense-overlap proof.
\Cref{cor:transported-deficient-shadow-certificate} is the corresponding
threshold-free reporter form: if the geometry supplies one bounded-congestion
shipment into a certified subset whose transported mass per congestion beats
the direct mixed price, the same deficient-shadow prefix closes immediately.
\Cref{lem:restricted-deficient-shadow-transport-cut} gives the exact residual
for one proposed subset: if such a shipment cannot be certified at a price level
that would close, the obstruction is a localized Hall cut with too much
guard-incidence load for the paid shadow available inside that subset.
\Cref{cor:flow-value-deficient-shadow-screen} is the family-level version:
preprocessing may solve the finite max-flow instances exactly, and a surviving
residual must have nonpositive flow-value surplus for every proposed subset and
congestion scale.
\Cref{lem:infinitesimal-flow-deficient-shadow} and
\cref{cor:flow-value-shadow-mass-equivalence} simplify this endpoint: if the
congestion scale is unrestricted, the supremum of the normalized flow value for
one subset is exactly its deficient-shadow mass.  Thus the max-flow screen is
not an additional geometric principle; it is a verifier for the same subset
shadow-mass certificate used by
\cref{cor:deficient-shadow-prefix-certificate}.
\Cref{cor:cardinality-net-deficient-shadow-reporter} removes the exact-size
artifact from this target: with dyadic retained prefix sizes, an arbitrary
reported superlevel in the forbidden interval is rounded down to a certified
prefix at only constant loss.  \Cref{cor:layer-cake-deficient-shadow-reporter}
is the averaged version: a range-reporting or list-decoding panel only has to
make captured deficient-shadow mass beat the aggregate query and storage moments
on one height window.
\Cref{cor:integral-deficient-shadow-moment-reporter} gives the continuous
Lorentz form, so the next geometric theorem may prove a truncated moment
inequality instead of materializing threshold levels.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-window-deficient-shadow-moment-reporter} makes that target
finite again: it is enough to prove positive surplus on the sum of dyadic height
windows, with no extra per-prefix layer-cake toll.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-window-deficient-shadow-residual-envelope} is the explicit
failure form: every capped deficient-shadow moment is bounded by the sum of
dyadic Renyi query/storage moments.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-log-lorentz-deficient-shadow-separator} specializes this to
the capped linear moment, leaving only dyadic threshold cardinalities on the
right hand side.  \Cref{cor:fractional-log-lorentz-deficient-shadow-panel}
makes the same target fully fractional over proposed containers and height
windows: a range reporter, list decoder, additive quantizer, or seeded
clustering routine only has to produce positive expected verified surplus, and
the deterministic proof then retains one positive record as an ordinary dense
filter-cover column.
\Cref{cor:certified-log-lorentz-deficient-shadow-panel} weakens the required
reporter output further: lower bounds on capped captured mass and upper bounds
on dyadic superlevel cardinalities are enough.  This is the rank-profile form
that a range-reporting or list-decoding theorem can certify without exactly
materializing the whole deficient-shadow degree sequence.
\Cref{cor:mass-support-log-lorentz-certificate} removes the interval choice
when the reporter has only coarse statistics: total captured shadow mass,
support size, and maximum degree determine a canonical interval that captures
half the mass.
\Cref{cor:average-density-mass-support-screen} divides this test by support
size: the target is now an average deficient-shadow density that beats a
query-price term decreasing in the support size and a storage-price term
increasing in the support size.
\Cref{cor:balanced-average-density-screen} evaluates this density test at the
stationary support scale, leaving a single threshold proportional to
\(\psi_W\mathfrak L A_+^{\rho_W}\sigma^{1-\rho_W}\), up to balance constants
and the coarse-statistics dynamic-range window count \(\mathfrak L\).
\Cref{cor:balanced-top-prefix-density-screen} is the sharper materialized-prefix
version: if the reporter can certify a top deficient-shadow prefix near the
stationary support scale, the dynamic-range factor disappears entirely, and
oversized coarse reports may be trimmed down to that scale.
\Cref{cor:fixed-threshold-balanced-density-screen} records the resulting direct
target density
\(\Xi\), where
\(\Xi\asymp\psi_WA_+^{\rho_W}\sigma^{1-\rho_W}\).
\Cref{cor:fractional-fixed-threshold-density-panel} restores the proposal-law
interface at this fixed level: positive expected density surplus over a finite
panel already contains one deterministic retained dense column.
\Cref{cor:sampled-fixed-threshold-density-search} is the build-time version:
with a positive surplus margin and a bound on positive surplus, repeated seeded
proposal panels find such a deterministic column with high probability, while
only the verified retained record is charged to the index.
\Cref{cor:fixed-threshold-hall-deficit-oracle} plugs this target back into the
Hall chain: every strict lower-hull Hall deficit is repaired once the reporter
finds a positive fixed-threshold density panel for the associated deficient
shadow.
\Cref{cor:single-record-fixed-threshold-hall-separator} removes the panel
artifact from this statement: a single verified balanced top prefix, or a coarse
report with a balanced trim, already gives the same repair.
\Cref{cor:flow-value-hall-deficit-oracle} is the sharper endpoint-facing form:
instead of reporting a balanced-density panel, the build stage may solve finite
max-flow instances on proposed certified subsets and use positive reduced flow
value as the separator.  The retained object is still the deterministic prefix
extracted by the deficient-shadow certificate.
\Cref{cor:shadow-mass-hall-deficit-oracle} removes the unrestricted congestion
parameter from that endpoint.  The current clean target is a finite certified
subcontainer with positive shadow-mass surplus \((SMH1)\); positive finite
panels harden immediately to one such subcontainer.

\begin{lemma}[Hall excess alone has no shadow-mass consequence]
   \label{lem:hall-excess-no-algebraic-shadow-surplus}
   In the abstract finite incidence model obtained by keeping only the Hall-load
   and deficient-shadow definitions, a positive-excess Hall sublayer does not
   imply the existence of a shadow-mass repair.

   More precisely, fix \(C_{\rm pair}>0\), a price \(R_0>0\), and
   \(\tau>0\).  There is an instance with one query \(q\), one paid point \(p\),
   \(a_q=1\), \(\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}=1\), and a guard sublayer \(G'(q)=G(q)\) of
   size \(M\), such that every guard center \(x\in G(q)\) has certified
   neighborhood \(W_x=\{p\}\), the Hall excess is positive, but every certified
   smaller-radius subset \(U\) satisfies
   \[
      D_{G'}(U)\le R_0
   \]
   whenever \(R_0\ge1\).  Thus \((SMH1)\) fails if the only available
   subcontainer is \(\{p\}\) with recursive price at least \(R_0\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Since every \(W_x\) contains \(p\), the certified paid neighborhood of the
   whole sublayer is \(N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)=\{p\}\).  Hence
   \[
      D_{G'}(\{p\})=1,
      \qquad
      C(G')=C_{\rm pair}.
   \]
   On the other hand
   \[
      L(G')=B_{\rm pc}=\tau M .
   \]
   Therefore
   \[
      \Delta(G')
      =
      L(G')-\frac{B_{\rm pc}}2-C(G')
      =
      \frac{\tau M}{2}-C_{\rm pair}.
   \]
   Choosing \(M>2C_{\rm pair}/\tau\) makes the Hall excess positive.  But the
   only nonempty subset has deficient-shadow mass \(1\), so no strict
   shadow-mass surplus is possible against any recursive price \(R_0\ge1\).
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:hall-excess-no-algebraic-shadow-surplus} is only an algebraic
obstruction; it is not a Euclidean counterexample and it ignores the actual
radius-contraction price constraints.  Its role is to identify what the
remaining theorem must use.  A proof of \((SMH1)\) cannot follow from
\(\Delta(G')>0\) and the weak-type shadow envelope alone, even when every guard
incidence reaches the paid point.  It must prove an additional geometric
richness statement: exposed high-correlation guard load either creates a
certified smaller-radius subset whose paid shadow beats its descendant price, or
falls into the low-correlation/list-size regime already handled by the spherical
and compressed-bucket estimates.

\begin{lemma}[Local list-size converts guard load to shadow mass]
   \label{lem:local-list-size-guard-shadow}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:shadow-mass-hall-deficit-oracle}, and let
   \(G'\) be an integral Hall-deficit sublayer.  For a certified subcontainer
   \(U\subseteq W\), define its visible guard load by
   \[
      H_{G'}(U)=
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}\tau_qa_q
      \left|
      \left\{
      x\in G'(q):
      \exists p\in U\text{ with }(p,q)\in\mathcal N,\ p\in W_x,
      \text{ and }(x,p)\text{ satisfying }(HPS1)
      \right\}
      \right|.
      \tag{LGS1}
   \]
   Suppose \(U\) has a local list-size certificate \(\kappa_U>0\), meaning that
   for every \(p\in U\), every \(q\in\mathcal Q_+\), and every near pair
   \((p,q)\in\mathcal N\),
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{x\in G'(q):\ p\in W_x\\
      (x,p)\text{ satisfying }(HPS1)}}\tau_qa_q
      \le
      \kappa_U a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{LGS2}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      H_{G'}(U)\le \kappa_U D_{G'}(U).
      \tag{LGS3}
   \]
   Consequently, if
   \[
      \frac{H_{G'}(U)}{\kappa_U}>R_W(|U|),
      \tag{LGS4}
   \]
   then \(U\) satisfies the shadow-mass surplus test \((SMH1)\), and the
   guarded residual closes.

   More generally, if a finite family of certified subcontainers
   \(U_i\subseteq W_i\) has local list-size certificates \(\kappa_i\) and
   nonnegative weights \(\lambda_i\) with
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_i
      \left(
         \frac{H_{G'}(U_i)}{\kappa_i}-R_{W_i}(|U_i|)
      \right)>0,
      \tag{LGS5}
   \]
   then one deterministic member of the family satisfies \((SMH1)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed \(q\) and \(x\in G'(q)\), the indicator that \(x\) is visible
   from \(U\) is at most the number of paid points \(p\in U\) adjacent to
   \((q,x)\) through the high-correlation relation in \((HPS1)\).  Therefore
   \[
      H_{G'}(U)
      \le
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}
      \sum_{p\in U:\ (p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \sum_{\substack{x\in G'(q):\ p\in W_x\\
      (x,p)\text{ satisfying }(HPS1)}}\tau_qa_q .
   \]
   Terms with no adjacent \(x\) have zero inner sum, so after applying
   \((LGS2)\) only pairs with \(p\in N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)\) remain.  Therefore
   \[
      H_{G'}(U)
      \le
      \kappa_U
      \sum_{p\in U}
      \sum_{\substack{q\in\mathcal Q_+\\p\in N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)}}
      a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      =
      \kappa_U D_{G'}(U).
   \]
   Thus \((LGS4)\) implies \(D_{G'}(U)>R_W(|U|)\), which is \((SMH1)\).
   The panel statement follows because a positive weighted average in
   \((LGS5)\) contains an index \(i\) with
   \(H_{G'}(U_i)/\kappa_i>R_{W_i}(|U_i|)\), and the one-subset argument applies
   to that member.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Fractional local list-size certificate]
   \label{lem:fractional-local-list-size-certificate}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:local-list-size-guard-shadow}.  Fix a
   certified subcontainer \(U\subseteq W\), and let \(\mathcal I_U\) be the
   visible guard incidences counted by \(H_{G'}(U)\):
   \[
      \mathcal I_U=
      \left\{
      (q,x):q\in\mathcal Q_+,\ x\in G'(q),\
      \exists p\in U\text{ with }(p,q)\in\mathcal N,\ p\in W_x,
      \text{ and }(x,p)\text{ satisfying }(HPS1)
      \right\}.
      \tag{FLS1}
   \]
   Let \(\mathcal J_U\) be the paid-pair shadow
   \[
      \mathcal J_U=
      \left\{
      (p,q):p\in U,\ q\in\mathcal Q_+,\ p\in N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)
      \right\},
      \tag{FLS2}
   \]
   with source weights \(b_{q,x}=\tau_qa_q\) and paid weights
   \(w_{p,q}=a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}\).  Join
   \((q,x)\in\mathcal I_U\) to \((p,q)\in\mathcal J_U\) when
   \[
      (p,q)\in\mathcal N,\qquad p\in W_x,\qquad
      (x,p)\text{ satisfying }(HPS1).
      \tag{FLS3}
   \]
   Suppose that for some \(\kappa>0\) there is a nonnegative assignment
   \(f_{q,x,p}\) supported on these edges such that every visible guard
   incidence is fully assigned,
   \[
      \sum_p f_{q,x,p}=b_{q,x}
      \qquad ((q,x)\in\mathcal I_U),
      \tag{FLS4}
   \]
   and every paid pair has congestion at most \(\kappa\),
   \[
      \sum_x f_{q,x,p}\le \kappa w_{p,q}
      \qquad ((p,q)\in\mathcal J_U).
      \tag{FLS5}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      H_{G'}(U)\le \kappa D_{G'}(U).
      \tag{FLS6}
   \]
   In particular, if
   \[
      \frac{H_{G'}(U)}{\kappa}>R_W(|U|),
      \tag{FLS7}
   \]
   then \(U\) satisfies \((SMH1)\), and the guarded residual closes.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Summing the full-assignment equations \((FLS4)\) gives
   \[
      H_{G'}(U)=\sum_{(q,x)\in\mathcal I_U}b_{q,x}
      =
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal J_U}\sum_x f_{q,x,p}.
   \]
   Applying \((FLS5)\) and then the definition of \(D_{G'}(U)\) gives
   \[
      H_{G'}(U)
      \le
      \kappa\sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal J_U}w_{p,q}
      =
      \kappa D_{G'}(U).
   \]
   Thus \((FLS7)\) implies \(D_{G'}(U)>R_W(|U|)\), and
   \cref{cor:shadow-mass-hall-deficit-oracle} closes the residual.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Local duplicate-guard cut]
   \label{lem:local-duplicate-guard-cut}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{lem:fractional-local-list-size-certificate}.  For
   \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal I_U\), let \(N_U(\mathcal A)\subseteq
   \mathcal J_U\) be its paid-pair neighborhood in the graph \((FLS3)\).  A
   full assignment satisfying \((FLS4)\)--\((FLS5)\) exists if and only if
   \[
      \sum_{(q,x)\in\mathcal A}b_{q,x}
      \le
      \kappa\sum_{(p,q)\in N_U(\mathcal A)}w_{p,q}
      \qquad(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal I_U).
      \tag{DGC1}
   \]
   Consequently, if
   \[
      H_{G'}(U)>\kappa R_W(|U|)
      \tag{DGC2}
   \]
   but \(U\) does not close the residual through \((SMH1)\), then there is a
   local duplicate-guard cut \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal I_U\) such that
   \[
      \sum_{(q,x)\in\mathcal A}\tau_qa_q
      >
      \kappa
      \sum_{(p,q)\in N_U(\mathcal A)}
      a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{DGC3}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   This is the max-flow/min-cut theorem for the bipartite network with source
   capacities \(b_{q,x}\), infinite middle edges \((FLS3)\), and sink capacities
   \(\kappa w_{p,q}\).  A finite cut is determined by the set
   \(\mathcal A\) of visible guard incidences kept on the source side; all of
   \(N_U(\mathcal A)\) must also be kept, and the cut condition for routing all
   source mass is exactly \((DGC1)\).

   If \((DGC1)\) holds, the full assignment exists.  Since \((DGC2)\) is the
   same as \((FLS7)\), \cref{lem:fractional-local-list-size-certificate} would
   close the residual.  Therefore, in a nonclosing residual, \((DGC1)\) must
   fail for some \(\mathcal A\), which is \((DGC3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Intrinsic local list-size]
   \label{cor:intrinsic-local-list-size}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:local-duplicate-guard-cut}.  Define the
   intrinsic local list-size of \(U\) by
   \[
      \kappa_U^*
      =
      \max_{\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal I_U}
      \frac{
         \sum_{(q,x)\in\mathcal A}b_{q,x}
      }{
         \sum_{(p,q)\in N_U(\mathcal A)}w_{p,q}
      },
      \tag{ILS1}
   \]
   with the convention that a positive numerator over a zero denominator gives
   \(+\infty\), while \(0/0\) contributes \(0\).  Then \(\kappa_U^*\) is the
   minimum congestion \(\kappa\) for which a full fractional assignment
   \((FLS4)\)--\((FLS5)\) exists.  Consequently, if \(\kappa_U^*<\infty\) and
   \[
      \frac{H_{G'}(U)}{\kappa_U^*}>R_W(|U|),
      \tag{ILS2}
   \]
   then \(U\) satisfies \((SMH1)\), and the guarded residual closes.

   Equivalently, if no proposed certified subcontainer closes by
   \((SMH1)\), then every proposed \(U\) satisfies the intrinsic residual bound
   \[
      H_{G'}(U)\le \kappa_U^* R_W(|U|),
      \tag{ILS3}
   \]
   where the bound is vacuous when \(\kappa_U^*=+\infty\).  More generally, a
   finite nonnegative panel of proposed subcontainers closes whenever
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_i
      \left(
         \frac{H_{G'}(U_i)}{\kappa_{U_i}^*}
         -
         R_{W_i}(|U_i|)
      \right)>0,
      \tag{ILS4}
   \]
   with terms of the form \(H_{G'}(U_i)/\infty\) interpreted as \(0\), and the
   harmless zero-load case \(H_{G'}(U_i)=\kappa_{U_i}^*=0\) also interpreted as
   \(0\).  In that case one deterministic member of the panel satisfies
   \((SMH1)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{lem:local-duplicate-guard-cut}, a congestion value \(\kappa\) is
   feasible exactly when it satisfies all cut inequalities \((DGC1)\).  This is
   equivalent to \(\kappa\ge\kappa_U^*\), with the stated conventions for zero
   denominators.  Thus, when \(\kappa_U^*<\infty\), there is a full assignment
   with congestion \(\kappa_U^*\).  Applying
   \cref{lem:fractional-local-list-size-certificate} with
   \(\kappa=\kappa_U^*\) gives the closing condition \((ILS2)\).

   The residual statement is the contrapositive of the one-subset condition.
   For the panel statement, a positive weighted sum in \((ILS4)\) contains an
   active index \(i\) with
   \(H_{G'}(U_i)/\kappa_{U_i}^*>R_{W_i}(|U_i|)\), and the one-subset argument
   closes for that member.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Slack duplicate-cut descent]
   \label{cor:slack-duplicate-cut-descent}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:intrinsic-local-list-size}.  Put
   \(R=R_W(|U|)\), \(H=H_{G'}(U)\), and, for
   \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal I_U\),
   \[
      B(\mathcal A)=\sum_{(q,x)\in\mathcal A}b_{q,x},
      \qquad
      P(\mathcal A)=\sum_{(p,q)\in N_U(\mathcal A)}w_{p,q}.
      \tag{SDD1}
   \]
   Suppose \(H>0\) and \(U\) does not satisfy \((SMH1)\).  If \(R>0\), then for
   every \(0<\varepsilon<1\) there is a duplicate-guard cut
   \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal I_U\) such that
   \[
      B(\mathcal A)>
      (1-\varepsilon)\frac{H}{R}\,P(\mathcal A).
      \tag{SDD2}
   \]
   If \(R=0\), then there is a cut with \(B(\mathcal A)>0\) and
   \(P(\mathcal A)=0\).

   In particular, if \(U\) captures an \(\eta\)-fraction of a positive-excess
   Hall sublayer, \(H\ge\eta L(G')\), then for every \(0<\varepsilon<1\) either
   \(U\) closes, or, when \(R>0\), there is a cut satisfying
   \[
      B(\mathcal A)>
      (1-\varepsilon)\frac{\eta L(G')}{R_W(|U|)}\,P(\mathcal A).
      \tag{SDD3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(U\) does not close, \(D_{G'}(U)\le R\).  If \(R=0\), then
   \(D_{G'}(U)=0\).  The full visible set \(\mathcal I_U\) has
   \(B(\mathcal I_U)=H>0\), while its paid neighborhood has total weight
   \(P(\mathcal I_U)=D_{G'}(U)=0\), so the zero-shadow cut exists.

   Assume now that \(R>0\).  If \(\kappa_U^*=+\infty\), the defining cut ratio
   already gives a cut with positive numerator and zero denominator, which
   satisfies \((SDD2)\).  Otherwise, by \cref{cor:intrinsic-local-list-size},
   \[
      H\le \kappa_U^*D_{G'}(U)\le \kappa_U^*R,
   \]
   so \(\kappa_U^*\ge H/R\).  Since the maximum in \((ILS1)\) is taken over a
   finite set, some \(\mathcal A\) attains \(\kappa_U^*\).  Its ratio is at
   least \(H/R\), and hence strictly larger than
   \((1-\varepsilon)H/R\), proving \((SDD2)\).  The captured-load statement
   follows by substituting \(H\ge\eta L(G')\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Canonical duplicate-cut closure]
   \label{lem:canonical-duplicate-cut-closure}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:local-duplicate-guard-cut}, and fix
   \(\kappa>0\).  For \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal I_U\), define the
   \(\kappa\)-excess
   \[
      E_\kappa(\mathcal A)
      =
      B(\mathcal A)-\kappa P(\mathcal A),
      \tag{DCC1}
   \]
   where \(B\) and \(P\) are as in \((SDD1)\).  If
   \(\max_{\mathcal A}E_\kappa(\mathcal A)\le0\), then the full local
   assignment \((FLS4)\)--\((FLS5)\) exists.

   Otherwise let \(\mathcal A^\star\) be the inclusion-maximal maximizer of
   \(E_\kappa\).  Then
   \[
      E_\kappa(\mathcal A^\star)>0,
      \qquad
      B(\mathcal A^\star)>\kappa P(\mathcal A^\star),
      \tag{DCC2}
   \]
   and the residual incidences outside \(\mathcal A^\star\) satisfy the
   incremental Hall inequalities
   \[
      B(\mathcal C)
      \le
      \kappa
      \sum_{(p,q)\in N_U(\mathcal C)\setminus N_U(\mathcal A^\star)}
      w_{p,q}
      \qquad
      (\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal I_U\setminus\mathcal A^\star).
      \tag{DCC3}
   \]
   Consequently, after deleting \(\mathcal A^\star\) and its paid-pair
   neighborhood \(N_U(\mathcal A^\star)\), all remaining visible guard
   incidences can be assigned with congestion \(\kappa\) to the remaining
   paid-pair capacities.

   Thus a failed local assignment has a single canonical duplicate closure:
   all further duplicate obstruction is contained in \(\mathcal A^\star\), while
   the complement is already pair-compatible once the closure's paid shadow has
   been charged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The function \(B\) is modular and
   \(\mathcal A\mapsto P(\mathcal A)\) is submodular, since \(P(\mathcal A)\)
   is the weighted size of the union \(N_U(\mathcal A)\).  Therefore
   \(E_\kappa\) is supermodular:
   \[
      E_\kappa(\mathcal A)+E_\kappa(\mathcal B)
      \le
      E_\kappa(\mathcal A\cup\mathcal B)
      +E_\kappa(\mathcal A\cap\mathcal B).
      \tag{DCC4}
   \]
   If the maximum excess is nonpositive, then
   \(B(\mathcal A)\le\kappa P(\mathcal A)\) for every \(\mathcal A\), which is
   exactly the cut criterion \((DGC1)\).  Hence
   \cref{lem:local-duplicate-guard-cut} gives a full assignment.

   If the maximum is positive, the family of maximizers is closed under unions:
   when \(\mathcal A\) and \(\mathcal B\) are maximizers, \((DCC4)\) and
   maximality force both \(\mathcal A\cup\mathcal B\) and
   \(\mathcal A\cap\mathcal B\) to be maximizers.  Since the ground set is
   finite, the union of all maximizers is the unique inclusion-maximal
   maximizer \(\mathcal A^\star\), and \((DCC2)\) follows.

   Let \(\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal I_U\setminus\mathcal A^\star\).  By
   maximality of \(E_\kappa(\mathcal A^\star)\),
   \[
      E_\kappa(\mathcal A^\star\cup\mathcal C)
      \le
      E_\kappa(\mathcal A^\star).
   \]
   Since \(\mathcal A^\star\) and \(\mathcal C\) are disjoint, this inequality
   is exactly
   \[
      B(\mathcal C)
      \le
      \kappa\bigl(P(\mathcal A^\star\cup\mathcal C)
      -P(\mathcal A^\star)\bigr).
   \]
   The difference of the two weighted neighborhoods is the right hand side of
   \((DCC3)\), because
   \(N_U(\mathcal A^\star\cup\mathcal C)=
   N_U(\mathcal A^\star)\cup N_U(\mathcal C)\).
   Applying the max-flow/min-cut criterion to the residual bipartite graph
   proves the final assignment statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Duplicate-closure shadow repair]
   \label{cor:duplicate-closure-shadow-repair}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:canonical-duplicate-cut-closure}.  Let
   \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal I_U\) be any duplicate closure, and define its
   closed paid-shadow degree on \(U\) by
   \[
      d_{\mathcal A}(p)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{q:\,(p,q)\in N_U(\mathcal A)}}w_{p,q}
      =
      \sum_{\substack{q:\,(p,q)\in N_U(\mathcal A)}}
      a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{DCS1}
   \]
   Let \(V\subseteq U\) be a certified subcontainer that inherits the price
   parameters of \(W\), and put \(h=|V|\ge1\).  If
   \[
      \sum_{p\in V}d_{\mathcal A}(p)>R_W(h),
      \tag{DCS2}
   \]
   then the guarded residual closes.

   In particular, suppose a finite repair family consists of ambient certified
   containers \(Y\subseteq U\) and available cardinalities \(\mathcal K_Y\), and
   that the top-\(h\) prefix of \(Y\) by \(d_{\mathcal A}\) is certified for
   every \(h\in\mathcal K_Y\).  If no such prefix closes, then every available
   pair satisfies the closed-shadow envelope
   \[
      D_{\mathcal A,Y}(h)
      \le R_Y(h),
      \qquad
      Y,\ h\in\mathcal K_Y,
      \tag{DCS3}
   \]
   where
   \[
      D_{\mathcal A,Y}(h)=
      \max_{\substack{V\subseteq Y\\|V|=h}}
      \sum_{p\in V}d_{\mathcal A}(p).
      \tag{DCS4}
   \]
   For the canonical closure \(\mathcal A^\star\), a surviving duplicate branch
   is therefore localized to two objects: the closed shadow
   \(N_U(\mathcal A^\star)\), whose certified prefixes obey \((DCS3)\), and the
   already-routable complement from \cref{lem:canonical-duplicate-cut-closure}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((p,q)\in N_U(\mathcal A)\), then by definition of the local graph
   \((FLS3)\) there is \(x\in G'(q)\) such that \(p\in W_x\),
   \((p,q)\in\mathcal N\), and \((x,p)\) is certified high-correlation.  Hence
   \(p\in N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)\), and
   \[
      d_{\mathcal A}(p)
      \le
      \sum_{\substack{q\in\mathcal Q_+\\p\in N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)}}
      a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      =
      d_{G'}(p).
   \]
   Thus \(X=\sum_{p\in V}d_{\mathcal A}(p)\) is a valid lower certificate for
   the deficient-shadow mass of \(V\).  If \((DCS2)\) holds,
   \cref{cor:deficient-shadow-prefix-certificate} closes the residual.

   The envelope \((DCS3)\) is the contrapositive applied to every certified
   top prefix in the finite repair family.  The final statement combines this
   no-prefix envelope with the complement-routing conclusion of
   \cref{lem:canonical-duplicate-cut-closure}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Query-layer duplicate-closure prefix compiler]
   \label{cor:query-layer-duplicate-closure-prefix}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:duplicate-closure-shadow-repair}, and assume the paid-prefix
   verifier of \cref{cor:hit-weighted-star-panel-prefix} is available for the
   current price system.  Let \(Y\subseteq U\) be an affordable certified
   container with price factor \(\psi_Y\), exponent \(\rho_Y\), and available
   cardinality \(h\).  For \(0\le y_q\le1\), \(q\in\mathcal Q_+\), define the
   query-layered duplicate-shadow degree
   \[
      d_{\mathcal A,y}(p)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{q:\,(p,q)\in N_U(\mathcal A)}}
      a_qy_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      \qquad(p\in Y),
      \tag{QDC1}
   \]
   and the top-prefix value
   \[
      D_{\mathcal A,Y,y}(h)
      =
      \max_{\substack{V\subseteq Y\\ |V|=h}}
      \sum_{p\in V}d_{\mathcal A,y}(p).
      \tag{QDC2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      D_{\mathcal A,Y,y}(h)
      >
      \psi_Y
      \left(
         h^{\rho_Y}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}\tau_qa_qy_q
         +\sigma h^{1+\rho_Y}
      \right),
      \tag{QDC3}
   \]
   then an available paid prefix has positive repair reduced gain.

   Moreover, if \((QDC3)\) holds for a fractional layer \(y\), then it holds
   for some Boolean query layer \(Q\subseteq\mathcal Q_+\), with
   \(y=\mathbf 1_Q\).  Thus the retained column may be taken to be the
   top-\(h\) prefix of \(Y\) for one ordinary query layer, charged by
   \[
      \psi_Y
      \left(
         h^{\rho_Y}\sum_{q\in Q}\tau_qa_q
         +\sigma h^{1+\rho_Y}
      \right).
      \tag{QDC4}
   \]

   Consequently, if no available query layer and prefix separates, then every
   fractional layer in the searched pool satisfies the reverse inequality in
   \((QDC3)\).  The all-query envelope \((DCS3)\) is the special case
   \(y_q\equiv1\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(V\subseteq Y\) attain \((QDC2)\), and put
   \(X=D_{\mathcal A,Y,y}(h)\).  Submit the one-record hit-weighted star panel
   with container \(Y\), update side \(V\), size certificate \(h\), query
   weights \(\widetilde y_q=a_qy_q\), lower certificate \(X\), and multiplicity
   \(1\).  Since \(0\le a_q\le1\), also \(0\le\widetilde y_q\le1\).  Because
   \(N_U(\mathcal A)\subseteq\mathcal N\),
   \[
      X
      \le
      \sum_{p\in V}
      \sum_{\substack{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}
      \widetilde y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
   \]
   so \((HSP1)\) holds.  The strict inequality \((QDC3)\) is exactly the
   one-record instance of \((HSP2)\).  Therefore
   \cref{cor:hit-weighted-star-panel-prefix} exposes a positive paid prefix.

   For the hardening statement, define
   \[
      F(y)=
      D_{\mathcal A,Y,y}(h)
      -
      \psi_Yh^{\rho_Y}\sum_q\tau_qa_qy_q
      -
      \psi_Y\sigma h^{1+\rho_Y}.
   \]
   The first term is the maximum, over \(h\)-subsets \(V\subseteq Y\), of a
   linear function of \(y\).  Hence \(F\) is convex on
   \([0,1]^{\mathcal Q_+}\).  If \(F(y)>0\) at some fractional layer, then the
   maximum of \(F\) over the cube is positive and is attained at an extreme
   point, which is the indicator of a Boolean query layer \(Q\).  This gives
   \((QDC3)\) with \(y=\mathbf 1_Q\), i.e. \((QDC4)\).

   The residual envelope is the contrapositive over the finite searched pool.
   Taking \(y_q\equiv1\) gives the degree \(d_{\mathcal A}\) and the price
   \(R_Y(h)\) from \cref{cor:duplicate-closure-shadow-repair}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Duplicate closures are finite-prefix residuals]
   \label{cor:duplicate-closure-finite-prefix-normal-form}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:query-layer-duplicate-closure-prefix}.  Associate to a duplicate
   closure \(\mathcal A\) the finite demand system
   \[
      \mathcal N_{\mathcal A}=N_U(\mathcal A)\subseteq U\times\mathcal Q_+,
      \qquad
      \widehat\gamma_{p,q}=a_q\gamma_{p,q},
      \qquad
      \widehat\tau_q=a_q\tau_q .
      \tag{DFP1}
   \]
   For a certified container \(Y\subseteq U\), cardinality \(h\), and
   fractional query layer \(0\le y_q\le1\), let
   \(D_{Y,y}^{\widehat\gamma,\mathcal A}(h)\) be the ordinary top-\(h\)
   finite-prefix value in this demand system:
   \[
      D_{Y,y}^{\widehat\gamma,\mathcal A}(h)
      =
      \max_{\substack{V\subseteq Y\\|V|=h}}
      \sum_{p\in V}
      \sum_{\substack{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N_{\mathcal A}}}
      y_q\widehat\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{DFP2}
   \]
   Then the duplicate-closure prefix objective is exactly the finite-prefix
   reduced-cost objective
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      &D_{\mathcal A,Y,y}(h)
      -
      \psi_Y
      \left(
         h^{\rho_Y}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}\tau_qa_qy_q
         +\sigma h^{1+\rho_Y}
      \right)  \\
      &\qquad =
      D_{Y,y}^{\widehat\gamma,\mathcal A}(h)
      -
      \psi_Y
      \left(
         h^{\rho_Y}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}\widehat\tau_qy_q
         +\sigma h^{1+\rho_Y}
      \right).
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{DFP3}
   \]
   Hence a positive finite-prefix reduced cost in the demand system
   \(\mathcal N_{\mathcal A}\) gives an available paid prefix with positive
   repair reduced gain, and failure of all searched finite-prefix tests is
   precisely the residual envelope
   \[
      D_{Y,y}^{\widehat\gamma,\mathcal A}(h)
      \le
      \psi_Y
      \left(
         h^{\rho_Y}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}\widehat\tau_qy_q
         +\sigma h^{1+\rho_Y}
      \right)
      \tag{DFP4}
   \]
   for every searched \((Y,h,y)\).

   In particular, for the canonical closure \(\mathcal A^\star\) of
   \cref{lem:canonical-duplicate-cut-closure}, a surviving infeasible local
   assignment branch is an ordinary finite-prefix residual on
   \(\mathcal N_{\mathcal A^\star}\), together with the already-routable
   complement from \((DCC3)\).  Thus cardinality-net, threshold, layer-cake, or
   reported-support finite-prefix separators may be applied to the duplicate
   branch with the substituted weights \((\widehat\gamma,\widehat\tau,\sigma)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The identity \((DFP3)\) follows by substituting
   \(\widehat\gamma_{p,q}=a_q\gamma_{p,q}\) and
   \(\widehat\tau_q=a_q\tau_q\) in \((DFP2)\): the resulting prefix value is
   exactly \((QDC2)\), and the query-price term is the one in \((QDC3)\).
   Therefore any strict violation of \((DFP4)\) is the positive surplus
   condition \((QDC3)\), so
   \cref{cor:query-layer-duplicate-closure-prefix} gives a positive paid
   prefix.  The envelope \((DFP4)\) is the contrapositive over the finite
   searched family.  The canonical-closure statement adds the complement
   routing certificate from \cref{lem:canonical-duplicate-cut-closure}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Local transport-to-star bridge]
   \label{cor:local-transport-to-star-bridge}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{lem:fractional-local-list-size-certificate}.  Suppose
   \(f_{q,x,p}\) satisfies \((FLS4)\)--\((FLS5)\) with congestion
   \(\kappa>0\).  For every triple with \(w_{p,q}>0\), define
   \[
      \eta_{x,p,q}=\frac{f_{q,x,p}}{\kappa w_{p,q}},
      \qquad
      w_{p,q}=a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
      \tag{LTB1}
   \]
   and put \(\eta_{x,p,q}=0\) when \(w_{p,q}=0\).  Let
   \[
      M_x(p)=
      \sum_{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal J_U}
      \eta_{x,p,q}w_{p,q}.
      \tag{LTB2}
   \]
   Then \(0\le\eta_{x,p,q}\le1\), the tensor is supported only on triples with
   \(p\in U\cap W_x\), \((p,q)\in\mathcal N\), and \((x,p)\) satisfying
   \((HPS1)\), and its total responsibility mass is
   \[
      \sum_x\sum_{p\in U}M_x(p)
      =
      \frac{H_{G'}(U)}{\kappa}.
      \tag{LTB3}
   \]

   For \(t>0\), let
   \[
      S_{x,t}=\{p\in U:M_x(p)\ge t\}.
      \tag{LTB4}
   \]
   Every nonempty \(S_{x,t}\) is a certified smaller-radius star container around
   \(x\), with the radius supplied by the high-correlation certificate in
   \((HPS1)\), and
   \[
      t|S_{x,t}|
      \le
      \sum_{p\in S_{x,t}}d_{G'}(p),
      \tag{LTB5}
   \]
   where \(d_{G'}\) is the deficient-shadow degree from \((DSP1)\).

   Consequently, if the descendant price of this star superlevel is
   \(R_x(|S_{x,t}|)\) and
   \[
      t|S_{x,t}|>R_x(|S_{x,t}|),
      \tag{LTB6}
   \]
   then the guarded residual closes.  Equivalently, in a residual where all such
   responsibility star superlevels have been proposed and no one closes, every
   nonempty superlevel satisfies the weak-type envelope
   \[
      t|S_{x,t}|\le R_x(|S_{x,t}|).
      \tag{LTB7}
   \]
   Thus any successful local assignment with \(H_{G'}(U)/\kappa\) large either
   already gives the shadow-mass certificate through
   \cref{lem:fractional-local-list-size-certificate}, or its mass must be
   distributed over high-correlation responsibility stars obeying \((LTB7)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(w_{p,q}=0\), then \((FLS5)\) forces
   \(\sum_x f_{q,x,p}=0\), so setting \(\eta_{x,p,q}=0\) loses no mass.  If
   \(w_{p,q}>0\), then \((FLS5)\) gives
   \(f_{q,x,p}\le \sum_{x'}f_{q,x',p}\le\kappa w_{p,q}\), hence
   \(0\le\eta_{x,p,q}\le1\).  The support statement is exactly the edge
   condition \((FLS3)\).  Summing and using \((FLS4)\),
   \[
      \sum_x\sum_pM_x(p)
      =
      \frac1\kappa\sum_{q,x,p}f_{q,x,p}
      =
      \frac1\kappa\sum_{(q,x)\in\mathcal I_U}b_{q,x}
      =
      \frac{H_{G'}(U)}{\kappa},
   \]
   proving \((LTB3)\).

   If \(p\in S_{x,t}\), then \(M_x(p)>0\), so some supporting triple has
   \((x,p)\) certified high-correlation.  The high-correlation certificate gives
   the smaller-radius containment exactly as in
   \cref{lem:high-correlation-pair-star-reporter}.  Moreover
   \[
      M_x(p)
      \le
      \sum_{\substack{q\in\mathcal Q_+\\p\in N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)}}
      a_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      =
      d_{G'}(p),
   \]
   because every active triple witnesses \(p\in N_{\rm hc}(G')(q)\) and
   \(0\le\eta_{x,p,q}\le1\).  Summing \(t\le M_x(p)\le d_{G'}(p)\) over
   \(p\in S_{x,t}\) gives \((LTB5)\).

   Finally, \((LTB5)\) makes \(X=t|S_{x,t}|\) a valid lower certificate for the
   deficient-shadow mass of the certified star superlevel.  If \((LTB6)\) holds,
   \cref{cor:deficient-shadow-prefix-certificate} closes the residual.  The
   envelope \((LTB7)\) is the contrapositive applied to every proposed
   responsibility star superlevel.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Integrated responsibility-star residual]
   \label{cor:integrated-responsibility-star-residual}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:local-transport-to-star-bridge}.  Assume every positive
   responsibility multiplicity \(M_x(p)\) lies in
   \([M_{\min},M_{\max}]\), with \(0<M_{\min}\le M_{\max}\).  Let
   \[
      \mathcal T=
      \{2^jM_{\min}:0\le j<J\},
      \qquad
      J=1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{M_{\max}}{M_{\min}}\right\rceil .
      \tag{IRS1}
   \]
   For \(t\in\mathcal T\), put \(h_{x,t}=|S_{x,t}|\), and let
   \(R_x(h_{x,t})\) be the certified descendant price of the corresponding
   high-correlation star superlevel.

   If every nonempty dyadic responsibility superlevel has been proposed and no
   one closes the residual, then
   \[
      \frac{H_{G'}(U)}{\kappa}
      \le
      2\sum_x\sum_{\substack{t\in\mathcal T\\h_{x,t}>0}}
      R_x(h_{x,t}).
      \tag{IRS2}
   \]
   Equivalently, if a local assignment satisfies the strict reverse inequality,
   then one dyadic responsibility star superlevel closes the guarded residual.

   Thus the positive side of the local duplicate-cut dichotomy has a
   cost-sensitive certificate: shipped guard mass need only beat the integrated
   recursive price of the responsibility levels that actually appear, not the
   number of possible centers times a worst-case price.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For every positive \(m\in[M_{\min},M_{\max}]\),
   \[
      m
      \le
      2\sum_{\substack{t\in\mathcal T\\t\le m}}t .
      \tag{IRS3}
   \]
   Applying this pointwise to \(m=M_x(p)\) and summing gives
   \[
      \frac{H_{G'}(U)}{\kappa}
      =
      \sum_x\sum_pM_x(p)
      \le
      2\sum_x\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}t\,h_{x,t}.
      \tag{IRS4}
   \]
   If no proposed dyadic responsibility star closes, then
   \cref{cor:local-transport-to-star-bridge} gives
   \(t\,h_{x,t}\le R_x(h_{x,t})\) for every nonempty level.  Substituting this in
   \((IRS4)\) proves \((IRS2)\).  The strict reverse inequality is the
   contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Local close-pay-cut trichotomy]
   \label{cor:local-close-pay-cut-trichotomy}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{lem:fractional-local-list-size-certificate}, and fix a certified
   subcontainer \(U\) with \(H=H_{G'}(U)>0\).  Let \(\kappa>0\).  A local
   assignment solve at congestion \(\kappa\) has the following complete
   certificate.

   If the assignment constraints \((FLS4)\)--\((FLS5)\) are infeasible, then the
   canonical duplicate closure \(\mathcal A^\star\) from
   \cref{lem:canonical-duplicate-cut-closure} satisfies
   \[
      B(\mathcal A^\star)>\kappa P(\mathcal A^\star),
      \tag{LCT1}
   \]
   where \(B\) and \(P\) are as in \((SDD1)\).  Moreover, after deleting
   \(\mathcal A^\star\) and its paid-pair neighborhood
   \(N_U(\mathcal A^\star)\), all remaining visible guard incidences are
   assignable with congestion \(\kappa\).

   If a feasible assignment \(f\) exists, form its responsibility multiplicities
   \(M_x(p)\).  Since \(H>0\), some responsibility mass is positive; put
   \[
      M_{\min}(f)=\min\{M_x(p):M_x(p)>0\},
      \qquad
      M_{\max}(f)=\max_{x,p}M_x(p),
   \]
   and let
   \[
      \mathcal T_f=
      \{2^jM_{\min}(f):0\le j<
      1+\lceil\log_2(M_{\max}(f)/M_{\min}(f))\rceil\}.
      \tag{LCT2}
   \]
   For the superlevels \(S_{x,t}=\{p\in U:M_x(p)\ge t\}\), define the
   integrated responsibility price
   \[
      \mathfrak R_\star(f)
      =
      \sum_x\sum_{\substack{t\in\mathcal T_f\\|S_{x,t}|>0}}
      R_x(|S_{x,t}|).
      \tag{LCT3}
   \]
   Then either the guarded residual closes, or both residual payment inequalities
   hold:
   \[
      \frac{H}{\kappa}\le R_W(|U|)
      \tag{LCT4}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \frac{H}{\kappa}\le 2\mathfrak R_\star(f).
      \tag{LCT5}
   \]
   Equivalently, a feasible assignment closes the residual whenever
   \[
      \frac{H}{\kappa}>
      \min\{R_W(|U|),\,2\mathfrak R_\star(f)\}.
      \tag{LCT6}
   \]

   Thus a surviving local residual at congestion \(\kappa\) is forced into one of
   two explicit objects: either a canonical duplicate closure whose complement
   is already routable, or a feasible high-correlation responsibility
   decomposition whose dyadic recursive price pays the transported guard mass.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the assignment constraints are infeasible, then
   \cref{lem:local-duplicate-guard-cut} gives
   \(\max_{\mathcal A}E_\kappa(\mathcal A)>0\).  Applying
   \cref{lem:canonical-duplicate-cut-closure} gives the canonical maximizer
   \(\mathcal A^\star\), the strict cut inequality \((LCT1)\), and the
   assignment of the complement after deleting \(N_U(\mathcal A^\star)\).

   Suppose now that \(f\) is feasible.  If \(H/\kappa>R_W(|U|)\), then
   \cref{lem:fractional-local-list-size-certificate} closes the residual, so a
   nonclosing residual must satisfy \((LCT4)\).  Construct the responsibility
   tensor from \(f\) as in \cref{cor:local-transport-to-star-bridge}.  If
   \(H/\kappa>2\mathfrak R_\star(f)\), then
   \cref{cor:integrated-responsibility-star-residual} exposes a closing dyadic
   responsibility star.  Hence a residual with no closing star satisfies
   \((LCT5)\).  The minimum form \((LCT6)\) is the contrapositive of these two
   closing tests.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Local finite-prefix residual normal form]
   \label{cor:local-finite-prefix-residual-normal-form}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:local-close-pay-cut-trichotomy}.  Fix a finite duplicate-prefix
   search pool: for every duplicate closure \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal I_U\)
   that may be exposed, the pool contains certified containers \(Y\subseteq U\),
   available cardinalities \(h\), and admissible fractional query layers
   \(0\le y_q\le1\).  Run the local assignment test at congestion \(\kappa\).
   Then exactly one of the following certified outcomes is obtained.

   First, the assignment is infeasible and the canonical duplicate closure
   \(\mathcal A^\star\) satisfies \((LCT1)\).  If some searched
   \((Y,h,y)\) violates the finite-prefix envelope \((DFP4)\) for
   \(\mathcal A^\star\), then the paid-prefix verifier exposes a positive
   repair prefix.  If no searched record violates \((DFP4)\), then the whole
   duplicate obstruction is localized to the ordinary finite-prefix residual
   \[
      D_{Y,y}^{\widehat\gamma,\mathcal A^\star}(h)
      \le
      \psi_Y
      \left(
         h^{\rho_Y}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_+}\widehat\tau_qy_q
         +\sigma h^{1+\rho_Y}
      \right)
      \tag{LFP1}
   \]
   for every searched \((Y,h,y)\), with
   \(\widehat\gamma_{p,q}=a_q\gamma_{p,q}\) and
   \(\widehat\tau_q=a_q\tau_q\), while the complement outside
   \(\mathcal A^\star\) is routable at congestion \(\kappa\).

   Second, the assignment is feasible.  Then either the guarded residual closes,
   or the whole-container and responsibility-star payment inequalities
   \((LCT4)\)--\((LCT5)\) both hold.

   Thus a local solve never creates a tree of duplicate children.  The failed
   duplicate branch contributes either one verified paid-prefix column or one
   finite-prefix residual instance plus an already packed complement.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{cor:local-close-pay-cut-trichotomy}.  In the infeasible branch,
   it returns the canonical closure \(\mathcal A^\star\), the strict cut
   inequality \((LCT1)\), and the complement assignment after deleting
   \(N_U(\mathcal A^\star)\).  Apply
   \cref{cor:duplicate-closure-finite-prefix-normal-form} to
   \(\mathcal A^\star\).  A strict violation of \((DFP4)\) is exactly a
   positive finite-prefix reduced cost and therefore gives the paid-prefix
   repair; if none exists, \((LFP1)\) holds for every searched record.  The
   feasible branch is the second branch of
   \cref{cor:local-close-pay-cut-trichotomy}.
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:fractional-local-list-size-certificate} weakens the pointwise
certificate \((LGS2)\): a proposed container only needs to fractionally assign
its captured guard load to the paid shadow with congestion \(\kappa\).  The
proof may therefore use exact build-time max-flow rather than a uniform
per-pair list-size bound.  \Cref{lem:local-duplicate-guard-cut} gives the
matching residual.  If a container captures enough guard load for its price but
cannot certify bounded local list size, then the obstruction is not vague
overlap; it is a smaller Hall cut of guard incidences whose paid-pair
neighborhood is too light.  \Cref{cor:intrinsic-local-list-size} packages this
as a scalar reduced-gain test \(H_{G'}(U)/\kappa_U^*-R_W(|U|)\).
\Cref{cor:slack-duplicate-cut-descent} gives the nonclosing form: captured
guard load that fails to close exposes a weighted incidence cut whose
paid-shadow mass is small at the container's own price density.
\Cref{lem:canonical-duplicate-cut-closure} shows that this cut family has a
canonical merge: the maximum-excess closure contains the whole duplicate
obstruction, and the complement is already routable once the closure's paid
shadow is charged.
\Cref{cor:duplicate-closure-shadow-repair} gives the matching repair/no-repair
interface for that closed shadow: any certified prefix whose cut-shadow mass
beats its recursive price closes the original deficient-shadow residual, while
failure leaves a no-prefix envelope localized to the duplicate closure.
\Cref{cor:query-layer-duplicate-closure-prefix} is the cost-refined version:
the same duplicate shadow can be searched with fractional query layers, charged
only by \(\sum_q\tau_qa_qy_q\), and any positive fractional certificate hardens
to one Boolean query layer and its top prefix.
\Cref{cor:duplicate-closure-finite-prefix-normal-form} makes this identification
literal: the duplicate closure is an ordinary finite-prefix demand system after
the weight substitution \(\widehat\gamma_{p,q}=a_q\gamma_{p,q}\),
\(\widehat\tau_q=a_q\tau_q\).  Thus the duplicate branch uses the same
finite-prefix reporter language as the closed Hall-shadow branch.
\Cref{cor:local-finite-prefix-residual-normal-form} is the resulting local
algorithmic form: a max-flow failure is either repaired by one verified
finite-prefix column or leaves one finite-prefix residual instance and an
already packed complement.
\Cref{cor:local-transport-to-star-bridge} gives the complementary positive
form: any successful local assignment is already a high-correlation
responsibility tensor, so the dense-star machinery only has to find a
responsibility superlevel violating its recursive price.  If no such superlevel
exists, the obstruction is the explicit weak-type envelope \((LTB7)\), not an
unstructured branching problem.
