\Cref{cor:integrated-responsibility-star-residual} integrates this envelope over
the dyadic responsibility levels and replaces the older global center-count loss
by the actual recursive price of the responsibility levels that appear.
\Cref{cor:local-close-pay-cut-trichotomy} packages the resulting local
separator: a max-flow solve either returns a duplicate cut, or returns a
responsibility decomposition whose integrated recursive price must pay the
captured load unless a verified dense column has already closed.

\begin{corollary}[Guard-capture Hall separator]
   \label{cor:guard-capture-hall-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:local-list-size-guard-shadow}.  Let
   \(G'\) be a positive-excess Hall sublayer, so
   \[
      L(G')=\sum_q\tau_qa_q|G'(q)|>\frac{B_{\rm pc}}2 .
      \tag{GCH1}
   \]
   Suppose a certified \(U\subseteq W\) has a local list-size certificate
   \(\kappa_U\), either pointwise as in \((LGS2)\) or fractionally as in
   \((FLS4)\)--\((FLS5)\), and captures an \(\eta\)-fraction of the guard load,
   \[
      H_{G'}(U)\ge \eta L(G')
      \tag{GCH2}
   \]
   for some \(\eta>0\).  If
   \[
      \eta L(G')>\kappa_U R_W(|U|),
      \tag{GCH3}
   \]
   then the guarded residual closes.  In particular, the simpler sufficient
   condition
   \[
      \frac{\eta B_{\rm pc}}2>\kappa_U R_W(|U|)
      \tag{GCH4}
   \]
   also closes.

   Hence, in any surviving no-shadow-mass residual, every certified
   subcontainer with a local list-size certificate must obey
   \[
      H_{G'}(U)\le \kappa_U R_W(|U|).
      \tag{GCH5}
   \]
   Equivalently, a container that captures an \(\eta\)-fraction of the exposed
   Hall load can survive only if
   \[
      \kappa_U R_W(|U|)\ge \eta L(G')>\frac{\eta B_{\rm pc}}2 .
      \tag{GCH6}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The first statement is immediate from
   \[
      \frac{H_{G'}(U)}{\kappa_U}
      \ge
      \frac{\eta L(G')}{\kappa_U}
      >
      R_W(|U|)
   \]
   and either \cref{lem:local-list-size-guard-shadow} or
   \cref{lem:fractional-local-list-size-certificate}.  Since
   \(\Delta(G')>0\) implies \(L(G')>B_{\rm pc}/2\), condition \((GCH4)\)
   implies \((GCH3)\).  The residual inequalities are the contrapositives of
   the same one-subset test.
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:local-list-size-guard-shadow} is the positive counterpart to
\cref{lem:hall-excess-no-algebraic-shadow-surplus}.  The obstruction in that
lemma duplicates many guard incidences against one paid point; here that
duplication is measured by \(\kappa_U\).  Thus a geometric proof of the
shadow-mass separator may target guard load rather than deficient-shadow degree:
find a smaller-radius container that captures enough exposed guard incidences
and certify that no paid pair in the container explains too many of them.
\Cref{cor:guard-capture-hall-separator} records the exact trilemma left by a
surviving residual: every searched container either captures too little of the
Hall load, has too large a recursive price, or has too large a local list-size
factor.  This is the form that list decoding, additive quantization, LP range
reporting, or seeded center proposals should try to violate.

\begin{corollary}[Tuple-profile distinct-storage certificate]
   \label{cor:tuple-profile-distinct-storage}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net} and
   \cref{lem:tuple-witness-distinct-child-tail}.  Suppose that for every price
   class \(i\) there are certified tuple-incidence envelopes
   \(J_i(\mathbf x)\ge0\) such that
   \[
      \E_z M_z(i,\mathbf x)\le J_i(\mathbf x)
      \qquad
      (\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)).
      \tag{TST1}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise let \(a_*\) be
   as in \((BNR1)\).  Suppose \(a_*>0\), the active first moments satisfy
   \((DCB2)\), and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      2\sum_i2^iR_i^{-1}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)}J_i(\mathbf x)
      \le
      a_*S .
      \tag{TST2}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Equivalently, if \(\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)\) is partitioned into profile
   classes \(\Pi_i\), each profile \(\pi\in\Pi_i\) has cardinality
   \(N_{i,\pi}\), and every tuple in \(\pi\) has
   \(J_i(\mathbf x)\le e^{-I_{i,\pi}}\), then it is enough to replace the inner
   tuple sum in \((TST2)\) by
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi_i}N_{i,\pi}e^{-I_{i,\pi}} .
      \tag{TST3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Taking expectations in \((TWT3)\) and using \((TST1)\) gives
   \[
      \E_zC_z(i)
      \le
      R_i^{-1}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)}J_i(\mathbf x).
   \]
   Substituting this into \((DDS1)\) shows that \((TST2)\) implies the dyadic
   distinct-child tail bound of
   \cref{cor:dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net}.  That corollary gives
   feasibility.  The profile form \((TST3)\) is just summation of the envelope
   \(J_i(\mathbf x)\le e^{-I_{i,\pi}}\) over each profile class.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Local-error tuple-profile distinct-storage certificate]
   \label{cor:local-error-tuple-profile-distinct-storage}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:local-error-dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net} and
   \cref{lem:tuple-witness-distinct-child-tail}.  Suppose that for every price
   class \(i\) there are certified tuple-incidence envelopes
   \(J_i(\mathbf x)\ge0\) such that
   \[
      \E_z M_z(i,\mathbf x)\le J_i(\mathbf x)
      \qquad
      (\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)).
      \tag{LTST1}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise let
   \(a_{\rm loc}\) be as in \((LBNR2)\).  Suppose \(a_{\rm loc}>0\), the active
   first moments satisfy \((LDCB2)\), and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      2\sum_i2^iR_i^{-1}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)}J_i(\mathbf x)
      \le
      a_{\rm loc}S .
      \tag{LTST2}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Equivalently, if \(\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)\) is partitioned into profile
   classes \(\Pi_i\), each profile \(\pi\in\Pi_i\) has cardinality
   \(N_{i,\pi}\), and every tuple in \(\pi\) has
   \(J_i(\mathbf x)\le e^{-I_{i,\pi}}\), then it is enough to replace the inner
   tuple sum in \((LTST2)\) by
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi_i}N_{i,\pi}e^{-I_{i,\pi}} .
      \tag{LTST3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Taking expectations in \((TWT3)\) and using \((LTST1)\) gives
   \[
      \E_zC_z(i)
      \le
      R_i^{-1}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)}J_i(\mathbf x).
   \]
   Substituting this into \((LDDS1)\) shows that \((LTST2)\) implies the
   local-error dyadic distinct-child tail bound.  Hence
   \cref{cor:local-error-dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net} gives
   feasibility.  The profile form \((LTST3)\) is just summation over the profile
   partition.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Multiplicity-discounted distinct-storage certificate]
   \label{cor:multiplicity-discounted-distinct-storage}
   Work in either of the following two settings:
   the scalar distinct-storage setting of
   \cref{cor:dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net}, with
   \(a=a_*\) and active first-moment condition \((DCB2)\), or the local-error
   setting of
   \cref{cor:local-error-dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net}, with
   \(a=a_{\rm loc}\) and active first-moment condition \((LDCB2)\).  In both
   cases use the multiplicity-discounted tuple incidences
   \(\widetilde M_z(i,\mathbf x)\) from
   \cref{lem:multiplicity-discounted-tuple-witness}.  Suppose that for every
   price class \(i\) there are certified envelopes
   \(\widetilde J_i(\mathbf x)\ge0\) such that
   \[
      \E_z\widetilde M_z(i,\mathbf x)
      \le
      \widetilde J_i(\mathbf x)
      \qquad
      (\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)).
      \tag{MDS1}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise suppose
   \(a>0\), the corresponding active first-moment condition holds, and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      2\sum_i2^iR_i^{-1}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)}
      \widetilde J_i(\mathbf x)
      \le
      aS .
      \tag{MDS2}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Thus an occurrence-based list-decoding or range-reporting analysis may be
   used after quotienting by canonical child identity: each occurrence is
   weighted by the reciprocal of the number of occurrences that induce the same
   stored child.  In regimes where many caps, residues, or decoder transcripts
   collapse to one net, this is the quantity that matches shared-DAG storage.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Taking expectations in \((MDT2)\) and using \((MDS1)\) gives
   \[
      \E_zC_z(i)
      \le
      R_i^{-1}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)}
      \widetilde J_i(\mathbf x).
   \]
   Hence \((MDS2)\) implies the dyadic distinct-child tail bound \((DDS1)\) in
   the scalar setting, and \((LDDS1)\) in the local-error setting.  The
   corresponding conclusion follows from
   \cref{cor:dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net} or
   \cref{cor:local-error-dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net}, respectively.
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:exact-near-set-filter-cover} is strictly weaker than
\cref{lem:finite-signature-filter-cover} when the exact near set is part of the
signature.  The all-pair LP covers every \(p\in N_{\sigma_0}\); the existential
LP covers only the event \(U_A\cap N_{\sigma_0}\ne\emptyset\), which is all ANN
needs.
This does not make exact near-set signatures free, but it separates the two
issues: pairwise robustness is no longer baked into the dense-overlap LP, and
any remaining cost of exact signatures is explicit metadata or decoder entropy.
\Cref{lem:exact-near-set-signature-dual} is the corresponding separation
statement: a failed existential signature cover prices signatures, not all near
pairs, and a proposed dense or spherical filter is accepted precisely when its
active update side intersects enough priced exact near sets per unit recursive
query and storage cost.
\Cref{lem:exact-signature-coverage-list-oracle} makes the corresponding dense
proposal target explicit.  In an exact-signature node, a list is scored by
weighted max coverage of the exact near sets \(N_{\sigma_0}\), not by additive
pair degree.  Thus \(k\)-means++, additive-quantization cells, range-reporting
violator search, and lattice/list-decoding panels can be used as seeded
proposal laws only through the checkable inequality \((ESL1)\); the retained
column is still the deterministic list and positive-margin signature layer
verified by \((ECL2)\)--\((ECL4)\).
\Cref{cor:hit-probability-exact-signature-proposal} is the probabilistic form:
the analysis may lower-bound only the chance that the proposed list hits each
exact near set.  For independent soft responsibilities, for example, this is
the computable quantity
\[
   1-\prod_{p\in N_{\sigma_0}\cap W_s}(1-\pi_{s,p}),
\]
or any certified lower bound on it, while the final retained column remains a
deterministic list exposed by the averaging argument.
\Cref{cor:variable-size-exact-signature-proposal} removes the fixed-list-size
artifact: the proof may charge the realized size \(k\) by its own recursive
prices \(T_{s,k},S_{s,k}\).  \Cref{cor:bernoulli-exact-signature-soft-bucket}
then gives the direct soft-bucket interface, where exact-signature gains are
computed from size-stratified hit probabilities of the independent
responsibility model.  This is the form in which additive quantization,
facility buckets, or randomized list decoders can be certified without
pretending their proposal lists have deterministic size.
\Cref{cor:capped-bernoulli-exact-signature-mass} gives the coarser but cleaner
mass-only screen: a responsibility bucket is capped and padded to one fixed
list size, and its useful coverage is certified from the total responsibility
mass it assigns to each exact near set.  This is the most direct fractional
form for analyzing soft \(k\)-means, additive-quantization, or list-decoding
proposal buckets.
\Cref{cor:normalized-exact-signature-coverage-obstruction} states the exact
residual left when those certified proposals fail: after normalizing the
signature prices to a probability distribution, every available list has
weighted exact-near-set coverage at most its recursive query/storage price.
This is the precise finite target for the remaining geometric theorem.
\Cref{cor:normalized-capped-mass-obstruction} is the corresponding coarser
target for fractional soft buckets: after normalization, every responsibility
bucket in the proposed build-time family has mass-screen value at most zero.
Ruling out this obstruction is exactly the theorem a soft \(k\)-means, AQ, or
list-decoding construction must prove.
\Cref{cor:saturated-mass-exact-signature-screen} linearizes this target into a
thresholded coverage inequality.  Up to the overflow tax, a bucket wins if it
places enough responsibility mass on the priced exact near sets, with each
signature saturated once its mass reaches the chosen threshold \(a\).  This is
the form that most closely resembles list recovery or LP range-reporting.
\Cref{cor:layer-cake-saturated-mass-screen} gives the matching weak-type
version: a failed soft-bucket proof leaves a normalized dual in which every
mass superlevel of every responsibility bucket has priced weight bounded by
storage plus overflow divided by the level.  This is the exact range-reporting
shape of the remaining obstruction.
\Cref{cor:unit-mass-weak-type-residual} removes the last nuisance normalization:
in the residual, the total priced signature mass of each bucket is at most one,
so a separator only has to find one responsibility-mass superlevel whose priced
weight beats recursive storage plus the certified overflow tail.
\Cref{cor:finite-exact-signature-superlevel-separator} makes this a finite
oracle: for each bucket, it is enough to inspect levels equal to actual
responsibility masses on exact near-set signatures.  Thus a \(k\)-means++,
additive-quantization, range-reporting, or list-decoding proposal only has to
solve a finite weighted superlevel search and then pass the deterministic
inequality \((EFS2)\).
\Cref{cor:randomized-superlevel-proposal} is the corresponding proposal-law
form.  A randomized \(k\)-means++, AQ, lattice-decoding, or range-reporting
routine is useful only through positive expected certified surplus; after
averaging, the retained certificate is still one deterministic bucket and one
deterministic responsibility-mass level.
\Cref{cor:multiplicative-level-net-separator} removes another materialization
artifact: a geometric net over mass levels is enough, losing only its
multiplicative density factor in surplus.  Dyadic mass thresholds therefore
suffice up to a factor two, which is the form needed by output-sensitive
range-reporting or list-decoding implementations.
\Cref{cor:reported-superlevel-separator} is the matching implementation
interface: a decoder or range reporter may output only a small panel of
candidate bucket-level pairs, possibly with certified lower and upper envelopes.
If the best reported certified surplus is positive, or if an approximate
reporter loses less than the available margin, the finite separator already
accepts one deterministic column.  The reporter work is build-time separation
work; it is not retained as recursive query overhead.
\Cref{cor:success-normalized-superlevel-law} rewrites the same test in the
compressed-bucket language: the relevant price is
\[
   \frac{\theta S_B+\varepsilon_B}{1-e^{-g}},
\]
the recursive query/storage cost per certified hit probability of the
superlevel.  Thus the exact-signature separator does not ask every bucket to be
small.  It asks that, averaged over the proposed bucket-level law, captured
priced exact-near-set mass beats this success-normalized cost.  This is the
finite LP form of the Renyi/list-size invariant used by the compressed-filter
DAG route.
\Cref{cor:exact-signature-moment-separator} makes the corresponding moment
target explicit.  For a reported superlevel, separate the captured signature
price \(X\) from the query-price load \(Y\); it is enough to prove that
\[
   \E(1-e^{-g})X
\]
beats the success-weighted recursive query moment plus the storage and overflow
moments.  When a bucket is charged by a compressed size \(K\), the sufficient
condition is exactly a Renyi form with \(K^\rho\) on query work and
\(K^{1+\rho}\) on storage.
\Cref{cor:exact-signature-renyi-residual} gives the matching obstruction:
if the reported universe cannot separate a normalized dual, then every finite
bucket-level law satisfies the reverse Renyi moment inequality \((EMRE3)\).
The remaining geometric proof can therefore be phrased without LP language:
rule out normalized exact-signature weights for which all spherical, AQ,
\(k\)-means-style, range-reporting, or list-decoding panels have captured
success mass no larger than their success-weighted query and storage moments.
\Cref{cor:observable-renyi-profile-separator} is the form to use for that
proof: a proposal mechanism only has to certify a hit vector, a Renyi query-load
vector, and storage/error moments.  If those observable quantities beat the
current dual prices, the deterministic verifier extracts one ordinary filter
column; if no such panel exists, \((ORPS4)\) is the exact pseudo-random
residual that the spherical/list-decoding analysis must contradict.
\Cref{cor:observable-renyi-profile-cover} turns the same condition back into a
primal fractional cover of exact signatures by observable profiles, with
certification error subtracted uniformly from every signature's hit mass.
\Cref{cor:local-error-observable-profile-cover} sharpens this by allowing an
error vector: overflow or certification loss is charged only to the exact
signatures it can affect, rather than being subtracted as a scalar tax from
every signature in the node.
\Cref{cor:local-error-decoded-bucket-panel-profile} propagates that sharpening
to decoded panels: the averaged hit spectrum only has to dominate the averaged
local error on the same exact signature.
\Cref{cor:single-panel-success-normalized-profile} records the simplest
success-normalized sufficient condition: a panel with hit probability \(a\) may
spend \(a\) times the local query and storage budgets, so large buckets are
acceptable precisely when their certified exact-near-set hit probability grows
with their recursive cost.
\Cref{cor:decoded-bucket-panel-profile} is the corresponding implementation
interface.  A decoder may output a whole panel of overlapping bucket records;
their hit contributions, success-weighted recursive query moments, storage
moments, and overflow certificates are simply added.  This is the form in which
large-range spherical filters, product-code tensor panels, additive
quantization cells, and range-reporting/list-decoding outputs should be proved:
show the three averaged spectrum inequalities \((DBP3)\)--\((DBP4)\), and the
finite exact-signature compiler handles the fractional overlap.
\Cref{cor:recursive-compressed-net-panel} specializes this to the recursive
bucket-net picture.  A record's query price is its certified success weight
times the smaller-child Renyi cost \(K^{\rho_{\rm child}}\), while its storage
price is \(K^{1+\rho_{\rm child}}\).  Thus the remaining geometric statement is
an average Renyi list-decoding theorem for compressed bucket nets: prove
\((RCN5)\)--\((RCN6)\) for the decoded panel, and the dense recursion is already
success-normalized.
\Cref{cor:bucket-net-ratio-form} is the same condition in the most useful
diagnostic form: after subtracting certification error, divide the query and
storage Renyi moments by the minimum certified hit mass.  This is the exact
``bucket cost per success probability'' invariant; false active buckets remain
charged through the query-active layer \(\mathcal Q_{z,b}\).
\Cref{cor:local-error-bucket-net-ratio} is the sharper ratio form: the
denominator is the minimum of
\(H_{\rm net}(\sigma)-E_{\rm net}(\sigma)\), not the minimum of
\(H_{\rm net}(\sigma)\) after a global scalar error toll.
\Cref{cor:first-moment-active-load-query} then removes the query-side Renyi
burden: since every child exponent is at most one, a first-moment active-load
bound already controls the query spectrum.  The storage spectrum is the real
Renyi list-decoding target.
\Cref{cor:local-error-first-moment-active-load} gives the same reduction with
the local-error denominator.
\Cref{cor:shared-canonical-panel-storage} and
\cref{cor:distinct-canonical-bucket-net} make that target the one paid by the
actual index: child storage is summed over distinct canonical child identifiers
inside a decoded panel, while occurrence multiplicity remains only as query load
and explicit metadata.
\Cref{cor:local-error-shared-canonical-panel-storage} gives the same
shared-DAG accounting with a signature-local error vector.
\Cref{cor:shared-canonical-panel-reduced-gain} is the dual-facing form: against
the current normalized prices, a whole decoded panel is accepted when its
useful priced hit mass beats its active query load plus its shared canonical
child-storage price.  This is the fully fractional bucket analogue of the
benefit-per-price dense-filter score.
\Cref{cor:one-sided-shared-panel-column-generation} makes the build-time role
explicit: a proposal routine may add only panels with verified one-sided
positive gain, while a no-positive certificate is sound only when it rules out
the full finite panel universe.
\Cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint} packages the same condition
at endpoint level: a nodewise positive shared-panel separator is enough to
construct the exact-signature covers used by the polylogarithmic induction.
\Cref{cor:weighted-shared-panel-renyi-separator} expands the positive-gain
condition into the weighted moment inequality a geometric analysis should
prove: priced useful hit mass must beat active Renyi query load plus shared
canonical child storage, with a first-moment query-load sufficient form.
\Cref{cor:certified-storage-weighted-panel-separator} lets the geometric proof
replace the exact shared storage by any certified upper envelope, so
tuple-profile or dyadic distinct-child estimates can be plugged into the same
positive-gain test.
\Cref{cor:certified-storage-weighted-residual} gives the matching obstruction:
if the finite panel universe cannot separate a normalized dual, every seed law
satisfies the reverse weighted useful-hit versus load-plus-storage inequality.
\Cref{cor:local-error-distinct-canonical-bucket-net},
\cref{cor:local-error-dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net}, and
\cref{cor:local-error-tuple-profile-distinct-storage} propagate this denominator
through the distinct-child, dyadic-tail, and tuple-profile storage certificates.
\Cref{lem:dyadic-tail-distinct-child-storage} and
\cref{cor:dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net} turn the same target into dyadic
large-child counting: prove, at each recursive price scale, that the number of
distinct canonical bucket nets is small enough.
\Cref{cor:layer-cake-distinct-storage-bucket-net} removes that discretization
from the theorem target by using the exact integrated tail count of distinct
children, and \cref{cor:integrated-tuple-tail-distinct-storage} gives the
matching tuple-witness form without first choosing dyadic price classes.
\Cref{cor:price-weighted-witness-packing-storage} is the most direct version:
assign each distinct stored child its own randomized witness atom and bound the
price-weighted congestion of these witnesses.
\Cref{cor:uniform-tuple-witness-packing-storage} makes this checkable for
compressed nets by choosing a uniform ordered tuple inside each child; with
two-tuples, the paid weight is at most the child price factor \(\psi\), leaving a
plain pair-congestion target up to that factor.
\Cref{cor:occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage} is the decoder-facing version:
when many decoded records induce the same canonical child, each occurrence is
weighted by the reciprocal of that child's multiplicity before pair congestion is
measured.
\Cref{cor:weighted-occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage} removes the integer
restriction from this statement: fractional Hall atoms, weighted cohorts, and
soft decoder records are divided by their total weighted multiplicity and still
group to one stored child.
\Cref{cor:reciprocal-multiplicity-pair-congestion} isolates the pair case:
bound that reciprocal-multiplicity pair congestion directly and the shared
canonical storage condition follows.
\Cref{cor:pair-profile-occurrence-discounted-storage} turns this into the finite
entropy-energy target: partition separated pairs into profiles and prove that
profile cardinality times reciprocal-multiplicity congestion energy sums to the
storage budget.
\Cref{cor:multiplicity-layer-pair-profile-storage} pushes the quotient directly
into that target: a profile at occurrence-multiplicity scale \(2^\ell\) pays
only \(2^{-\ell}\) times its undiscounted cap/list-decoding energy.
\Cref{cor:aggregate-multiplicity-profile-storage} removes the remaining
worst-pair envelope inside a profile: the geometric proof may bound the
aggregate profile-layer entropy-energy sum directly.
\Cref{cor:gaussian-aggregate-profile-layer-storage} gives the corresponding
Gaussian check: profile-layer storage is certified by weighted incidence
entropy, shifted-threshold margin, and maximum pair correlation.
\Cref{lem:high-correlation-pair-star-reporter} and
\cref{cor:dense-star-gaussian-profile-layer} explain what happens when that
incidence entropy is concentrated on genuinely high-correlation pairs: a dyadic
star superlevel is a certified smaller-radius dense proposal.
\Cref{cor:reciprocal-multiplicity-fixed-tail-storage} combines the
correlation split with the reciprocal-multiplicity discount: after dyadic
occurrence layering, the surviving storage endpoint is exactly low-correlation
Gaussian energy plus an explicit fixed high-correlation dense-repair tail.
\Cref{cor:local-entropy-slack-reciprocal-storage} makes this endpoint local:
for polylogarithmically many active profile layers, an \(O(\log\log n)\)
additive entropy-energy margin per low-correlation layer and a matching local
fixed-tail bound are enough to close the aggregate storage sum.
\Cref{cor:profile-entropy-local-storage-screen} sharpens the low-correlation
side further: if the layer is refined into polylogarithmically many
entropy-energy subprofiles, the storage charge depends on the number of
subprofiles rather than on their raw pair mass; failures are exactly the
spread-packing star-signal cases.
\Cref{cor:entropy-deficit-tail-local-storage-screen} gives the nonuniform form:
it is enough to prove a dyadic tail bound for the actual quantities
\(W_h e^{-I_h}\), or equivalently for the entropy deficits
\(\log W_h-I_h\).
\Cref{cor:positive-moment-entropy-deficit-screen} gives a still more compact
target: after choosing a cutoff \(\tau\), a positive moment of the excess
\((W_he^{-I_h}/\tau)^{1+\nu}\) plus the baseline \(\tau|\mathcal H|\) closes
the same storage check.
\Cref{cor:renyi-moment-entropy-deficit-screen} optimizes out that cutoff, so
the remaining low-correlation theorem can be stated directly as one
\(L_{1+\nu}\) moment of \(W_he^{-I_h}\).
\Cref{cor:near-first-moment-entropy-deficit-screen} chooses
\(\nu=1/\max\{1,\log|\mathcal H|\}\), removing the explicit profile-count loss
and leaving only a barely-superlinear moment target.
\Cref{cor:variational-near-first-moment-obstruction} rewrites failure of that
target as one tilted entropy-energy law over the low-correlation profiles.
\Cref{cor:gibbs-water-level-storage-screen} identifies the actual failing law:
the Gibbs law proportional to \((W_he^{-I_h})^{1+\nu}\), with one scalar water
level to compare against the local budget.
\Cref{cor:gibbs-weighted-guard-repair} gives the exact handoff from that law to
the guard-credit verifier: any positive Gibbs-average proposal surplus
materializes as one deterministic dense/star repair, so a surviving obstruction
must be both high-water and no-positive-panel.
\Cref{cor:partition-local-gibbs-residual} localizes this obstruction to one
class of any chosen finite profile partition, with only the explicit
\(J^{1/p}\) loss; this is the finite-band form needed by range-reporting,
tuple-profile, and list-decoding separators.
\Cref{cor:count-energy-cell-screen} converts a bounded dynamic-range cell into
the elementary statistic \(d^++p^{-1}\log|C|\), so the local target is again a
count-energy excess rather than an opaque Gibbs sum.
\Cref{cor:singleton-profile-gibbs-residual} takes the extreme finite partition:
for a polylogarithmic profile refinement, the obstruction is one ordinary
profile entropy-energy violation plus failure of all certified guard repairs.
\Cref{cor:singleton-spread-star-repair} composes this obstruction with the
spread/star layer-cake: a violating singleton must either fire the guard
verifier or make the certified low envelope plus twice the reported star prices
exceed its local water threshold.
\Cref{cor:partition-cell-spread-star-repair} is the corresponding coarse-cell
version: the same repair bridge may be applied after a finite reporter
partition, so the threshold pays the chosen cell count \(J\) rather than the raw
profile count.
\Cref{cor:shared-record-partition-cell-compiler} adds the needed shared-record
interface: profile contributions to the same dense/star record are aggregated in
\(\ell_p\), and that record's recursive price is charged only once in the cell
water test.
\Cref{cor:aggregate-shared-cell-water-budget} removes the artificial uniform
partition split: the reporter only has to fit the \(\ell_p\)-aggregate of the
certified cell costs inside the layer water budget.
\Cref{cor:layer-global-shared-record-water} removes one more bookkeeping
artifact: if the allocations to a dense/star record can be certified over the
whole active layer, that record's recursive price is charged once globally, not
once in each reporter cell where it appears.
\Cref{cor:no-discount-layer-global-water} records the corresponding limitation:
after all positive guard-credit records have been materialized, no fractional
shared allocation can cost less than the Gibbs water level itself.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-top-prefix-water-screen} then gives the finite normal form for
the remaining direct water proof: a surviving high-water layer must contain a
dyadic top prefix whose minimum profile weight times \(k^{1/p}\) exceeds the
local budget up to a logarithmic rank-net toll.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-prefix-spread-star-repair} feeds that prefix back into the
same spread-star guard verifier: if the prefix low envelope and reported star
prices fit the dyadic floor budget, the prefix is ruled out; otherwise the
remaining obstruction is one explicit prefix-price overflow.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-prefix-low-price-residual} normalizes this overflow into the
two scalar branches that remain to be proved: a low-envelope excess or a
one-time recursive star-price excess.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-prefix-high-star-mass} strengthens the high branch: once the
low envelope is below its slack budget, a surviving prefix must carry a large
lower-certified star-mass panel, and in a no-repair residual that panel is
price-saturated record by record.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-prefix-shared-capture-compression} then states the compression
test for that panel: any shared capture whose explicit tail plus one-time shared
price is below the forced high-star mass materializes a guard repair; otherwise
the residual is an exact shared-cover obstruction.
\Cref{cor:finite-dyadic-shared-capture-lp} makes this obstruction algorithmic:
the shared captures form a finite covering LP, and ordinary reduced-cost column
generation is complete for the dyadic high-star branch.
\Cref{cor:one-sided-dyadic-shared-capture-oracle} and
\cref{cor:dyadic-shared-capture-top-prefix-compiler} give the corresponding
verifier-facing build interface: a proposed cell is retained only if its
current dual-weighted top prefix beats the one-time recursive price.
\Cref{cor:generated-cell-dyadic-shared-cover-dichotomy} adds the exact
minimax residual: a finite generated-cell family either fractionally covers the
dyadic high-star mass at budget, or leaves one dual weighting obeying every
cell's top-prefix envelope.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-dual-mass-low-cover-closure} turns that residual into a
low-cover obstruction: any dual-heavy record set with a low Renyi-price cover
by generated cells would force a verified top-prefix column.
\Cref{cor:no-cell-dual-entropy-witness} converts the obstruction into a
dyadic entropy witness: a large no-cell dual mass has an almost-uniform layer
whose compatible generated-cell cover number is large unless the storage-price
term is already dominant.
\Cref{cor:no-cell-metric-cover-screen} makes the compatible cover geometric:
any certified low-entropy container cover of that layer closes the residual as
soon as its generated-template copies meet the Renyi threshold.
\Cref{cor:low-doubling-no-cell-density-screen} gives the quantitative form:
under a low-doubling generated cover, the no-cell layer's weight density
\(\theta\) is bounded by the cover entropy plus the storage term.
\Cref{lem:star-superlevel-column-verifier} and
\cref{cor:pair-star-dense-column-generator} add the finite LP check: the star
is retained only if its ball-thickened query side has positive reduced gain;
otherwise the exact no-star inequality becomes part of the diffuse residual.
\Cref{lem:star-prefix-weak-type-residual} and
\cref{cor:pair-star-weak-type-normal-form} sharpen this further: after a
geometric routine reports a center, the verifier may keep the best paid prefix
inside that smaller ball, and failure of all prefixes forces a weak-type
Renyi cap on every reported star.
\Cref{lem:certified-star-panel-separator} and
\cref{cor:paid-pair-star-panel-certificate} give the reporter-facing version:
a panel of reported stars needs only lower paid-mass and upper size
certificates, and any aggregate violation of the Renyi costs yields an exact
positive dense column.
\Cref{cor:spherical-star-panel-local-cover} plugs this into the finite-cover
duality: after spherical buckets fail, it is enough to construct one certified
paid star panel from the high-correlation residual.
\Cref{cor:hit-weighted-star-panel-prefix} identifies the same certificate in
the paid hit-kernel language: replace the direct dual prices by
\(\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}\), allow fractional query weights, and the paid-prefix
verifier extracts the Boolean top-prefix column.
\Cref{cor:guarded-star-panel-local-cover} narrows the reporter theorem further:
the star panel only has to be proved for normalized residuals that already carry
large activation-weighted high-correlation guard mass after spherical buckets
fail.
\Cref{cor:guarded-no-star-residual-envelope} gives the exact failure form:
without such a panel, every hit-weighted degree superlevel in every reported
star container obeys the Renyi weak-type envelope \((GNE1)\).
\Cref{cor:guard-shadow-transport-reporter} converts this into a transport
target: if the large guard co-load can be shipped with bounded congestion into
the hit-weighted near shadow of one affordable certified star container, the
no-star envelope is violated and the dense column is exposed.
\Cref{lem:guard-shadow-cut-normal-form} gives the exact min-cut obstruction to
that shipment: a surviving residual must contain a query sublayer whose raw
guard load exceeds the paid near-shadow capacity of the proposed container.
\Cref{lem:guard-shadow-credit-normal-form} rewrites the same obstruction in a
fully fractional form: minimize the uncredited guard load after assigning paid
near-shadow capacity of \(W\) to query demands.
\Cref{cor:half-mass-guard-shadow-deficit-obstruction} shows that a no-panel
residual leaves more than half of the guard co-load uncredited for every
affordable smaller-radius container.
\Cref{cor:fractional-guard-credit-panel-reporter} and
\cref{cor:joint-fractional-guard-credit-cover} give the corresponding
overlapping-filter form: a finite fractional flow may distribute guard demand
among many affordable containers, while recursive costs remain charged locally
to the receiving containers.
\Cref{cor:finite-guard-credit-flow-separator} makes this an ordinary finite LP
separator over the generated dense proposal pool, with whole certified
containers submitted directly to the star-panel verifier.
\Cref{lem:finite-guard-credit-flow-dual} gives its exact obstruction: if the
pool fails, point-side paid-shadow prices cancel every guard-credit edge at
zero total priced guard demand.
\Cref{cor:one-template-guard-credit-separation} turns this obstruction into a
single-template search rule: a new affordable container separates the failed
pool as soon as its active paid-shadow mass beats its recursive price.
\Cref{cor:scale-free-guard-credit-proposal} records the raw proposal form: a
proposal routine may output only a certified container and a congestion
certificate.
\Cref{cor:lower-certified-scale-free-guard-panel} is the reporter-facing form:
exact paid-shadow degrees are unnecessary, since lower mass certificates and
upper size certificates already feed the same direct surplus test.
\Cref{cor:high-correlation-stars-feed-guard-credit} connects this to the
high-correlation geometry: a pair-star superlevel becomes such a raw proposal
whenever its star multiplicity is dominated by paid near-shadow degree.
\Cref{cor:paid-responsibility-high-correlation-star} makes that domination
automatic when the star multiplicities are built from responsibility weights
inside the paid near-shadow.
\Cref{cor:pair-compatible-guard-responsibility-star} connects this back to
guard transport: a pair-compatible shipment of guard load into paid
near-shadow capacity immediately induces the responsibility tensor.
\Cref{lem:pair-compatible-guard-cut-normal-form} gives the exact finite
obstruction to such a shipment as a max-flow/min-cut inequality over guard
incidences and pairwise paid capacities.
\Cref{cor:geometric-hall-pair-compatible-guard} rewrites the same obstruction
geometrically: every guard sublayer must have enough paid near-pair capacity in
its certified high-correlation neighborhood.
\Cref{lem:fractional-pair-compatible-hall-obstruction} gives the equivalent
fractional bad-sublayer LP.  This is the exact dense-overlap obstruction at the
frontier: guard incidences may be fractional, but their paid-neighborhood
closure is charged by explicit variables and the relaxation has no integrality
gap.
\Cref{cor:exact-load-pair-compatible-hall-profile} turns the same obstruction
into a one-parameter exact-load closure profile; every bad fractional layer is
seen on the lower convex envelope of ordinary guard sublayers.
\Cref{cor:integral-hall-deficit-normal-form} removes the convex-combination
artifact: any strict profile deficit has one integral guard sublayer with
positive excess load over paid high-correlation closure.
\Cref{cor:hall-profile-repair-guarded-cover} gives the corresponding repair
interface: either the Hall profile supplies the half-shipment, or a proposal
oracle must convert a lower-hull deficit into a lower-certified guard-credit
panel on the loaded queries.
\Cref{cor:proposal-law-hall-profile-repair} gives the proposal-law form of this
target: a finite distribution over raw containers is enough if its expected
loaded paid-shadow surplus beats the recursive price.
\Cref{cor:lower-hull-hall-proposal-separator} names the resulting geometric
separator: every failed lower-hull Hall profile must yield such a positive
proposal law, with the lower-hull witness used only as build-time advice.
\Cref{cor:deficit-restricted-proposal-law} localizes that proposal search to the
paid shadow of one positive-excess Hall sublayer.
\Cref{cor:deficient-shadow-prefix-certificate} reduces the accepted proposal to
one certified top deficient-shadow prefix inside an affordable smaller-radius
container.
\Cref{cor:deficient-shadow-finite-prefix-normal-form},
\cref{cor:finite-prefix-hall-deficit-oracle}, and
\cref{cor:query-layer-deficient-shadow-residual-obstruction} give the sharper
remaining obstruction: positive Hall excess together with a finite-prefix
query-layer envelope for the weighted demand system
\((\mathcal N_{G'},\widehat\gamma,\widehat\tau)\).
\Cref{cor:no-prefix-deficient-shadow-envelope} and
\cref{cor:deficient-shadow-residual-obstruction} are the all-loaded-query
specialization \(y\equiv1\).
\Cref{cor:tail-deficient-shadow-envelope} converts that bound to threshold
superlevels, which is the form exposed by range-reporting or list-decoding
proposal mechanisms.
\Cref{cor:two-price-deficient-shadow-screen} splits any failed threshold layer
into a query-price or storage-price obstruction.
\Cref{cor:forbidden-middle-deficient-shadow-scale} rewrites this as a scale gap:
surviving layers are either query-small or storage-large.
\Cref{cor:cardinality-net-deficient-shadow-reporter} shows that a reporter need
only find an arbitrary superlevel in this forbidden gap; retained dyadic prefix
sizes round it to a certified proposal.
\Cref{cor:layer-cake-deficient-shadow-reporter} allows the same conclusion from
an aggregate panel whose captured mass beats its Renyi query/storage moments.
\Cref{cor:integral-deficient-shadow-moment-reporter} replaces the panel by a
truncated deficient-shadow moment estimate on one height window.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-window-deficient-shadow-moment-reporter} lets a proof sum over
dyadic height windows without reintroducing the per-prefix layer-cake charge.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-window-deficient-shadow-residual-envelope} records the matching
capped-moment envelope left if all such windows fail.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-log-lorentz-deficient-shadow-separator} reduces that envelope
to capped linear mass versus dyadic threshold cardinalities.
\Cref{cor:fractional-log-lorentz-deficient-shadow-panel} gives the matching
proposal-law form: a finite panel of containers and height windows closes as
soon as its total verified log-Lorentz surplus is positive.
\Cref{cor:certified-log-lorentz-deficient-shadow-panel} replaces exact
superlevel counts by lower captured-mass and upper rank certificates.
\Cref{cor:mass-support-log-lorentz-certificate} gives a still coarser
certificate using only mass, support, and maximum degree.
\Cref{cor:average-density-mass-support-screen} rewrites that certificate as an
average-density condition with separate query-price and storage-price sides.
\Cref{cor:balanced-average-density-screen} optimizes the support scale in that
condition, so a balanced record has to beat only one mixed query-storage
density threshold.
\Cref{cor:balanced-top-prefix-density-screen} is the top-prefix specialization:
materializing the balanced prefix replaces the coarse dynamic-range charge by a
direct mixed-density test, and oversized reports can be trimmed before
certification.
\Cref{cor:fixed-threshold-balanced-density-screen} records this noncircular
density target at the mixed query-storage scale.
\Cref{cor:fractional-fixed-threshold-density-panel} is the proposal-law version:
positive aggregate fixed-threshold density surplus in any finite panel exposes
one deterministic balanced dense column.
\Cref{cor:sampled-fixed-threshold-density-search} adds the expensive-build
wrapper: a positive-margin seeded panel law is enough, because repeated samples
are discarded after the verifier keeps one deterministic closing record.
\Cref{cor:fixed-threshold-hall-deficit-oracle} is the resulting local-cover
criterion: the lower-hull Hall repair law can be replaced by this
fixed-threshold balanced density panel for the one exposed deficient shadow.
\Cref{cor:single-record-fixed-threshold-hall-separator} is the minimal
deterministic form of that criterion: the geometric reporter only has to expose
one retained balanced prefix or one trimmable coarse record above the fixed
density threshold.
\Cref{cor:pair-compatible-hall-guarded-cover} assembles the chain back into the
local LP: a half-shipment with sufficient direct mixed-density surplus supplies the
guarded star-panel reporter and closes the residual.
\Cref{lem:tuple-witness-distinct-child-tail} and
\cref{cor:tuple-profile-distinct-storage} give the corresponding
entropy-energy normal form: each large canonical child supplies many separated
tuple witnesses, so it is enough to bound the expected canonical-child
incidence of every tuple profile.
\Cref{lem:multiplicity-discounted-tuple-witness} and
\cref{cor:multiplicity-discounted-distinct-storage} are the quotient-aware
version: if many decoded records induce the same stored child, each occurrence
is weighted by the reciprocal of that child's multiplicity before tuple
incidence is charged.

\begin{proposition}[Conditional fractional filter-cover endpoint]
   \label{prop:fractional-filter-cover-polylog}
   Fix \(c>1\) and \(\rho_c=1/(2c^2-1)\).  Suppose that after the usual
   bounded-diameter localization, every resident node \(P\), \(|P|=N\), admits a
   finite-signature filter-cover certificate of
   \cref{lem:finite-signature-filter-cover} with the following uniform bounds.
   The decoder computes \(\sigma(q)\) and the retained active filters in time
   \(d\,N^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n\).  Its entropy and witness size obey
   \[
      \log\left(2+\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}|W_{\sigma_0}|\right)
      \le \log^{O_c(1)}n.
      \tag{FE1}
   \]
   The signature budgets satisfy
   \[
      L_{\sigma_0}\le N^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S\le N^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n.
      \tag{FE2}
   \]
   Each filter is either terminal, in which case \(T_A\) is a verified normalized
   scan or smooth-product terminal price, or it invokes a child structure whose
   certified normalized query price and storage are \(T_A,S_A\).  Invoking a
   child of normalized price \(T_A\) costs \(O(d\,T_A)\) time.  Nonterminal
   filters have strictly smaller certified radius, so the inductive construction
   is acyclic.

   Then worst-case Euclidean ANN has query time and space
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
   Order all possible recursive nodes by certified radius, breaking ties by
   resident set size.  Terminal nodes have the stated prices by hypothesis.
   Assume all smaller children already have certified prices.  At a node \(P\),
   solve the finite signature LP using those child prices and materialize it by
   \cref{lem:finite-signature-filter-cover}.  By \((FE1)\), the rounding factor
   \(B\) is \(\log^{O_c(1)}n\).  Therefore \((FE2)\) gives retained active cost
   at most \(N^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n\) for every signature and retained storage
   at most \(N^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n\).

   The important point is that \(T_A\) is the full certified normalized query
   cost of the child structure, not just a local bucket size.  Thus a query at
   \(P\) pays the decoder cost plus
   \[
      d\sum_{A\in\mathcal R:a_A(q)=1}T_A
      \le
      d\,N^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
   \]
   so recursive overlap has already been charged inside the local LP.  Similarly,
   the retained node stores child structures of total certified storage
   \[
      \sum_{A\in\mathcal R}S_A
      \le
      N^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n.
   \]
   Routing correctness follows from the last conclusion of
   \cref{lem:finite-signature-filter-cover}: for every near pair, at least one
   active retained filter contains the near point, and that child is correct by
   its own certificate.  Final candidates are verified in the original metric.

   Applying this induction at the localized root with \(N=n\), and adding the
   single global storage of the original coordinates, gives the displayed
   bounds.  Standard constant-probability amplification and truncation affect
   only the logarithmic factors.
\end{proof}

The same induction applies if, at some node, the all-pair finite-signature
certificate of \cref{lem:finite-signature-filter-cover} is replaced by the
exact-near-set existential certificate of
\cref{lem:exact-near-set-filter-cover}, with the same decoder, query-budget,
and storage bounds, and with \((FE1)\) replaced by
\[
   \log(2+|\Sigma|+|\Sigma^+|)
   \le
   \log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \tag{FE1\({}^{\exists}\)}
\]
Indeed the existential materialization pays only for the number of exact
near-set signatures, not for the total size of the near sets represented by
those signatures.  The child reached by an active filter intersecting
\(N_{\sigma(q)}\) is a valid ANN child for that query, so the proof only changes
the routing sentence; the recursive cost accounting is identical.  Thus a proof
of polylogarithmic overhead may target exact-signature existential covers
wherever compact exact near-set signatures are available, and reserve per-pair
covers for robust all-witness certificates.

\begin{corollary}[One-sided finite-signature filter-cover endpoint]
   \label{cor:one-sided-finite-signature-filter-cover}
   Fix \(c>1\) and \(\rho_c=1/(2c^2-1)\).  Suppose that after bounded-diameter
   localization, every resident node \(P\), \(|P|=N\), has a finite signature
   system as in \cref{lem:finite-signature-filter-cover}, with budgets satisfying
   \[
      \log\left(2+\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}|W_{\sigma_0}|\right)
      \le\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      L_{\sigma_0}\le N^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S\le N^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
      \tag{OSF0}
   \]
   Let \(\mathcal F_\star\) be a finite, possibly implicitly represented,
   quotient of all admissible priced filters at the node.  The quotient may
   contain terminal spherical filters, radius-contracting dense filters,
   facility or additive-quantization buckets, list-decoder outputs, and any
   other certified columns; each column \(A\) has update side \(U_A\), signature
   activation bits \(a_A(\sigma_0)\), and certified prices \(T_A,S_A\).  Assume
   the atom bounds \((FS2)\), and assume the full signature LP
   \((\mathsf{SFC}_\Sigma)\) over \(\mathcal F_\star\) is feasible.

   At a restricted active set \(E\subseteq\mathcal F_\star\), let
   \((\alpha,\tau,\zeta)\) be any surplus Farkas certificate for the restricted
   signature LP: it has
   \[
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\sum_{p\in W_{\sigma_0}}\alpha_{p,\sigma_0}
      >
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}L_{\sigma_0}+\zeta S
      \tag{OSF1}
   \]
   and nonpositive reduced gain on every active column.  For any candidate
   column \(A\), define
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \operatorname{Gain}_{\alpha,\tau,\zeta}(A)
      &=
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}
      \sum_{p\in W_{\sigma_0}}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}
      \mathbf 1\{p\in U_A\}a_A(\sigma_0)  \\
      &\qquad
      -
      T_A\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}a_A(\sigma_0)
      -
      \zeta S_A .
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{OSF2}
   \]
   Suppose uncharged preprocessing has a one-sided separator which, for every
   such restricted dual state, either returns an inactive column
   \(A\in\mathcal F_\star\setminus E\) with a verifiable lower certificate
   \[
      0<X\le \operatorname{Gain}_{\alpha,\tau,\zeta}(A),
      \tag{OSF3}
   \]
   or certifies
   \[
      \operatorname{Gain}_{\alpha,\tau,\zeta}(A)\le0
      \qquad(A\in\mathcal F_\star\setminus E).
      \tag{OSF4}
   \]
   Then preprocessing can construct the finite-signature certificate required
   by \cref{prop:fractional-filter-cover-polylog}.  Consequently worst-case
   Euclidean ANN has
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   If the separator is randomized and returns a verifiable column satisfying
   \((OSF3)\) with probability at least \(p_E\) whenever one exists, Las Vegas
   repetition adds an improving column after expected at most \(1/p_E\) proposal
   calls at that restricted solve; failed proposals are not retained or charged
   to the index.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The finite signature LP is the filter-cover LP of
   \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual} applied to the demand set
   \[
      \mathcal N_\Sigma
      =
      \{(p,\sigma_0):\sigma_0\in\Sigma,\ p\in W_{\sigma_0}\}.
   \]
   Its Farkas dual is exactly \((OSF1)\) together with nonpositive reduced gain
   on the columns under consideration, with reduced gain given by \((OSF2)\).

   Run ordinary column generation on the finite quotient \(\mathcal F_\star\).
   If the restricted LP is feasible, stop.  If it is infeasible, take a surplus
   dual certificate for the restricted pool.  A returned column satisfying
   \((OSF3)\) violates that restricted Farkas certificate and is added to the
   active set.  If instead the separator certifies \((OSF4)\), then the active
   columns already had nonpositive gain by restricted dual feasibility, and all
   inactive columns have nonpositive gain by \((OSF4)\).  Hence the same dual
   certificate proves infeasibility of the full LP over \(\mathcal F_\star\),
   contradicting the assumed full feasibility.  Therefore column generation
   cannot stop with a no-positive certificate before finding a feasible
   restricted LP.  Since the quotient is finite, deterministic preprocessing
   adds at most \(|\mathcal F_\star|\) successful columns.

   Once the finite signature LP is feasible, \((OSF0)\), the atom bounds, and
   \cref{lem:finite-signature-filter-cover} give the retained finite cover with
   only logarithmic materialization loss.  Applying
   \cref{prop:fractional-filter-cover-polylog} at all localized nodes gives the
   displayed global query and space bounds.  The randomized statement is the
   usual geometric-waiting argument applied only to verified positive columns.
\end{proof}

This corollary is the fully fractional dense-overlap interface in endpoint
form.  There is no theorem-level choice of a disjoint dense-cluster family.
Preprocessing may spend arbitrary time proposing overlapping dense regions,
spherical buckets, facility panels, additive-code cells, or list-decoder
records, but the retained index only keeps columns that pass the finite
one-sided reduced-gain verifier.  Query overlap is then charged by the local LP
through \(\sum_Aa_A(\sigma_0)T_A\lambda_A\), and recursive overlap never appears
as a separate branching factor.

\begin{corollary}[Positive finite-signature separator endpoint]
   \label{cor:positive-finite-signature-separator-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:one-sided-finite-signature-filter-cover}, but do not assume in
   advance that the full signature LP over \(\mathcal F_\star\) is feasible.
   Assume instead the following nodewise positive reduced-gain theorem.  For
   every nonnegative price system \((\alpha,\tau,\zeta)\) satisfying the surplus
   inequality \((OSF1)\), the unified finite filter universe exposes a positive
   column:
   \[
      \max_{A\in\mathcal F_\star}
      \operatorname{Gain}_{\alpha,\tau,\zeta}(A)>0 .
      \tag{PFS1}
   \]
   Suppose also that the one-sided separator of
   \cref{cor:one-sided-finite-signature-filter-cover} implements this universe:
   on every restricted dual state it either returns a verifiable inactive column
   satisfying \((OSF3)\), or certifies the universal no-gain inequality
   \((OSF4)\) on the inactive quotient classes.  The signature decoder and
   active retained-column reporter have the time bound required in
   \cref{prop:fractional-filter-cover-polylog}.

   Then the full finite-signature cover exists and can be found by uncharged
   column generation.  Consequently worst-case Euclidean ANN has
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the full signature LP were infeasible, the finite filter-cover dual
   \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual}, applied to the signature demand set
   \(\mathcal N_\Sigma\), would give nonnegative prices satisfying
   \((OSF1)\) and
   \[
      \operatorname{Gain}_{\alpha,\tau,\zeta}(A)\le0
      \qquad(A\in\mathcal F_\star).
   \]
   This contradicts \((PFS1)\).  Hence the full LP is feasible.

   Now run restricted column generation.  At an infeasible restricted solve, the
   restricted Farkas certificate has nonpositive gain on every active column.
   By \((PFS1)\), some full-universe column has positive gain, and it must be
   inactive.  Therefore a valid no-gain certificate \((OSF4)\) cannot occur;
   the one-sided separator must expose a verified improving column satisfying
   \((OSF3)\).  Since the quotient universe is finite, this process reaches a
   feasible restricted signature LP after finitely many successful additions.
   The materialization and recursive endpoint are then exactly
   \cref{lem:finite-signature-filter-cover} and
   \cref{prop:fractional-filter-cover-polylog}.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:positive-finite-signature-separator-endpoint} is the cleanest finite
form of the desired polylogarithmic theorem.  The remaining geometric work is
precisely \((PFS1)\): every surplus dual obstruction must be separated by one
column from the unified family.  A spherical bucket may do it on pseudo-random
residuals; a radius-contracting dense core, facility bucket, additive-code
cell, or list-decoder output may do it on structured residuals.  The verifier
does not distinguish these cases once a positive reduced-gain column is
certified.

\begin{corollary}[Dense/spherical separator endpoint]
   \label{cor:dense-spherical-positive-separator-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:positive-finite-signature-separator-endpoint}, and split the
   unified finite filter universe as
   \[
      \mathcal F_\star
      =
      \mathcal F_{\rm str}\cup\mathcal F_{\rm sph},
   \]
   where \(\mathcal F_{\rm str}\) contains the radius-contracting structured
   columns--dense cores, facility buckets, additive-code cells, list-decoder
   regions, and any certified descendant filters--and
   \(\mathcal F_{\rm sph}\) contains the large-range spherical or terminal
   filter columns.  Suppose that every surplus price system
   \((\alpha,\tau,\zeta)\) satisfying \((OSF1)\) and
   \[
      \operatorname{Gain}_{\alpha,\tau,\zeta}(D)\le0
      \qquad(D\in\mathcal F_{\rm str})
      \tag{DSF1}
   \]
   has a positive spherical separator,
   \[
      \max_{Z\in\mathcal F_{\rm sph}}
      \operatorname{Gain}_{\alpha,\tau,\zeta}(Z)>0 .
      \tag{DSF2}
   \]
   Then the positive finite-signature separator condition \((PFS1)\) holds, and
   therefore the same
   \[
      d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n
      \quad\text{query time,}\qquad
      dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n
      \quad\text{space}
   \]
   endpoint follows.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix any surplus price system satisfying \((OSF1)\).  If some structured
   column \(D\in\mathcal F_{\rm str}\) has positive reduced gain, then
   \((PFS1)\) holds immediately.  Otherwise \((DSF1)\) holds for every
   structured column, so the hypothesis gives a spherical column satisfying
   \((DSF2)\).  Thus every surplus price system has a positive-gain column in
   \(\mathcal F_\star\), which is exactly \((PFS1)\).  Apply
   \cref{cor:positive-finite-signature-separator-endpoint}.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:dense-spherical-positive-separator-endpoint} is the LP-dual version of
the AR dense-versus-pseudo-random split.  Dense objects are not selected or
removed greedily: if any structured overlapping filter has positive reduced
gain, column generation keeps it.  Only after all such columns have nonpositive
gain does the proof need a spherical pseudo-randomness theorem, namely
\((DSF2)\).  This is the exact place where a geometric argument, range-reporting
separator, lattice/list decoder, or facility proposal must enter.

\begin{lemma}[Finite-signature spherical reduced-gain test]
   \label{lem:finite-signature-spherical-reduced-gain}
   Work in the finite-signature setting of
   \cref{cor:one-sided-finite-signature-filter-cover}.  Let
   \(\mathcal Z\subseteq\mathcal F_\star\) be a finite family of spherical
   columns with update buckets \(U_z\subseteq P\), signature activations
   \(\chi_z(\sigma_0)\in\{0,1\}\), and terminal prices
   \(T_z=S_z=|U_z|\).  Let \(\Pi\) be a probability law on \(\mathcal Z\), and
   let \(H_{\sigma_0}\subseteq P\) be certified high-correlation sets.  Suppose
   that for constants \(\pi_1,\pi_2,\pi_u>0\),
   \[
      \Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[p\in U_Z,\ \chi_Z(\sigma_0)=1]\ge\pi_1
      \qquad(p\in W_{\sigma_0}),
      \tag{FSS1}
   \]
   \[
      \Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[x\in U_Z,\ \chi_Z(\sigma_0)=1]\le\pi_2
      \qquad(x\notin H_{\sigma_0}),
      \tag{FSS2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[x\in U_Z]\le\pi_u
      \qquad(x\in P).
      \tag{FSS3}
   \]
   For a surplus signature dual \((\alpha,\tau,\zeta)\), put
   \[
      A_\alpha=
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\sum_{p\in W_{\sigma_0}}\alpha_{p,\sigma_0},
      \qquad
      L_\tau=\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}L_{\sigma_0},
      \tag{FSS4}
   \]
   and define its high-correlation spherical co-load by
   \[
      \mathsf C_H(\tau)
      =
      \E_{Z\sim\Pi}
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}
      \tau_{\sigma_0}\chi_Z(\sigma_0)|U_Z\cap H_{\sigma_0}|.
      \tag{FSS5}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \E_{Z\sim\Pi}
      \operatorname{Gain}_{\alpha,\tau,\zeta}(Z)
      \ge
      \pi_1A_\alpha
      -\pi_2|P|\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}
      -\mathsf C_H(\tau)
      -\pi_u|P|\zeta .
      \tag{FSS6}
   \]
   Consequently, if
   \[
      \pi_2|P|\le \frac{\pi_1L_{\sigma_0}}4
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \qquad
      \pi_u|P|\le\frac{\pi_1S}{4},
      \tag{FSS7}
   \]
   then every surplus dual satisfying \((OSF1)\) has a positive spherical
   column unless
   \[
      \mathsf C_H(\tau)>\frac{\pi_1}{2}A_\alpha .
      \tag{FSS8}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Average the signature reduced gain \((OSF2)\) over \(Z\sim\Pi\).  The useful
   coverage term is bounded below by \((FSS1)\):
   \[
      \E_Z
      \sum_{\sigma_0}\sum_{p\in W_{\sigma_0}}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}\mathbf 1\{p\in U_Z\}\chi_Z(\sigma_0)
      \ge \pi_1A_\alpha .
   \]
   For the query-price term, split each bucket into its high-correlation part
   and complement:
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \E_Z\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}\chi_Z(\sigma_0)|U_Z|
      &=
      \mathsf C_H(\tau) \\
      &\quad+
      \sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}
      \sum_{x\notin H_{\sigma_0}}
      \Pr[x\in U_Z,\ \chi_Z(\sigma_0)=1].
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   By \((FSS2)\), the second term is at most
   \(\pi_2|P|\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}\).  The storage term is bounded by
   \[
      \zeta\,\E_Z|U_Z|
      =
      \zeta\sum_{x\in P}\Pr[x\in U_Z]
      \le
      \pi_u|P|\zeta
   \]
   using \((FSS3)\).  This proves \((FSS6)\).

   Under \((FSS7)\),
   \[
      \pi_2|P|\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}
      +
      \pi_u|P|\zeta
      \le
      \frac{\pi_1}{4}(L_\tau+\zeta S).
   \]
   Surplus \((OSF1)\) says \(A_\alpha>L_\tau+\zeta S\).  If
   \(\mathsf C_H(\tau)\le\pi_1A_\alpha/2\), then \((FSS6)\) gives positive
   expected reduced gain over \(Z\sim\Pi\), so one spherical column in the
   support has positive gain.  The contrapositive is \((FSS8)\).
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:finite-signature-spherical-reduced-gain} is the signature-level
spherical half of \((DSF2)\).  It shows that a residual dual not separated by
spherical filters must concentrate query price on certified high-correlation
bucket mass.  The dense side of the proof can therefore target only that
co-load: produce one structured column with positive gain, or prove that the
co-load residual cannot occur for the chosen spherical family.

\begin{corollary}[High-correlation co-load separator endpoint]
   \label{cor:high-correlation-coload-separator-endpoint}
   Work in the split-universe setting of
   \cref{cor:dense-spherical-positive-separator-endpoint}.  Suppose
   \(\mathcal F_{\rm sph}\) contains a spherical subfamily \(\mathcal Z\)
   satisfying the finite-signature hypotheses \((FSS1)\)--\((FSS7)\).  Assume
   the structured universe is complete for the only spherical obstruction in
   the following sense: every surplus dual \((\alpha,\tau,\zeta)\) satisfying
   \((OSF1)\) and
   \[
      \mathsf C_H(\tau)>\frac{\pi_1}{2}A_\alpha
      \tag{HCS1}
   \]
   has a structured column \(D\in\mathcal F_{\rm str}\) with
   \[
      \operatorname{Gain}_{\alpha,\tau,\zeta}(D)>0 .
      \tag{HCS2}
   \]
   Then the dense/spherical separator condition \((DSF2)\) holds, and hence the
   polylogarithmic ANN endpoint of
   \cref{cor:dense-spherical-positive-separator-endpoint} follows.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a surplus dual satisfying \((OSF1)\) and assume every structured column
   has nonpositive gain, as in \((DSF1)\).  If no spherical column in
   \(\mathcal Z\) has positive gain, then
   \cref{lem:finite-signature-spherical-reduced-gain} and \((FSS1)\)--\((FSS7)\)
   imply the high-correlation co-load alternative \((HCS1)\).  By the assumed
   structured completeness, \((HCS1)\) exposes a structured column satisfying
   \((HCS2)\), contradicting \((DSF1)\).  Therefore some spherical column has
   positive gain.  This is exactly \((DSF2)\), and the endpoint follows from
   \cref{cor:dense-spherical-positive-separator-endpoint}.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:high-correlation-coload-separator-endpoint} is the finite theorem
target left after the spherical calculation.  The dense proposal family does
not need to explain all residual duals.  It only needs to separate the explicit
co-load residual \((HCS1)\); all lower-co-load residuals are already handled by
the spherical bucket law.

\begin{corollary}[Finite-signature star-panel co-load endpoint]
   \label{cor:finite-signature-star-panel-coload-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-coload-separator-endpoint}.  Suppose the
   structured universe contains, for every certified star template \(x\), every
   top-degree prefix column of a container \(W_x\subseteq P\) with certified
   signature activation \(a_x(\sigma_0)\in\{0,1\}\) and prices
   \[
      T_{x,K}=\psi_xK^{\rho_x},
      \qquad
      S_{x,K}=\psi_xK^{1+\rho_x}
      \qquad(1\le K\le |W_x|).
      \tag{FSP1}
   \]
   For a surplus signature dual, define the paid degree of \(p\in W_x\) by
   \[
      d_x(p)
      =
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,p\in W_{\sigma_0}}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}a_x(\sigma_0),
      \qquad
      A_x=\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}a_x(\sigma_0).
      \tag{FSP2}
   \]
   Assume that every dual satisfying the high-correlation co-load residual
   \((HCS1)\) admits a finite star panel.  A panel record \(i\) consists of a
   template \(x_i\), a proposed subset \(U_i\subseteq W_{x_i}\), a nonnegative
   weight \(\lambda_i\), a lower paid-mass certificate \(X_i\), and an upper size
   certificate \(K_i\), with
   \[
      0\le X_i\le\sum_{p\in U_i}d_{x_i}(p),
      \qquad
      |U_i|\le K_i .
      \tag{FSP3}
   \]
   The panel is separating if
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_iX_i
      >
      \sum_i\lambda_i\psi_{x_i}
      \left(
         A_{x_i}K_i^{\rho_{x_i}}
         +\zeta K_i^{1+\rho_{x_i}}
      \right).
      \tag{FSP4}
   \]
   If every residual \((HCS1)\) admits such a separating panel, then the
   structured completeness condition \((HCS2)\) holds, and hence the
   polylogarithmic ANN endpoint follows.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a residual dual satisfying \((HCS1)\), and suppose for contradiction that
   no structured prefix column has positive gain.  For a template \(x\), order
   the points of \(W_x\) by decreasing \(d_x(p)\), and let \(P_{x,K}\) be the
   top \(K\) points.  The reduced gain of the corresponding retained column is
   \[
      \sum_{p\in P_{x,K}}d_x(p)
      -
      \psi_xA_xK^{\rho_x}
      -
      \zeta\psi_xK^{1+\rho_x}.
   \]
   Nonpositive gain for every prefix therefore gives
   \[
      \sum_{p\in P_{x,K}}d_x(p)
      \le
      \psi_x\left(A_xK^{\rho_x}+\zeta K^{1+\rho_x}\right)
      \tag{FSP5}
   \]
   for every available \(x,K\).  For any panel record \(i\), the top
   \(K_i\)-prefix dominates every subset of size at most \(K_i\), so
   \[
      X_i
      \le
      \sum_{p\in U_i}d_{x_i}(p)
      \le
      \sum_{p\in P_{x_i,K_i}}d_{x_i}(p).
   \]
   Applying \((FSP5)\), multiplying by \(\lambda_i\), and summing over \(i\)
   gives the reverse of \((FSP4)\), contradicting the separating panel.
   Hence some structured prefix column has positive gain, which is \((HCS2)\).
   The endpoint is \cref{cor:high-correlation-coload-separator-endpoint}.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:finite-signature-star-panel-coload-endpoint} is the finite-signature
version of the pair-star reporter criterion.  The geometric routine may output
only coarse star sets with one-sided mass and size certificates.  The retained
index still stores the exact top-degree prefix selected by the current dual,
so this remains a column-generation proof rather than a clustering or Lloyd
optimality statement.

\begin{corollary}[Finite-signature responsibility star endpoint]
   \label{cor:finite-signature-responsibility-star-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-star-panel-coload-endpoint}.  Let
   \(\mathcal X\) be a finite set of certified star templates.  A responsibility
   reporter returns numbers
   \[
      0\le \eta_{x,p,\sigma_0}\le1
      \qquad
      (x\in\mathcal X,\ p\in W_x,\ \sigma_0\in\Sigma)
   \]
   supported only when \(p\in W_{\sigma_0}\) and \(a_x(\sigma_0)=1\).  For a
   surplus signature dual, define
   \[
      M_x(p)
      =
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,p\in W_{\sigma_0}}
      \eta_{x,p,\sigma_0}\alpha_{p,\sigma_0}a_x(\sigma_0).
      \tag{FRS1}
   \]
   For every level \(t>0\), put
   \[
      U_{x,t}=\{p\in W_x:M_x(p)\ge t\},
      \qquad
      X_{x,t}=t|U_{x,t}|.
      \tag{FRS2}
   \]
   Then every record \((x,U_{x,t},X_{x,t},|U_{x,t}|)\) satisfies the
   one-sided star-panel certificate \((FSP3)\).  Consequently, any finite panel
   of such responsibility superlevels satisfying \((FSP4)\) proves the
   structured completeness condition \((HCS2)\) and gives the polylogarithmic
   endpoint.

   In particular, suppose all positive \(M_x(p)\) lie in a certified range
   \([M_{\min},M_{\max}]\), and let
   \[
      J_{\rm resp}
      =
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{M_{\max}}{M_{\min}}\right\rceil ,
      \qquad
      W_{\rm resp}=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\sum_{p\in W_x}M_x(p).
      \tag{FRS3}
   \]
   Then some \(x\in\mathcal X\) and dyadic level \(t\) have
   \[
      X_{x,t}\ge \frac{W_{\rm resp}}{2|\mathcal X|J_{\rm resp}}.
      \tag{FRS4}
   \]
   Therefore a one-record star panel is separating whenever the right hand side
   of \((FRS4)\) is larger than
   \[
      \psi_x
      \left(
         A_x|U_{x,t}|^{\rho_x}
         +\zeta |U_{x,t}|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right)
      \tag{FRS5}
   \]
   for the exposed level.  A cruder sufficient condition is obtained by
   replacing \((FRS5)\) by any certified uniform upper bound over the dyadic
   superlevels generated by the reporter.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For \(p\in W_x\), the support and bound \(0\le\eta\le1\) give
   \[
      M_x(p)
      \le
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,p\in W_{\sigma_0}}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}a_x(\sigma_0)
      =
      d_x(p).
   \]
   Hence for every superlevel,
   \[
      X_{x,t}=t|U_{x,t}|
      \le
      \sum_{p\in U_{x,t}}M_x(p)
      \le
      \sum_{p\in U_{x,t}}d_x(p).
   \]
   Together with the exact size certificate \(|U_{x,t}|\), this is precisely
   \((FSP3)\).  Thus any finite panel satisfying \((FSP4)\) is separating by
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-star-panel-coload-endpoint}.

   For the dyadic statement, choose a center \(x\) with
   \[
      \sum_{p\in W_x}M_x(p)\ge W_{\rm resp}/|\mathcal X|.
   \]
   The same dyadic layer-cake estimate used in
   \cref{lem:high-correlation-pair-star-reporter} gives
   \[
      \sum_{j=0}^{J_{\rm resp}-1}
      2^jM_{\min}\,
      |\{p:M_x(p)\ge2^jM_{\min}\}|
      \ge
      \frac12\sum_{p\in W_x}M_x(p),
   \]
   so one dyadic level satisfies \((FRS4)\).  If that level also beats its
   certified Renyi price \((FRS5)\), the one-record panel satisfies
   \((FSP4)\).
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:finite-signature-responsibility-star-endpoint} is the build-facing
form of the dense theorem.  A facility assignment, additive-quantization panel,
or list/lattice decoder may return soft responsibilities rather than a hard
cluster.  The proof only asks that these responsibilities be supported on
certified smaller-radius templates and that the resulting layer-cake
superlevel beat the exact reduced-cost price.

\begin{corollary}[Aggregate finite-signature responsibility panel]
   \label{cor:aggregate-finite-signature-responsibility-panel}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-responsibility-star-endpoint}.  For each template
   \(x\in\mathcal X\), suppose the positive responsibility multiplicities
   \(M_x(p)\) lie in a certified range
   \([M_x^{\min},M_x^{\max}]\), and put
   \[
      J_x=1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{M_x^{\max}}{M_x^{\min}}\right\rceil .
      \tag{FRA1}
   \]
   For every dyadic level
   \(t_{x,j}=2^jM_x^{\min}\), \(0\le j<J_x\), define
   \[
      U_{x,j}=\{p\in W_x:M_x(p)\ge t_{x,j}\},
      \qquad
      X_{x,j}=t_{x,j}|U_{x,j}|.
      \tag{FRA2}
   \]
   Then the full dyadic responsibility panel satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\sum_{j=0}^{J_x-1}X_{x,j}
      \ge
      \frac12
      \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\sum_{p\in W_x}M_x(p)
      =
      \frac12 W_{\rm resp}.
      \tag{FRA3}
   \]
   Consequently, define its aggregate certified price by
   \[
      \mathsf P_{\rm resp}
      =
      \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\sum_{j=0}^{J_x-1}
      \psi_x
      \left(
         A_x|U_{x,j}|^{\rho_x}
         +\zeta |U_{x,j}|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{FRA4}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \frac12W_{\rm resp}>\mathsf P_{\rm resp},
      \tag{FRA5}
   \]
   then the dyadic responsibility panel satisfies \((FSP4)\), and hence exposes
   a positive structured prefix column.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed template \(x\), the dyadic layer-cake estimate used in
   \cref{lem:high-correlation-pair-star-reporter} gives
   \[
      \sum_{j=0}^{J_x-1}t_{x,j}|U_{x,j}|
      \ge
      \frac12\sum_{p\in W_x}M_x(p).
   \]
   Summing over \(x\) proves \((FRA3)\).

   Each record \((x,U_{x,j},X_{x,j},|U_{x,j}|)\) satisfies the one-sided
   certificate \((FSP3)\) by the first part of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-responsibility-star-endpoint}.  Taking all panel
   weights \(\lambda_{x,j}=1\), condition \((FRA5)\) is exactly \((FSP4)\) after
   lower-bounding the left side by \((FRA3)\) and writing the right side as
   \((FRA4)\).  Therefore
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-star-panel-coload-endpoint} exposes a positive
   structured prefix column.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:aggregate-finite-signature-responsibility-panel} avoids the
number-of-centers loss in the one-record form.  A proposal family may spread
responsibility mass over many facilities or code buckets, provided the aggregate
Renyi prefix price of the dyadic superlevels is still below the transported paid
mass.

\begin{corollary}[Finite-signature co-load transport endpoint]
   \label{cor:finite-signature-coload-transport-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-responsibility-star-endpoint}.  For the spherical
   law in \cref{lem:finite-signature-spherical-reduced-gain}, define the
   certified high-correlation co-load atoms
   \[
      g_{\sigma_0,x}
      =
      \mathbf 1\{x\in H_{\sigma_0}\}
      \Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[x\in U_Z,\ \chi_Z(\sigma_0)=1],
      \tag{FCT1}
   \]
   so that
   \[
      \mathsf C_H(\tau)
      =
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}
      \sum_{x\in P}g_{\sigma_0,x}.
      \tag{FCT2}
   \]
   Suppose every residual satisfying \((HCS1)\) admits a finite certified
   template set \(\mathcal X\subseteq P\), a transport loss \(C_{\rm tr}\ge1\),
   and responsibilities \(\eta_{x,p,\sigma_0}\) as in
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-responsibility-star-endpoint}, such that
   \[
      B_{\mathcal X}
      =
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}
      \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}g_{\sigma_0,x}
      >0,
      \qquad
      W_{\rm resp}\ge \frac{B_{\mathcal X}}{C_{\rm tr}} .
      \tag{FCT3}
   \]
   Assume the positive responsibility multiplicities lie in a certified range
   with dyadic factor \(J_{\rm resp}\), and that every dyadic superlevel
   generated from these responsibilities has certified Renyi price at most
   \(R_{\rm tr}\):
   \[
      \psi_x
      \left(
         A_x|U_{x,t}|^{\rho_x}
         +\zeta |U_{x,t}|^{1+\rho_x}
      \right)
      \le R_{\rm tr}.
      \tag{FCT4}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \frac{B_{\mathcal X}}
      {2C_{\rm tr}|\mathcal X|J_{\rm resp}}
      >
      R_{\rm tr},
      \tag{FCT5}
   \]
   then the residual has a separating finite-signature star panel.  Consequently,
   if every high-correlation co-load residual \((HCS1)\) admits such a transport
   certificate, the polylogarithmic ANN endpoint follows.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Equation \((FCT2)\) is just the definition \((FSS5)\) expanded by linearity
   of expectation.  Given \((FCT3)\), the responsibility multiplicities of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-responsibility-star-endpoint} have total mass
   \(W_{\rm resp}\ge B_{\mathcal X}/C_{\rm tr}\).  Therefore \((FRS4)\) exposes
   a dyadic superlevel with
   \[
      X_{x,t}
      \ge
      \frac{W_{\rm resp}}{2|\mathcal X|J_{\rm resp}}
      \ge
      \frac{B_{\mathcal X}}
      {2C_{\rm tr}|\mathcal X|J_{\rm resp}}.
   \]
   By \((FCT4)\)--\((FCT5)\), this superlevel beats its certified reduced-cost
   price, so the one-record panel satisfies \((FSP4)\).  The endpoint statement
   is then exactly
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-star-panel-coload-endpoint}.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:finite-signature-coload-transport-endpoint} is the current
proof-facing form of the dense geometry.  It asks for a bounded-loss transport
from the spherical high-correlation co-load atoms to paid responsibility mass
inside certified smaller-radius templates.  This is the finite analogue of a
guard-shadow transport theorem, and it is the object that facility, AQ,
range-reporting, or list/lattice proposal families should try to certify.

\begin{corollary}[Aggregate finite-signature co-load transport endpoint]
   \label{cor:aggregate-finite-signature-coload-transport-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-coload-transport-endpoint}.  Suppose a residual
   satisfying \((HCS1)\) admits responsibilities with
   \(W_{\rm resp}\ge B_{\mathcal X}/C_{\rm tr}\).  Form the full dyadic
   responsibility panel of
   \cref{cor:aggregate-finite-signature-responsibility-panel}, and let
   \(\mathsf P_{\rm resp}\) be its aggregate certified price \((FRA4)\).  If
   \[
      \mathsf P_{\rm resp}<\frac{B_{\mathcal X}}{2C_{\rm tr}},
      \tag{FTA1}
   \]
   then the residual has a separating finite-signature star panel, and the
   polylogarithmic ANN endpoint follows.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The transported responsibility mass and \((FTA1)\) give
   \[
      \frac12W_{\rm resp}
      \ge
      \frac{B_{\mathcal X}}{2C_{\rm tr}}
      >
      \mathsf P_{\rm resp}.
   \]
   Thus \((FRA5)\) holds, and
   \cref{cor:aggregate-finite-signature-responsibility-panel} exposes a positive
   structured prefix column.  The endpoint follows from
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-star-panel-coload-endpoint}.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:aggregate-finite-signature-coload-transport-endpoint} is the
polylog-friendly version of \cref{cor:finite-signature-coload-transport-endpoint}:
the proof pays the actual aggregate Renyi price of the reported responsibility
layers rather than losing a factor for the number of proposed centers.

\begin{lemma}[Finite-signature co-load Hall transport]
   \label{lem:finite-signature-coload-hall-transport}
   Work in the setting of
