   \cref{cor:finite-signature-coload-transport-endpoint}, and fix a finite
   template set \(\mathcal X\) and a loss \(C_{\rm tr}\ge1\).  Let the left
   nodes be
   \[
      \mathcal L=
      \{(\sigma_0,x):\sigma_0\in\Sigma,\ x\in\mathcal X,\ g_{\sigma_0,x}>0\}
   \]
   with scaled load
   \[
      b_{\sigma_0,x}=\frac{\tau_{\sigma_0}g_{\sigma_0,x}}{C_{\rm tr}},
      \tag{FHT1}
   \]
   and let the right nodes be
   \[
      \mathcal R=\{(p,\sigma_0):p\in W_{\sigma_0}\}
   \]
   with capacity \(c_{p,\sigma_0}=\alpha_{p,\sigma_0}\).  Join
   \((\sigma_0,x)\in\mathcal L\) to \((p,\sigma_0)\in\mathcal R\) when
   \(p\in W_x\) and \(a_x(\sigma_0)=1\).  A packed co-load shipment means a
   nonnegative flow that sends all scaled left load to the right nodes subject
   to the capacities \(c_{p,\sigma_0}\).  Such a shipment exists if and only if
   the Hall inequalities
   \[
      \sum_{(\sigma_0,x)\in A}
      \frac{\tau_{\sigma_0}g_{\sigma_0,x}}{C_{\rm tr}}
      \le
      \sum_{(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}\alpha_{p,\sigma_0}
      \qquad(A\subseteq\mathcal L),
      \tag{FHT3}
   \]
   hold, where \(N(A)\) is the neighborhood of \(A\) in \(\mathcal R\).

   Whenever \((FHT3)\) holds, it produces responsibilities satisfying
   \[
      W_{\rm resp}\ge B_{\mathcal X}/C_{\rm tr},
      \tag{FHT2}
   \]
   More precisely, these responsibilities are supported on the displayed
   edges with
   \[
      W_{\rm resp}=
      \frac1{C_{\rm tr}}
      \sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}g_{\sigma_0,x}
      =
      \frac{B_{\mathcal X}}{C_{\rm tr}}.
      \tag{FHT4}
   \]
   If \((FHT3)\) fails, then there is a finite Hall cut \(A\subseteq\mathcal L\)
   satisfying
   \[
      \sum_{(\sigma_0,x)\in A}\tau_{\sigma_0}g_{\sigma_0,x}
      >
      C_{\rm tr}
      \sum_{(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}\alpha_{p,\sigma_0}.
      \tag{FHT5}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Build the bipartite flow network with source edges of capacities
   \(b_{\sigma_0,x}\), infinite middle edges on the displayed adjacency relation,
   and sink edges of capacities \(\alpha_{p,\sigma_0}\).  By the max-flow
   min-cut theorem, all left scaled load can be shipped if and only if every
   subset \(A\subseteq\mathcal L\) has load at most the capacity of its
   neighborhood.  This is exactly \((FHT3)\).

   Given such a flow \(f_{\sigma_0,x,p}\), define
   \[
      \eta_{x,p,\sigma_0}
      =
      \begin{cases}
      f_{\sigma_0,x,p}/\alpha_{p,\sigma_0},
         & \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}>0,\\
      0, & \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}=0.
      \end{cases}
   \]
   The sink-capacity constraints give \(0\le\eta_{x,p,\sigma_0}\le1\), and the
   edge relation gives the support conditions in
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-responsibility-star-endpoint}.  Moreover
   \(a_x(\sigma_0)=1\) on every used edge, so the total responsibility mass is
   \[
      \sum_{x,p,\sigma_0}
      \eta_{x,p,\sigma_0}\alpha_{p,\sigma_0}a_x(\sigma_0)
      =
      \sum_{\sigma_0,x,p}f_{\sigma_0,x,p}
      =
      \sum_{\sigma_0,x}b_{\sigma_0,x},
   \]
   which is \((FHT4)\).  Conversely, any responsibilities with the stronger
   per-paid-atom packing condition
   \[
      \sum_x\eta_{x,p,\sigma_0}\le1
      \qquad(p,\sigma_0)\in\mathcal R
   \]
   define such a flow by
   \(f_{\sigma_0,x,p}=\eta_{x,p,\sigma_0}\alpha_{p,\sigma_0}\).  Thus
   \((FHT3)\) is the exact condition for the packed transport version, and it is
   a sufficient condition for the responsibility endpoint.  The failed-cut
   statement \((FHT5)\) is simply the negation of \((FHT3)\) after multiplying by
   \(C_{\rm tr}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite-signature Hall transport endpoint]
   \label{cor:finite-signature-hall-transport-endpoint}
   In \cref{cor:finite-signature-coload-transport-endpoint}, replace the
   assumed responsibilities \((FCT3)\) by the Hall inequalities \((FHT3)\) for
   the same \(\mathcal X\) and \(C_{\rm tr}\).  If the dynamic-range and price
   hypotheses \((FCT4)\)--\((FCT5)\) also hold for the induced responsibilities,
   then the residual has a separating finite-signature star panel, and the
   polylogarithmic ANN endpoint follows.  Alternatively, if the induced
   dyadic responsibility panel satisfies the aggregate price condition
   \((FTA1)\), the same endpoint follows without the one-record
   \( |\mathcal X| \)-loss.

   Equivalently, the only way this Hall-transport route can fail is through a
   cut \(A\subseteq\mathcal L\) satisfying \((FHT5)\).  Thus the remaining
   geometric theorem may be stated as ruling out these finite Hall cuts, or
   adding a richer certified template family that makes all of them feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{lem:finite-signature-coload-hall-transport}, \((FHT3)\) produces
   responsibilities with \(W_{\rm resp}=B_{\mathcal X}/C_{\rm tr}\).  Under
   \((FCT4)\)--\((FCT5)\), the one-record transport endpoint
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-coload-transport-endpoint} gives the separating
   star panel and endpoint.  Under \((FTA1)\), the aggregate endpoint
   \cref{cor:aggregate-finite-signature-coload-transport-endpoint} gives the
   same conclusion.  The failed-cut statement is \((FHT5)\).
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-transport-endpoint} is a sharper target than a
bare responsibility conjecture.  It gives the exact obstruction to responsibility
construction: a set of high-correlation co-load atoms whose paid neighborhood in
the proposed smaller-radius templates is too small by a factor \(C_{\rm tr}\).
This is the finite place where the next geometric argument has to operate.

\begin{lemma}[Maximal Hall-cut marginal normal form]
   \label{lem:maximal-hall-cut-marginal-normal-form}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{lem:finite-signature-coload-hall-transport}.  For
   \(A\subseteq\mathcal L\), write
   \[
      \ell(A)=\sum_{(\sigma_0,x)\in A}\tau_{\sigma_0}g_{\sigma_0,x},
      \qquad
      c(A)=\sum_{(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}\alpha_{p,\sigma_0},
      \tag{MHC1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \Phi(A)=\ell(A)-C_{\rm tr}c(A).
      \tag{MHC2}
   \]
   If the Hall inequalities fail, then there is a cut
   \(A^\star\subseteq\mathcal L\) with \(\Phi(A^\star)>0\) such that
   \(A^\star\) maximizes \(\Phi\), and, among maximizers, is inclusion-maximal.
   This cut satisfies the marginal closure condition
   \[
      \ell(B)
      \le
      C_{\rm tr}
      \sum_{(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A^\star\cup B)\setminus N(A^\star)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}
      \qquad(B\subseteq\mathcal L\setminus A^\star).
      \tag{MHC3}
   \]
   The inequality is strict for every nonempty \(B\) whose addition would
   strictly enlarge \(A^\star\).

   Equivalently, after passing to \(A^\star\), no remaining left co-load family
   has positive Hall surplus against only the new paid shadow it would add.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Since the Hall inequalities fail, some cut has \(\Phi(A)>0\).  The left
   universe is finite, so choose a maximizer \(A^\star\), inclusion-maximal
   among all maximizers.  For \(B\subseteq\mathcal L\setminus A^\star\),
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \Phi(A^\star\cup B)-\Phi(A^\star)
      &=
      \ell(B)
      -
      C_{\rm tr}
      \sum_{(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A^\star\cup B)\setminus N(A^\star)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}.
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   Maximality of \(\Phi(A^\star)\) gives \((MHC3)\).  If equality held for a
   nonempty \(B\) that enlarges the cut, then \(A^\star\cup B\) would be a
   strictly larger maximizer, contradicting the chosen inclusion maximality.
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:maximal-hall-cut-marginal-normal-form} is a useful hygiene step for
the failed-cut branch.  A geometric repair theorem may assume the exposed cut
has already absorbed every left atom whose co-load is cheap relative to its new
paid shadow.  What remains is not another Hall-transport failure of the same
kind; it is the cut-local shadow \(N(A^\star)\), which must be compressed into
one or more lower-price dense templates.

\begin{corollary}[Finite-signature Hall-cut repair endpoint]
   \label{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-coload-separator-endpoint}.  Suppose that every
   residual satisfying \((HCS1)\) has an uncharged repair routine with the
   following certified output.  The routine may first choose a finite template
   set \(\mathcal X\) and a loss \(C_{\rm tr}\), run the Hall transport test of
   \cref{lem:finite-signature-coload-hall-transport}, and use any failed Hall
   cut only as build-time advice.  It must certify one of the following two
   alternatives.

   First, the Hall transport succeeds and the induced aggregate responsibility
   panel is affordable:
   \[
      \text{\((FHT3)\) holds and the induced dyadic panel satisfies \((FTA1)\).}
      \tag{HCR1}
   \]
   Second, the Hall test exposes a cut \(A\subseteq\mathcal L\) satisfying
   \((FHT5)\), and the routine returns a finite star panel
   \((x_i,U_i,X_i,K_i,\lambda_i)_{i\in I}\) satisfying the one-sided
   certificates \((FSP3)\) and the positive aggregate surplus
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_iX_i
      >
      \sum_i\lambda_i\psi_{x_i}
      \left(
         A_{x_i}K_i^{\rho_{x_i}}
         +\zeta K_i^{1+\rho_{x_i}}
      \right).
      \tag{HCR2}
   \]
   Then the structured completeness condition \((HCS2)\) holds for every
   high-correlation co-load residual.  Consequently the dense/spherical
   separator condition \((DSF2)\) holds, and the polylogarithmic ANN endpoint
   follows.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a surplus dual satisfying the co-load residual \((HCS1)\).  If
   \((HCR1)\) holds, then
   \cref{cor:aggregate-finite-signature-coload-transport-endpoint} gives a
   separating finite-signature star panel.  If \((HCR2)\) holds, the displayed
   inequality is exactly the separating-panel condition \((FSP4)\), so
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-star-panel-coload-endpoint} again exposes a
   positive structured prefix column.  In both cases \((HCS2)\) is satisfied for
   the current residual.  Since the residual was arbitrary,
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-coload-separator-endpoint} gives the
   dense/spherical separator endpoint.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint} is the fully fractional
dense-overlap interface at the present bottleneck.  A failed Hall cut is not a
retained branch and carries no query or storage charge; it is only a dual
diagnostic that may guide an expensive build-time search.  The proof accepts the
repair only when it becomes an ordinary fractional star panel whose certified
lower paid mass beats its aggregate recursive query and storage price.

\begin{corollary}[Finite-signature Hall-shadow repair]
   \label{cor:finite-signature-hall-shadow-repair}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint}.  Suppose the repair
   routine uses a failed Hall cut \(A\subseteq\mathcal L\) only through its paid
   shadow \(N(A)\).  For a candidate repair template \(y\), define the cut-shadow
   degree
   \[
      d_{A,y}(p)
      =
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}a_y(\sigma_0).
      \tag{HSR1}
   \]
   Assume that whenever \((HCR1)\) is not certified, the routine returns a
   finite panel \((y_i,U_i,X_i,K_i,\lambda_i)_{i\in I}\) with
   \(U_i\subseteq W_{y_i}\), \(|U_i|\le K_i\), and
   \[
      0\le X_i\le \sum_{p\in U_i}d_{A,y_i}(p),
      \tag{HSR2}
   \]
   such that, with \(A_y\) defined as in \((FSP2)\),
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_iX_i
      >
      \sum_i\lambda_i\psi_{y_i}
      \left(
         A_{y_i}K_i^{\rho_{y_i}}
         +\zeta K_i^{1+\rho_{y_i}}
      \right).
      \tag{HSR3}
   \]
   Then the repair routine satisfies the Hall-cut repair alternative
   \((HCR2)\).  Consequently the polylogarithmic ANN endpoint follows under
   the hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(N(A)\subseteq\mathcal R\), every pair
   \((p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)\) has \(p\in W_{\sigma_0}\).  Therefore, for every
   template \(y\),
   \[
      d_{A,y}(p)
      \le
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,p\in W_{\sigma_0}}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}a_y(\sigma_0)
      =
      d_y(p),
   \]
   where \(d_y\) is the paid degree from \((FSP2)\).  Thus \((HSR2)\) implies
   the one-sided certificate \((FSP3)\) for each record.  The aggregate
   inequality \((HSR3)\) is the separating-panel inequality \((FSP4)\).  Hence
   \((HCR2)\) holds, and the endpoint is
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint}.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-shadow-repair} is the cut-local version of the
merge operation.  A failed Hall cut identifies exactly which paid
signature--witness atoms are relevant.  The geometric search does not need to
repair unrelated demand; it only has to find affordable smaller-radius
templates whose prefixes capture enough of the cut-shadow degree \((HSR1)\).

\begin{corollary}[One-record Hall-shadow merge]
   \label{cor:one-record-hall-shadow-merge}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-shadow-repair}.  Suppose that whenever
   \((HCR1)\) is not certified, the failed Hall cut \(A\) admits one repair
   template \(y\), one set \(U\subseteq W_y\), and one size certificate
   \(K\ge |U|\) such that, with
   \[
      X_A(U)=\sum_{p\in U}d_{A,y}(p),
      \tag{OHM1}
   \]
   one has
   \[
      X_A(U)
      >
      \psi_y
      \left(
         A_yK^{\rho_y}
         +\zeta K^{1+\rho_y}
      \right).
      \tag{OHM2}
   \]
   Then the Hall-shadow repair criterion holds with a one-record panel.

   In particular, for a fixed repair template \(y\) and cardinality \(K\), it is
   enough to test the top \(K\) points of \(W_y\) by the score \(d_{A,y}(p)\).
   If any subset of size at most \(K\) satisfies \((OHM2)\), the top-\(K\)
   prefix satisfies it as well.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The first statement is \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-shadow-repair} with a
   single panel record, \(\lambda=1\), and \(X=X_A(U)\).  For the prefix
   statement, the top \(K\) points by \(d_{A,y}(p)\) maximize
   \(\sum_{p\in U'}d_{A,y}(p)\) among all \(U'\subseteq W_y\) with
   \(|U'|\le K\).  Replacing \(U\) by that prefix can only increase the left
   side of \((OHM2)\), while the certified price with cardinality \(K\) is
   unchanged.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:one-record-hall-shadow-merge} is the deterministic version of the
template-enrichment target.  If packed transport fails, a successful enrichment
does not have to solve a new LP: one coarser or alternative template whose
cut-shadow top prefix beats its Renyi query and storage price is enough.  Thus
the remaining geometric theorem can be stated as a weighted range-reporting,
list-decoding, additive-quantization, or seeded-template guarantee for the
degree function \(d_{A,y}\) exposed by the failed Hall cut.

\begin{corollary}[Proposal-law Hall-shadow merge]
   \label{cor:proposal-law-hall-shadow-merge}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:one-record-hall-shadow-merge}.  Suppose
   that whenever \((HCR1)\) is not certified for a failed Hall cut \(A\),
   uncharged preprocessing supplies a finite seed law \(s\sim\nu\).  A seed
   declares a repair template \(y_s\) and a size certificate \(K_s\ge1\).  Let
   \(P_s\) be the top \(K_s\) points of \(W_{y_s}\) by the cut-shadow degree
   \(d_{A,y_s}(p)\), or all of \(W_{y_s}\) if \(|W_{y_s}|<K_s\), and define
   \[
      X(s)=\sum_{p\in P_s}d_{A,y_s}(p),
      \tag{PHM1}
   \]
   \[
      R(s)=
      \psi_{y_s}
      \left(
         A_{y_s}K_s^{\rho_{y_s}}
         +\zeta K_s^{1+\rho_{y_s}}
      \right),
      \qquad
      Z(s)=X(s)-R(s),
      \tag{PHM2}
   \]
   with \(A_y\) defined as in \((FSP2)\).  If
   \[
      \E_{s\sim\nu} Z(s)>0,
      \tag{PHM3}
   \]
   then some deterministic seed satisfies the one-record Hall-shadow merge
   condition \((OHM2)\), and the Hall-shadow repair criterion holds.

   More quantitatively, if
   \[
      \E_s Z(s)\ge \Gamma>0,
      \qquad
      Z(s)_+\le M
      \quad\text{almost surely},
      \tag{PHM4}
   \]
   then \(B\) independent build-time samples contain a valid one-record merge
   with probability at least
   \[
      1-\exp\left(-\frac{B\Gamma}{M}\right).
      \tag{PHM5}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((PHM3)\) holds, at least one seed has \(Z(s)>0\).  For that seed,
   \(P_s\subseteq W_{y_s}\), \(|P_s|\le K_s\), and \(X(s)>R(s)\), which is
   exactly \((OHM2)\) with \(U=P_s\), \(K=K_s\), and \(y=y_s\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:one-record-hall-shadow-merge} applies.

   For the sampled statement, \((PHM4)\) implies
   \[
      \E Z_+\ge\Gamma .
   \]
   Since \(Z_+\le M\), a seed has \(Z(s)>0\) with probability at least
   \(\Gamma/M\).  Therefore \(B\) independent seeds all fail with probability
   at most \((1-\Gamma/M)^B\le\exp(-B\Gamma/M)\).  A successful sampled seed is
   then verified by the deterministic one-record test above; failed seeds are
   discarded and never enter the retained filter cover.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:proposal-law-hall-shadow-merge} is the build-time-heavy version of the
same target.  A \(k\)-means++ seed, additive-quantization code, range-reporting
cell, or list-decoder output only has to generate positive expected
Hall-shadow prefix surplus against the current cut.  The retained index still
keeps only the verified top-prefix dense column.

\begin{corollary}[No-merge Hall-shadow envelope]
   \label{cor:no-merge-hall-shadow-envelope}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:one-record-hall-shadow-merge}.  Fix a failed
   Hall cut \(A\), and let \(\mathcal Y\) be a finite repair-template family.
   For each \(y\in\mathcal Y\), let
   \(\mathcal K_y\subseteq\{1,\ldots,|W_y|\}\) be the available prefix
   cardinalities.  Order \(W_y=\{p_{y,1},p_{y,2},\ldots\}\) by decreasing
   cut-shadow degree \(d_{A,y}(p)\), and put
   \[
      D_A(y,K)=\sum_{i\le K}d_{A,y}(p_{y,i})
      \qquad(K\in\mathcal K_y).
      \tag{NHE1}
   \]
   Then either some available pair \((y,K)\) satisfies
   \[
      D_A(y,K)>
      \psi_y
      \left(
         A_yK^{\rho_y}
         +\zeta K^{1+\rho_y}
      \right),
      \tag{NHE2}
   \]
   and hence gives a one-record Hall-shadow merge, or the failed cut obeys the
   top-prefix envelope
   \[
      D_A(y,K)\le
      \psi_y
      \left(
         A_yK^{\rho_y}
         +\zeta K^{1+\rho_y}
      \right)
      \qquad(y\in\mathcal Y,\ K\in\mathcal K_y).
      \tag{NHE3}
   \]

   Assume moreover that \(0<\rho_y<1\), and that \(\mathcal K_y\) is
   \(b\)-dense from below: every \(1\le h\le |W_y|\) has
   \(K\in\mathcal K_y\) with \(h/b\le K\le h\).  If the no-merge envelope
   \((NHE3)\) holds, then every nonempty cut-shadow superlevel
   \[
      H_{A,y,\delta}=\{p\in W_y:d_{A,y}(p)\ge\delta\},
      \qquad h=|H_{A,y,\delta}|,
      \tag{NHE4}
   \]
   satisfies
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      \psi_y\left(
         b^{1-\rho_y}A_yh^{\rho_y-1}
         +\zeta h^{\rho_y}
      \right).
      \tag{NHE5}
   \]
   Thus, when \(\zeta=0\),
   \[
      h
      \le
      \left(
         \frac{\psi_y b^{1-\rho_y}A_y}{\delta}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho_y)}.
      \tag{NHE6}
   \]
   When \(\zeta>0\), every such superlevel satisfies at least one of
   \[
      h
      \le
      \left(
         \frac{2\psi_y b^{1-\rho_y}A_y}{\delta}
      \right)^{1/(1-\rho_y)}
      \tag{NHE7}
   \]
   or
   \[
      h
      \ge
      \left(
         \frac{\delta}{2\psi_y\zeta}
      \right)^{1/\rho_y}.
      \tag{NHE8}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The alternatives \((NHE2)\)--\((NHE3)\) are complementary.  If \((NHE2)\)
   holds, then \cref{cor:one-record-hall-shadow-merge} applies with
   \(U=\{p_{y,1},\ldots,p_{y,K}\}\).

   Assume \((NHE3)\).  For a nonempty superlevel \(H_{A,y,\delta}\), choose
   \(K\in\mathcal K_y\) with \(h/b\le K\le h\).  The top \(K\) points all have
   cut-shadow degree at least \(\delta\), so
   \[
      \delta K\le D_A(y,K).
   \]
   Combining this with \((NHE3)\) and dividing by \(K\) gives
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      \psi_y\left(A_yK^{\rho_y-1}+\zeta K^{\rho_y}\right).
   \]
   Since \(\rho_y-1<0\), \(K\ge h/b\) gives
   \(K^{\rho_y-1}\le b^{1-\rho_y}h^{\rho_y-1}\), while \(K\le h\) gives
   \(K^{\rho_y}\le h^{\rho_y}\).  This proves \((NHE5)\).

   If \(\zeta=0\), rearranging \((NHE5)\) gives \((NHE6)\).  If \(\zeta>0\),
   at least one term on the right of \((NHE5)\) is at least \(\delta/2\).  The
   query-price case gives \((NHE7)\), and the storage-price case gives
   \((NHE8)\).
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:no-merge-hall-shadow-envelope} is the exact residual left by the
finite Hall-shadow target.  If all available template prefixes fail, then every
shadow superlevel is either small because of query price or large because of
storage price.  A geometric theorem for the polylog endpoint can therefore be
phrased as ruling out \((NHE5)\)--\((NHE8)\) for the Hall cut exposed by
\((FHT5)\), or as using that envelope to generate a richer repair-template
family.

\begin{corollary}[Maximal no-prefix Hall-cut normal form]
   \label{cor:maximal-no-prefix-hall-cut-normal-form}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{lem:finite-signature-coload-hall-transport} and
   \cref{cor:no-merge-hall-shadow-envelope}.  Fix a finite repair-template
   family \(\mathcal Y\) and available cardinality nets
   \(\mathcal K_y\).  If the Hall inequalities \((FHT3)\) fail, then there is
   an inclusion-maximal surplus cut \(A^\star\subseteq\mathcal L\) such that
   \[
      \ell(A^\star)>C_{\rm tr}c(A^\star),
      \tag{MPH1}
   \]
   \[
      \ell(B)
      \le
      C_{\rm tr}
      \sum_{(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A^\star\cup B)\setminus N(A^\star)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}
      \qquad(B\subseteq\mathcal L\setminus A^\star),
      \tag{MPH2}
   \]
   and one of the following two alternatives holds.

   First, for some \(y\in\mathcal Y\) and \(K\in\mathcal K_y\), the
   top-\(K\) cut-shadow prefix for \(A^\star\) satisfies \((NHE2)\), and hence
   gives a one-record Hall-shadow merge.

   Second, every available prefix obeys
   \[
      D_{A^\star}(y,K)\le
      \psi_y
      \left(
         A_yK^{\rho_y}
         +\zeta K^{1+\rho_y}
      \right)
      \qquad(y\in\mathcal Y,\ K\in\mathcal K_y).
      \tag{MPH3}
   \]
   If, moreover, \(0<\rho_y<1\) and \(\mathcal K_y\) is \(b\)-dense from below
   for every \(y\), then every cut-shadow superlevel
   \(H_{A^\star,y,\delta}\) satisfies the weak-type bounds
   \((NHE5)\)--\((NHE8)\).

   Consequently, in any separator route whose successful Hall transports
   certify \((HCR1)\), the only remaining dense-side obstruction is a cut
   satisfying \((MPH1)\)--\((MPH3)\).  If a geometric theorem rules out that
   combined obstruction for every high-correlation co-load residual satisfying
   \((HCS1)\), then \((HCS2)\) holds and the polylogarithmic ANN endpoint
   follows.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \((FHT3)\) fails, choose the inclusion-maximal surplus cut
   \(A^\star\) supplied by
   \cref{lem:maximal-hall-cut-marginal-normal-form}.  The inequality
   \((MPH1)\) is the positivity of \(\Phi(A^\star)\), and \((MPH2)\) is
   exactly the marginal closure condition \((MHC3)\).

   Apply \cref{cor:no-merge-hall-shadow-envelope} to this cut.  If \((NHE2)\)
   holds for some available \((y,K)\), the first alternative holds.  Otherwise
   the no-merge envelope \((NHE3)\) holds for every available prefix, which is
   \((MPH3)\).  Under the additional density and exponent assumptions, the
   weak-type conclusions are precisely the remaining conclusions of
   \cref{cor:no-merge-hall-shadow-envelope}.

   For the endpoint statement, fix a residual satisfying \((HCS1)\).  If the
   Hall transport succeeds and certifies \((HCR1)\), the successful branch of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint} applies.  If transport
   fails and the combined obstruction \((MPH1)\)--\((MPH3)\) is impossible,
   the first alternative gives a one-record Hall-shadow merge, hence \((HCR2)\)
   by \cref{cor:one-record-hall-shadow-merge}.  Thus every residual satisfies
   one of the two repair alternatives, and
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-coload-separator-endpoint} gives the claimed
   endpoint.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Maximal Hall frontier expansion]
   \label{cor:maximal-hall-frontier-expansion}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:maximal-no-prefix-hall-cut-normal-form}, and let
   \(A^\star\) be an inclusion-maximal surplus cut satisfying
   \((MPH1)\)--\((MPH2)\).  For
   \(B\subseteq\mathcal L\setminus A^\star\), write its novel paid shadow as
   \[
      c_{A^\star}^+(B)
      =
      \sum_{(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A^\star\cup B)\setminus N(A^\star)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}.
      \tag{MFE1}
   \]
   Then every outside family obeys the frontier expansion bound
   \[
      \ell(B)\le C_{\rm tr}c_{A^\star}^+(B)
      \qquad(B\subseteq\mathcal L\setminus A^\star).
      \tag{MFE2}
   \]
   In particular, every outside atom \((\sigma_0,x)\in\mathcal L\setminus
   A^\star\) satisfies
   \[
      \tau_{\sigma_0}g_{\sigma_0,x}
      \le
      C_{\rm tr}
      \sum_{\substack{p\in W_x:\\(p,\sigma_0)\in\mathcal R\setminus N(A^\star)}}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}.
      \tag{MFE3}
   \]

   Consequently, a maximal no-prefix residual has two disjoint certificates.
   On the closed shadow \(N(A^\star)\), every retained repair prefix obeys the
   no-merge envelope \((MPH3)\).  Outside the cut, every remaining co-load
   family must pay for itself by exposing novel paid shadow through \((MFE2)\).
   Thus any build-time enrichment whose query side has positive co-load but
   whose paid neighborhood is already contained in \(N(A^\star)\) must either
   be represented inside the cut or contradict maximality.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The bound \((MFE2)\) is exactly \((MPH2)\), with the novel shadow abbreviated
   by \((MFE1)\).  Taking \(B=\{(\sigma_0,x)\}\) gives \((MFE3)\), because the
   new right neighbors of this singleton are precisely the existing right atoms
   \((p,\sigma_0)\in\mathcal R\) with \(p\in W_x\), \(a_x(\sigma_0)=1\), and
   \((p,\sigma_0)\notin N(A^\star)\).  Since
   \((\sigma_0,x)\in\mathcal L\) already implies that edges to right atoms use
   \(a_x(\sigma_0)=1\), the displayed sum may be written over \(p\in W_x\).

   The final paragraph is the contrapositive of \((MFE2)\): if an outside
   family had positive co-load and no novel paid shadow, or more generally
   co-load larger than \(C_{\rm tr}\) times its novel paid shadow, then adding
   it to \(A^\star\) would increase the Hall surplus \(\Phi\), contradicting
   the maximal choice of the cut.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Outside transport after a maximal Hall cut]
   \label{cor:maximal-cut-outside-transport}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:maximal-hall-frontier-expansion}.  Let
   \[
      \mathcal L^+=\mathcal L\setminus A^\star,
      \qquad
      \mathcal R^+=\mathcal R\setminus N(A^\star),
      \tag{MRT1}
   \]
   and keep only the original Hall-transport edges from \(\mathcal L^+\) to
   \(\mathcal R^+\).  Give each outside left atom load
   \[
      b_{\sigma_0,x}^+
      =
      \frac{\tau_{\sigma_0}g_{\sigma_0,x}}{C_{\rm tr}},
      \tag{MRT2}
   \]
   and each novel right atom \((p,\sigma_0)\in\mathcal R^+\) capacity
   \(\alpha_{p,\sigma_0}\).  Then the residual outside network has a packed
   shipment of all outside load:
   \[
      \sum_{(p,\sigma_0)\in\mathcal R^+}f_{\sigma_0,x,p}
      =
      b_{\sigma_0,x}^+
      \qquad((\sigma_0,x)\in\mathcal L^+),
      \tag{MRT3}
   \]
   with right capacities
   \[
      \sum_{x}f_{\sigma_0,x,p}\le\alpha_{p,\sigma_0}
      \qquad((p,\sigma_0)\in\mathcal R^+).
      \tag{MRT4}
   \]

   Thus, after a maximal failed Hall cut is exposed, the failure is localized:
   the outside co-load can already be transported to paid shadow disjoint from
   \(N(A^\star)\).  A dense repair routine only has to handle the closed shadow
   \(N(A^\star)\) and the co-load atoms in \(A^\star\); the remaining atoms can
   be packed by \((MRT3)\)--\((MRT4)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For a subset \(B\subseteq\mathcal L^+\), its neighborhood in the residual
   outside network is exactly
   \(N(A^\star\cup B)\setminus N(A^\star)\).  Therefore the Hall inequalities
   for shipping the scaled loads \((MRT2)\) to capacities on \(\mathcal R^+\)
   are
   \[
      \sum_{(\sigma_0,x)\in B}
      \frac{\tau_{\sigma_0}g_{\sigma_0,x}}{C_{\rm tr}}
      \le
      \sum_{(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A^\star\cup B)\setminus N(A^\star)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0},
   \]
   for every \(B\subseteq\mathcal L^+\).  These are exactly \((MFE2)\) divided
   by \(C_{\rm tr}\).  The finite max-flow min-cut theorem gives the packed
   shipment \((MRT3)\)--\((MRT4)\).  The final statement is just this shipment
   interpreted as a decomposition of the failed transport into the closed cut
   and the already routable outside frontier.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Hall-shadow prefixes are finite-prefix separation]
   \label{cor:hall-shadow-finite-prefix-separation}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:one-record-hall-shadow-merge}.  Fix a
   failed Hall cut \(A\).  Form the cut-shadow demand system
   \[
      \mathcal N_A=N(A)\subseteq P\times\Sigma,
      \qquad
      \gamma_{p,\sigma_0}=\alpha_{p,\sigma_0},
      \qquad
      \sigma_{\rm st}=\zeta .
      \tag{HFP1}
   \]
   For a repair template \(y\), let its associated Boolean query layer be
   \[
      Q_y=\{\sigma_0:a_y(\sigma_0)=1\},
      \qquad
      A_y=\sum_{\sigma_0\in Q_y}\tau_{\sigma_0}.
      \tag{HFP2}
   \]
   Then for every available cardinality \(K\in\mathcal K_y\), the Hall-shadow
   top-prefix value is exactly the finite-prefix reduced-cost value of the
   container/query-layer/cardinality triple \((W_y,Q_y,K)\):
   \[
      D_A(y,K)
      -
      \psi_y
      \left(
         A_yK^{\rho_y}+\zeta K^{1+\rho_y}
      \right)
      =
      D_{W_y,\mathbf 1_{Q_y}}^\gamma(K)
      -
      \psi_y
      \left(
         K^{\rho_y}\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}\mathbf 1_{Q_y}(\sigma_0)
         +
         \sigma_{\rm st}K^{1+\rho_y}
      \right).
      \tag{HFP3}
   \]
   Hence a positive finite-prefix reduced cost for one such triple is precisely
   a one-record Hall-shadow merge, while failure of all such triples is
   precisely the restricted finite-prefix residual envelope on
   \(\mathcal N_A\).

   More generally, suppose a build-time oracle proposes any certified
   container \(W\), Boolean signature layer \(Q\subseteq\Sigma\), cardinality
   \(K\), and prices \((\psi,\rho)\) with
   \[
      D_{W,\mathbf 1_Q}^\gamma(K)
      >
      \psi
      \left(
         K^\rho\sum_{\sigma_0\in Q}\tau_{\sigma_0}
         +
         \zeta K^{1+\rho}
      \right).
      \tag{HFP4}
   \]
   If this triple is certified as a valid smaller-radius repair template with
   activation \(a(\sigma_0)=\mathbf 1_Q(\sigma_0)\), then it gives the
   Hall-cut repair alternative \((HCR2)\).  Consequently, any finite-prefix
   separator for the cut-shadow demand systems \(\mathcal N_A\), with
   \(r\equiv1\), can be used as the dense repair routine in
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For \(p\in W_y\), the paid degree in the cut-shadow demand system under the
   query layer \(Q_y\) is
   \[
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,(p,\sigma_0)\in\mathcal N_A}
      \gamma_{p,\sigma_0}\mathbf 1_{Q_y}(\sigma_0)
      =
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}a_y(\sigma_0)
      =
      d_{A,y}(p).
   \]
   Sorting \(W_y\) by this degree therefore gives the same top-\(K\) prefix and
   the same prefix mass \(D_A(y,K)\) on both sides of \((HFP3)\).  The query
   price identity is the definition of \(A_y\), and the storage price is
   \(\sigma_{\rm st}K^{1+\rho_y}=\zeta K^{1+\rho_y}\).  This proves
   \((HFP3)\).

   If the common value in \((HFP3)\) is positive, then \((NHE2)\) holds for
   \((y,K)\), and \cref{cor:one-record-hall-shadow-merge} gives the
   one-record repair.  If all such values are nonpositive, the displayed
   inequality is exactly \((NHE3)\), rewritten as the finite-prefix residual
   envelope restricted to the query layers \(Q_y\).

   Finally, a proposed certified triple satisfying \((HFP4)\) may be regarded
   as a new repair template with container \(W\), activation \(\mathbf 1_Q\),
   exponent \(\rho\), and price factor \(\psi\).  The first part then gives
   \((NHE2)\) for that new template, hence a one-record Hall-shadow merge and
   the Hall-cut repair alternative \((HCR2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Closed-shadow query-layer relaxation is tight]
   \label{cor:closed-shadow-query-layer-relaxation}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:hall-shadow-finite-prefix-separation}.  Let \(\mathcal P\) be a
   finite pool of certified closed-shadow prefix templates.  A template
   \(C\in\mathcal P\) consists of a certified container \(W_C\), an available
   cardinality \(K_C\), prices \((\psi_C,\rho_C)\), and a finite set
   \(\mathcal Q_C\) of certified Boolean signature layers
   \(Q\subseteq\Sigma\).  For every \(Q\in\mathcal Q_C\), the triple
   \((W_C,Q,K_C)\) is a valid smaller-radius repair template with activation
   \(a(\sigma_0)=\mathbf 1_Q(\sigma_0)\).

   For \(0\le y_\sigma\le1\), define \(D_{C,y}^\gamma(K_C)\) as the top
   \(K_C\) sum inside \(W_C\) for the degree
   \[
      p\mapsto
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}y_{\sigma_0}.
      \tag{QLR1}
   \]
   Suppose \(y\) lies in the convex hull of the layer indicators
   \(\{\mathbf 1_Q:Q\in\mathcal Q_C\}\).  If
   \[
      D_{C,y}^\gamma(K_C)
      >
      \psi_C
      \left(
         K_C^{\rho_C}\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}y_{\sigma_0}
         +
         \zeta K_C^{1+\rho_C}
      \right),
      \tag{QLR2}
   \]
   then some certified Boolean layer \(Q\in\mathcal Q_C\) satisfies the
   closed-shadow finite-prefix inequality \((HFP4)\), and hence gives the
   Hall-cut repair alternative \((HCR2)\).

   Consequently, if no template in \(\mathcal P\) gives a Hall-shadow repair,
   then every \(C\in\mathcal P\) and every
   \(y\in\operatorname{conv}\{\mathbf 1_Q:Q\in\mathcal Q_C\}\) obey the reverse
   inequality in \((QLR2)\).  In particular, if \(\mathcal Q_C\) contains all
   Boolean signature layers, the surviving residual satisfies this envelope for
   every \(y\in[0,1]^\Sigma\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For fixed \(C\), define
   \[
      F_C(y)=
      D_{C,y}^\gamma(K_C)
      -
      \psi_CK_C^{\rho_C}\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}y_{\sigma_0}
      -
      \psi_C\zeta K_C^{1+\rho_C}.
      \tag{QLR3}
   \]
   The prefix functional is
   \[
      D_{C,y}^\gamma(K_C)
      =
      \max_{\substack{U\subseteq W_C\\ |U|\le K_C}}
      \sum_{p\in U}
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}y_{\sigma_0},
   \]
   a maximum of linear functions of \(y\).  Hence \(F_C\) is convex on the
   convex hull of the certified layer indicators.  If \((QLR2)\) holds, then
   \(F_C(y)>0\), so the maximum of \(F_C\) over that finite polytope is
   positive and is attained at an extreme point.  Every extreme point is one of
   the certified layer indicators \(\mathbf 1_Q\).  For that \(Q\),
   \(F_C(\mathbf 1_Q)>0\) is exactly \((HFP4)\) for the certified repair
   template \((W_C,Q,K_C)\).  Therefore
   \cref{cor:hall-shadow-finite-prefix-separation} gives \((HCR2)\).

   The residual envelope is the contrapositive.  If all Boolean signature
   layers are certified, their convex hull is the full cube \([0,1]^\Sigma\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Closed-shadow soft proposals harden to prefixes]
   \label{cor:closed-shadow-soft-proposal-hardening}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:closed-shadow-query-layer-relaxation}.  Fix a certified closed
   shadow template \(C\), a fractional signature layer
   \(y\in\operatorname{conv}\{\mathbf 1_Q:Q\in\mathcal Q_C\}\), and fractional
   update memberships \(0\le\theta_p\le1\) on \(W_C\).  Put
   \[
      \mu=\sum_{p\in W_C}\theta_p,\qquad
      X\le
      \sum_{p\in W_C}\theta_p
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}y_{\sigma_0}.
      \tag{CSF1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      K_C\,\frac{X}{\max\{\mu,K_C\}}
      >
      \psi_C
      \left(
         K_C^{\rho_C}\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}y_{\sigma_0}
         +
         \zeta K_C^{1+\rho_C}
      \right),
      \tag{CSF2}
   \]
   then some certified Boolean layer \(Q\in\mathcal Q_C\) and the top
   \(K_C\)-prefix of \(W_C\) for that layer satisfy the Hall-shadow
   finite-prefix inequality \((HFP4)\).  Consequently the Hall-cut repair
   alternative \((HCR2)\) holds.

   Thus a closed-shadow proposal oracle may return only soft point memberships,
   a fractional signature layer, and a one-sided lower mass \(X\).  The verifier
   hardens any positive certificate to an ordinary Boolean query layer and
   top-degree update prefix before retaining a column.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Order \(W_C=\{p_1,p_2,\ldots\}\) by decreasing degree for the fractional
   signature layer \(y\), and let
   \(D_K=D_{C,y}^{\gamma}(K_C)=\sum_{i\le K_C}d_y(p_i)\).  The rearrangement
   inequality used in
   \cref{cor:soft-mass-clipped-hall-shadow-reporter} gives
   \[
      \frac{D_K}{K_C}\ge\frac{X}{\max\{\mu,K_C\}}.
      \tag{CSF3}
   \]
   Indeed, if \(\mu\le K_C\), the largest possible \(\theta\)-weighted degree
   mass of total weight \(\mu\) is bounded by the top \(K_C\) mass.  If
   \(\mu>K_C\), the average degree over the best fractional prefix of mass
   \(\mu\) is at most the average of the top \(K_C\) degrees.

   Combining \((CSF2)\) and \((CSF3)\) gives the fractional query-layer
   inequality \((QLR2)\) for the same \(C\) and \(y\).  Then
   \cref{cor:closed-shadow-query-layer-relaxation} produces a certified Boolean
   layer \(Q\) satisfying \((HFP4)\), and
   \cref{cor:hall-shadow-finite-prefix-separation} gives \((HCR2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Closed-shadow soft-proposal separator endpoint]
   \label{cor:closed-shadow-soft-proposal-separator-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint}.  Suppose that every
   high-correlation co-load residual satisfying \((HCS1)\) admits an uncharged
   closed-shadow soft-proposal separator with the following certified behavior.
   The separator chooses a finite template set \(\mathcal X\) and a loss
   \(C_{\rm tr}\), runs the Hall transport test of
   \cref{lem:finite-signature-coload-hall-transport}, and certifies one of two
   alternatives.

   First, the Hall-success alternative \((HCR1)\) holds.  Second, the Hall test
   fails, the separator replaces the failed cut by an inclusion-maximal surplus
   cut \(A^\star\) satisfying \((MPH1)\)--\((MPH2)\), and it returns one
   certified closed-shadow soft proposal for \(N(A^\star)\): a template \(C\),
   a fractional signature layer \(y\in\operatorname{conv}
   \{\mathbf 1_Q:Q\in\mathcal Q_C\}\), memberships \(0\le\theta_p\le1\), and a
   lower mass \(X\) satisfying \((CSF1)\) and the positive surplus inequality
   \[
      K_C\,\frac{X}{\max\{\mu,K_C\}}
      >
      \psi_C
      \left(
         K_C^{\rho_C}\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}y_{\sigma_0}
         +
         \zeta K_C^{1+\rho_C}
      \right).
      \tag{CSS1}
   \]
   Then the structured completeness condition \((HCS2)\) holds for every
   high-correlation co-load residual.  Consequently the dense/spherical
   separator condition \((DSF2)\) holds, and the polylogarithmic ANN endpoint
   follows.

   The same conclusion holds in Las Vegas build time if, in the second
   alternative, a randomized proposal routine returns certified soft proposals
   with surplus
   \[
      Z(s)=
      K_{C_s}\frac{X_s}{\max\{\mu_s,K_{C_s}\}}
      -
      \psi_{C_s}
      \left(
         K_{C_s}^{\rho_{C_s}}\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}y_s(\sigma_0)
         +
         \zeta K_{C_s}^{1+\rho_{C_s}}
      \right)
      \tag{CSS2}
   \]
   satisfying
   \[
      \E_sZ(s)\ge\Gamma>0,
      \qquad
      Z(s)_+\le M
      \quad\text{almost surely}.
      \tag{CSS3}
   \]
   Repeating
   \[
      B\ge \frac{M}{\Gamma}\log\frac1\delta
      \tag{CSS4}
   \]
   independent build-time seeds finds a deterministic Hall-shadow repair with
   probability at least \(1-\delta\); failed samples are discarded.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a surplus dual satisfying \((HCS1)\).  If \((HCR1)\) holds, then the
   first alternative of \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint}
   applies.  Otherwise the returned proposal satisfies \((CSF1)\) and
   \((CSF2)\), with \((CSS1)\) being exactly \((CSF2)\) for the closed cut
   \(A^\star\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:closed-shadow-soft-proposal-hardening} gives the Hall-cut repair
   alternative \((HCR2)\).  Therefore every residual satisfies one of the two
   alternatives of \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint}, giving
   \((HCS2)\), and
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-coload-separator-endpoint} gives the
   dense/spherical separator endpoint.

   For the sampled version, \((CSS3)\) implies
   \(\Pr_s[Z(s)>0]\ge\Gamma/M\).  Thus \(B\) independent failed samples have
   probability at most \(\exp(-B\Gamma/M)\).  A sample with \(Z(s)>0\) satisfies
   the deterministic second alternative, and failed samples are not retained.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Closed-shadow soft-proposal residual envelope]
   \label{cor:closed-shadow-soft-proposal-residual-envelope}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:closed-shadow-soft-proposal-separator-endpoint}, after a
   high-correlation residual satisfying \((HCS1)\) has failed Hall transport and
   has been localized to an inclusion-maximal surplus cut \(A^\star\) satisfying
   \((MPH1)\)--\((MPH2)\).  Let \(\mathcal P\) be any finite universe of
   certified closed-shadow proposal templates for \(N(A^\star)\).  For each
   \(C\in\mathcal P\), keep the data of
   \cref{cor:closed-shadow-query-layer-relaxation}: a container \(W_C\), an
   available cardinality \(K_C\), prices \((\psi_C,\rho_C)\), and certified
   Boolean query layers \(\mathcal Q_C\).

   Suppose no template in \(\mathcal P\), no fractional layer
   \(y\in\operatorname{conv}\{\mathbf 1_Q:Q\in\mathcal Q_C\}\), no membership
   vector \(0\le\theta_p\le1\), and no certified one-sided lower mass \(X\)
   satisfying \((CSF1)\) gives a positive surplus \((CSS1)\).  Then every such
   certified soft proposal obeys
   \[
      K_C\,\frac{X}{\max\{\mu,K_C\}}
      \le
      \psi_C
      \left(
         K_C^{\rho_C}\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}y_{\sigma_0}
         +
         \zeta K_C^{1+\rho_C}
      \right),
      \tag{CSSR1}
   \]
   where \(\mu=\sum_{p\in W_C}\theta_p\).  Equivalently, for the concrete
   soft-proposal surplus
   \[
      Z(C,y,\theta,X)
      =
      K_C\frac{X}{\max\{\mu,K_C\}}
      -
      \psi_C
      \left(
         K_C^{\rho_C}\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}y_{\sigma_0}
         +
         \zeta K_C^{1+\rho_C}
      \right),
      \tag{CSSR2}
   \]
   every build-time proposal law supported on \(\mathcal P\) has nonpositive
   certified surplus unless it returns a verified Hall-shadow repair:
   \[
      Z(C,y,\theta,X)\le0
      \tag{CSSR3}
   \]
   for every certified output in its support.

   Consequently, once the outside frontier has been discharged by
   \cref{cor:maximal-cut-outside-transport}, the only remaining dense-side
   obstruction for this proposal universe is a closed cut \(A^\star\) satisfying
   \((MPH1)\)--\((MPH2)\) together with the universal soft envelope
   \((CSSR1)\).  If a geometric theorem rules out this combined residual for
   every high-correlation residual satisfying \((HCS1)\), then the
   dense/spherical separator condition \((DSF2)\) holds and the
   polylogarithmic ANN endpoint follows.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If some certified soft proposal violates \((CSSR1)\), then it satisfies
   \((CSF1)\) and \((CSF2)\).  By
   \cref{cor:closed-shadow-soft-proposal-hardening}, the verifier hardens it to
   a certified Boolean query layer and the top-\(K_C\) Hall-shadow prefix
   satisfying \((HFP4)\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:hall-shadow-finite-prefix-separation} gives the Hall-cut repair
   alternative \((HCR2)\), contradicting the assumed failure of every positive
   proposal in \(\mathcal P\).  This proves \((CSSR1)\), and \((CSSR3)\) is the
   same inequality written for the surplus functional.

   The final statement is the preceding contrapositive composed with
   \cref{cor:maximal-cut-outside-transport} and
   \cref{cor:closed-shadow-soft-proposal-separator-endpoint}: after outside
   transport is packed, any residual that is not of the displayed closed-cut
   envelope form must provide either Hall success or a positive soft proposal,
   hence one of the two repair alternatives of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Closed-shadow fractional superlevel envelope]
   \label{cor:closed-shadow-fractional-superlevel-envelope}
   Work in the residual setting of
   \cref{cor:closed-shadow-soft-proposal-residual-envelope}.  Fix a certified
   template \(C\in\mathcal P\), a fractional layer
   \(y\in\operatorname{conv}\{\mathbf 1_Q:Q\in\mathcal Q_C\}\), and write
   \[
      d_{C,y}(p)=
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A^\star)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}y_{\sigma_0}
      \qquad(p\in W_C).
      \tag{CSW1}
   \]
   For \(\delta>0\), let
   \[
      H_{C,y,\delta}=\{p\in W_C:d_{C,y}(p)\ge\delta\},
      \qquad h=|H_{C,y,\delta}|,
      \qquad
      M=\sum_{p\in H_{C,y,\delta}}d_{C,y}(p).
      \tag{CSW2}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      R_C(y,K_C)=
      \psi_C
      \left(
         K_C^{\rho_C}\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}y_{\sigma_0}
         +
         \zeta K_C^{1+\rho_C}
      \right).
      \tag{CSW3}
   \]
   If no certified closed-shadow soft proposal in \(\mathcal P\) fires, then
   every nonempty superlevel obeys
   \[
      \min\{M,K_C\delta\}\le R_C(y,K_C).
      \tag{CSW4}
   \]
   Consequently, a reported fractional layer and superlevel with
   \[
      \min\{M,K_C\delta\}>R_C(y,K_C)
      \tag{CSW5}
   \]
   immediately gives a positive soft proposal, hence the Hall-cut repair
   alternative \((HCR2)\).

   More generally, suppose the proposal universe contains copies of the same
   certified container and admissible layer at a \(b\)-dense set of
   cardinalities: for every \(1\le h\le |W_C|\) there is an available copy
   \(C_K\) with \(h/b\le K\le h\), the same \((W_C,\mathcal Q_C)\), and the
   same prices \((\psi_C,\rho_C)\).  Then every surviving superlevel satisfies
   \[
      M\le
      b\psi_C
      \left(
         h^{\rho_C}\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}y_{\sigma_0}
         +
         \zeta h^{1+\rho_C}
      \right),
      \tag{CSW6}
   \]
   and therefore
   \[
      \delta\le
      b\psi_C
      \left(
         h^{\rho_C-1}\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}y_{\sigma_0}
         +
         \zeta h^{\rho_C}
      \right).
      \tag{CSW7}
   \]
   Thus the closed-shadow residual can be searched by weighted superlevel
   reporting: find one container, one fractional signature layer, and one
   degree threshold whose cumulative paid mass beats the recursive price density.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(h=0\), there is nothing to prove.  For \(h>0\), choose the soft
   membership vector \(\theta_p=\mathbf 1_{H_{C,y,\delta}}(p)\).  Then
   \(\mu=h\), and \(X=M\) satisfies \((CSF1)\) with equality.  Applying the
   residual envelope \((CSSR1)\) gives
   \[
      K_C\frac{M}{\max\{h,K_C\}}\le R_C(y,K_C).
      \tag{CSW8}
   \]
   If \(h\le K_C\), this is \(M\le R_C(y,K_C)\), hence \((CSW4)\).  If
   \(h>K_C\), then \(M/h\ge\delta\), so
   \[
      K_C\delta\le K_C\frac{M}{h}\le R_C(y,K_C),
   \]
   which again gives \((CSW4)\).  A violation \((CSW5)\) is the contrapositive
   and therefore gives a positive soft proposal; the repair conclusion is
   \cref{cor:closed-shadow-soft-proposal-hardening}.

   For the \(b\)-dense cardinality statement, choose the copy \(C_K\) with
   \(h/b\le K\le h\) and apply \((CSW8)\) to that copy.  Since \(K\le h\),
   \[
      M\le\frac hK R_{C_K}(y,K)\le bR_{C_K}(y,K).
   \]
   Also \(K^\rho\le h^\rho\) and \(K^{1+\rho}\le h^{1+\rho}\) for
   \(\rho=\rho_C\), so \((CSW6)\) follows.  Dividing by \(h\) and using
   \(M/h\ge\delta\) gives \((CSW7)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Closed-shadow dyadic layer-cake separator]
   \label{cor:closed-shadow-dyadic-layer-cake-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:closed-shadow-fractional-superlevel-envelope}.  Fix a certified
   container \(W_C\) and an admissible fractional layer \(y\), and put
   \[
      A_y=\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}y_{\sigma_0}.
      \tag{CSL1}
   \]
   Assume the proposal universe contains copies of this same container and
   layer at a \(b\)-dense set of cardinalities, as in the final part of
   \cref{cor:closed-shadow-fractional-superlevel-envelope}.  Let the positive
   values of \(d_{C,y}\) lie in a certified interval
   \([\delta_0,\delta_{\max}]\), and define dyadic thresholds
   \[
      \delta_j=2^j\delta_0,
      \qquad
      0\le j<J,
      \qquad
      J=1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{\delta_{\max}}{\delta_0}\right\rceil .
      \tag{CSL2}
   \]
   For each \(j\), let
   \[
      h_j=\left|\{p\in W_C:d_{C,y}(p)\ge\delta_j\}\right|.
      \tag{CSL3}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_{p\in W_C}d_{C,y}(p)
      >
      2b\psi_C
      \sum_{j:\,h_j>0}
      \left(
         A_yh_j^{\rho_C}
         +
         \zeta h_j^{1+\rho_C}
      \right),
      \tag{CSL4}
   \]
   then some dyadic threshold \(\delta_j\) and some available cardinality copy
   of \(C\) give a positive closed-shadow soft proposal, hence the Hall-cut
   repair alternative \((HCR2)\).

   Consequently, in any residual satisfying the no-proposal envelope, every
   such certified dyadic report obeys the reverse inequality in \((CSL4)\).
   Thus a build-time reporter does not need to guess the winning threshold: it
   may certify the whole dyadic layer-cake profile of one fractional layer, and
   the verifier extracts a single positive superlevel if the aggregate mass
   beats the aggregate recursive price.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For \(p\) with \(d=d_{C,y}(p)>0\), the thresholds not exceeding \(d\) form an
   initial segment, and their sum is at least \(d/2\).  Hence the dyadic
   layer-cake lower bound gives
   \[
      \sum_{j=0}^{J-1}\delta_jh_j
      =
      \sum_{p\in W_C}
      \sum_{\substack{0\le j<J:\\ \delta_j\le d_{C,y}(p)}}\delta_j
      \ge
      \frac12\sum_{p\in W_C}d_{C,y}(p).
      \tag{CSL5}
   \]
   If \((CSL4)\) holds, then for some \(j\) with \(h_j>0\),
   \[
      \delta_jh_j
      >
      b\psi_C
      \left(
         A_yh_j^{\rho_C}
         +
         \zeta h_j^{1+\rho_C}
      \right).
      \tag{CSL6}
   \]
   Choose an available cardinality copy \(C_K\) with \(h_j/b\le K\le h_j\).
   Since \(K\le h_j\),
   \[
      R_{C_K}(y,K)
      \le
      \psi_C
      \left(
         A_yh_j^{\rho_C}
         +
         \zeta h_j^{1+\rho_C}
      \right),
      \tag{CSL7}
   \]
   while \(K\ge h_j/b\) and \((CSL6)\) give
   \[
      K\delta_j>R_{C_K}(y,K).
      \tag{CSL8}
   \]
   For the superlevel \(H_j=\{p:d_{C,y}(p)\ge\delta_j\}\), its cumulative mass
   \(M_j\) satisfies \(M_j\ge h_j\delta_j\ge K\delta_j\).  Therefore
   \[
      \min\{M_j,K\delta_j\}=K\delta_j>R_{C_K}(y,K),
   \]
   which is the positive superlevel condition \((CSW5)\) for the copy \(C_K\).
   \Cref{cor:closed-shadow-fractional-superlevel-envelope} gives the positive
   soft proposal and then the Hall-cut repair alternative.  The residual
   statement is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Reported closed-shadow layer-cake separator]
   \label{cor:reported-closed-shadow-layer-cake-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:closed-shadow-dyadic-layer-cake-separator}.  A build-time reporter
   may return only one-sided certificates for one container/layer report, with
   \(0<\rho_C\le1\): a lower bound \(\widehat M\) on the total paid degree and
   upper bounds \(\widehat h_j\) on the dyadic superlevel cardinalities,
   \[
      0\le\widehat M\le\sum_{p\in W_C}d_{C,y}(p),
      \qquad
      h_j\le\widehat h_j
      \quad(0\le j<J).
      \tag{CRL1}
   \]
   If the certified surplus
   \[
      \widehat Z
      =
      \widehat M
      -
      2b\psi_C
      \sum_{j=0}^{J-1}
      \left(
         A_y\widehat h_j^{\rho_C}
         +
         \zeta\widehat h_j^{1+\rho_C}
      \right)
      \tag{CRL2}
   \]
   is positive, then the Hall-cut repair alternative \((HCR2)\) holds.

   The same conclusion holds in Las Vegas build time if a randomized reporter
   returns certified reports with
   \[
      \E_s\widehat Z(s)\ge\Gamma>0,
      \qquad
      \widehat Z(s)_+\le U
      \quad\text{almost surely}.
      \tag{CRL3}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      B\ge\frac U\Gamma\log\frac1\delta
      \tag{CRL4}
   \]
   independent build-time seeds find a deterministic positive report with
   probability at least \(1-\delta\); failed reports are discarded.

   Consequently, in
   \cref{cor:closed-shadow-soft-proposal-separator-endpoint}, the second
   alternative may return such a positive reported layer-cake certificate
   instead of an explicit soft membership vector.  If every high-correlation
   co-load residual has Hall success or such a reported certificate after
   maximal Hall localization, then \((HCS2)\), \((DSF2)\), and the
   polylogarithmic ANN endpoint follow.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(0\le\rho_C\le1\), the functions \(h\mapsto h^{\rho_C}\) and
   \(h\mapsto h^{1+\rho_C}\) are increasing on the nonnegative reals.  Thus
   \((CRL1)\)--\((CRL2)\) imply
   \[
      \sum_{p\in W_C}d_{C,y}(p)
      >
      2b\psi_C
      \sum_{j:\,h_j>0}
      \left(
         A_yh_j^{\rho_C}
         +
         \zeta h_j^{1+\rho_C}
      \right).
   \]
   This is \((CSL4)\), so
   \cref{cor:closed-shadow-dyadic-layer-cake-separator} gives a positive
   closed-shadow soft proposal and hence \((HCR2)\).

   For the sampled statement, \((CRL3)\) implies
   \(\Pr[\widehat Z(s)>0]\ge\Gamma/U\).  Therefore \(B\) independent reports
   all fail with probability at most \(\exp(-B\Gamma/U)\).  A positive report
   satisfies the deterministic part, and nonpositive reports are not retained.

   The endpoint statement is just this deterministic implication substituted
   into the second branch of
   \cref{cor:closed-shadow-soft-proposal-separator-endpoint}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Reported closed-shadow residual dichotomy]
   \label{cor:reported-closed-shadow-residual-dichotomy}
   Work after maximal Hall localization in the setting of
   \cref{cor:closed-shadow-soft-proposal-residual-envelope}.  Let
   \(\mathcal R\) be a finite universe of certified closed-shadow reports.
   Each report \(r\in\mathcal R\) specifies a template \(C_r\), an admissible
   fractional layer \(y_r\), a dyadic threshold net, a density parameter
   \(b_r\), and one-sided certificates
   \[
      0\le\widehat M_r
      \le
      \sum_{p\in W_{C_r}}d_{C_r,y_r}(p),
      \qquad
      h_{r,j}\le\widehat h_{r,j}.
      \tag{CRR1}
   \]
   Define the certified reduced surplus
   \[
      \widehat Z_r=
      \widehat M_r
      -
      2b_r\psi_{C_r}
      \sum_j
      \left(
         A_{y_r}\widehat h_{r,j}^{\rho_{C_r}}
         +
         \zeta\widehat h_{r,j}^{1+\rho_{C_r}}
      \right),
      \qquad
      A_{y_r}=\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}y_r(\sigma_0).
      \tag{CRR2}
   \]
   Then one of the following two alternatives holds.

   First, some report has \(\widehat Z_r>0\).  Then the Hall-cut repair
   alternative \((HCR2)\) holds.

   Second, every certified report obeys the residual inequality
   \[
      \widehat M_r
      \le
      2b_r\psi_{C_r}
      \sum_j
      \left(
         A_{y_r}\widehat h_{r,j}^{\rho_{C_r}}
         +
         \zeta\widehat h_{r,j}^{1+\rho_{C_r}}
      \right).
      \tag{CRR3}
   \]

   Consequently, suppose a geometric reporter theorem proves that every
   localized closed Hall residual satisfying \((MPH1)\)--\((MPH2)\) admits a
   finite certified report universe \(\mathcal R\) for which \((CRR3)\) is
   impossible.  Then
   \cref{cor:closed-shadow-soft-proposal-separator-endpoint} holds with the
   reported layer-cake certificate in its second branch, and hence the
   dense/spherical polylogarithmic ANN endpoint follows.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If some report has \(\widehat Z_r>0\), then it is a positive reported
   layer-cake certificate in the sense of
   \cref{cor:reported-closed-shadow-layer-cake-separator}, so \((HCR2)\) holds.
   If no report has positive surplus, then \(\widehat Z_r\le0\) for every
   \(r\), which is exactly \((CRR3)\) after rearranging \((CRR2)\).

   For the endpoint statement, fix a high-correlation residual.  If Hall
   transport succeeds, the first branch of
   \cref{cor:closed-shadow-soft-proposal-separator-endpoint} applies.  If Hall
   transport fails, replace the cut by the maximal localized cut.  The assumed
   reporter theorem rules out the residual alternative \((CRR3)\), so the first
   alternative above gives \((HCR2)\).  Therefore every high-correlation
   residual satisfies one of the two repair alternatives, and
   \cref{cor:closed-shadow-soft-proposal-separator-endpoint} gives the
   dense/spherical endpoint.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Routed-support reports feed closed-shadow layer-cake]
   \label{cor:routed-support-closed-shadow-report}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:reported-closed-shadow-layer-cake-separator}.  Suppose a reporter
   certifies a subcontainer \(S\subseteq W_C\) as a valid smaller-radius repair
   container with the same admissible fractional layer \(y\), exponent
   \(\rho_C\), and price factor \(\psi_C\).  Let
   \[
      X\le\sum_{p\in S}d_{C,y}(p)
      \tag{RSC1}
   \]
   be a one-sided lower paid-mass certificate.  Let the positive values of
   \(d_{C,y}\) on \(S\) lie in a certified range
   \([\delta_0,\delta_{\max}]\), and use the dyadic thresholds
   \(\delta_j=2^j\delta_0\), \(0\le j<J\), with
   \(J=1+\lceil\log_2(\delta_{\max}/\delta_0)\rceil\).  If the reporter
   certifies upper bounds
   \[
      |\{p\in S:d_{C,y}(p)\ge\delta_j\}|\le \widehat h_j,
      \tag{RSC2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      X>
      2b\psi_C
      \sum_{j=0}^{J-1}
      \left(
         A_y\widehat h_j^{\rho_C}
         +
         \zeta\widehat h_j^{1+\rho_C}
      \right),
      \qquad
      A_y=\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}y_{\sigma_0},
      \tag{RSC3}
   \]
   then the Hall-cut repair alternative \((HCR2)\) holds.

   In particular, with only the support size \(s=|S|\) reported, it is enough
   to have
   \[
      X>
      2bJ\psi_C
      \left(
         A_ys^{\rho_C}
         +
         \zeta s^{1+\rho_C}
      \right).
      \tag{RSC4}
   \]
   Thus support-price, atom-routing, list-decoding, or facility reports that
   certify a routed support and its paid mass are special cases of the reported
   closed-shadow layer-cake interface, losing only the dyadic dynamic-range
   factor when they do not report individual superlevel sizes.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{cor:reported-closed-shadow-layer-cake-separator} to the
   certified subcontainer \(S\), with \(\widehat M=X\) and the upper bounds
   \(\widehat h_j\) from \((RSC2)\).  The condition \((RSC3)\) is exactly the
   positivity of the certified surplus \((CRL2)\), so \((HCR2)\) follows.

   For the support-size version, use the valid upper bounds
   \(\widehat h_j=s\) for every dyadic level.  Substituting these bounds in
   \((RSC3)\) gives \((RSC4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Aggregate routed-support closed-shadow panel]
   \label{cor:aggregate-routed-support-closed-shadow-panel}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:routed-support-closed-shadow-report}.  Let \(i\in I\) range over a
   finite panel of routed-support reports.  Report \(i\) has a parent template
   \(C_i\), a certified subcontainer \(S_i\subseteq W_{C_i}\), layer \(y_i\),
   exponent \(\rho_i\), price factor \(\psi_i\), density factor \(b_i\), dyadic
   range length \(J_i\), support size \(s_i=|S_i|\), and one-sided mass lower
   bound, satisfying the support-size hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:routed-support-closed-shadow-report},
   \[
      X_i\le\sum_{p\in S_i}d_{C_i,y_i}(p).
      \tag{ARS1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_i X_i
      >
      \sum_i
      2b_iJ_i\psi_i
      \left(
         A_{y_i}s_i^{\rho_i}
         +
         \zeta s_i^{1+\rho_i}
      \right),
      \qquad
      A_{y_i}=\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}y_i(\sigma_0),
      \tag{ARS2}
   \]
   then some report in the panel gives the Hall-cut repair alternative
   \((HCR2)\).

   Consequently, if no reported closed-shadow repair exists, every finite
   routed-support panel satisfies the reverse inequality in \((ARS2)\).  In
   particular, a support-price or atom-routing certificate only has to make the
   routed paid mass larger than this aggregate support price; the verifier then
   extracts one ordinary reported layer-cake repair.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If every report in the panel failed the support-size condition \((RSC4)\),
   then for each \(i\),
   \[
      X_i\le
      2b_iJ_i\psi_i
      \left(
         A_{y_i}s_i^{\rho_i}
         +
         \zeta s_i^{1+\rho_i}
      \right).
   \]
   Summing would contradict \((ARS2)\).  Hence some report satisfies
   \((RSC4)\), and
   \cref{cor:routed-support-closed-shadow-report} gives \((HCR2)\).  The
   residual statement is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Reported support-price routing residual]
   \label{cor:reported-support-price-routing-residual}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:aggregate-routed-support-closed-shadow-panel}.  Let \(A\) be a
   failed closed Hall cut, and let \(\mathcal R_{\rm part}(A)\) be any finite
   family of partial routings of cut-shadow atoms to certified smaller-radius
   routed supports.  For \(r\in\mathcal R_{\rm part}(A)\), write \(X(r)\) for
   the routed paid mass and define its reported support price by
   \[
      \Psi_{\rm rep}(r)
      =
      \sum_{i\in I(r)}
      2b_iJ_i\psi_i
      \left(
         A_{y_i}s_i(r)^{\rho_i}
         +
         \zeta s_i(r)^{1+\rho_i}
      \right),
      \tag{RPR1}
   \]
   where \(I(r)\) ranges over the used routed supports, \(s_i(r)\) is the
   support size, and \(A_{y_i}=\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}y_i(\sigma_0)\).
   If some partial routing satisfies
   \[
      X(r)>\Psi_{\rm rep}(r),
      \tag{RPR2}
   \]
   then the Hall-cut repair alternative \((HCR2)\) holds.

   Equivalently, if no reported closed-shadow repair exists, then every partial
   routing in the certified family obeys
   \[
      X(r)\le\Psi_{\rm rep}(r).
      \tag{RPR3}
   \]
   For a full routing of all paid cut-shadow atoms,
   \(X(r)=M_A=\sum_{(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}\alpha_{p,\sigma_0}\).  Hence a
   surviving residual satisfies the scalar support-price obstruction
   \[
      M_A
      \le
      \inf_{r\in\mathcal R_{\rm full}(A)}\Psi_{\rm rep}(r)
      \tag{RPR4}
   \]
   whenever the displayed full-routing family is nonempty.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   A routing \(r\) determines a finite routed-support panel: one report for
   each used support, with lower mass equal to the paid mass routed to that
   support.  The sum of those lower masses is \(X(r)\), while the right side of
   \((ARS2)\) for this panel is exactly \(\Psi_{\rm rep}(r)\).  Therefore
   \((RPR2)\) is \((ARS2)\), and
   \cref{cor:aggregate-routed-support-closed-shadow-panel} gives \((HCR2)\).
   The residual inequality \((RPR3)\) is the contrapositive.  Restricting
   \((RPR3)\) to full routings gives \((RPR4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Reported marginal support-law certificate]
   \label{cor:reported-marginal-support-law}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:reported-support-price-routing-residual}.  Fix a finite set
   \(\mathcal I\) of reported support slots.  Slot \(i\in\mathcal I\) specifies
   a certified parent template \(C_i\), an admissible layer \(y_i\), a support
   container \(W_i\subseteq W_{C_i}\), and parameters
   \(b_i,J_i,\psi_i,\rho_i\), with \(0<\rho_i\le1\).  Every subset of \(W_i\)
   is allowed as the routed support for slot \(i\).

   A marginal stochastic routing law assigns, for every paid cut-shadow atom
   \((p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)\), probabilities \(z_{i,p,\sigma_0}\ge0\) and routed
   fractions \(\gamma_{i,\sigma_0}\) satisfying
   \[
      \sum_i z_{i,p,\sigma_0}\le1,
      \qquad
      0\le\gamma_{i,\sigma_0}\le y_i(\sigma_0),
      \tag{RML1}
   \]
   with \(z_{i,p,\sigma_0}=0\) unless \(p\in W_i\).  Choices for different
   data points are independent, while choices among the atoms of the same point
   may be arbitrarily coupled, subject to the displayed marginals.  Define
   \[
      X_z=
      \sum_{(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}
      \sum_i z_{i,p,\sigma_0}\gamma_{i,\sigma_0},
      \tag{RML2}
   \]
   and the marginal support upper bounds
   \[
      \nu_{i,p}=
      \min\left\{1,\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma_A(p)}z_{i,p,\sigma_0}\right\},
      \qquad
      \nu_i=\sum_p\nu_{i,p},
      \tag{RML3}
   \]
   where
   \(\Sigma_A(p)=\{\sigma_0:(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)\}\).  Put
   \[
      \widehat\Psi_{\rm rep}(z)
      =
      \sum_i
      2b_iJ_i\psi_i
      \left(
         A_{y_i}\nu_i^{\rho_i}
         +
         \zeta(\nu_i+\nu_i^{1+\rho_i})
      \right),
      \qquad
      A_{y_i}=\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}y_i(\sigma_0).
      \tag{RML4}
   \]
   If
   \[
      X_z>\widehat\Psi_{\rm rep}(z),
      \tag{RML5}
   \]
   then some deterministic partial routed-support report satisfies
   \((RPR2)\).  Consequently the Hall-cut repair alternative \((HCR2)\) holds.

   Equivalently, in any residual with no reported closed-shadow repair, every
   marginal stochastic routing law obeys
   \[
      X_z\le\widehat\Psi_{\rm rep}(z).
      \tag{RML6}
   \]
   Thus facility, additive-quantization, list-decoding, lattice-decoding, or
   seeded-clustering proposal laws may be analyzed only through their marginal
   support probabilities.  A positive law is rounded at build time and then
   verified as an ordinary deterministic reported support routing; no
   fractional support is retained in the index.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Sample independently over data points.  For each atom
   \((p,\sigma_0)\), choose at most one slot \(i\) with marginal probability
   \(z_{i,p,\sigma_0}\), and leave the atom unrouted with the remaining
   probability.  If slot \(i\) is chosen, route the fraction
   \(\gamma_{i,\sigma_0}\) of that atom to slot \(i\).  The expected routed paid
   mass is exactly \(X_z\).

   For a sampled deterministic routing \(r\), let
   \(S_i(r)\) be the set of data points whose atoms route positive mass to slot
   \(i\), and let \(s_i(r)=|S_i(r)|\).  Since
   \(\gamma_{i,\sigma_0}\le y_i(\sigma_0)\), the mass routed to slot \(i\)
   satisfies the one-sided report condition
   \[
      X_i(r)
      \le
      \sum_{p\in S_i(r)}
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}y_i(\sigma_0)
      =
      \sum_{p\in S_i(r)}d_{C_i,y_i}(p).
      \tag{RML7}
   \]
   Hence every sampled outcome is an admissible partial routing in the sense of
   \cref{cor:reported-support-price-routing-residual}.

   Let \(I_{i,p}\) be the indicator that point \(p\) appears in \(S_i(r)\), and
   let \(q_{i,p}=\E I_{i,p}\).  The union bound gives
   \(q_{i,p}\le\nu_{i,p}\), so
   \(\mu_i=\sum_pq_{i,p}\le\nu_i\).  The variables \(I_{i,p}\) are independent
   over \(p\).  For \(S_i=s_i(r)\), concavity gives
   \(\E S_i^{\rho_i}\le\mu_i^{\rho_i}\le\nu_i^{\rho_i}\).  For the storage
   moment, use
   \(k^{1+\rho}\le k+k(k-1)_+^\rho\) for \(k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) and
   \(0<\rho\le1\).  With
   \(S_i^{(p)}=\sum_{p'\ne p}I_{i,p'}\),
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \E S_i^{1+\rho_i}
      &\le
      \mu_i+
      \sum_p q_{i,p}\E\left(S_i^{(p)}\right)^{\rho_i}  \\
      &\le
      \mu_i+\sum_pq_{i,p}(\mu_i-q_{i,p})^{\rho_i}
      \le
      \mu_i+\mu_i^{1+\rho_i}
      \le
      \nu_i+\nu_i^{1+\rho_i}.
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{RML8}
   \]
   Multiplying by the reported support-price coefficients and summing over
   \(i\) yields
   \[
      \E_r\Psi_{\rm rep}(r)\le\widehat\Psi_{\rm rep}(z).
      \tag{RML9}
   \]
   Combining \((RML2)\), \((RML5)\), and \((RML9)\), we get
   \[
      \E_r\left[X(r)-\Psi_{\rm rep}(r)\right]>0.
   \]
   Thus some deterministic sampled routing has
   \(X(r)>\Psi_{\rm rep}(r)\), which is \((RPR2)\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:reported-support-price-routing-residual} gives \((HCR2)\).  The
   residual inequality \((RML6)\) is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Certified one-slot marginal support search]
   \label{cor:certified-one-slot-marginal-support-search}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:reported-marginal-support-law}.  Fix one
   reported support slot \(i\).  A certified one-slot marginal report consists
   of numbers \(z_{p,\sigma_0}\) and \(\gamma_{\sigma_0}\) with
   \(0\le z_{p,\sigma_0}\le1\), \(0\le\gamma_{\sigma_0}\le y_i(\sigma_0)\),
   supported only when \(p\in W_i\), together with one-sided certificates
   \[
      0\le\widehat X
      \le
      \sum_{(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}z_{p,\sigma_0}\gamma_{\sigma_0},
      \qquad
      \sum_p
      \min\left\{1,\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma_A(p)}z_{p,\sigma_0}\right\}
      \le\widehat\nu .
      \tag{RMS1}
   \]
   Define its certified one-slot surplus by
   \[
      \widehat Z_i
      =
      \widehat X
      -
      2b_iJ_i\psi_i
      \left(
         A_{y_i}\widehat\nu^{\rho_i}
         +
         \zeta(\widehat\nu+\widehat\nu^{1+\rho_i})
      \right).
      \tag{RMS2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \widehat Z_i>0,
      \tag{RMS3}
   \]
   then the Hall-cut repair alternative \((HCR2)\) holds.

   Conversely, if no reported closed-shadow repair exists, every certified
   one-slot marginal report satisfies \(\widehat Z_i\le0\).  Moreover, if a
   multi-slot marginal law satisfies the aggregate surplus condition
   \((RML5)\), then at least one used slot has positive exact one-slot surplus,
   and hence the same repair conclusion follows from that slot alone.

   The same conclusion holds in Las Vegas build time for a randomized one-slot
   proposal law.  If the law returns certified reports with
   \[
      \E_s\widehat Z_i(s)\ge\Gamma>0,
      \qquad
      \widehat Z_i(s)_+\le U
      \quad\text{almost surely},
      \tag{RMS4}
   \]
   then
   \[
      B\ge\frac U\Gamma\log\frac1\delta
      \tag{RMS5}
   \]
   independent build-time seeds find a deterministic reported repair with
   probability at least \(1-\delta\).  Nonpositive samples are discarded.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The report defines a singleton marginal law by setting
   \(z_{i,p,\sigma_0}=z_{p,\sigma_0}\) and all other slot probabilities to
   zero.  Let
   \[
      X_i=
      \sum_{(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}z_{p,\sigma_0}\gamma_{\sigma_0},
      \qquad
      \nu_i=
      \sum_p
      \min\left\{1,\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma_A(p)}z_{p,\sigma_0}\right\}.
   \]
   By \((RMS1)\), \(X_i\ge\widehat X\) and \(\nu_i\le\widehat\nu\).  Since the
   reported support price is increasing in \(\nu_i\), \((RMS3)\) implies the
   exact singleton surplus condition \((RML5)\).  Therefore
   \cref{cor:reported-marginal-support-law} gives \((HCR2)\).  The residual
   statement is the contrapositive applied to singleton laws.

   For the multi-slot statement, write \(X_i\) and \(P_i\) for the exact routed
   mass and exact marginal price of slot \(i\) in \((RML2)\)--\((RML4)\).  Since
   \(X_z=\sum_iX_i\) and \(\widehat\Psi_{\rm rep}(z)=\sum_iP_i\), condition
   \((RML5)\) implies \(X_i>P_i\) for at least one \(i\).  Restricting the law
   to that slot gives the preceding singleton case.

   Finally, \((RMS4)\) gives
   \[
      \Pr_s[\widehat Z_i(s)>0]\ge\Gamma/U.
   \]
   Thus \(B\) independent nonpositive samples have probability at most
   \(\exp(-B\Gamma/U)\).  A positive sample satisfies the deterministic
   one-slot condition and is then verified before any reported support is
   retained.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Point-coupled one-slot support law]
   \label{cor:point-coupled-one-slot-support-law}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:certified-one-slot-marginal-support-search}.  Fix one reported
   support slot \(i\).  Suppose a report gives point support probabilities
   \(0\le q_p\le1\), atom routing marginals \(z_{p,\sigma_0}\), and routed
   fractions \(\gamma_{\sigma_0}\), supported only when \(p\in W_i\), such that
   \[
      0\le z_{p,\sigma_0}\le q_p,
      \qquad
      0\le\gamma_{\sigma_0}\le y_i(\sigma_0).
      \tag{RCS1}
   \]
   Let
   \[
      0\le\widehat X
      \le
      \sum_{(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}z_{p,\sigma_0}\gamma_{\sigma_0},
      \qquad
      \sum_pq_p\le\widehat\nu .
      \tag{RCS2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \widehat X
      >
      2b_iJ_i\psi_i
      \left(
         A_{y_i}\widehat\nu^{\rho_i}
         +
         \zeta(\widehat\nu+\widehat\nu^{1+\rho_i})
      \right),
      \tag{RCS3}
   \]
   then the Hall-cut repair alternative \((HCR2)\) holds.

   In particular, define the point score
   \[
      d_i(p)=
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}y_i(\sigma_0).
      \tag{RCS4}
   \]
   For any soft point membership \(0\le\theta_p\le1\), the choice
   \(q_p=\theta_p\), \(z_{p,\sigma_0}=\theta_p\), and
   \(\gamma_{\sigma_0}=y_i(\sigma_0)\) is valid.  Thus a one-sided certificate
   \[
      0\le\widehat X\le\sum_p\theta_pd_i(p),
      \qquad
      \sum_p\theta_p\le\widehat\nu,
      \tag{RCS5}
   \]
   satisfying \((RCS3)\) already exposes a reported closed-shadow repair.
   This point-coupled form avoids the union-bound loss
   \(\min\{1,\sum_{\sigma_0}z_{p,\sigma_0}\}\) when many paid atoms of the same
   data point are routed together.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Independently for each data point \(p\), activate the slot with probability
   \(q_p\).  Conditional on activation, route atom \((p,\sigma_0)\) to slot
   \(i\) with probability \(z_{p,\sigma_0}/q_p\), interpreted as zero when
   \(q_p=0\), and route the fraction \(\gamma_{\sigma_0}\) if the atom is
   chosen.  The condition \(z_{p,\sigma_0}\le q_p\) makes this a valid
   conditional probability, and the expected routed paid mass is at least
   \(\widehat X\).

   For a sampled outcome, use the activated points as the reported support
   \(\mathsf S_i\).  Its routed mass is at most
   \[
      \sum_{p\in\mathsf S_i}
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}y_i(\sigma_0),
   \]
   so it is an admissible one-sided routed-support report.  If
   \(S_i=|\mathsf S_i|=\sum_pB_p\) is the number of activated points, then the
   Bernoulli variables \(B_p\) are independent and
   \(\mu=\E S_i=\sum_pq_p\le\widehat\nu\).  The moment calculation in
   \((RML8)\) gives
   \[
      \E S_i^{\rho_i}\le\widehat\nu^{\rho_i},
      \qquad
      \E S_i^{1+\rho_i}\le\widehat\nu+\widehat\nu^{1+\rho_i}.
      \tag{RCS6}
   \]
   Therefore the expected reported support price is at most the right hand
   side of \((RCS3)\).  If \((RCS3)\) holds, some sampled deterministic report
   has routed paid mass larger than its reported support price, so
   \cref{cor:reported-support-price-routing-residual} gives \((HCR2)\).

   The soft-membership specialization follows by substitution.  In that case
   \(z_{p,\sigma_0}=q_p=\theta_p\) couples all selected atoms of point \(p\) to
   the same support event, and the expected routed paid mass is
   \(\sum_p\theta_pd_i(p)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Reported soft support hardens to a top prefix]
   \label{cor:reported-soft-support-prefix-hardening}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:point-coupled-one-slot-support-law}.  Fix
   one reported support slot \(i\), and let \(d_i(p)\) be the point score from
   \((RCS4)\).  For soft memberships \(0\le\theta_p\le1\), put
   \[
      \mu=\sum_p\theta_p,
      \qquad
      X\le\sum_p\theta_pd_i(p).
      \tag{RSH1}
   \]
   For an available cardinality \(K\ge1\), let \(U_K\) be the top \(K\) points
   of \(W_i\) in decreasing order of \(d_i\), and write
   \(D_i(K)=\sum_{p\in U_K}d_i(p)\).  If
   \[
      K\,\frac{X}{\max\{\mu,K\}}
      >
      2b_iJ_i\psi_i
      \left(
         A_{y_i}K^{\rho_i}
         +
         \zeta K^{1+\rho_i}
      \right),
      \tag{RSH2}
   \]
   then the deterministic top-prefix support \(U_K\) satisfies \((RPR2)\), and
   hence the Hall-cut repair alternative \((HCR2)\) holds.

   Equivalently, in any residual with no reported closed-shadow repair, every
   soft membership vector and every available \(K\) obey the reverse inequality
   in \((RSH2)\).  Thus soft cluster, facility, or additive-quantization
   assignments are only proposal languages: the verifier retains the exact
   top-\(K\) support for the induced score \(d_i\).

   In particular, if every cardinality is available and
   \(\mu_+=\max\{1,\mu\}\), then the simpler condition
   \[
      X>
      4b_iJ_i\psi_i
      \left(
         A_{y_i}\mu_+^{\rho_i}
         +
         \zeta\mu_+^{1+\rho_i}
      \right)
      \tag{RSH3}
   \]
   already gives \((HCR2)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Order \(W_i=\{p_1,p_2,\ldots\}\) so that
   \(d_i(p_1)\ge d_i(p_2)\ge\cdots\).  The standard rearrangement bound gives
   \[
      D_i(K)\ge K\,\frac{X}{\max\{\mu,K\}}.
      \tag{RSH4}
   \]
   Indeed, if \(\mu\le K\), the top \(K\) integral prefix has at least the mass
   of any fractional vector \(0\le\theta\le1\) of total mass \(\mu\).  If
   \(\mu>K\), the average of the top \(K\) scores is at least the average score
   under any fractional mass \(\mu\).

   Combining \((RSH2)\) and \((RSH4)\), the reported support \(U_K\), with
   lower mass certificate \(D_i(K)\), has routed paid mass larger than its
   reported support price
   \[
      2b_iJ_i\psi_i
      \left(
         A_{y_i}K^{\rho_i}
         +
         \zeta K^{1+\rho_i}
      \right).
   \]
   This is a one-slot instance of \((RPR2)\), so
   \cref{cor:reported-support-price-routing-residual} gives \((HCR2)\).  The
   residual statement is the contrapositive.

   For the coarse scale, choose \(K=1\) if \(\mu<2\), and otherwise
   \(K=\lfloor\mu\rfloor\).  Then \(K\le\mu_+\) and
   \(K/\max\{\mu,K\}\ge1/2\).  Hence \((RSH3)\) implies \((RSH2)\) for this
   \(K\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Soft-support price envelope and panels]
   \label{cor:reported-soft-support-price-panel}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:reported-soft-support-prefix-hardening}.  For each reported
   support slot \(i\), let the available top-prefix cardinalities
   \(\mathcal K_i\) be \(\beta_i\)-dense from below: \(\beta_i\ge1\), \(1\in
   \mathcal K_i\), and for every \(1\le h\le |W_i|\) there is
   \(K\in\mathcal K_i\) with
   \[
      \max\{1,h/\beta_i\}\le K\le h .
      \tag{RSP1}
   \]
   For a soft support report on slot \(i\), put
   \[
      \mu_i=\sum_p\theta_{i,p},
      \qquad
      X_i\le\sum_p\theta_{i,p}d_i(p),
      \qquad
      \mu_{i,+}=\max\{1,\mu_i\},
      \tag{RSP2}
   \]
   and define its soft support price
   \[
      \mathsf P_i^{\rm soft}
      =
      4\beta_i b_iJ_i\psi_i
      \left(
         A_{y_i}\mu_{i,+}^{\rho_i}
         +
         \zeta\mu_{i,+}^{1+\rho_i}
      \right).
      \tag{RSP3}
   \]
   If one report satisfies
   \[
      X_i>\mathsf P_i^{\rm soft},
      \tag{RSP4}
   \]
   then the Hall-cut repair alternative \((HCR2)\) holds.

   More generally, let \(I\) be a finite panel of soft support reports with
   weights \(\lambda_i\ge0\).  If
   \[
      \sum_{i\in I}\lambda_iX_i
      >
      \sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i\mathsf P_i^{\rm soft},
      \tag{RSP5}
   \]
   then some reported top-prefix support repairs the closed Hall cut.  Hence in
