   any residual with no reported closed-shadow repair, every finite soft support
   panel satisfies the reverse inequality in \((RSP5)\).

   The same conclusion holds in Las Vegas build time for a randomized soft
   support panel law.  If the sampled certified surplus
   \[
      Z(s)=
      \sum_{i\in I_s}\lambda_i(s)X_i(s)
      -
      \sum_{i\in I_s}\lambda_i(s)\mathsf P_i^{\rm soft}(s)
      \tag{RSP6}
   \]
   satisfies
   \[
      \E_sZ(s)\ge\Gamma>0,
      \qquad
      Z(s)_+\le U
      \quad\text{almost surely},
      \tag{RSP7}
   \]
   then
   \[
      B\ge\frac U\Gamma\log\frac1\delta
      \tag{RSP8}
   \]
   independent build-time seeds find a deterministic reported top-prefix repair
   with probability at least \(1-\delta\).  Nonpositive sampled panels are
   discarded.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   First consider one report.  If \(\mu_i<2\), take \(h=1\); otherwise take
   \(h=\lfloor\mu_i\rfloor\).  Since \(0\le\theta_{i,p}\le1\), the case
   \(\mu_i\ge2\) has \(h\le |W_i|\).  By \((RSP1)\), choose an available
   \(K\in\mathcal K_i\) with \(\max\{1,h/\beta_i\}\le K\le h\).  Then
   \(K\le\mu_{i,+}\) and
   \[
      \frac{K}{\max\{\mu_i,K\}}\ge\frac1{2\beta_i}.
      \tag{RSP9}
   \]
   Thus \((RSP4)\) implies
   \[
      K\frac{X_i}{\max\{\mu_i,K\}}
      >
      2b_iJ_i\psi_i
      \left(
         A_{y_i}\mu_{i,+}^{\rho_i}
         +
         \zeta\mu_{i,+}^{1+\rho_i}
      \right).
   \]
   Since \(K\le\mu_{i,+}\), the right hand side is at least the recursive price
   at cardinality \(K\).  Hence \((RSH2)\) holds for this \(K\), and
   \cref{cor:reported-soft-support-prefix-hardening} gives \((HCR2)\).

   For the panel statement, if every \(i\) with \(\lambda_i>0\) had
   \(X_i\le\mathsf P_i^{\rm soft}\), then \((RSP5)\) would fail.  Therefore
   some positive-weight record satisfies \((RSP4)\), and the one-report
   implication applies.  The residual statement is the contrapositive.

   Finally, \((RSP7)\) gives \(\Pr[Z(s)>0]\ge\Gamma/U\).  With \(B\) independent
   seeds, all sampled panels are nonpositive with probability at most
   \(\exp(-B\Gamma/U)\).  A positive sampled panel satisfies the deterministic
   panel condition and is then verified into one reported top-prefix support.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Soft-support no-relaxation residual]
   \label{cor:soft-support-no-relaxation-residual}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:reported-soft-support-price-panel}.  For a
   reported support slot \(i\), order \(W_i\) by decreasing point score
   \(d_i(p)\), and let
   \[
      D_i(K)=\sum_{p\in U_{i,K}}d_i(p)
      \tag{RSN1}
   \]
   be the mass of the top \(K\)-prefix, for \(K\in\mathcal K_i\).  If no
   reported closed-shadow repair exists, then every searched cardinality obeys
   the prefix envelope
   \[
      D_i(K)
      \le
      2b_iJ_i\psi_i
      \left(
         A_{y_i}K^{\rho_i}
         +
         \zeta K^{1+\rho_i}
      \right).
      \tag{RSN2}
   \]

   Conversely, suppose a finite family of slots satisfies the envelopes
   \((RSN2)\) for all its available cardinalities.  Then no soft support report
   in this family can satisfy \((RSP4)\), and no finite weighted soft support
   panel can satisfy \((RSP5)\).  Thus the scalar soft-support screen introduces
   no retained fractional object: every positive soft or sampled panel contains
   one ordinary top-prefix violation of \((RSN2)\).

   In particular, when every cardinality is available, the same residual can be
   written as the weak soft envelope
   \[
      \sum_p\theta_pd_i(p)
      \le
      4b_iJ_i\psi_i
      \left(
         A_{y_i}\mu_+^{\rho_i}
         +
         \zeta\mu_+^{1+\rho_i}
      \right),
      \qquad
      \mu_+=\max\left\{1,\sum_p\theta_p\right\},
      \tag{RSN3}
   \]
   for every soft membership \(0\le\theta_p\le1\).  With a
   \(\beta_i\)-dense cardinality net, the same statement holds with the right
   hand side multiplied by \(\beta_i\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((RSN2)\) failed for some available \(K\), then the deterministic
   top-prefix support \(U_{i,K}\), with lower mass certificate \(D_i(K)\), would
   satisfy \((RPR2)\).  By
   \cref{cor:reported-support-price-routing-residual}, this would be a reported
   closed-shadow repair.  This proves the residual prefix envelope.

   For the converse, the proof of
   \cref{cor:reported-soft-support-price-panel} shows that any soft report
   satisfying \((RSP4)\) exposes an available \(K\) for which \((RSH2)\) holds.
   Combining \((RSH2)\) with the rearrangement lower bound \((RSH4)\) gives
   \(D_i(K)\) strictly larger than the right hand side of \((RSN2)\), a
   contradiction.  If a weighted panel satisfied \((RSP5)\), then at least one
   positive-weight report in the panel would satisfy \((RSP4)\), so the same
   contradiction applies.

   The all-cardinality soft envelope is the contrapositive of the coarse-scale
   part of \cref{cor:reported-soft-support-prefix-hardening}.  The
   \(\beta_i\)-dense version is exactly the contrapositive of the one-report
   implication in \cref{cor:reported-soft-support-price-panel}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact-prefix support reports avoid the layer-cake toll]
   \label{cor:exact-prefix-support-mass-no-layer-cake}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:closed-shadow-query-layer-relaxation}.  Fix one certified
   exact-prefix slot \(i\): a container \(W_i\), a fractional layer
   \(y_i\in\operatorname{conv}\{\mathbf 1_Q:Q\in\mathcal Q_i\}\), prices
   \((\psi_i,\rho_i)\) with \(0<\rho_i\le1\), and available top-prefix cardinalities
   \(\mathcal K_i\) which are \(\beta_i\)-dense from below in the sense of
   \((RSP1)\).  Assume that for every \(K\in\mathcal K_i\), the pool contains
   the corresponding certified prefix template with container \(W_i\),
   cardinality \(K\), prices \((\psi_i,\rho_i)\), and Boolean layer family
   \(\mathcal Q_i\).  Put
   \[
      d_i(p)=
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}y_i(\sigma_0),
      \qquad
      A_i=\sum_{\sigma_0}\tau_{\sigma_0}y_i(\sigma_0).
      \tag{EPM1}
   \]

   First, let \(S\subseteq W_i\) be a hard support of size \(s\ge1\), with a
   one-sided mass certificate
   \[
      X\le\sum_{p\in S}d_i(p).
      \tag{EPM2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      X>
      \beta_i\psi_i
      \left(
         A_is^{\rho_i}
         +
         \zeta s^{1+\rho_i}
      \right),
      \tag{EPM3}
   \]
   then the Hall-cut repair alternative \((HCR2)\) holds.

   Second, for soft memberships \(0\le\theta_p\le1\), put
   \[
      \mu=\sum_p\theta_p,
      \qquad
      \mu_+=\max\{1,\mu\},
      \qquad
      X\le\sum_p\theta_pd_i(p).
      \tag{EPM4}
   \]
   If
   \[
      X>
      2\beta_i\psi_i
      \left(
         A_i\mu_+^{\rho_i}
         +
         \zeta\mu_+^{1+\rho_i}
      \right),
      \tag{EPM5}
   \]
   then again \((HCR2)\) holds.

   Consequently, when exact top-prefix columns are available, support-mass and
   soft-support proposals do not need the reported layer-cake factor
   \(2b_iJ_i\).  The verifier replaces the proposed support by one exact
   top-\(K\) prefix and applies the finite-prefix separator directly.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Order \(W_i\) by decreasing \(d_i\), and let \(D_i(K)\) be the top-\(K\)
   prefix mass.  For a hard support \(S\) of size \(s\), choose
   \(K\in\mathcal K_i\) with \(s/\beta_i\le K\le s\).  Since the top \(K\)
   scores have average at least the average of the top \(s\) scores, and the top
   \(s\) scores dominate \(S\),
   \[
      D_i(K)\ge \frac Ks X.
      \tag{EPM6}
   \]
   Condition \((EPM3)\) and \(K/s\ge1/\beta_i\) give
   \[
      D_i(K)>
      \psi_i
      \left(
         A_is^{\rho_i}
         +
         \zeta s^{1+\rho_i}
      \right)
      \ge
      \psi_i
      \left(
         A_iK^{\rho_i}
         +
         \zeta K^{1+\rho_i}
      \right).
   \]
   This is \((QLR2)\) for slot \(i\), so
   \cref{cor:closed-shadow-query-layer-relaxation} gives \((HCR2)\).

   For the soft statement, choose \(h=1\) if \(\mu<2\), and
   \(h=\lfloor\mu\rfloor\) otherwise.  Let \(K\in\mathcal K_i\) satisfy
   \(\max\{1,h/\beta_i\}\le K\le h\).  The rearrangement bound \((RSH4)\)
   gives
   \[
      D_i(K)\ge K\frac{X}{\max\{\mu,K\}},
      \qquad
      \frac{K}{\max\{\mu,K\}}\ge\frac1{2\beta_i}.
      \tag{EPM7}
   \]
   Condition \((EPM5)\) and \(K\le\mu_+\) again imply \((QLR2)\), hence
   \((HCR2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Aggregate exact-prefix support-mass panel]
   \label{cor:aggregate-exact-prefix-support-mass-panel}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:exact-prefix-support-mass-no-layer-cake}.  Let \(I\) be a finite
   panel of exact-prefix support reports with weights \(\lambda_i\ge0\).  Each
   report is of one of the following two types.

   A hard report specifies \(S_i\subseteq W_i\), \(s_i=|S_i|\ge1\), and
   \[
      X_i\le\sum_{p\in S_i}d_i(p),
      \qquad
      P_i^{\rm ex}=
      \beta_i\psi_i
      \left(
         A_is_i^{\rho_i}
         +
         \zeta s_i^{1+\rho_i}
      \right).
      \tag{EPP1}
   \]
   A soft report specifies memberships \(0\le\theta_{i,p}\le1\),
   \[
      \mu_i=\sum_p\theta_{i,p},
      \qquad
      \mu_{i,+}=\max\{1,\mu_i\},
      \qquad
      X_i\le\sum_p\theta_{i,p}d_i(p),
      \tag{EPP2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      P_i^{\rm ex}=
      2\beta_i\psi_i
      \left(
         A_i\mu_{i,+}^{\rho_i}
         +
         \zeta\mu_{i,+}^{1+\rho_i}
      \right).
      \tag{EPP3}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_{i\in I}\lambda_iX_i
      >
      \sum_{i\in I}\lambda_iP_i^{\rm ex},
      \tag{EPP4}
   \]
   then the Hall-cut repair alternative \((HCR2)\) holds.  Consequently, in any
   residual with no reported closed-shadow repair, every finite exact-prefix
   support-mass panel obeys the reverse inequality in \((EPP4)\).

   The same conclusion holds in Las Vegas build time for a randomized
   exact-prefix support panel law.  If the sampled certified surplus
   \[
      Z(s)=
      \sum_{i\in I_s}\lambda_i(s)X_i(s)
      -
      \sum_{i\in I_s}\lambda_i(s)P_i^{\rm ex}(s)
      \tag{EPP5}
   \]
   satisfies
   \[
      \E_sZ(s)\ge\Gamma>0,
      \qquad
      Z(s)_+\le U
      \quad\text{almost surely},
      \tag{EPP6}
   \]
   then
   \[
      B\ge\frac U\Gamma\log\frac1\delta
      \tag{EPP7}
   \]
   independent build-time seeds find a deterministic exact-prefix repair with
   probability at least \(1-\delta\).  Nonpositive sampled panels are discarded.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If every positive-weight report had \(X_i\le P_i^{\rm ex}\), then
   \((EPP4)\) would fail.  Thus some positive-weight report has
   \(X_i>P_i^{\rm ex}\).  If it is hard, this is \((EPM3)\); if it is soft, it
   is \((EPM5)\).  In either case
   \cref{cor:exact-prefix-support-mass-no-layer-cake} gives \((HCR2)\).  The
   residual statement is the contrapositive.

   The sampled form follows from
   \(\Pr[Z(s)>0]\ge\Gamma/U\), so \(B\) independent samples are all nonpositive
   with probability at most \(\exp(-B\Gamma/U)\).  A positive sampled panel
   satisfies the deterministic part and is verified into one exact top-prefix
   repair.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Optimized exact-prefix support price]
   \label{cor:optimized-exact-prefix-support-price}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:exact-prefix-support-mass-no-layer-cake}.  For a hard support
   report with \(S_i\subseteq W_i\), \(s_i=|S_i|\ge1\), and
   \(X_i\le\sum_{p\in S_i}d_i(p)\), define the optimized exact-prefix price
   \[
      P_i^{\rm opt}(s_i)
      =
      \inf_{\substack{K\in\mathcal K_i\\ 1\le K\le s_i}}
      s_i\psi_i
      \left(
         A_iK^{\rho_i-1}
         +
         \zeta K^{\rho_i}
      \right).
      \tag{EOP1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      X_i>P_i^{\rm opt}(s_i),
      \tag{EOP2}
   \]
   then the Hall-cut repair alternative \((HCR2)\) holds.

   For a soft report with memberships \(0\le\theta_{i,p}\le1\),
   \[
      \mu_i=\sum_p\theta_{i,p},
      \qquad
      X_i\le\sum_p\theta_{i,p}d_i(p),
      \tag{EOP3}
   \]
   define
   \[
      P_i^{\rm opt}(\mu_i)
      =
      \inf_{K\in\mathcal K_i}
      \max\{\mu_i,K\}\psi_i
      \left(
         A_iK^{\rho_i-1}
         +
         \zeta K^{\rho_i}
      \right).
      \tag{EOP4}
   \]
   If
   \[
      X_i>P_i^{\rm opt}(\mu_i),
      \tag{EOP5}
   \]
   then \((HCR2)\) holds.

   More generally, any finite panel of hard or soft reports with weights
   \(\lambda_i\ge0\) and the corresponding optimized prices satisfies
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_iX_i>
      \sum_i\lambda_iP_i^{\rm opt}
      \tag{EOP6}
   \]
   only if some report exposes a deterministic exact top-prefix repair.  Hence
   in a surviving residual every such optimized exact-prefix panel obeys the
   reverse inequality in \((EOP6)\).

   Thus the support-size price in \((EPP1)\) and soft-mass price in \((EPP3)\)
   may be replaced by the discrete optimized price-density expressions
   \((EOP1)\) and \((EOP4)\).  The verifier chooses the winning cardinality
   after seeing the report; the proposal mechanism need not guess the recursive
   scale.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For the hard report, choose \(K\in\mathcal K_i\), \(K\le s_i\), whose value
   in \((EOP1)\) is strictly below \(X_i\).  As in \((EPM6)\), the top-\(K\)
   prefix mass satisfies
   \[
      D_i(K)\ge\frac{K}{s_i}X_i.
   \]
   The choice of \(K\) gives
   \[
      \frac{K}{s_i}X_i
      >
      \psi_i
      \left(
         A_iK^{\rho_i}
         +
         \zeta K^{1+\rho_i}
      \right).
   \]
   Therefore \((QLR2)\) holds for this cardinality, and
   \cref{cor:closed-shadow-query-layer-relaxation} gives \((HCR2)\).

   For the soft report, choose \(K\in\mathcal K_i\) whose value in \((EOP4)\)
   is strictly below \(X_i\).  The rearrangement bound \((RSH4)\) gives
   \[
      D_i(K)\ge K\frac{X_i}{\max\{\mu_i,K\}}.
   \]
   The choice of \(K\) implies this lower bound is larger than
   \(\psi_i(A_iK^{\rho_i}+\zeta K^{1+\rho_i})\), so \((QLR2)\) again holds.

   For the panel statement, if every positive-weight report had
   \(X_i\le P_i^{\rm opt}\), then \((EOP6)\) would fail.  Hence some report
   satisfies its one-report optimized condition, and the preceding paragraphs
   apply.  The residual statement is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Clipped optimized exact-prefix price]
   \label{cor:clipped-optimized-exact-prefix-price}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:optimized-exact-prefix-support-price}, and
   assume the available cardinalities \(\mathcal K_i\) are \(\beta_i\)-dense
   from below.  For \(m\ge1\), define
   \[
      f_i(K)=A_iK^{\rho_i-1}+\zeta K^{\rho_i}.
      \tag{EOC1}
   \]
   Let \(K_i^\natural(m)\in[1,m]\) be the clipped continuous minimizer of
   \(f_i\) on \([1,m]\):
   \[
      K_i^\natural(m)=
      \begin{cases}
      1, & A_i=0,\\
      m, & \zeta=0\text{ and }A_i>0,\\
      \min\!\left\{m,\max\!\left\{1,
      \dfrac{(1-\rho_i)A_i}{\rho_i\zeta}\right\}\right\},
         & A_i>0,\ \zeta>0 .
      \end{cases}
      \tag{EOC2}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      \Theta_i(m)=\psi_i f_i\!\left(K_i^\natural(m)\right).
      \tag{EOC3}
   \]

   For a hard support report of size \(s_i\), if
   \[
      X_i>\beta_i s_i\Theta_i(s_i),
      \tag{EOC4}
   \]
   then the Hall-cut repair alternative \((HCR2)\) holds.  For a soft report
   with \(\mu_i=\sum_p\theta_{i,p}\) and \(\mu_{i,+}=\max\{1,\mu_i\}\), if
   \[
      X_i>\beta_i\mu_{i,+}\Theta_i(\mu_{i,+}),
      \tag{EOC5}
   \]
   then \((HCR2)\) holds.

   More generally, any finite hard/soft panel whose aggregate certified mass
   beats the sum of the right sides of \((EOC4)\)--\((EOC5)\) contains one
   deterministic exact top-prefix repair.  Thus the optimized discrete prices
   \((EOP1)\) and \((EOP4)\) may be replaced, up to the cardinality-net factor
   \(\beta_i\), by the closed clipped density \(\Theta_i\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(m\ge1\), and abbreviate \(K^\natural=K_i^\natural(m)\).  By
   \((RSP1)\), there is an available \(K\in\mathcal K_i\) with
   \[
      \max\{1,K^\natural/\beta_i\}\le K\le K^\natural .
      \tag{EOC6}
   \]
   Since \(0<\rho_i\le1\), this implies
   \[
      f_i(K)
      =
      A_iK^{\rho_i-1}+\zeta K^{\rho_i}
      \le
      \beta_i
      \left(
         A_i(K^\natural)^{\rho_i-1}
         +
         \zeta (K^\natural)^{\rho_i}
      \right)
      =
      \beta_i f_i(K^\natural).
      \tag{EOC7}
   \]
   Also \(K\le K^\natural\le m\).

   For a hard support of size \(s_i\), take \(m=s_i\).  Equation \((EOC7)\)
   gives
   \[
      P_i^{\rm opt}(s_i)
      \le
      \beta_i s_i\psi_i f_i(K_i^\natural(s_i))
      =
      \beta_i s_i\Theta_i(s_i).
   \]
   Hence \((EOC4)\) implies \((EOP2)\), and
   \cref{cor:optimized-exact-prefix-support-price} gives \((HCR2)\).

   For a soft report, take \(m=\mu_{i,+}\).  If \(\mu_i\ge1\), then the
   available \(K\) above satisfies \(K\le\mu_i\), so
   \[
      P_i^{\rm opt}(\mu_i)
      \le
      \mu_i\psi_i f_i(K)
      \le
      \beta_i\mu_{i,+}\Theta_i(\mu_{i,+}).
   \]
   If \(\mu_i<1\), the cardinality \(K=1\) is available and gives
   \(P_i^{\rm opt}(\mu_i)\le\Theta_i(1)\le
   \beta_i\mu_{i,+}\Theta_i(\mu_{i,+})\).  Thus \((EOC5)\) implies
   \((EOP5)\), and again
   \cref{cor:optimized-exact-prefix-support-price} applies.

   The panel statement follows because aggregate surplus against these clipped
   upper bounds is also aggregate surplus against the optimized prices in
   \((EOP6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Clipped exact-prefix density residual]
   \label{cor:clipped-exact-prefix-density-residual}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:clipped-optimized-exact-prefix-price}.
   Suppose no exact-prefix support report in the searched family gives a
   reported closed-shadow repair.  Then every hard support report
   \(S_i\subseteq W_i\), \(s_i=|S_i|\ge1\), with
   \(X_i\le\sum_{p\in S_i}d_i(p)\), obeys the density envelope
   \[
      \frac{X_i}{s_i}
      \le
      \beta_i\Theta_i(s_i).
      \tag{ECD1}
   \]
   Every soft report with \(0\le\theta_{i,p}\le1\),
   \(\mu_i=\sum_p\theta_{i,p}\), \(\mu_{i,+}=\max\{1,\mu_i\}\), and
   \(X_i\le\sum_p\theta_{i,p}d_i(p)\), obeys
   \[
      \frac{X_i}{\mu_{i,+}}
      \le
      \beta_i\Theta_i(\mu_{i,+}).
      \tag{ECD2}
   \]

   Conversely, any hard or soft report violating \((ECD1)\) or \((ECD2)\)
   exposes a deterministic exact top-prefix repair.  More generally, any finite
   or sampled panel with aggregate excess over the corresponding clipped
   density prices contains one such prefix repair.  Therefore the surviving
   no-layer-cake dense obstruction for this proposal family is precisely the
   clipped support-density envelope \((ECD1)\)--\((ECD2)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   A violation of \((ECD1)\) is exactly \((EOC4)\), and a violation of
   \((ECD2)\) is exactly \((EOC5)\).  Thus the positive implications and the
   panel statement are \cref{cor:clipped-optimized-exact-prefix-price}.  The
   residual envelopes are the contrapositives.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Centerwise clipped exact-prefix proposal law]
   \label{cor:centerwise-clipped-exact-prefix-proposal-law}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:clipped-exact-prefix-density-residual}.
   A centerwise clipped proposal is a finite or sampled report \(R\) attached to
   one exact-prefix slot \(i\), of one of the following two types.

   In the hard case, \(R\) gives a support \(S_R\subseteq W_i\), its size
   \(m_R=|S_R|\ge1\), and a one-sided lower mass certificate
   \[
      0\le X_R\le\sum_{p\in S_R}d_i(p).
      \tag{CCP1}
   \]
   Its clipped surplus is
   \[
      Z(R)=X_R-\beta_i m_R\Theta_i(m_R).
      \tag{CCP2}
   \]
   In the soft case, \(R\) gives memberships \(0\le\theta_{R,p}\le1\),
   \[
      \mu_R=\sum_p\theta_{R,p},\qquad
      m_R=\max\{1,\mu_R\},
      \qquad
      0\le X_R\le\sum_p\theta_{R,p}d_i(p),
      \tag{CCP3}
   \]
   and its clipped surplus is again
   \[
      Z(R)=X_R-\beta_i m_R\Theta_i(m_R).
      \tag{CCP4}
   \]
   If a finite weighted panel of such proposals satisfies
   \[
      \sum_R\lambda_R Z(R)>0,
      \qquad \lambda_R\ge0,
      \tag{CCP5}
   \]
   then one deterministic exact top-prefix report gives a closed-shadow repair.
   Consequently, if no exact-prefix repair exists in the searched family, every
   finite centerwise clipped proposal panel has nonpositive total surplus.

   The same statement holds in Las Vegas build time.  If a randomized proposal
   routine returns a finite panel with certified surplus \(Z(s)\) satisfying
   \[
      \E_sZ(s)\ge\Gamma>0,
      \qquad
      Z(s)_+\le U
      \quad\text{almost surely},
      \tag{CCP6}
   \]
   then
   \[
      B\ge\frac U\Gamma\log\frac1\delta
      \tag{CCP7}
   \]
   independent build-time seeds find a deterministic exact-prefix repair with
   probability at least \(1-\delta\).  Failed or nonpositive sampled proposals
   are discarded and are not retained in the index.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((CCP5)\) holds, some positive-weight report has \(Z(R)>0\).  In the hard
   case this is exactly a violation of \((ECD1)\), and in the soft case it is
   exactly a violation of \((ECD2)\).  By
   \cref{cor:clipped-exact-prefix-density-residual}, either violation
   materializes one deterministic exact top-prefix repair.  The nonpositive
   panel statement is the contrapositive.

   For the sampled statement, \((CCP6)\) gives
   \[
      \Pr[Z(s)>0]\ge\frac{\Gamma}{U}.
   \]
   Hence \(B\) independent seeds all fail to produce positive surplus with
   probability at most \(\exp(-B\Gamma/U)\).  A positive sampled panel satisfies
   the deterministic part and is verified into one retained exact-prefix repair.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:centerwise-clipped-exact-prefix-proposal-law} is the no-layer-cake
interface for facility, additive-quantization, list-decoding, lattice-decoding,
or \(k\)-means++-style dense proposals.  Such routines may choose centers,
supports, or soft memberships by any expensive build-time rule, including rules
adapted to the current dual prices.  The verifier only reads the one-sided mass
certificate and the clipped recursive density price.  Positive expected surplus
is enough by averaging, while the retained object is again the ordinary
deterministic top prefix from
\cref{cor:clipped-exact-prefix-density-residual}.

\begin{corollary}[Balanced Hall-shadow density screen]
   \label{cor:balanced-hall-shadow-density-screen}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:no-merge-hall-shadow-envelope}.  Fix a
   repair template \(y\) with \(0<\rho_y<1\), \(A_y>0\), and \(\zeta>0\).  Put
   \[
      K_y^\circ=\frac{(1-\rho_y)A_y}{\rho_y\zeta},
      \qquad
      C_{\rho_y}=\rho_y^{-\rho_y}(1-\rho_y)^{-(1-\rho_y)} .
      \tag{BHE1}
   \]
   For an available prefix cardinality \(K\in\mathcal K_y\), define the
   cut-shadow prefix density
   \[
      \Delta_A(y,K)=\frac{D_A(y,K)}{K}.
      \tag{BHE2}
   \]
   If for some \(a\ge1\),
   \[
      a^{-1}K_y^\circ\le K\le aK_y^\circ
      \tag{BHE3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \Delta_A(y,K)>
      a\psi_yC_{\rho_y}A_y^{\rho_y}\zeta^{1-\rho_y},
      \tag{BHE4}
   \]
   then the prefix \((y,K)\) satisfies \((NHE2)\), and hence gives a
   one-record Hall-shadow merge.

   Conversely, if no available Hall-shadow merge exists, then every available
   balanced prefix satisfying \((BHE3)\) obeys the reverse inequality in
   \((BHE4)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(\rho=\rho_y\), \(A=A_y\), and \(K^\circ=K_y^\circ\).  The per-point
   reduced-cost threshold at cardinality \(K\) is
   \[
      \psi_y\left(AK^{\rho-1}+\zeta K^\rho\right).
   \]
   The function \(f(K)=AK^{\rho-1}+\zeta K^\rho\) has stationary point
   \(K^\circ=(1-\rho)A/(\rho\zeta)\), and
   \[
      f(K^\circ)=C_{\rho}A^\rho\zeta^{1-\rho}.
   \]
   If \(K=\lambda K^\circ\) with \(\lambda\in[a^{-1},a]\), then
   \[
      f(K)=
      \lambda^{\rho-1}A(K^\circ)^{\rho-1}
      +
      \lambda^\rho\zeta(K^\circ)^\rho
      \le a f(K^\circ).
   \]
   Thus \((BHE4)\) implies
   \[
      D_A(y,K)
      =
      K\Delta_A(y,K)
      >
      \psi_y\left(A_yK^{\rho_y}+\zeta K^{1+\rho_y}\right),
   \]
   which is \((NHE2)\).  The converse is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:balanced-hall-shadow-density-screen} isolates the scale at which a
Hall-shadow merge should be easiest to find.  When both query and storage prices
are active, a repair proposal does not need to search all prefix sizes: a
template with enough cut-shadow density near \(K_y^\circ\) immediately violates
the no-merge envelope.

\begin{corollary}[Clipped Hall-shadow price-density screen]
   \label{cor:clipped-hall-shadow-density-screen}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:no-merge-hall-shadow-envelope}.  Fix a
   repair template \(y\) with \(0<\rho_y<1\), and put
   \(m_y=|W_y|\).  For \(1\le K\le m_y\), write the per-point price density as
   \[
      f_y(K)=A_yK^{\rho_y-1}+\zeta K^{\rho_y}.
      \tag{CHP1}
   \]
   If \(A_y=\zeta=0\), then any available \(K\) with \(D_A(y,K)>0\) gives a
   one-record Hall-shadow merge.

   Otherwise define the clipped minimizer
   \[
      K_y^\natural=
      \begin{cases}
      1, & A_y=0,\\
      m_y, & \zeta=0,\\
      \min\!\left\{m_y,\max\!\left\{1,
      \dfrac{(1-\rho_y)A_y}{\rho_y\zeta}\right\}\right\},
         & A_y>0,\ \zeta>0 .
      \end{cases}
      \tag{CHP2}
   \]
   Let \(a\ge1\).  If an available cardinality \(K\in\mathcal K_y\) satisfies
   \[
      a^{-1}K_y^\natural\le K\le aK_y^\natural
      \tag{CHP3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \Delta_A(y,K)>
      a\psi_y f_y(K_y^\natural),
      \tag{CHP4}
   \]
   then \((y,K)\) satisfies \((NHE2)\), and hence gives a one-record
   Hall-shadow merge.

   Conversely, if no available Hall-shadow merge exists, then every available
   prefix satisfying \((CHP3)\) obeys the reverse inequality in \((CHP4)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The case \(A_y=\zeta=0\) is immediate from \((NHE2)\).  Assume from now on
   that at least one price is positive.  It is enough to prove
   \[
      f_y(K)\le a f_y(K_y^\natural)
      \tag{CHP5}
   \]
   whenever \((CHP3)\) holds.  Then \((CHP4)\) implies
   \[
      D_A(y,K)
      =
      K\Delta_A(y,K)
      >
      \psi_yKf_y(K)
      =
      \psi_y\left(A_yK^{\rho_y}+\zeta K^{1+\rho_y}\right),
   \]
   which is \((NHE2)\).

   If \(A_y>0\) and \(\zeta>0\) and the stationary point
   \((1-\rho_y)A_y/(\rho_y\zeta)\) lies in \([1,m_y]\), then
   \(K_y^\natural\) is that stationary point.  The same calculation as in
   \cref{cor:balanced-hall-shadow-density-screen} gives \((CHP5)\).

   If \(K_y^\natural=1\), then for \(1\le K\le a\),
   \[
      A_yK^{\rho_y-1}\le A_y,
      \qquad
      \zeta K^{\rho_y}\le a\zeta ,
   \]
   and hence \(f_y(K)\le a(A_y+\zeta)=a f_y(1)\).  This includes the case
   \(A_y=0\).

   If \(K_y^\natural=m_y\), then \(m_y/a\le K\le m_y\), and
   \[
      A_yK^{\rho_y-1}
      \le
      a^{1-\rho_y}A_ym_y^{\rho_y-1}
      \le
      aA_ym_y^{\rho_y-1},
      \qquad
      \zeta K^{\rho_y}\le a\zeta m_y^{\rho_y}.
   \]
   Thus \(f_y(K)\le a f_y(m_y)\).  This includes the case \(\zeta=0\).

   The converse is again the contrapositive of the merge implication.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:clipped-hall-shadow-density-screen} removes the artificial internal
balance assumption.  Each template now has one canonical proposal scale: the
minimizer of the recursive price density clipped to the available prefix range.
If query price dominates, the scale moves to the largest prefix; if storage
price dominates, it moves to the smallest prefix.  Thus a build-time proposal
routine can target a single clipped scale per template instead of splitting
into query-dominated, storage-dominated, and balanced cases.

\begin{corollary}[Fractional clipped Hall-shadow density panel]
   \label{cor:fractional-clipped-hall-shadow-density-panel}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:clipped-hall-shadow-density-screen}.  Let \(i\in I\) range over a
   finite panel of verified clipped Hall-shadow records with nonnegative
   weights \(\lambda_i\).  Record \(i\) consists of a repair template \(y_i\),
   an available prefix cardinality \(K_i\in\mathcal K_{y_i}\), and a slack
   factor \(a_i\ge1\) such that, when
   \(A_{y_i}\) and \(\zeta\) are not both zero,
   \[
      a_i^{-1}K_{y_i}^\natural\le K_i\le a_iK_{y_i}^\natural .
      \tag{FCH1}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      \Delta_i=\Delta_A(y_i,K_i),
      \qquad
      \Theta_i=
      \begin{cases}
      0, & A_{y_i}=\zeta=0,\\
      a_i\psi_{y_i}f_{y_i}(K_{y_i}^\natural),
         & \text{otherwise}.
      \end{cases}
      \tag{FCH2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_iK_i(\Delta_i-\Theta_i)>0,
      \tag{FCH3}
   \]
   then some record in the panel gives a one-record Hall-shadow merge.

   Consequently, if no available Hall-shadow merge exists, every finite
   nonnegative clipped panel has nonpositive surplus \((FCH3)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Positive total surplus implies that some record has
   \(\Delta_i>\Theta_i\).  If \(A_{y_i}=\zeta=0\), then
   \(D_A(y_i,K_i)=K_i\Delta_i>0\), so
   \cref{cor:clipped-hall-shadow-density-screen} gives a merge.  Otherwise
   \((FCH1)\)--\((FCH2)\) are exactly \((CHP3)\)--\((CHP4)\) for that record,
   and the same corollary applies.  The nonpositive-panel statement is the
   contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Support-mass clipped Hall-shadow reporter]
   \label{cor:support-mass-clipped-hall-shadow-reporter}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:fractional-clipped-hall-shadow-density-panel}.  A support-mass
   record consists of a repair template \(y\), a subset \(U\subseteq W_y\), a
   certified size bound \(s\ge |U|\), a certified lower shadow mass
   \[
      0\le X\le\sum_{p\in U}d_{A,y}(p),
      \tag{SMC1}
   \]
   an available prefix cardinality \(K\in\mathcal K_y\), and a slack factor
   \(a\ge1\) satisfying the clipped-scale condition \((FCH1)\) when
   \(A_y\) and \(\zeta\) are not both zero.  Define the certified density lower
   bound
   \[
      \widehat\Delta=\frac{X}{\max\{s,K\}},
      \tag{SMC2}
   \]
   and define \(\Theta\) from \(y,K,a\) as in \((FCH2)\).

   If a finite support-mass panel with nonnegative weights \(\lambda_i\)
   satisfies
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_iK_i(\widehat\Delta_i-\Theta_i)>0,
      \tag{SMC3}
   \]
   then the same records satisfy the clipped Hall-shadow panel surplus
   \((FCH3)\), and hence some record gives a one-record Hall-shadow merge.

   Consequently a proposal routine does not need to materialize the exact
   top-\(K_i\) prefix while searching.  It may certify only a support size and a
   one-sided shadow mass; the exact top prefix is used only by the verifier
   after the coarse surplus test is positive.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For one record, let \(D_A(y,K)\) be the top-\(K\) shadow mass from
   \((NHE1)\).  If \(K\ge |U|\), then the top \(K\) points of \(W_y\) have
   shadow mass at least \(\sum_{p\in U}d_{A,y}(p)\ge X\).  Since
   \(\max\{s,K\}\ge K\), this gives
   \[
      \frac{D_A(y,K)}{K}\ge\frac{X}{K}\ge\frac{X}{\max\{s,K\}}.
   \]
   If \(K<|U|\), the top \(K\) points of \(W_y\) have average shadow mass at
   least the average over \(U\), so
   \[
      D_A(y,K)
      \ge
      K\,\frac{\sum_{p\in U}d_{A,y}(p)}{|U|}
      \ge
      K\,\frac{X}{s}
      =
      K\,\frac{X}{\max\{s,K\}},
   \]
   where the last equality uses \(K<|U|\le s\).  Thus in all cases
   \[
      \Delta_A(y,K)=\frac{D_A(y,K)}K\ge\widehat\Delta .
      \tag{SMC4}
   \]
   Summing \((SMC4)\) with weights \(\lambda_iK_i\) shows that \((SMC3)\)
   implies \((FCH3)\).  The merge conclusion is
   \cref{cor:fractional-clipped-hall-shadow-density-panel}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sampled support-mass clipped Hall-shadow search]
   \label{cor:sampled-support-mass-clipped-hall-shadow-search}
   In the setting of
   \cref{cor:support-mass-clipped-hall-shadow-reporter}, suppose a randomized
   build-time proposal routine returns a finite support-mass panel \(I_s\) on
   seed \(s\), and define
   \[
      Z(s)=
      \sum_{i\in I_s}
      \lambda_{s,i}K_{s,i}
      \bigl(\widehat\Delta_{s,i}-\Theta_{s,i}\bigr).
      \tag{SSM1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \E_sZ(s)\ge\Gamma>0,
      \qquad
      Z(s)_+\le M
      \quad\text{almost surely},
      \tag{SSM2}
   \]
   then \(B\) independent build-time seeds contain a valid one-record
   Hall-shadow merge with probability at least
   \[
      1-\exp\left(-\frac{B\Gamma}{M}\right).
      \tag{SSM3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   As in \cref{cor:sampled-clipped-hall-shadow-density-search},
   \((SSM2)\) gives \(\Pr[Z(s)>0]\ge\Gamma/M\).  A seed with \(Z(s)>0\) is a
   positive support-mass panel by
   \cref{cor:support-mass-clipped-hall-shadow-reporter}, hence verifies into a
   deterministic one-record Hall-shadow merge.  The failure probability over
   \(B\) independent seeds is at most \(\exp(-B\Gamma/M)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Soft-mass clipped Hall-shadow reporter]
   \label{cor:soft-mass-clipped-hall-shadow-reporter}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:fractional-clipped-hall-shadow-density-panel}.  A soft-mass record
   consists of a repair template \(y\), fractional memberships
   \[
      0\le \theta_p\le1\qquad(p\in W_y),
   \]
   a certified lower shadow mass
   \[
      0\le X\le \sum_{p\in W_y}\theta_pd_{A,y}(p),
      \tag{SHM1}
   \]
   an available prefix cardinality \(K\in\mathcal K_y\), and a slack factor
   \(a\ge1\) satisfying the clipped-scale condition \((FCH1)\) when
   \(A_y\) and \(\zeta\) are not both zero.  Put
   \[
      \mu=\sum_{p\in W_y}\theta_p,
      \qquad
      \widetilde\Delta=\frac{X}{\max\{\mu,K\}},
      \tag{SHM2}
   \]
   and define \(\Theta\) from \(y,K,a\) as in \((FCH2)\).

   If a finite soft-mass panel with nonnegative weights \(\lambda_i\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_iK_i(\widetilde\Delta_i-\Theta_i)>0,
      \tag{SHM3}
   \]
   then the same records satisfy the clipped Hall-shadow panel surplus
   \((FCH3)\), and hence some record gives a one-record Hall-shadow merge.

   Consequently fractional facility assignments, additive-quantization posterior
   weights, learned scores converted to memberships, or list-decoder soft
   reliabilities may be verified directly.  The hard top-\(K\) prefix remains
   only the retained column chosen by the verifier.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix one record and order \(W_y=\{p_1,p_2,\ldots\}\) so that
   \(d_{A,y}(p_1)\ge d_{A,y}(p_2)\ge\cdots\).  Let
   \(D_K=D_A(y,K)=\sum_{i\le K}d_{A,y}(p_i)\).  We claim
   \[
      \frac{D_K}{K}
      \ge
      \frac{X}{\max\{\mu,K\}} .
      \tag{SHM4}
   \]
   If \(\mu\le K\), then the linear functional
   \(\sum_p\theta_pd_{A,y}(p)\) under the constraints
   \(0\le\theta_p\le1\) and \(\sum_p\theta_p=\mu\) is maximized by placing
   weight on the largest degrees.  Since \(K\ge\mu\) and all degrees are
   nonnegative, this maximum is at most \(D_K\).  Hence
   \(X\le D_K\), which gives \((SHM4)\).

   If \(\mu>K\), the same rearrangement bound gives
   \[
      \sum_p\theta_pd_{A,y}(p)
      \le
      \mu\,\frac{D_K}{K},
   \]
   because the maximizing fractional vector fills the largest degrees first,
   and the prefix average of a nonincreasing nonnegative sequence decreases as
   the fractional prefix length increases.  Equivalently, writing
   \(\mu=h+\lambda\), \(h=\lfloor\mu\rfloor\), \(0\le\lambda<1\), the maximum
   is
   \(\sum_{i\le h}d_{A,y}(p_i)+\lambda d_{A,y}(p_{h+1})\), whose average over
   mass \(\mu>K\) is at most \(D_K/K\).  Thus \(X/\mu\le D_K/K\), which is
   \((SHM4)\).

   Equation \((SHM4)\) says precisely that
   \(\Delta_A(y,K)\ge\widetilde\Delta\).  Multiplying by
   \(\lambda_iK_i\) and summing over the panel shows that \((SHM3)\) implies
   \((FCH3)\).  The merge conclusion is
   \cref{cor:fractional-clipped-hall-shadow-density-panel}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sampled soft-mass clipped Hall-shadow search]
   \label{cor:sampled-soft-mass-clipped-hall-shadow-search}
   In the setting of
   \cref{cor:soft-mass-clipped-hall-shadow-reporter}, suppose a randomized
   build-time proposal routine returns a finite soft-mass panel \(I_s\) on seed
   \(s\), and define
   \[
      Z(s)=
      \sum_{i\in I_s}
      \lambda_{s,i}K_{s,i}
      \bigl(\widetilde\Delta_{s,i}-\Theta_{s,i}\bigr).
      \tag{SSH1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \E_sZ(s)\ge\Gamma>0,
      \qquad
      Z(s)_+\le M
      \quad\text{almost surely},
      \tag{SSH2}
   \]
   then \(B\) independent build-time seeds contain a valid one-record
   Hall-shadow merge with probability at least
   \[
      1-\exp\left(-\frac{B\Gamma}{M}\right).
      \tag{SSH3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The same positive-part argument as in
   \cref{cor:sampled-clipped-hall-shadow-density-search} gives
   \(\Pr[Z(s)>0]\ge\Gamma/M\).  A positive seed is converted by
   \cref{cor:soft-mass-clipped-hall-shadow-reporter} into a deterministic
   one-record Hall-shadow merge.  Independent repetition gives \((SSH3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact-scale soft Hall-shadow reporter]
   \label{cor:exact-scale-soft-hall-shadow-reporter}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:no-merge-hall-shadow-envelope}.  A
   soft-mass record consists of a repair template \(y\), fractional memberships
   \(0\le\theta_p\le1\) on \(W_y\), a certified lower shadow mass
   \[
      0\le X\le \sum_{p\in W_y}\theta_pd_{A,y}(p),
      \tag{ESH1}
   \]
   and an available prefix cardinality \(K\in\mathcal K_y\).  Put
   \[
      \mu=\sum_{p\in W_y}\theta_p,
      \qquad
      \widetilde\Delta=\frac{X}{\max\{\mu,K\}},
      \qquad
      f_y(K)=A_yK^{\rho_y-1}+\zeta K^{\rho_y}.
      \tag{ESH2}
   \]
   If a finite exact-scale soft panel with nonnegative weights \(\lambda_i\)
   satisfies
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_iK_i
      \left(\widetilde\Delta_i-\psi_{y_i}f_{y_i}(K_i)\right)>0,
      \tag{ESH3}
   \]
   then some record in the panel gives a one-record Hall-shadow merge.

   Equivalently, a single soft proposal \((y,\theta,X)\) succeeds whenever
   \[
      \max_{K\in\mathcal K_y}
      K\left(
         \frac{X}{\max\{\sum_p\theta_p,K\}}
         -\psi_y\left(A_yK^{\rho_y-1}+\zeta K^{\rho_y}\right)
      \right)>0.
      \tag{ESH4}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The rearrangement argument in
   \cref{cor:soft-mass-clipped-hall-shadow-reporter} proves, for every record,
   \[
      \Delta_A(y,K)=\frac{D_A(y,K)}K
      \ge
      \frac{X}{\max\{\mu,K\}}
      =
      \widetilde\Delta .
      \tag{ESH5}
   \]
   Therefore \((ESH3)\) implies
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_iK_i
      \left(\Delta_A(y_i,K_i)-\psi_{y_i}f_{y_i}(K_i)\right)>0.
   \]
   Some record has a positive summand, which is exactly
   \[
      D_A(y_i,K_i)>
      \psi_{y_i}
      \left(
         A_{y_i}K_i^{\rho_{y_i}}
         +\zeta K_i^{1+\rho_{y_i}}
      \right).
   \]
   This is \((NHE2)\), so
   \cref{cor:no-merge-hall-shadow-envelope} gives a one-record Hall-shadow
   merge.  The optimized form \((ESH4)\) is the one-record version of the same
   inequality after maximizing over the verified cardinality net.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sampled exact-scale soft Hall-shadow search]
   \label{cor:sampled-exact-scale-soft-hall-shadow-search}
   In the setting of \cref{cor:exact-scale-soft-hall-shadow-reporter}, suppose
   a randomized build-time proposal routine returns a finite exact-scale soft
   panel \(I_s\) on seed \(s\), and define
   \[
      Z(s)=
      \sum_{i\in I_s}\lambda_{s,i}K_{s,i}
      \left(\widetilde\Delta_{s,i}-\psi_{y_{s,i}}f_{y_{s,i}}(K_{s,i})\right).
      \tag{SES1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \E_sZ(s)\ge\Gamma>0,
      \qquad
      Z(s)_+\le M
      \quad\text{almost surely},
      \tag{SES2}
   \]
   then \(B\) independent build-time seeds contain a valid one-record
   Hall-shadow merge with probability at least
   \[
      1-\exp\left(-\frac{B\Gamma}{M}\right).
      \tag{SES3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   From \((SES2)\), \(\E Z_+\ge\Gamma\).  Since \(Z_+\le M\), one seed has
   \(Z(s)>0\) with probability at least \(\Gamma/M\).  Such a seed is a
   positive exact-scale soft panel, hence verifies into a deterministic
   Hall-shadow merge by
   \cref{cor:exact-scale-soft-hall-shadow-reporter}.  Independent repetition
   gives \((SES3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Shadow-routing exact-scale soft reporter]
   \label{cor:shadow-routing-exact-scale-soft-reporter}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:exact-scale-soft-hall-shadow-reporter}.  Let \(\mathcal Y\) be a
   finite repair-template family.  A fractional shadow routing is a family
   \(0\le r_{y,p,\sigma_0}\le1\), supported only when
   \[
      y\in\mathcal Y,\qquad
      (p,\sigma_0)\in N(A),\qquad
      p\in W_y,\qquad
      a_y(\sigma_0)=1,
      \tag{SRT1}
   \]
   and satisfying
   \[
      \sum_{y\in\mathcal Y}r_{y,p,\sigma_0}\le1
      \qquad((p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)).
      \tag{SRT2}
   \]
   For \(y\in\mathcal Y\), define the routed shadow mass at \(p\) by
   \[
      m_y(p)=
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      r_{y,p,\sigma_0}\alpha_{p,\sigma_0},
      \qquad
      X_y=\sum_{p\in W_y}m_y(p),
      \tag{SRT3}
   \]
   and define memberships
   \[
      \theta_{y,p}=
      \begin{cases}
      m_y(p)/d_{A,y}(p), & d_{A,y}(p)>0,\\
      0, & d_{A,y}(p)=0.
      \end{cases}
      \tag{SRT4}
   \]
   Then \(0\le\theta_{y,p}\le1\), and each \(y\) with \(X_y>0\) is a valid
   soft-mass record:
   \[
      X_y=\sum_{p\in W_y}\theta_{y,p}d_{A,y}(p).
      \tag{SRT5}
   \]

   Consequently, if the routing and cardinalities \(K_y\in\mathcal K_y\)
   satisfy
   \[
      \sum_{y\in\mathcal Y}
      K_y\left(
         \frac{X_y}{\max\{\mu_y,K_y\}}
         -
         \psi_y\left(A_yK_y^{\rho_y-1}+\zeta K_y^{\rho_y}\right)
      \right)>0,
      \qquad
      \mu_y=\sum_{p\in W_y}\theta_{y,p},
      \tag{SRT6}
   \]
   then some \(y\) gives a one-record Hall-shadow merge.

   In particular, it is enough to route only part of the paid shadow.  If no
   exact-scale soft Hall-shadow merge exists for \(\mathcal Y\), then every
   fractional shadow routing and every choice of cardinalities satisfies the
   reverse of \((SRT6)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By the support condition \((SRT1)\),
   \[
      m_y(p)
      \le
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}a_y(\sigma_0)
      =
      d_{A,y}(p).
   \]
   Hence \(0\le\theta_{y,p}\le1\), and \((SRT5)\) follows from the definition
   of \(\theta\).  The records \((y,\theta_y,X_y,K_y)\) are therefore valid
   exact-scale soft records in the sense of
   \cref{cor:exact-scale-soft-hall-shadow-reporter}.  Condition \((SRT6)\) is
   precisely the panel surplus \((ESH3)\) for this induced panel, so that
   corollary gives a one-record Hall-shadow merge.  The final statement is the
   contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Thresholded shadow-routing screen]
   \label{cor:thresholded-shadow-routing-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:shadow-routing-exact-scale-soft-reporter}.  A thresholded shadow
   routing is a fractional shadow routing together with thresholds
   \(\delta_y>0\) such that routed mass for template \(y\) is supported only on
   \[
      d_{A,y}(p)\ge\delta_y .
      \tag{TSR1}
   \]
   Let \(X_y\) be the routed shadow mass from \((SRT3)\).  If there are
   available cardinalities \(K_y\in\mathcal K_y\) such that
   \[
      \sum_{y\in\mathcal Y}
      \left[
         \min\{X_y,K_y\delta_y\}
         -
         \psi_y
         \left(
            A_yK_y^{\rho_y}
            +\zeta K_y^{1+\rho_y}
         \right)
      \right]>0,
      \tag{TSR2}
   \]
   then some \(y\) gives a one-record Hall-shadow merge.

   Equivalently, a single thresholded route into \(y\) succeeds whenever
   \[
      \max_{K\in\mathcal K_y}
      \left[
         \min\{X_y,K\delta_y\}
         -
         \psi_y
         \left(
            A_yK^{\rho_y}
            +\zeta K^{1+\rho_y}
         \right)
      \right]>0 .
      \tag{TSR3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Use the memberships induced by the routing in \((SRT4)\).  By the threshold
   support condition \((TSR1)\),
   \[
      \mu_y
      =
      \sum_{p\in W_y}\frac{m_y(p)}{d_{A,y}(p)}
      \le
      \frac{X_y}{\delta_y}.
      \tag{TSR4}
   \]
   Hence for every \(K_y\),
   \[
      K_y\frac{X_y}{\max\{\mu_y,K_y\}}
      \ge
      K_y\frac{X_y}{\max\{X_y/\delta_y,K_y\}}
      =
      \min\{X_y,K_y\delta_y\}.
      \tag{TSR5}
   \]
   Therefore \((TSR2)\) implies the shadow-routing surplus \((SRT6)\), and
   \cref{cor:shadow-routing-exact-scale-soft-reporter} gives a one-record
   Hall-shadow merge.  The one-record optimized form \((TSR3)\) is the same
   implication after maximizing over the cardinality net.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sampled thresholded shadow-routing search]
   \label{cor:sampled-thresholded-shadow-routing-search}
   In the setting of \cref{cor:thresholded-shadow-routing-screen}, suppose a
   randomized build-time proposal routine returns a finite thresholded shadow
   routing panel on seed \(s\), and let \(Z(s)\) be the left side of \((TSR2)\)
   for that panel.  If
   \[
      \E_sZ(s)\ge\Gamma>0,
      \qquad
      Z(s)_+\le M
      \quad\text{almost surely},
      \tag{STS1}
   \]
   then \(B\) independent build-time seeds contain a valid one-record
   Hall-shadow merge with probability at least
   \[
      1-\exp\left(-\frac{B\Gamma}{M}\right).
      \tag{STS2}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   As before, \((STS1)\) implies \(\Pr[Z(s)>0]\ge\Gamma/M\).  A positive seed
   satisfies \((TSR2)\), so
   \cref{cor:thresholded-shadow-routing-screen} verifies it into a deterministic
   one-record Hall-shadow merge.  Independent repetition gives \((STS2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Layered thresholded shadow-routing screen]
   \label{cor:layered-thresholded-shadow-routing-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:shadow-routing-exact-scale-soft-reporter}.  Let \(\mathcal J\) be a
   finite set of layer labels.  Each layer \(\ell\in\mathcal J\) has a repair
   template \(y(\ell)\in\mathcal Y\) and a threshold \(\delta_\ell>0\).  A
   layered thresholded routing is a family
   \(0\le r_{\ell,p,\sigma_0}\le1\), supported only when
   \[
      (p,\sigma_0)\in N(A),\qquad
      p\in W_{y(\ell)},\qquad
      a_{y(\ell)}(\sigma_0)=1,\qquad
      d_{A,y(\ell)}(p)\ge\delta_\ell ,
      \tag{LTR1}
   \]
   and satisfying
   \[
      \sum_{\ell\in\mathcal J}r_{\ell,p,\sigma_0}\le1
      \qquad((p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)).
      \tag{LTR2}
   \]
   Define the routed mass of layer \(\ell\) by
   \[
      X_\ell=
      \sum_{p\in W_{y(\ell)}}
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      r_{\ell,p,\sigma_0}\alpha_{p,\sigma_0}.
      \tag{LTR3}
   \]
   If there are available cardinalities
   \(K_\ell\in\mathcal K_{y(\ell)}\) such that
   \[
      \sum_{\ell\in\mathcal J}
      \left[
         \min\{X_\ell,K_\ell\delta_\ell\}
         -
         \psi_{y(\ell)}
         \left(
            A_{y(\ell)}K_\ell^{\rho_{y(\ell)}}
            +\zeta K_\ell^{1+\rho_{y(\ell)}}
         \right)
      \right]>0,
      \tag{LTR4}
   \]
   then some layer gives a one-record Hall-shadow merge.

   Thus a proposal mechanism may split paid shadow fractionally across many
   degree superlevels of the same template.  Only the total routed mass of a
   near-pair atom is limited by \((LTR2)\); overlapping geometric reports are
   harmless once their verified layer surplus is positive.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Replace every layer \(\ell\) by a formal copy of its template
   \(y(\ell)\), with the same update set, activation predicate, prices, and
   cardinality net.  Conditions \((LTR1)\)--\((LTR2)\) are exactly the support
   and one-use constraints for a fractional shadow routing into this copied
   family, and each copied template is thresholded at level \(\delta_\ell\).
   Applying \cref{cor:thresholded-shadow-routing-screen} to the copied family
   gives a one-record Hall-shadow merge from the positive surplus
   \((LTR4)\).  Removing the formal copy notation leaves the same retained
   prefix for the original template \(y(\ell)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cardinality-optimized thresholded routing screen]
   \label{cor:cardinality-optimized-thresholded-routing-screen}
   In the setting of \cref{cor:thresholded-shadow-routing-screen}, fix one
   thresholded route into a template \(y\) with \(0<\rho_y<1\), routed mass
   \(X>0\), and threshold \(\delta>0\).  Put
   \[
      H=\frac X\delta,\qquad
      g_y(K)=A_yK^{\rho_y-1}+\zeta K^{\rho_y}.
      \tag{COT0}
   \]
   The one-layer success condition \((TSR3)\) is equivalent to the existence of
   an available cardinality \(K\in\mathcal K_y\) satisfying either
   \[
      K\le H,
      \qquad
      \delta>\psi_yg_y(K),
      \tag{COT1}
   \]
   or
   \[
      K\ge H,
      \qquad
      X>\psi_yK g_y(K).
      \tag{COT2}
   \]
   In particular, suppose \(b\ge1\), \(h\le H\), and the retained cardinality
   net contains \(K\in\mathcal K_y\) with \(h/b\le K\le h\).  Then the route
   succeeds whenever
   \[
      \delta>
      \psi_y\left(
         b^{1-\rho_y}A_yh^{\rho_y-1}
         +\zeta h^{\rho_y}
      \right).
      \tag{COT3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed \(K\), the surplus in \((TSR3)\) is
   \[
      \min\{X,K\delta\}-\psi_yK g_y(K).
   \]
   If \(K\le H=X/\delta\), this is positive exactly when
   \(K\delta>\psi_yK g_y(K)\), which is \((COT1)\).  If \(K\ge H\), it is
   positive exactly when \(X>\psi_yK g_y(K)\), which is \((COT2)\).

   For the net statement, \(K\le h\le H\) puts us in the first branch.  Since
   \(\rho_y-1<0\) and \(K\ge h/b\),
   \[
      K^{\rho_y-1}\le b^{1-\rho_y}h^{\rho_y-1},
   \]
   while \(K\le h\) gives \(K^{\rho_y}\le h^{\rho_y}\).  Thus \((COT3)\)
   implies \(\delta>\psi_yg_y(K)\), and \((COT1)\) applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Thresholded routing residual envelope]
   \label{cor:thresholded-routing-residual-envelope}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:cardinality-optimized-thresholded-routing-screen}.  Suppose no
   one-record Hall-shadow merge is exposed by this thresholded route.  Then every
   available cardinality \(K\in\mathcal K_y\) satisfying the positive
   price-density inequality
   \[
      K\delta>
      \psi_y\left(A_yK^{\rho_y}+\zeta K^{1+\rho_y}\right)
      \tag{TRE1}
   \]
   must obey the routed-mass bound
   \[
      X\le
      \psi_y\left(A_yK^{\rho_y}+\zeta K^{1+\rho_y}\right).
      \tag{TRE2}
   \]
   In particular, such a \(K\) must have \(K>X/\delta\).  Consequently, if
   \(b\ge1\), the retained cardinality net contains
   \(K\in\mathcal K_y\) with \(h/b\le K\le h\), and a surviving route satisfies
   \[
      \delta>
      \psi_y\left(
         b^{1-\rho_y}A_yh^{\rho_y-1}
         +\zeta h^{\rho_y}
      \right)
      \tag{TRE3}
   \]
   at this scale \(h\), then
   \[
      h>\frac X\delta
      \tag{TRE4}
   \]
   and
   \[
      X\le
      \psi_y\left(A_yh^{\rho_y}+\zeta h^{1+\rho_y}\right).
      \tag{TRE5}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((TRE1)\) holds and \(X>K\delta\), then
   \[
      \min\{X,K\delta\}=K\delta
      >
      \psi_y\left(A_yK^{\rho_y}+\zeta K^{1+\rho_y}\right),
   \]
   contradicting failure of \((TSR3)\).  If \(X\le K\delta\), failure of
   \((TSR3)\) gives
   \[
      X=\min\{X,K\delta\}
      \le
      \psi_y\left(A_yK^{\rho_y}+\zeta K^{1+\rho_y}\right).
   \]
   Thus the only possible case gives \((TRE2)\).
   If \(K\le X/\delta\), then \((TRE1)\) and \(X\ge K\delta\) would make
   \((TSR3)\) positive, so a surviving route must have \(K>X/\delta\).

   Now assume the net hypotheses and \((TRE3)\).  If \(h\le X/\delta\), the
   net statement of
   \cref{cor:cardinality-optimized-thresholded-routing-screen} would expose a
   merge, so a surviving route has \(h>X/\delta\).  The proof of
   \cref{cor:cardinality-optimized-thresholded-routing-screen} shows that
   \((TRE3)\) implies \(\delta>\psi_yg_y(K)\), hence \((TRE1)\).  Applying
   \((TRE2)\) and using \(K\le h\) gives \((TRE5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cumulative superlevel Hall-shadow reporter]
   \label{cor:cumulative-superlevel-hall-shadow-reporter}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:thresholded-shadow-routing-screen}.  For a repair template \(y\)
   and threshold \(\delta>0\), define the cumulative Hall-shadow superlevel mass
   \[
      M_A(y,\delta)=
      \sum_{\substack{p\in W_y:\\ d_{A,y}(p)\ge\delta}}d_{A,y}(p).
      \tag{CSH1}
   \]
   Suppose a record certifies a one-sided lower bound
   \[
      0\le \widehat M\le M_A(y,\delta)
      \tag{CSH2}
   \]
   and an available cardinality \(K\in\mathcal K_y\).  If
   \[
      \min\{\widehat M,K\delta\}
      >
      \psi_y\left(A_yK^{\rho_y}+\zeta K^{1+\rho_y}\right),
      \tag{CSH3}
   \]
   then \(y\) gives a one-record Hall-shadow merge.

   More generally, if a finite panel of independent records
   \((y_i,\delta_i,K_i,\widehat M_i)\) with nonnegative weights \(\lambda_i\)
   satisfies
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_i
      \left[
         \min\{\widehat M_i,K_i\delta_i\}
         -
         \psi_{y_i}
         \left(A_{y_i}K_i^{\rho_{y_i}}
         +\zeta K_i^{1+\rho_{y_i}}\right)
      \right]>0,
      \tag{CSH4}
   \]
   then some record in the panel gives a one-record Hall-shadow merge.

   Consequently, if no canonical cumulative-superlevel record exposes a merge,
   then every template, threshold, and available cardinality obeys the weak-type
   envelope
   \[
      \min\{M_A(y,\delta),K\delta\}
      \le
      \psi_y\left(A_yK^{\rho_y}+\zeta K^{1+\rho_y}\right).
      \tag{CSH5}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix one record.  Define a one-template thresholded routing by routing every
   paid shadow atom \((p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)\) to \(y\) when
   \[
      p\in W_y,\qquad a_y(\sigma_0)=1,\qquad d_{A,y}(p)\ge\delta,
   \]
   and routing no other atom.  This satisfies \((SRT1)\)--\((SRT2)\) for the
   one-template family \(\{y\}\), and its routed mass is exactly
   \(X=M_A(y,\delta)\).  Hence
   \[
      \min\{X,K\delta\}\ge \min\{\widehat M,K\delta\}.
   \]
   Condition \((CSH3)\) therefore implies the one-record thresholded surplus
   \((TSR3)\), so
   \cref{cor:thresholded-shadow-routing-screen} gives a Hall-shadow merge.

   For the panel statement, positive weighted surplus with
   \(\lambda_i\ge0\) implies at least one record satisfies \((CSH3)\).  The
   weak-type envelope is the contrapositive with
   \(\widehat M=M_A(y,\delta)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cumulative Hall-shadow price-density screen]
   \label{cor:cumulative-hall-shadow-price-density-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:cumulative-superlevel-hall-shadow-reporter}.  Fix a template \(y\),
   a threshold \(\delta>0\), and write \(M=M_A(y,\delta)\).  For an available
   cardinality \(K\in\mathcal K_y\), put
   \[
      f_y(K)=A_yK^{\rho_y-1}+\zeta K^{\rho_y}.
      \tag{CPD1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \delta>\psi_yf_y(K)
      \tag{CPD2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      M>\psi_yKf_y(K),
      \tag{CPD3}
   \]
   then \(y\) gives a one-record Hall-shadow merge.

   Conversely, if no canonical cumulative-superlevel record exposes a merge,
   then for every template, threshold, and available cardinality, at least one
   of the reverse inequalities in \((CPD2)\) and \((CPD3)\) holds.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Conditions \((CPD2)\)--\((CPD3)\) say exactly that both entries in
   \[
      \min\{M,K\delta\}
   \]
   are larger than
   \[
      \psi_yKf_y(K)
      =
      \psi_y\left(A_yK^{\rho_y}+\zeta K^{1+\rho_y}\right).
   \]
   Hence \((CSH3)\) holds with \(\widehat M=M\), and
   \cref{cor:cumulative-superlevel-hall-shadow-reporter} gives a merge.  The
   converse is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Clipped cumulative Hall-shadow screen]
   \label{cor:clipped-cumulative-hall-shadow-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:cumulative-superlevel-hall-shadow-reporter}.  Fix a repair template
   \(y\) with \(0<\rho_y<1\), put \(m_y=|W_y|\), and define \(f_y(K)\) and
   \(K_y^\natural\) as in \((CHP1)\)--\((CHP2)\).  Let \(a\ge1\), and let
   \(K\in\mathcal K_y\) satisfy
   \[
      a^{-1}K_y^\natural\le K\le aK_y^\natural
      \tag{CCH1}
   \]
   when \(A_y\) and \(\zeta\) are not both zero.  Define
   \[
      \Theta_y=
      \begin{cases}
      0, & A_y=\zeta=0,\\
      a\psi_yf_y(K_y^\natural), & \text{otherwise}.
      \end{cases}
      \tag{CCH2}
   \]
   If, for some threshold \(\delta>0\),
   \[
      \min\left\{\delta,\frac{M_A(y,\delta)}K\right\}>\Theta_y,
      \tag{CCH3}
   \]
   then \(y\) gives a one-record Hall-shadow merge.

   Consequently, if no cumulative superlevel report exposes a merge, then every
   template \(y\), threshold \(\delta\), and available cardinality \(K\) satisfying
   \((CCH1)\) obey
   \[
      \min\left\{\delta,\frac{M_A(y,\delta)}K\right\}\le\Theta_y .
      \tag{CCH4}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(A_y=\zeta=0\), then \(\Theta_y=0\) and \((CCH3)\) gives
   \(\min\{M_A(y,\delta),K\delta\}>0\).  Since the recursive price is zero,
   \((CSH3)\) applies.

   Otherwise, the proof of
   \cref{cor:clipped-hall-shadow-density-screen} shows that \((CCH1)\) implies
   \[
      f_y(K)\le a f_y(K_y^\natural).
   \]
   Thus \((CCH3)\) gives both
   \[
      \delta>\psi_yf_y(K),
      \qquad
      M_A(y,\delta)>\psi_yKf_y(K).
   \]
   \Cref{cor:cumulative-hall-shadow-price-density-screen} gives the merge.  The
   residual envelope is again the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Tail-mass cumulative Hall-shadow screen]
   \label{cor:tail-mass-cumulative-hall-shadow-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:clipped-cumulative-hall-shadow-screen}.  For a template \(y\) and
   level \(\theta\ge0\), put
   \[
      M_A^+(y,\theta)=
      \sum_{\substack{p\in W_y:\\ d_{A,y}(p)>\theta}}d_{A,y}(p).
      \tag{TMH1}
   \]
   Fix \(K\in\mathcal K_y\) satisfying \((CCH1)\), and let \(\Theta_y\) be the
   clipped price-density threshold from \((CCH2)\).  If a reporter certifies
   \[
      0\le \widehat M^+\le M_A^+(y,\Theta_y)
      \tag{TMH2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \widehat M^+>K\Theta_y,
      \tag{TMH3}
   \]
   then \(y\) gives a one-record Hall-shadow merge.

   Consequently, if no tail-mass cumulative report exposes a merge, then every
   template \(y\) and every available clipped-scale cardinality \(K\) obey
   \[
      M_A^+(y,\Theta_y)\le K\Theta_y .
      \tag{TMH4}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(\widehat M^+>K\Theta_y\), then the strict superlevel
   \(\{p\in W_y:d_{A,y}(p)>\Theta_y\}\) is nonempty.  Since \(W_y\) is finite,
   choose
   \[
      \delta=\min\{d_{A,y}(p):p\in W_y,\ d_{A,y}(p)>\Theta_y\}.
   \]
   Then \(\delta>\Theta_y\), and
   \[
      M_A(y,\delta)=M_A^+(y,\Theta_y)\ge\widehat M^+>K\Theta_y .
   \]
   Hence
   \[
      \min\left\{\delta,\frac{M_A(y,\delta)}K\right\}>\Theta_y,
   \]
   so \cref{cor:clipped-cumulative-hall-shadow-screen} gives the merge.  The
   residual inequality \((TMH4)\) is the contrapositive with
   \(\widehat M^+=M_A^+(y,\Theta_y)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Support-limited tail Hall-shadow screen]
   \label{cor:support-limited-tail-hall-shadow-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:tail-mass-cumulative-hall-shadow-screen}.  Fix a template \(y\), an
   available cardinality \(K\), and a slack \(a\ge1\) satisfying the clipped
   scale condition \((CCH1)\).  Let \(\Theta_y\) be the corresponding threshold
   from \((CCH2)\).
   Suppose a reporter certifies a finitely supported shadow submeasure
   \(0\le m(p)\le d_{A,y}(p)\) on \(W_y\), with
   \[
      |\{p:m(p)>0\}|\le K,
      \qquad
      X=\sum_{p\in W_y}m(p).
      \tag{SLT1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      X>2K\Theta_y,
      \tag{SLT2}
   \]
   then \(y\) gives a one-record Hall-shadow merge.

   Consequently, if no support-limited tail report exposes a merge, then every
   such submeasure obeys
   \[
      \sum_{p\in W_y}m(p)\le2K\Theta_y .
      \tag{SLT3}
   \]
   In particular, every subset \(U\subseteq W_y\) with \(|U|\le K\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U}d_{A,y}(p)\le2K\Theta_y .
      \tag{SLT4}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Split the support of \(m\) into
   \[
      U_+=\{p:m(p)>0,\ d_{A,y}(p)>\Theta_y\},
      \qquad
      U_0=\{p:m(p)>0,\ d_{A,y}(p)\le\Theta_y\}.
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U_+}d_{A,y}(p)>K\Theta_y,
   \]
   then \(M_A^+(y,\Theta_y)>K\Theta_y\), so
   \cref{cor:tail-mass-cumulative-hall-shadow-screen} gives a merge.  Otherwise,
   since \(m(p)\le d_{A,y}(p)\) and \(|U_0|\le K\),
   \[
      X
      =
      \sum_{p\in U_+}m(p)+\sum_{p\in U_0}m(p)
      \le
      K\Theta_y+|U_0|\Theta_y
      \le
      2K\Theta_y,
   \]
   contradicting \((SLT2)\).  Thus \((SLT2)\) forces a merge.  The residual
   statement is the contrapositive, and \((SLT4)\) follows by taking
   \(m(p)=d_{A,y}(p)\mathbf 1\{p\in U\}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Support-sensitive tail Hall-shadow screen]
   \label{cor:support-sensitive-tail-hall-shadow-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:tail-mass-cumulative-hall-shadow-screen}.  Fix a template \(y\), an
   available cardinality \(K\), and a slack \(a\ge1\) satisfying the clipped
   scale condition \((CCH1)\).  Let \(\Theta_y\) be the corresponding threshold
   from \((CCH2)\).  Suppose a reporter certifies a finitely supported shadow
   submeasure \(0\le m(p)\le d_{A,y}(p)\) on \(W_y\), with
   \[
      s=|\{p:m(p)>0\}|,
      \qquad
      X=\sum_{p\in W_y}m(p).
      \tag{SST1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      X>(K+s)\Theta_y,
      \tag{SST2}
   \]
   then \(y\) gives a one-record Hall-shadow merge.

   Consequently, if no support-sensitive tail report exposes a merge, then every
   such submeasure obeys
   \[
      \sum_{p\in W_y}m(p)\le (K+s)\Theta_y .
      \tag{SST3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Use the same split
   \[
      U_+=\{p:m(p)>0,\ d_{A,y}(p)>\Theta_y\},
      \qquad
      U_0=\{p:m(p)>0,\ d_{A,y}(p)\le\Theta_y\}.
   \]
   If \(\sum_{p\in U_+}d_{A,y}(p)>K\Theta_y\), then the tail-mass screen fires.
   Otherwise
   \[
      X
      \le
      \sum_{p\in U_+}d_{A,y}(p)+\sum_{p\in U_0}d_{A,y}(p)
      \le
      K\Theta_y+s\Theta_y,
   \]
   contradicting \((SST2)\).  Hence \((SST2)\) forces a merge, and the residual
   inequality is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Support-adaptive exact Hall-shadow tail screen]
   \label{cor:support-adaptive-exact-hall-shadow-tail-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:cumulative-hall-shadow-price-density-screen}.  Fix a template \(y\)
   and an available cardinality \(K\in\mathcal K_y\).  Put
   \[
      \theta_K=\psi_y\left(A_yK^{\rho_y-1}+\zeta K^{\rho_y}\right).
      \tag{SAH1}
   \]
   Suppose a reporter certifies a finitely supported shadow submeasure
   \(0\le m(p)\le d_{A,y}(p)\), with
   \[
      s=|\{p:m(p)>0\}|,
      \qquad
      X=\sum_p m(p).
      \tag{SAH2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      X>(K+s)\theta_K,
      \tag{SAH3}
   \]
   then \(y\) gives a one-record Hall-shadow merge.

   Consequently, if no support-adaptive exact tail report exposes a merge, then
   every such submeasure obeys
   \[
      X\le (K+s)\theta_K
      \qquad(K\in\mathcal K_y).
      \tag{SAH4}
   \]
   If, in addition, \(0<\rho_y<1\), \(b\ge1\), and the retained cardinality net
   contains \(K\in\mathcal K_y\) with \(s/b\le K\le bs\), then every surviving
   submeasure satisfies
   \[
      X
      \le
      (b+1)\psi_y
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_y}A_ys^{\rho_y}
         +b^{\rho_y}\zeta s^{1+\rho_y}
      \right).
      \tag{SAH5}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Split the support of \(m\) at the exact price-density level:
   \[
      U_+=\{p:m(p)>0,\ d_{A,y}(p)>\theta_K\},
      \qquad
      U_0=\{p:m(p)>0,\ d_{A,y}(p)\le\theta_K\}.
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U_+}d_{A,y}(p)>K\theta_K,
   \]
   then, as in the proof of
   \cref{cor:tail-mass-cumulative-hall-shadow-screen}, choosing the smallest
   degree strictly above \(\theta_K\) gives a threshold \(\delta>\theta_K\) with
   \(M_A(y,\delta)>K\theta_K\).  Thus \((CPD2)\)--\((CPD3)\) hold for this
   \(K\), and
   \cref{cor:cumulative-hall-shadow-price-density-screen} gives a merge.
   Otherwise
   \[
      X
      \le
      \sum_{p\in U_+}d_{A,y}(p)+\sum_{p\in U_0}d_{A,y}(p)
      \le
      K\theta_K+s\theta_K,
   \]
   contradicting \((SAH3)\).  This proves the merge implication and hence the
   contrapositive \((SAH4)\).

   For the net statement, \(K\le bs\) gives \(K+s\le(b+1)s\).  Also
   \(K\ge s/b\) and \(K\le bs\) give
   \[
      K^{\rho_y-1}\le b^{1-\rho_y}s^{\rho_y-1},
      \qquad
      K^{\rho_y}\le b^{\rho_y}s^{\rho_y}.
   \]
   Substituting these two bounds into \((SAH4)\) gives \((SAH5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cut-center routing obstruction]
   \label{cor:cut-center-routing-obstruction}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:shadow-routing-exact-scale-soft-reporter}, and take
   \(\mathcal Y\) to contain every template center \(x\) that appears in the
   failed cut \(A\).  Since every \((p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)\) has at least one
   adjacent \((\sigma_0,x)\in A\), there is an integral routing of all paid
   shadow mass to cut centers satisfying \((SRT1)\)--\((SRT2)\).  For every
   such routing,
   \[
      \sum_{x\in\mathcal Y}X_x
      =
      \sum_{(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}\alpha_{p,\sigma_0}.
      \tag{CCO1}
   \]

   Therefore, if no exact-scale soft Hall-shadow merge is exposed by any
   routing to the cut centers, then every assignment of each paid shadow atom
   to one adjacent cut center, and every choice of cardinalities
   \(K_x\in\mathcal K_x\), satisfies
   \[
      \sum_x
      K_x\frac{X_x}{\max\{\mu_x,K_x\}}
      \le
      \sum_x
      \psi_x
      \left(
         A_xK_x^{\rho_x}
         +\zeta K_x^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{CCO2}
   \]
   Together with the failed Hall cut \((FHT5)\), this is the cut-center
   residual obstruction that a richer geometric template family must beat.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For each right atom \((p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)\), choose one neighboring cut
   atom \((\sigma_0,x)\in A\).  Routing that atom to \(x\) satisfies
   \((SRT1)\)--\((SRT2)\), and routes every unit of paid shadow exactly once,
   proving \((CCO1)\).  If some assignment and cardinality choice violated
   \((CCO2)\), then \((SRT6)\) would hold and
   \cref{cor:shadow-routing-exact-scale-soft-reporter} would expose a
   one-record merge.  The displayed obstruction is therefore the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Support-limited cut-center tail obstruction]
   \label{cor:support-limited-cut-center-tail-obstruction}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:cut-center-routing-obstruction}, and assume
   the template family contains the cut centers.  Consider any fractional
   assignment of paid shadow atoms to adjacent cut centers,
   \(0\le r_{x,p,\sigma_0}\le1\), satisfying the support condition \((SRT1)\).
   Put
   \[
      m_x(p)=
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      r_{x,p,\sigma_0}\alpha_{p,\sigma_0},
      \qquad
      X_x=\sum_p m_x(p).
      \tag{SCT1}
   \]
   For each used center \(x\), choose an available cardinality
   \(K_x\in\mathcal K_x\) and a slack \(a_x\ge1\) satisfying the clipped scale
   condition \((CCH1)\).  Let \(\Theta_x\) be the corresponding clipped
   price-density threshold from \((CCH2)\), and assume the support-size condition
   \[
      |\{p:m_x(p)>0\}|\le K_x .
      \tag{SCT2}
   \]
   If no support-limited tail Hall-shadow report exposes a merge at any cut
   center, then
   \[
      X_x\le2K_x\Theta_x
      \qquad\text{for every used }x.
      \tag{SCT3}
   \]
   Hence any full assignment of every paid shadow atom to one adjacent cut center
   satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}\alpha_{p,\sigma_0}
      \le
      2\sum_xK_x\Theta_x .
      \tag{SCT4}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The support condition \((SRT1)\) gives, for every \(x,p\),
   \[
      m_x(p)
      \le
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}a_x(\sigma_0)
      =
      d_{A,x}(p).
   \]
   Thus \(m_x\) is an admissible support-limited shadow submeasure for
   \cref{cor:support-limited-tail-hall-shadow-screen}.  If no such report
   exposes a merge, \((SLT3)\) gives \((SCT3)\).  For a full assignment,
   summing \((SCT1)\) over centers gives the left side of \((SCT4)\), as in
   \((CCO1)\), and summing \((SCT3)\) gives the displayed bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Support-sensitive cut-center tail obstruction]
   \label{cor:support-sensitive-cut-center-tail-obstruction}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:support-limited-cut-center-tail-obstruction},
   but remove the support-size assumption \((SCT2)\).  For each used cut center
   define
   \[
      s_x=|\{p:m_x(p)>0\}|.
      \tag{SSC1}
   \]
   If no support-sensitive tail Hall-shadow report exposes a merge at any cut
   center, then
   \[
      X_x\le (K_x+s_x)\Theta_x
      \qquad\text{for every used }x.
      \tag{SSC2}
   \]
   Hence any full assignment of every paid shadow atom to one adjacent cut center
   satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}\alpha_{p,\sigma_0}
      \le
      \sum_x(K_x+s_x)\Theta_x .
      \tag{SSC3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   As in the proof of
   \cref{cor:support-limited-cut-center-tail-obstruction}, the support condition
   gives \(0\le m_x(p)\le d_{A,x}(p)\).  Thus
   \cref{cor:support-sensitive-tail-hall-shadow-screen} applies to each center
   and yields \((SSC2)\) if no report fires.  Summing \((SSC2)\) over a full
   assignment gives \((SSC3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Support-adaptive cut-center price obstruction]
   \label{cor:support-adaptive-cut-center-price-obstruction}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:support-sensitive-cut-center-tail-obstruction}.  Assume
   \(0<\rho_x<1\) for the used cut centers, and suppose the cardinality nets are
   factor-\(b\) complete in the following sense: for every used center \(x\) with
   support size \(s_x\ge1\), there is \(K_x\in\mathcal K_x\) satisfying
   \[
      s_x/b\le K_x\le bs_x .
      \tag{SAP1}
   \]
   If no support-adaptive exact tail report exposes a merge at any cut center,
   then
   \[
      X_x
      \le
      (b+1)\psi_x
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_x}A_xs_x^{\rho_x}
         +b^{\rho_x}\zeta s_x^{1+\rho_x}
      \right)
      \tag{SAP2}
   \]
   for every used center \(x\).  Hence any full assignment of every paid shadow
   atom to one adjacent cut center satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}\alpha_{p,\sigma_0}
      \le
      (b+1)
      \sum_x
      \psi_x
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_x}A_xs_x^{\rho_x}
         +b^{\rho_x}\zeta s_x^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{SAP3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   As before, the assigned mass
   \[
      m_x(p)=
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      r_{x,p,\sigma_0}\alpha_{p,\sigma_0}
   \]
   satisfies \(0\le m_x(p)\le d_{A,x}(p)\).  Apply
   \cref{cor:support-adaptive-exact-hall-shadow-tail-screen} with the
   cardinality \(K_x\) supplied by \((SAP1)\).  Its net conclusion \((SAH5)\)
   gives \((SAP2)\).  Summing over a full assignment gives \((SAP3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Support-price assignment separator]
   \label{cor:support-price-assignment-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:support-adaptive-cut-center-price-obstruction}.  Let
   \(\mathcal R_{\rm full}(A)\) be the set of fractional shadow routings into
   the cut centers satisfying equality in \((SRT2)\) for every paid shadow atom
   \((p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)\).  For \(r\in\mathcal R_{\rm full}(A)\), define
   \(m_x^r(p)\), \(X_x^r\), and
   \[
      s_x(r)=|\{p:m_x^r(p)>0\}|
   \]
   as in \((SRT3)\) and \((SSC1)\), and put
   \[
      \Phi_b(r)=
      \sum_{x:\,s_x(r)>0}
      \psi_x
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_x}A_xs_x(r)^{\rho_x}
         +b^{\rho_x}\zeta s_x(r)^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{SPA1}
   \]
   Let
   \[
      M_A=
      \sum_{(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}\alpha_{p,\sigma_0}.
   \]
   If there is a full fractional routing \(r\in\mathcal R_{\rm full}(A)\)
   such that
   \[
      M_A>(b+1)\Phi_b(r),
      \tag{SPA2}
   \]
   then some cut center exposes a support-adaptive exact tail Hall-shadow merge.

   Equivalently, if no support-adaptive exact tail report exposes a merge at
   any cut center, then
   \[
      M_A
      \le
      (b+1)\inf_{r\in\mathcal R_{\rm full}(A)}\Phi_b(r).
      \tag{SPA3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a full fractional routing \(r\).  Since equality holds in \((SRT2)\),
   summing \((SRT3)\) over centers gives
   \[
      \sum_xX_x^r=M_A .
      \tag{SPA4}
   \]
   The support condition \((SRT1)\) gives \(0\le m_x^r(p)\le d_{A,x}(p)\) for
   every center and point, as in the proof of
   \cref{cor:support-adaptive-cut-center-price-obstruction}.  If no
   support-adaptive exact tail report fires, then applying
   \cref{cor:support-adaptive-exact-hall-shadow-tail-screen} at the
   factor-\(b\) cardinality supplied for each used support gives
   \[
      X_x^r
      \le
      (b+1)\psi_x
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_x}A_xs_x(r)^{\rho_x}
         +b^{\rho_x}\zeta s_x(r)^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
   \]
   Summing over used centers and using \((SPA4)\) gives
   \(M_A\le(b+1)\Phi_b(r)\).  Thus any routing satisfying \((SPA2)\) forces a
   report to fire.  Since the same inequality holds for every full routing in a
   surviving residual, taking the infimum gives \((SPA3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Partial support-price assignment separator]
   \label{cor:partial-support-price-assignment-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:support-adaptive-cut-center-price-obstruction}.  A partial
   fractional shadow routing is a family \(0\le r_{x,p,\sigma_0}\le1\)
   satisfying the support condition \((SRT1)\) and
   \[
      \sum_x r_{x,p,\sigma_0}\le1
      \qquad((p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)).
      \tag{PSL1}
   \]
   Define \(m_x^r(p)\), \(X_x^r\), and \(s_x(r)\) as in
   \((SRT3)\) and \((SSC1)\), and put
   \[
      X(r)=\sum_xX_x^r
      =
      \sum_{(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}\sum_xr_{x,p,\sigma_0},
      \tag{PSL2}
   \]
   \[
      \Phi_b(r)=
      \sum_{x:\,s_x(r)>0}
      \psi_x
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_x}A_xs_x(r)^{\rho_x}
         +b^{\rho_x}\zeta s_x(r)^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{PSL3}
   \]
   If some partial routing satisfies
   \[
      X(r)>(b+1)\Phi_b(r),
      \tag{PSL4}
   \]
   then some cut center exposes a support-adaptive exact tail Hall-shadow merge.

   Equivalently, if no support-adaptive exact tail report exposes a merge at
   any cut center, then every partial routing obeys
   \[
      X(r)\le(b+1)\Phi_b(r).
      \tag{PSL5}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For each used center, the assigned submeasure
   \[
      m_x^r(p)=
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      r_{x,p,\sigma_0}\alpha_{p,\sigma_0}
   \]
   satisfies \(0\le m_x^r(p)\le d_{A,x}(p)\) by the support condition
   \((SRT1)\).  If no support-adaptive exact tail report fires, then
   \cref{cor:support-adaptive-exact-hall-shadow-tail-screen}, applied at the
   factor-\(b\) cardinality for the support \(s_x(r)\), gives
   \[
      X_x^r
      \le
      (b+1)\psi_x
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_x}A_xs_x(r)^{\rho_x}
         +b^{\rho_x}\zeta s_x(r)^{1+\rho_x}
      \right).
   \]
   Summing over centers gives \((PSL5)\).  Its contrapositive is the merge
   implication \((PSL4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Independent support-law assignment certificate]
   \label{cor:independent-support-law-assignment-certificate}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:support-price-assignment-separator}.  For each data point \(p\),
   let
   \[
      \Sigma_A(p)=\{\sigma_0:\,(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)\}.
   \]
   A pointwise routing map \(\varphi_p\) assigns every
   \(\sigma_0\in\Sigma_A(p)\) to one adjacent cut center \(x\), meaning
   \[
      (\sigma_0,x)\in A,\qquad p\in W_x,\qquad a_x(\sigma_0)=1 .
      \tag{ISL1}
   \]
   Suppose a randomized certificate chooses the maps \(\varphi_p\) independently
   over \(p\), with arbitrary dependence among the signatures of the same point.
   Let
   \[
      q_{x,p}=\Pr[x\in\varphi_p(\Sigma_A(p))],
      \qquad
      \mu_x=\sum_pq_{x,p}.
      \tag{ISL2}
   \]
   Define the marginal support price
   \[
      \widehat\Phi_b=
      \sum_x\psi_x
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_x}A_x\mu_x^{\rho_x}
         +b^{\rho_x}\zeta(\mu_x+\mu_x^{1+\rho_x})
      \right).
      \tag{ISL3}
   \]
   If
   \[
      M_A>(b+1)\widehat\Phi_b,
      \tag{ISL4}
   \]
   then some deterministic pointwise routing exposes a support-adaptive exact
   tail Hall-shadow merge.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   A sampled pointwise routing map induces an integral full routing
   \(r\in\mathcal R_{\rm full}(A)\) by routing the atom \((p,\sigma_0)\) to
   \(\varphi_p(\sigma_0)\).  For a fixed center \(x\), its support size is
   \[
      S_x=s_x(r)=\sum_p I_{x,p},
      \qquad
      I_{x,p}=\mathbf 1\{x\in\varphi_p(\Sigma_A(p))\}.
   \]
   The variables \(I_{x,p}\) are independent over \(p\), and
   \(\E S_x=\mu_x\).  Since \(0<\rho_x<1\) and \(u^{\rho_x}\) is concave,
   \[
      \E S_x^{\rho_x}\le\mu_x^{\rho_x}.
      \tag{ISL5}
   \]
   For the storage moment, use the elementary integer inequality
   \[
      k^{1+\rho}\le k+k(k-1)_+^\rho
      \qquad(k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0},\ 0<\rho<1),
      \tag{ISL6}
   \]
   which follows from
   \(k^\rho=(1+k-1)^\rho\le1+(k-1)^\rho\) for \(k\ge1\).  With
   \(S_x^{(p)}=\sum_{p'\ne p}I_{x,p'}\), independence gives
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \E S_x(S_x-1)_+^{\rho_x}
      &=
      \sum_p q_{x,p}\E\left(S_x^{(p)}\right)^{\rho_x}  \\
      &\le
      \sum_p q_{x,p}(\mu_x-q_{x,p})^{\rho_x}
      \le
      \mu_x^{1+\rho_x},
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{ISL7}
   \]
   again by concavity.  Combining \((ISL6)\)--\((ISL7)\) yields
   \[
      \E S_x^{1+\rho_x}\le\mu_x+\mu_x^{1+\rho_x}.
      \tag{ISL8}
   \]
   Therefore
   \[
      \E_r\Phi_b(r)\le\widehat\Phi_b.
      \tag{ISL9}
   \]
   If \((ISL4)\) holds, some sampled deterministic routing has
   \(M_A>(b+1)\Phi_b(r)\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:support-price-assignment-separator} gives a support-adaptive exact
   tail Hall-shadow merge.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Atom-marginal support-law certificate]
   \label{cor:atom-marginal-support-law-certificate}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:independent-support-law-assignment-certificate}.  Suppose a
   certificate gives stochastic atom-routing weights
   \(z_{x,p,\sigma_0}\ge0\), supported only on adjacent cut centers as in
   \((ISL1)\), such that
   \[
      \sum_x z_{x,p,\sigma_0}=1
      \qquad((p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)).
      \tag{AML1}
   \]
   For each center and point put
   \[
      \nu_{x,p}=
      \min\left\{1,\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma_A(p)}z_{x,p,\sigma_0}\right\},
      \qquad
      \nu_x=\sum_p\nu_{x,p},
      \tag{AML2}
   \]
   and define
   \[
      \overline\Phi_b=
      \sum_x\psi_x
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_x}A_x\nu_x^{\rho_x}
         +b^{\rho_x}\zeta(\nu_x+\nu_x^{1+\rho_x})
      \right).
      \tag{AML3}
   \]
   If
   \[
      M_A>(b+1)\overline\Phi_b,
      \tag{AML4}
   \]
   then some deterministic atom routing exposes a support-adaptive exact tail
   Hall-shadow merge.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Independently for each paid atom \((p,\sigma_0)\), choose one adjacent center
   \(x\) with probability \(z_{x,p,\sigma_0}\).  Choices for different data
   points are independent, so this is an independent pointwise routing law.
   For a fixed \(x,p\), the probability that point \(p\) uses center \(x\) is
   \[
      q_{x,p}
      =
      1-\prod_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma_A(p)}
      (1-z_{x,p,\sigma_0})
      \le
      \nu_{x,p}.
      \tag{AML5}
   \]
   Hence the support means \(\mu_x=\sum_pq_{x,p}\) from \((ISL2)\) satisfy
   \(\mu_x\le\nu_x\).  Since the marginal support price \((ISL3)\) is
