   coordinatewise increasing in \(\mu_x\), \(\widehat\Phi_b\le\overline\Phi_b\).
   Thus \((AML4)\) implies \((ISL4)\), and
   \cref{cor:independent-support-law-assignment-certificate} gives the merge.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Partial atom-marginal support-law certificate]
   \label{cor:partial-atom-marginal-support-law-certificate}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:partial-support-price-assignment-separator}.  Suppose a certificate
   gives partial stochastic atom-routing weights \(z_{x,p,\sigma_0}\ge0\),
   supported only on adjacent cut centers as in \((ISL1)\), such that
   \[
      \sum_x z_{x,p,\sigma_0}\le1
      \qquad((p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)).
      \tag{PAM1}
   \]
   Let the routed paid mass be
   \[
      X_z=
      \sum_{(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}\sum_xz_{x,p,\sigma_0}.
      \tag{PAM2}
   \]
   For each center and point put
   \[
      \nu_{x,p}=
      \min\left\{1,\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma_A(p)}z_{x,p,\sigma_0}\right\},
      \qquad
      \nu_x=\sum_p\nu_{x,p},
      \tag{PAM3}
   \]
   and define
   \[
      \overline\Phi_b(z)=
      \sum_x\psi_x
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_x}A_x\nu_x^{\rho_x}
         +b^{\rho_x}\zeta(\nu_x+\nu_x^{1+\rho_x})
      \right).
      \tag{PAM4}
   \]
   If
   \[
      X_z>(b+1)\overline\Phi_b(z),
      \tag{PAM5}
   \]
   then some deterministic partial atom routing exposes a support-adaptive
   exact tail Hall-shadow merge.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Independently for each paid atom \((p,\sigma_0)\), route it to center \(x\)
   with probability \(z_{x,p,\sigma_0}\), and leave it unrouted with the
   remaining probability.  This produces a random partial routing satisfying
   \((PSL1)\).  Its expected routed paid mass is exactly \(X_z\).

   For each \(x,p\), the probability that point \(p\) touches center \(x\) is
   at most \(\nu_{x,p}\) by the same union-bound calculation as \((AML5)\).
   The moment estimates \((ISL5)\)--\((ISL8)\), applied to the resulting
   independent support indicators, therefore give
   \[
      \E\Phi_b(r)\le\overline\Phi_b(z).
      \tag{PAM6}
   \]
   Hence \((PAM5)\) implies
   \[
      \E\left[X(r)-(b+1)\Phi_b(r)\right]>0.
   \]
   Some deterministic sampled partial routing satisfies \((PSL4)\), and
   \cref{cor:partial-support-price-assignment-separator} gives the merge.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Centerwise partial atom screen]
   \label{cor:centerwise-partial-atom-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:partial-atom-marginal-support-law-certificate}.  Fix one cut
   center \(x\).  Suppose a certificate gives weights
   \(0\le z_{p,\sigma_0}\le1\), supported only when
   \[
      (p,\sigma_0)\in N(A),\qquad
      (\sigma_0,x)\in A,\qquad
      p\in W_x,\qquad
      a_x(\sigma_0)=1 .
      \tag{CAP1}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      X_x(z)=
      \sum_{\sigma_0,p}\alpha_{p,\sigma_0}z_{p,\sigma_0},
      \qquad
      \nu_{x,p}(z)=
      \min\left\{1,\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma_A(p)}z_{p,\sigma_0}\right\},
      \tag{CAP2}
   \]
   \[
      \nu_x(z)=\sum_p\nu_{x,p}(z),
      \qquad
      \Pi_x(z)=
      \psi_x
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_x}A_x\nu_x(z)^{\rho_x}
         +b^{\rho_x}\zeta(\nu_x(z)+\nu_x(z)^{1+\rho_x})
      \right).
      \tag{CAP3}
   \]
   If
   \[
      X_x(z)>(b+1)\Pi_x(z),
      \tag{CAP4}
   \]
   then \(x\) exposes a support-adaptive exact tail Hall-shadow merge.

   Conversely, if a multi-center partial atom certificate satisfies
   \((PAM5)\), then at least one center \(x\) satisfies \((CAP4)\) after
   restricting \(z\) to that center.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For the first statement, form partial atom weights
   \(z_{x,p,\sigma_0}=z_{p,\sigma_0}\) for the fixed center and set all other
   center weights to zero.  Then \((PAM1)\) holds, \(X_z=X_x(z)\), and
   \(\overline\Phi_b(z)=\Pi_x(z)\).  Thus \((CAP4)\) is exactly \((PAM5)\), and
   \cref{cor:partial-atom-marginal-support-law-certificate} gives the merge.

   For the converse, write
   \[
      X_z=\sum_xX_x(z),
      \qquad
      \overline\Phi_b(z)=\sum_x\Pi_x(z).
   \]
   If every center had \(X_x(z)\le(b+1)\Pi_x(z)\), summing over centers would
   contradict \((PAM5)\).  Hence some center satisfies \((CAP4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Centerwise atom hardening]
   \label{cor:centerwise-atom-hardening}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:centerwise-partial-atom-screen}, and assume
   \(0<\rho_x<1\).  Let
   \[
      d_{A,x}(p)=
      \sum_{\sigma_0:\,(p,\sigma_0)\in N(A)}
      \alpha_{p,\sigma_0}a_x(\sigma_0),
      \tag{CAH1}
   \]
   and let \(D_A(x,K)\) be the sum of the largest \(K\) values of
   \(d_{A,x}(p)\) on \(W_x\).  For a centerwise atom certificate \(z\), put
   \[
      \mu=\nu_x(z),\qquad X=X_x(z).
      \tag{CAH2}
   \]
   Suppose \((CAP4)\) holds.  If \(\mu\ge1\), assume the retained cardinality
   net contains \(K\) with
   \[
      \mu\le K\le b\mu .
      \tag{CAH3}
   \]
   If \(0<\mu<1\), assume it contains \(K\) with
   \[
      1\le K\le b .
      \tag{CAH4}
   \]
   Then the top-\(K\) prefix of \(W_x\) by \(d_{A,x}\) satisfies
   \[
      D_A(x,K)>
      \psi_x
      \left(
         A_xK^{\rho_x}+\zeta K^{1+\rho_x}
      \right),
      \tag{CAH5}
   \]
   and hence gives a one-record Hall-shadow merge.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Define \(u_p=\nu_{x,p}(z)\).  The support condition \((CAP1)\) gives
   \[
      \sum_{\sigma_0}\alpha_{p,\sigma_0}z_{p,\sigma_0}
      \le u_p d_{A,x}(p)
      \qquad(p\in W_x),
      \tag{CAH6}
   \]
   because either \(\sum_{\sigma_0}z_{p,\sigma_0}\ge1\), in which case
   \(u_p=1\), or every \(z_{p,\sigma_0}\le u_p\).  Hence
   \[
      X\le\sum_pu_pd_{A,x}(p),
      \qquad
      \sum_pu_p=\mu,
      \qquad
      0\le u_p\le1 .
      \tag{CAH7}
   \]
   If \(\mu\ge1\) and \(K\ge\mu\), the top-\(K\) prefix dominates every
   fractional subset of total mass \(\mu\), so
   \[
      D_A(x,K)\ge X .
      \tag{CAH8}
   \]
   Using \(K\le b\mu\), the recursive price at \(K\) is at most
   \[
      \psi_x\left(A_xb^{\rho_x}\mu^{\rho_x}
      +\zeta b^{1+\rho_x}\mu^{1+\rho_x}\right).
      \tag{CAH9}
   \]
   Since \(b\ge1\) and \(0<\rho_x<1\),
   \[
      (b+1)b^{1-\rho_x}\ge b^{\rho_x},
      \qquad
      (b+1)b^{\rho_x}(\mu+\mu^{1+\rho_x})
      \ge b^{1+\rho_x}\mu^{1+\rho_x}.
      \tag{CAH10}
   \]
   Thus \((CAP4)\) gives \(X\) larger than the bound in \((CAH9)\), and
   \((CAH8)\) proves \((CAH5)\).

   If \(0<\mu<1\), then \((CAH7)\) implies that the largest degree is at least
   \(X/\mu\), so every prefix with \(K\ge1\) has
   \[
      D_A(x,K)\ge X/\mu .
      \tag{CAH11}
   \]
   From \(K\le b\), the recursive price at \(K\) is at most
   \[
      \psi_x(A_xb^{\rho_x}+\zeta b^{1+\rho_x}).
      \tag{CAH12}
   \]
   Dividing \((CAP4)\) by \(\mu\) gives
   \[
      X/\mu>
      (b+1)\psi_x
      \left(
         b^{1-\rho_x}A_x\mu^{\rho_x-1}
         +b^{\rho_x}\zeta(1+\mu^{\rho_x})
      \right).
      \tag{CAH13}
   \]
   Because \(\mu^{\rho_x-1}\ge1\), the right side of \((CAH13)\) dominates
   \((CAH12)\), again by \((CAH10)\).  Therefore \((CAH11)\) implies
   \((CAH5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Centerwise atom relaxation is tight]
   \label{cor:centerwise-atom-relaxation-tight}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:centerwise-atom-hardening}.  Assume the
   retained cardinality net is factor-\(b\) complete in the sense that every
   \(\mu>0\) occurring as \(\nu_x(z)\) in a centerwise atom certificate has an
   available \(K\) satisfying \((CAH3)\) when \(\mu\ge1\), and \((CAH4)\) when
   \(0<\mu<1\).  If the fixed center \(x\) has no profitable available
   Hall-shadow prefix,
   \[
      D_A(x,K)
      \le
      \psi_x
      \left(
         A_xK^{\rho_x}+\zeta K^{1+\rho_x}
      \right)
      \qquad(K\in\mathcal K_x),
      \tag{CAR1}
   \]
   then every centerwise atom certificate obeys
   \[
      X_x(z)\le(b+1)\Pi_x(z).
      \tag{CAR2}
   \]

   Consequently, if \((CAR1)\) holds for every cut center, then no partial
   atom-marginal certificate can satisfy \((PAM5)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If some centerwise atom certificate violated \((CAR2)\), then \((CAP4)\)
   would hold.  By \cref{cor:centerwise-atom-hardening}, the cardinality-net
   assumption gives an available \(K\) whose top prefix satisfies \((CAH5)\),
   contradicting \((CAR1)\).  This proves \((CAR2)\).

   If a multi-center partial atom certificate satisfied \((PAM5)\), then
   \cref{cor:centerwise-partial-atom-screen} would expose a center satisfying
   \((CAP4)\), contradicting \((CAR2)\) for that center.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fractional balanced Hall-shadow density panel]
   \label{cor:fractional-balanced-hall-shadow-density-panel}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:balanced-hall-shadow-density-screen}.  Let
   \(i\in I\) range over a finite panel of verified balanced Hall-shadow records
   with nonnegative weights \(\lambda_i\).  Record \(i\) consists of a repair
   template \(y_i\), an available prefix cardinality \(K_i\in\mathcal K_{y_i}\),
   and a balance factor \(a_i\ge1\) such that
   \[
      a_i^{-1}K_{y_i}^\circ\le K_i\le a_iK_{y_i}^\circ .
      \tag{FBH1}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      \Delta_i=\Delta_A(y_i,K_i),
      \qquad
      \Theta_i=
      a_i\psi_{y_i}C_{\rho_{y_i}}
      A_{y_i}^{\rho_{y_i}}\zeta^{1-\rho_{y_i}} .
      \tag{FBH2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_iK_i(\Delta_i-\Theta_i)>0,
      \tag{FBH3}
   \]
   then some record in the panel gives a one-record Hall-shadow merge.

   Consequently, if no available Hall-shadow merge exists, every finite
   nonnegative balanced panel has nonpositive surplus \((FBH3)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(\lambda_i\ge0\) and \(K_i>0\), positive total surplus implies that
   at least one record has \(\Delta_i>\Theta_i\).  Together with \((FBH1)\),
   this is exactly the balanced density condition \((BHE3)\)--\((BHE4)\) for
   that record.  Hence
   \cref{cor:balanced-hall-shadow-density-screen} gives a one-record
   Hall-shadow merge.  The nonpositive-panel statement is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sampled balanced Hall-shadow density search]
   \label{cor:sampled-balanced-hall-shadow-density-search}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:fractional-balanced-hall-shadow-density-panel}.  A randomized
   build-time proposal routine, on seed \(s\), returns a finite verified
   balanced panel \(I_s\) with nonnegative weights \(\lambda_{s,i}\).  Define
   its certified balanced surplus by
   \[
      Z(s)=
      \sum_{i\in I_s}
      \lambda_{s,i}K_{s,i}\bigl(\Delta_{s,i}-\Theta_{s,i}\bigr).
      \tag{SBH1}
   \]
   Suppose
   \[
      \E_s Z(s)\ge\Gamma>0,
      \qquad
      Z(s)_+\le M
      \quad\text{almost surely}.
      \tag{SBH2}
   \]
   Then \(B\) independent build-time seeds contain a valid one-record
   Hall-shadow merge with probability at least
   \[
      1-\exp\left(-\frac{B\Gamma}{M}\right).
      \tag{SBH3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   From \((SBH2)\), \(\E Z_+\ge\Gamma\).  Since \(Z_+\le M\), one seed has
   \(Z(s)>0\) with probability at least \(\Gamma/M\).  Thus \(B\) independent
   seeds all fail with probability at most
   \((1-\Gamma/M)^B\le\exp(-B\Gamma/M)\).  For any successful seed,
   \cref{cor:fractional-balanced-hall-shadow-density-panel} extracts a
   deterministic one-record Hall-shadow merge.  Failed samples are discarded.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:fractional-balanced-hall-shadow-density-panel} and
\cref{cor:sampled-balanced-hall-shadow-density-search} are the concrete
build-facing contracts for the Hall-shadow route.  A proposal mechanism may
generate many balanced templates, but it is analyzed only through the scalar
surplus \(K(\Delta-\Theta)\); any positive verified surplus collapses to one
ordinary retained dense prefix.

\begin{corollary}[Sampled clipped Hall-shadow density search]
   \label{cor:sampled-clipped-hall-shadow-density-search}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:fractional-clipped-hall-shadow-density-panel}.  A randomized
   build-time proposal routine, on seed \(s\), returns a finite verified
   clipped panel \(I_s\) with nonnegative weights \(\lambda_{s,i}\).  Define
   its certified clipped surplus by
   \[
      Z(s)=
      \sum_{i\in I_s}
      \lambda_{s,i}K_{s,i}\bigl(\Delta_{s,i}-\Theta_{s,i}\bigr).
      \tag{SCH1}
   \]
   Suppose
   \[
      \E_s Z(s)\ge\Gamma>0,
      \qquad
      Z(s)_+\le M
      \quad\text{almost surely}.
      \tag{SCH2}
   \]
   Then \(B\) independent build-time seeds contain a valid one-record
   Hall-shadow merge with probability at least
   \[
      1-\exp\left(-\frac{B\Gamma}{M}\right).
      \tag{SCH3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The proof is identical to
   \cref{cor:sampled-balanced-hall-shadow-density-search}, using
   \cref{cor:fractional-clipped-hall-shadow-density-panel} in place of
   \cref{cor:fractional-balanced-hall-shadow-density-panel}.  From \((SCH2)\),
   \(\E Z_+\ge\Gamma\), and \(Z_+\le M\) gives
   \(\Pr[Z(s)>0]\ge\Gamma/M\).  Thus \(B\) independent failed samples have
   probability at most \(\exp(-B\Gamma/M)\).  A successful sample is verified
   into one deterministic Hall-shadow merge, and failed samples are discarded.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Clipped Hall-shadow separator endpoint]
   \label{cor:clipped-hall-shadow-separator-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint}.  Suppose that every
   high-correlation co-load residual satisfying \((HCS1)\) admits an uncharged
   clipped Hall-shadow separator with the following certified behavior.  The
   separator chooses a finite template set \(\mathcal X\) and a loss
   \(C_{\rm tr}\), runs the Hall transport test of
   \cref{lem:finite-signature-coload-hall-transport}, and certifies one of two
   alternatives.

   First, the Hall-success alternative \((HCR1)\) holds.  Second, the Hall test
   exposes a cut \(A\subseteq\mathcal L\) satisfying \((FHT5)\), and the
   separator returns a finite clipped Hall-shadow density panel satisfying
   \((FCH1)\)--\((FCH3)\) for that cut.  Then the structured completeness
   condition \((HCS2)\) holds for every high-correlation co-load residual.
   Consequently the dense/spherical separator condition \((DSF2)\) holds, and
   the polylogarithmic ANN endpoint follows.

   The same conclusion holds in Las Vegas build time if, in the second
   alternative, a randomized proposal routine returns verified clipped panels
   whose surplus \(Z(s)\) satisfies \((SCH2)\) with \(\Gamma>0\).  Repeating
   \[
      B\ge \frac{M}{\Gamma}\log\frac1\delta
      \tag{CSE1}
   \]
   independent build-time seeds finds a deterministic Hall-shadow merge with
   probability at least \(1-\delta\); failed samples are discarded.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a surplus dual satisfying \((HCS1)\).  If \((HCR1)\) holds, the first
   alternative of \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint} applies.
   Otherwise the clipped panel has positive surplus \((FCH3)\), so
   \cref{cor:fractional-clipped-hall-shadow-density-panel} extracts a
   one-record Hall-shadow merge.  By
   \cref{cor:one-record-hall-shadow-merge}, this gives the Hall-shadow repair
   criterion, and
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-shadow-repair} supplies the Hall-cut repair
   alternative \((HCR2)\).  Thus every residual satisfies one of the two
   alternatives of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint}, giving \((HCS2)\), and
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-coload-separator-endpoint} gives the
   dense/spherical separator endpoint.

   The sampled statement follows from
   \cref{cor:sampled-clipped-hall-shadow-density-search} and \((CSE1)\).  Once
   a successful seed is verified, the deterministic argument above applies.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:clipped-hall-shadow-separator-endpoint} is the boundary-stable
version of the balanced endpoint.  The balanced test is still the clean
stationary case, but the clipped endpoint is the one an implementation should
use: it keeps the same fractional proof object while allowing the optimal
prefix scale to sit at \(1\), at \(|W_y|\), or at the internal balance point.

\begin{corollary}[Soft-mass Hall-shadow separator endpoint]
   \label{cor:soft-mass-hall-shadow-separator-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint}.  Suppose that every
   high-correlation co-load residual satisfying \((HCS1)\) admits an uncharged
   soft-mass Hall-shadow separator with the following certified behavior.  The
   separator chooses a finite template set \(\mathcal X\) and a loss
   \(C_{\rm tr}\), runs the Hall transport test of
   \cref{lem:finite-signature-coload-hall-transport}, and certifies one of two
   alternatives.

   First, the Hall-success alternative \((HCR1)\) holds.  Second, the Hall test
   exposes a cut \(A\subseteq\mathcal L\) satisfying \((FHT5)\), and the
   separator returns a finite soft-mass clipped Hall-shadow panel satisfying
   \((SHM1)\)--\((SHM3)\) for that cut.  Then the structured completeness
   condition \((HCS2)\) holds for every high-correlation co-load residual.
   Consequently the dense/spherical separator condition \((DSF2)\) holds, and
   the polylogarithmic ANN endpoint follows.

   The same conclusion holds in Las Vegas build time if, in the second
   alternative, a randomized proposal routine returns verified soft-mass panels
   whose surplus \(Z(s)\) satisfies \((SSH2)\) with \(\Gamma>0\).  Repeating
   \[
      B\ge \frac{M}{\Gamma}\log\frac1\delta
      \tag{SSE1}
   \]
   independent build-time seeds finds a deterministic Hall-shadow merge with
   probability at least \(1-\delta\); failed samples are discarded.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a surplus dual satisfying \((HCS1)\).  If \((HCR1)\) holds, the first
   alternative of \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint} applies.
   Otherwise \((SHM3)\) and
   \cref{cor:soft-mass-clipped-hall-shadow-reporter} imply the clipped panel
   surplus \((FCH3)\).  Then
   \cref{cor:fractional-clipped-hall-shadow-density-panel} extracts a
   one-record Hall-shadow merge.  As in
   \cref{cor:clipped-hall-shadow-separator-endpoint}, this gives the
   Hall-shadow repair criterion, supplies the Hall-cut repair alternative
   \((HCR2)\), and hence yields \((HCS2)\) and the dense/spherical endpoint.

   For the sampled version,
   \cref{cor:sampled-soft-mass-clipped-hall-shadow-search} and \((SSE1)\)
   expose a verified deterministic Hall-shadow merge with probability at least
   \(1-\delta\).  Failed proposal samples are discarded and do not enter the
   retained cover.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:soft-mass-hall-shadow-separator-endpoint} is the clipped-scale soft
version of the Hall-shadow endpoint.  It asks the geometric proposal mechanism
only for fractional memberships with enough cut-shadow mass near the clipped
price-density minimizer; the verifier performs all hardening, prefix selection,
and reduced-cost checking.

\begin{corollary}[Exact-scale soft Hall-shadow separator endpoint]
   \label{cor:exact-scale-soft-hall-shadow-separator-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint}.  Suppose that every
   high-correlation co-load residual satisfying \((HCS1)\) admits an uncharged
   exact-scale soft Hall-shadow separator with the following certified behavior.
   The separator chooses a finite template set \(\mathcal X\) and a loss
   \(C_{\rm tr}\), runs the Hall transport test of
   \cref{lem:finite-signature-coload-hall-transport}, and certifies one of two
   alternatives.

   First, the Hall-success alternative \((HCR1)\) holds.  Second, the Hall test
   exposes a cut \(A\subseteq\mathcal L\) satisfying \((FHT5)\), and the
   separator returns a finite exact-scale soft Hall-shadow panel satisfying
   \((ESH1)\)--\((ESH3)\) for that cut.  Then the structured completeness
   condition \((HCS2)\) holds for every high-correlation co-load residual.
   Consequently the dense/spherical separator condition \((DSF2)\) holds, and
   the polylogarithmic ANN endpoint follows.

   The same conclusion holds in Las Vegas build time if, in the second
   alternative, a randomized proposal routine returns verified exact-scale soft
   panels whose surplus \(Z(s)\) satisfies \((SES2)\) with \(\Gamma>0\).
   Repeating
   \[
      B\ge \frac{M}{\Gamma}\log\frac1\delta
      \tag{ESE1}
   \]
   independent build-time seeds finds a deterministic Hall-shadow merge with
   probability at least \(1-\delta\); failed samples are discarded.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a surplus dual satisfying \((HCS1)\).  If \((HCR1)\) holds, the first
   alternative of \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint} applies.
   Otherwise \((ESH3)\) and
   \cref{cor:exact-scale-soft-hall-shadow-reporter} produce a one-record
   Hall-shadow merge.  By
   \cref{cor:one-record-hall-shadow-merge} and
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-shadow-repair}, this supplies the Hall-cut
   repair alternative \((HCR2)\).  Hence every residual satisfies one of the
   alternatives of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint}, giving \((HCS2)\), and
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-coload-separator-endpoint} gives the
   dense/spherical separator endpoint.

   The sampled statement follows from
   \cref{cor:sampled-exact-scale-soft-hall-shadow-search} and \((ESE1)\).
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:exact-scale-soft-hall-shadow-separator-endpoint} is the most compact
form of the current dense-side target.  A proposal mechanism supplies
fractional memberships and a lower cut-shadow mass; the verifier chooses the
best retained prefix cardinality and checks the exact recursive price.  The
clipped and balanced screens are now search heuristics for finding positive
records, not theorem-level restrictions.

\begin{corollary}[Thresholded shadow-routing separator endpoint]
   \label{cor:thresholded-shadow-routing-separator-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint}.  Suppose that every
   high-correlation co-load residual satisfying \((HCS1)\) admits an uncharged
   thresholded shadow-routing separator with the following certified behavior.
   The separator chooses a finite template set \(\mathcal X\) and a loss
   \(C_{\rm tr}\), runs the Hall transport test of
   \cref{lem:finite-signature-coload-hall-transport}, and certifies one of two
   alternatives.

   First, the Hall-success alternative \((HCR1)\) holds.  Second, the Hall test
   exposes a cut \(A\subseteq\mathcal L\) satisfying \((FHT5)\), and the
   separator returns a finite layered thresholded shadow-routing panel satisfying
   \((LTR1)\)--\((LTR4)\) for that cut.  Then the structured completeness
   condition \((HCS2)\) holds for every high-correlation co-load residual.
   Consequently the dense/spherical separator condition \((DSF2)\) holds, and
   the polylogarithmic ANN endpoint follows.

   The same conclusion holds in Las Vegas build time if, in the second
   alternative, a randomized proposal routine returns verified layered
   thresholded panels whose surplus \(Z(s)\), the left side of \((LTR4)\),
   satisfies
   \[
      \E_sZ(s)\ge\Gamma>0,
      \qquad
      Z(s)_+\le M
      \quad\text{almost surely}.
      \tag{TSE1}
   \]
   Repeating
   \[
      B\ge \frac{M}{\Gamma}\log\frac1\delta
      \tag{TSE2}
   \]
   independent build-time seeds finds a deterministic Hall-shadow merge with
   probability at least \(1-\delta\); failed samples are discarded.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a surplus dual satisfying \((HCS1)\).  If \((HCR1)\) holds, the first
   alternative of \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint} applies.
   Otherwise the layered panel has positive surplus \((LTR4)\), so
   \cref{cor:layered-thresholded-shadow-routing-screen} extracts a one-record
   Hall-shadow merge.  By \cref{cor:one-record-hall-shadow-merge} and
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-shadow-repair}, this supplies the Hall-cut
   repair alternative \((HCR2)\).  Hence every residual satisfies one of the
   alternatives of \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint}, giving
   \((HCS2)\), and
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-coload-separator-endpoint} gives the
   dense/spherical separator endpoint.

   For the sampled statement, \((TSE1)\) implies
   \(\Pr[Z(s)>0]\ge\Gamma/M\).  Thus \(B\) independent failed samples have
   probability at most \(\exp(-B\Gamma/M)\).  A successful sample is verified
   into a deterministic merge by the argument above.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:thresholded-shadow-routing-separator-endpoint} is the most
range-reporting-friendly dense endpoint.  The proposal routine may return many
overlapping superlevel layers, but the verifier only uses the scalar surplus
\(\min\{X,K\delta\}\) minus the exact recursive price.  The cardinality split in
\cref{cor:cardinality-optimized-thresholded-routing-screen} is the local
benefit-per-cost test: either the routed layer supports a price-density-winning
prefix below \(X/\delta\), or its total mass pays for a larger prefix directly.
\Cref{cor:thresholded-routing-residual-envelope} is the matching obstruction:
on a surviving residual, every degree-superlevel whose density beats recursive
price is forced above \(X/\delta\) and has total routed mass no larger than its
recursive price.  The cumulative version
\cref{cor:cumulative-superlevel-hall-shadow-reporter} removes the routing
variables entirely for a proposed template: it is enough to certify a one-sided
lower bound on the mass of the superlevel
\(\{p:d_{A,y}(p)\ge\delta\}\).  The clipped cumulative screen
\cref{cor:clipped-cumulative-hall-shadow-screen} then reduces the reporter
target to one scalar density inequality at the canonical clipped price-density
scale \(K_y^\natural\).  The tail-mass screen
\cref{cor:tail-mass-cumulative-hall-shadow-screen} removes the last threshold
choice at that scale: it is enough to certify that the strict tail above the
price-density level \(\Theta_y\) has mass larger than \(K\Theta_y\).  Finally,
\cref{cor:support-limited-tail-hall-shadow-screen} and
\cref{cor:support-limited-cut-center-tail-obstruction} turn this into a
cut-center obstruction: a support-\(K\) assignment can carry at most
\(2K\Theta_y\) paid shadow unless it already exposes a merge.  The
support-sensitive form
\cref{cor:support-sensitive-cut-center-tail-obstruction} removes the support
restriction and leaves the explicit extra term \(s_x\Theta_x\) for large assigned
support.  The exact support-adaptive screen
\cref{cor:support-adaptive-cut-center-price-obstruction} then charges that
large-support branch by the recursive price at the assigned support size, up to
the retained cardinality-net factor.  Equivalently,
\cref{cor:support-price-assignment-separator} compresses the whole failed-cut
branch to one scalar optimization: minimize the support-recursive price
\(\Phi_b(r)\) over full fractional routings of the paid shadow.  If the paid
shadow mass beats this minimum price by the cardinality-net constant, a verified
dense merge already exists.  The independent support-law form
\cref{cor:independent-support-law-assignment-certificate} is the sampling
version of the same test: it is enough to control the expected number
\(\mu_x\) of data points touching each cut center, paying only
\(\mu_x^{\rho_x}\) for query and \(\mu_x+\mu_x^{1+\rho_x}\) for storage.  The
atom-marginal version
\cref{cor:atom-marginal-support-law-certificate} reduces this further to local
stochastic routing weights, with support probability bounded by a union bound
inside each data point.  The partial form
\cref{cor:partial-atom-marginal-support-law-certificate} is the sharpest of
these reductions: a proposal may discard low-value paid atoms and only needs a
positive surplus \(X_z-(b+1)\overline\Phi_b(z)\) on the submeasure it routes.
By \cref{cor:centerwise-partial-atom-screen}, even that partial surplus
separates by cut center: it is enough to find one center whose routed paid mass
beats its own marginal support price.  Finally,
\cref{cor:centerwise-atom-hardening} hardens such a centerwise certificate back
to an ordinary top-prefix Hall-shadow merge at a comparable retained
cardinality.  The converse obstruction
\cref{cor:centerwise-atom-relaxation-tight} says that, under the same
cardinality net, failed prefixes defeat every centerwise atom certificate and
hence every partial atom-marginal certificate.  Thus atom-routing weights are a
proposal language only; the retained dense column and the residual obstruction
are both exactly the standard certified prefix object.

\begin{corollary}[Support-price shadow-routing separator endpoint]
   \label{cor:support-price-shadow-routing-separator-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint}.  Suppose that every
   high-correlation co-load residual satisfying \((HCS1)\) admits an uncharged
   support-price shadow-routing separator with the following certified behavior.
   The separator chooses a finite template set \(\mathcal X\), a factor
   \(b\ge1\), and a loss \(C_{\rm tr}\), runs the Hall transport test of
   \cref{lem:finite-signature-coload-hall-transport}, and certifies one of two
   alternatives.

   First, the Hall-success alternative \((HCR1)\) holds.  Second, the Hall test
   exposes a cut \(A\subseteq\mathcal L\) satisfying \((FHT5)\), the cut-center
   cardinality nets are factor-\(b\) complete on the used supports, all used
   exponents satisfy \(0<\rho_x<1\), and the separator returns a full
   fractional routing \(r\in\mathcal R_{\rm full}(A)\) such that
   \[
      M_A>(b+1)\Phi_b(r),
      \tag{SPR1}
   \]
   with \(M_A\) and \(\Phi_b\) defined in
   \cref{cor:support-price-assignment-separator}.  Then the structured
   completeness condition \((HCS2)\) holds for every high-correlation co-load
   residual.  Consequently the dense/spherical separator condition \((DSF2)\)
   holds, and the polylogarithmic ANN endpoint follows.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a surplus dual satisfying \((HCS1)\).  If \((HCR1)\) holds, the first
   alternative of \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint} applies.
   Otherwise the returned routing satisfies \((SPR1)\), so
   \cref{cor:support-price-assignment-separator} implies that some cut center
   exposes a support-adaptive exact tail Hall-shadow merge.  This is a
   one-record Hall-shadow merge, hence
   \cref{cor:one-record-hall-shadow-merge} and
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-shadow-repair} supply the Hall-cut repair
   alternative \((HCR2)\).  Thus every residual satisfies one of the two
   alternatives of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint}, giving \((HCS2)\), and
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-coload-separator-endpoint} gives the
   dense/spherical separator endpoint.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Marginal support-law separator endpoint]
   \label{cor:marginal-support-law-separator-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint}.  Suppose that every
   high-correlation co-load residual satisfying \((HCS1)\) admits an uncharged
   marginal support-law separator with the following certified behavior.  The
   separator chooses a finite template set \(\mathcal X\), a factor \(b\ge1\),
   and a loss \(C_{\rm tr}\), runs the Hall transport test of
   \cref{lem:finite-signature-coload-hall-transport}, and certifies one of two
   alternatives.

   First, the Hall-success alternative \((HCR1)\) holds.  Second, the Hall test
   exposes a cut \(A\subseteq\mathcal L\) satisfying \((FHT5)\), the cut-center
   cardinality nets are factor-\(b\) complete on every support that can appear,
   all used exponents satisfy \(0<\rho_x<1\), and the separator returns an
   independent pointwise routing law in the sense of
   \cref{cor:independent-support-law-assignment-certificate} such that
   \[
      M_A>(b+1)\widehat\Phi_b .
      \tag{MRL1}
   \]
   Then the structured completeness condition \((HCS2)\) holds for every
   high-correlation co-load residual.  Consequently the dense/spherical
   separator condition \((DSF2)\) holds, and the polylogarithmic ANN endpoint
   follows.

   The same conclusion holds if, in the second alternative, the separator
   returns stochastic atom-routing weights satisfying \((AML1)\) and
   \[
      M_A>(b+1)\overline\Phi_b
      \tag{MRL2}
   \]
   in place of an explicit pointwise routing law.

   Finally, the same conclusion holds if the separator returns partial
   atom-routing weights satisfying \((PAM1)\) and
   \[
      X_z>(b+1)\overline\Phi_b(z).
      \tag{MRL3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a surplus dual satisfying \((HCS1)\).  For the pointwise-law version,
   if \((HCR1)\) holds, the first alternative of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint} applies.  Otherwise
   \((MRL1)\) and
   \cref{cor:independent-support-law-assignment-certificate} produce a
   deterministic pointwise routing exposing a support-adaptive exact tail
   Hall-shadow merge.  As in
   \cref{cor:support-price-shadow-routing-separator-endpoint}, this is a
   one-record Hall-shadow merge and hence supplies the Hall-cut repair
   alternative \((HCR2)\).  Therefore every residual satisfies one of the two
   alternatives of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint}, giving \((HCS2)\), and
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-coload-separator-endpoint} gives the
   dense/spherical separator endpoint.

   For the atom-routing variant, the \((HCR1)\) case is identical.  Otherwise
   \((MRL2)\) and \cref{cor:atom-marginal-support-law-certificate} first
   produce the deterministic support-adaptive Hall-shadow merge, and the same
   endpoint argument applies.

   For the partial atom-routing variant, use
   \cref{cor:partial-atom-marginal-support-law-certificate} in the same way.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Balanced Hall-shadow separator endpoint]
   \label{cor:balanced-hall-shadow-separator-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint}.  Suppose that every
   high-correlation co-load residual satisfying \((HCS1)\) admits an uncharged
   balanced Hall-shadow separator with the following certified behavior.  The
   separator chooses a finite template set \(\mathcal X\) and a loss
   \(C_{\rm tr}\), runs the Hall transport test of
   \cref{lem:finite-signature-coload-hall-transport}, and certifies one of two
   alternatives.

   First, the Hall-success alternative \((HCR1)\) holds.  Second, the Hall test
   exposes a cut \(A\subseteq\mathcal L\) satisfying \((FHT5)\), and the
   separator returns a finite balanced Hall-shadow density panel satisfying
   \((FBH1)\)--\((FBH3)\) for that cut.  Then the structured completeness
   condition \((HCS2)\) holds for every high-correlation co-load residual.
   Consequently the dense/spherical separator condition \((DSF2)\) holds, and
   the polylogarithmic ANN endpoint follows.

   The same conclusion holds in Las Vegas build time if, in the second
   alternative, a randomized proposal routine returns verified balanced panels
   whose surplus \(Z(s)\) satisfies \((SBH2)\) with \(\Gamma>0\).  Repeating
   \[
      B\ge \frac{M}{\Gamma}\log\frac1\delta
      \tag{BSE1}
   \]
   independent build-time seeds finds a deterministic Hall-shadow merge with
   probability at least \(1-\delta\); failed samples are discarded.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a surplus dual satisfying the high-correlation co-load residual
   \((HCS1)\).  If \((HCR1)\) holds, then the first alternative of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint} applies.  Otherwise the
   certified panel has positive surplus \((FBH3)\), so
   \cref{cor:fractional-balanced-hall-shadow-density-panel} extracts a
   one-record Hall-shadow merge.  By
   \cref{cor:one-record-hall-shadow-merge}, this gives the Hall-shadow repair
   criterion, and by
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-shadow-repair} it supplies the Hall-cut
   repair alternative \((HCR2)\).  Thus every residual satisfies one of the two
   alternatives of
   \cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint}; that corollary gives
   \((HCS2)\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-coload-separator-endpoint} gives the
   dense/spherical separator endpoint.

   For the sampled version,
   \cref{cor:sampled-balanced-hall-shadow-density-search} and \((BSE1)\) find a
   deterministic one-record Hall-shadow merge with probability at least
   \(1-\delta\).  Once found, the deterministic argument above applies.  Since
   unsuccessful samples are discarded, they do not affect the retained query or
   storage certificate.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:balanced-hall-shadow-separator-endpoint} is the current shortest
conditional route through the fractional dense-overlap program: after the
spherical reduced-gain test, every remaining residual must either have
affordable aggregate Hall transport or expose positive balanced Hall-shadow
density.  This is the precise theorem that a range-reporting, list-decoding,
additive-quantization, or seeded-template construction must prove to close the
polylogarithmic endpoint.

\begin{corollary}[Proposal-law finite-signature endpoint]
   \label{cor:proposal-law-finite-signature-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:positive-finite-signature-separator-endpoint}.  Suppose that for
   every surplus price system \((\alpha,\tau,\zeta)\) satisfying \((OSF1)\),
   uncharged preprocessing can produce a finite seed law \(s\sim\nu\).  A seed
   materializes a certified column \(A_s\in\mathcal F_\star\), and the verifier
   can evaluate or one-sided lower-certify its reduced gain.  If the seed law
   satisfies
   \[
      \E_{s\sim\nu}
      \operatorname{Gain}_{\alpha,\tau,\zeta}(A_s)>0,
      \tag{PFL1}
   \]
   then the positive finite-signature separator condition \((PFS1)\) holds, and
   the polylogarithmic ANN endpoint follows.

   More quantitatively, if for the current dual state
   \[
      \E_sG(s)\ge\Gamma>0,
      \qquad
      G(s)_+\le M,
      \qquad
      G(s)=\operatorname{Gain}_{\alpha,\tau,\zeta}(A_s),
      \tag{PFL2}
   \]
   then \(B\ge (M/\Gamma)\log(1/\delta)\) independent build-time samples contain
   a positive verified column with probability at least \(1-\delta\).  Failed
   samples are discarded and do not affect the retained query or space bounds.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((PFL1)\) holds, some seed in the finite support has positive reduced
   gain.  Thus every surplus price system satisfying \((OSF1)\) has a
   positive-gain column in \(\mathcal F_\star\), which is exactly \((PFS1)\).
   The endpoint follows from
   \cref{cor:positive-finite-signature-separator-endpoint}.

   The sampling statement is \cref{lem:sampled-proposal-law-separation} applied
   to the signature reduced-gain function \((OSF2)\).  Since retained columns
   are accepted only after verification, unsuccessful proposal samples are
   purely build-time work.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:proposal-law-finite-signature-endpoint} is the endpoint-level version
of \(k\)-means++ or facility seeding that is compatible with the proof.  A
sampler is useful only through its expected reduced gain against the current
dual prices.  Sampling by data mass, squared distance, code likelihood, or
lattice weight is therefore a proposal strategy, not an invariant: the final
certificate is the verified positive-gain column and the finite LP it augments.

\begin{corollary}[Decoded-panel endpoint certificate]
   \label{cor:decoded-panel-polylog-endpoint}
   Fix \(c>1\) and \(\rho_c=1/(2c^2-1)\).  Suppose that after bounded-diameter
   localization, every resident node \(P\), \(|P|=N\), has a finite exact-near-set
   signature system satisfying \((EN1)\), entropy
   \[
      \log(2+|\Sigma|+|\Sigma^+|)\le\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \tag{DPE1}
   \]
   and budgets
   \[
      L_{\sigma_0}\le N^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S\le N^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n.
      \tag{DPE2}
   \]
   Assume moreover that preprocessing supplies a finite decoded bucket-panel
   universe whose records have certified observable profiles, and that for each
   node some finite seed law satisfies the spectrum inequalities
   \((DBP3)\)--\((DBP4)\) with these budgets.  The decoder computes the
   signature and active retained filters in time
   \(d\,N^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n\).  Each nonterminal retained filter invokes a
   strictly smaller-radius child and is charged by that child's full certified
   query and storage prices.

   Then worst-case Euclidean ANN has
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   At each node, \cref{cor:decoded-bucket-panel-profile} converts the decoded
   panel spectrum certificate into feasibility of the existential signature LP
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\).  The exact-near-set version of the preceding
   endpoint proposition then applies with \((DPE1)\)--\((DPE2)\).  The key
   accounting point is unchanged: a retained decoded bucket is only a filter
   column, and its price is the full descendant cost.  Hence many overlapping
   decoded buckets do not multiply over recursive levels; their total active
   contribution has already been bounded by \((DBP4)\) inside the local LP.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Local-error decoded-panel endpoint]
   \label{cor:local-error-decoded-panel-polylog-endpoint}
   In \cref{cor:decoded-panel-polylog-endpoint}, the scalar decoded-panel
   hypothesis \((DBP3)\)--\((DBP4)\) may be replaced at every node by the
   local-error decoded-panel inequalities \((LDBP3)\)--\((LDBP4)\).  It is also
   enough, in the recursive compressed-net setting, to verify the local-error
   bucket-net ratio \((LBNR2)\)--\((LBNR3)\), the first-moment sufficient
   conditions \((LFAL1)\)--\((LFAL2)\), or the local-error shared-DAG storage
   certificates of
   \cref{cor:local-error-distinct-canonical-bucket-net},
   \cref{cor:local-error-dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net}, or
   \cref{cor:local-error-tuple-profile-distinct-storage}.  The
   multiplicity-discounted certificate
   \cref{cor:multiplicity-discounted-distinct-storage} may also be used in its
   local-error setting.

   Under any of these local-error replacements, worst-case Euclidean ANN still
   has
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   At each resident node,
   \cref{cor:local-error-decoded-bucket-panel-profile} converts
   \((LDBP3)\)--\((LDBP4)\) into feasibility of
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\).  The recursive bucket-net ratio version follows
   from \cref{cor:local-error-bucket-net-ratio}, and the first-moment version
   follows from \cref{cor:local-error-first-moment-active-load}.  The
   local-error shared-DAG storage variants already imply feasibility by
   \cref{cor:local-error-distinct-canonical-bucket-net},
   \cref{cor:local-error-dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net}, or
   \cref{cor:local-error-tuple-profile-distinct-storage}; the
   multiplicity-discounted variant implies the same dyadic local-error storage
   bound by \cref{cor:multiplicity-discounted-distinct-storage}.  Once the
   existential signature LP is feasible at each node, the exact-near-set version of
   \cref{prop:fractional-filter-cover-polylog} gives the same endpoint
   accounting as in \cref{cor:decoded-panel-polylog-endpoint}.  Localizing the
   error changes only the local feasibility certificate, not the recursive query
   or storage induction.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Shared-panel positive-separator endpoint]
   \label{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint}
   In \cref{cor:decoded-panel-polylog-endpoint}, replace the primal decoded-panel
   spectrum hypothesis by the following dual shared-panel separator.  At every
   resident node there is a finite universe \(\mathcal Z_\star\) of certified
   local-error shared-canonical decoded panels as in
   \cref{cor:one-sided-shared-panel-column-generation}.  Each panel's canonical
   children have strictly smaller certified radius, and their query and storage
   prices are the full certified descendant prices.  The represented filter
   atoms satisfy the atom bounds needed by
   \cref{lem:exact-near-set-filter-cover}.  For every normalized
   exact-signature price system \((\beta,\tau,\theta)\) satisfying \((ESNO1)\),
   the full panel universe exposes positive shared-panel gain:
   \[
      \max_{z\in\mathcal Z_\star}
      \operatorname{PGain}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(z)>0 .
      \tag{SPP1}
   \]
   Suppose moreover that uncharged preprocessing has a one-sided oracle for this
   universe in the sense of
   \cref{cor:one-sided-shared-panel-column-generation}, and that the exact
   signature decoder and retained active-filter reporter have the same time,
   entropy, and budget bounds \((DPE1)\)--\((DPE2)\).

   Then preprocessing constructs the local exact-signature covers required by
   the exact-near-set version of
   \cref{prop:fractional-filter-cover-polylog}.  Consequently worst-case
   Euclidean ANN has
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   The same conclusion holds with Las Vegas build time if, whenever a positive
   inactive panel exists during restricted column generation, a randomized
   proposal law returns a verified one-sided positive-gain panel with
   probability at least \(p_E>0\).  Failed proposals are discarded.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix one resident node and its finite panel universe.  Condition \((SPP1)\)
   is exactly \((OSPC3)\) for the local-error shared-panel profile LP.  Hence
   \cref{cor:one-sided-shared-panel-column-generation} constructs, by finite
   restricted column generation, a feasible local-error profile cover over the
   retained panels.  Applying
   \cref{cor:local-error-observable-profile-cover} converts this feasible
   profile cover into feasibility of the existential signature LP
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\).  The atom bounds then allow
   \cref{lem:exact-near-set-filter-cover} to materialize the local cover with
   only the logarithmic signature factor.

   Since every nonterminal canonical child in a retained panel is charged by its
   full already-certified descendant query and storage prices, recursive
   overlap is paid inside the local LP.  With \((DPE1)\)--\((DPE2)\), the
   exact-near-set version of \cref{prop:fractional-filter-cover-polylog}
   applies at all localized nodes and gives the displayed global query and
   storage bounds.  The Las Vegas statement is the randomized part of
   \cref{cor:one-sided-shared-panel-column-generation}; unsuccessful proposals
   are build-time work only.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Witness-law shared-panel endpoint]
   \label{cor:witness-law-shared-panel-endpoint}
   In \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint}, replace the
   positive-gain hypothesis \((SPP1)\) by the following nodewise witness-law
   hypothesis.  For every resident node and every normalized exact-signature
   price system \((\beta,\tau,\theta)\) satisfying \((ESNO1)\), there is a
   finite seed law \(\nu\) on the full certified panel universe
   \(\mathcal Z_\star\), certified envelopes
   \[
      U_z^{\rm sh}\le\widehat U_z
      \le
      \Gamma_z+\sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal K_z}u_{z,\kappa},
      \qquad u_{z,\kappa}\ge0,
      \tag{WLE1}
   \]
   and a finite witness universe \(\Omega\) with child witness laws
   \(\pi_{z,\kappa}\), such that the dual-priced congestion envelopes
   \(J(\omega)\) satisfy \((DPW2)\).  With
   \[
      A_\nu=\E_{z\sim\nu}\mathsf H_z(\beta),
      \qquad
      Q_\nu^{(\rho)}=\E_{z\sim\nu}\mathsf L_z^{(\rho)}(\tau),
      \tag{WLE2}
   \]
   assume that \(A_\nu>0\) and, for some \(q,u\ge0\) with \(q+u<1\),
   \[
      Q_\nu^{(\rho)}\le qA_\nu,
      \tag{WLE3}
   \]
   \[
      \theta\,\E_{z\sim\nu}\Gamma_z+
      \sum_{\omega\in\Omega}J(\omega)
      \le uA_\nu .
      \tag{WLE4}
   \]
   Then the positive shared-panel separator \((SPP1)\) holds at every node.
   Consequently the conclusion of
   \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint} applies:
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   The same endpoint follows from the first-moment version obtained by
   replacing \(Q_\nu^{(\rho)}\) in \((WLE2)\)--\((WLE3)\) by
   \(Q_\nu^{(1)}=\E_{z\sim\nu}\mathsf L_z^{(1)}(\tau)\).  Thus the remaining
   geometric theorem may be stated entirely as a dual-priced witness law: useful
   hit must beat active query load plus witness-congestion storage, with every
   retained child stored once through its canonical identifier.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a node and a normalized price system.  The hypotheses are exactly those
   of \cref{cor:dual-priced-witness-storage-separator}, with \((WLE1)\)
   supplying both the certified upper envelope \(U_z^{\rm sh}\le\widehat U_z\)
   and the witness decomposition \((DPW1)\).  Therefore the seed law satisfies
   the certified-storage separator inequality \((CSWP2)\).  Since
   \(\widehat U_z\ge U_z^{\rm sh}\), the proof of
   \cref{cor:certified-storage-weighted-panel-separator} converts this, for the
   fixed dual, into positive expected shared-panel gain.  A finite support law
   with positive expected gain contains some deterministic panel with positive
   shared-panel gain.  Since the price system was arbitrary, \((SPP1)\) holds at
   the node.

   Applying the same argument at every localized resident node gives the
   hypothesis of \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint}, which
   proves the displayed global query and storage bounds.  The first-moment
   variant is the first-moment clause of
   \cref{cor:dual-priced-witness-storage-separator}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Witness-law residual obstruction]
   \label{cor:witness-law-residual-obstruction}
   Work at one resident node in the setting of
   \cref{cor:witness-law-shared-panel-endpoint}.  Fix the class of admissible
   finite witness reports available to preprocessing.  Against a normalized
   exact-signature price system \((\beta,\tau,\theta)\), such a report
   \(\mathcal R\) consists of a finite seed law \(\nu_{\mathcal R}\), certified
   envelopes as in \((WLE1)\), a finite witness universe, child witness laws,
   and certified congestion envelopes satisfying \((DPW2)\).  Define
   \[
      A_{\mathcal R}
      =
      \E_{z\sim\nu_{\mathcal R}}\mathsf H_z(\beta),
      \qquad
      Q_{\mathcal R}
      =
      \E_{z\sim\nu_{\mathcal R}}\mathsf L_z^{(\rho)}(\tau),
      \tag{WRO1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      W_{\mathcal R}
      =
      \theta\,\E_{z\sim\nu_{\mathcal R}}\Gamma_z
      +
      \sum_{\omega\in\Omega_{\mathcal R}}J_{\mathcal R}(\omega).
      \tag{WRO2}
   \]
   The node satisfies the witness-law hypothesis of
   \cref{cor:witness-law-shared-panel-endpoint} for this report class if and
   only if no normalized price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\) has the residual
   property
   \[
      A_{\mathcal R}\le Q_{\mathcal R}+W_{\mathcal R}
      \qquad(\mathcal R\text{ admissible}).
      \tag{WRO3}
   \]

   Equivalently, for any \(0<\varepsilon<1\), a residual satisfying
   \((WRO3)\) has the following split for every admissible report with
   \(A_{\mathcal R}>0\): either
   \[
      Q_{\mathcal R}\ge(1-\varepsilon)A_{\mathcal R}
      \tag{WRO4}
   \]
   or
   \[
      W_{\mathcal R}\ge\varepsilon A_{\mathcal R}.
      \tag{WRO5}
   \]
   Thus the remaining geometric theorem may be phrased as a pure residual
   exclusion: every normalized dual must admit one certified report whose useful
   hit beats active load plus dual-priced witness storage.
   The same equivalence holds for the first-moment relaxation after replacing
   \(Q_{\mathcal R}\) by
   \(\E_{z\sim\nu_{\mathcal R}}\mathsf L_z^{(1)}(\tau)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed report with \(A_{\mathcal R}>0\), the inequalities
   \((WLE3)\)--\((WLE4)\) hold for some \(q,u\ge0\) with \(q+u<1\) if and only
   if
   \[
      Q_{\mathcal R}+W_{\mathcal R}<A_{\mathcal R}.
   \]
   Indeed, the forward direction is immediate, and the reverse direction follows
   by taking
   \(q=Q_{\mathcal R}/A_{\mathcal R}\) and
   \(u=W_{\mathcal R}/A_{\mathcal R}\).  Therefore failure of the witness-law
   hypothesis for the fixed report class is exactly the existence of a
   normalized price system for which every admissible report satisfies
   \((WRO3)\).  Finally, if both \((WRO4)\) and \((WRO5)\) failed for some
   report, then
   \(Q_{\mathcal R}+W_{\mathcal R}<A_{\mathcal R}\), contradicting
   \((WRO3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sampled witness-report separation]
   \label{cor:sampled-witness-report-separation}
   Work at one resident node and fix a normalized exact-signature price system
   \((\beta,\tau,\theta)\) satisfying \((ESNO1)\).  A build-time seed
   \(s\sim\Pi\) returns either \(\bot\), interpreted as zero surplus, or an
   admissible finite witness report \(\mathcal R_s\) in the sense of
   \cref{cor:witness-law-residual-obstruction}.  Let
   \[
      Z(s)=
      A_{\mathcal R_s}-Q_{\mathcal R_s}-W_{\mathcal R_s}
      \tag{SWR1}
   \]
   for non-null reports and \(Z(s)=0\) for \(\bot\).  Suppose the verifier
   certifies
   \[
      \E_s Z(s)\ge\Gamma>0,
      \qquad
      Z(s)_+\le M
      \quad\text{almost surely}.
      \tag{SWR2}
   \]
   Then \(B\) independent build-time samples contain an admissible report with
   positive witness surplus with probability at least
   \[
      1-\exp\left(-\frac{B\Gamma}{M}\right).
      \tag{SWR3}
   \]
   In particular,
   \[
      B\ge \frac{M}{\Gamma}\log\frac1\delta
      \tag{SWR4}
   \]
   suffices to find such a report with probability at least \(1-\delta\).

   A successful report satisfies the witness-law hypothesis for this fixed
   price system, and therefore exposes a deterministic positive shared-panel
   gain after the exact verifier expands its finite seed law.  If a sampler with
   \((SWR2)\) exists for every normalized residual price system at every node,
   then the witness-law shared-panel endpoint applies.  Failed samples and null
   reports are discarded and are never charged to query time or storage.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The proof is the same positive-part argument as
   \cref{lem:sampled-proposal-law-separation}.  Since
   \(Z=Z_+-Z_-\), \((SWR2)\) implies \(\E Z_+\ge\Gamma\).  With
   \(Z_+\le M\), this gives
   \[
      \Pr[Z(s)>0]\ge\Gamma/M.
   \]
   Hence \(B\) independent samples all fail with probability at most
   \((1-\Gamma/M)^B\le\exp(-B\Gamma/M)\).

   If \(Z(s)>0\), then
   \(A_{\mathcal R_s}>Q_{\mathcal R_s}+W_{\mathcal R_s}\), so
   \(A_{\mathcal R_s}>0\) and the proof of
   \cref{cor:witness-law-residual-obstruction} supplies
   \((WLE3)\)--\((WLE4)\) with
   \(q=Q_{\mathcal R_s}/A_{\mathcal R_s}\) and
   \(u=W_{\mathcal R_s}/A_{\mathcal R_s}\).  Thus
   \cref{cor:dual-priced-witness-storage-separator}, followed by the fixed-dual
   implication in the proof of
   \cref{cor:witness-law-shared-panel-endpoint}, exposes a deterministic
   positive shared-panel gain for this price system.  The final nodewise
   endpoint statement follows by invoking the same sampled search whenever
   restricted column generation exposes a normalized residual price system.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Witness-report panel hardening]
   \label{cor:witness-report-panel-hardening}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:witness-law-residual-obstruction}, and fix a normalized price
   system.  Let \(I\) be a finite panel of admissible witness reports with
   nonnegative weights \(\lambda_i\).  If
   \[
      \sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i
      \left(
         A_{\mathcal R_i}-Q_{\mathcal R_i}-W_{\mathcal R_i}
      \right)>0,
      \tag{WRP1}
   \]
   then some report \(\mathcal R_i\) with \(\lambda_i>0\) has positive witness
   surplus
   \[
      A_{\mathcal R_i}>Q_{\mathcal R_i}+W_{\mathcal R_i}.
      \tag{WRP2}
   \]
   Consequently it exposes a deterministic positive shared-panel gain for the
   fixed price system.

   Equivalently, in any residual satisfying \((WRO3)\), every finite
   nonnegative panel of admissible reports satisfies the reverse inequality in
   \((WRP1)\).  Thus a list decoder, range reporter, additive-quantization
   search, or facility routine may output a whole batch of candidate certified
   reports; only the aggregate surplus is needed for analysis, and the verifier
   retains one positive report.

   The same Las Vegas sampling guarantee as
   \cref{cor:sampled-witness-report-separation} holds for sampled panels: if a
   seed returns a finite weighted panel with surplus \(Z_{\rm pan}(s)\), and
   \[
      \E_sZ_{\rm pan}(s)\ge\Gamma>0,
      \qquad
      Z_{\rm pan}(s)_+\le M
      \quad\text{almost surely},
      \tag{WRP3}
   \]
   then \(B\ge(M/\Gamma)\log(1/\delta)\) independent build-time seeds find a
   panel containing a positive report with probability at least \(1-\delta\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If every positive-weight report had
   \(A_{\mathcal R_i}\le Q_{\mathcal R_i}+W_{\mathcal R_i}\), then the left side
   of \((WRP1)\) would be nonpositive.  Hence a positive aggregate surplus
   contains one positive-surplus report.  Applying the final paragraph of the
   proof of \cref{cor:sampled-witness-report-separation} to that report exposes
   positive shared-panel gain for the fixed price system.  The residual
   statement is the contrapositive.

   For sampled panels, apply the same positive-part argument to
   \(Z_{\rm pan}\): condition \((WRP3)\) gives
   \(\Pr[Z_{\rm pan}(s)>0]\ge\Gamma/M\), and a positive panel contains one
   positive report by the deterministic part.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Benefit-allocated witness-density screen]
   \label{cor:benefit-allocated-witness-density-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:witness-law-residual-obstruction}, and fix one admissible witness
   report \(\mathcal R\).  Let its witness universe be partitioned into finitely
   many classes
   \[
      \Omega_{\mathcal R}=\dot\bigcup_{\ell\in\mathcal L}\Omega_\ell .
   \]
   Suppose the verifier certifies nonnegative benefit allocations \(B_\ell\) and
   congestion upper bounds \(C_\ell\) such that
   \[
      \sum_{\ell\in\mathcal L}B_\ell
      \le
      A_{\mathcal R}-Q_{\mathcal R}
      -\theta\,\E_{z\sim\nu_{\mathcal R}}\Gamma_z,
      \tag{BAW1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{\omega\in\Omega_\ell}J_{\mathcal R}(\omega)
      \le C_\ell
      \qquad(\ell\in\mathcal L).
      \tag{BAW2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_{\ell\in\mathcal L}B_\ell
      >
      \sum_{\ell\in\mathcal L}C_\ell,
      \tag{BAW3}
   \]
   then \(\mathcal R\) has positive witness surplus and exposes a deterministic
   positive shared-panel gain for the fixed price system.  Moreover some class
   \(\ell\) satisfies
   \[
      B_\ell>C_\ell .
      \tag{BAW4}
   \]

   Consequently, in any residual satisfying \((WRO3)\), every certified
   benefit allocation over every admissible witness report satisfies the reverse
   of \((BAW3)\).  If the classes are tuple profiles, dyadic price scales,
   range-report cells, or list-decoder output types, the remaining geometric
   theorem may search for a single class with positive benefit-minus-congestion
   surplus.

   The same statement holds with first-moment active load after replacing
   \(Q_{\mathcal R}\) in \((BAW1)\) by
   \(\E_{z\sim\nu_{\mathcal R}}\mathsf L_z^{(1)}(\tau)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \((BAW2)\),
   \[
      \sum_{\omega\in\Omega_{\mathcal R}}J_{\mathcal R}(\omega)
      =
      \sum_{\ell\in\mathcal L}
      \sum_{\omega\in\Omega_\ell}J_{\mathcal R}(\omega)
      \le
      \sum_{\ell\in\mathcal L}C_\ell .
   \]
   Combining this with \((BAW1)\)--\((BAW3)\) gives
   \[
      A_{\mathcal R}-Q_{\mathcal R}
      -\theta\,\E_{z\sim\nu_{\mathcal R}}\Gamma_z
      >
      \sum_{\omega\in\Omega_{\mathcal R}}J_{\mathcal R}(\omega),
   \]
   which is exactly
   \(A_{\mathcal R}>Q_{\mathcal R}+W_{\mathcal R}\).  Thus
   \cref{cor:sampled-witness-report-separation} exposes positive shared-panel
   gain from this report.  If every class had \(B_\ell\le C_\ell\), then
   \((BAW3)\) would fail, so some class satisfies \((BAW4)\).  The residual and
   first-moment statements are the corresponding contrapositives and the same
   calculation with the relaxed query load.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Class-local witness-density screen]
   \label{cor:class-local-witness-density-screen}
   Work at one resident node and fix a normalized exact-signature price system.
   A class-local witness record is an admissible witness report
   \(\mathcal R_\ell\), together with certified numbers \(B_\ell,C_\ell\ge0\)
   satisfying
   \[
      B_\ell\le A_{\mathcal R_\ell}-Q_{\mathcal R_\ell},
      \qquad
      W_{\mathcal R_\ell}\le C_\ell .
      \tag{CLW1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      B_\ell>C_\ell,
      \tag{CLW2}
   \]
   then \(\mathcal R_\ell\) has positive witness surplus and exposes a
   deterministic positive shared-panel gain for the fixed price system.

   More generally, for any finite nonnegative panel of class-local witness
   records, if
   \[
      \sum_\ell\lambda_\ell B_\ell>
      \sum_\ell\lambda_\ell C_\ell,
      \tag{CLW3}
   \]
   then some record has positive witness surplus.  Hence in any residual
   satisfying \((WRO3)\), every class-local witness record obeys
   \[
      B_\ell\le C_\ell .
      \tag{CLW4}
   \]

   In the common tuple-profile or range-reporting form, suppose the congestion
   certificate has
   \[
      C_\ell=N_\ell e^{-I_\ell},
      \qquad N_\ell>0,
      \tag{CLW5}
   \]
   where \(N_\ell\) is a certified profile count or cell volume and \(I_\ell\)
   is a certified energy.  Then a residual can survive only if
   \[
      B_\ell\le N_\ell e^{-I_\ell}
      \quad\text{for every class-local record,}
      \tag{CLW6}
   \]
   equivalently, for \(B_\ell>0\),
   \[
      \log B_\ell-\log N_\ell+I_\ell\le0 .
      \tag{CLW7}
   \]
   Thus a tuple-profile proof may target one entropy-minus-energy violation:
   useful benefit density larger than the certified witness density.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   From \((CLW1)\)--\((CLW2)\),
   \[
      A_{\mathcal R_\ell}-Q_{\mathcal R_\ell}
      >
      W_{\mathcal R_\ell},
   \]
   so \(\mathcal R_\ell\) has positive witness surplus.  The conclusion follows
   from \cref{cor:sampled-witness-report-separation} applied to the point mass
   on this report.

   If \((CLW3)\) holds, at least one positive-weight record satisfies
   \(B_\ell>C_\ell\), and the one-record case applies.  The residual envelope
   \((CLW4)\) is the contrapositive.  Substituting \((CLW5)\) into
   \((CLW4)\) gives \((CLW6)\), and taking logarithms gives \((CLW7)\) when
   \(B_\ell>0\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Gaussian tuple-profile witness-density residual]
   \label{cor:gaussian-tuple-profile-witness-density}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:class-local-witness-density-screen}.  Let a materializable
   class-local record be indexed by a two-point Gaussian tuple profile
   \(\pi\).  The profile has cardinality \(M_\pi\), and there are parameters
   \(-1<\theta_\pi<1\) and \(\beta_\pi\ge0\) such that every
   \((x,y)\in\pi\) satisfies
   \[
      \ip{x}{y}\le\theta_\pi,
      \qquad
      T-\ip{\mu}{x}\ge\beta_\pi,
      \qquad
      T-\ip{\mu}{y}\ge\beta_\pi .
      \tag{GTW1}
   \]
   Suppose the verifier certifies useful benefit \(B_\pi\) for this class and
   its witness congestion is bounded by the Gaussian profile term
   \[
      C_\pi
      =
      M_\pi\exp\left(-\frac{\beta_\pi^2}{1+\theta_\pi}\right).
      \tag{GTW2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      B_\pi>
      M_\pi\exp\left(-\frac{\beta_\pi^2}{1+\theta_\pi}\right),
      \tag{GTW3}
   \]
   then the record exposes a deterministic positive shared-panel gain.
   Consequently, in any residual satisfying \((WRO3)\), every such
   materializable Gaussian pair-profile record obeys
   \[
      B_\pi
      \le
      M_\pi\exp\left(-\frac{\beta_\pi^2}{1+\theta_\pi}\right),
      \tag{GTW4}
   \]
   or, for \(B_\pi>0\),
   \[
      \log B_\pi-\log M_\pi+\frac{\beta_\pi^2}{1+\theta_\pi}\le0.
      \tag{GTW5}
   \]

   More generally, if the two threshold margins only satisfy
   \[
      T-\ip{\mu}{x}+T-\ip{\mu}{y}\ge s_\pi\ge0
      \tag{GTW6}
   \]
   throughout the profile, then the same statements hold with
   \(\beta_\pi^2/(1+\theta_\pi)\) replaced by
   \(s_\pi^2/(4(1+\theta_\pi))\).

   Thus the low-correlation tuple-profile part of the remaining theorem has the
   explicit entropy-energy form: a residual can survive only when profile
   benefit is at most profile entropy times the certified Gaussian collision
   probability.  Profiles violating this inequality must either be
   materialized as witness reports or handed to the high-correlation dense
   reporter.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{cor:two-point-tuple-profile-gaussian}, the Gaussian pair-profile
   contribution is bounded by the right side of \((GTW2)\), and by
   \(M_\pi\exp(-s_\pi^2/(4(1+\theta_\pi)))\) under \((GTW6)\).  These are
   exactly the congestion certificates \(C_\ell=N_\ell e^{-I_\ell}\) in
   \cref{cor:class-local-witness-density-screen}, with \(N_\ell=M_\pi\) and the
   displayed energy.  The positive and residual conclusions are therefore
   \((CLW2)\)--\((CLW7)\) specialized to this profile.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Correlation-split witness-profile residual]
   \label{cor:correlation-split-witness-profile-residual}
   Work at one resident node and fix the normalized dual prices used in
   \cref{cor:witness-law-residual-obstruction}.  Let a materializable two-point
   witness profile have useful benefit split as
   \[
      B_\pi=B_\pi^{\rm lo}+B_\pi^{\rm hi}.
      \tag{WPR1}
   \]
   Assume the low-correlation part is materializable in the sense of
   \cref{cor:gaussian-tuple-profile-witness-density}, with certified count
   \(M_\pi^{\rm lo}\), threshold margin \(\beta_\pi^{\rm lo}\), and pair
   correlation at most \(\theta_\pi^{\rm lo}\).  Put
   \[
      C_\pi^{\rm lo}
      =
      M_\pi^{\rm lo}
      \exp\!\left(
         -\frac{(\beta_\pi^{\rm lo})^2}{1+\theta_\pi^{\rm lo}}
      \right).
      \tag{WPR2}
   \]

   For the high-correlation part, suppose preprocessing reports a finite
   pair-star panel in the setting of
   \cref{cor:paid-pair-star-panel-certificate}.  Thus the panel has records
   \(i\in I\), weights \(\lambda_i\ge0\), lower paid-mass certificates \(X_i\),
   upper size certificates \(K_i\), query prices \(A_{x_i}\), and recursive
   price envelope
   \[
      P_i
      =
      \psi_\star
      \left(
         A_{x_i}K_i^{\rho_\star}
         +\sigma K_i^{1+\rho_\star}
      \right).
      \tag{WPR3}
   \]
   Let \(E_\pi^{\rm hi}\ge0\) be a certified unreported tail allowance, and
   assume the high-correlation benefit routed through this panel satisfies
   \[
      B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \le
      E_\pi^{\rm hi}+\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_iX_i .
      \tag{WPR4}
   \]

   If
   \[
      B_\pi
      >
      C_\pi^{\rm lo}
      +E_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_iP_i ,
      \tag{WPR5}
   \]
   then either the low-correlation record exposes a positive shared-panel gain,
   or the high-correlation panel exposes a positive smaller-radius dense prefix.
   Consequently, in any residual satisfying \((WRO3)\) and in which no reported
   pair-star prefix has positive reduced gain, every such split profile obeys
   \[
      B_\pi
      \le
      C_\pi^{\rm lo}
      +E_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_iP_i .
      \tag{WPR6}
   \]

   If the high-correlation report comes from the raw correlation split of
   \cref{cor:correlation-split-gaussian-profile-layer}, one may take
   \(E_\pi^{\rm hi}=2|P|J_{\rm hi}\Lambda\) after all star records with
   certified scale at least \(\Lambda\) have been offered to the dense verifier.
   In the fixed-threshold guarded version of
   \cref{cor:correlation-split-fixed-threshold-star-screen}, this becomes the
   explicit tail \(2|P|J_{\rm hi}\Lambda_0\).  Thus high-correlation overlap is
   not a separate branching loss: it is either converted into paid dense-prefix
   price or remains as a named residual tail.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose neither separator fires.  Since the low-correlation record does not
   expose positive gain, the residual conclusion of
   \cref{cor:gaussian-tuple-profile-witness-density} gives
   \(B_\pi^{\rm lo}\le C_\pi^{\rm lo}\).  Since no reported pair-star prefix has
   positive reduced gain, the converse statement in
   \cref{cor:paid-pair-star-panel-certificate} gives
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_iX_i\le\sum_i\lambda_iP_i .
   \]
   Combining this inequality with \((WPR1)\) and \((WPR4)\) yields
   \[
      B_\pi
      \le
      C_\pi^{\rm lo}
      +E_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +\sum_i\lambda_iP_i ,
   \]
   which is the negation of \((WPR5)\).  Therefore any violation of
   \((WPR5)\) must trigger one of the two certified separators, and the residual
   envelope \((WPR6)\) is the contrapositive.

   The final tail choices are exactly the no-large-star conclusions
   \((CSG4)\)--\((CSG7)\) and \((CFS5)\)--\((CFS6)\), read as unreported
   high-correlation benefit allowances.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Split-profile panel hardening]
   \label{cor:split-profile-panel-hardening}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:correlation-split-witness-profile-residual}.  Let \(\Pi\) be a
   finite family of split witness profiles, with nonnegative panel weights
   \(\eta_\pi\).  For each \(\pi\in\Pi\), let
   \[
      B_\pi=B_\pi^{\rm lo}+B_\pi^{\rm hi},\qquad
      C_\pi^{\rm lo},\qquad E_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \tag{WPP1}
   \]
   be the certified benefit split, low-correlation Gaussian congestion, and
   unreported high-correlation tail allowance.  Suppose the high-correlation
   part of profile \(\pi\) is routed through pair-star records \(i\in I_\pi\)
   with lower certificates \(X_{\pi,i}\), recursive price envelopes
   \(P_{\pi,i}\), and internal weights \(\lambda_{\pi,i}\ge0\), so that
   \[
      B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \le
      E_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +\sum_{i\in I_\pi}\lambda_{\pi,i}X_{\pi,i}.
      \tag{WPP2}
   \]
   Assume all reported star records belong to one finite dense-prefix verifier,
   so their disjoint union with weights \(\eta_\pi\lambda_{\pi,i}\) is an
   admissible panel for
   \cref{cor:paid-pair-star-panel-certificate}.

   If the aggregate split surplus is positive,
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi
      \left(
         B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo}-E_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \right)
      >
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi
      \sum_{i\in I_\pi}\lambda_{\pi,i}P_{\pi,i},
      \tag{WPP3}
   \]
   then either some low-correlation profile record exposes a positive
   shared-panel gain, or the union of the high-correlation star records exposes
   a positive smaller-radius dense prefix.

   Consequently, in any residual satisfying \((WRO3)\) and in which no reported
   pair-star prefix has positive reduced gain, every finite nonnegative
   split-profile panel obeys
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi B_\pi
      \le
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi
      \left(
         C_\pi^{\rm lo}
         +E_\pi^{\rm hi}
         +\sum_{i\in I_\pi}\lambda_{\pi,i}P_{\pi,i}
      \right).
      \tag{WPP4}
   \]
   Thus a list decoder, range reporter, facility routine, additive
   quantization search, or lattice decoder may be analyzed at the level of
   aggregate profile surplus.  The verifier still retains only one ordinary
   positive witness record or one ordinary smaller-radius dense prefix.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose no low-correlation profile record exposes positive shared-panel gain.
   Applying \cref{cor:gaussian-tuple-profile-witness-density} to each
   materialized low profile gives
   \[
      B_\pi^{\rm lo}\le C_\pi^{\rm lo}
      \qquad(\pi\in\Pi).
      \tag{WPP5}
   \]
   Combining \((WPP1)\), \((WPP2)\), and \((WPP5)\), the strict aggregate
   inequality \((WPP3)\) implies
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi
      \sum_{i\in I_\pi}\lambda_{\pi,i}X_{\pi,i}
      >
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi
      \sum_{i\in I_\pi}\lambda_{\pi,i}P_{\pi,i}.
      \tag{WPP6}
   \]
   This is exactly the paid pair-star panel inequality \((PPC2)\) for the union
   panel with weights \(\eta_\pi\lambda_{\pi,i}\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:paid-pair-star-panel-certificate} exposes a positive
   smaller-radius dense prefix.  The residual envelope \((WPP4)\) is the
   contrapositive of the positive statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Min-cost split-profile envelope]
   \label{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:split-profile-panel-hardening}, and fix the
   finite dense-prefix verifier for the reported high-correlation stars.  For a
   split profile \(\pi\), call a high-correlation routing certificate admissible
   if it consists of a tail allowance \(E_\pi^{\rm hi}\), records
   \(i\in I_\pi\), weights \(\lambda_{\pi,i}\ge0\), lower certificates
   \(X_{\pi,i}\), and price envelopes \(P_{\pi,i}\), satisfying \((WPP2)\) and
   admissible for the common paid pair-star verifier.  Define its cost by
   \[
      \operatorname{cost}_\pi(E,I,\lambda)
      =
      E_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +\sum_{i\in I_\pi}\lambda_{\pi,i}P_{\pi,i},
      \tag{WMC1}
   \]
   and let
   \[
      \Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}
      =
      \inf\operatorname{cost}_\pi(E,I,\lambda),
      \tag{WMC2}
   \]
   with value \(+\infty\) if no admissible certificate exists.

   If a finite nonnegative split-profile panel satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi
      \left(
         B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo}-\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \right)>0,
      \tag{WMC3}
   \]
   then either some low-correlation profile record exposes a positive
   shared-panel gain, or the dense verifier exposes a positive smaller-radius
   prefix.

   Consequently, in any residual satisfying \((WRO3)\) and in which no reported
   pair-star prefix has positive reduced gain, every finite nonnegative panel
   obeys the optimized scalar envelope
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi B_\pi
      \le
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi
      \left(
         C_\pi^{\rm lo}+\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \right).
      \tag{WMC4}
   \]
   Thus the high-correlation side of the dense-overlap proof can be treated as
   a fractional min-cost routing problem over certified star records and
   explicit tails.  The optimizer may be found by arbitrarily expensive
   preprocessing; only a verified positive prefix, if one exists, enters the
   retained index.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((WMC3)\) holds, then all profiles with \(\eta_\pi>0\) and positive
   contribution have finite \(\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}\).  Choose admissible routing
   certificates whose costs are within \(\varepsilon_\pi>0\) of
   \(\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}\), with
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi\varepsilon_\pi
      <
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi
      \left(
         B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo}-\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \right).
   \]
   Substituting these certificates turns \((WMC3)\) into the strict aggregate
   surplus condition \((WPP3)\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:split-profile-panel-hardening} exposes either a low-correlation
   positive witness record or a high-correlation positive dense prefix.
   The residual envelope \((WMC4)\) is the contrapositive, using the same
   approximation of the infimum if a strict violation of \((WMC4)\) occurred.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Atomized high-correlation routing dual]
   \label{cor:atomized-high-correlation-routing-dual}
   Fix one high-correlation split profile \(\pi\).  Let \(\mathcal A_\pi\) be a
   finite atom set with atom benefits \(b_a\ge0\), and write
   \[
      B_\pi^{\rm hi}=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_\pi}b_a .
      \tag{AHR1}
   \]
   Let \(I_\pi\) be a finite set of certified pair-star records.  Record \(i\)
   has price \(P_i\ge0\) and nonnegative atom lower certificates
   \(x_{i,a}\ge0\).  Put
   \[
      X_i=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_\pi}x_{i,a},
      \tag{AHR2}
   \]
   and assume that every finite panel of these records with lower certificates
   \(X_i\) is admissible for
   \cref{cor:paid-pair-star-panel-certificate}.

   Define the atomized high-correlation routing value by
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Phi_{\pi,{\rm at}}^{\rm hi}=\min
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{a\in\mathcal A_\pi}e_a+\sum_{i\in I_\pi}\lambda_iP_i\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        e_a+\sum_{i\in I_\pi}\lambda_ix_{i,a}\ge b_a
        \qquad(a\in\mathcal A_\pi),\\[0.8em]
      & e_a\ge0,\qquad \lambda_i\ge0 .
   \end{array}
      \tag{AHR3}
   \]
   Then the dual formula is
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Phi_{\pi,{\rm at}}^{\rm hi}=\max
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{a\in\mathcal A_\pi}b_ay_a\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        0\le y_a\le1
        \qquad(a\in\mathcal A_\pi),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{a\in\mathcal A_\pi}x_{i,a}y_a\le P_i
        \qquad(i\in I_\pi).
   \end{array}
      \tag{AHR4}
   \]

   Moreover, any feasible primal routing with
   \[
      \sum_a e_a+\sum_i\lambda_iP_i
      <
      B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \tag{AHR5}
   \]
   exposes a positive smaller-radius dense prefix.  Conversely, if no panel of
   these records exposes such a prefix, then
   \[
      X_i\le P_i\qquad(i\in I_\pi),
      \tag{AHR6}
   \]
   the all-ones dual vector \(y_a=1\) is feasible in \((AHR4)\), and therefore
   \[
      \Phi_{\pi,{\rm at}}^{\rm hi}=B_\pi^{\rm hi}.
      \tag{AHR7}
   \]

   Finally, any atomized routing feasible for \((AHR3)\) supplies an admissible
   high-correlation certificate for \(\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}\) in
   \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope} by taking
   \(E_\pi^{\rm hi}=\sum_ae_a\) and the aggregate lower certificates \(X_i\).
   Hence
   \[
      \Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}\le\Phi_{\pi,{\rm at}}^{\rm hi},
      \tag{AHR8}
   \]
   whenever this atomized record family is included in the admissible routing
   universe.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The program \((AHR3)\) is a finite covering LP.  Assign a nonnegative dual
   variable \(y_a\) to the constraint for atom \(a\).  The coefficient of
   \(e_a\) gives the dual upper bound \(y_a\le1\), and the coefficient of
   \(\lambda_i\) gives
   \(\sum_ax_{i,a}y_a\le P_i\).  Since the primal is feasible by taking
   \(e_a=b_a\) and is bounded below, finite LP duality gives \((AHR4)\).

   Let a feasible primal routing satisfy \((AHR5)\).  Summing its atom
   constraints over \(a\) gives
   \[
      B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \le
      \sum_ae_a+\sum_i\lambda_iX_i .
   \]
   Combining this with \((AHR5)\) yields
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_iX_i>\sum_i\lambda_iP_i .
   \]
   This is \((PPC2)\) for the panel with records \(i\) and weights
   \(\lambda_i\), so
   \cref{cor:paid-pair-star-panel-certificate} exposes a positive
   smaller-radius dense prefix.

   If no panel exposes a positive prefix, applying the same corollary to the
   one-record panel for \(i\) gives \(X_i\le P_i\).  Thus \(y_a=1\) satisfies
   all dual constraints in \((AHR4)\) and has value \(B_\pi^{\rm hi}\).  The
   primal solution \(e_a=b_a,\lambda_i=0\) has the same value, proving
   \((AHR7)\).

   For the final claim, sum the atom constraints of \((AHR3)\) to obtain
   \(B_\pi^{\rm hi}\le E_\pi^{\rm hi}+\sum_i\lambda_iX_i\).  This is exactly
   \((WPP2)\), and the cost in \((WMC1)\) is the objective of \((AHR3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Layer-cake atom-cut normal form]
   \label{cor:layer-cake-atom-cut-normal-form}
   Work in the dual program \((AHR4)\) from
   \cref{cor:atomized-high-correlation-routing-dual}.  Let \(y\) be any dual
   feasible vector, and define the threshold atom cuts
   \[
      A_t=\{a\in\mathcal A_\pi:y_a\ge t\},
      \qquad 0<t\le1.
      \tag{AHC1}
   \]
   Write
   \[
      B(t)=\sum_{a\in A_t}b_a,
      \qquad
