      X_i(t)=\sum_{a\in A_t}x_{i,a}.
      \tag{AHC2}
   \]
   Then every threshold cut satisfies the scaled no-star inequalities
   \[
      t\,X_i(t)\le P_i
      \qquad(i\in I_\pi,\ 0<t\le1),
      \tag{AHC3}
   \]
   and the dual value has the layer-cake representation
   \[
      \sum_ab_ay_a=\int_0^1B(t)\,dt .
      \tag{AHC4}
   \]

   Moreover, suppose all positive dual coordinates lie in
   \([\eta,1]\), where \(0<\eta\le1\), and let
   \[
      J_\eta=1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac1\eta\right\rceil .
      \tag{AHC5}
   \]
   Then some dyadic level
   \(t\in\{1,2^{-1},\ldots,2^{-(J_\eta-1)}\}\) satisfies
   \[
      t\,B(t)\ge
      \frac{1}{2J_\eta}\sum_ab_ay_a .
      \tag{AHC6}
   \]
   Therefore any positive atomized high-correlation dual obstruction contains a
   single threshold atom cut whose scaled benefit is a logarithmic fraction of
   the dual value and whose scaled incidence against every certified star is
   below that star's recursive price.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(a\in A_t\), then \(t\le y_a\).  Hence, for each star record \(i\),
   \[
      tX_i(t)
      =
      t\sum_{a\in A_t}x_{i,a}
      \le
      \sum_{a\in A_t}x_{i,a}y_a
      \le
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal A_\pi}x_{i,a}y_a
      \le P_i,
   \]
   which proves \((AHC3)\).  The layer-cake identity follows from
   \(y_a=\int_0^1\mathbf 1\{y_a\ge t\}\,dt\) and summing over atoms.

   For the dyadic statement, put \(t_j=2^{-j}\) for
   \(0\le j<J_\eta\).  Since every positive \(y_a\ge\eta\), the geometric sum
   over all dyadic levels not exceeding \(y_a\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{0\le j<J_\eta:\\ t_j\le y_a}}t_j\ge y_a/2 .
   \]
   Therefore
   \[
      \sum_{j=0}^{J_\eta-1}t_jB(t_j)
      =
      \sum_ab_a
      \sum_{\substack{0\le j<J_\eta:\\ t_j\le y_a}}t_j
      \ge
      \frac12\sum_ab_ay_a .
   \]
   One dyadic level has value at least the average over the \(J_\eta\) levels,
   proving \((AHC6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[High-correlation atom-cut star screen]
   \label{cor:high-correlation-atom-cut-star-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:layer-cake-atom-cut-normal-form}, and fix one threshold \(t\).
   Suppose every atom \(a\in A_t\) is represented by an ordered pair
   \((c_a,p_a)\in P\times P\) satisfying
   \[
      \ip{c_a}{p_a}\ge\underline\theta
      \qquad(-1<\underline\theta<1).
      \tag{ACS1}
   \]
   Give atom \(a\) scaled weight \(\omega_a=tb_a\), and define
   \[
      M_x(p)=
      \sum_{\substack{a\in A_t:\\ c_a=x,\ p_a=p}}\omega_a,
      \qquad
      W_t=\sum_{a\in A_t}\omega_a=tB(t).
      \tag{ACS2}
   \]
   Assume all positive \(M_x(p)\) lie in
   \([M_{\min},M_{\max}]\), and let
   \[
      J_{\rm cut}=
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{M_{\max}}{M_{\min}}\right\rceil .
      \tag{ACS3}
   \]
   Suppose the atomized routing record family contains every dyadic star
   superlevel
   \[
      U_{x,s}=\{p\in P:M_x(p)\ge s\},
      \qquad
      s\in\{2^jM_{\min}:0\le j<J_{\rm cut}\},
      \tag{ACS4}
   \]
   with certified radius
   \[
      U_{x,s}\subseteq P\cap B\!\left(x,\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)}\right),
      \tag{ACS5}
   \]
   atom lower certificates satisfying
   \[
      x_{(x,s),a}\ge
      b_a\,\mathbf 1\{c_a=x,\ p_a\in U_{x,s}\},
      \tag{ACS6}
   \]
   and recursive price envelope \(P_{x,s}\le P_0\).

   If no such star record exposes a positive smaller-radius dense prefix, then
   the scaled cut benefit obeys
   \[
      tB(t)=W_t\le 2|P|J_{\rm cut}P_0 .
      \tag{ACS7}
   \]
   Equivalently, if \(tB(t)>2|P|J_{\rm cut}P_0\), then one dyadic
   high-correlation atom-cut star record exposes a positive dense prefix.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{lem:high-correlation-pair-star-reporter} to the weighted edge
   family with one edge record for each atom \(a\in A_t\), weight
   \(\omega_a=tb_a\), and edge set \(\{(c_a,p_a)\}\).  Conditions \((ACS1)\)
   and \((ACS2)\) are exactly \((HPS1)\)--\((HPS2)\).  Hence either
   \(W_t=0\), in which case \((ACS7)\) is immediate, or there are \(x\) and a
   dyadic level \(s\) such that
   \[
      s|U_{x,s}|\ge \frac{W_t}{2|P|J_{\rm cut}} .
      \tag{ACS8}
   \]

   For the corresponding atomized routing record, \((ACS6)\) gives
   \[
      tX_{x,s}(t)
      =
      t\sum_{a\in A_t}x_{(x,s),a}
      \ge
      \sum_{\substack{a\in A_t:\\ c_a=x,\ p_a\in U_{x,s}}}tb_a
      =
      \sum_{p\in U_{x,s}}M_x(p)
      \ge
      s|U_{x,s}| .
      \tag{ACS9}
   \]
   If no dense prefix is exposed, the no-star inequality \((AHC3)\) applied to
   this record gives
   \[
      tX_{x,s}(t)\le P_{x,s}\le P_0 .
   \]
   Combining with \((ACS8)\)--\((ACS9)\) proves \((ACS7)\).  The final
   statement is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[High-correlation atom-cut aggregate star-price screen]
   \label{cor:high-correlation-atom-cut-aggregate-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-atom-cut-star-screen}, but keep the individual
   recursive prices \(P_{x,s}\) of the dyadic star records.  If no such star
   record exposes a positive smaller-radius dense prefix, then
   \[
      tB(t)=W_t
      \le
      2\sum_{x\in P}\sum_{s}P_{x,s},
      \tag{ACA1}
   \]
   where the second sum ranges over the dyadic levels used for \(M_x\).
   In particular, \((ACS7)\) follows from \((ACA1)\) when
   \(P_{x,s}\le P_0\) and there are at most \(J_{\rm cut}\) levels for each
   center.

   Thus the high-correlation cut pays the aggregate recursive star price, not
   the worst record price times the number of possible centers.  A center
   proposal mechanism may therefore be analyzed by the total price of the
   certified stars it actually reports.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(W_t=0\) there is nothing to prove.  For each center \(x\), dyadic
   layer-cake gives
   \[
      \sum_s s|U_{x,s}|
      =
      \sum_{p:M_x(p)>0}
      \sum_{\substack{s:\\ s\le M_x(p)}}s
      \ge
      \frac12\sum_pM_x(p).
      \tag{ACA2}
   \]
   Summing over \(x\) gives
   \[
      W_t\le2\sum_{x,s}s|U_{x,s}| .
      \tag{ACA3}
   \]
   For each dyadic star, \((ACS9)\) and the no-star inequality \((AHC3)\)
   imply
   \[
      s|U_{x,s}|\le tX_{x,s}(t)\le P_{x,s}.
      \tag{ACA4}
   \]
   Combining \((ACA3)\)--\((ACA4)\) proves \((ACA1)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Reported-center atom-cut star-price screen]
   \label{cor:reported-center-atom-cut-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:high-correlation-atom-cut-star-screen}, but let
   \(C\subseteq P\) be any reported center set, and assume the atomized record
   family contains the dyadic star superlevels only for centers \(x\in C\).
   Define the scaled unreported-center tail
   \[
      E_C(t)=
      \sum_{\substack{a\in A_t:\\ c_a\notin C}}tb_a .
      \tag{RCA1}
   \]
   If no reported star record exposes a positive smaller-radius dense prefix,
   then
   \[
      tB(t)
      \le
      E_C(t)+2\sum_{x\in C}\sum_sP_{x,s},
      \tag{RCA2}
   \]
   where the second sum ranges over the reported dyadic levels for \(M_x\).

   Thus a build-time center proposal does not need to report all possible
   centers.  Its missing high-correlation incidence appears as an explicit
   tail \(E_C(t)\), while reported incidence is charged by the aggregate
   recursive star price of the reported centers and levels.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Split the scaled cut mass as
   \[
      tB(t)=E_C(t)+\sum_{x\in C}\sum_pM_x(p).
      \tag{RCA3}
   \]
   Applying the dyadic layer-cake inequality \((ACA2)\) only to the reported
   centers gives
   \[
      \sum_{x\in C}\sum_pM_x(p)
      \le
      2\sum_{x\in C}\sum_s s|U_{x,s}| .
      \tag{RCA4}
   \]
   For each reported dyadic star, the same argument as in \((ACA4)\) gives
   \(s|U_{x,s}|\le P_{x,s}\) unless that star exposes a positive dense prefix.
   Substituting this into \((RCA3)\)--\((RCA4)\) proves \((RCA2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Reported-center benefit-price screen]
   \label{cor:reported-center-benefit-price-screen}
   Work with one threshold atom cut in the setting of
   \cref{cor:reported-center-atom-cut-screen}.  For a reported center set
   \(C\), define its captured scaled atom mass and aggregate star price by
   \[
      M_C(t)=
      \sum_{\substack{a\in A_t:\\ c_a\in C}}tb_a,
      \qquad
      P_C=\sum_{x\in C}\sum_sP_{x,s}.
      \tag{RCB1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      M_C(t)>2P_C,
      \tag{RCB2}
   \]
   then some reported dyadic star record exposes a positive smaller-radius
   dense prefix.  Consequently, if no reported star record exposes such a
   prefix, every reported center set satisfies
   \[
      M_C(t)\le2P_C .
      \tag{RCB3}
   \]

   The same statement holds for finite or sampled center proposal laws: if a
   law over certified center sets satisfies
   \[
      \E M_C(t)>2\,\E P_C,
      \tag{RCB4}
   \]
   then one deterministic sampled center set has positive surplus
   \(M_C(t)-2P_C\), and hence exposes a positive dense prefix after
   verification.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(E_C(t)=tB(t)-M_C(t)\), \((RCA2)\) gives
   \(M_C(t)\le2P_C\) whenever no reported star prefix fires.  This proves the
   deterministic contrapositive.  The law version follows by linearity: if the
   expected surplus is positive, at least one center set in the support has
   positive surplus, and the deterministic statement applies.  For a sampled
   law, preprocessing samples until such a set is verified; failed samples are
   discarded.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Singleton reported-center reduced-cost screen]
   \label{cor:singleton-reported-center-screen}
   Work with one threshold atom cut in the setting of
   \cref{cor:reported-center-benefit-price-screen}.  For each center put
   \[
      m_x(t)=
      \sum_{\substack{a\in A_t:\\ c_a=x}}tb_a,
      \qquad
      P_x=\sum_sP_{x,s},
      \tag{SRC1}
   \]
   where the second sum ranges over the dyadic star records materialized for
   \(x\).  Assume the reported-center universe contains the singleton panel
   \(\{x\}\) whenever these records are materialized.  Then the following are
   equivalent:
   \begin{enumerate}
      \item some finite reported center set \(C\) has positive surplus
      \(M_C(t)>2P_C\);
      \item some finite or sampled reported-center law has positive expected
      surplus \(\E M_C(t)>2\E P_C\);
      \item some singleton center satisfies
      \[
         m_x(t)>2P_x .
         \tag{SRC2}
      \]
   \end{enumerate}
   Whenever these conditions hold, the singleton panel \(\{x\}\) exposes a
   positive smaller-radius dense prefix after verification.  If no singleton
   satisfies \((SRC2)\), then every deterministic center set and every sampled
   center law satisfies the residual inequality \(M_C(t)\le2P_C\) in
   expectation.

   Thus, cut-locally, additive reported-center prices collapse the fractional
   center-search problem to a one-center benefit-density test.  Expensive
   build-time routines may still be used to propose promising centers, but the
   proof oracle need only verify the scalar inequality \((SRC2)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Additivity gives, for every finite center set,
   \[
      M_C(t)-2P_C
      =
      \sum_{x\in C}\bigl(m_x(t)-2P_x\bigr).
      \tag{SRC3}
   \]
   Hence a deterministic set has positive surplus only if at least one
   singleton summand is positive, and any positive singleton gives a positive
   deterministic set.  The same identity and linearity give
   \[
      \E\bigl[M_C(t)-2P_C\bigr]
      =
      \sum_x\Pr[x\in C]\bigl(m_x(t)-2P_x\bigr)
      \tag{SRC4}
   \]
   for any sampled center law.  Positive expected surplus again requires a
   positive singleton summand, and a positive singleton gives a sampled law
   supported on that singleton.  Finally,
   \cref{cor:reported-center-benefit-price-screen} applied to \(C=\{x\}\)
   shows that any singleton satisfying \((SRC2)\) exposes a positive dense
   prefix.  If no singleton satisfies \((SRC2)\), then all summands in
   \((SRC3)\)--\((SRC4)\) are nonpositive, proving the residual inequalities.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One-sided singleton center certificate]
   \label{cor:one-sided-singleton-center-certificate}
   Work with one threshold atom cut in the setting of
   \cref{cor:singleton-reported-center-screen}.  A one-sided singleton center
   certificate consists of a center \(x\), a lower certified captured mass
   \(\underline m_x\), and an upper certified star price \(\overline P_x\)
   satisfying
   \[
      0<\underline m_x\le m_x(t),
      \qquad
      P_x\le\overline P_x,
      \qquad
      \underline m_x>2\overline P_x .
      \tag{OSC1}
   \]
   Any such certificate exposes a positive smaller-radius dense prefix after
   exact verification of the singleton's dyadic star records.

   If a finite center universe is searched by a deterministic verifier which
   either returns a certificate satisfying \((OSC1)\) or correctly certifies
   that no center satisfies the exact singleton inequality \(m_x(t)>2P_x\),
   then the cut-local center oracle is complete for all reported-center sets
   and all sampled center laws over that universe.  If a randomized build-time
   proposal returns a verifiable certificate satisfying \((OSC1)\) with
   probability at least \(p_E>0\) whenever such a certificate exists, Las Vegas
   repetition finds a valid dense-prefix augmentation after expected at most
   \(1/p_E\) proposals; failed proposals are discarded.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   From \((OSC1)\),
   \[
      m_x(t)\ge\underline m_x>2\overline P_x\ge2P_x .
   \]
   Hence the singleton satisfies \((SRC2)\), and
   \cref{cor:singleton-reported-center-screen} exposes a positive dense prefix.
   If the verifier certifies that no exact positive singleton exists, then
   \cref{cor:singleton-reported-center-screen} implies that no center set or
   sampled law over the same universe has positive surplus.  The Las Vegas
   claim is the standard repeat-until-accepted argument: the first \(B\)
   proposals all fail with probability at most \((1-p_E)^B\), and only the
   first accepted verified singleton is retained.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Reduced-cost singleton center search]
   \label{cor:reduced-cost-singleton-center-search}
   Work with one threshold atom cut and a finite center universe
   \(\mathcal X\) in the setting of
   \cref{cor:singleton-reported-center-screen}.  Put
   \[
      \Delta_x=m_x(t)-2P_x\qquad(x\in\mathcal X).
      \tag{RCS1}
   \]
   If \(\max_{x\in\mathcal X}\Delta_x\le0\), then no deterministic center set and
   no sampled center law supported on \(\mathcal X\) has positive surplus.  If
   \(\max_{x\in\mathcal X}\Delta_x>0\), then any maximizer exposes a positive
   smaller-radius dense prefix.

   In the one-sided certified form, suppose a proposal returns a center \(x\) and
   numbers \(\underline m_x,\overline P_x\) as in
   \cref{cor:one-sided-singleton-center-certificate}.  Let
   \[
      \underline\Delta_x=\underline m_x-2\overline P_x .
      \tag{RCS2}
   \]
   A proposal with \(\underline\Delta_x>0\) is accepted and exposes a positive
   dense prefix.  If a randomized proposal law has
   \(p_+=\Prb[\underline\Delta_x>0]\), Las Vegas repetition succeeds after
   expected at most \(1/p_+\) proposals.  If uncharged preprocessing maximizes
   \(\underline\Delta_x\) over a finite certified candidate list, that search is
   complete for all one-sided certifiable positive singleton centers in the list.

   Thus the proof primitive is price-aware reduced-cost maximization.  Geometry
   routines such as \(k\)-means++, facility search, additive quantization, or
   list/lattice decoding are useful only as ways to propose centers whose
   certified scalar surplus \(\underline m_x-2\overline P_x\) can be checked.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If every \(\Delta_x\le0\), then for every deterministic center set \(C\),
   \[
      M_C(t)-2P_C=\sum_{x\in C}\Delta_x\le0,
   \]
   and for every sampled center law the same inequality holds in expectation by
   \((SRC4)\).  Hence no set or law has positive surplus.  If some
   \(\Delta_x>0\), then \(m_x(t)>2P_x\), and
   \cref{cor:singleton-reported-center-screen} exposes a positive dense prefix.

   The one-sided statements are exactly
   \cref{cor:one-sided-singleton-center-certificate}: the inequality
   \(\underline\Delta_x>0\) is \((OSC1)\).  Independent repetition has geometric
   mean \(1/p_+\), and an exact finite maximizer finds a certifiable positive
   whenever one exists.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Clipped singleton center-cover formula]
   \label{cor:clipped-singleton-center-cover}
   Work with one threshold atom cut in the setting of
   \cref{cor:singleton-reported-center-screen}.  Let \(\mathcal X\) be a finite
   materialized center universe, with captured masses \(m_x(t)\) and additive
   singleton star prices \(P_x\).  Consider the singleton fractional cover
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Xi_t^{\rm sing}=\min
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}m_x(t)e_x
        +2\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}P_x\lambda_x\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & e_x+\lambda_x\ge1\qquad(x\in\mathcal X),\\[0.3em]
      & e_x,\lambda_x\ge0 .
   \end{array}
      \tag{CSC1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \Xi_t^{\rm sing}
      =
      \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\min\{m_x(t),2P_x\}.
      \tag{CSC2}
   \]
   Moreover, suppose a reported-center panel universe contains every singleton
   \(\{x\}\) and every panel \(C\) has additive price
   \(P_C=\sum_{x\in C}P_x\).  Then the full fractional center-cover LP
   \((RCC2)\) over that panel universe has the same optimum \((CSC2)\).

   Consequently, for additive reported-center prices,
   \[
      \Xi_t^{\rm sing}<W_t:=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}m_x(t)
      \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
      \exists x\in\mathcal X:\ m_x(t)>2P_x.
      \tag{CSC3}
   \]
   In that case the singleton center \(x\) exposes a positive smaller-radius
   dense prefix.  If no such singleton exists, the clipped cover value is the
   tail-only value \(W_t\), so no deterministic set or sampled center law over
   \(\mathcal X\) can improve the cut-local tail certificate.

   Thus the additive center-cover problem has no hidden fractional or
   correlated-set advantage: the exact reduced price is the scalar clipped sum
   \(\sum_x\min\{m_x(t),2P_x\}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The singleton LP separates over centers.  For fixed \(x\), an optimal
   solution has \(e_x+\lambda_x=1\) and \(0\le\lambda_x\le1\), so its
   contribution is
   \[
      \min_{0\le\lambda\le1}
      \bigl[m_x(t)(1-\lambda)+2P_x\lambda\bigr]
      =
      \min\{m_x(t),2P_x\}.
   \]
   Summing over \(x\) proves \((CSC2)\).

   Now allow arbitrary reported center panels with additive prices.  Any panel
   solution \((e,\lambda_C)\) can be expanded into a singleton solution by
   replacing each \(\lambda_C\) by the singleton increments
   \(\lambda_x\leftarrow\lambda_x+\lambda_C\) for all \(x\in C\).  The cover
   constraints remain satisfied and the objective is unchanged because
   \(P_C=\sum_{x\in C}P_x\).  Conversely, singleton variables are feasible in
   the full panel LP because singleton panels are present.  Hence the optima
   coincide.

   Finally, \(\Xi_t^{\rm sing}<W_t\) holds exactly when at least one summand
   in \((CSC2)\) is strictly smaller than \(m_x(t)\), namely when
   \(m_x(t)>2P_x\).  The dense-prefix conclusion and the residual statement
   are \cref{cor:singleton-reported-center-screen}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fractional reported-center cover dual]
   \label{cor:fractional-reported-center-cover-dual}
   Work with one threshold atom cut as in
   \cref{cor:reported-center-benefit-price-screen}.  Put
   \[
      m_x(t)=\sum_{\substack{a\in A_t:\\ c_a=x}}tb_a,
      \qquad
      W_t=\sum_xm_x(t),
      \tag{RCC1}
   \]
   so that \(M_C(t)=\sum_{x\in C}m_x(t)\).  Let \(\mathcal C_t\) be a finite
   universe of certified reported-center panels \(C\), each with the dyadic
   star records needed by \cref{cor:reported-center-atom-cut-screen} and
   aggregate price \(P_C\).  Consider the finite fractional center-cover
   program
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Xi_t=\min
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_xm_x(t)e_x+2\sum_{C\in\mathcal C_t}\lambda_CP_C\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        e_x+\sum_{\substack{C\in\mathcal C_t:\\ x\in C}}\lambda_C\ge1
        \qquad(x\in P),\\[0.8em]
      & e_x\ge0,\qquad \lambda_C\ge0 .
   \end{array}
      \tag{RCC2}
   \]
   Its dual is
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Xi_t=\max
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_xm_x(t)y_x\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & 0\le y_x\le1\qquad(x\in P),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{x\in C}m_x(t)y_x\le2P_C
        \qquad(C\in\mathcal C_t).
   \end{array}
      \tag{RCC3}
   \]

   If \(\Xi_t<W_t\), then some reported-center panel in \(\mathcal C_t\)
   exposes a positive smaller-radius dense prefix.  Conversely, if no panel in
   \(\mathcal C_t\) exposes such a prefix, then
   \[
      \Xi_t=W_t,
      \tag{RCC4}
   \]
   and the all-ones dual vector \(y_x=1\) is feasible in \((RCC3)\).

   Thus the center-search problem is an exact finite reduced-cost problem.
   Uncharged preprocessing may solve \((RCC2)\) over any finite universe
   proposed by \(k\)-means++, facility search, additive quantization, or
   list/lattice decoding.  A strict improvement over tailing all cut mass is
   not retained as a fractional object; it is immediately hardened to one
   ordinary positive dense-prefix column.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The program is feasible by taking \(e_x=1\) for all \(x\), and is bounded
   below.  Assign a nonnegative dual variable \(z_x\) to the covering
   constraint for center \(x\).  The coefficient of \(e_x\) gives
   \(z_x\le m_x(t)\), and the coefficient of \(\lambda_C\) gives
   \(\sum_{x\in C}z_x\le2P_C\).  Writing
   \(z_x=m_x(t)y_x\), with arbitrary \(y_x\in[0,1]\) when \(m_x(t)=0\), gives
   \((RCC3)\).  Finite LP duality proves equality of \((RCC2)\) and
   \((RCC3)\).

   Suppose a feasible primal solution has value \(<W_t\).  Multiplying the
   constraint for \(x\) by \(m_x(t)\) and summing gives
   \[
      W_t
      \le
      \sum_xm_x(t)e_x+\sum_C\lambda_CM_C(t).
      \tag{RCC5}
   \]
   Since the primal objective is
   \(\sum_xm_x(t)e_x+2\sum_C\lambda_CP_C<W_t\), \((RCC5)\) implies
   \[
      \sum_C\lambda_CM_C(t)>2\sum_C\lambda_CP_C .
      \tag{RCC6}
   \]
   Hence at least one panel with \(\lambda_C>0\) satisfies \(M_C(t)>2P_C\).
   By \cref{cor:reported-center-benefit-price-screen}, that panel exposes a
   positive smaller-radius dense prefix.

   Conversely, if no panel exposes a positive prefix, then
   \cref{cor:reported-center-benefit-price-screen} gives
   \(M_C(t)\le2P_C\) for every \(C\in\mathcal C_t\).  Thus \(y_x=1\) satisfies
   all constraints of \((RCC3)\), with value \(W_t\).  The tail-only primal
   solution has value \(W_t\), so \(\Xi_t=W_t\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sampled reported-center tail certificate]
   \label{cor:sampled-reported-center-tail-certificate}
   Work with one threshold atom cut in the setting of
   \cref{cor:fractional-reported-center-cover-dual}.  Let \(\nu\) be a finite
   law over certified reported-center panels \(C\in\mathcal C_t\).  Define
   \[
      \mathfrak T_\nu(t)
      =
      \E_{C\sim\nu}\left[
         E_C(t)+2P_C
      \right]
      =
      W_t-\E_{C\sim\nu}M_C(t)+2\E_{C\sim\nu}P_C .
      \tag{RCT1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \mathfrak T_\nu(t)<W_t,
      \tag{RCT2}
   \]
   then some panel in the support of \(\nu\) exposes a positive
   smaller-radius dense prefix.  Conversely, if no panel in the support exposes
   such a prefix, then
   \[
      W_t\le\mathfrak T_\nu(t),
      \qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
      \E_{C\sim\nu}M_C(t)\le2\E_{C\sim\nu}P_C .
      \tag{RCT3}
   \]

   Therefore randomized center generation has the same reduced-cost target as a
   deterministic panel: it must capture more scaled cut mass than twice its
   aggregate recursive star price.  No extra rounding, set-cover, or branching
   loss is introduced by using a distribution over center proposals; a positive
   expected surplus contains one verified deterministic dense-prefix column.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If no panel in the support exposes a positive prefix, then
   \cref{cor:reported-center-atom-cut-screen} gives
   \(W_t\le E_C(t)+2P_C\) for every \(C\) in the support.  Taking expectation
   gives \(W_t\le\mathfrak T_\nu(t)\).  Since
   \(E_C(t)=W_t-M_C(t)\), this is equivalent to the second inequality in
   \((RCT3)\).  The positive statement is the contrapositive.  Equivalently,
   \((RCT2)\) says
   \(\E(M_C(t)-2P_C)>0\), so some deterministic support point has
   \(M_C(t)>2P_C\), and
   \cref{cor:reported-center-benefit-price-screen} verifies a positive dense
   prefix.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Atomized high-correlation fixed-tail bound]
   \label{cor:atomized-high-correlation-fixed-tail}
   Work in the atomized high-correlation routing dual
   \((AHR4)\) for one split profile \(\pi\).  Let
   \(B_\pi^{\rm hi}=\sum_ab_a\).  Fix \(0<\varepsilon\le1\) and put
   \[
      J_\varepsilon=
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac1\varepsilon\right\rceil .
      \tag{AHF1}
   \]
   Assume that every atom with positive benefit is represented by an ordered
   high-correlation pair \((c_a,p_a)\in P\times P\), and that, for every
   dyadic threshold cut arising from the \(\varepsilon\)-truncation of any
   feasible dual vector, preprocessing certifies a reported center set
   \(C(t)\), the dyadic star superlevels used in
   \cref{cor:reported-center-atom-cut-screen} for those centers, and two
   envelopes
   \[
      E_{C(t)}(t)\le\mathfrak E_\star,
      \qquad
      \sum_{x\in C(t)}\sum_sP_{x,s}\le\mathfrak P_\star .
      \tag{AHF2}
   \]

   Then every feasible dual vector \(y\) satisfies the dichotomy
   \[
      \sum_ab_ay_a
      \le
      \varepsilon B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2J_\varepsilon\mathfrak E_\star
      +4J_\varepsilon\mathfrak P_\star,
      \tag{AHF3}
   \]
   or some dyadic high-correlation atom-cut star record exposes a positive
   smaller-radius dense prefix.
   Consequently, if no such dense prefix is exposed, then
   \[
      \Phi_{\pi,{\rm at}}^{\rm hi}
      \le
      \varepsilon B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2J_\varepsilon\mathfrak E_\star
      +4J_\varepsilon\mathfrak P_\star.
      \tag{AHF4}
   \]
   If this atomized record family is included in the admissible routing
   universe of \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope}, then also
   \[
      \Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \le
      \varepsilon B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2J_\varepsilon\mathfrak E_\star
      +4J_\varepsilon\mathfrak P_\star
      \tag{AHF5}
   \]
   unless a positive smaller-radius dense prefix has already been found.

   The full-center aggregate-price form is the special case
   \(\mathfrak E_\star=0\).  The previous uniform-price form further uses
   \(\mathfrak P_\star\le |P|J_\star P_0\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a feasible dual vector \(y\).  Define its
   \(\varepsilon\)-truncation by
   \[
      y_a^{(\varepsilon)}=
      y_a\,\mathbf 1\{y_a\ge\varepsilon\}.
   \]
   Since \(0\le y^{(\varepsilon)}\le y\) coordinatewise, it is feasible for
   \((AHR4)\).  Moreover
   \[
      \sum_ab_ay_a
      \le
      \varepsilon B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +\sum_ab_ay_a^{(\varepsilon)} .
      \tag{AHF6}
   \]
   If the second term in \((AHF6)\) is zero, then \((AHF3)\) follows.  Otherwise
   all positive coordinates of \(y^{(\varepsilon)}\) lie in
   \([\varepsilon,1]\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:layer-cake-atom-cut-normal-form} to
   \(y^{(\varepsilon)}\), some dyadic threshold \(t\) satisfies
   \[
      tB(t)
      \ge
      \frac{1}{2J_\varepsilon}
      \sum_ab_ay_a^{(\varepsilon)} .
      \tag{AHF7}
   \]
   For this cut, \cref{cor:reported-center-atom-cut-screen} gives either a
   positive dense prefix or
   \[
      tB(t)\le\mathfrak E_\star+2\mathfrak P_\star .
      \tag{AHF8}
   \]
   Combining \((AHF6)\)--\((AHF8)\) proves \((AHF3)\).

   Taking the supremum over feasible dual vectors in \((AHR4)\) gives
   \((AHF4)\) by finite LP duality from
   \cref{cor:atomized-high-correlation-routing-dual}.  Finally,
   \((AHF5)\) follows from \((AHR8)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sampled-center high-correlation fixed-tail bound]
   \label{cor:sampled-center-high-correlation-fixed-tail}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:atomized-high-correlation-fixed-tail}, but replace the
   deterministic reported center set \(C(t)\) at each dyadic threshold cut by a
   finite law \(\nu_t\) over certified reported-center panels.  Assume that,
   for every such cut, preprocessing certifies
   \[
      \E_{C\sim\nu_t}E_C(t)\le\mathfrak E_\star,
      \qquad
      \E_{C\sim\nu_t}P_C\le\mathfrak P_\star .
      \tag{SCH1}
   \]
   Then the same dichotomy and bounds \((AHF3)\)--\((AHF5)\) hold: every
   feasible atomized high-correlation dual satisfies
   \[
      \sum_ab_ay_a
      \le
      \varepsilon B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2J_\varepsilon\mathfrak E_\star
      +4J_\varepsilon\mathfrak P_\star,
      \tag{SCH2}
   \]
   or one sampled reported-center panel exposes a positive smaller-radius dense
   prefix.  Consequently, if no sampled panel exposes such a prefix, then
   \[
      \Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \le
      \varepsilon B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2J_\varepsilon\mathfrak E_\star
      +4J_\varepsilon\mathfrak P_\star .
      \tag{SCH3}
   \]

   Thus a \(k\)-means++, facility, additive-quantization, or list-decoding
   routine may be analyzed entirely as a randomized center-panel law.  The
   retained index still receives only verified deterministic dense prefixes;
   all unsuccessful samples are build-time work.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Repeat the proof of
   \cref{cor:atomized-high-correlation-fixed-tail} up to the dyadic threshold
   cut satisfying \((AHF7)\).  For that cut, if no sampled panel exposes a
   positive dense prefix, then
   \cref{cor:sampled-reported-center-tail-certificate} gives
   \[
      tB(t)
      \le
      \E_{C\sim\nu_t}\left[E_C(t)+2P_C\right]
      \le
      \mathfrak E_\star+2\mathfrak P_\star .
      \tag{SCH4}
   \]
   Combining \((SCH4)\) with \((AHF6)\)--\((AHF7)\) gives \((SCH2)\).  Taking
   the supremum over feasible atomized duals and using \((AHR8)\) gives
   \((SCH3)\), exactly as in the deterministic proof.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Clipped-singleton high-correlation fixed-tail bound]
   \label{cor:clipped-singleton-high-correlation-fixed-tail}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:atomized-high-correlation-fixed-tail}.  For each dyadic threshold
   cut \(A_t\) arising from the \(\varepsilon\)-truncation, suppose
   preprocessing materializes a finite center universe \(\mathcal X(t)\).  For
   \(x\in\mathcal X(t)\), let
   \[
      m_x(t)=
      \sum_{\substack{a\in A_t:\\ c_a=x}}tb_a,
      \qquad
      P_x=\sum_sP_{x,s},
      \tag{CLH1}
   \]
   where the second sum is over the dyadic star records reported for \(x\).
   Let the unreported-center tail be
   \[
      E_{\mathcal X}(t)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{a\in A_t:\\ c_a\notin\mathcal X(t)}}tb_a,
      \tag{CLH2}
   \]
   and define the clipped singleton tail-price
   \[
      \Gamma_{\rm clip}(t)
      =
      E_{\mathcal X}(t)
      +
      \sum_{x\in\mathcal X(t)}
      \min\{m_x(t),2P_x\}.
      \tag{CLH3}
   \]
   Assume that all such cuts have the certified envelope
   \[
      \Gamma_{\rm clip}(t)\le\mathfrak G_\star .
      \tag{CLH4}
   \]
   Then every feasible atomized high-correlation dual satisfies
   \[
      \sum_ab_ay_a
      \le
      \varepsilon B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2J_\varepsilon\mathfrak G_\star,
      \tag{CLH5}
   \]
   or one materialized singleton center exposes a positive smaller-radius dense
   prefix.  Consequently, if no such singleton dense prefix is exposed and this
   atomized record family is included in the admissible routing universe of
   \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope}, then
   \[
      \Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \le
      \varepsilon B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2J_\varepsilon\mathfrak G_\star .
      \tag{CLH6}
   \]

   Equivalently, the sampled-center bound may use the single clipped price
   \(A_\pi^{\rm clip}=2\mathfrak G_\star\) in place of
   \(A_\pi^{\rm samp}=2\mathfrak E_\star+4\mathfrak P_\star\).  The
   high-correlation proposal theorem therefore only has to certify a cut-wise
   clipped singleton envelope; any strict improvement over tailing the
   materialized cut mass is automatically an ordinary singleton dense-prefix
   column.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a feasible dual vector \(y\), truncate it at level \(\varepsilon\), and
   apply \cref{cor:layer-cake-atom-cut-normal-form} exactly as in the proof of
   \cref{cor:atomized-high-correlation-fixed-tail}.  Thus either the truncated
   mass is zero, or some threshold cut \(A_t\) satisfies
   \[
      tB(t)
      \ge
      \frac{1}{2J_\varepsilon}
      \sum_ab_ay_a^{(\varepsilon)} .
      \tag{CLH7}
   \]
   For this cut, decompose
   \[
      tB(t)
      =
      E_{\mathcal X}(t)
      +
      \sum_{x\in\mathcal X(t)}m_x(t).
      \tag{CLH8}
   \]
   If \(\Gamma_{\rm clip}(t)<tB(t)\), then some summand satisfies
   \(m_x(t)>2P_x\), and
   \cref{cor:clipped-singleton-center-cover} exposes a positive singleton
   dense prefix.  Otherwise
   \(tB(t)\le\Gamma_{\rm clip}(t)\le\mathfrak G_\star\).  Combining this with
   \((CLH7)\) and the truncation inequality \((AHF6)\) gives \((CLH5)\).
   Taking the supremum over feasible atomized duals and using \((AHR8)\) gives
   \((CLH6)\), as in the proof of
   \cref{cor:atomized-high-correlation-fixed-tail}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Integrated clipped-singleton high-correlation bound]
   \label{cor:integrated-clipped-singleton-high-correlation}
   Work in the atomized high-correlation routing dual \((AHR4)\) for one split
   profile \(\pi\).  Fix \(0<\varepsilon\le1\), put
   \(J_\varepsilon=\lceil\log_2(1/\varepsilon)\rceil\), and let
   \[
      \mathcal T_\varepsilon=\{2^{-j}:0\le j\le J_\varepsilon\}.
      \tag{ICL1}
   \]
   For a feasible dual vector \(y\), define the threshold cuts
   \(A_t(y)=\{a:y_a\ge t\}\).  Suppose that for every
   \(t\in\mathcal T_\varepsilon\), preprocessing materializes a finite center
   universe for the cut \(A_t(y)\), and let \(\Gamma_{\rm clip}^y(t)\) be the
   clipped singleton tail-price of that cut as in \((CLH3)\).

   Then either one materialized singleton center exposes a positive
   smaller-radius dense prefix, or
   \[
      \sum_ab_ay_a
      \le
      \varepsilon B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +
      2\sum_{t\in\mathcal T_\varepsilon}\Gamma_{\rm clip}^y(t).
      \tag{ICL2}
   \]

   Consequently, if for every feasible dual \(y\) the corresponding dyadic cuts
   have certified clipped prices satisfying
   \[
      \sum_{t\in\mathcal T_\varepsilon}\Gamma_{\rm clip}^y(t)
      \le \mathfrak G_{\Sigma,\pi},
      \tag{ICL3}
   \]
   and the atomized record family is included in the admissible routing
   universe of \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope}, then, unless a
   singleton dense prefix has already been exposed,
   \[
      \Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \le
      \varepsilon B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2\mathfrak G_{\Sigma,\pi}.
      \tag{ICL4}
   \]

   This replaces the earlier \(J_\varepsilon\) times worst-cut envelope by the
   actual dyadic sum of clipped singleton cut prices.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(y^{(\varepsilon)}=y\,\mathbf 1\{y\ge\varepsilon\}\).  As in
   \((AHF6)\),
   \[
      \sum_ab_ay_a
      \le
      \varepsilon B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +\sum_ab_ay_a^{(\varepsilon)} .
      \tag{ICL5}
   \]
   For every \(u\in[\varepsilon,1]\),
   \[
      u
      \le
      2\sum_{\substack{t\in\mathcal T_\varepsilon:\\ t\le u}}t .
      \tag{ICL6}
   \]
   Indeed, if \(2^{-k}\le u<2^{-k+1}\), then the sum on the right contains
   \(2^{-k}\ge u/2\).  Applying \((ICL6)\) to every positive coordinate of
   \(y^{(\varepsilon)}\) gives
   \[
      \sum_ab_ay_a^{(\varepsilon)}
      \le
      2\sum_{t\in\mathcal T_\varepsilon}tB_y(t),
      \tag{ICL7}
   \]
   where \(B_y(t)=\sum_{a\in A_t(y)}b_a\).

   For a fixed dyadic cut, if
   \(\Gamma_{\rm clip}^y(t)<tB_y(t)\), then the proof of
   \cref{cor:clipped-singleton-high-correlation-fixed-tail}, using
   \cref{cor:clipped-singleton-center-cover}, exposes a positive singleton
   dense prefix.  If no singleton prefix is exposed, then
   \(tB_y(t)\le\Gamma_{\rm clip}^y(t)\) for every \(t\).  Combining this with
   \((ICL5)\)--\((ICL7)\) proves \((ICL2)\).

   Taking the supremum over feasible atomized duals and applying \((AHR8)\)
   gives \((ICL4)\) under the uniform certificate \((ICL3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Integrated singleton reduced-cost screen]
   \label{cor:integrated-singleton-reduced-cost-screen}
   Work with the dyadic cuts \(\mathcal T_\varepsilon\) of
   \cref{cor:integrated-clipped-singleton-high-correlation}.  For each
   \(t\in\mathcal T_\varepsilon\), let \(\mathcal X(t)\) be a finite
   materialized center universe for the cut \(A_t(y)\).  For
   \(x\in\mathcal X(t)\), write
   \[
      m_{x,t}=
      \sum_{\substack{a\in A_t(y):\\ c_a=x}}tb_a,
      \qquad
      P_{x,t}=\sum_sP_{x,t,s},
      \tag{ISC1}
   \]
   where the second sum is over the dyadic star records reported for center
   \(x\) at cut \(t\).  Assume each individual center-cut record is an
   admissible singleton reported-center panel for the corresponding threshold
   cut, in the sense of \cref{cor:singleton-reported-center-screen}.

   If a finite panel of center-cut records has nonnegative weights
   \(\lambda_{x,t}\) and positive integrated surplus
   \[
      \sum_{t\in\mathcal T_\varepsilon}
      \sum_{x\in\mathcal X(t)}
      \lambda_{x,t}\bigl(m_{x,t}-2P_{x,t}\bigr)>0,
      \tag{ISC2}
   \]
   then some individual center-cut record satisfies
   \[
      m_{x,t}>2P_{x,t},
      \tag{ISC3}
   \]
   and therefore exposes a positive smaller-radius dense prefix.

   In particular, if the same center \(x\) is proposed across several cuts and
   its integrated captured mass and price are
   \[
      M_x^\Sigma=\sum_{t:x\in\mathcal X(t)}m_{x,t},
      \qquad
      P_x^\Sigma=\sum_{t:x\in\mathcal X(t)}P_{x,t},
      \tag{ISC4}
   \]
   then
   \[
      M_x^\Sigma>2P_x^\Sigma
      \tag{ISC5}
   \]
   already exposes a positive dense prefix at one cut.  Thus a facility,
   list-decoding, range-reporting, or \(k\)-means++-style proposal may score a
   center by its integrated dyadic surplus before the verifier materializes the
   single winning cut.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((ISC2)\) holds, at least one record with \(\lambda_{x,t}>0\) has
   \(m_{x,t}-2P_{x,t}>0\), proving \((ISC3)\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:singleton-reported-center-screen} to that one threshold cut
   exposes a positive dense prefix.  The centerwise statement is the special
   case in which the panel consists of all cut records for one center with unit
   weights.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Integrated clipped-price surplus identity]
   \label{cor:integrated-clipped-price-surplus-identity}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:integrated-singleton-reduced-cost-screen}.  For each cut let the
   unreported-center tail be
   \[
      E(t)=
      \sum_{\substack{a\in A_t(y):\\ c_a\notin\mathcal X(t)}}tb_a,
      \tag{ICI1}
   \]
   and define the cut and integrated clipped prices by
   \[
      \Gamma_{\rm clip}(t)
      =
      E(t)+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X(t)}\min\{m_{x,t},2P_{x,t}\},
      \qquad
      \mathfrak G_\Sigma=\sum_{t\in\mathcal T_\varepsilon}
      \Gamma_{\rm clip}(t).
      \tag{ICI2}
   \]
   Also put
   \[
      \mathcal A_\Sigma
      =
      \sum_{t\in\mathcal T_\varepsilon}tB_y(t),
      \qquad
      \mathcal S_\Sigma
      =
      \sum_{t\in\mathcal T_\varepsilon}
      \sum_{x\in\mathcal X(t)}
      (m_{x,t}-2P_{x,t})_+ .
      \tag{ICI3}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \mathfrak G_\Sigma
      =
      \mathcal A_\Sigma-\mathcal S_\Sigma .
      \tag{ICI4}
   \]
   Consequently, if the integrated clipped price is a small fraction of the
   dyadic cut area, then the positive singleton surplus
   \(\mathcal S_\Sigma\) accounts for the missing area and some center-cut
   record exposes a positive dense prefix whenever \(\mathcal S_\Sigma>0\).

   Thus a surviving residual with no singleton dense prefix has
   \[
      \mathfrak G_\Sigma=\mathcal A_\Sigma.
      \tag{ICI5}
   \]
   In such a residual, any improvement in the integrated high-correlation bound
   must come from reducing unreported tail or recursive star prices enough to
   create a positive singleton surplus.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For each fixed cut,
   \[
      tB_y(t)
      =
      E(t)+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X(t)}m_{x,t}.
   \]
   Also
   \[
      \min\{m_{x,t},2P_{x,t}\}
      =
      m_{x,t}-(m_{x,t}-2P_{x,t})_+.
   \]
   Substituting and summing over cuts gives \((ICI4)\).  If
   \(\mathcal S_\Sigma>0\), some summand has \(m_{x,t}>2P_{x,t}\), and
   \cref{cor:integrated-singleton-reduced-cost-screen} exposes a positive dense
   prefix.  The residual identity \((ICI5)\) follows by contraposition.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Shared integrated star-prefix screen]
   \label{cor:shared-integrated-star-prefix-screen}
   Work in the atomized high-correlation dual \((AHR4)\) for one split profile
   \(\pi\).  Fix \(0<\varepsilon\le1\), let
   \(\mathcal T_\varepsilon\) be as in \((ICL1)\), and let
   \(y\) be a feasible atomized dual vector.  For \(t\in\mathcal T_\varepsilon\)
   write \(A_t(y)=\{a:y_a\ge t\}\).

   Let \(I\) be a finite family of shared star-prefix records.  Record \(i\)
   has a recursive price \(P_i\ge0\) and nonnegative atom certificates
   \(x_{i,a}\ge0\).  Assume that, for this fixed dual \(y\), every finite panel
   of these records with lower certificates
   \[
      Y_i(y)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_\pi}x_{i,a}y_a
      \tag{SIS1}
   \]
   and prices \(P_i\) is admissible for the paid pair-star verifier of
   \cref{cor:paid-pair-star-panel-certificate}.  Define the integrated
   dyadic captured mass of record \(i\) by
   \[
      X_i^\Sigma(y)
      =
      \sum_{t\in\mathcal T_\varepsilon}
      t\sum_{a\in A_t(y)}x_{i,a}.
      \tag{SIS2}
   \]
   If a finite panel with weights \(\lambda_i\ge0\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_iX_i^\Sigma(y)
      >
      2\sum_i\lambda_iP_i,
      \tag{SIS3}
   \]
   then one shared record exposes a positive smaller-radius dense prefix.
   Conversely, if no shared record in the panel exposes such a prefix, then
   every finite nonnegative panel satisfies
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_iX_i^\Sigma(y)
      \le
      2\sum_i\lambda_iP_i .
      \tag{SIS4}
   \]

   Thus a prefix that is meaningful across many layer-cake cuts pays its
   recursive price once, up to the dyadic factor \(2\).  The cut-local integrated
   screen \((ISC5)\) is the special case in which each cut has its own record and
   hence its own price.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For every \(u\in[0,1]\),
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{t\in\mathcal T_\varepsilon:\\ t\le u}}t\le2u .
      \tag{SIS5}
   \]
   Therefore
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      X_i^\Sigma(y)
      &=
      \sum_a x_{i,a}
      \sum_{\substack{t\in\mathcal T_\varepsilon:\\ t\le y_a}}t  \\
      &\le
      2\sum_a x_{i,a}y_a
      =
      2Y_i(y).
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   If \((SIS3)\) holds, then
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_iY_i(y)>\sum_i\lambda_iP_i .
   \]
   By the admissibility hypothesis and
   \cref{cor:paid-pair-star-panel-certificate}, some record in the panel exposes
   a positive smaller-radius dense prefix.  The residual inequality \((SIS4)\)
   is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Shared integrated high-correlation tail bound]
   \label{cor:shared-integrated-high-correlation-tail}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:integrated-clipped-singleton-high-correlation}, but replace the
   cut-specific singleton center records by a finite shared star-prefix panel
   \(I\).  For the feasible atomized dual \(y\), suppose preprocessing supplies
   nonnegative atom assignments \(z_{i,a}\) for \(i\in I\) satisfying
   \[
      0\le\sum_{i\in I}z_{i,a}\le b_a
      \qquad(a\in\mathcal A_\pi),
      \tag{SIH1}
   \]
   and shared record prices \(P_i\), and suppose these records are admissible for
   \cref{cor:shared-integrated-star-prefix-screen} with \(x_{i,a}=z_{i,a}\).
   Define the integrated unassigned tail and shared price by
   \[
      E_\Sigma^y
      =
      \sum_{t\in\mathcal T_\varepsilon}
      t\sum_{a\in A_t(y)}
      \left(b_a-\sum_i z_{i,a}\right),
      \qquad
      P_\Sigma=\sum_iP_i .
      \tag{SIH2}
   \]
   Then either one shared star-prefix record exposes a positive smaller-radius
   dense prefix, or
   \[
      \sum_ab_ay_a
      \le
      \varepsilon B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2E_\Sigma^y+4P_\Sigma .
      \tag{SIH3}
   \]

   Consequently, if for every feasible dual \(y\) there are certified envelopes
   \[
      E_\Sigma^y\le\mathfrak E_{\Sigma,\pi},
      \qquad
      P_\Sigma\le\mathfrak P_{\Sigma,\pi},
      \tag{SIH4}
   \]
   and the shared records belong to the admissible routing universe of
   \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope}, then, unless a shared prefix has
   already fired,
   \[
      \Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \le
      \varepsilon B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2\mathfrak E_{\Sigma,\pi}
      +4\mathfrak P_{\Sigma,\pi}.
      \tag{SIH5}
   \]

   This is the fully fractional integrated replacement for the clipped singleton
   price: a shared dense record may cover overlapping mass from many cuts, while
   its recursive cost is charged once.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let
   \[
      \mathcal A_\Sigma(y)=
      \sum_{t\in\mathcal T_\varepsilon}tB_y(t).
      \tag{SIH6}
   \]
   The dyadic layer-cake estimate \((ICL5)\)--\((ICL7)\) gives
   \[
      \sum_ab_ay_a
      \le
      \varepsilon B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2\mathcal A_\Sigma(y).
      \tag{SIH7}
   \]
   By \((SIH1)\)--\((SIH2)\),
   \[
      \mathcal A_\Sigma(y)
      =
      E_\Sigma^y+\sum_iX_i^\Sigma(y),
   \]
   with \(X_i^\Sigma(y)\) defined by \((SIS2)\) for \(x_{i,a}=z_{i,a}\).  If no
   shared record exposes a positive prefix, \cref{cor:shared-integrated-star-prefix-screen}
   with unit panel weights gives
   \[
      \sum_iX_i^\Sigma(y)\le2P_\Sigma .
   \]
   Substituting this in \((SIH7)\) proves \((SIH3)\).

   Taking the supremum over feasible atomized duals and using the admissibility of
   the shared records in \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope} gives
   \((SIH5)\), exactly as in the proof of
   \cref{cor:integrated-clipped-singleton-high-correlation}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite shared integrated cover dual]
   \label{cor:finite-shared-integrated-cover-dual}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:shared-integrated-high-correlation-tail}.  For the fixed feasible
   atomized dual \(y\), define the dyadic layer-cake weights
   \[
      \ell_a^\Sigma(y)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{t\in\mathcal T_\varepsilon:\\ t\le y_a}}t,
      \qquad
      \mathcal A_\Sigma(y)=\sum_ab_a\ell_a^\Sigma(y).
      \tag{SIC1}
   \]
   Let \(\mathcal R\) be a finite family of shared star-prefix records.  Record
   \(i\in\mathcal R\) has price \(P_i\ge0\) and nonnegative atom certificates
   \(h_{i,a}\ge0\), and every finite panel with lower certificates
   \(\sum_ah_{i,a}y_a\) is admissible for
   \cref{cor:shared-integrated-star-prefix-screen}.

   Consider the finite shared integrated cover program
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Psi_\Sigma(y)=\min
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_a\ell_a^\Sigma(y)e_a+2\sum_{i\in\mathcal R}\lambda_iP_i\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        e_a+\sum_{i\in\mathcal R}\lambda_i h_{i,a}\ge b_a
        \qquad(a\in\mathcal A_\pi),\\[0.8em]
      & e_a\ge0,\qquad \lambda_i\ge0 .
   \end{array}
      \tag{SIC2}
   \]
   Its dual is
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \Psi_\Sigma(y)=\max
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_ab_au_a\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & 0\le u_a\le \ell_a^\Sigma(y)
        \qquad(a\in\mathcal A_\pi),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_ah_{i,a}u_a\le2P_i
        \qquad(i\in\mathcal R).
   \end{array}
      \tag{SIC3}
   \]

   If a feasible solution of \((SIC2)\) has value
   \(C_\Sigma<\mathcal A_\Sigma(y)\), then some shared record exposes a positive
   smaller-radius dense prefix.  Conversely, if no shared record in
   \(\mathcal R\) exposes such a prefix, then
   \[
      \Psi_\Sigma(y)=\mathcal A_\Sigma(y),
      \tag{SIC4}
   \]
   and \(u_a=\ell_a^\Sigma(y)\) is feasible for \((SIC3)\).

   More generally, any feasible cover solution with value \(C_\Sigma\) gives the
   dichotomy
   \[
      \sum_ab_ay_a
      \le
      \varepsilon B_\pi^{\rm hi}+2C_\Sigma,
      \tag{SIC5}
   \]
   or one shared record exposes a positive smaller-radius dense prefix.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The program \((SIC2)\) is feasible by taking \(e_a=b_a\), and it is bounded
   below.  Assign a nonnegative dual variable \(u_a\) to the covering constraint
   for atom \(a\).  The coefficient of \(e_a\) gives
   \(u_a\le\ell_a^\Sigma(y)\), and the coefficient of \(\lambda_i\) gives
   \(\sum_ah_{i,a}u_a\le2P_i\).  Finite LP duality proves \((SIC3)\).

   Let \((e,\lambda)\) be feasible, and put
   \[
      X_i^\Sigma(y)=
      \sum_a h_{i,a}\ell_a^\Sigma(y).
      \tag{SIC6}
   \]
   Multiplying the covering constraints by \(\ell_a^\Sigma(y)\) and summing over
   \(a\) gives
   \[
      \mathcal A_\Sigma(y)
      \le
      \sum_a\ell_a^\Sigma(y)e_a+\sum_i\lambda_iX_i^\Sigma(y).
      \tag{SIC7}
   \]
   If the cover value is \(C_\Sigma<\mathcal A_\Sigma(y)\), then
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_iX_i^\Sigma(y)>2\sum_i\lambda_iP_i .
   \]
   This is exactly \((SIS3)\) for the panel with atom certificates \(h_{i,a}\),
   so \cref{cor:shared-integrated-star-prefix-screen} exposes a positive dense
   prefix.

   If no shared prefix fires, the same screen gives
   \(X_i^\Sigma(y)\le2P_i\) for every single-record panel.  Hence
   \(u_a=\ell_a^\Sigma(y)\) satisfies all constraints of \((SIC3)\) and has value
   \(\mathcal A_\Sigma(y)\).  The tail-only primal solution has the same value,
   proving \((SIC4)\).

   Finally, for any feasible solution of value \(C_\Sigma\), either the above
   positive-prefix alternative fires or no shared prefix fires.  In the latter
   case \((SIC7)\) and \cref{cor:shared-integrated-star-prefix-screen} imply
   \[
      \mathcal A_\Sigma(y)\le C_\Sigma .
   \]
   Combining this with the layer-cake estimate \((SIH7)\) proves \((SIC5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Shared integrated cover column generation]
   \label{cor:shared-integrated-cover-column-generation}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-shared-integrated-cover-dual}, with a finite full shared
   record universe \(\mathcal R\).  Let \(E\subseteq\mathcal R\) be the active
   restricted record set, and let \(\Psi_\Sigma^E(y)\) be the cover value
   \((SIC2)\) with records restricted to \(E\).  Its dual has the constraints
   \[
      0\le u_a\le\ell_a^\Sigma(y),
      \qquad
      \sum_ah_{i,a}u_a\le2P_i\quad(i\in E).
      \tag{SCG1}
   \]

   Suppose \(u^E\) is an optimal restricted dual solution.  If some inactive
   record \(i\in\mathcal R\setminus E\) has positive shared reduced cost
   \[
      \operatorname{SGain}_{u^E}(i)
      =
      \sum_ah_{i,a}u_a^E-2P_i>0,
      \tag{SCG2}
   \]
   then adding \(i\) is a valid column-generation step: the current restricted
   dual certificate is not feasible for the enlarged restricted LP, and hence it
   cannot certify the full shared-cover value.

   Conversely, if no inactive record satisfies \((SCG2)\), then \(u^E\) is
   feasible for the full dual \((SIC3)\), and
   \[
      \Psi_\Sigma^E(y)=\Psi_\Sigma(y).
      \tag{SCG3}
   \]
   Therefore exhaustive column generation over \(\mathcal R\) terminates after at
   most \(|\mathcal R|\) successful additions with the exact full shared-cover
   value.

   In particular, for any target \(C_\Sigma\), the procedure either finds a
   feasible shared cover of value at most \(C_\Sigma\), or certifies
   \[
      \Psi_\Sigma(y)>C_\Sigma
      \tag{SCG4}
   \]
   together with a full-dual obstruction \(u\) satisfying every shared-record
   inequality.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The restricted primal and dual are the finite programs \((SIC2)\)--\((SIC3)\)
   with \(\mathcal R\) replaced by \(E\), so strong duality holds.  If
   \((SCG2)\) holds, then \(u^E\) violates the dual constraint for the enlarged
   active set \(E\cup\{i\}\).  Thus it is not a valid certificate for that
   enlarged problem.

   If no inactive record violates \((SCG2)\), then \(u^E\) satisfies every dual
   constraint for every record in \(\mathcal R\), so it is feasible for the full
   dual.  Since the full primal is a relaxation of the restricted primal,
   \[
      \Psi_\Sigma^E(y)\ge\Psi_\Sigma(y).
   \]
   Since \(u^E\) is full-dual feasible and has value \(\Psi_\Sigma^E(y)\), weak
   duality gives the reverse inequality, proving \((SCG3)\).  Each successful
   addition strictly enlarges the active set, so finite termination is immediate.
   The target statement follows by comparing the final exact value with
   \(C_\Sigma\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One-sided shared integrated cover oracle]
   \label{cor:one-sided-shared-integrated-cover-oracle}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:shared-integrated-cover-column-generation}.  A one-sided shared
   record oracle takes a restricted dual \(u\) and either returns a record
   \(i\in\mathcal R\) with a verifiable certificate
   \[
      \underline H_i>2\overline P_i,
      \qquad
      0\le\underline H_i\le\sum_ah_{i,a}u_a,
      \qquad
      P_i\le\overline P_i,
      \tag{SIO1}
   \]
   or correctly certifies that no record in \(\mathcal R\) has positive shared
   reduced cost \((SCG2)\).  Then this oracle is complete for shared-cover
   column generation: every accepted record is a valid column, and a no-record
   certificate proves full optimality of the current restricted shared cover.

   The positive branch may be implemented in Las Vegas build time.  If a
   randomized proposal law returns an accepted certificate satisfying \((SIO1)\)
   with probability at least \(p_E>0\) whenever a positive shared-reduced-cost
   record exists, repeat proposals until one is accepted; failed or unverifiable
   proposals are discarded.  The no-record branch remains an exact finite
   certificate over \(\mathcal R\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   A certificate \((SIO1)\) implies
   \[
      \sum_ah_{i,a}u_a\ge\underline H_i>2\overline P_i\ge2P_i,
   \]
   hence \((SCG2)\) holds and the record may be added by
   \cref{cor:shared-integrated-cover-column-generation}.  If the oracle correctly
   certifies that no positive record exists, the same corollary proves full
   optimality of the restricted cover.  For the Las Vegas positive branch, the
   probability that the first \(B\) independent proposals all fail is at most
   \((1-p_E)^B\), and only verified records are retained.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Shared top-prefix reduced-cost compiler]
   \label{cor:shared-top-prefix-reduced-cost-compiler}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:one-sided-shared-integrated-cover-oracle}.  A shared prefix
   template \(B\) consists of a certified smaller-radius container \(W_B\subseteq
   P\), nonnegative atom contributions
   \[
      h_{B,p,a}\ge0\qquad(p\in W_B,\ a\in\mathcal A_\pi),
      \tag{SPF1}
   \]
   available cardinalities \(\mathcal K_B\), and prices \(P_B(K)\ge0\).  Assume
   that for every \(K\in\mathcal K_B\) and every \(U\subseteq W_B\) with
   \(|U|=K\), the shared record
   \[
      h_{U,a}=\sum_{p\in U}h_{B,p,a},
      \qquad
      P_U=P_B(K),
      \tag{SPF2}
   \]
   is admissible for
   \cref{cor:shared-integrated-cover-column-generation}.  For a restricted
   shared-cover dual \(u\), define the shared degree
   \[
      d_B^u(p)=\sum_ah_{B,p,a}u_a,
      \tag{SPF3}
   \]
   and order \(W_B=\{p_1,p_2,\ldots\}\) by nonincreasing \(d_B^u(p)\).

   If for some \(K\in\mathcal K_B\)
   \[
      \sum_{j\le K}d_B^u(p_j)>2P_B(K),
      \tag{SPF4}
   \]
   then the top prefix \(U_K=\{p_1,\ldots,p_K\}\) has positive shared reduced
   cost and may be added by
   \cref{cor:shared-integrated-cover-column-generation}.  Conversely, if
   \((SPF4)\) fails for every \(K\in\mathcal K_B\), then no admissible subset of
   this template and available cardinality has positive shared reduced cost:
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U}d_B^u(p)\le2P_B(K)
      \qquad
      (K\in\mathcal K_B,\ U\subseteq W_B,\ |U|=K).
      \tag{SPF5}
   \]

   Thus a \(k\)-means++, facility, additive-quantization, range, list-decoding,
   or lattice-decoding proposal only has to produce a certified container
   template whose top shared-prefix degree beats the one-time recursive price.
   The retained object is the same deterministic top-prefix shared record used by
   the finite cover verifier.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For any fixed cardinality \(K\), the top \(K\) points in the order maximize
   \(\sum_{p\in U}d_B^u(p)\) over all \(K\)-subsets of \(W_B\).  If \((SPF4)\)
   holds, then for \(U_K\)
   \[
      \sum_ah_{U_K,a}u_a
      =
      \sum_{p\in U_K}d_B^u(p)
      >
      2P_B(K)=2P_{U_K},
   \]
   so \((SCG2)\) holds.  The column-generation corollary may add this shared
   record.  If \((SPF4)\) fails for every available \(K\), top-prefix optimality
   gives \((SPF5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One-sided shared top-prefix certificate]
   \label{cor:one-sided-shared-top-prefix-certificate}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:shared-top-prefix-reduced-cost-compiler}.  A one-sided top-prefix
   certificate for a template \(B\) consists of an available cardinality
   \(K\in\mathcal K_B\), a reported prefix \(U\subseteq W_B\) with \(|U|=K\), and
   numbers \(\underline H,\overline P\) satisfying
   \[
      0\le\underline H\le\sum_{p\in U}d_B^u(p),
      \qquad
      P_B(K)\le\overline P,
      \qquad
      \underline H>2\overline P .
      \tag{SPC1}
   \]
   Then \(U\) is a valid positive shared-cover column.  If the reporter instead
   certifies that \((SPF4)\) fails for every template in a finite family and every
   available cardinality, then no record from that family has positive shared
   reduced cost.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The first two inequalities in \((SPC1)\) give
   \[
      \sum_ah_{U,a}u_a
      =
      \sum_{p\in U}d_B^u(p)
      \ge \underline H
      >2\overline P
      \ge2P_B(K).
   \]
   Hence \((SCG2)\) holds for the record \(U\), so it is a valid
   column-generation addition.  The no-record statement is the contrapositive of
   \cref{cor:shared-top-prefix-reduced-cost-compiler} applied to each template in
   the finite family.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Reduced-cost top-prefix router search]
   \label{cor:reduced-cost-top-prefix-router-search}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:shared-top-prefix-reduced-cost-compiler}, and fix a finite family of
   shared prefix templates \(\mathcal B\).  For each \(B\in\mathcal B\) and
   \(K\in\mathcal K_B\), order \(W_B=\{p_1,p_2,\ldots\}\) by nonincreasing
   shared degree \(d_B^u\) and define
   \[
      \Delta_{B,K}
      =
      \sum_{j\le K}d_B^u(p_j)-2P_B(K).
      \tag{RTR1}
   \]
   If \(\max_{B,K}\Delta_{B,K}\le0\), then no admissible subset of any template
   in \(\mathcal B\), at any available cardinality, has positive shared reduced
   cost.  If \(\max_{B,K}\Delta_{B,K}>0\), then the corresponding top prefix is a
   valid positive shared-cover column.

   In the one-sided form of
   \cref{cor:one-sided-shared-top-prefix-certificate}, a proposal
   \((B,K,U,\underline H,\overline P)\) with
   \[
      \underline H-2\overline P>0
      \tag{RTR2}
   \]
   is accepted.  A randomized router proposal law that produces such an accepted
   certificate with probability \(p_+\) succeeds after expected at most
   \(1/p_+\) Las Vegas proposals, and an exact finite maximization over certified
   candidates is complete for all one-sided positive top-prefix columns in that
   family.

   Hence a data-dependent router does not need a special proof for Lloyd steps or
   any particular clustering heuristic.  The proof-relevant object is the
   certified top-prefix reduced cost \((RTR1)\), with the recursive price
   \(P_B(K)\) in the same units as the shared-cover dual.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For fixed \(B\) and \(K\), the top \(K\) prefix maximizes
   \(\sum_{p\in U}d_B^u(p)\) over all \(K\)-subsets of \(W_B\).  Therefore
   \(\Delta_{B,K}\le0\) for every \(B,K\) is exactly the family of inequalities
   \((SPF5)\), and no subset in the family has positive reduced cost.  If some
   \(\Delta_{B,K}>0\), then \((SPF4)\) holds for that template and cardinality, so
   \cref{cor:shared-top-prefix-reduced-cost-compiler} adds the top prefix as a
   positive shared-cover column.

   The one-sided proposal condition \((RTR2)\) is precisely \((SPC1)\).  Thus
   \cref{cor:one-sided-shared-top-prefix-certificate} verifies the proposed
   column.  Repetition is geometric with mean \(1/p_+\), and exact finite
   maximization is complete for the certifiable positive candidates because it
   returns a positive value whenever any candidate has one.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Shared prefix weak-type residual]
   \label{cor:shared-prefix-weak-type-residual}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:shared-top-prefix-reduced-cost-compiler}.  Suppose a template \(B\)
   has prices
   \[
      P_B(K)=\psi_B\left(A_BK^{\rho_B}+\zeta_BK^{1+\rho_B}\right),
      \qquad 0<\rho_B<1,
      \tag{SHW1}
   \]
   and that the available cardinalities \(\mathcal K_B\) are \(b_B\)-dense from
   below: for every \(1\le h\le |W_B|\), some \(K\in\mathcal K_B\) satisfies
   \(h/b_B\le K\le h\).  If no available top prefix of \(B\) has positive shared
   reduced cost, then every degree superlevel
   \[
      H_{B,\delta}=\{p\in W_B:d_B^u(p)\ge\delta\},
      \qquad h=|H_{B,\delta}|,
      \tag{SHW2}
   \]
   obeys
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      2\psi_B\left(
         b_B^{1-\rho_B}A_Bh^{\rho_B-1}
         +\zeta_Bh^{\rho_B}
      \right)
      \qquad(h>0).
      \tag{SHW3}
   \]
   Equivalently, if a reported container certifies a level \(\delta\) and
   cardinality \(h>0\) violating \((SHW3)\), then some available shared top prefix
   in that container is a positive shared-cover column.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(h>0\) and choose \(K\in\mathcal K_B\) with \(h/b_B\le K\le h\).  The top
   \(K\) prefix has every point of degree at least \(\delta\), so
   \[
      K\delta\le\sum_{j\le K}d_B^u(p_j).
   \]
   Since no available top prefix is positive, \((SPF4)\) fails:
   \[
      \sum_{j\le K}d_B^u(p_j)
      \le2P_B(K)
      =
      2\psi_B\left(A_BK^{\rho_B}+\zeta_BK^{1+\rho_B}\right).
   \]
   Dividing by \(K\) gives
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      2\psi_B\left(A_BK^{\rho_B-1}+\zeta_BK^{\rho_B}\right).
   \]
   Since \(\rho_B-1<0\), \(K\ge h/b_B\) gives
   \(K^{\rho_B-1}\le b_B^{1-\rho_B}h^{\rho_B-1}\), while \(K\le h\) gives
   \(K^{\rho_B}\le h^{\rho_B}\).  This proves \((SHW3)\).  The positive
   statement is the contrapositive followed by
   \cref{cor:shared-top-prefix-reduced-cost-compiler}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Shared prefix price-density screen]
   \label{cor:shared-prefix-price-density-screen}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:shared-prefix-weak-type-residual}.  For
   \(K\ge1\), put
   \[
      f_B(K)=A_BK^{\rho_B-1}+\zeta_BK^{\rho_B}.
      \tag{SHD1}
   \]
   If, for some available \(K\in\mathcal K_B\) and some threshold \(\delta>0\),
   the superlevel mass
   \[
      M_B(\delta)=\sum_{p:\ d_B^u(p)\ge\delta}d_B^u(p)
      \tag{SHD2}
   \]
   satisfies
   \[
      \delta>2\psi_B f_B(K),
      \qquad
      M_B(\delta)>2\psi_BKf_B(K),
      \tag{SHD3}
   \]
   then \(B\) contains a positive shared top-prefix column.  Consequently, in a
   residual where all shared prefixes of \(B\) fail, at least one of the reverse
   inequalities in \((SHD3)\) holds for every threshold and available \(K\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Conditions \((SHD3)\) say that both entries in
   \[
      \min\{M_B(\delta),K\delta\}
   \]
   are larger than
   \[
      2\psi_BKf_B(K)=2P_B(K).
   \]
   Let \(h=|H_{B,\delta}|\).  If \(h\ge K\), then the top \(K\) points all have
   degree at least \(\delta\), so their total shared degree is larger than
   \(2P_B(K)\).  If \(h<K\), then the top \(K\) prefix contains all of
   \(H_{B,\delta}\), so its total shared degree is at least \(M_B(\delta)\), again
   larger than \(2P_B(K)\).  In either case \((SPF4)\) holds and
   \cref{cor:shared-top-prefix-reduced-cost-compiler} gives a positive shared
   prefix.  The residual statement is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Shared prefix density panels]
   \label{cor:shared-prefix-density-panel}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:shared-prefix-price-density-screen}.  Let
   \(I\) be a finite panel of shared prefix templates.  For each \(i\in I\),
   choose a template \(B_i\), an available cardinality
   \(K_i\in\mathcal K_{B_i}\), a threshold \(\delta_i>0\), and a nonnegative
   panel weight \(\lambda_i\).  Put
   \[
      f_i=f_{B_i}(K_i),
      \qquad
      M_i=M_{B_i}(\delta_i).
      \tag{SPD1}
   \]
   Suppose every active record is above its local price density,
   \[
      \delta_i>2\psi_{B_i}f_i
      \qquad(\lambda_i>0),
      \tag{SPD2}
   \]
   and the aggregate captured shared mass beats the aggregate prefix price,
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_iM_i
      >
      2\sum_i\lambda_i\psi_{B_i}K_if_i .
      \tag{SPD3}
   \]
   Then at least one template in the panel contains a positive shared top-prefix
   column.

   More generally, it is enough to certify lower masses
   \(\underline M_i\le M_i\) and upper prices
   \(\overline P_i\ge\psi_{B_i}K_if_i\) such that
   \[
      K_i\delta_i>2\overline P_i
      \qquad(\lambda_i>0),
      \tag{SPD4}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_i\lambda_i\underline M_i
      >
      2\sum_i\lambda_i\overline P_i .
      \tag{SPD5}
   \]
   Thus a facility, additive-quantization, range-reporting, list-decoding, or
   lattice proposal may be analyzed as a whole weighted panel, while the
   retained object is still one deterministic shared top prefix.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose no template in the panel contains a positive shared prefix.  By
   \cref{cor:shared-prefix-price-density-screen}, for each active \(i\) at
   least one of the two inequalities in \((SHD3)\) must fail.  Condition
   \((SPD2)\) is the first inequality in \((SHD3)\), so the second one must
   fail:
   \[
      M_i\le2\psi_{B_i}K_if_i
      \qquad(\lambda_i>0).
   \]
   Multiplying by \(\lambda_i\) and summing contradicts \((SPD3)\).  Hence some
   record contains a positive shared top-prefix column.

   For the one-sided form, \((SPD4)\) implies
   \[
      \delta_i>2\overline P_i/K_i\ge2\psi_{B_i}f_i,
   \]
   and \((SPD5)\), together with \(\underline M_i\le M_i\) and
   \(\overline P_i\ge\psi_{B_i}K_if_i\), implies \((SPD3)\).  The first part
   applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sampled shared prefix density search]
   \label{cor:sampled-shared-prefix-density-search}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:shared-prefix-density-panel}.  A randomized
   build-time proposal routine, on seed \(s\), returns a finite verified panel
   \(I_s\) with nonnegative weights \(\lambda_{s,i}\).  Every active record in
   the returned panel satisfies the one-sided local density condition
   \[
      K_{s,i}\delta_{s,i}>2\overline P_{s,i}
      \qquad(\lambda_{s,i}>0),
      \tag{SPS1}
   \]
   and has certified lower mass \(\underline M_{s,i}\) and upper price
   \(\overline P_{s,i}\) as in \((SPD4)\)--\((SPD5)\).  Define the certified
   shared-prefix surplus
   \[
      Z(s)=
      \sum_{i\in I_s}
      \lambda_{s,i}\bigl(\underline M_{s,i}-2\overline P_{s,i}\bigr).
      \tag{SPS2}
   \]
   Suppose
   \[
      \E_sZ(s)\ge\Gamma>0,
      \qquad
      Z(s)_+\le M
      \quad\text{almost surely}.
      \tag{SPS3}
   \]
   Then \(B\) independent build-time seeds contain a verified panel that exposes
   a positive shared top-prefix column with probability at least
   \[
      1-\exp\left(-\frac{B\Gamma}{M}\right).
      \tag{SPS4}
   \]

   Thus expensive randomized preprocessing may search a large family of
   \(k\)-means++, facility, AQ, range, list-decoding, or lattice panels.  Only
   the first verified positive panel is used, and
   \cref{cor:shared-prefix-density-panel} immediately hardens it to one
   deterministic retained top prefix.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   From \((SPS3)\), \(\E Z_+\ge\Gamma\).  Since \(Z_+\le M\), one seed has
   \(Z(s)>0\) with probability at least \(\Gamma/M\).  Thus \(B\) independent
   seeds all fail to produce a positive-surplus panel with probability at most
   \[
      \left(1-\frac{\Gamma}{M}\right)^B
      \le
      \exp\left(-\frac{B\Gamma}{M}\right).
   \]
   For any successful seed, \((SPS1)\) and \(Z(s)>0\) are exactly the one-sided
   panel conditions \((SPD4)\)--\((SPD5)\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:shared-prefix-density-panel} returns a positive shared top-prefix
   column.  Failed samples are discarded before materialization.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Clipped shared prefix price-density screen]
   \label{cor:clipped-shared-prefix-density-screen}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:shared-prefix-price-density-screen}.  Put
   \(m_B=|W_B|\) and
   \[
      f_B(K)=A_BK^{\rho_B-1}+\zeta_BK^{\rho_B}.
      \tag{SHC1}
   \]
   If \(A_B=\zeta_B=0\), then any available top prefix with positive shared
   degree is a positive shared-cover column.  Otherwise define the clipped
   minimizer
   \[
      K_B^\natural=
      \begin{cases}
      1, & A_B=0,\\[0.2em]
      m_B, & \zeta_B=0,\\[0.4em]
      \min\!\left\{m_B,\max\!\left\{1,
      \dfrac{(1-\rho_B)A_B}{\rho_B\zeta_B}\right\}\right\},
         & A_B>0,\ \zeta_B>0 .
      \end{cases}
      \tag{SHC2}
   \]
   Let \(a\ge1\).  If an available cardinality \(K\in\mathcal K_B\) satisfies
   \[
      a^{-1}K_B^\natural\le K\le aK_B^\natural
      \tag{SHC3}
   \]
   and some threshold \(\delta>0\) satisfies
   \[
      \delta>2a\psi_Bf_B(K_B^\natural),
      \qquad
      M_B(\delta)>2a\psi_BKf_B(K_B^\natural),
      \tag{SHC4}
   \]
   then \(B\) contains a positive shared top-prefix column.

   Conversely, in a residual where all shared prefixes of \(B\) fail, every
   available \(K\) satisfying \((SHC3)\) and every threshold \(\delta>0\) obeys
   at least one reverse inequality in \((SHC4)\).  Thus the shared-prefix
   separator may focus on the clipped stationary support scale
   \(K_B^\natural\), up to the available-cardinality net factor.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(A_B=\zeta_B=0\), then \(P_B(K)=0\) for every available \(K\).  Any
   positive-degree prefix has positive shared reduced cost by
   \cref{cor:shared-top-prefix-reduced-cost-compiler}.

   Assume at least one price is positive.  It is enough to show that
   \[
      f_B(K)\le a f_B(K_B^\natural)
      \tag{SHC5}
   \]
   whenever \((SHC3)\) holds.  If the unclipped stationary point lies in
   \([1,m_B]\), write \(K=\lambda K_B^\natural\) with
   \(\lambda\in[a^{-1},a]\).  Then
   \[
      f_B(K)
      =
      \lambda^{\rho_B-1}A_B(K_B^\natural)^{\rho_B-1}
      +
      \lambda^{\rho_B}\zeta_B(K_B^\natural)^{\rho_B}
      \le a f_B(K_B^\natural),
   \]
   since \(0<\rho_B<1\).  If \(K_B^\natural=1\), then \(K\in[1,a]\) and the
   first term of \(f_B\) is nonincreasing while the second term grows by at most
   \(a\).  If \(K_B^\natural=m_B\), then \(K\in[m_B/a,m_B]\) and the first term
   grows by at most \(a\) while the second term is nondecreasing and bounded by
   its value at \(m_B\).  These boundary cases also give \((SHC5)\).

   Conditions \((SHC4)\) and \((SHC5)\) imply
   \[
      \delta>2\psi_Bf_B(K),
      \qquad
      M_B(\delta)>2\psi_BKf_B(K).
   \]
   This is exactly \((SHD3)\), so
   \cref{cor:shared-prefix-price-density-screen} gives a positive shared
   top-prefix column.  The residual statement is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Tail-mass clipped shared prefix screen]
   \label{cor:tail-mass-clipped-shared-prefix-screen}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:clipped-shared-prefix-density-screen}.
   Assume \(A_B\) and \(\zeta_B\) are not both zero, let \(a\ge1\), and choose an
   available \(K\in\mathcal K_B\) satisfying \((SHC3)\).  Define the clipped
   shared density threshold
   \[
      \Theta_B=2a\psi_Bf_B(K_B^\natural),
      \tag{SHT1}
   \]
   and the strict tail mass
   \[
      M_B^+(\Theta_B)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{p\in W_B:\\ d_B^u(p)>\Theta_B}}d_B^u(p).
      \tag{SHT2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      M_B^+(\Theta_B)>K\Theta_B,
      \tag{SHT3}
   \]
   then \(B\) contains a positive shared top-prefix column.

   Consequently, in any residual where all shared prefixes of \(B\) fail, every
   available \(K\) near the clipped scale obeys
   \[
      M_B^+(\Theta_B)\le K\Theta_B .
      \tag{SHT4}
   \]
   This is the most direct price-density residual for a geometric reporter:
   after prices are fixed, all shared degree mass above the clipped threshold is
   at most the support scale times that threshold.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(M_B^+(\Theta_B)>0\), the set
   \[
      T=\{p\in W_B:d_B^u(p)>\Theta_B\}
   \]
   is nonempty.  Since \(W_B\) is finite, choose
   \(\delta\) with
   \[
      \Theta_B<\delta\le\min_{p\in T}d_B^u(p).
   \]
   Then \(T\subseteq\{p:d_B^u(p)\ge\delta\}\), so
   \[
      M_B(\delta)\ge M_B^+(\Theta_B)>K\Theta_B
      =
      2a\psi_BKf_B(K_B^\natural),
   \]
   while \(\delta>\Theta_B=2a\psi_Bf_B(K_B^\natural)\).  Thus \((SHC4)\) holds,
   and \cref{cor:clipped-shared-prefix-density-screen} gives a positive shared
   top-prefix column.  The residual statement is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cardinality-net clipped shared tail residual]
   \label{cor:cardinality-net-clipped-shared-tail}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:shared-prefix-weak-type-residual}, and
   assume no available shared top prefix of \(B\) has positive shared reduced
   cost.  If \(A_B=\zeta_B=0\), then \(d_B^u(p)=0\) for every \(p\in W_B\).
   Otherwise let \(K_B^\natural\) be the clipped minimizer \((SHC2)\).  Suppose
   the available cardinalities are \(b_B\)-dense from below as in
   \cref{cor:shared-prefix-weak-type-residual}.  Define
   \[
      \Theta_B^{\rm net}
      =
      4b_B\psi_Bf_B(K_B^\natural),
      \tag{SCN1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      M_B^+(\Theta_B^{\rm net})
      =
      \sum_{\substack{p\in W_B:\\ d_B^u(p)>\Theta_B^{\rm net}}}d_B^u(p).
      \tag{SCN2}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      M_B^+(\Theta_B^{\rm net})
      \le
      2K_B^\natural\Theta_B^{\rm net}.
      \tag{SCN3}
   \]

   Thus, after cardinality rounding, the no-prefix residual for a shared
   container is a single clipped tail inequality.  A geometric proof no longer
   has to choose a threshold or a prefix size: it must beat the explicit
   tail cap \((SCN3)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(A_B=\zeta_B=0\) and some \(p\) had \(d_B^u(p)>0\), the available prefix
   containing the top positive-degree point would have positive reduced cost,
   since its price is zero.  Hence all degrees are zero.

   Assume at least one price is positive.  Put
   \(h=\lceil K_B^\natural\rceil\).  Since
   \(1\le K_B^\natural\le m_B=|W_B|\), we have \(h\le m_B\) and
   \(h\le2K_B^\natural\).  By \(b_B\)-density from below, choose
   \(K\in\mathcal K_B\) with
   \[
      h/b_B\le K\le h .
   \]
   Then
   \[
      (2b_B)^{-1}K_B^\natural\le K\le2K_B^\natural,
   \]
   so \((SHC3)\) holds with \(a=2b_B\).  The threshold \((SHT1)\) for this
   choice of \(a\) is exactly \(\Theta_B^{\rm net}\).  Since no shared prefix
   fires, \cref{cor:tail-mass-clipped-shared-prefix-screen} gives
   \[
      M_B^+(\Theta_B^{\rm net})\le K\Theta_B^{\rm net}
      \le2K_B^\natural\Theta_B^{\rm net},
   \]
   proving \((SCN3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Subset form of the clipped shared tail]
   \label{cor:subset-clipped-shared-tail-residual}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-clipped-shared-tail}, and assume at least one of
   \(A_B,\zeta_B\) is positive.  Put
   \[
      \Theta=\Theta_B^{\rm net},
      \qquad
      K^\natural=K_B^\natural .
      \tag{CST1}
   \]
   If the clipped tail cap \((SCN3)\) holds, then every subset
   \(U\subseteq W_B\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U}d_B^u(p)
      \le
      \bigl(|U|+2K^\natural\bigr)\Theta .
      \tag{CST2}
   \]
   Conversely, if preprocessing certifies a subset \(U\subseteq W_B\) and a
   lower mass \(V\) with
   \[
      0\le V\le\sum_{p\in U}d_B^u(p),
      \qquad
      V>\bigl(|U|+2K^\natural\bigr)\Theta ,
      \tag{CST3}
   \]
   then \(B\) violates the single clipped tail cap \((SCN3)\), and therefore
   contains a positive shared top-prefix column.

   Thus the remaining geometric separator may search for any certified
   smaller-radius subset with paid mass above the fixed affine threshold
   \((|U|+2K_B^\natural)\Theta_B^{\rm net}\).  It need not guess a degree
   threshold or a prefix cardinality.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Split \(U\) into points of degree at most \(\Theta\) and greater than
   \(\Theta\).  If \((SCN3)\) holds, then
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \sum_{p\in U}d_B^u(p)
      &\le
      |U|\Theta+
      \sum_{\substack{p\in W_B:\\ d_B^u(p)>\Theta}}d_B^u(p) \\
      &\le
      \bigl(|U|+2K^\natural\bigr)\Theta,
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   proving \((CST2)\).  The certified inequality \((CST3)\) contradicts
   \((CST2)\), so \((SCN3)\) fails.  By the contrapositive of
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-clipped-shared-tail}, some available shared top
   prefix has positive reduced cost.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Transported subset clipped-tail certificate]
   \label{cor:transported-subset-clipped-tail-certificate}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:subset-clipped-shared-tail-residual}.  Let \(U\subseteq W_B\) be a
   certified smaller-radius subset.  Suppose preprocessing certifies a
   nonnegative transported load \(\ell_p\) on \(U\), total mass \(M\), and
   congestion \(C>0\) such that
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U}\ell_p=M,
      \qquad
      \ell_p\le C\,d_B^u(p)\quad(p\in U).
      \tag{CTS1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \frac{M}{C}>
      \bigl(|U|+2K_B^\natural\bigr)\Theta_B^{\rm net},
      \tag{CTS2}
   \]
   then \(B\) violates the clipped shared-tail cap \((SCN3)\), and hence
   contains a positive shared top-prefix column.

   Thus a high-correlation transport theorem may certify one transported subset
   directly.  When the subset size is known, no dyadic layer-cake extraction or
   multiplicity dynamic-range factor is needed before invoking the shared-prefix
   verifier.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Summing the pointwise congestion bounds in \((CTS1)\) gives
   \[
      \frac{M}{C}\le\sum_{p\in U}d_B^u(p).
   \]
   With \(V=M/C\), condition \((CTS2)\) is exactly the certified subset
   violation \((CST3)\).  The conclusion follows from
   \cref{cor:subset-clipped-shared-tail-residual}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Transported clipped-tail panel separator]
   \label{cor:transported-clipped-tail-panel-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:transported-subset-clipped-tail-certificate}, for a finite family
   \(\mathcal B\) of shared prefix templates with prices
   \(P_B(K)=\psi_B(A_BK^{\rho_B}+\zeta_BK^{1+\rho_B})\),
   \(0<\rho_B<1\), and cardinality-net clipped scales
   \(K_B^\natural,\Theta_B^{\rm net}\).  Fix a no-prefix dual \(u\) and its
   shared degrees \(d_B^u\).  A transported panel consists of records \(i\in I\),
   nonnegative weights \(\lambda_i\), templates \(B_i\in\mathcal B\), certified
   smaller-radius subsets \(U_i\subseteq W_{B_i}\), transported loads
