   \(\ell_{i,p}\), masses \(M_i\), and congestions \(C_i>0\) such that
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U_i}\ell_{i,p}=M_i,
      \qquad
      \ell_{i,p}\le C_i\,d_{B_i}^u(p)
      \quad(p\in U_i).
      \tag{TSP1}
   \]
   Suppose every active template has nonzero clipped price
   \((A_{B_i},\zeta_{B_i})\ne(0,0)\).  If the panel has positive transported
   clipped-tail surplus
   \[
      \sum_{i\in I}\lambda_i
      \left(
         \frac{M_i}{C_i}
         -
         \bigl(|U_i|+2K_{B_i}^\natural\bigr)\Theta_{B_i}^{\rm net}
      \right)>0,
      \tag{TSP2}
   \]
   then some \(B_i\) violates its clipped shared-tail cap and therefore contains
   a positive shared top-prefix column.

   In particular, a randomized build-time proposal law that returns transported
   panels with certified surplus \(Z(s)\), with
   \[
      \E_s Z(s)\ge\Gamma>0,
      \qquad
      Z(s)_+\le M_{\rm prop}
      \quad\text{almost surely},
      \tag{TSP3}
   \]
   finds a panel containing a positive shared top-prefix column after \(N\)
   independent proposals with probability at least
   \[
      1-\exp\left(-\frac{N\Gamma}{M_{\rm prop}}\right).
      \tag{TSP4}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((TSP2)\) holds, then some active record \(i\) has
   \[
      \frac{M_i}{C_i}
      >
      \bigl(|U_i|+2K_{B_i}^\natural\bigr)\Theta_{B_i}^{\rm net}.
   \]
   Condition \((TSP1)\) is exactly \((CTS1)\) for \(B_i,U_i\), and the displayed
   inequality is \((CTS2)\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:transported-subset-clipped-tail-certificate} gives a clipped-tail
   violation and a positive shared top-prefix column.

   For the randomized statement, \(\E Z_+\ge\Gamma\) and \(Z_+\le M_{\rm prop}\)
   imply that one proposal has positive surplus with probability at least
   \(\Gamma/M_{\rm prop}\).  Independent repetition gives \((TSP4)\), and every
   positive-surplus panel is handled by the deterministic part.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Flow-value clipped-tail screen]
   \label{lem:flow-value-clipped-tail-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:transported-clipped-tail-panel-separator}.  Fix one template
   \(B\), a certified subset \(U\subseteq W_B\), a finite source set
   \(\mathcal I\) with loads \(\mu_i\ge0\), and a finite adjacency relation
   \(E_U\subseteq\mathcal I\times U\).  Assume
   \((A_B,\zeta_B)\ne(0,0)\), so \(K_B^\natural\) and
   \(\Theta_B^{\rm net}\) are defined.  For \(C>0\), let \(\Phi_{B,U}(C)\) be
   the maximum mass of a nonnegative flow \(f_{i,p}\) supported on \(E_U\),
   subject to
   \[
      \sum_{p:(i,p)\in E_U} f_{i,p}\le \mu_i
      \qquad(i\in\mathcal I),
      \tag{CTV1}
   \]
   \[
      \sum_{i:(i,p)\in E_U} f_{i,p}\le C\,d_B^u(p)
      \qquad(p\in U).
      \tag{CTV2}
   \]
   For \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal I\), let
   \(N_U(\mathcal A)=\{p\in U:\exists i\in\mathcal A,\ (i,p)\in E_U\}\).  Then
   \[
      \Phi_{B,U}(C)=
      \min_{\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal I}
      \left\{
         \sum_{i\in\mathcal I\setminus\mathcal A}\mu_i
         +
         C\sum_{p\in N_U(\mathcal A)}d_B^u(p)
      \right\}.
      \tag{CTV3}
   \]

   Consequently, if
   \[
      \frac{\Phi_{B,U}(C)}{C}>
      \bigl(|U|+2K_B^\natural\bigr)\Theta_B^{\rm net},
      \tag{CTV4}
   \]
   then \(B\) contains a positive shared top-prefix column.  More generally, for
   a finite panel of such flow records, positive aggregate flow surplus
   \[
      \sum_j\lambda_j
      \left(
         \frac{\Phi_{B_j,U_j}(C_j)}{C_j}
         -
         \bigl(|U_j|+2K_{B_j}^\natural\bigr)
         \Theta_{B_j}^{\rm net}
      \right)>0
      \tag{CTV5}
   \]
   already exposes one positive shared top-prefix column.

   Conversely, if no transported clipped-tail repair exists for this record and
   \(M/C>(|U|+2K_B^\natural)\Theta_B^{\rm net}\), then there is a finite cut
   \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal I\) satisfying
   \[
      \sum_{i\in\mathcal A}\mu_i
      >
      C\sum_{p\in N_U(\mathcal A)}d_B^u(p)
      +
      \sum_{i\in\mathcal I}\mu_i
      -M .
      \tag{CTV6}
   \]
   Thus a failed flow proposal leaves an explicit localized source/capacity cut.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The identity \((CTV3)\) is the finite max-flow/min-cut theorem on the
   bipartite network with source capacities \(\mu_i\), infinite-capacity edges
   \((i,p)\in E_U\), and sink capacities \(C d_B^u(p)\).  A finite cut is
   determined by the set \(\mathcal A\) of source-side left vertices; all
   adjacent right vertices \(N_U(\mathcal A)\) must also remain source-side, and
   the displayed expression is exactly the cut capacity.

   Let \(f\) be an optimal flow of value \(\Phi_{B,U}(C)\), and define
   \[
      \ell_p=\sum_{i:(i,p)\in E_U}f_{i,p}.
   \]
   Then \(\sum_p\ell_p=\Phi_{B,U}(C)\), and \((CTV2)\) gives
   \(\ell_p\le C d_B^u(p)\).  Hence \((CTV4)\) is exactly the transported
   subset certificate \((CTS2)\), so
   \cref{cor:transported-subset-clipped-tail-certificate} gives a positive
   shared top-prefix column.  If the aggregate inequality \((CTV5)\) holds, one
   panel record has positive bracketed surplus and the one-record conclusion
   applies.

   Finally, if \(M/C\) is above the affine threshold and no transported repair
   exists, then \(\Phi_{B,U}(C)<M\).  By \((CTV3)\), some cut has value below
   \(M\); rewriting that strict inequality gives \((CTV6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Opened-support flow screen]
   \label{cor:opened-support-flow-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{lem:flow-value-clipped-tail-screen}, but do not preselect the right
   support.  Fix a template \(B\), a finite source set \(\mathcal I\) with loads
   \(\mu_i\ge0\), an adjacency relation
   \(E\subseteq\mathcal I\times W_B\), and \(C>0\).  Put
   \[
      \Theta=\Theta_B^{\rm net},
      \qquad
      K=K_B^\natural .
      \tag{OSFS0}
   \]
   For \(S\subseteq W_B\), let \(\Phi_B(S;C)\) be the max-flow value defined as
   in \((CTV1)\)--\((CTV2)\), using the right vertex set \(S\) and the restricted
   edge set \(E\cap(\mathcal I\times S)\).  Define the opened-support surplus
   \[
      \mathfrak S_{B,E}(C)
      =
      \max_{S\subseteq W_B}
      \left\{
         \frac{\Phi_B(S;C)}{C}-|S|\Theta
      \right\}.
      \tag{OSFS1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \mathfrak S_{B,E}(C)>2K\Theta ,
      \tag{OSFS2}
   \]
   then \(B\) contains a positive shared top-prefix column.

   More generally, for a finite panel of source systems
   \((B_j,E_j,C_j)\) with nonnegative weights \(\lambda_j\), positive aggregate
   opened-support surplus
   \[
      \sum_j\lambda_j
      \left(
         \mathfrak S_{B_j,E_j}(C_j)
         -
         2K_{B_j}^\natural\Theta_{B_j}^{\rm net}
      \right)>0
      \tag{OSFS3}
   \]
   exposes one positive shared top-prefix column.

   This strictly subsumes the fixed-subset flow test: for every proposed
   \(U\subseteq W_B\),
   \[
      \mathfrak S_{B,E}(C)
      \ge
      \frac{\Phi_{B,U}(C)}{C}-|U|\Theta .
      \tag{OSFS4}
   \]
   Conversely, in any residual where no shared top-prefix column of \(B\) has
   positive reduced cost,
   \[
      \mathfrak S_{B,E}(C)\le2K\Theta
      \tag{OSFS5}
   \]
   for every source set, load vector, adjacency relation, and congestion \(C\).

   Thus the flow verifier may score a branch by
   \[
      \text{transported mass}/C
      -
      \Theta\cdot\text{opened support size},
   \]
   leaving only the fixed clipped-tail overhead \(2K\Theta\).  A proposal does
   not pay for the whole candidate container, only for the points that actually
   receive flow.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(S\) and an optimal flow \(f\) witness a value in \((OSFS1)\) larger than
   \(2K\Theta\).  Let
   \[
      S_0=\left\{p\in S:\sum_i f_{i,p}>0\right\},
      \qquad
      M=\sum_{i,p}f_{i,p}.
   \]
   The same flow is feasible for the restricted support \(S_0\), and
   \(|S_0|\le |S|\).  Hence
   \[
      \frac{M}{C}-|S_0|\Theta
      \ge
      \frac{M}{C}-|S|\Theta
      >
      2K\Theta .
   \]
   With
   \[
      \ell_p=\sum_i f_{i,p}\qquad(p\in S_0),
   \]
   the sink-capacity constraints give \(\ell_p\le C d_B^u(p)\), while the last
   display says
   \[
      \frac{M}{C}>(|S_0|+2K)\Theta .
   \]
   This is exactly the transported subset clipped-tail certificate
   \((CTS1)\)--\((CTS2)\), so
   \cref{cor:transported-subset-clipped-tail-certificate} gives a positive
   shared top-prefix column.  The aggregate statement follows because
   \((OSFS3)\) makes at least one active bracket positive.

   Inequality \((OSFS4)\) is immediate by taking \(S=U\) in the maximum
   \((OSFS1)\).  Finally assume no shared top prefix of \(B\) is positive.  For
   every \(S\subseteq W_B\), the total sink capacity bounds
   \[
      \frac{\Phi_B(S;C)}{C}\le\sum_{p\in S}d_B^u(p).
   \]
   Applying \cref{cor:subset-clipped-shared-tail-residual} to \(S\) gives
   \[
      \sum_{p\in S}d_B^u(p)\le(|S|+2K)\Theta .
   \]
   Therefore every bracket in \((OSFS1)\) is at most \(2K\Theta\), proving
   \((OSFS5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fractional opened-support flow LP]
   \label{cor:fractional-opened-support-flow-lp}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:opened-support-flow-screen}.  Write
   \(d_p=d_B^u(p)\), and define the fractional opened-support value
   \(\widehat{\mathfrak S}_{B,E}(C)\) as the optimum of the finite linear
   program
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \text{\rm maximize} &
      \displaystyle
      \sum_{(i,p)\in E}x_{i,p}-\Theta\sum_{p\in W_B}z_p \\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to} &
      \displaystyle
      \sum_{p:(i,p)\in E}x_{i,p}\le \mu_i/C
      \qquad(i\in\mathcal I), \\[0.8em]
   &
      \displaystyle
      \sum_{i:(i,p)\in E}x_{i,p}\le d_pz_p
      \qquad(p\in W_B), \\[0.8em]
   &
      x_{i,p}\ge0,\qquad 0\le z_p\le1 .
   \end{array}
      \tag{FOF1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \mathfrak S_{B,E}(C)\le \widehat{\mathfrak S}_{B,E}(C).
      \tag{FOF2}
   \]
   Moreover finite LP duality gives the exact dual formula
   \[
      \widehat{\mathfrak S}_{B,E}(C)
      =
      \min_{\substack{\alpha_i,\beta_p\ge0\\
                      \alpha_i+\beta_p\ge1\ ((i,p)\in E)}}
      \left\{
         \sum_i\frac{\mu_i}{C}\alpha_i
         +
         \sum_{p\in W_B}(d_p\beta_p-\Theta)_+
      \right\}.
      \tag{FOF3}
   \]

   If
   \[
      \widehat{\mathfrak S}_{B,E}(C)>2K\Theta ,
      \tag{FOF4}
   \]
   then \(B\) contains a positive shared top-prefix column.  Conversely, in any
   residual where no shared top-prefix column of \(B\) has positive reduced
   cost,
   \[
      \widehat{\mathfrak S}_{B,E}(C)\le2K\Theta
      \tag{FOF5}
   \]
   for every source set, load vector, adjacency relation, and congestion \(C\).

   More generally, for a finite panel of such fractional source systems with
   nonnegative weights \(\lambda_j\), positive aggregate fractional surplus
   \[
      \sum_j\lambda_j
      \left(
         \widehat{\mathfrak S}_{B_j,E_j}(C_j)
         -
         2K_{B_j}^\natural\Theta_{B_j}^{\rm net}
      \right)>0
      \tag{FOF6}
   \]
   exposes one positive shared top-prefix column.

   Thus the nonconvex support choice in \((OSFS1)\) may be replaced, for
   separation purposes, by one ordinary finite LP.  If the LP fails to beat the
   clipped-tail overhead, its dual prices \((\alpha,\beta)\) are the exact
   finite obstruction: source mass is either paid directly by \(\alpha\), or any
   remaining incident point mass is charged through the clipped point price
   \((d_p\beta_p-\Theta)_+\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Given an integral support \(S\) and a feasible flow \(f\) for
   \(\Phi_B(S;C)\), set \(x_{i,p}=f_{i,p}/C\) and
   \(z_p=\mathbf 1_{\{p\in S\}}\).  This is feasible for \((FOF1)\), with
   objective \(\sum f_{i,p}/C-\Theta |S|\).  Maximizing over \(S\) and \(f\)
   proves \((FOF2)\).

   To derive \((FOF3)\), assign dual variables \(\alpha_i\ge0\) to the source
   constraints, \(\beta_p\ge0\) to the sink-capacity constraints, and
   \(\gamma_p\ge0\) to the bounds \(z_p\le1\).  The dual is
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \text{\rm minimize} &
      \displaystyle
      \sum_i(\mu_i/C)\alpha_i+\sum_p\gamma_p \\[0.6em]
   \text{\rm subject to} &
      \alpha_i+\beta_p\ge1\qquad((i,p)\in E),\\
   &
      \gamma_p\ge d_p\beta_p-\Theta,\qquad
      \alpha_i,\beta_p,\gamma_p\ge0 .
   \end{array}
   \]
   For fixed \(\alpha,\beta\), the best choice is
   \(\gamma_p=(d_p\beta_p-\Theta)_+\), giving \((FOF3)\).

   Now suppose \((x,z)\) is feasible for \((FOF1)\).  Since
   \(\sum_i x_{i,p}\le d_pz_p\),
   \[
      \sum_{(i,p)\in E}x_{i,p}-\Theta\sum_pz_p
      \le
      \sum_pz_p(d_p-\Theta)
      \le
      \sum_{\substack{p\in W_B:\\ d_p>\Theta}}(d_p-\Theta).
      \tag{FOF7}
   \]
   If the optimum is larger than \(2K\Theta\), the tail
   \(T=\{p\in W_B:d_p>\Theta\}\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{p\in T}d_p>(|T|+2K)\Theta .
   \]
   This is the subset clipped-tail violation \((CST3)\), and
   \cref{cor:subset-clipped-shared-tail-residual} gives a positive shared
   top-prefix column.

   Conversely, if no shared top prefix of \(B\) is positive, the same corollary
   applied to the tail \(T\) gives
   \[
      \sum_{p\in T}d_p\le(|T|+2K)\Theta .
   \]
   Inequality \((FOF7)\) then bounds every feasible fractional objective by
   \(2K\Theta\), proving \((FOF5)\).  Finally, if \((FOF6)\) holds, one active
   panel record has \(\widehat{\mathfrak S}_{B_j,E_j}(C_j)>
   2K_{B_j}^\natural\Theta_{B_j}^{\rm net}\), so the one-record conclusion
   applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Thresholded dual form of a failed fractional flow]
   \label{cor:thresholded-dual-failed-fractional-flow}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:fractional-opened-support-flow-lp}, and
   suppose that
   \[
      \widehat{\mathfrak S}_{B,E}(C)\le L .
      \tag{TDF1}
   \]
   Then, for every \(0<\eta<1\), there are feasible dual prices
   \((\alpha_i,\beta_p)\) for \((FOF3)\) such that
   \[
      \sum_i\frac{\mu_i}{C}\alpha_i
      +
      \sum_{p\in W_B}(d_p\beta_p-\Theta)_+
      \le L ,
      \tag{TDF2}
   \]
   and, with
   \[
      \mathcal I_{\rm hi}=\{i:\alpha_i>\eta\},\qquad
      \mathcal I_{\rm lo}=\mathcal I\setminus\mathcal I_{\rm hi},
      \qquad
      P_{\rm lo}=N_E(\mathcal I_{\rm lo}),
      \tag{TDF3}
   \]
   one has
   \[
      \sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{\rm hi}}\frac{\mu_i}{C}
      \le \frac{L}{\eta},
      \tag{TDF4}
   \]
   \[
      \beta_p\ge1-\eta\qquad(p\in P_{\rm lo}),
      \tag{TDF5}
   \]
   and hence
   \[
      \sum_{p\in P_{\rm lo}}\bigl((1-\eta)d_p-\Theta\bigr)_+
      \le L .
      \tag{TDF6}
   \]
   Equivalently, the low-price source neighborhood satisfies the raised clipped
   tail bound
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{p\in P_{\rm lo}:\\ d_p>\Theta/(1-\eta)}}
      \left(d_p-\frac{\Theta}{1-\eta}\right)
      \le \frac{L}{1-\eta}.
      \tag{TDF7}
   \]

   In particular, in a no-prefix residual one may take
   \(L=2K\Theta\).  Thus failure of the fractional flow screen has a canonical
   thresholded form: after paying at most \(L/\eta\) normalized source load,
   all remaining sources see only a point neighborhood whose shared-degree tail
   is clipped at the slightly larger threshold \(\Theta/(1-\eta)\).
   The half-threshold specialization is
   \[
      \sum_{i:\alpha_i>1/2}\frac{\mu_i}{C}\le4K\Theta,
      \qquad
      \sum_{\substack{p\in N_E(\{i:\alpha_i\le1/2\}):\\ d_p>2\Theta}}
      (d_p-2\Theta)
      \le4K\Theta .
      \tag{TDF8}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By the exact dual formula \((FOF3)\), choose dual prices satisfying
   \((TDF2)\).  The source part of \((TDF2)\) gives
   \[
      \eta\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{\rm hi}}\frac{\mu_i}{C}
      <
      \sum_{i\in\mathcal I_{\rm hi}}\frac{\mu_i}{C}\alpha_i
      \le L,
   \]
   which proves \((TDF4)\).  If \(p\in P_{\rm lo}\), then some
   \(i\in\mathcal I_{\rm lo}\) is adjacent to \(p\), so the dual constraint
   \(\alpha_i+\beta_p\ge1\) gives \((TDF5)\).  Therefore
   \[
      \bigl((1-\eta)d_p-\Theta\bigr)_+
      \le
      (d_p\beta_p-\Theta)_+
      \qquad(p\in P_{\rm lo}).
   \]
   Summing over \(P_{\rm lo}\) and using \((TDF2)\) gives \((TDF6)\), and
   \((TDF7)\) is just \((TDF6)\) divided by \(1-\eta\).  The no-prefix
   specialization follows from \((FOF5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Source-retention form of a failed fractional flow]
   \label{cor:source-retention-failed-fractional-flow}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:thresholded-dual-failed-fractional-flow}, and put
   \[
      M_{\rm src}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}\frac{\mu_i}{C}.
      \tag{SRF1}
   \]
   If \(\widehat{\mathfrak S}_{B,E}(C)\le L\), then, for every
   \(0<\eta<1\), there is a source subset
   \(J\subseteq\mathcal I\) such that
   \[
      \sum_{i\in J}\frac{\mu_i}{C}
      \ge M_{\rm src}-\frac{L}{\eta},
      \tag{SRF2}
   \]
   and, writing \(P_J=N_E(J)\),
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{p\in P_J:\\ d_p>\Theta/(1-\eta)}}
      \left(d_p-\frac{\Theta}{1-\eta}\right)
      \le \frac{L}{1-\eta}.
      \tag{SRF3}
   \]
   Consequently, if \(M_{\rm src}>L/\eta+M_0\), then \(J\) may be chosen with
   normalized source load larger than \(M_0\).

   In a no-prefix residual, taking \(L=2K\Theta\) and \(\eta=1/2\) gives the
   concrete form
   \[
      \sum_{i\in J}\frac{\mu_i}{C}
      \ge M_{\rm src}-4K\Theta,
      \qquad
      \sum_{\substack{p\in N_E(J):\\ d_p>2\Theta}}(d_p-2\Theta)
      \le4K\Theta .
      \tag{SRF4}
   \]
   Thus a failed fractional flow cannot make a large source system disappear:
   apart from the explicit \(O(K\Theta)\) paid source load, the remaining
   sources have a neighborhood obeying a single raised clipped-tail cap.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{cor:thresholded-dual-failed-fractional-flow} and take
   \(J=\mathcal I_{\rm lo}\).  The source-load bound \((SRF2)\) is the
   complement of \((TDF4)\), and \((SRF3)\) is \((TDF7)\) with
   \(P_J=P_{\rm lo}\).  The lower bound by \(M_0\) and the half-threshold
   specialization are immediate.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Common retained residual for many failed flow screens]
   \label{cor:common-retained-failed-flow-panel}
   Let \(\mathcal I\) be a common finite source set with source weights
   \(\nu_i\ge0\).  For each \(j\in J_0\), let
   \((B_j,E_j,C_j)\) be a fractional opened-support source system as in
   \cref{cor:fractional-opened-support-flow-lp}, with the same left vertex set
   \(\mathcal I\), with normalized source loads
   \[
      \frac{\mu_i^{(j)}}{C_j}=\nu_i
      \qquad(i\in\mathcal I),
      \tag{CRF1}
   \]
   and with clipped parameters \(K_j,\Theta_j\) and degrees \(d_{j,p}\).  Suppose
   that, for numbers \(L_j\ge0\),
   \[
      \widehat{\mathfrak S}_{B_j,E_j}(C_j)\le L_j
      \qquad(j\in J_0).
      \tag{CRF2}
   \]
   Then, for every choice \(0<\eta_j<1\), there is a common source subset
   \(I_\star\subseteq\mathcal I\) such that
   \[
      \sum_{i\in I_\star}\nu_i
      \ge
      \sum_{i\in\mathcal I}\nu_i
      -
      \sum_{j\in J_0}\frac{L_j}{\eta_j},
      \tag{CRF3}
   \]
   and, for every failed screen \(j\), its \(I_\star\)-neighborhood satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{p\in N_{E_j}(I_\star):\\
                      d_{j,p}>\Theta_j/(1-\eta_j)}}
      \left(d_{j,p}-\frac{\Theta_j}{1-\eta_j}\right)
      \le \frac{L_j}{1-\eta_j}.
      \tag{CRF4}
   \]

   In particular, if each screen is in a no-prefix residual and
   \(L_j=2K_j\Theta_j\), then with \(\eta_j=1/2\),
   \[
      \sum_{i\in I_\star}\nu_i
      \ge
      \sum_i\nu_i
      -
      \sum_{j\in J_0}4K_j\Theta_j,
      \tag{CRF5}
   \]
   while every retained neighborhood obeys
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{p\in N_{E_j}(I_\star):\\ d_{j,p}>2\Theta_j}}
      (d_{j,p}-2\Theta_j)
      \le4K_j\Theta_j .
      \tag{CRF6}
   \]

   Thus many build-time proposal families may be tested against the same source
   measure: failed fractional screens consume source mass only additively, and a
   surviving common residual is simultaneously tail-clipped for all of them.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{cor:source-retention-failed-fractional-flow} separately to each
   screen \(j\), obtaining a retained set \(I_j\subseteq\mathcal I\).  Define
   \(I_\star=\bigcap_{j\in J_0}I_j\).  By the union bound for the discarded
   source weights and \((SRF2)\),
   \[
      \sum_{i\notin I_\star}\nu_i
      \le
      \sum_{j\in J_0}\sum_{i\notin I_j}\nu_i
      \le
      \sum_{j\in J_0}\frac{L_j}{\eta_j},
   \]
   which proves \((CRF3)\).  Since \(I_\star\subseteq I_j\), we have
   \(N_{E_j}(I_\star)\subseteq N_{E_j}(I_j)\), so the tail bound \((CRF4)\)
   follows from \((SRF3)\) for record \(j\).  The half-threshold specialization
   is immediate.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Adaptive retained residual for sequential failed screens]
   \label{cor:adaptive-retained-failed-flow-sequence}
   Let \(I_0\) be a finite source set with weights \(\nu_i\ge0\).  For
   \(t=1,\ldots,T\), suppose that after seeing the previously retained set
   \(I_{t-1}\), preprocessing chooses a fractional opened-support source system
   \((B_t,E_t,C_t)\) whose left vertex set is \(I_{t-1}\), whose normalized
   source loads are
   \[
      \frac{\mu_i^{(t)}}{C_t}=\nu_i
      \qquad(i\in I_{t-1}),
      \tag{ARF1}
   \]
   and whose degrees and clipped parameters are \(d_{t,p}\), \(K_t\), and
   \(\Theta_t\).  Assume the chosen screen fails with
   \[
      \widehat{\mathfrak S}_{B_t,E_t}(C_t)\le L_t .
      \tag{ARF2}
   \]
   Then, for every \(0<\eta_t<1\), the retained sets may be chosen
   adaptively so that \(I_t\subseteq I_{t-1}\) and, for the final residual
   \(I_T\),
   \[
      \sum_{i\in I_T}\nu_i
      \ge
      \sum_{i\in I_0}\nu_i
      -
      \sum_{t=1}^T\frac{L_t}{\eta_t}.
      \tag{ARF3}
   \]
   Moreover every failed screen remains certified on the final residual:
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{p\in N_{E_t}(I_T):\\
                      d_{t,p}>\Theta_t/(1-\eta_t)}}
      \left(d_{t,p}-\frac{\Theta_t}{1-\eta_t}\right)
      \le \frac{L_t}{1-\eta_t}
      \qquad(t=1,\ldots,T).
      \tag{ARF4}
   \]

   In the no-prefix half-threshold case \(L_t=2K_t\Theta_t\),
   \(\eta_t=1/2\), this becomes
   \[
      \sum_{i\in I_T}\nu_i
      \ge
      \sum_{i\in I_0}\nu_i
      -
      \sum_{t=1}^T4K_t\Theta_t,
      \tag{ARF5}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{p\in N_{E_t}(I_T):\\ d_{t,p}>2\Theta_t}}
      (d_{t,p}-2\Theta_t)
      \le4K_t\Theta_t
      \qquad(t=1,\ldots,T).
      \tag{ARF6}
   \]

   Thus the build phase may use failed fractional-flow screens as adaptive
   advice.  If no positive screen fires, the only loss is the displayed
   additive source budget, and the final source residual is simultaneously
   clipped for every screen that was tried.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   At step \(t\), apply
   \cref{cor:source-retention-failed-fractional-flow} to the source system on
   \(I_{t-1}\), and let \(I_t\) be the returned retained subset.  Then
   \[
      \sum_{i\in I_t}\nu_i
      \ge
      \sum_{i\in I_{t-1}}\nu_i-\frac{L_t}{\eta_t}.
   \]
   Summing these inequalities over \(t\) gives \((ARF3)\).  The same application
   gives the raised clipped-tail bound on \(N_{E_t}(I_t)\).  Since
   \(I_T\subseteq I_t\), the final neighborhood is smaller:
   \(N_{E_t}(I_T)\subseteq N_{E_t}(I_t)\), so \((ARF4)\) follows.  The
   half-threshold specialization is immediate.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Value-retained adaptive failed-screen normal form]
   \label{cor:value-retained-adaptive-failed-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:adaptive-retained-failed-flow-sequence}, and write
   \[
      V_0=\sum_{i\in I_0}\nu_i,
      \qquad
      \Delta_T=\sum_{t=1}^T\frac{L_t}{\eta_t}.
      \tag{VAF1}
   \]
   If all \(T\) screens fail, then the final retained residual satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{i\in I_T}\nu_i\ge V_0-\Delta_T .
      \tag{VAF2}
   \]
   In particular, if \(\Delta_T\le\varepsilon V_0\), then \(I_T\) retains
   at least a \((1-\varepsilon)\)-fraction of the initial source value, while
   still satisfying every raised tail cap \((ARF4)\).

   More generally, fix a target residual value \(\Lambda_{\rm rem}\ge0\).  For
   a concrete failed transcript, interpret \(N_{E_t}(J)\) for an arbitrary
   \(J\subseteq I_0\) as \(N_{E_t}(J\cap I_{t-1})\), since screen \(t\) is only
   defined on the left set \(I_{t-1}\).  If
   \[
      \Delta_T\le V_0-\Lambda_{\rm rem},
      \tag{VAF3}
   \]
   and no subset \(J\subseteq I_0\) with
   \(\sum_{i\in J}\nu_i\ge\Lambda_{\rm rem}\) satisfies all of the transcript
   caps
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{p\in N_{E_t}(J):\\
                      d_{t,p}>\Theta_t/(1-\eta_t)}}
      \left(d_{t,p}-\frac{\Theta_t}{1-\eta_t}\right)
      \le \frac{L_t}{1-\eta_t}
      \qquad(t=1,\ldots,T),
      \tag{VAF4}
   \]
   then not all \(T\) screens can have failed.

   In the no-prefix half-threshold specialization \(L_t=2K_t\Theta_t\) and
   \(\eta_t=1/2\), the value loss is
   \[
      \Delta_T=\sum_{t=1}^T4K_t\Theta_t .
      \tag{VAF5}
   \]
   If a transcript-exhaustion certificate forces some screen not to fail in
   this specialization, then
   \(\widehat{\mathfrak S}_{B_t,E_t}(C_t)>2K_t\Theta_t\), so
   \cref{cor:fractional-opened-support-flow-lp} exposes a positive shared
   top-prefix column.

   Thus an adaptive build-time proposal search may spend only this declared
   value budget on failed fractional-flow screens.  Unless that budget has paid
   for the obstruction value, a high-value residual remains and is
   simultaneously clipped for every screen in the failed transcript.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The retained value bound \((VAF2)\) is exactly \((ARF3)\).  The
   \((1-\varepsilon)\)-statement follows by substituting
   \(\Delta_T\le\varepsilon V_0\), and the inherited tail caps are \((ARF4)\).

   For the transcript-exhaustion statement, assume for contradiction that all
   screens fail.  Then
   \cref{cor:adaptive-retained-failed-flow-sequence} returns a nested final
   residual \(I_T\).  Since \(I_T\subseteq I_{t-1}\) for every \(t\), the
   convention for \(N_{E_t}(J)\) agrees with the actual neighborhoods when
   \(J=I_T\).  By \((VAF2)\) and \((VAF3)\),
   \[
      \sum_{i\in I_T}\nu_i\ge\Lambda_{\rm rem},
   \]
   while \((ARF4)\) gives all inequalities in \((VAF4)\).  This contradicts the
   claimed absence of such a subset \(J\).  The half-threshold formula is
   \((ARF5)\) written as a value loss.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Template-complete shared-cover obstruction]
   \label{cor:template-complete-shared-cover-obstruction}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-shared-integrated-cover-dual} and
   \cref{cor:shared-top-prefix-reduced-cost-compiler}.  Fix a feasible atomized
   high-correlation dual \(y\), a target \(\Lambda\ge0\), and a finite family
   \(\mathcal B\) of certified shared prefix templates.  Let
   \(\mathcal R_{\mathcal B}\) be the finite record universe consisting of every
   admissible prefix record
   \[
      h_{U,a}=\sum_{p\in U}h_{B,p,a},
      \qquad
      P_U=P_B(K),
      \qquad
      B\in\mathcal B,\ K\in\mathcal K_B,\ |U|=K,
      \tag{TCO1}
   \]
   and let \(\Psi_{\mathcal B}(y)\) be the value of the shared-cover program
   \((SIC2)\) restricted to \(\mathcal R_{\mathcal B}\).

   If \(\Psi_{\mathcal B}(y)>\Lambda\), then there is a vector \(u\) such that
   \[
      0\le u_a\le\ell_a^\Sigma(y)
      \qquad(a\in\mathcal A_\pi),
      \tag{TCO2}
   \]
   \[
      \sum_ab_au_a>\Lambda,
      \tag{TCO3}
   \]
   and, for every \(B\in\mathcal B\) and \(K\in\mathcal K_B\), if
   \(p_1,p_2,\ldots\) are ordered by the shared degree
   \(d_B^u(p)=\sum_ah_{B,p,a}u_a\), then
   \[
      \sum_{j\le K}d_B^u(p_j)\le2P_B(K).
      \tag{TCO4}
   \]
   Conversely, any \(u\) satisfying \((TCO2)\)--\((TCO4)\) is a feasible dual
   certificate proving \(\Psi_{\mathcal B}(y)>\Lambda\).

   Moreover, if the prices of each template have the form
   \[
      P_B(K)=\psi_B\left(A_BK^{\rho_B}+\zeta_BK^{1+\rho_B}\right),
      \qquad 0<\rho_B<1,
      \tag{TCO5}
   \]
   and the available cardinalities of \(B\) are \(b_B\)-dense from below, then
   every obstruction \(u\) above satisfies the clipped tail cap of
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-clipped-shared-tail} for every \(B\in\mathcal B\).

   Thus failure of a constant-fraction shared integrated cover has an exact
   finite normal form: one no-prefix dual \(u\) with large value and with all
   certified containers obeying their top-prefix, equivalently clipped-tail,
   envelopes.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply finite LP duality to \((SIC2)\) with the record set
   \(\mathcal R_{\mathcal B}\).  If
   \(\Psi_{\mathcal B}(y)>\Lambda\), an optimal dual \(u\) satisfies
   \((TCO2)\), has objective value \((TCO3)\), and obeys every record constraint
   \[
      \sum_ah_{U,a}u_a\le2P_U .
      \tag{TCO6}
   \]
   For fixed \(B\) and \(K\), the top \(K\) points maximize
   \(\sum_{p\in U}d_B^u(p)\) among all \(K\)-subsets of \(W_B\).  Applying
   \((TCO6)\) to this top prefix gives \((TCO4)\).

   Conversely, \((TCO4)\) implies \((TCO6)\) for every \(K\)-subset \(U\subseteq
   W_B\), again by top-prefix maximality.  Together with \((TCO2)\), this makes
   \(u\) feasible for the restricted dual \((SIC3)\).  Its objective value is
   larger than \(\Lambda\), so weak duality gives
   \(\Psi_{\mathcal B}(y)>\Lambda\).

   Under \((TCO5)\) and cardinality-net closure, \((TCO4)\) says exactly that no
   available shared top prefix of \(B\) has positive reduced cost.  Therefore
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-clipped-shared-tail} gives the clipped tail cap for
   each template.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Template-search form of the shared-integrated target]
   \label{cor:template-search-shared-integrated-target}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:child-panel-shared-integrated-endpoint}.  Suppose that, after the
   sponsor/generated-prefix, low-correlation, and verified dense-prefix exits
   fail, the surviving residual admits one split profile \(\pi\) with
   \[
      D_\pi=(B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo})_+>0,
      \qquad
      B_\pi^{\rm hi}\le n^{K_{\rm dyn}}D_\pi .
      \tag{TCE1}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      \varepsilon_\pi=\min\{1,1/(4n^{K_{\rm dyn}})\},
      \tag{TCE2}
   \]
   and use the dyadic layer-cake cuts associated with this truncation.
   For every feasible atomized high-correlation dual \(y\) for this profile,
   suppose preprocessing may choose a finite template family
   \(\mathcal B_y\), all of whose positive top-prefix records lie in
   \(\mathcal Z_\star\), and run the template-complete shared-cover search of
   \cref{cor:template-complete-shared-cover-obstruction} with target
   \[
      \Lambda_\pi=D_\pi/4 .
      \tag{TCE3}
   \]
   Assume that the search always returns one of the following two certified
   outcomes:
   \[
      \Psi_{\mathcal B_y}(y)\le D_\pi/4,
      \tag{TCE4}
   \]
   or a verified positive shared top-prefix column in \(\mathcal Z_\star\).
   Then the positive shared-panel separator \((SPP1)\) holds at every node, and
   hence
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,\qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   Equivalently, by
   \cref{cor:template-complete-shared-cover-obstruction}, the remaining
   geometric theorem may be stated as ruling out every obstruction
   \((TCO2)\)--\((TCO4)\) of value \(>D_\pi/4\), or making one certified
   container violate its clipped tail cap.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a resident node and a normalized exact-signature price system.  If one of
   the explicit exits fires, it gives \((SPP1)\) as in
   \cref{cor:child-panel-shared-integrated-endpoint}.  Otherwise fix the profile
   \(\pi\).  If the template search for some feasible dual \(y\) returns a
   positive top-prefix column, this column belongs to \(\mathcal Z_\star\), so
   \((SPP1)\) holds.

   It remains to consider the case in which no such positive column fires.  Then
   \((TCE4)\) holds for every feasible atomized high-correlation dual \(y\).
   By \((TCE1)\),
   \(\varepsilon_\pi B_\pi^{\rm hi}\le D_\pi/4\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:finite-shared-integrated-cover-dual} to the feasible cover of value
   at most \(D_\pi/4\) gives, for every feasible \(y\),
   \[
      \sum_ab_ay_a
      \le
      \varepsilon_\pi B_\pi^{\rm hi}+2(D_\pi/4)
      \le 3D_\pi/4 .
      \tag{TCE5}
   \]
   Taking the supremum over atomized high-correlation duals yields
   \(\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}<D_\pi\).  Hence
   \(B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo}-\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}>0\), and
   \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope} exposes a positive
   low-correlation shared-panel record or a positive dense prefix in
   \(\mathcal Z_\star\).  Thus \((SPP1)\) holds for the fixed price system.
   Since the node and price system were arbitrary,
   \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint} gives the displayed
   bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Transport form of the template obstruction target]
   \label{cor:transport-template-obstruction-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:template-search-shared-integrated-target}, except replace the
   asserted template-search outcome by the following obstruction-separation
   condition.  For every feasible atomized high-correlation dual \(y\),
   preprocessing may choose a finite template family \(\mathcal B_y\) whose
   positive top-prefix records lie in \(\mathcal Z_\star\), whose available
   cardinalities are dense from below, and whose prices have the form
   \[
      P_B(K)=\psi_B\left(A_BK^{\rho_B}+\zeta_BK^{1+\rho_B}\right),
      \qquad 0<\rho_B<1 .
      \tag{TOE1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \Psi_{\mathcal B_y}(y)>D_\pi/4,
      \tag{TOE2}
   \]
   then every exact no-prefix dual obstruction \(u\) supplied by
   \cref{cor:template-complete-shared-cover-obstruction} admits a transported
   clipped-tail panel satisfying \((TSP1)\)--\((TSP2)\), with all resulting
   top-prefix records contained in \(\mathcal Z_\star\).

   Then the positive shared-panel separator \((SPP1)\) holds at every node, and
   hence
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,\qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   Thus the remaining geometric theorem can be stated entirely in transport
   form: a high-value no-prefix dual must move enough of its mass into one
   certified smaller-radius subset, with bounded congestion, to beat the affine
   clipped-tail threshold.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix \(y\).  If \(\Psi_{\mathcal B_y}(y)\le D_\pi/4\), the first outcome of
   \cref{cor:template-search-shared-integrated-target} holds.  Otherwise
   \(\Psi_{\mathcal B_y}(y)>D_\pi/4\), so
   \cref{cor:template-complete-shared-cover-obstruction} gives an exact
   no-prefix dual obstruction \(u\) satisfying \((TCO2)\)--\((TCO4)\) with value
   \(>D_\pi/4\).  By hypothesis this obstruction has a transported clipped-tail
   panel with positive surplus.  Applying
   \cref{cor:transported-clipped-tail-panel-separator} yields a positive shared
   top-prefix column in \(\mathcal Z_\star\).  Hence, for every \(y\), the
   template search has one of the two certified outcomes required by
   \cref{cor:template-search-shared-integrated-target}.  That corollary gives
   \((SPP1)\) at every node and the displayed bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Flow-value form of the template obstruction target]
   \label{cor:flow-value-template-obstruction-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:transport-template-obstruction-endpoint}.  Replace the transported
   panel hypothesis by the following max-flow hypothesis.  Whenever
   \(\Psi_{\mathcal B_y}(y)>D_\pi/4\) and
   \cref{cor:template-complete-shared-cover-obstruction} supplies an exact
   no-prefix dual obstruction \(u\), preprocessing can certify a finite panel of
   flow records of the form in
   \cref{lem:flow-value-clipped-tail-screen}, with all template top-prefix
   records contained in \(\mathcal Z_\star\), such that
   \[
      \sum_j\lambda_j
      \left(
         \frac{\Phi_{B_j,U_j}(C_j)}{C_j}
         -
         \bigl(|U_j|+2K_{B_j}^\natural\bigr)
         \Theta_{B_j}^{\rm net}
      \right)>0 .
      \tag{FVO1}
   \]
   Then the positive shared-panel separator \((SPP1)\) holds at every node, and
   hence
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,\qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   Equivalently, if this max-flow condition fails for a proposed record, the
   remaining obstruction is the explicit finite cut \((CTV6)\).  The geometric
   proof target can therefore be phrased as: every high-value no-prefix dual has
   one certified flow panel whose value beats the affine clipped-tail prices, or
   it exposes a localized source/capacity cut to be merged by a richer template.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the restricted cover value is at most \(D_\pi/4\), the template-search
   outcome already holds.  Otherwise take the exact obstruction \(u\).  The
   positive flow-value panel \((FVO1)\) and
   \cref{lem:flow-value-clipped-tail-screen} expose a positive shared top-prefix
   column in \(\mathcal Z_\star\).  Thus the hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:transport-template-obstruction-endpoint} are satisfied, and that
   corollary gives \((SPP1)\) and the displayed bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Opened-support form of the template obstruction target]
   \label{cor:opened-support-template-obstruction-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:flow-value-template-obstruction-endpoint}.  Replace the fixed-subset
   max-flow hypothesis \((FVO1)\) by the following support-penalized hypothesis.
   Whenever \(\Psi_{\mathcal B_y}(y)>D_\pi/4\) and
   \cref{cor:template-complete-shared-cover-obstruction} supplies an exact
   no-prefix dual obstruction \(u\), preprocessing can certify a finite panel of
   source systems with nonnegative weights \(\lambda_j\), of the form in
   \cref{cor:opened-support-flow-screen}, with all template top-prefix records
   contained in \(\mathcal Z_\star\), such that
   \[
      \sum_j\lambda_j
      \left(
         \mathfrak S_{B_j,E_j}(C_j)
         -
         2K_{B_j}^\natural\Theta_{B_j}^{\rm net}
      \right)>0 .
      \tag{OSFT1}
   \]
   Then the positive shared-panel separator \((SPP1)\) holds at every node, and
   hence
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,\qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   Equivalently, the branch-selection score may be taken to be opened-support
   flow surplus.  The verifier can accept either an exact maximizer in
   \((OSFS1)\) or any one-sided lower certificate consisting of a support \(S\)
   and a feasible flow whose value makes the corresponding bracket in
   \((OSFT1)\) positive.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the restricted cover value is at most \(D_\pi/4\), the template-search
   outcome of \cref{cor:template-search-shared-integrated-target} already holds.
   Otherwise take the exact no-prefix obstruction \(u\).  The positive
   opened-support panel \((OSFT1)\) and
   \cref{cor:opened-support-flow-screen} expose a positive shared top-prefix
   column in \(\mathcal Z_\star\).  Thus, for every feasible dual \(y\), the
   template search either has a cover of value at most \(D_\pi/4\) or finds a
   verified positive shared top-prefix column.  Applying
   \cref{cor:template-search-shared-integrated-target} gives \((SPP1)\) and the
   displayed query and storage bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fractional opened-support template obstruction endpoint]
   \label{cor:fractional-opened-support-template-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:opened-support-template-obstruction-endpoint}.  Replace the
   opened-support hypothesis \((OSFT1)\) by the following fractional LP
   hypothesis.  Whenever \(\Psi_{\mathcal B_y}(y)>D_\pi/4\) and
   \cref{cor:template-complete-shared-cover-obstruction} supplies an exact
   no-prefix dual obstruction \(u\), preprocessing can certify a finite panel of
   fractional source systems with nonnegative weights \(\lambda_j\), of the form
   in \cref{cor:fractional-opened-support-flow-lp}, with all template
   top-prefix records contained in \(\mathcal Z_\star\), such that
   \[
      \sum_j\lambda_j
      \left(
         \widehat{\mathfrak S}_{B_j,E_j}(C_j)
         -
         2K_{B_j}^\natural\Theta_{B_j}^{\rm net}
      \right)>0 .
      \tag{FOT1}
   \]
   Then the positive shared-panel separator \((SPP1)\) holds at every node, and
   hence
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,\qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   In particular, the current verifier-facing obstruction target may be stated
   as a finite LP separation problem: either the fractional opened-support LP
   has positive surplus above the clipped-tail overhead, or its dual
   \((FOF3)\) is an explicit source/point price certificate blocking that
   proposed source system.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the restricted cover value is at most \(D_\pi/4\), the template-search
   outcome of \cref{cor:template-search-shared-integrated-target} already holds.
   Otherwise take the exact no-prefix obstruction \(u\).  The positive
   fractional panel \((FOT1)\) and
   \cref{cor:fractional-opened-support-flow-lp} expose a positive shared
   top-prefix column in \(\mathcal Z_\star\).  Hence every feasible dual \(y\)
   has one of the two outcomes required by
   \cref{cor:template-search-shared-integrated-target}, which gives \((SPP1)\)
   and the displayed bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Adaptive fractional-flow exhaustion endpoint]
   \label{cor:adaptive-fractional-flow-exhaustion-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:fractional-opened-support-template-endpoint}.  Replace the
   fractional-panel hypothesis \((FOT1)\) by the following adaptive
   exhaustion condition.

   Whenever \(\Psi_{\mathcal B_y}(y)>D_\pi/4\) and
   \cref{cor:template-complete-shared-cover-obstruction} supplies an exact
   no-prefix dual obstruction \(u\), preprocessing has a finite adaptive
   proposal rule.  The rule starts from a finite source set \(I_0\) with weights
   \(\nu_i\ge0\).  After a failed prefix has retained \(I_{t-1}\), it proposes a
   fractional opened-support source system \((B_t,E_t,C_t)\), with left set
   \(I_{t-1}\), whose normalized source loads satisfy
   \[
      \frac{\mu_i^{(t)}}{C_t}=\nu_i
      \qquad(i\in I_{t-1}),
      \tag{AFF1}
   \]
   and whose template top-prefix records all lie in \(\mathcal Z_\star\).  Put
   \[
      K_t=K_{B_t}^\natural,
      \qquad
      \Theta_t=\Theta_{B_t}^{\rm net}.
      \tag{AFF2}
   \]

   The proposal rule is called value-complete if every possible all-failed
   transcript has a certified target \(\Lambda_{\rm rem}\ge0\) such that, with
   \[
      V_0=\sum_{i\in I_0}\nu_i,
      \qquad
      \Delta_T=\sum_{t=1}^T4K_t\Theta_t,
      \tag{AFF3}
   \]
   one has
   \[
      \Delta_T\le V_0-\Lambda_{\rm rem},
      \tag{AFF4}
   \]
   and there is no subset \(J\subseteq I_0\) with
   \[
      \sum_{i\in J}\nu_i\ge\Lambda_{\rm rem}
      \tag{AFF5}
   \]
   satisfying all transcript tail caps
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{p\in N_{E_t}(J\cap I_{t-1}):\\ d_{t,p}>2\Theta_t}}
      (d_{t,p}-2\Theta_t)
      \le4K_t\Theta_t
      \qquad(t=1,\ldots,T).
      \tag{AFF6}
   \]

   If such a value-complete adaptive proposal rule exists for every exact
   obstruction \(u\), then the positive shared-panel separator \((SPP1)\) holds
   at every node, and hence
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,\qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   Equivalently, the remaining build-time theorem may be stated as finite
   transcript exhaustion: for every high-value no-prefix obstruction, adaptive
   proposal search must either find a half-threshold fractional flow screen or
   prove that no high-value residual can satisfy all failed-screen caps.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix \(y\) and suppose first that
   \(\Psi_{\mathcal B_y}(y)\le D_\pi/4\).  Then the first outcome of
   \cref{cor:template-search-shared-integrated-target} holds.  Otherwise take
   the exact obstruction \(u\) supplied by
   \cref{cor:template-complete-shared-cover-obstruction}, and run the adaptive
   proposal rule.

   If some proposed screen has
   \[
      \widehat{\mathfrak S}_{B_t,E_t}(C_t)>2K_t\Theta_t,
   \]
   then \cref{cor:fractional-opened-support-flow-lp} exposes a positive shared
   top-prefix column in \(\mathcal Z_\star\).  This is the second outcome
   required by \cref{cor:template-search-shared-integrated-target}.

   It remains to rule out the case in which every proposed screen fails:
   \[
      \widehat{\mathfrak S}_{B_t,E_t}(C_t)\le2K_t\Theta_t
      \qquad(t=1,\ldots,T).
   \]
   Apply \cref{cor:value-retained-adaptive-failed-screen} with
   \(L_t=2K_t\Theta_t\) and \(\eta_t=1/2\).  The value-completeness certificate
   gives \((AFF4)\) and asserts that no subset satisfying \((AFF5)\)--\((AFF6)\)
   exists.  But \cref{cor:value-retained-adaptive-failed-screen} says that, if
   all screens failed, the final retained residual \(I_T\) would have value at
   least \(\Lambda_{\rm rem}\) and would satisfy exactly the caps \((AFF6)\).
   This contradiction shows that not all screens fail.  Therefore a positive
   fractional opened-support screen exists.

   Thus every feasible dual \(y\) has either a restricted cover of value at most
   \(D_\pi/4\) or a verified positive top-prefix column in
   \(\mathcal Z_\star\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:template-search-shared-integrated-target} gives \((SPP1)\) and the
   displayed query and storage bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Obstruction-sourced adaptive flow exhaustion]
   \label{cor:obstruction-sourced-flow-exhaustion}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:adaptive-fractional-flow-exhaustion-endpoint}.  It is enough to
   verify the adaptive exhaustion condition with the source measure forced by
   the no-prefix dual itself.  Namely, whenever
   \(\Psi_{\mathcal B_y}(y)>D_\pi/4\) and
   \cref{cor:template-complete-shared-cover-obstruction} returns an exact
   obstruction \(u\), put
   \[
      I_0(u)=\{a\in\mathcal A_\pi:\ b_au_a>0\},
      \qquad
      \nu_a=b_au_a,
      \qquad
      V(u)=\sum_ab_au_a .
      \tag{OSX1}
   \]
   Suppose preprocessing has a finite adaptive proposal rule of the form used
   in \cref{cor:adaptive-fractional-flow-exhaustion-endpoint}, with initial
   source set \(I_0(u)\) and weights \(\nu_a\), such that every possible
   all-failed transcript satisfies
   \[
      \Delta_T=\sum_{t=1}^T4K_t\Theta_t\le \frac{V(u)}2,
      \tag{OSX2}
   \]
   and there is no subset \(J\subseteq I_0(u)\) with
   \[
      \sum_{a\in J}b_au_a\ge \frac{V(u)}2
      \tag{OSX3}
   \]
   satisfying all transcript caps
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{p\in N_{E_t}(J\cap I_{t-1}):\\ d_{t,p}>2\Theta_t}}
      (d_{t,p}-2\Theta_t)
      \le4K_t\Theta_t
      \qquad(t=1,\ldots,T).
      \tag{OSX4}
   \]
   Then the positive shared-panel separator \((SPP1)\) holds at every node, and
   hence
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,\qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   Since \(V(u)>D_\pi/4\) by \((TCO3)\), an all-failed transcript would have to
   leave a residual carrying more than \(D_\pi/8\) of the original shared-cover
   obstruction.  Thus the remaining geometric theorem can be tested directly on
   atom subsets of the exposed no-prefix dual: either a proposed flow screen
   fires, or no half-value atom residual can obey the transcript's tail caps.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For each obstruction \(u\), take the source set and weights in
   \((OSX1)\), and set
   \[
      \Lambda_{\rm rem}=V(u)/2 .
   \]
   The condition \((OSX2)\) is exactly \((AFF4)\), and
   \((OSX3)\)--\((OSX4)\) are \((AFF5)\)--\((AFF6)\) for this source measure.
   Therefore the value-completeness hypothesis of
   \cref{cor:adaptive-fractional-flow-exhaustion-endpoint} holds.  That
   corollary gives \((SPP1)\) and the displayed bounds.  The final observation
   is the inequality \(V(u)>D_\pi/4\) from \((TCO3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Failed-transcript residual LP certificate]
   \label{cor:failed-transcript-residual-lp}
   Fix one all-failed transcript in the setting of
   \cref{cor:obstruction-sourced-flow-exhaustion}, with initial source set
   \(I_0\), source weights \(\nu_i\ge0\), retained prefixes \(I_{t-1}\), and
   screens \((B_t,E_t,C_t)\).  Put
   \[
      P_t^+=\{p\in W_{B_t}:\ d_{t,p}>2\Theta_t\},
      \qquad
      c_{t,p}=d_{t,p}-2\Theta_t\quad(p\in P_t^+),
      \tag{TRL1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      B_t^{\rm tail}=4K_t\Theta_t .
      \tag{TRL2}
   \]
   Define the fractional residual value of the transcript by the finite LP
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \mathfrak R_{\rm tr}(\nu)=\max
      & \displaystyle \sum_{i\in I_0}\nu_i z_i \\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & 0\le z_i\le1\qquad(i\in I_0),\\[0.4em]
      & y_{t,p}\ge0\qquad(t=1,\ldots,T,\ p\in P_t^+),\\[0.4em]
      & z_i\le y_{t,p}
        \qquad(i\in I_{t-1},\ (i,p)\in E_t,\ p\in P_t^+),\\[0.4em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{p\in P_t^+}c_{t,p}y_{t,p}\le B_t^{\rm tail}
        \qquad(t=1,\ldots,T).
   \end{array}
      \tag{TRL3}
   \]
   Every integral residual \(J\subseteq I_0\) satisfying all transcript caps
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{p\in N_{E_t}(J\cap I_{t-1}):\\ p\in P_t^+}}c_{t,p}
      \le B_t^{\rm tail}
      \qquad(t=1,\ldots,T)
      \tag{TRL4}
   \]
   has value at most \(\mathfrak R_{\rm tr}(\nu)\).  Hence, if
   \[
      \mathfrak R_{\rm tr}(\nu)<\Lambda_{\rm rem},
      \tag{TRL5}
   \]
   then no residual subset of source value at least \(\Lambda_{\rm rem}\)
   satisfies the failed transcript caps.

   Moreover finite LP duality gives the exact certificate
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \mathfrak R_{\rm tr}(\nu)=\min
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{t=1}^T B_t^{\rm tail}\lambda_t+\sum_{i\in I_0}\sigma_i\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        \sigma_i+
        \sum_{\substack{t:\ i\in I_{t-1}}}
        \sum_{\substack{p\in P_t^+:\\ (i,p)\in E_t}}
        \alpha_{t,i,p}
        \ge \nu_i
        \qquad(i\in I_0),\\[1.0em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{\substack{i\in I_{t-1}:\\ (i,p)\in E_t}}
        \alpha_{t,i,p}
        \le \lambda_t c_{t,p}
        \qquad(t=1,\ldots,T,\ p\in P_t^+),\\[1.0em]
      & \lambda_t,\sigma_i,\alpha_{t,i,p}\ge0 .
   \end{array}
      \tag{TRL6}
   \]
   Thus a failed transcript may be exhausted by a finite weighted tail-budget
   certificate: source value is either paid directly by \(\sigma_i\), or routed
   through failed-screen neighborhoods into the priced tail capacities
   \(\lambda_t c_{t,p}\).

   In particular, in the obstruction-sourced setting of
   \cref{cor:obstruction-sourced-flow-exhaustion}, condition \((OSX3)\)--\((OSX4)\)
   follows from the checkable sufficient condition
   \[
      \mathfrak R_{\rm tr}\bigl((b_a u_a)_a\bigr)
      <\frac12\sum_a b_a u_a .
      \tag{TRL7}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(J\subseteq I_0\) satisfies \((TRL4)\), set
   \(z_i=\mathbf 1_{\{i\in J\}}\) and
   \[
      y_{t,p}=\mathbf 1_{\{p\in N_{E_t}(J\cap I_{t-1})\}}
      \qquad(p\in P_t^+).
   \]
   The edge constraints in \((TRL3)\) hold by definition of the neighborhood,
   and the tail constraints are exactly \((TRL4)\).  Therefore the integral
   residual value \(\sum_{i\in J}\nu_i\) is bounded by
   \(\mathfrak R_{\rm tr}(\nu)\), proving \((TRL5)\).

   To derive the dual, assign multipliers \(\alpha_{t,i,p}\ge0\) to the
   constraints \(z_i-y_{t,p}\le0\), multipliers \(\lambda_t\ge0\) to the tail
   constraints, and multipliers \(\sigma_i\ge0\) to \(z_i\le1\).  The dual
   objective is the first line of \((TRL6)\).  The coefficient of \(z_i\) gives
   the source-cover constraint, and the coefficient of \(y_{t,p}\) gives
   \[
      \lambda_t c_{t,p}-
      \sum_{i\in I_{t-1}:\ (i,p)\in E_t}\alpha_{t,i,p}\ge0 .
   \]
   This is exactly \((TRL6)\).  Strong duality applies because the finite primal
   is feasible and bounded.  Finally, \((TRL7)\) is \((TRL5)\) with the
   obstruction-sourced weights and \(\Lambda_{\rm rem}=V(u)/2\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fully fractional failed-transcript accounting]
   \label{cor:fractional-failed-transcript-accounting}
   The failed-transcript LP is not merely an integral residual relaxation; it is
   also the direct accounting state for a fractional failed-screen process.  Let
   \(I_0\) be a finite source set with weights \(\nu_i\ge0\), and start with
   intensities \(z_i^{(0)}=1\).  At step \(t\), after the previous failed
   screens have produced intensities \(0\le z_i^{(t-1)}\le1\), let
   \(I_{t-1}^+=\{i:z_i^{(t-1)}>0\}\).  Suppose preprocessing proposes a
   fractional opened-support source system \((B_t,E_t,C_t)\) with left set
   \(I_{t-1}^+\), normalized source loads
   \[
      \frac{\mu_i^{(t)}}{C_t}=\nu_i z_i^{(t-1)}
      \qquad(i\in I_{t-1}^+),
      \tag{FFA1}
   \]
   degrees \(d_{t,p}\), and clipped parameters \(K_t,\Theta_t\).  If the screen
   fails at the half-threshold value
   \[
      \widehat{\mathfrak S}_{B_t,E_t}(C_t)\le2K_t\Theta_t,
      \tag{FFA2}
   \]
   then one may choose \(z^{(t)}\) with \(0\le z^{(t)}\le z^{(t-1)}\) such that
   \[
      \sum_i\nu_i\bigl(z_i^{(t-1)}-z_i^{(t)}\bigr)
      \le4K_t\Theta_t ,
      \tag{FFA3}
   \]
   and, writing
   \[
      P_t^+=\{p\in W_{B_t}:d_{t,p}>2\Theta_t\},
      \qquad c_{t,p}=d_{t,p}-2\Theta_t,
      \tag{FFA4}
   \]
   there are numbers \(y_{t,p}\ge0\) satisfying
   \[
      z_i^{(t)}\le y_{t,p}
      \qquad(i\in I_{t-1}^+,\ (i,p)\in E_t,\ p\in P_t^+),
      \tag{FFA5}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{p\in P_t^+}c_{t,p}y_{t,p}\le4K_t\Theta_t .
      \tag{FFA6}
   \]

   Consequently, for any all-failed fractional transcript, the final intensity
   vector \(z^{(T)}\) is feasible for the residual LP
   \(\mathfrak R_{\rm tr}(\nu)\) of
   \cref{cor:failed-transcript-residual-lp}, with retained prefixes
   \(I_{t-1}=I_{t-1}^+\), and
   \[
      \mathfrak R_{\rm tr}(\nu)
      \ge
      \sum_i\nu_i z_i^{(T)}
      \ge
      \sum_i\nu_i-\sum_{t=1}^T4K_t\Theta_t .
      \tag{FFA7}
   \]
   Hence, if a proposed all-failed transcript satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{t=1}^T4K_t\Theta_t
      \le
      \sum_i\nu_i-\Lambda_{\rm rem}
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      \mathfrak R_{\rm tr}(\nu)<\Lambda_{\rm rem},
      \tag{FFA8}
   \]
   then not all screens in the transcript can fail.  Some screen has
   \(\widehat{\mathfrak S}_{B_t,E_t}(C_t)>2K_t\Theta_t\), and
   \cref{cor:fractional-opened-support-flow-lp} exposes a positive shared
   top-prefix column.

   Thus the adaptive branching score may be made fully fractional: failed
   screens shrink source intensities by their own dual prices, while the
   residual LP is the finite certificate that no high-value fractional source
   state remains.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix one failed step and abbreviate
   \(L=2K_t\Theta_t\), \(\Theta=\Theta_t\), \(K=K_t\).  By the dual formula
   \((FOF3)\), choose feasible dual prices \(\alpha_i,\beta_p\ge0\) with
   \[
      \sum_i\nu_i z_i^{(t-1)}\alpha_i
      +
      \sum_{p\in W_{B_t}}(d_{t,p}\beta_p-\Theta)_+
      \le L .
      \tag{FFA9}
   \]
   Define the next source intensities by
   \[
      z_i^{(t)}=
      z_i^{(t-1)}(1-2\alpha_i)_+
      \qquad(i\in I_{t-1}^+),
      \tag{FFA10}
   \]
   and \(z_i^{(t)}=0\) outside \(I_{t-1}^+\).  Since
   \(1-(1-2\alpha_i)_+\le2\alpha_i\),
   \[
      \sum_i\nu_i(z_i^{(t-1)}-z_i^{(t)})
      \le
      2\sum_i\nu_i z_i^{(t-1)}\alpha_i
      \le2L=4K\Theta ,
   \]
   proving \((FFA3)\).

   If \(z_i^{(t)}>0\), then \(\alpha_i<1/2\).  For every adjacent point \(p\),
   the dual constraint \(\alpha_i+\beta_p\ge1\) gives \(\beta_p>1/2\).  Hence,
   on the neighborhood
   \[
      P_{\rm lo}=\{p:\exists i\in I_{t-1}^+,\ z_i^{(t)}>0,\ (i,p)\in E_t\},
   \]
   one has
   \[
      (d_{t,p}-2\Theta)_+
      \le2(d_{t,p}\beta_p-\Theta)_+ .
   \]
   Therefore
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{p\in P_{\rm lo}:\\ d_{t,p}>2\Theta}}
      (d_{t,p}-2\Theta)
      \le
      2\sum_{p\in W_{B_t}}(d_{t,p}\beta_p-\Theta)_+
      \le2L=4K\Theta .
      \tag{FFA11}
   \]
   Set
   \[
      y_{t,p}=
      \max\{z_i^{(t)}:i\in I_{t-1}^+,\ (i,p)\in E_t\}
      \qquad(p\in P_t^+),
   \]
   with the maximum interpreted as \(0\) when there is no incident source.
   Then \(0\le y_{t,p}\le1\), \((FFA5)\) holds, and the support of \(y_t\) is
   contained in \(P_{\rm lo}\).  Thus \((FFA6)\) follows from \((FFA11)\).

   Iterate this construction over the failed transcript.  Since
   \(z^{(T)}\le z^{(t)}\) for every \(t\), the same \(y_{t,p}\), or the smaller
   maxima formed with \(z^{(T)}\), satisfy all edge constraints in
   \((TRL3)\).  The tail bounds are \((FFA6)\), and \(0\le z_i^{(T)}\le1\), so
   \(z^{(T)}\) is feasible for \(\mathfrak R_{\rm tr}(\nu)\).  Summing
   \((FFA3)\) over \(t\) gives \((FFA7)\).  Finally, \((FFA8)\) contradicts
   \((FFA7)\) if every screen fails; hence some screen has value above
   \(2K_t\Theta_t\), and \cref{cor:fractional-opened-support-flow-lp} gives the
   positive shared top-prefix column.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Capped residual LP continuation]
   \label{cor:capped-residual-lp-continuation}
   The fractional failed transcript can be driven by the residual LP itself,
   provided already-paid source mass is kept as an explicit cap.  For a cap
   vector \(0\le r_i\le1\), let
   \(\mathfrak R_{\rm tr}(\nu;r)\) be the capped variant of \((TRL3)\), obtained
   by replacing \(0\le z_i\le1\) with
   \[
      0\le z_i\le r_i\qquad(i\in I_0).
      \tag{CRL1}
   \]
   Its finite dual is the capped version of \((TRL6)\):
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \mathfrak R_{\rm tr}(\nu;r)=\min
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{t=1}^T B_t^{\rm tail}\lambda_t
        +\sum_{i\in I_0}r_i\sigma_i\\[0.8em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        \sigma_i+
        \sum_{\substack{t:\ i\in I_{t-1}}}
        \sum_{\substack{p\in P_t^+:\\ (i,p)\in E_t}}
        \alpha_{t,i,p}
        \ge \nu_i
        \qquad(i\in I_0),\\[1.0em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{\substack{i\in I_{t-1}:\\ (i,p)\in E_t}}
        \alpha_{t,i,p}
        \le \lambda_t c_{t,p}
        \qquad(t=1,\ldots,T,\ p\in P_t^+),\\[1.0em]
      & \lambda_t,\sigma_i,\alpha_{t,i,p}\ge0 .
   \end{array}
      \tag{CRL2}
   \]

   Now fix a partial failed transcript, a cap vector \(r\), and an optimal
   primal solution \(z^\star,y^\star\) for
   \(\mathfrak R_{\rm tr}(\nu;r)\).  Let
   \(I^+=\{i:z_i^\star>0\}\).  Suppose preprocessing proposes one more
   fractional opened-support screen \((B,E,C)\) with left set \(I^+\),
   normalized source loads
   \[
      \frac{\mu_i}{C}=\nu_i z_i^\star\qquad(i\in I^+),
      \tag{CRL3}
   \]
   degrees \(d_p\), and clipped parameters \(K,\Theta\).  If this proposed
   screen fails,
   \[
      \widehat{\mathfrak S}_{B,E}(C)\le2K\Theta,
      \tag{CRL4}
   \]
   then, after appending this screen to the transcript with tail set
   \(P^+=\{p:d_p>2\Theta\}\), there is a new cap vector \(r^+\) satisfying
   \(0\le r_i^+\le z_i^\star\le r_i\) and
   \[
      \mathfrak R_{\rm tr}^{+}(\nu;r^+)
      \ge
      \mathfrak R_{\rm tr}(\nu;r)-4K\Theta .
      \tag{CRL5}
   \]
   If instead \((CRL4)\) fails, then
   \cref{cor:fractional-opened-support-flow-lp} exposes a positive shared
   top-prefix column.

   Consequently, an adaptive rule may repeat the following entirely finite
   step: solve the current capped residual LP, use its optimal \(z^\star\) as
   the next source measure, and either materialize a positive screen or update
   the cap.  After an all-failed transcript with caps \(r^{(T)}\),
   \[
      \mathfrak R_T(\nu;r^{(T)})
      \ge
      \sum_i\nu_i-\sum_{t=1}^T4K_t\Theta_t .
      \tag{CRL6}
   \]
   Therefore, if the terminal capped dual certificate proves
   \[
      \mathfrak R_T(\nu;r^{(T)})<\Lambda_{\rm rem}
      \quad\text{while}\quad
      \sum_{t=1}^T4K_t\Theta_t
      \le
      \sum_i\nu_i-\Lambda_{\rm rem},
      \tag{CRL7}
   \]
   not all screens could have failed.

   The cap is essential: it prevents later residual LPs from resurrecting source
   mass that an earlier failed-screen dual has already paid for.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The capped dual \((CRL2)\) is the same calculation as \((TRL6)\), except
   that the multiplier \(\sigma_i\) for \(z_i\le r_i\) contributes
   \(r_i\sigma_i\) to the objective.

   Assume the new screen fails and choose feasible dual prices
   \(\alpha_i,\beta_p\) for its opened-support LP satisfying
   \[
      \sum_i\nu_i z_i^\star\alpha_i+
      \sum_{p\in W_B}(d_p\beta_p-\Theta)_+
      \le2K\Theta .
      \tag{CRL8}
   \]
   Define
   \[
      r_i^+=z_i^\star(1-2\alpha_i)_+
      \qquad(i\in I^+),
      \tag{CRL9}
   \]
   and \(r_i^+=0\) for \(i\notin I^+\).  Then \(0\le r_i^+\le z_i^\star\le r_i\),
   and
   \[
      \sum_i\nu_i(z_i^\star-r_i^+)
      \le
      2\sum_i\nu_i z_i^\star\alpha_i
      \le4K\Theta .
      \tag{CRL10}
   \]

   The old transcript constraints remain feasible because \(r^+\le z^\star\):
   keep the old \(y^\star\) variables, or decrease them if desired.  For the new
   screen, the same argument as in
   \cref{cor:fractional-failed-transcript-accounting} gives variables
   \[
      y_p^+=\max\{r_i^+:(i,p)\in E\}
      \qquad(p\in P^+)
   \]
   satisfying the new edge constraints and
   \[
      \sum_{p\in P^+}(d_p-2\Theta)y_p^+\le4K\Theta .
   \]
   Thus \(z=r^+\), together with the old variables and \(y^+\), is feasible for
   the appended capped LP.  Its objective is at least
   \[
      \sum_i\nu_i z_i^\star-4K\Theta
      =
      \mathfrak R_{\rm tr}(\nu;r)-4K\Theta,
   \]
   which proves \((CRL5)\).  If the screen does not fail, then its value is
   above \(2K\Theta\), and the positive-column conclusion is exactly
   \cref{cor:fractional-opened-support-flow-lp}.

   Starting from the empty transcript with cap \(r_i^{(0)}=1\), the residual LP
   value is \(\sum_i\nu_i\).  Iterating \((CRL5)\) proves \((CRL6)\), and
   \((CRL7)\) contradicts \((CRL6)\) in an all-failed transcript.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Downward residual normal form for LP-guided search]
   \label{cor:downward-residual-lp-normal-form}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:template-complete-shared-cover-obstruction}.  Let \(u\) be an
   exact no-prefix obstruction for a template family \(\mathcal B\), and let
   \(0\le z_a\le1\) be any fractional residual intensity vector.  Define the
   downward residual dual
   \[
      u_a^z=u_az_a,
      \qquad
      \nu_a^z=b_au_a^z,
      \qquad
      V_z=\sum_a\nu_a^z .
      \tag{DRN1}
   \]
   Then \(u^z\) is itself a no-prefix obstruction for the same template family:
   it satisfies \((TCO2)\), and for every \(B\in\mathcal B\) and every
   available cardinality \(K\),
   \[
      \sum_{j\le K}d_B^{u^z}(p_j^z)\le2P_B(K),
      \tag{DRN2}
   \]
   where \(p_1^z,p_2^z,\ldots\) are ordered by nonincreasing
   \(d_B^{u^z}(p)\).  Consequently, under the price and cardinality-net
   hypotheses of \cref{cor:template-complete-shared-cover-obstruction}, every
   old template \(B\in\mathcal B\) also obeys its clipped tail cap for the
   residual degrees \(d_B^{u^z}\).

   If \(z\) is the primal source vector of an optimal capped residual LP
   \(\mathfrak R_{\rm tr}(\nu;r)\), with \(\nu_a=b_au_a\), then
   \[
      V_z=\mathfrak R_{\rm tr}(\nu;r).
      \tag{DRN3}
   \]

   Now let \(B'\) be any new certified template whose top-prefix records belong
   to the admissible shared-panel universe, and form a fractional opened-support
   source system on \(I^+=\{a:z_a>0\}\) with normalized source loads
   \[
      \frac{\mu_a}{C}=\nu_a^z
      \qquad(a\in I^+),
      \tag{DRN4}
   \]
   and with point degrees \(d_{B'}^{u^z}\).  If
   \[
      \widehat{\mathfrak S}_{B',E}^{\,u^z}(C)
      >
      2K_{B'}^\natural\Theta_{B'}^{\rm net},
      \tag{DRN5}
   \]
   then \(B'\) contains a positive shared top-prefix column.  Conversely, if no
   top prefix of \(B'\) has positive reduced cost against \(u^z\), then every
   such source system satisfies the reverse inequality in \((DRN5)\).

   Thus the geometric part of the LP-guided algorithm can be stated entirely on
   the current downward residual dual \(u^z\).  The failed-transcript and cap
   variables are only the finite mechanism for choosing \(z\) and preventing
   source mass already paid by previous failed screens from reappearing.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The bound \(u^z_a\le u_a\le\ell_a^\Sigma(y)\) gives \((TCO2)\).  Fix
   \(B\) and \(K\), and let \(U_z=\{p_1^z,\ldots,p_K^z\}\).  Since
   \(d_B^{u^z}(p)\le d_B^u(p)\) pointwise,
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U_z}d_B^{u^z}(p)
      \le
      \sum_{p\in U_z}d_B^u(p)
      \le
      \sum_{j\le K}d_B^u(p_j)
      \le2P_B(K),
   \]
   where \(p_1,p_2,\ldots\) is the ordering for \(u\), and the last inequality
   is \((TCO4)\).  This proves \((DRN2)\).  The clipped-tail conclusion is the
   final clause of
   \cref{cor:template-complete-shared-cover-obstruction} applied to \(u^z\).

   If \(z\) is an optimal primal vector of the capped residual LP, its objective
   value is \(\sum_a\nu_az_a=\sum_ab_au_az_a=V_z\), proving \((DRN3)\).

   The last assertions are exactly
   \cref{cor:fractional-opened-support-flow-lp}, applied with the no-prefix dual
   \(u^z\), point degrees \(d_{B'}^{u^z}\), and the source loads in
   \((DRN4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Capped atom-capture support screen]
   \label{cor:capped-atom-capture-support-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:downward-residual-lp-normal-form}.  Fix a downward residual dual
   \(u^z\) and a certified template \(B\) whose top-prefix records belong to the
   admissible shared-panel universe.  For a support \(S\subseteq W_B\), define
   the atom load and capped atom-capture value
   \[
      H_{B,S,a}=\sum_{p\in S}h_{B,p,a},
      \qquad
      \mathcal C_B^{u^z}(S)
      =
      \sum_a u_a^z\min\{b_a,H_{B,S,a}\}.
      \tag{CAS1}
   \]
   Suppose at least one of \(A_B,\zeta_B\) is nonzero, so that
   \(K_B^\natural\) and \(\Theta_B^{\rm net}\) are defined.  If preprocessing
   certifies a support \(S\) with
   \[
      \mathcal C_B^{u^z}(S)>
      \bigl(|S|+2K_B^\natural\bigr)\Theta_B^{\rm net},
      \tag{CAS2}
   \]
   then \(B\) contains a positive shared top-prefix column.

   Conversely, if no top prefix of \(B\) has positive reduced cost against
   \(u^z\), then every support \(S\subseteq W_B\) satisfies
   \[
      \mathcal C_B^{u^z}(S)
      \le
      \bigl(|S|+2K_B^\natural\bigr)\Theta_B^{\rm net}.
      \tag{CAS3}
   \]

   The set function \(S\mapsto\mathcal C_B^{u^z}(S)\) is monotone submodular.
   Thus a facility, range-reporting, additive-quantization, lattice, or
   list-decoding proposal does not have to solve the opened-support flow LP
   directly: it may return any support with a one-sided lower certificate for
   the capped atom-capture surplus
   \(\mathcal C_B^{u^z}(S)-|S|\Theta_B^{\rm net}\).  A positive certificate is
   immediately hardened to one deterministic shared top-prefix column; a
   no-prefix residual obeys the explicit capped-coverage inequality \((CAS3)\)
   for every materializable support.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(I^+=\{a:u_a^z>0\}\), and form the fractional opened-support LP for
   \(B\) with right support contained in \(S\), normalized source capacities
   \(\mu_a/C=b_au_a^z\), degrees \(d_B^{u^z}(p)\), and adjacency
   \[
      E_S=\{(a,p):a\in I^+,\ p\in S,\ h_{B,p,a}>0\}.
   \]
   For each atom put
   \[
      \lambda_a=
      \begin{cases}
      \min\{1,b_a/H_{B,S,a}\}, & H_{B,S,a}>0,\\
      0, & H_{B,S,a}=0 .
      \end{cases}
      \tag{CAS4}
   \]
   Define
   \[
      x_{a,p}=\lambda_a h_{B,p,a}u_a^z
      \quad(a\in I^+,\ p\in S),
      \qquad
      z_p=\mathbf 1_{\{p\in S\}} .
      \tag{CAS5}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \sum_{p\in S}x_{a,p}
      =
      u_a^z\min\{H_{B,S,a},b_a\}
      \le b_au_a^z,
      \tag{CAS6}
   \]
   so the source constraints of \((FOF1)\) hold.  Also
   \[
      \sum_a x_{a,p}
      \le
      \sum_a h_{B,p,a}u_a^z
      =
      d_B^{u^z}(p)
      =
      d_B^{u^z}(p)z_p
      \qquad(p\in S),
      \tag{CAS7}
   \]
   and the point constraints hold, with zero flow outside \(S\).  The feasible
   objective value is
   \[
      \sum_{a,p}x_{a,p}-\Theta_B^{\rm net}|S|
      =
      \mathcal C_B^{u^z}(S)-\Theta_B^{\rm net}|S|.
      \tag{CAS8}
   \]
   If \((CAS2)\) holds, this value is larger than
   \(2K_B^\natural\Theta_B^{\rm net}\), so
   \cref{cor:fractional-opened-support-flow-lp} exposes a positive shared
   top-prefix column.

   Conversely, if no top prefix of \(B\) is positive, then
   \cref{cor:fractional-opened-support-flow-lp} gives
   \(\widehat{\mathfrak S}_{B,E}(C)\le2K_B^\natural\Theta_B^{\rm net}\) for
   every source system.  Applying this to the feasible solution above yields
   \((CAS3)\).

   Finally, \(H_{B,S,a}\) is a nonnegative modular function of \(S\), and the
   truncation \(t\mapsto\min\{b_a,t\}\) is nondecreasing concave on
   \(\mathbb R_{\ge0}\).  A nondecreasing concave function applied to a
   nonnegative modular function is submodular; nonnegative sums preserve
   monotonicity and submodularity.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Routed capped-capture support screen]
   \label{cor:routed-capped-capture-support-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:capped-atom-capture-support-screen}.  Let \(S\subseteq W_B\), and
   suppose preprocessing certifies nonnegative routed atom loads
   \(r_{a,p}\) for \(p\in S\) such that
   \[
      0\le r_{a,p}\le h_{B,p,a},
      \qquad
      \sum_{p\in S}r_{a,p}\le b_a
      \qquad\text{for every atom }a.
      \tag{RAS1}
   \]
   Define the routed captured value
   \[
      \mathcal R_B^{u^z}(S,r)
      =
      \sum_a u_a^z\sum_{p\in S}r_{a,p}.
      \tag{RAS2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \mathcal R_B^{u^z}(S,r)>
      \bigl(|S|+2K_B^\natural\bigr)\Theta_B^{\rm net},
      \tag{RAS3}
   \]
   then \(B\) contains a positive shared top-prefix column.

   Conversely, if no top prefix of \(B\) has positive reduced cost against
   \(u^z\), then every such routed certificate satisfies the reverse inequality
   in \((RAS3)\).

   Thus a geometric proposal does not have to evaluate the full capped
   submodular objective.  It may lower-certify any feasible atom-to-support
   routing; the verifier compares the routed mass to the same affine support
   price.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \((RAS1)\),
   \[
      \sum_{p\in S}r_{a,p}
      \le
      \min\left\{b_a,\sum_{p\in S}h_{B,p,a}\right\}
      =
      \min\{b_a,H_{B,S,a}\}.
      \tag{RAS4}
   \]
   Multiplying by \(u_a^z\), summing over \(a\), and using \((CAS1)\) gives
   \[
      \mathcal R_B^{u^z}(S,r)\le\mathcal C_B^{u^z}(S).
      \tag{RAS5}
   \]
   Hence \((RAS3)\) implies \((CAS2)\), and
   \cref{cor:capped-atom-capture-support-screen} gives the positive top prefix.
   If no top prefix is positive, then \((CAS3)\) and \((RAS5)\) give the
   reverse inequality for every routed certificate.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Averaged routed capped-capture proposals]
   \label{cor:averaged-routed-capped-capture-proposals}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:routed-capped-capture-support-screen}.  Let \(\omega\sim\nu\) be a
   finite proposal law.  Proposal \(\omega\) returns a support
   \(S_\omega\subseteq W_B\), routed loads \(r^\omega_{a,p}\) satisfying
   \((RAS1)\), and a certified lower routed mass \(\underline R_\omega\) with
   \[
      0\le \underline R_\omega
      \le
      \mathcal R_B^{u^z}(S_\omega,r^\omega).
      \tag{ARCS1}
   \]
   Define its certified routed surplus
   \[
      Z_\omega=
      \underline R_\omega
      -
      \bigl(|S_\omega|+2K_B^\natural\bigr)\Theta_B^{\rm net}.
      \tag{ARCS2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \E_{\omega\sim\nu} Z_\omega>0,
      \tag{ARCS3}
   \]
   then some proposal in the support of \(\nu\) satisfies \((RAS3)\), and hence
   \(B\) contains a positive shared top-prefix column.

   Conversely, if no top prefix of \(B\) has positive reduced cost against
   \(u^z\), then every finite one-sided routed proposal law has
   \[
      \E_{\omega\sim\nu} Z_\omega\le0.
      \tag{ARCS4}
   \]

   The positive branch has a Las Vegas sampled form.  If
   \[
      \E Z_\omega\ge\Gamma>0,
      \qquad
      Z_\omega^+\le M_{\rm prop}
      \quad\text{almost surely},
      \tag{ARCS5}
   \]
   then \(N\) independent proposal draws contain a valid positive routed
   certificate with probability at least
   \[
      1-\exp\left(-\frac{N\Gamma}{M_{\rm prop}}\right).
      \tag{ARCS6}
   \]

   Thus a \(k\)-means++, facility, range-reporting, AQ, lattice, or
   list-decoding analysis may be purely averaged: it suffices to lower-bound
   expected routed captured mass minus the exact affine support price.  The
   retained data structure still materializes only the first verified
   deterministic top-prefix column.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((ARCS3)\) holds, then some \(\omega\) has \(Z_\omega>0\).  By
   \((ARCS1)\)--\((ARCS2)\),
   \[
      \mathcal R_B^{u^z}(S_\omega,r^\omega)
      >
      \bigl(|S_\omega|+2K_B^\natural\bigr)\Theta_B^{\rm net}.
   \]
   This is \((RAS3)\), so
   \cref{cor:routed-capped-capture-support-screen} gives the positive top
   prefix.

   If no top prefix is positive, then the converse part of
   \cref{cor:routed-capped-capture-support-screen} gives
   \[
      \mathcal R_B^{u^z}(S_\omega,r^\omega)
      \le
      \bigl(|S_\omega|+2K_B^\natural\bigr)\Theta_B^{\rm net}
   \]
   for every proposal.  Together with \((ARCS1)\), this gives
   \(Z_\omega\le0\) pointwise, and hence \((ARCS4)\).

   Under \((ARCS5)\), \(\E Z_\omega^+\ge\Gamma\).  Since
   \(Z_\omega^+\le M_{\rm prop}\), one proposal has positive surplus with
   probability at least \(\Gamma/M_{\rm prop}\).  Independent repetition gives
   \[
      \Pr[\text{no positive proposal in }N\text{ draws}]
      \le
      \left(1-\frac{\Gamma}{M_{\rm prop}}\right)^N
      \le
      \exp\left(-\frac{N\Gamma}{M_{\rm prop}}\right).
   \]
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fractional capped-capture threshold screen]
   \label{cor:fractional-capped-capture-threshold-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:capped-atom-capture-support-screen}.  Let
   \(x=(x_p)_{p\in W_B}\in[0,1]^{W_B}\) be any finite fractional support
   profile, and for \(\theta\in(0,1]\) put
   \[
      S_\theta(x)=\{p\in W_B:x_p\ge\theta\}.
      \tag{CCT1}
   \]
   Define the layer-cake capped-capture value
   \[
      \mathcal L_B^{u^z}(x)
      =
      \int_0^1
      \mathcal C_B^{u^z}(S_\theta(x))\,d\theta .
      \tag{CCT2}
   \]
   Equivalently, if the positive coordinates of \(x\) take distinct values
   \(1\ge\theta_1>\theta_2>\cdots>\theta_m>0\), and
   \(\theta_{m+1}=0\), then
   \[
      \mathcal L_B^{u^z}(x)
      =
      \sum_{j=1}^m(\theta_j-\theta_{j+1})
      \mathcal C_B^{u^z}(S_{\theta_j}(x)).
      \tag{CCT3}
   \]
   If preprocessing certifies
   \[
      \mathcal L_B^{u^z}(x)>
      \Theta_B^{\rm net}\sum_{p\in W_B}x_p
      +
      2K_B^\natural\Theta_B^{\rm net},
      \tag{CCT4}
   \]
   then one threshold support \(S_{\theta_j}(x)\) satisfies \((CAS2)\), and
   hence \(B\) contains a positive shared top-prefix column.

   Conversely, if no top prefix of \(B\) has positive reduced cost against
   \(u^z\), then every fractional support profile obeys
   \[
      \mathcal L_B^{u^z}(x)
      \le
      \Theta_B^{\rm net}\sum_{p\in W_B}x_p
      +
      2K_B^\natural\Theta_B^{\rm net}.
      \tag{CCT5}
   \]

   Thus a proposal routine may be fully fractional.  It only has to provide a
   lower certificate for the layer-cake surplus
   \(\mathcal L_B^{u^z}(x)-\Theta_B^{\rm net}\sum_px_p\); the deterministic
   threshold support with positive surplus is then found by scanning the
   finitely many levels of \(x\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The layer-cake identity for cardinality gives
   \[
      \int_0^1|S_\theta(x)|\,d\theta
      =
      \sum_{p\in W_B}x_p.
      \tag{CCT6}
   \]
   If every threshold support violated \((CAS2)\), then
   \[
      \mathcal C_B^{u^z}(S_\theta(x))
      \le
      \bigl(|S_\theta(x)|+2K_B^\natural\bigr)\Theta_B^{\rm net}
      \qquad(0<\theta\le1)
   \]
   outside the finitely many jump levels, and hence, after integration and
   \((CCT6)\),
   \[
      \mathcal L_B^{u^z}(x)
      \le
      \Theta_B^{\rm net}\sum_px_p
      +
      2K_B^\natural\Theta_B^{\rm net}.
   \]
   Therefore \((CCT4)\) forces at least one threshold support to satisfy
   \((CAS2)\), and
   \cref{cor:capped-atom-capture-support-screen} gives the positive top prefix.

   If no top prefix is positive, then \((CAS3)\) holds for every support
   \(S_\theta(x)\).  Integrating those inequalities and using \((CCT6)\) gives
   \((CCT5)\).  The discrete formula \((CCT3)\) is the same integral written
   over the finitely many constant intervals of \(\theta\mapsto S_\theta(x)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[LP-guided capped-flow exhaustion endpoint]
   \label{cor:lp-guided-capped-flow-exhaustion-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:fractional-opened-support-template-endpoint}.  Replace the
   fractional-panel hypothesis \((FOT1)\) by the following capped residual-LP
   exhaustion condition.

   Whenever \(\Psi_{\mathcal B_y}(y)>D_\pi/4\) and
   \cref{cor:template-complete-shared-cover-obstruction} supplies an exact
   no-prefix dual obstruction \(u\), preprocessing uses the obstruction-sourced
   measure
   \[
      I_0(u)=\{a\in\mathcal A_\pi:\ b_au_a>0\},
      \qquad
      \nu_a=b_au_a,
      \qquad
      V(u)=\sum_ab_au_a,
      \tag{LGE1}
   \]
   and sets \(\Lambda_{\rm rem}=V(u)/2\).  It then runs a finite
   LP-guided proposal rule.  Initially the transcript is empty and
   \(r_a^{(0)}=1\).  At step \(t\), after the current failed transcript and cap
   \(r^{(t-1)}\) have been certified, preprocessing solves the capped residual
   LP and obtains an optimal primal vector \(z^{(t-1)}\).  If
   \[
      \mathfrak R_{t-1}(\nu;r^{(t-1)})<\Lambda_{\rm rem},
      \tag{LGE2}
   \]
   it stops.  Otherwise it proposes a fractional opened-support source system
   \((B_t,E_t,C_t)\) whose template top-prefix records lie in
   \(\mathcal Z_\star\), whose left side is
   \(I_{t-1}^+=\{a:z_a^{(t-1)}>0\}\), and whose normalized source loads are
   \[
      \frac{\mu_a^{(t)}}{C_t}=\nu_a z_a^{(t-1)}
      \qquad(a\in I_{t-1}^+).
      \tag{LGE3}
   \]
   Equivalently, by
   \cref{cor:downward-residual-lp-normal-form}, this step is a separator search
   against the downward residual dual
   \(u_a^{(t-1)}=u_az_a^{(t-1)}\); the failed transcript only determines the
   cap-constrained optimizer \(z^{(t-1)}\).
   By \cref{cor:capped-atom-capture-support-screen}, one sufficient positive
   branch is a certified support whose capped atom-capture value beats the
   affine clipped support price.  By
   \cref{cor:routed-capped-capture-support-screen}, it is enough to lower-certify
   any feasible atom-to-support routing with that surplus.  By
   \cref{cor:averaged-routed-capped-capture-proposals}, an averaged routed
   proposal law with positive certified surplus can be sampled Las Vegas until
   one deterministic certificate verifies.  By
   \cref{cor:fractional-capped-capture-threshold-screen}, the same branch may
   be proposed fractionally and then rounded by thresholding the layer-cake
   surplus.
   Put
   \[
      K_t=K_{B_t}^\natural,
      \qquad
      \Theta_t=\Theta_{B_t}^{\rm net}.
      \tag{LGE4}
   \]
   If the proposed screen fails, preprocessing appends it to the failed
   transcript and updates the cap using the dual-price rule of
   \cref{cor:capped-residual-lp-continuation}.  The rule is called
   capped-value-complete if every possible all-failed terminal transcript
   satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{t=1}^T4K_t\Theta_t\le\frac{V(u)}2
      \tag{LGE5}
   \]
   and terminates only with the certified capped residual bound
   \[
      \mathfrak R_T(\nu;r^{(T)})<\frac{V(u)}2 .
      \tag{LGE6}
   \]
