   If such a capped-value-complete LP-guided proposal rule exists for every
   exact no-prefix obstruction \(u\), then the positive shared-panel separator
   \((SPP1)\) holds at every node, and hence
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,\qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   Thus the remaining geometric theorem may be stated as an LP-guided
   separator: every high-value no-prefix obstruction, when restricted to the
   current capped residual-LP optimizer, equivalently every high-value downward
   residual dual \(u^z\), must either produce a half-threshold opened-support
   screen---for instance by a capped atom-capture support surplus---or force the
   capped residual LP below half the exposed obstruction value before half that
   value has been spent on failed screens.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a resident node and a feasible dual \(y\).  If
   \(\Psi_{\mathcal B_y}(y)\le D_\pi/4\), then the cover outcome of
   \cref{cor:template-search-shared-integrated-target} already holds.  Otherwise
   let \(u\) be the exact obstruction returned by
   \cref{cor:template-complete-shared-cover-obstruction}, and run the
   LP-guided proposal rule above.

   If at some step
   \[
      \widehat{\mathfrak S}_{B_t,E_t}(C_t)>2K_t\Theta_t,
   \]
   then \cref{cor:fractional-opened-support-flow-lp} exposes a positive shared
   top-prefix column in \(\mathcal Z_\star\).  This is the second outcome
   required by \cref{cor:template-search-shared-integrated-target}.

   Suppose instead that every proposed screen fails.  By capped-value
   completeness, the terminal transcript satisfies \((LGE5)\)--\((LGE6)\).
   Applying \cref{cor:capped-residual-lp-continuation} with
   \(V_0=\sum_a\nu_a=V(u)\) gives
   \[
      \mathfrak R_T(\nu;r^{(T)})
      \ge
      V(u)-\sum_{t=1}^T4K_t\Theta_t
      \ge
      \frac{V(u)}2,
   \]
   contradicting \((LGE6)\).  Hence not all proposed screens can fail, and a
   positive shared top-prefix column is found.

   Therefore every feasible dual \(y\) has one of the two outcomes required by
   \cref{cor:template-search-shared-integrated-target}.  That corollary gives
   \((SPP1)\), and \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint} gives the
   displayed query and storage bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Shared integrated cover-cost endpoint]
   \label{cor:shared-integrated-cover-cost-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint}.  Suppose the full
   certified panel universe \(\mathcal Z_\star\) contains every materializable
   low-correlation class-local profile record used in
   \cref{cor:gaussian-tuple-profile-witness-density} and every smaller-radius
   dense prefix verified by the paid dense-prefix verifier below.  For the
   high-correlation side, use a finite shared cover universe \(\mathcal R_\pi\)
   as in \cref{cor:finite-shared-integrated-cover-dual}.
   Suppose that at every resident node of size at most \(n\), and for every
   normalized exact-signature price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\), preprocessing
   can certify one split profile \(\pi\), an atomized high-correlation
   representation included in the admissible routing universe of
   \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope}, a truncation
   \(0<\varepsilon_\pi\le1\), and a number \(\mathfrak C_{\Sigma,\pi}\) such that
   every feasible atomized dual \(y\) for that profile satisfies
   \[
      \Psi_\Sigma(y)\le\mathfrak C_{\Sigma,\pi},
      \tag{SIE1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      D_\pi=(B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo})_+>0,
      \tag{SIE2}
   \]
   \[
      \varepsilon_\pi B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2\mathfrak C_{\Sigma,\pi}
      <D_\pi .
      \tag{SIE3}
   \]
   Then worst-case Euclidean ANN has
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   Thus the shared dense-overlap target can be stated as one finite LP: every
   high-correlation dual should admit a shared cover whose integrated unassigned
   tail plus twice the one-time recursive price is a constant fraction of the
   profile's residual benefit.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a resident node and normalized price system, and take the certified
   profile from the hypothesis.  If a shared record fires while certifying
   \((SIE1)\), then this is already a positive column in \(\mathcal Z_\star\).
   Otherwise \cref{cor:finite-shared-integrated-cover-dual} gives, for every
   feasible atomized high-correlation dual \(y\),
   \[
      \sum_ab_ay_a
      \le
      \varepsilon_\pi B_\pi^{\rm hi}+2\mathfrak C_{\Sigma,\pi}.
   \]
   Taking the supremum over feasible atomized duals and using \((AHR8)\) yields
   \[
      \Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \le
      \varepsilon_\pi B_\pi^{\rm hi}+2\mathfrak C_{\Sigma,\pi}
      <D_\pi .
   \]
   The rest is identical to the proof of
   \cref{cor:shared-integrated-dense-profile-endpoint}: apply
   \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope} to expose a positive
   low-correlation shared-panel record or a positive dense prefix, then invoke
   \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Shared integrated dense-profile endpoint]
   \label{cor:shared-integrated-dense-profile-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint}.  Suppose the full
   certified panel universe \(\mathcal Z_\star\) contains every materializable
   low-correlation class-local profile record used in
   \cref{cor:gaussian-tuple-profile-witness-density} and every smaller-radius
   dense prefix verified by the paid dense-prefix verifier below.

   Suppose that at every resident node of size at most \(n\), and for every
   normalized exact-signature price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\), preprocessing
   can certify one split profile \(\pi\), an atomized high-correlation
   representation included in the admissible routing universe of
   \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope}, a truncation
   \(0<\varepsilon_\pi\le1\), and shared integrated certificates satisfying
   \((SIH4)\), such that
   \[
      D_\pi=(B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo})_+>0
      \tag{SID1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \varepsilon_\pi B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2\mathfrak E_{\Sigma,\pi}
      +4\mathfrak P_{\Sigma,\pi}
      <D_\pi .
      \tag{SID2}
   \]
   Then worst-case Euclidean ANN has
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   In particular, it is sufficient to certify polynomial dynamic range
   \(B_\pi^{\rm hi}\le n^{K_{\rm dyn}}D_\pi\) and
   \[
      2\mathfrak E_{\Sigma,\pi}
      +4\mathfrak P_{\Sigma,\pi}
      \le D_\pi/2,
      \tag{SID3}
   \]
   because then one may take
   \(\varepsilon_\pi=\min\{1,1/(4n^{K_{\rm dyn}})\}\) outside the bounded-size
   scan base case.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a resident node and normalized price system, and take the certified
   profile supplied by the hypothesis.  If a shared star-prefix record fires
   while certifying \((SIH4)\), then this is already a positive column in
   \(\mathcal Z_\star\).  Otherwise
   \cref{cor:shared-integrated-high-correlation-tail} gives
   \[
      \Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \le
      \varepsilon_\pi B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2\mathfrak E_{\Sigma,\pi}
      +4\mathfrak P_{\Sigma,\pi}
      <D_\pi .
   \]
   Hence \(B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo}-\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}>0\), and
   \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope} exposes either a positive
   low-correlation shared-panel record or a positive dense prefix.  In both cases
   the verified object is in \(\mathcal Z_\star\), so \((SPP1)\) holds for the
   fixed normalized price system.  Since the price system and node were
   arbitrary, \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint} gives the
   displayed query and storage bounds.

   Under the sufficient conditions, the displayed choice of \(\varepsilon_\pi\)
   gives \(\varepsilon_\pi B_\pi^{\rm hi}\le D_\pi/4\), while \((SID3)\) supplies
   at most \(D_\pi/2\) more.  Hence the left side of \((SID2)\) is at most
   \(3D_\pi/4<D_\pi\).  Bounded-size nodes are handled by resident scan and
   absorbed into the logarithmic constants.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Single-tail shared separator endpoint]
   \label{cor:single-tail-shared-separator-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint}.  Suppose the full
   certified panel universe \(\mathcal Z_\star\) contains every materializable
   low-correlation class-local profile record used in
   \cref{cor:gaussian-tuple-profile-witness-density} and every shared top-prefix
   record generated by a family \(\mathcal B\) of certified smaller-radius
   templates.  For each template \(B\in\mathcal B\), assume the available
   cardinalities are \(b_B\)-dense from below and that, against any normalized
   exact-signature price system, the reduced gain of the top \(K\)-prefix is
   represented as
   \[
      \sum_{j\le K}d_B(p_j)
      -
      \psi_B\left(A_BK^{\rho_B}+\zeta_BK^{1+\rho_B}\right),
      \qquad 0<\rho_B<1,
      \tag{CTE1}
   \]
   where \(p_1,p_2,\ldots\) are ordered by nonincreasing \(d_B(p)\).

   Assume that at every resident node and for every normalized exact-signature
   price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\), at least one of the following holds.
   First, some materializable low-correlation profile record in
   \(\mathcal Z_\star\) has positive shared-panel gain.  Second, some
   \(B\in\mathcal B\) violates its cardinality-net clipped tail cap:
   \[
      M_B^+(\Theta_B^{\rm net})
      >
      2K_B^\natural\Theta_B^{\rm net},
      \tag{CTE2}
   \]
   where \(K_B^\natural\), \(\Theta_B^{\rm net}\), and \(M_B^+\) are defined
   from \(A_B,\zeta_B,\psi_B,\rho_B,b_B\) as in
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-clipped-shared-tail}.

   Then the positive shared-panel separator \((SPP1)\) holds at every node.
   Consequently worst-case Euclidean ANN has
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   Thus the dense side of the remaining theorem can be stated without
   threshold or prefix-size choices: after the low-correlation Gaussian records
   fail, geometry only has to force one certified shared container whose clipped
   degree tail exceeds \((CTE2)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a resident node and normalized exact-signature price system.  If the
   first alternative holds, then \((SPP1)\) holds immediately.  Otherwise take a
   template \(B\) satisfying \((CTE2)\).  If no shared top prefix of \(B\) had
   positive reduced gain, then applying
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-clipped-shared-tail} to the degrees \(d_B\) and
   prices in \((CTE1)\) would give the reverse inequality
   \[
      M_B^+(\Theta_B^{\rm net})
      \le
      2K_B^\natural\Theta_B^{\rm net},
   \]
   contradicting \((CTE2)\).  Hence \(B\) contains a positive shared top-prefix
   record, and this record belongs to \(\mathcal Z_\star\) by hypothesis.  Thus
   \((SPP1)\) holds for the fixed price system.  Since the node and price system
   were arbitrary, \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint} gives the
   displayed bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One-sided integrated singleton center certificate]
   \label{cor:one-sided-integrated-singleton-center}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:integrated-singleton-reduced-cost-screen}.  A one-sided
   integrated center certificate consists of a center \(x\), a set of dyadic
   cuts on which it is materialized, and numbers
   \[
      \underline M_x^\Sigma,\qquad
      \overline P_x^\Sigma
   \]
   satisfying
   \[
      0<\underline M_x^\Sigma\le M_x^\Sigma,
      \qquad
      P_x^\Sigma\le\overline P_x^\Sigma,
      \qquad
      \underline M_x^\Sigma>2\overline P_x^\Sigma .
      \tag{OIS1}
   \]
   Any such certificate exposes a positive smaller-radius dense prefix after
   the verifier checks the reported cut records.  If a randomized build-time
   proposal returns a verifiable certificate satisfying \((OIS1)\) with
   probability at least \(p_E>0\) whenever one exists in the finite proposal
   universe, Las Vegas repetition finds a valid dense-prefix augmentation after
   expected at most \(1/p_E\) proposals; failed proposals are discarded.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   From \((OIS1)\),
   \[
      M_x^\Sigma\ge \underline M_x^\Sigma
      >2\overline P_x^\Sigma
      \ge2P_x^\Sigma .
   \]
   Hence \((ISC5)\) holds, and
   \cref{cor:integrated-singleton-reduced-cost-screen} exposes a positive dense
   prefix at one cut.  The Las Vegas statement is the standard
   repeat-until-accepted argument; only the verified cut record that fires is
   retained.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Explicit split-profile tail separator]
   \label{cor:explicit-split-profile-tail-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope}.  Let \(\Pi\) be a finite
   split-profile panel with panel weights \(\eta_\pi\ge0\).  For each
   \(\pi\in\Pi\), suppose its high-correlation part has an atomized
   representation satisfying
   \cref{cor:atomized-high-correlation-fixed-tail} with parameters
   \(\varepsilon_\pi,J_{\varepsilon,\pi},
   \mathfrak E_{\star,\pi},\mathfrak P_{\star,\pi}\).  Define the
   explicit high-correlation tail
   \[
      \Psi_\pi^{\rm hi}
      =
      \varepsilon_\pi B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2J_{\varepsilon,\pi}\mathfrak E_{\star,\pi}
      +4J_{\varepsilon,\pi}\mathfrak P_{\star,\pi}.
      \tag{EST1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi
      \left(
         B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo}-\Psi_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \right)>0,
      \tag{EST2}
   \]
   then either some low-correlation profile record exposes positive
   shared-panel gain, or a high-correlation atom-cut star record exposes a
   positive smaller-radius dense prefix.

   Hence a sufficient fully explicit replacement for \((MSP1)\) is: for every
   normalized exact-signature dual, preprocessing can certify a finite panel
   for which \((EST2)\) holds and whose low records and star-prefix records
   belong to the certified shared-panel universe.  Under that replacement,
   \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-separator-endpoint} gives the same
   \(d\,n^{\rho_c}\polylog n\) query and
   \(dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\polylog n\) storage bounds.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If a high-correlation atom-cut star record exposes a positive dense prefix,
   we are done.  Otherwise \((AHF4)\) gives
   \(\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}\le\Psi_\pi^{\rm hi}\) for every profile in the panel.
   Thus \((EST2)\) implies
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi
      \left(
         B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo}-\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \right)>0 .
   \]
   Applying \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope} exposes either a
   low-correlation positive shared-panel record or a positive dense prefix.
   The endpoint clause is exactly
   \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-separator-endpoint} with this explicit
   upper envelope for \(\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sampled-center split-profile separator]
   \label{cor:sampled-center-split-profile-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope}.  Let \(\Pi\) be a finite
   split-profile panel with panel weights \(\eta_\pi\ge0\).  For each
   \(\pi\in\Pi\), suppose the high-correlation part has an atomized
   representation satisfying
   \cref{cor:sampled-center-high-correlation-fixed-tail} with parameters
   \[
      \varepsilon_\pi,\qquad
      J_{\varepsilon,\pi},\qquad
      \mathfrak E_{\star,\pi},\qquad
      \mathfrak P_{\star,\pi}.
   \]
   Put
   \[
      \Psi_{\pi,{\rm samp}}^{\rm hi}
      =
      \varepsilon_\pi B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2J_{\varepsilon,\pi}\mathfrak E_{\star,\pi}
      +4J_{\varepsilon,\pi}\mathfrak P_{\star,\pi}.
      \tag{SCS1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi
      \left(
         B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo}-\Psi_{\pi,{\rm samp}}^{\rm hi}
      \right)>0,
      \tag{SCS2}
   \]
   then either some low-correlation profile record exposes positive
   shared-panel gain, or one sampled high-correlation reported-center panel
   exposes a positive smaller-radius dense prefix.

   Consequently, the endpoint hypothesis \((MSP1)\) in
   \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-separator-endpoint} may be replaced by the
   sampled-center aggregate surplus condition \((SCS2)\), provided the sampled
   reported-center panels are verified by the same paid dense-prefix universe.
   Thus the remaining build-time theorem can be stated without choosing a
   deterministic dense decomposition: for every normalized exact-signature dual,
   produce a finite split-profile panel and randomized center laws whose
   aggregate sampled surplus is positive.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If one sampled reported-center panel exposes a positive dense prefix, the
   second alternative holds.  Otherwise
   \cref{cor:sampled-center-high-correlation-fixed-tail} gives
   \(\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}\le\Psi_{\pi,{\rm samp}}^{\rm hi}\) for every profile in
   the panel.  Hence \((SCS2)\) implies
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi
      \left(
         B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo}-\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \right)>0 .
   \]
   Applying \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope} exposes either a
   low-correlation positive shared-panel record or a positive dense prefix.
   The endpoint replacement follows by the same argument as
   \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-separator-endpoint}: the verified low record
   or dense prefix is an ordinary certified panel column.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sampled-center split-profile residual envelope]
   \label{cor:sampled-center-split-profile-residual}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:sampled-center-split-profile-separator}.  Suppose the current
   normalized exact-signature residual has no low-correlation profile record
   with positive shared-panel gain and no sampled reported-center panel that
   exposes a positive smaller-radius dense prefix.  Then every finite
   split-profile panel \((\Pi,\eta)\) equipped with sampled center laws as in
   \cref{cor:sampled-center-split-profile-separator} satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi B_\pi
      \le
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi
      \left(
         C_\pi^{\rm lo}
         +\varepsilon_\pi B_\pi^{\rm hi}
         +2J_{\varepsilon,\pi}\mathfrak E_{\star,\pi}
         +4J_{\varepsilon,\pi}\mathfrak P_{\star,\pi}
      \right).
      \tag{SCSR1}
   \]

   Equivalently, any geometric, facility, additive-quantization, range-reporting,
   or list/lattice-decoding theorem that violates \((SCSR1)\) for every
   normalized residual immediately supplies the sampled-center split-profile
   separator and hence the shared-panel endpoint.  This is the current
   high-correlation counterexample format: low-correlation Gaussian congestion,
   expected unreported center tail, and expected recursive star price must
   account for all priced benefit.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((SCSR1)\) failed for some finite panel, then the strict reverse
   inequality is exactly \((SCS2)\).  By
   \cref{cor:sampled-center-split-profile-separator}, either a low-correlation
   profile record has positive shared-panel gain or one sampled reported-center
   panel exposes a positive dense prefix, contradicting the residual
   hypothesis.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Optimized sampled-center split-profile residual]
   \label{cor:optimized-sampled-center-split-profile-residual}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:sampled-center-split-profile-residual}.  Suppose that for each
   profile \(\pi\), the sampled center laws and their certificates are available
   with the same envelopes
   \(\mathfrak E_{\star,\pi},\mathfrak P_{\star,\pi}\) for every
   \(0<\varepsilon\le1\).  Put
   \[
      A_\pi^{\rm samp}
      =
      2\mathfrak E_{\star,\pi}+4\mathfrak P_{\star,\pi},
      \tag{OSR1}
   \]
   and define
   \[
      \Theta(B,A)=
      \inf_{0<\varepsilon\le1}
      \left[
         \varepsilon B+
         A\left(1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac1\varepsilon\right\rceil\right)
      \right],
      \tag{OSR2}
   \]
   with \(\Theta(B,0)=0\).  Then any surviving residual satisfies, for every
   finite sampled-center split-profile panel,
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi B_\pi
      \le
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi
      \left(
         C_\pi^{\rm lo}
         +
         \Theta(B_\pi^{\rm hi},A_\pi^{\rm samp})
      \right).
      \tag{OSR3}
   \]
   Conversely, any strict violation of \((OSR3)\) exposes either a
   low-correlation positive shared-panel record or one sampled high-correlation
   dense prefix.

   Moreover, for a universal constant \(C_0\),
   \[
      \Theta(B,A)
      \le
      C_0 A
      \left(
         1+\log_+\frac{B}{A}
      \right)
      \qquad(A>0),
      \tag{OSR4}
   \]
   and \(\Theta(B,0)=0\).  Hence a simpler sufficient residual envelope is
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi B_\pi
      \le
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi
      \left[
         C_\pi^{\rm lo}
         +
         C_0A_\pi^{\rm samp}
         \left(
            1+\log_+\frac{B_\pi^{\rm hi}}{A_\pi^{\rm samp}}
         \right)
      \right],
      \tag{OSR5}
   \]
   with the logarithmic term interpreted as \(0\) when
   \(A_\pi^{\rm samp}=0\).

   This removes the free truncation parameter from the high-correlation
   obstruction.  The remaining sampled-center theorem only has to make the
   expected unreported tail plus recursive star price logarithmically smaller
   than the useful high-correlation benefit.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a finite panel and assume no positive low-correlation record or sampled
   dense prefix exists.  For any choice of
   \(0<\varepsilon_\pi\le1\), the residual envelope \((SCSR1)\) gives
   \[
      \sum_\pi\eta_\pi B_\pi
      \le
      \sum_\pi\eta_\pi
      \left(
         C_\pi^{\rm lo}
         +\varepsilon_\pi B_\pi^{\rm hi}
         +A_\pi^{\rm samp}
          \left(1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac1{\varepsilon_\pi}\right\rceil\right)
      \right),
      \tag{OSR6}
   \]
   because \(J_{\varepsilon_\pi}=1+\lceil\log_2(1/\varepsilon_\pi)\rceil\).
   Taking the infimum independently over the finitely many
   \(\varepsilon_\pi\) proves \((OSR3)\); if a strict violation of \((OSR3)\)
   occurred, choose each \(\varepsilon_\pi\) within a small enough additive
   error of the infimum to obtain a strict violation of \((SCSR1)\), and apply
   \cref{cor:sampled-center-split-profile-residual}.

   It remains to prove \((OSR4)\).  If \(B\le A\), choose
   \(\varepsilon=1\), giving \(\Theta(B,A)\le B+A\le2A\).  If \(B>A\), choose
   \(k=\lfloor\log_2(B/A)\rfloor\) and \(\varepsilon=2^{-k}\).  Then
   \(\varepsilon B\le2A\) and
   \(1+k\le1+\log_2(B/A)\).  Therefore
   \[
      \Theta(B,A)
      \le
      2A+A\left(1+\log_2\frac BA\right)
      \le
      C_0A\left(1+\log_+\frac BA\right)
   \]
   for a universal \(C_0\).  The case \(A=0\) follows directly from
   \((OSR2)\) by taking \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Clipped-singleton logarithmic density endpoint]
   \label{cor:clipped-singleton-density-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint}.  Suppose the full
   certified panel universe \(\mathcal Z_\star\) contains every materializable
   low-correlation class-local profile record used in
   \cref{cor:gaussian-tuple-profile-witness-density} and every smaller-radius
   dense prefix that can be verified by the paid dense-prefix verifier for the
   high-correlation records used below.

   Let \((\Pi,\eta)\) be a finite split-profile panel.  For each
   \(\pi\in\Pi\), suppose its high-correlation part has an atomized
   representation included in the admissible routing universe of
   \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope}, and suppose that for every
   \(0<\varepsilon\le1\) the dyadic cuts in
   \cref{cor:clipped-singleton-high-correlation-fixed-tail} admit the same
   clipped singleton envelope \(\mathfrak G_{\star,\pi}\).  Put
   \[
      A_\pi^{\rm clip}=2\mathfrak G_{\star,\pi}.
      \tag{CDE1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi
      \left(
         B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo}
         -\Theta(B_\pi^{\rm hi},A_\pi^{\rm clip})
      \right)>0,
      \tag{CDE2}
   \]
   then the fixed normalized price system exposes either a positive
   low-correlation shared-panel record or a positive smaller-radius dense
   prefix.

   Consequently, suppose that at every resident node of size at most \(n\), and
   for every normalized exact-signature price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\),
   preprocessing can certify one such split profile \(\pi\) with
   \[
      D_\pi=(B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo})_+>0,
      \tag{CDE3}
   \]
   \[
      B_\pi^{\rm hi}\le n^{K_{\rm dyn}}D_\pi,
      \tag{CDE4}
   \]
   and
   \[
      A_\pi^{\rm clip}
      \le
      \frac{D_\pi}{\log^{K_{\rm den}}n}
      \qquad(K_{\rm den}>1).
      \tag{CDE5}
   \]
   Then, after increasing the logarithmic constants in the local budgets and
   treating bounded \(n\) by the resident scan base case, worst-case Euclidean
   ANN has
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   Thus the remaining high-correlation theorem may be stated without sampled
   center panels: under every normalized residual, certify one profile whose
   cut-wise clipped singleton price is an inverse-polylogarithmic fraction of
   its residual benefit; strict clipping gain is the special case in which the
   dense prefix is already witnessed by one singleton center.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   First prove the panel statement.  Assume no low-correlation record and no
   positive dense prefix is positive.  For any choice of
   \(0<\varepsilon_\pi\le1\), \cref{cor:clipped-singleton-high-correlation-fixed-tail}
   gives
   \[
      \Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \le
      \varepsilon_\pi B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +
      A_\pi^{\rm clip}
      \left(1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac1{\varepsilon_\pi}\right\rceil\right).
      \tag{CDE6}
   \]
   If \((CDE2)\) holds, choose each \(\varepsilon_\pi\) within a small enough
   additive error of the infimum defining \(\Theta\) to obtain
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi
      \left(
         B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo}-\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \right)>0.
   \]
   Then \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope} exposes either a positive
   low-correlation record or a positive dense prefix, contradicting the
   residual assumption.  Hence a violation of the clipped logarithmic envelope
   gives one of the stated positive columns.

   For the endpoint, use the same arithmetic as in
   \cref{cor:polylog-sampled-center-density-endpoint}, with
   \(A_\pi^{\rm clip}\) in place of \(A_\pi^{\rm samp}\).  Conditions
   \((CDE4)\)--\((CDE5)\) imply, for all sufficiently large \(n\), that either
   \(A_\pi^{\rm clip}=0\), in which case
   \(\Theta(B_\pi^{\rm hi},A_\pi^{\rm clip})=0<D_\pi\), or else
   \[
      C_0A_\pi^{\rm clip}
      \left(
         1+\log_+\frac{B_\pi^{\rm hi}}{A_\pi^{\rm clip}}
      \right)
      <D_\pi .
   \]
   In the latter case, \((OSR4)\) implies
   \[
      \Theta(B_\pi^{\rm hi},A_\pi^{\rm clip})<D_\pi.
   \]
   Therefore the one-profile panel satisfies \((CDE2)\) for every normalized
   price system at every sufficiently large node.  The panel statement gives a
   verified positive column in \(\mathcal Z_\star\), so \((SPP1)\) holds at
   every such node.  Bounded-size nodes are handled by resident scan, and
   \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint} gives the displayed
   query and storage bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Integrated clipped-singleton density endpoint]
   \label{cor:integrated-clipped-singleton-density-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint}.  Suppose the full
   certified panel universe \(\mathcal Z_\star\) contains every materializable
   low-correlation class-local profile record used in
   \cref{cor:gaussian-tuple-profile-witness-density} and every smaller-radius
   dense prefix verified by the paid dense-prefix verifier below.

   Suppose that at every resident node of size at most \(n\), and for every
   normalized exact-signature price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\),
   preprocessing can certify one split profile \(\pi\), an atomized
   high-correlation representation included in the admissible routing universe
   of \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope}, a truncation
   \(0<\varepsilon_\pi\le1\), and a uniform integrated clipped certificate
   \(\mathfrak G_{\Sigma,\pi}\) satisfying \((ICL3)\), such that
   \[
      D_\pi=(B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo})_+>0
      \tag{ICE1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \varepsilon_\pi B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2\mathfrak G_{\Sigma,\pi}
      <D_\pi .
      \tag{ICE2}
   \]
   Then worst-case Euclidean ANN has
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   In particular, it is sufficient to certify constants \(K_{\rm dyn}\ge0\)
   with
   \[
      B_\pi^{\rm hi}\le n^{K_{\rm dyn}}D_\pi
      \tag{ICE3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \mathfrak G_{\Sigma,\pi}\le D_\pi/4,
      \tag{ICE4}
   \]
   because then one may take
   \(\varepsilon_\pi=\min\{1,1/(4n^{K_{\rm dyn}})\}\), giving
   \(\varepsilon_\pi B_\pi^{\rm hi}\le D_\pi/4\) and hence \((ICE2)\).

   Thus the sharpest clipped-singleton target is an integrated dyadic
   statement: the sum of clipped singleton prices over the
   \(O_c(\log n)\) relevant layer-cake cuts should be a constant fraction of
   the residual benefit.  A per-cut inverse-polylogarithmic bound is only a
   convenient sufficient condition.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a resident node and normalized price system, and take the certified
   profile supplied by the hypothesis.  If a singleton dense prefix is exposed
   while certifying \((ICL3)\), then this is already a positive column in
   \(\mathcal Z_\star\).  Otherwise
   \cref{cor:integrated-clipped-singleton-high-correlation} gives
   \[
      \Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \le
      \varepsilon_\pi B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2\mathfrak G_{\Sigma,\pi}
      <D_\pi .
   \]
   Since \(D_\pi=(B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo})_+\), this implies
   \[
      B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo}-\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}>0.
   \]
   Applying \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope} to the one-profile panel
   exposes either a positive low-correlation shared-panel record or a positive
   dense prefix.  In both cases the verified object is in \(\mathcal Z_\star\),
   so \((SPP1)\) holds for the fixed normalized price system.  Since the price
   system and node were arbitrary, \((SPP1)\) holds at every resident node, and
   \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint} gives the displayed
   bounds.

   The sufficient conditions \((ICE3)\)--\((ICE4)\) imply \((ICE2)\) by the
   displayed choice of \(\varepsilon_\pi\), after treating bounded \(n\) by the
   resident scan base case and absorbing constants into the logarithmic
   budgets.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One-sided integrated clipped profile oracle]
   \label{cor:one-sided-integrated-clipped-profile-oracle}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:integrated-clipped-singleton-density-endpoint}, and fix a finite
   universe \(\mathcal P_{\Sigma}\) of materializable split profiles equipped
   with atomized high-correlation representations and dyadic clipped singleton
   certificates.  A one-sided integrated clipped certificate consists of a
   profile \(\pi\in\mathcal P_{\Sigma}\), a truncation
   \(0<\varepsilon_\pi\le1\), and numbers
   \[
      \underline D_\pi,\qquad
      \overline B_\pi^{\rm hi},\qquad
      \overline G_{\Sigma,\pi}
   \]
   satisfying
   \[
      0<\underline D_\pi\le B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo},
      \qquad
      B_\pi^{\rm hi}\le\overline B_\pi^{\rm hi},
      \qquad
      \mathfrak G_{\Sigma,\pi}\le\overline G_{\Sigma,\pi},
      \tag{OIC1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \varepsilon_\pi\overline B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2\overline G_{\Sigma,\pi}
      <\underline D_\pi .
      \tag{OIC2}
   \]
   Suppose that at every resident node and for every normalized
   exact-signature price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\), uncharged preprocessing
   has an oracle which returns such a certificate, or correctly certifies that
   no profile in \(\mathcal P_{\Sigma}\) has such a one-sided certificate.  If
   the no-certificate outcome never occurs on a normalized residual, then the
   full \(d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n\) query and
   \(dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n\) storage endpoint follows.

   The same statement holds in Las Vegas build time: if a randomized proposal
   law returns a verifiable certificate satisfying \((OIC1)\)--\((OIC2)\) with
   probability at least \(p_E>0\) whenever one exists in the finite universe,
   repeat proposals until the first accepted certificate.  Failed or
   unverifiable proposals are discarded and are not charged to the retained
   index.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   A returned certificate gives
   \(D_\pi=(B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo})_+\ge\underline D_\pi>0\), and
   \[
      \varepsilon_\pi B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2\mathfrak G_{\Sigma,\pi}
      \le
      \varepsilon_\pi\overline B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2\overline G_{\Sigma,\pi}
      <\underline D_\pi
      \le D_\pi .
   \]
   Hence \((ICE1)\)--\((ICE2)\) hold for the returned profile, and
   \cref{cor:integrated-clipped-singleton-density-endpoint} gives the endpoint
   if this happens at every normalized residual.

   For Las Vegas sampling, the probability that the first \(B\) independent
   proposals all fail is at most \((1-p_E)^B\), so repeat-until-accepted
   terminates almost surely with expected at most \(1/p_E\) proposals.  The
   retained index contains only the first verified certificate, so failed
   proposals have no query or storage cost.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One-sided clipped-singleton profile oracle]
   \label{cor:one-sided-clipped-singleton-profile-oracle}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:clipped-singleton-density-endpoint}, and fix a finite universe
   \(\mathcal P_{\rm clip}\) of materializable split profiles equipped with
   clipped singleton center universes for every truncation level.  A one-sided
   clipped profile certificate consists of a profile
   \(\pi\in\mathcal P_{\rm clip}\) and numbers
   \[
      \underline D_\pi,\qquad
      \overline B_\pi^{\rm hi},\qquad
      \overline A_\pi^{\rm clip}
   \]
   satisfying
   \[
      0<\underline D_\pi\le B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo},
      \qquad
      B_\pi^{\rm hi}\le\overline B_\pi^{\rm hi},
      \qquad
      A_\pi^{\rm clip}\le\overline A_\pi^{\rm clip}.
      \tag{OCD1}
   \]
   Suppose that at every resident node of size at most \(n\), and for every
   normalized exact-signature price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\), uncharged
   preprocessing has an oracle which returns such a certificate with
   \[
      \overline B_\pi^{\rm hi}\le n^{K_{\rm dyn}}\underline D_\pi,
      \tag{OCD2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \overline A_\pi^{\rm clip}
      \le
      \frac{\underline D_\pi}{\log^{K_{\rm den}}n}
      \qquad(K_{\rm den}>1),
      \tag{OCD3}
   \]
   or correctly certifies that no profile in \(\mathcal P_{\rm clip}\) has
   such a one-sided certificate.  If the no-certificate outcome never occurs on
   a normalized residual, then the same
   \(d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n\) query and
   \(dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n\) storage endpoint follows.

   The same statement holds in Las Vegas build time.  If a randomized proposal
   law returns a verifiable certificate satisfying \((OCD1)\)--\((OCD3)\) with
   probability at least \(p_E>0\) whenever one exists in the finite universe,
   repeat proposals until the first accepted certificate.  The expected number
   of proposal calls is at most \(1/p_E\), and failed or unverifiable proposals
   are discarded before they affect the retained index.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   A returned certificate gives
   \(D_\pi=(B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo})_+\ge\underline D_\pi>0\).  Conditions
   \((OCD1)\)--\((OCD2)\) imply
   \[
      B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \le
      n^{K_{\rm dyn}}\underline D_\pi
      \le
      n^{K_{\rm dyn}}D_\pi,
   \]
   and \((OCD1)\)--\((OCD3)\) imply
   \[
      A_\pi^{\rm clip}
      \le
      \frac{\underline D_\pi}{\log^{K_{\rm den}}n}
      \le
      \frac{D_\pi}{\log^{K_{\rm den}}n}.
   \]
   Thus \((CDE3)\)--\((CDE5)\) hold for the returned profile, and
   \cref{cor:clipped-singleton-density-endpoint} gives the endpoint if this
   happens for every normalized residual.

   For the Las Vegas statement, the probability that the first \(B\)
   independent proposals all fail is at most \((1-p_E)^B\), so the
   repeat-until-accepted search terminates almost surely with expected at most
   \(1/p_E\) proposals.  Since only a deterministically verified certificate is
   retained, query work and storage are exactly those certified by the clipped
   density endpoint.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Logarithmic sampled-center separator endpoint]
   \label{cor:log-sampled-center-separator-endpoint}
   In the setting of
   \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint}, suppose the full
   certified panel universe \(\mathcal Z_\star\) contains every materializable
   low-correlation class-local profile record used in
   \cref{cor:gaussian-tuple-profile-witness-density} and every smaller-radius
   dense prefix that can be verified from a sampled reported-center panel.
   Assume that, at every resident node and for every normalized exact-signature
   price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\), preprocessing can certify a finite
   split-profile panel with sampled center laws, uniform over truncation levels
   as in \cref{cor:optimized-sampled-center-split-profile-residual}, such that
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi
      \left(
         B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo}
         -\Theta(B_\pi^{\rm hi},A_\pi^{\rm samp})
      \right)>0 .
      \tag{LSE1}
   \]
   Then the positive shared-panel separator \((SPP1)\) holds at every node.
   Consequently worst-case Euclidean ANN has
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   It is enough to prove the more explicit logarithmic sufficient condition
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi
      \left[
         B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo}
         -C_0A_\pi^{\rm samp}
         \left(
            1+\log_+\frac{B_\pi^{\rm hi}}{A_\pi^{\rm samp}}
         \right)
      \right]>0,
      \tag{LSE2}
   \]
   with the same convention as in \((OSR5)\) when
   \(A_\pi^{\rm samp}=0\).  In particular, if a certified panel has
   \[
      1+\log_+\frac{B_\pi^{\rm hi}}{A_\pi^{\rm samp}}\le H
      \qquad(\eta_\pi>0,\ A_\pi^{\rm samp}>0)
      \tag{LSE3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi(B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo})
      >
      C_0H\sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi A_\pi^{\rm samp},
      \tag{LSE4}
   \]
   then the same endpoint follows.  Thus the remaining sampled-center theorem
   may be phrased as an inverse-logarithmic benefit-density target: under every
   normalized residual, find a panel whose expected unreported center tail plus
   recursive star price is smaller than the residual benefit by the relevant
   logarithmic dynamic range.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a resident node and normalized exact-signature price system.  If
   \((LSE1)\) holds, then \((OSR3)\) is strictly violated.  By
   \cref{cor:optimized-sampled-center-split-profile-residual}, either a
   low-correlation profile record exposes positive shared-panel gain, or a
   sampled reported-center panel exposes a positive smaller-radius dense
   prefix.  In both cases the verified object is a member of
   \(\mathcal Z_\star\) by hypothesis, so
   \[
      \max_{z\in\mathcal Z_\star}
      \operatorname{PGain}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(z)>0 .
   \]
   Since the price system was arbitrary, \((SPP1)\) holds at the node.  Applying
   \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint} at every resident node
   gives the displayed query and storage bounds.

   The implication from \((LSE2)\) to \((LSE1)\) is \((OSR4)\), with \(C_0\)
   chosen as in \cref{cor:optimized-sampled-center-split-profile-residual}.
   Finally, \((LSE3)\)--\((LSE4)\) imply \((LSE2)\) by summing the pointwise
   upper bound
   \[
      C_0A_\pi^{\rm samp}
      \left(
         1+\log_+\frac{B_\pi^{\rm hi}}{A_\pi^{\rm samp}}
      \right)
      \le C_0H A_\pi^{\rm samp}.
   \]
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Single-profile logarithmic density screen]
   \label{cor:single-profile-log-density-screen}
   Work at one resident node in the setting of
   \cref{cor:log-sampled-center-separator-endpoint}.  Fix a normalized
   exact-signature price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\).  Suppose preprocessing
   can certify one split profile \(\pi\), with sampled center laws uniform over
   truncation levels, and a number \(H_\pi\ge1\) such that
   \[
      1+\log_+\frac{B_\pi^{\rm hi}}{A_\pi^{\rm samp}}\le H_\pi
      \qquad(A_\pi^{\rm samp}>0),
      \tag{SLD1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo}
      >
      C_0H_\pi A_\pi^{\rm samp}.
      \tag{SLD2}
   \]
   If \(A_\pi^{\rm samp}=0\), interpret \((SLD1)\) as vacuous and
   \((SLD2)\) as \(B_\pi>C_\pi^{\rm lo}\).  Then the fixed price system
   exposes either a positive low-correlation shared-panel record or one
   sampled high-correlation dense prefix.  Consequently, if such a profile can
   be certified for every normalized price system at every node, the
   \(d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n\) query and
   \(dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n\) storage endpoint follows.

   More generally, any finite weighted panel satisfying
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi(B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo})
      >
      C_0\sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi H_\pi A_\pi^{\rm samp}
      \tag{SLD3}
   \]
   with \((SLD1)\) for every active profile contains at least one profile
   satisfying \((SLD2)\).  Thus the sampled-center build oracle may search for
   one high-density profile at a time; panels are only a convenient averaging
   language.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For a single profile, conditions \((SLD1)\)--\((SLD2)\) are exactly
   \((LSE3)\)--\((LSE4)\) for the one-profile panel with \(H=H_\pi\).  Hence
   the conclusion follows from
   \cref{cor:log-sampled-center-separator-endpoint} restricted to the fixed
   price system: a violation of the logarithmic residual envelope exposes a
   verified positive panel column.

   For the panel statement, if every active profile failed \((SLD2)\), then
   multiplying those non-strict inequalities by \(\eta_\pi\) and summing would
   contradict \((SLD3)\).  Therefore some active profile satisfies
   \((SLD2)\), and the first part applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Inverted sampled-center density residual]
   \label{cor:inverted-sampled-center-density-residual}
   Work at one resident node in the setting of
   \cref{cor:single-profile-log-density-screen}, and suppose the current
   normalized exact-signature residual exposes no positive low-correlation
   shared-panel record and no sampled high-correlation dense prefix.  For any
   certified split profile with sampled center laws, put
   \[
      D_\pi=(B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo})_+,
      \qquad
      A_\pi=A_\pi^{\rm samp}.
      \tag{ISD1}
   \]
   If \(D_\pi>0\), then \(A_\pi>0\) and
   \[
      D_\pi
      \le
      C_0A_\pi
      \left(
         1+\log_+\frac{B_\pi^{\rm hi}}{A_\pi}
      \right).
      \tag{ISD2}
   \]
   Consequently there is a universal constant \(c_0>0\) such that every
   surviving residual satisfies
   \[
      A_\pi
      \ge
      c_0\,
      \frac{D_\pi}{
         1+\log_+\frac{B_\pi^{\rm hi}}{D_\pi}
      } .
      \tag{ISD3}
   \]
   Here \(\log_+0\) is interpreted as \(0\).

   Equivalently, a build-time proposal mechanism separates the residual if it
   certifies one profile with positive residual benefit \(D_\pi\) and sampled
   center price below the right-hand side of \((ISD3)\).  Thus the remaining
   density theorem may be phrased without the unknown denominator \(A_\pi\)
   inside the logarithm: sampled-center cost must be an inverse-logarithmic
   fraction of the residual benefit.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(D_\pi>0\) and \(A_\pi=0\), then \((SLD2)\) holds under the convention of
   \cref{cor:single-profile-log-density-screen}, contradicting survival of the
   residual.  Hence \(A_\pi>0\).  If \((ISD2)\) failed, then taking
   \(H_\pi=1+\log_+(B_\pi^{\rm hi}/A_\pi)\) would satisfy \((SLD1)\) and
   \((SLD2)\), again contradicting the residual hypothesis.  This proves
   \((ISD2)\).

   Let
   \[
      q=\frac{D_\pi}{C_0A_\pi},
      \qquad
      R=\frac{B_\pi^{\rm hi}}{D_\pi}.
   \]
   If \(q\le2\), then \(A_\pi\ge D_\pi/(2C_0)\), which is stronger than
   \((ISD3)\) after decreasing \(c_0\).  Assume \(q>2\).  From \((ISD2)\),
   \[
      q\le 1+\log_+(C_0qR).
      \tag{ISD4}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      L=2+\log_+R+\log_+(2C_0).
   \]
   Since \(q>2\), \((ISD4)\) implies
   \[
      q\le L+\log q .
      \tag{ISD5}
   \]
   For \(q\ge2\), \(\log q\le q/2\).  Hence \((ISD5)\) gives
   \(q\le2L\).  Substituting the definition of \(L\) and absorbing constants
   gives
   \[
      q
      \le
      C_1
      \left(
         1+\log_+R
      \right),
   \]
   and \((ISD3)\) follows with \(c_0=(C_0C_1)^{-1}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Polylog sampled-center density endpoint]
   \label{cor:polylog-sampled-center-density-endpoint}
   Work in the endpoint setting of
   \cref{cor:log-sampled-center-separator-endpoint}.  Fix constants
   \(K_{\rm dyn}\ge0\) and \(K_{\rm den}>1\).  Suppose that at every resident
   node of size at most \(n\), and for every normalized exact-signature price
   system satisfying \((ESNO1)\), preprocessing can certify one split profile
   \(\pi\) with sampled center laws uniform over truncation levels such that
   \[
      D_\pi=(B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo})_+>0,
      \tag{PSD1}
   \]
   \[
      B_\pi^{\rm hi}\le n^{K_{\rm dyn}}D_\pi,
      \tag{PSD2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      A_\pi^{\rm samp}
      \le
      \frac{D_\pi}{\log^{K_{\rm den}} n}.
      \tag{PSD3}
   \]
   Then, after increasing the logarithmic constants in the local budgets and
   treating bounded \(n\) by the resident scan base case, the positive
   shared-panel separator \((SPP1)\) holds at every node.  Consequently
   worst-case Euclidean ANN has
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   More quantitatively, it is enough for \((PSD3)\) to hold with
   \(\log^{K_{\rm den}}n\) replaced by
   \[
      2C_0
      \left(
         1+K_{\rm dyn}\log n+K_{\rm den}\log\log n
      \right),
      \tag{PSD4}
   \]
   for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Thus the remaining sampled-center
   proposal theorem may target a purely polylogarithmic density statement:
   the expected unreported center tail plus recursive star price should be
   smaller than the profile's residual benefit by any fixed power of \(\log n\)
   exceeding one, assuming only polynomial global dynamic range.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(A=A_\pi^{\rm samp}\) and \(D=D_\pi\).  If \(A=0\), then
   \cref{cor:single-profile-log-density-screen} applies immediately.  Otherwise
   \((PSD2)\)--\((PSD3)\) imply
   \[
      1+\log_+\frac{B_\pi^{\rm hi}}{A}
      \le
      1+K_{\rm dyn}\log n+K_{\rm den}\log\log n .
      \tag{PSD5}
   \]
   Under the quantitative hypothesis \((PSD4)\), this gives
   \[
      C_0A
      \left(
         1+\log_+\frac{B_\pi^{\rm hi}}{A}
      \right)
      \le D/2<D .
   \]
   Therefore \((SLD1)\)--\((SLD2)\) hold for
   \(H_\pi=1+\log_+(B_\pi^{\rm hi}/A)\), and
   \cref{cor:single-profile-log-density-screen} exposes a positive verified
   panel column for the fixed price system.  Since the price system was
   arbitrary, \((SPP1)\) holds at every node, and
   \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint} gives the displayed
   bounds.

   Finally, because \(K_{\rm den}>1\), for all sufficiently large \(n\),
   \[
      \log^{K_{\rm den}}n
      \ge
      2C_0
      \left(
         1+K_{\rm dyn}\log n+K_{\rm den}\log\log n
      \right).
   \]
   Hence \((PSD3)\) implies the quantitative hypothesis outside a bounded
   range of \(n\).  Bounded-size resident nodes are handled by direct scan and
   are absorbed into the constant in the logarithmic overhead.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One-sided polylog sampled-center profile oracle]
   \label{cor:one-sided-polylog-sampled-center-profile-oracle}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:polylog-sampled-center-density-endpoint}, and fix a finite universe
   \(\mathcal P_\star\) of materializable split profiles with sampled center
   laws.  A one-sided profile certificate consists of a profile
   \(\pi\in\mathcal P_\star\) and numbers
   \[
      \underline D_\pi,\qquad
      \overline B_\pi^{\rm hi},\qquad
      \overline A_\pi^{\rm samp}
   \]
   satisfying
   \[
      0<\underline D_\pi\le B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo},
      \qquad
      B_\pi^{\rm hi}\le\overline B_\pi^{\rm hi},
      \qquad
      A_\pi^{\rm samp}\le\overline A_\pi^{\rm samp}.
      \tag{OSP1}
   \]
   Suppose that at every resident node of size at most \(n\), and for every
   normalized exact-signature price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\), uncharged
   preprocessing has an oracle which returns such a certificate with
   \[
      \overline B_\pi^{\rm hi}\le n^{K_{\rm dyn}}\underline D_\pi,
      \tag{OSP2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \overline A_\pi^{\rm samp}
      \le
      \frac{\underline D_\pi}{\log^{K_{\rm den}}n}
      \qquad(K_{\rm den}>1),
      \tag{OSP3}
   \]
   or correctly certifies that no profile in \(\mathcal P_\star\) has such a
   one-sided certificate.  If the no-certificate outcome never occurs on a
   normalized residual, then the same
   \(d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n\) query and
   \(dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n\) storage endpoint follows.

   Conversely, if for some normalized residual the oracle certifies no such
   profile in \(\mathcal P_\star\), then every profile in the finite universe
   fails at least one of the three checkable conditions: positive certified
   residual benefit, polynomial certified dynamic range, or inverse-polylog
   sampled-center price.  This is the finite verifier format for build-time
   proposals: heuristics may propose candidates, but only one-sided certified
   density violations enter the retained column-generation process.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the oracle returns a certificate, then
   \(D_\pi=(B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo})_+\ge\underline D_\pi>0\).  Conditions
   \((OSP1)\)--\((OSP2)\) give
   \[
      B_\pi^{\rm hi}\le n^{K_{\rm dyn}}\underline D_\pi
      \le n^{K_{\rm dyn}}D_\pi,
   \]
   and \((OSP1)\)--\((OSP3)\) give
   \[
      A_\pi^{\rm samp}
      \le
      \frac{\underline D_\pi}{\log^{K_{\rm den}}n}
      \le
      \frac{D_\pi}{\log^{K_{\rm den}}n}.
   \]
   Thus the hypotheses \((PSD1)\)--\((PSD3)\) of
   \cref{cor:polylog-sampled-center-density-endpoint} hold for the returned
   profile.  If this happens for every normalized residual at every node, that
   corollary gives the endpoint.  The converse statement is just the meaning of
   a correct no-certificate report over the finite universe.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Las Vegas sampled-center profile oracle]
   \label{cor:las-vegas-sampled-center-profile-oracle}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:one-sided-polylog-sampled-center-profile-oracle}.  Suppose that,
   for each resident node and each normalized exact-signature price system,
   preprocessing has a randomized proposal law over candidate profiles and
   candidate numerical certificates.  A deterministic verifier accepts a
   proposal only when the proposed profile and numbers satisfy
   \((OSP1)\)--\((OSP3)\).

   Assume that whenever a profile in the finite universe
   \(\mathcal P_\star\) admits such a one-sided certificate, one proposal is
   accepted with probability at least \(p_E>0\).  Then repeating proposals
   until the first accepted certificate is a Las Vegas implementation of the
   profile oracle, with expected at most \(1/p_E\) proposal calls.  Rejected
   proposals and unverifiable certificates are discarded and are never charged
   to the retained index.

   Consequently, if every normalized residual has some profile in
   \(\mathcal P_\star\) admitting a certificate satisfying
   \((OSP1)\)--\((OSP3)\), and the proposal law hits one with positive
   probability, then the same
   \(d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n\) query and
   \(dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n\) storage endpoint follows.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed resident node and price system, the probability that the first
   \(B\) independent proposals are all rejected is at most \((1-p_E)^B\).
   Thus the repeat-until-accepted procedure terminates almost surely and has
   expected number of proposals at most \(1/p_E\).  Every accepted proposal is,
   by deterministic verification, a valid one-sided profile certificate in the
   sense of
   \cref{cor:one-sided-polylog-sampled-center-profile-oracle}.  Failed
   proposals are preprocessing artifacts only.  The retained column-generation
   process sees exactly the first accepted certified profile, so query work and
   storage are those certified by
   \cref{cor:one-sided-polylog-sampled-center-profile-oracle}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Min-cost split-profile separator endpoint]
   \label{cor:min-cost-split-profile-separator-endpoint}
   In the setting of
   \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint}, suppose the full
   certified panel universe \(\mathcal Z_\star\) contains:
   \begin{itemize}
      \item every materializable low-correlation class-local profile record
      used in \cref{cor:gaussian-tuple-profile-witness-density};
      \item every one-record smaller-radius dense prefix that can be certified
      by the paid pair-star verifier used in
      \cref{cor:paid-pair-star-panel-certificate}.
   \end{itemize}
   Assume that, for every resident node and every normalized exact-signature
   price system \((\beta,\tau,\theta)\) satisfying \((ESNO1)\), preprocessing
   can certify a finite nonnegative split-profile panel
   \((\Pi,\eta_\pi)\) in the sense of
   \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope} such that
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi
      \left(
         B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo}-\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \right)>0.
      \tag{MSP1}
   \]
   Then the positive shared-panel separator \((SPP1)\) holds at every node.
   Consequently worst-case Euclidean ANN has
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   Thus one remaining sufficient theorem for the polylogarithmic endpoint is
   the following purely fractional geometric statement: every normalized
   exact-signature dual admits a split-profile panel whose priced benefit
   exceeds low-correlation Gaussian witness congestion plus the optimized
   high-correlation dense-routing price.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a resident node and normalized price system.  By \((MSP1)\) and
   \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope}, either some low-correlation
   profile record exposes positive shared-panel gain, or the paid pair-star
   verifier exposes a positive smaller-radius dense prefix.  In the first case
   the record is a member of \(\mathcal Z_\star\) by hypothesis.  In the second
   case the corresponding one-record dense-prefix panel is also in
   \(\mathcal Z_\star\) by hypothesis.  Hence
   \[
      \max_{z\in\mathcal Z_\star}
      \operatorname{PGain}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(z)>0 .
   \]
   This is exactly \((SPP1)\) for the fixed dual.  Since the dual was
   arbitrary, \((SPP1)\) holds at the node.  Applying
   \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint} at every localized
   resident node gives the displayed query and storage bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Common child-panel residual endpoint]
   \label{cor:child-panel-split-profile-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-separator-endpoint}.  Suppose that every
   normalized exact-signature dual that reaches a no-prefix child-panel residual
   from \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-low-cover-screen},
   \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-packing-energy-screen},
   \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-high-correlation-return}, or
   \cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-cap-star-storage-split}, or from
   \cref{cor:generic-unsponsored-cut-generated-column} or
   \cref{cor:generic-unsponsored-cut-packing-energy}
   has the following certificate.  After discarding alternatives that already
   give a sponsor flow, a positive generated prefix, or a low-correlation
   entropy-energy payment, preprocessing can encode the remaining weighted
   packing/high-correlation signal as a finite split-profile panel
   \((\Pi,\eta)\) satisfying
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\eta_\pi
      \left(
         B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo}-\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \right)>0,
      \tag{CPE1}
   \]
   with all low-correlation records and high-correlation dense prefixes contained
   in the certified panel universe \(\mathcal Z_\star\).
   Then the positive shared-panel separator \((SPP1)\) holds at every node, and
   hence
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,\qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   Thus the generic child-panel, unsponsored-cut, sponsor-tail, and cap-overload
   branches leave one common theorem to prove: every normalized no-prefix
   weighted packing residual either is already paid by the certified
   low-correlation energy bound or admits a positive min-cost split-profile
   certificate.  The theorem is not a geometry-only storage statement; by
   \cref{lem:unsponsored-child-panel-obstruction}, duplicated child records must
   be handled by sponsorship, canonical generated merging, or this
   split-profile certificate.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The cited child-panel and unsponsored-cut reductions have only the following
   terminal alternatives.  A sponsor flow pays the represented storage directly
   by \cref{cor:generic-child-panel-sponsor-flow}.  A positive generated prefix
   or dense prefix is already a retained shared-panel column.  A
   low-correlation entropy-energy payment is one of the low records allowed in
   \(\mathcal Z_\star\).  If none of these alternatives occurs, the hypothesis
   gives a finite split-profile panel satisfying \((CPE1)\), which is exactly
   \((MSP1)\) for that normalized dual.  Therefore
   \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-separator-endpoint} supplies \((SPP1)\) for
   the dual.  Since the dual was arbitrary at the node,
   \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint} gives the displayed query
   and storage bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Common child-panel single-profile density endpoint]
   \label{cor:child-panel-single-profile-density-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:child-panel-split-profile-endpoint}.  Fix constants
   \(K_{\rm dyn}\ge0\) and \(K_{\rm den}>1\).  Suppose that, for every resident
   node of size at most \(n\) and every normalized exact-signature price system
   satisfying \((ESNO1)\), the generic child-panel and unsponsored-cut reductions
   have the following outcome.  Either a sponsor flow, positive generated prefix,
   low-correlation entropy-energy payment, or verified dense prefix already
   fires; or the surviving no-prefix weighted packing residual admits one split
   profile \(\pi\), with sampled-center laws uniform over truncation levels, such
   that
   \[
      D_\pi=(B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo})_+>0,
      \tag{CPD1}
   \]
   \[
      B_\pi^{\rm hi}\le n^{K_{\rm dyn}}D_\pi,
      \tag{CPD2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      A_\pi^{\rm samp}\le\frac{D_\pi}{\log^{K_{\rm den}}n},
      \tag{CPD3}
   \]
   with all low records and sampled high-correlation dense prefixes contained in
   the certified panel universe \(\mathcal Z_\star\).  Then the positive
   shared-panel separator \((SPP1)\) holds at every node, and hence
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,\qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   Thus the common child-panel residual can be attacked by a single-profile
   inverse-polylogarithmic density theorem.  The build-time search does not need
   to coordinate an aggregate split-profile panel: after the proved reductions,
   one profile whose sampled-center price is an inverse-logarithmic fraction of
   its residual benefit already separates the normalized dual.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a resident node and a normalized price system.  If one of the explicit
   terminal alternatives fires, it gives \((SPP1)\) exactly as in
   \cref{cor:child-panel-split-profile-endpoint}.  Otherwise take the profile
   \(\pi\) supplied by the hypothesis.  Conditions \((CPD1)\)--\((CPD3)\) are
   precisely the hypotheses \((PSD1)\)--\((PSD3)\) of
   \cref{cor:polylog-sampled-center-density-endpoint} for this fixed price
   system.  The proof of that corollary is pointwise: outside a bounded-size
   base case, \((CPD2)\)--\((CPD3)\) imply
   \[
      C_0A_\pi^{\rm samp}
      \left(
         1+\log_+\frac{B_\pi^{\rm hi}}{A_\pi^{\rm samp}}
      \right)
      <D_\pi ,
   \]
   so \cref{cor:single-profile-log-density-screen} exposes either a positive
   low-correlation shared-panel record or one sampled high-correlation dense
   prefix.  By the universe hypothesis, this verified object lies in
   \(\mathcal Z_\star\), so \((SPP1)\) holds for the fixed dual.  Since the dual
   and node were arbitrary, \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint}
   gives the displayed global query and storage bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Common child-panel shared-integrated endpoint]
   \label{cor:child-panel-shared-integrated-endpoint}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:child-panel-split-profile-endpoint}.  Suppose that, for every
   resident node of size at most \(n\) and every normalized exact-signature price
   system satisfying \((ESNO1)\), the generic child-panel and unsponsored-cut
   reductions have the following outcome.  Either a sponsor flow, positive
   generated prefix, low-correlation entropy-energy payment, or verified dense
   prefix already fires; or the surviving no-prefix weighted packing residual
   admits one split profile \(\pi\), an atomized high-correlation representation
   included in the admissible routing universe of
   \cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope}, a truncation
   \(0<\varepsilon_\pi\le1\), and shared integrated certificates satisfying
   \((SIH4)\), such that
   \[
      D_\pi=(B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo})_+>0
      \tag{CSI1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \varepsilon_\pi B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2\mathfrak E_{\Sigma,\pi}
      +4\mathfrak P_{\Sigma,\pi}
      <D_\pi ,
      \tag{CSI2}
   \]
   with all low records and shared high-correlation dense prefixes contained in
   the certified panel universe \(\mathcal Z_\star\).  Then the positive
   shared-panel separator \((SPP1)\) holds at every node, and hence
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,\qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]

   In particular, it is sufficient to certify polynomial dynamic range
   \(B_\pi^{\rm hi}\le n^{K_{\rm dyn}}D_\pi\) and
   \[
      2\mathfrak E_{\Sigma,\pi}
      +4\mathfrak P_{\Sigma,\pi}
      \le D_\pi/2,
      \tag{CSI3}
   \]
   because then one may take
   \(\varepsilon_\pi=\min\{1,1/(4n^{K_{\rm dyn}})\}\) outside the resident scan
   base case.

   Thus the strongest current child-panel target is an integrated shared-cover
   theorem, not a cut-local sampled-center theorem: the same dense record may
   capture mass from many layer-cake cuts while paying its recursive price once.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a resident node and a normalized price system.  If one of the explicit
   terminal alternatives fires, it gives \((SPP1)\) as in
   \cref{cor:child-panel-split-profile-endpoint}.  Otherwise take the profile
   and shared integrated certificates from the hypothesis.  If a shared
   star-prefix record fires while certifying \((SIH4)\), it is a positive column
   in \(\mathcal Z_\star\).  If not,
   \cref{cor:shared-integrated-high-correlation-tail} gives
   \[
      \Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}
      \le
      \varepsilon_\pi B_\pi^{\rm hi}
      +2\mathfrak E_{\Sigma,\pi}
      +4\mathfrak P_{\Sigma,\pi}
      <D_\pi .
   \]
   Hence \(B_\pi-C_\pi^{\rm lo}-\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}>0\), so the one-profile panel
   satisfies the min-cost split-profile condition for the fixed dual.
   \Cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope} exposes either a positive
   low-correlation shared-panel record or a positive dense prefix; by hypothesis
   the verified object lies in \(\mathcal Z_\star\).  Thus \((SPP1)\) holds for
   the fixed dual, and since the dual and node were arbitrary,
   \cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint} gives the displayed
   bounds.

   Under \((CSI3)\) and the displayed dynamic-range bound, the chosen
   \(\varepsilon_\pi\) gives
   \(\varepsilon_\pi B_\pi^{\rm hi}\le D_\pi/4\).  Together with \((CSI3)\), the
   left side of \((CSI2)\) is at most \(3D_\pi/4<D_\pi\).  Bounded resident nodes
   are handled by direct scan and absorbed into the logarithmic constants.
\end{proof}

The role of \cref{asm:weighted-dense-spherical-dichotomy} is now precise.  It is
not an additional recursion rule; it is the separation theorem that would prove
the finite signature LPs used in \cref{prop:fractional-filter-cover-polylog}
feasible.  Once feasibility is certified, the recursive accounting is already
closed because every dense child is priced by its full descendant cost.
The sharper paid-prefix route is the concrete way to prove that dichotomy:
\[
   \text{spherical primitive hit law}
   \Longrightarrow
   \text{paid hit-kernel cover}
   \Longrightarrow
   \text{finite signature filter cover}
   \Longrightarrow
   d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
\]
\Cref{cor:paid-prefix-hit-kernel-cover} supplies the middle implication once
the geometric separator violates a container-prefix envelope for every surplus
paid dual.  Equivalently, by
\cref{cor:list-proposal-hit-kernel-cover}, it is enough to produce a random
list, seeded list, or marginal-incidence list whose expected paid value beats
the query/storage list moments for every such surplus dual.  By
\cref{lem:query-layer-random-list-proposal} and
\cref{cor:query-layer-seeded-marginal-proposals}, any such successful
fractional-query certificate has an ordinary threshold query layer with the
same surplus.  Equivalently,
\cref{cor:boolean-query-layer-list-proposal-separator} states the remaining
list-proposal theorem directly in Boolean-query form, and
\cref{cor:joint-query-list-proposal-separator} lets the container, query layer,
and list be proposed jointly by an arbitrary seed law.
\Cref{cor:query-free-list-proposal-separator} removes the query-side proposal as
well: a law over container/list pairs is enough, because the verifier takes the
positive-margin query layer.  More generally,
\cref{cor:query-free-marginal-proposal-separator} allows the seed to output only
soft update marginals and a second-moment certificate; this is the fractional
form suited to overlapping dense filters, additive vector quantization, and
responsibility-weighted facility proposals.
\Cref{cor:independent-soft-proposal-separator} makes the default realization
explicit by independent thinning, replacing the second-moment certificate by the
checkable bound \(\mu+\mu^2\).
\Cref{cor:finite-soft-bucket-separation} then says that unbounded preprocessing
may search any finite soft-bucket universe by exact reduced-gain maximization;
only buckets whose verifier exposes a positive Boolean prefix are retained.
\Cref{cor:positive-soft-gain-hard-list} and
\cref{cor:finite-hard-list-separation} simplify this endpoint further: every
positive soft bucket already contains a positive hard-list certificate in the
same container, so the final separator may be stated purely over certified
container/list pairs with the canonical positive-margin query side.
\Cref{cor:hard-list-prefix-separation} then replaces arbitrary lists by
top-degree prefixes for ordinary query layers, which is the form naturally
served by range-reporting, tensor/list-decoding, and additive-code proposal
oracles.
\Cref{cor:fractional-query-prefix-separation} adds the matching convex
relaxation: fractional query prices may be used in the dual analysis, but a
positive fractional prefix certificate always thresholds to one Boolean query
layer before the filter is retained.
\Cref{cor:finite-prefix-separation} packages this as a finite oracle over
container/cardinality templates: positivity of the top-\(K\) reduced-cost
objective \((FPS1)\) is exactly the remaining dense column-generation
certificate.
\Cref{cor:hit-weighted-star-panel-prefix} shows that certified star panels are
one concrete way to satisfy this oracle: a panel with lower hit-weighted paid
mass and upper list-size certificates forces a positive paid prefix.
\Cref{cor:guarded-star-panel-local-cover} combines this with the spherical
reduced-gain residual: only price systems satisfying the normalized guard-mass
obstruction \((GSP1)\)--\((GSP3)\) need such a panel.
\Cref{cor:guarded-no-star-residual-envelope} records the corresponding
counterexample: large guard co-load must coexist with a no-star weak-type cap
on all certified smaller-radius containers.
\Cref{cor:guard-shadow-transport-reporter} states the positive form: any
bounded-congestion transport from that guard co-load into paid near-shadow mass
inside an affordable container immediately yields the missing star panel.
\Cref{cor:half-mass-guard-shadow-cut-obstruction} gives the negative form:
after fixing an affordable container, no panel implies a half-mass query cut
with too much guard load for its paid near shadow.
\Cref{lem:guard-shadow-credit-normal-form} and
\cref{cor:half-mass-guard-shadow-deficit-obstruction} give the equivalent
fractional form: every affordable container fails to credit more than half of
the guard load using its paid near-shadow capacity.
\Cref{cor:fractional-guard-credit-panel-reporter} and
\cref{cor:joint-fractional-guard-credit-cover} remove the last single-container
restriction: the verified object may be an overlapping fractional panel, with
query demand used once and recursive cost paid per container.
\Cref{cor:finite-guard-credit-flow-separator} gives the build-facing LP: a
finite proposal pool succeeds exactly by exposing positive verified
guard-credit surplus from whole certified containers.
\Cref{lem:finite-guard-credit-flow-dual} is the matching finite-pool
certificate of failure, so a proposal oracle only has to separate that explicit
dual obstruction.
\Cref{cor:one-template-guard-credit-separation} gives the corresponding
reduced objective for one additional proposal: after zero-load queries are
removed, find a certified container whose reachable paid-shadow degree \(D_B\)
satisfies \(D_B>R_B\).
\Cref{cor:scale-free-guard-credit-proposal} makes this a proposal-law
criterion over raw containers: positive expected \(D-R\) under any finite seed
law already contains a deterministic separating container.
\Cref{cor:lower-certified-scale-free-guard-panel} weakens the required
observable further to a lower certificate \(X\le D\), so the geometric reporter
may overestimate sizes and underestimate captured paid mass.
\Cref{cor:high-correlation-stars-feed-guard-credit} gives the current concrete
star-reporter objective: prove that the high-correlation incidence multiplicity
inside a smaller ball lower-bounds paid near-shadow mass by enough to make
\(X\) beat recursive price.
\Cref{cor:paid-responsibility-high-correlation-star} reduces this further to a
responsibility assignment problem: any subassignment of paid near-shadow mass to
high-correlation centers already provides valid lower certificates.
\Cref{cor:pair-compatible-guard-responsibility-star} gives a transport version:
if the large guard co-load can be shipped to paid near-shadow capacity
pair-by-pair with bounded congestion and high-correlation support, the
responsibility star separator follows.
\Cref{lem:pair-compatible-guard-cut-normal-form} records the matching
obstruction: some guard-incidence sublayer has more load than its neighboring
paid pair capacities, up to the allowed unshipped mass.
\Cref{cor:geometric-hall-pair-compatible-guard} is the half-mass version needed
for the dense proof: if a \(B_{\rm pc}/2\)-shipment fails, a guard sublayer of
load \(>B_{\rm pc}/2\) has too little high-correlation paid neighborhood.
\Cref{cor:pair-compatible-hall-guarded-cover} packages the positive side as the
remaining separator theorem: every guarded residual must have such a
half-shipment with enough direct star surplus.
Conversely,
\cref{cor:paid-prefix-residual-envelope} says that a failed dense separator has
only one possible form: a paid residual whose every certified container obeys
the weighted degree envelopes \((PPRE1)\)--\((PPRE2)\).  Thus the remaining
geometry is no longer an overlap or branching question; it is to show that such
a residual is either impossible after the spherical reduced-gain test, or is
itself spherical-pseudo-random enough to close the dichotomy.

\begin{corollary}[Paid-prefix separator gives a local filter cover]
   \label{cor:paid-prefix-local-filter-cover}
   Work in one finite local demand system
   \(\mathcal N\subseteq P\times\mathcal Q\).  Suppose a finite primitive
   spherical law produces high-correlation primitive slices \(V_{z,q}\), with
   hit kernel
   \[
      r_{p,q}=\sum_z\Pi(z)\mathbf 1\{p\in V_{z,q}\}
      \ge \pi_1>0
      \qquad((p,q)\in\mathcal N).
      \tag{PPLC1}
   \]
   Let the Boolean core universe contain the primitive singleton records and
   the query-side threshold activations of the paid-prefix records generated by
   a family \(\mathcal W\) satisfying
   \cref{asm:paid-atomized-prefix-separator}, with local budgets \(L,S\).
   Then the ordinary finite filter-cover LP
   \((\mathsf{FC}_{\mathcal N})\) is feasible over these Boolean core records,
   with query budget \(L\) for every \(q\in\mathcal Q\) and storage budget \(S\).

   Consequently, if the atom bounds of
   \cref{lem:poisson-filter-cover-materialization} hold, the same local
   certificate materializes into retained overlapping filters with only the
   usual logarithmic inflation in query and storage budgets.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{cor:paid-prefix-hit-kernel-cover}, the paid-prefix separator gives a
   feasible primitive hit-kernel cover
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\).  Let \(\lambda_R\) be such a feasible
   solution and scale it by
   \[
      \widehat\lambda_R=\lambda_R/\pi_1 .
   \]
   For every demanded pair, \((PPLC1)\) gives
   \[
      \sum_R\widehat\lambda_R b_R(p,q)
      \ge
      r_{p,q}/\pi_1
      \ge1 .
   \]
   The query and storage constraints of
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) are \(\pi_1L\) and \(\pi_1S\), so the scaled
   solution has query load at most \(L\) at every query constraint and storage
   at most \(S\).  Interpreting each Boolean core record \(R=(U_R,Q'_R)\) as
   the filter \(A_R=(U_R,\mathbf 1_{Q'_R},T_R,S_R)\), these are exactly the
   constraints of \((\mathsf{FC}_{\mathcal N})\).  The materialization statement
   is \cref{lem:poisson-filter-cover-materialization}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite prefix separator gives a local filter cover]
   \label{cor:finite-prefix-local-filter-cover}
   Work in the local setting of
   \cref{cor:paid-prefix-local-filter-cover}, with the same primitive hit
   kernel satisfying \((PPLC1)\), budgets \(L,S\), and finite demand system
   \(\mathcal N\).  Instead of assuming the abstract paid-prefix separator,
   suppose the Boolean core universe and a finite prefix-template pool satisfy
   the hypotheses of \cref{cor:finite-prefix-separation} for every nonnegative
   paid price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\).  Then the ordinary finite filter-cover LP
   \((\mathsf{FC}_{\mathcal N})\) is feasible with query budget \(L\) for every
   \(q\in\mathcal Q\) and storage budget \(S\).

   Consequently, under the atom bounds of
   \cref{lem:poisson-filter-cover-materialization}, the local certificate
   materializes into retained overlapping filters with logarithmic query and
   storage inflation.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{cor:finite-prefix-separation}, the finite prefix-template
   hypothesis gives feasibility of the primitive hit-kernel cover
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\).  Scaling that feasible solution by
   \(1/\pi_1\) and interpreting each Boolean core as a filter column is exactly
   the argument in the proof of \cref{cor:paid-prefix-local-filter-cover}.
   The same materialization corollary applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Paid-prefix separator endpoint]
   \label{prop:paid-prefix-polylog-endpoint}
   Fix \(c>1\) and \(\rho_c=1/(2c^2-1)\).  Suppose that after bounded-diameter
   localization, every resident node \(P\), \(|P|=N\), has a finite-signature
   system as in \cref{lem:finite-signature-filter-cover}, with decoder time
   \(d\,N^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n\), signature entropy satisfying \((FE1)\), and
   local budgets
   \[
      L=N^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S=N^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
      \tag{PPE1}
   \]
   Assume that, for the induced finite demand set
   \[
      \mathcal N_\Sigma
      =
      \{(p,\sigma_0):\sigma_0\in\Sigma,\ p\in W_{\sigma_0}\},
   \]
   preprocessing supplies a primitive spherical law and a paid-prefix family
   satisfying the hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:paid-prefix-local-filter-cover}.  Each nonterminal paid prefix is
   a strictly smaller certified child and is charged by its full descendant
   query and storage prices.

   Then worst-case Euclidean ANN has query time and space
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
   At each resident node, apply
   \cref{cor:paid-prefix-local-filter-cover} to the finite demand set
   \(\mathcal N_\Sigma\).  This gives feasibility of the finite-signature cover
   LP with uniform budget \(L\), hence with
   \(L_{\sigma_0}\le L\) for every signature.  The storage budget is \(S\).
   Thus the hypotheses \((FE1)\)--\((FE2)\) of
   \cref{prop:fractional-filter-cover-polylog} hold at every node.  That
   proposition gives the displayed global query and space bounds, because the
   paid-prefix columns are ordinary filters and their prices are full
   descendant prices, so their overlap has already been charged locally.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite prefix separator endpoint]
   \label{cor:finite-prefix-polylog-endpoint}
   In \cref{prop:paid-prefix-polylog-endpoint}, the nodewise local-cover
   hypothesis supplied by \cref{cor:paid-prefix-local-filter-cover} may be
   replaced by the finite prefix-template hypothesis supplied by
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-local-filter-cover}.  Under this replacement the same
   worst-case Euclidean ANN bounds hold:
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n .
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Use \cref{cor:finite-prefix-local-filter-cover} at every resident node in
   place of \cref{cor:paid-prefix-local-filter-cover}.  This gives the same
   finite-signature filter-cover feasibility with the same local budgets
   \((PPE1)\).  The recursive accounting is then unchanged from
   \cref{prop:paid-prefix-polylog-endpoint}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Certified scalar-reporter endpoint]
   \label{cor:certified-scalar-reporter-polylog-endpoint}
   Fix \(c>1\) and \(\rho_c=1/(2c^2-1)\).  Suppose that after bounded-diameter
   localization, every resident node \(P\), \(|P|=N\), has a finite-signature
   system as in \cref{lem:finite-signature-filter-cover}, with decoder time
   \(d\,N^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n\), signature entropy satisfying \((FE1)\), and
