      \int_{\substack{Y,i:\ \xi/2\le k_i(Y)/m\le\xi\\
                      p\in P_i(Y)\subseteq\Ball(q,cr)}}
      L_Y(q)^{s_\alpha}
      \left(\frac{k_i(Y)}m\right)^\rho
      \bigl(r_i^\alpha-r_{i+1}^\alpha\bigr)\,d\gamma_t(Y)
      \ge c_c .
      \tag{ILL2}
   \]
   Every hidden label counted in \((ILL2)\) reports a leader in
   \(\Ball(q,cr)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The identity for \(W_{q,\xi}\) is \((LI)\) summed over leaders.  Before the
   quotient, it is exactly the total active-prefix intensity at scale \(\xi\).
   Since every prefix on this scale has mass
   \(\mu_i(Y)=k_i(Y)/m\ge\xi/2\),
   \[
      W_{q,\xi}
      =
      \int_{\xi/2\le\mu_i(Y)\le\xi}d\lambda_q(Y,i)
      \le
      (\xi/2)^{-\rho}
      \int_{\xi/2\le\mu_i(Y)\le\xi}\mu_i(Y)^\rho\,d\lambda_q(Y,i).
   \]
   The last integral is the active \(\rho\)-moment bounded by
   \cref{lem:ideal-likelihood-scale-profile}; hence \((ILL1)\), after
   absorbing the fixed dependence on \(c,\rho,\alpha\) into \(C_c\).

   Let \(V_\xi\) be the pure negative-moment contribution at scale \(\xi\):
   \[
      V_\xi=
      \int_{\substack{Y,i:\ \xi/2\le\mu_i(Y)\le\xi\\
                      p\in P_i(Y)\subseteq\Ball(q,cr)}}
      L_Y(q)^{s_\alpha}
      \bigl(r_i^\alpha-r_{i+1}^\alpha\bigr)\,d\gamma_t(Y).
   \]
   By \cref{lem:ideal-likelihood-scale-profile} and
   \cref{thm:continuous-likelihood-balls},
   \(\sum_{\xi\le\eta}V_\xi\ge\delta_c\).  On the scale \(\xi\),
   \(\mu_i(Y)^\rho\ge(\xi/2)^\rho\), so the contribution of the same pure
   labels to the left-hand side of \((ILL2)\) is at least
   \(2^{-\rho}V_\xi\).  Summing over scales gives
   \(c_c=2^{-\rho}\delta_c\).  If the counted prefix is pure, then its leader
   belongs to \(P_i(Y)\subseteq\Ball(q,cr)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Scale-amplified likelihood collapses to max-tilted leaders]
   \label{lem:scale-amplified-alpha-leader}
   In the notation of \cref{lem:likelihood-rank-prefix}, let
   \[
      M_Y=\max_{x\in S}L_Y(x),
      \qquad
      \ell(Y)\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in S}L_Y(x)
   \]
   with deterministic tie-breaking.  Let the dyadic scale windows
   \([\xi/2,\xi]\), \(\xi\in[1/m,1]\), partition the possible prefix masses.
   Then, for every fixed \(Y\),
   \[
      2^{-\rho}M_Y^\alpha
      \le
      \sum_{\xi}\xi^{-\rho}B_\xi(Y)
      \le
      M_Y^\alpha .
      \tag{AL1}
   \]
   Thus the scale-amplified quotient posterior process is, up to constants
   depending only on \(\rho\), the max-tilted leader process with point
   intensities
   \[
      \widetilde\Lambda_q(x)
      =
      \int_{\{\ell(Y)=x\}}
      L_Y(q)^{s_\alpha}M_Y^\alpha\,d\gamma_t(Y).
      \tag{AL2}
   \]

   If
   \[
      \alpha=\kappa/\log m,\qquad
      t=C_c\log m/r^2
   \]
   with \(\kappa=\kappa(c)\) sufficiently small and \(C_c=C_c(c)\)
   sufficiently large, then the total mass of \((AL2)\) is bounded by a
   constant:
   \[
      \widetilde W_q=\sum_x\widetilde\Lambda_q(x)
      =
      \int L_Y(q)^{s_\alpha}M_Y^\alpha\,d\gamma_t(Y)
      \le C_c .
      \tag{AL3}
   \]
   Moreover, for every near pair \(\|p-q\|\le r\),
   \[
      \sum_{x\in S\cap\Ball(q,cr)}\widetilde\Lambda_q(x)\ge c_c .
      \tag{AL4}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For fixed \(Y\), write
   \(\mu_i(Y)=k_i(Y)/m\) and
   \(\Delta_i(Y)=r_i^\alpha-r_{i+1}^\alpha\).  Each rank prefix belongs to a
   unique dyadic window \([\xi/2,\xi]\), and on that window
   \[
      2^{-\rho}\le \xi^{-\rho}\mu_i(Y)^\rho\le1 .
   \]
   Let \(\xi(i)\) denote this unique dyadic scale for prefix \(i\).  Therefore
   \[
      \sum_{\xi}\xi^{-\rho}B_\xi(Y)
      =
      \sum_i \xi(i)^{-\rho}\mu_i(Y)^\rho\Delta_i(Y)
   \]
   lies between \(2^{-\rho}\sum_i\Delta_i(Y)\) and
   \(\sum_i\Delta_i(Y)\).  The latter sum telescopes to
   \(r_1^\alpha=M_Y^\alpha\), proving \((AL1)\).  Since every prefix reports
   the same leader \(\ell(Y)\), multiplying the scale-\(\xi\) process by
   \(\xi^{-\rho}\) and summing over scales gives \((AL2)\) up to the constants
   in \((AL1)\).

   For the total mass, put \(Z_Y=m^{-1}\sum_{x\in S}L_Y(x)\).  Since
   \(M_Y\le mZ_Y\),
   \[
      M_Y^\alpha\le m^\alpha Z_Y^\alpha .
   \]
   The Jensen/affinity calculation in
   \cref{lem:ideal-likelihood-scale-profile} gives
   \[
      \int L_Y(q)^{s_\alpha}Z_Y^\alpha\,d\gamma_t(Y)\le1.
   \]
   Because \(m^\alpha=e^\kappa\), this proves \((AL3)\).

   For the valid mass, use the tilted probability measure proportional to
   \[
      L_Y(p)^\alpha L_Y(q)^{s_\alpha}\,d\gamma_t(Y).
   \]
   Its normalizing constant is
   \[
      A_{p,q}
      =
      \exp\!\left(-\frac{\alpha s_\alpha t}{2}\|p-q\|^2\right)
      \ge c_c
   \]
   for the displayed choice of \(\alpha,t\).  The same Gaussian margin
   calculation as in \cref{thm:continuous-likelihood-balls} shows that, after
   increasing \(C_c\), with tilted probability at least \(1-O(m^{-2})\) every
   invalid point \(z\notin\Ball(q,cr)\) satisfies \(L_Y(z)<L_Y(p)\).  On this
   event the leader \(\ell(Y)\) is valid and \(M_Y^\alpha\ge L_Y(p)^\alpha\).
   Hence
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \sum_{x\in S\cap\Ball(q,cr)}\widetilde\Lambda_q(x)
      &=
      \int L_Y(q)^{s_\alpha}M_Y^\alpha
      \mathbf 1_{\{\ell(Y)\in\Ball(q,cr)\}}\,d\gamma_t(Y)\\
      &\ge
      A_{p,q}(1-O(m^{-2}))
      \ge c_c ,
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   after adjusting the constant.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Voronoi-capture form of the max-tilted leader law]
   \label{lem:alpha-leader-voronoi-capture}
   Work in the notation of \cref{lem:scale-amplified-alpha-leader}, and let
   \(s_\alpha=1-\alpha\).  For a point \(x\in S\), let
   \[
      \mathcal V_x
      =
      \{Y:\ell(Y)=x\}
   \]
   be its score-leader cell, using the same deterministic tie-breaking as
   before.  Then the max-tilted leader intensity has the exact form
   \[
      \widetilde\Lambda_q(x)
      =
      \int_{\mathcal V_x}
      L_Y(q)^{s_\alpha}L_Y(x)^\alpha\,d\gamma_t(Y)
      \tag{VC1}
   \]
   and, after writing \(Z=Y/t\),
   \[
      \widetilde\Lambda_q(x)
      =
      \exp\!\left(
         -\frac{\alpha s_\alpha t}{2}\|x-q\|^2
      \right)
      \Pr\!\left[
         x=\operatorname{NN}_S(Z)
      \right],
      \tag{VC2}
   \]
   where
   \[
      Z\sim
      N\!\left(s_\alpha q+\alpha x,\frac1t I_d\right)
   \]
   and \(\operatorname{NN}_S\) denotes exact nearest neighbor in \(S\) with the
   same tie-breaking.  Consequently,
   \[
      \widetilde\Lambda_q(x)
      \le
      \exp\!\left(
         -\frac{\alpha s_\alpha t}{2}\|x-q\|^2
      \right).
      \tag{VC3}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   On the cell \(\mathcal V_x\), the maximum likelihood is \(M_Y=L_Y(x)\).
   Substituting this into \((AL2)\) gives \((VC1)\).

   The Gaussian affinity identity used in
   \cref{thm:continuous-likelihood-balls} gives, for every measurable event
   \(E\),
   \[
      \int_E L_Y(q)^{s_\alpha}L_Y(x)^\alpha\,d\gamma_t(Y)
      =
      \exp\!\left(
         -\frac{\alpha s_\alpha t}{2}\|x-q\|^2
      \right)
      \Pr_{Y\sim N(t(s_\alpha q+\alpha x),tI_d)}[Y\in E].
   \]
   Apply this with \(E=\mathcal V_x\).  Finally,
   \[
      L_Y(z)
      =
      \exp\!\left(
         \frac{t}{2}\|Y/t\|^2
         -\frac{t}{2}\|z-Y/t\|^2
      \right),
   \]
   so maximizing \(L_Y(z)\) over \(z\in S\) is exactly nearest-neighbor
   search for \(Z=Y/t\) with the same tie-breaking.  This proves \((VC2)\).
   The upper bound \((VC3)\) follows because the probability in \((VC2)\) is
   at most one.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Query-centered nearest-cell reweighting]
   \label{cor:query-centered-cell-reweighting}
   Suppose the localized node lies in dimension \(D\).  Let
   \[
      H\ge\max\{D,\log m,2\},\qquad
      \alpha=\kappa/H,\qquad
      t=C H/r^2 ,
      \tag{QC0}
   \]
   where \(\kappa=\kappa(c)>0\) is sufficiently small and
   \(C=C(c)>0\) is sufficiently large.  Then the total-mass and valid-mass
   conclusions \((AL3)\)--\((AL4)\) of
   \cref{lem:scale-amplified-alpha-leader} remain true for the max-tilted law
   \((AL2)\) with these parameters.

   Let \(Z\sim N(q,I_D/t)\), and let
   \[
      N_S(Z)=\operatorname{NN}_S(Z)
   \]
   be the exact nearest resident point with the fixed tie-breaking.  Define
   \[
      R_q(Z)
      =
      \exp\!\left(
         \frac{\alpha t}{2}
         \bigl(\|Z-q\|^2-\|Z-N_S(Z)\|^2\bigr)
      \right).
      \tag{QC1}
   \]
   For every \(A\subseteq S\),
   \[
      \sum_{x\in A}\widetilde\Lambda_q(x)
      =
      \E_{Z\sim N(q,I_D/t)}
      \left[
         \mathbf 1_{\{N_S(Z)\in A\}}R_q(Z)
      \right].
      \tag{QC2}
   \]
   Moreover, for every \(L\ge0\),
   \[
      \E\left[
         R_q(Z)\mathbf 1_{\{\log R_q(Z)>L\}}
      \right]
      \le
      e^{2\kappa}e^{-L}.
      \tag{QC3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Reinspect the proofs of \cref{thm:continuous-likelihood-balls} and
   \cref{lem:scale-amplified-alpha-leader}.  They use
   \(\alpha t r^2=\Theta_c(1)\), \(t r^2\ge C_c\log m\), and
   \(m^\alpha=O_c(1)\).  The parameter choice \((QC0)\) has all three
   properties: \(\alpha t r^2=\kappa C\),
   \(t r^2\ge C\log m\), and \(m^\alpha\le e^\kappa\).  Taking \(C\) large
   enough for the Gaussian separation tail and \(\kappa\) small enough for the
   affinity constants therefore gives \((AL3)\)--\((AL4)\) with adjusted
   constants.

   To prove \((QC2)\), use \((VC2)\) and compare the Gaussian law
   \(N(q+\alpha(x-q),I_D/t)\) with \(N(q,I_D/t)\).  For
   \(u=x-q\), the density ratio at \(Z\) is
   \[
      \exp\!\left(
         \alpha t\langle Z-q,u\rangle
         -\frac{\alpha^2t}{2}\|u\|^2
      \right).
   \]
   Multiplying by the affinity factor
   \(\exp(-\alpha(1-\alpha)t\|u\|^2/2)\) from \((VC2)\) gives
   \[
      \exp\!\left(
         \alpha t\langle Z-q,u\rangle
         -\frac{\alpha t}{2}\|u\|^2
      \right)
      =
      \exp\!\left(
         \frac{\alpha t}{2}
         (\|Z-q\|^2-\|Z-x\|^2)
      \right).
   \]
   On the event \(N_S(Z)=x\), this is exactly \(R_q(Z)\).  Summing over
   \(x\in A\) proves \((QC2)\).

   Finally,
   \[
      \log R_q(Z)
      \le
      \frac{\alpha t}{2}\|Z-q\|^2
      =
      \frac{\alpha}{2}\chi_D^2 ,
   \]
   where \(\chi_D^2\) denotes a chi-square random variable with \(D\) degrees
   of freedom.  Since
   \[
      R_q(Z)\mathbf 1_{\{\log R_q(Z)>L\}}
      \le e^{-L}R_q(Z)^2 ,
   \]
   we get
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \E\left[R_q(Z)\mathbf 1_{\{\log R_q(Z)>L\}}\right]
      &\le
      e^{-L}
      \E\exp\!\left(\alpha\chi_D^2\right)\\
      &=
      e^{-L}(1-2\alpha)^{-D/2}
      \le
      e^{2\kappa}e^{-L},
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   after decreasing \(\kappa\) so that \(\alpha\le1/4\), and using
   \(\alpha D\le\kappa\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Truncated nearest-cell sampler compiler]
   \label{cor:truncated-nearest-cell-compiler}
   Work in the setting and with the dimension-aware parameters of
   \cref{cor:query-centered-cell-reweighting}.  Suppose a retained query
   primitive can return \(N_S(Z)\) exactly for any query point \(Z\), with
   query work \(T_{\rm cell}(m)\) and retained space \(S_{\rm cell}(m)\).
   Let \(B=\log^{A_c}m\), with \(A_c\) large enough.  One trial of the
   following rejection procedure costs \(T_{\rm cell}(m)+O(D)\):
   sample \(Z\sim N(q,I_D/t)\), compute \(x=N_S(Z)\), put
   \[
      \Delta(Z)=
      \frac{\alpha t}{2}
      \bigl(\|Z-q\|^2-\|Z-x\|^2\bigr),
   \]
   and accept \(x\) with probability \(e^{\Delta(Z)}/B\) if
   \(\Delta(Z)\le\log B\), rejecting otherwise.

   If a near pair exists in the localized node, then
   \(O_c(B)\) independent trials, followed by ordinary metric verification of
   accepted points, return a valid \(cr\)-neighbor with constant probability.
   The query work is
   \[
      O_c\!\left(B(T_{\rm cell}(m)+D)\right)
   \]
   and the retained space is \(S_{\rm cell}(m)+dm\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \((QC2)\), the untruncated acceptance numerator over any set
   \(A\subseteq S\) is exactly \(\sum_{x\in A}\widetilde\Lambda_q(x)\).  The
   truncation discards only the mass where \(\log R_q(Z)>\log B\).  By
   \((QC3)\), the total discarded mass is at most \(e^{2\kappa}/B\).  Taking
   \(A_c\) large makes this less than half of the valid mass lower bound
   \(c_c\) in \((AL4)\).  Thus one trial accepts a valid point with probability
   at least
   \[
      \frac{c_c/2}{B}.
   \]
   Repeating \(O_c(B)\) times gives constant probability of at least one
   accepted valid point.  Every accepted point is verified in the original
   metric, so invalid accepted points do not cause false positives.  The work
   and space bounds are immediate.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Smoothed witness-list compiler]
   \label{lem:smoothed-witness-list-compiler}
   Work in the setting and with the dimension-aware parameters of
   \cref{cor:query-centered-cell-reweighting}.  Fix a query \(q\), a near
   witness \(p\in S\cap\Ball(q,r)\), and a retained candidate-list routine
   which, on input \((q,Z)\), returns a set
   \[
      \mathcal L(q,Z)\subseteq S .
   \]
   Put
   \[
      R_{p,q}(Z)
      =
      \exp\!\left(
         \frac{\alpha t}{2}
         \bigl(\|Z-q\|^2-\|Z-p\|^2\bigr)
      \right),
      \qquad Z\sim N(q,I_D/t).
      \tag{WL0}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \E R_{p,q}(Z)
      =
      \exp\!\left(
         -\frac{\alpha(1-\alpha)t}{2}\|p-q\|^2
      \right)
      \ge a_c>0 ,
      \tag{WL1}
   \]
   where \(a_c\) depends only on \(c\).  Suppose further that the list routine
   has tilted witness loss
   \[
      \E\left[
         R_{p,q}(Z)\mathbf 1_{\{p\notin\mathcal L(q,Z)\}}
      \right]
      \le a_c/4 .
      \tag{WL2}
   \]
   Let \(B=\log^{A_c}m\), with \(A_c\) large enough.  One trial of the
   following procedure succeeds with probability at least
   \(\Omega_c(1/B)\): sample \(Z\sim N(q,I_D/t)\), form
   \(\mathcal L(q,Z)\), verify all listed candidates in the original metric,
   and for every verified valid \(x\in\mathcal L(q,Z)\cap\Ball(q,cr)\) define
   \[
      \Delta_x(Z)=
      \frac{\alpha t}{2}
      \bigl(\|Z-q\|^2-\|Z-x\|^2\bigr).
   \]
   Let
   \[
      W_{\rm val}(Z)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{x\in\mathcal L(q,Z)\cap\Ball(q,cr)\\
                      \Delta_x(Z)\le\log B}}
      e^{\Delta_x(Z)} .
   \]
   Accept with probability \(\min\{1,W_{\rm val}(Z)/B\}\); conditional on
   accepting, return a listed valid point with probability proportional to
   \(e^{\Delta_x(Z)}\) over the capped valid candidates.  Thus
   \(O_c(B)\) independent trials return a valid \(cr\)-neighbor with constant
   probability.  The query work is \(O_c(B)\) times the cost of producing and
   verifying one list.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The identity \((WL1)\) is the same Gaussian affinity calculation used above:
   multiplying the density of \(N(q,I_D/t)\) by \(R_{p,q}\) gives the density
   of \(N((1-\alpha)q+\alpha p,I_D/t)\), times the normalizing factor
   displayed in \((WL1)\).  Since \(\|p-q\|\le r\) and
   \(\alpha t r^2=\Theta_c(1)\), this factor is bounded below by a positive
   constant \(a_c\).

   As in the proof of \((QC3)\),
   \[
      \Delta_p(Z)
      \le
      \frac{\alpha t}{2}\|Z-q\|^2
      =
      \frac{\alpha}{2}\chi_D^2 ,
   \]
   and therefore
   \[
      \E\left[
         R_{p,q}(Z)\mathbf 1_{\{\Delta_p(Z)>\log B\}}
      \right]
      \le e^{2\kappa}/B .
      \tag{WL3}
   \]
   On the event \(p\in\mathcal L(q,Z)\) and \(\Delta_p(Z)\le\log B\), the
   candidate \(p\) is valid and contributes \(e^{\Delta_p(Z)}\) to
   \(W_{\rm val}(Z)\).  Because \(e^{\Delta_p(Z)}\le B\),
   \[
      \min\{1,W_{\rm val}(Z)/B\}
      \ge
      B^{-1}R_{p,q}(Z)
      \mathbf 1_{\{p\in\mathcal L(q,Z),\,\Delta_p(Z)\le\log B\}} .
   \]
   Taking expectations and using \((WL1)\)--\((WL3)\) gives one-trial success
   probability at least
   \[
      \frac1B\left(a_c-a_c/4-e^{2\kappa}/B\right)
      =
      \Omega_c(1/B),
   \]
   after choosing \(A_c\) large.  The returned point is explicitly verified,
   so false positives cannot occur.  Independent repetition gives constant
   success probability.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Facility-bucket witness form]
   \label{cor:facility-bucket-witness}
   In the setting of \cref{lem:smoothed-witness-list-compiler}, suppose the
   retained structure consists of bucket sets \(\{S_a:a\in\mathcal A\}\) and a
   query reporter which, on input \((q,Z)\), outputs labels
   \(\mathcal A(q,Z)\subseteq\mathcal A\).  Let
   \[
      \mathcal L(q,Z)=\bigcup_{a\in\mathcal A(q,Z)}S_a .
   \]
   If, for every near pair \(p,q\),
   \[
      \E\left[
         R_{p,q}(Z)
         \mathbf 1_{\{p\notin\bigcup_{a\in\mathcal A(q,Z)}S_a\}}
      \right]
      \le a_c/4,
      \tag{FB1}
   \]
   and the reported bucket union has expected scan size
   \(m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m\), then \(O_c(\log^{A_c}m)\) trials of the bucket
   procedure return a valid neighbor with constant probability using expected
   scan work \(D\,m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m\), up to the cost of reporting the
   labels.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{lem:smoothed-witness-list-compiler} to the candidate list
   \(\mathcal L(q,Z)\).  The scan-size assumption bounds the verification work,
   and \((FB1)\) is exactly the tilted witness-loss condition \((WL2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Poisson multi-assignment rate coverage]
   \label{lem:poisson-rate-coverage}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:smoothed-witness-list-compiler}.  Let
   \(\mathcal A\) be a finite label universe.  For every point \(x\in S\), let
   \(\mu_x\) be a probability distribution on \(\mathcal A\), and let
   \(a_x\ge0\) be its replication budget.  During preprocessing, draw a
   Poisson number \(N_x\) of labels with mean \(a_x\), independently over
   points, and place \(x\) into each sampled label bucket.  A query reporter,
   on input \((q,Z)\), returns a set of labels
   \(\mathcal A(q,Z)\subseteq\mathcal A\), and the candidate list is the union
   of the reported buckets.

   For a label set \(B\subseteq\mathcal A\), write
   \[
      \mu_x(B)=\sum_{a\in B}\mu_x(a).
   \]
   Conditional on \(\mathcal A(q,Z)=B\), the probability over preprocessing
   that a fixed point \(p\) is absent from the reported bucket union is exactly
   \[
      \exp(-a_p\mu_p(B)).
      \tag{RC0}
   \]
   Consequently, if for every near pair \(p,q\),
   \[
      \E_{Z\sim N(q,I_D/t)}
      \left[
         R_{p,q}(Z)
         \exp(-a_p\mu_p(\mathcal A(q,Z)))
      \right]
      \le a_c/4 ,
      \tag{RC1}
   \]
   then the randomized bucket structure satisfies the tilted witness-loss
   condition \((WL2)\) in expectation over preprocessing.  If in addition, for
   every query \(q\),
   \[
      \E_{Z\sim N(q,I_D/t)}
      \sum_{x\in S}a_x\mu_x(\mathcal A(q,Z))
      \le
      m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m ,
      \tag{RC2}
   \]
   then the expected reported incidence count per trial is
   \(m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m\).  The expected stored incidence count is
   \[
      \sum_{x\in S}a_x .
      \tag{RC3}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Poisson thinning gives \((RC0)\): among the \(N_p\) independent labels drawn
   for \(p\), the number landing in \(B\) is Poisson with mean
   \(a_p\mu_p(B)\).  Thus no copy of \(p\) appears in a reported bucket with
   probability \(\exp(-a_p\mu_p(B))\).

   Multiplying this conditional miss probability by the tilted weight
   \(R_{p,q}(Z)\) and averaging over \(Z\) gives \((RC1)\), which is exactly the
   expectation form of \((WL2)\).  For the load, a point \(x\) contributes to
   the reported incidence count with expected multiplicity
   \(a_x\mu_x(\mathcal A(q,Z))\) conditional on \(Z\).  Summing over points and
   averaging gives \((RC2)\).  Finally, the expected total number of stored
   incidences is the sum of the Poisson means, proving \((RC3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Intensity form of rate coverage]
   \label{cor:rate-coverage-intensity}
   The normalized laws \(\mu_x\) in \cref{lem:poisson-rate-coverage} are only a
   parametrization.  Equivalently, assign a nonnegative intensity
   \(b_{x,a}\ge0\) to every point-label pair and, during preprocessing, place
   \(x\) into bucket \(a\) with independent Poisson multiplicity of mean
   \(b_{x,a}\).  For \(B\subseteq\mathcal A\), write
   \[
      b_x(B)=\sum_{a\in B}b_{x,a}.
   \]
   Then the miss probability for \(p\) from reported labels \(B\) is
   \[
      \exp(-b_p(B)),
      \tag{RI0}
   \]
   the expected reported incidence count for a query outcome \(B\) is
   \[
      \sum_{x\in S}b_x(B),
      \tag{RI1}
   \]
   and the expected stored incidence count is
   \[
      \sum_{x\in S}\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}b_{x,a}.
      \tag{RI2}
   \]
   Thus the rate-coverage conditions are exactly
   \[
      \E_Z\left[
         R_{p,q}(Z)\exp(-b_p(\mathcal A(q,Z)))
      \right]\le a_c/4
      \tag{RI3}
   \]
   for every near pair \(p,q\), and
   \[
      \E_Z
      \sum_{x\in S}b_x(\mathcal A(q,Z))
      \le m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m
      \tag{RI4}
   \]
   for every promised query \(q\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply Poisson thinning independently to each point-label pair.  The total
   number of copies of \(p\) whose labels fall in \(B\) is Poisson with mean
   \(b_p(B)\), giving \((RI0)\).  Linearity of expectation gives
   \((RI1)\) and \((RI2)\).  The displayed conditions are \((RC1)\)--\((RC2)\)
   after writing \(b_{x,a}=a_x\mu_x(a)\), with the convention that points with
   \(a_x=0\) have arbitrary \(\mu_x\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Finite-signature rate-coverage envelope]
   \label{lem:finite-signature-rate-coverage}
   Let \(\mathcal Q\) be an arbitrary, possibly continuous, query domain for
   one localized node, and let \(\Lambda\) be a finite label universe.  A
   retained reporter maps each query and random outcome to a label set
   \[
      B(q,\omega)=A(q,\omega)\subseteq\Lambda .
   \]
   All probabilities and expectations below are with respect to the reporter
   outcome law for the queried point \(q\).
   Suppose preprocessing supplies a finite signature set \(\Sigma\) and a map
   \(\sigma:\mathcal Q\to\Sigma\).  For each signature \(\sigma_0\), let
   \(N_{\sigma_0}\subseteq S\) contain every possible near witness for queries
   of that signature:
   \[
      \{p\in S:\exists q\in\mathcal Q,\ \sigma(q)=\sigma_0,\ \|p-q\|\le r\}
      \subseteq N_{\sigma_0}.
      \tag{FS1}
   \]
   Assume that for every signature \(\sigma_0\), every label set
   \(B\subseteq\Lambda\), and every \(p\in N_{\sigma_0}\), preprocessing has
   certified finite upper envelopes
   \[
      U_{p,\sigma_0,B}
      \ge
      \E_{\omega}\!\left[
         R_{p,q}(\omega)\,
         \mathbf 1\{B(q,\omega)=B\}
      \right]
      \tag{FS2}
   \]
   for all \(q\in\mathcal Q\) with \(\sigma(q)=\sigma_0\) and
   \(\|p-q\|\le r\), and
   \[
      V_{\sigma_0,B}
      \ge
      \Pr_{\omega}[B(q,\omega)=B]
      \tag{FS3}
   \]
   for all \(q\in\mathcal Q\) with \(\sigma(q)=\sigma_0\).  Let
   \(b_{x,a}\ge0\) be point-label intensities and write
   \(b_x(B)=\sum_{a\in B}b_{x,a}\).  If the finite inequalities
   \[
      \sum_{B\subseteq\Lambda}
      U_{p,\sigma_0,B}\exp(-b_p(B))
      \le \tau
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma,\ p\in N_{\sigma_0})
      \tag{FS4}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{B\subseteq\Lambda}
      V_{\sigma_0,B}
      \sum_{x\in S}b_x(B)
      \le \ell
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma)
      \tag{FS5}
   \]
   hold, then the continuous-query rate-coverage conditions
   \[
      \E_{\omega}\!\left[
         R_{p,q}(\omega)\exp(-b_p(B(q,\omega)))
      \right]\le\tau
      \tag{FS6}
   \]
   for every promised near pair \(\|p-q\|\le r\), and
   \[
      \E_{\omega}\sum_{x\in S}b_x(B(q,\omega))\le\ell
      \tag{FS7}
   \]
   for every \(q\in\mathcal Q\), both hold.  The storage bound remains
   \(\sum_{x,a}b_{x,a}\).

   Thus a continuous query domain can be certified without a metric net: it is
   enough to enumerate or decode finitely many reporter signatures and to prove
   finite upper envelopes for their tilted miss and load coefficients.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a promised near pair \((p,q)\), and put
   \(\sigma_0=\sigma(q)\).  By \((FS1)\), \(p\in N_{\sigma_0}\).  Decompose the
   expectation according to the finite label set \(B(q,\omega)\):
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \E_\omega\!\left[
         R_{p,q}(\omega)e^{-b_p(B(q,\omega))}
      \right]
      &=
      \sum_{B\subseteq\Lambda}
      e^{-b_p(B)}
      \E_\omega\!\left[
         R_{p,q}(\omega)\mathbf 1\{B(q,\omega)=B\}
      \right]  \\
      &\le
      \sum_{B\subseteq\Lambda}
      U_{p,\sigma_0,B}e^{-b_p(B)}
      \le \tau .
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   This proves \((FS6)\).  The load bound is identical:
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \E_\omega\sum_xb_x(B(q,\omega))
      &=
      \sum_{B\subseteq\Lambda}
      \Pr[B(q,\omega)=B]\sum_xb_x(B)\\
      &\le
      \sum_{B\subseteq\Lambda}
      V_{\sigma_0,B}\sum_xb_x(B)
      \le\ell .
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   Poisson materialization gives the same stored incidence count as in
   \cref{cor:rate-coverage-intensity}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Finite Poisson realization for rate coverage]
   \label{lem:finite-poisson-rate-coverage-realization}
   Fix a finite label universe \(\Lambda\).  Let \(\mathcal I\) be a finite
   set of tilted-miss constraints and \(\mathcal J\) a finite set of load
   constraints.  For each \(i\in\mathcal I\), fix a point \(p_i\in S\) and
   nonnegative coefficients \(U_{i,B}\), \(B\subseteq\Lambda\).  For each
   \(j\in\mathcal J\), fix coefficients
   \(c_{j,x,a}\in[0,1]\), \(x\in S\), \(a\in\Lambda\).  Let
   \(b_{x,a}\ge0\) be fractional point-label intensities and write
   \(b_x(B)=\sum_{a\in B}b_{x,a}\).  Put
   \[
      U_*=
      \begin{cases}
      \max_{i\in\mathcal I}\sum_{B\subseteq\Lambda}U_{i,B},
      &\mathcal I\ne\emptyset,\\
      0,&\mathcal I=\emptyset,
      \end{cases}
      \qquad
      S_0=\sum_{x\in S}\sum_{a\in\Lambda}b_{x,a}.
   \]
   Suppose that, for some target \(\tau>0\),
   \[
      \sum_{B\subseteq\Lambda}U_{i,B}e^{-b_{p_i}(B)}
      \le
      \frac{\tau}{8e}
      \qquad(i\in\mathcal I),
      \tag{FR1}
   \]
   and, for load targets \(\ell_j\),
   \[
      \sum_{x\in S}\sum_{a\in\Lambda}c_{j,x,a}b_{x,a}
      \le \ell_j
      \qquad(j\in\mathcal J).
      \tag{FR2}
   \]
   Let \(K\ge1\), and if \(\mathcal I\ne\emptyset\) assume also
   \[
      K\ge
      \left\lceil
      \log\frac{64|\mathcal I|U_*}{\tau}
      \right\rceil .
      \tag{FR3}
   \]
   Materialize a
   retained bucket structure by drawing independent Poisson multiplicities
   \[
      N_{x,a}\sim\operatorname{Poisson}(K b_{x,a}).
   \]
   For the realized structure define
   \[
      M_i(N)=
      \sum_{B\subseteq\Lambda}
      U_{i,B}\,
      \mathbf 1\!\left\{\sum_{a\in B}N_{p_i,a}=0\right\}
      \tag{FR4}
   \]
   and
   \[
      L_j(N)=
      \sum_{x\in S}\sum_{a\in\Lambda}c_{j,x,a}N_{x,a}.
      \tag{FR5}
   \]
   With positive probability, the same realized structure satisfies all finite
   certificates
   \[
      M_i(N)\le\tau/4
      \qquad(i\in\mathcal I),
      \tag{FR6}
   \]
   \[
      L_j(N)\le (e-1)K\ell_j+\log(8\max\{1,|\mathcal J|\})
      \qquad(j\in\mathcal J),
      \tag{FR7}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{x,a}N_{x,a}\le(e-1)KS_0+\log 8 .
      \tag{FR8}
   \]

   Therefore a finite rate-coverage certificate with constant miss slack can be
   converted, by a Las Vegas preprocessing search, into one fixed retained
   bucket structure.  If the number of finite constraints is polynomial in
   \(m\), the extra storage and reported-load factors are only
   \(O(\log m)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Fix \(i\in\mathcal I\).  Split label sets into
   \(B\) with \(b_{p_i}(B)<1\) and \(b_{p_i}(B)\ge1\).  The first part is
   deterministically bounded, using \((FR1)\), by
   \[
      \sum_{B:\ b_{p_i}(B)<1}U_{i,B}
      \le
      e\sum_B U_{i,B}e^{-b_{p_i}(B)}
      \le \tau/8 .
      \tag{FR9}
   \]
   For the second part, Poisson thinning gives
   \[
      \Pr\!\left[\sum_{a\in B}N_{p_i,a}=0\right]
      =
      e^{-K b_{p_i}(B)}
      \le e^{-K}.
   \]
   Hence the expected high-coverage contribution to \(M_i(N)\) is at most
   \(e^{-K}U_*\le\tau/(64|\mathcal I|)\).  Markov's inequality gives
   probability at most \(1/(8|\mathcal I|)\) that this contribution exceeds
   \(\tau/8\).  A union bound over \(i\) shows that all miss inequalities
   \((FR6)\) fail with probability at most \(1/8\).

   For a load constraint \(j\), the exponential moment satisfies
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \E e^{L_j(N)}
      &=
      \exp\!\left(
         \sum_{x,a}K b_{x,a}(e^{c_{j,x,a}}-1)
      \right) \\
      &\le
      \exp\!\left(
         (e-1)K\sum_{x,a}c_{j,x,a}b_{x,a}
      \right)
      \le
      \exp((e-1)K\ell_j),
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   since \(0\le c_{j,x,a}\le1\).  Exponential Markov gives
   \[
      \Pr\!\left[
         L_j(N)>(e-1)K\ell_j+\log(8\max\{1,|\mathcal J|\})
      \right]
      \le\frac1{8\max\{1,|\mathcal J|\}}.
   \]
   Union bounding over \(j\) gives failure probability at most \(1/8\).
   The same calculation with all coefficients equal to \(1\) gives
   \((FR8)\) with failure probability at most \(1/8\).  Thus all displayed
   certificates hold simultaneously with probability at least \(5/8\).
   Because the certificates are finite and checkable, preprocessing can sample
   fresh Poisson realizations until one passes.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite-signature retained bucket certificate]
   \label{cor:finite-signature-retained-buckets}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:finite-signature-rate-coverage}.  Put
   \[
      \mathcal I=
      \{(\sigma_0,p):\sigma_0\in\Sigma,\ p\in N_{\sigma_0}\},
      \qquad
      \mathcal J=\Sigma .
   \]
   For \(a\in\Lambda\), define the load-envelope coefficients
   \[
      C_{\sigma_0,a}
      =
      \sum_{B\subseteq\Lambda:\ a\in B}V_{\sigma_0,B},
      \qquad
      C_V=\max\{1,\max_{\sigma_0,a}C_{\sigma_0,a}\}.
      \tag{FRC0}
   \]
   Suppose the fractional intensities \(b_{x,a}\) satisfy the strengthened
   finite miss inequalities
   \[
      \sum_{B\subseteq\Lambda}
      U_{p,\sigma_0,B}\exp(-b_p(B))
      \le \frac{\tau}{8e}
      \qquad((\sigma_0,p)\in\mathcal I),
      \tag{FRC1}
   \]
   and the finite load inequalities
   \[
      \sum_{B\subseteq\Lambda}
      V_{\sigma_0,B}\sum_{x\in S}b_x(B)
      \le \ell
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma).
      \tag{FRC2}
   \]
   Let
   \[
      S_0=\sum_{x,a}b_{x,a},
      \qquad
      U_*=\max_{(\sigma_0,p)\in\mathcal I}
      \sum_{B\subseteq\Lambda}U_{p,\sigma_0,B},
   \]
   with \(U_*=0\) if \(\mathcal I=\emptyset\), and choose
   \[
      K\ge1,\qquad
      K\ge
      \left\lceil
      \log\frac{64|\mathcal I|U_*}{\tau}
      \right\rceil
      \quad\text{when }\mathcal I\ne\emptyset .
      \tag{FRC3}
   \]
   Then preprocessing can find a fixed retained bucket structure
   \(N_{x,a}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) such that, for every promised near pair
   \(p,q\),
   \[
      \E_\omega\!\left[
         R_{p,q}(\omega)
         \mathbf 1\{p\text{ has no retained copy in }B(q,\omega)\}
      \right]
      \le \tau/4 ,
      \tag{FRC4}
   \]
   and, for every query \(q\) with signature \(\sigma_0\),
   \[
      \E_\omega
      \sum_{x\in S}\sum_{a\in B(q,\omega)}N_{x,a}
      \le
      (e-1)K\ell+C_V\log(8\max\{1,|\Sigma|\}).
      \tag{FRC5}
   \]
   The total retained incidence count satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{x,a}N_{x,a}\le(e-1)KS_0+\log8 .
      \tag{FRC6}
   \]

   In particular, if the finite signature certificate has polynomially many
   constraints, \(U_*/\tau\le m^{O(1)}\), and the additive envelope term
   \(C_V\log(8\max\{1,|\Sigma|\})\) is within the intended load budget, then
   the conversion from fractional intensities to a fixed retained bucket index
   costs only a logarithmic factor in storage and reported incidence load.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{lem:finite-poisson-rate-coverage-realization} with miss
   constraints \(i=(\sigma_0,p)\) and coefficients
   \(U_{i,B}=U_{p,\sigma_0,B}\).  For a load constraint \(\sigma_0\), use the
   normalized coefficients
   \[
      c_{\sigma_0,x,a}=C_{\sigma_0,a}/C_V\in[0,1].
   \]
   By \((FRC2)\),
   \[
      \sum_{x,a}c_{\sigma_0,x,a}b_{x,a}
      =
      C_V^{-1}
      \sum_{B\subseteq\Lambda}
      V_{\sigma_0,B}\sum_xb_x(B)
      \le \ell/C_V .
   \]
   The realization lemma therefore gives one checkable Poisson realization
   satisfying \((FR6)\), \((FR7)\), and \((FR8)\).

   Fix a promised near pair \((p,q)\), let \(\sigma_0=\sigma(q)\), and
   decompose by \(B(q,\omega)\).  The event that \(p\) has no retained copy in
   \(B\) is exactly
   \[
      \left\{\sum_{a\in B}N_{p,a}=0\right\}.
   \]
   Therefore \((FS2)\) and \((FR6)\) give
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      &\E_\omega\!\left[
         R_{p,q}(\omega)
         \mathbf 1\{p\text{ has no retained copy in }B(q,\omega)\}
      \right] \\
      &\qquad\le
      \sum_{B\subseteq\Lambda}
      U_{p,\sigma_0,B}
      \mathbf 1\!\left\{\sum_{a\in B}N_{p,a}=0\right\}
      \le\tau/4 .
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   This proves \((FRC4)\).

   For load, \((FS3)\) gives
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \E_\omega
      \sum_{x}\sum_{a\in B(q,\omega)}N_{x,a}
      &\le
      \sum_{B\subseteq\Lambda}
      V_{\sigma_0,B}\sum_x\sum_{a\in B}N_{x,a}\\
      &=
      \sum_{x,a}C_{\sigma_0,a}N_{x,a}
      =
      C_V L_{\sigma_0}(N).
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   Multiplying the normalized-load bound \((FR7)\) by \(C_V\) gives
   \((FRC5)\), and \((FRC6)\) is \((FR8)\).  Since the displayed inequalities
   are finite, preprocessing can sample and check realizations until one passes.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite decoder-transcript rate-coverage envelope]
   \label{cor:finite-transcript-rate-coverage}
   In the setting of \cref{lem:finite-signature-rate-coverage}, suppose the
   retained reporter is implemented by a finite transcript decoder.  That is,
   for each query signature \(\sigma_0\) there is a finite transcript set
   \(\mathcal Z_{\sigma_0}\), and the reporter maps each outcome to
   \[
      \zeta(q,\omega)\in\mathcal Z_{\sigma(q)} .
   \]
   For each transcript \(\zeta\in\mathcal Z_{\sigma_0}\), the decoder reports
   a fixed label set \(B_{\sigma_0,\zeta}\subseteq\Lambda\) and spends at most
   \(d_{\sigma_0,\zeta}\ge0\) extra work.  Assume preprocessing certifies
   \[
      U_{p,\sigma_0,\zeta}
      \ge
      \E_\omega\!\left[
         R_{p,q}(\omega)\,
         \mathbf 1\{\zeta(q,\omega)=\zeta\}
      \right]
      \tag{DT1}
   \]
   for every \(q\) of signature \(\sigma_0\) with \(\|p-q\|\le r\), and
   \[
      V_{\sigma_0,\zeta}
      \ge
      \Pr_\omega[\zeta(q,\omega)=\zeta]
      \tag{DT2}
   \]
   for every \(q\) of signature \(\sigma_0\).  If
   \[
      \sum_{\zeta\in\mathcal Z_{\sigma_0}}
      U_{p,\sigma_0,\zeta}
      \exp\!\bigl(-b_p(B_{\sigma_0,\zeta})\bigr)
      \le \tau
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma,\ p\in N_{\sigma_0})
      \tag{DT3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{\zeta\in\mathcal Z_{\sigma_0}}
      V_{\sigma_0,\zeta}
      \left(
         d_{\sigma_0,\zeta}
         +\sum_{x\in S}b_x(B_{\sigma_0,\zeta})
      \right)
      \le \ell
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \tag{DT4}
   \]
   then the tilted miss bound \((FS6)\) holds and the expected reporter-plus-scan
   work is at most \(\ell\) for every query.

   Thus a code, trellis, polar, or lattice quotient need not expose all
   subsets of the label universe.  It is enough that its possible decoder
   transcripts are finite or compactly decodable, and that preprocessing proves
   transcript-level envelopes.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a promised near pair \((p,q)\), and put \(\sigma_0=\sigma(q)\).  By
   \((FS1)\), \(p\in N_{\sigma_0}\).  Decomposing over decoder transcripts
   gives
   \[
      \E_\omega\!\left[
         R_{p,q}(\omega)
         e^{-b_p(B_{\sigma_0,\zeta(q,\omega)})}
      \right]
      \le
      \sum_{\zeta\in\mathcal Z_{\sigma_0}}
      U_{p,\sigma_0,\zeta}
      e^{-b_p(B_{\sigma_0,\zeta})}
      \le\tau .
   \]
   For an arbitrary query \(q\) with signature \(\sigma_0=\sigma(q)\), the
   expected reporter-plus-scan work is bounded by
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      &\E_\omega\!\left[
         d_{\sigma_0,\zeta(q,\omega)}
         +\sum_xb_x(B_{\sigma_0,\zeta(q,\omega)})
      \right]  \\
      &\qquad\le
      \sum_{\zeta\in\mathcal Z_{\sigma_0}}
      V_{\sigma_0,\zeta}
      \left(
         d_{\sigma_0,\zeta}
         +\sum_xb_x(B_{\sigma_0,\zeta})
      \right)
      \le\ell .
   \end{aligned}
   \]
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Compressed decoder-DAG rate-coverage envelope]
   \label{cor:compressed-decoder-dag-rate-coverage}
   In the setting of \cref{lem:finite-signature-rate-coverage}, suppose the
   retained reporter for each signature \(\sigma_0\) is represented by a finite
   acyclic decoder graph \(G_{\sigma_0}=(V_{\sigma_0},E_{\sigma_0})\) with
   source \(s_{\sigma_0}\) and terminal set \(T_{\sigma_0}\).  For every query
   \(q\) with \(\sigma(q)=\sigma_0\) and outcome \(\omega\), the decoder visits
   one source-to-terminal path
   \[
      \Pi(q,\omega)\subseteq V_{\sigma_0},
      \qquad
      t(q,\omega)\in T_{\sigma_0}.
   \]
   A terminal \(t\) reports the fixed label set \(B_t\subseteq\Lambda\), and a
   visited state \(v\) costs at most \(d_v\ge0\) units of reporter work.

   Assume preprocessing certifies state-reach envelopes
   \[
      U_{p,\sigma_0,v}
      \ge
      \E_\omega\!\left[
         R_{p,q}(\omega)\mathbf 1\{v\in\Pi(q,\omega)\}
      \right]
      \tag{DG1}
   \]
   for every \(q\) of signature \(\sigma_0\) with \(\|p-q\|\le r\), and
   \[
      V_{\sigma_0,v}
      \ge
      \Pr_\omega[v\in\Pi(q,\omega)]
      \tag{DG2}
   \]
   for every \(q\) of signature \(\sigma_0\).  If
   \[
      \sum_{t\in T_{\sigma_0}}
      U_{p,\sigma_0,t}\exp(-b_p(B_t))
      \le \tau
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma,\ p\in N_{\sigma_0})
      \tag{DG3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{v\in V_{\sigma_0}}V_{\sigma_0,v}d_v
      +
      \sum_{t\in T_{\sigma_0}}
      V_{\sigma_0,t}\sum_{x\in S}b_x(B_t)
      \le \ell
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \tag{DG4}
   \]
   then the tilted miss bound \((FS6)\) holds and the expected
   reporter-plus-scan work is at most \(\ell\) for every query.

   Thus the proof object can be the compact state graph of a list-recovery,
   trellis, polar, or lattice-enumeration decoder.  The full transcript tree is
   only an analysis unfolding; the retained certificate stores state reach
   envelopes and terminal bucket sets.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a promised near pair \((p,q)\), let \(\sigma_0=\sigma(q)\), and write
   \(t=t(q,\omega)\).  Since \(p\in N_{\sigma_0}\), terminal decomposition gives
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \E_\omega\!\left[
         R_{p,q}(\omega)e^{-b_p(B_{t(q,\omega)})}
      \right]
      &=
      \sum_{t\in T_{\sigma_0}}
      e^{-b_p(B_t)}
      \E_\omega\!\left[
         R_{p,q}(\omega)\mathbf 1\{t(q,\omega)=t\}
      \right]  \\
      &\le
      \sum_{t\in T_{\sigma_0}}
      U_{p,\sigma_0,t}e^{-b_p(B_t)}
      \le\tau .
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   For the work bound, the acyclic path visits every state at most once, so
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      &\E_\omega\!\left[
         \sum_{v\in\Pi(q,\omega)}d_v
         +\sum_xb_x(B_{t(q,\omega)})
      \right]  \\
      &\qquad=
      \sum_{v\in V_{\sigma_0}}d_v\Pr[v\in\Pi(q,\omega)]
      +
      \sum_{t\in T_{\sigma_0}}
      \Pr[t(q,\omega)=t]\sum_xb_x(B_t)  \\
      &\qquad\le
      \sum_{v\in V_{\sigma_0}}V_{\sigma_0,v}d_v
      +
      \sum_{t\in T_{\sigma_0}}
      V_{\sigma_0,t}\sum_xb_x(B_t)
      \le\ell .
   \end{aligned}
   \]
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Output-sensitive decoder-DAG rate coverage]
   \label{cor:output-sensitive-decoder-dag-rate-coverage}
   In the setting of \cref{lem:finite-signature-rate-coverage}, suppose the
   retained reporter for each signature \(\sigma_0\) is represented by a finite
   acyclic decoder graph with state set \(V_{\sigma_0}\) and terminal-output
   set \(T_{\sigma_0}\).  For query \(q\) and outcome \(\omega\), the decoder
   visits a state set
   \[
      W(q,\omega)\subseteq V_{\sigma(q)}
   \]
   and reports a nonempty terminal set
   \[
      O(q,\omega)\subseteq T_{\sigma(q)} .
   \]
   A no-output outcome is represented by a dummy terminal \(t_\emptyset\) with
   \(B_{t_\emptyset}=\emptyset\).  Each terminal \(t\) has a fixed label set
   \(B_t\subseteq\Lambda\), and each visited state \(v\) costs at most
   \(d_v\ge0\).  The reported query label set is
   \[
      B(q,\omega)=\bigcup_{t\in O(q,\omega)}B_t .
      \tag{OD0}
   \]
   Finally, let \(\alpha_t(q,\omega)\in[0,1]\) be terminal responsibility
   weights supported on \(O(q,\omega)\), with
   \[
      \sum_{t\in T_{\sigma(q)}}\alpha_t(q,\omega)=1 .
      \tag{OD1}
   \]

   Assume preprocessing certifies
   \[
      U_{p,\sigma_0,t}
      \ge
      \E_\omega\!\left[
         R_{p,q}(\omega)\alpha_t(q,\omega)
      \right]
      \tag{OD2}
   \]
   for every \(q\) of signature \(\sigma_0\) with \(\|p-q\|\le r\), and
   \[
      V^{\rm state}_{\sigma_0,v}
      \ge
      \Pr_\omega[v\in W(q,\omega)],
      \qquad
      V^{\rm out}_{\sigma_0,t}
      \ge
      \Pr_\omega[t\in O(q,\omega)]
      \tag{OD3}
   \]
   for every \(q\) of signature \(\sigma_0\).  If
   \[
      \sum_{t\in T_{\sigma_0}}
      U_{p,\sigma_0,t}\exp(-b_p(B_t))
      \le\tau
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma,\ p\in N_{\sigma_0})
      \tag{OD4}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{v\in V_{\sigma_0}}V^{\rm state}_{\sigma_0,v}d_v
      +
      \sum_{t\in T_{\sigma_0}}
      V^{\rm out}_{\sigma_0,t}\sum_{x\in S}b_x(B_t)
      \le\ell
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \tag{OD5}
   \]
   then \((FS6)\) holds and the expected reporter-plus-scan work is at most
   \(\ell\) for every query.

   The responsibility weights are only an analysis certificate.  They let the
   miss proof charge one useful reported terminal, or a convex mixture of useful
   terminals, while the actual scan cost remains charged to every reported
   bucket.  This is the natural rate-coverage interface for output-sensitive
   list recovery, polar list decoding, and pruned lattice sphere enumeration.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a promised near pair \((p,q)\), and put \(\sigma_0=\sigma(q)\).  Since
   \(\alpha_t(q,\omega)\) is supported on \(O(q,\omega)\), every terminal with
   positive responsibility satisfies \(B_t\subseteq B(q,\omega)\).  Thus
   \(b_p(B(q,\omega))\ge b_p(B_t)\), and by \((OD1)\),
   \[
      e^{-b_p(B(q,\omega))}
      \le
      \sum_{t\in T_{\sigma_0}}
      \alpha_t(q,\omega)e^{-b_p(B_t)} .
   \]
   Therefore
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \E_\omega\!\left[
         R_{p,q}(\omega)e^{-b_p(B(q,\omega))}
      \right]
      &\le
      \sum_{t\in T_{\sigma_0}}
      e^{-b_p(B_t)}
      \E_\omega\!\left[
         R_{p,q}(\omega)\alpha_t(q,\omega)
      \right]  \\
      &\le
      \sum_{t\in T_{\sigma_0}}
      U_{p,\sigma_0,t}e^{-b_p(B_t)}
      \le\tau .
   \end{aligned}
   \]

   For the work bound, nonnegativity of the point-label intensities gives
   \[
      b_x(B(q,\omega))
      =
      b_x\!\left(\bigcup_{t\in O(q,\omega)}B_t\right)
      \le
      \sum_{t\in O(q,\omega)}b_x(B_t).
   \]
   Hence
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      &\E_\omega\!\left[
         \sum_{v\in W(q,\omega)}d_v
         +\sum_xb_x(B(q,\omega))
      \right]  \\
      &\qquad\le
      \sum_{v\in V_{\sigma_0}}
      V^{\rm state}_{\sigma_0,v}d_v
      +
      \sum_{t\in T_{\sigma_0}}
      V^{\rm out}_{\sigma_0,t}\sum_xb_x(B_t)
      \le\ell .
   \end{aligned}
   \]
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Scalar redundancy water filling]
   \label{lem:scalar-redundancy-waterfill}
   Work in the Poisson multi-assignment model of
   \cref{lem:poisson-rate-coverage}, but fix the label reporter
   \(\mathcal A(q,Z)\) and the point assignment laws \(\mu_x\).  Let
   \(\mathcal N\) be a finite set of tilted near-pair constraints, and attach
   nonnegative prices \(\lambda_{p,q}\) to them.  For \(s\ge0\), define the
   scalar residual loss and marginal coverage of point \(p\) by
   \[
      F_p(s)
      =
      \sum_{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \lambda_{p,q}
      \E_Z\!\left[
         R_{p,q}(Z)
         \exp\!\left(-s\,\mu_p(\mathcal A(q,Z))\right)
      \right],
      \tag{RW1}
   \]
   \[
      D_p(s)
      =
      \sum_{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \lambda_{p,q}
      \E_Z\!\left[
         R_{p,q}(Z)\,
         \mu_p(\mathcal A(q,Z))
         \exp\!\left(-s\,\mu_p(\mathcal A(q,Z))\right)
      \right].
      \tag{RW2}
   \]
   For a storage price \(\gamma>0\), the optimal replication budgets for the
   priced scalar problem
   \[
      \inf_{a_p\ge0}
      \left\{
      \sum_p F_p(a_p)+\gamma\sum_pa_p
      \right\}
      \tag{RW3}
   \]
   are independent over points and satisfy
   \[
      a_p=0\quad\text{if }D_p(0)\le\gamma,
      \tag{RW4}
   \]
   while every positive optimum satisfies the water-level equation
   \[
      D_p(a_p)=\gamma .
      \tag{RW5}
   \]
   If \(D_p\) has flat intervals, any point in the corresponding solution
   interval is optimal.

   Equivalently, for a hard total storage budget
   \[
      \sum_pa_p\le A,
      \tag{RW6}
   \]
   an optimum is obtained by choosing a water level \(\gamma\ge0\) so that the
   solutions of \((RW4)\)--\((RW5)\) have total budget \(A\), unless the
   unconstrained \(\gamma=0\) optimum already uses less.  Thus extra
   replication is assigned exactly to points whose current marginal tilted
   coverage \(D_p(a_p)\) is largest.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(0\le\mu_p(\mathcal A(q,Z))\le1\), differentiating under the
   expectation is justified by dominated convergence.  The function \(F_p\) is
   convex and nonincreasing, and
   \[
      F_p'(s)=-D_p(s).
   \]
   The function \(D_p\) is nonincreasing in \(s\).  The objective in \((RW3)\)
   separates over \(p\), so \(a_p\) minimizes \(F_p(s)+\gamma s\) on
   \([0,\infty)\).  The right derivative at \(0\) is \(\gamma-D_p(0)\).  If it
   is nonnegative, convexity makes \(s=0\) optimal.  Otherwise every positive
   minimizer must have zero subgradient, which is exactly \((RW5)\), with the
   usual interval convention when the convex function has a flat minimum.

   The constrained statement is the KKT form of the same convex program with a
   Lagrange multiplier \(\gamma\) for \((RW6)\).  If the storage constraint is
   active, complementary slackness chooses the water level for which
   \(\sum_pa_p=A\); if it is inactive, the multiplier is zero.  The marginal
   interpretation follows directly from \((RW2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Finite rate-coverage feasibility is convex]
   \label{lem:finite-rate-coverage-convex}
   Fix a finite label universe \(\mathcal A\), a finite set of resident points
   \(S\), a finite promised query set \(\mathcal Q\), and a finite set of near
   witnesses \(\mathcal N\subseteq S\times\mathcal Q\).  For each
   \(q\in\mathcal Q\), let \(\nu_q\) be a probability law on an outcome space
   \(\Omega_q\), and let the retained reporter map each
   \(\omega\in\Omega_q\) to a label set \(A_q(\omega)\subseteq\mathcal A\).
   For each \((p,q)\in\mathcal N\), let
   \(r_{p,q}(\omega)\ge0\) be an integrable tilted witness weight.  Given
   targets \(\tau_{p,q}>0\), \(\ell_q>0\), and \(S_0>0\), consider the intensity
   variables \(b_{x,a}\ge0\) and the constraints
   \[
      M_{p,q}(b)
      :=
      \int r_{p,q}(\omega)
      \exp\!\left(-\sum_{a\in A_q(\omega)}b_{p,a}\right)
      d\nu_q(\omega)
      \le \tau_{p,q},
      \tag{FC1}
   \]
   \[
      L_q(b)
      :=
      \int
      \sum_{x\in S}\sum_{a\in A_q(\omega)}b_{x,a}
      d\nu_q(\omega)
      \le \ell_q,
      \tag{FC2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{x\in S}\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}b_{x,a}\le S_0 .
      \tag{FC3}
   \]
   The feasible set is convex.

   Moreover, infeasibility has the following dual certificate: there exist
   nonnegative multipliers \(\lambda_{p,q}\), \(\theta_q\), and \(\gamma\), not
   all zero, such that
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \inf_{b\ge0}\Bigg\{
      &\sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\lambda_{p,q}M_{p,q}(b)
       +\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}\theta_qL_q(b)
       +\gamma\sum_{x,a}b_{x,a}
      \Bigg\} \\
      &>
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\lambda_{p,q}\tau_{p,q}
      +\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}\theta_q\ell_q
      +\gamma S_0 .
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{FC4}
   \]
   Conversely, any multipliers satisfying \((FC4)\) prove infeasibility.
   The infimum in \((FC4)\) separates over data points.  If
   \[
      c_a=
      \gamma+
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}\theta_q
      \nu_q\{\omega:\ a\in A_q(\omega)\},
      \tag{FC5}
   \]
   then the left side of \((FC4)\) equals
   \[
      \sum_{x\in S}
      \inf_{b_x\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^{\mathcal A}}
      \left\{
      \sum_{q:\,(x,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \lambda_{x,q}
      \int r_{x,q}(\omega)
      e^{-\sum_{a\in A_q(\omega)}b_{x,a}}\,d\nu_q(\omega)
      +
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_ab_{x,a}
      \right\}.
      \tag{FC6}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Each function \(M_{p,q}\) is convex because it is an integral of the
   exponential of an affine function of \(b\).  The load and storage
   constraints are linear.  Hence the feasible set is convex.

   If a feasible \(b\) exists, then for every nonnegative multiplier vector the
   weighted sum on the left of \((FC4)\), evaluated at that \(b\), is at most
   the weighted target on the right.  Therefore \((FC4)\) is impossible.

   Conversely, suppose the finite system is infeasible.  Let \(F(b)\) be the
   vector of violations
   \[
      \left(M(b)-\tau,\ L(b)-\ell,\ \sum_{x,a}b_{x,a}-S_0\right),
   \]
   and form the upper hull
   \[
      \mathcal C=\{F(b)+u:\ b\ge0,\ u\ge0\}.
   \]
   The system is feasible exactly when \(0\in\mathcal C\).  The set
   \(\mathcal C\) is convex: each miss coordinate is convex, the load and
   storage coordinates are linear, and adding the nonnegative orthant converts
   convex-coordinate interpolation into an upper hull.  It is also closed.  If
   \(F(b_n)+u_n\) converges, then the storage coordinate bounds
   \(\sum_{x,a}b_{n,x,a}\) from above, since \(u_n\ge0\); a subsequence of
   \(b_n\) therefore converges in the finite-dimensional nonnegative orthant,
   and dominated convergence for the miss integrals gives the limiting point of
   \(\mathcal C\).

   Since the system is infeasible, \(0\notin\mathcal C\).  Strict separation of
   the point \(0\) from the closed convex set \(\mathcal C\) gives a vector of
   multipliers whose inner product is positive on all of \(\mathcal C\).  The
   upper-hull property forces all multiplier coordinates to be nonnegative.
   Writing these coordinates as \(\lambda_{p,q}\), \(\theta_q\), and \(\gamma\)
   gives
   \[
      \inf_{b\ge0}
      \left(
      \sum_{(p,q)}\lambda_{p,q}(M_{p,q}(b)-\tau_{p,q})
      +\sum_q\theta_q(L_q(b)-\ell_q)
      +\gamma\left(\sum_{x,a}b_{x,a}-S_0\right)
      \right)>0,
   \]
   which is \((FC4)\).

   Finally, the load and storage terms contribute
   \[
      \sum_{x,a}
      \left(
         \gamma+
         \sum_q\theta_q\nu_q\{\omega:\ a\in A_q(\omega)\}
      \right)b_{x,a}.
   \]
   The miss terms for witness \((p,q)\) involve only the variables
   \(b_{p,a}\).  Therefore the Lagrangian infimum separates by point, giving
   \((FC6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Reduced-cost rule for adding one rate label]
   \label{lem:rate-coverage-column-gain}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:finite-rate-coverage-convex}.  Fix
   nonnegative dual multipliers \(\lambda,\theta,\gamma\), and fix current
   intensities \(b\) on a retained label universe \(\mathcal A\).  A proposed
   new label \(a_*\) is specified, for each query \(q\), by the event
   \[
      h_q(\omega)=\mathbf 1\{a_*\in A_q^+(\omega)\}\in\{0,1\},
   \]
   where \(A_q^+(\omega)\) is the reporter after adding \(a_*\).  Define its
   dual load-storage price
   \[
      c_*=
      \gamma+\sum_q\theta_q\int h_q(\omega)\,d\nu_q(\omega),
      \tag{CG0}
   \]
   and, for a point \(x\), its residual tilted witness value
   \[
      G_x(a_*)
      =
      \sum_{q:\,(x,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \lambda_{x,q}
      \int
      r_{x,q}(\omega)h_q(\omega)
      \exp\!\left(
         -\sum_{a\in A_q(\omega)}b_{x,a}
      \right)d\nu_q(\omega).
      \tag{CG1}
   \]
   If \(x\) is assigned intensity \(s\ge0\) to this new label, with all other
   intensities fixed, then the dual Lagrangian changes by
   \[
      \Delta_{x,a_*}(s)
      =
      G_x(a_*)\bigl(e^{-s}-1\bigr)+c_*s .
      \tag{CG2}
   \]
   Consequently the best one-column update has the closed form
   \[
      \inf_{s\ge0}\Delta_{x,a_*}(s)
      =
      \begin{cases}
      0, & G_x(a_*)\le c_*,\\[2mm]
      c_*-G_x(a_*)+c_*\log\!\bigl(G_x(a_*)/c_*\bigr),
         & G_x(a_*)>c_*>0,\\[2mm]
      -G_x(a_*), & c_*=0,
      \end{cases}
      \tag{CG3}
   \]
   where the middle case is achieved by
   \(s=\log(G_x(a_*)/c_*)\).  In particular, a label with
   \(G_x(a_*)>c_*\) is a rigorous improving column for the dual obstruction,
   while any obstruction that remains valid after adding a whole candidate label
   class must satisfy
   \[
      G_x(a)\le
      \gamma+\sum_q\theta_q\Pr_{\nu_q}[a\in A_q(\omega)]
      \tag{CG4}
   \]
   for every candidate label \(a\) and every data point \(x\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Only witness constraints with first coordinate \(x\) depend on the new
   intensity \(s\).  On the event \(h_q(\omega)=1\), the miss exponential for
   witness \((x,q)\) is multiplied by \(e^{-s}\); on the complement it is
   unchanged.  Therefore the total change in the weighted miss terms is
   \[
      (e^{-s}-1)
      \sum_{q:\,(x,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \lambda_{x,q}
      \int r_{x,q}(\omega)h_q(\omega)
      e^{-\sum_{a\in A_q(\omega)}b_{x,a}}\,d\nu_q(\omega),
   \]
   which is the first term of \((CG2)\).  The load and storage terms add
   \(c_*s\) by \((CG0)\).

   The one-variable function
   \(G(e^{-s}-1)+cs\) is convex.  If \(G\le c\), its derivative at \(0\) is
   nonnegative, so \(s=0\) is optimal.  If \(G>c>0\), the derivative vanishes at
   \(s=\log(G/c)\), giving the middle line of \((CG3)\).  If \(c=0\), the
   infimum is obtained as \(s\to\infty\) and equals \(-G\).  Thus
   \(G_x(a_*)>c_*\) gives a strictly negative reduced-cost update.  Conversely,
   if a nonnegative dual vector is a valid obstruction after a candidate label
   has been added, no such single-coordinate update can reduce its Lagrangian,
   which gives \((CG4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Whole-bucket reduced gain]
   \label{cor:whole-bucket-reduced-gain}
   In the setting of \cref{lem:rate-coverage-column-gain}, suppose a proposed
   label \(a_*\) may receive arbitrary nonnegative intensities
   \(s_x=b_{x,a_*}\) for all points \(x\in S\).  With \(c_*\) and \(G_x(a_*)\)
   as in \((CG0)\)--\((CG1)\), the best simultaneous update has value
   \[
      \inf_{s_x\ge0}
      \sum_{x\in S}
      \left[
         G_x(a_*)\bigl(e^{-s_x}-1\bigr)+c_*s_x
      \right]
      =
      -\sum_{x\in S}\Phi_{c_*}(G_x(a_*)),
      \tag{BG1}
   \]
   where the reduced-gain function is
   \[
      \Phi_c(G)=
      \begin{cases}
      0, & G\le c,\\[1mm]
      G-c-c\log(G/c), & G>c>0,\\[1mm]
      G, & c=0.
      \end{cases}
      \tag{BG2}
   \]
   The minimizing assignment is
   \[
      s_x=\log(G_x(a_*)/c_*)_+
      \tag{BG3}
   \]
   when \(c_*>0\), with the evident \(s_x\to\infty\) limiting convention on
   coordinates with \(c_*=0<G_x(a_*)\).  Thus the scalar
   \[
      \operatorname{Gain}(a_*)=
      \sum_{x\in S}\Phi_{c_*}(G_x(a_*))
      \tag{BG4}
   \]
   is exactly the best dual-improvement supplied by the proposed bucket label.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   After the reporter event of \(a_*\) is fixed, the Lagrangian change is the
   sum over \(x\) of the one-coordinate changes in \((CG2)\).  There is no
   coupling between the variables \(s_x\), because storage and reported load are
   charged per point-label incidence.  Applying \((CG3)\) independently to each
   point gives \((BG1)\)--\((BG3)\), and \((BG4)\) is just the negative of the
   minimized Lagrangian change.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Variational form of reduced-gain separation]
   \label{lem:reduced-gain-variational-separation}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:finite-rate-coverage-convex}, with a
   current finite active set \(E\), nonnegative dual multipliers
   \((\lambda,\theta,\gamma)\), and current active intensities \(b^E\).  A
   proposed label \(a\) is represented by measurable reporter events
   \(h_{q,a}(\omega)=\mathbf 1\{a\in A_q^+(\omega)\}\).  Define its dual price
   \[
      c_a=\gamma+\sum_q\theta_q\int h_{q,a}(\omega)\,d\nu_q(\omega).
   \]
   For each witness \((x,q)\), define the residual tilted density
   \[
      W^E_{x,q}(\omega)
      =
      \lambda_{x,q}r_{x,q}(\omega)
      \exp\!\left(
         -\sum_{a'\in A_q(\omega)}b^E_{x,a'}
      \right),
      \tag{VG0}
   \]
   with the convention that \(W^E_{x,q}=0\) when \((x,q)\notin\mathcal N\).
   Put
   \[
      G_x^E(a)=
      \sum_q\int W^E_{x,q}(\omega)h_{q,a}(\omega)d\nu_q(\omega),
   \]
   and
   \[
      \operatorname{Gain}_E(a)=\sum_x\Phi_{c_a}(G_x^E(a)).
   \]
   For an intensity profile \(s=(s_x)_{x\in S}\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^S\), put
   \[
      \|s\|_1=\sum_xs_x
   \]
   and define the signed coverage surplus of a candidate label \(a\) by
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \Psi_E(a;s)
      &=
      \sum_q
      \int
      h_{q,a}(\omega)
      \left[
         \sum_x(1-e^{-s_x})W^E_{x,q}(\omega)
         -\theta_q\|s\|_1
      \right]d\nu_q(\omega)  \\
      &\qquad -\gamma\|s\|_1 ,
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{VG1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \operatorname{Gain}_E(a)
      =
      \sup_{s\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^S}\Psi_E(a;s).
      \tag{VG2}
   \]
   Consequently, \(a\) has positive reduced gain if and only if there is an
   intensity profile \(s\) for which the signed weighted coverage problem
   \[
      \Psi_E(a;s)>0
      \tag{VG3}
   \]
   succeeds.

   In particular, an implicit label family \(\mathcal U\) has no positive-gain
   label exactly when
   \[
      \sup_{a\in\mathcal U}\Psi_E(a;s)\le0
      \qquad\text{for every }s\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^S .
      \tag{VG4}
   \]
   Thus a separator for signed weighted coverage objectives of the form
   \((VG1)\), together with any exact outer maximization over \(s\), implements
   the reduced-gain separator of
   \cref{lem:implicit-reduced-gain-separation}.  Approximate separation is also
   sound in the one-sided sense: any returned label with verified
   \(\Psi_E(a;s)>0\) is an improving column, while a no-positive certificate
   must certify \((VG4)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For \(c,G\ge0\), the reduced-gain function satisfies
   \[
      \Phi_c(G)=\sup_{s\ge0}\{G(1-e^{-s})-cs\}.
      \tag{VG5}
   \]
   Indeed, if \(G\le c\), the derivative \(Ge^{-s}-c\) is nonpositive at
   \(s=0\) and stays nonpositive, so the optimum is \(0\).  If \(G>c>0\), the
   optimum is at \(s=\log(G/c)\) and has value
   \(G-c-c\log(G/c)\).  If \(c=0\), the supremum is \(G\), approached as
   \(s\to\infty\).

   Applying \((VG5)\) independently for each point gives
   \[
      \operatorname{Gain}_E(a)
      =
      \sup_{s_x\ge0}
      \sum_x
      \left[
         G_x^E(a)(1-e^{-s_x})-c_a s_x
      \right].
      \tag{VG6}
   \]
   Substitute
   \[
      G_x^E(a)=
      \sum_q\int W^E_{x,q}(\omega)h_{q,a}(\omega)d\nu_q(\omega)
   \]
   and
   \[
      c_a=\gamma+\sum_q\theta_q\int h_{q,a}(\omega)d\nu_q(\omega).
   \]
   Rearranging the finite sums and integrals in \((VG6)\) gives exactly
   \((VG1)\), proving \((VG2)\).

   The positive-gain equivalence follows immediately from \((VG2)\).  Taking
   the supremum over \(a\in\mathcal U\) gives \((VG4)\).  Finally, when a
   candidate label and profile satisfy \((VG3)\), equation \((VG2)\) implies
   \(\operatorname{Gain}_E(a)>0\), so the verified label is an improving column
   by \cref{cor:whole-bucket-reduced-gain}.  Conversely, a no-positive answer
   is valid only if it proves the universal inequality \((VG4)\), which is
   precisely the no-gain hypothesis used by
   \cref{lem:implicit-reduced-gain-separation}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Layer-cake coverage separation]
   \label{lem:layer-cake-reduced-gain-separation}
   Work in the notation of
   \cref{lem:reduced-gain-variational-separation}.  For a subset
   \(U\subseteq S\) and a scalar \(\beta\in(0,1]\), define the one-layer
   signed coverage surplus
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \Omega_E(a;U,\beta)
      &=
      \sum_q
      \int
      h_{q,a}(\omega)
      \left[
         \beta\sum_{x\in U}W^E_{x,q}(\omega)
         -|U|\theta_q
      \right]d\nu_q(\omega)\\
      &\qquad - |U|\gamma .
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{LC1}
   \]
   Then a label \(a\) has positive reduced gain if and only if there are
   \(U\subseteq S\) and \(\beta\in(0,1]\) with
   \[
      \Omega_E(a;U,\beta)>0 .
      \tag{LC2}
   \]

   More precisely, for any intensity profile \(s\), let
   \(U_t=\{x:\ s_x>t\}\).  Then
   \[
      \Psi_E(a;s)
      =
      \int_0^\infty
      \Omega_E(a;U_t,e^{-t})\,dt .
      \tag{LC3}
   \]
   Conversely, if \(\Omega_E(a;U,e^{-t_0})>0\), then the uniform profile
   \(s_x=t_0\mathbf 1\{x\in U\}\), or an arbitrarily small positive multiple of
   \(\mathbf 1_U\) when \(t_0=0\), has positive surplus.

   Consequently, if a positive-gain label has a witnessing profile with
   \(0\le s_x\le B\), then it has a positive one-layer witness with
   \(\beta\ge e^{-B}\).  In that \(B\)-truncated case it is enough to test the
   dyadic grid
   \[
      \beta_j=2^{-j},
      \qquad
      0\le j\le\lceil B/\log 2\rceil,
      \tag{LC4}
   \]
   because increasing \(\beta\) can only increase \(\Omega_E(a;U,\beta)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The layer-cake identities
   \[
      s_x=\int_0^\infty \mathbf 1\{s_x>t\}\,dt,
      \qquad
      1-e^{-s_x}=\int_0^\infty e^{-t}\mathbf 1\{s_x>t\}\,dt
   \]
   turn \((VG1)\) into \((LC3)\) after exchanging the finite sums and
   integrable layer terms.  If \(\Psi_E(a;s)>0\), then \((LC3)\) implies that
   \(\Omega_E(a;U_t,e^{-t})>0\) for some \(t\), proving one direction of
   \((LC2)\).

   Conversely, assume \(\Omega_E(a;U,e^{-t_0})>0\).  For every \(0\le t<t_0\),
   monotonicity in the first argument gives
   \[
      \Omega_E(a;U,e^{-t})
      \ge
      \Omega_E(a;U,e^{-t_0})>0 .
   \]
   Hence the profile \(s_x=t_0\mathbf 1\{x\in U\}\) has positive surplus by
   \((LC3)\) when \(t_0>0\).  If \(t_0=0\), the same strict inequality persists
   on a short interval \([0,\varepsilon]\), so
   \(s_x=\varepsilon\mathbf 1\{x\in U\}\) has positive surplus for sufficiently
   small \(\varepsilon>0\).  By
   \cref{lem:reduced-gain-variational-separation}, positive surplus is
   equivalent to positive reduced gain.

   If \(s_x\le B\), then any layer exposed by \((LC3)\) has
   \(t\le B\), hence \(\beta=e^{-t}\ge e^{-B}\).  Choose \(j\) with
   \(\beta\le 2^{-j}\le 2\beta\); this \(j\) lies in the range \((LC4)\).
   Since \(\Omega_E(a;U,\beta)\) is nondecreasing in \(\beta\), the dyadic
   value \(2^{-j}\) is also a positive witness.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Pointwise reduced-cost separation]
   \label{cor:pointwise-reduced-cost-separation}
   Work in the notation of
   \cref{lem:reduced-gain-variational-separation}.  For a candidate label
   \(a\), the following are equivalent:
   \[
      \operatorname{Gain}_E(a)>0,
      \tag{PW1}
   \]
   \[
      \exists x\in S:\quad G_x^E(a)>c_a,
      \tag{PW2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \exists x\in S:\quad
      \sum_q\int h_{q,a}(\omega)W^E_{x,q}(\omega)d\nu_q(\omega)
      >
      \gamma+\sum_q\theta_q\int h_{q,a}(\omega)d\nu_q(\omega).
      \tag{PW3}
   \]
   Equivalently, a reduced-gain separator may search over point-label pairs
   with the signed point score
   \[
      \operatorname{Score}_E(x,a)
      =
      \sum_q\int h_{q,a}(\omega)W^E_{x,q}(\omega)d\nu_q(\omega)
      -
      \gamma-\sum_q\theta_q\int h_{q,a}(\omega)d\nu_q(\omega).
      \tag{PW4}
   \]
   Returning any pair with \(\operatorname{Score}_E(x,a)>0\) is a valid
   improving column.  Conversely, if
   \[
      \operatorname{Score}_E(x,a)\le0
      \qquad(x\in S,\ a\in\mathcal U)
      \tag{PW5}
   \]
   for an implicit label universe \(\mathcal U\), then the no-positive-gain
   condition \((IG3)\) of \cref{lem:implicit-reduced-gain-separation} holds on
   \(\mathcal U\), and the current dual obstruction rules out every
   finite-support extension inside that universe.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By definition,
   \[
      \operatorname{Gain}_E(a)=\sum_x\Phi_{c_a}(G_x^E(a)).
   \]
   The scalar formula \((BG2)\) gives
   \(\Phi_c(G)>0\) exactly when \(G>c\), including the case \(c=0\).  Therefore
   the sum is positive exactly when at least one point satisfies
   \(G_x^E(a)>c_a\), proving \((PW1)\iff(PW2)\).  Expanding the definitions of
   \(G_x^E(a)\) and \(c_a\) gives \((PW2)\iff(PW3)\), and \((PW4)\) is the same
   inequality written as a score.

   A pair with positive score gives positive gain, so it is an improving column
   by \cref{cor:whole-bucket-reduced-gain}.  If \((PW5)\) holds, then
   \(G_x^E(a)\le c_a\) for every \(x\) and \(a\), hence every
   \(\Phi_{c_a}(G_x^E(a))\) vanishes.  Thus
   \(\operatorname{Gain}_E(a)=0\) for every \(a\in\mathcal U\), which is
   exactly \((IG3)\).  The final claim is
   \cref{lem:implicit-reduced-gain-separation}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[LP range reporting as an offline separator]
   \label{rem:lp-range-reporting-separator}
   The reduced-cost separator above has the same logical shape as the
   fixed-dimensional linear-programming query literature.  In the
   Matousek--Chan--Ramos line of work, one optimizes over a small candidate
   basis and then uses halfspace range reporting to expose constraints violated
   by the candidate; Chan's LP-with-violations algorithms similarly organize
   the search by low-level violators rather than by scanning all
   constraints~\cite{Cha96LP,Ram00LP,Cha04Viol}.

   This is not an online ANN primitive for the present problem.  Those data
   structures are strongest in constant geometric dimension, while our
   terminal dimension is logarithmic or polylogarithmic, and the ANN exponent
   target is controlled by storage/far-load/near-mass spectrum rather than by
   ordinary halfspace query time.  The useful transfer is instead
   \emph{offline}: if an implicit label family has a low-dimensional
   parameterization and the reporter events \(h_{q,a}\) are halfspace or
   constant-complexity semialgebraic conditions in \(a\), then
   \((PW4)\) is exactly a weighted range-reporting or range-maximization
   objective.  Expensive preprocessing may therefore build a violator reporter
   that either returns a point-label pair with positive reduced cost or
   certifies that no such low-dimensional label exists.  Exact verification by
   \cref{cor:pointwise-reduced-cost-separation} keeps the retained ANN index
   self-contained: failed or approximate range-reporting proposals are simply
   discarded, while accepted labels still have to pass the same finite convex
   certificate.
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[Finite rate-coverage column generation]
   \label{lem:finite-rate-coverage-column-generation}
   Fix a finite candidate label family \(\mathcal B\) and a reporter
   \(A_q(\omega)\subseteq\mathcal B\).  Let
   \(E\subseteq S\times\mathcal B\) be an active set of point-label variables,
   and consider the restricted version of \((FC1)\)--\((FC3)\) in which
   \(b_{x,a}\) is allowed to be nonzero only for \((x,a)\in E\).  Suppose this
   restricted system is infeasible and has a dual certificate
   \((\lambda,\theta,\gamma)\) as in \((FC4)\).  Assume the corresponding
   restricted Lagrangian infimum is attained at \(b^E\).

   For any candidate pair \((x,a)\in S\times\mathcal B\), define
   \[
      c_a=\gamma+\sum_q\theta_q\Pr_{\nu_q}[a\in A_q(\omega)]
      \tag{GC0}
   \]
   and
   \[
      G_x^E(a)
      =
      \sum_{q:\,(x,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \lambda_{x,q}
      \int
      r_{x,q}(\omega)\mathbf 1\{a\in A_q(\omega)\}
      \exp\!\left(
         -\sum_{a'\in A_q(\omega)}b^E_{x,a'}
      \right)d\nu_q(\omega),
      \tag{GC1}
   \]
   with \(b^E_{x,a'}=0\) outside \(E\).  If
   \[
      G_x^E(a)\le c_a
      \qquad\text{for every inactive }(x,a)\notin E,
      \tag{GC2}
   \]
   then the same dual certificate proves infeasibility of the full convex system
   over all variables \(S\times\mathcal B\).

   Consequently, if the full candidate system over \(\mathcal B\) is feasible,
   then every infeasible restricted solve with an attained dual minimizer has an
   inactive pair \((x,a)\notin E\) with
   \[
      G_x^E(a)>c_a .
      \tag{GC3}
   \]
   Adding such a pair is a valid column-generation step.  Since
   \(S\times\mathcal B\) is finite, exhaustive column generation reaches a
   feasible restricted certificate whenever the full finite candidate family is
   feasible.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(\mathcal L_E\) be the dual Lagrangian in \((FC4)\), restricted to the
   active variables.  Since \(b^E\) attains its infimum on the nonnegative active
   orthant, the directional derivative in every active coordinate is
   nonnegative when the coordinate is zero and is zero when the coordinate is
   positive.  In the notation above, this is
   \[
      G_x^E(a)\le c_a,\qquad
      b^E_{x,a}\bigl(c_a-G_x^E(a)\bigr)=0
      \qquad((x,a)\in E).
      \tag{GC4}
   \]
   These are the KKT conditions for the convex differentiable Lagrangian on the
   active orthant.

   If \((GC2)\) also holds for inactive variables, then \(b^E\), extended by
   zero outside \(E\), satisfies the KKT conditions for the full nonnegative
   orthant \(S\times\mathcal B\).  Convexity therefore makes it a global
   minimizer of the full Lagrangian.  The restricted dual certificate has
   \[
      \mathcal L_E(b^E)>
      \sum_{(p,q)}\lambda_{p,q}\tau_{p,q}
      +\sum_q\theta_q\ell_q+\gamma S_0 ,
   \]
   and the full Lagrangian has the same value at the zero-extended \(b^E\).
   Hence the full infimum is also larger than the weighted target, so
   \((FC4)\) holds for the full system.  This proves full infeasibility.

   The contrapositive gives \((GC3)\) whenever the full candidate system is
   feasible.  Adding a positive-gain inactive pair strictly enlarges \(E\).
   There are only \(|S|\,|\mathcal B|\) pairs, so exhaustive repetition either
   reaches a feasible restricted system or exhausts all pairs.  The latter would
   contradict feasibility of the full system by the first part.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Seeded reduced-gain search]
   \label{lem:seeded-reduced-gain-search}
   Work in the finite candidate setting of
   \cref{lem:finite-rate-coverage-column-generation}.  At an infeasible
   restricted solve with attained minimizer \(b^E\) and dual multipliers
   \((\lambda,\theta,\gamma)\), define \(c_a\), \(G_x^E(a)\), and
   \(\Phi_c\) by \((GC0)\), \((GC1)\), and \((BG2)\).  For a candidate label
   \(a\in\mathcal B\), put
   \[
      \operatorname{Gain}_E(a)
      =
      \sum_{x\in S}\Phi_{c_a}\!\left(G_x^E(a)\right).
      \tag{SG1}
   \]
   Let \(\mathsf P_E\) be any possibly randomized preprocessing proposal
   routine that outputs labels in \(\mathcal B\).  Suppose that, whenever the
   full finite candidate system over \(\mathcal B\) is feasible but the current
   restricted system is infeasible,
   \[
      \Pr_{a\sim\mathsf P_E}\!\left[
         \operatorname{Gain}_E(a)>0
      \right]\ge p_E .
      \tag{SG2}
   \]
   Then exact verification of proposed labels and Las Vegas repetition finds a
   positive-gain label after expected at most \(1/p_E\) proposals.  Adding all
   inactive pairs
   \[
      (x,a)\notin E
      \qquad\text{with}\qquad
      G_x^E(a)>c_a
      \tag{SG3}
   \]
   is a valid column-generation augmentation.

   Consequently, if \(p_E\ge p_0>0\) at every infeasible restricted solve, the
   seeded column-generation algorithm reaches a feasible active certificate in
   expected at most
   \[
      |S|\,|\mathcal B|/p_0
   \]
   proposal calls.  More generally, the same conclusion holds with total
   expected proposal count bounded by the sum of \(1/p_E\) over the
   augmentations that occur.  If instead one runs
   \(R=\lceil p_E^{-1}\log(1/\delta)\rceil\) independent proposals at a fixed
   restricted solve, a positive-gain label is found with probability at least
   \(1-\delta\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{cor:whole-bucket-reduced-gain}, \(\operatorname{Gain}_E(a)>0\)
   is equivalent to the existence of at least one point \(x\) with
   \(G_x^E(a)>c_a\), and the simultaneous assignment \(s_x\) in \((BG3)\)
   strictly decreases the dual Lagrangian.  Thus every pair in \((SG3)\) is an
   improving inactive column in the sense of
   \cref{lem:finite-rate-coverage-column-generation}.

   Exact verification computes \(\operatorname{Gain}_E(a)\) for each proposed
   label and accepts precisely when it is positive.  Under \((SG2)\), the
   number of proposals until acceptance is stochastically dominated by a
   geometric random variable of mean \(1/p_E\), and \(R\) independent proposals
   fail with probability at most \((1-p_E)^R\le\delta\).

   Each successful augmentation adds at least one previously inactive pair
   \((x,a)\) and never removes active pairs.  There are only
   \(|S|\,|\mathcal B|\) such pairs.  If the full candidate system is feasible,
   \cref{lem:finite-rate-coverage-column-generation} guarantees that an
   infeasible restricted solve always has a positive-gain inactive pair; the
   exposure hypothesis \((SG2)\) lets the seeded proposal routine find one with
   the displayed expected effort.  Summing the geometric waiting times over the
   finitely many augmentations proves the expected proposal bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Implicit reduced-gain separation]
   \label{lem:implicit-reduced-gain-separation}
   Let \(\mathcal U\) be an arbitrary implicit label universe.  For each
   \(a\in\mathcal U\) and query \(q\), let
   \(h_{q,a}(\omega)=\mathbf 1\{a\in A_q(\omega)\}\) be a measurable reporter
   event.  Let \(E\subseteq S\times\mathcal U\) be finite, and consider the
   restricted rate-coverage system in which only variables in \(E\) may be
   nonzero.  Suppose this restricted system is infeasible, has a dual
   certificate \((\lambda,\theta,\gamma)\), and has an attained restricted
   dual minimizer \(b^E\).

   For every \(a\in\mathcal U\), define
   \[
      c_a=\gamma+\sum_q\theta_q\int h_{q,a}(\omega)\,d\nu_q(\omega),
      \tag{IG0}
   \]
   \[
      G_x^E(a)
      =
      \sum_{q:\,(x,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \lambda_{x,q}
      \int
      r_{x,q}(\omega)h_{q,a}(\omega)
      \exp\!\left(
         -\sum_{(x,a')\in E}
         h_{q,a'}(\omega)b^E_{x,a'}
      \right)d\nu_q(\omega),
      \tag{IG1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \operatorname{Gain}_E(a)
      =
      \sum_{x\in S}\Phi_{c_a}\!\left(G_x^E(a)\right).
      \tag{IG2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \operatorname{Gain}_E(a)=0
      \qquad(a\in\mathcal U),
      \tag{IG3}
   \]
   then the same dual certificate proves infeasibility of every finite-support
   extension of \(E\) inside \(S\times\mathcal U\).  Equivalently, no feasible
   rate-coverage certificate with finite label support exists in
   \(\mathcal U\).

   Thus an exact reduced-gain separator for \(\mathcal U\), which either
   returns a label \(a\) with \(\operatorname{Gain}_E(a)>0\) or certifies
   \((IG3)\), is a complete build-time separation oracle for finite-support
   certificates.  If the finite-support system over \(\mathcal U\) is feasible
   and the current restricted system is infeasible, the separator must return a
   positive-gain label.

   Moreover, suppose labels are quotient by the equivalence relation
   \(a\sim a'\) when
   \(h_{q,a}=h_{q,a'}\) \(\nu_q\)-almost everywhere for every \(q\), and the
   quotient has \(N\) classes.  If column generation keeps at most one
   representative of each quotient class and adds all pairs
   \((x,a)\) with \(G_x^E(a)>c_a\) for every positive-gain representative it
   receives, then an exact separator over quotient representatives either
   produces a feasible active certificate or proves finite-support
   infeasibility after at most \(|S|N\) successful augmentations.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The attained minimizer \(b^E\) satisfies the active KKT conditions exactly
   as in the proof of \cref{lem:finite-rate-coverage-column-generation}:
   \[
      G_x^E(a)\le c_a,\qquad
      b^E_{x,a}\bigl(c_a-G_x^E(a)\bigr)=0
      \qquad((x,a)\in E).
      \tag{IG4}
   \]
   Since \(\Phi_c(G)=0\) is equivalent to \(G\le c\), condition \((IG3)\)
   implies \(G_x^E(a)\le c_a\) for every inactive pair
   \((x,a)\notin E\).  Hence \(b^E\), extended by zero, satisfies the KKT
   conditions on \(E\cup F\) for every finite set
   \(F\subseteq S\times\mathcal U\).  Convexity of the finite-dimensional
   Lagrangian on that active orthant makes this extension a global minimizer
   over \(E\cup F\).

   The restricted dual certificate has Lagrangian value strictly larger than
   the weighted target in \((FC4)\).  The zero-extended point has the same value
   on every finite extension \(E\cup F\), and it is the minimizer there.  Thus
   the same multipliers satisfy \((FC4)\) for every finite extension.  Every
   finite-support rate-coverage certificate uses some such finite set \(F\), so
   no finite-support feasible certificate can exist.

   The separator statement is the contrapositive: if a finite-support feasible
   certificate exists and the current restricted system is infeasible, then
   \((IG3)\) cannot hold, so some label has positive gain and an exact separator
   must return one.  The quotient statement follows because all quantities
   \((IG0)\)--\((IG2)\), and all primal constraints involving a label, depend
   only on the reporter events \(h_{q,a}\) up to \(\nu_q\)-null sets.  With one
   representative per quotient class, each successful augmentation adds at
   least one previously inactive pair in the finite set of size \(|S|N\).
   If the process exhausts those pairs without feasibility, the no-positive-gain
   certificate above proves finite-support infeasibility over the entire
   quotient universe.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One-sided reduced-gain column generation]
   \label{cor:one-sided-reduced-gain-column-generation}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:implicit-reduced-gain-separation}, at an
   infeasible restricted solve with attained minimizer \(b^E\) and dual
   multipliers \((\lambda,\theta,\gamma)\).  A point report is a tuple
   \((x,a,X)\) satisfying the one-sided certificate
   \[
      0<X\le G_x^E(a)-c_a,
      \tag{ORG1}
   \]
   and a label report is a tuple \((a,X)\) satisfying
   \[
      0<X\le \operatorname{Gain}_E(a).
      \tag{ORG2}
   \]
   Suppose a preprocessing oracle, for every restricted dual state, either
   returns a point report, returns a label report whose exact point scores can
   be evaluated for the reported label, or certifies the no-positive condition
   \[
      G_x^E(a)\le c_a
      \qquad(x\in S,\ a\in\mathcal U).
      \tag{ORG3}
   \]
   Then this one-sided oracle is a complete column-generation oracle for
   finite-support rate-coverage certificates inside \(\mathcal U\).

   On a point report, add the single pair \((x,a)\).  On a label report, first
   verify \((ORG2)\) by exact evaluation of \(G_x^E(a)\) and \(c_a\), then add
   all pairs \((x,a)\) with \(G_x^E(a)>c_a\).  At least one such pair exists.
   If labels are quotiented into \(N\) reporter-event classes as in
   \cref{lem:implicit-reduced-gain-separation}, repeated one-sided column
   generation either finds a feasible active certificate or proves
   finite-support infeasibility after at most \(|S|N\) successful
   augmentations.

   The same statement holds for randomized proposal laws: if, whenever a
