   Finally, Chebyshev gives \(D(v)=rh+o(r)\) with probability \(1-o(1)\);
   substituting \(r=\kappa\log m\) and \(|Q|\le\log^C m\) gives \((GTK4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Product-sign scale tradeoff for query lists]
   \label{cor:product-sign-scale-tradeoff}
   The entropy obstruction in
   \cref{lem:growing-product-sign-top-k-barrier} is not removed by increasing
   the product-sign bit scale.  Fix \(a\in(0,1)\), \(\kappa,b>0\), and let
   \[
      r=\lceil\kappa\log m\rceil,
      \qquad
      \beta=b/\log m .
   \]
   In the ideal Gaussian product-sign model, let
   \[
      (U_i,V_i)=\sigma_m(G_i,H_i),
      \qquad
      \operatorname{Corr}(G_i,H_i)=a,
   \]
   independently over \(i\), where \(1\le\sigma_m\le\log m\).  Let
   \(K_p,K_q\) be the corresponding product-sign laws, let
   \(\mathsf A_\beta(p,q)=\sum_sK_p(s)^\beta K_q(s)^{1-\beta}\), and let
   \(W_{p,q}\) be the tilted label law.  For every fixed list exponent \(C\)
   and every fixed \(A\), with probability \(1-o(1)\) over the bit logits,
   every query-facing label set \(Q\subseteq\{\pm1\}^r\) with
   \(|Q|\le\log^C m\) satisfies
   \[
      \mathcal H_{\xi,Q}(p,q)
      \le
      \log^{-A}m .
      \tag{PSTrade1}
   \]

   More quantitatively, there are constants \(c_1,c_2>0\), depending only on
   \(a,\kappa,b\), such that for each fixed \(C'\) the same event gives the two
   simultaneous bounds
   \[
      \mathcal H_{\xi,Q}(p,q)
      \le
      |Q|\exp\!\left\{-c_1\frac{\log m}{\sigma_m}\right\},
      \tag{PSTrade2}
   \]
   whenever \(\log m/\sigma_m\ge C'\log\log m\), and
   \[
      \mathcal H_{\xi,Q}(p,q)
      \le
      \mathsf A_\beta(p,q)
      \le
      \exp\{-c_2\sigma_m\}
      \tag{PSTrade3}
   \]
   whenever \(\sigma_m\le\log m\).  Thus one cannot tune the bit scale to make
   a growing-width product-sign panel output-sensitive: making the tilted law
   spiky enough for a polylogarithmic list forces \(\sigma_m\) large, but then
   the Hellinger affinity factor in the finite-channel value is already
   smaller than every inverse polylogarithm.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   First consider the tilted min-entropy.  In the notation of
   \cref{lem:growing-product-sign-top-k-barrier}, put
   \(v_i=\beta U_i+(1-\beta)V_i\).  Then
   \[
      D(v)=\sum_{i=1}^r\log(1+e^{-2|v_i|})
   \]
   is the negative logarithm of the largest atom of the tilted product-sign
   law.  Each \(v_i\) is a centered Gaussian with standard deviation between
   \((1-a)^{1/2}\sigma_m/2\) and \(2\sigma_m\) for all large \(m\).  Hence, for
   \(\sigma\ge1\),
   \[
      \E\log(1+e^{-2\sigma |H|})
      \ge \frac{c}{\sigma},
      \tag{PSTrade4}
   \]
   because on \(|H|\le1/\sigma\) the summand is bounded below by an absolute
   constant and that event has probability \(\Theta(1/\sigma)\).  The summands
   are independent and bounded, so Bernstein's inequality implies that, when
   \(r/\sigma_m\ge C'\log\log m\) with \(C'\) large enough,
   \[
      D(v)\ge c_1\frac{\log m}{\sigma_m}
   \]
   with probability \(1-o(1)\).  Combining this with
   \((GTK2)\)--\((GTK3)\) gives \((PSTrade2)\).

   For the affinity side, write the one-bit log-affinity as
   \[
      F_\beta(U,V)
      =
      \log\cosh(\beta U+(1-\beta)V)
      -\beta\log\cosh U
      -(1-\beta)\log\cosh V .
   \]
   By Holder, \(F_\beta\le0\).  Put \(\theta=\beta\sigma\).  The expectation
   has the following uniform negative drift.  First,
   \[
      \left.\frac{d}{d\beta}\E F_\beta(\sigma G,\sigma H)\right|_{\beta=0}
      =
      -(1-a)\E[\sigma H\tanh(\sigma H)]
      \le -c\sigma ,
      \tag{PSTrade5a}
   \]
   uniformly for \(\sigma\ge1\), and the second derivative is
   \(O(\sigma^2)\).  Hence, when \(\theta\le\theta_0\) for a sufficiently small
   fixed \(\theta_0\),
   \[
      \E F_\beta(\sigma G,\sigma H)\le -c\theta .
      \tag{PSTrade5b}
   \]
   On the complementary range, \(\theta\ge\theta_0\), we have
   \(\sigma\to\infty\) because \(\beta=b/\log m\).  For every fixed
   \(\theta\in[\theta_0,b]\),
   \[
      \E F_{\theta/\sigma}(\sigma G,\sigma H)
      \to
      \theta\E[G\operatorname{sign}H-|G|]
      =
      -\theta(1-a)\sqrt{\frac2\pi},
      \tag{PSTrade5}
   \]
   where the contribution from \(|H|=O(1/\sigma)\) is negligible.  Compactness
   in \(\theta\in[\theta_0,b]\) then gives a negative constant upper bound in
   this range.  Combining the two regimes, for all \(1\le\sigma_m\le\log m\)
   and all large \(m\),
   \[
      \E F_\beta(U,V)
      \le
      -c\min\{\beta\sigma_m,1\}.
      \tag{PSTrade6}
   \]
   The same parameter controls concentration.  Since \(\log\cosh\) is
   \(1\)-Lipschitz,
   \[
      -2\beta |U_i-V_i|
      \le
      F_\beta(U_i,V_i)
      \le0 ,
      \tag{PSTrade7}
   \]
   so the centered variables are sub-exponential with scale
   \(O(\beta\sigma_m)\) when \(\beta\sigma_m\le1\), and with constant scale
   when \(\beta\sigma_m\ge1\).  Bernstein's inequality therefore gives
   \[
      \log\mathsf A_\beta(p,q)
      =
      \sum_{i=1}^rF_\beta(U_i,V_i)
      \le
      -c_2\min\{\beta\sigma_m,1\}r
      \le
      -c_2\sigma_m
   \]
   with probability \(1-o(1)\), using \(r=\kappa\log m\) and
   \(\beta=b/\log m\).  Since
   \(\mathcal H_{\xi,Q}\le\mathcal H_\xi\le\mathsf A_\beta\), this proves
   \((PSTrade3)\).

   Finally choose \(C'\) in the first case large enough compared with
   \(A+C\).  If \(\log m/\sigma_m\ge C'\log\log m\), then
   \((PSTrade2)\) gives \(\mathcal H_{\xi,Q}\le\log^{-A}m\).  Otherwise
   \(\sigma_m\ge \log m/(C'\log\log m)\), and \((PSTrade3)\) is
   superpolylogarithmically small.  This proves \((PSTrade1)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Sampled product-sign storage/far-load obstruction]
   \label{lem:sampled-product-sign-rate-obstruction}
   Consider the ideal iid Gaussian product-sign panel with \(r=\kappa\log m\)
   bits and \(B=2^r\) labels.  Store \(x\) in label \(s\) when
   \[
      \Psi_s(x)\ge rt,
   \]
   and on query \(q\) sample \(s\) from the product-sign query law \(K_q\).
   Let
   \[
      I_\sigma(t)=
      \sup_{\theta\ge0}
      \left\{\theta t-\log\E e^{\theta(Z-\log\cosh Z)}\right\},
      \qquad Z\sim N(0,\sigma^2),
   \]
   be the fixed-label upper-tail rate.  If this sampled panel has expected
   per-point storage \(m^{\rho+o(1)}\) and sampled far-bucket probability
   \(m^{-(1-\rho)+o(1)}\), then necessarily
   \[
      \frac{I_\sigma(t)}{\log2}\ge1-\rho-o(1).
      \tag{SPR1}
   \]
   In particular, if near success requires \(t<\mu_0\) and
   \[
      \sup_{t<\mu_0}\frac{I_\sigma(t)}{\log2}<1-\rho
      \tag{SPR2}
   \]
   for the chosen bit law, then query-Gibbs sampling of the same growing
   product-sign panel cannot satisfy \cref{prop:sampled-structured-panel}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed data point, symmetry gives
   \[
      \E[\#\{s:\Psi_s(x)\ge rt\}]
      =
      2^r\Pr\!\left[\sum_{a=1}^r
      (Z_a-\log\cosh Z_a)\ge rt\right]
      =
      \exp\{r(\log2-I_\sigma(t)+o(1))\}.
   \]
   The storage bound therefore implies
   \[
      \kappa(\log2-I_\sigma(t))\le\rho+o(1).
      \tag{SPR3}
   \]
   For a far point with zero query correlation, the query-sampled signs have the
   same unconditional fixed-label tail for \(\Psi_s(x)\), so the sampled far
   probability is \(\exp\{-r(I_\sigma(t)+o(1))\}\).  The far-load target implies
   \[
      \kappa I_\sigma(t)\ge1-\rho-o(1).
      \tag{SPR4}
   \]
   Adding \((SPR3)\) and \((SPR4)\), or equivalently eliminating \(\kappa\),
   gives \((SPR1)\).  If \((SPR2)\) holds, no threshold below the near mean can
   satisfy this necessary storage/far-load condition.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Stable small quotients do not rescue product-sign sampling]
   \label{cor:stable-small-quotient-product-sign-obstruction}
   Work in the product-sign setting of
   \cref{lem:sampled-product-sign-rate-obstruction}.  Let the sign labels be
   partitioned into classes \(A_\ell\), and let the quotient bucket be the
   ordinary union
   \[
      C_\ell=\{x:\exists s\in A_\ell,\ \Psi_s(x)\ge rt\}.
   \]
   For a query \(q\), let \(K_q(s)\) be the product-sign query law and let
   \(\Pi_q(\ell)=\sum_{s\in A_\ell}K_q(s)\).  Suppose that
   \[
      |A_\ell|\le M_m=\log^{O_c(1)}m
      \tag{PSQ1}
   \]
   for every quotient class, and that ordinary union scanning is stable in the
   sense that, for all query/load pairs under consideration,
   \[
      \mathbf 1_{\{x\in C_\ell\}}\Pi_q(\ell)
      \le
      K_m\sum_{s\in A_\ell}K_q(s)
      \mathbf 1_{\{\Psi_s(x)\ge rt\}},
      \qquad
      K_m=\log^{O_c(1)}m .
      \tag{PSQ2}
   \]
   If the quotient panel satisfies the sampled terminal bounds
   \((SP1)\)--\((SP3)\) with polylogarithmic slack, then the unquotiented
   product-sign sampled panel satisfies the same storage and far-load bounds,
   and its near hit probability is smaller by at most the polylogarithmic
   factor \(K_m\).  Consequently the necessary rate condition
   \[
      \frac{I_\sigma(t)}{\log2}\ge1-\rho-o(1)
      \tag{PSQ3}
   \]
   still holds.  In particular, a stable quotient with polylogarithmic class
   size cannot evade the sampled product-sign obstruction.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Write
   \[
      U_x(s)=\mathbf 1_{\{\Psi_s(x)\ge rt\}} .
   \]
   The hidden, unquotiented storage is controlled by the quotient storage:
   for every data point \(x\),
   \[
      \sum_s U_x(s)
      =
      \sum_\ell\sum_{s\in A_\ell}U_x(s)
      \le
      M_m\sum_\ell\mathbf 1_{\{x\in C_\ell\}} .
   \]
   Summing over \(x\) and using \((PSQ1)\), a quotient satisfying \((SP1)\)
   gives the original product-sign labels the same storage exponent, up to a
   polylogarithmic factor.

   For far load, the hidden sampled incidence is no larger than the quotient
   union incidence, because \(U_x(s)=1\) and \(s\in A_\ell\) imply
   \(x\in C_\ell\):
   \[
      \sum_sK_q(s)U_x(s)
      \le
      \sum_\ell\Pi_q(\ell)\mathbf 1_{\{x\in C_\ell\}} .
   \]
   Thus quotient \((SP2)\) implies the hidden product-sign far-load bound.

   Finally, applying the stability inequality \((PSQ2)\) with \(x=p\) and
   summing over \(\ell\) gives
   \[
      \sum_{\ell:p\in C_\ell}\Pi_q(\ell)
      \le
      K_m\sum_sK_q(s)U_p(s).
   \]
   Hence a quotient near mass at least \(\log^{-O_c(1)}m\) implies hidden
   product-sign near mass at least \(\log^{-O_c(1)}m\).  The hidden sampled
   panel therefore has the same polynomial storage and far-load exponents as
   in \cref{lem:sampled-product-sign-rate-obstruction}.  Applying that lemma
   yields \((PSQ3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Ordinary product-sign quotient class-size lower bound]
   \label{cor:ordinary-product-sign-quotient-class-size}
   Work in the same ideal iid Gaussian product-sign model, and let the sign
   labels be partitioned into ordinary union buckets \(C_\ell\) as in
   \cref{cor:stable-small-quotient-product-sign-obstruction}.  Put
   \[
      M_m=\max_\ell |A_\ell|,
      \qquad
      \delta_m=\frac{\log M_m}{\log m}.
   \]
   Suppose that the quotient has expected per-point bucket storage
   \(m^{\rho+o(1)}\), and that for a zero-correlation far point the quotient
   sampled bucket probability is at most \(m^{-(1-\rho)+o(1)}\).  If
   \(I_\sigma(t)>0\), then necessarily
   \[
      \delta_m
      \ge
      \frac{(1-\rho)\log2}{I_\sigma(t)}-1-o(1).
      \tag{OQB1}
   \]
   Equivalently, if all quotient classes have size \(m^{\delta+o(1)}\), then
   \[
      \frac{I_\sigma(t)}{\log2}
      \ge
      \frac{1-\rho}{1+\delta}-o(1).
      \tag{OQB2}
   \]
   Thus an ordinary union quotient at a threshold whose fixed-label rate
   fraction is \(\zeta=I_\sigma(t)/\log2<1-\rho\) must merge at least
   \(m^{(1-\rho)/\zeta-1-o(1)}\) hidden product-sign labels in some stored
   bucket class before storage and far-load can both hold.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(U_x(s)=\mathbf 1_{\{\Psi_s(x)\ge rt\}}\).  For a fixed data point,
   the hidden product-sign incidence count has expectation
   \[
      \E\sum_sU_x(s)
      =
      \exp\{r(\log2-I_\sigma(t)+o(1))\}
      =
      m^{\kappa(\log2-I_\sigma(t))+o(1)}.
      \tag{OQB3}
   \]
   Since every hidden label belongs to one quotient class and each class has
   size at most \(M_m\),
   \[
      \sum_sU_x(s)
      \le
      M_m\sum_\ell\mathbf 1_{\{x\in C_\ell\}} .
   \]
   The quotient storage bound therefore gives
   \[
      \kappa(\log2-I_\sigma(t))
      \le \rho+\delta_m+o(1).
      \tag{OQB4}
   \]
   For a zero-correlation far point,
   \[
      \sum_sK_q(s)U_x(s)=m^{-\kappa I_\sigma(t)+o(1)}
   \]
   in the ideal iid model, and this hidden sampled incidence is no larger than
   the quotient sampled incidence.  The quotient far-load bound implies
   \[
      \kappa I_\sigma(t)\ge1-\rho-o(1).
      \tag{OQB5}
   \]
   Combining \((OQB4)\) with the lower bound on \(\kappa\) from \((OQB5)\)
   gives
   \[
      \delta_m
      \ge
      (1-\rho)\left(\frac{\log2-I_\sigma(t)}{I_\sigma(t)}\right)-\rho-o(1)
      =
      \frac{(1-\rho)\log2}{I_\sigma(t)}-1-o(1),
   \]
   which is \((OQB1)\).  Rearranging gives \((OQB2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Aggregate-responsibility product-sign rate obstruction]
   \label{cor:aggregate-responsibility-product-sign-obstruction}
   Consider the ideal iid Gaussian product-sign panel with \(r=\kappa\log m\),
   but now give the quotient the strongest possible storage aggregation: all
   hidden labels may be represented by one bucket, and the query may emit a
   point \(x\) with probability \(\theta_q(x)\) comparable to its hidden
   product-sign responsibility
   \[
      h_q(x)=
      \Pr_{s\sim K_q}\!\left[\Psi_s(x)\ge rt\right],
      \qquad
      h_q(x)\le\theta_q(x)\le \log^{O_c(1)}m\,h_q(x).
      \tag{ARP1}
   \]
   Assume zero-correlation far points and near pairs whose per-bit product-sign
   logit correlation is \(a\in(0,1)\).  Let
   \[
      \mu_{\sigma,a}
      =
      \E[Z-\log\cosh Z]
      +
      a\sigma^2\E[\operatorname{sech}^2 Z],
      \qquad Z\sim N(0,\sigma^2),
      \tag{ARP2}
   \]
   be the near per-bit mean of \(\Psi_s(p)\) under \(s\sim K_q\), and let
   \(I_\sigma\) be the fixed-label rate from
   \cref{lem:sampled-product-sign-rate-obstruction}.  If the aggregate
   responsibility sampler has far emitted load \(m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m\) and
   emits every near witness with probability at least \(\log^{-O_c(1)}m\), then
   necessarily
   \[
      \frac{I_\sigma(\mu_{\sigma,a})}{\log2}
      \ge
      1-\rho-o(1).
      \tag{ARP3}
   \]
   Therefore, if \(I_\sigma(\mu_{\sigma,a})/\log2<1-\rho\), even a perfect
   aggregate bucket with responsibility-thinned output cannot turn this
   product-sign threshold panel into a sampled terminal ANN panel.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For a zero-correlation far point \(x\), the query signs are independent of
   the data logits, so
   \[
      h_q(x)
      =
      \Pr\!\left[
         \sum_{b=1}^r
         (Z_b-\log\cosh Z_b)\ge rt
      \right]
      =
      m^{-\kappa I_\sigma(t)+o(1)} .
   \]
   Since \(\theta_q(x)\ge h_q(x)\), the far-load bound over \(m\) possible far
   points forces
   \[
      \kappa I_\sigma(t)\ge1-\rho-o(1).
      \tag{ARP4}
   \]

   For a near pair \(p,q\), the per-bit summands of \(\Psi_s(p)\) under
   \(s\sim K_q\) are iid with mean \(\mu_{\sigma,a}\).  If
   \(t\ge\mu_{\sigma,a}+\varepsilon\) for some fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), the
   Cramer upper tail under the near law is \(m^{-\Omega_{\varepsilon}(1)}\).
   The upper comparison in \((ARP1)\) would then give
   \(\theta_q(p)=m^{-\Omega_{\varepsilon}(1)}\), contradicting the required
   inverse-polylogarithmic near emission probability.  Hence
   \(t\le\mu_{\sigma,a}+o(1)\).  The fixed-label upper-tail rate is continuous
   and nondecreasing on the upper-tail side, so
   \[
      I_\sigma(t)\le I_\sigma(\mu_{\sigma,a})+o(1).
   \]
   Combining this inequality with \((ARP4)\) proves \((ARP3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Posterior-rank margin certificate]\label{lem:posterior-rank-margin}
   Let
   \[
      \mathsf A_\beta(p,q)=\sum_j K_p(j)^\beta K_q(j)^{1-\beta}
   \]
   If $\mathsf A_\beta(p,q)=0$, then the right-hand side below is interpreted as $0$. Otherwise let $W_{p,q}$ be the tilted outcome law
   \[
      W_{p,q}(j)=\frac{K_p(j)^\beta K_q(j)^{1-\beta}}{\mathsf A_\beta(p,q)}.
   \]
   For $\Delta\ge0$, define
   \[
      G_\Delta(p)=\{j:R_j(p)\ge e^\Delta\tau_j\}.
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \mathcal H_\xi(p,q)
      \ge
      (1-e^{-\beta\Delta})\,
      \mathsf A_\beta(p,q)\,
      W_{p,q}(G_\Delta(p)).
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   On $G_\Delta(p)$,
   \[
      R_j(p)^\beta-\tau_j^\beta
      \ge (1-e^{-\beta\Delta})R_j(p)^\beta.
   \]
   Multiplying by $\mu_j^\beta K_q(j)^{1-\beta}$ gives
   \[
      (1-e^{-\beta\Delta})K_p(j)^\beta K_q(j)^{1-\beta}.
   \]
   Summing over $G_\Delta(p)$ proves the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Bounded rank margins already give polylog value]
   \label{cor:bounded-rank-margin-polylog-value}
   Keep the notation of \cref{lem:posterior-rank-margin}.  Fix
   \(\Delta_0>0\).  If
   \[
      \mathsf A_\beta(p,q)\ge a_m,
      \qquad
      W_{p,q}(G_{\Delta_0}(p))\ge w_m,
   \]
   then, whenever \(\beta\Delta_0\le1\),
   \[
      \mathcal H_\xi(p,q)
      \ge
      \frac{\beta\Delta_0}{2}\,a_mw_m.
   \]
   In particular, for \(\beta=\Theta_c(1/\log m)\), inverse-polylogarithmic
   lower bounds on \(a_m\) and \(w_m\) imply the
   \(\log^{-O_c(1)}m\) restricted value required by the finite-channel
   compiler.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For \(0\le x\le1\), \(1-e^{-x}\ge x/2\).  Apply this to
   \(x=\beta\Delta_0\) in \cref{lem:posterior-rank-margin}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Small-width product-sign ceiling barrier]
   \label{lem:product-sign-ceiling-barrier}
   Fix \(\sigma,\gamma,\Delta_0>0\).  Let
   \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_r\) be independent \(N(0,\sigma^2)\) variables and put
   \[
      S_r=\sum_{a=1}^r\bigl(Z_a-\log\cosh Z_a\bigr).
   \]
   Let
   \[
      Q_{r,\eta}:=\sup\{t:\Prb[S_r\ge t]\ge\eta\}
   \]
   be the upper \(\eta\)-threshold of \(S_r\), and set
   \(\eta=m^{-\gamma}\).  If
   \[
      r(1+\log^2 r)=o(\log m),
      \tag{PSB}
   \]
   then, for all sufficiently large \(m\),
   \[
      Q_{r,\eta}\ge r\log2-\Delta_0/2 .
   \]
   Consequently the fixed-margin event
   \[
      \Psi_s(p)\ge Q_{r,\eta}+\Delta_0
   \]
   is impossible for the product-sign score \((PSS)\), since
   \(\Psi_s(p)\le r\log2\).  In particular, fixed-width product-sign
   channels, and product-sign channels with only polylogarithmically many
   outcomes, cannot be the asymptotic proof of the bounded-margin target when
   the Gaussian bit variance is bounded.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The deficit of one fixed-label bit from its ceiling is
   \[
      \log2-\bigl(Z-\log\cosh Z\bigr)
      =
      \log(1+e^{-2Z}).
   \]
   Choose \(t_r=\frac12\log(4r/\Delta_0)\).  On the event
   \(Z_a\ge t_r\) for every \(a\),
   \[
      r\log2-S_r
      =
      \sum_a\log(1+e^{-2Z_a})
      \le
      \sum_a e^{-2t_r}
      =
      \Delta_0/4 .
   \]
   A standard Gaussian tail lower bound gives
   \[
      \Prb[Z\ge t_r]
      \ge
      \exp\{-C_\sigma(1+\log^2 r)\}
   \]
   with \(C_\sigma\) depending only on \(\sigma\).  Hence
   \[
      \Prb[S_r\ge r\log2-\Delta_0/4]
      \ge
      \exp\{-C_\sigma r(1+\log^2 r)\}
      =
      m^{-o(1)}
   \]
   under \((PSB)\).  This probability is larger than \(m^{-\gamma}\) for all
   sufficiently large \(m\), so the upper \(m^{-\gamma}\)-quantile lies at
   least at \(r\log2-\Delta_0/4\), and therefore at least at
   \(r\log2-\Delta_0/2\).  Adding the margin \(\Delta_0\) puts the required
   score above the absolute ceiling \(r\log2\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Product-sign mean-gap certificate]
   \label{lem:product-sign-mean-gap-certificate}
   Fix a product-sign near pair \(p,q\), and write
   \(u^p_a=u_a(p)\), \(u^q_a=u_a(q)\), and
   \[
      v_a=\beta u^p_a+(1-\beta)u^q_a .
   \]
   Under the tilted label law
   \[
      W_{p,q}(s)\propto K_p(s)^\beta K_q(s)^{1-\beta},
      \qquad s\in\{\pm1\}^r,
   \]
   the signs are independent and
   \[
      \E_{W_{p,q}}s_a=\tanh v_a .
   \]
   Hence the product-sign score \(Y=\Psi_s(p)\) has conditional mean and
   variance
   \[
      M_{p,q}
      =
      \sum_{a=1}^r
      \bigl(u^p_a\tanh v_a-\log\cosh u^p_a\bigr),
      \tag{PSM}
   \]
   \[
      V_{p,q}
      =
      \sum_{a=1}^r
      (u^p_a)^2\bigl(1-\tanh^2 v_a\bigr).
      \tag{PSV}
   \]
   Let \(T\) be any posterior-score threshold and \(\Delta_0\ge0\).  If
   \[
      \Gamma=M_{p,q}-(T+\Delta_0)>0,
   \]
   then
   \[
      W_{p,q}\{\Psi_s(p)\ge T+\Delta_0\}
      \ge
      \frac{\Gamma^2}{V_{p,q}+\Gamma^2}.
      \tag{PSC}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The tilted law factorizes because
   \[
      K_p(s)^\beta K_q(s)^{1-\beta}
      \propto
      \exp\!\left(\sum_a s_a
      (\beta u^p_a+(1-\beta)u^q_a)\right).
   \]
   Thus each sign has natural parameter \(v_a\), giving
   \(\E s_a=\tanh v_a\) and
   \(\operatorname{Var}(s_a)=1-\tanh^2v_a\).  Substituting in
   \[
      \Psi_s(p)=\sum_a(s_au^p_a-\log\cosh u^p_a)
   \]
   gives \((PSM)\) and \((PSV)\).  Cantelli's one-sided Chebyshev inequality
   gives
   \[
      W_{p,q}\{Y-M_{p,q}\le-\Gamma\}
      \le
      \frac{V_{p,q}}{V_{p,q}+\Gamma^2},
   \]
   which is exactly \((PSC)\) after taking complements.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[I.i.d. Gaussian growing-width criterion]
   \label{cor:gaussian-growing-width-product-sign}
   Let \((U,V)\) be centered jointly Gaussian with variance \(\sigma^2\) in
   each coordinate and correlation \(a>0\).  Let
   \(\beta=\beta_m\in[0,1]\), and put
   \[
      X=Z-\log\cosh Z,\qquad Z\sim N(0,\sigma^2),
   \]
   and
   \[
      A_m=U\tanh(\beta_m U+(1-\beta_m)V)-\log\cosh U.
   \]
   Suppose a sequence \(r=r(m)\to\infty\) and thresholds \(T_m\) satisfy
   \[
      \Prb\left[\sum_{a=1}^r X_a\ge T_m\right]\le \eta_m
      \tag{GWC1}
   \]
   and, for some fixed \(\varepsilon>0\),
   \[
      T_m+\Delta_0\le r(\E A_m-2\varepsilon)
      \tag{GWC2}
   \]
   for all large \(m\).  Then, for independent \(r\)-bit Gaussian product-sign
   pairs with this coordinate law,
   \[
      W_{p,q}\{\Psi_s(p)\ge T_m+\Delta_0\}
      \ge
      1-O_{\sigma,a,\varepsilon}(1/r)
   \]
   with probability \(1-O_{\sigma,a,\varepsilon}(1/r)\) over the bit
   logits \((u^p,u^q)\).  In particular, taking \(T_m\) to be any valid upper
   \(\eta_m\)-threshold for the fixed-label score proves the distributional
   bounded-margin target in the ideal product-sign model.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For all \(\beta_m\in[0,1]\), the \(A_m\)'s have uniformly bounded second
   moments depending only on \(\sigma\).  The empirical mean of the
   coordinate copies has variance \(O(1/r)\), so by Chebyshev it is at least
   \(\E A_m-\varepsilon\) with probability
   \(1-O(1/r)\).  The empirical average of
   \(U_a^2(1-\tanh^2(\beta_m U_a+(1-\beta_m)V_a))\) also has uniformly
   bounded second moment, so Chebyshev gives that it is \(O(1)\) with the
   same probability.  On this event,
   \(M_{p,q}-(T_m+\Delta_0)\ge r\varepsilon\) and \(V_{p,q}=O(r)\).  Applying
   \cref{lem:product-sign-mean-gap-certificate} gives
   \(1-O(1/r)\) tilted good mass.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cramer-rate product-sign closure in the ideal model]
   \label{cor:cramer-product-sign-closure}
   Keep the notation of \cref{cor:gaussian-growing-width-product-sign}, and
   assume \(\beta_m\to0\).  Define
   \[
      \mu_X=\E[Z-\log\cosh Z],
      \qquad
      \mu_0=\mu_X+a\sigma^2\E[\operatorname{sech}^2 Z],
      \qquad Z\sim N(0,\sigma^2),
   \]
   and the upper-tail Cramer rate
   \[
      I_\sigma(t)
      =
      \sup_{\theta\ge0}
      \left\{\theta t-
      \log\E\exp\bigl(\theta(Z-\log\cosh Z)\bigr)\right\}.
   \]
   For every \(t\in(\mu_X,\mu_0)\) and every
   \(\kappa>\gamma/I_\sigma(t)\), where \(\eta_m=m^{-\gamma}\), the choice
   \[
      r=\lceil\kappa\log m\rceil
   \]
   satisfies the distributional bounded-margin target of
   \cref{cor:gaussian-growing-width-product-sign}.  Moreover, if
   \(\kappa\log2<1\), then the number of product-sign labels
   \(B=2^r=m^{\kappa\log2+o(1)}\) is within the outcome envelope of
   \cref{prop:query-top-k-channel-compiler} for a polynomially small
   \(\xi\ge1/m\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Stein's identity gives
   \[
      \E[U\tanh V]
      =
      \operatorname{Cov}(U,V)\E[\operatorname{sech}^2V]
      =
      a\sigma^2\E[\operatorname{sech}^2Z],
   \]
   so \(\mu_0\) is the \(\beta_m\to0\) limit of \(\E A_m\).  Since
   \(a>0\), \(\mu_0>\mu_X\).  The random variable
   \(X=Z-\log\cosh Z\) has finite moment generating function for every
   real \(\theta\), and therefore \(I_\sigma(t)>0\) for
   \(t>\mu_X\).  Chernoff's bound gives
   \[
      \Prb\!\left[\sum_{a=1}^r X_a\ge rt\right]
      \le
      \exp(-rI_\sigma(t))
      \le
      m^{-\gamma}
   \]
   for all sufficiently large \(m\), by the choice of \(\kappa\).  Thus
   \((GWC1)\) holds with \(T_m=rt\).  Since \(\E A_m\to\mu_0\) and
   \(t<\mu_0\), choose \(\varepsilon>0\) so that
   \(t+\Delta_0/r\le\E A_m-2\varepsilon\) for all large \(m\).  This is
   \((GWC2)\), and \cref{cor:gaussian-growing-width-product-sign} applies.
   The statement about \(B\) follows from \(B=2^{\lceil\kappa\log m\rceil}\)
   and the hypothesis \(\kappa\log2<1\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Whitening-metric calibration]
   \label{lem:whitening-metric-calibration}
   Let \(p,q\in S^{d-1}\), let \(a=\ip{p}{q}\), and let \(H\) be a
   deterministic linear map satisfying
   \[
      \left\|d^{-1}H^\top H-I_d\right\|_{\rm op}\le\delta<1 .
      \tag{WMC1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \lambda^2(1-\delta)
      \le
      \lambda^2\frac{\|Hp\|^2}{d},
      \lambda^2\frac{\|Hq\|^2}{d}
      \le
      \lambda^2(1+\delta),
      \tag{WMC2}
   \]
   and the whitened-metric near-pair correlation
   \[
      a_H=\frac{\ip{Hp}{Hq}}{\|Hp\|\,\|Hq\|}
   \]
   obeys
   \[
      |a_H-a|\le \frac{(1+|a|)\delta}{1-\delta}
      \le \frac{2\delta}{1-\delta}.
      \tag{WMC3}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Write \(d^{-1}H^\top H=I+E\) with \(\|E\|_{\rm op}\le\delta\).  Then
   \(d^{-1}\|Hp\|^2=1+\ip{p}{Ep}\) and similarly for \(q\), proving
   \((WMC2)\).  Also
   \[
      a_H=\frac{a+\ip{p}{Eq}}
      {\sqrt{(1+\ip{p}{Ep})(1+\ip{q}{Eq})}}.
   \]
   The denominator is at least \(1-\delta\), and its reciprocal differs from
   one by at most \(\delta/(1-\delta)\).  Since
   \(|\ip{p}{Eq}|\le\delta\), \((WMC3)\) follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Whitened Gaussian-row product-sign transfer]
   \label{lem:whitened-product-sign-row-law}
   Let \(H:\R^d\to\R^d\) be a deterministic whitening map, let
   \(g_1,\ldots,g_r\) be independent \(N(0,I_d)\) rows, and define the
   implemented product-sign bit logits
   \[
      u_a(x)=\lambda\,d^{-1/2}\ip{g_a}{Hx}.
   \]
   For fixed \(p,q\), conditional on \(H,p,q\), the pairs
   \((u_a(p),u_a(q))\) are independent centered Gaussians with
   \[
      \sigma_p^2=\lambda^2\frac{\|Hp\|^2}{d},
      \qquad
      \sigma_q^2=\lambda^2\frac{\|Hq\|^2}{d},
      \qquad
      a_{p,q}=\frac{\ip{Hp}{Hq}}{\|Hp\|\,\|Hq\|}.
      \tag{WRL}
   \]
   Suppose \(\beta_m\to0\), \(r=\lceil\kappa\log m\rceil\), and
   \(\eta_m=m^{-\gamma}\).  Let \(\mathcal K\) be a compact set of triples
   \((\sigma_p,\sigma_q,a)\) with \(\sigma_p,\sigma_q>0\) and \(a>0\), and
   suppose that all relevant near pairs have their parameters in
   \(\mathcal K\).  Assume there are \(t\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that,
   for every \((\sigma_p,\sigma_q,a)\in\mathcal K\), if
   \((U,V)\) is centered Gaussian with these standard deviations and
   correlation \(a\), then
   \[
      \E\bigl[U\tanh V-\log\cosh U\bigr]\ge t+3\varepsilon
      \tag{WRM}
   \]
   and, for \(U\sim N(0,\sigma_p^2)\),
   \[
      I_{\sigma_p}(t)
      :=
      \sup_{\theta\ge0}
      \left\{\theta t-
      \log\E e^{\theta(U-\log\cosh U)}\right\}
      >
      \gamma/\kappa .
      \tag{WRI}
   \]
   Then the distributional bounded-margin target of
   \cref{cor:gaussian-growing-width-product-sign} holds uniformly for these
   implemented rows, with \(T_m=rt\).  If \(\kappa\log2<1\), the resulting
   product-sign label count is still within the outcome envelope of
   \cref{prop:query-top-k-channel-compiler}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The first assertion is immediate from Gaussian linearity:
   each row contributes the centered Gaussian vector
   \[
      \lambda d^{-1/2}
      \bigl(\ip{g_a}{Hp},\ip{g_a}{Hq}\bigr),
   \]
   and different rows use independent \(g_a\)'s.  Its covariance matrix is
   exactly \((WRL)\).

   Conditional on \(H,p,q\), the product-sign score therefore has the same
   independent-coordinate form as in
   \cref{cor:gaussian-growing-width-product-sign}, except that the two
   marginal variances need not be equal.  The proof of that corollary uses
   only independence, a fixed-label upper-tail bound for
   \(\sum_a(U_a-\log\cosh U_a)\), and a tilted mean gap.  By \((WRI)\) and
   compactness of \(\mathcal K\), Chernoff gives
   \[
      \Prb\left[
        \sum_{a=1}^r(U_a-\log\cosh U_a)\ge rt
      \right]
      \le m^{-\gamma}
   \]
   for all large \(m\), uniformly over \(\mathcal K\).  Since
   \(\beta_m\to0\), the tilted per-bit mean
   \(\E[U\tanh(\beta_mU+(1-\beta_m)V)-\log\cosh U]\) is at least
   \(t+2\varepsilon\) for all large \(m\), again uniformly on
   \(\mathcal K\).  The Chebyshev/Cantelli argument in
   \cref{cor:gaussian-growing-width-product-sign} then gives
   \(1-O_{\mathcal K,\varepsilon}(1/r)\) tilted good mass above
   \(rt+\Delta_0\).  The label-count statement is the same calculation as in
   \cref{cor:cramer-product-sign-closure}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Reference product-sign threshold from scalar covariance]
   \label{lem:product-sign-reference-covariance-transfer}
   For \(s\in\{\pm1\}^r\), put
   \[
      \Phi_s(z)=\sum_{a=1}^r(s_az_a-\log\cosh z_a).
   \]
   Let \(Z\sim N(0,\Sigma)\), let \(Z_0\sim N(0,\sigma^2I_r)\), and assume
   \[
      \left\|\sigma^{-2}\Sigma-I_r\right\|_{\rm op}\le\varepsilon\le1.
      \tag{RCT1}
   \]
   Then for every \(A\ge1\), every \(t\in\R\), and every label \(s\),
   \[
      \Prb\{\Phi_s(Z)\ge r(t+2A\sigma\varepsilon)\}
      \le
      \Prb\{\Phi_s(Z_0)\ge rt\}
      +
      \Prb\{\|G\|_2>A\sqrt r\},
      \tag{RCT2}
   \]
   where \(G\sim N(0,I_r)\).  In particular,
   \[
      \Prb\{\|G\|_2>A\sqrt r\}
      \le
      \exp\left\{
        -\frac r2(A^2-1-\log A^2)
      \right\}
      \qquad(A\ge1).
      \tag{RCT3}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Couple \(Z\) and \(Z_0\) by writing
   \(Z=\Sigma^{1/2}G\) and \(Z_0=\sigma G\), with
   \(G\sim N(0,I_r)\).  From \((RCT1)\),
   \[
      \|\Sigma^{1/2}-\sigma I_r\|_{\rm op}\le\sigma\varepsilon .
   \]
   Also
   \[
      \|\nabla\Phi_s(z)\|_2^2
      =
      \sum_a(s_a-\tanh z_a)^2
      \le 4r,
   \]
   so \(\Phi_s\) is \(2\sqrt r\)-Lipschitz.  On
   \(\{\|G\|_2\le A\sqrt r\}\),
   \[
      |\Phi_s(Z)-\Phi_s(Z_0)|
      \le
      2\sqrt r\,\|\Sigma^{1/2}-\sigma I_r\|_{\rm op}\,\|G\|_2
      \le
      2A\sigma\varepsilon r .
   \]
   This proves \((RCT2)\).  The final bound is the standard Chernoff bound
   for the upper tail of \(\chi^2_r\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Random-row reference threshold transfer]
   \label{cor:random-row-reference-threshold-transfer}
   Suppose the whitened reference distribution is Gaussian with covariance
   \(I_d\), and use product-sign rows
   \(u_a(x)=\lambda d^{-1/2}\ip{g_a}{x}\), with independent
   \(g_a\sim N(0,I_d)\).  Let \(r=\lceil\kappa\log m\rceil\) and
   \(\eta=m^{-\gamma}\).  If the \(r\times r\) row Gram matrix satisfies
   \[
      \left\|d^{-1}GG^\top-I_r\right\|_{\rm op}\le\varepsilon ,
      \tag{RRT1}
   \]
   and if
   \[
      \Prb_{Z\sim N(0,\lambda^2)}
      \left[
        \sum_{a=1}^r(Z_a-\log\cosh Z_a)\ge rt
      \right]
      \le \eta/2,
      \tag{RRT2}
   \]
   while \(\Prb\{\|N(0,I_r)\|_2>A\sqrt r\}\le\eta/2\), then the common
   reference threshold
   \[
      Q^{\rm ref}=r(t+2A\lambda\varepsilon)
      \tag{RRT3}
   \]
   satisfies
   \[
      \Prb_X\{\Psi_s(X)\ge Q^{\rm ref}\}\le\eta
      \qquad\text{for every }s\in\{\pm1\}^r .
   \]
   Moreover, the Gram event \((RRT1)\) holds with probability at least
   \(1-2e^{-u}\) whenever
   \[
      \varepsilon
      \ge
      C\left(\sqrt{\frac{r+u}{d}}+\frac{r+u}{d}\right)
      \tag{RRT4}
   \]
   for a universal constant \(C\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Conditional on \(G\), the reference bit vector
   \((u_1(X),\ldots,u_r(X))\) is centered Gaussian with covariance
   \(\lambda^2d^{-1}GG^\top\).  Apply
   \cref{lem:product-sign-reference-covariance-transfer} with
   \(\sigma=\lambda\).  The iid term is \((RRT2)\), and the Gaussian norm
   tail is at most \(\eta/2\), so \((RRT3)\) is a simultaneous valid
   threshold for all labels.  The last display is the standard Gaussian
   singular-value concentration bound for \(G/\sqrt d\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Spherical shell replacement for product-sign scores]
   \label{lem:product-sign-spherical-shell-transfer}
   For \(s\in\{\pm1\}^r\), write
   \[
      \Phi_s(z)=\sum_{a=1}^r(s_az_a-\log\cosh z_a).
   \]
   Let \(Y\sim N(0,I_d)\), \(X=Y/\|Y\|\), and let \(M:\R^d\to\R^r\) be
   deterministic.  Put
   \[
      Z_{\rm sph}=MX,\qquad Z_{\rm gau}=M(Y/\sqrt d).
   \]
   Then for every \(0<\delta<1\), \(L>0\), \(t\in\R\), and label \(s\),
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \Prb\{\Phi_s(Z_{\rm sph})\ge r(t+2L\delta/(1-\delta))\}
      \le{}&
      \Prb\{\Phi_s(Z_{\rm gau})\ge rt\}  \\
      &+\Prb\{|\|Y\|/\sqrt d-1|>\delta\}
       +\Prb\{\|Z_{\rm gau}\|_2>L\sqrt r\}.
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{SST}
   \]
   Moreover
   \[
      \Prb\{|\|Y\|/\sqrt d-1|>\delta\}
      \le 2\exp(-c\delta^2d)
      \tag{SST2}
   \]
   for a universal constant \(c>0\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   On the shell event \(|\|Y\|/\sqrt d-1|\le\delta\),
   \[
      Z_{\rm sph}=\frac{\sqrt d}{\|Y\|}Z_{\rm gau},
      \qquad
      \|Z_{\rm sph}-Z_{\rm gau}\|_2
      \le \frac{\delta}{1-\delta}\|Z_{\rm gau}\|_2 .
   \]
   The gradient bound used in
   \cref{lem:product-sign-reference-covariance-transfer} gives
   \(\|\nabla\Phi_s(z)\|_2\le2\sqrt r\).  Hence, on the shell event and on
   \(\{\|Z_{\rm gau}\|_2\le L\sqrt r\}\),
   \[
      |\Phi_s(Z_{\rm sph})-\Phi_s(Z_{\rm gau})|
      \le 2L\delta(1-\delta)^{-1}r .
   \]
   This proves \((SST)\).  The final estimate is the standard chi-square shell
   bound.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Spherical random-row reference threshold transfer]
   \label{cor:spherical-random-row-reference-threshold-transfer}
   Let \(X\) be uniform on \(S^{d-1}\), let \(H:\R^d\to\R^d\) be deterministic,
   and use product-sign rows
   \[
      u_a(x)=\lambda d^{-1/2}\ip{g_a}{Hx},
      \qquad g_a\sim N(0,I_d)
   \]
   independently.  Let \(G\) be the \(r\times d\) matrix with rows \(g_a\), and
   suppose
   \[
      \left\|d^{-1}HH^\top-I_d\right\|_{\rm op}\le\delta_H,
      \qquad
      \left\|d^{-1}GG^\top-I_r\right\|_{\rm op}\le\varepsilon_G .
      \tag{SRR1}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      \zeta=\varepsilon_G+\delta_H(1+\varepsilon_G)
      \tag{SRR2}
   \]
   and assume \(\zeta\le1\).  If
   \[
      \Prb_{Z\sim N(0,\lambda^2)}
      \left[
        \sum_{a=1}^r(Z_a-\log\cosh Z_a)\ge rt
      \right]\le \eta_0 ,
      \tag{SRR3}
   \]
   then, for every \(A\ge1\), \(0<\delta_s<1\), and every label \(s\),
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \Prb_X\{\Psi_s(X)\ge
      r(t+2A\lambda\zeta
          +2A\lambda\sqrt{1+\zeta}\,\delta_s/(1-\delta_s))\}
      \le{}&
      \eta_0
      +2\Prb\{\|N(0,I_r)\|_2>A\sqrt r\}  \\
      &+2\exp(-c\delta_s^2d).
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{SRR4}
   \]
   Consequently, when \(r=\Theta(\log m)\), \(d/\log m\to\infty\), and
   \(\delta_H\to0\), the spherical reference threshold has the same per-bit
   level \(t+o(1)\) as the scalar Gaussian reference threshold on the standard
   row-Gram event.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Conditional on \(G,H\), the coupled Gaussian reference vector is
   \[
      Z_{\rm gau}=\lambda d^{-1}GHY ,
      \qquad Y\sim N(0,I_d),
   \]
   with covariance
   \[
      \Sigma=\lambda^2d^{-2}GHH^\top G^\top .
   \]
   Since \(W=d^{-1}HH^\top\) satisfies \(\|W-I\|_{\rm op}\le\delta_H\),
   \[
      \left\|\lambda^{-2}\Sigma-I_r\right\|_{\rm op}
      =
      \left\|d^{-1}GWG^\top-I_r\right\|_{\rm op}
      \le
      \varepsilon_G+\delta_H\|G\|_{\rm op}^2/d
      \le \zeta .
   \]
   Thus \(\Sigma\preceq\lambda^2(1+\zeta)I_r\), so
   \[
      \Prb\{\|Z_{\rm gau}\|_2>A\lambda\sqrt{1+\zeta}\sqrt r\}
      \le
      \Prb\{\|N(0,I_r)\|_2>A\sqrt r\}.
   \]
   Apply \cref{lem:product-sign-spherical-shell-transfer} with
   \(M=\lambda d^{-1/2}GH\) and
   \(L=A\lambda\sqrt{1+\zeta}\).  Then apply
   \cref{lem:product-sign-reference-covariance-transfer} to the Gaussian
   reference vector \(Z_{\rm gau}\), using \((SRR3)\).  The two Gaussian norm
   exceptional events and the spherical shell event give \((SRR4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Empirical spherical whitening calibration]
   \label{lem:empirical-spherical-whitening-calibration}
   Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_m\) be independent uniform points on \(S^{d-1}\), let
   \[
      \widehat\Sigma_c
      =
      \frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m (X_i-\bar X)(X_i-\bar X)^\top,
      \qquad
      \bar X=\frac1m\sum_iX_i,
   \]
   and suppose
   \[
      \|d\widehat\Sigma_c-I_d\|_{\rm op}\le\delta<1 .
      \tag{EWC1}
   \]
   For the exact whitening map \(H=\widehat\Sigma_c^{-1/2}\),
   \[
      \left\|d^{-1}H^\top H-I_d\right\|_{\rm op}
      \le \frac{\delta}{1-\delta}.
      \tag{EWC2}
   \]
   Moreover, the event \((EWC1)\) holds with probability at least
   \(1-2e^{-u}\) whenever
   \[
      \delta
      \ge
      C\left(\sqrt{\frac{d+u}{m}}+\frac{d+u}{m}\right)
      \tag{EWC3}
   \]
   for a universal constant \(C\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The eigenvalues of \(d\widehat\Sigma_c\) lie in
   \([1-\delta,1+\delta]\).  Hence the eigenvalues of
   \(d^{-1}H^\top H=(d\widehat\Sigma_c)^{-1}\) lie in
   \([(1+\delta)^{-1},(1-\delta)^{-1}]\), proving \((EWC2)\).  The final
   display is the standard sample-covariance concentration bound for the
   isotropic subgaussian vectors \(\sqrt d\,X_i\); centering subtracts the
   positive semidefinite rank-one matrix \(\bar X\bar X^\top\) and is covered by
   the same bound after adjusting the universal constant.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Uniform empirical product-sign threshold transfer]
   \label{lem:product-sign-empirical-quantile-transfer}
   Let \(\mathcal S\) be a finite product-sign label set of size \(B\), and
   let \(X_1,\ldots,X_m\) be independent samples from a reference
   distribution \(\mathcal D\).  For each \(s\in\mathcal S\), let
   \(\Psi_s\) be the product-sign score \((PSS)\), and let
   \(Q_s^{\rm node}\) be the empirical upper \(\eta\)-threshold: the smallest
   level whose empirical upper tail is at most \(\eta\).  If numbers
   \(Q_s^{\rm ref}\) satisfy
   \[
      \Prb_{X\sim\mathcal D}\{\Psi_s(X)\ge Q_s^{\rm ref}\}\le\eta-\delta
      \qquad(s\in\mathcal S)
   \]
   for some \(0<\delta<\eta\), then
   \[
      \Prb\{\exists s\in\mathcal S:\ Q_s^{\rm node}>Q_s^{\rm ref}\}
      \le
      B\exp(-2m\delta^2).
      \tag{EQT}
   \]
   In particular, with \(\delta=\eta/2\), \(\eta=m^{-\gamma}\), and
   \(B\le m^C\), the failure probability is
   \[
      \exp\{-\Omega(m^{1-2\gamma})\}
   \]
   for every fixed \(\gamma<1/2\) and \(C<\infty\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a label \(s\), and write
   \(Z_i=\mathbf 1\{\Psi_s(X_i)\ge Q_s^{\rm ref}\}\).  By assumption
   \(\E Z_i\le\eta-\delta\).  If \(Q_s^{\rm node}>Q_s^{\rm ref}\), then the
   empirical upper tail at \(Q_s^{\rm ref}\) is larger than \(\eta\), so
   \(m^{-1}\sum_iZ_i>\eta\).  Hoeffding's inequality gives probability at
   most \(\exp(-2m\delta^2)\).  Union bound over \(B\) labels proves
   \((EQT)\), and the final display substitutes the stated parameters.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Finite-panel product-sign transfer check]
   \label{lem:product-sign-transfer-check}
   Fix a concrete product-sign panel with bit logits \(u_a(x)\), and let
   \(Q_s^{\rm ref}\) be reference upper thresholds satisfying
   \[
      \Prb_{X\sim\mathcal D}\{\Psi_s(X)\ge Q_s^{\rm ref}\}\le\eta
      \qquad(s\in\{\pm1\}^r).
   \]
   Suppose the node empirical thresholds obey
   \(Q_s^{\rm node}\le Q_s^{\rm ref}+E\) for every label \(s\), and put
   \(T=\max_s Q_s^{\rm ref}+E\).  For a near pair \(p,q\), let
   \(M_{p,q}\) and \(V_{p,q}\) be the tilted mean and variance in
   \cref{lem:product-sign-mean-gap-certificate}.  If, for some
   \(\Delta_0,\Gamma,V_0>0\),
   \[
      M_{p,q}\ge T+\Delta_0+\Gamma,
      \qquad
      V_{p,q}\le V_0 ,
   \]
   then
   \[
      W_{p,q}\{\Psi_s(p)\ge Q_s^{\rm node}+\Delta_0\}
      \ge
      \frac{\Gamma^2}{V_0+\Gamma^2}.
   \]
   In particular, if \(T\le rt\), \(M_{p,q}\ge r(t+\varepsilon)\),
   \(V_{p,q}=O(r)\), and \(\Delta_0=O(1)\), then the tilted good mass is
   \(1-O_{\varepsilon}(1/r)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(Q_s^{\rm node}\le T\) for every label, the event
   \(\{\Psi_s(p)\ge T+\Delta_0\}\) is contained in the posterior-rank good
   event \(\{\Psi_s(p)\ge Q_s^{\rm node}+\Delta_0\}\).  Apply
   \cref{lem:product-sign-mean-gap-certificate} with threshold \(T\) and use
   \(M_{p,q}-(T+\Delta_0)\ge\Gamma\), \(V_{p,q}\le V_0\).  The final
   statement takes \(\Gamma\ge r\varepsilon-\Delta_0\).
\end{proof}

Thus the finite special case would follow from a posterior-rank margin statement: for every near pair not handled by the resident guard, a non-negligible fraction of the tilted affinity must lie on outcomes for which $p$ is inside the top-$\xi$ posterior child by enough margin. This is only a sufficient condition. By \cref{lem:soft-surplus-decomposition}, a failed fixed-margin test can still have large \(\mathcal H_\xi\) if the tilted winner, or a few near-winner outcomes, have moderate posterior surplus. The diagnostic should therefore report not only $\mathcal H_\xi$, but also $\mathsf A_\beta(p,q)$, the soft surplus \(\mathcal H_\xi/\mathsf A_\beta\), the tilted winner's contribution fraction from \cref{lem:soft-surplus-decomposition}, \(W_{p,q}(G_\Delta(p))\), and the certified lower bound in \cref{lem:posterior-rank-margin}, for a margin such as $\Delta=1/\beta$. For the balanced-softmax candidate
\[
   K_x(j)=
   \frac{\exp(\lambda_{\rm sm}\ip{a_j}{x}+b_j)}
   {\sum_\ell\exp(\lambda_{\rm sm}\ip{a_\ell}{x}+b_\ell)},
\]
the offsets $b_j$ should first be balanced so that $\mu_j\approx1/B$, and the inverse temperature $\lambda_{\rm sm}$ should be swept rather than fixed by an arbitrary normalization of the panel. Writing
\[
   A(x)=\log\sum_j\exp(\lambda_{\rm sm}\ip{a_j}{x}+b_j),
\]
the unrestricted affinity has the exact form
\[
   \sum_j K_p(j)^\beta K_q(j)^{1-\beta}
   =
   \exp\!\left(A(z)-\beta A(p)-(1-\beta)A(q)\right),
   \qquad z=\beta p+(1-\beta)q.
\]
Moreover the tilted law $W_{p,q}$ is exactly $K_z$. Thus $\lambda_{\rm sm}$ controls both the local curvature $\nabla^2A(x)=\lambda_{\rm sm}^2\operatorname{Cov}_{K_x}(a_j)$ and the effective support of the certificate distribution $K_z$. The diagnostic should compare Gaussian, whitened Gaussian, cross-polytope, and learned panels; report lower quantiles rather than only averages; and track the effective support and Hessian condition number of $K_z$. For the boosted-leader route of \cref{cor:boosted-leader-skeleton-value-delivery}, it should also report the local repetition proxy
\[
   \frac{\log(1/\varepsilon)}{\mathcal H_\xi(p,q)},
   \qquad
   \varepsilon=(H+1)^{-2},
\]
because zeros or heavy lower tails in \(\mathcal H_\xi\) are exactly local
leader-reporter obstructions. These measurements distinguish the two hoped-for
regimes: well-conditioned softmax curvature gives score separation, while
concentrated $K_z$ should give posterior contraction by placing most tilted
mass on $G_\Delta(p)$.
One should also separate the resident-guard regime from the genuine finite-channel regime. On the critical random sphere, the guard density can already be constant, so $g(q)$ masks the posterior term. A sharper stress test uses isolated planted pairs with smaller radius, where $g(q)\simeq1/m$ and the lower quantiles of $\mathcal H_\xi(p,q)$ carry the conjectural content.

\begin{remark}[Boosted-leader diagnostic evidence]
   A compact sweep of the above diagnostic is useful evidence and a design
   constraint, but not a theorem.  In the critical random-sphere regime, all
   tested boosted-overhead quantiles were finite, but the mean guard density
   was \(0.502\); the best \(90\%\) overhead proxy was about \(30.1\), so this
   experiment mostly measures the resident guard rather than the posterior
   term.  In isolated planted-pair tests, where the guard density is \(1/m\),
   the signal is much sharper.  For whitened Gaussian panels at inverse
   temperature scale \(8\), the \(90\%\) boosted-overhead proxy was
   \(8.97\)--\(10.68\) for \(m=300\) and \(10.37\)--\(11.84\) for \(m=1000\),
   with lower \(5\%\) quantiles of \(\mathcal H_\eta\) in
   \(0.452\)--\(0.539\) and \(0.446\)--\(0.502\).  In focused
   \(m=3000,10000\) runs, whitened scales \(8\) and \(12\) kept the same
   \(90\%\) proxy in \(11.57\)--\(16.57\), the \(99\%\) proxy in
   \(19.89\)--\(39.75\), and the lower \(5\%\) quantile of \(\mathcal H_\eta\)
   in \(0.289\)--\(0.406\).  The effective-support lower quantile was
   essentially one, while the median Hessian condition number was
   \(10^8\)--\(10^{10}\).  Thus the positive numerical signal is posterior
   contraction and leader selection, not well-conditioned softmax curvature.
   Conversely, cold/coarse panels are genuine obstructions: at scale \(0.5\),
   non-whitened panel families had \(90\%\) overhead proxies around
   \(10^3\)--\(2.3\cdot10^3\), and even whitened panels were around
   \(1.6\cdot10^2\)--\(3.0\cdot10^2\).  The constructive theorem should
   therefore target tuned, balanced, whitening-based leader reporters, or else
   prove that this posterior-contraction signal cannot be made uniform.
   A follow-up winner-decomposition run supports the same interpretation but
   also exposes the lower-tail work still to do: for isolated \(m=1000,3000\)
   whitened panels at scales \(8,12\), the lower \(5\%\) soft-surplus quantile
   was \(0.468\)--\(0.793\), the lower \(5\%\) tilted-top-mass quantile was
   \(0.433\)--\(0.611\), and the median fraction of \(\mathcal H_\eta\) carried
   by the top tilted outcome was \(0.950\)--\(0.997\).  However the lower
   \(5\%\) top-outcome contribution fraction was only \(0.441\)--\(0.632\).
   The typical state is therefore almost winner-led, but a uniform theorem
   still needs a lower-tail backup rather than only an argmax reporter.
   Measuring the prefix in \cref{cor:top-k-tilted-backup} gives the more useful
   target: on the same isolated \(m=1000,3000\) whitened scale \(8,12\) sweep,
   top two tilted outcomes captured lower \(5\%\) contribution fraction
   \(0.724\)--\(0.962\), while top four captured \(0.988\)--\(1.000\) and top
   eight captured all of the measured value.  This points to a constant-size
   hidden prefix reporter as the next constructive object.  It is not yet a
   proof, because the query algorithm must recover this witness-dependent
   tilted prefix without being given \(p\).
   The query-visible prefix test in \cref{cor:query-top-k-backup} removes that
   caveat for the same compact sweep: ordering outcomes by \(K_q\), top four
   captured lower \(5\%\) contribution fraction \(0.988\)--\(1.000\) at
   whitened scales \(8,12\), and top eight again captured all measured value.
   Thus, in this model, the constructive target is no longer a
   witness-dependent decoder; it is an output-sensitive top-\(k\) softmax
   outcome reporter for the retained panel, plus a uniform proof of the
   query-prefix lower tail.
   A larger check at \(m=10000,30000\) preserved the same signal: at whitened
   scales \(8,12\), query top four captured lower \(5\%\) contribution
   fraction \(0.963\)--\(0.999\), query top eight captured all measured value,
   and the boosted-overhead \(90\%\) proxy stayed in \(12.21\)--\(17.56\).
   \Cref{prop:query-top-k-channel-compiler} records the resulting arithmetic:
   once those top labels are reported output-sensitively, the query no longer
   pays the \(B\simeq\xi^{-1}\) enumeration factor.
   \Cref{lem:query-tilted-prefix-stability} gives a tempting direct proof
   route from the hidden tilted prefix to the query prefix: if the query
   top-\(k\) logit gap dominates the centered tilt radius, the two prefixes
   are identical.  A focused stability diagnostic shows that this route is too
   strong to be the whole proof.  On isolated whitened Gaussian panels with
   \(m=1000,3000\), scales \(8,12\), and the same near-pair model as above,
   query top four captured lower \(5\%\) contribution fraction
   \(0.988\)--\(1.000\), but the lower \(5\%\) stability margin
   \(g_4(q)-2\Delta_{p,q}\) was negative, between \(-1.86\) and \(-0.91\),
   and only \(55.0\%\)--\(69.4\%\) of rows were certified stable.  The larger
   \(m=10000,30000\) run kept query top-four capture at \(0.963\)--\(0.999\),
   while the top-four stability margin lower tail was still negative
   \((-1.44\) to \(-0.70)\) and the stable fraction was only
   \(55.0\%\)--\(68.1\%\).  Thus the observed lower tail is not explained by
   worst-case top-\(k\) order invariance.

   The same lemma also gives a useful positive route after enlarging the query
   backup.  It suffices for the query rank-four to rank-nine gap
   \(g_{4,8}(q)\) to dominate \(2\Delta_{p,q}\), because then the hidden tilted
   top four labels are contained in the query top eight labels.  This
   condition matches the data much better.  On the compact
   \(m=1000,3000\) sweep, the certified containment fraction for
   \(T_4(p,q)\subseteq Q_8(q)\) was \(100\%\) in every tuned whitened run,
   with lower \(5\%\) containment margin \(g_{4,8}-2\Delta\) between
   \(2.83\) and \(7.60\) at scales \(8,12\).  On the larger
   \(m=10000,30000\) sweep, the same fraction was \(99.4\%\)--\(100\%\), with
   lower \(5\%\) margin \(2.23\)--\(4.30\).  Since the hidden top-four prefix
   already carried lower \(5\%\) contribution fraction \(0.970\)--\(0.999\)
   in the large tuned runs, this gives a concrete proof target for the
   query-visible top-eight backup: prove a uniform lower tail for
   \(g_{4,8}(q)-2\Delta_{p,q}\) and for the hidden top-four surplus capture.

   A structured product-sign panel gives a concrete reporter rather than only
   an existence target.  Labels are sign vectors and
   \cref{lem:product-sign-top-k-reporter} reports the exact query top eight
   from the \(r=\log B\) bit logits.  In fixed-\(B=16\) isolated planted-pair
   diagnostics, the unwhitened product-sign panel was a real barrier:
   \(\mathcal H_\eta\) lower \(5\%\) quantiles were only \(0.041\)--\(0.159\)
   at scales \(8,12\) for \(m=1000,3000\), with boosted-overhead \(90\%\)
   proxies \(33.5\)--\(117.4\).  Whitening the bit directions changed the
   picture.  For \(m=10000,30000\), whitened product-sign panels at scales
   \(8,12\) had \(\mathcal H_\eta\) lower \(5\%\) quantiles
   \(0.212\)--\(0.333\), query top-eight contribution lower \(5\%\)
   \(0.997\)--\(1.000\), hidden top-four contribution lower \(5\%\)
   \(0.908\)--\(0.994\), and certified \(T_4(p,q)\subseteq Q_8(q)\) on
   \(99.4\%\)--\(100\%\) of rows.  \Cref{lem:product-sign-containment-tail}
   explains why the containment part is not the main fixed-width obstruction:
   for nondegenerate random bit directions, the query top-eight containment
   failure is only an inverse-polylogarithmic small-gap event.

   A width sweep reinforces the fixed-small-\(B\) choice rather than suggesting
   another certificate form.  In four runs of
   \texttt{python impl/finite\_channel\_sweep.py --n 10000,30000 --d 32
   --queries 200 --panels whitened\_product\_sign --scales 8,12 --seeds
   0,1,2 --B B0 --near-corr 0.95 --route-depth 16} with
   \(B\in\{8,16,32,64\}\), \(B=16\) kept
   \(\mathcal H_\eta\) lower \(5\%\) quantiles \(0.237\)--\(0.394\), hidden
   top-four contribution \(0.921\)--\(0.998\), query top-eight contribution
   \(0.999\)--\(1.000\), and certified containment in every row.  \(B=32\)
   improved \(\mathcal H_\eta\) to \(0.299\)--\(0.467\), while hidden top-four
   and query top-eight lower tails remained \(0.821\)--\(0.954\) and
   \(0.973\)--\(0.999\), with containment \(98.5\%\)--\(100\%\).  By \(B=64\),
   \(\mathcal H_\eta\) rose further to \(0.354\)--\(0.501\), but fixed top
   eight began to leak: hidden top-four contribution fell to
   \(0.700\)--\(0.882\), query top-eight to \(0.896\)--\(0.986\), and
   containment to \(95.5\%\)--\(99.0\%\).  Thus the constructive branch should
   either keep a fixed small product-sign width, such as \(B=16\) or \(32\),
   or let \(k\) grow with \(B\).  For the fixed top-eight endpoint, the real
   unresolved theorem is now the posterior-surplus lower tail for the hidden
   top-four labels of the whitened product-sign panel.

   Measuring the direct restricted value, rather than multiplying separate
   quantiles of \(\mathcal H_\eta\) and contribution fractions, gives the same
   conclusion.  The sweep now reports
   \[
      \mathcal H_{\eta,4}^{\rm hid}
      =
      \sum_{j\in T_4(p,q)}
      \mu_j^\beta K_q(j)^{1-\beta}
      \left(R_j(p)^\beta-\tau_j^\beta\right)_+
   \]
   and the analogous query top-eight value.  In
   \texttt{python impl/finite\_channel\_sweep.py --n 10000,30000 --d 32
   --queries 220 --panels whitened\_product\_sign --scales 8,12 --seeds
   0,1,2 --B B0 --near-corr corr --route-depth 16}, with
   \(B0\in\{16,32\}\) and \({\rm corr}\in\{0.90,0.95,0.98\}\), the lower
   \(5\%\) quantile of \(\mathcal H_{\eta,4}^{\rm hid}\) ranged from
   \(0.116\) to \(0.579\), and the query top-eight restricted value ranged
   from \(0.124\) to \(0.602\).  The weakest \(1\%\) row was the harder
   \({\rm corr}=0.90\), \(m=30000\), \(B=16\), scale \(12\) case, where
   \(\mathcal H_{\eta,4}^{\rm hid}\) was still \(0.034\) and essentially all
   of the low tail came from \(\mathcal H_\eta\) itself
   (\(\mathcal H_\eta\) lower \(1\%\) \(0.035\)).  Decomposing
   \(\mathcal H_\eta=\mathsf A_\beta\cdot{\rm soft\ surplus}\), the affinity
   lower \(5\%\) quantiles stayed in \(0.444\)--\(0.942\), while soft-surplus
   lower \(5\%\) quantiles ranged from \(0.180\) to \(0.700\).  Thus neither
   prefix truncation nor tilted affinity is the observed bottleneck at fixed
   width.  The remaining proof should target the product-sign posterior rank
   thresholds that keep the soft surplus bounded below.

   The hard-margin curve identifies the right scale for that target.  Applying
   \cref{lem:posterior-rank-margin} with the original
   \(\Delta=1/\alpha\) is too cold: its lower \(5\%\) certified value is zero
   in several of the same fixed-width runs.  The half-log margin
   \(\Delta=0.5/\alpha\) is also intermittent.  At the quarter-log margin
   \(\Delta=0.25/\alpha\), however, the tilted good-mass lower \(5\%\)
   quantiles were \(0.277\)--\(0.997\), and the certified restricted-value
   lower \(5\%\) quantiles were \(0.036\)--\(0.175\), across
   \(B\in\{16,32\}\) and correlations \(0.90,0.95\).  The \(1\%\) tail in the
   hardest \(B=16\), correlation \(0.90\) run was still fragile
   (certified value \(0.0012\)), so this is not yet a uniform theorem.  It is
   a concrete non-equivalent target: prove a fixed-width product-sign
   posterior-rank lower tail at margin \(\Omega(1/\alpha)\) with a small
   enough constant, or find a genuine low-tail obstruction there.

   \Cref{lem:product-sign-posterior-score} removes one possible distraction:
   the sizeable output-mass imbalance of zero-offset product-sign panels does
   not enter the rank-margin event.  It only shifts all posterior scores for a
   label by the same constant.  A held-out threshold check confirms that the
   observed quarter-log target is not mainly finite-node threshold noise.
   Recomputing \((\pi_s,\tau_s)\) on \(10^5\) independent spherical reference
   points, while keeping the same node, panel, and near pairs, changed the
   top-\(\eta\) threshold logs by median \(0.025\)--\(0.138\) and \(90\%\)
   quantile \(0.085\)--\(0.310\).  The lower \(5\%\) quantiles of
   \(\mathcal H_\eta\), soft surplus, hidden top-four value, and the
   quarter-log certified value were essentially unchanged across
   \(B\in\{16,32\}\) and correlations \(0.90,0.95\).  Thus the next theorem
   should be stated for the distributional quantiles of the bit score
   \(\Psi_s\), with a standard empirical-quantile transfer as a separate
   concentration step.

   For the polylogarithmic endpoint, however, the quarter-log target is
   stronger than necessary.  By
   \cref{cor:bounded-rank-margin-polylog-value}, a fixed margin
   \(\Delta_0=O_c(1)\) already contributes the factor
   \(\Theta_c(1/\log m)\), which is an allowed polylogarithmic repetition
   loss.  This also matches the bounded nature of fixed-width product-sign
   scores: \(\Psi_s(x)\le r\log2\), so margins growing like \(\log m\) cannot
   be the right asymptotic target at fixed \(r\).  The bounded-margin stress
   test is correspondingly much cleaner.  At \(\Delta_0=1\), the tilted
   good-mass lower \(5\%\) quantiles were \(0.624\)--\(0.998\), and the
   certified-value lower \(5\%\) quantiles were \(0.0368\)--\(0.0831\), across
   \(B\in\{16,32\}\) and correlations \(0.90,0.95\).  Dividing by
   \(\alpha\) gives constants \(0.38\)--\(0.79\).

   This fixed-width evidence should not be extrapolated to the endpoint.
   \Cref{lem:product-sign-ceiling-barrier} shows the actual asymptotic
   obstruction: for bounded Gaussian bit variance and
   \(r(1+\log^2r)=o(\log m)\), the top-\(\eta=m^{-\Theta_c(1)}\)
   distributional score threshold is within \(o(1)\) of the ceiling
   \(r\log2\), so even a fixed positive margin is eventually impossible.
   A direct ideal-Gaussian stress test of the same \(\Psi_s\) normal form
   agrees with this barrier.  With \(\sigma=3.5\), correlation \(0.9\), and
   \(\Delta_0=1\), the first tested bit counts whose lower \(5\%\) tilted
   good mass exceeded \(0.1\) were \(r=12,16,24\) at
   \(m=10^{12},10^{18},10^{24}\), respectively.  A selected three-seed repeat
   at \(m=10^{24}\) had \(r=8\) ceiling-blocked in every seed, \(r=16\) lower
   \(5\%\) good mass \(0.033\)--\(0.039\), and \(r=24\) lower \(5\%\) good
   mass \(0.585\)--\(0.599\).  Varying
   \(\sigma\in\{1.5,2.5,3.5,5.0\}\) kept the same first successful bit counts
   in this sweep.

   \Cref{lem:product-sign-mean-gap-certificate} turns this numerical tail into
   a proof target without changing normal form: compute the conditional tilted
   mean \(M_{p,q}\), variance \(V_{p,q}\), and the gap
   \(M_{p,q}-(Q_{r,\eta}+\Delta_0)\).  The same ideal-Gaussian diagnostic now
   reports the resulting Cantelli lower bound.  At correlation \(0.9\),
   \(m=10^{24}\), and \(\sigma=3.5\), \(r=24\) was still borderline:
   lower \(5\%\) mean gap \(0.262\)--\(0.837\), Cantelli good-mass lower
   \(5\%\) \(0.003\)--\(0.026\), but empirical tilted good-mass lower \(5\%\)
   \(0.545\)--\(0.568\).  Increasing to \(r=32\) made the crude proof already
   strong: lower \(5\%\) mean gap \(9.07\)--\(9.95\), Cantelli lower \(5\%\)
   \(0.734\)--\(0.769\), and empirical lower \(5\%\) \(0.939\)--\(0.959\).
   At the lower correlation \(0.75\), the transition moved upward: for
   \(m=10^{24}\), \(r=48\) had Cantelli lower \(5\%\)
   \(0.078\)--\(0.249\) and empirical lower \(5\%\) \(0.597\)--\(0.722\),
   while \(r=64\) had Cantelli lower \(5\%\) \(0.776\)--\(0.783\) and
   empirical lower \(5\%\) \(0.959\)--\(0.967\).  Thus the current proof
   obligation is precise: prove the Gaussian rate gap \((GWC1)\)--\((GWC2)\)
   at an \(r=O_c(\log m)\) width allowed by the compiler, or sharpen the
   borderline \(r\) regime with a Bernstein or local-CLT lower-tail bound.
   \Cref{cor:cramer-product-sign-closure} discharges that obligation for the
   ideal i.i.d. Gaussian bit model whenever the Cramer constant fits the
   outcome envelope.  For the \(c=2\), \(a=0.75\) critical correlation,
   deterministic Gauss-Hermite quadrature with score level
   \(t=\mu_0-0.1\) gives the following reproducible constants:
   at \(\sigma=2.5,3.5,5.0\), the Cramer rates are approximately
   \(0.150,0.163,0.143\), so the minimum label exponents
   \((\gamma/I_\sigma(t))\log2\) are \(0.577,0.531,0.606\), all below \(1\).
   At correlation \(0.9\), the corresponding exponents are
   \(0.339,0.309,0.363\).  Thus the ideal Gaussian product-sign channel is no
   longer blocked at the all-label bounded-margin tail.  However,
   \cref{lem:growing-product-sign-top-k-barrier} exposes a separate
   output-sensitive obstruction.  The same deterministic quadrature gives
   fixed-bit tilted mode deficits \(0.116,0.077,0.045\) at
   \(\sigma=2.5,3.5,5.0\).  At the minimum Cramer widths above, any
   polylogarithmic label list has tilted mass at most
   \(m^{-0.096},m^{-0.059},m^{-0.040+o(1)}\) in the \(a=0.75\) case, and at
   most \(m^{-0.057},m^{-0.035},m^{-0.024+o(1)}\) in the \(a=0.9\) case.  This
   is polynomially smaller than the inverse-polylogarithmic value required by
   \cref{prop:query-top-k-channel-compiler}.

   The most natural sampled escape hatch also fails for this same panel.
   \Cref{lem:sampled-product-sign-rate-obstruction} shows that query-Gibbs
   sampling of product-sign labels must have
   \(I_\sigma(t)/\log2\ge1-\rho\) to meet storage and sampled far-load
   simultaneously.  For \(c=2\), this threshold is \(6/7\).  At the same
   deterministic \(a=0.75\), \(\sigma=2.5,3.5,5.0\) points above, the sampled
   rate fractions are only \(0.217,0.236,0.206\); at \(a=0.9\) they are
   \(0.369,0.404,0.344\).  Thus neither polylog top-\(k\) reporting nor direct
   query-Gibbs sampling rescues the fixed-entropy growing product-sign branch.
   Moreover, \cref{cor:stable-small-quotient-product-sign-obstruction} rules
   out the first ordinary quotient attempt: if the quotient classes have only
   polylogarithmic size and union scanning is stable in the sense of
   \cref{lem:stable-quotient-sampled-spectrum}, then the hidden unquotiented
   sampled panel would already satisfy the same polynomial storage and far-load
   exponents, contradicting the same rate test.  Therefore a quotient rescue
   would have to merge superpolylogarithmically many hidden labels, use
   responsibility-thinned output, or sample aggregate bucket mass directly.
   In fact, \cref{cor:ordinary-product-sign-quotient-class-size} shows that
   ordinary union quotienting needs polynomially large hidden classes before
   even storage and far-load can both hold at these thresholds.  The required
   class-size exponents \( (1-\rho)/(I_\sigma(t)/\log2)-1\) are
   \(2.956,2.638,3.158\) for \(a=0.75\), \(\sigma=2.5,3.5,5.0\), and
   \(1.325,1.121,1.492\) for \(a=0.9\).  Thus the quotient would need to merge
   more than \(m\) hidden labels in all these rows; even the least-bad
   \(a=0.9,\sigma=3.5\) row exceeds the minimum all-label exponent by \(0.811\).
   Nor is the issue only the ordinary union storage charge:
   \cref{cor:aggregate-responsibility-product-sign-obstruction} gives the
   one-bucket responsibility-thinned obstruction.  At the actual near tilted
   mean, the fixed-label rate fractions are only \(0.262,0.270,0.226\) for
   \(a=0.75\), \(\sigma=2.5,3.5,5.0\), and \(0.445,0.464,0.378\) for
   \(a=0.9\), still far below the required \(6/7\).
   The remaining work is therefore not another threshold certificate: it is
   either a genuinely compressed all-outcome storage/evaluation scheme whose
   bucket quotient changes the storage/far-load arithmetic, a construction whose
   tilted output entropy is \(O(\log\log m)\), or a proof that this entropy/rate
   barrier rules out the product-sign route to the endpoint.

   The first transfer stress test keeps exactly this normal form.  The script
   \texttt{impl/product\_sign\_transfer\_stress.py} measures the concrete bit
   logits of the retained product-sign panel, the reference and node
   \(\Psi_s\)-thresholds, the exact whitening-metric row law in
   \cref{lem:whitened-product-sign-row-law}, the fitted Gaussian rate level,
   and the exact tilted good mass whenever \(B\) is small enough to enumerate
   all labels.  With
   \(d=32\), near correlation \(0.95\), target bit standard deviation \(3.5\),
   and whitened product-sign panels, exact \(B=16,32\) runs at
   \(m=10000\) had fitted bit standard deviations \(3.14\)--\(3.77\), q95
   absolute cross-bit correlations \(0.224\)--\(0.371\), and q95 threshold
   levels below the fitted Gaussian Cramer level by \(0.91\)--\(1.24\) per
   bit.  The exact tilted good-mass lower \(5\%\) quantiles were
   \(0.813\)--\(0.981\), and the certified value divided by \(\alpha\) was
   \(0.648\)--\(0.778\).  A wider exact \(B=256\) check gave whitening-metric
   bit standard deviations \(3.497\)--\(3.502\), metric pair-correlation lower
   \(5\%\) \(0.9483\)--\(0.9486\), exact good-mass lower \(5\%\)
   \(0.9988\)--\(0.9996\), and per-bit Cramer slack \(1.35\)--\(1.50\).
   A sampled-threshold \(B=4096\) run kept sampled
   good-mass lower \(5\%\) equal to \(1\) and per-bit Cramer slack
   \(1.55\)--\(1.70\), but this is evidence rather than a uniform
   all-label theorem.  The same diagnostic catches the known bad control:
   without whitening in the \(B=256\) run, the fitted bit standard deviation
   fell to \(0.57\)--\(0.63\), the minimum label exponent rose to
   \(1.95\)--\(2.73\), and the lower \(5\%\) mean gap was negative.  The same
   diagnostic now couples spherical reference points \(Y/\|Y\|\) to Gaussian
   shell points \(Y/\sqrt d\).  In a compact \(d=128\), \(B=256\), two-seed
   check, the relative shell deviation q95 was \(0.120\)--\(0.123\), the
   spherical threshold exceeded the coupled Gaussian threshold by at most
   \(0.026\)--\(0.034\), and the exact tilted good-mass lower \(5\%\) stayed at
   \(0.9995\)--\(0.9997\).  Thus the
   row-randomness part of the transfer is now explicit rather than hidden by
   a reformulation: \cref{lem:whitened-product-sign-row-law} reduces it to
   whitening-metric norm and correlation slack.  The empirical node quantile
   part is also standard in the iid-node model by
   \cref{lem:product-sign-empirical-quantile-transfer}: since
   \(\eta=m^{-\gamma}\) has \(\gamma<1/2\) for every \(c>1\), the union bound
   over \(B\le m^{O(1)}\) labels is negligible.  The near-pair metric
   calibration is the elementary spectral statement
   \cref{lem:whitening-metric-calibration}.  The Gaussian-reference all-label
   threshold is reduced to a standard row-Gram event:
   \cref{lem:product-sign-reference-covariance-transfer} and
   \cref{cor:random-row-reference-threshold-transfer}
   compare the implemented \(\Psi_s\) tail with the iid Cramer tail whenever
   the reference bit covariance is close to scalar.  The spherical reference
   case is no longer a separate assumption: \cref{lem:product-sign-spherical-shell-transfer}
   couples it to the Gaussian reference on the ordinary chi-square shell, and
   \cref{cor:spherical-random-row-reference-threshold-transfer} combines that
   coupling with the same row-Gram event.  Finally,
   \cref{lem:empirical-spherical-whitening-calibration} proves the metric event
   for the exact empirical whitening map in the iid spherical model.

   Thus the all-label product-sign transfer is closed for the standard iid
   spherical local model in the high-dimensional regime where
   \(r=\Theta(\log m)\), \(d/\log m\to\infty\), and the empirical whitening
   covariance concentrates.  The explicit slack in \((SRR4)\) also records the
   barrier in the borderline \(d=\Theta(\log m)\) regime: the proof only works
   when the row-Gram, whitening, and shell terms leave a positive per-bit
   Cramer gap.

   The frozen product-sign target is therefore not another certificate form:
   it is the same distributional bounded-margin posterior-rank lower tail for
   \(\Psi_s\), but with a growing bit count beyond the ceiling-barrier scale,
   together with empirical quantile transfer.  The output-sensitive query
   prefix is not solved by this all-label theorem: by
   \cref{lem:growing-product-sign-top-k-barrier}, a polylogarithmic query
   top-\(k\) reporter cannot capture enough value in the fixed-entropy
   growing-width product-sign model, and by
   \cref{cor:product-sign-scale-tradeoff} increasing the bit scale does not
   repair this.  Low scale leaves the tilted law with superpolylogarithmic
   min-entropy, while high scale makes the Hellinger affinity factor
   \(\mathsf A_\beta\) superpolylogarithmically small.  By
   \cref{lem:sampled-product-sign-rate-obstruction} direct query-Gibbs sampling
   of the same labels violates the sampled storage/far-load rate test.  By
   \cref{cor:stable-small-quotient-product-sign-obstruction}, stable quotients
   with only polylogarithmic hidden labels per bucket class inherit that same
   obstruction, and \cref{cor:ordinary-product-sign-quotient-class-size} shows
   that ordinary union quotients need polynomial hidden class sizes at the
   observed rate points.  Even the one-bucket responsibility version is blocked
   by \cref{cor:aggregate-responsibility-product-sign-obstruction} for the same
   constants.  The clean endpoint now hinges on changing the channel so the
   tilted entropy is only \(O(\log\log m)\), switching to a different structured
   Gaussian/code/lattice sampler whose far rate reaches the near mean, or
   accepting this as a barrier to the product-sign branch.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Conditional finite-channel polylog endpoint]\label{prop:finite-channel-polylog}
   Under \cref{asm:finite-restricted-channel}, the posterior-superlevel recursion gives worst-case Euclidean ANN bounds
   \[
      Q(n,d)=d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n,
      \qquad
      S(n,d)=dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n.
   \]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
   At a node of size $m$, repeat the finite channel
   \[
      R=\xi^{-\rho}\log^{O_c(1)}m
   \]
   times. By \cref{asm:finite-restricted-channel} and the top-$\xi$ collapse, a true near point enters at least one active child with inverse-polylogarithmic probability, unless the resident guard already succeeds. The local channel-evaluation work is
   \[
      dRB\log^{O_c(1)}m
      \le
      d\,\xi^{-(1+\rho)}\log^{O_c(1)}m
      =
      d\,m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m,
   \]
   because $\vartheta(1+\rho)=\rho$.

   The expected number of active recursive children over all repetitions is polylogarithmic, since one group contributes $O_c(\xi^\rho)$ active children. Every recursive child has size at most $\xi m=m^{1-\vartheta}$. Hence the query recurrence is
   \[
      Q(m)\le d\,m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m+\log^{O_c(1)}m\,Q(m^{1-\vartheta}),
   \]
   which solves to $d\,m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m$ over $O_c(\log\log m)$ macro levels.

   For space, each stored child has size at most $\xi m$. The total stored-child $(1+\rho)$ power over all repeated channel groups is bounded by
   \[
      R\cdot B\cdot(\xi m)^{1+\rho}\log^{O_c(1)}m
      \le
      m^{1+\rho}\log^{O_c(1)}m,
   \]
   again using $RB=\xi^{-(1+\rho)}\log^{O_c(1)}m$. Summing over macro levels and adding the original data storage gives the displayed space bound. Polylogarithmic amplification and the standard truncation paragraph convert the inverse-polylogarithmic local success into constant success probability.
\end{proof}

\section{Audit trail and extensions}

The main self-contained proof path is the restartable slice route of \cref{prop:slice-two-thirds}. The following notes explain which pieces are closed, which one-tree milestones are conditional, and which older formulations remain useful as comparisons or possible extensions.

\paragraph{Spherical stage.}
The continuation-mass spherical decoder is proved in \cref{lem:continuation-work}, \cref{lem:good-first-moment}, \cref{lem:tame-second-moment}, and \cref{cor:spherical-survival}. The one-sided analytical upper barrier controls prolific early prefixes in the proof, while the algorithm itself enforces only continuation-mass pruning. Independently, \cref{thm:smooth-product-terminal} gives a constant-recall terminal spherical engine by smooth product filtering. The adaptive decoder is for carrying score through localization; the smooth product filter is for the final localized spherical search. \Cref{lem:flat-shell-obstruction} explains why this terminal filter cannot simply be applied to all radial shells of the bounded-diameter instance: without recentering to the critical normalization, the exponent becomes $1/c^2$ rather than $\rho_c$.

\paragraph{Restartable \(2/3\) stage.}
\Cref{prop:slice-two-thirds} proves the restartable $2/3$ rung and is the proof of \cref{thm:main}. It reaches a subpolynomial overhead using deliberate restarts and leaf-conditioned slices.

\paragraph{Randomized \(1/3\) stage.}
\Cref{prop:one-third} records the cube-root parameter choice from the one-tree notes. The direct tube calculation is kept only as intuition; the formal proposition uses \cref{lem:adaptive-continuation} for whole-lineage score survival and assumes only the cube-root geometric frontier inequality \cref{asm:mixed-operator}. Thus the central open issue is already the work-side first-hit accounting, not near-pair score survival.

\paragraph{Randomized polylog stage.}
\Cref{lem:adaptive-continuation} replaces the tube proof in the predictable-score setting, so near-pair survival is no longer the obstacle for the randomized one-tree endpoint. \Cref{asm:mixed-continuation-operator} is the direct remaining work-side target after \cref{lem:cap-free-scan-accounting}: it must prove thinned cap-split contraction over branching cap-discovery frontiers. Conditional on that operator, \cref{prop:randomized-polylog} shows that choosing $\eta\asymp(\log\log n)/\log n$ gives polylogarithmic query and space overhead. The sharper budget-thinned variant proves the activated geometric work bound by optional stopping in \cref{lem:canonical-mixed-budget} and \cref{lem:budget-thinned-opportunities}. It now has its own conditional endpoint, \cref{prop:budget-thinned-polylog}: the only remaining assumption is aggregate fractional value delivery. For laminar tame-route families, \cref{lem:lca-value-flow} reduces the second-moment version to the two quantities $V(\varnothing)$ and $\sum_uA(u)V(u)^2$, while \cref{lem:saturated-value-recursion} and \cref{lem:saturated-value-mincut} give a simpler sufficient target: every route cut should have inverse-polylogarithmic prefix-success mass. The route-law cut-energy certificate \cref{lem:cut-energy-route-law} gives the most stopping-time-compatible sufficient condition for this min-cut target.

\paragraph{Certified-cover route.}
\Cref{lem:certified-cover-compiler} abstracts the empirical $k$-means
multi-assignment mechanism as an overlapping certified filter cover. This gives
a deterministic routing guarantee by triangle inequality, but a flat
inflated-ball cover can be circular unless its children are genuinely smaller
and can be useless on concentrated high-dimensional nodes where most inflated
balls are stabbed. The stronger \cref{asm:power-cover} is the additive-cover
target: construct a query-decodable cover whose inflated-ball power stabbing
contracts by $1-\Theta(\eta^2)$ and whose storage power does not grow.
Conditional on that cover theorem, \cref{prop:power-cover-polylog} gives the
desired polylogarithmic ANN bound.

The more promising practical-theory interface is the score-cover variant:
\cref{lem:cap-slack-cover}, \cref{lem:lipschitz-score-cover}, and
\cref{lem:shell-normalized-cap-cover} turn overlapping cap or Lipschitz-score
filters into deterministic certified covers with the same active-power
accounting. Thus $k$-means is best viewed as an initializer or fallback for a
recursive fixed-overlap angular score-filter tree, not as a worst-case theorem
by itself.  The sharper form is the near-pair fractional filter cover of
\cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual}: dense regions and spherical filters are
columns \(A=(U_A,a_A,T_A,S_A)\), coverage is imposed directly on demands
\((p,q)\), and overlap is charged only through the query-local sum
\(\sum_Aa_A(q)T_A\lambda_A\).  \Cref{cor:filter-cover-column-generation} turns a
failed cover into demand, query-load, and storage prices, so the dense merge
operation becomes a positive reduced-gain separation problem rather than a
greedy clustering rule.  \Cref{cor:benefit-per-price-proposal} records the
corresponding proposal score exactly: after size-biasing by certified recursive
price, a proposal law is useful precisely when its mean dual benefit per price
is larger than one.  \Cref{lem:poisson-filter-cover-materialization} then
rounds any finite feasible cover with only a logarithmic factor in the number of
certified signatures.  The remaining geometric theorem is
\cref{asm:weighted-dense-spherical-dichotomy}: every surplus dual obstruction
must either buy a radius-contracting dense filter or be pseudo-random enough for
a large-range spherical filter.  \Cref{lem:finite-signature-filter-cover} is the
all-query version: signatures record the active-filter pattern and a superset of
possible near witnesses, so a finite LP certifies every continuous near pair.
\Cref{prop:fractional-filter-cover-polylog} closes the recursive accounting
conditional on such certificates: child prices are full descendant prices, hence
dense overlap is charged locally and does not multiply over levels.
The current endpoint-level formulation is
\cref{cor:one-sided-finite-signature-filter-cover},
\cref{cor:positive-finite-signature-separator-endpoint}, and
\cref{cor:dense-spherical-positive-separator-endpoint}: it is enough to separate
every finite-signature surplus dual by one positive reduced-gain column in the
unified dense/spherical universe.  The spherical side reduces such a dual to a
high-correlation co-load residual by
\cref{lem:finite-signature-spherical-reduced-gain} and
\cref{cor:high-correlation-coload-separator-endpoint}.  The dense side is now a
finite transport target:
\cref{cor:aggregate-finite-signature-coload-transport-endpoint} closes it when
responsibility mass has affordable aggregate dyadic price,
\cref{lem:finite-signature-coload-hall-transport} identifies the exact Hall cut
when packed transport fails, and
\cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-cut-repair-endpoint} states the remaining
repair obligation.  A failed Hall cut may guide build-time search, but the
retained proof object must still be a verified fractional star panel or a
successful aggregate responsibility transport.  The sharper
\cref{cor:finite-signature-hall-shadow-repair} and
\cref{cor:one-record-hall-shadow-merge} reduce this repair to the cut-shadow
degree \(d_{A,y}\): one affordable top-prefix merge for that degree is already a
valid dense column.  \Cref{cor:proposal-law-hall-shadow-merge} is the matching
build-time sampler form, and \cref{cor:no-merge-hall-shadow-envelope} gives the
explicit weak-type residual if every such merge fails.  The balanced-scale
screen \cref{cor:balanced-hall-shadow-density-screen} reduces the positive test
to one density threshold near the stationary prefix size, while
\cref{cor:fractional-balanced-hall-shadow-density-panel} and
\cref{cor:sampled-balanced-hall-shadow-density-search} give the batched and
sampled surplus forms.  The boundary-stable version is
\cref{cor:clipped-hall-shadow-density-screen},
\cref{cor:fractional-clipped-hall-shadow-density-panel}, and
\cref{cor:sampled-clipped-hall-shadow-density-search}: each template is tested
near the clipped minimizer of its recursive price density
