a heavy lister is already the clean trellis/code/lattice endpoint.
\Cref{cor:conditional-hidden-sampling-heavy-lister} gives a direct Monte Carlo
compiler for that lister when conditional hidden paths and their raw subbuckets
can be sampled and scanned cheaply: \(O(L_m)\) conditional paths find a
heavy witness with constant probability on each heavy bucket, and the expected
raw-scan work is the all-resident marked load
\(\sum_x Z_{q,x}^{\ge T}/Z_q\) times \(O(L_m)\).
\Cref{lem:random-sparse-aggregate-responsibility-barrier} instantiates that
barrier in the random sparse model: merging \(H\) hidden filters inflates the
expected union scan by \((1-(1-s)^H)/s=\Theta(\min\{H,s^{-1}\})\).
\Cref{lem:random-sparse-heavy-responsibility-screen} adds the complementary
positive sanity check: after inverse-polylogarithmic responsibility
thresholding, random far passengers survive only with binomial
large-deviation probability, so the remaining bottleneck is a heavy-resident
lister rather than the marked tail itself.
\Cref{rem:code-lattice-responsibility-audit} translates this target back into
coding language: Construction-A theta quotients, GMD/Chase, OSD information
sets, Tanner/polar/BCJR decoders, and recursive lattice decoders are useful
only insofar as they provide this point-indexed heavy posterior lister or
expose a failure of the heavy near-mass condition.
\Cref{cor:osd-heavy-responsibility-compiler} gives the first concrete
compiler for that lister: if the heavy-ratio test implies a soft-score
threshold over a linear residue code and the minimum information-set entropy
at that threshold is controlled, ordered-statistics decoding lists all heavy
residents before exact marked-ratio filtering; the only extra accounting is the
sampled number of resident signatures expanded from the listed codewords.
\Cref{lem:tilted-weight-linear-feasibility} shows that, for a fixed retained
pool, choosing those weights is just a linear feasibility problem after
clearing the tilted partition functions.  Failure has a concrete dual
certificate assigning prices to bad queries and near witnesses; a structured
label family must provide a nonpositive-reduced-obstruction label for every
such dual.
\Cref{lem:continuous-gaussian-finite-witness} checks the corresponding
positive fact for the unrestricted Gaussian label universe: every finite test
set has feasible tilted weights with strict slack.  Hence the missing theorem
is not weight existence in the ideal spectrum, but a finite low-storage,
query-decodable quadrature for that spectrum.
\Cref{cor:small-signature-gaussian-quadrature} adds the useful boundary case:
if the all-query constraints collapse to at most \(m^\rho\polylog m\) exact
signatures, the Caratheodory support itself is small enough to store and to
sample by a direct scan.
\Cref{prop:las-vegas-small-signature-gaussian} makes this boundary case
algorithmic under the uncharged preprocessing model: repeated Gaussian batches
and the finite tilted-weight LP eventually find the retained support.  The
\Cref{prop:finite-envelope-gaussian-quadrature} variant removes the need for
exact query representatives: finite signed upper envelopes for the homogeneous
tilted-weight coefficients are enough, provided their Gaussian means have
strict slack.  The
remaining obstruction is therefore signature entropy and compact decoding, not
the finite weighted Gaussian calculation.
\Cref{rem:metric-net-signature-barrier} rules out the most naive source of
such signatures: a metric net fine enough to preserve the critical tilted near
mass has size \(m^{\Theta(\log\log m)}\) in logarithmic dimension.  The
signatures must therefore be reliability or decoder states, not uniform
spherical cells.
\Cref{rem:outer-list-recovery-codebook} records the stronger alternative
suggested by list-decoding codes and lattices: instead of decoding the full
Cartesian product, retain a sparse outer code or lattice coset and use a
certified decoder to enumerate high-score global codewords.  Direct
Euclidean-metric decoding avoids the repeated-coordinate lift when the score is
an embedded squared distance; otherwise the lift remains a polylogarithmic
fallback for bounded scores.  This can reduce the index description and query
enumeration while keeping the same certification interface, provided the
retained panel satisfies the random-like spectrum.
\Cref{lem:reliability-erasure-sweep} isolates the lowest-overhead version of
that idea: a GMD-style sweep gives a compact \(O(h)\)-transcript reporter when
the useful route has enough confidence-weighted hard agreement.
\Cref{lem:soft-score-gmd-margin} reduces that agreement condition to a
top-gap soft-score margin, while Chase-style low-confidence branching gives
the corresponding small-list extension.
\Cref{cor:gmd-block-certificate} is the resulting retained-block certificate:
high-margin signatures can use ordinary errors-and-erasures decoding instead
of a full soft list-recovery oracle.
\Cref{cor:chase-gmd-block-certificate} extends this to signatures with a
polylogarithmic ambiguity list: a few unreliable coordinates may be guessed
explicitly, and the remaining coordinates only need the stronger top-gap
margin outside that guessed set.
\Cref{lem:budget-stable-prefix-list} and
\cref{cor:canonical-budget-stable-decoder} take one step in that direction:
the canonical mixed Bellman budget itself is an admissible list-decoding
potential for budget-stable recentering opportunities, leaving only
budget-unstable opportunities for the sampled value-delivery layer.
\Cref{cor:canonical-budget-defect-toll} then rewrites the sampled layer's
route-law toll as the cumulative log deficit
\(\log_+(\Gamma/\mathcal B_q^{\rm mix})\) of those unstable opportunities.
\Cref{lem:pruned-budget-thinning} and
\cref{cor:pruned-budget-defect-toll} add the lattice extreme-pruning analogue:
an offline-certified multiplier profile may reallocate activation probability
toward reliable near-route prefixes, so the relevant toll becomes the pruned
defect \(\log_+(\Gamma/(r\mathcal B_q^{\rm mix}))\).
\Cref{lem:budget-allocation-thinning} and
\cref{cor:allocation-defect-toll} simplify this further: the algorithm only
needs a directly certified activation allocation \(Y\), and the toll becomes
\(\log_+(\Gamma/Y)\).  Thus the remaining profile problem can be stated as a
single decodable subprobability allocation over first opportunities, rather
than as a multiplier of the canonical budget.
\Cref{lem:waterfilled-allocation} and
\cref{cor:waterfilled-allocation-defect} make the allocation normal form
canonical for any fixed route law: allocate \(y_e=\min\{a_e,t\ell_e\}\), where
\(\ell_e\) is the route-law occupation probability and \(a_e\) is the
normalized recursive charge.  A polylogarithmic endpoint through this route now
requires only a decodable representation of that water-filled allocation and an
\(O_c(\log\log n)\) bound on its scalar defect.
\Cref{cor:transition-waterfilled-allocation} sharpens this by keeping the
route-law transition probability \(\lambda_e\) that the coarser defect bound
discarded.  The exact edge toll is controlled by
\(\log_+(\lambda_ea_e/y_e)\), so the water-filled charge should be
\(\lambda_ea_e\), not \(a_e\).  In the raw-log certificate this cancels the
child branch probability:
for \(e=u\to w\),
\[
   \ell_e=\Lambda(u)\lambda_e
   \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
   \frac{H_0\lambda_ea_e}{\ell_e}=\frac{H_0a_e}{\Lambda(u)} .
\]
The concrete target is therefore bounded prefix charge density
\(H_0a_e\le C\Lambda(u)\), rather than the stronger edge-density condition
\(H_0a_e\le C\ell_e\).  This is also the bridge to the square-energy view:
the ideal allocation \(y_e=\lambda_ea_e\) gives \(\gamma_e\ge\lambda_e\), so
the local square multiplier is at most one; water-filling is the
budget-constrained version of that square-benign profile.  The robust envelope
form \cref{cor:robust-transition-envelope-raw-log} preserves this improvement
whenever the witness route laws share, or admit a decodable upper envelope for,
their local transition probabilities.
\Cref{lem:antichain-prefix-density-flow} removes another arbitrary choice: a
route law with the required prefix densities exists exactly when the
corresponding node demands have total mass at most one on every antichain.
Applied with demand \(H_0a_*(u)/C\), where \(a_*(u)\) is the largest outgoing
normalized charge at prefix \(u\), this gives
\cref{cor:antichain-transition-waterfill}: it is enough to prove the cut-style
charge bound
\[
   \sum_{u\in\mathcal C}a_*(u)\le C/H_0
\]
for every antichain of required prefixes.  This is closer to the existing
min-cut and stopping-frontier certificates: instead of guessing a route law,
one proves that no prefix-free frontier carries too much maximum local charge,
then the law and the transition-aware water-filled allocation are forced by a
finite flow argument.
\Cref{lem:local-antichain-charge-potential} turns this global frontier
condition into a local proof obligation: find a nonnegative potential
\(\Phi\) with \(a_*(u)\le\Phi(u)\),
\(\sum_w\Phi(w)\le\Phi(u)\), and
\(\Phi(\varnothing)\le C/H_0\).  The stronger drop form
\(a_*(u)+\sum_w\Phi(w)\le\Phi(u)\) is enough and telescopes through every
stopping frontier.  \Cref{lem:superharmonic-potential-route-law} then turns
the same potential into an explicit top-down leaf law whose prefix masses
dominate \(H_0a_*(u)/C\).  Thus a decodable superharmonic potential supplies
both the route law and the transition-aware water-filled allocation; no
separate antichain-flow materialization is needed.  \Cref{cor:local-potential-antichain-fano}
packages this with the Fano decoder, so the remaining geometric theorem can be
attacked by local potential inequalities rather than by explicitly
constructing the route law.
\Cref{lem:least-superharmonic-majorant} makes the certificate canonical: the
least feasible \(\Phi^*\) is computed by a backward dynamic program and
\(\Phi^*(\varnothing)\) is exactly the maximum antichain charge.  Hence
\cref{cor:offline-superharmonic-route-verifier} gives a finite offline
acceptance test for any proposed successful-route trie.  Expensive
preprocessing may search over route tries, score panels, and saturated covers,
but the retained index only needs a decodable accepted trie, its canonical
potential, and the corresponding Fano threshold reporter.
\Cref{cor:finite-accepted-route-trie-compiler} is the resulting local
algorithmic certificate.  A trie is accepted by four finite checks: the
canonical superharmonic root bound, the raw reliability margin, the unpriced
prefix exponential moment, and the terminal-price exponential moment.  Passing
these checks with \(H_0\log C=O_c(\log\log m)\) gives the desired polylogarithmic
overhead for that local state.  Thus the remaining geometric theorem is now
not an allocation theorem or a route-law theorem; it is the construction of
accepted route tries for all unresolved local ANN states.
\Cref{cor:compressed-route-dag-verifier} is the code/lattice form of the same
certificate.  A trellis, recursive code decoder, product-panel stack decoder,
or lattice-enumeration DAG may be verified on its compact state graph as long
as a state potential satisfies the same superharmonic inequalities; the
explicit route trie is only the path unfolding used in the proof.  This is the
right way to import list-decoding ideas: not as a black-box nearest-lattice
oracle, but as a compact Fano-biased decoder whose state potential and path
moments pass the accepted-route checks.
\Cref{lem:moment-dominated-superharmonic} and
\cref{cor:prefix-moment-accepted-route-compiler} remove one remaining
duplication in this certificate.  If the maximum outgoing recursive charge at
each prefix is dominated by the normalized prefix-moment mass in its descendant
subtree, then the antichain/superharmonic root test follows from that same
moment bound.  Thus a future geometric construction does not need to prove an
independent route-law theorem: it may instead prove a suffix charge-density
inequality against the list-decoder prefix measure.  Same-prefix domination is
only a convenient stronger sufficient condition.
\Cref{lem:harmonic-resistance-normal-form} writes the optimal route law as an
ordinary series/parallel resistance calculation.  In particular,
\cref{lem:unit-success-skeleton-contraction} removes the ordinary score-only
part from the harmonic target: a deterministic unit-success region with exit
frontier \(\mathcal F\) satisfies
\[
   \frac1{W(r)}
   \le
   \frac1{\sum_{z\in\mathcal F}W(z)}
   +h_{\mathcal F}(r).
\]
\Cref{lem:ported-unit-region-contraction} gives the sharper ported form: the
first thinned or fractional-delivery exits contribute only through the single
conductance \(\sum_{e=(a,b)}\gamma_eW(b)\), plus the unit-region depth.  Thus
score branching, deterministic residual edges, and budget-stable recenterings
add only polylogarithmic harmonic resistance.  The remaining near-value theorem
can be stated on the contracted skeleton of genuinely thinned geometric or
fractional-delivery ports.  \Cref{lem:port-skeleton-saturated-comparison} and
\cref{cor:skeleton-cut-conductance} give the exact skeleton-level sufficient
condition: every cut of that port skeleton must carry inverse-polylogarithmic
activation mass, and the only additional loss is the sum of contracted
unit-region depths along a skeleton route.
\Cref{cor:existential-antichain-fano} composes this with the Fano decoder in
the ANN-correct existential form: if the union of valid terminal routes has the
same antichain charge bound and every such route has \(O_c(\log\log n)\) raw
reliability margin, then one deterministic biased stack decoder lists a valid
route with polylogarithmic overhead.  The remaining geometric theorem can
therefore be stated as an antichain charge bound plus a raw-margin/list-moment
bound for the successful-route trie, rather than as a separate allocation,
sampling, or cohort-materialization problem.
\Cref{lem:finite-convex-minimax} and
\cref{lem:robust-waterfilled-minimax} upgrade this from one route law to a
finite witness family: a single query allocation is optimal exactly when tested
against mixtures of the witness occupation profiles, so the remaining near-set
problem is a robust water-filled defect bound rather than a separate profile
for each possible near point.
\Cref{lem:waterfilled-layercake} and
\cref{cor:robust-waterfilled-tail} restate that robust defect as a tail
condition on high charge-to-occupation ratios above the water level.  The next
geometric proof target is therefore a uniform summable tail estimate for those
ratios over all finite mixtures of unresolved near-route laws.
\Cref{lem:waterfilled-moment-certificate} and
\cref{cor:robust-waterfilled-moment} give a more compact sufficient target:
it is enough to bound a small positive moment
\(\sum \ell^\alpha((a/(t_\alpha\ell^\alpha))^p-1)_+\) uniformly over
mixtures, with \(M/p=O_c(\log\log n)\).  Thus the remaining estimate can be
attacked as a low-temperature energy bound for the charge/occupation ratios,
rather than by proving every dyadic tail separately.
\Cref{lem:waterfilled-raw-moment-certificate} and
\cref{cor:robust-waterfilled-raw-moment} remove the implicit water level from
that target: if every mixture has total occupation at most \(H_0\), then
\(\tau=1/H_0\) is a valid lower bound on the water level, and it is enough to
bound the raw logarithmic defect
\[
   \sum_e\ell^\alpha_e
   \log_+\frac{H_0a_e}{\ell^\alpha_e},
\]
or more strongly the raw positive moment
\[
   \sum_e\ell^\alpha_e
   \left(
   \left(\frac{H_0a_e}{\ell^\alpha_e}\right)^p-1
   \right)_+
\]
with \(M/p=O_c(\log\log n)\).  A particularly concrete sufficient condition
is bounded charge density \(H_0a_e\le C\ell^\alpha_e\) on occupied unstable
opportunities, together with \(H_0=O_c(\log\log n)\); then the defect is at
most \(H_0\log C\).  For \(H_0=\log^{O_c(1)}n\), taking
\(p\asymp1/\log\log n\) still keeps the moment normalization \(H_0^p\)
constant, so the remaining theorem can be stated without solving for
\(t_\alpha\).
The guard refinement
\cref{lem:low-guard-shadow} further removes points whose entire near-query
neighborhood is already high-density: the finite dual now prices only the
low-guard shadow, so the remaining score-cover theorem is about sparse exposed
regions rather than dense clusters that resident sampling already solves.
\Cref{cor:shadow-finite-pool-dual} makes this formal in the LP: proposals are
intersected with the exposed shadow before their storage and active weights are
computed, and point prices vanish outside that shadow.
\Cref{lem:shadow-price-density-compiler} packages the exact remaining
score-cover theorem: every surplus shadow dual must expose a certified parent
proposal whose highest-price exposed prefix has positive reduced gain.  If this
separation holds for a finite low-guard pattern universe, column generation and
pattern-complete materialization produce the stored cover required by
\cref{asm:weak-offline-score-cover}.

\paragraph{Structured posterior route.}
\Cref{lem:posterior-superlevel-compiler} records the negative-moment identity suggested by the latest notes. \Cref{lem:explicit-enumeration-barrier} makes the coarse-child obstruction precise: the scale $\xi=m^{-1/(2c^2)}$ is the price of explicitly enumerating $B\simeq\xi^{-1}$ outcomes, not a geometric limit. \Cref{lem:oblivious-sparsification-barrier} adds the complementary warning that the moment bounds alone still permit $\Omega(\xi^{-1})$ disjoint possible witnesses, so direct random sparsification cannot replace structured decoding without an additional sensitivity theorem. \Cref{lem:scale-window-compiler} and \cref{lem:dyadic-structured-amplification} isolate the important arithmetic: if mass windows can be decoded output-sensitively, then $\xi^{-\rho}$ repetitions at each dyadic scale convert negative-moment value into constant hit probability, and summing all scales down to $1/m$ still fits the $m^\rho$ query budget. This scale-aware amplification is essential; a raw negative-moment diagnostic alone does not imply that the near point is actually listed with inverse-polylogarithmic probability. \Cref{cor:dyadic-affinity-boost} adds the skeleton-value refinement: multiplying the local repetitions by \(O(\log H)\) makes the outgoing-affinity deficit \(O(H^{-2})\), so the affinity-proportional toll is summable over a polylogarithmic-depth port skeleton rather than paid as a per-level recall loss.

The continuous likelihood-ball family now proves both analytic sides of the desired posterior decoder: \cref{thm:continuous-likelihood-balls} gives the guard-or-pure-child value, and \cref{lem:ideal-likelihood-scale-profile} gives the scale-normalized query and storage moments. \Cref{lem:likelihood-rank-prefix} further collapses the threshold continuum to rank gaps of a random score order. \Cref{cor:likelihood-prefix-leader} removes another artificial materialization cost: for ANN, every pure prefix may report the same score leader, so the decoder can aggregate prefix mass by leader buckets instead of storing one representative per prefix. \Cref{lem:dyadic-leader-quotient} records the full amplification in this hidden-label form and contributes no per-prefix storage term. \Cref{cor:dyadic-leader-affinity-boost} adds the skeleton-value refinement for the quotient itself: after the \(O(\log H)\)-boosted repetitions, the actual merged leader ports have total useful outgoing affinity \(1-O(H^{-2})\). \Cref{cor:boosted-leader-skeleton-toll} then composes this with affinity-proportional routing: quotienting prefixes by leader gives only constant total square toll over a depth-\(H\) port skeleton, not a hidden per-level recall loss. \Cref{cor:likelihood-leader-intensity} identifies the exact quotient law as the rank-gap weighted measure over score leaders. \Cref{lem:ideal-likelihood-leader-law} further proves that this quotient law has constant total intensity per scale and constant scale-weighted valid intensity under guard failure. \Cref{lem:poissonized-normalized-leader-sampler} removes the remaining all-listing requirement from a sampled implementation: computing the total intensity and sampling from the normalized tilted law gives the exact Poisson leader process. Finally, \cref{lem:scale-amplified-alpha-leader} shows that the dyadic repetitions cancel the rank powers, collapsing the whole amplified posterior to the max-tilted leader law \((AL2)\), with constant total mass and constant valid mass for every near pair. The clean measure target is therefore \cref{asm:alpha-leader-sampler}; conditional on it, \cref{prop:alpha-leader-polylog} gives the desired polylogarithmic ANN bounds. \Cref{lem:alpha-leader-voronoi-capture} gives an equivalent geometric normal form for that same target: the max-tilted intensity of \(x\) is a Gaussian Voronoi-cell capture probability for the interpolated center \((1-\alpha)q+\alpha x\), multiplied by the explicit distance tilt \(\exp(-\alpha(1-\alpha)t\|x-q\|^2/2)\). \Cref{cor:query-centered-cell-reweighting} and \cref{cor:truncated-nearest-cell-compiler} then reduce max-tilted sampling to query-centered nearest-cell decoding plus scalar rejection. The weakest current algorithmic posterior target is \cref{asm:smoothed-witness-list}: list the true near witness with constant tilted mass and scan the verified list. Conditional on it, \cref{prop:witness-list-polylog} gives the same polylogarithmic ANN bound. The facility form \cref{cor:facility-bucket-witness} is the version most directly connected to \(k\)-means++ or other build-time bucket proposals. \Cref{lem:poisson-rate-coverage}, \cref{lem:finite-signature-rate-coverage}, \cref{lem:finite-poisson-rate-coverage-realization}, \cref{cor:finite-signature-retained-buckets}, \cref{cor:finite-transcript-rate-coverage}, \cref{cor:compressed-decoder-dag-rate-coverage}, \cref{cor:output-sensitive-decoder-dag-rate-coverage}, \cref{lem:scalar-redundancy-waterfill}, and \cref{asm:rate-coverage-panel} sharpen this further into the redundancy theorem object: point-label intensities, query label sets, finite coefficient envelopes, one fixed retained Poisson realization, transcript-level and state-DAG decoder work, responsibility-weighted enumerator coverage, the marginal replication water level, the tilted miss bound, and the scan-load bound. \Cref{lem:finite-rate-coverage-convex} gives the finite convex feasibility test and dual obstruction for proposed panels. Conditional on that finite rate-coverage panel, \cref{prop:rate-coverage-polylog} gives the same endpoint. The scale-resolved sampler \cref{asm:ideal-likelihood-leader-law-sampler}, the hidden-label sampler \cref{asm:normalized-likelihood-leader-sampler}, the structured nearest-cell decoder \cref{asm:smoothed-nearest-cell}, and the older all-listing \cref{asm:multiscale-structured-likelihood} remain stronger sufficient implementation forms.

\Cref{lem:seeded-reduced-gain-search} is the build-time bridge from this
finite certificate to list-decoding and lattice-decoding proposals: the
proposal mechanism only has to expose a positive reduced-gain label against
the current dual obstruction, because the retained panel is accepted by the
same exact convex verifier.  \Cref{lem:implicit-reduced-gain-separation}
turns this into a true separation-oracle statement for implicit quotient
families: if a code, lattice, trellis, or facility universe cannot expose
positive gain, the dual obstruction rules out every finite-support panel from
that universe.  \Cref{lem:reduced-gain-variational-separation} gives the
search form of the oracle: after choosing tentative point intensities, the
label generator only solves a signed weighted coverage problem, and exact
verification converts any positive surplus into a valid column.
\Cref{lem:layer-cake-reduced-gain-separation} removes the remaining continuous
profile from that search, replacing it by a single point subset and scalar
layer, with a dyadic scalar grid whenever the retained intensities are capped.
\Cref{cor:pointwise-reduced-cost-separation} sharpens the final separator:
to certify completeness it is enough to find one point and one implicit label
whose residual tilted coverage exceeds its query-load and storage price.
\Cref{cor:soft-list-decoding-reduced-cost-separator} converts this into the
standard soft-decoding interface when the score is coordinatewise additive:
threshold-list codewords, lattice residues, or trellis paths by the dual-priced
reliability score, then exactly filter the returned candidates.
\Cref{cor:threshold-event-reduced-cost} records the corresponding exact target
for ordinary threshold reporters: solve a signed weighted coverage problem over
the satisfied threshold tests.
\Cref{cor:positive-coverage-screen} reduces candidate generation to the
nonnegative part of that coverage objective; signed terms are checked only
after a candidate label is returned.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-positive-list-recovery} then converts arbitrary nonnegative
dual weights into dyadic unweighted list-recovery calls, with the exact
weighted reduced cost checked only at the filter step.
\Cref{cor:ordinary-list-recovery-positive-coverage} identifies those calls
with ordinary list recovery on repeated coordinates for code, trellis, or
lattice-residue membership tests.
\Cref{cor:unified-soft-decoded-rate-coverage} is the corresponding full panel
contract: offline separation is a build-time concern, while online decoder
output, candidate incidence load, and stored replication are charged as three
separate resources.

\Cref{lem:smoothed-max-score-margin} gives a still simpler non-channel target: a query-centered Gaussian score direction separates every invalid point from the true near point by an additive $\Theta_c(tr^2)$ score margin, with high probability. The softest resulting primitive is \cref{asm:smoothed-gibbs}: with inverse-polylogarithmic probability, report a list carrying inverse-polylogarithmic mass under the Gaussian Gibbs kernel on data points. Sampling from the kernel restricted to that list gives a pointwise dominated output law by \cref{lem:captured-gibbs-domination}, and \cref{lem:smoothed-gibbs-suffices} then returns a valid answer because invalid points have negligible Gibbs mass and cannot be oversampled too much. This mass-capture target is now known not to be a universal theorem as stated: \cref{lem:medium-valid-plateau-gibbs-obstruction} gives medium-size valid plateaus where the guard test fails but every \(m^\rho\polylog m\)-sized list has only polynomially small Gibbs mass. Hence this branch must either add a direct valid-output mechanism for that regime or move to a primitive that certifies one high-score valid point. A more exact sampling route is certified additive Gumbel-MIPS: \cref{lem:gumbel-additive-domination} shows that an $O(\log\log m)$ additive optimizer for the Gumbel-perturbed scores gives precisely the required one-sided Gibbs domination, yielding \cref{prop:gumbel-mips-polylog}. A stronger but different implementation route is smoothed additive nearest-neighbor search for the perturbed center $Y/t$ with additive squared-distance error $\Theta_c(r^2)$, exactly equivalent to additive score maximization by \cref{lem:score-max-additive-nn}. These oracles would bypass dyadic scales and representatives entirely, as recorded in \cref{prop:smoothed-gibbs-polylog}, \cref{prop:gumbel-mips-polylog}, and \cref{prop:smoothed-score-max-polylog}. They are targets, not implemented theorems; \cref{rem:gumbel-mips-not-ann} explains why black-box multiplicative ANN does not supply the Gumbel primitive. The older finite restricted-channel compiler \cref{asm:finite-restricted-channel} and \cref{prop:finite-channel-polylog} remain as a coarse explicit-enumeration special case and as a useful diagnostic framework.

\paragraph{Cohort-or-leaf.}
\Cref{asm:cohort-or-leaf} is the original full-child route-level condition for the broader posterior-cohort endpoint, but \cref{lem:prefix-slice-accounting} shows that a prefix-conditioned formulation is cleaner. Work accounting for opened children is no longer the hard part: \cref{lem:vote-budget} pays opened recursive calls from realized detector votes. The preferred remaining target for that more general route is \cref{asm:prefix-slice-survival}: prove that one cumulative near-pair score path either reaches a cap-free residual scan or receives enough detector votes to follow prefix-conditioned certified slices to a resident scan. \Cref{lem:detector-inflation} and \cref{lem:off-spine-inflation} reduce the detector-shadowing part of this target to early activation prefixes with large enough continuation mass $H(v)$ and logarithmic spine-ratio sum $\sum H(u^+)/H(u)$; \cref{rem:linear-spine-ratio} explains why long score routes need an aggregate detector-mass argument instead. This should be tested against the hard cases: an isolated near point next to a massive far cluster, a near point on a cluster boundary, a tiny child that becomes heavy only late, and symmetric far shells. The proof must show a whole-lineage inverse-polylogarithmic event, not merely an inverse-polylogarithmic event at each level.

\section{Conclusion}

The algorithmic target is a cumulative score-and-ball tree with query time
\[
   d\,n^{1/(2c^2-1)}\log^{O_c(1)}n
\]
and space
\[
   dn+n^{1+1/(2c^2-1)}\log^{O_c(1)}n.
\]
The exact pieces now aligned for the randomized cap-thinning route are: continuation-mass pruning gives optimal expected spherical work, adaptive continuation gives whole-lineage near survival, thinned cap splitting gives radius-potential contraction, and cap-free terminal scans are paid by low-correlation collisions.

The compressed-bucket route from \cref{prop:success-normalized-bucket-dag} is
now separated just as cleanly.  The recursion accounting is finished: a finite
approximation ladder gives \(n^{\rho_c}\polylog n\) query time once each rung
has a cost-normalized fractional probing law and a shared-DAG storage moment.
\Cref{lem:bucket-net-recursion-geometry} is the deterministic geometric core:
replacing a bucket by an \((\alpha-1)r\)-net changes the child problem to
\((c/\alpha,\alpha r)\)-ANN and preserves parent verification.
\Cref{cor:fractional-probe-compressed-bucket} folds the old near-hit lower bound
and query Renyi moment into one invariant: recursive one-probe price divided by
near-witness coverage.  The query moment is therefore no longer a separate
list-decoding problem; by \cref{lem:first-moment-query-compression}, the usual
success-normalized expected bucket load implies the Renyi child-work bound, and
\cref{cor:first-moment-active-load-query} is the exact finite-profile version
with false active buckets included in the active layer.
\Cref{cor:compressed-bucket-rung-checklist} packages this into the current
minimal rung test: ordinary success-normalized candidate load plus distinct
canonical-net storage.  Thus the remaining list-decoding theorem for compressed
buckets is a storage/canonicalization theorem, not a query theorem.
\Cref{cor:low-high-compressed-cap-storage} sharpens that storage target for
large-range centered cap buckets: \(K^{1+s}\le K^2\) reduces the distinct-child
moment to the diagonal, low-correlation pair co-load, and one explicit
high-correlation ordered-pair tail.  The diagonal and
\(O(\log\log m/\log m)\)-correlation pairs are already polylogarithmic, so any
polynomial compressed-bucket storage survivor must be a high-correlation tail
for the dense/star or sponsor verifier.
\Cref{cor:diffuse-compressed-cap-rung} makes the contrapositive endpoint
explicit: if the realized bucket nets contain no such high-correlation pairs,
or if that tail is certified polylogarithmic, then the entire compressed-cap
rung already satisfies the success-normalized polylogarithmic checklist.  Thus
the random-position/diffuse case is closed before invoking dense-overlap
machinery.
\Cref{cor:compressed-cap-high-tail-prefix-pricing} sends that tail through the
cap-centered paid-prefix verifier: the paid part is either a quadratic
same-prefix repair or a fixed dyadic tail, leaving only the overload where cap
incidence exceeds paid near-pair degree.
\Cref{cor:compressed-cap-high-tail-storage-only} composes this with the
quadratic toll compiler: repeated paid-prefix high-tail repairs have only
polylogarithmic total geometric toll, so the remaining positive-correlation
work is the storage/sponsorship of the overload \(H_{\rm over}\).
\Cref{cor:compressed-cap-overload-hall-tail} identifies that overload with the
standard cap-centered Hall residual: bounded transport sends it back to the
paid-prefix mechanism, while failed transport exposes a pure overload star that
is charged once by shared-child storage.
\Cref{cor:compressed-cap-overload-generated-column} closes the bookkeeping for
that branch: use raw multiplicity for reciprocal occurrence storage but use the
smaller excess mass \(H_{\rm over}\) as the sponsor pool; any unsponsored
survivor is a single generated-cover LP dual layer.
\Cref{cor:compressed-cap-overload-dual-low-cover-screen} then dyadically
unweights that layer: a low-price generated cover or generated-metric ball
cover would already violate the dual and fire a positive prefix, so any
survivor has an explicit entropy/packing lower bound.
\Cref{cor:compressed-cap-overload-packing-energy-endpoint} feeds the resulting
packing into the usual entropy-energy test: centered cap panels pay the
one-point and low-correlation pair mass, and any remaining high-correlation
star must have generated price at least its dual mass.
\Cref{cor:compressed-cap-overload-cap-star-storage-split} converts those
remaining stars into the usual fixed-tail/storage-dominated split: medium stars
would already be positive generated prefixes, small stars are a bounded tail,
and large stars become another priced child panel.
\Cref{cor:distinct-canonical-bucket-net} further sharpens the storage target:
the recursive child index is charged once per distinct canonical bucket net, not
once per decoded occurrence, with only occurrence pointers left in the metadata
budget.  \Cref{cor:finite-signature-compressed-bucket-bridge} is the formal
bridge to the fractional dense-overlap picture: a compressed bucket panel is
just a finite exact-signature filter-cover certificate once its useful hit
denominator, active-load overlap, and distinct canonical storage are normalized
by the same \(a_{\rm cb}\).  The dual form is
\cref{cor:shared-canonical-panel-reduced-gain}: against the current exact
signature prices, a whole decoded panel is scored by useful hit mass minus
active recursive query load and shared canonical child storage.  Thus
success-normalized bucket compression is another reduced-gain column-generation
interface, not a separate hard branching rule.
\Cref{cor:one-sided-shared-panel-column-generation} is the corresponding
offline search procedure: arbitrary preprocessing may sample or optimize over
decoded panels, but only verified positive-gain panels enter the restricted
profile cover.  \Cref{cor:shared-panel-positive-separator-endpoint} is the
nodewise endpoint statement: proving this positive separator for the finite
panel universe at every localized node gives the \(n^{\rho_c}\polylog n\)
query and \(n^{1+\rho_c}\polylog n\) space bounds.
\Cref{cor:weighted-shared-panel-renyi-separator} is the weighted
list-decoding form of that target: under every normalized dual, a seed law must
capture more priced useful hit mass than its active first-moment/Renyi query
load plus shared child-storage moment.
\Cref{cor:certified-storage-weighted-panel-separator} permits the storage term
in that inequality to be any certified upper envelope, which is how tuple
profiles, dyadic tails, and multiplicity-discounted witnesses feed the
shared-panel endpoint without changing the retained child DAG.
\Cref{cor:certified-storage-weighted-residual} is the exact counterexample
format left for geometry: a normalized dual under which every finite proposed
panel law has useful hit at most active load plus certified storage envelope.
\Cref{cor:certified-storage-residual-split} isolates the two possible
obstructions in such a counterexample: either the proposal's active-load ratio
is already near its useful hit mass, or its certified shared-storage envelope
must carry a comparable fraction of that mass.  Thus the remaining
list-decoding theorem may be attacked by proving both a first-moment active-load
gap and a storage-envelope bound for one dual-priced panel law.
\Cref{cor:dual-priced-witness-storage-separator} gives the corresponding
storage interface: distribute each distinct canonical child's storage price
over certified witnesses, bound the dual-priced witness congestion, and combine
that bound with the active-load gap to obtain a positive separator immediately.
\Cref{cor:witness-law-shared-panel-endpoint} packages this into the current
shortest endpoint theorem: at every localized node, a dual-priced witness law
with \(Q/A+W/A<1\) implies the shared-panel positive separator and hence the
full \(n^{\rho_c}\polylog n\) query and \(n^{1+\rho_c}\polylog n\) space
bounds.
\Cref{cor:witness-law-residual-obstruction} gives the exact negation over any
fixed certified report class: a surviving normalized dual makes every report
satisfy \(A\le Q+W\), hence every query-efficient report must pay comparable
dual-priced witness storage.
\Cref{cor:sampled-witness-report-separation} is the sampled build-time version:
a proposal routine only has to produce certified reports with positive expected
surplus \(A-Q-W\); after enough uncharged samples, one positive report is
verified and reduced to an ordinary positive shared-panel column.
\Cref{cor:witness-report-panel-hardening} removes another artificial
restriction: a proposal may return a finite weighted panel of reports, and a
positive aggregate surplus already contains one deterministic positive report.
\Cref{cor:benefit-allocated-witness-density-screen} pushes the same hardening
inside one report: after allocating net useful benefit to witness classes, a
positive aggregate benefit-minus-congestion certificate contains a class whose
benefit beats its certified witness congestion.
\Cref{cor:class-local-witness-density-screen} states the corresponding
materialized profile target: if a tuple profile, range cell, or decoder output
type can be made into an admissible class-local report, the residual envelope is
the explicit density inequality \(B_\ell\le N_\ell e^{-I_\ell}\).
\Cref{cor:gaussian-tuple-profile-witness-density} specializes this to Gaussian
pair profiles: the low-correlation residual inequality is
\(B_\pi\le M_\pi\exp(-\beta_\pi^2/(1+\theta_\pi))\), or the analogous
two-margin bound.
\Cref{cor:correlation-split-witness-profile-residual} combines this with the
high-correlation star reporter in the same fractional residual language: a
surviving split profile must have benefit bounded by low-correlation Gaussian
congestion, explicit unreported high-correlation tail, and the paid recursive
price of reported star prefixes.  Thus dense overlap is charged as panel price,
not as a branching factor.
\Cref{cor:split-profile-panel-hardening} removes the single-profile
restriction: any finite nonnegative panel of split profiles with positive
aggregate surplus contains either a low-correlation witness violation or a
paid high-correlation dense-prefix violation.  This is the form needed for
build-time list/range/facility/AQ/lattice proposal oracles.
\Cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-envelope} optimizes out the chosen
high-correlation routing: each profile pays the infimum over certified star
routings and explicit tails, leaving a scalar residual envelope
\(B_\pi\le C_\pi^{\rm lo}+\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}\) in aggregate.  This is the
closest current form to the desired fractional dense-filter cover theorem.
\Cref{cor:atomized-high-correlation-routing-dual} gives the finite LP dual for
one concrete implementation of \(\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}\): atom benefits are routed
either to explicit tail or to certified pair-star records, and the dual is a
weighted no-star condition \(0\le y\le1\) with every star's weighted atom mass
below its recursive price.
\Cref{cor:layer-cake-atom-cut-normal-form} thresholds that fractional dual into
one atom cut: at some dyadic level, scaled cut benefit is a logarithmic fraction
of the dual value while the scaled mass seen by every certified star is still
below its recursive price.  This is the current cut-style high-correlation
obstruction.
\Cref{cor:high-correlation-atom-cut-star-screen} then applies the geometric
pair-star reporter to such a cut: if the scaled high-correlation incidence is
larger than the fixed star price tail \(2|P|J_{\rm cut}P_0\), a
smaller-radius dense prefix must fire.
\Cref{cor:high-correlation-atom-cut-aggregate-screen} sharpens this by charging
the aggregate recursive price \(\sum_{x,s}P_{x,s}\) of the reported dyadic
stars; the uniform \(2|P|J_{\rm cut}P_0\) term is only a fallback
specialization.
\Cref{cor:reported-center-atom-cut-screen} is the build-facing version: a
center proposal may report only \(C\subseteq P\), paying an explicit
unreported-center tail \(E_C(t)\) plus the aggregate recursive price of its
reported stars.
\Cref{cor:reported-center-benefit-price-screen} is the corresponding reduced
cost test: if a proposed center set captures scaled mass \(M_C(t)>2P_C\), then
one reported star must already be a positive dense prefix; randomized center
laws are judged by the expected surplus \(M_C(t)-2P_C\).
\Cref{cor:singleton-reported-center-screen} sharpens this cut-local search:
because both captured mass and reported star price are additive over centers,
any positive set or sampled-law surplus contains one singleton center with
\(m_x(t)>2P_x\).  Thus the verifier may enumerate or sample centers one at a
time at a fixed cut.
\Cref{cor:one-sided-singleton-center-certificate} is the build-facing
certificate: a proposed center need only lower-certify its captured cut mass and
upper-certify its recursive star price; if \(\underline m_x>2\overline P_x\),
the usual verified dense prefix fires.
\Cref{cor:clipped-singleton-center-cover} gives the closed-form LP value in
the additive case: the fractional center-cover price is exactly
\(\sum_x\min\{m_x(t),2P_x\}\), and any strict improvement over tailing all cut
mass is already a positive singleton.
\Cref{cor:fractional-reported-center-cover-dual} packages center search as a
finite LP: either fractional reported-center panels lower the tail-only cost,
which hardens to one positive dense-prefix column, or the all-ones no-center
dual is feasible.
\Cref{cor:sampled-reported-center-tail-certificate} gives the same statement
for randomized center laws: surviving residuals satisfy
\(\E M_C(t)\le2\E P_C\), so positive expected center surplus already contains
one deterministic verified prefix.
\Cref{cor:atomized-high-correlation-fixed-tail} aggregates this over the whole
atomized routing dual: after \(\varepsilon\)-truncation, either a dense prefix
fires or
\(\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}\le
\varepsilon B_\pi^{\rm hi}
+2J_\varepsilon\mathfrak E_\star
+4J_\varepsilon\mathfrak P_\star\).
\Cref{cor:sampled-center-high-correlation-fixed-tail} is the build-facing
variant with a randomized center-panel law at each cut.
\Cref{cor:clipped-singleton-high-correlation-fixed-tail} is the scalar
singleton version: a cut-wise clipped envelope
\(\Gamma_{\rm clip}=E_{\mathcal X}+\sum_x\min\{m_x,2P_x\}\) gives the same
bound with \(A^{\rm clip}=2\Gamma_{\rm clip}\), and any strict clipping gain
already fires one singleton dense prefix.
\Cref{cor:clipped-singleton-density-endpoint} feeds this scalar envelope
directly into the logarithmic endpoint: polynomial dynamic range and
\(A^{\rm clip}\le D/\log^{1+\Omega(1)}n\) already imply the full
\(n^{\rho_c}\polylog n\) theorem.
\Cref{cor:integrated-clipped-singleton-high-correlation} removes the
worst-cut multiplier: the high-correlation price is bounded by the actual
dyadic sum of clipped singleton prices over the layer-cake cuts.
\Cref{cor:integrated-singleton-reduced-cost-screen} turns positive integrated
center surplus into one winning cut, and
\cref{cor:integrated-clipped-price-surplus-identity} identifies the integrated
clipped price as dyadic cut area minus positive singleton surplus.
\Cref{cor:reduced-cost-singleton-center-search} makes the cut-local search
complete over any finite center universe: a center set, randomized law, or
\(k\)-means++-style proposal is useful only through one certified singleton
surplus \(m_x-2P_x>0\).
\Cref{cor:shared-integrated-star-prefix-screen} is the sharper fractional
variant: one star-prefix record may accumulate mass over all dyadic cuts and is
charged its recursive price once, up to the dyadic constant.
\Cref{cor:shared-integrated-high-correlation-tail} turns this into an integrated
tail bound
\(\Phi_\pi^{\rm hi}\le\varepsilon B_\pi^{\rm hi}
+2\mathfrak E_{\Sigma,\pi}+4\mathfrak P_{\Sigma,\pi}\), and
\cref{cor:finite-shared-integrated-cover-dual} packages the same certificate as
a finite LP.  Its objective is integrated unassigned tail plus twice the
one-time recursive price, and its dual is the exact no-shared-record residual.
\Cref{cor:shared-integrated-cover-column-generation} and
\cref{cor:one-sided-shared-integrated-cover-oracle} give the corresponding
build-time reduced-cost interface: a proposed shared record is useful exactly
when \(\sum_ah_{i,a}u_a>2P_i\), with one-sided certificates allowed on the
positive branch.
\Cref{cor:shared-top-prefix-reduced-cost-compiler} and
\cref{cor:one-sided-shared-top-prefix-certificate} reduce that record search to
the usual exact top-prefix operation inside a certified smaller-radius
container: sort points by shared-cover degree and test whether one prefix beats
twice its one-time recursive price.
\Cref{cor:reduced-cost-top-prefix-router-search} records the resulting router
oracle: a data-dependent partition or container generator is a proposal
mechanism, while the proof object is exact reduced-cost maximization over its
certified top prefixes.
\Cref{cor:shared-prefix-weak-type-residual} and
\cref{cor:shared-prefix-price-density-screen} record the matching residual:
if every such prefix fails, the shared degrees in every certified container
obey an explicit weak-type envelope, while a height-and-mass density violation
materializes one positive top-prefix column.
\Cref{cor:shared-prefix-density-panel} is the panel hardening of this screen:
finite or sampled facility, AQ, range, list, or lattice proposals may be scored
by aggregate shared-degree surplus, but any positive panel still reduces to one
deterministic verified top prefix.
\Cref{cor:sampled-shared-prefix-density-search} gives the Las Vegas
build-time wrapper: a positive expected certified surplus is amplified by
repetition, while failed panels are discarded before materialization.
\Cref{cor:clipped-shared-prefix-density-screen} is the corresponding core
simplification: once the query and storage prices of a shared container are
fixed, the residual need only be challenged near the clipped minimizer of
\(A K^{\rho-1}+\zeta K^\rho\), rather than across all prefix sizes.
\Cref{cor:tail-mass-clipped-shared-prefix-screen} gives the clean tail form:
in a surviving residual, shared-degree mass above the clipped threshold is at
most the clipped support scale times that threshold.
\Cref{cor:cardinality-net-clipped-shared-tail} removes the remaining choice of
prefix size under the usual cardinality-net closure: every surviving shared
container satisfies one explicit tail cap at its clipped stationary scale.
\Cref{cor:subset-clipped-shared-tail-residual} rewrites that tail cap as an
all-subsets obstruction: any certified subset whose paid mass beats
\((|U|+2K^\natural)\Theta^{\rm net}\) already forces the same deterministic
shared top-prefix column.
\Cref{cor:transported-subset-clipped-tail-certificate} is the transport-facing
form: a bounded-congestion shipment into one certified subset separates as soon
as its transported mass beats this affine clipped-tail threshold, without an
extra layer-cake dynamic-range loss.
\Cref{cor:transported-clipped-tail-panel-separator} is the panel version:
facility, AQ, range, list, lattice, or other proposal families may return a
weighted collection of transported subsets, and positive aggregate transported
surplus still hardens to one deterministic shared top-prefix column.
\Cref{lem:flow-value-clipped-tail-screen} replaces explicit transported loads
by finite max-flow values and gives the matching localized min-cut obstruction
when a proposed flow panel fails.
\Cref{cor:opened-support-flow-screen} removes the remaining fixed-container
overcharge: the flow branch score is transported mass divided by congestion,
minus the clipped baseline times the actually opened sink support.  Thus a
large proposal set may be used as a search universe without paying for points
that receive no flow.
\Cref{cor:fractional-opened-support-flow-lp} replaces even this nonconvex
support maximization by a finite fractional opening LP.  The relaxation is
still sound in the no-prefix residual: if its value beats the clipped overhead,
the positive degree tail itself violates the clipped subset cap; if it does
not, the LP dual is an explicit source/point price obstruction.
\Cref{cor:thresholded-dual-failed-fractional-flow} turns that dual obstruction
into a thresholded normal form: only \(L/\eta\) normalized source load can be
paid by large \(\alpha\)-prices, and the remaining low-\(\alpha\) sources have a
neighborhood satisfying a raised clipped-tail bound.
\Cref{cor:source-retention-failed-fractional-flow} makes the retained mass
explicit: a high-mass failed source system leaves a high-mass low-\(\alpha\)
subsystem unless the explicit paid source term already accounts for it.
\Cref{cor:common-retained-failed-flow-panel} is the finite-panel version: many
failed source systems sharing the same normalized source measure delete source
mass only additively, leaving one common residual that is tail-clipped for all
of the failed proposal families.
\Cref{cor:adaptive-retained-failed-flow-sequence} removes the last static
restriction: the next proposal family may be chosen after seeing the previous
failed screens, and the same additive source-deletion bound still holds.
\Cref{cor:value-retained-adaptive-failed-screen} translates this into the
dual-obstruction language: failed screens consume an explicit amount of source
value, so unless that budget pays for the obstruction, a high-value residual
survives with all transcript tail caps.
\Cref{cor:template-complete-shared-cover-obstruction} gives the exact finite
LP normal form for the remaining shared-cover target: if the cover value at
level \(D/4\) is too large, the obstruction is one dual \(u\) of value
\(>D/4\) whose every certified template obeys the top-prefix inequality and,
under cardinality-net closure, the clipped tail cap.
\Cref{cor:template-search-shared-integrated-target} packages this as the
current build-time target with arbitrary preprocessing: solve the finite
template cover, or make the returned obstruction violate one certified
container tail cap.
\Cref{cor:transport-template-obstruction-endpoint} is the current transport
normal form of that target: every high-value no-prefix dual must admit a
bounded-congestion transported panel whose affine clipped-tail surplus is
positive.
\Cref{cor:flow-value-template-obstruction-endpoint} is the equivalent
verifier-facing form in terms of max-flow values; a failed record leaves the
explicit cut \((CTV6)\).
\Cref{cor:opened-support-template-obstruction-endpoint} is the sharper current
form: it is enough to find positive opened-support flow surplus, so support
selection, cohort materialization, and transported subset choice are all part
of one branching-score maximization.
\Cref{cor:fractional-opened-support-template-endpoint} is the LP-facing version
of the same target: preprocessing may solve the fractional opened-support LP
and keep only a verified positive top-prefix column, while failed proposals
leave finite dual prices rather than an unstructured failed support search.
\Cref{cor:adaptive-fractional-flow-exhaustion-endpoint} is the finite
build-time-complete version: adaptive proposal search may keep failing only if
the declared failed-screen budgets have already paid for every high-value
tail-capped residual.
\Cref{cor:obstruction-sourced-flow-exhaustion} removes the last free source
measure from that statement: for a no-prefix obstruction \(u\), sources are the
atoms \(a\) with weights \(b_au_a\), and it is enough to rule out a residual
carrying half of this exposed value.
\Cref{cor:failed-transcript-residual-lp} makes that last residual test finite
and dual: an all-failed transcript is exhausted once a weighted tail-budget LP
has value below the target residual mass.
\Cref{cor:fractional-failed-transcript-accounting} strengthens this from an
integral-retained-set relaxation to a fully fractional process: failed screens
shrink source intensities by their own LP dual prices, and the final intensity
vector is feasible for the same residual LP.
\Cref{cor:capped-residual-lp-continuation} makes the build-time loop
LP-guided: solve the current capped residual LP, use its primal optimizer as
the next source measure, and update the cap after a failed screen so previously
paid source mass cannot reappear.
\Cref{cor:downward-residual-lp-normal-form} removes transcript history from the
geometric side of that loop: the current optimizer \(z\) simply forms a smaller
no-prefix dual \(u^z\), and separator search is against this downward residual.
\Cref{cor:capped-atom-capture-support-screen} gives the preferred support-level
certificate for such a separator: a proposed container only has to lower-certify
capped atom capture
\(\sum_a u_a^z\min\{b_a,\sum_{p\in S}h_{B,p,a}\}\) above the affine clipped
support price, a monotone-submodular coverage objective that facility,
range-reporting, AQ, lattice, or list-decoding proposal routines can try to
maximize in build time.
\Cref{cor:routed-capped-capture-support-screen} gives the lower-certified
interface for such routines: they may route atom mass into a support under the
same atom caps instead of evaluating the full capped capture objective.
\Cref{cor:averaged-routed-capped-capture-proposals} adds the sampled proposal
form: positive expected one-sided routed surplus is enough, because verification
hardens the first positive sample to a deterministic prefix.
\Cref{cor:fractional-capped-capture-threshold-screen} makes this proposal layer
fully fractional: if a routine certifies layer-cake capped capture above the
fractional support price, one deterministic threshold support gives the same
positive branch.
\Cref{cor:lp-guided-capped-flow-exhaustion-endpoint} feeds this back into the
ANN endpoint: it is enough to prove that the LP-guided loop either finds a
half-threshold opened-support screen or drives the capped residual LP below
half the exposed obstruction value before spending half that value.
\Cref{cor:single-tail-shared-separator-endpoint} packages this into the
current sharp proof target: every normalized exact-signature dual must either
produce a materializable low-correlation profile record or force one certified
shared container to violate that single clipped tail cap.
\Cref{cor:shared-integrated-cover-cost-endpoint} and
\cref{cor:shared-integrated-dense-profile-endpoint} are the corresponding
polylogarithmic endpoints.  This is the current clean fractional-overlap target:
prove that the shared integrated cover value is a constant fraction of the
residual benefit under every normalized high-correlation dual.
\Cref{cor:child-panel-shared-integrated-endpoint} routes the common child-panel
residual to this stronger target: after the sponsor/generated-prefix and
low-correlation exits fail, a single split profile with constant-fraction shared
integrated cost is enough.
\Cref{cor:one-sided-integrated-singleton-center} gives the corresponding
one-sided build-time certificate.
\Cref{cor:integrated-clipped-singleton-density-endpoint} is the corresponding
endpoint: it is enough that this dyadic sum be a constant fraction of the
residual benefit after a polynomial dynamic-range truncation.
\Cref{cor:one-sided-integrated-clipped-profile-oracle} is the verifier-facing
form of this sharper target: certify upper bounds on the high-correlation mass
and integrated clipped price, plus the truncation, so that
\(\varepsilon\overline B^{\rm hi}+2\overline G_\Sigma<\underline D\).
\Cref{cor:one-sided-clipped-singleton-profile-oracle} gives the verifier form:
build-time search only needs lower residual benefit and upper high-correlation
mass/clipped-price certificates, and Las Vegas sampling may discard every
failed proposal.
\Cref{cor:explicit-split-profile-tail-separator} feeds this explicit tail into
the split-profile panel separator, replacing the abstract min-cost
high-correlation price by a checkable scalar envelope.
\Cref{cor:sampled-center-split-profile-separator} is the final sampled
interface at this level: split-profile panels may use randomized center laws
for their high-correlation pieces, and positive aggregate surplus still
hardens to one ordinary verified panel column.
\Cref{cor:sampled-center-split-profile-residual} records the exact surviving
counterexample envelope \(B\le C^{\rm lo}+\varepsilon B^{\rm hi}
+2J_\varepsilon\mathfrak E_\star+4J_\varepsilon\mathfrak P_\star\).
\Cref{cor:optimized-sampled-center-split-profile-residual} optimizes out
\(\varepsilon\) when the sampled-center certificates are uniform over
truncation levels, giving the logarithmic toll
\(A(1+\log_+(B^{\rm hi}/A))\) with
\(A=2\mathfrak E_\star+4\mathfrak P_\star\).
\Cref{cor:log-sampled-center-separator-endpoint} packages this as the current
polylog endpoint target: every normalized dual must admit a sampled-center
split-profile panel whose residual benefit beats that logarithmic toll.
\Cref{cor:single-profile-log-density-screen} removes even this panel
coordination from the search target: a successful weighted panel contains one
profile with residual benefit density above its sampled-center logarithmic
price.
\Cref{cor:inverted-sampled-center-density-residual} gives the contrapositive
price-density form: surviving residuals force
\(A^{\rm samp}\gtrsim D/(1+\log_+(B^{\rm hi}/D))\), where
\(D=(B-C^{\rm lo})_+\).
\Cref{cor:polylog-sampled-center-density-endpoint} is the concrete polylog
target: polynomial dynamic range and sampled-center price
\(A^{\rm samp}\le D/\log^{1+\Omega(1)}n\) already imply the endpoint.
\Cref{cor:one-sided-polylog-sampled-center-profile-oracle} gives the verifier
form of that target using only one-sided certificates: lower residual benefit
and upper high-correlation/sample-price bounds.
\Cref{cor:las-vegas-sampled-center-profile-oracle} is the build-time sampling
form: any proposal law that hits such a one-sided certificate with positive
probability can be repeated until accepted, while failed proposals are
discarded before they affect the retained index.
\Cref{cor:min-cost-split-profile-separator-endpoint} turns this scalar envelope
into an endpoint statement: if every normalized exact-signature dual violates
the optimized envelope for some finite split-profile panel, and the resulting
low records or dense prefixes are represented in the certified panel universe,
then the full \(n^{\rho_c}\polylog n\) theorem follows.
\Cref{cor:child-panel-single-profile-density-endpoint} sharpens the common
child-panel residual target further: after sponsor/generated-prefix and
low-correlation alternatives are removed, one split profile with
inverse-polylogarithmic sampled-center price is enough.
\Cref{cor:tuple-profile-compressed-bucket-storage}
gives the direct
low-correlation certificate for this target: first list moment plus two-point
Gaussian tuple-profile energy imply the needed occurrence moment, and the
shared-DAG distinct-net sum is smaller.
\Cref{cor:polylog-low-correlation-coload} instantiates that certificate at the
critical spherical threshold: pair correlations up to
\(O(\log\log m/\log m)\) contribute only a polylogarithmic factor, so any
polynomial storage obstruction must be in the complementary positive-correlation
branch.
\Cref{cor:low-high-compressed-cap-storage} packages the same fact directly for
compressed bucket nets: after \(K^{1+s}\le K^2\), the only unpaid occurrence
storage is the realized high-correlation ordered-pair tail.
\Cref{cor:diffuse-compressed-cap-rung} records the immediate endpoint of this
calculation: in random-position or otherwise pairwise-diffuse resident data,
the high tail vanishes and the compressed-cap rung satisfies the full
success-normalized checklist with only polylogarithmic overhead.
\Cref{cor:compressed-cap-high-tail-prefix-pricing} clips that tail by the
cap-centered paid degree; after prefix search, the only potentially polynomial
survivor is the overload \(H_{\rm over}\), which is the Hall/sponsor object
handled by the later overload machinery.
\Cref{cor:compressed-cap-high-tail-storage-only} makes this obstruction
statement quantitative: the paid clipped side either closes the rung or fires
quadratic same-prefix repairs whose lineage product is polylogarithmic.
\Cref{cor:compressed-cap-overload-hall-tail} makes that statement exact for
compressed buckets: \(H_{\rm over}\) is the excess of one cap-centered Hall cut,
and any failed transport contains a dyadic pure overload star whose weighted
occurrences are charged by one shared child price.
\Cref{cor:compressed-cap-overload-generated-column} then applies the generic
child-panel sponsor/generated-column screen with sponsor weights equal to the
positive excess \(O_x(y)\).  Thus a surviving compressed-cap overload is not a
new cap branch: it is an explicit dyadic generated-cover dual obstruction.
\Cref{cor:compressed-cap-overload-dual-low-cover-screen} converts that dual
obstruction into the same low-cover and packing endpoint used by the generic
child-panel branch: range/list/AQ/facility/tensor covers must be large unless a
positive generated prefix already exists.
\Cref{cor:compressed-cap-overload-packing-energy-endpoint} then applies the
second-moment packing screen directly to this compressed-cap residual: either a
bucket/list-decoding law pays the packing entropy, or the only excess is a
dyadic high-correlation star whose generated-record price blocks merging.
\Cref{cor:compressed-cap-overload-cap-star-storage-split} removes that last
star-specific branch: the nonmergeable high-correlation stars contribute a
bounded fixed tail plus a storage-dominated priced child panel for the generic
shared-cover/distinct-storage interfaces.
\Cref{cor:flattened-child-panel-closure} then removes the last accounting
ambiguity in this handoff: all storage-dominated panels reachable from such
returns may be included in one finite build-time closure LP, so a surviving
compressed-cap overload is represented by one no-prefix dual obstruction rather
than by an adaptive sequence of returned panels.
\Cref{cor:flattened-dual-panel-screen} is the corresponding separator
interface: any aggregate lower-certified capture panel against that one dual
hardens to a deterministic generated top prefix, so range/list/AQ/facility or
lattice proposals only have to prove positive panel surplus.
\Cref{cor:flattened-dual-dyadic-low-cover} removes the arbitrary weighting from
that target: a surviving flattened dual contains one dyadic heavy layer, and
any certified assigned cover of that layer must obey the explicit
cover-number/list-size lower bound \((FDY7)\)--\((FDY9)\).
\Cref{cor:flattened-dyadic-packing-witness} gives the corresponding metric
form: if generated-metric balls are materializable, a surviving layer contains a
separated packing at that same entropy scale.
\Cref{cor:flattened-dyadic-entropy-energy-handoff} feeds that packing into the
standard second-moment screen: either the spherical/list-decoding energy pays
the packing or an explicit high-correlation star is exposed for the dense
verifiers.
\Cref{cor:flattened-high-correlation-star-screen} puts that star back into the
flattened column-generation interface: it either gives a one-record
lower-certified panel, a bounded fixed tail, or a storage-dominated returned
child record for the closure LP.
\Cref{cor:budgeted-flattened-star-closure} records the scalar budget at this
last step: after prefix search, a high-correlation profile is paid by its low
part, bounded star tail, and returned-storage price, or that returned price is
the explicit residual handed to the closure/sponsor separator.
\Cref{cor:returned-star-sponsor-cut-normal-form} removes the ambiguity in that
handoff: the returned-storage residual is either paid by a sponsor flow, fires
a generated shared merge, or exposes one strong dyadic returned-star price
layer with an explicit generated-cover/list-size lower bound.
\Cref{cor:average-generated-record-returned-star-layer} is the proposal-facing
form of that layer: any tensor/range/AQ/facility/list-decoding proposal with
enough marginal hit per expected generated price is hardened to one positive
merge.
\Cref{cor:fractional-generated-cover-returned-star-layer} is the deterministic
LP form: a surviving layer has one dual-heavy sublayer on which every certified
low-price generated cover must be large.
\Cref{cor:returned-star-dual-packing-energy-handoff} pushes that sublayer
through the same packing, entropy-energy, and high-correlation star screen used
by the flattened and cap-overload duals, so the final returned-star obstruction
is an explicit star-price tail rather than an undefined branching process.
\Cref{cor:returned-star-tail-shared-cover-adapter} routes that tail back into
the same finite shared-cover LP interface: it is either paid at its
shared-canonical price or exposes a top-prefix dual obstruction inside the
flattened closure universe.
\Cref{cor:flattened-panel-separator-endpoint} packages this as the current
conditional endpoint for the overload storage branch: every flattened closure
must either be paid by its LP value or admit one such lower-capture panel; under
that condition the branch contributes no additional overhead.
\Cref{cor:weighted-polylog-low-correlation-coload} makes the same low branch
homogeneous in cap multiplicity: fractional or weighted cap panels obey the
same bound with the integer occurrence count replaced by total weight.  This is
the low-correlation companion to the weighted overload-storage handoff.
\Cref{cor:tiny-positive-cap-chain} records the matching radius fact for that
branch: a cap margin as small as \(K\log\log n/\log n\) still permits only
\(O_{K}(\log^2 n/\log\log n)\) consecutive recenterings inside the localized
polylog-radius ball.
\Cref{cor:quadratic-cap-margin-budget} gives the sharper accounting form:
the squared margins along any such lineage sum to only \(O(\log\log n)\), so a
positive-correlation repair that pays a local \(O(\gamma^2)\) toll has
polylogarithmic total cost even when there are many tiny-margin recenterings.
\Cref{cor:quadratic-positive-toll-compiler} packages this as the current
positive-correlation proof target: the endpoint no longer needs a bound on the
number of dense repairs, but it still needs a same-prefix dense/star or
shared-prefix repair with local loss \(\exp(O(\gamma^2))\) at margin \(\gamma\).
\Cref{cor:padded-radius-quadratic-reprice} and
\cref{cor:cap-centered-pair-star-reporter} isolate the geometric part of that
target: a high-correlation star is a cap-centered child of radius
\(R\sqrt{1-\gamma^2}\), and repricing the padded recursive potential from the
parent radius to this child costs only \(\exp(O(\gamma^2))\).  What remains is
therefore not another geometric depth issue, but the paid-prefix reduced-gain or
shared-prefix inequality inside that cap-centered child.
\Cref{cor:cap-centered-paid-prefix-quadratic} gives the explicit finite
criterion: a cap-centered paid prefix whose degree mass beats its
\(e^{O(\gamma^2)}\)-padded child price is already a quadratic local repair; if
no such prefix exists, every cap-centered paid superlevel satisfies the
weak-type envelope \((CPQ9)\).
\Cref{cor:high-correlation-stars-feed-cap-prefix} connects this criterion back
to the high-correlation layer-cake: whenever the reported star multiplicity is
dominated by the cap-centered paid degree, a large dyadic star either fires as a
quadratic repair or contributes only the cap-centered child price in
\((HCP5)\).  Thus positive-correlation mass is paid at the same cap-centered
scale that gives the quadratic radius toll.
\Cref{cor:clipped-cap-centered-high-correlation-handoff} removes the
all-or-nothing domination assumption from this statement: every
high-correlation layer splits into a cap-paid part, which satisfies the same
quadratic price envelope after clipping to \(d_x^+\), and an explicit overload
\(\sum_{x,p}(M_x(p)-d_x^+(p))_+\).
\Cref{cor:cap-centered-responsibility-prefix-compiler} gives the matching
positive certificate: any bounded-congestion assignment or transport of
high-correlation mass into cap-centered paid degrees is already a valid
same-prefix quadratic repair certificate.  The live obstruction is therefore
the untransported overload, not geometric branching through the star itself.
\Cref{lem:cap-centered-transport-hall} and
\cref{cor:cap-centered-overload-dichotomy} make that overload finite: either
the atom mass admits a bounded-congestion flow into cap-centered paid query
capacities, or one explicit Hall cut has more high-correlation atom mass than
its paid neighborhood plus the allowed tail.  This is the next geometric
separator target.
\Cref{cor:cap-centered-hall-overload-stars} compresses any such cut further:
after selecting one admissible center per atom, the excess appears as a single
dyadic cap-centered pure overload star where
\((B_x/C-d_x^+)_+\) has large layer-cake mass.  Thus the remaining separator
does not have to reason about arbitrary Hall set systems; it has to rule out or
repair these pointwise overload stars.
\Cref{cor:cap-centered-overload-weighted-storage} identifies the storage form
of such a star: if the selected weighted atoms are canonicalized to one shared
child, reciprocal weighted multiplicity charges exactly one child-storage price,
not one price per atom.  The overload branch therefore becomes a weighted
tuple-congestion theorem for shared canonical children, rather than an
integer-cohort materialization problem.
\Cref{cor:weighted-overload-cohort-correlation-split} composes this handoff
with the low-correlation cutoff: once canonical overload children carry a
Gaussian or list-decoding cap certificate in a fixed price class, their
price-weighted pair congestion splits into a proved polylogarithmic
low-correlation term and explicit cap-centered high-correlation stars.  Thus
the remaining overload theorem is no longer an integer-cohort or diffuse-pair
problem; it is the finite task of sending those high stars to the paid-prefix
verifier or to the shared-child tuple-congestion certificate.
\Cref{cor:overload-cohort-cap-prefix-tail} performs the paid-prefix part of
that task: in a no-repair residual, the high-correlation cohort congestion is
bounded by its explicit cap-centered overload plus a fixed tail
\(2mJ_{\rm pay}\Lambda\).  Thus any surviving polynomial high-cohort storage
obstruction must be concentrated in the same overload object already handled by
the Hall transport and weighted shared-storage machinery.
\Cref{cor:overload-cohort-tail-hall-cut} makes this identification exact:
after atomizing each high-cohort incidence as a singleton-center Hall atom,
\(\mathcal W_{\rm over}\) is precisely the Hall-cut excess of the overloaded
pairs.  Therefore a large \(\mathcal W_{\rm over}\) automatically supplies a
dyadic pure overload star, and after canonicalization that star is charged once
by the weighted reciprocal-multiplicity storage theorem.
\Cref{cor:hall-tail-overload-exact-storage} closes the bookkeeping for these
stars: reciprocal weighted multiplicity makes their pair-congestion witness
sum exactly equal to the total distinct child storage price.  Thus the remaining
Hall-tail theorem is not another materialization or pair-envelope problem; it is
the geometric bound on
\(\E_z\sum_{\kappa\in\mathcal C_z^{\rm tail}}u_{z,\kappa}\).
\Cref{cor:benefit-priced-hall-tail-materialization} gives the matching
build-time rule for this target: materialize only Hall-tail children whose
recursive price is sponsored by the Hall atom mass that exposed them.  Then
storage is paid by a bounded-overlap Hall-mass estimate; a surviving failure is
an explicit unsupported child with too little Hall mass per unit recursive
price.
\Cref{cor:disjoint-sponsored-hall-tail-schedule} records the overlap-one
implementation: reserve disjoint Hall-atom sponsor cohorts for retained
children.  The remaining geometric question is therefore whether this disjoint
sponsored schedule captures enough of the Hall-tail obstruction, or whether the
unreserved residue must feed a different dense/prefix repair.
\Cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-hall-cut} makes this question finite: either a
fractional sponsor flow pays every retained Hall-tail child from compatible
Hall atom mass, or one explicit child set has recursive price larger than
\(\beta\) times all compatible sponsor mass.  This is the new sharp residual
object for the Hall-tail storage branch.
\Cref{cor:sponsor-cut-generated-column-screen} connects that residual to the
ordinary generated-column machinery: a generated cell, range/list-decoded
container, additive-code bucket, or seeded cluster is useful exactly when its
top child-price prefix captures more cut price than its one-time retained
recursive price.  If no such prefix exists, every dyadic child-price layer in
the sponsor cut obeys the same metric-entropy lower bound as the no-cell
residual.  Thus the remaining geometric proof target is no longer another Hall
accounting statement; it is a low-price generated cover, or a spherical
separator, for strong sponsor-cut layers.
\Cref{cor:sponsor-cut-inflate-or-layer} removes weak failures from this target:
if all sponsor cuts are small relative to their child price, a constant
inflation \(\beta\mapsto\beta/(1-\varepsilon)\) restores the sponsor flow.
Otherwise one strong cut contains a single dyadic child-price layer carrying a
\(1/O(\log\operatorname{range})\) fraction of the cut price, and this is the
only layer that the generated-cover or spherical separator must attack.
\Cref{cor:strong-sponsor-layer-generated-entropy} gives the numerical
threshold for that attack: a generated cover whose Renyi price is below the
exposed layer mass immediately produces a positive top-prefix column.  If no
column appears and the storage term is not already dominant, the layer's
certified generated-cover number is bounded below by the explicit
\((SGE5)\) entropy expression, in terms of the sponsor-cut excess.
\Cref{cor:low-doubling-sponsor-layer-close} rewrites this as a
dimension-density screen: a low-doubling, range-reporting, additive-code, or
list-decoded cover closes the sponsor layer whenever its growth exponent makes
\((SGD2)\) or the cut-excess form \((SGD3)\) hold.  A surviving non-storage
layer therefore has an explicit generated-dimension lower bound \((SGD5)\).
\Cref{cor:sponsor-layer-packing-witness} turns that lower bound into the
geometric object needed by the spherical branch: for any certified generated
metric, a surviving layer contains a separated packing of the same entropy
scale.  \Cref{cor:sponsor-packing-spherical-energy-screen} then applies the
ordinary second-moment entropy-energy test to representatives of that packing,
and \cref{cor:sponsor-profile-star-signal} gives the contrapositive handoff:
any weighted profile not paid by the low-correlation energy bound contains a
dyadic high-correlation sponsor star.  The remaining sponsor obstruction is
therefore no longer an unnamed high-entropy layer; it is a finite family of
star superlevels for the generated-column, dense-star, and shared-prefix
verifiers.
\Cref{cor:generated-sponsor-star-envelope} feeds those superlevels back into
the sponsor-cut column generator: if a star's layer-price mass beats its
one-time generated price, it fires immediately; if none fires, the whole
high-correlation profile is bounded by the integrated generated-price envelope
\((GSE3)\)--\((GSE5)\).
\Cref{cor:no-column-sponsor-star-price-gap} sharpens this envelope locally:
after generated-column search, no medium-cardinality sponsor star survives.
Every remaining high-correlation star is either in the bounded-cardinality
sublinear branch \(h\le H_-\), or, when \(\zeta>0\), in the storage-dominated
large-star branch \(h\ge H_+\).
\Cref{cor:balanced-sponsor-star-scalar-gate} identifies the only way this
forbidden window can disappear: the balanced scalar price
\(A^\rho\zeta^{1-\rho}\) is already at the capture scale.  Otherwise a medium
star is automatically a generated column, and the geometric residual is split
cleanly into the small-star and large-storage tails.
\Cref{cor:bounded-sponsor-stars-fixed-tail} closes the small-star side up to an
explicit fixed tail: if no large storage-dominated star has dyadic scale above
\(\Lambda_+\), then \(W_{\rm hi}\) is at most
\(2|E|J_\omega\max\{\omega_{\max}H_-,\Lambda_+\}\).  More sharply,
\cref{cor:storage-dominated-sponsor-stars-fractional-tail} removes the need to
select a single large star: every storage-dominated superlevel contributes to
one integrated fractional storage tail
\(\sum_s\psi_\star\zeta\,t_s h_s^{1+\rho}\), while the bounded-cardinality
part remains the fixed tail \(2|E|J_\omega\omega_{\max}H_-\).  Thus the live
sponsor-star target is a distinct-storage certificate for these fractional
star children, not another dense-branching materialization rule.
\Cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-shared-cover-compiler} abstracts the finite
object used from here on: any priced fractional child panel may be attacked by
one shared-cover LP, generated top-prefix columns, and a single no-prefix dual
residual.
\Cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-low-cover-screen} abstracts the next step as
well: any no-prefix child-panel residual with a low-price generated cover would
already have a positive prefix, so a surviving non-storage-dominated layer has
large generated-cover entropy and, in any certified generated metric, a
separated packing witness.
\Cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-packing-energy-screen} abstracts the
second-moment endpoint for that witness: a bucket or list-decoding law either
pays the separated child-panel packing by profile entropy-energy, or one
energy-deficient profile becomes the high-correlation signal returned to the
prefix machinery.
\Cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-high-correlation-return} abstracts that
return path too: a high-correlation profile either contains a positive
generated shared-cover prefix, or its dyadic cap stars are charged by the
integrated generated-price envelope.
\Cref{cor:fractional-child-panel-cap-star-storage-split} closes the returned
cap-star loop generically: after generated-prefix search, no medium returned
star survives, and the remaining high-correlation mass is a bounded fixed tail
plus a storage-dominated priced child panel that reuses the same shared-cover
and distinct-storage interfaces.
\Cref{cor:flattened-child-panel-closure} flattens all such returned
storage-dominated panels into one finite generated-cover closure.  Thus heavy
build-time search can enumerate the reachable returned records, solve one LP,
and either pay them collectively or expose a single exact no-prefix dual for
the geometric/list-decoding separator.
\Cref{cor:flattened-dual-panel-screen} gives the proposal-facing form of that
