separator: a weighted panel of lower-certified generated captures either obeys
the closure dual budget or produces one positive top-prefix record in the
flattened universe.
\Cref{cor:flattened-dual-dyadic-low-cover} then extracts a single almost-uniform
dual layer from any surviving flattened obstruction; on that layer, low-cover,
low-doubling, range-reporting, AQ, facility, lattice, or list-decoding proposals
must satisfy the precise lower bound \((FDY7)\), unless a positive generated
prefix is already present.
\Cref{cor:flattened-dyadic-packing-witness} converts the same lower bound into
a separated packing witness whenever the proposal geometry supplies
materializable generated balls, which is the input expected by the
spherical/list-decoding energy screens.
\Cref{cor:flattened-dyadic-entropy-energy-handoff} records the exact endpoint
of that handoff: low cover, entropy-energy payment, or one returned
high-correlation star.
\Cref{cor:flattened-high-correlation-star-screen} normalizes the returned star:
positive scale is already a lower-certified generated prefix, while failed
stars contribute only a bounded tail plus storage-dominated child records for
the flattened closure.
\Cref{cor:budgeted-flattened-star-closure} gives the exact arithmetic form:
any remaining unpaid high-correlation profile certifies proportional
returned-storage price, instead of opening another recursive branch.
\Cref{cor:returned-star-sponsor-cut-normal-form} then applies the sponsor-cut
dichotomy directly to that price: weak cuts pay it after constant inflation,
while strong cuts feed the ordinary generated-column and packing screens.
\Cref{cor:average-generated-record-returned-star-layer} and
\cref{cor:fractional-generated-cover-returned-star-layer} convert those strong
cuts into the final finite separator target: prove a proposal law with
normalized marginal hit beating expected generated price, or rule out the
resulting dyadic dual-heavy low-cover obstruction.
\Cref{cor:returned-star-dual-packing-energy-handoff} gives the next reduction of
that obstruction: materializable generated balls yield a separated packing,
entropy-energy pays low-correlation profiles, and any high-correlation survivor
is a finite star whose price either violates the returned-star dual or becomes
an explicit bounded/storage tail.
\Cref{cor:returned-star-tail-shared-cover-adapter} then prevents that tail from
starting a new recursion: after adding its records to the build-time closure, it
is handled by the same shared-cover value/top-prefix dual dichotomy as the
original returned panel.
\Cref{cor:flattened-panel-separator-endpoint} turns this interface into the
nodewise endpoint: if every flattened returned panel is either LP-paid or
panel-separated, then the remaining child-panel residuals satisfy the positive
shared-panel separator and hence the polylogarithmic bounds.
\Cref{cor:generic-child-panel-pair-witness-storage} gives the exact storage
identity for that generic child panel: distribute each stored child's price over
ordered separated pairs in its witness set, with reciprocal weighted
multiplicity when many decoded records point to the same child.  The remaining
storage theorem is therefore a direct pair-profile congestion/list-decoding
bound in child-panel notation, not a bucket-net-specific accounting statement.
\Cref{cor:generic-child-panel-sponsor-flow} then states the exact positive
condition under which that pair-congestion storage is paid by exposed Hall,
guard, or detector atom mass: a fractional sponsor flow is equivalent to all
child-price Hall cuts being affordable.  \Cref{lem:unsponsored-child-panel-obstruction}
is the corresponding warning.  Pair geometry alone cannot bound storage,
because arbitrarily many unsponsored canonical children may have the same
witness set and identical pair profiles.  The live theorem must therefore
produce sponsor mass, a shared generated merge, or a dense/spherical separator
for every unsponsored child-price cut.
\Cref{cor:generic-unsponsored-cut-generated-column} is the corresponding
cut-local normal form: if all cuts are only weakly unsupported, a constant
inflation of the sponsor parameter closes them; otherwise a strong cut exposes
one dyadic child-price layer.  A generated template whose top prefix captures
more layer price than its one-time recursive cost is an immediate positive
merge.  If no such merge exists, that layer has the explicit generated-cover
entropy lower bound \((UCG12)\) unless it is already storage-dominated.  This
is the precise input expected from range-reporting, additive-quantization,
facility, lattice, or list-decoding separators.
\Cref{cor:generic-unsponsored-cut-packing-energy} continues the same
cut-local residual without returning to hard branching: once balls in a
certified generated metric are themselves generated template parts, a strong
no-merge layer contains a large separated packing.  Any bucket, spherical, code,
or list-decoding law then either pays that packing by the profile
second-moment energy, or a dyadic high-correlation star is exposed and sent
back to the generated-merge/dense-prefix verifier.  Thus the unsponsored
storage obstruction has the same terminal object as the generic child-panel
packing residual, rather than a separate materialization problem.
\Cref{cor:unsponsored-cut-low-correlation-cap-closure} instantiates this
terminal object for large-range centered Gaussian caps: an exposed packing's
first list moment and all pairs with correlation
\(O(\log\log m/\log m)\) are automatically bounded by
\(m^{1+\rho}\operatorname{polylog}m\).  Therefore a polynomial unsponsored-cut
cap-panel residual cannot hide in diffuse low-correlation co-load; it must
contain one dyadic high-correlation cap star, which is exactly the finite
object already routed to generated-merge and dense-prefix tests.
\Cref{cor:unsponsored-cut-cap-prefix-tail} performs that routing at the
cap-centered paid-prefix scale.  After clipping the exposed high-correlation
cap-panel weights by the local paid degree, the paid part either fires a
same-prefix quadratic repair or contributes only a fixed dyadic tail.  The only
potentially polynomial survivor is the explicit overload
\((\omega_{g,g'}-d_g^+(g'))_+\), so the unsponsored-cut cap branch rejoins the
Hall/sponsor-flow and shared-child storage interfaces instead of spawning a new
high-correlation recursion.
\Cref{cor:unsponsored-cap-overload-hall-tail} makes that rejoining formal in
the unsponsored notation.  The overloaded cap incidences form singleton-center
Hall atoms whose cut excess is exactly \(W_{\rm over}\); any positive tail
therefore contains a dyadic cap-centered pure overload star, and after
canonicalization reciprocal weighted multiplicity charges one shared child
price.  The residual is now a priced child-panel sponsor/generated-column
problem, not another cap-star materialization branch.
\Cref{cor:unsponsored-cap-overload-generated-column} spells out the resulting
normal form for those canonical overload children: a fractional sponsor flow
pays their shared storage, or a generated top prefix merges a strong
child-price cut, or one dyadic layer survives with an explicit generated-cover
entropy lower bound.  The remaining separator target is therefore a
range/list/AQ/facility cover theorem for that one layer.
\Cref{cor:average-generated-cell-cap-overload} gives the proposal-law version
of the same target.  Any randomized generated cell law whose layer hit mass
beats twice its expected one-time price contains a deterministic positive
generated merge; hence a surviving strong layer forces an average
Renyi/list-size lower bound for every tensor, range-reporting, AQ, facility, or
list-decoding proposal law that covers the layer with nontrivial marginal
probability.
\Cref{cor:fractional-generated-cover-cap-overload} removes the sampling
notation altogether: if a finite generated-record family fractionally covers
the exposed layer below half its cut mass, one record has positive reduced cost.
Failure exposes a single dual weight \(y_\kappa\) on the layer for which every
generated record captures at most its certified price.  This is the exact
weighted range/list-decoding obstruction left by cap overload.
\Cref{cor:cap-overload-dual-low-cover-screen} then dyadically unweights that
obstruction: any dual-heavy layer with a certified low-Renyi-price generated
cover would violate the same dual constraint and hence fire a positive prefix.
The remaining cap-overload separator is therefore a high generated-cover entropy
layer, modulo the explicit storage-dominated term.
\Cref{cor:cap-overload-dual-centered-cap-endpoint} feeds that weighted layer into
the centered Gaussian cap endpoint.  Once a certified generated metric supplies
balls, the dual-heavy layer contains a separated packing; centered cap panels pay
the one-point and low-correlation two-point mass polylogarithmically, so any
excess must expose a dyadic high-correlation cap star.  Such a star is already a
positive generated prefix whenever its certified record price is below its dual
mass.
\Cref{cor:cap-overload-dual-cap-star-storage-split} applies the same scalar gate
to these returned cap-overload stars.  After generated-prefix search, no
medium-cardinality high-correlation star survives: the return is a bounded fixed
tail plus a storage-dominated priced child panel with dyadic intensity absorbed
into its price.  This sends the cap-overload high-correlation branch back to the
generic shared-cover and distinct-storage interfaces.
\Cref{cor:cap-overload-storage-tail-shared-cover} makes that routing explicit:
the storage-dominated overload stars have one finite shared-cover LP, one exact
dual, and the same generated top-prefix column rule as the sponsor-tail
pipeline.
\Cref{cor:cap-overload-storage-tail-generated-cover} then gives the matching
generated-cover handoff: a failed cover exposes one dual-heavy layer, and any
low-cover certified generated metric yields the same separated packing witness
as the generic child-panel residual.
\Cref{cor:cap-overload-storage-tail-packing-energy} feeds that packing into the
common entropy-energy endpoint: an unpaid high-correlation profile either fires
a generated prefix or returns only a bounded fixed tail plus another priced
child panel.
\Cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-shared-cover} then removes duplicated large
stars from that target by a finite shared-cover LP: either residual fractional
star copies plus shared records have total price inside the storage allowance,
or the LP dual gives one weighting \(y_s\le u_s^{\rm frac}\) that every
retained shared record fails to capture above its price.
\Cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-generated-prefix} gives the verifier-facing
form of this dual: a generated range/list/AQ/facility template is useful exactly
when its current \(y_s\)-weighted top prefix beats its certified shared-child
price; otherwise the template satisfies the same weak-type envelope as the
earlier shared-capture residuals.
\Cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-generated-cover-dichotomy} makes this a
single finite generated-cover alternative: generated prefixes either cover the
fractional sponsor tail within the storage allowance, or one dual \(y_s\) fails
all top-prefix tests in the chosen generated family.  Then
\cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-low-cover-closure} and
\cref{cor:low-doubling-fractional-sponsor-tail-screen} show that any
dual-heavy layer with a low-Renyi-price generated cover would already fire as a
shared-cover column.  The live fractional-tail residual is therefore the same
generated entropy/list-decoding obstruction as the earlier dyadic shared-cover
residual, not a separate large-star materialization problem.
\Cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-packing-witness} turns that entropy
obstruction into a separated packing in any certified generated metric, and
\cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-packing-energy-screen} is the corresponding
sponsor-tail specialization of the generic second-moment test.  Thus the
fractional sponsor-tail branch now terminates at the same low-correlation
energy versus high-correlation dense-star signal as the non-storage sponsor
layers.
\Cref{cor:fractional-sponsor-tail-high-correlation-return} makes the return
path explicit in the sponsor-tail notation: every energy-deficient
high-correlation profile either contains a generated shared-cover prefix with
positive reduced cost, or its dyadic cap stars are bounded by the integrated
generated-price envelope.  This closes the formal loop between the fractional
large-star tail and the existing generated-prefix verifier.
\Cref{cor:fractional-tail-cap-star-price-gap} applies the same scalar gate to
those returned cap stars in the sponsor-tail notation: no medium cardinality
survives generated-prefix search, and the remaining high-correlation return is
only a bounded fixed tail plus a storage-dominated fractional subtail.  Thus
the fractional-tail high-correlation loop has the same normal form as the
original sponsor-star loop.
\Cref{cor:fractional-tail-cap-star-storage-interface} routes that
storage-dominated cap-star subtail into the same generic child-panel interface
as the fractional sponsor tail, after absorbing the dyadic cap intensity into
the child price factor.  The returned
high-correlation branch therefore rejoins the existing shared-canonical
distinct-storage target rather than introducing a cap-specific recursion.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net} rewrites that target as a dyadic
large-child counting problem: for every recursive price scale, bound the number
of distinct canonical bucket nets whose shared child index has that price.
\Cref{cor:layer-cake-distinct-storage-bucket-net} and
\cref{cor:integrated-tuple-tail-distinct-storage} remove this dyadic
discretization when a geometric proof can bound the integrated tail directly.
\Cref{cor:price-weighted-witness-packing-storage} removes the tail parameter
altogether: each distinct child may choose a randomized tuple witness, and the
storage theorem becomes a bound on price-weighted witness congestion.
\Cref{cor:uniform-tuple-witness-packing-storage} gives the canonical choice for
bucket nets: sample a uniform tuple from the child itself.  In the pair case this
reduces the remaining theorem to bounding distinct-child pair congestion weighted
by \(\psi |A|^{\rho-1}\le\psi\).
\Cref{cor:reciprocal-multiplicity-pair-congestion} is the resulting simplest
pair form: after the query first moment is paid, it is enough to bound, for each
separated pair, the expected sum of child price factors over decoded occurrences
whose canonical child contains the pair, with each occurrence divided by the
child's multiplicity.
\Cref{cor:occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage} gives the tuple-order version of
the same decoder statistic.
\Cref{cor:pair-profile-occurrence-discounted-storage} is the finite
entropy-energy check for that statistic; it is now enough to show that each pair
profile has small discounted congestion \(B_\pi\), with
\(\sum_\pi N_\pi B_\pi\) inside the storage budget.
\Cref{cor:multiplicity-layer-pair-profile-storage} refines this into a
high-multiplicity-or-high-energy target: after dyadic multiplicity
stratification, layer \(\ell\) receives a \(2^{-\ell}\) quotient discount.
\Cref{cor:aggregate-multiplicity-profile-storage} is the sharpest current
storage certificate: prove the discounted aggregate entropy-energy sum over
profile layers, without first proving a uniform bound for every pair in the
profile.
\Cref{cor:gaussian-aggregate-profile-layer-storage} turns the Gaussian-cap
instance of this target into the explicit inequality
\[
   \sum_{\pi,\ell}2^{-\ell}
   C_{\pi,\ell}\exp\!\left(
      H_{\pi,\ell}
      -\frac{\beta_{\pi,\ell}^2}{1+\theta_{\pi,\ell}}
   \right)
   \le aS
\]
up to metadata, where \(H\) is weighted incidence entropy, \(\beta\) is the
shifted-threshold margin, and \(\theta\) is the worst pair correlation.
\Cref{lem:high-correlation-pair-star-reporter} adds the matching dense
alternative: if a profile layer has large weighted incidence on pairs with
correlation at least \(\underline\theta\), then some dyadic star superlevel lies
inside a ball of radius \(\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)}\) and carries incidence
at least the average layer mass up to a logarithmic dynamic-range factor.
\Cref{cor:correlation-split-gaussian-profile-layer} packages the actual
worst-case split: low-correlation edges are paid by the Gaussian
entropy-energy term, while the high-correlation part is either below a chosen
star scale or exposes a smaller-radius star proposal for the dense verifier.
\Cref{cor:correlation-split-fixed-threshold-star-screen} makes that proposal
threshold noncircular: once the star scale beats its recursive guard-credit
price, excessive high-correlation profile incidence
forces a one-record dense repair; otherwise the high-correlation contribution
is charged by the fixed tail \(2|P|J_{\rm hi}\Lambda_0\).
\Cref{cor:aggregate-correlation-split-fixed-tail-storage} feeds these local
screens back into the storage compiler: if no profile layer fires its dense
repair, the discounted aggregate storage sum uses the low-correlation Gaussian
envelope plus the fixed high-correlation tails.
\Cref{cor:noncircular-fixed-tail-scale-choice} removes the last circular scale
choice by setting \(\Lambda_i^\circ=2R_i\), so the tail becomes the explicit
quantity \(4|P|J_i^{\rm hi}R_i\).
\Cref{cor:reciprocal-multiplicity-fixed-tail-storage} is the compressed-bucket
endpoint form of this statement: reciprocal occurrence multiplicity supplies the
\(2^{-\ell}\) layer discount, low-correlation layers are paid by Gaussian
entropy-energy, and any unpaid high-correlation layer must expose a verified
smaller-radius dense/star repair.
\Cref{cor:local-entropy-slack-reciprocal-storage} removes the need for a global
aggregate calculation when the active profile set is polylogarithmic: each
low-correlation layer only needs the local entropy slack \((LES2)\), and each
high-correlation layer only needs its fixed tail to fit its local budget.
\Cref{cor:profile-entropy-local-storage-screen} replaces the raw
low-correlation weight in that slack by a profile-count term whenever the
spread-packing entropy-energy inequality holds profile-by-profile, so a
polylogarithmic subprofile family costs only another \(O(\log\log n)\) energy
margin.
\Cref{cor:entropy-deficit-tail-local-storage-screen} records the sharper
tail form: a few mildly bad profiles are harmless if the dyadic sum of
\(W_h e^{-I_h}\) over all low-correlation profiles still fits the local budget.
\Cref{cor:positive-moment-entropy-deficit-screen} converts this into the
positive-moment form that a tensorized spherical, lattice, or range/list-decoder
estimate is more likely to prove directly.
\Cref{cor:renyi-moment-entropy-deficit-screen} removes the auxiliary cutoff and
makes the target a single Renyi list-size moment for each active layer.
\Cref{cor:near-first-moment-entropy-deficit-screen} sharpens this again: with
the exponent \(1+1/\log H_i\), the \(H_i\)-factor in the optimized bound is
constant, so polylogarithmically many profiles do not require an additional
\(\log H_i\) energy margin.
\Cref{cor:variational-near-first-moment-obstruction} gives the exact dual
object left by failure: a Gibbs-weighted profile law whose entropy plus average
weight beats its average Gaussian energy after the multiplicity discount.
\Cref{cor:gibbs-water-level-storage-screen} packages the same object as a
water-level test, so a build-time separator can focus on one weighted law per
failing layer.
\Cref{cor:gibbs-weighted-guard-repair} then removes a possible ambiguity in
using that law: Gibbs weighting is only an analysis distribution over proposed
repairs, while the retained index receives a single verified positive
guard-credit record.
\Cref{cor:partition-local-gibbs-residual} adds the class-local form: a failing
layer has a failing partition cell unless all cells pass with the displayed
\(J^{1/p}\) discount, and a positive cell-local proposal still hardens to one
guard-credit record.
\Cref{cor:count-energy-cell-screen} is the reporter-facing bounded-range
version: if a cell's \(d=\log W-I\) values are nearly flat, water level is
equivalent up to that range to a max-plus-count entropy-energy statistic.
\Cref{cor:singleton-profile-gibbs-residual} records the resulting endpoint for
polylogarithmic refinements: one bad profile must either feed the guard-credit
verifier or be ruled out by the spread-packing entropy-energy estimate.
\Cref{cor:singleton-spread-star-repair} makes this endpoint quantitative: after
the high-correlation star layer-cake is reported, absence of a guard repair
forces \(X_h\) below the threshold whenever \(L_h+2\sum R_b\) fits that
threshold.
\Cref{cor:partition-cell-spread-star-repair} lifts the same statement back to
coarser reporter cells, replacing singleton profile accounting by a class
\(\ell_p\) certificate and the partition-count toll \(J^{1/p}\).
\Cref{cor:shared-record-partition-cell-compiler} connects that cell certificate
to shared dense records: a record helping many profiles contributes through its
profile-allocation \(\ell_p\) norm but pays one recursive price.
\Cref{cor:aggregate-shared-cell-water-budget} then replaces per-cell uniform
thresholds by one layer-level \(\ell_p\) budget for those certified costs.
\Cref{cor:layer-global-shared-record-water} is the cross-cell version: a
record shared by several reporter cells is charged through one layer-global
allocation norm, so partitions remain only a certification device.
\Cref{cor:no-discount-layer-global-water} then prevents a false optimization
target: once positive guard-credit records are absent, the optimal global
allocation value is exactly the Gibbs water level.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-top-prefix-water-screen} converts any remaining water failure
into one sorted dyadic top-prefix excess, the form most compatible with exact
prefix, range-reporting, list-decoding, and facility proposal oracles.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-prefix-spread-star-repair} then states the corresponding
repair interface: each such prefix either satisfies the existing spread-star
price test, fires one lower-certified guard record, or remains as a concrete
prefix-price overflow.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-prefix-low-price-residual} splits that overflow with an
arbitrary slack parameter, leaving only the low-envelope branch and the
recursive star-price branch.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-prefix-high-star-mass} refines the latter: under a controlled
low envelope, the recursive-price branch is backed by large certified star
mass, so shared-prefix and integrated-cover reporters can be scored against
actual paid mass rather than against price alone.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-prefix-shared-capture-compression} gives the corresponding
score: shared records may capture many original star records, but a no-repair
residual must have explicit tail plus one-time shared price at least the forced
dyadic high-star mass.
\Cref{cor:finite-dyadic-shared-capture-lp} is the exact finite-dual form of
that residual, with a positive-dual-surplus shared record as the build-time
oracle target.
\Cref{cor:one-sided-dyadic-shared-capture-oracle} and
\cref{cor:dyadic-shared-capture-top-prefix-compiler} specialize the target to
certified top prefixes inside generated cells.
\Cref{cor:generated-cell-dyadic-shared-cover-dichotomy} packages any finite
cell family as an exact generated-cover LP, so a surviving residual has one
dual whose top-prefix envelope fails nowhere in that family.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-dual-mass-low-cover-closure} shows that this dual cannot put
large \(X_bu_b\)-mass on a set with a low-price generated-cell cover.
\Cref{cor:no-cell-dual-entropy-witness} extracts a dyadic superlevel from any
large such mass and lower-bounds its compatible cover number, unless the
storage term in the generated-cell price already accounts for the mass.
\Cref{cor:no-cell-metric-cover-screen} turns any certified metric, range, AQ,
or list-decoded cover of that superlevel into the compatible generated-cell
cover required by the dual-mass test.
\Cref{cor:low-doubling-no-cell-density-screen} rewrites that test as a
dimension-sensitive density envelope for the exposed dyadic layer.
\Cref{lem:star-superlevel-column-verifier} and
\cref{cor:pair-star-dense-column-generator} turn such a superlevel into an
ordinary fractional-cover column by using the certified query activation
\(\|q-x\|\le\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)}+r\); failure of every such column is
the explicit no-star reduced-gain inequality \((PSG4)\).
\Cref{lem:star-prefix-weak-type-residual} and
\cref{cor:pair-star-weak-type-normal-form} replace exact reported stars by the
best dual-price prefix in the same certified ball; if no prefix is profitable,
every reported star has paid near-pair mass bounded by the query/storage
Renyi envelope \((PWN3)\).
\Cref{lem:certified-star-panel-separator} and
\cref{cor:paid-pair-star-panel-certificate} are the matching one-sided reporter
interface: a range-reporting, clustering, AQ, or list-decoding routine may
return a whole panel of stars with lower paid-mass certificates and upper size
certificates; a strict aggregate surplus is enough for the finite verifier to
retain one positive prefix.
\Cref{cor:spherical-star-panel-local-cover} packages this as a local theorem
target: every surplus dual that survives the spherical reduced-gain test must
admit such a certified panel, otherwise the finite LP cover is already feasible.
\Cref{cor:hit-weighted-star-panel-prefix} gives the paid-prefix normalization of
that target: a panel certified against \(\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}\) is already a
finite-prefix separator witness, so the star-panel and paid-prefix endpoints
share the same remaining reporter theorem.
\Cref{cor:guarded-star-panel-local-cover} is the current sharp local target:
the reporter only has to work on normalized residuals with unit primitive hit
mass, below-budget price, large guard co-load, and no profitable primitive
singleton slice.
\Cref{cor:guarded-no-star-residual-envelope} is its exact negation in reporter
language: if this target fails, every certified star container has only the
Renyi amount of hit-weighted paid mass at every degree superlevel.
\Cref{cor:guard-shadow-transport-reporter} isolates the bridge still missing
from geometry: a bounded-congestion shipment of the large guard co-load into
that paid shadow would contradict the no-star envelope.
In this guard-shadow route the certified container itself is submitted as the
hit-weighted star record, so a successful transport pays no dyadic
dynamic-range loss.
\Cref{lem:guard-shadow-cut-normal-form} and
\cref{cor:half-mass-guard-shadow-cut-obstruction} turn failure of that shipment
into a concrete cut: a high-price query sublayer with large guard load and
small paid near shadow inside the tested container.
\Cref{lem:guard-shadow-credit-normal-form} and
\cref{cor:half-mass-guard-shadow-deficit-obstruction} remove the all-subsets
language from the same obstruction: a surviving residual defeats every
fractional assignment of paid near-shadow capacity to guard-load demand, leaving
more than half of the guard load uncredited.
\Cref{cor:fractional-guard-credit-panel-reporter} and
\cref{cor:joint-fractional-guard-credit-cover} are the panel version needed for
the dense-overlap program: many proposed dense containers may jointly receive a
fractional guard-credit flow, and only their verified local recursive costs are
charged.
\Cref{cor:finite-guard-credit-flow-separator} turns that into the finite
column-generation target for practical proposal families: if the generated pool
contains a positive guard-credit LP solution, the ordinary star-panel verifier
closes the residual.
\Cref{lem:finite-guard-credit-flow-dual} gives the corresponding oracle state
when the current generated pool fails: a zero-mass guard-demand price and
per-template capacity prices blocking every candidate edge.
\Cref{cor:one-template-guard-credit-separation} eliminates that per-template
block for a new proposal: in the normalized zero-price obstruction, the only
quantity to report is the paid-shadow mass reachable from positive guard-load
queries, compared with the recursive price \(R_B\).
\Cref{cor:scale-free-guard-credit-proposal} further says that exact mass-scale
guessing is unnecessary; a raw container proposal law is useful exactly through
the averaged direct surplus \(D-R\).
\Cref{cor:lower-certified-scale-free-guard-panel} gives the implementation
version of the same target: a panel of containers with certified lower masses
\(X_i\) closes the residual when \(\sum_i\lambda_i(X_i-R_i)>0\).
\Cref{cor:high-correlation-stars-feed-guard-credit} shows how a high-correlation
pair-star panel supplies those \(X_i\)'s: the only extra certificate is the
pointwise domination of the reported star multiplicity by paid near-shadow
degree inside the proposed smaller-radius container.
\Cref{cor:paid-responsibility-high-correlation-star} supplies a canonical way
to get that certificate: build the multiplicities from responsibility weights
\(\eta_{x,p,q}y_q\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}\), supported only on certified
high-correlation pairs.
\Cref{cor:pair-compatible-guard-responsibility-star} is the equivalent
guard-load form: pair-compatible high-correlation transport of mass \(M\)
produces responsibility mass \(M/C\).
\Cref{lem:pair-compatible-guard-cut-normal-form} makes the failure certificate
finite and explicit: a subset of guard incidences whose high-correlation
neighbors have insufficient paid pair capacity.
\Cref{cor:geometric-hall-pair-compatible-guard} removes the graph notation from
that certificate and identifies the bad object as a high-load guard sublayer
with small paid near-pair neighborhood.
\Cref{lem:fractional-pair-compatible-hall-obstruction} gives the matching
fractional LP for this bad object, with explicit variables for guard incidences
and their paid-neighborhood closure and no integrality loss.
\Cref{cor:exact-load-pair-compatible-hall-profile} reduces the same bad object
to an exact-load lower convex envelope over ordinary guard sublayers, which is
the build-time profile a proposal oracle must separate.
\Cref{cor:integral-hall-deficit-normal-form} shows that a strict profile deficit
already contains one integral positive-excess sublayer.
\Cref{cor:hall-profile-repair-guarded-cover} records the accepted separation
format for that profile: a lower-hull Hall deficit is useful only after a
verified guard-credit repair panel beats its recursive price on the loaded
queries.
\Cref{cor:proposal-law-hall-profile-repair} is the operational version: a finite
proposal law may search with any heuristic or expensive preprocessing, but only
its certified positive loaded-query surplus is retained by the proof.
\Cref{cor:lower-hull-hall-proposal-separator} identifies the sharp remaining
geometric obligation: convert every strict lower-hull Hall deficit into such a
positive proposal law.
\Cref{cor:deficit-restricted-proposal-law} further restricts this obligation to
the paid shadow of the one positive-excess sublayer.
\Cref{cor:deficient-shadow-prefix-certificate} is the concrete separator form:
find one top deficient-shadow prefix whose certified mass beats its inherited
recursive price.
\Cref{cor:transported-deficient-shadow-certificate} is the transport-facing
variant: a bounded-congestion shipment into one certified subset gives the same
lower mass certificate without exposing all deficient-shadow degrees.
\Cref{lem:restricted-deficient-shadow-transport-cut} is its one-subset
max-flow/min-cut normal form and turns failed shipment into a localized
deficient-shadow Hall cut.
\Cref{cor:flow-value-deficient-shadow-screen} packages this verifier view:
every proposed subset and congestion scale must have nonpositive flow-value
surplus in a surviving all-loaded residual.
\Cref{lem:infinitesimal-flow-deficient-shadow} then collapses the unrestricted
congestion parameter: for a fixed subset, the largest normalized flow value is
exactly the subset's deficient-shadow mass.  Consequently
\cref{cor:flow-value-shadow-mass-equivalence} says that the max-flow endpoint is
equivalent to finding one certified subset with deficient-shadow mass above its
recursive price; flow is only a lower-certification mechanism.
\Cref{cor:deficient-shadow-finite-prefix-normal-form},
\cref{cor:finite-prefix-hall-deficit-oracle}, and
\cref{cor:query-layer-deficient-shadow-residual-obstruction} state the sharper
residual if the finite-prefix search fails: the positive-excess Hall sublayer
must satisfy the query-layer envelope \((QLDS2)\) on every searched affordable
prefix.  The older no-prefix residual
\cref{cor:deficient-shadow-residual-obstruction} is recovered by setting
\(y\equiv1\).
\Cref{cor:query-layer-random-list-deficient-shadow-repair} gives the matching
proposal-law criterion for this sharper residual: positive expected surplus of
a random list or marginal center law rules out \((QLDS2)\), and the verifier
keeps only a deterministic query layer and prefix.
\Cref{cor:query-free-deficient-shadow-list-gain} is the operational scoring
form of the same statement: the proposal routine returns only a list or soft
support, while the proof chooses the profitable query layer by thresholding the
hinge \(h(q)-\psi K^\rho\widehat\tau_q\).
\Cref{cor:price-compatible-query-free-refinement} identifies the only safe
way to split such a list into compact pieces: the radius/potential decrease of
the pieces must make \(\sum_i\psi_iK_i^\rho\) and
\(\sum_i\psi_iK_i^{1+\rho}\) fit under the parent query and storage prices.
Under that condition one refined piece has positive gain, so compactification
is a theorem rather than a heuristic.
\Cref{cor:bounded-fanout-radius-discount-refinement} makes this check
geometric: if \(J\) refined balls all reduce the padded radius potential by
at least \(J^{1-\rho}\), the price compatibility follows automatically.  This
is the exact fanout-versus-contraction inequality that a \(k\)-means, facility,
or range-reporting ball decomposition must certify.
\Cref{cor:renyi-spread-hall-shadow-obstruction} is the stronger
distribution-sensitive version: if a proposed refinement does not contain a
positive child, then the normalized child sizes \(z_i\) must satisfy
\(\sum_i z_i^\rho>\Psi(R)/\Psi(R_\star)\).  Thus the right clustering objective
is not just small fanout but small Renyi-effective fanout after radius
discounting.
\Cref{cor:renyi-cover-hall-shadow-closure} gives the corresponding positive
assigned-cover theorem: an overlapping cover may be used with any assignment
whose radius-discounted Renyi query price and storage price fit below the
parent.  The metric-entropy test is only the balanced Hölder corollary of this
sharper objective.
\Cref{cor:soft-renyi-cover-assignment-hardening} hardens this further from
soft memberships to one deterministic assignment: if the marginal child loads of
a certified soft cover have Renyi price at most the parent price, Jensen gives a
hard assigned cover satisfying the same closure criterion.
\Cref{lem:reduced-gain-quotient-refinement} and
\cref{cor:low-spread-quotient-closure} prove the same statement directly for
positive reduced-gain quotient columns in the finite dense/spherical LP, so the
spread obstruction is not tied to one Hall-shadow normal form.
\Cref{cor:quotient-spread-packing-entropy} then extracts a separated packing
from any quotient that survives all smaller-radius children, giving the
tuple-profile entropy side a concrete witness to charge.
\Cref{cor:inherited-activation-renyi-center-law} is the same handoff in the
same-activation branch with the unbalanced cell masses preserved: every failed
point-centered cover yields a separated center law of large Renyi effective
support, and one dyadic level gives a uniform subpacking with only logarithmic
loss if the later screen needs uniform centers.
\Cref{cor:weighted-gaussian-paid-fiber-separator} removes that need on the
Gaussian paid-fiber side itself: the paid-product moment, active-load monitor,
and high-correlation prefix price may all be computed against the weighted center
law directly.
\Cref{cor:weighted-margin-tail-obstruction} is the corresponding no-prefix
normal form.  Once \(A_\lambda\) is a constant fraction of paid mass and inherited
high-correlation price is a strict fraction of \(A_\lambda\), survival forces
both \(\bar p_\lambda\) and \(P_Y/B_Y\) to be large.
\Cref{cor:bipartite-paid-transport-spread-handoff} and
\cref{cor:transport-gaussian-paid-fiber-separator} give the assigned-cover
variant needed to avoid a false product-law bottleneck: transported weights
\(w_{x,y}\le b(y)\) preserve the same inherited-prefix charging, and an assigned
near-center map \(c(y)\) supplies \(A_w\ge aB_w\) from the pointwise
co-activation lower bound on \((c(y),y)\).
\Cref{cor:assigned-gaussian-transport-lower-bound} gives a concrete sufficient
version of that pointwise condition from \(\ip{c(y)}{y}\ge\theta_->0\) and
bounded margins.
\Cref{cor:upper-margin-assigned-transport-load} then checks the quantity that
matters for the retained filter cover: under an upper margin cutoff
\(M=O(\sqrt{\log\log n})\), the transported endpoint active loads normalized by
the assigned hit mass \(A_w\) are only \(\log^{O_c(1)}n\).
\Cref{cor:bounded-margin-assigned-truncation} makes the residual explicit: if
too little paid mass lies below that cutoff, then almost all assigned mass is on
a high-margin center or paid endpoint.
\Cref{cor:high-margin-assigned-prefix-spread} removes the remaining ambiguity:
that high-margin complement either contains a positive inherited finite-prefix
repair inside one assigned cell, or it is a high-Renyi-spread assigned cover
residual.
\Cref{cor:assigned-gaussian-transport-trichotomy} makes this the formal branch
rule: upper-margin assigned mass gives the desired inverse-polylogarithmic
Gaussian handoff, a finite prefix closes immediately, and the only surviving
case is the priced high-margin Renyi-cover residual.  The unresolved content is
therefore the geometric construction of assigned transports with query-local
certificates, plus the existing Renyi-spread/list-decoding payment for the
priced complement.
\Cref{cor:assigned-high-margin-storage-split} records why this is a query-side
obligation: once the high-margin cells are deterministically assigned, their
recursive storage is subadditive and the surviving residual must appear as
large Renyi query price.
\Cref{cor:assigned-high-margin-endpoint-split} adds the endpoint accounting:
the paid-high part is already a small one-point paid tail, and the center-high
part carries only a Gaussian-tail fraction of its Renyi query price as active
query load.  \Cref{cor:high-margin-tail-rate-screen} turns this into the
quantitative residual: once inherited high-correlation prefixes are priced, each
restricted endpoint side either has only tail-scale paid-product rate
\(e^{-\Lambda}+\overline\Phi(M)\), or a lower-bound certificate above that rate
forces a positive prefix.
\Cref{cor:high-margin-polylog-exposure-threshold} records the exact scale: for
\(M^2,\Lambda=\Theta(\log\log n)\), an inverse-polylogarithmic combined
paid-product lower bound on the high-margin residual suffices.  The remaining
payment theorem therefore has to produce only that inverse-polylog lower-bound
certificate from the existing list-decoding/entropy-energy witness, or show that
tail-rate activity is already budgeted.
\Cref{cor:two-cutoff-high-margin-window} further localizes this target: a
bounded high-margin window \((M,U]\) is already a usable inverse-polylog
subtransport when it carries inverse-polylog mass, so the genuine hard residual
may be pushed to an arbitrarily chosen very-high cutoff \(U\) within the
\(O(\sqrt{\log\log n})\) margin range.
\Cref{cor:high-margin-margin-ladder} removes the remaining cutoff choice: a
polylogarithmic-size ladder either finds such a bounded window or leaves a
constant fraction of the residual above the final cutoff, where the same
endpoint-tail suppression applies.
\Cref{cor:spread-packing-entropy-energy-screen} records the corresponding
charge: each separated-pair profile is harmless when its intersection energy
dominates its entropy, and otherwise it is the high-correlation dense signal.
\Cref{cor:profile-entropy-local-storage-screen} feeds this charge directly into
the reciprocal-storage endpoint: after dyadic occurrence discounting, a
polylogarithmic number of such harmless profiles closes the low-correlation
storage budget with only an \(O(\log\log n)\) local margin.
\Cref{cor:entropy-deficit-tail-local-storage-screen} is the exact nonuniform
version of the same requirement; the remaining list-decoding theorem can target
an exponential tail for positive entropy deficits rather than a maximum deficit
bound.
\Cref{cor:positive-moment-entropy-deficit-screen} is the averaged version of
that target: bound a positive moment of the normalized entropy excess and pay
the cutoff times the number of subprofiles.
\Cref{cor:renyi-moment-entropy-deficit-screen} is the cutoff-free form: it asks
for a raw \(L_{1+\nu}\) moment of the entropy-deficit weights, exactly the
average Renyi list-decoding estimate suggested by the compressed-bucket route.
\Cref{cor:near-first-moment-entropy-deficit-screen} is the minimal-moment
version: the moment exponent may be taken as
\(1+1/\max\{1,\log|\mathcal H|\}\), so the proof only needs a barely positive
entropy-excess moment rather than a fixed higher moment.
\Cref{cor:variational-near-first-moment-obstruction} is the corresponding
entropy-energy normal form: every failure produces a tilted law on profiles,
and the remaining geometric theorem only has to dominate or repair those laws.
\Cref{cor:gibbs-water-level-storage-screen} removes even that universal
quantifier for a concrete layer: the only law needing attention is the Gibbs
water-level law of the entropy-deficit weights.
\Cref{cor:gibbs-weighted-guard-repair} states the residual after all
Gibbs-weighted dense proposals have been verified: the proof need only rule out
a high-water low-correlation law with no positive guard-credit panel.
\Cref{cor:partition-local-gibbs-residual} lets that proof choose a finite
profile partition first, so the irreducible residual may be assumed to live in
one cell after paying \(J^{1/p}\).
\Cref{cor:count-energy-cell-screen} shows that bounded-range cells reduce this
again to a concrete count-energy violation, the form most compatible with
tuple-profile and range-reporting certificates.
\Cref{cor:singleton-profile-gibbs-residual} gives the most aggressive finite
version: if \(H_i\) is polylogarithmic, the irreducible residual is a single
high-deficit profile with no positive certified guard proposal.
\Cref{cor:singleton-spread-star-repair} reduces that residual to one concrete
price inequality for the profile's certified low part and reported star panel;
failure of the inequality is now the named storage-side theorem to prove.
\Cref{cor:partition-cell-spread-star-repair} gives the non-singleton form of the
same target: for a polylogarithmic reporter partition, prove the class low
envelope plus reported star prices fit the cell water threshold, or obtain a
guard repair.
\Cref{cor:shared-record-partition-cell-compiler} sharpens the target further by
allowing the reported star records to be shared across all profiles in a cell;
the remaining proof should therefore construct shared allocation certificates,
not profilewise duplicate star copies.
\Cref{cor:aggregate-shared-cell-water-budget} first removes the uniform
per-cell budget split.  \Cref{cor:layer-global-shared-record-water} is the
cross-cell charging form, but \cref{cor:no-discount-layer-global-water} shows
that this cannot beat the Gibbs water level in a no-repair residual.  The
current storage target is therefore sharper and simpler: by
\cref{cor:dyadic-top-prefix-water-screen}, either every sorted dyadic prefix
obeys the water envelope and \((GWL2)\) follows, or one materializable prefix
has the count-energy excess that a geometric reporter must repair.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-prefix-spread-star-repair} makes this repair target exact:
absence of a guard repair forces any certified split of that prefix to exceed
the dyadic floor budget through its low envelope plus reported star prices.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-prefix-low-price-residual} is the scalar normal form of that
excess: for any chosen slack, the surviving prefix is either a low-envelope
failure or a recursive star-price failure.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-prefix-high-star-mass} shows that the second branch is a
large certified paid-mass star panel which becomes price-saturated only because
no individual guard record is profitable.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-prefix-shared-capture-compression} is the shared-record normal
form of that branch: every surviving shared capture pays through explicit tail
plus one-time shared recursive price.
\Cref{cor:finite-dyadic-shared-capture-lp} supplies the matching finite
minimax certificate and column-generation oracle, so the high branch can now be
attacked as an ordinary reduced-cost shared-cover problem.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-shared-capture-top-prefix-compiler} is the concrete
cell-search form of this attack: generated clusters, AQ cells, or decoded lists
are useful exactly when their top dual prefix violates the price envelope.
\Cref{cor:generated-cell-dyadic-shared-cover-dichotomy} is the corresponding
global generated-cell dichotomy; the remaining geometry must rule out its
no-cell-dual residual, not an informal branching process.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-dual-mass-low-cover-closure} gives the exact metric-entropy
form of that residual: surviving dual-heavy sets have no compatible low-price
cover by the generated cells.
\Cref{cor:no-cell-dual-entropy-witness} sharpens this to one almost-uniform
dyadic layer, so the remaining separator can be stated as an entropy or
list-decoding theorem for a single weighted layer rather than an arbitrary
weighted mass.
\Cref{cor:no-cell-metric-cover-screen} is the certified-cover bridge: a
low-doubling, range-reporting, additive-code, or lattice/list-decoded cover only
has to materialize generated-template copies for that one layer.
\Cref{cor:low-doubling-no-cell-density-screen} is the corresponding
dimension-density obstruction: a surviving low-doubling layer must have weight
density below the explicit Renyi cover envelope.
\Cref{cor:metric-entropy-hall-shadow-closure} and
\cref{cor:low-doubling-hall-shadow-close} sharpen the remaining geometric
obligation: any positive Hall shadow of certified covering number below
\((\Psi(R)/\Psi(R_\star))^{1/(1-\rho)}\) closes, and in the large-radius regime
any low-doubling shadow of dimension below \(4/(1-\rho)\) closes after a
constant radius drop.  Thus a residual not closed by smaller-radius balls must
be a high-entropy object, which is exactly the kind of residual the spherical
or range/list-decoding side should exploit.
\Cref{cor:low-diameter-query-free-hall-seeding} connects this score to seeded
cluster proposals: a hidden low-diameter positive-gain list is found by
residual or dual weighted cap seeding with the usual \(e^{-\alpha T}\) miss
probability, and by exhaustive center enumeration deterministically.  This is
the precise theorem justified by the empirical success of \(k\)-means-like
centers; the remaining proof obligation is still the geometric existence of
such a compact positive-gain Hall shadow, or an alternate range/list-decoding
certificate.
\Cref{cor:certified-ball-repair-cap-enumerable} shows that, once a candidate
repair is certified by an actual smaller Euclidean ball, compactness is not an
extra assumption: shell normalization turns the ball into a cap around every
resident point it contains.  Thus large build-time enumeration can eliminate
the probabilistic seeding loss for certified ball repairs.
\Cref{cor:tail-deficient-shadow-envelope} rewrites the same residual as a bound
on every searched deficient-shadow threshold layer.
\Cref{cor:two-price-deficient-shadow-screen} records the scale dichotomy left by
such a failure: each threshold layer is blocked either by query price or by
storage price.
\Cref{cor:forbidden-middle-deficient-shadow-scale} turns that dichotomy into the
explicit forbidden middle cardinality interval for every reported threshold.
\Cref{cor:cardinality-net-deficient-shadow-reporter} removes exact cardinalities
from the search: a reported superlevel is rounded down to a retained prefix and
still closes if it lies in the constant-slack forbidden interval.
\Cref{cor:layer-cake-deficient-shadow-reporter} is the corresponding averaged
form for panels or moment bounds on one threshold-height window.
\Cref{cor:integral-deficient-shadow-moment-reporter} is the Lorentz/moment
version for analytic range-reporting or list-decoding estimates.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-window-deficient-shadow-moment-reporter} is the finite
multiscale form, with each height window charged by its own \(J\)-factor.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-window-deficient-shadow-residual-envelope} is the explicit
capped-moment inequality that a geometric theorem must violate.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-log-lorentz-deficient-shadow-separator} is the most concrete
current scalar target: capped deficient-shadow mass must beat a dyadic
cardinality envelope.
\Cref{cor:fractional-log-lorentz-deficient-shadow-panel} is the corresponding
fully fractional target for proposal families.
\Cref{cor:certified-log-lorentz-deficient-shadow-panel} is the reporter-facing
rank-certificate version.
\Cref{cor:mass-support-log-lorentz-certificate} is the corresponding
three-scalar container certificate.
\Cref{cor:average-density-mass-support-screen} is the scale-free density form
of the same certificate.
\Cref{cor:balanced-average-density-screen} reduces the balanced case to a
single mixed density threshold at the stationary support scale.
\Cref{cor:balanced-top-prefix-density-screen} gives the sharper materialized
prefix form and trims oversized coarse reports to the same stationary scale.
\Cref{cor:fixed-threshold-balanced-density-screen} records the resulting direct
mixed-density threshold.
\Cref{cor:fractional-fixed-threshold-density-panel} gives the corresponding
finite proposal-law surplus test.
\Cref{cor:sampled-fixed-threshold-density-search} says that this test can be
met by expensive build-time sampling from any positive-margin panel law; the
sampled panels are discarded after one deterministic closing record is
certified.
\Cref{cor:fixed-threshold-hall-deficit-oracle} then replaces the lower-hull
Hall repair law by the single fixed-threshold density-panel obligation on the
exposed positive-excess Hall shadow.
\Cref{cor:single-record-fixed-threshold-hall-separator} sharpens this to a
one-record target: positive fixed-threshold surplus need only be certified for
one balanced prefix or one coarse report with an available balanced trim.
\Cref{cor:fixed-threshold-hall-deficit-polylog-endpoint} is the corresponding
global endpoint: if this fixed-threshold Hall-deficit separator is available at
every resident node, the fractional filter-cover induction gives
\(d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n\) query time and
\(dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n\) space.
\Cref{cor:flow-value-hall-deficit-oracle} and
\cref{cor:flow-value-hall-deficit-polylog-endpoint} replace the
fixed-threshold density target by the exact max-flow reduced-gain target
\((FVS1)\).
\Cref{cor:shadow-mass-hall-deficit-oracle} and
\cref{cor:shadow-mass-hall-deficit-polylog-endpoint} collapse the unrestricted
congestion parameter from this statement.  This is the cleanest current
Hall-deficit endpoint: prove that every exposed positive-excess shadow has one
affordable subset whose deficient-shadow mass beats recursive price.
\Cref{cor:finite-prefix-hall-deficit-polylog-endpoint} is the sharper endpoint
matching the current bottleneck: it is enough to produce one positive
finite-prefix record for the weighted demand system
\((\mathcal N_{G'},\widehat\gamma,\widehat\tau)\), possibly through the
random-list criterion above, and the same
\(d\,n^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n\) query and
\(dn+n^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}n\) space bounds follow.
\Cref{cor:pair-compatible-hall-guarded-cover} states the final local theorem
target in this language: prove the Hall expansion and the resulting
direct mixed-density repair inequality for every guarded residual.
\Cref{lem:tuple-witness-distinct-child-tail} and
\cref{cor:tuple-profile-distinct-storage} reduce each dyadic count to tuple
incidence: a large separated child contains many ordered witness tuples, so the
storage proof can be stated as an entropy-energy bound on how often a tuple
profile can appear in distinct canonical children.  The storage side is
therefore a distinct-net geometric target.
\Cref{lem:multiplicity-discounted-tuple-witness} adds the quotient
normalization needed for occurrence-style analyses: if many decoded records
induce the same canonical child, each record contributes only the reciprocal of
that child's multiplicity to the tuple incidence.  Thus a list-decoding or
range-reporting proof may bound multiplicity-discounted occurrence energy,
which is exactly the shared-DAG storage quantity.
\Cref{lem:occurrence-moments-dominate-dag},
\cref{lem:packing-list-tuple-moment},
\cref{lem:gaussian-cap-intersection-energy}, and
\cref{cor:tuple-profile-renyi-certificate} give a sufficient occurrence
co-load route: count separated tuples in a bucket and subtract their Gaussian
cap-intersection energy.  The actual shared-DAG theorem is weaker still,
because it charges each distinct canonical bucket net once and charges
occurrence multiplicity only as metadata.  Thus the remaining theorem for this
route is a distinct-net entropy-energy inequality for separated spherical
buckets.  \Cref{lem:positive-correlation-occurrence-obstruction} shows that
occurrence co-load is only a sufficient certificate and is false as a final
worst-case target in positive-correlation tangent caps.

For the randomized cap-thinning route, one remaining task is the branching first-split work estimate in \cref{asm:mixed-continuation-operator}: prove that the thinned geometric child potentials contract over random cap-discovery frontiers without replacing the branching decoder by a normalized path law. The newer budget-thinned variant proves the expected work bound from a canonical prefix supermartingale and packages the remaining near-side issue as \cref{asm:aggregate-value-delivery}: prove that the saturated value, or equivalently every route-cut prefix mass, is inverse-polylogarithmic rather than tracking a product along one distinguished path. For laminar route tries, \cref{lem:lca-value-flow} turns the second-moment version into the concrete LCA target
\[
   V(\varnothing)\ge\log^{-O_c(1)}n,
   \qquad
   \sum_uA(u)V(u)^2
   \le
   \log^{O_c(1)}n\,V(\varnothing)^2 .
\]
\Cref{lem:local-lca-energy} further reduces this to a local Bellman multiplier, and \cref{cor:square-nonexpansive-routes} shows that square-nonexpansive value branching costs only the polylogarithmic route depth. Equivalently, \cref{lem:energy-spine-toll} says that it is enough to prove only $O_c(\log\log n)$ positive square-energy toll along the energy-biased route spine. The capped-flow certificate \cref{lem:unit-capped-value-flow}, the Bellman recursion \cref{lem:saturated-value-recursion}, and the min-cut dual \cref{lem:saturated-value-mincut} give a still simpler sufficient formulation: prove that every route cut has inverse-polylogarithmic prefix-success mass. The equivalent dominated-law form in \cref{lem:dominated-route-law} says to construct a tilted law on tame routes whose prefix probabilities are dominated by activation prefix masses up to a polylogarithmic factor; by \cref{cor:typical-route-law-toll}, it is enough to prove only $O_c(\log\log n)$ expected positive domination toll under that route law and prune the bad tail. The cut-energy form \cref{lem:cut-energy-route-law} is closer to stopping-time proofs: it asks only for polylogarithmic $\sum_{u\in\mathcal C}\Lambda(u)^2/A(u)$ on each route cut $\mathcal C$. By \cref{lem:frontier-square-toll}, this is equivalent to bounding the positive square toll of the square-biased route spine up to each stopped frontier, with no all-prefix depth summation. The stronger all-prefix bound in \cref{cor:route-law-prefix-energy} remains an LCA-compatible sufficient condition. \Cref{lem:unit-success-skeleton-contraction} contracts ordinary score-only regions into additive harmonic resistance, so the remaining value theorem can be stated on the skeleton of genuinely thinned opportunities. The finite accepted-route certificate of \cref{prop:accepted-route-certificates-imply-value} is the computable version: a decoded route trie with a superharmonic antichain potential and transition-aware water-filled allocation already implies \cref{asm:aggregate-value-delivery}. The boosted leader skeleton certificate \cref{cor:boosted-leader-skeleton-value-delivery} gives the positive construction path after the full balanced-prefix antichain barrier: quotient posterior handoffs by verified leaders until each nonunit skeleton state has almost-unit useful outgoing affinity. Conditional on either aggregate value statement, \cref{prop:budget-thinned-polylog} gives the desired polylogarithmic ANN theorem. This is a fully non-channel route; the smooth product terminal filter can be used after localization and no longer contributes an inverse-polylogarithmic table-recall penalty. The structured posterior route replaces the cap-frontier obstacle by the tilted witness-list target \cref{asm:smoothed-witness-list}: prove a compact reporter whose verified candidate list contains the true near point with constant mass under the query-centered tilted Gaussian law. The rate-coverage panel \cref{asm:rate-coverage-panel} is the most concrete facility version of this target: a multi-assignment scheme is certified by the closed-form miss term \(\exp(-a_p\mu_p(B))\), the reported-load bound, and the total replication budget. The stronger max-tilted sampler \cref{asm:alpha-leader-sampler} and nearest-cell decoder \cref{asm:smoothed-nearest-cell} remain clean implementation normal forms, but k-means++-style or lattice/code buckets only need the rate-coverage certificates. The smoothed sampling route replaces both by \cref{asm:smoothed-gibbs} or \cref{asm:gumbel-mips}: prove either an optimal-exponent reporter that captures inverse-polylogarithmic Gaussian Gibbs mass, or a certified $O(\log\log n)$-additive Gumbel-MIPS primitive. Smoothed additive nearest neighbor is another stronger sufficient primitive. The detector-vote cohort-or-leaf route is a separate possible generalization to arbitrary certified child hierarchies, where the remaining issue is near-lineage coupling between ordinary continuation paths and detector activations.
\Cref{cor:affinity-proportional-route-law} gives the cleanest current
list-decoding interpretation of the posterior handoff: once the reporter
decodes an outgoing port list, branch by local affinity and pay only the
cumulative deficit in the list's total affinity.  Thus the score-tree/lattice
analogy has become a concrete theorem target: prove that the decoded port
lists have inverse-polylogarithmic affinity across every skeleton cut.

\appendix

\section{More detail on the spherical exponent calculation}

For completeness, we verify the algebra leading to $\rho(a,b)$. Let $B$ be the branching factor and $\ell_B=\log B$. With
\[
   t^2=(1+a)\ell_B
\]
and
\[
   k=
   \frac{2(1+b)\log m}
   {(1+a)(1-b)\ell_B}
   +O(1),
\]
the expected number of accepting leaves for one point has logarithm
\begin{align*}
   k\ell_B-\frac{kt^2}{2}+O(\log k)
                                                                                                                  &=
                                                                                                                  \frac{k\ell_B(1-a)}{2}+O(\log k)\\
                                                                                                                                                                                                 &=
                                                                                                                                                                                                 \frac{(1-a)(1+b)}{(1+a)(1-b)}\log m+O(\log\log m).
\end{align*}
Thus it equals
\[
   m^{\rho(a,b)}\log^{O(1)}m.
\]

For a pair of correlation at most $b$, the expected number of common accepting leaves has logarithm at most
\begin{align*}
   k\ell_B-\frac{kt^2}{1+b}
                                                                                                                  &=
                                                                                                                  k\ell_B\left(1-\frac{1+a}{1+b}\right)\\
                                                                                                                                                                                                 &=-\frac{k\ell_B(a-b)}{1+b}\\
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           &=-\frac{2(a-b)}{(1+a)(1-b)}\log m+O(1).
\end{align*}
A direct calculation shows
\[
   1-\rho(a,b)
   =
   \frac{2(a-b)}{(1+a)(1-b)}.
\]
Hence one ordinary far point contributes at most
\[
   m^{-(1-\rho(a,b))}\log^{O(1)}m
\]
common leaves, and all $m$ ordinary far points contribute at most
\[
   m^{\rho(a,b)}\log^{O(1)}m.
\]

\section{Bellman cancellation algebra}

We record the cancellation with no surrounding notation. Let $s=1-\rho$, let a parent contain $m$ points in radius $R$, and let a child have relative size $\alpha$ and relative radius $\lambda$. With
\[
   F(m,R)=m^\rho\left(\frac Rr\right)^{2s}
\]
and activation threshold $\tau=\lambda^2$, the first-hit bound charges at most $(\alpha/\lambda^2)^s$ query mass to the child. The recursive charge is therefore
\begin{align*}
   \left(\frac{\alpha}{\lambda^2}\right)^s
   F(\alpha m,\lambda R)
   &=
   \alpha^s\lambda^{-2s}
   \alpha^\rho m^\rho
   \lambda^{2s}\left(\frac Rr\right)^{2s}\\
   &=
   \alpha F(m,R).
\end{align*}
Thus the radius improvement pays exactly for the posterior threshold, and disjoint children sum to at most the parent potential.

\section{Bibliographic note}

The one-sided spherical proof is motivated by the Ahle--Knudsen manuscript supplied with this project, but it uses continuation mass and an analytical upper barrier instead of the two-sided tube proof there. The score-and-ball tree follows the geometric ideas of Andoni and Razenshteyn while replacing dense-cap restart accounting by randomized cap thinning inside one cumulative score process. The local Bellman-game viewpoint is inspired by the robust learned hashing framework of Andoni and Beaglehole. The posterior-cohort route is retained as a possible extension to more general certified child hierarchies.
